alex-getting-started.job: onboard owner and capture working preferences
alex-getting-started.summary: First-run onboarding for Alex: a brief hello, one 'what and for whom' question played back as a problem statement, an immediate jump into real work, skippable one-at-a-time preference questions saved to memory, a connection check, a starter menu, opt-in routines, and a human-style 30/60/90 arc.
strengths: Starts the real deliverable immediately and treats every question as skippable. That avoids the usual onboarding interrogation.
The two-line problem-statement playback is cheap, useful, and catches a wrong read early.
Saves one fact per line to named memory keys, including the decision maker who gates every commitment.
Routines stay off until the user says yes, run in the user's timezone, and stage drafts rather than sending.
A paste or CSV fallback means a missing connector never blocks work.
missing: Explicit handoff lines for off-edge requests (code, design mockups, closing deals) at first contact
A way to show the saved preference block and let the owner correct it
A rule for reading existing workspace files (old PRDs, roadmaps) before asking
A fallback when the owner gives only a company name and no product line

issues.quote: Week one runs day by day: stakeholder one-on-ones, a buddy from day one, use
issues.problem: This is a human PM new-hire onboarding plan (30/60/90, buddy, one-on-ones, 'use the product like a customer every day'). It doesn't fit an AI teammate. A model following it will tell the owner it needs a buddy and meetings, which costs credibility and bloats the first message.
issues.fix: Delete the arc. If an arc is wanted, replace it with a concrete first-week deliverable list tied to the starter menu and the routines the owner switched on.

issues.quote: Look at what is connected before you ask for anything, and tell them what is
issues.problem: The section says 'first' but comes after 'Ask the rest one at a time'. A model that follows headings in order asks 'where do specs live' and 'where do numbers live' before it checks Notion, Sheets or Linear, which breaks 'never re-ask'.
issues.fix: Move this section above the question list and say plainly: skip any question a connected source already answers.

issues.quote: The saved preference block, what you found connected, and a first real
issues.problem: The first message must hold the preference block, the connection report, a deliverable, a five-item menu, three routine offers and a 90-day arc. That contradicts the persona's 'answer first and stays brief' voice and buries the deliverable.
issues.fix: Set a message order and cap: deliverable first, then one line on connections, then the menu. Offer routines only after the first deliverable lands.

issues.quote: timezone, and stages a draft rather than sending anything. Save the timezone
issues.problem: The timezone is a skippable question, but routines can't be offered until it is saved. There's no fallback when it is skipped.
issues.fix: When the timezone is unset at the routine offer, ask once, or propose a timezone inferred from context and confirm it.

issues.quote: and their product analytics stay outside the connectors: read exports, links,
issues.problem: This is too absolute. The owner may have connected a Figma, PostHog, Amplitude or Mixpanel MCP server that run_mcp_tool can reach. Also, Linear is pushed as 'the one worth doing' but is missing from the persona's list of sources to check.
issues.fix: Check the MCP connections for design and analytics tools first, and fall back to exports only when none exist. Keep the connector list in line with the persona.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Alex, we're a 6-person B2B SaaS doing invoice automation for agencies. Here's our backlog CSV. Where do we start?
scenarios.why: The good parts work. 'Ask one thing first' gives a sharp problem-statement playback, and 'Start the first real item at once' sends it to backlog scoring. But the Output section also requires the preference block, the connection report and a 30/60/90 arc with 'a buddy from day one' and 'stakeholder one-on-ones' in the same message, so the first reply is bloated and partly nonsensical for an AI teammate.

scenarios.prompt: I don't want a questionnaire. Our numbers are in Mixpanel, which you can't reach, there's no roadmap doc, and I just need to know whether to build a Slack integration next.
scenarios.why: 'When they skip everything' and 'Start the first real item at once' drop the questions and do the work. The Mixpanel gap becomes an export or paste request rather than a blocker. One nit: the timezone stays unset, so the rule to save it before offering routines quietly blocks the routine offer with no fallback.

product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals.job: scope AI feature and design evals
product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals.summary: Scopes an AI or agent feature by playing back the job and its harm, building a 12-20 prompt eval set, defining a four-rung quality ladder with examples, grading captured outputs, scoring over three runs, and specifying the quality, latency, cost and safety trade-offs and RAG behaviour.
strengths: Builds the prompt set before any talk of which model to use. This is the right order.
The four-rung ladder with a required example per rung makes grading concrete.
'Capture before you judge' with exact quotes blocks grading from memory.
Explicitly handles retrieval returning nothing relevant.
A hard refusal to quote any quality number that was not measured, and a human gate on high-harm outputs.
missing: Error analysis and failure taxonomy workflow
LLM-as-judge calibration against human labels
Baseline comparison (current non-AI flow or previous model)
Online evaluation and production drift monitoring
Eval-plan and scoreboard template
PII handling for eval datasets and AI disclosure requirements
Agent trajectory and tool-use evaluation

issues.quote: Build the prompt set first: twelve to twenty prompts across the real kinds
issues.problem: 12-20 prompts over four kinds gives 3-5 per cell. 'Counts by rung broken down by prompt kind' then has no power to detect a regression. Nothing seeds the set from real traffic or grows it through error analysis of failures.
issues.fix: Seed 30-50 cases from real or expected inputs. Grow the set by open-coding failures into a failure taxonomy, set a minimum per slice, and report counts with uncertainty.

issues.quote: Capture before you judge: collect the model's exact outputs first, then
issues.problem: The skill never says who runs the model or how outputs arrive. The sandbox has no user secrets. Nor does it say who grades: if Alex grades, that is an uncalibrated LLM judge with no check against human labels.
issues.fix: Say that outputs come from the owner or engineering as a CSV or harness export. Have the owner hand-label a sample, measure grader agreement with those labels, and only then scale up LLM grading.

issues.quote: three-run trend rule. One run is noise; three runs is a read.
issues.problem: It is ambiguous whether this means three samples of the same config (nondeterminism) or three successive releases. Either way, three runs doesn't establish a difference between versions.
issues.fix: Define both: N samples per prompt at a pinned model, temperature and prompt version, and a paired comparison between versions with a stated decision threshold.

issues.section: When the outputs are not measured
issues.problem: No privacy or regulatory guardrails. Real user inputs copied into eval sets can carry PII. There is no AI-disclosure or sector-rule check (e.g. EU AI Act transparency, regulated advice) and no fairness slice across user groups.
issues.fix: Add rules: redact or synthesize PII in eval data, flag disclosure and regulatory checks to the owner or legal, and include demographic or segment slices where outputs affect people.

issues.quote: Use this when the user names an AI feature, an agent, a prompt, retrieval, evals,
issues.problem: On AutoGPT, 'agent' and 'prompt' are everyday words, because users build agents on the platform. The trigger will fire on requests to write a prompt or build an AutoGPT agent, which are not product eval scoping.
issues.fix: Narrow the trigger to scoping or measuring an AI feature in the owner's product, and exclude building or configuring agents on the platform itself.

issues.quote: Spec the trade-offs: quality against latency, cost per task, and safety.
issues.problem: There is nothing agent-specific: no task-success or trajectory and tool-call evaluation, no prompt-injection or data-exfiltration red team for tool-using agents, and no production monitoring or sampling after launch.
issues.fix: Add an agent branch (task success, tool-call correctness, injection red-team) and a post-launch step that samples live traffic into the eval set.

issues.quote: prompt changes. Point at an existing open-source eval harness for the running
issues.problem: There is no template for the eval plan or scoreboard, no example harness named, and no requirement to record model id, version and settings on the board.
issues.fix: Ship a scoreboard template (prompt, kind, rung, quote, model/version, run). Name example harnesses (promptfoo, Inspect, DeepEval) as options, not requirements.

scenarios.prompt: We're adding an AI summary of support tickets for our human agents. Scope it and set up evals before we pick a model.
scenarios.why: The steps produce a credible v0: the job and its harm playback (step 1), a varied prompt set with must-not-regress items (step 2), the ladder with examples (step 3), and the latency, cost and safety trade-offs (step 6). A senior would push for a bigger set, but as a starting plan this is sound.

scenarios.prompt: Our RAG support bot got worse after we switched models. I have 300 logged conversations in a CSV plus the thumbs-down rate. Is the new model actually worse?
scenarios.why: The skill steers toward building a fresh 12-20 prompt set instead of mining the 300 production logs. It gives no paired old-versus-new comparison method, no statistical test, and no calibration for the grader (Alex grading its own outputs). 'Three runs is a read' doesn't answer a regression question. The refusal to quote unmeasured numbers does hold.

product-discovery-and-user-research.job: plan user research and synthesize feedback themes
product-discovery-and-user-research.summary: Plans user research around one question with a story-opener interview guide and screener, or synthesizes transcripts into count-ranked themes led by verbatim quotes mapped onto an opportunity-solution tree with a roadmap verdict per theme, plus a weekly voice-of-customer rollup mode.
strengths: Forces one outcome and one question per study and asks what a yes or no would each change.
The interview craft is right: a 'tell me about the last time' story opener, probes instead of a question list, no leading questions, no pitching mid-call, and a pilot of the guide.
Keeps verbatims with speaker, role and date, and keeps numbers separate with their period.
Maps themes onto an outcome-opportunity-solution-assumption tree.
Gives every theme a verdict, keeps a dedupe log, a quiet week gets one line, and it refuses a verdict on a thin sample.
missing: Consent, recording and PII redaction rules
Segment and severity weighting in theme ranking
Survey design and analysis guidance
Said-versus-did triangulation with behavioural or quant data
Interview guide, screener and synthesis templates
Jobs-to-be-done framing option

issues.section: Plan it, run it, mine it
issues.quote: Mine for themes. Rank by count, lead each theme with the two or three
issues.problem: Ranking by frequency alone lets a loud low-value segment outrank a severe problem in the target segment or a large account.
issues.fix: Rank by frequency × severity × segment fit (ICP, plan, revenue at stake). Tag each quote with its segment and show the weighting.

issues.section: Plan it, run it, mine it
issues.quote: Work transcripts one at a time: verbatim quotes with speaker, role, and
issues.problem: Named verbatims are saved to files with no consent, recording-consent, redaction or retention guidance. That is a privacy risk, especially under GDPR, or when quotes flow into exec briefs.
issues.fix: Require documented consent and a recording notice in the plan. Pseudonymize speakers in saved notes unless the owner approves names, and never export quotes externally without a yes.

issues.quote: No users to reach means you draft the recruiting ask and
issues.problem: Recruiting outreach, intercepts and calendar invites reach real customers, but the skill has no draft-then-approve gate before anything is sent. The persona forbids contacting customers without a yes.
issues.fix: State that recruiting emails, intercepts and invites are drafts. Nothing goes to a user without the owner's yes, and incentives need owner sign-off.

issues.quote: Use this when the user names interviews, user research, a survey, a beta, or a
issues.problem: The description promises surveys and betas, but the procedure only covers interviews and transcript synthesis. There is no survey design (sampling, question bias, response rate), no open-text coding at scale, and no beta program structure.
issues.fix: Add a short survey branch and a beta branch, possibly in references/, or drop them from the trigger.

issues.section: Plan it, run it, mine it
issues.quote: the guide on one or two sessions, then run thirty to sixty minutes with a
issues.problem: Alex can't run a live interview, and the skill never says who interviews, whether Alex works from recordings, or how debriefs flow back. 'Keep recruiting self-scheduling' is advice with no action behind it.
issues.fix: Say the owner or team runs the sessions. Alex supplies the guide, a note-taking template and a same-day debrief format.

issues.section: Plan it, run it, mine it
issues.quote: Three accounts saying it is a pattern; one is an anecdote.
issues.problem: A fixed threshold ignores sample size and segment. The thin-sample refusal asks for 'how many more conversations' but gives no method.
issues.fix: Use saturation (no new codes over the last N sessions per segment) and state the confidence alongside the count.

issues.quote: The interview plan or the dated theme brief, with the roadmap verdict on each
issues.problem: There is no template for the screener, the interview guide or the synthesis table, so output structure varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the screener, the guide (opener, probes, wrap-up) and the theme table (theme, count, segments, quotes, verdict).

scenarios.prompt: Plan 8 interviews with customers who churned after trial so we learn why they left.
scenarios.why: Step 1 forces one question and what a yes or no would change. Step 2 gives a screener, a story opener ('tell me about the last time you...'), probes, no leading questions and a pilot. A senior researcher would accept the plan, though it arrives without a consent script or note template.

scenarios.prompt: Here are 40 NPS verbatims, 6 support tickets and 2 call transcripts, mixed from free users and our biggest account. What should go on the roadmap?
scenarios.why: Step 4 ranks by count and treats three accounts as a pattern, so 30 free-user comments outrank the biggest account's churn risk. There is no segment or revenue weighting, no method for mixing survey text with transcripts, and no redaction of named speakers before quotes are saved. The verdicts and thin-sample refusal still work.

product-exec-briefing.job: write executive or board product briefing
product-exec-briefing.summary: Writes an exec, board or steering brief for one named room: a three-line narrative spine, a KPI scorecard graded against target with sources and owned misses, roadmap changes mapped to the room's goals, risks with contingencies, and asks with owners and dates, drafted for approval.
strengths: Forces one audience and names what that room must leave believing or approving.
A three-line narrative spine comes before any section.
Every number is sourced, every miss is owned with a fix beside it, and roadmap changes are never reordered silently.
Visible [need this] gaps with the name of whoever fills each one, instead of invented numbers.
Drafts only, and nothing goes out before the owner approves it.
missing: Options, recommendation and cost-of-delay block for decisions
Anticipated-questions / Q&A prep
Audience variants for board versus exec versus steering, with confidentiality
Post-meeting recap step
Pre-read length rule and template
Handoff to finance or IR for board numbers

issues.quote: Name the risks with a contingency on each, and the asks with owners and
issues.problem: Decision asks get owners and dates but no options-with-recommendation structure (options, trade-offs, recommendation, cost of delay). There is also no Q&A prep for likely challenges, which is the core of a senior exec brief.
issues.fix: For each decision, add a block: 2-3 options, their trade-offs, a recommendation and the cost of not deciding. Add an anticipated-questions appendix.

issues.quote: Use this when the user names an exec review, a board update, a steering
issues.problem: A board update is handled like an internal review. There is no board altitude (strategy and risk, not features), no confidentiality or material-information handling, and no coordination with finance or IR for board numbers.
issues.fix: Add audience variants: exec, board, steering. For board packs, consult the finance or IR teammate and mark the material confidential.

issues.quote: The dated brief or deck outline, with the pre-read and the recap saved beside
issues.problem: No step produces the recap: capturing decisions, owners and follow-ups after the meeting. The output also has no length rule or template for the brief or the deck outline.
issues.fix: Add a post-meeting step that records decisions, owners and dates against the asks. Ship a one-page pre-read template and a slide-outline template.

issues.quote: Ask who is in the room and what they must leave believing or approving. A
issues.problem: It stops at the room as a whole. There's no per-attendee map of what each exec cares about or will object to, and no pre-wiring of key stakeholders before the meeting.
issues.fix: Add a short stakeholder map (person, stake, likely objection) and suggest pre-wiring the decision owner before the meeting.

issues.quote: Grade the scorecard: each KPI against target with a one-line why. Every
issues.problem: No instruction to keep the same KPI set as the last dated brief, which the persona requires to stop bad metrics being dropped, or to compute deltas in the sandbox from the connected sheet.
issues.fix: Compare against the previous saved brief, keep a fixed KPI table, and compute deltas with bash_exec from the sourced data.

scenarios.prompt: Monthly exec review Thursday with the CEO and CTO. Here's the KPI sheet and our roadmap. Draft the pre-read.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-5 give an audience-first spine, a graded scorecard with sources, roadmap changes with reasons, risks with contingencies and dated asks, delivered as a draft. That is a usable pre-read, though its length and structure aren't specified.

scenarios.prompt: Board meeting in 3 days and I need the product section. Half the metrics are in a Mixpanel I can't export, and the CEO wants to leave out the slipped enterprise launch.
scenarios.why: The skill handles the gaps well ([need this] with named fillers) and the 'never soften a miss' rule. But there's no guidance on board altitude or confidentiality, no coordination with the finance or investor-relations teammate who owns board numbers, and no route for escalating when the CEO asks to hide a miss.

product-experiment-design.job: design A/B test and read results
product-experiment-design.summary: Designs an experiment around one bottleneck belief: it compares candidate tests, fixes one primary metric plus guardrails, sizes the sample from the baseline and MDE at 95% and 80% power, precommits scale, extend and kill bands, then reads out with SRM and guardrail checks.
strengths: One bottleneck belief, with candidate tests compared on information gain, cost, time and reversibility.
One primary metric, mandatory guardrails, pre-declared segments, and a business threshold stated beside the p-value.
Precommitted bands with observable numbers and a ban on moving them after the data lands.
A sample-ratio-mismatch check in the readout.
Honest low-traffic alternatives: a longer run, a bigger effect, a painted door, or a qualitative read.
missing: Quasi-experimental and pre/post method
Sandbox-computed sample size with a shown formula
Randomization unit and cluster handling
Multiple-comparison handling for segments and metrics
Early-stop-for-harm rule
Plan and readout templates
Ethics and legal check for pricing tests

issues.quote: before-and-after read. The output is a plan whose verdict is decided before the
issues.problem: The description and intro promise before-and-after reads, but the procedure covers only randomized A/B. There's no method for non-randomized changes: comparison windows, seasonality, holdouts, diff-in-diff or interrupted time series.
issues.fix: Add a quasi-experimental branch: a matched comparison period, a seasonality check, a holdout where possible, and an explicit statement that causality is weaker.

issues.quote: from the baseline plus the minimum detectable effect at 95% significance
issues.problem: The sample size must be 'computed', but there's no formula, no script and no instruction to use the sandbox. A model doing it mentally will produce wrong numbers that a senior practitioner would catch.
issues.fix: Compute in bash_exec with a stated two-proportion or t-test formula, show every input and label assumptions. Ideally, ship a small scripts/sample_size.py.

issues.quote: Write the design: control and variant; ONE primary success metric;
issues.problem: The unit of randomization is never chosen (user vs account vs workspace), which matters for B2B clustering and interference. There's also no correction for multiple guardrails and segments, and no allowance for novelty or primacy effects.
issues.fix: Require the randomization unit and analysis unit to match. Treat segment reads as exploratory unless corrected, and note novelty-effect checks over the run.

issues.section: When the traffic is not there
issues.quote: test before one to two full weeks and the precomputed sample size.
issues.problem: The blanket rule against calling a test early leaves no pre-declared stop for harm when a guardrail breaches badly mid-run, and it doesn't mention sequential testing when the owner's tool supports it.
issues.fix: Add a precommitted guardrail kill switch that allows an early stop for harm, and allow sequential methods only when declared up front.

issues.quote: Precommit the interpretation bands with observable numbers: the upgrade band
issues.problem: There is no template for the plan or the readout, so bands, guardrails and the call vary in format between runs and can't be compared against the last saved plan.
issues.fix: Ship plan and readout templates (belief, metric, guardrails, unit, sample, duration, bands, result, call).

issues.problem: No ethics or legal check for experiments on pricing, dark patterns or regulated flows. Price tests can raise fairness or consumer-law issues.
issues.fix: Flag pricing and consent-flow experiments for owner or legal review before launch.

scenarios.prompt: We want to test a new onboarding checklist. About 4,000 signups a week with a 22% activation baseline. Design the A/B test.
scenarios.why: Step 3 sets activation as the primary metric, adds guardrails, sizes the sample from the 22% baseline and an MDE at 95% and 80% power, runs at least one to two weeks, and pre-declares segments. Step 4 precommits the bands. A capable model produces a senior-grade plan, though it may do the sample-size arithmetic in its head.

scenarios.prompt: We're B2B with about 150 new accounts a month, and we already shipped the new pricing page last Tuesday. Did it work?
scenarios.why: This is a before-and-after read on a change that already shipped, with very low traffic. The traffic fallback suggests a longer run, a painted door or a qualitative read, but the skill has no pre/post method (seasonality, a comparison period, diff-in-diff, a holdout) and no guidance on account-level units. The model will either refuse or improvise.

product-launch-plan.job: plan product launch with go/no-go gate
product-launch-plan.summary: Plans a release: it sizes the launch tier, writes a messaging doc including what not to claim, packs sales enablement, back-plans every asset with an owner and date, holds a concrete go/no-go gate including a rollback plan, and sets a 30/60/90-day measure and retrospective.
strengths: Tier sizing on revenue, competitive shift and press-worthiness sets the effort level, and the skill states why that tier was chosen.
The messaging doc includes 'what you will not claim' and takes one round of edits before anything is built on it.
A concrete go/no-go gate (support briefed, legal vetted, pricing signed off, rollback plan) where anything untrue blocks launch.
Splits the ship date from the launch date, and an unapproved date stays 'proposed', not committed.
Per-asset approval before publishing, and live deals stay with sales.
missing: Pricing-change branch (notice, grandfathering, billing, legal)
Staged rollout and feature-flag plan
Customer comms for breaking changes and migrations
Pre-launch baseline capture for the 90-day measure
Marketing and comms handoff for tentpole launches
Checklist, RACI and gate template
Sourcing rule for ROI math

issues.quote: Use this when the user names a release, a launch date, a pricing change, or
issues.problem: The skill triggers on pricing changes but treats them as one gate line. There's no existing-customer notice, grandfathering, billing-system change, contract or notice-period check, or churn-risk read.
issues.fix: Add a pricing-change branch covering customer notice timing, grandfathering, billing migration, finance and legal sign-off, and a churn watch. Or route it to a pricing or finance teammate.

issues.quote: answer why us and why now, and the ROI math. Live deals stay with sales —
issues.problem: ROI math is the most likely place for invented numbers. There's no rule to source the inputs or label assumptions, even though the persona requires FACT, INFERENCE and UNKNOWN labels.
issues.fix: Build ROI only from customer-sourced or owner-given inputs, compute it in the sandbox, and label every assumption.

issues.quote: to watch. Then run it — ship the assets, keep the checklist current, report
issues.problem: 'Ship the assets' reads as permission to publish, which conflicts with the per-asset approval rule at the bottom. The 30/60/90 reports have no baseline captured before launch and no scheduling mechanism.
issues.fix: Say 'stage each asset for approval'. Capture baselines before launch and set the 30/60/90 reads with schedule_followup.

issues.quote: Size the tier first: net-new revenue, competitive shift, and
issues.problem: Tiering ignores customer impact and risk. Breaking changes, migrations or deprecations need customer comms and docs even when a launch is quiet. Staged rollout (flags, beta cohort, % ramp) is also absent.
issues.fix: Add a customer-impact/risk axis, a staged-rollout plan, and docs, changelog and in-app comms to the asset list.

issues.quote: tentpole gets all of that plus an event, press, and a paid plan drafted for
issues.problem: Events, press and paid media are marketing and comms work. The skill has Alex draft them with no consult or handoff to the marketing teammate, which blurs the edges between experts.
issues.fix: Have Alex own the plan, positioning and gate, and consult or delegate campaign, press and paid execution to the marketing or comms expert.

issues.quote: The dated launch plan: tier and why, messaging doc, enablement pack,
issues.problem: There is no template for the back-planned checklist (asset, owner, due, status, approval) or the gate, so plans vary in shape and can't be tracked week to week.
issues.fix: Ship a checklist and gate template, optionally as a Google Sheet via run_block.

scenarios.prompt: We ship SSO for enterprise workspaces on Nov 12. Plan the launch.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-6 give a two-line playback, a justified tier, a messaging doc with proof points and no-claims, an enablement pack, back-planned owners and dates, the gate list and a 90-day measure, all as drafts. Senior quality for a feature launch.

scenarios.prompt: We're raising Pro prices 20% on Jan 1. Sales is panicking, marketing wants a Product Hunt launch the same week, and legal hasn't reviewed the ToS change.
scenarios.why: The gate catches 'legal vetted' and 'pricing signed off', and the date is carried as proposed. But there's no existing-customer notice period, grandfathering, billing migration or churn-risk plan. There's no way to resolve the clash with marketing's launch or hand off to the marketing teammate, and the 'ROI math' has no sourcing rule.

product-market-and-competitor-read.job: brief competitor moves and pricing changes
product-market-and-competitor-read.summary: Tiers a competitor watch list, logs fetched changelog/pricing/product pages, records linked and dated changes, builds a pricing table from real pages, and translates material moves into owned roadmap implications and graded differentiation bets.
strengths: Hard evidence rule: every change cites a page and read date, and an unlinked claim stays out
Declines the pricing read rather than working from recall when pages are unavailable
Separates a positioning read (launch) from a packaging read (price change) and says 'unclear' plus what would settle it
The quiet-market single line and the no-repeat dedupe discipline
Ticket filing is gated on the owner's yes, one issue per change with link and date
missing: First-run baseline snapshot and change-detection method (saved snapshot or Wayback diff)
Market-brief and pricing-table template
Where the briefed-changes log lives and a step to read it first
Inline A-E evidence-grade definitions
Feature parity/gap matrix
Pricing value-metric and packaging-fence analysis
Review-site, job-posting and win-loss signals
CI ethics and legal limits
Handoff boundary to Zara for battlecards

issues.quote: Record what changed, grouped under each competitor. Every line cites
issues.problem: There is no method to establish that something changed. On a first run, or for pricing and product pages that carry no dates, there is no prior snapshot to diff against, so 'changes' become guesses.
issues.fix: On the first run, save a dated baseline snapshot of each page (to the workspace) and label that run a baseline, not a list of changes. On later runs, diff against the saved snapshot or a Wayback Machine capture, and cite both dates.

issues.quote: A dated market brief with every source linked, plus a running log of the
issues.problem: No brief template is shipped. The running log that prevents re-briefing has no stated home (memory_store or a workspace file), and no step says to read it before writing, so dedupe depends on state the platform may not keep.
issues.fix: Add templates/market-brief.md (coverage line, per-competitor changes, pricing table, implications with owners, bets, source ledger including failures). Add a step 0: read the last brief and the briefed-changes log from the workspace, and write the log back after the brief is saved.

issues.quote: each with its evidence grade (A to E, as in strategy work).
issues.problem: The A-E scale is defined only in product-strategy-and-bets. Loaded on its own, this skill hands the model an undefined grading scheme.
issues.fix: Restate the A-E definitions inline (A payment/repeat usage ... E assertion), or ship them in references/evidence-grades.md and link it by relative path.

issues.quote: Use when the user names competitors, pricing, positioning, a market read, or battlecard input for the roadmap
issues.problem: It promises battlecard input but defines no battlecard-input format, and it overlaps Zara's competitive-intelligence, which owns battlecards. There is no handoff boundary.
issues.fix: Drop 'battlecard' from the description or define the input block (discriminators, proof links). Add a line that sales-facing battlecards go to Zara via consult_teammate/handoff.

issues.quote: a level deeper: strategy shifts, longer trends, and what they imply for the
issues.problem: 'Every so often' sets no cadence and no sections for the deep read, so it will be skipped or improvised.
issues.fix: Make it monthly (or the first run of each planning cycle), with named sections: direction shifts, forming trends, and implications for next quarter's bets.

issues.quote: failed, and that competitor's line is left out rather than filled from
issues.problem: Silently omitting a competitor whose page failed makes 'no section' ambiguous. The reader cannot tell 'did nothing' from 'could not read'.
issues.fix: Add a coverage line listing unread competitors and the failure. Try browser_navigate before giving up, and ask the user for a screenshot or export as the fallback.

issues.problem: The signal sources stop at changelog, pricing and product pages. There are no review sites, job postings, win-loss notes or community chatter, and no tool routing (web_search, web_fetch vs browser for JS-rendered pricing).
issues.fix: Add a sources list by tier and name the tools: web_search to discover, web_fetch for static pages, browser_navigate for JS pricing pages, and Firecrawl/Exa blocks where connected.

issues.problem: There are no competitive-intelligence ethics limits. Nothing forbids pretexting, fake trial sign-ups, reading gated or login-only material, or ignoring site terms.
issues.fix: Add one line: public sources only, no misrepresentation to obtain competitor information, respect robots/ToS, and never use a competitor's confidential material a customer or hire forwards.

scenarios.prompt: Build me a watch list for Linear, Jira and Shortcut and read their pricing pages. I need to decide whether our Team plan should cap seats or projects before Q1.
scenarios.why: Steps 1, 4 and 5 cover this directly: tier the list, build a per-plan table with fetch date and the limits that constrain a buyer, then write a packaging read with a named owner. The 'quote only prices you read on a page' rule stops hallucinated prices.

scenarios.prompt: Competitor X's pricing page now says 'contact sales', their changelog 403s, and our AE says they undercut us 30% on the Acme deal. Did they reprice, and should we respond?
scenarios.why: The skill logs the failed fetch and declines the pricing read, which is correct. It then drops the competitor entirely ('that competitor's line is left out'). It offers no fallback (browser_navigate, a Wayback snapshot, or asking for a screenshot), and it gives no way to grade the AE's anecdote as low-grade evidence or route it to win-loss. The owner gets silence where a labelled UNKNOWN plus a plan to settle it was needed.

product-metrics-and-instrumentation.job: define product metrics and diagnose movement
product-metrics-and-instrumentation.summary: Names a North Star with two or three input drivers, writes an instrumentation spec when events are missing, and reads what moved: it decomposes the headline, scores metrics red/yellow/green with counter-metrics, and closes with a roadmap call.
strengths: A single North Star with 2-3 inputs and a three-part validity check
Counter-metrics and guardrails that catch gaming of the North Star
Explicit refusal of verdicts on thin samples, naming the volume that would settle it
Honest fallback: analytics is not connected, so work from an export, link or paste
Ends in a decision ('or nothing, said plainly') instead of observations
missing: Mode routing between define, spec and diagnose
Ordered movement-diagnosis method (data quality, releases, seasonality, segments, mix vs rate)
Tracking-plan template with naming convention, property types and QA
PII and consent rule for events
Use of bash_exec for computation on exports
Normal-variance or control-band test for 'thin' or 'noise'
Metric definition fields (formula, grain, source, owner)
Handoff to experiment design when causality needs a test

issues.quote: Name the one North Star metric — the single metric that best captures value
issues.problem: Every request is forced through North Star definition first, including a simple 'why did X drop' read. The skill needs to branch between three modes: define metrics, spec instrumentation, diagnose a movement.
issues.fix: Open with a mode switch. Define: North Star tree plus counter-metrics. Spec: tracking plan. Read: movement diagnosis. In Read mode, reuse the saved North Star tree if it exists and skip redefining it.

issues.quote: Read what moved first, then why. Decompose the headline into its drivers
issues.problem: There is no diagnostic method. A senior analyst checks, in order: data and tracking breakage, releases and incidents, calendar or seasonality, then segment cuts and mix-vs-rate before claiming a cause.
issues.fix: Add an ordered diagnosis checklist (in references/ if long). Require bash_exec to compute the segment deltas from the export, and attribute the change to segments with shown arithmetic.

issues.quote: If the events do not exist, write the instrumentation spec: event names,
issues.problem: There is no privacy rule for instrumentation. Nothing prevents emails, names, free text or other PII going into event properties, and nothing mentions consent (GDPR/CCPA) for tracking.
issues.fix: Add: no PII or free text in properties; use IDs only; flag any consent or cookie requirement; route questions to the privacy/compliance teammate.

issues.quote: The dated read saved next to the last one, so every report compares against the
issues.problem: Neither deliverable has a template, and no save location is named (workspace file or Sheets). Output quality will vary run to run and comparison to 'the last one' is not guaranteed.
issues.fix: Ship templates/metrics-read.md (headline, movers, decomposition table, RAG, counter-metrics, call) and templates/tracking-plan.csv (event, trigger, properties+types, owner, platform, QA status). Name the workspace path.

issues.quote: properties, and where each one fires.
issues.problem: The spec is too thin for engineering to implement. It has no naming convention (object_action), property types, identity handling, owner, or verification step.
issues.fix: Add the convention and a QA step: verify each event fires in staging with expected properties before the dashboard is trusted.

issues.quote: Score input and output metrics red, yellow, or green against their targets.
issues.problem: It does not say what to do when there are no targets, which is common for small teams, so RAG gets invented.
issues.fix: When no targets exist, score against the prior period or trailing average and label it INFERENCE, or ask for targets in one question.

issues.quote: Say it is thin and refuse the verdict; name the period or the volume that would
issues.problem: 'Thin' has no test, so the refusal is arbitrary.
issues.fix: Define thin as a change inside the normal week-over-week variance band, or below a minimum event count (e.g. under 100 conversions per arm/period), computed in bash.

issues.quote: to read. No source means you write the instrumentation spec first and read
issues.problem: It conflates 'the user did not hand over data' with 'the events do not exist'. The data may sit in a warehouse or analytics tool that is simply not connected.
issues.fix: Ask once for an export or pasted view. Write the spec only if the events are confirmed missing.

scenarios.prompt: Activation fell from 42% to 35% last week. Here's the Amplitude CSV export. What happened, and what should we do?
scenarios.why: Step 1 forces the model to name a North Star before it answers, which is a detour. Step 3 says 'decompose the headline into its drivers' but gives no order: check tracking breaks and releases first, then segment by platform, channel and cohort, then split mix from rate. It never says to compute from the CSV in bash_exec. A strong model will improvise a decent read; the skill adds little beyond FACT/INFERENCE labels and 'the call'.

scenarios.prompt: We have no tracking at all and onboarding v2 ships Friday. Set up what we need so we can tell in two weeks whether it worked.
scenarios.why: Step 2 routes to an instrumentation spec (event names, properties, where each fires). It gives no naming convention, no property types, no identity (user_id vs anonymous), no QA/verification step, and no rule against PII in properties or on consent. It also says nothing about capturing a pre-launch baseline, so the two-week read will have nothing to compare against.

product-prd-and-acceptance-criteria.summary: Writes a dated PRD: header table, a one-paragraph bet, an in/out/later scope line with reasons, validated assumptions, user stories with testable acceptance criteria, wireframe-level UX states, a baseline-to-target metric with a kill line, and owned open questions. Tickets are filed only on a yes.
strengths: Scope-line gate: outs are drafted and approved before any story is written
'The outs are as much the spec as the ins', with a one-line reason per out
Assumptions list with a validation method and date, revisited through the project
Empty, loading and error states named explicitly, and design owns the pixels
Traceability rule: no requirement without a user, bet or prior yes, and no invented API shapes
missing: Non-functional requirements (performance, security, privacy, accessibility, permissions)
Dependencies and risks with owners
Rollout, migration and feature-flag plan
Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria format and priority scheme
Routing to the AI-feature and instrumentation skills
PRD template file
Handling of a fixed external date against open scope

issues.problem: The PRD has no non-functional requirements (performance, security, privacy, accessibility, permissions), no dependencies, and no rollout/migration/feature-flag plan. These are exactly the questions engineering comes back with.
issues.fix: Add a step after the stories: NFRs by category, dependencies with owners, rollout (flag, beta cohort, migration, backward compatibility), and analytics events. Add them to the Output section list.

issues.quote: tester can check without asking you a question, plus a priority.
issues.problem: There is no acceptance-criteria format and no priority scheme, so criteria drift into prose and priorities are ad hoc.
issues.fix: Require Given/When/Then with at least one negative or edge path per story, and a stated scheme (P0/P1/P2 or MoSCoW).

issues.quote: means you write the smallest shippable bet and mark the goal UNKNOWN. No scope
issues.problem: This conflicts with step 6, which requires a baseline-to-target-by-date metric. The model is not told how to write the metric when the goal is UNKNOWN.
issues.fix: When the goal is UNKNOWN, write the metric as a proposed placeholder labelled INFERENCE and put 'confirm goal and target' as the first owned open question.

issues.quote: events behind it, and the kill line. A PRD with no metric is a wish.
issues.problem: It asks for instrumented events but does not route to product-metrics-and-instrumentation when those events do not exist. The kill line is undefined (metric, threshold, date).
issues.fix: Add: if the events are missing, produce the tracking plan via the metrics skill. Define the kill line as metric plus threshold plus review date.

issues.quote: participants, status, target release.
issues.problem: A target release in the header can read as a date commitment, against the persona boundary that no date is promised without the decision maker's yes.
issues.fix: Label the target release 'proposed' until the decision maker approves it, and log the approval.

issues.quote: round of edits, then file the stories as tickets only on a yes. Engineering
issues.problem: The tracker and ticket format are unnamed, and 'one round of edits' is an arbitrary cap.
issues.fix: Name the route (Linear/GitHub/Notion via run_block, or a CSV for import when unconnected), give the ticket body template (story, criteria, link to PRD), and allow iteration until the scope yes.

issues.problem: There is no boundary with the sibling AI skill. AI features (prompt, agent, retrieval) should load product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals instead of, or alongside, this PRD.
issues.fix: Add one line: if the feature's core is model behaviour, use the AI scoping skill for the quality ladder and evals, and reference it from the PRD.

issues.problem: No PRD template or worked example is shipped, so the header table and section order will vary between runs.
issues.fix: Ship templates/prd.md with the header table and all sections, plus one short example.

scenarios.prompt: Write a PRD for bulk CSV import of contacts. Here are the 12 customer requests we've logged. Engineering starts next sprint.
scenarios.why: The inputs step captures problem, users and goal. Step 2 draws in/out/later with reasons, step 4 turns requests into stories with checkable criteria, step 5 names the error and empty states, and step 6 sets the metric. Filing waits on a yes. Import limits (file size, dedupe, row errors) may be thin because nothing prompts for non-functional requirements, but the output is usable.

scenarios.prompt: The CEO wants 'AI summaries' on the dashboard by end of month. We have no usage data, and eng says it depends on a vendor API we haven't picked. Spec it.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks help: goal marked UNKNOWN, outs drafted and approved first, assumptions carry validation dates, API shapes are never invented, and gaps become owned open questions. But nothing routes an AI feature to product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals (evals, quality ladder). There is no guidance on a fixed date against open scope. And step 6 demands baseline-to-target by date while the goal is UNKNOWN, with no rule for reconciling the two.

product-roadmap-and-prioritization.summary: Rewrites backlog items as user/job/outcome lines, scores them with RICE on correct scales, cuts before ordering, lays survivors into capacity-checked now/next/later with owners and promotion triggers, and runs a shipped/slipped/stuck review with red/yellow/green scoring and one yes/no call.
strengths: RICE with the correct Intercom scales and a one-line reason per score so the order can be argued with
Cut before you order, with reasons, and nothing returns without new evidence
'Later' items keep an explicit promotion trigger
A capacity check that forces 'what drops' instead of silent overload
The review format: shipped/slipped/stuck, a slip with no date is red, a fixed KPI table, asks with owner and date, one yes/no call
missing: Reach fallback when usage metrics are absent
Rule for already-promised external commitments
Dependency sequencing step
Scored-backlog template and a named home (Sheets/Notion/workspace)
Score sensitivity check (does the order flip under plausible estimate changes)
Goal/theme capacity allocation across buckets

issues.quote: cycle from real metrics. Impact is 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 3 on how much it
issues.problem: Reach must come from real metrics, but there is no fallback when usage data is absent, which is the common case for small teams. The model will either stall or invent reach.
issues.fix: Add: with no usage data, use request counts or account counts from tickets/CRM, or a band. Label reach INFERENCE, and drop confidence to 50% for any item whose reach is a band.

issues.quote: numbers, minimum 0.5. Show the score and a one-line reason beside each, so
issues.problem: 'Whole numbers, minimum 0.5' contradicts itself, and the persona's voice sample uses effort 1.5.
issues.fix: Say: person-months rounded to 0.5, minimum 0.5.

issues.quote: The candidate items, the goal they serve, any dates already promised, and the
issues.problem: Promised dates are collected, but no rule says how they interact with scores (fixed constraint, flagged risk, or renegotiation ask).
issues.fix: Add: already-promised external commitments are placed first and marked COMMITTED with who promised it. If one crowds out a higher-scored item, raise the trade-off as the one call.

issues.quote: log of reviewed items so the same stuck thing is never re-flagged without
issues.problem: The reviewed-items log has no stated home, so dedupe across runs assumes persistent state.
issues.fix: Store the log as a dated workspace file next to the roadmap (or in memory_store with a stable key), and read it at the start of each review.

issues.quote: full sheet lives where the team reads it. File now-items as tickets only on a
issues.problem: No scored-sheet column template, no route to Google Sheets or Notion, and no instruction to compute scores in the sandbox for large backlogs.
issues.fix: Ship templates/scored-backlog.csv (item, user/job/outcome, R, I, C, E, score, reason, evidence grade, bucket, owner, promotion trigger). Compute scores in bash_exec. Write to Sheets via run_block on a yes, or hand back the CSV.

issues.quote: yellow, or green — a slip with no new date is red. Show the same fixed KPI
issues.problem: The fixed KPI set is undefined for the first review.
issues.fix: On the first review, propose the KPI set (the North Star and its inputs from the metrics skill), get a yes, then freeze it.

issues.problem: Dependencies only appear as an exception in the guesswork section. Ordering does not sequence prerequisites, so a high-score item can land 'now' before what it depends on.
issues.fix: Add a step between cut and order: map hard dependencies and move prerequisites ahead, noting the reason.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our 40-item backlog in a Google Sheet. We have 4 engineers and the goal this quarter is cutting churn. What do we build?
scenarios.why: Steps 1-5 map directly: rewrite each item as user/job/outcome, RICE-score with a reason, cut duplicates and non-goal items, fit 'now' to 4 engineers' capacity and ask what drops if it overflows. The chat carries the top three and the first cut. A capable model will produce a defensible ordering.

scenarios.prompt: Sales promised Acme SSO by March, the CEO wants the AI assistant, and we have no usage data or estimates. Reorder the roadmap.
scenarios.why: Missing effort is handled with person-month bands and flagged as a sizing ask. But reach must come 'from real metrics' and has no fallback. The promised Acme date is collected as an input with no rule for treating it as a fixed constraint and raising the renegotiation ask. Only the vague 'table-stakes bet may jump the order' covers it, so a model may either score SSO normally or silently honour the promise.

product-strategy-and-bets.job: write product strategy and bet case
product-strategy-and-bets.summary: Turns a proposed direction or bet into a dated strategy doc: a one-line bet, why change / why now / why us, evidence graded A-E for and against, substitutes including doing nothing, a banded business case with a kill line, and an explicit ask.
strengths: A-E evidence scale with explicit definitions and 'never call a D or an E validation'
Evidence against is required, not optional
Substitutes include spreadsheets, manual work and doing nothing
Every business-case number is banded and labelled FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN
The doc must end in a concrete ask with a date
missing: Alternative bets compared
Trade-offs and 'not doing' list
Target segment/ICP definition
Kill line defined as metric, threshold and date
Bottom-up sizing method with horizon
Risk section (value/usability/feasibility/viability)
Leading indicators
Handoff to product-exec-briefing for board or exec audiences

issues.quote: what are we not doing
issues.problem: This is a trigger, but the procedure has no trade-offs or non-goals step, so the skill loads for a question it never answers.
issues.fix: Add a step: the explicit 'not doing' list (segments, features, channels), each with the reason and what would reopen it.

issues.quote: Say back the bet in one line: who wins, what changes, and why now.
issues.problem: Strategy is a choice among options, but the skill only stress-tests one bet against substitutes. It never generates or compares two or three alternative bets.
issues.fix: After the say-back, list 2-3 alternative bets and compare them on evidence grade, cost band, time to signal and reversibility. Recommend one and say why the others lost.

issues.quote: the kill line where you stop. Bands over point estimates, and every number
issues.problem: The kill line is not defined as a metric, threshold and date. There is no sizing method (bottom-up reach x conversion x price), no time horizon, and no instruction to compute in the sandbox.
issues.fix: Define the kill line as 'metric < X by date Y, then stop or shrink'. Add a bottom-up sizing formula in bash_exec with low/base/high bands over a named horizon.

issues.quote: or asks whether to build a thing at all
issues.problem: This overlaps the PRD skill's 'a build decision' trigger, so the router may load the wrong one.
issues.fix: Clarify the split: 'whether to invest' goes here, 'how to build a decided thing' goes to the PRD. Mirror the wording in both descriptions.

issues.quote: edits, then save it. Offer to turn the first bet into roadmap items — only on
issues.problem: There is no save location and no gate or handoff for sharing the doc with execs or the board.
issues.fix: Name the workspace or Docs location. Route exec or board presentation through product-exec-briefing, and share only on the owner's yes.

issues.quote: assumption. If the user cannot name the user, say so and do not write the doc
issues.problem: The hard stop prevents useful work when the segment is the open question (e.g. a move upmarket).
issues.fix: Draft 2-3 segment hypotheses labelled INFERENCE and ask the owner to pick one before writing the full doc.

issues.problem: There is no risk section (value, usability, feasibility, viability) and no leading indicators that would show early whether the bet is working.
issues.fix: Add risks by type, each with a mitigation or test, plus 1-2 leading indicators tied to the kill line.

scenarios.prompt: Should we build a native Slack integration? Three customers asked, and two churned accounts mentioned it in exit surveys.
scenarios.why: The bet is said back in one line. The three whys are sourced. The evidence is graded both ways: exit-survey mentions sit at B/C, a single request is E. Substitutes include Zapier and doing nothing. The business case uses bands and a kill line, and the doc closes with an ask. The grading rules stop 'two churned' from being called validation.

scenarios.prompt: Write our 2027 product strategy for the board. We're moving from SMB to mid-market, but we have no mid-market customers or data yet.
scenarios.why: The thin-evidence rules help: a smaller bet, a loud UNKNOWN, and the one piece of evidence that would raise a grade. But the structure is single-bet. It has no target-segment definition, no options compared, no trade-offs or 'not doing' list, no sequencing of bets, and no leading indicators. A board strategy needs all of these, so the model must improvise beyond the skill.

product-assumption-testing.job: design experiments to validate product assumptions
product-assumption-testing.summary: A thin upstream prompt (phuryn/pm-skills) that asks the model to clarify an idea's assumptions and propose cheap validation experiments (fake door, Wizard of Oz, spikes, prototypes, A/B) as a table of assumption, experiment, metric and success threshold.
strengths: The right core principle: measure behaviour, not opinions
A useful palette of low-cost methods (fake door, Wizard of Oz, spikes, first-click)
Asks for risk mitigation on production tests
Clean attribution and MIT licence retained
missing: Assumption prioritisation (impact x uncertainty) and typing
Failure bands and decision rules
Sample size, traffic check and duration
Approval gate before production tests
Ethics and consumer-law limits for fake doors and Wizard of Oz
Cost, owner and date per experiment
Shipped method reference in place of external links (ATTRIBUTION also cites provenance/files.json, which is not in the package)

issues.quote: You are helping a product team design experiments for **$ARGUMENTS**.
issues.problem: $ARGUMENTS is a Claude-Code slash-command placeholder. In AutoGPT's harness it renders literally, leaving the framing sentence broken.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'for the idea and assumptions the user describes', or drop the sentence.

issues.quote: Use when validating assumptions, testing feature ideas cheaply, or planning product experiments.
issues.problem: 'Planning product experiments' collides head-on with Alex's product-experiment-design, so the router has two skills for the same request and the weaker one may win.
issues.fix: Drop this package and fold its method palette into product-experiment-design's candidate-tests step. If kept, narrow the description to pre-build assumption mapping only.

issues.quote: **Clarify the idea and assumptions**: Confirm what the team wants to build and what they need to validate.
issues.problem: Nothing ranks assumptions by impact and lack of evidence, or types them (desirability/usability/feasibility/viability), so effort is spread across low-risk beliefs. The canvas is only an external link.
issues.fix: Add a step: list assumptions by type, score each on impact x uncertainty, and test the top 1-3 first.

issues.quote: **Success threshold**: The expected value if we are right
issues.problem: There is only a success threshold. It has no failure or ambiguous band, decision rule, sample size, duration, cost, owner or date, so results can be rationalised after the fact.
issues.fix: Require precommitted pass/ambiguous/fail bands with the action for each, the minimum sample and duration, cost, and owner and date.

issues.quote: Test responsibly — don't put users or the business at risk
issues.problem: The guardrail is vague. There is no approval gate before any production test, fake door or Wizard of Oz, and no disclosure or ethics rule for faked functionality or pricing, and no privacy limits.
issues.fix: Add: draft the plan and launch nothing without the owner's yes. Fake doors must show an honest 'coming soon' message. No fake prices where consumer law forbids them. Keep collected data minimal.

issues.quote: [Continuous Product Discovery Masterclass (CPDM)](https://www.productcompass.pm/p/cpdm) (video course)
issues.problem: The package promotes the author's paid newsletter and course, and the methodology it depends on lives off-package at those links.
issues.fix: Remove the Further Reading block, or replace it with a short shipped references/experiment-methods.md.

issues.quote: Think step by step. Present experiments in a clear table or structured format. Save as markdown if substantial.
issues.problem: The deliverable is loose: no named artefact, no save location, no template.
issues.fix: Define a dated 'assumption test plan' saved via write_workspace_file with fixed columns.

scenarios.prompt: We think teams will pay for auto-assign. How can we test that cheaply before we build it?
scenarios.why: Step 2's method list (fake door, Wizard of Oz) and step 4's table give a plausible answer. But nothing prioritises which assumption is riskiest. The success threshold has no failure rule, sample or duration. There is no approval gate before a production fake door. The user gets ideas, not a runnable plan.

scenarios.prompt: We have 10 assumptions behind a new pricing tier, about 300 weekly active accounts, and legal says we can't show fake prices to EU users. Design the tests.
scenarios.why: There is no step to rank the 10 assumptions (the prioritisation canvas is only an external link). There is no traffic or sample-size check, and 300 accounts is too thin for an A/B test. There is no handling of consumer-protection limits on fake-door pricing. The literal '$ARGUMENTS' placeholder also leaves the context line broken in AutoGPT's harness.

16:hiring-pipeline-analytics.job: report hiring pipeline funnel and recruiting metrics
16:hiring-pipeline-analytics.summary: Runs bundled stdlib Python scripts over Sofia's hiring tracker or a normalised ATS export. They produce a FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN-labelled read covering funnel, pacing, mix, quality and hygiene, plus the Friday weekly review with snapshot diffs and a name-free share copy, and never compute rates by protected group.
strengths: Five stdlib scripts with clear exit codes. Both examples (Northwind Friday review, Greenhouse hard case) reproduce expected/report.md, diff.md, hygiene.csv and report-share.md exactly when re-run (ignoring CRLF line endings).

Precise metric definitions: time to hire and time to fill kept apart, cohort view vs all-rows view, open-cohort caveat, prospects excluded from applicant counts, 'we rejected' kept apart from 'they withdrew', medians not means, zero-day and evergreen traps, and the ANSI/SHRM cost-per-hire formula with owner estimates labelled INFERENCE.

Strong protected-class guardrail: protected columns are dropped on read by list and regex, rates by protected group are refused, and adverse-impact work is routed to HR or counsel on aggregated self-ID data, with the four-fifths caveat cited.

share_safe.py builds the shared copy from report.json rather than scrubbing report.md, and fails closed on any candidate-name residue, with an --allow path for interviewers who share a candidate's name.

Tool usage matches the live platform. find_capability/run_capability, tool:read_skill, the post_to_chat_platform gate, write_workspace_file(source_path=...) and the ~/skills/<slug> package path were all verified against the backend source. The send is drafted, gated and never automatic.
Snapshot diffs turn repeated stalls into ROLLUP lines with the date first reported, and the follow-up rule mirrors passive-candidate-outreach's followups_due.py, so both skills give the same list.
Graceful fallbacks: no Python, no entry dates, the first run, missing matplotlib or openpyxl, non-UTF-8 files and semicolon-delimited CSVs are all handled.
missing: Hiring-plan attainment and forecast: will each open req fill by target_start, and pipeline coverage per req
Median time spent in each stage, to find bottlenecks by duration and not only stalls over the bar
Small-cell suppression (n<5) in shared copies
Reading interview-coordination's stage_since column for stage entry and hire dates
Recruiter and interviewer capacity: reqs per recruiter and interview hours per panelist over time
Candidate-experience signal (candidate survey or NPS) alongside hiring-manager satisfaction
Offer-to-start and renege tracking after acceptance
Optional cited external benchmarks for conversion and time to hire, clearly separated from the owner's numbers

issues.quote: with no movement and the age of each open req; the oldest five stuck
issues.problem: funnel.py's over_bar() compares the tracker's days_in_stage directly with a business-day bar. interview-coordination defines that column as calendar days since stage_since, and funnel.py never reads stage_since. The package's own Northwind output flags Tom Becker and Aisha Bello, each at exactly 5 business days, as NEW STALL under '5 business days', so 2 of the 4 reported stalls are false. The stall list also disagrees with interview-coordination's sweep on the same tracker.
issues.fix: Alias stage_since to stage_entered and compute business days from it. When only days_in_stage exists and the bar is in business days, convert the calendar days before comparing. Add the Northwind case as a regression check.

issues.quote: time-to-hire trend by role family and offer acceptance over the
issues.problem: Sofia's tracker has no applied, offer or accepted dates, and funnel.py ignores stage_since. A hire made during the window therefore gives time to hire UNKNOWN and offer acceptance UNKNOWN, and the first-Friday trend has 0 rows even with snapshot history (tested). The weekly-pipeline-review routine's monthly promise never delivers unless an ATS export is supplied.
issues.fix: When a row reaches offer or hired, take its offer_out and accepted dates from stage_since (label them INFERENCE) and carry them into the snapshots. Otherwise, state that these metrics need an ATS export and ask for one on the first Friday of the month.

issues.quote: Unmapped columns or stages, ambiguous dates: ask once
issues.problem: This step sits under export normalisation, but normalize_export.py reports unmapped columns, not unmapped stage values. funnel.py then drops rows with unknown stages ('Tech screen', 'Hiring manager interview', Lever's 'On-site interview') from the funnel and the stall counts, keeps the FACT labels, and lists the stages only in the hygiene section at the bottom. In a test, 3 of 5 rows vanished and the report said 'Stalled: 0 [FACT]'. The walkthrough's 'The first run stopped on Portfolio review' is not what the script does.
issues.fix: Make funnel.py exit non-zero, or add a top banner such as 'N rows excluded: unmapped stages', whenever a stage is unmapped, and label the affected counts INFERENCE. Apply the ask to tracker runs as well as exports, and add common stage names to DEFAULT_STAGES.

issues.quote: Shared copies carry role-level numbers only and no per-candidate
issues.problem: The share copy prints per-role offer acceptance, withdrawal counts, early attrition and stalled-by-stage even when n is 1 or 2. In a team channel where everyone knows the single finalist, 'Offer acceptance 0.0 [n=1]' identifies that person.
issues.fix: Suppress or band every cell with n<5 in share_safe.py (show '<5'), and state the rule in the guardrail.

issues.quote: FACT (from a named file), INFERENCE (arithmetic and assumptions shown),
issues.problem: references/metric-definitions.md says conversions are labelled INFERENCE when the cohort is open. funnel.py only adds a note to the basis field and keeps the FACT label: the Northwind Product Designer conversions are FACT with 4 people still active.
issues.fix: Label open-cohort conversions INFERENCE in funnel.py, as the definition says.

issues.quote: (add `--hires`, `--costs`, `--hm-survey` when supplied)
issues.problem: The canonical funnel.py command uses '…' placeholders for --shortlist and --outreach and never mentions --stage-map or --date-order, although step 2 collects those answers. The owner's stage mapping is therefore easy to lose between the two steps; the walkthrough needs --stage-map.
issues.fix: Write out the full command with $H paths, and list --stage-map, --date-order and --role as the flags that carry step 2's answers.

issues.problem: The skill never checks tracker next_step and waiting_on against loops.csv. The expected review tells the owner to book Aisha's loop when loops.csv already shows it booked for 13 Oct, so a 'needs a human' line is stale.
issues.fix: Have funnel.py mark a stall 'loop already booked <date>' when loops.csv has a future booking for that candidate, and have the read drop the action.

issues.problem: The skill does not measure progress against the hiring plan. 'How is hiring going' from a founder usually means 'will we fill these reqs on time', and roles.csv already carries target_start, yet no step compares the pipeline per open req with the target date or with historical conversion.
issues.fix: Add one line per role: target_start, days left, candidates at loop or offer stage, and the conversion-implied hires expected by that date, labelled INFERENCE and shown only above min_sample.

scenarios.prompt: It's Friday. How is hiring going on Senior Backend and Product Designer compared with last week? Who's stuck?
scenarios.why: Steps 1-6 run funnel.py on the tracker with --history, then snapshot_and_chart.py, then templates/weekly-pipeline-review.md. Movement, new sourcing by recorded tier, follow-ups due and the next-week load all come out correct and reproducible (verified against the Northwind expected files). The stall list is wrong, though. funnel.py compares the tracker's days_in_stage (calendar days in interview-coordination's schema) directly with '5 business days'. Tom Becker (6 calendar days, 5 business days) and Aisha Bello (7 calendar days, 5 business days) are therefore reported as NEW STALL at a bar they have not passed: 2 of the 4 stalls are false, and the count disagrees with interview-coordination's sweep. The review also tells the owner to 'book the loop' for Aisha although loops.csv already has her loop booked on 13 Oct. Time to hire and offer acceptance are UNKNOWN because the tracker carries no accepted dates.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Lever export (xlsx) with the EEO columns still in. Leadership wants pass-through by gender, plus Q3 time to hire and cost per hire. Finance's numbers are job boards 4.200,00 EUR, agency 12.000,00 EUR.
scenarios.why: The protected-group request is handled well. The step 2 refusal, the protected-column drop reported in one line, the Lever trap about archive-reason IDs, the openpyxl requirement for xlsx and the 'bad cost line' check all hold, so cost per hire stays UNKNOWN until the amounts are rewritten. The funnel is the gap. Lever stage names such as 'Reached out' and 'On-site interview' are not in DEFAULT_STAGES. normalize_export.py reports only unmapped columns, not unmapped stage values, so step 2's 'ask once' never fires. funnel.py then drops those rows from a funnel still labelled FACT, and the only signal is a hygiene line at the bottom. A model following the steps would likely report understated pass-through as fact.

better: v1 was prose only. v2 adds tested scripts whose output reproduces both worked examples exactly, so no number is typed by hand.
Protected columns are dropped on read, and rates by protected group are explicitly refused with routing to HR or counsel. v1 said nothing on this.
v1's 'candidate details stay out' becomes a share copy built from report.json with a name-residue check that fails closed.

Adds precise definitions for the two clocks, time to slate, open vs closed cohorts, prospects vs applicants, 'we rejected' vs 'they withdrew', and cost per hire under ANSI/SHRM with estimates labelled.
Snapshot and diff give real week-over-week movement and ROLLUP stall lines, which v1 could only ask for.
Adds vendor traps (Greenhouse Harvest v1/v2 removed, Ashby PDF, Lever reason IDs, LinkedIn export caps), refuses to guess ambiguous dates, and flags zero-day and evergreen hires.
Uses concrete, verified platform calls: find/run_capability, the post_to_chat_platform gate, write_workspace_file(source_path=...) and a Gmail draft rather than a send.
Adds fallbacks for no Python, no entry dates, the first run, and missing chart or xlsx libraries.
worse: SKILL.md roughly doubles in length and is dense: long commands and tool calls sit inside Guardrails, and the Output contract, Quality self-check and checklist overlap.
The stall count now mechanically over-flags people by comparing calendar-day tracker values with a business-day bar, and labels the result FACT.
Rows with unmapped stages now leave FACT-labelled counts silently. v1 left the model to read every row.
The monthly time-to-hire trend and offer-acceptance promise cannot be met from the tracker alone, so the routine reports UNKNOWN every first Friday.
Adds a pip install of matplotlib to the pre-flight step.

vip-and-white-glove-care.job: manage VIP and executive customer cases
vip-and-white-glove-care.summary: A 49-line playbook for premium or exec-flagged cases: tier the case from the record, name one owner, send updates on the tier's cadence, keep a separate exec stakeholder line, and close with a logged check-in.
strengths: "Confirm the tier from the record, not the tone" plus the explicit untiered-loud-customer rule stops VIP inflation
Keeps the customer thread (plain progress) separate from the internal work thread and carries the SLA clock across every handoff
Exec updates wait for the owner's yes, and a missing tier list falls back to INFERENCE
missing: Default update cadence per tier and severity
Account-team notification (CSM, AE, exec sponsor) and internal swarm or war-room coordination
Commercial context: ARR, renewal date, contractual SLA and service credits
Parent/child account hierarchy handling
Customer-facing RCA for P1 incidents
Exec-update and close-out templates
Explicit hand-off boundary with escalations-and-incidents and own-to-closure

issues.quote: Use this when a premium-tier, enterprise, or exec-flagged customer needs
issues.problem: Robin's escalations-and-incidents also triggers on VIP and exec cases ('VIP escalation', 'VIP down'), and this skill's triggers ('exec escalation', 'enterprise customer escalation') collide with it. Neither says which one owns severity rating, the packet and paging, and which owns relationship care.
issues.fix: State the split: escalations-and-incidents rates severity and builds or pages the packet, and this skill owns the customer relationship, cadence and exec comms. Say so in both descriptions and cross-link them by slug.

issues.quote: first-update time, and updates on the tier's cadence even when the news is
issues.problem: Everything hangs on a cadence from prefs, but no default is given, and the fallback only covers a missing tier list. A new desk gets no update rhythm.
issues.fix: Add a default cadence table (e.g. P1 VIP every 60 min, P2 every 4 h, P3 daily), marked as a default until the owner confirms it, and save the confirmed cadence to memory.

issues.quote: The case, the customer's tier and history, the VIP tiers and exec path from
issues.problem: The inputs leave out what senior enterprise support checks first: the account team (CSM, AE, exec sponsor), ARR and renewal date, contractual SLA and service credits, and parent/child account hierarchy.
issues.fix: Add these inputs, with a CRM lookup (HubSpot block) or an ask_question fallback, and put the account team on the internal update list.

issues.quote: A VIP down is P1; a VIP ask with a path keeps its priority but gets the
issues.problem: Matches Robin's P1 definition, but the sibling escalations skill rates 'a VIP down' SEV2. The same expert gives two severities for the same event and this skill never hands off to the packet or paging path.
issues.fix: Map P1 to a SEV level explicitly and route P1 VIP outages to escalations-and-incidents for the packet and on-call page.

issues.quote: The tiered case, the cadence plan, staged customer and stakeholder updates,
issues.problem: The deliverables are named but have no format, so exec updates and close-out logs will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/: a customer update (status, impact, next step, next update time), an exec stakeholder note (impact, actions, owner, next update), and a close-out log row.

issues.quote: Close white-glove: confirm the fix with the customer, summarize what
issues.problem: A white-glove close normally includes a customer-facing RCA for P1s, a service-credit check against contract, and a debrief with the account team. None of these are here.
issues.fix: Add an RCA summary draft for P1/P2, a credit-eligibility check routed to billing, and an account-team debrief line.

issues.quote: Work the issue with the matching skill (Enterprise identity SSO support,
issues.problem: Refers to sibling skills by display name, not slug, and leaves out the most common VIP paths: billing-refunds-and-exceptions and escalations-and-incidents.
issues.fix: List the sibling skills by slug and add billing and escalations.

scenarios.prompt: Acme (Platinum tier) says their SSO login is broken for everyone and their CTO just emailed our CEO. Take it.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-4 lead the model to confirm Platinum from the record, call it P1, name an owner with a first-update time, route the work to the SSO skill and draft the exec stakeholder line for approval. It never says what the cadence is when prefs are empty, never tells the model to notify the CSM or AE or to check contractual SLA credits, and gives no exec-update template, so the update's quality depends on the model.

scenarios.prompt: A customer on our Basic plan says they know our CEO and wants a refund plus hourly updates. Their parent company is a $200k enterprise account renewing next month.
scenarios.why: Step 1 correctly refuses to call a loud untiered customer a VIP. Nothing covers account hierarchy (parent vs child), renewal or revenue exposure, or routing the refund demand to billing-refunds-and-exceptions: step 3's skill list leaves billing out. The model has to improvise the one call that matters here.

voice-and-phone-support.job: run support calls, callbacks, and IVR
voice-and-phone-support.summary: Bundles four phone jobs in one skill: staged call plans with recording disclosure and PCI pause, callback queue rules including calling hours and a DNC check, an IVR audit checklist, and scorecard coaching from recordings.
strengths: Correct PCI practice: pause or DTMF-mask at the payment moment and never store CVV, PIN or track data in audio, screen or transcript
Concrete callback discipline: caller picks with numbers, no callback for urgent calls or waits under ~5 min, oldest promise first, overdue callback becomes P2
A usable IVR audit checklist (agent escape, greeting 8s or less, menu 30s or less, customer vocabulary, IVR-collected data passed to the agent)
Never dial without the owner's yes, and never score a call it cannot hear or read
missing: Explicit no-telephony fallback (human dials from the staged plan)
Call plan, callback queue and IVR audit templates
PCI incident routing to sensitive-data-safe-handling
All-party-consent default for recording
Voice KPIs beyond IVR (ASA, FCR, callback-kept rate, transfer rate by reason)
Warm-transfer script and identity-verification method options
A split into narrower skills, or at least a clear boundary with the quality and live-queue skills

issues.quote: Use this when a case needs a call: place or review calls, run callbacks to
issues.problem: AutoGPT has no telephony or dialer block, but the skill promises to 'place' calls and deliver a 'placed-call log'. There is no fallback telling the model that a human dials from the staged plan.
issues.fix: Say the agent stages call plans and callback lists for a human to dial, and only logs outcomes the user reports back. If an MCP voice tool is connected, dial only after the owner approves that specific call.

issues.quote: Calibrate scoring across reviewers first, then score the call against the
issues.problem: This duplicates quality-csat-and-coaching (calibration, quoted-line scoring, one fix per rep per week) inside a skill that already carries three other jobs, so the two skills compete on 'coach this call'.
issues.fix: Keep only voice-specific rubric items (disclosure, hold handling, dead air, transfer) and hand scoring and coaching to quality-csat-and-coaching.

issues.section: Run the call in three beats
issues.quote: screen, or transcript. Redact any slip immediately. Keep after-call
issues.problem: Stored card data or CVV is a PCI incident, not just a redaction. There is no containment step, no route to sensitive-data-safe-handling, and no compliance-owner notification.
issues.fix: On any SAD exposure, stop, route to sensitive-data-safe-handling, draft the compliance-owner notice, and flag the recording and transcript for purge in the source system.

issues.quote: automated coverage across 100% of calls for disclosure, consent, and
