issues.problem: No speech-analytics tool exists in the harness, so '100% automated coverage' cannot be done as written and has no fallback.
issues.fix: Only when a transcript export is supplied, run a keyword or regex scan for disclosure and prohibited phrases in bash_exec. Otherwise say coverage is limited to the calls provided.

issues.section: Run the call in three beats
issues.quote: caller location, one-party vs two-party) logged as call metadata, plus
issues.problem: Following only the caller's location is incomplete. When either party is in an all-party-consent jurisdiction, the stricter rule applies, and GDPR-region callers need a lawful basis.
issues.fix: Default to all-party disclosure on every recorded call and name the owner's compliance path for cross-border calls.

issues.quote: Deliver the staged call plan or placed-call log, the callback state, the IVR
issues.problem: Four deliverables are named with no format for any of them.
issues.fix: Ship templates: call plan, callback queue table (promise time, timezone, attempts, status), IVR audit table, voice scorecard.

issues.quote: Offer the choice with numbers: estimated wait, estimated callback time,
issues.problem: The callback rules overlap live-channel-queue-operations ('overdue callback list', 'callback past its time is P2'), and nothing marks which skill owns the callback queue.
issues.fix: Let live-channel-queue-operations order the queue and this skill run individual calls, and cross-reference them by slug.

scenarios.prompt: Maria has called twice about a double charge and we promised her a callback by 3pm Pacific. Prep the call.
scenarios.why: 'Stage the call plan' produces who, why, the two outcomes that count as resolved, and the talk track. The three beats add disclosure, identity check and the PCI pause at the payment moment, and the callback section adds the promise-time and timezone checks. The owner-yes gate before dialing holds.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a transcript of yesterday's call. The agent read back the customer's full card number and CVV. The customer is in California. Score the call and tell me what to do.
scenarios.why: The skill says 'Redact any slip immediately' and never store CVV, and 'Coach from recordings' gives a scoring frame. It never treats stored CVV as a PCI incident: no route to sensitive-data-safe-handling, no compliance-owner notification, no purge of the recording from the call platform. It also scores in parallel with quality-csat-and-coaching, and its consent rule ('follows caller location') leaves out all-party states like California.

voice-of-customer-and-feedback.job: synthesize customer feedback into ranked themes
voice-of-customer-and-feedback.summary: Mines a batch of tickets into themes, each with a count, two verbatim quotes, the channel and ticket IDs, and drafts a ranked product brief plus issue and thank-you drafts, logged for next week's dedupe.
strengths: Every theme carries a count, two verbatims, the channel and the ticket IDs behind it
Refuses to scale counts by assumed ratios and names under-counting honestly
Separates feature asks (file an issue) from praise (thank-you draft, never a roadmap promise)
Logs themes with dates so the next batch dedupes against them
missing: Unique-account counting with segment and ARR weighting
Persistent theme codebook or taxonomy
PII anonymisation of quotes
Sandbox method for large ticket exports
Period-over-period trend
Product brief template
Close-the-loop notification to affected customers
A clear boundary with weekly-ticket-themes, feedback-synthesis and product-research-synthesis

issues.quote: Read every thread, pull the exact customer words with speaker and
issues.problem: Speaker identity goes into a brief for product and engineering with no anonymisation or PII redaction. Reading every thread also fails on real exports of hundreds of tickets.
issues.fix: Attribute quotes to segment or plan and a ticket ID, not names, and strip PII. For batches over about 100, tag in bash_exec with a codebook, or sample and state the sampling.

issues.quote: mentions is a hint, ten is a pattern; say which each theme is.
issues.problem: Counts mentions, not unique customers or accounts, and sets arbitrary thresholds. It also conflicts with sibling skills ('three accounts is a pattern') and ignores segment or ARR weight.
issues.fix: Count unique accounts and mentions separately, add segment, plan and ARR where available, and let one named churn risk or a blocked enterprise account escalate regardless of count.

issues.section: File each theme as sourced evidence
issues.quote: Draft the product brief: themes ranked by count and pain, the top
issues.problem: 'Pain' is undefined, so the ranking is subjective and cannot be reproduced. There is also no trend against the prior period.
issues.fix: Define a severity scale (blocked / workaround / annoyance) and rank on accounts × severity, with change vs the last period shown.

issues.quote: You need the ticket or thread batch with dates, survey or review quotes
issues.problem: The skill triggers on 'survey responses' but has no survey handling (response rate, NPS or CSAT segment splits), and that trigger collides with product-research-synthesis and feedback-synthesis.
issues.fix: Either drop the survey trigger and hand surveys to the research skill, or add survey handling with response rate and segment splits.

issues.problem: There is no contact-reason taxonomy or codebook, so theme names drift week to week and the dedupe log stops working.
issues.fix: Keep a persistent theme codebook in memory (name, definition, example IDs) and code new batches against it first.

issues.section: File each theme as sourced evidence
issues.quote: Log the themes against the intake with dates so next week's batch
issues.problem: No storage location or dedupe key is named, so the log may not persist between runs.
issues.fix: Use memory_store or a named Sheet, with theme code + week as the key.

issues.section: File each theme as sourced evidence
issues.quote: Deliver the ranked theme brief plus staged issue and thank-you drafts.
issues.problem: There is no brief template and no close-the-loop step to tell affected customers when a theme ships.
issues.fix: Ship a brief template and add a closed-loop step: when a filed issue ships, draft notices to the tagged tickets for approval.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV of last month's 600 support tickets. What are customers complaining about most, and what should product fix first?
scenarios.why: 'Mine the batch' says to read every thread and build themes with counts, quotes and ticket IDs, and the brief ranks them. 600 tickets cannot be read in context and the skill never says to tag or sample in bash_exec. 'Pain' is undefined, so the ranking is subjective, and speaker names flow into the product brief.

scenarios.prompt: Combine these 40 NPS comments with the ticket export and tell me if 'slow sync' is a real pattern. One enterprise account is threatening to churn over it.
scenarios.why: The skill mentions survey quotes but gives no way to merge survey and ticket sources or dedupe the same customer across channels. It counts mentions, not accounts, and has no revenue or churn weighting, so the 'three is a hint, ten is a pattern' rule can bury the single churn-risk account a senior would escalate.

workforce-and-capacity-planning.job: forecast support volume and schedule agent staffing
workforce-and-capacity-planning.summary: Runs the support WFM cycle in five steps: forecast contacts by interval, convert to heads with a shrinkage formula, build shifts, watch adherence with staged intraday moves, and close the loop weekly on forecast vs actual.
strengths: Covers the full WFM loop (forecast → heads → schedule → real-time → weekly accuracy) at the right altitude for a support desk
Shows the math in one checkable block and names the after-call-work convention
Schedule changes wait for the schedule owner, and every intraday move carries its cost
A clear boundary with ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan, which explicitly excludes support shift scheduling
missing: Erlang C/A calculation with a service-level or ASA target and an occupancy cap
Chat concurrency and email or backlog workload models
Forecasting method and accuracy metric (WAPE/MAPE)
A correct shrinkage definition, planned vs unplanned
Labor-law and scheduling-notice constraints
Adherence vs conformance formulas and a snapshot fallback
A bundled calculator script and output templates
Scenario or sensitivity table (±10% volume, ±30 s AHT)

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: Turn the forecast into required heads: staffed heads = base requirement /
issues.problem: The central step is never specified: nothing turns volume, AHT and the service-level target into a base requirement. There is no Erlang C/A, no occupancy cap, no chat concurrency and no email backlog math.
issues.fix: Add: workload = volume × AHT / interval, then Erlang C (or Erlang A with patience) to hit the SL/ASA target, occupancy cap around 85-88%, concurrency divisor for chat, and backlog/turnaround math for email. Ship scripts/erlang.py for bash_exec.

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: (1 - shrinkage/100), where shrinkage = (unavailable hours / logged-in
issues.problem: Shrinkage is measured against total paid or scheduled hours, not logged-in time. Absent or training agents are not logged in, so this ratio is mis-specified and understates or distorts shrinkage.
issues.fix: Define shrinkage = paid hours unavailable for contact work / total paid (scheduled) hours, split into planned and unplanned.

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: queues, so it tends to overstaff multi-skill or bursty queues — say so
issues.problem: This is wrong in two ways. Erlang C assumes random Poisson arrivals, not 'steady' ones. And bursty or overdispersed arrivals make Erlang C understaff, not overstaff; only the abandonment assumption and siloed skills push it to overstaff.
issues.fix: Rewrite: Erlang C overstaffs when callers abandon (use Erlang A) or when skills pool, and understaffs when arrivals are bursty or peaked; add a buffer or simulate.

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: Forecast volume per channel and interval from history, naming trend,
issues.problem: No forecasting method (day-of-week and intraday distribution curves, same-period-last-year, weighted moving average or Holt-Winters) and no accuracy metric. The 'miss band' is undefined.
issues.fix: Name a default method run in bash_exec, report WAPE or MAPE at daily and interval level, and set the miss band from backtest error.

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: and time-off, then assign agents to shifts honoring bids, prefs, and
issues.problem: No labor-law constraints: meal and rest-break rules, overtime thresholds, predictive-scheduling or fair-workweek notice periods. Intraday overtime moves carry legal exposure.
issues.fix: Add a constraint check that asks the owner which jurisdictions apply and flags schedules or moves that breach notice, break or overtime rules.

issues.section: Forecast, staff, schedule, watch, close the loop
issues.quote: Watch real-time adherence: adherence means agents doing the scheduled
issues.problem: Needs a live ACD or WFM feed the harness does not have, gives no fallback for a pasted snapshot, and does not distinguish adherence from conformance or give the formula.
issues.fix: Give formulas for adherence (in-state time / scheduled time) and conformance, and work from a pasted or exported snapshot when no feed exists.

issues.quote: The forecast with its math, the staged schedule, the intra-day moves, and
issues.problem: There is no output template, so schedules and weekly reads will not be comparable week to week.
issues.fix: Ship templates: interval requirement table (CSV), schedule grid, intraday move log, weekly accuracy card.

scenarios.prompt: Here's 12 weeks of phone and chat volume by half-hour. AHT is 6 min, our target is 80/20, shrinkage is 32%. How many agents do I need per interval next week?
scenarios.why: Step 1 forecasts from history and step 2 applies base/(1-shrinkage). Nothing turns volume, AHT and the 80/20 target into the base requirement, and nothing covers occupancy caps or chat concurrency. No Erlang script ships despite bash_exec. A capable model may know Erlang C, but the skill does not ensure it, and the shrinkage definition it gives is off.

scenarios.prompt: Promo launches Monday for a new product line with no history, three agents are out sick, and the email backlog is 400. What do I do today?
scenarios.why: The thin-records fallback marks the promo forecast INFERENCE, and step 4 stages intraday moves with a cost, which fits. It has no method for deferred channels (backlog workload, turnaround targets), no promo-uplift analog method, and no labor-law check on the overtime it suggests.

knowledge-base-article-writing.job: write help-center article from resolved tickets
knowledge-base-article-writing.summary: Anthropic's kb-article packaged as-is: turns a resolved ticket or common question into a typed KB article (how-to, troubleshooting, FAQ, known issue), with searchability rules, per-type templates, publishing metadata and maintenance-cadence guidance.
strengths: Per-type templates (how-to, troubleshooting, FAQ, known issue) with sharp best practices such as leading with symptoms and answering in the first sentence
Search guidance: customer-language titles, exact error strings, synonyms, and a good/bad title table
A metadata and publishing-notes block that records source, overlapping articles, SME reviewer and review date
Clear update-vs-create rules and an article lifecycle
missing: Draft-only and owner-approval gate before publishing
PII and internal-note scrubbing
A verified-steps-only rule with [VERIFY] markers
AutoGPT connector mapping with a paste or export fallback
Reference-article template
Screenshot, alt-text and accessibility guidance
A clear boundary with help-article-from-tickets and knowledge-centered-service

issues.quote: Include the specific path: "Go to Settings > Integrations > API Keys"
issues.problem: It pushes for exact UI paths and expected screens but never says to use only steps verified from the ticket or product and to mark the rest, which invites hallucinated menu paths in a public article.
issues.fix: Add: every step must trace to the ticket resolution or verified docs. Mark unverified steps [VERIFY] in the draft and list them under Review needed.

issues.problem: The skill pulls ticket threads and internal notes but never says to strip customer names, account IDs or internal-only notes before drafting a public article.
issues.fix: Add a redaction step: generalise customer wording, remove identifiers, and keep internal notes in Publishing Notes only.

issues.quote: /kb-article <resolved issue, ticket reference, or topic description>
issues.problem: The heading '# /kb-article' and this Usage block are a Claude Code slash command. The AutoGPT harness ignores argument-hint and never invokes skills this way.
issues.fix: Replace Usage with 'What you need first' (resolved issue or ticket, audience, product version) and drop the slash heading.

issues.quote: Present the draft with metadata:
issues.problem: There is no approval gate. With a Notion or WordPress block connected, nothing stops the model from publishing, and nothing says the article stays a draft until the owner approves.
issues.fix: State that output is a draft only and that publishing or filing to the KB happens only after the owner's explicit yes, logged with date.

issues.quote: [Expected fix date or current status]
issues.problem: This invites a public fix date that engineering may not have committed to, which is a customer-promise risk.
issues.fix: Only include a date engineering has confirmed in writing; otherwise write 'We'll update this article when a fix is scheduled.'

issues.quote: Pull the ticket thread, resolution, and any internal notes
issues.problem: The ~~support platform, ~~knowledge base and ~~project tracker placeholders map in CONNECTORS.md to Intercom, Guru and Jira, which are not AutoGPT blocks, and no fallback is given when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Map to the harness (Notion, Google Docs/Drive, Linear, GitHub blocks, or run_mcp_tool) and fall back to asking for pasted threads or an export.

issues.quote: How-to, troubleshooting, FAQ, known issue, or reference (see article types below)
issues.problem: 'Reference' is offered as a type but has no template below.
issues.fix: Add a reference-article template (parameters or options table, limits, examples) or drop the type.

issues.quote: Knowledge bases decay without maintenance. Follow this schedule:
issues.problem: Program-level KB maintenance and taxonomy content sits inline in a single-article drafting skill. It inflates the body and overlaps knowledge-centered-service's Evolve loop.
issues.fix: Move cadence, lifecycle and taxonomy to references/maintenance.md and keep the body focused on drafting one article.

scenarios.prompt: Ticket #4521: a customer couldn't export more than 10k rows; we solved it by having them use the API with pagination. Turn this into a KB article.
scenarios.why: Step 1 identifies problem, solution, audience and type. Step 2 applies the troubleshooting or how-to template and the title rules. Step 3 wraps it in the metadata block with source and SME review, which gives a publish-ready draft. The one weakness is that it never tells the model to strip the customer's identifiers.

scenarios.prompt: Write a known-issue article for the Safari 16 chart bug. Engineering hasn't committed to a fix date, all I have is this Slack thread, and our KB isn't connected.
scenarios.why: The known-issue template is good, but its 'Fix Timeline [Expected fix date or current status]' slot invites a date nobody approved, and nothing forbids it. The ~~knowledge base duplicate check has no stated fallback when unconnected, and internal Slack detail may leak into the public article because nothing separates internal from public content.

product-research-synthesis.job: synthesize user research into prioritized findings
product-research-synthesis.summary: Anthropic's synthesize-research packaged as-is: gathers interviews, surveys and tickets, extracts observations, runs thematic analysis into 5-8 prioritised findings with confidence levels, and adds long methodology sections on affinity mapping, triangulation, survey pitfalls, personas and opportunity sizing.
strengths: Rigorous method: familiarisation → coding → theme review, plus affinity mapping and three forms of triangulation
Strong epistemics: behaviour over stated preference, a quote is evidence not a finding, and contradictions often reveal segments
A clear findings format with evidence, frequency, impact and a confidence level per finding
Privacy-aware attribution to participant type, not name
missing: Sandbox-based coding for large datasets, with a codebook and consistency check
A SOURCED or ASSUMED label on every sizing number
A verbatim-quote traceability rule
Link from findings to an opportunity-solution tree or JTBD
Saving the synthesis to a research repository in memory for later dedupe
Sampling-bias and saturation notes for small-n interviews
AutoGPT-native connector mapping

issues.quote: /synthesize-research $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command with $ARGUMENTS, which the AutoGPT harness does not support; argument-hint is also dropped.
issues.fix: Replace with 'What you need first' (research question, decision it informs, sources and counts) and remove the slash usage.

issues.quote: How many users could benefit from addressing this? Use product analytics, survey data, or market data to estimate.
issues.problem: It invites user counts and percentages with no requirement to label each as sourced or assumed. When analytics are not connected, the model will invent plausible numbers like the '2,000 users per month' example.
issues.fix: Require each sizing input to be labelled SOURCED (with source and period) or ASSUMED, and omit sizing when no source exists rather than estimating.

issues.quote: For each source, extract:
issues.problem: No approach for large datasets. Hundreds of survey rows or tickets cannot be hand-read in context, and there is no codebook or consistency check.
issues.fix: For batches over about 100 items, build a codebook, code in bash_exec (or in batches with a saved codebook), report counts per code, and spot-check a sample.

issues.quote: Synthesize user research from multiple sources into structured insights and recommendations.
issues.problem: Proposed for robin, alex, sasha and priya, each of whom already has a feedback or research synthesis skill. The description's 'support tickets' clause collides with Robin's VoC and Sasha's weekly-ticket-themes.
issues.fix: Assign to one product expert as the research-synthesis owner and cut 'support tickets' from the trigger, or merge it into product-discovery-and-user-research.

issues.quote: (Users affected) x (Frequency) x (Severity) = impact score
issues.problem: Multiplies ordinal scales (daily/weekly, blocker/annoyance) as if they were ratio data, which gives false precision. That contradicts the skill's own warning about treating Likert scales as interval data.
issues.fix: Use a banded rubric or rank order, and show the components side by side instead of a product score.

issues.quote: Quotes are powerful evidence. Include them generously, with attribution to participant type (not name).
issues.problem: There is no rule that quotes must be verbatim and traceable to a source line. Paraphrases can be presented as quotes.
issues.fix: Require verbatim quotes with a source reference (file, row or timestamp), and mark paraphrase explicitly.

issues.quote: (if connected): Pull usage data, funnel metrics, behavioral data
issues.problem: The ~~ placeholders map in CONNECTORS.md to Amplitude, Pendo, Fireflies and Dovetail, none of which have AutoGPT blocks.
issues.fix: Map to the available blocks (Notion, Google Drive/Sheets, run_mcp_tool) and keep the paste or upload path as the default.

issues.quote: Personas should emerge from research data, not imagination:
issues.problem: The persona and opportunity-sizing sections are separate jobs inlined into the body (324 lines), which dilutes the core synthesis procedure.
issues.fix: Move the methodology, persona and sizing sections to references/ and route to them from steps 3-5.

scenarios.prompt: Here are notes from 8 customer interviews about our onboarding. Synthesize the findings and recommend what to build.
scenarios.why: Step 1 asks for the research question and the decision it informs. Steps 2-3 extract observations and quotes and run thematic analysis with a frequency × impact matrix. Step 4 outputs findings with evidence, frequency and confidence, plus recommendations and open questions. That is senior-quality work, with participant-type attribution protecting privacy.

scenarios.prompt: I have 1,200 open-ended survey responses in a CSV plus 5 interview transcripts that contradict the survey. Leadership wants a sized opportunity by Friday.
scenarios.why: 'When Sources Disagree' and the survey guidance handle the contradiction well. Nothing tells the model to code 1,200 rows in bash_exec with a codebook rather than read them in context. Opportunity sizing invites 'addressable users' estimates with no rule to label each number sourced or assumed when analytics are not connected, and its impact score multiplies ordinal categories.

productivity-task-sync.job: sync task list and capture missed commitments
productivity-task-sync.summary: Reconciles a local TASKS.md against tasks assigned in a project tracker or GitHub, flags overdue and stale items for triage, asks the user to decode unknown people and projects into a CLAUDE.md plus memory/ file store, and in comprehensive mode scans chat, email, docs and calendar for commitments nobody has tracked.
strengths: A diff-and-confirm pattern: the external-vs-local matching table ends in 'Present diff and let user decide', so nothing is added or closed silently.
Pulling commitments ('I'll send the updated mockups by Friday') from chat and email, with source and date quoted, is what a senior EA actually does.
Decoding unknown shorthand in tasks (PSR, Phoenix, Todd) and asking only about the gaps is a distinctive, useful idea.
An explicit rule: 'Never auto-add tasks or memories without user confirmation'. No external writes happen.
The SKILL.md body is compact, with concrete worked examples for each step.
missing: A stable external ID or link stored on each task so re-syncs are idempotent
Added and waiting-since dates in the task format, so age and staleness can be computed
A connect_integration or CSV/paste fallback when no tracker, chat or email source is connected
Drafted nudges for overdue Waiting On items, sent only with approval
Optional write-back to the tracker (close or update) with an approval gate, or an explicit statement that sync is read-only
A default lookback window, and a scheduled cadence via schedule_routine (e.g. a daily sync)
Incoming asks (requests made to the principal), not only the principal's own sent promises
Privacy rules for what may be stored about people found in DMs and email
Prioritisation of the synced list (due date, who it is owed to) ending in a 'top 3 today' line
A report that lists every change made, with its source, so the user can undo it

issues.quote: Read `TASKS.md` and `memory/` directory. If they don't exist, suggest `/productivity:start` first.
issues.problem: Every new Frankie or Kai user hits this gate, and it points to a slash command the harness does not register (the Usage block has the same problem). The bundled references/start.md is not routed to here, so the skill stalls or the model has to improvise.
issues.fix: If there is no task list, create one in the workspace with write_workspace_file from the template (or read references/start.md to set it up), or work from an in-conversation list. Remove the /productivity:* Usage block and choose default or comprehensive mode from what the user asks.

issues.quote: **Status changes** ("launch done") → update project status, demote from CLAUDE.md
issues.problem: CLAUDE.md and a memory/people|projects|glossary file tree are Claude Code working-memory conventions. On AutoGPT, durable memory is memory_store/memory_search, so this writes a parallel store the expert will never consult in other conversations.
issues.fix: Map people, projects and glossary entries to memory_store with typed tags, and run memory_search before asking the user about a term. Keep only the task list as a workspace file.

issues.quote: **GitHub Issues** (if in a repo): `gh issue list --assignee=@me`
issues.problem: The sandbox has no repo and no user GitHub credentials, and 'if MCP available' ignores run_block (Linear, GitHub, Todoist, Notion, Airtable). 'If no sources are available, skip to Step 3' silently drops the sync instead of offering to connect a tracker.
issues.fix: List the supported run_block/run_mcp_tool trackers. If none is connected, call connect_integration or ask for a CSV/export or a paste, and state in the report which sources were and were not checked.

issues.quote: | In TASKS.md, not in external | No match | Flag as potentially stale |
issues.problem: Every personal task that never came from a tracker gets flagged stale on every run. Matching is by fuzzy title only, with no stored external ID, so renamed tasks duplicate. No row covers a task done locally but still open in the tracker.
issues.fix: Store source and ID/link on each synced task (e.g. `[LIN-123](url)`) and match on ID first, title second. Flag a missing task only when its recorded source is that tracker. Add a conflict row that asks which side is right.

issues.quote: Tasks in Active for 30+ days
issues.problem: The TASKS.md format in references/task-management.md records no created or added date, so task age cannot be computed and the model will guess.
issues.fix: Add 'added YYYY-MM-DD' (and 'since' for Waiting On) to the task format, compute ages with bash_exec, and report 'age unknown' when a task has no date.

issues.quote: **Chat:** Search recent messages, read active channels
issues.problem: There is no lookback window, no limit to the principal's own threads, no consent step before reading DMs, and no rule on what personal details may be stored as memory. Email is limited to sent messages, so incoming asks are missed.
issues.fix: Default to a stated window (e.g. 14 days, confirmed with the user) and only messages to or from the principal. Quote and link each source, include incoming requests, and never store health, HR, compensation or personal-life details about others.

issues.problem: Waiting On items are never chased and the tracker is never updated. The triage offers only done, reschedule or Someday, so the principal still has to write every nudge and every status change in the tracker by hand.
issues.fix: For Waiting On items past a threshold, draft a nudge to the owner, and offer to close or update tracker items. Both go through the approval flow, and the report logs what was sent or changed.

issues.quote: The dashboard source is `assets/dashboard.html` in this skill package.
issues.problem: The 98 KB dashboard needs a browser with the File System Access API pointed at the same files the agent edits. The sandbox workspace cannot give it that (ATTRIBUTION.md lists this as unresolved), so the file is dead weight and a false promise.
issues.fix: Drop the asset, or replace it with a Google Sheet or Notion view created through run_block, if a visual board is wanted.

scenarios.prompt: Pull everything assigned to me in Linear into my task list and tell me what's overdue or going stale.
scenarios.why: Step 2's matching table and 'Present diff and let user decide' produce a good add/complete diff if the model maps 'if MCP available' to run_block Linear. But Step 1 blocks a fresh workspace with 'suggest /productivity:start', a command that does not exist, and SKILL.md does not send the model to the bundled references/start.md. In Step 3, 'Tasks in Active for 30+ days' cannot be computed because the TASKS.md format stores no added date. Every personal task not in Linear gets flagged 'potentially stale'. Steps 4-5 then ask memory-decoding questions the user did not ask for.

scenarios.prompt: Over the last two weeks I promised people things in Slack and email. Find what I haven't tracked. Slack isn't connected and I don't keep a TASKS.md.
scenarios.why: The 'Possible Missing Tasks' format, with a dated quote per item and 'Add to TASKS.md?', is the right deliverable, and searching sent mail catches 'I'll send…' promises. But Step 1 gates on TASKS.md existing. SKILL.md has no fallback for the missing Slack connection: no connect_integration, no export or paste option, not even start.md's 'skip it and note the gap'. It scans only sent mail, so it misses asks the principal received and has not answered. 'Suggest New Memories' builds mention-frequency profiles of people from DMs with no privacy rule, which conflicts with Kai's 'keep what you read private' boundary.

task-list-management.job: maintain personal task and commitment list
task-list-management.summary: Keeps a TASKS.md checklist (Active / Waiting On / Someday / Done) in the working directory and maps common phrases (what's on my plate, add, done, waiting on) to file edits. It offers to pull commitments out of meeting summaries, and it bundles a browser dashboard plus verbatim copies of the productivity start and update commands.
strengths: Clear four-section TASKS.md template (Active / Waiting On / Someday / Done) with a scannable line format: bold title, for-whom, due date, since-date for waiting items.
Maps natural phrasings ('what's on my plate', 'remind me to', 'done with X', 'what am I waiting on') to concrete edits, which makes the trigger easy to hit.
'Extracting Tasks' pulls in commitments the user made and requires confirmation before adding ('don't auto-add without confirmation').
Short SKILL.md (about 90 lines of body). The bundled update.md has a useful external-versus-local diff table (offer to add / flag stale / offer to mark done).
missing: A clear system-of-record decision: use the user's connected Todoist/Linear/Notion/Google Tasks via run_block, with TASKS.md only as a fallback
Persistent storage via workspace files or memory_store instead of the sandbox cwd
ISO due dates, timezone handling, and a priority field so overdue and urgent can be computed
A defined output template for the 'what's on my plate' / daily digest summary
A two-way commitments ledger (owed by me / owed to me) with drafted nudges for stale Waiting On items, sent only on approval
Weekly review routine (schedule_routine) that triages stale, overdue and context-less items, taking over from productivity-task-sync
Recurring tasks and a split between scheduled date and deadline
Privacy rule for extraction from inbox and chat: don't carry one person's message into another context
Handoffs: tasks extracted by meeting-follow-up-draft land here; weekly-priorities-review reads from here
Disambiguation and confirmation before completing, moving or deleting items

issues.quote: Always use `TASKS.md` in the current working directory.
issues.problem: On AutoGPT the bash_exec working directory is an ephemeral sandbox, so the task list does not survive between sessions, and persistence is the whole point of the skill. The rule also forces a parallel list even when the user already runs Todoist, Linear or Notion, all of which have blocks.
issues.fix: Store the list at a named workspace path via read_workspace_file/write_workspace_file (e.g. tasks/TASKS.md). At first use, ask which system of record to use; if Todoist/Linear/Notion is connected, read and write it via run_block (with approval before writing) and treat TASKS.md only as a fallback or mirror.

issues.quote: Inform the user: "I've added the dashboard. Run `/productivity:start` to set up the full system."
issues.problem: This tells the user to run a slash command that the platform doesn't have and the package itself says it doesn't register. The first interaction dead-ends.
issues.fix: Delete the instruction. If setup is needed, do it in the skill: ask for the minimum inputs (where tasks live, timezone, key people) and store preferences with memory_store.

issues.quote: If not, copy it from `assets/dashboard.html` in this skill package to the current working directory
issues.problem: The 98 KB dashboard needs the browser's File System Access API (showOpenFilePicker/showDirectoryPicker) pointed at the same local files the agent edits, which is impossible when the agent writes in a sandbox. It also loses data: parseTaskMarkdown keeps only checkbox sub-items, and toMarkdown rewrites the file, so the plain 'Sub-bullets for additional details' and the '~~Task~~ (date)' completed format are dropped or mangled on auto-save.
issues.fix: Remove the dashboard section and assets/dashboard.html. If a visual view is wanted, render a read-only summary table or a Google Sheet via run_block instead.

issues.quote: Highlight anything overdue or urgent
issues.problem: Due dates are free text ('due [date]', e.g. 'due Friday'), and the skill has no priority field, date normalization or timezone, so 'overdue or urgent' can't be computed reliably, and nothing defines the order of the summary.
issues.fix: Require ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) resolved from relative phrases against today in the user's timezone (confirm when ambiguous), plus an optional priority marker. Define the plate summary template: Overdue, Due today, This week, Waiting > N days, with owner and date per line.

issues.quote: Note how long each item has been waiting
issues.problem: Waiting On items get an age but no threshold and no next action. A senior EA would flag stale items and draft a nudge to the person who owes the item.
issues.fix: Flag items waiting longer than a set threshold (default 5 business days, adjustable). Offer a short nudge draft to the owner, routed through reply-draft-in-your-voice, and send only on explicit approval of that exact message.

issues.quote: Keep Done section for ~1 week, then clear old items
issues.problem: This silently deletes the user's records, which conflicts with Kai's rule to delete nothing without a clear yes, and it leaves no history for weekly reviews.
issues.fix: Move items older than a week to an archive file (e.g. tasks/DONE-YYYY-MM.md) and say so, or ask before clearing.

issues.quote: Find the task
issues.problem: No rule for zero or multiple matches when the user says 'done with X', so the wrong task can be closed.
issues.fix: If there isn't exactly one confident match, list the candidates and ask which one. Echo the change (task, section moved, date) after editing.

issues.quote: Native `/productivity:start` and `/productivity:update` command references remain unchanged; this package does not register those commands.
issues.problem: The package's references are verbatim copies of the productivity-setup and productivity-task-sync packages. They carry Claude/Cowork-only constructs (CLAUDE.md working memory, 'in Cowork, the agent runs in a VM', `gh issue list`, `~~category` placeholders), and the dashboard is duplicated across all four productivity packages. This adds noise and triple-counts the same kit.
issues.fix: Merge into one task skill. Keep update.md's triage and diff table as a single reference rewritten for run_block/MCP sources, drop start.md and CONNECTORS.md, and move CLAUDE.md memory duties to memory_store/workplace-memory-management.

scenarios.prompt: Kai, add two things to my list: send Priyanka the board deck by Friday, and remind me to book the Lisbon venue. Then tell me what's on my plate this week.
scenarios.why: The 'add a task' and 'what's on my plate' handlers produce correctly formatted Active entries and a summary. But File Location says to write TASKS.md to the current working directory, which on AutoGPT is the ephemeral E2B sandbox, so the list is gone next session unless the model decides on its own to use write_workspace_file. On first run the skill copies dashboard.html and tells the user to run the nonexistent `/productivity:start`. 'due Friday' is stored as free text, so the later 'overdue' check can't be computed reliably. There is no template for the plate summary (overdue / today / this week / waiting).

scenarios.prompt: Go through my inbox and last week's meeting notes and tell me what I promised people and what's now overdue. I also keep some stuff in Todoist, so don't lose that.
scenarios.why: SKILL.md's 'Extracting Tasks' correctly says to ask before adding. But 'Always use TASKS.md' forces a second list next to Todoist, with no run_block Todoist path and no statement of which list is the system of record. The inbox scan lives only in references/update.md (comprehensive mode), which SKILL.md never routes to for this request. That flow starts with 'If they don't exist, suggest /productivity:start first' (it needs CLAUDE.md/memory), then relies on `~~chat` placeholders and `gh issue list`. Overdue status depends on free-text dates, and the skill has no rule about keeping one sender's message out of another context, which Kai's persona requires.

16:job-offer-and-close-plan.job: shape, negotiate and close a job offer
16:job-offer-and-close-plan.summary: Takes Sofia from a finalist to a signed offer. It sets the band before anything else and composes with offer_math.py, writes an approval brief and fills the letter from the company template only, cross-checking figures and dates with check_terms.py. It compares and logs counters, and runs a dated single-owner close plan that checks FCRA/ADA contingency order and schedules the answer-by follow-up.
strengths: The band-first rule is enforced in code: offer_math.py exits 3 without a band and a named approver, and it never proposes a figure.

check_terms.py cross-checks every money figure and date in the letter and email against approved terms. I confirmed it catches wrong bases written as 'EUR 5k', '150.000 euros', '10.714,29 Euro' and mismatched currencies, and treats template-fixed figures as INFO.

fill_offer_template.py touches placeholders only, keeps binding clauses byte-for-byte, handles Word placeholders split across runs, forces DRAFT in the filename, and refuses a template with no placeholders.
The pay-history rule holds even when history is volunteered: a shared detector refuses such terms, and the counter log records the ask minus the history.

close_plan.py rejects the candidate or the assistant as a track owner, requires IANA timezones, and enforces standalone FCRA disclosure before the check and medical/drug tracks after acceptance, with an honest note on where the house rule is stricter than the ADA.

The Marco walkthrough is a realistic hard case: a sales OTE offer, volunteered pay, an above-band ask, a competing offer and a missing FCRA disclosure, plus California/SF fair-chance flags routed to counsel.
The 'Not for' line gives clear routing to siblings, and templates/attorney-brief.md makes the legal hand-off concrete.

It uses real platform capabilities: Gmail drafts only via validate_only and never a send tool, schedule_followup as the last action, memory without figures, a review-only consult_teammate check, and a Linear hand-off with no comp. Fallbacks cover no Python, no template and no Gmail.
missing: Resignation coaching and prep for a buy-back counteroffer from the current employer
Accept-to-start engagement and renege-risk tracks (v1 had them)
A give/get record in the counter log
A check that the offer sits inside any posted pay range (US states, EU Pay Transparency Directive)
Non-US offer norms: EU/UK notice and probation, right-to-work checks, GDPR retention of offer files
In-policy sales levers as paired gives (draw, ramp guarantee, territory/quota relief via the plan owner)
A candidate-facing equity explainer built from approver-supplied numbers (shares, strike, vesting, exercise window)
Visa sponsorship and relocation terms
A holding message and expedited approval path for an expiring competing offer

issues.quote: Errors go to the owner first. Above band needs `above_band_approval`
issues.problem: check_terms.py parses base_pay with to_number(), which strips only commas and spaces. I tested this: with base_pay 'EUR 125,000' on a 95-110k band the band check is skipped silently (0 errors), and '125.000' in European grouping reads as 125, giving only a below-min WARN. The script already has a term_amount() that parses both formats correctly. So the skill's central above-band guardrail can be bypassed just by formatting the value.
issues.fix: Parse base_pay, band min/max and above_band_approval.amount with term_amount()/parse_amount(). Raise an ERROR when base_pay is not numeric. Add a regression case to the examples.

issues.quote: hand the hire to the first-week owner with the
issues.problem: v1 covered resignation coaching and accept-to-start engagement. v2 drops both, so there is no pre-close question on counteroffer (buy-back) risk, no 'resignation submitted' track, and no pre-start touchpoints. Buy-back counteroffers and reneging between signature and start are the most common late-stage losses, and the close plan now ends at signature plus hand-off.
issues.fix: Add a pre-close question on how they will resign and what they will do if their employer counters. Add 'resignation submitted' and 'pre-start check-in' tracks to templates/close-plan.csv and a short section on each in references/negotiation-and-close.md.

issues.quote: gives offer vs ask vs proposal; then the paired give and the walk-away
issues.problem: The skill calls it a 'paired give', but nothing records what the company gets in return. counter-log.csv has no column for it, and the Priya example concedes the full ask (108k proposal = 108k ask) with no trade. offer_math.py also takes bonus percentages only, with no bonus amount, for the offer/ask/proposal columns.
issues.fix: Add an in_exchange_for column to counter-log.csv. Show a real trade in the example (e.g. base up, signing dropped, answer-by brought forward). Add --offer/--ask/--proposal-bonus-amount.

issues.quote: paste its table. Comp evidence is only the band, company grids, or
issues.problem: references/pay-history-and-transparency.md says to check that the offer sits inside any range posted for the role. Neither the procedure, check_terms.py nor the checklist does this. An offer outside a posted range is a compliance exposure in CO/WA/NY/CA and under the EU Pay Transparency Directive.
issues.fix: Add an optional posted_range block to offer-terms.json, a WARN in check_terms.py when base falls outside it, and a checklist line.

issues.quote: No band: say so and ask; do not compose around the gap. No template:
issues.problem: With no band, the skill simply stops. Its own reference allows posted pay data with links as evidence for the approver, and a senior recruiter would use that to get a band set quickly, especially when a competing offer is expiring.
issues.fix: Add: offer to compile posted ranges with links for the approver, each labelled FACT, never proposing a figure, and put a holding message to the candidate on the close plan.

issues.quote: so every money figure (currency-marked or "k") and date matches, in the
issues.problem: Steps 6-8 pack script internals into the SKILL.md body: k-suffix parsing, INFO semantics, derived-term handling, exit codes and the repeated 'cd ~/skills/... &&' prefix. At 173 lines it is harder to scan, and the examples read partly like script regression fixtures (pt-euros-mistake.md, de-euro-mistake.md).
issues.fix: Move the script behaviour into a references/scripts.md and keep one command line per step in the body. Move the locale regression fixtures out of examples/ or into a tests folder.

issues.quote: Contingency wording and order come only from the template. An adverse
issues.problem: The legal references are US-centric (FCRA, ADA, California) with a single UK line, yet the main walkthrough is a Lisbon hire. The EU Pay Transparency Directive (transposition deadline June 2026), UK right-to-work checks, EU notice and probation norms, and GDPR retention of offer files are all missing, so a non-US hard case gets no flags.
issues.fix: Add a short non-US section to contingency-order.md and pay-history-and-transparency.md that lists the flags and routes to the people lead or attorney. Dated, 'may apply, confirm with counsel'.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: save_to_path="/home/user/offer/<cand>/template.docx")
issues.problem: The template is saved to scratch /home/user/offer while every output goes to durable ~/workspace/hiring/offers, so the source template is not kept with the offer files. references/contingency-order.md and sources.md also cite docs/research/recruiting.md, which the package does not ship.
issues.fix: Save the template under ~/workspace/hiring/offers/<role>-<cand>/. Replace the dossier path citation with the shipped references/sources.md only.

scenarios.prompt: Lena signed off on Priya Nair for the Senior Backend role. Band is EUR 95-110k base, approved by Tom in finance on 1 Sep. She says base matters most and has one month's notice. Shape the offer, write the approval brief, and fill our letter template (attached .docx).
scenarios.why: Step 1 records the band and approver. Step 2 captures values and notice in her words. Step 3 has offer_math.py produce the table (I confirmed the in-band position and midpoint maths), and step 4 fills templates/offer-brief.md. Step 5 runs check_terms.py and step 6 fills the .docx; I tested split Word runs and they fill correctly, then the letter and email are cross-checked. Step 8 dates the close plan with internal owners and step 9 schedules the answer-by check. The deliverables are complete, reusable and gated on approval.

scenarios.prompt: Our SF AE finalist told the recruiter he's on 105 now, wants 115 base, and says he has a 230 OTE offer expiring Friday. Band is 90-105 but Rita hasn't put it in writing, our template is a PDF with no placeholders, and we haven't done background-check disclosures. Get me something I can send today.
scenarios.why: The guardrails fire correctly. Pay history gets dropped with a one-line note, and the band must be confirmed in writing (step 1). The offer_math counter table flags the ask as USD 10k over band and says to escalate. The missing FCRA disclosure is flagged and fixed in the close plan. A PDF template exits 2 and the letter falls back to [COMPANY TEMPLATE REQUIRED] plus the attorney brief. Where it falls short: the exploding competing deadline is only an escalation checkbox, with no expedited approval track and no holding message to buy time before a counter exists. It proposes no in-policy sales levers (draw, ramp guarantee, signing) as paired gives, and the no-band fallback just stops instead of offering the approver a linked posted-range evidence pack.

better: A table of inputs with source and 'if missing' behaviour, replacing a one-sentence inputs line
Executable enforcement v1 only asserted: the band and approver gate, pay-history refusal, the above-band approval record, OTE arithmetic and figure/date consistency across letter and email
Reusable artefacts that v1 lacked: offer brief, terms.json, letter outline, close-plan.csv with contingency rows, counter log, close messages, attorney brief, pre-send checklist
Sales offers (OTE, pay mix, commission plan carried as approved text) and FCRA/ADA contingency ordering are now covered
Explicit 'Not for' routing to siblings and the attorney, and an output contract with file locations and blockers-first replies
Platform wiring with approval: Gmail drafts only, schedule_followup for answer-by, memory without figures, a teammate review, a Linear hand-off
Two worked walkthroughs, including a realistic hard sales case
worse: Dropped v1's resignation coaching and accept-to-start engagement (paperwork, gear, day-one logistics); the plan now stops at signature plus hand-off
Dropped the 'what should we pay this finalist' trigger, even though step 1 is built for exactly that question
SKILL.md roughly doubled (82 to 173 lines) with script trivia inline, and the package grew to about 2,270 lines including regression-style fixtures
Introduced a band-check parsing bug: a formatted base_pay skips or misreads the above-band check
Cites an unshipped research dossier path in its references

run-regulated-partnership-motions.job: run partnerships under regulatory compliance constraints
run-regulated-partnership-motions.summary: A 58-line outline telling Anika to name the governing regime and Legal owner first, run payments, US federal, tender or medical-education motions 'inside the frame' with rule citations, keep a dated compliance log, pause on any flag until written clearance, and review standing each quarter.
strengths: Frame-before-motion ordering is correct, and 'a verbal clear is not a clear' is a strong, testable gate
Unclear rules mean pausing with a drafted question for counsel rather than proceeding on a guess
Flags pause the motion until a written clear, and the quarterly continue/pivot/exit call must cite its evidence
Explicit no-send rule for bids, filings, dispute responses and regulated communications
missing: Per-regime reference checklists with primary-source links
Anti-bribery/anti-kickback third-party due diligence and sanctions screening
Instruction to fetch and quote the rule text instead of recalling it
Non-US procurement regimes (EU directives, UK Procurement Act 2023)
Healthcare specifics: ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence, Sunshine Act/Open Payments, PhRMA/EFPIA/MedTech codes
Data-protection overlay (HIPAA, GDPR) where regulated data moves between partners
Frame-brief and compliance-log templates
'Not legal advice' notice and a counsel handoff template

issues.section: Run the motion inside the frame
issues.quote: Payments: scheme-rule checks and dispute triage.
issues.problem: Each regime gets one line with no checks, thresholds or sources. There is nothing on card-scheme third-party agent/ISO registration, PCI DSS scope, chargeback-ratio monitoring programs, or the payfac/sponsor-bank relationship, so the 'motion plan' has no substance.
issues.fix: Ship one reference per regime (references/payments.md, federal.md, tenders.md, medical-education.md), each with the gating checks, primary sources and typical partner-motion pitfalls. Route from this section by relative path.

issues.section: Run the motion inside the frame
issues.quote: Each step names its rule citation, or it stays INFERENCE.
issues.problem: It demands citations but never says to retrieve and quote the primary text. That invites fabricated clause numbers, which in a regulated context is worse than no citation.
issues.fix: Require web_fetch of the primary source (acquisition.gov, scheme rulebook, ACCME standards, the tender notice). Quote the clause verbatim with its URL and retrieval date. If it cannot be retrieved, mark it UNKNOWN and add it to the counsel question list.

issues.section: Run the motion inside the frame
issues.quote: Federal: vehicle qualification and bid compliance against the Federal
issues.problem: US-only and imprecise: it pairs FAR with DFARS as if DFARS always applies, and omits GSA MAS, SAM/UEI, TAA, limitation on subcontracting, OCI, FedRAMP/CMMC. 'Tenders' ignores non-US regimes such as the EU procurement directives and the UK Procurement Act 2023.
issues.fix: Split by jurisdiction and buyer (civilian vs DoD, EU/UK public procurement), with a qualification checklist per vehicle type.

issues.section: Run the motion inside the frame
issues.problem: No anti-corruption or third-party due-diligence step. Channel partners and resellers into government and healthcare are the classic FCPA/UK Bribery Act/Anti-Kickback exposure. Partner vetting and fee/commission reasonableness are core to a regulated partner motion.
issues.fix: Add a 'Vet the partner' step: ownership, government/HCP ties, sanctions screening, commission reasonableness, and anti-bribery certifications. Log each check with its owner.

issues.quote: Which regime governs, which clauses bind us, and who in Legal or
issues.problem: No triage procedure. It gives no question list for identifying the regime and no rule for when several regimes or jurisdictions apply at once, which is the common hard case.
issues.fix: Add a short triage question set (buyer type, jurisdiction, money flow, HCP involvement, data type). Add a precedence rule: the strictest regime governs and each conflict goes to counsel.

issues.quote: No Legal owner means the owner holds compliance until one is named, and
issues.problem: This makes the business owner the interim compliance interpreter. There is also no statement that the output is not legal advice.
issues.fix: Say that without named counsel the skill only prepares the frame brief and the counsel questions, with no motion steps. Add a one-line 'not legal advice; counsel decides' notice to every deliverable.

issues.quote: Dated entries per check, flag, and ruling, each with its owner.
issues.problem: No log schema or storage location, so the log will not persist across conversations and cannot feed the quarterly review.
issues.fix: Give a log template (date, motion, rule citation, check, result, flag, owner, written-clear reference). Persist it with write_workspace_file or memory_store.

issues.quote: federal vehicles, tenders, or medical education — frame first.
issues.problem: 'Frame first' and 'federal vehicles' are insider jargon. The description does not separate this skill from orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids, which also covers bids and teaming.
issues.fix: Rephrase in plain terms, e.g. government contracts, public tenders, card-network rules, pharma/medical education. Name the boundary: this skill sets the compliance frame and the bid mechanics stay in orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids.

scenarios.prompt: We want to team with a GSA Schedule reseller to bid on a VA software RFQ due in three weeks. What do we have to check before we co-bid, and can you set up the compliance log?
scenarios.why: 'Name the frame first' gives a Legal owner and a log. But the federal line only says 'vehicle qualification and bid compliance against the Federal Acquisition Regulation and its defence supplement'. DFARS does not govern a VA buy, and nothing covers GSA MAS terms, SAM registration, TAA, limitation on subcontracting or teaming/OCI rules. The model has to supply all of that unaided and may cite wrongly.

scenarios.prompt: A pharma customer wants us and our device-distributor partner to co-sponsor a CME webinar series in the US and Germany. Legal hasn't been assigned yet and marketing wants the invite out Friday.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks hold correctly: nothing regulated leaves, the question for counsel is drafted, no send without a yes. But 'approved-content rules and healthcare-professional interaction rules' is the only medical-education guidance. There is no ACCME independence standard, Open Payments reporting, AKS or EU industry code, and no rule for which frame wins when jurisdictions conflict.

run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence.job: run weekly partner co-sell and deal registration
run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence.summary: Weekly co-sell rhythm with an active partner: prep the call most-stuck-first, enforce deal-registration hygiene with specific SLA and protection-window defaults, diagnose stuck joint deals in a fixed order to one rescue move, and close on one partner ask. It also folds in a quarterly partner prune and conflict report.
strengths: Concrete registration defaults (two-business-day decision, 90-day protection, 7-day expiry alert, one 30-day renewal, never auto-renew) with 'program rules win — cite them'
Ordered stuck-deal diagnosis (champion, buyer, competitor, paper, partner deprioritised) leading to exactly one move with owner, date and failure path
'One ask, not a list' discipline and the most-stuck-first ordering
Clear boundary: direct-sales closing goes to the AE with a clean brief
Stale-data fallback refuses to invent progress
missing: Account mapping and rules of engagement (who leads each mapped account)
Default rulings for multi-partner, customer-choice and reverse-registration cases
A call-prep template and registration table
CRM/partner-portal read path and persistence of open actions between calls
Explicit no-write gate for registration submissions, approvals and declines
Link to handle-partner-conflict-and-churn for disputes and to track-partner-pipeline for sourced/influenced proof

issues.problem: No account-mapping or rules-of-engagement step. Mapping overlapping accounts (Crossbeam/Reveal-style overlap) and naming who leads each deal is the core of modern co-sell, and the persona defines co-sell by those rules of engagement.
issues.fix: Add a step: refresh the account overlap (connected tool, CSV or pasted list), tag each mapped account with lead side and play, and flag deals whose lead side is unclear.

issues.section: Rescue stuck joint deals with exactly one motion
issues.quote: Run a quarterly prune alongside the rescues: cut partners with no
issues.problem: Scope creep. Cutting partners is a portfolio/exit decision owned by manage-partner-renewals-and-exits and the portfolio review. Here it has no approval gate, which contradicts the persona's rule that exits are staged drafts the owner decides.
issues.fix: Remove the prune, or reduce it to 'flag candidates for the portfolio review'. Keep only the conflict-report count if it is needed for the weekly rhythm.

issues.quote: Track every registration through Submitted, In-review, Approved, or
issues.problem: The triggers include 'register this partner deal', but the skill never says the model must not submit, approve or decline a registration in the partner portal or CRM itself. The persona forbids registering deals on anyone's behalf.
issues.fix: Add: registration submissions, approvals, declines and renewals are staged as drafts with evidence, and the model never writes to the portal or CRM without the owner's yes.

issues.quote: for 90 days, alert 7 days before expiry, and allow exactly one 30-day
issues.problem: The registration defaults are restated with differences in design-the-partner-program and scale-the-partner-channel ('renewable on activity' vs 'exactly one 30-day renewal'). Anika can give contradictory answers depending on which skill loads.
issues.fix: Keep the registration policy in one place, owned by design-the-partner-program or a shared reference, and have this skill apply it and cite it.

issues.quote: Pre-write the edge rulings so nobody improvises them live: multi-partner
issues.problem: It names the edge cases (multi-partner splits, customer picks another partner, reverse registration) but gives no default ruling. The model will improvise exactly what the skill says must not be improvised.
issues.fix: State defaults: first-to-register with activity wins, customer choice overrides with documented consent, split credit under a named rule. Route disputes to handle-partner-conflict-and-churn.

issues.quote: reviews, quarterly business planning. Score partner fit per opportunity
issues.problem: It asks for a per-opportunity partner-fit score without criteria or a scale. The bi-weekly/quarterly rhythm design and quota-relief proposals are program-design work inside a weekly prep skill.
issues.fix: Give a three-to-four-criterion fit check (coverage in account, relevant certification, prior win, active champion). Move the rhythm and comp design to run-partner-strategy-and-operations.

issues.quote: No CRM movement to read means you prep from the last call notes and the
issues.problem: The only data fallback is 'no movement'. There is no route to read the CRM (HubSpot block, a Salesforce MCP) or to ask for an export, and no place to persist the open actions between weekly calls.
issues.fix: Add: check connected CRM → run_block/run_mcp_tool; else ask for CSV/paste. Store open actions and the ask in memory_store so next week's prep starts from them.

issues.quote: The call prep (moved, stalled, actions), the registration hygiene list,
issues.problem: The deliverables are named but have no template, so the output shape drifts week to week and cannot be diffed.
issues.fix: Ship templates/co-sell-call-prep.md with fixed sections and a registration hygiene table (ID, date, state, window end, conflict check, flag).

scenarios.prompt: Prep my Thursday call with Brightline Consulting. Here's the HubSpot export of our joint deals and last week's notes.
scenarios.why: The steps map directly: moved/stalled with one action per side per stuck deal, a registration hygiene list with IDs, windows and conflict checks, a rescue line from the ordered diagnosis, and one partner ask. The fallback avoids inventing progress.

scenarios.prompt: Two partners both registered Globex. One registration expired yesterday, the other has no activity logged, our AE says the customer prefers partner B, and our CRM isn't connected. Sort it out and tell me what to say to each partner.
scenarios.why: The skill flags expired and no-activity registrations and says to 'pre-write the edge rulings' for multi-partner splits and customer choice, but it supplies no default ruling. It does not route the dispute to handle-partner-conflict-and-churn, and it gives no path to get the data (HubSpot block, CSV) when the CRM is missing. The model will improvise the ruling the skill says must not be improvised.

run-the-partner-marketing-engine.job: plan and run partner co-marketing campaigns
run-the-partner-marketing-engine.summary: Turns co-marketing into an evergreen system: a dated calendar on a three-to-five format menu, partner-field ABM plays gated on product alignment, campaign briefs with proof approval flags and spend pre-approval, and an MDF return report using (growth minus cost) over cost.
strengths: 'An undated idea is a backlog line, not a commitment', and every item must trace to a plan metric
One-to-many by default, with one-to-one reserved for proven bets, which is sound scale economics
ABM plays gated on a real integration and prioritised on shared ICP and active integration users over logos
Clear ownership split: Product owns integration quality, Partnerships the relationship, Marketing the story
No committed spend without the owner's yes; proof carries approval-state flags
missing: Lead-sharing consent, data-sharing terms and joint lead follow-up SLA
Co-branding/trademark and customer-reference approval gates
Campaign brief and calendar templates
Attribution definition tied to sourced/influenced proof, with a baseline
Benchmarks per format (webinar show rates, MQL-to-SQL), labelled as assumptions
Tool path for calendar storage and campaign data (Sheets, HubSpot)

issues.section: Run account-based plays with partner field teams
issues.problem: No handling of joint-lead and account-data sharing. Exchanging named-account lists, webinar registrants or leads between companies needs consent language, a data-sharing agreement and a follow-up SLA. Without them the plays create GDPR/CAN-SPAM exposure and leads nobody follows up.
issues.fix: Add a 'Lead handling' block to every brief: who collects consent, who owns the lead, the share mechanism and legal basis, and the follow-up SLA per side. Route contract questions to structure-the-partner-agreement/Legal.

issues.section: Report the objectives and the return
issues.quote: Return is (MDF-driven growth minus MDF cost) divided by MDF cost, with
issues.problem: 'MDF-driven growth' is undefined, and mixing influenced revenue into return conflicts with the persona's sourced/influenced proof rules. There is no baseline or incrementality, so the ROI can be inflated and the case with no MDF is undefined.
issues.fix: Define growth as proven sourced revenue per track-partner-pipeline, with influenced reported separately and never summed in. Name the window and baseline. When MDF cost is zero, report outcomes without a ratio.

issues.section: Report the objectives and the return
issues.quote: Run only proven campaigns through the channel — test new plays with
issues.problem: This duplicates design-the-partner-program's MDF loop almost verbatim, including the formula, proven-first and quarterly reallocation. The Toran partner-co-marketing package also sits on Anika, so ownership is muddy.
issues.fix: Keep MDF policy in design-the-partner-program and reference it. Scope this skill to running the calendar, plays and reporting, and name the boundary with partner-co-marketing (partner ideation) and onboard-and-enable-partners (first motion).

issues.quote: The message, the proof with its approval-state flags, the assets with
issues.problem: No brief template. Co-branding and trademark approval by the partner, and customer-reference consent for stories, are not called out as gates.
issues.fix: Ship templates/campaign-brief.md with message, audience, proof (approval state and source), co-brand approval owner, assets, spend lines, lead handling, metric, and dates.

issues.quote: Dated items only. Each carries an owner on each side, the audience it
issues.problem: No calendar format or persistence. The 'central source of truth' is not named, so the calendar is rebuilt every conversation.
issues.fix: Keep the calendar in a Google Sheet via run_block, or a workspace file with a fixed schema. Read it first on each run and write back only after the owner approves.

issues.quote: Use when co-marketing needs an engine rather than a one-off: the dated calendar, account-based plays, campaign briefs, and the return narrative.
issues.problem: This competes with the Toran partner-co-marketing skill ('co-marketing', 'joint campaign') also assigned to Anika. The distinction ('engine vs one-off') is subtle for a router.
issues.fix: Add an explicit exclusion: not for finding partners or brainstorming a single campaign (use partner-co-marketing), and not for the first post-signing motion (onboard-and-enable-partners).

scenarios.prompt: Build our Q1 co-marketing calendar with our three integration partners. We have $40K of MDF, and I want one ABM play with Partner A's field team.
scenarios.why: The calendar rules (dated, dual owners, audience, metric), the format menu, the ABM prioritisation on shared ICP and active integration users, and the brief with spend lines plus pre-approval produce a usable plan. Spend waits for the owner's yes.

scenarios.prompt: Our German partner wants to co-host a webinar and send us the attendee list afterwards. We have no MDF left and no past campaign results, and leadership wants an ROI number for the board next month.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks handle no budget (organic-only) and no history (baselines). But nothing covers consent or data-sharing terms for the attendee list, a GDPR issue. The ROI formula's 'MDF-driven growth' is undefined, and with zero MDF the formula divides by zero while leadership still expects a number.

scale-the-partner-channel.job: scale reseller, MSP and distributor channel activation
scale-the-partner-channel.summary: Territory-scale channel activation for resellers, MSPs and distributors: per-tier recruit-enable-first-deal-repeat funnel with time bars, a coverage plan with market-entry gates kept out of forecast, distributor operations (quoting SLA, registration rules, split-margin kicker, lead feedback, sell-through), and growth-to-strategic development plans.
strengths: A tier missing its bar gets a dated rescue play, never a lower bar
Enablement graded on trained reps attached to real opportunities, not signed logos
Market-entry gates (licensing, data, tax, employment) keep a territory in the plan but out of the forecast
Registration margin kicker is a concrete, well-known mechanism for forcing registration compliance
Distributor fallback reconciles both sides' exports with source labels, consistent with the persona's show-both rule
missing: Consistent, sourced funnel time and conversion bars per tier
Two-tier distribution mechanics (POS, price protection, rebates, stock rotation, inventory checks)
MSP-specific motion (consumption billing, NFR, PSA/RMM integrations)
Coverage math and direct-vs-channel rules of engagement
Owner and Finance gate on margin and kicker changes
Templates for funnel read, coverage plan and distributor checklist

issues.section: Run the activation funnel per tier
issues.quote: 10 to 16, a repeat deal by week 16.
issues.problem: The time bars conflict: a first close allowed as late as week 16 cannot precede a repeat deal due by week 16, and a first close at week 10 sits before the week-12 registration bar. The conversion bars are promised but never given, and none are labelled as defaults or sourced.
issues.fix: Make the bars sequential per tier, for example first registration ≤ week 8, first close ≤ week 16, repeat ≤ week 26. Label them as defaults that program rules override, and add conversion bars between stages.

issues.quote: Sell-through reads per distributor.
issues.problem: Two-tier distribution is reduced to one line. There is nothing on POS reporting cadence, sell-in vs sell-through, inventory and channel-stuffing checks, price protection, stock rotation, rebates or credit, and MSP mechanics (consumption billing, NFR licences, PSA/RMM integration) are absent despite MSPs being in the description.
issues.fix: Add a distributor-ops checklist and an MSP section in references/, and route to them from here.

issues.quote: registration kicker, for example 20 plus 10 of 30 — so the split forces
issues.problem: Margin structure is presented as something to set, with no owner approval gate. The persona lists margin tiers and discount floors as owner-only decisions, and the gate here covers only 'territory commitments and anything partner-facing'.
issues.fix: Stage any margin or kicker change as a draft with a model from model-the-partnership-commercials, and require the owner's (and Finance's) yes before it enters partner terms.

issues.quote: two business days, a 90-day protection window renewable on activity,
issues.problem: This is the third copy of the registration policy (also in design-the-partner-program and run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence), with inconsistent renewal terms.
issues.fix: Reference the single registration policy instead of restating it.

issues.quote: Coverage by geography and segment, the named gaps, and the attach motion
issues.problem: No coverage math (addressable accounts per territory against partner capacity or active reps) and no channel-conflict rules with direct sales, the main source of friction at territory scale.
issues.fix: Add a coverage ratio calculation run in bash_exec from CRM or partner data, plus rules of engagement with direct sales per segment.

issues.quote: The named plays that move a growth partner to strategic, each with a bar,
issues.problem: Tier graduation criteria are owned by design-the-partner-program. Here they are unanchored, so the development bars may not match the program's tier bars.
issues.fix: Pull the tier bars from the program design and plan against those gaps. Tier changes stay drafts for the owner.

issues.problem: No templates for the funnel read, the coverage plan or the distributor checklist, and no read path for partner-portal or CRM data beyond the fallback.
issues.fix: Ship a funnel table and distributor checklist template. Name the data path: connected CRM or PRM, else a requested CSV.

scenarios.prompt: We've signed 40 resellers in DACH over six months and only 6 have closed anything. Give me an activation read and a rescue plan per tier.
scenarios.why: The per-tier funnel, the 'rescue play not a lower bar' rule and enablement graded on engaged reps give a strong frame. But the time bars ('first registration by week 12, first close in weeks 10 to 16, a repeat deal by week 16') contradict each other. There are no conversion-rate bars, and no step for collecting the reseller data, so the read can mis-grade partners.

scenarios.prompt: Our distributor's monthly POS file doesn't match our bookings, we want to launch in Brazil next quarter, and our MSPs are asking for monthly consumption billing. What's the plan?
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly reconciles distributor exports against ours with every number source-labelled. The Brazil launch sits behind market-entry gates and stays out of forecast. But the skill has nothing on POS/sell-in versus sell-through reconciliation rules, price protection or rebates, and nothing on MSP consumption billing, so two of the three asks get generic answers.

scope-the-tech-partnership.job: scope integration partnership before engineering handoff
scope-the-tech-partnership.summary: Pre-engineering scoping of an integration partnership: a scoping brief (program selection, APIs, data flows, auth, rate limits, owned open questions), a ranked voice-of-partner input for Product, launch readiness with a certification gate, and a clean handoff tracked on adoption, attach and retention outcomes.
strengths: Hard boundary: 'This hands off to engineering. It never implements.'
Every unknown needs an owner and date: 'An unknown with no owner is not scoped.'
Voice of partner ranked with evidence (who asked, deal or adoption attached, frequency), plus an explicit won't-build list with reasons
A launch with no support path stays in beta
Success tracked on adoption, attach and retention lift rather than build progress
missing: Joint use case and business case at the top of the brief
Security, privacy and legal review (DPA/BAA, OAuth scopes, data residency, API ToS)
Build, maintain and support ownership matrix with deprecation policy
Partner-facing approval gate
Scoping brief and handoff templates
Marketplace listing and commercial terms of the integration (rev share, listing fees) as a pointer to model-the-partnership-commercials

issues.problem: No security, privacy or legal review. Data classification (PII/PHI), OAuth scopes and least privilege, DPA or BAA, data residency, SOC 2 evidence, and API terms of use and trademark use are the items that most often block integration partnerships.
issues.fix: Add a 'Data and trust' block: data classes crossing the boundary, scopes, agreements needed (DPA/BAA/API ToS), security evidence required from each side. Route regulated data to run-regulated-partnership-motions and Legal.

issues.quote: Platform and program selection first — pricing, program features, case
issues.problem: This puts the partner program's pricing and case studies ahead of the joint use case and business case. A senior scoping brief opens with the customer problem, the target accounts and the revenue or retention at stake, which drives everything after it.
issues.fix: Reorder: joint use case and ICP → business case (accounts, pipeline, attach target, labelled FACT/INFERENCE) → program selection → technical surface → open questions.

issues.problem: No build-and-maintain ownership model: who builds (us, partner, SI, embedded iPaaS), who maintains it, versioning and deprecation notice, the support SLA split and escalation path. These decide whether the integration survives past launch.
issues.fix: Add an ownership matrix (build, host, maintain, support tier 1/2, deprecation notice) to the brief and the handoff.

issues.problem: This is the only skill of the set without the 'nothing partner-facing leaves without your yes' line. Questions to partner engineering, beta invitations and joint messaging are all partner-facing.
issues.fix: Add: questions, beta invites and joint messaging are drafted and wait for the owner's explicit yes.

issues.quote: Pass the certification and technical-validation gate on performance,
issues.problem: The gate has no criteria, owner or evidence, so the model cannot tell whether it passed.
issues.fix: Name the gate owner, the minimum evidence per dimension (load test result, security review sign-off, interop test matrix) and where the evidence lives.

issues.section: Synthesize the voice of partner for Product
issues.quote: Ranked partner asks with their evidence: who asked, what deal or adoption
issues.problem: It says 'ranked' without a ranking method, so different runs rank inconsistently.
issues.fix: Give a simple score, e.g. revenue attached × frequency × strategic fit, computed in bash_exec with inputs labelled.

issues.quote: The brief, one named owner on each side, and a date. Then track the
issues.problem: No tool path for the handoff or tracking (Linear/GitHub issue draft via run_block, fetching API docs with web_fetch), and no output templates.
issues.fix: Ship templates/scoping-brief.md and a handoff issue template. Suggest web_fetch for docs and a drafted Linear/GitHub issue pending the owner's yes.

scenarios.prompt: Salesforce's ISV team wants us on AppExchange with a native integration. Scope it so I can take it to our VP Product next week.
scenarios.why: The brief gets program selection, API surface, auth and rate limits, open questions with owners, and a readiness checklist with a security validation gate. It never asks who builds and maintains the integration, what the business case or target accounts are, or what data leaves our system, so Product receives a technically framed brief without the reason to prioritise it.
