scenarios.prompt: A healthcare partner wants bi-directional sync of patient records. They have no public docs, just a Postman collection their PM forwarded. Our roadmap is locked until Q3. Draft the scoping and the email asking their engineers our questions.
scenarios.why: The fallback marks public material as INFERENCE and makes the documentation request step one. But nothing flags PHI, BAA or HIPAA review or routes to run-regulated-partnership-motions or Legal. The email to partner engineering has no approval gate in this skill. The locked roadmap is handled only by 'Product decides'.

set-board-level-alliance-strategy.job: set alliance portfolio strategy for the board
set-board-level-alliance-strategy.summary: Builds the board-grade alliance thesis: a one-page thesis tied to three corporate bets, a portfolio-to-thesis map with fund/grow/hold/exit calls scored quantitatively and qualitatively with sunset provisions, a sourced board pack shipped as a pre-read, and an annual/quarterly/out-of-cycle review rhythm.
strengths: 'A thesis with no named corporate bet behind it is a wish, not a strategy': every claim needs evidence or UNKNOWN
Sunset and exit provisions written at the time of the fund call, not when it goes wrong
Pre-read three business days out, with the session opened on members' mark-ups
Leave out any slide whose source is missing and say so, a strong no-invented-numbers rule
Out-of-cycle triggers named (failed bet, rival alliance, market shock) and each forum owns one decision
missing: Weighted scoring rubric with bars for fund/grow/hold/exit
Investment asks against expected returns and the build/buy/partner alternative
Board-pack and one-page thesis templates
Board confidentiality and MNPI handling
Change-of-control/rival-alliance playbook for out-of-cycle reads
Competitive alliance landscape as an input to where-we-win

issues.section: Map the portfolio to the thesis
issues.quote: Score each fund bet quantitatively (mutual customers, pipeline, overlap
issues.problem: It lists dimensions without weights, scale or thresholds, so fund/grow/hold/exit calls are not reproducible across runs or years.
issues.fix: Provide a scoring rubric (1-5 per dimension, weights, bars per call). Compute it in bash_exec and show the inputs with their sources and windows.

issues.section: Map the portfolio to the thesis
issues.problem: No capital-allocation framing. Board asks need the investment (dollars, headcount, MDF, SE hours) against expected return, payback and the build/buy/partner alternative, and this should pull from own-the-alliance-pnl and map-the-partner-ecosystem.
issues.fix: Add an 'Asks and returns' table per fund bet sourced from the alliance P&L, with the alternative considered, and reference those sibling skills.

issues.quote: No thesis, fund call, or board pack goes to a partner, a board member, or
issues.problem: This treats sending a board pack to a partner as allowed with a yes. Board materials hold confidential and possibly material non-public information and should never go to a partner. The skill gives no confidentiality marking or access guidance.
issues.fix: State that board packs and fund calls are internal and confidential, never partner-facing. Add confidentiality marking and a distribution list confirmed by the owner, with IR/Legal check for public companies.

issues.quote: Where we started (last year's thesis and calls), portfolio economics with
issues.problem: The pack sections are listed but there is no template or output format, and no route to produce slides or docs (Google Slides/Docs blocks), so format varies each year and cannot be compared year on year.
issues.fix: Ship templates/board-pack-outline.md and a one-page thesis template. Offer Google Slides/Docs creation via run_block as a draft.

issues.section: Write the thesis in one page
issues.quote: The three corporate bets alliances have to serve, the partner archetypes
issues.problem: The fixed 'three' bets is arbitrary and may force-fit a company with two or five strategic priorities.
issues.fix: Say 'the corporate bets (usually two to four)' and require each to be quoted from the corporate plan or marked INFERENCE.

issues.quote: An annual thesis review with the board. Quarterly business reviews — the
issues.problem: The rhythm overlaps run-partner-strategy-and-operations and run-global-partner-executive-councils with no clear handoff of which skill owns which forum.
issues.fix: Name the owner skill per forum (P&L close → own-the-alliance-pnl, councils → run-global-partner-executive-councils) and keep only the board forum and out-of-cycle trigger here.

scenarios.prompt: Board meeting in three weeks. The CEO wants a view on our 12 alliances: which to double down on, which to exit, and what we're asking for.
scenarios.why: The thesis, the portfolio map with fund/grow/hold/exit and one line of evidence, the board pack sections (where we started, economics, calls, new bets and asks, top three risks) and the three-business-day pre-read rule produce a credible pack. Unsourced slides are dropped with a note.

scenarios.prompt: There's no written corporate strategy, finance only has influenced revenue for half our alliances, and our biggest partner was just acquired by our main competitor. I need a board read this week.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks cover owner-stated bets marked INFERENCE and thesis-first when economics are missing, and 'a rival alliance' is a named out-of-cycle trigger. But there is no playbook for the change-of-control event (contract review, customer exposure, exit provisions) and no guidance on showing half-sourced economics without skewing the fund calls.

bug-report-handoff.summary: Collects evidence from linked tickets, redacts sensitive data, and drafts a nine-field engineering bug report plus a list of what stays unconfirmed, without filing it or guessing a root cause.
strengths: Redaction rules are specific and practical: credentials, tokens and other customers' data become [redacted], and exact error text is kept only after redaction
Keeps what customers reported apart from what support actually reproduced, and lists open questions and who is waiting on them
Clear draft-only boundary: it never files, sets priority, or guesses a root cause or fix date
The report fields match what engineering triage actually needs (steps from a clean start, expected vs actual, frequency, affected accounts)
missing: A step that decides whether the report is a bug, a documented limit, a how-to, or a feature request
Attaching to an existing issue instead of filing a duplicate
A security/data-exposure incident path
A severity scale mapped to the team's definitions
An attempt-to-reproduce step with a success rate
Business impact (account value, number of seats affected, SLA exposure)
A holding reply to affected customers, and a loop to update them when engineering responds
A Linear/GitHub issue template and create-after-approval route

issues.quote: Check the status page and known-issue list for a match.
issues.problem: It says to look for a match but never says what to do when one exists. The likely result is a duplicate bug report instead of adding this occurrence (count, accounts, new evidence) to the existing issue.
issues.fix: Add a branch: if it matches an open issue or known-issue entry, draft a comment for that issue with the new ticket ids, account count and any new environment details, and don't open a new report. If it matches a status-page incident, link the incident and skip the handoff.

issues.quote: Impact on the customer: blocked, slowed, or cosmetic.
issues.problem: The impact scale has no category for data exposure, data loss, security, or billing errors, and no path for escalating them. A cross-tenant data leak would go through the normal bug queue.
issues.fix: Add a severity step before writing: data exposure, data loss, security, or wrong charges go immediately to the named security/incident owner (from setup memory) with a minimal redacted packet and no ordinary ticket. Map everything else to the team's severity scale.

issues.quote: Use this when one or more tickets point to something broken in the product.
issues.problem: There is no step that classifies the report first. Documented plan limits (e.g. a 10,000-row export cap), user error, configuration problems, and feature requests all get written up as bugs, which wastes engineering time.
issues.fix: Add a first step: check the plans/limits doc and help centre. Classify the report as bug, limit working as designed, how-to, or feature request. Only bugs continue; send the others to support-reply-draft or a feature-request note.

issues.quote: Steps to reproduce, numbered, from a clean start.
issues.problem: It never asks support to try to reproduce the bug (test account, same plan and browser), so 'steps to reproduce' are often just the customer's story written as steps.
issues.fix: Add an attempt-to-reproduce step and record the result as reproduced by support (N of M tries), seen only in logs, or reported only.

issues.quote: Frequency: how many tickets and accounts, since when.
issues.problem: It leaves out the regression details engineers use to bisect: last known good date or release, request/trace IDs, exact timestamps with timezone, and HAR/console logs.
issues.fix: Add 'first bad release or date / last known good', request IDs and timestamps (with timezone), and a one-line ask for HAR or console output when the bug is browser-side.

issues.quote: Do not file the bug or change its priority yourself; draft it for the owner.
issues.problem: It doesn't say what format to use or where the draft goes. Linear and GitHub blocks exist, but nothing routes to them after approval, and there is no fallback when neither is connected.
issues.fix: Output the draft as a Linear/GitHub-ready issue (title, body, labels). After approval, offer run_block to create it, and fall back to copy-paste markdown when the tracker is not connected.

issues.quote: "ticket escalation"
issues.problem: This trigger is broad enough to fire for refund, VIP, or churn-threat escalations, and it overlaps with refund-and-exception-brief and the Toran customer-escalation package.
issues.fix: Replace it with bug-specific phrasing such as 'customer found a bug', 'something is broken', or 'file a bug from these tickets'.

scenarios.prompt: Tickets 4812, 4820 and 4833 all say Safari users get stuck in a login loop since Tuesday. Write this up for engineering.
scenarios.why: Gather-the-evidence collects browser/version/first-seen/error text, and the nine-field report covers steps, expected vs actual, environment, frequency, affected ticket ids and impact. The 'What stays unknown' section keeps customer claims apart from what support reproduced. The output is a solid report, though it is not in a tracker-ready format.

scenarios.prompt: One customer says they can see another company's invoices on their billing page and sent a screenshot. Escalate this to engineering.
scenarios.why: The redaction rules would keep the other company's data out of the report. But the impact scale stops at 'blocked, slowed, or cosmetic'. There is no step that treats a data exposure as a security incident, pages the security or incident owner right away instead of the normal bug queue, or tells support to stop copying the screenshot around. A model following the skill would write a routine bug report for what is really a privacy incident.

help-article-from-tickets.job: write help-centre article from repeat tickets
help-article-from-tickets.summary: Picks one repeat question, counts the tickets behind it, and drafts a customer-worded help article with confirmed steps plus a separate internal approval note listing sources and open questions.
strengths: Uses customers' own phrasing for titles because that's what they search for, which is good KCS practice
One action per step, exact UI labels, and a 'what you should see' line
Strict rule to document only confirmed steps, never untested workarounds
The internal approval note (ticket ids, who confirmed each step, open questions) stays out of the publishable text
Redacts and generalises customer wording before reusing it
missing: A revision path for existing articles, including merge and redirect
Article-type templates (troubleshooting, known issue, reference)
Search keywords/synonyms and related-article links
Owner and last-reviewed date
A deflection check after publish
Screenshot and alt-text conventions
Rules for what counts as internal-only and must stay out of public articles (roadmap, internal tool names)
A handoff to support-macro-library for the matching saved reply

issues.quote: should be fixed rather than replaced.
issues.problem: When an article already exists there is no branch for it. The skill never says to produce a revision with the changed sections marked, or to handle merges and redirects, so the default output is a new article that duplicates the existing one.
issues.fix: Add: if an article exists, output a revision (section-by-section changes, reason for each, and any article to merge or retire). Write a new article only when none covers the question.

issues.quote: a title in the customer's words, phrased as the task or question;
issues.problem: The article has no findability metadata: no search keywords or synonyms, category, related-article links, owner, or last-reviewed date. Help-centre search and deflection depend on these.
issues.fix: Add a metadata block: title, 3–6 search synonyms from ticket wording, category, related articles, owner, and a last-reviewed date.

issues.quote: numbered steps, one action each, with the exact button or menu name;
issues.problem: The template only fits how-to articles. Troubleshooting and known-issue articles need symptom, cause, fix, status, and last-updated sections, and conceptual or FAQ articles need a different shape again.
issues.fix: Choose the article type first (how-to, troubleshooting, known issue, reference) and give a short template for each.

issues.quote: Choose one question.
issues.problem: There is no rule for which repeat question earns an article (volume threshold, handle time, blocked vs how-to), so priorities come down to whim.
issues.fix: Rank candidates by ticket volume × handle time, with blocked-customer issues first, and say why this one was chosen.

issues.problem: Nothing happens after publish: no plan to check deflection (ticket volume on the topic afterwards, article views, feedback) and no review cadence tied to releases.
issues.fix: Add a follow-up line: a date to re-count tickets on this question and a review trigger on the next release that touches these screens. Offer schedule_followup.

issues.quote: Do not publish the article or edit the help centre yourself.
issues.problem: The skill doesn't say how the draft is delivered or how to read the current help centre when it isn't connected.
issues.fix: Read the public help centre with web_fetch, or ask for a paste or export. Deliver the draft as a Google Doc or Notion page via run_block, or as a workspace file, for the owner to publish.

issues.quote: "write docs"
issues.problem: This trigger is too generic: it would fire for API docs, internal runbooks, or product specs.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'turn tickets into a help article' or 'update the help centre article'.

scenarios.prompt: We got 23 tickets this month asking how to add a teammate to a workspace. Here are the tickets and our product notes. Can you write a help article?
scenarios.why: Pick-the-question sets the count and period and pulls the customer phrases. The article template gives a task-phrased title, who it's for, numbered steps with UI labels, what success looks like, and common problems. The approval note cites the ticket ids. The draft would be publishable after a screenshot pass.

scenarios.prompt: Our 'Exporting data' article is out of date since the new export screen shipped. 40 tickets about it. The help centre is on Zendesk Guide, which you can't log into, and the product notes only cover half of the new flow.
scenarios.why: The skill notices that an existing article 'should be fixed rather than replaced' but gives no revision procedure (changed sections, what to remove, redirects). It has no fallback for reading the help centre, such as web_fetch on the public URL or asking for a paste. It would correctly mark the unconfirmed half of the steps, but the result is a new article with gaps, not a clean revision the owner can apply.

refund-and-exception-brief.job: prepare refund or policy-exception approval brief
refund-and-exception-brief.summary: Builds a decision brief for a named approver on a refund, credit, or policy exception: verified facts, quoted policy with source, two or three costed options with precedent and deadlines, and a decision date.
strengths: Makes the approver the decision-maker and gives them costed options instead of a single recommendation
Includes the precedent each option sets, which is a genuinely senior consideration
Refuses to invent a policy when none is written
Marks unverified facts and records the customer's ask in their own words
Hard gate: no promise to the customer before the approver decides, and no billing changes
missing: An open chargeback/dispute path
Checks on statutory consumer rights and contract SLA credits
Named data sources (Stripe block or invoice export) and a missing-record fallback
Approval-limit lookup from setup memory
Customer value, tenure, prior-credit, and abuse-pattern context
Refund mechanics (method, proration, tax reversal)
Holding reply and post-decision reply
A decision log so later cases can cite precedent

issues.quote: For each give the cost, the precedent it sets, and any chargeback or legal
issues.problem: A chargeback is treated as a deadline to note, not a different path. Refunding a charge that is already disputed can pay the customer twice, and the response window and evidence pack belong to finance.
issues.fix: Add a branch: if a dispute or chargeback is open, don't propose a refund. Draft the dispute-evidence summary and deadline for the finance owner, and note that any goodwill must be coordinated with the dispute outcome.

issues.quote: Quote the refund or exception policy that applies, with its source and date.
issues.problem: Only the company's refund policy is checked. Contract or SLA credit terms (e.g. outage credits) and statutory consumer rights (cooling-off periods, auto-renewal notice rules) can override it, so the brief can recommend something unlawful or miss money the customer is owed.
issues.fix: Also check the customer's contract or order form for SLA credits. Flag the customer's jurisdiction and any likely statutory right as 'needs legal review' and route it to the legal teammate rather than deciding it.

issues.quote: Give the customer, plan, billing dates, amounts charged, what they asked for
issues.problem: It never names where the facts come from or what to do when a record is missing. The Stripe block could read charges; otherwise the skill should ask for an invoice or export.
issues.fix: Add an inputs line: read-only charge history (Stripe block when connected, else an invoice/export/paste), the policy doc, and the approval limits from setup memory. A missing charge record means the brief waits and says which record would unblock it.

issues.quote: a partial refund or credit, with the amount;
issues.problem: The options ignore customer value and risk context that approvers weigh: account value and tenure, churn signal, past refunds or credits, and abuse patterns. They also skip mechanics: refund vs account credit, proration, tax/VAT reversal, and whether money goes back to the original payment method.
issues.fix: Add a context row (tenure, spend, prior credits, churn risk) and for each option state the method (original payment method vs credit), proration basis, and tax treatment. Calculate amounts with the sandbox.

issues.quote: Name the approver and the date a decision is needed.
issues.problem: It assumes the approver is known. There is no link to approval limits (who can approve what amount) and no instruction for when no approver has been set.
issues.fix: Read approval limits and owners from memory. If the amount is above the limit or no owner is set, ask with ask_question before drafting.

issues.quote: Never promise a refund, credit, or exception to the customer before the
issues.problem: The skill blocks promises but gives the customer nothing while the approver decides, and has no step for the reply after the decision.
issues.fix: Add a short holding-reply draft (received, under review, when they'll hear back, no commitment). After the decision, hand off to support-reply-draft with the outcome.

scenarios.prompt: Customer on annual Pro renewed 20 days ago, forgot to cancel, and wants a full refund. Our policy is 14 days. Please prep this for Priya in finance.
scenarios.why: State-the-facts records plan, dates, amount, and the ask in the customer's words. Compare-with-policy quotes the 14-day clause and marks the request outside it. The options (decline per policy, prorated partial, full) each come with cost and precedent, and the approver and decision date are named. A finance lead could decide from this brief.

scenarios.prompt: A German customer has already opened a chargeback with their bank. They also say last week's outage wrecked their launch. Our policy says no refunds on monthly plans. Stripe isn't connected. What should we do?
scenarios.why: The skill mentions a chargeback deadline but never says an open dispute changes the path: refunding now can pay out twice, and the right move is dispute evidence through finance. It doesn't check contract or SLA outage credits, or flag EU consumer rights that may override the written policy. It also doesn't say to ask for an invoice export when Stripe is missing. The brief would recommend 'follow policy' on shaky legal ground.

support-getting-started.job: set up support desk on first use
support-getting-started.summary: Interviews the user for support sources (queue, help centre, policies, escalation paths), priority rules, approval owners, and tone, then returns a five-part setup brief with up to ten tickets ready to triage.
strengths: Covers the right setup areas: sources, priority definitions, approval owners for each action type, tone and banned words, escalation paths
Records owner and last-refresh date for each source and names unreadable ones
Ends with concrete tickets ready to triage, which bridges into real work
Consistent draft-only guardrail and a no-guessing rule for gaps
missing: Saving setup facts to memory and having sibling skills read them
A check of connected integrations and a CSV/paste fallback for help desks without a block
A work-first flow with questions asked one at a time and skippable
SLAs per channel, business hours, timezone, VIP tiers
Approval amount limits, not just owners
Offers of standing routines (daily queue, weekly themes)
A short intro and a starter menu for the next jobs
A regulated-data and redaction policy

issues.quote: Give the user:
issues.problem: The setup brief exists only in chat. Nothing is saved to memory, so support-reply-draft, refund-and-exception-brief and ticket-triage can't read approvers, priority rules or tone later, and the user gets asked again every session.
issues.fix: Save each agreed fact to memory with memory_store (one fact per line: approver per action type, priority definitions, SLAs, tone and banned words, source locations). Have the sibling skills read memory first.

issues.quote: Use this before triaging tickets or drafting replies.
issues.problem: This makes setup a gate in front of all work, and the skill loads again for every triage or reply request. Users with a live queue get a questionnaire.
issues.fix: Scope it to the first chat, or to when memory has no support prefs. Work the first pasted ticket or queue right away with safe defaults, then ask the remaining questions one at a time and let the user skip any.

issues.quote: Ask for the help-desk tool and queue views, the help centre, product notes,
issues.problem: It asks for everything instead of checking what is already connected, and has no fallback for help desks without a block (Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout, Freshdesk).
issues.fix: First check connected integrations (Gmail, Slack, Notion, Linear, HubSpot, Google Drive/Sheets) and say what was found. Offer connect_integration for gaps. Accept CSV exports or pasted threads for the queue and use web_fetch for a public help centre.

issues.quote: "help desk", "ticket queue"
issues.problem: These triggers are generic and collide with ticket-triage ('sort the queue') and reply requests, so the setup skill loads when the user wants work done.
issues.fix: Use setup-specific triggers: 'set up support', 'first time with Sasha', 'learn how our desk works', 'support preferences'.

issues.quote: Agree how the team defines urgent, high, normal, and low, and which accounts
issues.problem: It leaves out setup facts later skills need: channels and where each lives, first-response and resolution SLAs per channel, business hours and timezone, VIP tiers, approval amount limits, and any regulated data in scope.
issues.fix: Add these to the working-rules list and to the memory schema.

issues.problem: It doesn't offer the standing work the persona promises (a daily triaged queue, weekly ticket themes), and doesn't set a timezone for it.
issues.fix: After the first case, offer schedule_routine for a weekday queue brief and a weekly-ticket-themes run, each off until the user says yes and never sending to customers.

issues.quote: Confirm how missing account
issues.problem: 'Confirm how missing account data is handled' is vague and gives no default, so each skill improvises.
issues.fix: State a default: mark the fact UNVERIFIED, ask one question, and name who can confirm. Save any team override to memory.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Sasha, we're a four-person SaaS support team on Help Scout. Here's our help centre URL and refund policy. Get yourself set up.
scenarios.why: Map-the-sources and Set-the-working-rules would produce a thorough setup brief. But Help Scout has no block and the skill offers no export/paste fallback. It never uses web_fetch on the public help centre or memory_store for the answers, so priority rules, approvers, and tone vanish before the next session and the reply and refund skills can't use them.

scenarios.prompt: I don't have time for setup. Here's a CSV of 60 open tickets, just tell me which ones are on fire.
scenarios.why: The trigger 'ticket queue' and 'Use this before triaging tickets' pull this skill in first, and it asks for about twelve sources and eight rules before triaging. Only the fifth output item touches tickets. A good onboarding would triage the CSV right away with default priority rules and ask the setup questions later, one at a time.

support-macro-library.job: build saved-reply macros from repeat answers
support-macro-library.summary: Mines sent replies and closed tickets for repeated answers and drafts one-question macros with placeholders, source citations, tags, exclusion cases, and an owner, for approval before they go into the help desk.
strengths: One macro per question, with the customer's own wording as the matching key
Each step is tied to a confirming source, and unconfirmed steps are banned
An explicit 'when not to use' list (other plans, known bugs, angry or legal threads, refunds) prevents misfires
Names an owner for keeping each macro current
Checks answers against the current docs before turning them into macros
missing: Audit of the existing library (keep/update/merge/retire)
Inclusion threshold and volume × handle-time ranking
A personalisation slot and channel variants
Last-verified date and review cadence
An import-ready CSV or sheet output
A naming and category convention
Macro usage and CSAT check after rollout
A link from each macro to its help article (help-article-from-tickets)

issues.quote: Search sent replies and closed tickets for answers that share the same steps
issues.problem: It starts from tickets and never from the existing macro library, so it can't find duplicates, conflicts, or stale macros, and new macros pile up on top of old ones.
issues.fix: Add a first step: pull the existing macros (export or paste) and mark each keep, update, merge, or retire with usage count and reason. Write new macros only for gaps.

issues.quote: Count how often each one went out, over what period, and cite the
issues.problem: There is no threshold for what counts as 'repeated' and no ranking, so a library can fill up with one-off answers or miss the costly ones.
issues.fix: Set an inclusion bar (the team's number per month, default about 5) and rank by volume × handle time. Report candidates below the bar separately.

issues.quote: the reply, with `{placeholders}` for name, plan, dates, and links;
issues.problem: The template has no slot for a line specific to the ticket and no channel variants, so macros go out verbatim and read as canned, and email-length text lands in chat.
issues.fix: Add a required {personal_line} placeholder that the agent must fill, plus short-chat and email variants where the channel differs.

issues.quote: Name the person who owns keeping it current.
issues.problem: An owner without a review date means macros go stale after the next release.
issues.fix: Add a last-verified date and a review trigger (every N months or on any release touching the cited feature).

issues.quote: Do not add macros to the help desk yourself; draft them for approval.
issues.problem: It doesn't specify a delivery format or a data fallback. Most help desks import macros from CSV, and the sent replies usually come as an export, not a connector.
issues.fix: Deliver a table or CSV (name, category, body, tags, source, exclusions, owner, review date) via write_workspace_file or the Google Sheets block. Ask for a ticket export or paste when no help-desk connector exists.

issues.quote: a short name agents can search for;
issues.problem: There is no naming convention, so agents searching 100+ macros get inconsistent names.
issues.fix: Use a category prefix convention (e.g. 'Billing › Update card', 'Export › Row limit').

scenarios.prompt: Here's an export of last month's 400 solved tickets. Build us macros for the top repeat questions.
scenarios.why: Find-repeat-answers counts each answer over a period with ticket ids and drops answers that no longer match the docs. Write-the-macro gives a searchable name, the customer question, a placeholder reply, and a source per step. The 'When not to use it' section adds exclusions and an owner. A capable model would produce usable macros, though with no volume threshold and no import format.

scenarios.prompt: We already have 120 Zendesk macros. Half are stale and some contradict each other. Clean up the library before our new hires start.
scenarios.why: The skill has no audit path for an existing library: no keep/update/merge/retire decision, no use of usage stats, and no conflict resolution between contradicting macros. Only the 'drop any that no longer match' check carries over. The model would likely build new macros alongside the old ones, which makes the conflict worse.

support-reply-draft.job: draft customer support reply from docs
support-reply-draft.summary: Lists each question in a ticket, finds and cites the confirming doc for each, and drafts an answer-first, phone-length reply with one clarifying question at most, headed by an approval note of sources and approver.
strengths: Answer first, in the customer's words, questions handled in the order asked: current best practice
At most one clarifying question, and every answer cited or marked unknown with who can find out
Short enough to read on a phone, one action per line
The approval note above the draft makes review fast
Explicit bans on blaming the customer and promising it won't happen again
missing: Routing to refund, bug, and escalation paths before drafting
A rule that update timelines must be confirmed
De-escalation guidance for upset or high-stakes customers
Channel variants (chat, email, social)
Memory read for tone, banned words, and approver
A multi-language reply rule (reply in the customer's language, flag for review)
A follow-up check (schedule_followup) when the reply promises an update

issues.quote: Use this for one ticket or a short thread.
issues.problem: There's no routing step before drafting. Refund asks, suspected bugs, and legal, security, or churn threats all get a normal reply instead of the sibling skill or the named owner.
issues.fix: Add step 0: if the ticket asks for money, run refund-and-exception-brief and draft only a holding reply. If it's a suspected bug, also run bug-report-handoff. If it has a legal, security, or churn threat or a VIP account, flag the owner from memory and don't send a templated answer.

issues.quote: say plainly what is not known yet and when the team will update;
issues.problem: 'When the team will update' pushes the model to invent a timeline, which conflicts with the persona's ban on invented dates.
issues.fix: Use only a confirmed update cadence from setup memory or a teammate. Otherwise leave a {next_update} placeholder for the approver and list it in the approval note.

issues.quote: open with the answer, not an apology script;
issues.problem: There's no guidance for upset or blocked customers. Banning scripted sympathy with nothing in its place can produce replies that sound cold when a customer is losing money.
issues.fix: Add one line: when the customer is blocked or upset, name the specific impact in one sentence, then give the answer and next step, with no generic apology.

issues.quote: keep it short enough to read on a phone.
issues.problem: It has no channel adaptation. Chat replies, email, and public social replies need different length and privacy handling.
issues.fix: Add channel rules: chat is 1–3 short lines, email follows the full structure, and a public or social reply acknowledges briefly and moves details to a private channel.

issues.quote: Above the draft, list the sources used, any placeholder left for a teammate,
issues.problem: It doesn't read the team's tone, banned words, or approver from setup memory, so these get re-asked or guessed.
issues.fix: Start with memory_search for support tone, banned phrases and reply approver. If none are saved, use the persona's voice and ask once.

issues.quote: Do not send the reply, close the ticket, or change the account yourself.
issues.problem: It doesn't say what inputs to use when the help desk isn't connected, or where the approved draft goes.
issues.fix: Accept a pasted thread or export. After approval, offer to create a Gmail draft via run_block, or give copy-ready text for the help desk.

issues.quote: "customer email"
issues.problem: This trigger is generic enough to fire for sales or marketing emails to customers.
issues.fix: Use 'reply to this ticket' or 'answer this support email'.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a reply to ticket #5521. The customer asks why their export stopped at 10,000 rows and whether they can get the full file. Our plan-limits article is attached.
scenarios.why: Find-the-confirmed-answer lists both questions, cites the plan-limits article, and checks the account's plan. The draft opens with the answer, gives the workaround steps in order, and asks one question. The approval note names sources and approver. The result matches the persona's own voice sample.

scenarios.prompt: Enterprise admin, third email this week. SSO is broken for 200 of their users, they're threatening to cancel and mention their lawyer. Engineering has no fix yet. Draft a reply.
scenarios.why: The skill gives an answer-first draft that states the unknown plainly and asks one question. But there is no branch for a legal threat, churn threat, or VIP escalation, no handoff to bug-report-handoff or to the account owner, and no guidance on acknowledging a big business impact without scripted sympathy. 'When the team will update' invites making up a commitment.

escalations-and-incidents.job: package and route a support escalation
escalations-and-incidents.summary: Rates a hot case SEV1-SEV4, assembles an escalation packet (impact, repro, what was tried, draft customer update, named owner) and stages the page or handoff for the owner's approval.
strengths: Every page and handoff is a draft that waits for the owner's approval, and the skill never promises an outcome
The packet names the right core fields: minimal repro, what was tried with dates, who is hurt and how many, and a named owner
The warm-handoff line and full-thread transfer stop the customer having to re-explain
The fallback labels a rating UNVERIFIED and names the one question that would settle it
missing: Default severity-to-cadence table (internal and customer)
Escalate-vs-handle criteria
Duplicate/known-incident check
Business impact quantification (ARR, count, contractual SLA)
Emergency path when the owner can't be reached
Legal-threat handling (no admission, counsel routing, preservation)
De-escalation, close and SEV1/2 postmortem prompt
Shipped packet template

issues.quote: SEV2 is a VIP down or major flow broken
issues.problem: The severity scale contradicts Robin's persona, triage-and-prioritize and vip-and-white-glove-care, which all treat 'VIP down' as P1. No mapping links SEV to P levels, and security incidents or data exposure are missing from SEV1.
issues.fix: Adopt one scale that matches the persona (SEV1=P1 ... SEV4=P4) with a mapping table, and add security/data exposure and imminent safety harm to SEV1.

issues.quote: Fraud, abuse, legal threats, and safety words jump the queue to the hold
issues.problem: Four different paths are collapsed into one. 'Freeze the state' is undefined and could be read as locking an account, which the boundaries forbid without the owner's yes. Nothing routes to fraud-and-chargeback-defense, trust-and-safety-escalations, sensitive-data-safe-handling or legal counsel.
issues.fix: Add a routing table: fraud → fraud skill, abuse/self-harm → trust-and-safety, data spill → sensitive-data, legal threat → counsel with a no-substantive-reply rule. Define 'freeze' as pausing outbound replies and preserving the thread, never an account action.

issues.quote: SEV1 and SEV2 go now to on-call or the exec path with the
issues.problem: 'Go now' collides with 'Every handoff is a draft the owner approves before anything sends or pages'. There is no rule for an owner who can't be reached, so a SEV1 or imminent-harm case can stall overnight.
issues.fix: Let the owner pre-authorise a SEV1/imminent-harm paging path (stored in memory), set an approval timeout, and name the fallback contact.

issues.problem: There are no escalate-vs-handle criteria, no duplicate or known-incident check against the open queue (the persona requires one), and no business-impact quantification (affected count, ARR, contractual SLA).
issues.fix: Add a step before rating: check the open queue and incidents for duplicates, quantify breadth, depth, duration, revenue and contract exposure, and confirm the case warrants escalation.

issues.quote: add the update cadence from the matrix.
issues.problem: Update cadence exists only when a matrix exists. There is no default by severity and no de-escalation, close-out or postmortem step, yet Robin's escalation-and-sla-watch routine expects postmortem prompts for SEV1/SEV2 closes.
issues.fix: Ship a default cadence table (internal and customer, by severity), a de-escalation rule, and a SEV1/2 close with a postmortem prompt (owner, date, timeline).

issues.quote: The escalation packet plus the staged handoff. Offer to file it as a tracked
issues.problem: The packet fields are buried in step 2 prose and there is no reusable template, so packets will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Add templates/escalation-packet.md (Toran's customer-escalation brief is a ready source) and point to it from step 2.

issues.quote: Track MTTA (time to acknowledge) alongside resolve time.
issues.problem: Nothing says where the acknowledge/page/resolve timestamps are recorded or how MTTA is computed, so the number will be invented or skipped.
issues.fix: Record the timestamps on the case and compute MTTA and MTTR in the sandbox, labelled with their source.

scenarios.prompt: Acme (enterprise, ~$180k ARR) says SSO has been failing for all 400 of their users since 9am and their CTO wants an exec call. Build the escalation for engineering.
scenarios.why: Step 1 labels this SEV2 ('VIP down'). triage-and-prioritize and vip-and-white-glove-care both call it P1, so the case goes out with conflicting severity labels. Step 2 produces a reasonable repro-and-impact packet, but the skill never asks for ARR or contract SLA, never checks for duplicate reports, and gives no default update cadence if the matrix is missing. The packet is usable but lighter than a senior's.

scenarios.prompt: 2am Saturday: a chat customer says our charger caught fire and they're calling a lawyer, and they were also double-charged. No escalation matrix saved yet.
scenarios.why: Step 1 sends fire, legal and billing all down one 'hold path: freeze the state... hand to the named human'. No human is named, and the fallback only yields an UNVERIFIED rating plus one question. Nothing separates product-safety handling (preserve the device and photos, no admission of liability, possible regulator reporting) from the billing issue, and nothing covers an owner who can't be reached. Step 3 makes even the page wait for the owner's yes, so imminent harm sits unescalated.

fraud-and-chargeback-defense.summary: Verifies a flagged transaction or chargeback from records, builds a for/against risk profile separating account takeover from first-party abuse, stages a hold or clears, and assembles a reason-code-matched representment packet for approval.
strengths: Evidence is matched to the reason code, which is the correct core of representment
Account takeover signals are checked separately from first-party (friendly) fraud
A hard gate forbids holding funds, locking an account or accusing the customer without the owner's yes
A case with no transaction record stays UNKNOWN and never becomes 'confirmed fraud'
It tracks win rate per reason code and plans the pre-arbitration path after a loss
missing: Fight-vs-accept economics
Never-refund-an-open-dispute guardrail
Processor due-by date as the governing deadline
Visa CE3.0, 3DS liability shift, current Mastercard flow
Pre-dispute alerts and dispute-ratio monitoring
Account-takeover containment playbook and verified-channel contact
PCI/PII redaction route
Reason-code evidence reference and packet templates
Stripe block usage with export fallback

issues.problem: There is no fight-or-accept decision (amount vs dispute fee vs win likelihood vs evidence strength) and no guardrail against refunding a transaction that is already disputed, which loses the money twice.
issues.fix: Add a pre-step: check refund and dispute state first, never refund an open dispute, and compute the expected value of fighting before building the packet.

issues.quote: Clear with a one-line reason when the evidence is thin, or stage a hold for
issues.problem: The decision rule is incomplete. It covers only thin evidence (clear) and money still moving (hold). Strong evidence on a settled charge, account takeover needing account security, and repeat abusers are all unaddressed, and signals have no weighting.
issues.fix: Replace with a small decision table: signal strength × money state × takeover vs first-party, each mapped to a staged action and its approver.

issues.quote: resubmitting evidence to the card network. Track win rate per code;
issues.problem: The operative deadline is the processor's or acquirer's response due-by date, often much shorter than the network window. Diarising a network deadline risks missing the real one.
issues.fix: Read the due-by date from the processor (Stripe block or notice), schedule a follow-up a few days before it, and state that the processor's date governs.

issues.quote: after a loss, stage the second-chargeback or pre-arbitration path.
issues.problem: 'Second chargeback' is outdated Mastercard terminology, and current network mechanics are missing: Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0 for 10.4, 3DS liability shift, pre-dispute alerts (Ethoca, Verifi RDR) and dispute-ratio monitoring programmes.
issues.fix: Add a short reference file on current Visa and Mastercard dispute flows, CE3.0 criteria, liability shift and ratio thresholds, labelled with an as-of date.

issues.quote: Confirm the amount, method, date, and account, each labeled FACT or UNKNOWN.
issues.problem: Verification and evidence packets handle card data and PII, yet nothing routes to sensitive-data-safe-handling or requires PAN masking before the packet is shared or filed.
issues.fix: Add: mask PAN to the last 4 digits and redact PII in the profile and packet, and run sensitive-data-safe-handling before anything leaves the chat.

issues.problem: Account-takeover detection has no follow-through: no staged containment (credential reset, session revoke, MFA prompt) and no rule to contact the owner through a verified channel rather than the changed email.
issues.fix: Add a takeover branch: staged containment actions for the owner's yes, plus a verified-channel contact rule.

issues.quote: Look up the reason code first and match compelling evidence to that code: the
issues.problem: The package ships no reason-code-to-evidence table and names no tool (the Stripe block can pull disputes and submit evidence), so the lookup is left to model memory.
issues.fix: Ship references/reason-codes.md with evidence per common code, and name the Stripe block plus a paste/CSV fallback.

issues.quote: Deliver the risk profile, the hold-or-clear call, and the staged hold or
issues.problem: There is no template for the risk profile, evidence index or rebuttal letter, so the deliverable varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Add templates for the risk profile block and the representment packet (cover letter, evidence index, timeline).

scenarios.prompt: Stripe shows a $329 chargeback on order #4471, Visa 13.1 'merchandise not received'. We have UPS delivery confirmation. Help me fight it.
scenarios.why: The Defend section drives the right shape: reason code first, delivery proof, receipts, policy quote, rebuttal letter, file after approval. But the deadline is described as the card network's rather than the processor's due-by date. There is no check that the charge wasn't already refunded, no fight-vs-accept math, and no letter or evidence-index template, so the packet quality depends on the model.

scenarios.prompt: A customer says someone took over their account, changed the email and bought $1,200 in gift cards. They already disputed it with their bank and want a refund now. Stripe isn't connected.
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly produces an UNKNOWN profile, names the access need, and gates any hold or lock on the owner. But the skill never warns that refunding a charge already under dispute causes a double loss. It gives no takeover containment playbook (contact via a verified channel rather than the changed email, revoke sessions, freeze unredeemed gift codes) and no route to sensitive-data-safe-handling.

help-center-answers-and-kb.job: answer how-to question from help docs
help-center-answers-and-kb.summary: Answers how-to questions from the governing help-center passage with a citation, shapes the steps for the channel, and turns repeat questions into a saved reply and a skeletal KB draft staged for approval.
strengths: Docs-first with a hard rule against inventing steps or citations
Channel-aware answer shape: numbered steps, success state, what to send back if it fails
Hands onboarding sequencing to the onboarding skill instead of duplicating it
Marks uncited answers UNVERIFIED and files them as the top KB candidate
missing: Doc search procedure with named tools
Stale or conflicting doc handling
Plan/version eligibility check
Repeat threshold and data source
Saved-reply template
Update-vs-create rule
Deflection or reuse measurement

issues.quote: The customer question, the help-center or docs passages that govern it, and
issues.problem: It expects the governing passage as an input and has no retrieval step: nothing about searching the help center in the customer's words (web_fetch/web_search, the Notion or Drive blocks, the KB location in memory), and nothing about multiple, conflicting or stale passages or plan/version eligibility.
issues.fix: Add a step 0: look up the KB location in memory, search with the customer's words, pick the governing passage by recency and plan, and flag conflicts or staleness to the KB owner.

issues.section: Answer from the docs, then mint the asset
issues.quote: and, for true gaps, a knowledge-base (KB) draft with title, steps, and
issues.problem: The KB draft is a three-field skeleton that duplicates knowledge-centered-service and Toran's knowledge-base-article-writing, with no duplicate check, no update-vs-create rule and no article-type template.
issues.fix: Keep the saved reply here and hand KB drafting to a single merged KB-article skill, with a one-line route.

issues.section: Answer from the docs, then mint the asset
issues.quote: When the question repeats, mint the asset: a saved reply for the queue
issues.problem: 'Repeats' is undefined. There is no threshold and no source for 'the repeat history', so the model will guess or skip it.
issues.fix: Define a threshold (e.g. 3+ tickets on the same intent in 30 days, from ticket tags or a search), say how to count it, and give a fallback when no history is available.

issues.quote: No governing doc means an answer built from the product and the owner's
issues.problem: 'Built from the product' invites unverified steps, in tension with 'Never invent a step', and the skill doesn't say the UNVERIFIED answer must wait for the owner to confirm the steps before it reaches the customer.
issues.fix: Require the owner to confirm the steps (or verify them in the product via the browser when access exists) before any customer-facing send.

issues.quote: Use this for how-to questions, repeat issues, and onboarding guidance.
issues.problem: The trigger overlaps draft-the-reply (docs-grounded replies), knowledge-centered-service ('knowledge base') and Toran's customer-support-research, so the model has no clear rule for which to load.
issues.fix: Narrow it to 'how-to and setup questions with a documented answer' and add a line routing general replies to draft-the-reply and articles to the KB skill.

issues.quote: The cited answer plus any saved reply or KB draft. Offer to file the KB
issues.problem: There is no template for the saved reply (when to use it, variables, tone, citation), so the reusable asset won't be consistent.
issues.fix: Ship templates/saved-reply.md and an answer skeleton.

issues.section: Answer from the docs, then mint the asset
issues.quote: Log the answer against the ticket, with its citation when a governing
issues.problem: The skill never states that the customer answer itself is a staged draft for the owner's yes (only the KB assets are gated), and 'log against the ticket' names no tool or fallback.
issues.fix: State that the answer is staged for approval, and log it via the connected ticket or Sheets tool, or return it in chat.

scenarios.prompt: Customer on the Pro plan asks how to add a teammate to their workspace. Our help center is help.acme.com. Draft the answer.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-2 produce a cited, numbered answer naming the customer's setup, what success looks like and what to send back if it fails. A capable model will fetch the help page on its own even though the skill doesn't say to, and the no-fake-citation rule keeps it honest.

scenarios.prompt: Sixth ticket this week asking how to export invoices to CSV. Our help article is from 2023 and the UI has since changed. Draft the reply and fix the KB.
scenarios.why: Step 1 says to answer docs-first, but the doc is stale and the skill has no rule for a governing passage that contradicts the current product. Step 3 mints a KB draft only 'for true gaps'; this is an update, and the skill has no update-vs-create path. The model will likely either quote the stale steps or improvise, and the stale article never gets flagged to its owner (knowledge-centered-service covers that).

knowledge-centered-service.job: run KCS knowledge capture and KB health
knowledge-centered-service.summary: Applies KCS: capture articles in the customer's words during the solve, fix-or-flag and score articles on findability, accuracy and completeness, track weekly Solve Loop metrics, coach capture habits and run a monthly Evolve content-health review.
strengths: Correct KCS v6 practices: capture in the customer's words, search early and often, reuse is review, fix it or flag it, New-vs-Known analysis
Scores article quality on findability, accuracy and completeness rather than prose
Stale articles are flagged to the KB owner, never silently edited
Unverifiable steps are cut rather than guessed, and URLs and review dates are never invented
missing: Request-type router
Default KCS article template (issue, environment, resolution, cause)
AQI checklist
Metric definitions (link rate, participation, reuse, self-service success) with data sources
Article states and visibility
AI licensing rule
Weekly and monthly report templates
Anti-quota coaching guidance

issues.quote: Run the Solve Loop on every case: search early and search often with the
issues.problem: There is no router by request type, so one article request, a health report or a coaching ask all get the six-step programme. 'Every case' also assumes this skill is loaded on every case, which the harness only does on trigger.
issues.fix: Open with a router (capture one article / improve an article / weekly Solve metrics / monthly Evolve review / coaching note), and move per-case capture into a one-line hook that draft-the-reply and own-to-closure call.

issues.quote: Track the Solve Loop weekly: reuse rate, self-serve resolution, failed
issues.problem: The metrics have no formulas, data sources, periods or fallback when search logs or case-article links are missing, and the core KCS measures (link rate, participation rate, citation rate) are absent.
issues.fix: Ship references/kcs-metrics.md with a definition, data source and proxy per metric, and require INFERENCE labels whenever a proxy is used.

issues.quote: The staged article or fix, the quality score with evidence, the weekly Solve
issues.problem: It relies on an article template 'from prefs' that most users won't have, and ships no default KCS article structure (issue, environment, resolution, cause), no AQI checklist and no weekly or monthly report format.
issues.fix: Add templates/kcs-article.md, checklists/article-quality-index.md and templates/solve-weekly.md plus evolve-monthly.md.

issues.quote: Use this when an answer should outlive the case. Capture knowledge in the
issues.problem: The 'write a KB article' trigger collides with Toran's knowledge-base-article-writing and with the KB-draft half of help-center-answers-and-kb, leaving three skills that draft articles for the same expert.
issues.fix: Position this as the KCS process and health skill, and route single-article drafting to one merged article skill (Toran's templates plus KCS capture rules).

issues.quote: delete existing ones. If confident and licensed, fix it; otherwise flag it.
issues.problem: Licensing is undefined for an AI teammate, so 'fix it' could be read as permission to edit live articles, which clashes with 'Never publish before the owner says yes'.
issues.fix: State that the AI is never publisher-licensed: 'fix' means stage an edit for the owner's yes.

issues.quote: Coach the team on capture: one quoted miss per rep per week (solved
issues.problem: It doesn't say coaching notes go to the owner as drafts rather than to reps, and doesn't warn against the KCS anti-pattern of article-count quotas.
issues.fix: Route coaching notes to the owner only, and add 'never set article-count targets; coach behaviours, not volume'.

issues.problem: There are no article lifecycle states (work in progress, not validated, validated, archived) and no internal-vs-external visibility rule, both central to KCS governance.
issues.fix: Add states and visibility to the article template and to the retire/merge step.

scenarios.prompt: We just solved a tricky case: the Zapier integration fails when the workspace name contains an emoji. Capture it as a KB article.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-2 steer correctly: search first, write the problem in the customer's words, environment, steps verified against the case, the fix with its receipt, a source per step, and nothing published without a yes. If no template is in memory the model must improvise the structure, but the fields named in step 2 are enough for a solid article.

scenarios.prompt: Give me last month's KB health report: reuse rate, top failed searches and which articles to retire. All we have is a Zendesk Guide CSV of article views plus ticket tags, no search logs.
scenarios.why: Step 4 names reuse rate and failed searches but defines neither and gives no fallback when link or search data is missing (the fallback covers only 'No KB access'). The model will either invent proxies without labelling them or stall. Retirement criteria rely on 'stale article past review', with no review dates in the export.

live-channel-queue-operations.job: prioritize live chat, phone, and social queues
live-channel-queue-operations.summary: Sweeps chat, phone and social queues against SLA clocks, orders the work by promise age, SLA risk and heat, caps chat concurrency, stages short talk tracks and public-to-private replies, and writes a shift-close handoff.
strengths: Sweeps every surface once before working any item, and marks what is already breached
Treats an overdue callback as P2 minimum and converts stuck chats to a callback with a time
Caps chat concurrency and says plainly what won't be reached and who it hands to
Shift-close note covers what breached, what was promised and what the next shift picks up first
Keeps customer details out of public posts, and nothing is dialled, sent or posted without a yes
missing: Real-time metric definitions (service level, ASA, abandon, occupancy)
Capacity levers when demand exceeds staff
Surge detection and handoff to mass-recovery
Impact-first ordering tied to P1-P4
Batch approval of talk tracks and macros for the shift
Shift-close template
Stored state for dedupe

issues.quote: Oldest promise first, then SLA risk, then channel heat, then arrival. A
issues.problem: The ordering ignores impact priority: a stale soft promise outranks an outage chat, and a breach due in 5 minutes waits behind old promises. This contradicts the persona's ranking by impact, affected count and SLA clock.
issues.fix: Order by P-level and safety first (per triage-and-prioritize), then imminent breach, then overdue promises, then heat, then arrival.

issues.quote: Say plainly which items will not be reached this shift and
issues.problem: There are no real-time capacity levers (move email agents to chat, disable proactive chat, callback-in-queue, IVR or status banner, a macro for the common contact) and no surge rule that switches to mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms or the workforce skill's intra-day moves.
issues.fix: Add a levers list with the cost of each, plus a surge trigger (e.g. N contacts on one topic within M minutes) that routes to mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms.

issues.quote: The live state of every surface — chat waits and concurrency, the phone
issues.problem: None of the standard real-time metrics are named or defined (service level X/Y, ASA, longest wait, abandon rate, occupancy), and no targets are read from memory, so 'read the clocks against the targets' has nothing concrete to compare.
issues.fix: Define the metrics and pull the targets from memory, asking once if they're missing.

issues.quote: callbacks and replies, and the shift-close note. Nothing dialed, sent, or
issues.problem: Working a live queue with a separate owner yes on every chat message is impractical, and the skill offers no batch-approval pattern for real-time work.
issues.fix: Add a shift-start step that gets the talk tracks and macros approved as a set, and state that the skill plans and stages while humans execute live.

issues.quote: The public reply is under two sentences, acknowledges without admitting
issues.problem: This section and the phone mechanics restate social-and-community-support and voice-and-phone-support almost verbatim, so the rules will drift apart over time.
issues.fix: Replace both with one-line routes to those skills.

issues.quote: Chat concurrency stays inside the floor's limit — usually two to three
issues.problem: A default number is asserted without a source and could be taken as the customer's limit.
issues.fix: Read the concurrency limit from memory, and label the fallback as an assumed default.

issues.section: Hand off and close the shift
issues.quote: promised, and what the next shift picks up first. Dedupe against the last
issues.problem: Deduping requires the previous sweep's state, but nothing tells the model to store or look up that state.
issues.fix: Store each sweep summary with memory_store and read the last one with memory_search before paging.

issues.quote: The ordered call and queue list with a plan per item, the staged first
issues.problem: There is no template for the ordered list or the shift-close note.
issues.fix: Ship templates/shift-close.md with columns for item, clock, priority, next action, owner and due.

scenarios.prompt: It's 2pm. Chat wait is 14 minutes (target 2), we owe 9 callbacks and there are 3 angry tweets. Here's the Zendesk dashboard paste. What do we do first?
scenarios.why: The sweep marks breaches, the ordering puts overdue callbacks first, public replies get the private-move line, and a shift note is produced. But the skill gives no levers to bring a 14-minute chat wait back to target (reassign email agents, pause proactive chat, callback-in-queue, banner). It only says to name what won't be reached, so the owner gets a triage list, not a recovery plan.

scenarios.prompt: Our phone system was down for 40 minutes: 60 voicemails, chat flooding with the same question, and a journalist tweeted at us. Two agents on shift, no dashboard access. I'll paste what I can.
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly marks the list INFERENCE, and the press mention jumps to escalation. But 'Work each item short' drives one-by-one talk tracks for 60 near-identical contacts. Nothing tells the model to recognise a surge and switch to mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms (one bulk message, a status banner, a macro), so a senior would handle this completely differently.

logistics-shipment-and-customs.job: trace shipments and prepare customs paperwork
logistics-shipment-and-customs.summary: Traces shipments from carrier data, expedites late freight via carrier escalation or reroute, classifies and files customs line items by HTS code, and keeps one liaison thread per shipment with logged commitments.
strengths: An UNKNOWN trace is never presented as 'on the truck', and scan events or entry numbers are never invented
Never promises a delivery date the carrier hasn't given
Routes an unsourced classification to the broker instead of guessing a duty code
One thread per shipment with logged commitments and a single chase before escalating
missing: Broker-packet framing instead of filing
HS vs national tariff and destination-country handling
Incoterms responsibility check
Partner-agency and licensing, sanctions and restricted-party screening
ISF and entry timing, current de minimis rules
Loss/damage claims with filing windows
Demurrage and detention clocks
Mode-specific handling (parcel/LTL/FTL/ocean/air)
Cost approval for expedite and reroute
Scope boundary vs orders-returns-and-warranty

issues.section: Classify and file customs by the book
issues.quote: File each line item with its HTS code — the Harmonized Tariff Schedule
issues.problem: It directs the AI support rep to file customs entries with no approval gate. Entries are filed by the importer of record or a licensed broker, and misclassification or undervaluation carries penalties.
issues.fix: Reframe as 'prepare the broker packet' (line items, adequate description, value, origin, candidate HS code with its source) staged for broker and owner approval, and never submit an entry.

issues.section: Classify and file customs by the book
issues.quote: classification — plus value and origin from the invoice, through the
issues.problem: The customs content is US-HTS-only and shallow: no HS 6-digit vs national tariff distinction, and nothing on Incoterms (who clears and pays duty), invoice description adequacy, partner-agency or licensing requirements, ISF/entry timing, current de minimis rules, or sanctions and restricted-party screening.
issues.fix: Ship references/customs-checklist.md with these checks, dated and labelled by jurisdiction, and ask for the destination country up front.

issues.quote: Use this when goods are moving: trace and expedite shipments, file
issues.problem: The scope is too broad and collides with orders-returns-and-warranty ('track this order', 'where is my order'), which already has deeper tracing (lost-in-transit threshold, delivery dispute). The triggers 'track this shipment' and 'late delivery' will misfire.
issues.fix: Scope to B2B and freight exceptions and inbound/import paperwork, and route consumer parcel tracking questions to orders-returns-and-warranty.

issues.quote: Work in order: carrier escalation with the reference IDs, reroute or
issues.problem: Reroute, reschedule or expedite commits money and changes delivery with no cost comparison and no owner-approval gate in the skill.
issues.fix: Stage each option with its cost and ETA change for the owner's yes, and never book a reroute or upgrade unapproved.

issues.problem: Loss and damage handling is missing: carrier claims and their filing windows, concealed-damage notice, proof of delivery, demurrage and detention clocks, and differences by mode (parcel/LTL/FTL/ocean/air).
issues.fix: Add a claims-and-exceptions section by mode, with deadlines labelled by source and as-of date.

issues.section: Liaise in one thread per shipment
issues.quote: Deliver the trace read, the expedite or entry packet, the staged
issues.problem: No template is given for the trace read, the broker packet or the shipment log.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the trace read, the broker packet and the commitment log.

issues.quote: You need the tracking or order IDs, the carrier and warehouse portals
issues.problem: It assumes portal access 'from prefs' but names no tool path (browser_navigate or web_fetch for public tracking pages, generic HTTP or MCP for carrier APIs). The only fallback is customer screenshots.
issues.fix: Add a tool order: connected MCP or API, then the public tracking page via browser, then a customer screenshot marked INFERENCE.

scenarios.prompt: Customer's pallet (PRO 123456, XPO LTL) was due Monday and has shown 'at terminal' since Friday. They need it for a Thursday install. What do we do?
scenarios.why: 'Trace first' and 'Expedite' produce the right skeleton: last scan with time, UNKNOWN if there's no carrier read, carrier escalation with the PRO, no promised date the carrier hasn't given. But there is no LTL specific (terminal exception codes, delivery appointment, guaranteed-service upgrade), no cost comparison, and no owner approval for a paid reroute or expedite, and the skill never says to check public carrier tracking via the browser.

scenarios.prompt: We're importing 200 Bluetooth speakers from Shenzhen. The broker wants HTS codes and the invoice just says 'electronic goods'. Can you file the entry so it clears before the weekend?
scenarios.why: The customs section instructs 'File each line item with its HTS code ... through the broker or portal' with no approval gate. 'Never guess a duty code' helps, but nothing flags that the invoice description is inadequate for customs, and nothing covers FCC or other agency requirements, Section 301 exposure, or Incoterms. Nothing establishes that Robin prepares a packet and the broker or importer of record files. A capable model following it could attempt a filing or promise weekend clearance.

feature-request-triage.job: triage feature requests by underlying problem
feature-request-triage.summary: Takes a pasted backlog of feature requests, records who asked and in what words, merges them by the underlying problem with request and account counts, and sorts them into four buckets (look closer, already planned, needs evidence, not now), each with a reason and a follow-up owner.
strengths: Separates the problem from the requested solution and merges by problem 'even when they ask for different' solutions.
Counts distinct accounts as well as raw requests.
Marks the problem 'unknown' rather than guessing it.
Names who should follow up with which customer and what to ask.
Clear guardrails: no replies to customers, no promises, no tracker edits, no invented requesters, counts or revenue.
missing: Entry criteria for each triage bucket
Intake with integration or CSV fallback, and code-based counting
An outcome for already-possible, bug, docs-gap and workaround requests
Handling of deal-blocking and churn-risk requests relayed by sales or CS
Matching against existing tracker items
A fixed output table (problem, requests, accounts, segments, proposed solutions, bucket, reason, follow-up owner)
Drafted close-the-loop replies for approval
Use of goals and roadmap from setup memory

issues.quote: Sort items into **look closer**, **already planned**, **needs evidence**, and
issues.problem: None of the four buckets has entry criteria, and 'already planned' needs a roadmap the skill never asks for. Placement depends on the model's judgement and cannot be repeated consistently.
issues.fix: Define each bucket: look closer = at least N distinct accounts in a target segment or tied to a stated goal; needs evidence = problem unknown or one account; already planned = matches a supplied roadmap item (cite it); not now = off-goal, with a reason. Ask for the roadmap and goals, or read them from the setup memory.

issues.quote: Use this for a backlog of requests from customers, sales, or the team.
issues.problem: There is no intake step. It does not say where requests live (Linear, HubSpot, Notion, Airtable, Canny), how to fetch them, what to do if nothing is connected, or how to count large exports. A model will hand-count hundreds of rows.
issues.fix: Add an intake step: read through run_block or a connected MCP where available, otherwise ask for a CSV or paste. Load the rows in bash_exec, dedupe and count accounts with code, and report how many rows have account or plan data.

issues.problem: There is no outcome for requests that are already possible (a docs or education gap), that are really bugs, or that have an adequate workaround. Senior triage routinely clears a large share of a backlog this way.
issues.fix: Add 'already possible / bug' buckets that route to support or docs (with a drafted reply for approval) or to the QA/engineering teammate.

issues.quote: segments and plans, and any revenue the team has supplied;
issues.problem: Requests relayed by sales or CS are not distinguished from requests by end users. Deal-blocking and churn-risk requests get no flag, and the counting unit agreed in product-getting-started (ticket, account or revenue) is never used.
issues.fix: Record the channel (user, sales, CS). Flag deal-blocking or churn-risk requests with their source and amount as supplied. Rank using the counting unit agreed at setup.

issues.quote: Merge requests that share a problem even when they ask for different
issues.problem: Although 'duplicate requests' is a trigger, the skill never matches merged items against existing tracker issues. Merging is also not held to a test of whether two items really share a problem.
issues.fix: Search the tracker read-only for existing issues and list the matching IDs. Merge only when the job and the failure point match; otherwise mark the items as related.

issues.section: Find the problem behind the ask
issues.quote: For each request note who asked, their plan and segment, the date, and the
issues.problem: It keeps requester identities and exact words in a list that will be shared, with no redaction rule. Opportunity-brief in the same kit has one.
issues.fix: Redact contact details and unrelated customer data before quoting; refer to accounts by ID or segment in shared outputs.

issues.quote: Sort feature requests by the problem behind them, who asked, how often, and what is missing.
issues.problem: The description has no boundary against feedback-synthesis, which also groups by problem, so either skill can load for 'what are customers asking for'.
issues.fix: Add: 'Use when the input is explicit feature asks and the output is a triage decision per item; for themes across mixed feedback use feedback-synthesis.'

issues.section: Find the problem behind the ask
issues.quote: exact words. Ask what they were trying to do when they wanted it, what they
issues.problem: 'Ask' reads as an instruction to contact the requester, which the guardrail forbids. The intended meaning is to look for this in the request text.
issues.fix: Say: 'Look in the request and notes for what they were trying to do; if absent, mark unknown and add a follow-up question to the draft.'

scenarios.prompt: Here are 45 feature requests pasted from our HubSpot notes and Canny board for Q3. Which ones should we look at for next quarter?
scenarios.why: The steps under 'Find the problem behind the ask' and 'Merge and count' give a sound merged list with requests and distinct accounts. But 'Triage list' gives no criteria for any bucket and never asks for the roadmap, so 'already planned' is guessed and the other buckets depend on the model's judgement. There is no table format, so two runs will produce lists that cannot be compared.

scenarios.prompt: Sales says we lose Acme ($120k ARR) unless we build Salesforce sync by November. Also here is a 600-row Canny export with vote counts but no account or plan columns. Triage it for Monday's planning.
scenarios.why: The skill does not say how to read or count a 600-row export (no bash_exec), how to treat votes versus requests, or what to do when plan and segment are missing. A model will count in context and likely get the numbers wrong. Revenue is only 'any revenue the team has supplied', with no rule for deal-blocking requests that reach the PM through sales rather than users, so the Acme ask gets either too much weight or too little.

feedback-synthesis.job: synthesise customer feedback into evidence-backed themes
feedback-synthesis.summary: Cleans and tags a batch of feedback, groups it by user problem rather than requested solution, and returns an evidence table (items, accounts, segments, sources, a verbatim quote) with a strong, moderate or thin rating per theme and a list of what the data cannot show.
strengths: Groups by the problem, not the requested solution, and keeps what users said separate from what is inferred.
'One loud request is not a pattern, and silence is not satisfaction.'
A clear evidence table with items, accounts, segments, sources and a quote.
Marks vague items rather than forcing them into a theme, and says what the data cannot show.
Forbids dropping disagreeing feedback to make a theme look stronger.
missing: Thresholds for evidence strength
A codebook method, with coding and counting in bash_exec for large sets
A join to CRM data or a coverage rule when metadata is missing
Quote redaction
Survey score handling (NPS/CSAT splits, response rate)
Integration intake with an export fallback
Themes ranked against goals, with recommended next steps
A reusable coded dataset attached to the synthesis

issues.quote: Mark each theme
issues.problem: Strong, moderate and thin have no thresholds, so ratings are arbitrary and cannot be compared across runs or with feature-request-triage.
issues.fix: Define them, e.g. strong = at least 5 distinct accounts across at least 2 source types in the period; moderate = 3-4 accounts or one source type; thin = 2 or fewer accounts. Flag themes concentrated in one segment.

issues.quote: Group by the problem the user has, not the solution they asked for. For each
issues.problem: There is no coding method: no draft codebook, no rule for items with several tags, no merge or split pass, no spot check. At scale the model will eyeball themes and counts.
issues.fix: Build a codebook from a sample, apply it to every row in a CSV with bash_exec, count with code, spot-check about 10%, and attach the coded file so every count can be traced.

issues.quote: Tag each item with the account, segment,
issues.problem: It assumes every item carries account, segment and plan. Anonymous surveys, app-store reviews and forum posts do not, and there is no instruction to join to CRM data or report coverage.
issues.fix: Join to a CRM or Sheets export where possible (run_block HubSpot or Sheets). Otherwise mark the field unknown, report the share of rows with segment data, and do not break down by segment below that coverage.

issues.quote: Quote users word for word, with the source and date.
issues.problem: Quotes and the Accounts column can expose names, emails and account identifiers in a synthesis meant for wide sharing. Opportunity-brief in the same kit redacts; this skill does not.
issues.fix: Redact names, contact details and account identifiers as [redacted] before quoting. Use account IDs or segments in shared tables.

issues.quote: State the sources, the period, and the number of items from each. Remove
issues.problem: It does not say how to get the feedback (Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot, Sheets, Notion) or what to do when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Read through run_block or MCP where connected; otherwise ask for an export or paste and proceed with it.

issues.problem: 'Survey analysis' is a trigger, but scored responses (NPS or CSAT distribution, response rate, non-response bias, detractor vs promoter themes) are not handled.
issues.fix: Add a survey sub-step: report n and the response rate, split themes by score band, and caveat non-response bias.

issues.problem: There is no so-what: themes are not ranked against the team's goals and no next step is given (interview, opportunity brief, or nothing), so the synthesis stops short of a PM recommendation.
issues.fix: Add a short 'What this means' section that ranks themes by strength and relevance to goals and names the next skill or teammate for each.

issues.quote: Group raw feedback into problems with counts, sources, segments, and verbatim examples.
issues.problem: The description overlaps feature-request-triage and gives no boundary.
issues.fix: State that this is for mixed feedback themes, and that for triage decisions on explicit feature asks the model should use feature-request-triage.

scenarios.prompt: Here are 80 support tickets and 12 interview notes from August. What are users actually saying?
scenarios.why: 'Clean and tag', 'Group into problems' and 'Evidence table' produce a usable synthesis at this size: sources and period stated, duplicates removed, problem-level themes, verbatim quotes with source and date, and what the data cannot show. The strength ratings are subjective but come with a reason.
