scenarios.prompt: Attached is our 2,300-response NPS survey CSV (score plus comment, no account IDs) and an Intercom export. Give me the top themes by segment.
scenarios.why: 'Tag each item with the account, segment, plan' cannot be done on anonymous survey rows, and the skill offers no join to CRM data or a fallback that marks the field unknown. There is no instruction to code and count in bash_exec, so counts over 2,300 rows will be eyeballed. Promoter and detractor splits are not handled despite the 'survey analysis' trigger. The guardrails stop invented segments, but 'by segment' goes unanswered and the counts are unreliable.

opportunity-brief.job: write opportunity brief for a product bet
opportunity-brief.summary: Writes a brief on one problem: who has it, the evidence (redacted, with counts, sources and dates, rated strong, moderate or thin, and linked to a team goal), two to four options including doing nothing, and the decision needed, who makes it, by when, and open questions.
strengths: Requires two to four options, including doing nothing, with what each rules out and how to know it worked.
Effort only as supplied by engineering or marked as a guess.
Competitor claims only with a link and date.
Redacts PII before quoting.
Ends with the exact decision, the owner and the deadline.
missing: Opportunity sizing (reach, frequency and severity, supplied revenue) and cost of delay
An explicit recommendation with confidence
Riskiest assumptions and the cheapest validating test when evidence is thin
A one-page template
A verification step for competitor claims (web_search/web_fetch)
Reading goals from setup memory

issues.quote: Close with the exact decision, who makes it, by when, and the open questions
issues.problem: There is no recommendation step. The persona says 'You recommend; the team decides', but the brief ends neutral, leaving readers to weigh the options themselves.
issues.fix: Add 'Recommendation: the option Priya would pick, why, confidence, and the evidence that would change it', placed before the decision block.

issues.problem: Nothing sizes the opportunity: no reach (accounts or users affected, from usage data), no severity or frequency, no revenue at risk or upside from supplied figures, and no cost of delay or why-now. These are core to an opportunity assessment.
issues.fix: Add a 'Size and timing' section: reach, frequency and severity, and supplied revenue impact, each labelled sourced or assumed and computed in bash_exec, plus why now.

issues.quote: Use this for one problem the team is deciding whether to work on.
issues.problem: There is no decision point for when evidence is absent or the input is only a solution idea. The model will write a speculative brief instead of redirecting to discovery.
issues.fix: If evidence is thin or absent, say so first, list the riskiest assumptions, and propose the cheapest test (5 interviews through user-interview-guide, a fake door, a data pull) before listing options.

issues.quote: unrelated customer data. Keep only the words needed to show the problem.
issues.problem: 'Keep only the words needed' conflicts with 'keep all other words unchanged' and does not say how to mark trimmed text. The redaction rule is also split across the paragraph, after the quoting rule.
issues.fix: Use one ordered rule: redact first; mark removed PII as [redacted] and trimmed text as '…'; never paraphrase inside quotation marks.

issues.problem: 'One-pager' is a trigger, but there is no fixed skeleton or length limit, so output shape varies.
issues.fix: Ship a one-page template (Problem, Evidence and strength, Size and timing, Options table, Recommendation, Decision, Open questions).

issues.quote: Keep claims about competitors to what a source shows, with the link and date.
issues.problem: It does not say how to get sources, so the model may cite competitor features from memory.
issues.fix: Verify each claim with web_fetch of the competitor's docs, pricing or changelog and record the access date. Otherwise omit the claim.

issues.quote: Link the problem to one of the team's stated goals.
issues.problem: It does not say where goals come from or what to do if none are known.
issues.fix: Read goals from product-getting-started memory. If there are none, ask one question or mark the link 'goal unconfirmed'.

scenarios.prompt: We've had 14 tickets and 3 interviews asking for bulk tag editing. Write a one-pager on whether we should build it.
scenarios.why: 'Problem and evidence', 'Options and trade-offs' and 'Decision needed' give a clean, honest brief. But nothing asks for the size of the opportunity (accounts affected, frequency and severity) or for Priya's recommended option, so the brief ends with neutral options and open questions rather than the recommendation a senior PM would give.

scenarios.prompt: All our competitors launched AI assistants this quarter. Should we? We have no customer data on it, just a board member pushing.
scenarios.why: The skill would mark the evidence 'thin' and requires competitor claims to carry a link and date. But it never says to verify those claims with web_search or web_fetch, and it has no branch for 'no evidence yet': no riskiest assumptions and no cheap test (interviews, fake door, data pull). The options would be speculative, and the board pressure would get no framing beyond 'do nothing' as an option.

product-getting-started.job: onboard product expert to team context
product-getting-started.summary: Asks the user for goals, user types, segments, roadmap, feedback sources, metrics, prioritisation method and decision owners, then returns a five-part setup brief ending with three problems worth a closer look.
strengths: Records system, owner, date range and last refresh for each source and flags stale or missing sources.
Agrees the counting unit (ticket, account or revenue) up front.
Names decision owners for roadmap, specs, release notes and date conversations.
Guardrails against promising dates and editing the tracker or changelog.
missing: memory_search before asking and memory_store after
Three must-have questions with skip paths
An integration check, connect_integration and export fallback
A step that derives the first three problems from real data
A default prioritisation method for teams without one
An offer of recurring routines
A handoff map to teammates (support for tickets, engineering for estimates)

issues.quote: Give the user:
issues.problem: The setup is returned only in chat. It is never saved with memory_store and memory is not checked first with memory_search, so the other Priya skills that rely on 'the team's chosen method' and goals will ask again every time.
issues.fix: Start with memory_search. Save goals, source map, method, counting unit and owners as a named memory block, and confirm what was saved. On later runs, update the block instead of asking again.

issues.quote: Ask for the company and product goals for this period, the main user types,
issues.problem: About fifteen questions come at once, with no priority or skip path. The persona's audience (founders and small teams) will stall.
issues.fix: Ask three must-haves (current goal, main users, where feedback lives) with ask_question. Allow skips, infer the rest from any files supplied, and defer the other questions to when a skill needs them.

issues.quote: The first three problems worth a closer look, with reasons.
issues.problem: No step reads any source, so the model has to invent candidate problems from the goals, which contradicts 'Never fill a gap in the data with a guess'.
issues.fix: Add a step that runs a light feedback-synthesis pass on the most accessible source (e.g. the last 30 days of tickets). If there is no data, say so and name what to pull.

issues.quote: for the usage metrics and where they live. Record the system, owner, date
issues.problem: It records where sources live but never checks what is connected (run_block for Linear, HubSpot, Notion or Sheets, or run_mcp_tool), never offers connect_integration, and never accepts an export as a fallback.
issues.fix: Check connections before asking, offer connect_integration for gaps, and treat a pasted export or CSV as equivalent so the work never waits on a connection.

issues.quote: Set up product work from goals, users, feedback sources, metrics, and decision owners.
issues.problem: The description does not say 'first conversation' or 'when memory has no product setup'. The triggers 'roadmap setup' and 'product goals' collide with roadmap-prioritisation, so the skill may load mid-task.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Use on the first conversation with Priya, or when memory has no product setup…' and drop 'roadmap setup'.

issues.quote: Agree the prioritisation method the team trusts and who supplies effort
issues.problem: There is no default for teams without a method, so the step blocks.
issues.fix: Propose a default (goals-first, then RICE with effort left blank until engineering supplies it) and record that it was proposed, not agreed.

issues.problem: It never offers a recurring rhythm (weekly feedback digest, monthly roadmap review) even though schedule_routine exists.
issues.fix: Offer one or two routines with a cadence and owner, created only on the user's approval.

scenarios.prompt: I'm the founder of a 6-person SaaS. Help me set up product management; our feedback lives in Intercom and a Notion page.
scenarios.why: 'Map goals and sources' and 'Set the working rules' produce a reasonable source map and owner list, but only after a long list of questions. Nothing is saved with memory_store, so feedback-synthesis and roadmap-prioritisation will ask again. There is no check of or connect step for Notion or Intercom, and item 5 ('first three problems') has no step that reads the feedback.

scenarios.prompt: Just get going. I don't have goals written down, no metrics tool, and I'm the only decision maker.
scenarios.why: Every step is 'Ask for…' or 'Agree…', with no default path, no suggested method (unlike roadmap-prioritisation, which proposes one), and no fast path for a solo founder. The brief would be mostly blanks or guesses, and item 5 would be invented, which breaks the skill's own rule 'Never fill a gap in the data with a guess'. Nothing persists.

product-requirements-draft.job: write PRD with scope and acceptance criteria
product-requirements-draft.summary: Drafts a requirements doc once a problem is agreed: problem and evidence, one measurable goal with baseline, user stories, out of scope, testable acceptance criteria, edge cases, dependencies, open questions (who answers, whether blocking), and risks with stop conditions.
strengths: A measurable goal with an explicit baseline, and says so when there is none.
Acceptance criteria per story that both an engineer and a tester can check.
Edge-case prompts (empty states, limits, permissions, errors).
Open questions carry an owner and a blocking flag, plus stop or change-course conditions.
'Describe what the user must be able to do, not how to build it.'
missing: Non-functional, security and accessibility requirements
An instrumentation and analytics spec for the success metric
A rollout, flag, migration and rollback plan
Prioritised stories and a smallest-shippable-version cut
A target, timeframe and counter-metric for the goal
A PRD template with header metadata
Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria examples
Support, docs and launch impact

issues.problem: It has no non-functional requirements (performance, accessibility, security and privacy, data retention), no analytics events to measure the goal, no rollout plan (flag, beta, migration, rollback), and no support, docs or launch impact.
issues.fix: Add sections for non-functional requirements, instrumentation (events that feed the goal metric), rollout and rollback, and launch and support needs.

issues.quote: user stories in the form "As a ..., I want ..., so that ...";
issues.problem: Stories are not prioritised and there is no MVP cut, so the doc cannot guide the smallest shippable slice when time is tight.
issues.fix: Tag each story must, should or could (or P0-P2) and state the smallest shippable version explicitly.

issues.quote: Use this once the team has agreed which problem to solve.
issues.problem: There is no decision point for the common 'write a PRD for feature X' request with no agreed problem or evidence. The model will write rationale that nothing supports.
issues.fix: If there is no agreed problem or evidence, mark the problem section 'unvalidated', list the evidence gaps, and recommend opportunity-brief first, or ask one question.

issues.quote: Give one goal that can be measured, the current baseline, and how
issues.problem: There is no target value, timeframe or counter-metric, and no check that the tracking actually exists.
issues.fix: Require a target, a review date and one guardrail metric, and flag missing instrumentation as a dependency.

issues.quote: for each story, testable conditions an engineer
issues.problem: There is no format or example for acceptance criteria and no prompt for negative paths, so criteria are often vague.
issues.fix: Suggest Given/When/Then with at least one failure or permission-denied case per story.

issues.problem: There is no document skeleton or header (owner, status, version, reviewers, linked brief), so outputs vary and are hard to track.
issues.fix: Ship templates/prd.md with a header and the section order.

issues.quote: yourself; draft for approval. Never invent a metric, quote, or estimate.
issues.problem: 'Draft for approval' names no approver and no destination. There is no option to create the doc in Google Docs or Notion after sign-off.
issues.fix: Name the spec approver from the setup memory, and offer to write to Docs or Notion through run_block only after explicit approval; otherwise return markdown.

scenarios.prompt: We've agreed to build bulk tag editing. Here's the opportunity brief. Write the PRD for engineering.
scenarios.why: 'Problem and goal', 'Scope and criteria' and 'Open questions' cover what engineers need for a simple CRUD feature: a baseline, stories, testable criteria, edge cases (empty, limits, permissions, errors), dependencies, and blocking questions. It lacks instrumentation and rollout sections, but for this feature the draft is usable.

scenarios.prompt: Write a spec for SAML SSO. Sales says three enterprise deals depend on it closing by end of Q4, we need it for SOC 2, and we have no baseline metric.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly says 'If there is no baseline yet, say so' and forbids committing to a date. But there is no non-functional or security requirements section, no rollout, migration or flag plan, and no priority on stories to find a smallest shippable slice under date pressure. Those are exactly what SSO needs (IdP matrix, JIT/SCIM, audit logging), so coverage depends entirely on the model's own knowledge.

release-notes-draft.job: draft customer-facing release notes from shipped changes
release-notes-draft.summary: Confirms what shipped (ticket or PR, date, who confirmed, plans and regions, flag status), writes benefit-led customer-facing notes in the customer's words, and puts an approval note above the draft listing sources, held-back changes, open questions and the approver.
strengths: Includes only confirmed shipped changes, with ticket or PR, date and who confirmed.
Covers plans, platforms, regions, flags and rollout status.
Leads with what the user can now do, and says who it is for and where to find it.
The approval note lists sources, held-back changes, open questions and the approver.
Does not publish, edit the changelog or promise future dates.
missing: A breaking-change, deprecation and required-action section
A security-fix disclosure rule
A release-notes template with groups and a version header
Channel variants (changelog, in-app, email, internal enablement)
Intake through GitHub or Linear, with internal-change filtering
A path to confirm unconfirmed items
A customer-naming consent rule

issues.problem: Breaking changes, deprecations, migrations, pricing or plan changes, and required customer actions are not handled. These must lead release notes and carry dates and steps.
issues.fix: Add an 'Action required' block at the top with what changes, who is affected, the deadline from the supplied schedule, and migration steps with a doc link.

issues.quote: list fixes plainly, without blaming anyone.
issues.problem: 'Plainly' can expose exploit details of security fixes before every customer is patched or before coordinated disclosure.
issues.fix: Describe security fixes at a high level ('fixed an authentication issue'), clear the wording with the security owner, and cite a CVE only once it is published.

issues.quote: List each change with its ticket or pull request, the release date, and who
issues.problem: There is no intake route (GitHub releases or merged PRs, Linear completed issues through run_block, or a paste), no filter for changes that only matter internally, and no path when 'confirmed live' is unknown.
issues.fix: Pull merged PRs or issues through run_block, or accept a paste. Drop internal-only changes and list them in the approval note. Mark unconfirmed items [unconfirmed] and ask the release owner rather than silently dropping them.

issues.quote: one short paragraph or bullet per change;
issues.problem: There is no structure: no headline, no grouping (Action required, New, Improved, Fixed), no ordering by impact, no version or date header, and no variants for the changelog, in-app, email or internal sales/CS enablement.
issues.fix: Ship a template with those sections and a short channel-variant table.

issues.quote: use the words customers used when they asked for it;
issues.problem: It does not name where customer wording comes from, and there is no rule against naming or quoting requesting customers publicly without permission.
issues.fix: Take the wording from feedback-synthesis or tracker notes, paraphrase in the customer's vocabulary, and never name a customer without written permission.

issues.quote: Keep it honest about limits. Do not call a change "new" if it only reached
issues.problem: This is a blunt prohibition with no replacement wording, so partial rollouts get vague descriptions.
issues.fix: Prescribe labels: 'Beta', 'Rolling out over N days', 'Available on <plan>'.

issues.quote: "ship announcement", "product update"
issues.problem: 'Product update' also matches internal stakeholder or investor updates, so the skill may load for the wrong job.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'what shipped this release' or 'customer changelog'.

scenarios.prompt: Here are the 8 Linear issues we shipped in v3.2 on Tuesday. Draft the release notes.
scenarios.why: 'Confirm what shipped', 'Write the notes' and 'Approval note' give benefit-led bullets with audience and location, plainly listed fixes, honesty about partial rollouts, and an approval header. There is no grouping template, but a capable model will produce clean, usable notes at this size.

scenarios.prompt: Draft notes from these 60 merged GitHub PRs since v2.3. Two are behind flags, one removes the v1 API, and one patches an auth bypass. Ship tomorrow.
scenarios.why: There is no instruction to filter internal PRs (refactors, CI, dependency bumps), no breaking-change or deprecation handling to put the v1 API removal first with migration steps, and 'list fixes plainly' pushes toward describing the auth bypass in detail. 'Leave out anything not confirmed' has no path to get confirmation, so the draft either drops most items or guesses.

crm-duplicate-review.job: find and triage duplicate CRM records
crm-duplicate-review.summary: A 39-line outline that tells the model to state tiered match rules, list candidate duplicate pairs with evidence and a suggested survivor, and return strong/likely/ruled-out lists for a person to merge.
strengths: Match rules are written and graded strong/likely/weak before any matching, so every pair traces to a stated rule.
Groups with open deals or different owners are kept apart for human review, which is exactly where bad merges do damage.
The ruled-out list and 'which reports will change' make the review auditable and tie it to reporting impact.
Clear no-merge / no-edit / no-guessing boundary that matches Omar's persona.
missing: Normalisation rules and free-mail domain exclusion list
Fuzzy-match method and thresholds for names/companies
Transitive clustering of pairs into groups
Cross-object (lead vs contact) matching
Survivor order and field-level survivorship proposals
Sandbox matching script and CSV merge-file template
Sample precision check before 'ready' label
Root cause by creation source and a prevention rule
PII handling for contact exports

issues.quote: Write the rules before matching, for example exact email, same domain and
issues.problem: The example 'same domain and surname' rule has no free-mail/ISP domain exclusion and no normalisation (lowercasing, trimming, phone to E.164, a legal-suffix list beyond Ltd/Inc), so it floods the output with false positives.
issues.fix: Add a normalisation step and a free-mail domain exclusion list. Name the fuzzy method and threshold for names and companies (e.g. token-sort ratio ≥ 90 on the normalised company name, email domain root match), and treat domain-only matches as weak.

issues.quote: which record looks like the survivor, and why.
issues.problem: The survivor is picked ad hoc and there are no field-level survivorship rules. Combined with 'do not guess which value is correct', the reviewer gets no usable merge recommendation for conflicting fields.
issues.fix: Give a default survivor order (has open deals > most recent activity > oldest created > most complete) and propose per-field winner rules (e.g. latest non-blank phone, owner of the survivor), labelled as proposals for the CRM owner to approve.

issues.quote: Use this for contacts, leads, or accounts from a dated export.
issues.problem: The skill names no tools and no fallback. It does not say to load and match the file in bash_exec (pairwise comparison over thousands of rows is unreliable in context), to read via the HubSpot block read-only, or to ask for an export when there is no integration.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step: ask for an export (or read it via the HubSpot block read-only), record date/object/row count, then run normalisation, blocking and matching in bash_exec and keep the pair table as a workspace file.

issues.quote: For each pair or group show:
issues.problem: There is no method for building groups from pairs (transitive A~B, B~C) and no cross-object check (lead vs contact, contact under the wrong account), which are common duplicate sources.
issues.fix: Cluster pairs into groups by connected components with the weakest link's strength shown, and add an optional lead-to-contact and contact-to-account pass.

issues.quote: Return three lists: strong matches ready for review, likely matches that need a
issues.problem: Output is prose lists with no column spec or machine-usable file, so an admin can't feed it to a merge tool or track decisions.
issues.fix: Ship a template: group id, record ids, object, rule, strength, survivor id, open deals, owners, decision (blank). Write it as a CSV to the workspace alongside the summary counts.

issues.problem: The skill has no root-cause or prevention step. It never shows which source, import or form creates the duplicates, and never proposes an at-entry duplicate rule.
issues.fix: Break the duplicate groups down by created source/date and propose one prevention change (duplicate rule, form dedupe key, import matching) for the owner.

issues.problem: There is no precision check before labelling matches 'strong ... ready for review', and no note on personal-data handling for contact exports.
issues.fix: Hand-check a sample of 10–20 strong pairs and report the observed false-positive count. Keep contact PII in the workspace file and out of memory, and flag records tied to deletion or erasure requests.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our HubSpot contacts export (8,200 rows). Find the duplicates we should merge and tell me which record to keep.
scenarios.why: The steps give the right structure: rules with strengths, pair evidence and three lists with counts. But the example rule 'same domain and surname' has no free-mail exclusion, so gmail.com/outlook.com pairs flood the likely list. No normalisation step (case, whitespace, phone format) is given. Survivor choice is 'looks like the survivor' with no rule order. The skill never says to do the pairwise work in bash_exec, so an in-context pass over 8k rows will miss or invent pairs.

scenarios.prompt: Many of our Salesforce leads are probably already contacts, and accounts show up as 'Acme Inc', 'ACME Corporation' and 'acme.io'. You can't connect to Salesforce. Just tell me what to merge.
scenarios.why: 'from a dated export' implies asking for an export, but there is no explicit fallback, and Salesforce has no block. Cross-object matching (lead to contact) and fuzzy company matching beyond stripping 'Ltd'/'Inc' (domain root, Corp/Corporation, TLD variants) are not covered. The transitive group A~B~C has no clustering rule. The guardrails still hold, so the output is safe but shallow.

crm-field-audit.job: audit CRM field quality and usage
crm-field-audit.summary: A 41-line outline that tells the model to record the export, measure fill rate, format problems, distinct values, usage and ownership for each field, flag placeholders, and label each field keep/fix/retire for the CRM owner.
strengths: Starts by recording export date, object, filter, row count and whether the export is partial, before any figure.
Flags placeholder values ('n/a', 'tbc', default dates) that inflate fill rates, which is a senior-practitioner catch.
'fix' asks for the smallest change (picklist, required rule, backfill from a named source), not a rebuild.
'retire' requires listing dependents, and every label ties to the report it affects.
missing: Conditional (applicable-population) fill rates
A way to get field metadata and usage data, with an UNKNOWN fallback
Decision criteria for keep/fix/retire and a merge label for overlapping fields
Picklist value sprawl and integration-written vs manual value analysis
Staged deprecation procedure
Profiling script and output table template
Top-issues summary tied to named reports

issues.quote: fill rate as a count and a percentage;
issues.problem: A raw fill rate across all rows mislabels conditional fields: stage-dependent fields, record-type-specific fields, and fields created after older records existed. That leads to wrong 'retire' calls.
issues.fix: Compute fill rate over the population where the field applies (by stage, record type, and created-after-field-creation date), and show both the raw and the applicable rate.

issues.quote: whether a report, rule, or automation uses it;
issues.problem: An export cannot show usage, and the skill gives no source, so the model will guess or leave it blank. Retire decisions then rest on nothing.
issues.fix: Ask for field metadata (type, created date, last modified, property usage / 'Where is this used', report list). Where it is missing, mark usage UNKNOWN and block any retire label until usage is confirmed.

issues.problem: The skill has no tool routing or fallback. It never says to profile the file in bash_exec, read HubSpot properties via the block, or ask for an export when none is attached, and profiling 85+ columns by eye is unreliable.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step (export plus metadata, or HubSpot block read-only) and a profiling step in bash_exec that writes a per-field table to the workspace.

issues.quote: Label each field **keep**, **fix**, or **retire**, with one line of reason and
issues.problem: No criteria for each label, so decisions are inconsistent across fields. There is no 'merge' outcome for duplicate or overlapping fields (e.g. two Industry fields).
issues.fix: State default criteria as assumptions the owner can change (e.g. retire when applicable fill < 5%, no usage and no owner). Add a 'merge into X' label for overlapping fields.

issues.quote: For **retire**, list what
issues.problem: Retirement has no safe deprecation path, so hard deletion of history remains an implied option.
issues.fix: Propose staged deprecation: hide from layouts, stop writes, archive the values to a file, delete only after a notice period, all approved by the owner.

issues.quote: Return the list for the CRM owner to approve.
issues.problem: No output template or summary. The owner gets a long list with no view of the few fields that hurt named reports most.
issues.fix: Provide a table template (field, type, applicable fill %, placeholder %, distinct values, used by, owner, label, reason, report affected) plus a top-5 summary.

scenarios.prompt: Audit the fields on our Deals object. Here's a CSV export of 2,300 deals with 85 columns. Which fields should we keep, fix, or kill?
scenarios.why: The model will produce fill rate, formats, distinct values and keep/fix/retire labels. But 'Loss reason' or 'Signed date' will show low fill because the rate is not computed only over deals where the field applies. The 'whether a report, rule, or automation uses it' column can't be filled from a CSV, and the skill neither says to ask for property-usage metadata nor to mark it UNKNOWN.

scenarios.prompt: We're migrating from Salesforce to HubSpot. Tell me which of our 400 custom Account fields to bring over. I only have a data export, no admin access and no field metadata.
scenarios.why: 'One object at a time' fits, and the no-guessing guardrail keeps it honest. But with no usage data, 'For retire, list what still reads the field' is impossible, and the skill has no instruction to mark usage unknown and request the Field Usage / 'Where is this used' report. Duplicate fields (two Industry fields) have no 'merge' label. With no thresholds, 400 labels will be inconsistent, and the skill never says to profile 400 columns in bash_exec.

crm-hygiene-report.job: report recurring CRM data health trends
crm-hygiene-report.summary: A 39-line outline for a periodic CRM health report: headline counts against last period (no owner, low fill, open duplicates, stale deals, unowned leads), a breakdown by owner and object, and three to five ordered fixes.
strengths: Opens with export dates and row counts, consistent with the persona.
Picks the single change that matters most and names the report it affects.
Neutral framing ('fix the data, not rank people') is right for a report that names owners.
Fixes carry count cleared, report helped, approver and date, and carry-over fixes from the last report are tracked.
missing: Snapshot persistence and first-run baseline
schedule_routine setup for weekly/monthly runs
Defined thresholds for key fields, fill rates and staleness
Rates normalised by volume, not raw counts
Close-date slippage, missing next step, orphaned contacts, bounced emails
Fixed report template with prior/current/delta
Drafted distribution with approval before posting
Explicit sequencing on top of crm-field-audit and crm-duplicate-review outputs

issues.quote: Use this weekly or monthly, from dated exports compared with the last report.
issues.problem: The skill assumes a prior report and persistent state that the platform does not keep automatically. It has no first-run baseline, no snapshot save, and no schedule.
issues.fix: On first run, label the output as a baseline. Save the metric snapshot and open-fix list with write_workspace_file (with a pointer in memory_store). Next run, retrieve them via memory_search. Offer schedule_routine for weekly/monthly runs.

issues.quote: key fields below the agreed fill rate;
issues.problem: The skill never says where the 'agreed' key fields and fill thresholds come from, so the model will invent them and trends will be meaningless.
issues.fix: Pull key fields and thresholds from the revops-getting-started working rules or ask_question. If none exist, state defaults as labelled assumptions and keep them fixed across periods.

issues.quote: deals past close date or stale in stage;
issues.problem: 'Stale' is undefined. The skill also misses the common hygiene signals: pushed close dates, deals with no next step or no activity in N days, and contacts not associated to an account.
issues.fix: Define stale (e.g. days in stage > 2x historical median from pipeline-stage-definitions, or no activity in 30 days) and add close-date push count, missing next step, and orphaned contacts.

issues.quote: "CRM report", "pipeline hygiene", "stale deals"
issues.problem: 'Stale deals' collides with Omar's own sales-forecast-rollup ('Risks and stale deals'), and 'CRM report' is so generic it fires on any reporting request. Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast and sales-ops-coverage-and-quota also trigger on 'CRM hygiene'.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to a recurring cross-object data-health rollup that aggregates field-audit and duplicate-review results. Drop 'CRM report' and 'stale deals' and add 'weekly CRM health', 'data quality trend'.

issues.quote: Break the counts down by object and by owner. Show where problems cluster and
issues.problem: Raw counts by owner penalise large books and in effect rank people, which contradicts the stated aim. 'New or old' needs record-level snapshot comparison, and the skill has no method for it.
issues.fix: Report rates per owner (issues / records owned) with n. Mark a record as new or old by comparing its IDs to the saved prior snapshot.

issues.problem: The skill defines no report template and no distribution step. It doesn't say who receives the report or that any post or email is a draft pending approval.
issues.fix: Add a fixed report skeleton (headline table with prior/current/delta, by-owner rate table, fix list) and draft the Slack/email version for approval before sending.

scenarios.prompt: Give me this month's CRM hygiene report. Here are exports of contacts, companies and deals from HubSpot.
scenarios.why: The headline list is sensible, but 'against the last period' has no source and the skill has no first-run baseline rule. 'Agreed fill rate' and 'stale in stage' are undefined, so the model will invent thresholds or stall. The breakdown uses counts, not rates, so large books look worse.

scenarios.prompt: Set this up to run every Monday, compare with last week, and post the summary to #revops in Slack.
scenarios.why: The skill never mentions schedule_routine or saving each week's snapshot and open-fix list (write_workspace_file / memory_store) for the next run. It has no guidance for drafting the Slack post and getting approval before posting. The trend comparison, which is the core of the report, has no mechanism on this platform.

lead-routing-rules.job: design lead routing and assignment rules
lead-routing-rules.summary: A 38-line outline that tells the model to list every routing case with 90-day volumes, write ordered first-match-wins rules with owner, response time and backup plus a named fallback, and back-test the draft against past leads.
strengths: Starts from real volume per case and the 'no owner after a day' count, so the rules target observed failures.
First-match-wins ordering and a named-person fallback make coverage provably complete and exclusive.
Each rule carries response time and a backup owner for absence or capacity.
The back-test reports unmatched, multi-matched and changed-owner leads plus the shift in load per owner before anything goes live.
Conditions must use fields that exist and are filled, which prevents rules nobody can evaluate.
missing: Lead-to-account matching method
In-queue distribution (round robin, weights, caps, absence skip)
SLA breach escalation and re-routing
Sourced enrichment path for missing region/size
Partner/channel conflict and named-account overrides
Recycled or re-engaged lead rules
Scripted back-test in the sandbox
Rollout plan and post-launch monitoring
Rule-table template ready for CRM configuration

issues.quote: handle: region, company size, product, source, existing account, existing
issues.problem: 'Existing account' is a case but the skill gives no lead-to-account matching method (normalised domain, fuzzy company name), and that is where most B2B routing breaks.
issues.fix: Add a matching step before routing: normalise email domain, exclude free-mail, match to account domain or fuzzy name, and route matched leads to the account owner with the match strength shown.

issues.quote: the owner or queue it routes to;
issues.problem: Distribution within a queue is left out: round robin vs weighted, capacity caps, skipping reps who are away. Uneven distribution is a top complaint in routing reviews.
issues.fix: For each queue, specify the distribution method, per-rep weights or caps, and the absence handling, and show expected leads per rep from the back-test.

issues.quote: the time the owner has to respond;
issues.problem: The skill sets a response time but no action when it is missed, so the 'wait too long' failure named in the intro is not solved.
issues.fix: Add an SLA breach rule per queue (re-route to backup after X hours, alert the manager) and a metric for measuring speed-to-first-touch after go-live.

issues.quote: Run the draft rules on the last 90 days of leads on paper.
issues.problem: A 'paper' test over thousands of leads produces estimates, not the exact counts the report needs.
issues.fix: Encode the draft rules as a script in bash_exec, run it on the export, and write the per-lead assignment and the summary tables to the workspace.

issues.quote: missing region or size.
issues.problem: Forbidding guesses without offering sourced enrichment leaves many leads in the fallback queue indefinitely.
issues.fix: Allow enrichment from a named source (Apollo/Enrichlayer block, email domain, form IP country), labelled as enriched with its source. Otherwise route to a triage queue with its own owner and response time.

issues.quote: The sales lead approves the rules before anyone turns
issues.problem: The skill has no rollout plan: no effective date, no handling of in-flight leads, no rep communication, and no post-launch check.
issues.fix: Add a rollout section: effective date, what happens to existing open leads, a one-page change note for reps, and a 2-week re-check of unmatched and SLA-breach counts.

issues.problem: The skill does not ask for rep capacity, working hours or territory ownership lists, which the rules and backups depend on.
issues.fix: Name these inputs up front and ask_question for any that are missing.

scenarios.prompt: Website demo requests sit unassigned for days. Here's the Q2 lead export and our current round-robin rules. Rewrite the routing so nothing falls through.
scenarios.why: The steps are enough for a good result. Cases with 90-day volume and unowned-after-a-day counts diagnose the gap, ordered rules with response time and backup, plus a named fallback, close it, and the back-test shows unmatched, double-matched and changed-owner leads. The weak points are depth: no round-robin weighting or capacity caps, and no escalation when the response time is missed.

scenarios.prompt: Next month we add a partner channel and split EMEA into two territories. 30% of leads have no country, many are from existing customer accounts, and we're on Salesforce, which you can't access.
scenarios.why: 'Do not guess a missing region' is right, but there is no sourced alternative: enrichment via Apollo/Enrichlayer or email domain, labelled as enriched, or a triage queue. 'Existing account' is listed but the skill gives no lead-to-account matching method. Partner channel conflict and the cutover of in-flight leads on the effective date are not covered. There is no fallback for the missing Salesforce access beyond the implied export.

lost-deal-analysis.summary: A 39-line outline that tells the model to check loss-reason quality first, break closed-lost deals down by reason, stage, segment, age and owner, compare with won deals where possible, and state what the data cannot show.
strengths: Gates the analysis on reason quality ('other', free text, reasons added long after close) and says the breakdown is weak when over a quarter lack a reason.
Owner-level cuts only where the count supports it, and quotes only verbatim with a deal id.
'What the data cannot say' names real biases: short pick-lists, deals lost before entry, inconsistent logging.
Suggests the smallest next check (calls with lost buyers) instead of over-reading the CRM.
missing: Closure-type classification (competitor, no decision, disqualified, admin)
Stage history requirement for stage at loss
Win rates rather than loss counts, with n per cell
Minimum sample size rule
Competitor, discount and time-trend cuts
Hypothesis test against a stated belief
Output template and proposed reason-list redesign
Win-loss interview guide or handoff to competitive-intelligence (Zara)

issues.quote: stage at loss;
issues.problem: In most CRMs a closed-lost deal's stage is 'Closed Lost', so stage at loss needs stage history or a last-open-stage field. The skill doesn't say to request it or mark it unknown.
issues.fix: List stage history (date-entered-stage properties / OpportunityHistory) as a required input. If it is absent, mark stage at loss UNKNOWN rather than reporting the terminal stage.

issues.quote: Count lost deals and their value. Then count how many have a loss reason, how
issues.problem: Real competitive losses are not separated from disqualified, no-decision, duplicate or admin cleanup closures, which inflate early-stage losses and distort every breakdown.
issues.fix: First classify closures (lost to competitor, no decision, disqualified, duplicate/admin), with counts, and analyse genuine losses separately.

issues.quote: Compare with won deals over the same period where you can.
issues.problem: Won-deal comparison is optional, but without it the analysis shows only the mix of losses, not where the team actually loses more often. Loss counts by segment track volume, not weakness.
issues.fix: Make won deals a required input and report win rate = won/(won+lost) by segment, size, source and stage reached, with n for each cell.

issues.quote: owner, only where the count is large enough to mean something.
issues.problem: 'Large enough' is undefined, so the model will over-read small cells.
issues.fix: Set a minimum (e.g. n ≥ 20 closed deals per cell), show n everywhere, and group smaller cells as 'other'.

issues.problem: The breakdown has no competitor, discount or price-to-list, or time-trend cuts, which are the usual ways to test hypotheses like 'we lose on price'.
issues.fix: Add a hypothesis-test step: take the stated belief, pick the fields that could refute it (discount %, competitor, amount band of won vs lost), and report supported / not supported / cannot tell.

issues.quote: the smallest next check, such as five calls with lost buyers.
issues.problem: There is no output template, no draft interview guide, and no handoff to Zara's competitive-intelligence / win-loss work for buyer interviews.
issues.fix: Define the deliverable (headline paragraph, win-rate tables, reason-quality box, limits, proposed reason-list changes) and offer a 5-question interview guide or a consult_teammate handoff.

issues.problem: The skill has no inputs list and no sandbox use. Crosstabs across five dimensions are error-prone in context.
issues.fix: Name the inputs (closed-lost and closed-won export, period, stage history, reason pick-list) and compute the tables in bash_exec.

scenarios.prompt: Why are we losing deals this year? Here's our closed-lost export from HubSpot for January to August.
scenarios.why: The reason-quality check and breakdowns will run, but a HubSpot closed-lost export shows 'Closed lost' as the deal stage. The skill never says to request stage history or a last-open-stage field, so 'stage at loss' is missing or wrong. Without won deals the output is the share of losses, not the rate at which segments lose. Owner cuts have no minimum n.

scenarios.prompt: The CEO says we lose on price. 40% of lost deals say 'Other', the rest come from a 5-item dropdown, and SDRs closed out a lot of junk as lost. Prove or disprove the price theory.
scenarios.why: The >25% gate fires correctly, and 'never infer a reason from the amount' prevents a fake answer. But the skill has no step to separate disqualified or junk closures from real losses, no discount or competitor comparison of won vs lost to test the hypothesis, and no guidance on presenting an inconclusive result against a senior stakeholder's view.

pipeline-stage-definitions.summary: A 38-line outline that tells the model to review stage usage from a deal export, write per-stage meaning, entry rule, exit rule, proof and data-based time in stage, and list open deals that would move under the new rules.
strengths: Starts from how stages are actually used (skipped stages, months-long stalls, differing rep interpretations) rather than a template.
Every stage has an entry rule, exit rule and a named proof artefact in the CRM.
Time in stage comes from data, not a target, which avoids aspirational SLAs.
Lists open deals that would sit in a different stage, with owner and amount, without moving them.
Marks rules that need a new field, which surfaces CRM change requests explicitly.
missing: Stage-history data requirement and fallback
Buyer-verifiable exit criteria and qualification framework mapping
Historical stage-to-won rates with n
Rules for regression, skips and closed-lost capture
Guidance on separate pipelines per sales motion and stage count
Executable rep-input method (survey draft or ask_question)
Definitions table template and rep one-pager
Validation-rule proposals and adoption re-check

issues.quote: From a dated deal export, count deals by stage, median days in stage, and
issues.problem: A snapshot export can't give days in stage or stage-to-stage conversion. These need stage history, which the skill never requests and has no fallback for.
issues.fix: Require stage-history data (date-entered-stage properties, OpportunityHistory, or a history report). If it is missing, mark the time and conversion metrics UNKNOWN and use current age only as a labelled proxy.

issues.quote: the exit rule: what must be true to move it on;
issues.problem: The skill gives no guidance that exit criteria should be buyer-verifiable outcomes, and no mapping to the team's qualification framework. Without it, rules drift to seller activities ('proposal sent') that don't predict closing.
issues.fix: State that exit rules must be buyer actions or verified facts (e.g. economic buyer identified and met, mutual close plan agreed). Map each to the team's framework (MEDDICC/BANT/SPICED) if one exists.

issues.quote: two or three reps how they decide to move a deal.
issues.problem: The expert cannot interview reps directly, so this step either stalls or gets fabricated.
issues.fix: Draft a 3-question rep survey for the user to send, or ask_question the user. Mark rep input as pending until answers come back.

issues.quote: the expected time in stage, from the data, not a target.
issues.problem: The skill has no fallback when there is no history. It also leaves out historical stage-to-won rates, which sales-forecast-rollup's weighted figure depends on. The skill forbids guessed probabilities but gives no way to derive them.
issues.fix: Compute the historical win rate from each stage over closed deals, with n, as the evidence-based probability. Mark it UNKNOWN when n is small or history is absent.

issues.problem: The skill has no rules for backward movement, stage skipping, a required closed-lost reason at exit, or separate pipelines for different motions (new business, renewal, partner).
issues.fix: Add a short policy block covering regression, skips, loss-reason capture, and when a separate pipeline is warranted.

issues.quote: List open deals that would sit in a different stage under the new rules, with
issues.problem: The skill has no rollout plan: no validation or required-field proposals, no rep one-pager, and no re-check after adoption.
issues.fix: Add a rollout step: proposed validation rules per stage for the CRM owner, a one-page rep guide, and a 30-day re-run of stage usage.

scenarios.prompt: Our reps use 'Proposal' differently and the forecast is unreliable. Here's our deal export. Write stage definitions everyone will follow.
scenarios.why: The model will produce a clean per-stage table with entry, exit and proof, plus a list of deals that don't fit. But median days in stage and conversion need stage history, which a snapshot export lacks, and the skill doesn't flag this. Exit rules will likely be seller activities ('sent proposal') rather than buyer-verified outcomes. 'Ask two or three reps' can't be done by the expert.

scenarios.prompt: We're a 6-person startup tracking deals in a Google Sheet with a free-text 'status' column. We need stages that work for direct and partner-led deals.
scenarios.why: 'Expected time in stage, from the data' has no fallback when there is no history, so the model must improvise (it should mark UNKNOWN). The skill has no guidance on separate pipelines for different motions, how many stages to use, or mapping free-text statuses into stages. The guardrails keep it honest, but the design guidance is thin for a from-scratch build.

mom-test.job: plan and run customer discovery interviews
mom-test.summary: Teaches Rob Fitzpatrick's Mom Test for customer conversations (non-leading past-behaviour questions, deflecting compliments/fluff/ideas, securing commitments, sourcing and processing interviews) and scores a conversation against a seven-row diagnostic, with six deep references and four worked case studies.
strengths: Faithful, practitioner-grade coverage of Fitzpatrick: the three rules; compliments, fluff and ideas with a deflection for each; commitment currencies with escalation ladders; zombie leads; dream/realistic/minimum advance planning; 'scary questions'.
Good progressive disclosure: each section ends with a 'See: references/... when ...' pointer that says when to open the file, and all six reference files ship in the package.

Reusable material in the references: bad-to-good question rewrite tables, recovery phrases, a post-conversation gut check, conversation-log columns, three-belief statement templates, cold outreach and intro email templates.
The Quick Diagnostic plus the 'state score, name failing rows, give fix' instruction yields a concrete, checkable critique of a transcript.
The description carries specific user phrasings ('users say they want it but dont buy', 'leading questions') that make triggering reliable.
missing: An intake step: stage, target customer slice (Fitzpatrick's who-where segmentation), the 'Big 3' learning goals, and the request type.
Deliverable templates: an interview script (opener, Big 3, follow-up probes, close with a prepared ask), a transcript scorecard, and a conversation log file.
A rule that commitments must cost something now, with no hypothetical 'if I built it, would you' closes.
Guardrails: outreach drafted for approval, recording consent, handling of participants' personal details in memory and notes, incentives, no fabricated or paraphrased quotes presented as verbatim.

Platform wiring: ask_question for inputs, write_workspace_file or a Sheets/Notion block for the conversation log, memory_store for the three core beliefs, and a paste/export fallback when the notes integration isn't connected.
Handoffs: to synthesis, JTBD and opportunity-brief skills after a batch of interviews, and to the sales teammate when a discovery conversation turns into a live deal.
Sample-size and confidence caveats in place of fixed percentage thresholds.
Guidance for remote/async modes (video calls, recorded sessions, surveys) and for talking to existing customers, not just pre-product founders.

issues.quote: If I built this, would you be willing to pilot it for 30 days?
issues.problem: This sample question is a hypothetical, future-tense 'would you', which breaks Rule 2 and the skill's own 'would you buy' trap. references/commitment-advancement.md repeats the pattern ('if we build this, would you pre-order at $X?', 'If we build this, would you be willing to be one of our first case studies?'), and every 'Commitment Test' in case-studies.md is hypothetical. The model will reproduce these as closing asks, the exact false-positive the skill exists to prevent.
issues.fix: Replace them with asks that cost something now: a dated calendar slot, a named intro sent today, a refundable deposit, or an LOI signed this week. State the rule outright: a commitment is only real if it costs the person time, reputation or money now.

issues.problem: The skill hands out cold-outreach, intro and follow-up templates but never says to draft them for approval instead of sending. It says nothing about recording consent (the reference has only a single line on it), handling interviewees' names and quotes in memory or shared notes, participant incentives, or sensitive groups. The only guard is a one-line ethical boundary about disguised sales calls.
issues.fix: Add a Guardrails section. Outreach and follow-ups are drafts for the user's approval. Get consent before recording. Keep participant PII out of durable memory, or minimise it there. Never fabricate or 'tidy' a quote. Flag regulated or vulnerable populations and escalate them.

issues.problem: There is no intake step and no workflow. The body is a set of concept sections (core concept, why it works, insights, applications, sample questions), so the model is never told to collect the idea and stage, the target segment, the learning goals, or which job the user wants (write a script, review a transcript, plan outreach, synthesise a batch). Each job needs a different deliverable, and none has a template (for example, no interview-script format).
issues.fix: Add a short 'Start here' block. Ask for stage, segment (a who-where slice), the 3 things the user must learn, and the request type, using ask_question if needed. Then route to the matching reference and name the output: a script template, a transcript scorecard, an outreach draft, or a conversation log plus a belief update.

issues.quote: A problem named by 7 of 10 people is real; 1 of 10 might not be
issues.problem: These are arbitrary cut-offs presented as fact. references/processing-learning.md adds '>50% = strong signal', '>30% = real market' and '>20% = real interest', and finding-conversations.md gives unsourced response rates by channel. The model will repeat them as benchmarks even though the platform forbids invented numbers.
issues.fix: Remove the thresholds and response-rate table, or label them as rough heuristics. Require reporting 'N of M, segment, unprompted vs prompted' with an explicit small-sample caveat.

issues.quote: Score a conversation (or interview plan) by the seven-row Quick Diagnostic below
issues.problem: Several diagnostic rows cannot be judged for a plan (whether they gave a commitment, did most of the talking, whether beliefs were updated), yet the score is mandatory. A good script would score low simply because the call hasn't happened.
issues.fix: Split the rubric in two: a pre-call checklist for plans and scripts (no idea mentioned, past-specific questions, scary questions included, ask prepared) and the existing post-call diagnostic for conversations.

issues.quote: https://www.amazon.com/Mom-Test-customers-business-everyone/dp/1492180742?tag=wondelai00-20
issues.problem: This is an Amazon affiliate link that earns money for the upstream vendor (a sponsor/vendor signal in the brief). The 'About the Author' section that follows is filler the model does not need at runtime.
issues.fix: Replace both with a one-line attribution to Rob Fitzpatrick's book, with no link or an untagged one, and delete 'About the Author'.

issues.quote: For rapid prototype testing, see design-sprint.
issues.problem: No design-sprint skill exists in the catalog. The broad triggers 'customer interviews' and 'interview script' also collide with user-interview-guide (Priya) and product-discovery-and-user-research (Alex), so the wrong skill may load.
issues.fix: Drop the design-sprint pointer. Narrow the description to non-leading technique and validation evidence, and point to the sibling skill that owns interview guides and synthesis.

issues.quote: realistic SaaS, consumer, B2B, and marketplace interviews scored against this diagnostic
issues.problem: case-studies.md scores on a /10 scale, not the 7-row diagnostic. Case 4 also declares 'The hypothesis is validated' after two conversations that used 'What would that look like ideally?' and hypothetical $15 asks, which models weak evidence as validation.
issues.fix: Rescore the cases on the 7-row diagnostic. Rewrite case 4's close as a real booked and paid session, and soften 'validated' to 'promising, needs N more with commitments'.

scenarios.prompt: Here are the 12 questions I plan to ask independent restaurant owners next week about my inventory-app idea. Fix anything leading and tell me how to end each call.
scenarios.why: Rules 1-2 in SKILL.md plus references/question-patterns.md (bad-vs-good rewrite tables, the 5-tier hierarchy, the Idea Purge and Specificity Drill, and Common Mistakes in Questioning such as double-barreled questions and anchoring with numbers) give the model what it needs to rewrite each question. commitment-advancement.md 'Designing the End of a Conversation' and the dream/realistic/minimum ask table supply a proper close. Two caveats. The mandatory 'score out of 7' is ill-defined for a plan, because the commitment, talk-ratio and belief-update rows cannot pass before the call happens. And the Section 4 sample line 'If I built this, would you be willing to pilot it for 30 days?' could be copied into the close.

scenarios.prompt: We've done 14 calls about our SOC 2 automation tool. Notes for 9 are in a Google Doc; the other 5 I only remember. About half said they'd 'definitely buy'. Have we validated demand? Then email the 4 warmest from my Gmail asking them to sign an LOI.
scenarios.why: avoiding-bad-data.md correctly classifies 'definitely buy' as hypothetical fluff, and processing-learning.md supplies the three core beliefs and a conversation spreadsheet, so the verdict would probably be 'not validated'. Several gaps remain. Nothing tells the model to fetch the Doc (connect_integration) or fall back to a paste. Nothing says to mark memory-only calls as low-reliability instead of reconstructing them. The model may present the unsourced '>50% / >30% / >20%' thresholds as benchmarks. There is no LOI template. commitment-advancement.md models hypothetical asks ('if we build this, would you pre-order at $X?'). And there is no draft-and-approve step before sending from Gmail.

nda-risk-review.summary: Sorts an inbound NDA into GREEN (sign), YELLOW (a lawyer checks named items) or RED (stop) against the team's attorney-reviewed, side-specific NDA positions. It first checks whether the document carries obligations beyond confidentiality and has an output template for each bucket. Every position, header, approver and setup step is read from a Claude Code plugin config path (~/.claude/..., 31 references) that does not exist in AutoGPT.
strengths: The scope check auto-escalates an 'NDA in disguise' (standstill, non-solicit, licence grant, IP assignment, ROFR, MFN, broad arbitration). A senior commercial lawyer would recognise this insight.
GREEN is issued only against attorney-reviewed positions, and a non-lawyer must give an explicit yes before signature, backed by a one-page brief of questions for the attorney.
A one-way NDA questionnaire, with M&A, employment and investment NDAs excluded and routed to legal.
The clean-NDA rule and the complexity filter keep the sales-facing output short and limited to mechanical edits.
Three reusable bucket templates, each with a check table and a next step. RED also says 'do not tell the counterparty we'll sign', and no CLM record is created on RED.
Determines the side (sales or purchasing, whose paper) before applying positions, and runs a destination/privilege-circle check before sharing output.
Calibrates to the counterparty: large enterprises rarely negotiate their paper, while startups usually accept ours.
missing: An AutoGPT-native playbook: stored with memory_store or as a workspace file, with ask_question-driven setup and a documented fallback when no playbook exists.
A shipped NDA positions template (per-term GREEN/YELLOW/RED criteria, with the attorney reviewer and date).

Checks for purpose and use restriction, representatives and affiliates, compelled-disclosure procedure, remedies, no licence or warranty, return/destruction certification, assignment, publicity, and the DTSA notice.
A non-advisory label mode that fits Ellis (MATCH / DEVIATION / MISSING / UNCLEAR, with quoted playbook text).
Worked GREEN, YELLOW and RED example NDAs, or evals, to calibrate the buckets.
A batch intake mode for sales volume: several NDAs triaged into a log or register with status and approver.
An explicit handoff to counsel (counsel-escalation-brief or consult_teammate), with any email to legal drafted and approved before it is sent.
Handling for scanned or PDF NDAs, and exhibits or order forms that incorporate the NDA.

issues.quote: If the matching side is `[Not configured]`, stop and tell the user to run `/commercial-legal:cold-start-interview --side <side>` before this triage can proceed.
issues.problem: The whole skill reads its positions, work-product header, approvers, closing_action and matter context from ~/.claude/plugins/config/.../CLAUDE.md (31 references). Setup is gated on slash commands (/commercial-legal:cold-start-interview, :matter-workspace, :review) that are not registered in AutoGPT. With the preamble's stop-and-setup rule, a clean run stops and sends the user to a nonexistent command.
issues.fix: Replace the config layer with AutoGPT primitives. Look up NDA positions with memory_search or a workspace file (for example nda-playbook.md); if absent, ask the user to upload or paste the playbook via ask_question. Store confirmed positions with memory_store. Remove all ~/.claude paths, slash commands and the matter-workspace paragraph. Replace the CLM section with 'draft the record and ask for approval' or 'log to a Sheet'.

issues.section: RED — stop, talk to legal first
issues.quote: Recommended response: [use our paper instead | push back with specific language | walk]
issues.problem: The skill's only proposed expert is Ellis, who is non-advisory: Ellis must not decide risk, acceptability or recommend positions. The templates emit legal-risk ratings, 'Likely resolution: accept', 'Recommended response: walk' and 'GREEN — route to signature', which contradicts Ellis's identity and boundaries.
issues.fix: For Ellis, express findings as MATCH / DEVIATION / MISSING / UNCLEAR against quoted playbook text, with a 'counsel decision needed' line. Drop the risk ratings and recommendations unless the supplied playbook defines them, and attribute any label to the playbook.

issues.quote: That section is the source of truth for what makes an NDA GREEN, YELLOW, or RED for *this* team on *this* side.
issues.problem: The shipped references/practice-profile-template.md has no 'NDA triage positions' subsection. It only covers limitation of liability, indemnity, data protection, term and governing law. So the skill's source of truth has no schema, and a user filling in the template cannot populate it.
issues.fix: Ship references/nda-positions-template.md with one row per term (mutuality, CI definition, carveouts, residuals, term and survival, restrictive covenants, fees, backup and archival, governing law, purpose). Each row needs GREEN/YELLOW/RED criteria and a 'reviewed by attorney / date' field.

issues.quote: Then record the answer in `~/.claude/plugins/config/claude-for-legal/commercial-legal/CLAUDE.md` and proceed with the triage using the new position.
issues.problem: An ad-hoc answer from whoever is triaging (often a sales rep) is written into the standing playbook with no reviewer or date. It then silently governs later reviews, and the GREEN gate ('attorney-reviewed positions') has no way to tell these entries apart from counsel-set ones.
issues.fix: Record user-supplied answers as provisional, with source, name and date, and get approval before saving. Only attorney-confirmed positions count toward GREEN. Queue provisional positions for counsel through counsel-escalation-brief.

issues.problem: The check list omits core NDA terms that a senior reviewer, and Ellis's own nda-playbook-review, cover: purpose and use restriction, representatives and affiliates, compelled-disclosure procedure, remedies and injunctive relief, no licence or warranty, return/destruction certification, assignment, publicity and confidentiality of the discussions, and the DTSA whistleblower notice where individuals sign. A 'GREEN' can pass without these ever being checked.
issues.fix: Add these categories to the check reference and the positions template. Treat the use restriction and representatives definition as mandatory checks.

issues.quote: Loaded by /commercial-legal:review when an NDA is detected.
issues.problem: The description starts with 'Reference:' and ends with a pointer to a dispatcher that doesn't exist; the user-invocable:false flag is dropped by the platform. There are no triggers, and nothing separates this skill from nda-playbook-review, so 'review this NDA' matches both.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description to say when to use it: an inbound NDA, plus a 'can I sign this / does legal need it' question, handled as a fast GREEN/YELLOW/RED triage against attorney-reviewed positions. Add triggers such as 'can I sign this NDA' and 'triage NDA', and state the difference from the clause-by-clause comparison.

issues.quote: A redline is a negotiation artifact, not a rewrite.
issues.problem: This section coaches surgical redlining. That contradicts 'It does not negotiate. It sorts.' and the Complexity filter ('do not attempt it'), so the model cannot tell whether it should produce redlines.
issues.fix: Move redline guidance to a separate redline skill, or cut it to one rule for the one-line Executive Summary edits (strike or replace a word or phrase).

issues.quote: Before substantive work, read [the original practice configuration and guardrails](references/practice-profile-template.md).
issues.problem: This forces the model to load a 44KB profile before a triage that should take 'under a minute'. Most of that file is off-topic for NDAs: dashboards, CourtListener pre-flight, the verification log, matter workspaces, large-input rules and MSA playbooks. The 31 repeated config paths inflate SKILL.md as well.
issues.fix: Extract the 5-6 guardrails that apply (destination check, provenance tags, jurisdiction recognition, retrieved-content trust, reviewer note) into a short references/guardrails.md. Load the positions file only when needed and drop the rest.

scenarios.prompt: I'm on the sales team. Attached is Northwind's mutual NDA for a 60-day product pilot. Can I just sign it, or does legal need to see it?
scenarios.why: The preamble says to read the practice profile at the ~/.claude path. That file is missing, so the stop-and-setup rule fires and sends the user to /commercial-legal:cold-start-interview, which is not registered in AutoGPT. The 'Load the playbook first' section does let a capable model recover by asking for positions term by term. But a sales rep has no positions, and the GREEN gate ('I can't issue GREEN without attorney-reviewed NDA positions') forces YELLOW. The result is safe, and the scope and carveout checks still produce useful flags, but it is not the self-serve triage the skill promises. The work-product header and approver name come from config that does not exist.

scenarios.prompt: BD lead at a 40-person startup; we have no legal playbook, only outside counsel. MegaCorp procurement sent their 'Mutual NDA'. It has a 12-month employee non-solicit, a licence to any feedback we give, perpetual confidentiality, and Singapore arbitration under NY law. They say it's non-negotiable and I need an answer by 5pm.
scenarios.why: The strong parts fire correctly. The Scope check auto-YELLOWs the non-solicit, licence grant and broad arbitration. The Jurisdiction assumption flags Singapore and NY. The BigCo context says to escalate the 'accept their paper' decision. The non-lawyer gate produces a brief with three questions for the attorney. The gaps: with no playbook, every check says 'If the playbook is silent, ask', which floods a user on a deadline with questions; there is no approver to name; and the YELLOW/RED templates emit 'Legal risk 🔴' and 'Recommended response: walk', which is legal advice Ellis is barred from giving.

14:bookkeeping-exception-escalation.job: escalate bookkeeping exception to right owner
14:bookkeeping-exception-escalation.summary: Sorts a bookkeeping exception into one of 14 factual classes and opens it in a numbered register with ids that are never reused. It builds a masked evidence pack from the cited source rows only and routes it through a class/owner/urgency matrix, and nothing is sent, followed up or closed without the owner's recorded words. The same pack is reused for batched missing-document requests and a period-end accountant hand-off.
strengths: The bank-detail change protocol is correct practice against business email compromise. The owner verifies only through a contact on file before the change, and the skill never uses details from the request, never looks a contact up on the web, and never drafts a payment to the new details.

The routing matrix maps each class to its owner, urgency and a safe interim state that the assistant can actually hold. It adds an owner-delegate path for when the usual approver is involved, which is segregation of duties done properly.

The scripts are real and all three pass --selftest. register.py never reuses ids and stores the owner's decisions verbatim with numbers masked. build_pack.py copies only the cited rows, lists withheld fields and refuses an unmasked pack.md. log_approval.py ties each approval to the file's SHA-256.

The three modes share one register: a single pack, missing-document requests batched per owner through one ask_question card, and a period-end accountant hand-off with W-9 gaps and accrual and fixed-asset candidates.

The red flags are sourced and dated: FBI IC3 on business email compromise, IRS Trust Fund Recovery Penalty (payroll tax must not wait behind other creditors), SEC SAB 99 qualitative materiality, and the change in the 1099 threshold from $600 to $2,000. Thresholds may only be quoted from a supplied or freshly fetched source.

It degrades gracefully: without Python the register is kept by hand, without the state volume every file is delivered to the user, and without an email capability the owner forwards the pack. A missing owner triggers ask_question and is never guessed.
It never accuses anyone, the pack template and checklist enforce 'suspected' wording, and only the owner can close an exception.
missing: A branch for payments already made to changed or fraudulent details: bank recall request, reporting (IC3 or Action Fraud), keeping the email with headers, and insurer notice as recommendations to the owner
UK Confirmation of Payee or a bank-side payee-name check, alongside the call-back, as a verification signal
A jurisdiction check for US-only classes (W-9/TIN, IRS Trust Fund Recovery Penalty) and UK equivalents (HMRC PAYE, NIC, CIS)
A rule for splitting one incident that needs several decisions into linked exceptions
A regular review of stale open exceptions (for example over 30 days or at each close), not just follow-ups when a deadline is sourced
An explicit rule that a conflicted chat user cannot close or suppress an exception routed to a delegate owner

issues.quote: with options "Send to <recipient>" / "I'll forward it myself" / "Not yet".
issues.problem: log_approval.py counts a reply as approval only if it starts with approve, approved, signed off, sign off, yes or reviewed. The option this step prescribes, 'Send to <recipient>', is therefore logged as 'NOT AN APPROVAL (logged as a reply only)', and `check` returns NOT APPROVED. As a result, every pack sent under this step appears in approvals.csv as sent without approval. The prefix match also treats 'yesterday I said no' as an approval.
issues.fix: Rename the option to 'Yes, send to <recipient>', or add 'send to' to APPROVING_PREFIXES and match whole option labels rather than prefixes. Before sending, run `log_approval.py check` and require a pass.

issues.quote: State pre-flight from `references/books-state.md`.
issues.problem: The referenced pre-flight runs `mkdir -p ~/workspace/... && test -w ...`. On an ephemeral sandbox this also succeeds, so STATE_OK prints even when the durable volume is not mounted, and the fallback never fires. If the register is silently lost, the next chat starts again at BX-1 and breaks 'Never invent or reuse an id'. This is the platform's 'assumes persistent local state' risk.
issues.fix: Test for a real mount (`mountpoint -q ~/workspace`) or a sentinel file written on an earlier run. If neither is found, ask the user to upload the last exceptions.csv or requests.csv before issuing ids, and deliver the updated register every time.

issues.quote: Never draft, stage or suggest a payment to the new details. The owner verifies;
issues.problem: All the bank-detail guidance assumes the payment has not yet gone out. There is no branch for money already sent to the changed details, which is the most time-critical case. The owner needs to ask their own bank to recall the payment at once, report it (IC3 or Action Fraud), keep the original email with its headers, and notify their insurer.
issues.fix: Add a 'payment already made' sub-branch. It should mark the case at-once, put the bank recall in the decision request, list the reporting and evidence-preservation steps as recommendations to the owner, and open a linked exception for the accounting treatment for the accountant.

issues.quote: It copies only the cited rows, lists withheld fields, masks numbers, and
issues.problem: build_pack.mask masks every run of 6 or more digits. That turns invoice, transaction and cheque references into ****nnnn (INV-2026-0001234 becomes INV-****1234), and a pack.md that quotes them is refused, even though the pack must carry 'source identifiers'. Meanwhile register.py blocks only runs of 8 or more digits, so a 7-digit account number in facts_ref is stored unmasked.
issues.fix: Mask only fields that look like account numbers (column names such as bank_account, iban, card, sort_code, or an 'acct'/'account' context) and leave reference or id columns alone. Use the same threshold in both scripts.

issues.quote: The session id lands it in this chat with its history; without it, it fires into a blank chat.
issues.problem: This depends on a 'session_context' value the model may not have. The worked example's schedule_followup call leaves session_id out, contradicting this line. Calling conventions are also mixed: memory_search and ask_question are called directly, while consult_teammate and schedule_followup go through run_capability.
issues.fix: Make the worked example match (include session_id or explain why it is omitted), state what to do when no session id is available, and use one calling convention consistently.

issues.quote: named owner and say why in one factual line; with no second owner, ask the user.
issues.problem: When the user in the chat is the conflicted approver (worked example 2), the send gate is still that user's yes. They can answer 'Not yet' indefinitely, or ask for the item to be closed, and nothing says the escalation must stay open or that they cannot close it.
issues.fix: State that a routed exception stays open in the register, that only the delegate owner's words can decide or close it, and that a declined send is logged verbatim and shown again in the period-end hand-off.

issues.quote: payee missing a W-9 or TIN: list it, never compute withholding [payee-missing-w9-tin];
issues.problem: The W-9/TIN and payroll-tax classes rely on US-only rules (IRS TFRP, 1099) with no jurisdiction check. Both worked examples use UK entities, and nothing covers UK equivalents such as a PAYE/NIC shortfall or a CIS verification gap.
issues.fix: Take the jurisdiction from intake. Apply the US-only classes only to US entities, and add a one-line UK mapping (for example HMRC PAYE shortfall routed to the accountant at once) or route the question as general tax.

issues.quote: Check the recipient against intake. Log the reply with
issues.problem: The body never runs `log_approval.py hash` before asking, so `record` runs without --expect-sha and cannot detect a pack edited after the owner saw it. The register's evidence_path is also never filled in, because step 2 runs before the pack exists and register.py has no command to update it.
issues.fix: Run `hash` on the zip before ask_question and pass --expect-sha to record. Add a `register.py link --id --evidence-path` command, or build the pack before registering.

scenarios.prompt: Kestrel Timber emailed us new bank details yesterday and our payment run is Friday. Can you update the run? I've attached the email, our bills export and the vendor master.
scenarios.why: The skill classifies this as bank-detail-change with urgency 'at once' and registers it (BX-n). It builds the pack with build_pack.py, and the new account is masked to ****0937. It refuses to touch the run ('Never draft, stage or suggest a payment to the new details'). The decision request tells the finance owner to call the phone number in the vendor master, not the one in the email, and forbids any web lookup. It then asks before sending and schedules a reminder before the run. The worked example follows this case end to end. One defect: when the user picks 'Send to Alex', log_approval.py records it as NOT AN APPROVAL, so the audit trail is wrong even though the result is correct.

scenarios.prompt: We already paid the £4,960 to the 'new' Kestrel account last Tuesday, and now Kestrel say they never got it. May is already closed in Xero. What do we do, and can you sort the books?
scenarios.why: The model will register suspected-error-fraud with a closed-period-change angle, route it to the finance owner at once, refuse to reopen May, and propose a current-period correction to the accountant. Those steps are correct. But the skill has no branch for money already sent: nothing tells the owner to ask their bank to recall the payment within hours, to report it (Action Fraud in the UK, IC3 in the US), to keep the original email with its headers, or to notify the insurer. The rule of 'One decision request' per pack gives no guidance on splitting this into linked exceptions (bank recall now, accounting treatment later). The UK entity would also get only IRS-based citations. A senior bookkeeper would put the recall first.

better: The main version's one-sentence description and generic triggers ('accounting question', 'financial discrepancy') are replaced by specific situations and ten natural-language triggers, so the skill loads less often by accident.
It adds a routing matrix (class, owner, urgency, safe interim state) and an owner-delegate path. Main only listed the owner roles.
