It adds six classes that match real practice: payroll-tax shortfall, worker classification, receipt with no payment line or possibly generated, payee missing W-9/TIN, closed-period change, and unusual payment separated from bank-detail change.
It adds qualitative materiality triggers: an item that flips loss to profit or back, touches a loan covenant or owner pay, may involve illegality, or involves a related party.

The pack is now reproducible: a register with ids that are never reused, a masked pack builder that copies only cited rows and lists withheld fields, and SHA-256 approval logging, all with passing selftests.
It adds a bank-detail change protocol (call-back only to a contact on file before the change, no web lookup, no payment to the new details), which main lacked.
It adds two new modes with templates: batched missing-document requests and an accountant hand-off pack.
Delivery is explicitly a draft, sending needs a yes naming the recipient, and it explains the limits of workspace:// links and chat posts; main said only 'never contact'.
Sourced, dated red flags replace unsourced assertions, and main's action 'restrict access', which the assistant cannot perform, becomes 'recommend that the owner restricts access'.
worse: The body grows from 53 to 182 lines and the description from one sentence to about 700 characters. More of it is exact call syntax that can drift.
It now depends on shared kit state (intake.json, open-items.csv, ~/workspace durability) with a pre-flight that cannot detect an ephemeral volume. Main had no such dependency.
It adds US-specific rules (TFRP, W-9/1099) without a jurisdiction check, whereas main was jurisdiction-neutral.

The new scripts bring new defects: the prescribed 'Send to <recipient>' reply is logged as not an approval, masking over-reaches onto invoice and transaction references, and the two scripts use different digit thresholds.

monthly-profit-and-loss-summary.job: draft monthly P&L summary with variance commentary
monthly-profit-and-loss-summary.summary: A 53-line, text-only procedure that fixes the scope of a supplied P&L export, checks that the detail sums to the totals, lays out standard P&L lines against a prior period and writes a 3-5 point brief with open items, with strong limits on accounting and tax advice.
strengths: Starts with scope controls: entity, period, currency, basis, gross vs net of tax, intercompany, export date, and detail tied to report totals before any analysis.
Requires causes to be labelled as hypotheses unless records prove them, and warns against percentages on a zero or near-zero base. Both prevent invented narratives and false precision.
Requires an explicit include/exclude statement for each material open item and never calls an unreviewed draft final.
Keeps cash movement apart from profit and bars forecasting solvency or giving tax, financing or investment advice, which matches Mina's boundaries.
Concise, with no filler; the standard P&L line structure is correct.
missing: A fallback for bank-only or cash-basis data when no chart of accounts or P&L export exists
A materiality threshold for variance commentary, and normalisation of one-off vs recurring items
A cutoff check for missing recurring bills or revenue (accrual gaps)
Reconciliation or close status stated on the summary
Same-month-last-year, YTD and budget comparison columns
A reusable output template and a worked example
Intake route (workspace, Google Sheets, CSV) and sandbox computation of all figures
Gross margin % and operating margin % called out explicitly
An approval gate before sharing with third parties, and a named escalation path

issues.quote: Show, from the supplied chart of accounts:
issues.problem: Assumes a mapped chart of accounts or a ready-made P&L report. Mina's small-business users often have only bank, card or Stripe exports, and there is no decision point for that case.
issues.fix: Add a branch. If there is no mapped P&L or GL, either run expense-categorization first or produce a view explicitly labelled 'cash-basis approximation, not a P&L', with uncategorised items listed. Never present bank movement as profit.

issues.quote: Explain the largest movements with linked source items.
issues.problem: 'Largest' is undefined: there is no materiality threshold and no split between one-off and recurring items. There is also no cutoff check for missing recurring bills or revenue (a month with no rent bill looks falsely profitable).
issues.fix: Set a default threshold (e.g. change greater than 10% and greater than a stated amount, or the top 5 by absolute change) that the user can override. Add a step comparing expected recurring vendors and customers to the prior period and flag any that are missing as possible cutoff gaps.

issues.quote: Check that the detail sums to the report totals. List unmapped accounts,
issues.problem: Only checks internal tie-out. It never asks whether this period's bank and card statements are reconciled, so a P&L built from unreconciled books goes out without that caveat.
issues.fix: Require a reconciliation-status line, fed by statement-reconciliation or month-end-close-checklist. If the reconciliation is incomplete, label the summary 'prepared from unreconciled records'.

issues.problem: No intake or tool guidance: nothing on read_workspace_file, the Google Sheets block, or asking for a CSV export when QuickBooks or Xero isn't connectable. Variances are not computed in bash_exec, which raises the risk of arithmetic errors in a finance deliverable.
issues.fix: Name the intake order (workspace file, then Sheets block, then pasted or exported CSV) and require all totals, changes and percentages to be computed in bash_exec, with each figure labelled sourced or derived.

issues.quote: export date, and comparison period.
issues.problem: Allows only one comparison period. A senior monthly pack also shows the same month last year (seasonality), year-to-date, and budget or plan when supplied.
issues.fix: Default to prior month plus the same month prior year where data exists. Add YTD and budget columns when supplied, and state which comparisons were unavailable.

issues.quote: Lead with three to five supported points: what changed, the amount, the period,
issues.problem: The deliverable is described in prose, with no template or example, so the layout will vary from run to run and owners can't reuse it month to month.
issues.fix: Ship templates/pnl-summary.md with a header block (entity, period, basis, currency, source, coverage, reconciliation status, draft status), the line table, a drivers section, open items with owners, and the include/exclude statement. Add one worked example.

issues.quote: investment. Route material misstatements, unusual entries, tax matters, fraud,
issues.problem: Routes to 'the accountant or finance owner' with no mechanism: no link to bookkeeping-exception-escalation and no consult_teammate path for forecast or plan-variance questions. There is also no approval step before the summary is shared with lenders or investors.
issues.fix: Route escalations through bookkeeping-exception-escalation. Say to consult a finance teammate for forecasting. Require owner approval before the draft is shared outside the business.

scenarios.prompt: Attached are our Xero P&L exports for August and July 2026 plus the GL detail. Draft the August P&L summary for me and our accountant and explain the big swings.
scenarios.why: 'Fix the scope' pins down period, basis, currency and gross vs net, and checks that the detail sums to the totals. 'Build the summary' gives current, prior, change, % and share of revenue, and causes are labelled as hypotheses. 'Write the brief' leads with sourced points and open items. Two gaps weaken it: 'big' is undefined (no materiality threshold) and there is no same-month-last-year or YTD view.

scenarios.prompt: We don't use accounting software. Here are September's bank CSV and our Stripe payout report. Give me a September P&L vs August and tell me why profit fell.
scenarios.why: 'Build the summary' assumes 'the supplied chart of accounts'. Nothing covers cash-only inputs: no step to categorise first via expense-categorization, and no instruction to produce a clearly labelled cash-basis view. 'Keep cash movement apart from profit' forbids the conflation but offers no alternative. Stripe payouts are net of fees and refunds; the gross-vs-net check flags this but doesn't say how to gross them up. The model will likely either stall or produce a mislabelled cash statement.

statement-reconciliation.summary: A 54-line, text-only procedure that records balances and controls for one account and period, matches statement to ledger in five ordered passes, and reports matched, timing, one-sided, duplicate and unexplained items with owners, without ever editing transactions.
strengths: Tiered matching passes, ordered exact, then timing window, then batch, then special items, then leave-uncertain-unmatched, which is how an experienced bookkeeper works.
Explicitly bans matching on amount alone when duplicates exist, and allows batch matches only with exact sums plus a shared reference.
Requires a row identifier for both sides of every match, so the result is auditable.
Separates pending from posted and confirms the sign convention up front, two common card and bank pitfalls.
Strong fraud and control escalation: changed bank details, duplicate payments, unknown withdrawals. No create, edit or merge of transactions; adjusting entries are drafts for the accountant.
Refuses to force agreement: every open item gets an owner and a next step.
missing: Prior-period outstanding items carried forward, and the opening balance tied to the last reconciled close
Standard two-sided adjusted statement/ledger reconciliation layout as a template
Classification of reconciling items (timing vs adjustment needed vs error) with aging and stale thresholds
Deterministic matching script in the sandbox, plus a match-table CSV deliverable
Intake fallbacks for PDF statements and for bank or accounting integrations that aren't connectable
Card statement cycle vs month-end cutoff handling
FX difference and inter-account transfer rules
Materiality threshold for 'large' differences, and preparer/reviewer sign-off
Explicit handoff to bookkeeping-exception-escalation

issues.quote: Use the equation that fits the account and show it in the report.
issues.problem: Neither the reconciliation equation nor 'unexplained difference' is defined relative to identified reconciling items. Models may report known bank fees or deposits in transit as 'unexplained', or net them inconsistently. Card accounts also invert the signs.
issues.fix: Ship the two-sided format. Adjusted statement = statement closing +/- deposits in transit and outstanding payments. Adjusted ledger = ledger closing +/- unrecorded bank items and errors. Unexplained = adjusted statement minus adjusted ledger. Include a card-account variant and put it in templates/.

issues.problem: Doesn't tie the statement opening balance to the prior reconciled closing balance, doesn't bring forward last period's outstanding items, and doesn't check the statement's own arithmetic (opening + movements = closing).
issues.fix: Add a first step. Load the prior reconciliation's outstanding items and clear them first. Confirm opening = prior reconciled closing. Prove the statement's arithmetic before matching.

issues.problem: No tooling guidance. For hundreds of rows the model will eyeball matches instead of running them deterministically in bash_exec. There is no intake fallback for PDF statements or a missing bank feed, and no match-table artefact.
issues.fix: Tell the model to load both sides via read_workspace_file, Sheets or CSV and run the passes in bash_exec (pandas). Ship scripts/match.py, and write a match-table CSV (statement row ID, ledger row ID, pass, difference) alongside the report.

issues.quote: Match known timing differences within a stated date window.
issues.problem: There is no default window and no aging of reconciling items, so stale outstanding cheques and payments never surface.
issues.fix: Give defaults (e.g. card and ACH 1-5 business days, cheques until cleared) and age every reconciling item. Flag anything past a stated threshold, such as 60 or 90 days, as stale.

issues.quote: Review fees, interest, refunds, reversals, transfers, and foreign-currency
issues.problem: 'Review separately' gives no rule. FX settlements need matching on the settled home-currency amount, with the rate difference shown as its own item. Inter-account transfers need both legs confirmed.
issues.fix: Add one rule per type: FX differences become a separate reconciling item for accountant review, and transfers must match the counter-account's entry.

issues.quote: Record the entity, account, currency, statement period, statement opening and
issues.problem: Doesn't handle statement cycles that don't line up with the ledger period (card statements often close mid-month), which is a frequent source of false differences.
issues.fix: Tell the model to reconcile to the statement closing date, or to use a month-end export or balance, and to state which choice was made.

issues.quote: Escalate unknown withdrawals, changed bank details, duplicate payments, large or repeated differences, and suspected fraud at once.
issues.problem: 'Large' is undefined, and there is no named target or evidence-pack format for the escalation.
issues.fix: Set a materiality threshold with the owner at intake and route escalations through bookkeeping-exception-escalation with the source rows attached.

issues.quote: result has an unexplained difference of zero. If it does not, label it open and
issues.problem: The output has no preparer, reviewer, date or status field. Nothing stops the model from reporting a zero-difference rec as 'reconciled' before the owner signs off.
issues.fix: Add status values (prepared, ready for review, approved by named owner) and a sign-off block to the report.

scenarios.prompt: Reconcile our August business checking statement (CSV) to the QuickBooks bank register export for the same account and tell me what doesn't tie.
scenarios.why: 'Set the controls' captures both opening and closing balances, pending vs posted, and the sign convention. The five passes, with the no-amount-only rule and row IDs on both sides, produce an auditable match. The report lists matched count and value, one-sided items and the unexplained difference, with owners. Presentation will vary because 'Use the equation that fits the account' gives no standard adjusted-balance layout.

scenarios.prompt: Reconcile our Amex statement (PDF, cycle closes Aug 27) to Xero for August. Last month's rec left 3 items open, and several EUR charges are booked in Xero at different USD amounts.
scenarios.why: The skill has no step to bring forward last month's open items or tie the opening balance to the prior reconciled close. It gives no rule for a card cycle that closes mid-month versus a ledger month-end, and no FX treatment beyond 'Review ... foreign-currency settlements separately'. There is no route for parsing a PDF. The model will likely leave the EUR items unmatched and report prior-period items as unexplained differences.

revops-getting-started.job: map CRM setup, owners and change rules
revops-getting-started.summary: A 41-line intake checklist for starting RevOps work. It asks for CRM exports, field definitions, stage and routing rules, report owners and change approvers, then returns a five-item setup brief. There are no supporting files and no tool routing.
strengths: States export metadata (date, object, filter, row count, currency) up front, which suits Omar's voice and makes later work traceable.
Asks which reports go to the board or finance, a good instinct for what matters most.
Sets clear change approvals by type (merge, delete, reassign, field, stage, routing) before any work starts.
Short and plain, with no filler.
missing: A minimum-input set, with a HubSpot block or CSV fallback
A working-rules/RACI record saved with memory_store for sibling skills
A field-profiling step (fill rate, placeholders, overloaded fields) run in bash_exec
Lifecycle stage and hand-off definitions (MQL, SQL, opportunity)
A system and integration map with sync direction
Fiscal calendar, currency settings, and quota/territory structure
Criteria for choosing the first three pieces of work, each routed to a sibling skill
Handling of personal data in exports
A template for the setup brief

issues.quote: Agree who approves a merge, a deletion, a reassignment, a field change, a new
issues.problem: The rules agreed here (approvers per change type, how missing values display, the forecast date field, commit authority, forecast sign-off) are not among the five output items. Nothing saves them, so sibling skills such as sales-forecast-rollup and crm-duplicate-review start without them.
issues.fix: Add output item 6: a working-rules table (change type, approver, forecast date field, commit caller, forecast signer, missing-value display). Save it with memory_store so later skills can read it.

issues.quote: Ask for the CRM in use, the objects that matter (accounts, contacts, leads,
issues.problem: The intake asks for everything at once and names no minimum set. It never mentions the HubSpot block (run_block), connect_integration, or a CSV fallback, and gives no rule for proceeding with partial exports.
issues.fix: Name the minimum (deals export plus stage list plus owner of the CRM) and ask for it with ask_question. Offer a read-only HubSpot pull through run_block or connect_integration, otherwise a CSV. Treat every other item as optional and list what is still missing.

issues.quote: Fields that are empty, undefined, or used in more than one way.
issues.problem: The deliverable needs field analysis, but no step says how to do it. The model may eyeball the columns or guess.
issues.fix: Add a quick-profile step: in bash_exec, compute fill count and % per field, distinct values, and placeholders ('n/a', 'tbc', default dates). Hand the full audit to crm-field-audit.

issues.quote: The first three pieces of work, with reasons.
issues.problem: No criteria for picking or ordering the work, so the priorities could be anything.
issues.fix: Rank by impact on board or finance reports, then records affected, then effort. Name the Omar skill each item routes to (field audit, duplicate review, stage definitions, routing, forecast).

issues.quote: Ask who owns the CRM, who owns each report, and which reports go to the board
issues.problem: No path when there is no owner. The approval rules below cannot be agreed, and the skill gives no escalation.
issues.fix: If there is no CRM owner, make that finding 1. Ask the user to name an interim approver before proposing any change, and record 'owner: none' rather than inferring one.

issues.problem: Contact and lead exports hold personal data, but nothing covers minimising columns, keeping data out of outputs, or retention.
issues.fix: Ask only for the columns needed. Keep the exports in the workspace, show only aggregates or masked examples in the brief, and do not copy personal data into memory.

issues.problem: The scope misses things a senior RevOps lead maps on day one: lifecycle stages (lead to MQL to SQL to opportunity), connected systems and sync direction (marketing automation, CPQ, billing, enrichment), fiscal calendar, currency settings, quota and territory structure, and whether field history is available.
issues.fix: Add a short 'systems and definitions' checklist covering these items, each marked known or unknown.

issues.quote: Set up RevOps work from CRM objects, field definitions, stage rules, reports, and system owners.
issues.problem: The description never says when to load the skill (at the start of an engagement or on a first CRM export). The broad triggers 'sales operations' and 'CRM review' collide with crm-hygiene-report and crm-field-audit.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Use at the start of RevOps work or when a new CRM export arrives and no working rules exist yet...'. Drop 'CRM review' from the triggers.

scenarios.prompt: We run HubSpot. Here are CSV exports of companies, contacts and deals from this morning. Can you get set up as our RevOps person and tell me where to start?
scenarios.why: The model records export metadata ('For each export record the date, object, filter, row count, and currency'), asks about owners and approvers, and returns the five-point brief. Nothing tells it how to find empty or overloaded fields (no profiling step, no bash_exec). The working rules it agrees on (forecast date field, who may call commit) are not in the brief or saved to memory, so sales-forecast-rollup and other sibling skills cannot reuse them. 'The first three pieces of work' has no ranking rule, so the choice is arbitrary.

scenarios.prompt: I'm the first ops hire. We're on Salesforce but I can only get a deals export. Nobody knows who owns the CRM and there are no field definitions. Where do I even begin?
scenarios.why: The skill asks for every object, every definition and every owner, with no minimum scope and no path for one export only. 'Agree who approves a merge...' cannot happen when there is no owner, and nothing says to escalate or name an interim approver. Nothing covers the missing Salesforce block or falls back to a CSV. The model will note undefined fields, which 'Note fields that no one can define' covers. It gets no help turning the gaps into a scoped plan.

sales-forecast-rollup.job: build bottom-up sales forecast from open deals
sales-forecast-rollup.summary: A 40-line procedure that builds a period forecast from a dated open-deals export. It flags data gaps, gives a per-deal table, the stage-weighted figure, the rep-called commit and best case, totals by owner and stage, and the gap between weighted and called. It lists stale or at-risk deals without removing them.
strengths: Keeps the weighted figure and the rep's call separate and explains the gap by naming the deals behind it.
Handles currency with discipline: no conversion without an owner-approved rate, rate date and source.
Data gaps are kept in the count and marked, never filled.
Stale deals stay in the forecast and are marked. Pulling them is the sales lead's call, which is the right boundary.
'Every total must trace back to the deals in the list' is the right standard.
missing: Closed-won or booked-to-date in the period
Quota, gap-to-target and coverage
A source for stage probabilities or historical win-rate calibration
Exclusive per-deal forecast categories with cumulative totals and an 'uncalled' bucket
Movement against the last forecast (pushed, pulled, new, lost) and close-date slip counts
Rep forecast accuracy history
Default thresholds for stale and large deals
Computing in the sandbox, plus a deal-level output file and a forecast note template
Saving each forecast snapshot to memory for next period's comparison

issues.quote: Use this for a quarter or month, from a dated export of open deals.
issues.problem: A period forecast is booked-to-date plus the open forecast. Using open deals alone understates the landing number, and with no quota there is no gap-to-target or coverage.
issues.fix: Ask for closed-won in the period and the quota. Report booked, booked + commit, booked + commit + best case, and booked + weighted, each against quota, with coverage of the remaining gap.

issues.quote: the weighted figure from stage probabilities, with the probabilities stated;
issues.problem: No source is given for the probabilities, so the model may use generic percentages that look authoritative.
issues.fix: Use the CRM's stage-probability field if the export has it. Otherwise ask the user, or derive conversion by stage from closed history with the sample size shown. Label each figure as sourced or assumed.

issues.quote: the rep-called commit and best case, kept separate;
issues.problem: The skill does not say whether the categories are exclusive per deal or cumulative in the totals, which risks double counting. Deals with no rep call have no bucket.
issues.fix: Treat categories as exclusive per deal (commit, best case, pipeline, uncalled, omitted). Report cumulative totals (commit; commit + best case). List uncalled deals as a data gap instead of assigning them a category.

issues.quote: List deals past their close date, deals in one stage well past the median, and
issues.problem: 'Well past', 'large' and 'recent activity' are undefined, and many exports have no last-activity field, so results vary from run to run.
issues.fix: State default thresholds, such as more than 1.5 times the median days in stage, top-decile amount, and no activity in 14 or 30 days. Let the user override them. If there is no activity field, say that check was not run.

issues.quote: Record the export date, period, currency, and deal count.
issues.problem: No rule for scoping deals to the period. An open-pipeline export includes deals closing in later periods, which would inflate the numbers.
issues.fix: Filter by close date within the period. List out-of-period and past-dated deals separately with their counts and values.

issues.quote: Every total must trace back to the deals in the list.
issues.problem: The traceability standard has no mechanism: no bash_exec calculation, no deal-level file, no output template or headline line.
issues.fix: Compute in bash_exec. Write a deal-level CSV or sheet with the category and weight columns, then a short forecast note that opens with the date, deal count and totals, as in Omar's voice sample.

issues.problem: There is no movement view against the last forecast (new, pulled in, pushed, slipped, lost) and no count of close-date pushes, which are the main signals in a weekly forecast call.
issues.fix: If a prior snapshot exists (in the workspace or memory), add a movement waterfall and a list of deals whose close date moved twice or more. Save this snapshot for next time.

issues.problem: No data route or fallback. It never mentions a read-only HubSpot pull, connect_integration, or asking for a CSV when no CRM is connected.
issues.fix: Offer a read-only HubSpot pull through run_block. Otherwise ask for a CSV export, and confirm the period and currency with ask_question.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our HubSpot deals export as of today for Q3. Build the forecast: commit, best case and weighted, by rep.
scenarios.why: The model records export metadata, flags deals with missing amounts or dates, builds the per-deal table, separates weighted from called, totals by owner and stage, and explains the gap, all as the skill specifies. But the skill works only from open deals, so closed-won in the quarter is missing and the 'Q3 forecast' understates where Q3 will land. It also cannot be compared to quota. Nothing says where the stage probabilities come from ('the weighted figure from stage probabilities'), so the model may state invented percentages.

scenarios.prompt: Board call tomorrow. Export attached, mixed USD and EUR, about a third of deals have no forecast category, and the CEO wants to show $2M. Can you get the forecast to $2M?
scenarios.why: The guardrails hold: 'Never adjust a number to reach a target', currencies stay separate until an owner approves a rate, and stale deals stay visible. But the skill gives no bucket for deals with no rep call, no way to present the gap to target (booked + commit versus $2M, and which deals would have to convert), and no quota or coverage view. A senior analyst would decline to inflate the number and still give the CEO a constructive gap-to-target read. This skill only gets as far as the refusal.

release-readiness-checklist.summary: A 36-line pre-release checklist for Casey that lists the changes, records test evidence as tested, partly tested or not tested, and covers rollback, monitoring, on-call and sign-off, with a strong no-evidence-no-pass guardrail.
strengths: Clear, distinct description and triggers within Casey's kit
Flags high-risk change types: migrations, config, dependencies, flags, public API, stored data
Three-state test evidence (tested / partly / not) with a requirement to link the run
Gaps listed first, and accepted known bugs named with who accepted them
Strong boundary: never mark ready without evidence; the release owner makes the call
missing: Go/no-go blocking criteria and recommendation format
Reusable checklist template and worked example
Named inputs (release range, previous tag, CI runs, tracker) with a paste fallback
Expand/contract migration checks, deploy ordering, a tested backup and restore
Staged rollout, canary, feature-flag kill switch, rollback rehearsal
Post-deploy smoke test, rollback thresholds, watch window and owner
Dependency, security and licence scan changes
Release notes, support and comms readiness with a teammate handoff

issues.quote: Who signs off, and the go/no-go call with its reasons.
issues.problem: No decision criteria. Nothing says what blocks a release (an untested high-risk change, an irreversible migration without a tested backup, an open blocker bug, a red required check), so the recommendation rests on unstated judgment.
issues.fix: Add explicit no-go triggers and a recommendation format: Go / Go with conditions (each with an owner) / No-go, with the evidence behind it.

issues.quote: Return the checklist with every gap listed first.
issues.problem: No template, so each run produces a different layout and the team cannot reuse or diff checklists between releases.
issues.fix: Ship templates/release-checklist.md: release ID and range, a change table (PR, owner, risk flags, test status, evidence link), gaps, accepted bugs, a rollback plan per risky change, the watch window, and sign-off.

issues.quote: List every change in the release: pull request, owner, and a one-line
issues.problem: Inputs are not named, and nothing says how to get the change list: the release tag or range, the previous tag, CI runs, the tracker. There is no fallback when there is no repo access.
issues.fix: Ask up front for the release range and previous tag. Pull merged PRs and check runs through the GitHub block, or accept a pasted changelog, and record what could not be read.

issues.quote: Whether a migration can be reversed, and what happens to new data.
issues.problem: Missing current migration practice: expand/contract, the order of code and schema deploys, compatibility while old and new versions run side by side, and a verified backup and restore before destructive DDL.
issues.fix: Add a migration sub-checklist covering expand/contract, deploy order, the mixed-version window, a backup taken and its restore tested, and whether data written after release survives a rollback.

issues.quote: What to watch after the release: metrics, logs, and alerts.
issues.problem: No rollback triggers or watch window. Nothing says which threshold means roll back, for how long to watch, or who is watching.
issues.fix: Require named metrics with baseline, threshold and rollback trigger, a watch window, and an owner, plus a post-deploy smoke test.

issues.problem: No staged rollout, canary, feature-flag kill switch or rollback rehearsal. These are the main ways to reduce release risk today.
issues.fix: Add a line per risky change: is it behind a flag, is it staged or canaried, and has the rollback been rehearsed.

issues.quote: For each change record what was tested, where, and the link to the run or
issues.problem: It does not route to Casey's sibling skills: regression-risk-review for risk, test-plan-draft for gaps, flaky-test-triage for a red check. It also does not say how to read check results.
issues.fix: Reference those skills at the decision points, and read check-run status through the GitHub block when it is connected.

issues.problem: No customer-facing readiness: release notes, support briefing, docs, or a handoff to the release-notes owner.
issues.fix: Add a comms-readiness line and hand release-notes drafting to the teammate who owns release-notes-draft.

scenarios.prompt: We're cutting v2.14 Thursday. Here are the 12 PRs merged since v2.13 and the CI links. Build the go/no-go checklist.
scenarios.why: The model would list each PR with owner and summary, flag migrations and config changes, and mark test status. With no template, though, the layout depends on the model, and with no blocking criteria the go/no-go call in 'Rollback and sign-off' is unstructured.

scenarios.prompt: Release tonight includes a migration that drops a column. One required CI job is red and probably flaky, I can't give you CI access (pasted summary only), and the PM wants a go.
scenarios.why: 'Whether a migration can be reversed' raises the right question, but nothing covers expand/contract, backups or a restore test. Nothing says how to treat a red flaky check or to route it to flaky-test-triage, and nothing says pasted-only evidence must be labelled. The model keeps the no-pass-without-evidence rule but has to improvise the recommendation.

test-plan-draft.job: draft a test plan for a change
test-plan-draft.summary: A 39-line risk-based test plan for one change: list the failure modes with who they hurt and how they would be noticed, write cases in risk order (setup and data, steps, expected result, level, existing coverage), and list uncovered gaps with an owner who accepts each.
strengths: Risk-first framing: who it hurts and how it would be noticed
Concrete failure classes seniors check (time zones, retries, old data, concurrency, permissions)
Per-case fields include test level and whether an existing test covers it
Prefers a few high-signal cases over happy-path repetition
Coverage gaps named with a reason and an owner who accepts each
Guardrail against marking cases passed without seeing them run
missing: Named inputs and a paste fallback
A test-plan template and a filled example
Risk scoring (likelihood x impact)
Test-design techniques (boundaries, equivalence, state, pairwise)
Non-functional coverage (performance, security, accessibility)
Feature-flag states and migration or backward-compatibility cases
Exit criteria linked to release readiness
A strategy-level mode for new services (levels, environments, contract tests)

issues.problem: Inputs are not named: the diff or PR, the requirement or acceptance criteria, existing tests, environments, release date. There is no step to read existing tests (GitHub block) and no fallback to a pasted diff.
issues.fix: Open with an inputs step that asks for the minimum set, and say what to do when only a description is available.

issues.quote: Write the cases in risk order. For each give:
issues.problem: No template or grouping, so the output is a free-form list that is hard to turn into tickets or track.
issues.fix: Ship templates/test-plan.md: a summary, a risk table, a case table (ID, risk, level, data, steps, expected, existing coverage, priority), gaps, and exit criteria.

issues.quote: From the change and the code around it, list the ways it can fail: wrong
issues.problem: 'Risk order' is undefined. There is no likelihood-by-impact scoring and no test-design technique (boundary values, equivalence classes, state transitions, pairwise) for choosing cases.
issues.fix: Add a short scoring rule and a references/test-design-techniques.md with when to use each technique.

issues.quote: output, bad input, empty or large data, permissions, concurrency, time zones,
issues.problem: No non-functional or deployment risks: performance, security or authz abuse, accessibility, feature-flag on and off states, migration and backward compatibility, and rollback.
issues.fix: Extend the failure-class list, or add an optional non-functional checklist.

issues.quote: List what the plan does not cover and why: no test data, no environment, cost,
issues.problem: No exit criteria, so the plan never says what must pass before merge or release, and it does not feed release-readiness-checklist.
issues.fix: Add an exit-criteria section and point to release-readiness-checklist.

issues.quote: "QA plan", "test strategy"
issues.problem: The 'test strategy' trigger collides with software-test-planning, and this skill cannot handle system-level strategy.
issues.fix: After the merge, keep one test-planning skill with a change mode and a strategy mode, or drop the 'test strategy' trigger here.

issues.quote: setup and test data;
issues.problem: No guidance on test data privacy or on synthetic versus production data.
issues.fix: Add: use synthetic or anonymised data, never copy production PII into fixtures, and state where the data comes from.

scenarios.prompt: PR #482 adds coupon codes to checkout. What should we test before merge?
scenarios.why: The failure-mode list (bad input, empty or large data, permissions, concurrency, time zones, old data) maps well onto coupons: expiry time zones, double redemption and stacking. The per-case fields plus the coverage-gaps section give a senior-looking plan. The layout will vary without a template.

scenarios.prompt: Give me a test strategy for our new payments service. There's only a design doc, no code yet, and we have no staging environment.
scenarios.why: The skill is scoped to 'a change' and 'the code around it', so it offers nothing on levels across a whole system, contract tests with the payment provider, or environments. The gaps section does record 'no environment', but without strategy-level guidance the model improvises the part that matters most.

code-review-quality.job: review a pull request for bugs and risk
code-review-quality.summary: A 541-line human-oriented code-review etiquette guide (wshobson code-review-excellence): review goals, time-boxed review phases, generic security, performance and testing checklists, Python and TS pitfalls, severity labels, feedback phrasing and a PR comment template ending in an Approve verdict.
strengths: Clear severity labels (blocking / important / nit / suggestion / praise)
Reasonable security and performance checklists
Good advice on separating linter concerns from human review
Constructive guidance on handling author disagreement and escalation
A PR review comment template with Required Changes, Suggestions and Questions
missing: Finding fields: file:line, triggering input, confidence, read-versus-run
A boundary against approving, merging or pushing
Reading the code around the diff (callers and callees)
Fetching the diff and CI status through the GitHub block, with a paste fallback
A strategy for large or truncated diffs
A standards-document template, if kept for team standards

issues.quote: If it's working and not a critical issue, approve it.
issues.problem: Tells the model to approve PRs. Casey reviews and drafts; the reviewer of record approves and merges.
issues.fix: Remove it, or change it to 'recommend approval to the reviewer of record'.

issues.quote: Make clear decision:
issues.problem: Frames the output as an approve or request-changes decision rather than a recommendation, and conflicts with the persona boundary and the approval flow.
issues.fix: Output a recommendation with blockers listed; the human submits the review.

issues.problem: No evidence discipline. Findings are not required to cite file:line, the triggering input or state, confidence, or read-versus-run, so the checklists invite generic 'consider X' comments.
issues.fix: Adopt pull-request-review's finding fields. Better still, drop this skill and keep pull-request-review.

issues.quote: Master effective code review practices to provide constructive feedback, catch bugs early, and foster knowledge sharing while maintaining team morale.
issues.problem: The generic description collides with pull-request-review for every 'review this PR' request and gives no clear reason to load this one.
issues.fix: If kept, retarget it to 'set team code-review standards and severity conventions'. Otherwise drop it.

issues.quote: Instead of stating problems, ask questions to encourage thinking:
issues.problem: For an AI reviewer, turning a known defect into a Socratic question hides the finding. Casey's voice samples state the defect concretely, then mark real unknowns as questions.
issues.fix: State known defects directly, and use questions only for genuine uncertainty.

issues.quote: Check PR size (>400 lines? Ask to split)
issues.problem: It gives no way to get the diff (GitHub block), and does not ask the model to read callers beyond the diff. It also does not handle truncated diffs or a CI status it cannot see.
issues.fix: Add steps to fetch the diff and CI status through the GitHub block, read callers and callees, and list what could not be read.

issues.quote: Check for Python-specific issues
issues.problem: About 90 lines of language pitfall snippets inline, and only for Python and TS. They add bulk without progressive disclosure.
issues.fix: Move them to references/language-pitfalls.md or remove them.

issues.quote: 60 minutes max, take breaks
issues.problem: Human-reviewer ergonomics (time blocks, 24-hour turnaround, emoji rapport) are irrelevant to an agent and are filler.
issues.fix: Cut the human-only practices.

scenarios.prompt: Review this PR that adds a new /orders endpoint: github.com/acme/api/pull/231
scenarios.why: Phases 1-4 and the checklists would surface generic concerns, but nothing requires file:line, the triggering input, confidence, or whether a finding comes from reading or running the code. Phase 4 and the template end in an Approve or Request Changes decision that Casey must not make.

scenarios.prompt: Our 5-person team keeps fighting in reviews. Draft review standards and a severity scheme, and also review this 1,800-line PR we need merged today.
scenarios.why: The severity labels, pitfalls and disagreement steps give material for standards, but there is no procedure or template for a standards document. For the large PR the only guidance is 'Ask to split'. There is nothing on reviewing in slices, prioritising risky files, or saying what was not read.

software-incident-response.job: run incident response and draft postmortem
software-incident-response.summary: Anthropic's incident-response command, packaged as a skill: slash-command modes (new, update, postmortem), a four-phase ASCII diagram, a generic SEV1-4 table, status-update and postmortem templates, and connector actions (page on-call, post to chat) behind ~~placeholders.
strengths: A reusable status-update template with status states and next-update content
A full postmortem template with impact, timeline, what went well or poorly, and owned action items
Sound tips: start writing immediately, factual updates, blameless framing
Covers the lifecycle from triage to postmortem in one place
missing: Approval gates for paging, posting and ticket creation
A mapping to AutoGPT blocks and MCP tools, with a paste fallback
Numbered triage steps with a mitigate or roll back decision
Incident commander, comms and scribe responsibilities, and update cadence by severity
Contributing-factor analysis with per-entry evidence and gap marking
Detection, mitigation and resolution time metrics
Security or PII escalation to legal, and a handoff to the comms teammate
Action items categorised as detect, mitigate or prevent

issues.quote: Page on-call responders
issues.problem: Outward side effects (paging, creating PagerDuty incidents, posting to incident channels, creating war rooms) have no draft-and-approve step. This breaks the platform approval model and Casey's draft-only boundary.
issues.fix: Draft every page, post and incident record, and send each through the approval flow. Name who authorises paging.

issues.quote: /incident-response $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command with $ARGUMENTS, plus slash-style modes. AutoGPT has neither, and argument-hint is dropped.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain-language modes chosen from the user's message, and ask_question when the phase is unclear.

issues.quote: If **~~monitoring** is connected:
issues.problem: The ~~placeholders are not mapped to AutoGPT tools. Slack is a block; PagerDuty and Datadog have no block. There is no fallback to pasted alerts, logs or graphs, and CONNECTORS.md points to an upstream MCP config.
issues.fix: Map chat to the Slack block and trackers to Linear or GitHub. Use run_mcp_tool or connect_integration where available, and otherwise ask for pasted exports.

issues.quote: Assess severity (SEV1-4)
issues.problem: The procedure is a box diagram with no ordered steps or decision points: no mitigate-first rule (roll back the suspect deploy), no incident-commander handoff, and no cadence rule.
issues.fix: Write numbered triage steps: impact, severity, owner, mitigate or roll back, first update with next-update time, and when to escalate.

issues.quote: Why did [cause 4]? → [Root cause]
issues.problem: A fixed 5-whys chain forces a single linear root cause. Current practice separates the trigger from contributing factors, and this template invites invented links when evidence is thin.
issues.fix: Replace it with trigger, contributing factors and evidence per factor with confidence, and mark 'unproven' where the evidence is missing. Merge into incident-postmortem-draft.

issues.quote: Service down, all users affected
issues.problem: Generic SEV criteria are presented as fixed. They have no data-loss, security or privacy triggers, and the response times may not match the organisation.
issues.fix: Ask for the organisation's severity matrix, and fall back to this one labelled as a default. Add data-loss and security criteria.

issues.quote: Draft customer communication (if needed)
issues.problem: No handoff to the comms owner (holding-statement-draft) and no escalation to legal for breach or regulatory notification.
issues.fix: Route external statements to the comms teammate for approval, and flag security or PII incidents for legal review.

issues.quote: Generate postmortem from incident data
issues.problem: It duplicates Casey's incident-postmortem-draft, which has stronger evidence rules, so the two will compete on postmortem requests.
issues.fix: Remove the postmortem mode here and point to incident-postmortem-draft, or merge the templates into it.

scenarios.prompt: Checkout is returning 500s for about 30% of users since the 14:05 deploy. Help me triage and draft the first internal update.
scenarios.why: The SEV table would give SEV2 and the status-update template produces a clean draft. Nothing tells the model to consider rolling back the 14:05 deploy first, to assign or confirm an incident commander, or to set an update cadence by severity. The ~~chat section would post to Slack without asking for approval first.

scenarios.prompt: Write the postmortem for last Tuesday's outage. Here's a Slack export with gaps and timestamps in two time zones; the logs have rotated out.
scenarios.why: The template's 'Time (UTC)' column helps with normalisation. But the template has five fixed why-slots ending in a single [Root cause], and there is no instruction to cite a source per timeline entry or mark gaps, so it pushes the model to invent causal links that Casey's persona forbids. incident-postmortem-draft handles this case better.

software-test-planning.job: draft a test plan for a change
software-test-planning.summary: A 45-line testing-strategy note: an ASCII test pyramid, one-line strategies per component type, what to cover or skip, and a one-sentence output spec for a test plan.
strengths: Concise strategy hints per component type (API contract tests, pipeline idempotency, frontend accessibility and visual regression)
A sensible 'skip trivial getters, framework code' note
missing: Ordered procedure and named inputs
Risk ranking
Case template with data and expected results
Guardrails on evidence and suite changes
Exit criteria
A path for legacy or characterization testing, if 'write tests for' is kept

issues.problem: No procedure or inputs. There are no steps for gathering the change, requirements or existing tests, ranking risk, or choosing levels.
issues.fix: Drop it in favour of test-plan-draft, or add ordered steps.

issues.quote: "write tests for", "test plan", "what tests do we need"
issues.problem: Collides with test-plan-draft on 'test plan' and pulls in test-writing requests the skill cannot serve.
issues.fix: Remove this skill, or narrow it to system-level 'test strategy' only.

issues.quote: Produce a test plan with: what to test, test type for each area, coverage targets, and example test cases.
issues.problem: The output has no template, and 'coverage targets' invites invented percentage goals with no basis.
issues.fix: Use test-plan-draft's case fields and template, and state targets only when the team supplies them.

issues.problem: No guardrails: nothing against claiming coverage or passing tests without evidence, changing the suite, or inventing existing coverage.
issues.fix: Adopt Casey's evidence and no-modification boundaries.

issues.quote: Focus on: business-critical paths, error handling, edge cases, security boundaries, data integrity.
issues.problem: A generic list with no risk-ranking method and no link to the specific change.
issues.fix: Use likelihood x impact per failure mode.

issues.quote: Identify gaps in existing coverage.
issues.problem: No method for finding existing coverage: reading tests or coverage reports through GitHub, or asking for them.
issues.fix: Add a step to read the relevant tests or ask for a coverage report.

issues.quote: Few, slow, high confidence
issues.problem: The pyramid is presented as a universal rule, with no tradeoffs (testing trophy, contract tests, the cost of flaky E2E tests).
issues.fix: Add a sentence on choosing levels by risk and feedback speed.

scenarios.prompt: What tests do we need for the new CSV import endpoint?
scenarios.why: The 'API endpoints' and 'Data pipelines' bullets point at unit, integration, contract and idempotency tests. With no steps, no risk ranking and a one-line output spec, the model produces a generic pyramid-shaped list rather than risk-ranked cases with data and expected results.

scenarios.prompt: Write tests for our legacy billing module. It has zero coverage and we can't use production data.
scenarios.why: 'write tests for' triggers this skill, but it has nothing on writing tests: no characterization tests, synthetic data or seams for legacy code. It also has no guardrail against modifying the suite or claiming coverage.

verification-before-completion.job: verify evidence before claiming work is done
verification-before-completion.summary: obra's discipline skill that requires running a fresh verification command and reading its output before any claim of done, fixed or passing, with a five-step gate, a table mapping claims to evidence, red-green regression checks, and rationalization counters.
strengths: A crisp claim-to-evidence table (tests, build, bug fixed, requirements, delegated work)
A red-green regression check: revert the fix, confirm the test fails, then restore
Treats delegated or agent success reports as claims to verify
Directly reinforces Casey's 'never claim a test passed without evidence' boundary
missing: A trigger phrased around user and QA requests, not self-state
A fallback and 'unverified' status when checks cannot run in the sandbox
CI run logs accepted as evidence, with the commit SHA pinned
A verification record template
Repeat-run guidance for intermittent failures

issues.quote: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs
issues.problem: It triggers on the model's internal state and on commit or PR moments. Casey never commits, and user requests ('confirm the fix', 'is CI really green') do not match it, so in AutoGPT it will under-trigger.
issues.fix: Retarget: 'Use before reporting that a bug is fixed, a test or check passed, or a release item is done — including claims from teammates or CI.'

issues.quote: RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
issues.problem: No fallback when the sandbox cannot run the check (private repo, secrets, databases, services), and a cited CI run is not accepted as evidence.
issues.fix: Allow evidence from a linked CI run or log with commit SHA, fetched through the GitHub block. Otherwise report 'unverified' and list exactly what is needed.

issues.problem: No output format, so evidence is not recorded in a reusable way.
issues.fix: Add a verification record: claim, command or source, commit SHA and environment, output excerpt, exit code, date, and verdict (verified / failed / unverified).

issues.quote: Test original symptom: passes
issues.problem: One passing run is weak proof for intermittent bugs, and there is no repeat-run guidance.
issues.fix: For intermittent symptoms, require N reruns and link to flaky-test-triage.

issues.quote: Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
issues.problem: Assumes delegated work shows up as a VCS diff. On AutoGPT, delegated teammates often return documents or tool results.
issues.fix: Generalise to checking the artefact or tool result the teammate produced.

issues.quote: Tired and wanting work over
issues.problem: Human-psychology framing, repeated across Red Flags, Rationalization Prevention and When To Apply. It adds length without new instruction.
issues.fix: Collapse these into one short list.

scenarios.prompt: Dev says PR #231 fixes the invoice timezone bug. Can you confirm it's actually fixed before we close the ticket?
scenarios.why: If loaded, the gate (identify the command, run it, read it, verify it) and the red-green pattern lead to the right check. However, the description is phrased around the model's own completion claims, so it may not load for this request. If it does load, nothing covers a private repo or missing secrets in the E2B sandbox, and there is no report format for the evidence.

scenarios.prompt: Slack says CI is green on the release branch. Tick the test items on the release checklist as passed.
scenarios.why: 'Trusting agent success reports' rightly blocks accepting the Slack message. But 'RUN: Execute the FULL command' assumes local execution; the skill does not recognise a linked CI run log (read through the GitHub block) as evidence, or give a way to mark items 'unverified' with what is needed.

marketing-copywriting.job: write conversion copy for a web page
marketing-copywriting.summary: Corey Haines' conversion-copywriting guide: gathers page/audience/offer context, applies clarity-first principles, headline and CTA formulas and page-type templates, and returns sectioned page copy with annotations and 2-3 headline/CTA alternatives.
strengths: Clear, practical page-type guidance (homepage, landing, pricing, feature, about) and a strong section framework
Good reusable output spec: copy by section, annotations with rationale, 2-3 alternatives for headlines and CTAs, meta content
copy-frameworks.md adds real depth: the 'Now you can' test, the Human Action Model spine, the Perception Gap by segment, and page templates
Explicitly prefers customer language and specificity, and rejects fabricated testimonials
missing: Proof-gap handling ([PROOF NEEDED] placeholders) and a claims or legal review gate
Explicit draft-and-approve step before any CMS or WordPress publish
Memory/workspace-based context retrieval instead of dotfile paths
Awareness-stage framing (Schwartz) and a message hierarchy before drafting
A voice-of-customer mining step (reviews, tickets, calls) using web_fetch or pasted sources
SEO inputs (target query, intent) for the SEO-content expert
A worked end-to-end example of a finished page output

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups)
issues.problem: Context lookup relies on Claude-Code/repo dotfile paths. On AutoGPT, context lives in memory_store or a workspace file, so the model either looks for a file that doesn't exist or skips stored context and re-asks everything.
issues.fix: Replace with: run memory_search for product, audience, voice and proof; check the workspace for the product-marketing context file written by product-marketing-context; ask only for what is missing.

issues.quote: clearer positioning and copy is associated with +81% conversions, a 38% shorter sales cycle, 28% lower CAC, and 175% more referrals
issues.problem: Unsourced statistics sit in a skill whose own rule forbids fabricated stats, and the model may repeat them to users or put them in client copy (the reference repeats them plus an unsourced SavvyCal 3x claim).
issues.fix: Delete the figures or cite a source, and state that illustrative numbers in the skill must never appear in deliverables.

issues.quote: Fabricated statistics or testimonials erode trust and create legal liability
issues.problem: This is the only guardrail: a principle with no procedure. Nothing covers missing proof, comparative or superlative claims, regulated-industry claims, or publishing, and copy can be pushed to a CMS via the WordPress block.
issues.fix: Add a Proof & claims step. Use only the proof the user supplied and insert [PROOF NEEDED: …] placeholders. Flag comparative, superlative and regulated claims for owner or legal sign-off. Deliver as a draft and never publish without explicit approval.

issues.quote: For email copy, see emails. For popup copy, see popups. For editing existing copy, see copy-editing.
issues.problem: The routing names don't resolve in the catalog. 'emails', 'popups', 'copy-editing' and 'offers', plus 'cro', 'popups' and 'ab-testing' under Related Skills, are upstream names; installed slugs differ or don't exist, so handoffs dead-end.
issues.fix: Remap to installed slugs (lifecycle-email-marketing, marketing-copy-editing, conversion-rate-optimization, product-experiment-design) or to teammates, and remove popups and offers.

issues.quote: Gather this context (ask if not provided):
issues.problem: It lists ~13 questions with no minimum input set and no ordered drafting steps (message hierarchy, then hero, then sections, then self-check, then alternatives). A model may interrogate the user or skip straight to prose.
issues.fix: Name the 4-5 minimum inputs (page type, one primary action, audience, key differentiator, available proof), then add numbered steps with a self-check using the Quick Quality Check and the 'Now you can' test before output.

issues.quote: Use this whenever someone is working on website text that needs to persuade or convert.
issues.problem: The catch-all trigger overlaps marketing-copy-editing, conversion-rate-optimization, Maria's on-page-seo-audit and Maya's channel-draft-shapes. Rewrite requests like 'improve this copy' will load it instead of the editor.
issues.fix: Scope it to net-new or substantially rewritten page copy. Send line edits to marketing-copy-editing and ranking problems to on-page-seo-audit.

issues.quote: Page title (for SEO)
issues.problem: For Maria (whose job is copy that ranks), SEO is an optional afterthought. There are no inputs for target query or search intent and no alignment of title, H1 and first paragraph.
issues.fix: Add optional SEO inputs (target query, intent) and a check that title, H1 and opening answer that intent, or hand off to seo-content-brief or on-page-seo-audit.

issues.quote: See [references/natural-transitions.md](references/natural-transitions.md)
issues.problem: The 274-line phrase list adds little to conversion copy, and it ends with an external GitHub link to a file the package doesn't ship.
issues.fix: Trim it to the 'AI tells to avoid' list, fold that into the Quick Quality Check, and drop the external link.

scenarios.prompt: Write the homepage copy for our shift-scheduling app for restaurants. Here's our feature list, pricing and two customer quotes.
scenarios.why: Before Writing asks for page purpose, audience and proof. The Page Structure Framework, hero formulas and the 'Now you can' test shape the draft, and Output Format gives sectioned copy, annotations and 2-3 headline/CTA options. With the inputs supplied, a capable model produces a senior-grade draft.

scenarios.prompt: Rewrite our pricing page so it converts and ranks for 'restaurant scheduling software'. We have no customer stats yet and legal won't let us name competitors.
scenarios.why: Pricing Page guidance and 'Honest over sensational' help, but no step puts [PROOF NEEDED] placeholders where stats would go and there is no claims or legal review gate. SEO appears only as an optional title and meta description, with no target-query or intent handling. The skill's own unsourced figures (+81% conversions, SavvyCal 3x) invite reuse, and it first looks for a .agents/.claude context file that does not exist on the platform.

product-marketing-context.job: capture shared product marketing context document
product-marketing-context.summary: Interviews the user (or auto-drafts from a repo) to build a 12-section product marketing context document covering product, audience, personas, pains, competitors, differentiation, objections, switching forces, customer language, voice, proof and goals, then saves it at a fixed path with versioning and a changelog for other skills to reuse.
strengths: Comprehensive, well-chosen sections: competitive alternatives by type, the JTBD four forces, a buying-committee persona table, anti-personas, verbatim customer language
Reusable markdown template with an explicit version header and a newest-first changelog, plus sensible bump rules (typo fixes don't bump)
Good interviewing guidance: one section at a time, ask for examples, validate as you go, skip what doesn't apply
A review loop before saving (show the draft, ask what's wrong or missing)
missing: Memory-based persistence and retrieval (memory_store/memory_search)
Website- and document-based auto-draft instead of codebase
FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN (or sourced/assumed) labeling per field
A handoff to positioning/ICP skills or teammates when positioning is unresolved
A staleness review cadence (e.g., quarterly re-read or routine)
A consent and freshness check on testimonials, logos and metrics

issues.quote: You'll study the repo—README, landing pages, marketing copy, package.json, etc.—and draft a V1 of the context document.
issues.problem: The recommended path assumes a code repository. AutoGPT marketing users have a website, decks and a CRM, not a repo, so the default option has no input.
issues.fix: Auto-draft from the live site (web_fetch or browser on the homepage, pricing, about and case-study pages), from uploaded docs via read_workspace_file, from HubSpot or Notion via run_block, and from memory_search.

issues.quote: First, check if `.agents/product-marketing.md` already exists.
issues.problem: The storage model is Claude-Code dotfiles (.agents/.claude). The platform's durable store is memory_store plus workspace files, and the hard-coded paths mean an existing doc saved elsewhere is missed.
issues.fix: Persist key facts with memory_store and the full doc with write_workspace_file under a stated name. Before asking anything, run memory_search and search workspace files for an existing context doc.

issues.quote: Draft all sections based on what you find
issues.problem: No provenance labeling. An auto-draft will fill objections, competitors, metrics and 'verbatim' quotes with inferences that later skills treat as fact.
issues.fix: Label each field SOURCED (with URL or doc), INFERRED or UNKNOWN. Leave Proof Points, Current metrics and Customer Language blank unless supplied, and never synthesize quotes.

issues.quote: Also use when the user mentions 'product context,' 'marketing context,' 'set up context,' 'positioning,' 'who is my target audience,'
issues.problem: 'positioning', 'ICP' and 'target audience' collide with icp-and-positioning (Nadia), positioning-and-messaging (Zara) and messaging-and-tone-matrix (Maya). This skill records context; it doesn't decide positioning.
issues.fix: Restrict triggers to creating or updating the shared context doc, and route positioning and ICP decisions to the dedicated skill or teammate, then record the result here.

issues.quote: Run `/product-marketing` anytime to update it.
issues.problem: This is a slash command under the upstream name; it doesn't exist on AutoGPT.
issues.fix: Replace with 'Ask me to update your product marketing context any time.'

issues.quote: Other marketing skills will now use this context automatically.
issues.problem: This is false on the platform. Only a few Corey-derived skills look for this file; native Maria, Maya and Zara skills read memory or their own files, so the user is misled.
issues.fix: Store the key facts in memory and tell the user which teammates or skills will read it, without promising automatic use.

issues.quote: Key metrics or results to cite
issues.problem: Testimonials, logos and metrics go into a shared doc with no check that they are approved for public use or current, so downstream copy may publish unapproved customer names.
issues.fix: Add 'approved for public use (Y/N/unknown)' and 'as-of date' columns to the Proof Points table.

issues.quote: After gathering information, create `.agents/product-marketing.md` with this structure:
issues.problem: The ~120-line template restates the Sections to Capture list, so the SKILL.md body carries both.
issues.fix: Move the template to templates/product-marketing-context.md and reference it by relative path.

scenarios.prompt: Before you start writing anything, set up our product context. We're acme.com; we sell AP automation to mid-market finance teams.
scenarios.why: Step 1 recommends 'Auto-draft from codebase' (README, package.json), and the user has no repo. A capable model may improvise with web_fetch, and the 12-section template and changelog then give a strong doc. But it saves to a .agents path rather than memory, tells the user to run a nonexistent '/product-marketing' command, and falsely promises other skills will read it automatically.

scenarios.prompt: We're repositioning from SMB to enterprise. Here are three interview transcripts; our old context doc is somewhere in the workspace. Update it but keep the history.
scenarios.why: Step 4's version bump, prepended changelog and 'say so plainly when repositioning' rule are exactly right, and Step 2's push for verbatim language fits the transcripts. But Step 1 checks only four hard-coded paths, never searches the workspace or memory, and may miss the old doc. It also doesn't separate deciding the repositioning (a positioning skill or teammate) from recording it, and inferred content goes unlabeled.

seo-report-generation.job: render SEO findings as shareable HTML report
seo-report-generation.summary: OpenSEO's report-delivery subroutine: dedupes against existing reports, then writes one self-contained HTML page from a fixed CSS starter template with strict writing, title and HTML rules, and saves it via OpenSEO's save_report tool, returning three bullets and a link.
strengths: An excellent reporting discipline: one spine, verdict first, measured vs estimated vs hypothesis, and every charted number also printed
A polished, print-ready, mobile-safe HTML/CSS starter with well-explained primitives (rail, finding, note, table, bars)
Honest-number rules: write 'unknown' rather than invent a cell, and a caveat note for anything unverified
Tight chat-output discipline (three bullets and a link), with a report summary written for readers who won't open the page
missing: A delivery path that works without the OpenSEO MCP (workspace file, Google Doc)
Vendor-neutral attribution and footer
A standalone template file under templates/
A narrow trigger scoped to SEO research outputs
A connect_integration step or explicit OpenSEO prerequisite in the description

issues.quote: saved to the project with `save_report`, so anyone on the team can open it in the app, read it on a phone, and print it to PDF.
issues.problem: The whole flow (list_reports, get_report, list_report_templates, save_report, appendResearchLog) depends on OpenSEO MCP tools and its app viewer. The skill gives no fallback and no connect step.
issues.fix: If kept at all, save the HTML with write_workspace_file (or a Google Docs/Drive block) when OpenSEO isn't connected, and drop project and report-list semantics.

issues.quote: Do not paste the report body into chat, and do not offer to write it to a local file instead.
issues.problem: Combined with the save_report dependency, this bans every delivery route AutoGPT actually has, so the model must stall.
issues.fix: Allow a workspace HTML file or Google Doc as the delivery target, with the three-bullet chat summary pointing to it.

issues.quote: Use when a skill has finished its research, and whenever the user asks for a report, check-in, or summary, or names a report template.
issues.problem: The trigger is far too broad. Any report, summary or check-in request (Maria's content-pipeline-check routine, Maya's weekly read) could load an SEO-specific HTML protocol.
issues.fix: Don't expose it as a standalone skill. Keep it only as a reference inside website-seo-audit.

issues.quote: Every OpenSEO skill that produces a recommendation delivers through this skill.
issues.problem: It is redundant: the only OpenSEO producer in the catalog (website-seo-audit) ships this file verbatim as references/seo-report.md, so two copies will drift.
issues.fix: Drop the standalone package and maintain the single copy inside website-seo-audit.

issues.section: The closing section: how this report was made
issues.quote: The URL is always `https://openseo.so/docs/skills/` followed by the skill's directory name
issues.problem: Every AutoGPT-produced report would link to a third-party vendor's docs and carry a 'Prepared with OpenSEO' footer. That misattributes the expert's work and advertises a vendor.
issues.fix: Replace with a neutral line, e.g., 'Prepared by Maria (AutoGPT) using the website SEO audit skill on DATE'. Remove the openseo.so link and the footer branding.

issues.quote: Codex passes the argument through a JavaScript template literal, where both are syntax.
issues.problem: This is a stale, client-specific constraint (Codex) that doesn't apply to AutoGPT's tool calls and confuses the model.
issues.fix: Remove it, or restate it as a generic 'avoid backticks if your transport requires it'.

issues.quote: Copy this, keep the CSS as it is, and replace the ALL-CAPS placeholders.
issues.problem: About 150 lines of inline CSS/HTML sit in the SKILL.md body, so every load pays for them.
issues.fix: Move them to templates/report.html and reference the file by relative path.

scenarios.prompt: Package the keyword research you just did into a report I can forward to my CEO.
scenarios.why: 'Before you write' calls list_reports, and delivery requires save_report, both OpenSEO MCP tools absent unless the user connected that server. The Guardrails forbid pasting into chat or writing a local file, so the model has no permitted delivery path. It passes only if OpenSEO is connected via run_mcp_tool.

scenarios.prompt: Give me a quick summary of what content shipped this week.
scenarios.why: The description fires on 'summary' and 'check-in', so a non-SEO pipeline update loads an SEO HTML protocol. That brings OpenSEO title conventions, an openseo.so docs link, a 'Prepared with OpenSEO' footer and a three-bullet chat ceiling, none of which fit the request.

website-seo-audit.job: audit website SEO and prioritise top fixes
website-seo-audit.summary: OpenSEO's domain-level SEO audit: crawls the site and pulls rankings, backlinks, SERP checks and keyword demand through OpenSEO MCP tools, shortlists 5-10 opportunities across page families, sizes benefit honestly, runs a reviewer pass, and delivers a 1-3 recommendation HTML report via the bundled seo-report reference.
strengths: Opportunity-first method: research broadly, recommend 1-3, and justify every rejected shortlist row with a real reason
Rigorous evidence rules: count organic listings yourself, record query/country/date, treat a failed lookup as unknown, keep observation date separate from retrieval date
Honest sizing: volume is not visits, size the cluster rather than one term, no invented conversion rates or global multipliers, label position-one scenarios hypothetical
Mature judgment calls: protect pages that already rank, observations are not causes, access/indexing/dead-domain issues jump the queue
A built-in adversarial review step before writing
missing: A non-OpenSEO data path (DataForSEO/Firecrawl blocks, web_fetch, GSC/GA export upload)
Target country/language and key-conversion inputs up front
Spend or credit approval before paid lookups
Optional technical-SEO modules (Core Web Vitals, JS rendering, hreflang, structured-data validation, internal-link graph)
Handoff to seo-content-brief or on-page-seo-audit for executing the top recommendation
Vendor-neutral report attribution
A follow-up routine to re-check rankings for the recommended pages after changes ship

issues.quote: If OpenSEO is not connected, stop and ask the user to connect it.
issues.problem: This is a hard dependency on one vendor's MCP with no fallback, although AutoGPT has DataForSEO, Firecrawl, web_fetch/browser and GSC exports. Most users will hit a dead stop.
issues.fix: Add a tool map with fallbacks: DataForSEO via run_block for SERP, ranked keywords and volumes; Firecrawl or web_fetch for crawl, sitemap and page reads; an uploaded GSC CSV or connect_integration for first-party clicks. With no rank data, run a crawl-and-content audit and mark demand and positions 'unknown'.

issues.quote: Deliver using the bundled `seo-report` instructions in [references/seo-report.md](references/seo-report.md), saving with `skill: "seo-audit"`.
issues.problem: The bundled reference delivers only via OpenSEO save_report and forbids local files or chat, so even a successful audit has no permitted output on AutoGPT.
issues.fix: Adapt references/seo-report.md to save the HTML with write_workspace_file (or a Google Doc) when save_report is unavailable, keeping the writing and HTML rules.

issues.quote: Domain to audit and `projectId` (`list_projects`; if no project matches, `create_project`).
issues.problem: Inputs are framed around OpenSEO's project model. The skill never asks for target country and language, the conversion that matters, or a spend budget, all of which change the recommendations.
issues.fix: Ask up front, in one message, for the domain, target market (country/language), the key conversion page or action, and an allowed data or credit budget. Keep projectId only when OpenSEO is connected.

issues.quote: For expert-facing analysis of a competitor or market, use `competitor-analysis` or `competitive-landscape` instead.
issues.problem: These skills (and `seo-project-setup`, later in Inputs) aren't installed in the catalog, so the routing dead-ends.
issues.fix: Route to competitor-profiling or consult_teammate (Nadia/Zara) for market analysis, and replace seo-project-setup with product-marketing-context or Maria's getting-started flow.

issues.quote: confirm the connection and credits before spending
issues.problem: It checks the balance but never asks the user to approve the spend. Site audits and keyword research consume paid credits (or DataForSEO calls).
issues.fix: Estimate the calls or credits for the crawl and research plan and get an explicit yes before run_site_audit, then report actual spend in the closing section.

issues.quote: Demand figures are US unless stated; never multiply into an invented global number.
issues.problem: Defaulting to US demand misleads non-US sites, and the inputs never capture the market.
issues.fix: Use the target market captured in inputs for all volume and SERP calls, and state it in every column header.

issues.quote: the fixed skill link line from `seo-report` (URL `https://openseo.so/docs/skills/seo-audit`, text "OpenSEO SEO Audit skill")
issues.problem: Reports produced by an AutoGPT expert would link to and credit a third-party vendor.
issues.fix: Use a neutral method line naming the expert and skill, and list the data providers actually used.

issues.problem: There is no routing to Maria's page-level on-page-seo-audit, and no handoff to seo-content-brief when the top recommendation is a new or rewritten page. The trigger overlaps on 'SEO audit'.
issues.fix: State the boundary (site-level opportunity audit vs single-page on-page check) in the description, and end with an offer to brief or draft the leading page via seo-content-brief.

scenarios.prompt: Run an SEO audit on northwind.io and tell me the two or three things worth doing this quarter. OpenSEO is connected.
scenarios.why: The steps cover orienting and crawling, reading page families (best and worst page each), live SERP checks for the deciding queries, and a shortlist across at least three opportunity types. Choose and Size apply click-share scenarios labeled hypothetical, a reviewer argues for the runner-up, and the Output format yields 'Your next SEO move', 1-3 recommendations with evidence tables, and a 'What else we checked' table. That is senior-grade.

scenarios.prompt: Audit our site for SEO. We don't use OpenSEO. Here's a Search Console CSV export and our sitemap; budget is tight.
scenarios.why: 'OpenSEO MCP tools' says stop and ask the user to connect OpenSEO. The skill never offers the pasted GSC export, the DataForSEO or Firecrawl blocks, or web_fetch as a data path, and delivery requires save_report. A model following it literally stalls despite having enough data for a useful audit.

obviously-awesome.job: define product positioning and market category
obviously-awesome.summary: An upstream (wondelai) summary of April Dunford's Obviously Awesome method: five positioning components rolled up into a 10-row canvas, a 0-10 score, and long references on interviews, attribute checks, value mapping, segmentation, category choice, workshops and case studies.
strengths: Faithful, well-ordered rendering of Dunford's components: alternatives, then attributes, then value, then best-fit, then category. It opens on 'positioning is context, not messaging', which is the correct senior framing.

Deep, practical references: an interview script with switch and trigger questions, a do-nothing analysis, 'only we', truth and time-horizon tests for attributes, an actionability test for segments with negative cases, and a category decision framework that accounts for the education tax.
Good progressive disclosure: every step routes to a shipped reference with a clear 'see X when doing Y' clause, and every linked file exists.
Useful diagnostics: a Common Mistakes table, a Quick Diagnostic, and a canvas review checklist with stress tests and red flags.
Each step carries an ethical-boundary line: base alternatives on research, and never claim uniqueness a competitor shares.
missing: An intake step naming the minimum inputs (product, best customers, win/loss or call notes, competitor list, current homepage or pitch), with ask_question when they are missing
An evidence column on every canvas row marking each entry as sourced or assumed, with a citation
A pre-launch or no-customer path: a hypothesis canvas plus an interview and message-test plan
An explicit deliverable, saved with write_workspace_file and summarised in memory_store so messaging, pricing and sales skills downstream can reuse it
Checking 'only we' claims against competitor sites, docs and reviews via web_search/web_fetch
A draft-first step and approval gate before positioning reaches the website or sales decks, plus a substantiation requirement for comparative and superlative claims
A validation loop with pass criteria: the 30-second comprehension test with prospects, landing-page or ad tests, and win-rate tracking
