Guidance for deciding between one positioning and several when segments have different alternatives
Handoff boundaries to messaging, pricing and sales-enablement teammates
Dunford's actual Sales Pitch narrative structure

issues.quote: Rate any product's positioning 0-10 using the bands below, and always state the current score with the specific improvements needed to reach 10/10.
issues.problem: This is the only instruction addressed to the agent. The rest of SKILL.md reads as a book summary ('Core concept / Why it works / Copy patterns'), with no ordered workflow, no decision points and no definition of what to hand back. The model is forced to give a subjective score even when it has no evidence.
issues.fix: Add a 'How to run this' section before the canvas. 1) Intake. 2) Gather evidence from workspace files and URLs. 3) Draft the canvas with an evidence column. 4) Run the stress tests from references/positioning-canvas.md. 5) Deliver the canvas, the evidence map, open questions and a validation plan. 6) Score only when evidence exists, and otherwise say 'unscored: no customer evidence'.

issues.quote: Interview 15-20 existing happy customers, not prospects -- they can tell you what they actually switched from
issues.problem: The agent cannot run interviews, and the skill names no minimum inputs and has no fallback when research is missing (for example pre-launch, or a founder with only opinions). Every step then rests on data the model does not have, so the model either stalls or invents alternatives.
issues.fix: Name the inputs up front: product, 5-10 best customers, win/loss or call notes, competitor list, current homepage or pitch. Use ask_question for gaps. With no customer data, draft a canvas with every row marked HYPOTHESIS, source alternatives from reviews and competitor sites via web_search, and output the interview plan from references/competitive-alternatives.md.

issues.section: Step 3: Map Attributes to Customer Value
issues.quote: [Number]% of customers report [value] within [timeframe]
issues.problem: The copy patterns and the example canvas ('Save 10 hours/week', 'close the books 3 days faster') show made-up figures as the expected output. SKILL.md never requires a number or proof point to be sourced, so the model will fill these slots with invented stats.
issues.fix: Add a rule: every number and proof point cites its source (file, call, URL), or is written as [needs proof]. Never fill a numeric copy pattern without data. Add a 'Source / Assumed' column to the canvas.

issues.quote: it walks through repositioning wins, niche discovery, and category creation end to end.
issues.problem: references/case-studies.md presents precise results ('Average deal size increased 4x', 'Sales cycle shortened by 35%', 'Won a new Gartner category') attributed to named or thinly veiled real companies (it merges Chorus.ai and Gong into one, and clearly describes MongoDB and Segment). The disclaimer admits the details are 'composited'. A model told to 'model a real engagement on' these may repeat invented facts to users as precedent.
issues.fix: Replace these with Dunford's documented cases, or strip company names and metrics and label each case 'illustrative composite'. Add a line saying these are never cited as evidence.

issues.quote: Define product positioning by mapping competitive alternatives, unique attributes, and best-fit customers to the right market category.
issues.problem: This runs the same five-component Dunford spine as Zara's positioning-and-messaging (NICK), and overlaps Nadia's icp-and-positioning (ORIGINAL). All three trigger on 'positioning', so assigning this alongside either one would split routing. The description also points to crossing-the-chasm, which is not in the catalog.
issues.fix: Merge: keep positioning-and-messaging as the routed skill and move this package's references (interview script, attribute verification, category decision framework, canvas template) in as its references/. If this skill stays separate, narrow its trigger to canvas workshops and category choice or repositioning, and delete the crossing-the-chasm pointer.

issues.quote: The only [category] that [unique attribute]
issues.problem: It encourages 'only', 'unlike [competitor]' and new-category claims, and team-exercise.md schedules website and sales-deck updates. There is no draft-first step, no approval gate, and no note that superlative or comparative claims need substantiation (advertising-standards risk).
issues.fix: State that positioning outputs are internal drafts. External copy with 'only/first/best' or a named-competitor comparison needs a linked proof file and the owner's approval before it is published.

issues.quote: Problem -> old way -> new way -> our solution -> proof
issues.problem: The skill cites Dunford's Sales Pitch, but this narrative arc is not her structure (insight or market shift, alternatives and their limits, perfect world, our approach, differentiated value, proof, objections). The SKILL.md canvas and statement template also differ from the template in references/positioning-canvas.md (Key Proof Points vs Primary Message, 'unlike...' clause).
issues.fix: Align the narrative row to Dunford's Sales Pitch sequence, and make the SKILL.md canvas identical to the reference template.

issues.quote: https://www.amazon.com/Obviously-Awesome-Product-Positioning-Customers/dp/1999023005?tag=wondelai00-20
issues.problem: These are vendor affiliate-tracked links, and together with 'About the Author' they are human-oriented filler that spends agent context. The references also carry heavy in-room workshop logistics (sticky notes, cameras on, room booking).
issues.fix: Remove the affiliate tags and the Further Reading and About the Author sections, or cite title and year only. Cut the workshop logistics down to what an agent can prepare: pre-read, agenda and canvas.

scenarios.prompt: We sell scheduling software to home-health agencies. Attached are our homepage copy, notes from 6 won and lost deals, and 4 competitors. Prospects keep lumping us in with generic calendar apps. Work out our positioning and fill in the canvas.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-5 map directly onto the materials. The model can cluster alternatives (generic calendars, whiteboards, schedulers bundled with the EHR), apply the only-we/truth/time-horizon tests from references/unique-attributes.md, run so-what chains from references/value-mapping.md, choose a subcategory with the Q1-Q3 framework in references/market-category.md, and fill the template and review checklist in references/positioning-canvas.md. One gap: nothing tells the model to cite which deal note backs each row, so proof points may come out generic or assumed.

scenarios.prompt: We're pre-launch with no customers yet. Our founder insists we're creating a new category called 'autonomous revenue orchestration'. Here's our competitor list. Give me the positioning and a homepage headline I can publish by Friday.
scenarios.why: The 'Creating a new category prematurely' row and Q3 of the category framework (resources for the education tax) let the model push back toward a subcategory, which is the senior answer. But Steps 1-4 all assume 15-20 happy-customer interviews, and the skill has no path for a product with no customers. It never says to mark alternatives and best-fit as hypotheses, draw them from beta users or founder sales calls, or return an interview and message-test plan. The Scoring section also forces a 0-10 score with no evidence behind it. And nothing gates the publish-ready headline, or any 'only/first' claim, behind proof and the user's approval.

14:expense-categorization.job: categorize expense transactions to chart of accounts
14:expense-categorization.summary: Codes card/bank exports and receipts to the owner's own chart. Five stdlib Python scripts normalise the export, check the control total, flag duplicates, special lines and receipt ties, propose accounts from rules and history, then validate the table and split it into ready-to-post and needs-review files, with an ask_question queue and rule capture.
strengths: The scripts are deterministic, use exact-decimal money and pass their selftests. They refuse ragged CSV rows, rows with both debit and credit filled, ambiguous dates, edited amounts, out-of-chart accounts and split parts that do not add up.
A receipt counts as evidence only when it ties to a payment line. A receipt with no card line is reported as an exception, and duplicates are kept and asked about, never deleted.

special-lines.md is practitioner-grade. It covers refunds, transfers, card payments, owner items, loan interest vs principal, VAT as a liability, processor payouts net of fees, foreign currency and bank-rule auto-adds, each with a question to ask and who decides.
Confidence caps from rules and history are enforced at validation time, so a row the model marks 'high' above its cap cannot reach Ready to post.

Guardrails are tight. Ledger access is read-only with no posting, thresholds are never quoted from memory, tax options are never offered, a Google Sheet append happens only after approval, and the skill stops after two failures.
The worked examples (bramble-april-card, hard-lines) include fixtures, the expected output and a list of 'what a wrong answer looks like' traps.

It uses real platform constructs: run_capability skill: ids, ~/skills/<slug> package paths and write_workspace_file delivery. It falls back to hand computation when Python is missing and to delivering files when state is unavailable.
missing: Out-of-pocket and reimbursement path: a receipt with no card line that was paid personally should lead to an employee or owner expense claim, including mileage.
Prepayment/accrual flag for annual or multi-period charges, such as annual SaaS paid upfront, left for the accountant to decide.
Card-statement lines such as interest charges, annual or late fees and cashback/rewards credits are not in the special-line patterns.
Vendor alias table (payee normalisation, e.g. AMZN MKTP / AMAZON.CO.UK) so that rules and history match across description variants.
1099 vendor tracking (W-9 on file, payee type) for US contractor payees, beyond the classification flag.
The foreign-currency regex also matches the home currency (e.g. 'GBP 45' for a GBP entity), so the entity's base currency should be excluded.

issues.quote: save the table to `<state>/expenses/<YYYY-MM>-review.csv`
issues.problem: propose_from_history.load_history only counts rows that have a `final_account` column and status=approved. The review template this step saves has `proposed_account` and `status` but no `final_account`. As a result, next month's history lookup silently ignores this skill's own saved tables. I verified this: a saved April table with status=approved gave basis 'none' on all 8 rows. Only the hand-built example history file works.
issues.fix: Have load_history fall back to proposed_account when status=approved, or add a final_account column that step 7 fills. Add a selftest that saves a review table and reads it back as history.

issues.quote: answering "which account does this go in"
issues.problem: This one-off use case is in both the triggers and 'Use when', but the only procedure requires intake.json (or loading bookkeeping-getting-started), normalisation and four scripts. A single-charge question gets a heavyweight workflow or an improvised answer.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Single item' branch. Ask for the chart, or propose from the chart if given, cite the account definition, state the confidence and the one missing fact, flag special-line or fixed-asset kinds, and skip the scripts and state.

issues.problem: VAT/GST shown on receipts is not captured. The worked example is a UK Ltd in GBP, but the template has no net, tax or tax-code column, and the 'never offer a tax option' rule may lead the model to drop tax codes. Xero or QBO UK/AU lines then cannot be posted without rework. Recording the VAT printed on a receipt is a fact, not tax advice.
issues.fix: Add optional `tax_on_receipt` and `tax_code` columns. Fill the amount only as printed on the receipt, and take the code only from the owner's or accountant's supplied list. Leave recoverability to the accountant.

issues.quote: add a second `--tx` to check card and bank together, which
issues.problem: write_review.py accepts a single --tx, so a combined card+bank review table fails with 'not in the source export'. The instruction 'fix the table, never the export' could lead the model to drop rows. expense_checks' --control-total also compares the combined net (and mixed currencies) to one statement total.
issues.fix: Say to run write_review once per source file with that file's rows, and give per-file control totals. Alternatively make write_review accept repeated --tx and tie totals per file and currency.

issues.quote: A receipt counts as support only when it ties to a card or bank line [60].
issues.problem: expense_checks ties a receipt on absolute amount, currency and a 3-day window only; the merchant is never compared. A £45 receipt from a different vendor can 'tie' to FIGMA and help a row reach Ready to post, which undercuts the fake-receipt rationale the skill cites.
issues.fix: Add a fuzzy merchant check using norm_text on the receipt merchant vs the description. A merchant mismatch should mark the tie 'amount only' and keep the row out of Ready.

issues.quote: In chat show only the Needs review rows and the totals
issues.problem: write_review sends excluded rows (card payments, money in) to needs-review.csv and includes them in the review total. The chat 'Needs review' list then shows lines that need no decision, which contradicts special-lines.md ('Exclude from expense coding').
issues.fix: Write excluded rows to a separate excluded.csv or section with their reasons, and keep them out of the Needs review count and amount.

issues.quote: each export (once the owner has confirmed date format and sign):
issues.problem: No script in this package detects date-format ambiguity or sign convention. normalize_export's docstring and error message say 'run profile_sources.py first', and books-state.md cites scripts/log_approval.py, but neither ships in this package. Without an intake from bookkeeping-getting-started, the model has no bundled way to profile the file.
issues.fix: Expose bkio.detect_date_formats through a `--profile` flag on normalize_export (dates ambiguous?, sign hint from description words), or say plainly that profiling lives in bookkeeping-getting-started.

issues.quote: Full pre-delivery list: `checklists/before-delivery.md`.
issues.problem: 'Checks', 'Quality self-check' and checklists/before-delivery.md overlap heavily. Inline citation markers ([59][44][100]) add tokens to the body without helping the model act.
issues.fix: Keep one checklist in checklists/before-delivery.md and one line in the body pointing to it. Move the citations to references/sources.md.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Amex CSV for September and the receipt PDFs. Code them to our chart (intake is already set up with you) and tell me what needs my input.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-8 cover the whole job. normalize_export needs a confirmed date format and sign, and expense_checks stops on a control-total mismatch and ties receipts to payment lines. propose_from_history applies approved rules with caps, write_review refuses edited, dropped or out-of-chart rows and splits ready vs review, and ask_question settles the 10 largest items. Special lines and duplicates are kept out of Ready. The output contract and templates give a reusable deliverable.

scenarios.prompt: Month two: here are the Chase checking and Amex CSVs for August plus last month's reviewed table. There's a Gusto payroll debit, an SBA loan payment, a Venmo to my brother and a few charges I can't place. Code everything.
scenarios.why: Special-line handling is excellent: payroll, loan and transfer are routed and not coded, and card payments are excluded. Three gaps hurt the run. The saved April-format table has no final_account column, so propose_from_history ignores it; I ran it and all 8 rows came back basis 'none'. write_review.py takes one --tx, so a combined card+bank table fails with 'not in the source export'. The --control-total in checks nets both files together, so a single statement total will not tie. Unknown charges are correctly sent to bookkeeping-exception-escalation.

scenarios.prompt: Quick question, nothing set up yet: which account should a £1,450 APPLE STORE charge on the company card go in? We use Xero.
scenarios.why: The trigger fires on 'which account does this go in', but the body requires intake.json and otherwise loads bookkeeping-getting-started, then normalisation and four scripts. There is no one-line answer path. A capable model would still flag a possible fixed asset (special-lines.md section 3) and ask for the chart, but the skill pushes it toward a heavy setup the user did not ask for.

better: The v1 placeholder was a table of fields and five checks. v2 adds deterministic scripts for normalisation, a control-total stop, duplicate and special-line detection, receipt-to-payment ties, rule and history proposals with confidence caps, and validation that no row was dropped or edited.
A clear 'Do not use for' boundary and routing to bookkeeping-exception-escalation, statement-reconciliation and bookkeeping-getting-started.
A defined deliverable: review CSV template, column guide, ready-to-post and needs-review files, totals.md, optional xlsx, and an ask_question card template.
special-lines.md and substantiation-us.md give accountant-grade handling of transfers, loans, VAT, payroll, processors, FX, fixed assets and contractors, where v1 had a single 'keep apart' sentence.
Owner-approved coding rules are captured with approver and date, so later months get faster.
Worked examples with fixtures and expected outputs, plus selftests that pass.
worse: About 3.5x longer body plus 5 references and 5 scripts. It is heavy for a one-off 'which account' question, and there is no light path.
It now depends on intake.json from bookkeeping-getting-started for any run.
The history feature is silently broken for its own saved tables because of a final_account vs proposed_account mismatch.
Adds inline citation noise and three overlapping checklists.

alliance-co-commercialization.job: govern a strategic alliance's joint selling
alliance-co-commercialization.summary: A 59-line list of rules for running a strategic alliance: one signed operating model, a jointly scored overlap list with an owner on each side, steering packs and minutes, milestone tracking, and a log of conflict rulings.
strengths: Clear approval gate: nothing goes to the partner and no joint commitment is made without the owner's yes
'Joint tiers are earned by joint activity, not by logo size' is a sharp, correct rule
Requires written minutes with owners and dates after every steering meeting
The conflict log with precedent is a distinctive, useful idea
missing: Rules of engagement and deal-registration policy
Partner-sourced vs partner-influenced attribution definitions
Account-mapping method and data-sharing consent
Joint business plan with revenue targets
Steering pack and operating model templates
Handoff to Anika for alliance-level governance

issues.quote: Write one model doc, signed by both sides: joint account targeting rules,
issues.problem: The operating-model and steering content is near-verbatim with Anika's govern-the-strategic-alliance (same inputs, same steering-pack sentence, same fallback). Two experts will claim the same job.
issues.fix: Drop from Max. Keep alliance governance with Anika and have Max consult or hand off to her for alliance-level work.

issues.quote: explicit yes. Channel motions belong to the co-sell skill; alliance governance
issues.problem: The boundary with partner-and-channel-co-sell sits in the last line of the body, not in the description, so it never affects triggering. Joint targeting and joint metrics (sourced pipeline, co-sell win rate) repeat that skill.
issues.fix: Merge the deal-registration and precedent-log rules into partner-and-channel-co-sell and name that slug exactly.

issues.quote: Deal-registration clashes, messaging drift, and delivery slips each have a
issues.problem: No rules of engagement: first-to-register, proof of prior engagement, registration expiry, margin split on disputes. There is also no fallback for when no model exists.
issues.fix: Add a short rules-of-engagement checklist and an interim ruling procedure for when the operating model is missing.

issues.quote: Track shared milestones: sourced pipeline, co-sell win rate, and launch or
issues.problem: The metrics are named but not defined. Partner-sourced vs partner-influenced attribution is the usual fight in alliance reviews and is left open.
issues.fix: Define each metric, its evidence (registration ID, CRM source field) and the data source.

issues.quote: Score the overlap list, tier it, and assign one owner per side per account.
issues.problem: No scoring criteria and no account-mapping method. It also ignores that sharing CRM account lists with a partner needs an NDA or data-sharing basis.
issues.fix: Give the scoring inputs, an account-mapping method (a mapping tool or hashed CSV overlap), and a privacy check before any list is exchanged.

issues.quote: The operating model, the joint target list with dual owners, the steering
issues.problem: Five deliverables are named without a template or format, so the output changes on every run.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the operating model, the steering pack and the conflict log.

issues.quote: No joint list means you draft the overlap from CRM and partner data and mark
issues.problem: No tool routing (HubSpot or Sheets blocks) and no paste/CSV fallback for the partner's side of the data.
issues.fix: Name the blocks to use and ask for the partner export as a paste or upload when there is no integration.

issues.quote: Use this when a strategic alliance needs joint selling governance. Start from
issues.problem: Alliance governance falls outside the Account Executive persona. Max's identity covers partner deals, not running alliances.
issues.fix: Remove from Max's kit and add a consult_teammate handoff to Anika.

scenarios.prompt: Our Snowflake alliance steering committee is next Thursday. Here's the joint pipeline sheet. Build the steering pack and flag which milestones we missed.
scenarios.why: 'Prep and follow through on steering' supplies the right skeleton: milestones hit and missed in FACT numbers, the decisions needed, and dated asks. But it gives no pack template, no definitions of sourced vs influenced pipeline or co-sell win rate, and no step to parse the sheet or compute in the sandbox. The model gets the shape right and has to guess the metric rules.

scenarios.prompt: The partner's rep registered the Acme deal two weeks after we started working it and now wants partner margin. We never wrote an operating model. What's the call? Also draft a note to their alliance lead.
scenarios.why: 'Resolve conflicts through the model' assumes a model with a named arbiter already exists. The fallbacks don't cover a missing model, and the skill has no rules of engagement: no first-to-register rule, no proof-of-prior-engagement evidence such as CRM timestamps, no registration expiry. The model can only give generic advice, though the approval gate does keep the note as a draft.

build-the-target-list.summary: Builds a person-per-row prospect list with a fixed column schema and status ladder, grades each company strong, maybe or weak by fit plus a sourced trigger, fills three buying seats per company with linkable titles, refuses guessed contacts, dedupes and suppresses, and previews before saving.
strengths: Fixed column schema and status ladder that downstream skills (draft-a-first-touch) actually read
'Fit with no trigger is a maybe; a trigger never makes a poor fit strong' is expert-grade grading logic
No guessed emails or profile URLs, and an unconfirmed title holds the row at new
Suppresses do-not-contact entries, open deals and customers, and names everyone struck
Preview-then-save, a 25-row first pass and no CRM write without a yes
Research depth scales with the fit grade
missing: Named save location and memory pointer
Handling of vendor-sourced or verified contacts
Privacy and lawful-basis rules
CSV/Sheet formula neutralisation
Firmographic columns
Hook freshness window
One worked example row

issues.quote: The contact field holds only what you found published and can link;
issues.problem: No rule for contacts that arrive in the user's own Apollo or HubSpot export or from enrichment blocks. The model will either strip licensed data or keep it without a verification status.
issues.fix: Allow imported contacts with contact_source=export and a verification state (for example from a ZeroBounce check), while still never generating a contact from a naming pattern.

issues.quote: Show ten rows with fit reasons, let them edit once, then save.
issues.problem: No save destination is named, though every downstream skill reads these rows. Runs will scatter lists across chat, files and sheets.
issues.fix: Default to a workspace CSV or a connected Google Sheet via run_block, and record the list location in memory for the routines to use.

issues.problem: No privacy limits: no GDPR, UK or CASL lawful basis for EU and UK prospects, no data minimisation, no opt-out handling.
issues.fix: Add a short rule: collect only business-role data, note a lawful basis by region, and honour opt-outs through suppression.

issues.problem: Scraped fields (names, titles, hooks) go into CSVs or Sheets without neutralising leading = + - @. This formula-injection risk is why Toran's prospecting package was deferred.
issues.fix: Prefix or escape formula-leading cells before any CSV or Sheet write.

issues.quote: Who: prospect_id (a key you never reuse), company, company_url, person,
issues.problem: No firmographic columns (industry, headcount, region) and no source column for person or title. The fit reason exists only as free text in notes.
issues.fix: Add company_size, industry, region and title_source_url.

issues.quote: If all you have is an ideal customer, seed 10 to 20 fitting companies from
issues.problem: No tool routing. It skips the Apollo, Exa and web_search blocks and Max's preloaded Lead Finder and Decision Maker workflows.
issues.fix: Name the preferred sources in order and the fallback to a web search.

issues.quote: Why now: hook, never without hook_source_url and hook_date; enriched_on
issues.problem: No staleness window, so a hook from months ago still counts as 'why now'.
issues.fix: Re-check hooks older than about 90 days, and move rows with stale hooks back to new.

issues.quote: or Apollo export, or a Google Sheet starts with a readback: name the columns
issues.problem: Large exports get no instruction to use the sandbox for parsing, deduping and scoring.
issues.fix: Route files over a few dozen rows through bash_exec and show counts before and after each cut.

scenarios.prompt: We sell warehouse management software to US 3PLs with 50-500 employees. Build me a starter list.
scenarios.why: The skill seeds 10-20 companies from the web with a cited page each, grades fit with a named trigger, fills buyer, champion and user seats with linkable titles, leaves unfound contacts blank, previews ten rows and caps the first pass at 25. The result is senior-quality. Only the save destination is left to the model.

scenarios.prompt: Here's an Apollo export of 400 contacts. Cut it to the best 50. Some are already customers but HubSpot isn't connected. I need emails for all of them.
scenarios.why: The readback, dedupe and 'check HubSpot, or ask' steps apply. But 'The contact field holds only what you found published and can link' gives no rule for emails that come from the user's licensed Apollo export: the model may strip legitimate data or keep it without a verification status. There is also no instruction to process 400 rows in the sandbox.

business-case-and-roi-selling.job: build buyer ROI business case and proposal
business-case-and-roi-selling.summary: Builds a deal's value case from buyer quotes, then an outcome-led demo and PoC plan, an ROI model (cost delta, payback, TCO, NPV) from cited inputs, and a proposal. The proposal section also carries concession sequencing, walk-away, recap memo and CRM concession logging.
strengths: 'A metric the buyer never said stays out' blocks seller-invented value
The demo is built around three buyer outcomes with a proof line each, not a feature tour, with per-stakeholder variants
PoC with entry and exit criteria, dated owners on both sides, and what a pass earns
Price stays inside approved bands, and priced pages need the owner's explicit yes
Fallback turns a missing metric into the exact question for the next call
missing: Scenario and sensitivity ranges
Discount rate and horizon source
Cost-of-inaction quantification
Benchmark handling with a validation plan
ROI model and proposal templates
Executive one-page summary
Handoff to Daniel (finance) for model review

issues.section: Model the ROI with cited numbers only
issues.quote: input is FACT with a source or it stays out; assumptions get their own box
issues.problem: This contradicts itself: inputs must be FACT or stay out, yet assumptions are allowed. Every real ROI model depends on assumed improvement rates, and the skill gives no rule for benchmarks, ranges or sensitivity.
issues.fix: Split inputs into buyer-stated FACT and labelled assumptions with source and range. Require conservative, expected and upside scenarios, with the headline on the conservative case.

issues.section: Draft the proposal from the case
issues.quote: Every concession names its paired buyer give (term, timing, scope), sequenced
issues.problem: Concession sequencing, walk-away, procurement counters, price realisation and recap memos repeat objection-and-negotiation and enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans. The paragraph bloats the skill and blurs its trigger.
issues.fix: Keep scope, price band and the one dated ask here, and route concessions to objection-and-negotiation by slug.

issues.quote: The ROI business case with sourced numbers, the demo or proof-of-concept plan,
issues.problem: No template for the ROI model, the one-page CFO summary, the demo plan or the proposal outline, so each run invents its own structure.
issues.fix: Ship templates/roi-model.csv (inputs with source and assumption flags) and a proposal/exec-summary outline.

issues.section: Model the ROI with cited numbers only
issues.quote: Current-state cost, future-state cost, the delta, payback period, total cost
issues.problem: NPV and payback are named with no discount rate, horizon or calculation method, and no instruction to compute in bash_exec.
issues.fix: Take the discount rate and horizon from the owner or finance, compute in the sandbox, and show formulas and inputs next to results.

issues.quote: next call must answer before the case goes anywhere. No approved price band
issues.problem: Too rigid under deadline pressure: no labelled preliminary value hypothesis from benchmarks.
issues.fix: Allow a benchmark-based draft marked ASSUMED with a validation plan, kept internal until buyer numbers land.

issues.section: Draft the proposal from the case
issues.quote: the CRM with give, get, approver, and rationale.
issues.problem: Tells the model to write to the CRM without restating the owner-approval step the persona requires for every CRM change.
issues.fix: Stage the concession log as a draft and write it to the CRM only after an explicit yes.

issues.section: Plan the demo from the case
issues.quote: and the trap questions to avoid — not a feature tour. Write per-stakeholder
issues.problem: 'Trap questions to avoid' is unclear. Practitioners prepare answers for landmine questions and competitor-planted traps; they don't avoid them.
issues.fix: Reword to name the likely landmine questions and the prepared answer for each.

scenarios.prompt: Build the ROI case for Acme. On the call they said 3 FTEs at about $85k each reconcile invoices, and they want close in 5 days instead of 12. We're $60k a year.
scenarios.why: 'Build the case from buyer words only' and the ROI section produce the current-state cost, delta and payback. But future-state savings need an assumed efficiency gain, NPV needs a discount rate the skill never sources, there are no conservative/expected ranges, and nothing sends the math to the sandbox. The output is decent but not CFO-grade.

scenarios.prompt: Their CFO wants an ROI model by Friday, but the buyer never gave us numbers. We only have Gartner benchmarks and two case studies. Procurement is also asking for 25% off.
scenarios.why: The fallback stops at naming the gap and writing one question, and 'goes anywhere' blocks the case entirely. There is no path to a benchmark-based preliminary value hypothesis, labelled assumed and pending buyer validation, which is standard practice under deadline. The discount is handled safely by the price-band rule, but that work belongs to objection-and-negotiation.

cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling.job: sell through cloud marketplace private offers
cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling.summary: Guides deals that run through hyperscaler commits and marketplace private offers. It separates MACC, EDP and Google commits from the private offer, separates MACC-eligible from Co-Sell Ready, builds burn-down math and plays, and models marketplace fees from the current schedule. It adds a private-offer checklist and back office, then repeats MEDDPICC and the paper track.
strengths: Tells the model to check drawdown eligibility before promising it, and to pull the current fee schedule instead of trusting memory
Correct, rarely stated split between MACC-eligible, Co-Sell Ready and IP co-sell incentive eligibility
Burn-down gap stated in dollars with a named state (on pace, behind, at risk)
Flags marketplace-specific acceptance, expiry and renewal-replacement mechanics as things to check
Names back-office steps: disbursement reconciliation, revenue recognition, CRM sync
missing: Channel offer names per cloud (CPPO, MPO/CSP, reseller private offer)
Separate treatment of the seller's own consumption-contract burn-down
Rollover and true-up options table
Boundary and handoff to Anika's marketplace ops skill
Burn-down calculation template
Handoff to finance for revenue recognition and disbursement

issues.quote: Channel Partner Private Offer (CPPO) with the partner transacting, or
issues.problem: CPPO is AWS's program name, yet it sits under the Azure heading. Microsoft uses multiparty private offers and CSP, and Google uses reseller private offers, so the model is steered to the wrong term for two of the three clouds.
issues.fix: Give the channel offer type per cloud (AWS CPPO, Microsoft MPO/CSP, Google reseller private offer) and tell the model to confirm names in the current seller guide.

issues.quote: Build the burn-down math from FACT numbers only: commit total, consumed to
issues.problem: This merges two problems: the buyer's hyperscaler commit, which funds the purchase, and the seller's own consumption contract with the buyer, which carries renewal and true-up risk. The plays ('which workloads or teams absorb the gap') only fit one of them.

issues.section: Qualify and run the paper track
issues.quote: Score the deal on MEDDPICC before any proposal goes out: Metrics, Economic
issues.problem: The whole section, including 'redlines kill enterprise deals as surely as feature gaps', is copied from discovery-and-qualification and enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans. It also sits after the proposal work that it says must come first.
issues.fix: Replace with a one-line route to those two skills and keep only the marketplace-specific paper items.

issues.quote: Register the co-sell motion in the cloud provider's own partner portal
issues.problem: The checklist and the 'visibility, not pipeline' rule match Anika's run-hyperscaler-marketplace-co-sell nearly word for word. The seller-side and partner-ops boundary is undefined.
issues.fix: Keep the offer terms seller-side, and hand listing, co-sell registration and fund capture to Anika by slug.

issues.quote: Use when a deal involves a cloud consumption commit, a marketplace private offer, or a multi-year enterprise agreement.

issues.section: Pick the vehicle with the buyer

issues.problem: It treats commit programs as vehicles to compare. The seller's real choice is direct paper, a direct private offer, or a reseller private offer; commits are just the funding source.

issues.quote: true-up or true-down mechanics, and what happens to unused commit. Model the

issues.quote: The vehicle pick with trade-offs, the burn-down read with the gap in

issues.fix: Ship a burn-down template computed in bash_exec and hand revenue recognition to Mina or Daniel.

scenarios.prompt: Buyer has a $5M AWS commit with $1.8M unspent and 7 months left. Can our $400k deal go through AWS Marketplace and count against it?
scenarios.why: 'Pick the vehicle' says a private offer can draw down the commit only when it qualifies, never promise before checking, and pull the current seller guide and fee schedule. The burn-down math gives the required run rate, and the private-offer checklist covers duration and acceptance. A capable model gives a correct, hedged, sourced answer.

scenarios.prompt: Customer buys Microsoft through their CSP reseller and wants our deal MACC-eligible. Separately, their consumption commit with us is 40% behind with 3 months left and they want the unused balance rolled into renewal.

On rollover, the skill only names 'what happens to unused commit' with no options (rollover caps, term extension, true-up, renewal uplift), and it merges the buyer's hyperscaler commit with the seller's own consumption contract.

compliance-gated-deal-execution.job: clear compliance gates before deal close
compliance-gated-deal-execution.summary: Lists a deal's compliance gates (licensing, suitability, privacy, industry codes) with owners and states, reviews compliance at opportunity stage, keeps an audit-ready deal file, tracks title and registration filings, and treats pending gates as Best Case in the forecast.
strengths: A failed gate stops the deal, and a Commit deal with a pending gate drops to Best Case
Review runs at opportunity stage, not at signature
'A stranger can re-run the deal from the file' is a clear audit standard
Gates are marked INFERENCE until legal confirms when no list exists
missing: Named regime and gate library by vertical
Rule that only the gate owner clears a gate
KYC/AML, sanctions and anti-bribery gates
Escalation to compliance or legal teammate
Gate checklist template
Records-retention standard

issues.quote: Nothing buyer-facing sends and no gated deal advances without your

issues.quote: Cover licensing checks, suitability review, privacy and ethics rules,
issues.problem: No named regimes or standard B2B gates: KYC/AML, sanctions screening, anti-bribery and public-sector gift rules, export control, best-interest suitability, HIPAA BAAs, DORA and outsourcing notices.
issues.fix: Add a references/gate-library.md grouped by vertical and jurisdiction, each gate with its owner role and required evidence.

issues.quote: No gate list: draft from the last approved deal's checks and mark
issues.problem: A previous deal's gates may not fit a different product, customer type or jurisdiction, so copying them creates false confidence.
issues.fix: Ask the compliance owner for the gate list first, use the gate library as a draft, and hand off to Lena (compliance-escalation-brief) when unclear.

issues.quote: Title, registration, or transfer work each carry an owner,
issues.problem: Mixes real-estate and vehicle titling with finserv and SaaS in one skill. The software line repeats enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans and overlaps regulated-access-and-clinical-selling.

issues.quote: misses become rep coaching, tracked as a scored metric.

issues.quote: Gate checklist with states and owners, opportunity review with
issues.problem: No gate-record fields or template: regime, owner, evidence link, state, cleared-by, cleared-on.
issues.fix: Ship templates/gate-checklist.csv with those columns.

issues.problem: No escalation path to a compliance or legal teammate, and no records-retention rule for the audit file.
issues.fix: Add consult_teammate to Lena for determinations and a retention note tied to the regime.

scenarios.prompt: We sell annuities through licensed agents. The Henderson deal has to close by the 30th. Build the gate checklist and tell me what's still pending.
scenarios.why: 'List every gate first' produces a generic licensing, suitability and privacy checklist with owners and states, and the forecast rule applies. But with no named regime (best-interest suitability, state producer appointment, replacement forms, free-look), the checklist misses the gates a compliance principal would expect.

scenarios.prompt: Selling our SaaS to a German state bank. No gate list exists, procurement wants to sign Friday, the security review and DPA are still open, and our Frankfurt rep isn't sure we need a BaFin outsourcing notification.
scenarios.why: The fallback drafts gates from the last approved deal and marks them INFERENCE until legal confirms. That is safe, but the last deal's gates probably don't cover DORA or BaFin outsourcing. Nothing routes the question to counsel or the compliance teammate, and 'no gated deal advances without your explicit yes' leaves room for the seller to push Friday through.

credit-term-sheet-structuring.summary: Lender-side sequence for credit products: read the borrower's cash flow with numbers kept UNKNOWN until statements arrive, structure inside approval bands, draft a plain-terms sheet, get internal risk sign-off before the founder sees terms, and track conditions precedent to funding.
strengths: Numbers stay UNKNOWN until statements arrive, and founder figures are recorded as attributed claims
Internal risk consensus comes before the founder sees terms, which is the real failure mode in lending sales
Legal language waits for counsel, and the sheet stays in commercial plain terms
Each condition precedent carries an owner and date, and funding waits on all of them
'Not a SaaS order form' clearly separates this skill from the generic deal skills
missing: Underwriting metrics and document checklist by product type
Term sheet template
Fee, amortisation, prepayment and warrant structures
Lien search and intercreditor check
Regulatory disclosure, licensing and KYC gate
Decline and adverse-action path
Sandbox computation of covenant headroom
Handoff to Daniel (finance) for model review

issues.section: Discover cash flow like an underwriter
issues.quote: Inflows, burn or seasonality, existing facilities, and what the new
issues.problem: No underwriting metrics or document checklist: DSCR, leverage, liquidity and runway after funding, ARR multiple or borrowing base, customer concentration, AR aging.
issues.fix: Add references/underwriting-metrics.md by product type (term loan, ABL, RBF, venture debt) with each metric's formula, the document it comes from, and sandbox computation.

issues.problem: No regulatory limits: commercial-financing disclosure laws (California, New York and others), ECOA/Reg B adverse-action notices, state lending licences, KYC/AML and beneficial-ownership checks.
issues.fix: Add a regulatory gate: confirm disclosure and licensing requirements with compliance before any offer, and route declines through adverse-action handling.

issues.section: Draft the sheet in plain terms
issues.quote: Economics, conditions precedent, key covenants, and the path from
issues.problem: No term sheet template: amount, index and margin, fees (origination, unused, prepayment), amortisation, collateral, covenant levels and test dates, reporting, events of default, warrants, non-binding clause, expiry.
issues.fix: Ship templates/term-sheet.md with those sections and a plain-language explanation per line.

issues.quote: Size, tenor, pricing, covenants, and collateral shaped to the risk
issues.problem: Existing facilities are noted but never checked for lien priority, intercreditor or subordination needs, or UCC search results, which decide whether a facility can fund at all.
issues.fix: Add a lien and intercreditor step: run or request a UCC search, and name the payoff, subordination or intercreditor path before structuring.

issues.quote: Use when the deal is a credit facility or capital product that needs underwriting and a term sheet, not a SaaS order form.
issues.problem: The bare triggers 'term sheet' and 'underwriting' also match equity fundraising, partner term sheets (Anika's structure-the-partner-agreement) and insurance underwriting.
issues.fix: Use 'credit term sheet', 'loan term sheet' and 'credit underwriting' as triggers, and exclude equity rounds in the description.

issues.section: Draft the sheet in plain terms
issues.quote: sign. Legal language waits for counsel. Label the term_state drafting
issues.problem: term_state is a state field with no stated home (memory, CRM or sheet), so it won't persist between sessions.
issues.fix: Store term_state in memory or the deal tracker the owner names, and read it back at the start of each run.

issues.section: Sell consensus inside your own house first
issues.quote: Risk, ops, and exec each get the sheet with the risks named, not
issues.problem: No path for an internal decline or counter-structure, and no borrower communication for a decline.
issues.fix: Add a decline and counteroffer branch with a drafted borrower message held for approval.

scenarios.prompt: A $12M ARR SaaS founder wants a $3M growth term loan. Here are 12 months of P&L and bank statements. Our bands: up to 0.5x ARR, 36 months, SOFR+6-8%. Draft the underwriting read and term sheet.
scenarios.why: The skill leads to a sourced cash-flow read, a structure inside bands and a plain-terms sheet with internal review first. But it names no metrics (runway after the loan, burn multiple, ARR multiple, retention, customer concentration), no covenant levels and no term sheet sections (fees, prepayment, amortisation, warrants, reporting, events of default, expiry). The model would improvise below senior-lender quality.

scenarios.prompt: A California restaurant group wants a $400k revenue-based line. They only sent a revenue screenshot, there's an SBA loan with a blanket lien, and they want the offer today.
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly treats the screenshot as an attributed claim and lists the statements needed, and the approval gate blocks promises. But nothing prompts a lien search or subordination and intercreditor check against the SBA lender's blanket lien. Nothing flags California's commercial-financing disclosure requirement or licensing either. The model could draft a sheet that cannot legally or practically fund.

rfp-and-competitive-bid-response.job: respond to RFP or competitive bid
rfp-and-competitive-bid-response.summary: A 59-line checklist for formal bids that covers a four-question bid/no-bid call, a win strategy (buyer criteria, three discriminators, competitor counter, price posture), process discipline, answers graded compliant, partial or non-compliant, library reuse and bid-state tracking, with submission held for approval.
strengths: The bid/no-bid decision comes first, and a no-bid is one line with the reason and stops there.
The win strategy is framed in the buyer's own decision criteria, with proof per discriminator and pricing kept 'inside approved bands'.
Library reuse requires re-validation, and new answers are saved with their source and date.
It forbids backchanneling outside the stated procurement process and gates submission on an explicit yes.
Unverifiable requirements are marked UNKNOWN with a named owner rather than guessed.
missing: Compliance matrix template with requirement IDs and evaluation weights
Weighted bid/no-bid scorecard with threshold
Reverse-scheduled response calendar with color-team review gates
Price-to-win and pricing-structure compliance check
Terms and conditions exceptions list routed to counsel or deal desk
Executive summary and win themes mapped to evaluation criteria
Answer-library structure (content owner, last-verified date, expiry)
Post-award debrief request on win or loss
Handoff to Lena for security questionnaires

issues.quote: Answer the RFP requirement by requirement: compliant, partial with the gap
issues.problem: There is no requirements shred or compliance matrix. The model is never told to extract every shall/must, map each to its RFP section and evaluation weight, or track response location and owner, so requirements get missed and scoring is not addressed.
issues.fix: Add a first drafting step: shred the RFP into a compliance matrix (req ID, RFP section, requirement text, evaluation weight, compliance state, response location, owner, evidence source, status). Build it as an xlsx/csv in the sandbox and draft answers against it.

issues.quote: information), a security questionnaire, or a head-to-head competitive
issues.problem: Security questionnaires are claimed but get no procedure. The skill duplicates Lena's original security-questionnaire-answers skill, which has the evidence rules this one lacks: source document, version and date, never yes to a certification without evidence, and legal items on a separate list.
issues.fix: Either route questionnaires to security-questionnaire-answers (consult Lena) or import its evidence rules explicitly. Drop 'security questionnaire' from the triggers if routing.

issues.quote: Grade bid-or-no-bid first: do we meet the must-haves, is there a champion
issues.problem: 'Grade' has no scale, weights or threshold. It also omits the strongest predictors: whether we shaped the RFP or saw it coming, incumbent position, response cost and capacity against deal margin, and strategic value.
issues.fix: Add a weighted bid/no-bid scorecard (fit, relationship/shaping, competitive position, capacity, margin, strategic value) with a stated pass threshold, and require a written rationale for any override.

issues.quote: Track bid state per bid (drafting, in review, submitted, closed) with
issues.problem: States are tracked, but there is no calendar planned back from the due date and no review gates (pink/red/gold team, pricing and executive sign-off). 'In review' has no definition of who reviews what.
issues.fix: Add a reverse-scheduled bid calendar: Q&A deadline, section drafts, red-team review against evaluation criteria, pricing approval, legal review, final QA and a submission buffer. Name the approver per gate.

issues.problem: There is no handling of exceptions to the buyer's terms and conditions, contract deviations or pricing approvals. Bids routinely require a deviations list reviewed by legal or the deal desk before submission.
issues.fix: Add a step that builds the exceptions and deviations list and routes it to counsel or the deal desk (enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans) before pricing and terms are final.

issues.quote: named, or non-compliant with the workaround.
issues.problem: Pairing every non-compliance with a 'workaround' pushes the model to soften a no into a qualified yes, which evaluators penalise and which can create contractual exposure.
issues.fix: State that a no stays a no. Offer a workaround only when it is real, dated and approved, and never restate a non-compliance as partial.

issues.quote: bid answers, saved to file. Show the win strategy and the draft answers in
issues.problem: Showing all draft answers in chat does not scale to real RFPs. It also gives no file format or location, even though bids must return in the buyer's template.
issues.fix: Show the win strategy, bid/no-bid verdict, gaps and exceptions in chat. Write the full answer set into the buyer's template (docx/xlsx via the sandbox) as a workspace file.

issues.quote: Use when a formal bid lands: RFP, RFI, security questionnaire, or a head-to-head competitive deal that needs its win strategy.
issues.problem: The description overlaps the sibling industrial-pursuit-tender-handover (tender and bid deadline) and objection-and-negotiation (competition), with no boundary stated.
issues.fix: State the boundary in the description: document-driven bids and competitive win plans here, engineered and EPC tenders in industrial-pursuit, and live price or competitor pushback in objection-and-negotiation.

scenarios.prompt: A state university sent us a 120-requirement RFP for our LMS, due in three weeks. PDF attached, and our past answers are in a Drive folder. Should we bid, and can you draft the response?
scenarios.why: The 'Bid or no-bid' questions and the 'Answers and library' compliance states give a usable skeleton, and 'never backchannel' covers the public-sector quiet period. But there is no step to shred the PDF into a requirement-ID compliance matrix mapped to the evaluation criteria, and no calendar back from the due date (Q&A cutoff, internal draft, red-team review, pricing approval, submission buffer). 'Show the win strategy and the draft answers in chat' is impractical for 120 answers. A capable model produces decent prose but not a bid-manager-grade package.

scenarios.prompt: A SIG Lite spreadsheet (300 rows) came in on a competitive deal against Salesforce. Our SOC 2 Type II is still in progress. Answers are due Friday.
scenarios.why: 'A requirement nobody can verify means UNKNOWN with the owner' and 'Every claim carries its source' help. But the skill gives no rules for questionnaire evidence (document, version, date), no rule against answering yes to a certification without evidence, and no handling of an in-progress audit (bridge letter, target date). It says nothing about processing the xlsx in the sandbox or routing to the security owner or Lena's security-questionnaire-answers skill. 'non-compliant with the workaround' invites spin on a hard no.

sales-ops-coverage-and-quota.job: design sales coverage, quota and comp plan
sales-ops-coverage-and-quota.summary: A dense sales-ops playbook covering account tiering and book balancing, capacity modelling, top-down and bottom-up quota allocation with fairness validation and an annual planning calendar, comp design, tiered CRM hygiene and executive reporting, all behind an approval gate.
strengths: Capacity is sized to ramped reality, with 'the quota curve to the capacity, not the wish'.
The top-down vs bottom-up gap is named in dollars and resolved in the plan, not the forecast.
Pre-rollout validation covers attainment distribution, fairness across tenure, geo and territory size, and a backtest.
A single midyear change window with credit-transfer, proration and appeals rules is senior practice.
Hiring comes last after turnover, productivity and comp levers.
Inferred tiers are labelled INFERENCE, and nothing rep-facing or final ships without an explicit yes.
missing: Capacity and quota workbook template built in the sandbox
Quota over-assignment policy
OTE, pay mix, quota-to-OTE ratio and payout curve modelling
Crediting, split and account-transfer rules
Written comp plan document with acknowledgement and legal/HR review
Account potential scoring method (TAM, ICP fit, propensity)
A single ramp curve shared with sales-team-leadership
Rep-data privacy handling
Handoffs to Daniel (cost of sales, plan-to-budget) and James (headcount)

issues.section: Draft comp to the behavior you want
issues.quote: Base and variable mix, accelerators past 100 percent, sales incentive bonuses
issues.problem: Comp design is far too thin for the stakes. There is no OTE or pay mix by role, no quota-to-OTE ratio, no caps or decelerators, no crediting and split rules, no payout modelling at 50/100/150% attainment, no cost-of-sales check, and no requirement for a written, acknowledged plan reviewed by finance, HR and legal (several US states require written commission agreements).
issues.fix: Expand into a comp procedure: role pay mix and OTE, quota-to-OTE ratio, rate table and accelerators, crediting rules, payout scenarios modelled in the sandbox, cost-of-sales check with Daniel (finance), and a written plan document with legal/HR review before an approval gate.

issues.quote: Use when designing coverage, cutting books, allocating quota, setting comp, or cleaning CRM hygiene at scale.
issues.problem: Triggers collide with siblings. 'coverage' and 'quota' also trigger territory-and-account-planning, and 'CRM hygiene' is pipeline-review-and-forecast's job. The skill also carries executive reporting that the Monday and Wednesday routines already own.
issues.fix: Scope this to planning-cycle design (coverage model, capacity, quota, comp). Move CRM hygiene and weekly exec reporting to pipeline-review-and-forecast, and say so in the description.

issues.section: Segment the universe before cutting books
issues.quote: has a named owner and cadence: A-weekly, B-monthly, C-watched past roughly 25
issues.problem: This is ambiguous. It is unclear whether 25 is a book-size cap or the threshold at which C accounts move to a watch list. The '3-step overlap audit' and how potential and propensity are scored are never defined, so a model cannot execute them.
issues.fix: Define the tiering inputs and scoring method, the per-tier cadence, the maximum accounts per rep by segment, and spell out the three overlap-audit steps.

issues.quote: capacity at 100 percent of fully ramped reps plus 50 percent of new hires,
issues.problem: A flat 50% new-hire factor is presented as fact. It conflicts with the 40/75/100 ramp curve in sales-team-leadership and ignores start dates and attrition timing.
issues.fix: Model capacity month by month from actual start dates and the team's own ramp curve (default to one shared curve across Max's skills, labelled as an assumption). Compute it in the sandbox and show the assumptions table.

issues.section: Allocate quota top-down and bottom-up until they meet
issues.quote: Name the gap in dollars and resolve it in the plan, never in
issues.problem: Quota over-assignment (the buffer of rep quota above the company number) is never named. It is the standard way the gap is absorbed and the most common source of unfair quotas.
issues.fix: Add an explicit over-assignment policy (typical 10-20% above target, documented and approved) and a check that the total quota does not exceed modelled capacity.

issues.section: Allocate quota top-down and bottom-up until they meet
issues.quote: Validate before rollout: attainment must bell-curve around 100
issues.problem: 'Bell-curve around 100' is a loose validation rule. The usual health target is the share of reps at or above quota (often about 60-70%), and 'fairness whiskers' is unexplained jargon.
issues.fix: Replace it with named checks: percentage of reps at or above quota on the backtest, attainment distribution by segment, and a potential-to-quota ratio per book with a tolerance band.

issues.section: Report up in one exec read
issues.quote: Dashboards for the week, weekly and monthly business-review write-ups, and QBR
issues.problem: This is scope creep. Weekly dashboards and business reviews duplicate pipeline-review-and-forecast and Max's Monday and Wednesday routines, which bloats the skill.
issues.fix: Keep only the planning-cycle readout (coverage, capacity and quota pack for exec sign-off) and point weekly reporting to pipeline-review-and-forecast.

issues.quote: The coverage model with tiered books, the capacity model, the quota allocation
issues.problem: There are six deliverables but no template, columns or file format. Rep-level comp and attainment data is sensitive and the skill has no handling or sharing rule for it.
issues.fix: Define workbook tabs and columns for books, capacity and quota. Write them as a workspace xlsx. Restrict rep-level comp and attainment views to the owner and never store individual pay in memory.

scenarios.prompt: FY27 planning: 18 AEs, 4 more starting in Q1, a $24M company number. Here's the account list with firmographics and last year's attainment by rep. Cut the books and allocate quota.
scenarios.why: The steps are all present: segment, capacity, top-down/bottom-up, name the gap, validate with a backtest. But 'C-watched past roughly 25 accounts per rep' and the '3-step overlap audit' are undefined. New-hire capacity is a flat 50% rather than the 40/75/100 curve used in sales-team-leadership. Quota over-assignment is never mentioned. Nothing tells the model to build the capacity and allocation model in the sandbox as a reusable workbook. The result is directionally right but not a plan a RevOps lead could take into kickoff.

scenarios.prompt: Redesign our AE comp plan. Reps are sandbagging and we lost three top performers to competitors. The current plan PDF is attached, I don't have an attainment export yet, and kickoff is next week.
scenarios.why: 'Draft comp to the behavior you want' is four lines: base/variable mix, accelerators, SPIFs, clawbacks. There is no OTE or pay-mix guidance by role, no quota-to-OTE ratio, no anti-sandbagging mechanics (decelerators, rollover, quarterly vs annual measurement), no payout modelling at attainment bands, no cost-of-sales check, and no written-plan or legal/HR/finance review. The Fallbacks do not cover missing attainment data for comp. The model would produce generic advice.

sales-team-leadership.job: hire, ramp and coach sales reps
sales-team-leadership.summary: Covers the people side of sales management: hiring bar and structured loops, a 30/60/90 onboarding with cert gates and a ramp curve, evidence-based 1:1 call coaching, skill/will/fit diagnosis with a dated improvement plan, and a succession bench, all behind an approval gate.
strengths: The skill/will/fit diagnosis explicitly checks selling time and structural causes before judging the rep.
'Coach behaviors, never outcomes', with call scoring on quotes and one dated habit fix per week.
The repeat-miss escalation (two calls with the same miss becomes the week's drill) makes coaching systematic.
The improvement plan carries start and end dates, a review point, rep acknowledgement and a plain verdict.
The succession bench has a named successor, readiness gap and dated development plan per critical seat.
Nothing rep-facing, and no hire, plan or exit decision, is communicated without an explicit yes.
missing: HR involvement and 'not legal advice' boundary for PIPs and exits
Fair-hiring guardrails for loops and scorecards
Templates for scorecard, 1:1 coaching log and improvement plan
Rep-data privacy handling
Retention and flight-risk signals (stay conversations) for top performers
Book reassignment and customer continuity when a rep exits
Consult or handoff to Sofia or Harper for recruiting mechanics

issues.quote: co-write a dated 30-60-day improvement plan with the rep: goals that are
issues.problem: Formal improvement plans and 'exited' verdicts are employment actions. The skill never requires HR partnership, consistent documentation across comparable reps, or handling of leave and accommodation. It has no 'not legal advice' boundary, so a manager could issue a legally risky PIP.
issues.fix: Require an HR review before any formal plan or exit recommendation. Keep documentation factual and behaviour-based, exclude health and protected-class information, flag leave or accommodation situations for HR, and state that the skill is not legal advice.

issues.quote: Use when hiring, onboarding, coaching, or performance-managing sellers: hiring loops, ramp plans, 1:1s, improvement plans, and succession.
issues.problem: 'onboarding' and 'ramp plan' are also triggers of enablement-playbooks-certification, which owns the Learn/Apply/Lead curriculum. Hiring loops duplicate Sofia's role-intake-and-scorecard and hiring-debrief-and-decision and Harper's hiring-rubric-design.
issues.fix: Scope this to the individual rep: the sales-specific hiring bar, a per-rep ramp plan, 1:1 coaching, performance plans and succession. Leave curriculum to enablement and loop logistics to a consult with Sofia, and remove the generic 'onboarding' trigger.

issues.quote: No scorecard means you draft the bar from the top rep's
issues.problem: A top-rep profile is not a job-related bar. It invites similarity bias, and the skill has no fair-hiring rules: consistent questions, no protected-characteristic questions, and evidence-anchored scoring.
issues.fix: Draft the bar from role outcomes and observable competencies, using top-rep behaviours only as evidence. Add fair-hiring guardrails or defer to Sofia's scorecard skill.

issues.quote: the productive activities that close the FACT gap
issues.problem: 'FACT gap' is undefined here and collides with the FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labelling convention the persona uses, which confuses the model.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain language, for example 'the activity gap between current and required pipeline behaviours', or define the acronym.

issues.quote: quarters on a 40/75/100 quota curve or pipeline-first target, weighted by
issues.problem: The ramp benchmark is stated as fact and conflicts with sales-ops-coverage-and-quota's flat 50% new-hire capacity factor.
issues.fix: Label it a default assumption, prefer the company's own ramp data, and share one curve across both skills.

issues.quote: for the same reason means the bar is wrong, not the candidates.
issues.problem: This oversimplifies. Repeated passes can also mean a sourcing or comp-band problem, and the rule could push the bar down.
issues.fix: Treat three same-reason passes as a trigger to review the bar, the sourcing channel and the comp band, and record which one changed.

issues.quote: The scorecard and loop plan with debrief record, the 30/60/90 with
issues.problem: Five artifacts are named, but none has a template or fields (for example, 1:1 log columns or improvement-plan sections), so output varies run to run.
issues.fix: Add short templates in references/ for the scorecard, 1:1 coaching log and improvement-plan document.

issues.problem: There is no privacy rule for rep performance, call and coaching data. It could be saved to shared memory or shown to teammates.
issues.fix: State that rep-level performance records stay with the manager, are not stored in shared memory, and are shared only with HR on request.

scenarios.prompt: Jordan on my team is at 38% of quota at mid-year. Here are his last five call transcripts and his CRM activity. Help me work out what's wrong and put a plan together.
scenarios.why: 'Improvement plans' tells the model to diagnose skill, will or fit, check selling time and structural causes first, score calls with quotes, and co-write a SMART plan with weekly check-ins, a 6-8 week review and written acknowledgement, which is strong. But there is no step to involve HR before a formal plan, no guidance on consistent documentation or accommodations, and 'the FACT gap' is undefined. The result is good coaching but not HR-safe performance management.

scenarios.prompt: I need to hire three enterprise AEs by Q1. I have no scorecard, and my VP also wants to know who backfills me if I'm promoted.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks say to 'draft the bar from the top rep's profile', which risks encoding non-job-related traits and cloning bias with no fair-hiring check. Loop mechanics are a sentence each, while Sofia's role-intake-and-scorecard and hiring-debrief-and-decision do this in depth, and no consult or handoff is named. The succession section covers the backfill question adequately.

showroom-fi-and-internet-bdc.job: run dealership showroom, F&I and BDC flow
showroom-fi-and-internet-bdc.summary: A short vertical playbook for car-dealership or big-ticket retail selling: one staged deal flow, BDC speed-to-lead with escalation, demo debrief, F&I 'as part of the sale', a referral log and a manager report, with no price, payment or rate promised without approval.
strengths: A single staged deal board where every deal has one stage, a dated next step and an owner.
A missed lead-response window escalates to the manager rather than 'aged quietly'.
The test-drive debrief records the one reason to buy and the one remaining objection.
'Numbers are FACT from the CRM, never recall', plus an explicit gate on promising price, payment or rate.
missing: Contact-consent and DNC checks for calls and texts
Rules for handling credit-application data
F&I menu-selling, consent and cancellation procedure with compliance escalation
Desking and trade-appraisal step
Inventory feed and aged-unit tie-in to lead routing
Dealership KPI set (PVR, penetration, closing ratio by source, days' supply)
Equity mining and lease-maturity outreach
CSI and delivery follow-up
Templates for the deal board, BDC log and F&I checklist

issues.quote: speed-to-lead target, script-led calls and emails, credit-app flow where it
issues.problem: The BDC outreach has no consent rules: express consent for automated calls and texts, opt-out handling, DNC lists and quiet hours. The credit-app flow also has no rule for handling customer financial information (SSNs, income) under data-safeguards requirements, so the model may ask for or store it in chat.
issues.fix: Add a consent check before any SMS or call draft, honour opt-outs and DNC, and never collect or store credit-application data in chat or memory. Route applicants to the dealer's secure credit-app portal.

issues.section: F&I as part of the sale
issues.quote: disclose plainly, and keep the docs checklist exact.
issues.problem: F&I is reduced to a slogan. There is no menu presentation of every product with and without add-ons, no documented voluntary consent per product, no rule against payment packing, no adverse-action or rate-markup awareness, no cancellation or refund path, and no escalation to compliance. State rules on add-ons (for example California's CARS Act) are ignored.
issues.fix: Add an F&I procedure: menu with base payment shown, signed opt-in per product, cancellation and refund handling, a docs-and-funding checklist with lender stipulations, and escalation to the dealer's compliance officer on any dispute. Mark it 'not legal advice'.

issues.quote: Report to the manager in their format: units, gross, lead response times,
issues.problem: The report misses the standard dealership KPIs: front and back gross per unit, F&I PVR and product penetration, closing ratio by lead source, appointment show rate, and days' supply or aged-inventory units. A manager would find it thin.
issues.fix: List the default KPI set with definitions, computed in the sandbox from the export, and label benchmarks as assumptions.

issues.quote: Use for high-velocity vehicle or big-ticket retail where the showroom floor, the finance and insurance desk, and the internet team share one deal flow.
issues.problem: Max's persona is a B2B Account Executive ('Researches prospects, drafts outreach... through signature'). A dealership floor, BDC and F&I motion is a different job, and 'big-ticket retail' is vague enough to misfire on furniture or appliance retail questions.
issues.fix: Move this to a vertical automotive retail expert, or tighten the description to franchise or independent vehicle dealers and add a boundary line in Max's persona.

issues.quote: Run one deal flow from hello to delivery: lot engagement, needs, demo or
issues.problem: The 'numbers' stage ignores desking and trade appraisal (ACV, payoff, equity). There is also no inventory-aware step to match leads to stock or flag aged units.
issues.fix: Add desking and trade-appraisal steps plus an inventory-feed check (in stock, days in stock) before the demo is booked.

issues.quote: Build the referral and repeat engine: ask every delivered buyer, log the
issues.problem: Owner-base work on a 'dated rotation' misses the highest-yield dealership play: equity mining from service-lane and lease-maturity data.
issues.fix: Add equity and lease-maturity mining from the DMS or service export, with consent-checked outreach.

issues.quote: The staged deal board with dated next steps, the BDC response log with
issues.problem: None of the five artifacts has fields or a template (for example, the docs checklist contents or the response log columns).
issues.fix: Ship templates in references/ for the deal board, BDC log and F&I docs checklist.

scenarios.prompt: Here's yesterday's VinSolutions lead export: 42 internet leads. Tell me which ones didn't get a response within 15 minutes, draft the BDC texts and emails, and give the GSM the morning report.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks allow working from a pasted export, 'BDC speed' escalates missed windows, and the scripts get manager approval. But nothing checks texting or calling consent or opt-outs before drafting SMS, and there is no lead-source breakdown. The manager report lists only units, gross, response times and set/show, with no closing ratio by source, front/back gross or aged-inventory tie-in. The output is usable but not what a BDC director would sign off.

scenarios.prompt: A deal funded short because the lender wants proof of income. The F&I manager sold a service contract and GAP, and now the customer says they never agreed to GAP. What do we do?
scenarios.why: The only guidance is 'disclose plainly' and 'A funding delay gets an owner and a date'. There is nothing on product cancellation or refund, menu and consent documentation, payment-packing risk, compliance or legal escalation, or state-specific add-on rules. Following the skill yields a dated to-do, not a compliant resolution.

signature-to-launch-and-account-ops.job: run post-signature customer onboarding and launch
signature-to-launch-and-account-ops.summary: Turns a signed deal into a launch plan with exit-tested milestones, runs a cross-team onboarding tracker and per-site activation view, and maintains account-ops records (SOP, rate file, contacts, contract log). It then adds health guardrails, a white-space expansion table, an exec-sponsor plan and a multi-threading rule, with buyer-facing dates gated on approval.
strengths: Every milestone has one owner, one date, and entry and exit criteria, and moves only when the exit test passes.
'The buyer sees one plan, not five queues' is the right orchestration stance.
Stale artifacts are flagged with a last-verified date rather than trusted.
'Launch health first, upsell second' prevents premature expansion pitches.
Buyer-side gaps are drafted blank for confirmation, and no launch date or SLA is promised without a yes.
missing: Launch charter with customer success criteria and first-value metric
RAID log
Change-request and scope-control process
Go-live readiness checklist and hypercare exit criteria
Escalation matrix including finance and legal for commercial disputes
Formal handoff to the CS or support owner after hypercare
Tracker and launch-plan templates

issues.quote: Use after signature to run onboarding, implementation, and the standing account-ops artifacts that keep the account healthy.
issues.problem: This overlaps next-step-and-handoff (won deal passed to implementation), renewal-expansion-and-qbr (health and expansion), exec-engagement-and-sponsorship (exec-sponsor plan) and multithread-and-stakeholder-maps. Across experts it overlaps Robin's onboarding-and-adoption and Riley's customer-onboarding-plan. The 'white-space' trigger also collides with territory-and-account-planning.
issues.fix: Scope this to launch and implementation coordination through go-live and hypercare. Drop the 'white-space' trigger and point expansion to renewal-expansion-and-qbr, exec cadence to exec-engagement, and post-launch adoption to the support/CS expert.

issues.section: Feed expansion back, then build white-space
issues.quote: stable. Launch health first, upsell second. Once stable, build the enterprise
issues.problem: The white-space table and quarterly exec-sponsor plan are scope creep that re-implement parts of renewal-expansion-and-qbr and exec-engagement-and-sponsorship in a launch skill.
issues.fix: Replace the section with a one-line handoff: once launch exit criteria pass, hand to renewal-expansion-and-qbr for expansion and exec-engagement-and-sponsorship for the sponsor program.

issues.section: Turn signature into a launch plan within days
issues.quote: Kickoff date, owners per side, milestone dates, and the go-live or first-value
issues.problem: The plan never captures the customer's success criteria or first-value metric, and there is no RAID (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies) log, change-control process for scope drift, go-live readiness checklist or hypercare period.
issues.fix: Add a launch charter step (customer outcome, first-value metric, acceptance criteria), a RAID log, a change-request rule routed to the deal desk, and a go-live checklist with a defined hypercare window and exit.

issues.quote: The SOP, the rate file, the contact list, and the contract upkeep log
issues.problem: The rate file, customs and site activation are logistics-specific artifacts left over from the source role. For a SaaS or services user they are unexplained and may produce irrelevant outputs.
issues.fix: Generalise to 'the operating runbook, commercial terms reference, contact and escalation list, and contract log', with the logistics variants as conditional examples.

issues.quote: Ops, implementation, customer success, and customs or compliance where they
issues.problem: 'You run the tracker' sits uneasily with the persona's boundary that engineering implementation is out of scope. It is unclear whether Max coordinates or owns delivery, and there is no named handoff to the implementation or CS owner.
issues.fix: State that Max coordinates the tracker and buyer communications, while delivery teams own execution. Name the handoff point to CS or support after hypercare.

issues.section: Hold account-health guardrails in every review
issues.quote: Metric performance, revenue quality, and pay and contract-terms adherence. A
issues.problem: A breach gets a 'dated correction', but there is no escalation matrix. SLA credits, invoice disputes and contract-term breaches need finance or legal involvement, not only an owner and a date.
issues.fix: Add escalation tiers: owner, then sponsors, then finance or legal for commercial or contractual breaches, with approval before any credit or concession is offered.

issues.section: Feed expansion back, then build white-space
issues.quote: Multi-thread every key account across 3 to 5
issues.problem: This contradicts multithread-and-stakeholder-maps, which sets four or more threads over $50K and five to seven with dual sponsors over $150K. The same expert gives two different rules.
issues.fix: Remove it here and defer to multithread-and-stakeholder-maps as the single source.

issues.quote: The launch plan with dated milestones, the onboarding tracker across teams,
issues.problem: Six artifacts are named, but none has columns or a template, and nothing says where the tracker lives (Sheets, Notion or Linear blocks exist).
issues.fix: Ship a launch-plan and tracker template, and offer to create it through the Sheets or Notion block with a CSV fallback.

scenarios.prompt: We just signed Acme Logistics: a three-year deal across 12 warehouse sites with a January 15 go-live target. Build the launch plan and onboarding tracker.
scenarios.why: 'Turn signature into a launch plan' and 'Track implementations line by line' give milestones with owners, dates, exit tests and a per-site tracker. The Fallbacks correctly leave buyer-side owners blank to confirm. But it never asks for the customer's success criteria or time-to-first-value measure, and there is no RAID log, go-live readiness checklist or hypercare window.
