The plan will look tidy but lacks the risk and acceptance scaffolding an implementation lead expects.

scenarios.prompt: Three of the 12 sites are six weeks late because their IT hasn't provisioned SSO. Their COO is threatening to withhold the second invoice, and my VP wants an expansion plan for their EU business unit this quarter.
scenarios.why: 'Launch health first, upsell second' resolves the conflicting asks well, and a breach gets a dated correction with an owner. But there is no escalation path for a customer-caused delay (change order, re-baselined dates, sponsor escalation), and no routing of the invoice dispute to finance or legal. The white-space table would be built regardless, and it duplicates territory and renewal skills.

territory-and-account-planning.job: write territory and named-account sales plans
territory-and-account-planning.summary: Builds a territory plan in five parts (motion, tiers, coverage map, pipe-gen targets, risks) and named-account plans in seven parts (status, why buy, buying roles, blockers, next three meetings, 30/60/90, change signals). It opens with a numbers pass on coverage, a commit gate and forecast accuracy, labels assumptions, and saves after one edit round.
strengths: The seven-part account plan with a full buying-role list and 'the signals that would change the plan' is practical and reusable.
The territory plan ends with top three risks and what would prove or kill each.
'Why they would buy (in the account's own words)' keeps the plan buyer-centred.
Assumptions are labelled in place and listed up front when there are more than a couple.
Plans stay internal, and anything shared with the buyer waits for a yes.
missing: Account tiering criteria and scoring
Rep-capacity check against book size
Backward funnel math from quota to pipe-gen targets by tier
Whitespace matrix with sizing
Quarterly operating plan variant
Fallback for unknown win rate
Account research inputs (strategic priorities from filings or news) and competitive presence
Plan templates and a defined save location
Pointers to research-an-account and multithread-and-stakeholder-maps for the buying-role section

issues.quote: Every number is ledger-sourced or UNKNOWN,
issues.problem: Planning requires estimates: pipe-gen targets, whitespace sizing and tier potential. The 'never estimated' rule contradicts the 'Assumptions up front' section and leaves the model unsure whether it may set targets at all.
issues.fix: Require sourcing for actuals only, and allow targets and sizing as labelled ASSUMPTION or INFERENCE with the method shown.

issues.quote: Coverage target is 1 over the historical win rate (floor 3x; enterprise
issues.problem: This duplicates pipeline-review-and-forecast and contradicts it: that skill flags under 3x and alarms under 2x, while this one uses 1/win-rate with a 3x floor and alarms 1x below target. The commit gate and forecast-accuracy formula are forecast-review work, not planning.
issues.fix: Move the commit gate and accuracy scoring to pipeline-review-and-forecast. Define one coverage rule for all of Max's skills, and keep only 'pipe needed to hit quota' in planning.

issues.quote: "coverage", "whitespace", "quota", "GTM", "30-60-90"
issues.problem: These triggers collide with pipeline-review-and-forecast ('coverage'), sales-ops-coverage-and-quota ('quota', 'coverage model'), regional-category-gtm-strategy and go-to-market-strategy ('GTM'), and sales-team-leadership (30/60/90 ramp), so the wrong skill will load.
issues.fix: Use specific triggers: 'territory plan', 'account plan', 'named account plan', 'whitespace map', 'book of business plan', 'quarter plan'.

issues.quote: its effort, the coverage map of who works what, the pipe-gen targets per
issues.problem: There are no tiering criteria, no rep-capacity check and no backward funnel math. The persona's routines use backward funnel math, but this skill never shows how pipe-gen targets derive from quota, win rate, deal size and cycle.
issues.fix: Add tiering inputs (ICP fit, potential, engagement), an accounts-per-rep capacity check, and backward math (quota ÷ win rate ÷ average deal = opportunities needed per quarter, by tier) computed in the sandbox.

issues.quote: pipe over quota, and whitespace where they have presence but no deal.
issues.problem: This whitespace definition is shallow: there is no product × business-unit matrix and no sizing. signature-to-launch-and-account-ops builds a separate white-space table, so two skills own whitespace.
issues.fix: Own the whitespace matrix here (products × BUs or regions, with size and evidence) and have signature-to-launch point to it.

issues.quote: Write the territory plan in five short parts: the go-to-market motion per
issues.problem: The description promises 'the quarter', but there is no quarterly operating plan section with weekly pipe-gen and activity targets, key dates or a review cadence.
issues.fix: Add a short quarter-plan variant, or remove 'the quarter' from the description.

issues.quote: No CRM access means you plan from their export or pasted numbers and say
issues.problem: There is no fallback when the historical win rate is unknown (new rep, new segment), even though the coverage target depends on it.
issues.fix: Fall back to team or segment win rate if available, otherwise a labelled assumption (for example a 3x floor), and flag it for recalibration after one quarter.

issues.quote: and only then write it to the plan location.
issues.problem: 'The plan location' is never defined, and there is no template file.
issues.fix: Ask for or default to a workspace path (or a Docs/Notion block), and ship territory and account plan templates in references/.

scenarios.prompt: I just inherited the Northeast mid-market territory: 140 accounts, $1.8M quota. Here's the Salesforce export. Build my territory plan and account plans for my top five.
scenarios.why: The five-part territory plan and seven-part account plan give a solid shape, and the Fallbacks handle an export. But there are no tiering criteria, no rep-capacity check on how many accounts one rep can truly work, and no backward funnel math from quota to pipe-gen targets. The 'Every number is ledger-sourced or UNKNOWN, never estimated' rule may block the pipe-gen targets and whitespace sizing the plan needs. The model spends its opening on commit-gate and accuracy checks that belong to the forecast review.

scenarios.prompt: Build my Q3 plan and a 30-60-90. I'm new with no history, my win rate is unknown, half the opportunities in the export have no amount, and my manager wants it by Monday.
scenarios.why: Missing amounts correctly become UNKNOWN. But the coverage target depends on 'the historical win rate' with no fallback beyond a 3x floor. The description promises a quarter plan and the '30-60-90' trigger fires, yet the only 30/60/90 is per account, and a new-rep 30-60-90 belongs to sales-team-leadership. The model has to improvise the quarter plan.

monthly-investor-update.summary: Gives a fixed eight-section structure for a monthly investor update drafted from approved, dated records, with rules for provisional figures and definition changes, a pre-release approval checklist, and a never-send rule.
strengths: The fixed structure gives misses the same weight as wins: target, actual, cause or open hypothesis, and owner action.
It keeps forecasts, targets and actuals apart, and when a metric definition changes it must either show both definitions or drop the comparison.
It asks for specific help (a named introduction, a candidate profile, an expert question) rather than a vague request.
Its safety rules are strong: never send, never invent a metric, cause, quote or milestone, and route legal, securities and disclosure questions to counsel.
Under 50 lines with no filler.
missing: A report back on last month's asks and a thank-you to those who helped
Required cash, net burn, runway and fundraising-status rows
The same KPI set each month, kept in memory
Separate handling for existing shareholders and prospective investors
A rule for conflicting sources
A template with a subject line, a length target and an example
Tool steps: Sheets or Stripe through run_block with a CSV fallback, bash_exec calculations, a Gmail draft after approval, and a monthly routine through schedule_routine

issues.quote: only approved figures, periods, and scenario labels.
issues.problem: Cash is treated as optional context. Experienced operators report cash on hand, net burn, runway in months (with its assumption) and fundraising status in every update. Leaving them optional lets a runway problem go unmentioned.
issues.fix: Make cash, net burn, runway in months (with assumptions) and fundraising status required rows. Mark any that are missing as OPEN and ask the finance owner for them.

issues.quote: Check names, figures, periods, links, customer permissions, board-sensitive
issues.problem: The skill never separates existing shareholders from prospective investors or people the update might be forwarded to. Sending the update to prospects is a different communication with confidentiality and securities-solicitation implications.
issues.fix: Ask up front whether the audience is existing investors, prospects or both. For prospects, stop and route to counsel and the finance owner. Add a 'do not forward' line.

issues.quote: Require the reporting period, prior update, approved KPI table with definitions,
issues.problem: Everything is listed as required, with no step for when an item is missing, which is common. The model will either stall or draft around the gap without saying so.
issues.fix: Split the inputs into blocking (period, KPI table, audience) and optional ones. Collect missing items with ask_question and draft the rest with OPEN markers.

issues.quote: Record each source and cutoff date.
issues.problem: The skill records sources but gives no rule for when two sources disagree (billing export versus finance sheet). The sibling skill board-and-investor-metrics-brief has that rule; this one does not.
issues.fix: Add: 'If two sources disagree, report both with their cutoffs and ask the finance owner which one governs; never pick one silently.'

issues.problem: There are no tool steps and no fallbacks. It never says to pull KPIs from Google Sheets or Stripe through run_block (or ask for a CSV), do the change maths in bash_exec, save the last update and KPI set in memory, or create a Gmail draft only after approval.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Sources and tools' step covering run_block Sheets and Stripe with a CSV fallback, bash_exec for the calculations, memory_store and memory_search for continuity, and a Gmail draft only after explicit approval.

issues.quote: named introduction, candidate profile, expert question, or other
issues.problem: The skill never reports back on last month's asks. Thanking investors who helped and saying what their help produced is standard practice and brings more help next time.
issues.fix: Add a line reporting on last month's asks: who helped, the outcome, and what is still open.

issues.quote: current, prior, change, definition, and source.
issues.problem: Nothing requires the same KPI set every month. Swapping metrics from month to month is a known credibility killer.
issues.fix: Keep a fixed KPI set in memory, and flag any metric added or dropped with the reason.

issues.problem: There is no guidance on format or length (email versus doc, subject line, a TL;DR that fits on one screen) and no template or example, so the style will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship a templates/investor-update.md with a subject line, a TL;DR of at most 3 bullets, the eight sections, and a worked example.

scenarios.prompt: Draft our September investor update. Attached: the KPI sheet (MRR, net burn, cash, customers), August's update, and our asks: intros to two Series A leads in climate and help finding a senior backend engineer.
scenarios.why: The 'Gather the update pack' step records sources and the cutoff date. The fixed structure covers metrics (current, prior, change, definition, source), misses with an owner action, and asks as named profiles. 'Review before release' returns an approval checklist and the audience. Two gaps: nothing puts runway up front or reports what happened with August's asks. The draft would still be credible and safe.

scenarios.prompt: Stripe shows $182k MRR but finance's sheet says $171k, our activation definition changed mid-month, runway is down to 5 months, and I also want to BCC two prospective investors on this update.
scenarios.why: The definition-change rule ('show both definitions or stop the comparison') and the provisional labels handle activation. But the skill has no rule for two sources that disagree, so the model may quietly pick one MRR figure. 'Cash context' is framed as optional approved context, so a 5-month runway may be understated. The recipient check is generic and never says that sending to prospects is a different, counsel-reviewed communication.

pitch-deck-review.summary: Reviews a pitch deck against company records along a seven-question investor decision path, builds a FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN claim table with consistency checks, and returns the five highest-impact fixes with replacement copy.
strengths: The FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN claim table with source and source date makes the review something others can check and audit.
Its reconciliation checks go beyond style feedback: metric definitions across slides, numerator and denominator, chart units, period and sample.
It follows the investor's decision path rather than forcing a fixed slide order.
It ranks fixes by their effect on trust, with replacement copy or chart instructions, and puts style notes last.
Its guardrails suit Theo: no valuation or terms advice, approval required for logos and quotes, forecasts presented as scenarios.
missing: Checks for why now, competition, go-to-market and unit economics
Stage and investor-type calibration
Use of funds tied to milestones and runway to the next round
A skim test: slide titles written as assertions, readable in 3 minutes
A bottom-up market sizing check
A way to read the deck (PDF, PPTX, Slides, DocSend) and web checks of market sources
An output template with a readiness verdict
A rule on keeping the deck confidential

issues.quote: Check whether the deck answers:
issues.problem: The decision path leaves out why now, competition and alternatives, go-to-market or distribution, and unit economics. These are standard investor questions, so a deck missing them passes the review.
issues.fix: Add why now, competition and alternatives with a basis for differentiation, go-to-market motion, and unit economics as appropriate for the stage.

issues.quote: Review the deck against the approved company records. Improve clarity without
issues.problem: The inputs are never listed up front: the deck file, round stage and size, target investor type, whether the deck is sent ahead or presented live, and the source metrics. There is also no path for the common case where only the deck is supplied.
issues.fix: Add an 'Inputs' step that asks for the deck, stage, raise, audience and metrics export. If the records are missing, proceed with every metric claim marked OPEN and list the records needed.

issues.problem: The skill never says how to read the deck (a PDF or PPTX through read_workspace_file plus bash_exec text extraction, Google Slides through run_block, DocSend through the browser). It never says to check cited market sources with web_search, or to keep the confidential deck out of third-party tools.
issues.fix: Add a short ingestion step with those routes and a fallback of asking for a PDF export, plus a confidentiality line.

issues.quote: What the company is raising, for what period and uses.
issues.problem: The ask is not tied to the milestones it buys or to runway before the next round, which is the core test investors apply to use of funds.
issues.fix: Check that use of funds maps to named milestones and runway of about 18–24 months before the next round, and label any assumptions.

issues.problem: There is no stage calibration (pre-seed, seed, Series A) and no audience lens (lead VC, angel, strategic). The same deck gets the same critique whatever the round.
issues.fix: Add a short stage-expectations table in references/ and ask which round and audience the deck is for.

issues.quote: market figures cite a current source and method.
issues.problem: It checks that a source is cited but not whether the sizing method is sound (a top-down TAM only, with no bottom-up customers × ACV check).
issues.fix: Require a bottom-up cross-check or mark the market claim as an INFERENCE.

issues.quote: Lead with the five changes that most affect trust or understanding. For each,
issues.problem: The output has no overall readiness verdict, no slide-by-slide notes and no headline or skim test (slide titles written as assertions), and it ships no template.
issues.fix: Add an output template: a readiness verdict, the top five fixes, the claim table, slide notes, and open questions with an owner for each.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our seed deck (PDF) and the metrics export. Tear it apart before we start sending it to funds next week.
scenarios.why: The evidence pass (claim table, definitions consistent across slides, chart units, numerator and denominator checks, logo permissions) and the top-five edits with replacement copy would be senior-grade. But the seven-question decision path leaves out why now, competition and alternatives, and go-to-market. A deck missing a competition slide or a go-to-market story can get through unflagged, and the output has no overall readiness verdict.

scenarios.prompt: I only have the Google Slides link to our Series A deck, no data room yet. The TAM slide cites a 2019 Gartner $50B figure, and ARR is $1.2M on slide 3 but $1.4M on slide 9.
scenarios.why: The consistency check catches the ARR mismatch, and 'cite a current source and method' flags the 2019 TAM figure. With no records, claims correctly become OPEN. But the skill gives no way to read the deck (a run_block Google Slides read, or asking for a PDF export), no bottom-up market sizing check, and no Series A calibration (for example, whether the traction supports a Series A).

board-deck-builder.summary: Supplies an 11-section, C-suite-owned SaaS board deck structure with a fill-in template, a four-act narrative, a bad-news framework and reference benchmarks, but no step for gathering inputs and no approval gate.
strengths: The complete fill-in template (templates/board-deck-template.md) uses [TBD] instead of invented numbers.
The four-act narrative (where we said we'd be, where we are, why the gap, what we're doing) and the bad-news framework reflect real board practice.
It insists that forecasts carry confidence levels and that asks name a specific person or introduction.
It gives cadence guidance (quarterly, monthly, when to meet more often).
Its good and bad example sentences teach the tone concretely.
missing: An input-gathering step and a rule for dropping sections with no owner or data
An approval gate, confidentiality labels and privileged-session handling
Governance items: consent agenda, minutes, option grants, resolutions routed to counsel, executive session
Metric sets for businesses that aren't SaaS
A rendering path (Google Slides or Docs through run_block, or PPTX) and a check that every figure ties to its source
Carrying forward last meeting's action items and a post-meeting follow-up draft
Handoff to Daniel for the numbers and consult_teammate for section owners

issues.quote: Assembles comprehensive board and investor update decks by pulling perspectives from all C-suite roles.
issues.problem: The upstream C-suite advisor skills this relies on do not exist here. 'Investor updates' and 'fundraising narratives' in the description collide with monthly-investor-update, pitch-deck-review, board-and-investor-metrics-brief and finance-board-and-investor-reporting, so which skill loads is ambiguous.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to board-meeting decks (quarterly or monthly), exclude investor emails and pitch decks, and replace 'C-suite roles' with 'section owners or teammates via consult_teammate'.

issues.quote: Ask for a board deck in natural language, naming cadence and stage:
issues.problem: This is written to the user. The model gets no ordered procedure: collect the stage, cadence, prior deck and targets, metric sources and section owners; choose which sections apply; draft the text; tie out the figures; get approval.
issues.fix: Replace Quick Start with a 6-step procedure that names the inputs, a rule for dropping sections that have no owner or data, a tie-out check, and an approval step.

issues.quote: Full deck, all sections, 20-30 slides. Sent 48 hours in advance.
issues.problem: It schedules distribution with no approval gate. There is no board-confidential or privileged handling and no rule to label figures as final, management draft or provisional.
issues.fix: Add a Guardrails section: draft only, the CEO or finance owner approves before anything is sent, figures carry a status label, privileged items go in a separate counsel-reviewed section, and nothing goes out without explicit approval.

issues.quote: Key decisions needed from the board
issues.problem: There are no governance mechanics: a consent agenda, minutes approval, option grants or 409A, counsel-drafted resolutions, an executive session. For Theo, recommending on financing or terms breaches his persona boundaries.
issues.fix: Add an 'Approvals and resolutions' slide routed to counsel, and state that deal-term and financing decisions are presented as options without a recommendation.

issues.problem: The worked example numbers do not tie out. ARR going from $1.97M to $2.4M (the same figures as the reference waterfall) gives about 99.7% NRR, not 112%, and 8.1% MoM growth compounds to about 26% QoQ, not the 22% in the summary. This teaches the model to present numbers that don't reconcile.
issues.fix: Make the illustrative numbers consistent or clearly mark them as unrelated placeholders.

issues.quote: Opens with market/vision, closes with ask. See `references/deck-frameworks.md` for Sequoia format.
issues.problem: Fundraising decks are a different deliverable and belong to pitch-deck-review. The reference also calls Sequoia's pitch template a board-deck structure and credits burn-multiple benchmarks to Point Nine.
issues.fix: Remove fundraising from scope and fix the attributions in references/deck-frameworks.md.

issues.quote: ARR waterfall: starting → new → expansion → churn → ending
issues.problem: The whole structure assumes venture-backed SaaS, with no metric set for services, marketplace, hardware or usage-based businesses.
issues.fix: Add a short metric-set chooser by business model in references/ and ask for the model up front.

issues.quote: board deck, investor update, board meeting, board pack, investor relations, quarterly review
issues.problem: The loader never reads the Keywords section, and the bad-news and cadence material is repeated in references/deck-frameworks.md, which wastes tokens.
issues.fix: Move keywords into the triggers frontmatter, remove the packaging banner, and keep one copy of the bad-news framework.

scenarios.prompt: Build our Q3 board deck. We're a Series A SaaS company; here's the metrics sheet and last quarter's deck.
scenarios.why: The template gives a clean 10-slide draft, and the four-act frame compares results to last quarter's targets. But no step gathers inputs or drops sections, so the CTO, CHRO and CISO slides fill with [TBD]. There is no consent agenda or approval items (minutes, option grants), no draft-and-approve step, and no rendering to Google Slides.

scenarios.prompt: We missed Q3 ARR by 18%, runway is 7 months, our CFO just left and we're negotiating a bridge note. Prep the board deck. We're a services-plus-software business and don't track NRR.
scenarios.why: The bad-news framework and the scenario table (a key exec leaving, a delayed fundraise) fit well, and the cadence notes say to meet more often near 6 months of runway. But the metrics assume SaaS (ARR waterfall, NRR). Nothing routes bridge-note terms to counsel or keeps negotiation details in a privileged session. The template's 'recommendation: [A/B]' invites Theo to recommend deal terms, which his boundaries forbid.

multi-source-research-synthesis.job: synthesize multi-source search results with citations
multi-source-research-synthesis.summary: Anthropic's upstream enterprise-search guidance for turning already-retrieved chat, email, document and tracker results into a deduplicated, cited, confidence-weighted answer, written with unresolved ~~category placeholders.
strengths: Its dedupe signals and a 'what NOT to deduplicate' list keep differing viewpoints and different versions of a decision separate.
It requires every claim to carry a source, location and date.
It scales the answer format to the number of results (1–5, 5–15, 15+).
It shows concrete wording for high, moderate and low confidence and for conflicting sources.
It leads with the answer and groups by topic, not by source.
missing: A 'Use when' trigger and a name that matches the scope
A retrieval plan and a coverage statement (what was and wasn't searched)
Authority tiers for public and web sources and an independence check
Freshness thresholds that depend on claim type
Access and privacy scope and a prompt-injection rule
Normalizing numbers (units, periods, currency) when sources give different figures
A mapping of source types to AutoGPT blocks and MCP tools, with a paste or export fallback

issues.quote: Combines search results from multiple sources into coherent, deduplicated answers with source attribution.
issues.problem: There is no 'Use when' clause. The name suggests web research, but the body is internal enterprise-search synthesis ('The last mile of enterprise search'), so the skill loads for the wrong requests or not at all.
issues.fix: Rename it or scope it: 'Use when answering a question from several workspace sources (Slack, Gmail, Drive, Notion, Linear) or when combining several web results.' Add triggers.

issues.quote: Always name the source type (~~chat, ~~email, ~~cloud storage, etc.)
issues.problem: These are unresolved upstream plugin placeholders. The body never points to references/CONNECTORS.md, which lists Microsoft 365 and Guru rather than AutoGPT blocks and links to an external .mcp.json. The model may put '~~chat' into user-facing answers.
issues.fix: Replace the placeholders with real source names (Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Linear, web) and point to the run_block or run_mcp_tool route for each. Rewrite or drop CONNECTORS.md.

issues.quote: [Raw results from all sources]
issues.problem: The workflow starts from results that are already in hand. There is no step to scope the question, plan queries across sources, notice gaps, or state what was not searched, so the answer can look more complete than it is.
issues.fix: Add step 0: scope, source plan and queries. End with a coverage line: 'Searched: …; not searched or not connected: …'. Use connect_integration or ask for an export when a source is missing.

issues.quote: | Official wiki / knowledge base | Highest — curated, maintained |
issues.problem: The authority tiers cover only internal sources. There are none for public or web sources (primary filings, company or fund site, regulator, press, aggregators, forums) and no check that corroborating sources are independent rather than syndicated copies.
issues.fix: Add a public-source tier table and a rule that syndicated or derivative copies count as one source.

issues.problem: There is no privacy or access scope: nothing stops it surfacing DM or private-email content to a wider audience. There is also no instruction to treat retrieved text as data rather than instructions (prompt injection).
issues.fix: Add rules: cite only content the requester can access, don't quote private messages into shared outputs without consent, and ignore instructions found inside retrieved content.

issues.quote: | Older than a month | Lower confidence — flag as potentially outdated |
issues.problem: One freshness threshold is applied to every claim type. It over-penalizes stable facts (policies, founding dates) and under-penalizes fast-moving ones (deal status, pricing).
issues.fix: Tie the freshness thresholds to claim type: status is hours to days, public investor or pricing facts are months, policy lasts until superseded.

issues.quote: Lead with the answer, not the search process
issues.problem: Anti-Patterns repeats Summarization Rules almost word for word, and the REST/GraphQL example appears five times, which adds tokens without adding guidance.
issues.fix: Merge Anti-Patterns into Summarization Rules and keep one worked example.

scenarios.prompt: What did we decide about the Q4 offsite venue? Check Slack, my email and the planning doc in Drive.
scenarios.why: The dedupe signals, conflict surfacing ('Always surface conflicts') and the source list would give a good answer. But the skill says nothing about retrieval, so the model gets no search plan and no coverage note, and it may print the literal '~~chat:' and '~~email:' labels copied from the examples.

scenarios.prompt: Summarise what's public about Northwind Ventures' current seed activity. Their site says $1–3M cheques, Crunchbase shows a $6M lead last month, and a 2023 article says they paused new investments.
scenarios.why: Conflict surfacing and the freshness table would flag the 2023 article. But the authority table ranks only internal sources (wiki, chat, email), so nothing orders the fund website against Crunchbase and the press. There is no check that sources are independent, and nothing stops the model inferring current interest. investor-targeting-and-research is the right skill for this.

contract-clause-comparison.job: compare contract clause versions side by side
contract-clause-comparison.summary: A 32-line, text-only instruction to lay two clause versions (or a clause and playbook text) side by side, list what changed, apply MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR only when a playbook exists, and describe effects neutrally.
strengths: The rule tying MATCH/DEVIATION labels to a supplied playbook, and forbidding them as a policy judgment without one, matches the persona.
The change checklist (defined terms, amounts, periods, cross-references that no longer resolve, missing schedules) is what a contracts person actually checks.
The neutral-effect examples ('notice changes from email to courier') show the model the right register.
No redline is created or sent without replacement text from counsel.
missing: Deterministic diff via the sandbox
Section alignment for renumbered or moved text
Tracing a changed defined term into every clause that uses it
A comparison-table template and worked example
A way to read PDF/DOCX files and OCR confidence handling
Routing to the triage and counsel-brief skills

issues.quote: text unchanged in meaning and wording;
issues.problem: Deciding that text is 'unchanged in meaning' is an interpretive call the persona forbids. A reworded clause can be silently bucketed as unchanged.
issues.fix: Bucket only by wording. Report any rewording as changed, and raise 'does the meaning differ?' as an UNCLEAR counsel question.

issues.quote: Preserve section numbers and defined terms. Show:
issues.problem: There is no method for exactness. A model reading two long clauses will miss single-word changes, which are the ones that matter most.
issues.fix: Add steps: extract and normalise text (whitespace, numbering), run a word-level diff in bash_exec (python difflib), render the result with [+added+]/[-removed-] markup, and have the model annotate only the diff output.

issues.quote: Return the side-by-side text, change list, broken references, and questions for counsel.
issues.problem: No output format: no column layout, no markup convention, no rule for where the playbook column sits or how to handle long clauses. Results will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/comparison-table.md with the columns Section | Baseline | Revised | Playbook | Label | Change type | Neutral effect | Counsel question, plus one worked example.

issues.problem: No handling for renumbered or moved sections, clean counterparty returns without tracked changes, or a changed definition that alters every clause using the term.
issues.fix: Add an alignment step: match sections by heading and content, flag moved text, and when a defined term changes, list every section that uses it as affected.

issues.quote: Use source text the user supplies. Name each source and version before comparing.
issues.problem: No input check. It does not say which version is the baseline, what to do when only one version is supplied or versions are unlabelled, or how to read PDF/DOCX files and scans.
issues.fix: Require a named baseline and revised version (with date and author) and use ask_question if either is missing. Read files via read_workspace_file plus bash_exec extraction, and mark OCR-derived text UNCLEAR.

issues.quote: Compare clause versions or a clause with supplied playbook text, showing exact additions, removals, and open decisions.
issues.problem: The scope overlaps nda-playbook-review and msa-playbook-review ('redline' triggers) and Toran's contract-amendment-history (amendment chains), with no routing note.
issues.fix: State the scope: one clause, or two versions of one document. Route whole-agreement playbook reviews to nda-/msa-playbook-review and multi-amendment chains to an amendment-history skill.

issues.problem: No handoff. DEVIATION and UNCLEAR rows stop at the table instead of feeding contract-deviation-triage and counsel-escalation-brief.
issues.fix: End with: pass labelled rows to contract-deviation-triage, and draft a counsel-escalation-brief for any item that needs a decision.

scenarios.prompt: Here's NDA §4 from our v2 and the counterparty's v3 markup, plus our playbook line on retained copies. What changed, and does it match the playbook?
scenarios.why: The inputs are short and labelled. The checklist under 'Produce a literal comparison', the rule for when to use playbook labels, and 'Describe, do not advise' are enough for a capable model to return a clean side-by-side with a DEVIATION label and a neutral counsel question.

scenarios.prompt: They sent the MSA back as a clean PDF with no tracked changes. Sections are renumbered and they rewrote the 'Confidential Information' definition. Compare it to our v4 Word draft and tell me every change.
scenarios.why: Nothing says to extract text from the PDF and DOCX in the sandbox, to align sections by content rather than number, to run a deterministic word diff, or to trace a changed definition into every clause that uses it. An eyeballed diff of a long agreement will miss one-word edits (shall/may, and/or), and 'unchanged in meaning' invites the model to wave through reworded text.

contract-deviation-triage.job: prioritize and route contract deviations to owners
contract-deviation-triage.summary: Takes a finished playbook comparison and labels each deviation with the user's escalation rules, or with five neutral process labels when there are none. It returns one row per issue with owner, deadline, fallback and decision, and never grades legal risk.
strengths: The five neutral labels (COUNSEL DECISION, BUSINESS INPUT, DOCUMENT GAP...) separate process status from legal risk.
It never creates high/medium/low risk grades unless the playbook defines them.
'Never infer authority from a job title' is a sharp, real-world guardrail.
The row columns include blocker, supplied fallback and exact decision, and approvals stay pending until the named owner records them.
missing: A default sort order when no priority is supplied
Mapping from comparison labels to triage labels
A fallback route when no comparison exists
Issue IDs and linked-issue handling across negotiation rounds
Rules for unknown owners and informal guidance
Persistence of the queue and handoff to the counsel brief

issues.quote: Use a completed playbook comparison. Triage is queue order, not legal risk advice.
issues.problem: No path when there is no completed comparison, which is the common case when a raw redline or counterparty issues list arrives. The model either stalls or triages uncompared text.
issues.fix: If no comparison exists, route to nda-/msa-playbook-review or contract-clause-comparison first. Alternatively, accept an issues list but label every item UNCLEAR until it is compared.

issues.problem: No default ordering when the playbook sets no priority, although ordering is the whole point of triage.
issues.fix: Add a neutral default sort: signing blockers first, then earliest deadline, then COUNSEL DECISION > BUSINESS INPUT > DOCUMENT GAP. State the sort rule in the output header.

issues.quote: `PLAYBOOK MATCH` — the supplied position matches;
issues.problem: Matches are mixed into a deviation queue, and nothing maps the comparison labels (MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR) to the triage labels, so UNCLEAR has no defined destination.
issues.fix: Add a mapping table: MATCH goes to a closed list outside the queue; DEVIATION with a supplied fallback goes to BUSINESS INPUT or COUNSEL DECISION; MISSING goes to DOCUMENT GAP; UNCLEAR goes to COUNSEL DECISION.

issues.quote: Return one row per issue with source section, playbook rule, label, owner, deadline, blocker, supplied fallback, and exact decision.
issues.problem: No issue IDs, no links between related issues (for example a liability cap and indemnity carve-outs traded together), no status across negotiation rounds, and no summary header of blockers to signature.
issues.fix: Add issue ID, linked-issues, round/status and last-updated columns, plus a header with counts by label and signing blockers.

issues.quote: Never infer authority from a job title.
issues.problem: The rule is good, but nothing says what to do when no owner is supplied, so the owner column is left blank or guessed.
issues.fix: Mark such rows OWNER NEEDED and ask the user with ask_question, never assigning one.

issues.quote: If the user's playbook names escalation classes, thresholds, owners, or fallbacks, apply them and cite the rule.
issues.problem: Silent on informal guidance (counsel emails, Slack notes). The model may treat it as an approved playbook.
issues.fix: Treat informal guidance as UNCONFIRMED and cite it as such. Ask counsel to confirm it before it is used as a playbook rule.

issues.problem: No handoff or persistence. COUNSEL DECISION rows are not sent to counsel-escalation-brief, and the queue is not saved anywhere for the next round.
issues.fix: Draft counsel-escalation-brief for COUNSEL DECISION rows. Offer to save the queue as a workspace file or Sheet, with an approval log.

scenarios.prompt: Here's the deviation table from the Acme MSA review and our escalation matrix (GC for liability and indemnity, CFO for payment terms beyond Net 45). Build the review queue.
scenarios.why: 'Apply only supplied rules' tells the model to apply and cite the matrix, and the Output line gives the row columns. A clean routed queue results.

scenarios.prompt: Counterparty sent back 23 redlines on our DPA. We don't have a formal playbook, just some notes from legal in Slack, and it has to sign Friday. Which ones do I push to legal first?
scenarios.why: The skill assumes 'a completed playbook comparison' and never says whether informal Slack notes count as a playbook. With no supplied priority it offers labels but no sort key, so it cannot answer 'which first'. It also never routes the user back to a comparison skill.

contract-key-term-extraction.job: extract contract key terms into tracker
contract-key-term-extraction.summary: Lists about 30 contract fields to capture. Each value carries document, section, exact passage and a STATED/CALCULATED/MISSING/CONFLICT/UNCLEAR status, and the skill forbids resolving ambiguity or conflicts.
strengths: The per-value status (STATED, CALCULATED, MISSING, CONFLICT, UNCLEAR) plus the exact source passage makes the tracker auditable.
'Do not turn missing text into none' and 'keep conflicts across amendments visible' are the right senior instincts.
It explicitly refuses to choose a controlling document or state legal consequences.
It frames the summary as an index to the source rather than a replacement.
missing: Date-calculation conventions and sandbox computation
Document inventory and amendment ordering
A field dictionary by document type (termination for convenience, MFN, exclusivity, change of control, audit)
A tracker schema/template and Sheets/workspace output
PDF/scan extraction and OCR confidence handling
Batch handling for a portfolio of contracts

issues.quote: For a calculated notice date, show the source date, period, and formula.
issues.problem: No date convention: business versus calendar days, whether 'at least N days prior' counts inclusively, evergreen renewal chains, time zones. The date is not computed in the sandbox either. A wrong notice date is the costliest error this skill can make.
issues.fix: Compute dates in bash_exec and state the convention used (calendar days unless the contract says otherwise). Mark business-day or inclusivity ambiguity UNCLEAR. For auto-renewals, compute the next deadline within the current renewal term.

issues.problem: No intake or ordering step. The skill never establishes which documents form the contract set (MSA, order forms, SOWs, DPA, amendments), their signed or draft status, or the order of the amendments before extraction starts.
issues.fix: Add steps: 1) inventory the documents with date and signed status; 2) order the amendments; 3) extract from the base agreement, then apply each amendment field by field, marking CONFLICT where they collide.

issues.quote: Capture document name and version, legal parties, effective date, signature date, start, end, initial term, renewal, notice period and method, fees, currency,
issues.problem: The flat field list omits commonly tracked terms: termination for convenience, renewal price-uplift caps, exclusivity, non-solicit, MFN, change of control, audit rights, minimum commitments. It is also not tailored by document type (NDA versus MSA versus order form).
issues.fix: Move the field list into references/field-dictionary.md, grouped by document type, with a one-line definition per field, and add the missing terms.

issues.quote: Return the tracker, missing documents, conflicts, and review queue.
issues.problem: No schema: one row per field or per agreement, column order, CSV/Sheet output, or how to cover a multi-contract portfolio.
issues.fix: Ship templates/key-terms.csv (agreement_id, field, value, status, doc, section, source_quote, formula, checked_on) and offer to write it to the workspace or to Google Sheets via run_block after approval.

issues.problem: No guidance on reading PDF, DOCX or scanned documents, so source quotes from OCR may be wrong but still marked STATED.
issues.fix: Read files via read_workspace_file and extract text in bash_exec. Mark values UNCLEAR when the source text came from OCR and cannot be verified.

issues.quote: Send unclear dates, defined terms, and document priority to counsel or the contract owner.
issues.problem: No named handoff. It does not point to counsel-escalation-brief, to contract-obligation-tracker, or to Vera's contract-renewal-tracker, which duplicates the renewal and notice extraction.
issues.fix: Name the downstream skills and teammates. Leave renewal action planning to Vera via consult_teammate.

scenarios.prompt: Pull the key terms from this signed SaaS order form and MSA into a tracker. I mainly need renewal, notice, fees and the liability language.
scenarios.why: The field list covers these terms, and each value gets a cite, source passage and status. The CALCULATED notice date shows its formula. A capable model produces a trustworthy tracker for two documents.

scenarios.prompt: There are 40 vendor contracts in a Drive folder. Some are scans and some have two or three amendments. Build one sheet with every notice deadline for the next 12 months.
scenarios.why: The skill has no multi-document batching, no Drive/Sheets or sandbox extraction guidance, and no OCR handling. Notice dates have no business-versus-calendar-day or auto-renewal-chain convention. Amendment conflicts are 'kept visible', but with no chronological ordering step the output will be inconsistent and the deadlines unreliable.

contract-obligation-tracker.summary: Builds a one-action-per-row obligation tracker from signed agreements only, with party, trigger, recurrence, evidence, owner, status, source text and formula-shown dates. It forbids completion claims without owner evidence, breach calls, and sending notices.
strengths: Only signed agreements create duties; drafts do not.
It will not mark completion without owner evidence (OWNER CONFIRMED COMPLETE, EVIDENCE READY).
Continuing duties are kept separate from one-time duties, and amendments are linked rather than overwritten.
It explicitly refuses breach, validity-of-notice and bearer-of-duty judgments.
missing: Recurring review and reminders via schedule_routine
Tracker persistence with stable IDs and merge on rerun
A sweep list of obligation categories (counterparty duties, survival, insurance, data return)
A defined look-ahead window and overdue escalation
Date-calculation conventions
An owner-assignment step

issues.quote: Return the tracker, upcoming owner actions, missing evidence, and unclear items.
issues.problem: 'Upcoming' is undefined and there is no recurring mechanism, although obligation tracking is ongoing work. There are no lead-time reminders, no review cadence and no overdue escalation.
issues.fix: Define a user-set look-ahead window (for example 30/60/90 days). Offer a weekly review via schedule_routine that drafts internal owner reminders for approval and escalates overdue rows to the contract owner.

issues.problem: No persistence or update rule. It does not say where the tracker lives, gives no stable row ID, and does not say how a rerun merges with existing statuses, so owner evidence can be wiped.
issues.fix: Use a stable ID (agreement + section + action). Save to a workspace file or Google Sheet, merge on rerun while preserving status and evidence, and keep a change log.

issues.quote: Record the responsible party, action, beneficiary, due date or trigger, recurrence, notice method, required evidence, dependency, business owner,
issues.problem: No sweep list of obligation types, so models under-extract obligations the counterparty owes us (SLA reports, breach notices), on-request duties, obligations that survive termination, insurance certificates, and data return or deletion.
issues.fix: Add references/obligation-sweep.md listing these categories, and require one pass per category.

issues.quote: Calculate a date only where the trigger and period are clear; show the formula.
issues.problem: No business-versus-calendar-day or inclusivity convention, and no sandbox calculation.
issues.fix: Compute in bash_exec, state the convention, and mark ambiguity UNCLEAR.

issues.problem: There is a business owner column but no step to obtain owners. The model will guess or leave it blank.
issues.fix: Ask the user for owners by obligation type. Mark missing ones UNASSIGNED and never infer them from job titles.

issues.quote: Use the final signed agreement and all signed amendments. Drafts do not create tracker duties.
issues.problem: No check that a document is actually executed. Users often supply a 'final' copy that is unsigned.
issues.fix: Confirm execution status. Label rows PROVISIONAL until the executed copy is supplied.

scenarios.prompt: We just signed the Globex MSA and DPA. Build an obligations tracker so we don't miss anything.
scenarios.why: 'Use the final signed agreement' plus the column list and statuses produce a sound one-shot tracker, with continuing and one-time duties separated and unclear items routed to counsel.

scenarios.prompt: Track obligations across our 12 customer contracts (half have amendments), tell me what's due next month, and nudge the owners every Monday.
scenarios.why: 'Upcoming' is undefined and there is no schedule_routine, no draft owner reminders with approval, and no persisted tracker with stable row IDs. Each run rebuilds from scratch and can lose owner-confirmed evidence. 'Link amendments to the rows they change' has no format for doing that across 12 agreements.

contract-ops-getting-started.job: set up contract review intake and preferences
contract-ops-getting-started.summary: Lists the intake items for a contract review and a seven-step review path (completeness, extraction, comparison, labelling, triage, counsel brief, obligations), with a hard non-advisory gate.
strengths: A clear rule that without a supplied playbook, work is limited to extraction, version comparison and questions.
'Never invent a house standard from another contract or general practice' closes a common failure.
An ordered review path that ends with obligations only after the signed version exists.
A strong, explicit gate on legal characterisations and binding actions.
missing: Memory persistence of playbook, owners and counsel
A minimum-input intake via ask_question
Named sibling-skill routing per step
A review-plan template
A first-day quick win (for example, extracting key terms from one contract)
A no-counsel-available path

issues.quote: Collect the complete agreement and amendments, document type, version, legal entities, business owner, contract owner, qualified counsel, value, term,
issues.problem: It asks for about 15 inputs up front with no minimum, which delays first value and pushes users toward giving up.
issues.fix: Minimum inputs: the agreement, the playbook (or an explicit 'none') and the named counsel. Ask for the rest with ask_question only when a later step needs it.

issues.problem: Nothing is persisted. The playbook location, approved positions, owners, counsel contacts and preferred tracker location are not stored, so every Ellis conversation repeats the intake.
issues.fix: memory_store the setup facts, and memory_search at the start of every Ellis skill. Trigger this skill when memory has no playbook or counsel on file.

issues.quote: Compare clauses only with supplied playbook text.
issues.problem: The review path never names the sibling skills, so the model will not load nda-playbook-review, msa-playbook-review, contract-key-term-extraction, contract-deviation-triage or counsel-escalation-brief.
issues.fix: Name the skill to load at each step, and choose NDA versus MSA review by document type.

issues.quote: Return the review plan, missing sources, owners, and counsel decisions needed.
issues.problem: The 'review plan' is not defined, so the output format varies.
issues.fix: Add a short template: documents received/missing, playbook status, owners, counsel, steps to run with skill names, and decisions pending.

issues.quote: Set up a non-advisory contract review using user-supplied agreements, playbooks, owners, and counsel gates.
issues.problem: No first-conversation framing, unlike the NICK getting-started skills. The trigger 'review an agreement' collides with nda-/msa-playbook-review.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description as 'Use on the first conversation with Ellis, or whenever memory has no playbook or counsel on file...', and drop the generic review trigger.

issues.problem: No path when no qualified counsel is named or available, although every decision routes to counsel.
issues.fix: Require a named counsel, or record 'counsel TBD' and stop at unsent briefs, telling the user who must be named before any decision.

issues.quote: Without one, report only the version difference and mark gaps `MISSING` or `UNCLEAR`.
issues.problem: Without a playbook it is unclear what MISSING is measured against, which invites an implied standard.
issues.fix: Limit MISSING to missing schedules, definitions, exhibits and cross-references in the supplied documents.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Ellis, we need to start reviewing inbound vendor MSAs. Here's our playbook doc, and our GC is Priya Shah.
scenarios.why: The model will run through the long intake list and return a review plan. But nothing saves the playbook location, owners or counsel via memory_store, and step 3 does not say to load msa-playbook-review. The next conversation starts from zero, and the user gets no first-day value.

scenarios.prompt: Legal is out for two weeks and sales needs this customer NDA signed tomorrow. There's no playbook, just tell me if it's OK to sign.
scenarios.why: The no-playbook rule limits the work to extraction and questions, and the Gate forbids calling text safe or approved or signing. A capable model declines to approve, extracts terms and drafts a counsel brief. There is no guidance on who to escalate to when no counsel is available.

counsel-escalation-brief.job: brief counsel on contract decision needed
counsel-escalation-brief.summary: Defines a decision-first, 10-part brief for counsel (question, deadline, source text, playbook position, neutral difference, owner context, counterparty position, approved options, missing facts, owners) and returns it as an unsent draft with no recommendation.
strengths: Decision first: the exact question and deadline lead the brief.
Keeps facts, counterparty claims, playbook text and open questions separate, and attributes the counterparty position to its source.
'Options already approved for discussion' stops the model inventing fallbacks.
An explicit unsent-draft gate: counsel decides, and an authorised person sends.
missing: Privileged-and-confidential header and distribution rules
A multi-issue decision-table format
Closed-option decision framing with the supplied fallback text
Asking the owner for missing business context
A decision log and feedback to the triage queue and playbook
A delivery path through the approval flow

issues.problem: No privilege or confidentiality handling. A brief to counsel should carry a privileged-and-confidential header, be addressed only to counsel, stay within the privilege circle, and never be forwarded to the counterparty.
issues.fix: Add a header line and a distribution rule. Strip internal notes before anything leaves the company.

issues.quote: Use this for every contract issue that needs legal judgment, a new fallback, or approval.
issues.problem: It implies one 10-section brief per issue, which is unworkable for a typical review with 10 to 20 counsel decisions. There is no batching format.
issues.fix: Use one brief per agreement: a decision table with one row per issue (question, section, options, deadline), then full detail only for signing blockers.

issues.quote: exact question counsel must answer;
issues.problem: Nothing tells the model to frame the question as closed options, as the persona's voice sample does (accept / use supplied fallback / counsel to propose).
issues.fix: Require a closed-option question that names the supplied fallback text when one exists.

issues.quote: business context supplied by the owner: value, service, data, timing, and leverage;
issues.problem: No instruction for when the owner has not supplied context. 'Leverage' also invites Ellis to characterise the negotiating position.
issues.fix: Ask the owner via ask_question and quote their words. Mark any gap as missing, and never characterise leverage yourself.

issues.quote: Return an unsent draft. Counsel decides; an authorised person sends and negotiates.
issues.problem: No delivery or record loop. There is no draft through the Gmail/Slack block pending approval, no logging of counsel's decision, and no feedback to the triage queue or to candidate playbook updates.
issues.fix: Offer an email or Slack draft via run_block under the approval flow. Record the decision with a date and the decider, update the triage row, and flag recurring decisions as candidate playbook entries.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a brief for our GC on the liability cap in the Acme MSA §9.2. We need a decision by Friday, and the deal is $84k ARR.
scenarios.why: The ordered 'Brief structure' puts the question and deadline first, then quotes §9.2 beside the playbook position, then adds the owner's context. The Gate keeps it recommendation-free and unsent, which matches the persona's voice sample.

scenarios.prompt: Legal wants one note covering the 9 open issues on the Initech DPA. The counterparty says their cap is 'market standard', the business owner hasn't given me deal value, and we sign Monday.
scenarios.why: Point 7 correctly attributes the 'market standard' claim to the counterparty, and point 9 flags the missing value. But 'every contract issue' implies nine separate 10-section briefs with no consolidated decision table. There is no privileged-and-confidential header, and nothing tells the model to ask the owner for the value.

16:hiring-debrief-and-decision.job: run interview debrief and record hiring decision
16:hiring-debrief-and-decision.summary: Snapshots filed scorecards and runs a roll-call, builds a competency-grouped debrief brief with protected remarks redacted, labels quoted as challenges, and a junior-first/HM-last running order, then records the decision-maker's verbatim decision in decisions.csv and the tracker, with scripts, templates and two worked examples.
strengths: Four working scripts (all selftests pass). collate_scorecards.py redacts protected-characteristic sentences from the saved brief with numbered markers and never computes an average or rank. snapshot_scorecards.py freezes versions and diffs any change after filing. decision_log.py enforces a verbatim reason on a no and flags loose anchors.

Research-grounded anti-anchoring design: evidence grouped by competency rather than by person, independent filing before discussion, junior speaks first and HM last, optional estimate-talk-estimate, and 'No decision' counted separately rather than as a neutral vote.

Clear scope and handoffs ('Do not use for' naming interview-kit-design, interview-coordination and job-offer-and-close-plan). The scorecard and kit formats match interview-kit-design's templates exactly, so the two skills chain end to end.

Strong gates: panel sends are drafts only and go by DM, never a group channel; unattended runs make no external writes; tracker rows change only after the owner confirms; embedded instructions in candidate documents are treated as data; fraud is never inferred from name, accent or location.

Platform calls check out against the backend: run_capability/find_capability with skill:<slug> ids, TodoWrite, write_workspace_file(source_path=...), the ~/skills/<slug> package directory and the durable ~/workspace volume.
Two end-to-end examples, including a hard case: a missing scorecard, a card changed after filing, hidden text in a take-home, and 'just tell me who to hire'.
missing: Lead the agenda with any below-bar rating on a must-have and with divergent overall recommendations, not only with rating splits
Jurisdiction check with country-specific rules for background checks and candidate data (UK DBS, Equality Act, GDPR; US fair-chance individualised assessment)
Retention period and candidate data-access (DSAR) awareness for briefs, scorecard versions and decisions.csv
Decision rights confirmed before the meeting: who decides and whether anyone (e.g. a bar-raiser) holds a veto
A feedback-safe summary of the no's reason for the interview-coordination decline draft (what may be shared with the candidate)
A structured reference-check format as the open-question fix (the reference acknowledges this gap)

issues.quote: sentence with two or more flagged words, or a word that only describes a
issues.problem: The script's KEEPABLE list includes words that describe a person: young, confident, calm, family, hair, weight, polished, church. Tested: `--keep` restored "She is quite young for this." and "Very confident presenter." and the brief then printed "Restored #1: the flagged word is a technical term". The SKILL.md presents the script as a hard stop, but it lets age and affect remarks back into the brief with a false label.
issues.fix: Cut KEEPABLE to terms that are only technical in context, restorable only when the sentence also matches an EXEMPT-style technical phrase. Or require the restored sentence to contain no person pronoun plus the flagged word. Add a selftest for "she is young".

issues.quote: ("great culture fit"). Two points or more apart is a split; lead with
issues.problem: interview-kit-design gives each must-have exactly one owner, and this skill excludes out-of-slot ratings from split detection. So by default a split can almost never occur, and because len(nums)==1 marks every block 'thin', the minutes are spread evenly. What the meeting most needs to spend time on goes unflagged: a single below-bar rating (≤2) on a must-have, and divergent overall recommendations (three hires vs one no hire in the Priya example).
issues.fix: Lead the brief and weight the minutes toward any must-have rated at or below the bar, and toward competencies whose owner's overall recommendation diverges from the rest. Still list recommendations, never tally them. Keep splits for loops where a competency has two or more owners.

issues.quote: the record says the FCRA process applies before any decline.
issues.problem: The legal framing is US-only (FCRA, EEOC), while both worked examples are UK/Portugal. For a UK role with a DBS check this puts incorrect statutory text into the decision record. US fair-chance laws requiring an individualised assessment before an adverse action on criminal history are also absent.
issues.fix: Ask for or read the role's jurisdiction. Add a short jurisdiction table to references covering US (FCRA plus state fair-chance rules), UK (DBS, Equality Act, UK GDPR) and EU (GDPR), and default to 'background-check rules apply; route to the attorney' when the jurisdiction is unknown.

issues.quote: in one line without repeating it. For labels, fit, pedigree or
issues.problem: flag_remarks.py prints the full text of every CUT remark to stdout (text[:160] plus the match), so the age and affect remarks land in the model's tool output. Nothing tells the model not to relay that output to chat or into the brief; the walkthrough had to abridge it by hand.
issues.fix: Add a --redacted mode that prints only category and location for CUT hits and make it the default in the SKILL command. Or add an explicit rule: never paste flag_remarks output; report counts and categories only.

issues.quote: every sentence the step 3 lexicon would cut replaced with a numbered
issues.problem: Step 2 depends on step 3's output ('Check each one against the flag_remarks output') before step 3 runs. It also packs about 20 lines of --keep implementation detail into the core procedure. This hurts followability and repeats what the script docstring and the checklist already say.
issues.fix: Run flag_remarks as part of step 1 or merge steps 2 and 3. Move the --keep/restore rules into references/debrief-integrity-checklist.md and leave one line in the SKILL body.

issues.problem: There is no retention or data-access rule. snapshot_scorecards.py keeps every version in versions/, and decisions.csv keeps verbatim reasons indefinitely. Nothing tells the model that under UK/EU GDPR (and CCPA for California applicants) candidates can request their interview notes and debrief record.
issues.fix: Add a guardrail: write the brief and record as if the candidate will read them, and follow the owner's retention period, asking once and storing it in preferences. Deleting a candidate removes their versions, ledger rows and decisions row.

issues.quote: Never rate or accept ratings of affect or demeanour (confidence, nerves,
issues.problem: This is a blanket cut, with the lexicon auto-redacting 'calm', 'confident' and 'presence'. It removes valid behavioural evidence for roles where composure or stakeholder handling is an anchored competency, e.g. 'stayed calm and walked the customer through the outage'. The cited EU AI Act rule prohibits AI systems inferring emotions; it does not govern a human interviewer's observed behaviour.
issues.fix: Cut affect adjectives only when no observed behaviour is attached. When the sentence also describes what the candidate did, send it as a challenge instead. Correct the rationale in the reference.

issues.problem: references/debrief-integrity-checklist.md says its [n] numbers follow 'the recruiting research dossier (section 8)' and points to 'the dossier's section 7.3'. references/notes-and-mail-inputs.md cites [114] with no source entry. None of these ship with the package.
issues.fix: Drop the dossier pointers, or include the cited sections. Give [114] a source row or remove it.

scenarios.prompt: Priya's loop for Senior Backend Engineer finished yesterday and all four scorecards are in the hiring folder. Lena (HM) is running the debrief tomorrow at 11:00 Lisbon. Pull the brief and a running order together, and once Lena decides, log it.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-8 map directly onto the request. The snapshot, collate (roll-call 4/4), flag_remarks, INFERENCE lines, open questions with cheapest fixes, running order, decision_log append (after the owner's yes) and report all run, and the priya-debrief walkthrough shows the exact output. One caveat: every competency has a single owner, so no split is detected and minutes come out even (M1 8, M2 8, M3 7, M4 7). Ana's lone no-hire on M2 is surfaced only through the out-of-slot challenge and an open question, not as the lead agenda item a senior recruiter would make it.

scenarios.prompt: Kofi's platform-engineer loop (London) ended yesterday. Only Dev and Ana have filed. Lena forwarded Slack DMs saying he's 'older than everyone' and 'went to a top school', a DBS/criminal-record check is still running, Greenhouse isn't connected, the debrief is in two hours, and Lena says 'it's basically a tie, just tell me who to hire.'
scenarios.why: The skill handles most of this well; the hard-case example covers it almost line for line. The roll-call gives 2 of 4 with a below-bar warning naming M3 and M4, and nudges are drafted, not sent. The pasted DMs are marked unfiled, the age remarks are cut, 'top school' becomes a pedigree challenge, the refusal to pick is scripted and the tie goes back to the HM. It falls short on jurisdiction. Step 7 and the template write 'the FCRA process applies before any decline', a US statute that does not apply to a UK role with a DBS check. Nothing covers UK GDPR subject-access to debrief notes or Equality Act exposure. The model would put wrong legal text in the record unless it improvises.

better: The description now states the deliverable and the refusal ('Never rates the candidate, breaks a tie or says who to hire') instead of only a trigger sentence, and adds 'Do not use for' routing to sibling skills.

Adds an inputs table with file paths and preference fallbacks, a pre-flight step, and graceful degradation (no Python means hand-counting labelled 'not script-checked'; no loop log means asking for the owner's list).

Adds four tested scripts. Snapshot/versioning puts v1's 'frozen once filed' rule into practice, collate redacts protected remarks automatically, and decision_log enforces a verbatim reason on a no and flags loose anchors.
Adds reusable templates (competency brief, decision record, scorecard format, remark lexicon, decisions.csv header), a debrief-day checklist and two worked examples, including a hard case.

New guardrails v1 lacked: affect and demeanour, transcripts never stored, prompt injection in candidate documents, identity-verification facts, background checks before a decline, DM-only panel sends, no external writes in unattended runs.
Adds out-of-slot rating handling, 'No decision' counted separately, optional estimate-talk-estimate, and explicit handoffs via run_capability.
worse: About 2.5x longer (206 vs 81 lines), with step 2 overloaded by --keep implementation detail and rules repeated across the SKILL, the checklist and the reference.
The new KEEPABLE restore path can put age and affect remarks back into the brief labelled as 'technical term', a failure mode v1 (manual cutting) did not have.
Excluding out-of-slot ratings, combined with the kit's one-owner rule, means v2's 'lead with splits' rarely fires, whereas v1 compared any ratings on the same competency.
The new legal text is US-only (FCRA), which is wrong for the UK/EU loops used in the examples.
flag_remarks.py echoes removed remarks verbatim to stdout, which works against the 'noted, never repeated' rule.

calendar-conflict-review.job: review calendar for conflicts and overload
calendar-conflict-review.summary: Scans a stated period for clashes, missing travel time, overload, out-of-hours events and lapsing holds, ranks them against priorities, and offers lettered move/shorten/delegate/decline/keep options with drafted messages, acting only on a yes.
strengths: Opens by stating which calendars were read and warns that clashes with unsynced calendars will not show
A concrete problem taxonomy covering clashes, travel gaps, overload, out-of-hours events and lapsing tentative holds
Options come as a letter/yes list with drafted messages, which suits a fast principal approval
A firm gate: nothing is accepted, declined, moved or deleted without a yes, and no one is told the principal is free before every calendar is checked
missing: Calendar retrieval via the Calendar block and a paste/ICS fallback
Time-zone normalisation for travel and remote organisers
Free/busy check on proposed new slots and organiser-versus-attendee handling
Recurring series versus single-instance changes
Prep-time and buffer checks before high-stakes meetings
All-day events and OOO blocks treated as constraints
Defaults when no setup rules exist in memory
A summary header (period, calendars read, counts by problem type)

issues.quote: State the period and which calendars you could read. If only one calendar
issues.problem: It never says how to read the calendar or what to do when a calendar is not connected. The persona requires saying so once and asking; here the model just reports the gap and moves on.
issues.fix: Read events through the Google Calendar block or a connected MCP. If a calendar is missing, say so once and offer connect_integration or an ICS export or pasted list. Mark any day that could not be fully checked as 'unverified'.

issues.problem: There is no time-zone handling, the most common cause of executive calendar errors (travel, remote organisers, invites created in another zone).
issues.fix: Normalise every event to the principal's zone for each day, including the destination zone on travel days. Flag events that land outside working hours only because of a zone shift, and show both zones for cross-zone meetings.

issues.quote: For each problem give one to three options: move, shorten, delegate, decline,
issues.problem: A 'move' option is not checked against free/busy, so it can create a new clash. It also ignores whether the principal organised the event (they can move it) or is only an attendee (they must ask), and whether one instance or the whole series is affected.
issues.fix: For each move, propose 2-3 slots that are free on every readable calendar and inside working hours. Note organiser versus attendee, and whether the change applies to one instance or the series. Name the delegate from the key-people list.

issues.quote: principal's working hours, focus blocks, and travel buffers from setup.
issues.problem: It relies on setup data but never says to look it up (memory_search) or what to do if setup never happened. Overload and buffer rules then become guesses.
issues.fix: memory_search the calendar rules saved by executive-assistant-getting-started. If there are none, ask once or state labelled defaults (e.g. 15-minute buffer between in-person meetings) and offer to run setup.

issues.quote: Rank the problems by what they put at risk, using the stated priorities.
issues.problem: 'What they put at risk' gives no way to decide which side of a clash yields. A senior EA ranks by movability.
issues.fix: Add a movability rubric: external, board and customer meetings and the 'meetings that always win' list stay. Internal recurring 1:1s and status meetings move first. Personal commitments follow the principal's rule.

issues.quote: Say who each option affects and draft any message it needs.
issues.problem: Nothing stops a reschedule or decline message from revealing the competing event's title or attendees, which breaks the persona's privacy rule.
issues.fix: Drafted messages give no reason beyond 'a conflict' unless the principal approves more, and never name the other meeting, its attendees or personal events.

issues.quote: "reschedule", "busy week"
issues.problem: 'busy week' overlaps weekly-priorities-review ('week ahead', 'plan my week'). 'reschedule' pulls a one-event move into a full calendar review.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description as 'Use when the principal asks about clashes, double bookings, travel gaps or an overloaded day...'. Move 'busy week' to weekly-priorities-review and handle a single reschedule as a one-problem run.

scenarios.prompt: Check next week's calendar for double bookings and tell me what I should move.
scenarios.why: The 'List the problems' checklist catches clashes (with organisers), missing travel time, overload and lapsing holds. 'Options to approve' returns lettered options with drafted messages and waits for a yes. The one weakness is that proposed new slots are not checked against other calendars.

scenarios.prompt: Only my work Google Calendar is connected; the kids' pickups live in my personal iCloud. I fly to London Thursday: sort out conflicts Thu-Mon and just move whatever you need.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly flags that only one calendar synced and refuses to move anything without a per-action yes. It never asks for the iCloud events (connect or paste), has no time-zone step (so London early and late clashes and travel-day buffers are missed), and a 'move' option is not verified free for either side.

executive-assistant-getting-started.job: onboard owner and capture working preferences
executive-assistant-getting-started.summary: Runs an intake for priorities, key people and how to handle each, ten sample sent emails, calendar habits and per-action approval rules, and returns a five-part setup brief.
strengths: Covers the right onboarding topics: quarterly priorities, key people and how to handle each, writing voice, calendar habits and approval rules
Sets 'every action needs a yes' as the default, action by action
Records connected and unconnected accounts up front
The setup brief has a clear five-part structure ending in the next three actions
missing: Saving each setup part to memory and checking memory first
Inferring voice and key people from the connected sent folder
A minimum-viable fast path with safe defaults
A signature convention (as principal versus on behalf of)
Time zone and brief-delivery schedule (schedule_routine)
A first real deliverable on screen (triage or next-meeting brief)
Travel preferences and VIP escalation channel

issues.quote: Give the user:
issues.problem: The setup exists only in chat. Nothing is saved with memory_store, yet calendar-conflict-review, reply-draft-in-your-voice and inbox-triage all rely on 'setup', 'key-people notes' and 'stated priorities'.
issues.fix: memory_store each part under stable keys (priorities, key_people with handling notes, voice_profile, calendar_rules, approval_rules, connected_accounts). Start by memory_search-ing those keys and only fill gaps.

issues.quote: sent emails that show how the principal writes. Ask for calendar habits:
issues.problem: It makes the principal paste ten emails and answer a long intake all at once, when connected Gmail and Calendar could supply most of it.
issues.fix: If Gmail is connected, read the last 20-30 sent messages through the Gmail block and draft a voice profile (greeting, sign-off, length, formality by recipient type) and a top-correspondents list to confirm. Infer working hours from the calendar. Use ask_question for a short staged intake (priorities first).

issues.quote: declining, booking, paying, and deleting. The default is that every one does.
issues.problem: 'Agree, action by action' suggests the principal can pre-authorise sends, declines or deletes. That contradicts the persona: never without a clear yes for that exact action.
issues.fix: State that the persona boundaries are a floor that setup cannot lower. Setup may only add narrow internal conveniences (such as labelling) and must log them. Every outward action still goes through the platform approval flow.

issues.quote: Note which accounts and calendars are connected, and which are not. Ask rather
issues.problem: It notes the gaps but never asks the principal to connect an account, and gives no fallback.
issues.fix: Call connect_integration for Gmail and Google Calendar when they are missing, or accept exports or pastes. Say once what cannot be done until they are connected.

issues.problem: It misses setup items the other Kai skills need: home time zone, whether Kai signs as the principal or 'on behalf of', reply-time expectations for VIPs, when and where the morning brief goes, and travel preferences for travel-plan.
issues.fix: Add these items to the intake and to the saved setup.

issues.quote: The first three things to do, with reasons.
issues.problem: It ends on a to-do list rather than the day_one deliverables (a sorted inbox, a brief before the next meeting).
issues.fix: If access exists, run inbox-triage or meeting-prep-brief for the next meeting straight away, and offer schedule_routine for a daily morning brief.

issues.quote: "manage my inbox", "personal assistant"
issues.problem: 'manage my inbox' collides with inbox-triage, and the description never says when setup applies, so it may re-run or never run.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description as 'Use on the first conversation with Kai, or when memory has no EA preferences yet...' and drop 'manage my inbox'.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Kai, I've just hired you. Get set up so you can run my email and calendar.
scenarios.why: It produces a sensible questionnaire and a five-part setup brief. Nothing is written to memory, so later triage and draft runs cannot find the priorities, voice or rules. There is no connect_integration step, and it ends on a list of 'first three things' instead of doing the first one.

scenarios.prompt: No questionnaire please. Gmail is connected, calendar isn't. Just learn from my mail and get going.
scenarios.why: Every step is 'Ask for...'. There is no path to infer voice and key people from the sent folder, no minimum-viable intake or safe defaults, and no prompt to connect the calendar. The model either pushes the refused questionnaire or improvises without guidance.

inbox-triage.summary: Reads mail for a period against priorities and key people, sorts each message into needs-you, draftable, read-later or no-action with a one-line why, and leads with up to five items needing the principal today.
strengths: A clear four-bucket taxonomy that matches the persona
When unsure between two groups it picks the higher one and says why
Opens with a decision-first short list with deadlines, and says so when nothing needs the principal
Treats newsletters, receipts and alerts as no-action unless they hold a deadline
No invented deadlines, and no quoting one person's mail to another
missing: Mail retrieval through the Gmail block and a paste fallback
