issues.problem: No step asks the hiring manager to approve the kit and record it. check_kit warns while the status is draft, and the example shows 'status: approved by Lena Ortiz 2026-10-14', but the procedure never says to set it.
issues.fix: Add a step: after the owner's yes, set 'status: approved by <name> <date>' and log the approval before interview-coordination books the loop.

scenarios.prompt: We agreed the scorecard for a Senior Product Designer yesterday (5 must-haves, in the hiring folder). Panel is me, the design lead, a PM and an engineer, four 45-minute slots. Build the interview kit: who asks what, the questions, and the scorecards.
scenarios.why: Step 1 maps the 5 must-haves onto 4 slots, with one slot owning two, and orders them knockout-first. Step 2 fills templates/kit.md with strong-answer notes and probes. Step 3 sets clocks. Step 4 writes anchors in this role's real work plus 'not assessed'. Step 5 runs question_lint and check_kit --scorecard, which turn missing owners, bad clocks and missing anchors into mechanical ERRORs. The kit is handed back as a draft. The only weak spot: question-bank-patterns gives no portfolio-review or work-sample guidance for a design role.

scenarios.prompt: Kit for a Data Engineer at our pediatric therapy-scheduling startup. HM's questions attached: 'Do you have kids? Helps with empathy for our users', 'How would you model children's therapy session histories?', 'What changed in our mental health app's release process when you joined?'. Only three interviewers are free.
scenarios.why: The lint correctly ERRORs 'kids', and the rewrites table offers a job-related version. But I ran the domain questions through question_lint.py and they also ERROR on 'children', 'therapy' and 'mental health'. Step 5 tells the model to mark such lines lint-ok, yet the script honours overrides only for its AMBIGUOUS word set, so it prints 'override not honoured'. The quality self-check requires exit 0, so the model must either strip the product's own vocabulary from the questions or hand back a failing kit, and the skill gives no path out. The three-interviewer limit is handled, since one person can own two must-haves.

better: Main's 110-line prose is turned into scripts that enforce its rules: exactly one owner, clocks that add up, full anchors, protected-trait lint, time-zone-safe packets and quote verification with negation and number checks.
Adds an inputs table with workspace paths and fallbacks, a pre-flight step, and numbered procedures for the kit and for packets, including the 'no interviews: post nothing' rule for routine runs.
Adds sourced references (structured-interview research, a table of unlawful questions with rewrites, AI and affect rules) where main cited nothing.
Adds kit, scorecard and packet templates plus a worked end-to-end example and a hard case, all reproducible.
Approval gating goes from one sentence ('Nothing reaches the panel...') to precise draft-only Gmail, DM-only Slack and no external writes in routine runs.

New substance: hire/no-hire only after the ratings, the 'with or without reasonable accommodation' wording, a candidate AI-use policy line, a line flagging AI-interview laws with counsel, and no scoring of polish.
worse: SKILL.md is more than twice as long and repeats script internals (override rules, quote-matching rules), which hurts efficiency.
The description changed from a crisp 'Use when...' sentence to a long feature list, and the trigger conditions come last.
New failure mode: domain terms that cannot be overridden (therapy, children, mental health) can block a legitimate kit, which main's model-judgement approach would not.
Heavier coupling to preferences.md keys and a folder layout maintained by sibling skills.
The UNVERIFIED-quote allowance leaves a hole in the new quote-only rule.

campaign-brief-and-asset-plan.job: turn a campaign goal into a brief
campaign-brief-and-asset-plan.summary: Turns a campaign goal into a one-line measurable goal, a short brief (audience, insight, message, channel mix, owned and dated asset list), two or three measures with a headline, a backwards timeline and idea rows on the editorial calendar, with paid spend held for per-line approval.
strengths: Saying the goal back in one measurable line before any planning stops work being built on a vague goal
Stops a one-channel campaign being padded into a mix, and flags unowned assets as requests
Clear money gate: per-line approval, never approval of the plan as a whole
Ties the plan to execution by writing assets onto the calendar as idea rows
missing: Reverse-funnel target math from baseline rates, with a feasibility check
Tracking, UTM and attribution plan per channel
Offer and CTA per channel or funnel stage
Itemized budget table template
Messaging-matrix and claims check on the campaign message
Risks, dependencies and brand or legal review step
Named handoffs to launch and paid-media teammates
A brief template or worked example file

issues.section: Feed the calendar in the same reply
issues.quote: Show the plan in chat, take one round of edits, then save it and add every
issues.problem: It says to take a round of edits and also to write the calendar rows 'in the same reply', which cannot both happen. It gives no fallback when no calendar exists or none is connected.
issues.fix: Sequence it: show the plan, take edits, then write the rows in the next turn. If no calendar exists, create one using editorial-calendar-ops's row schema, as a workspace CSV or a Sheet.

issues.section: Pick two or three measures, and name the headline
issues.quote: Sourced pipeline, the rate at which marketing-qualified leads become
issues.problem: It lists kinds of metric but has no baseline, no target value, no reverse-funnel feasibility check, no split between leading and lagging indicators, and no tracking or UTM plan. The campaign cannot be judged afterwards.
issues.fix: Add a step that works back from the headline target to the volume needed at each stage, using baseline rates labelled FACT or ASSUMED, with the arithmetic done in the sandbox. Then add a tracking line per channel covering UTM convention, conversion event and source of truth.

issues.quote: The message, in two sentences.
issues.problem: The message is written from scratch. It is never drawn from, or checked against, the messaging matrix's positioning line, proof points and never-make claims, although Maya's persona says anything customer-facing passes the matrix first.
issues.fix: Pull the positioning line and relevant proof points from messaging-and-tone-matrix. Check the message against the never-make list, and flag when no matrix exists yet.

issues.quote: work, and it goes to whoever owns launches.
issues.problem: The boundary is vague. Maya's kit has no launch skill and it names no teammate, so the model has nowhere to route the work.
issues.fix: Name the handoff (a GTM or product teammate's launch skill, via consult_teammate or handoff_to_expert). If no such teammate is hired, run the campaign brief and flag launch-readiness items as out of scope.

issues.quote: Never commit a dollar of paid spend. The plan proposes money; the named
issues.problem: This conflicts with 'stays UNKNOWN until the approver fills in the itemized lines': it is unclear whether Maya proposes figures or leaves them blank, and no budget table format is given.
issues.fix: Define an itemized budget table (line, purpose, proposed amount with basis marked ASSUMED or left UNKNOWN, approver, approval status) and state which of the two modes applies.

issues.quote: The audience plus the one insight that actually moves them.
issues.problem: There is no guidance on where the insight comes from (customer quotes, win/loss, research). The model will invent a plausible insight rather than source one.
issues.fix: Require the insight to cite a source (a customer quote, call note or data) or be labelled INFERENCE, with one question back to confirm it.

issues.section: Put dates on it, counting back from launch
issues.quote: lessons — at least one of each per person — then cause, fix and prevention on
issues.problem: A per-person ritual is odd for an AI-run async retro. The retro is never tied back to the headline measure.
issues.fix: Frame the retro around the headline measure against target, what drove the gap, and one change for next time. Save it dated next to the brief.

scenarios.prompt: We want 40 demo requests from mid-market ops leads by Nov 30. Channels are LinkedIn, email and one webinar. Plan the campaign.
scenarios.why: The model would say the goal back, list the brief sections, pick a headline measure and date the assets backwards, which gives a usable brief. Nothing prompts it to work back from 40 demos through baseline conversion rates to the traffic and lead volume needed, to check feasibility, or to set UTM and attribution. A senior marketer would treat those as table stakes.

scenarios.prompt: The CEO wants a 'big splash' in Q4 around the new feature shipping Oct 15. Budget TBD, audience fuzzy, and we have no calendar yet.
scenarios.why: The skill marks budget and audience UNKNOWN correctly. But 'a dated product release... goes to whoever owns launches' names no teammate or skill, there is no step for when the goal cannot be made measurable, and 'add every asset to the editorial calendar' has no fallback when no calendar exists.

channel-draft-shapes.job: draft copy shaped for a specific channel
channel-draft-shapes.summary: Turns notes, bullets or a transcript into one draft shaped for a named channel (email, landing page, social, blog, DM, release notes). It marks missing facts in place as [need this: …] and returns the reader-and-action line, a gap list and two alternative openers.
strengths: The [need this: …] in-place marker makes missing facts impossible to hide
Customer quotes need permission and otherwise are paraphrased with the name dropped
Concrete, opinionated shape rules per channel, with a 'borrow the closest shape' fallback
Two alternative openers from a different angle rather than a reword, plus a gap list naming who holds each answer
missing: Broadcast email shape with an unsubscribe and sender compliance footer
Per-platform character limits and fold positions
Accessibility (alt text, descriptive link text)
UTM tagging on CTA links
Use of preloaded workflows for first drafts
An example draft showing markers, gap list and openers

issues.quote: not a greeting. 50 to 125 words, three to six sentences, a single request
issues.problem: One email rule covers both 1:1 and broadcast. The 50–125 word, single-request shape fits a sales-style email but not a newsletter, announcement or customer story. Broadcast email also needs an unsubscribe link, sender identity and a postal address (CAN-SPAM/CASL/GDPR).
issues.fix: Split into 1:1 email and broadcast/newsletter shapes. For broadcast, add a compliance footer checklist and route list sends to nurture-sequence-build-and-readout.

issues.quote: A first line that stops the scroll alone, then three to
issues.problem: There are no per-platform limits or conventions (LinkedIn's ~210-character 'see more' fold and 3,000-character cap, X's 280 characters, link placement, alt text), so drafts can break on the actual platform.
issues.fix: Add a short references/platform-limits.md table and say to check the draft against the named platform's row.

issues.quote: Two to four sentences: why this person, then one next
issues.problem: Prospecting DMs are a sales teammate's job (first-touch drafting). There is no boundary, so Maya may draft outbound sales messages.
issues.fix: State that outbound prospect DMs go to the sales teammate. Maya's DMs are for community, partner or existing-customer contexts.

issues.quote: From the voice guide, choose the three rules this piece is likeliest to break
issues.problem: No skill in Maya's kit produces a voice guide; messaging-and-tone-matrix explicitly excludes it. The dependency usually resolves to the 'plain house style' fallback.
issues.fix: Point to the voice rules noted at the top of the messaging matrix, or consult a brand-voice teammate, before falling back to house style.

issues.section: Settle the channel and the job
issues.quote: No channel named: ask once. If they shrug, pick the likeliest and say why at
issues.problem: There is no mention of the preloaded LinkedIn Post Generator or AI Webpage Copy Improver workflows, which the persona says produce first drafts to refine.
issues.fix: Add a line: for a LinkedIn post or a web page, optionally run the matching preloaded workflow for a first draft, then apply this shape and the voice rules to it.

issues.quote: not a reword. Save the draft dated.
issues.problem: It does not say where to save the draft or how the dated draft links back to the calendar row, so later skills cannot find it.
issues.fix: Name the destination from saved preferences and add the draft link to the calendar row. Status moves to drafted only when the named owner accepts it.

scenarios.prompt: Here are my bullet notes on the v2.3 release. Turn them into release notes, and a LinkedIn post announcing it.
scenarios.why: It settles the reader and action, inventories facts with visible markers, and applies the release-notes shape (sorted by what users can newly do, plain verbs, no ticket numbers) and the social shape (a first line that stands alone, 3–8 lines, at most two hashtags). It then returns a gap list and two openers. This is senior-quality output.

scenarios.prompt: Turn this sales-call transcript into a customer-story email to our whole list. The customer said we 'cut our scheduling time in half'.
scenarios.why: It handles quote permission correctly (paraphrase, drop the name, log permission as a gap). But the email shape caps a broadcast story at 50–125 words, a 1:1 sales heuristic. There is no unsubscribe or sender or compliance footer, and no routing of a list send to the nurture skill or its send approval.

content-brief-writer-handoff.job: write a content brief for a writer
content-brief-writer-handoff.summary: Turns a topic, calendar row or URL into a writer-ready brief: angle, reader, outline, proof with named owners, links, titles and meta, CTA, practicals and voice rules, with an optional self-labelled search-intent read. It then files the brief and moves the calendar row to briefed.
strengths: Every proof item is paired with a named person who can supply it, and unknown owners stay blank rather than being assigned
Finds the angle from the gap the existing pages all miss
Labels its own intent read as a read rather than research when no SEO input exists
Moves calendar status only once the brief has actually landed
missing: Search intent type, target length and format taken from the SERP
Funnel stage and distribution plan
Messaging-matrix pull: positioning, proof points, claims to avoid, legal review flag
Meta title and description length limits
SME interview questions for proof gathering
A brief template file

issues.quote: Close with the two or three voice rules this asset is likeliest to trip over,
issues.problem: The brief pulls voice rules but not the positioning line, the relevant proof points or the claims the company never makes. The persona requires customer-facing work to pass the messaging matrix, and comparison or competitor pages carry legal risk.
issues.fix: Add a 'Messaging' block: the positioning line, which of the three proof points apply, the never-make claims relevant to this piece, and whether legal or approver review is required.

issues.quote: queries, what the ranking pages cover, and the gap) and label it as your read
issues.problem: The intent read has no structure. It lacks an intent type (answer, compare, how-to, considering), a target length from the SERP median, a format, and the people-also-ask questions, so it is a weaker version of the original seo-content-brief.
issues.fix: Fold in the intent taxonomy, length and format from the top results, and the questions to answer, or consult the SEO/content teammate when one is hired.

issues.quote: Two title options plus a draft meta title and meta description
issues.problem: There are no length limits (about 60 characters for the title, about 155 for the description), and the brief has no funnel stage or distribution plan.
issues.fix: Add length limits, and add funnel stage and distribution (where it is promoted after it ships) to the brief.

issues.quote: If the team has an SEO specialist or an SEO brief for
issues.problem: It does not say how to find that specialist or brief (teammate consult, memory, workspace file).
issues.fix: Say to check memory and the workspace for an SEO brief and to consult_teammate when an SEO or content teammate is hired.

scenarios.prompt: Brief the writer on the 'shift swap policy template' calendar row that ships next Thursday.
scenarios.why: It confirms the target in one line, reads the ranking pages for the gap, fills every brief section (proof paired with named holders, real URLs, titles and meta, one CTA, reviewer and approver from the row), files the brief and moves the row to briefed. This is a complete, reusable handoff.

scenarios.prompt: Brief a writer on an 'Us vs. Deputy' comparison page. We have no SEO person, and legal is touchy about competitor claims.
scenarios.why: It does a self-labelled intent read and marks unsourced claims [need this], but the brief never pulls the messaging matrix's never-make claims or flags legal review. It closes only with voice rules, so comparative claims are left for the writer to handle.

editorial-calendar-ops.summary: Sets up or extends a content calendar with a fixed row schema and six statuses. It schedules backwards from ship dates, runs a four-part recurring check (ships this week, late, stuck, unowned), moves statuses only on evidence, and does monthly and quarterly reviews.
strengths: A fixed six-status vocabulary; a row with no owner or ship date stays an idea
Status moves only on evidence, and publishing is a separate yes on that specific asset
The recurring check is ordered and terse, with a one-line 'on track' and no padding
Never silently drops a row; a dropped row is logged with who dropped it and why
missing: Approver, waiting_on, status_changed_at, campaign and link columns
Mapping from existing calendar statuses to the six
Default lead times per format and a per-owner capacity check
A saved last-check state for diffs
Storage fallback when no Sheets or Notion is connected
Idea backlog dedupe and prioritisation
Template calendar CSV

issues.quote: call to action (CTA), target metric, suggested internal links, owner, brief
issues.problem: The schema has no approver, waiting-on or blocker, status-changed date, campaign link or brief and draft links. The check's 'stuck waiting on one person' and the rule 'approval given by the named approver' cannot be read from a row, and campaign assets cannot be traced back.
issues.fix: Add id, campaign, approver, waiting_on, status_changed_at, brief_link, draft_link and notes columns, and ship a template CSV.

issues.section: Read what exists before you build anything
issues.quote: Never rebuild a calendar they already have — extend it.
issues.problem: This conflicts with 'Statuses are... Nothing else.' It gives no instruction for mapping an existing calendar's statuses (In review, Blocked, Published) onto the six.
issues.fix: Show a mapping table from their statuses to the six (for example, Blocked becomes its current status plus waiting_on). Ask once about ambiguous ones and keep their original value in a column.

issues.quote: track in one line rather than padding it. Speak up the moment something newly
issues.problem: 'Since the last check' and 'newly slips' need saved state, but the skill never says to save each check or diff against it. The routine's 'never flag the same stuck row two runs running unless worse' rule is absent.
issues.fix: Save each check dated (a workspace file or memory), diff against the previous one, and suppress repeat flags unless the item got worse.

issues.section: Schedule backwards from the ship date
issues.quote: Work back from the ship date and put the intermediate dates in the row rather
issues.problem: There are no default lead times per format and no owner capacity or WIP check, so back-scheduling is guesswork and can overload one person.
issues.fix: Add editable default lead times per format (marked ASSUMED), a per-owner weekly load check, and use the owner's timezone for due and late calculations.

issues.quote: Keep the calendar wherever the team can edit it — a sheet in Google Sheets, a
issues.problem: There is no fallback when no Sheets or Notion integration is connected, and it does not say how writes happen.
issues.fix: Fall back to a workspace CSV or pasted export. Write through the Sheets or Notion blocks when connected, and say which.

issues.quote: Quarterly, read the calendar against the business goals and re-tier what the
issues.problem: 'Re-tier' is undefined, and the monthly 'what worked by channel' needs performance data this skill never gathers. It overlaps weekly-marketing-read.
issues.fix: Define the review, or hand the performance half to weekly-marketing-read and keep this to calendar coverage and gaps.

issues.quote: hands over a pile of ideas that need dates and owners.
issues.problem: There is no procedure for ingesting an ideas pile (dedupe, tie to goals or campaigns, prioritise, which ones get dates).
issues.fix: Add an intake step: dedupe, link each idea to a campaign or goal, rank, and date only what has an owner and capacity. The rest stay ideas.

scenarios.prompt: What ships this week and what's stuck? The calendar is in our Google Sheet.
scenarios.why: It reads the existing sheet, says back rows by status, and runs the ordered four-part check one line per item. It gives a one-line 'on track' when nothing changed. With a reasonably complete sheet this is a senior-quality pipeline read.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a Slack dump of 30 content ideas and half-promises from four people, plus our Notion board with statuses like 'In review' and 'Blocked'. Consolidate it all into one calendar.
scenarios.why: 'Extend, never rebuild' conflicts with 'six statuses, nothing else', and it gives no mapping for 'In review' or 'Blocked'. There is no dedupe or prioritisation step for the idea pile and no owner capacity check. 'Stuck waiting on one person' cannot be read because the schema has no waiting-on or last-changed field.

maya-getting-started.job: onboard a new user to the expert
maya-getting-started.summary: Runs Maya's first-chat onboarding. It opens briefly, asks what they sell and who buys it, plays back a positioning read, and collects optional preferences one at a time. It checks and offers connections, surfaces the three preloaded workflows, and ends with a five-item starter menu and opt-in routines.
strengths: Gives value immediately with a two-line positioning playback after the first answer
Optional questions asked one at a time and saved as they arrive; skipped ones stay unset
Checks existing connections first and offers a single pick-list; CSV or paste fallback, never stalls
Preloaded workflow names match the seeded agents, and their output is treated as a first draft
Routines are opt-in, set in the user's timezone, and draft-only
missing: Memory key schema that sibling skills read
A routing table from the first request to the matching skill
A default first deliverable
INFERENCE labelling on the instant positioning read
Check for existing teammate artefacts (for example a positioning doc) before re-asking

issues.quote: The moment they hand you a topic, a URL, numbers or a date, drop the remaining
issues.problem: The key branching rule sits at the very end, under a heading about approvals. A model following the steps in order will run intake before doing the task the user brought.
issues.fix: Move this to the top as step 0: if they bring work, route to the matching skill (a brief, a draft, the calendar, the read) and collect preferences around it. Otherwise run the intake.

issues.section: Collect the rest one at a time, each marked optional
issues.quote: Save each answer as it arrives, one fact per line. A question they skip stays
issues.problem: There are no named memory keys. Sibling skills (approver, destinations, calendar location, voice samples, never-make claims, timezone) cannot reliably find these facts, and 'memory holds no marketing preferences' has no defined test.
issues.fix: List the keys, for example offer, buyer, approver_customer_facing, approver_spend, destinations, calendar_location, voice_samples, off_limits, timezone. Say which skills read each.

issues.section: Ask one thing first, then give something back
issues.quote: say back in two lines how you would position it. That gives them something
issues.problem: The instant positioning read is not labelled INFERENCE, which the persona requires for reasoning-based lines. It could harden into fact in later briefs.
issues.fix: Label it INFERENCE, ask for a yes or correction, and offer messaging-and-tone-matrix for the full version.

issues.quote: Saved preferences, whatever connections they chose, one real deliverable on
issues.problem: The procedure never says which deliverable to build by default or which skill builds it. 'Once the first output is on screen' has no defined output.
issues.fix: Set a default (a first-pass messaging matrix, which works from what they sell alone) and route to the named skill for each starter-menu option.

issues.section: Put a starter menu in front of them
issues.quote: Once the first output is on screen, offer five options as a question widget,
issues.problem: Stacking a connections list, three workflows, a five-option menu and three routines in one first session strains the persona's one-decision-per-message rule.
issues.fix: Offer workflows and routines only after the first deliverable is accepted, one decision per message.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Maya, we sell a shift-scheduling app to restaurant managers. Where do we start?
scenarios.why: It gives a two-line intro, plays back positioning immediately, gathers the rest singly as optional, checks connections and offers the rest in one list, offers a preloaded workflow, then shows the five-item starter menu via a question widget. That is a smooth, useful first session.

scenarios.prompt: I need a LinkedIn post for our launch tomorrow, here's our URL. No brand guide, and I don't want to connect anything.
scenarios.why: The rule 'drop the remaining questions and do the job' exists but sits last, under 'Approval gate'. A model reading top-down will likely run the what-you-sell question and the connection pick-list first. There is also no routing line to channel-draft-shapes or the LinkedIn Post Generator for the immediate job.

messaging-and-tone-matrix.summary: Builds a messaging layer above the voice guide: a positioning statement in Moore's template, three sourced proof points, an explicit never-make-claims list, per-persona variants, use and avoid word lists drawn from their own writing, and a formal-to-casual tone line per context (sales, support, marketing, social).
strengths: The explicit 'claims we never make' page with a reason on each
A hard cap of three proof points, each backed by an example or cut
Word lists taken from the company's own writing rather than a generic banned-words list
Defers to an existing positioning read instead of writing a conflicting second one
Only user-confirmed proof goes in; no research on companies the user did not name
missing: Competitive alternatives step before the positioning line
Message pillars and objection handling per persona
Multi-dimension tone model and high-risk situations (pricing, incidents)
Legal or approver sign-off and review dates on never-make claims
Named artefact location for sibling skills
Message validation with customers or sales

issues.quote: If a positioning read already exists — from an ideal customer profile
issues.problem: It largely duplicates Zara's positioning-and-messaging (positioning line, proof, never-make claims, per-persona variants). A team with both experts gets two competing documents, and 'start from it' names no mechanism.
issues.fix: Consume the GTM teammate's message house via consult_teammate or a workspace read when present. Scope this skill to the tone matrix, word lists and an operational claims list. Otherwise merge.

issues.quote: Every blank is filled from something they told you or something published.
issues.problem: This contradicts 'only what the user confirms goes in the matrix' under What not to do, leaving it unclear whether published web copy can fill a blank.
issues.fix: Allow their own published pages as a source, but label each such blank INFERENCE until the user confirms it.

issues.quote: For [who], [product] is a [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [alternative], we
issues.problem: The Moore template is filled with no step to identify competitive alternatives, including the status quo. 'Unlike [alternative]' invites a named-competitor comparison that may need legal sign-off.
issues.fix: Add a short alternatives step first (status quo, manual process, named competitors). Default to the status-quo alternative unless the comparison is on the approved list.

issues.quote: One line per context, each with a quoted example, saying where the voice sits
issues.problem: A single formal-to-casual axis is too thin to guide tone shifts. The high-risk situations (pricing, outage or incident, bad news) are missing.
issues.fix: Use three or four tone dimensions (for example formal/casual, serious/playful, matter-of-fact/enthusiastic) and add rows for pricing, incidents and bad news.

issues.quote: comparisons legal will not sign, the guarantees the product cannot keep, the
issues.problem: There is no named sign-off or escalation per claim, and no regulated-claim categories (compliance certifications, 'free', guarantees, superlatives, health or financial claims).
issues.fix: Add an approver and a review date to each claim, plus a checklist of regulated-claim categories to ask about.

issues.quote: Show the whole thing in chat, take one round of edits, then save it. Rewrite it
issues.problem: It gives no artefact name or location, so channel-draft-shapes and content-brief-writer-handoff, which depend on the matrix, cannot reliably find it.
issues.fix: Name the file (for example messaging-matrix.md at the saved destination) and store a memory pointer to it.

issues.quote: positioning, own language, own proof points, own call to action (CTA). Do not
issues.problem: Variants lack buying stage and objection handling, which a PMM would expect in per-persona messaging.
issues.fix: Add the top objection and the counter-proof per persona, and optionally a stage (awareness, consideration, decision).

scenarios.prompt: Build our messaging matrix. Here's our homepage, two sales emails that worked, and our support macros.
scenarios.why: It notes the voice rules visible in their writing, fills the positioning template from confirmed facts, caps proof points at three with examples, writes the never-make list with reasons, draws word lists from their own copy and quotes a tone example per context. This is usable as-is.

scenarios.prompt: We sell to clinic managers and hospital IT. Legal says we can't say 'HIPAA compliant' yet, and Zara's positioning doc says something different from our website.
scenarios.why: It correctly starts from the existing positioning read and would put the HIPAA claim on the never-make list. It gives no step for surfacing the website-versus-doc conflict to the approver, no legal sign-off or review date on claims, and per-persona variants lack buying stage and objections.

design-the-partner-program.job: design partner program tiers and incentives
design-the-partner-program.summary: A single-file guide to redesigning a partner program: a weighted, losable tier scorecard with a shadow-score pilot, an incentive portfolio, a full MDF request-to-ROI loop, and the deal-registration and certification rules to enforce in the PRM.
strengths: The MDF loop is complete and concrete: accrual vs business-case funding, demand-gen intake scoring, 60-day lead time, proof-of-performance, no roll-forward, and ROI defined as (growth - cost) / cost.
Tier bars have teeth: tiers are recomputed quarterly, can be lost, and a program with no demotions in twelve months is called a ratchet.
Pilot-before-publish with a shadow score and 60-90 days' notice matches how mature programs roll out changes.
Registration rules are specific (a 2-business-day approval SLA, a 90-day window renewable on activity, named decline reasons) and paired with automation triggers.
Fallbacks for a missing PRM or a missing MDF pool are stated plainly.
missing: Program architecture: tracks per partner type (referral, reseller, SI/MSP, ISV) with a requirements/benefits matrix
Partner value proposition and discount/margin ladder
Program KPIs (active-partner ratio, revenue per partner, time to first deal, MDF utilisation)
Cost-to-serve per tier
Launch and change-communication plan, including grandfathering existing partners
Legal/Finance review of the program guide and incentive terms
Benchmark against competitors' partner programs
Shipped templates (tier sheet, MDF policy, PRM rule list)

issues.quote: Three tiers by default, four at most.
issues.problem: There is one tier ladder whatever the partner type. Referral, reseller, SI/MSP and ISV/technology partners need separate tracks, each with its own requirements and benefits. A small or greenfield program should not be tiered at all.
issues.fix: Add a first step that chooses the program architecture: tracks per partner type, a requirements/benefits matrix per track, and a minimum partner count before tiering applies (otherwise named partners only).

issues.quote: Publish a partner-facing tier sheet draft with
issues.problem: define-the-partner-icp also produces 'three tiers with their bars' and a 'partner-facing tier sheet draft'. Two Anika skills own tiering, so they can produce conflicting tier definitions depending on which one triggers.
issues.fix: Make this skill the single owner of tiers and the tier sheet. Cut tiers from define-the-partner-icp (or have it hand off here), and remove the overlapping 'tier sheet' triggers.

issues.quote: MDF, sales performance incentive funds (SPIFs), rebates, and co-sell
issues.problem: The guardrail bands are never defined: no values, no approval owner, no source. The discount/margin ladder, the core of partner economics, is missing entirely. Incentives are not linked to model-the-partnership-commercials.
issues.fix: Add a band table (instrument, band, approval owner, source/assumption) and a margin/discount ladder per track. Send the modelling to model-the-partnership-commercials and run the arithmetic in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Tier changes, fund approvals, and anything partner-facing wait for your
issues.problem: The only gate is the owner's yes. SPIFs paid to partner reps, rebates and tier-differentiated pricing, and MDF in high-risk markets all carry legal exposure (partner-employer consent, price discrimination and antitrust, anti-bribery). Changing program terms may also require notice under existing partner agreements.
issues.fix: Route the program guide, incentive terms and any change to existing partners' economics through Legal and Finance before publishing. Add a grandfathering and notice step for current partners.

issues.section: Run the MDF loop end to end
issues.quote: Size the pool at roughly 1 to 2 percent of top line as the usual
issues.problem: The benchmark is unsourced and ambiguous (company revenue or channel revenue?). The persona requires every number to be labelled as sourced or assumed.
issues.fix: Size it as a percentage of channel or partner-sourced revenue, label it ASSUMPTION, and ask the owner for the budget envelope before sizing.

issues.problem: The inputs are listed, but there is no step to diagnose the current program before redesigning it: active-partner ratio, revenue concentration, MDF utilisation, time to first deal, certification coverage. There is no FACT/INFERENCE labelling either.
issues.fix: Add a baseline read with named KPIs, each labelled FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN with its source, and state the program goals it must move.

issues.quote: Pilot before you publish: shadow-score fifteen to twenty-five partners on
issues.problem: There is no method: no scoring formula, weights or normalisation. The skill does not say to compute it in the sandbox from a CSV/PRM export or what to ask for when the data is missing.
issues.fix: Give the scorecard formula and tell the model to compute the shadow score and tier distribution with bash_exec from an exported sheet (via Sheets/HubSpot block or upload).

issues.quote: The tier sheet draft, the incentive portfolio with its bands, the MDF
issues.problem: The deliverables are named but have no structure, and no templates ship with the package, so the output format varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/tier-sheet.md, templates/mdf-policy.md and a rule-list table (rule, trigger, owner, system).

scenarios.prompt: We have 140 resellers in three tiers and nobody has been demoted in two years. Here's our trailing-12-month partner revenue and certification export. Redesign the tiers and tighten our MDF rules.
scenarios.why: Set the tier framework covers this directly: a weighted scorecard with partial credit, the 'bar is a ratchet' call-out, the 60-70% middle-tier check and a shadow score on trailing twelve-month data. The MDF loop supplies the intake scoring, 50/50 co-funding, proof-of-performance, no-roll-forward and ROI rules. A capable model can compute the shadow score from the export without being told to.

scenarios.prompt: We're launching our first partner program: 12 referral partners, 5 SIs and 2 ISV integrations. No PRM, no MDF budget approved yet, and Finance wants rebates capped. Draft the program.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks cover the missing PRM (tracked sheet) and missing MDF (organic-only). There is no greenfield branch and no track design by partner type, so the model forces one three-tier ladder onto 19 mixed partners. It is also told to shadow-score 15-25 partners on trailing data that does not exist. Nothing defines the rebate guardrail band or who owns the cap.

drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investme.job: evaluate partner acquisition or strategic investment
drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investme.summary: Takes an existing partner from acquisition or investment screen to a seven-lane diligence read, an investment memo with base/low/high returns, and a corporate-development handoff with a negotiation brief, gated through Legal and Finance.
strengths: Screening through the alliance lens (sourced pipeline, attach rate, integration deployments, executive chemistry) uses evidence only a partnerships team has.
Met/Partial/Missing scoring with a quoted source and an early exit on two Missing scores keeps the shortlist honest.
Any lane marked stop pauses the deal until the owner overrides it in writing, and gaps stay UNKNOWN as open items instead of being filled in.
The memo structure is solid (thesis fit, why now, deal shape and guardrails, base/low/high returns, top three risks, integration thesis).
The negotiation brief (walk-away, must-haves, their likely asks) and dated stage gates give corp dev a clean handoff.
missing: NDA, clean-team, MNPI and gun-jumping controls
Deal-type branching (minority, CVC, JV, acquisition) with a term checklist for each
Valuation method and a sandbox-built returns model
People/key-person, tax, material-contracts/change-of-control and regulatory-approval lanes
Impact on the rest of the partner ecosystem and on channel conflict
Explicit consult/handoff to the Finance teammate and outside counsel
Templates for the memo, diligence tracker and open-items list

issues.section: Drive alliance M&A and strategic investments
issues.quote: Mergers, acquisitions, and investment motions always route through Legal
issues.problem: The confidentiality controls M&A depends on are missing: NDA before any data request, a need-to-know list, MNPI and insider-trading handling when either party is public, clean-team rules for competitively sensitive partner data, and no gun-jumping. Deal details could also end up in shared memory or routines.
issues.fix: Add a pre-diligence gate: NDA signed, clean-team and MNPI protocol confirmed by Legal, a code name used, and nothing stored in shared memory or surfaced by the sensing routine without the owner's yes.

issues.section: Drive alliance M&A and strategic investments
issues.quote: Use this when a partner could become equity or ownership — from first
issues.problem: Minority stake, CVC-style investment, JV and full acquisition follow one path. Their diligence depth, key terms (pro-rata, info rights, observer seats vs control, earn-outs) and who leads are very different.
issues.fix: Add a deal-type branch up front that sets diligence depth, term checklist and lead owner (partnerships vs corp dev) for each type.

issues.quote: the team assessment, the deal shape and guardrails (valuation bands,
issues.problem: No valuation method (comps, precedent transactions, DCF) and no model are given for the base/low/high returns, which invites invented numbers.
issues.fix: Build the returns in bash_exec from labelled inputs, cite comps with sources, and consult the Finance teammate (unit-economics-and-roi) for the model.

issues.quote: Legal and regulatory: pending suits, liens, licensing restrictions, the
issues.problem: The model is told to give go/concern/stop reads on legal, financial, IP chain-of-title and cyber lanes it cannot competently evidence. Those lanes belong to counsel, Finance and advisers; the partnerships role should gather inputs and track open items.
issues.fix: Mark the Financial, Legal, IP and Cyber lanes as owned by named specialists. Anika collects evidence and open items, and specialists issue the read.

issues.quote: Cultural: how they decide, how they have escalated, sponsor stability.
issues.problem: The lanes omit people and key-person retention, tax, material contracts with change-of-control clauses (including our own partner agreement), regulatory approvals (HSR, CFIUS, EU), and the effect on the rest of our ecosystem when we buy one partner.
issues.fix: Add People, Tax, Material contracts and Ecosystem-impact lanes, plus a regulatory-approval check flagged to Legal.

issues.quote: the target means commercial diligence from public sources only, marked as
issues.problem: No research method or tools are named (web_search, filings via web_fetch, Exa/Perplexity blocks, CRM export for joint pipeline), and there is no ask_question for the minimum inputs.
issues.fix: Name the public sources and platform tools, and ask for a CRM/CSV export of joint pipeline when HubSpot isn't connected.

issues.section: Hand off to corporate development clean
issues.quote: thesis — who runs it day one, what changes, what stays.
issues.problem: The integration thesis never says what happens to the existing partnership agreement, the target's other vendor alliances, or customers mid-delivery.
issues.fix: Add a disposition plan for the existing partner agreement and the target's customers, and hand the ecosystem-reaction plan to set-board-level-alliance-strategy.

scenarios.prompt: Our top ISV partner Acme is raising a Series C and offered us a strategic $5M allocation with a board observer seat. Should we do it? Draft the memo.
scenarios.why: The screen and seven lanes run, and the memo covers thesis fit, why-now, returns and risks. But the skill treats every deal as an acquisition. Minority terms (pro-rata, information rights, observer vs seat, preference stack) and how our other partners will react are never raised. 'Valuation bands' has no method, so the returns can end up invented.

scenarios.prompt: The CEO wants a quiet read on acquiring our largest SI partner. We're public, I only have their public filings plus our joint pipeline in HubSpot, and this must not leak to the rest of the partner team.
scenarios.why: The public-sources fallback and the Legal/Finance routing apply. Nothing covers need-to-know/MNPI handling, NDA and clean-team rules, gun-jumping, change-of-control clauses in the partner agreement, or the reaction of rival partners. A 'market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM)' section also doesn't fit a services acquisition.

govern-the-strategic-alliance.job: govern strategic alliance operating model and steering
govern-the-strategic-alliance.summary: Sets up governance for a GSI or consulting alliance: a signed operating model, a dated practice plan with a quarterly health read, a co-innovation pipeline, sponsor maps and steering packs with minutes.
strengths: Pitched above deal cadence at the right altitude for a GSI (practice build, reference architectures, co-innovation).
'A play with no target account is a lab note, not a play' is a sharp, usable bar.
Steering discipline: FACT numbers, decisions needed, dated asks, and minutes with owners after every meeting.
The 90-day early review for new alliances and 'give each partner something unique' reflect real alliance practice.
The fallback waits for the owner's yes before inviting anyone to a proposed cadence.
missing: GSI value exchange and alliance economics
Joint metric set with bands and system of record
Joint account planning and account mapping
IP, co-branding and co-investment rules for co-innovation
Protocol for sponsor turnover and competing practices (non-exclusivity)
Alliance maturity or health scorecard with decision thresholds
Clear boundaries to multi-year plan, councils, partner strategy-ops and Max's alliance skill

issues.quote: One model document, both sides signed. A motion with no owner is paused
issues.problem: This line, the steering-pack rule and the fallback cadence are near-verbatim Max's alliance-co-commercialization. A team that hires both experts gets two skills competing for 'alliance steering', with diverging content.
issues.fix: Merge them into one alliance-governance skill, or cut Max's version down to account-level joint selling and have it defer here for alliance governance.

issues.quote: The sponsor map on both sides. Steering packs carrying milestones hit and
issues.problem: Sponsors, steering and governance are also defined in plan-the-multi-year-partnership, run-global-partner-executive-councils and run-partner-strategy-and-operations. Nothing says which one owns what.
issues.fix: Add a boundary line, e.g. 'annual/3-5 year horizon goes to plan-the-multi-year-partnership; a multi-alliance exec forum goes to councils; this skill runs one GSI alliance's operating model and steering'.

issues.quote: Joint solutions and repeatable plays, each with a scope, a launch date,
issues.problem: Co-built solutions create joint IP, co-branding, liability and funding commitments. There is no Legal gate and no approval for co-investment or POC funding.
issues.fix: Require an IP and co-branding position (Legal) and an owner-approved funding line before any joint solution is scoped with the partner.

issues.problem: There is no GSI value exchange or economics (services revenue, practice-building funds, POC funding, referral or influence fees) and no joint metric set with bands (influenced ACV, SI-led deals, services attach, certified-to-staffed ratio).
issues.fix: Add a value-exchange block and a metric set of at most five, each with band, source and owner per side.

issues.quote: Practice health reads quarterly: certified heads, staffed deals, delivery
issues.problem: There are no bars, ratios, data source or action on red, so the health read cannot drive a decision.
issues.fix: Set bands (e.g. certified-to-staffed conversion), name the source (partner tracker, CRM) and say what a red triggers (rescue plan, or a de-invest call staged for the owner).

issues.quote: Align the alliance manager's compensation to alliance outcomes. Schedule
issues.problem: Compensation is the owner's or HR's decision. The line reads as an instruction to act, not as a recommendation.
issues.fix: Phrase it as a recommendation for the owner, labelled as such.

issues.quote: The operating model, the practice plan, the co-innovation pipeline, and
issues.problem: Four deliverables are named with no templates. No steering-pack format or tool is specified (e.g. a Google Slides or Docs block).
issues.fix: Ship templates for the operating model and steering pack, and say to draft them to the workspace or Docs for the owner's review.

scenarios.prompt: We just signed an alliance with a GSI's cloud practice. Set up the governance: operating model, practice plan, and a first steering pack for next month.
scenarios.why: The model will produce an operating model, a practice plan with dated owners and a steering pack skeleton. Nothing tells it to define the joint metric set or the GSI's value exchange (services revenue, practice funding), or to build joint account plans, so the result is structurally right but generic.

scenarios.prompt: Our alliance with a big-four firm is two years in. Their sponsor just left, they have 40 certified consultants but only 3 staffed deals, and they've announced a practice with our main competitor. Steering is in two weeks. Fix it.
scenarios.why: The sponsor map, the practice health read (certified heads vs staffed deals) and the 'no pre-read, no steering' rule help. There is no sponsor-turnover protocol, no diagnosis of why certified capacity isn't converting (field alignment, account mapping), no guidance on a competing practice or non-exclusivity, and no bar that triggers an invest or de-tier call.

handle-partner-conflict-and-churn.job: resolve partner conflicts and churn risk
handle-partner-conflict-and-churn.summary: Diagnoses a partner deal conflict, missed commitment or fade in one evidenced line, routes it through the sponsors with a staged escalation draft and a proposed ruling, and runs a save-or-exit call on churn risk with a dated conflict log.
strengths: Forces a one-line, typed diagnosis (deal conflict, missed commitment, fade) with evidence and FACT, then INFERENCE, then UNKNOWN ordering.
Horizontal vs vertical conflict labelling is real channel practice.
An escalation with no sponsor behind it is refused ('just a complaint'), and a sponsor is requested first.
Clear prohibitions: never override a registration, never promise credits, exceptions or term changes.
'A clean wind-down, not a slow fade' sets the right posture for exits.
missing: Rules-of-engagement lookup and precedent search before ruling
Defined partner health scorecard and exit bar
Root-cause taxonomy for fading partners
Save-plan structure (commitments per side, 30/60/90 checkpoints)
Legal/competition-law gate for pricing remedies
Customer-impact protection during conflicts and exits
Templates for the escalation note and conflict log

issues.quote: a price war gets a minimum-advertised-price option
issues.problem: MAP and other resale-price remedies are competition-law sensitive: resale price maintenance is a hardcore restriction in the EU/UK, and only unilateral policies are safe in the US. Offering MAP as a routine option with no Legal gate risks advice that coordinates partners' prices.
issues.fix: Route any pricing remedy through Legal. Never propose or relay pricing between partners. Offer non-price remedies first (territory or account split, registration enforcement).

issues.section: Run the save-or-exit call on churn risk
issues.quote: A health score built from activity, pipeline, and sponsorship. The one
issues.problem: The health score has no weights, window, thresholds or source, and the exit bar is never defined, so the save-or-exit decision is arbitrary. It also duplicates the health grade in manage-partner-renewals-and-exits.
issues.fix: Define one shared partner health scorecard (components, weights, window, source, save and exit thresholds) and reference it from both skills.

issues.quote: Propose the ruling or the remedy
issues.problem: Agreement terms are listed as an input, but the ruling step never applies the rules of engagement or registration policy, or checks the conflict log for precedent, so rulings can be inconsistent.
issues.fix: Add: cite the governing clause or rule of engagement and the closest precedent from the conflict log before proposing the ruling.

issues.section: Run the save-or-exit call on churn risk
issues.quote: A partner below the exit bar gets a clean wind-down, not a slow fade.
issues.problem: This overlaps manage-partner-renewals-and-exits, which owns exit plans and notice timelines. There is no handoff, so two skills can each draft an exit.
issues.fix: Once an exit is chosen, hand off to manage-partner-renewals-and-exits for the notice, transition and statement.

issues.section: Name the problem in one line
issues.quote: Fade: the last joint activity and the pipeline trend.
issues.problem: This captures symptoms only. There is no cause taxonomy (economics, competing vendor incentives, enablement gap, sponsor loss, product fit), and the cause should decide the save motion.
issues.fix: Add a short root-cause checklist and map each cause to a save motion.

issues.quote: Keep a conflict log: the issue, both sides, the ruling, the date.
issues.problem: No location is given for the log (workspace file, sheet or memory), and nothing says to search it before ruling. The platform won't keep this state implicitly.
issues.fix: Store it with write_workspace_file or a Sheets block (memory_store for a summary), and search it at the start of each case.

issues.quote: plus an average-deal remedy to choose between.
issues.problem: 'Average-deal remedy' is undefined jargon, so the model will make up what it means.
issues.fix: Define the remedy concretely or remove it.

scenarios.prompt: Two of our resellers both claim the Northwind deal. We registered it for Partner A on 3 March and Partner B says they registered on 11 March. Draft the ruling and the note to B's partner manager.
scenarios.why: The steps map cleanly: a one-line diagnosis with both registration dates, labelled horizontal, a three-line sponsor brief, a staged escalation draft, a dated ruling and a conflict-log entry, with the registration left untouched until the owner says yes. A capable model will apply first-to-register, as the persona's voice sample does.

scenarios.prompt: Our biggest SI partner has gone quiet for two quarters: pipeline down 60%, their alliance lead left, and they just launched a practice with our competitor. Meanwhile two of their resellers are undercutting each other in EMEA. What do we do?
scenarios.why: The model can split this into a fade (vertical) and a price war (horizontal). The fade gets symptoms but no root cause. The health score and exit bar are undefined, so the save-or-exit call is arbitrary. The price-war branch suggests a minimum-advertised-price option in the EU with no warning that resale-price interventions are competition-law sensitive.

manage-partner-renewals-and-exits.job: run partner renewals, amendments, and exits
manage-partner-renewals-and-exits.summary: Covers the partnership lifecycle tail: logging change requests with dated amendments, opening a renewal play 120 days out with a health grade and motion choice, staging exit plans, and keeping a lifecycle log.
strengths: Opening the renewal window at 120 days to beat the notice deadline, not just meet it, is the right discipline.
Change control requires a dated amendment note, and scope creep is called out rather than absorbed.
Renegotiation pairs every ask with a concession inside guardrail bands.
A lifecycle log with trigger and outcome makes the next cycle evidence-based.
The fallback for a missing agreement marks terms INFERENCE and flags Legal first.
missing: Notice-date computation from the contract, with a scheduled reminder
Renewal motion decision criteria
Renewal economics review (trailing revenue, cost-to-serve, MDF return)
Exit checklist of post-termination obligations
Legal review and jurisdictional distributor/agent-law check for exits
Customer communication plan during exits
Templates for the renewal proposal, amendment note and lifecycle log

issues.quote: The 90-day mark is the standard non-renewal notice deadline, and the play
issues.problem: Notice periods are contract-specific (30, 60, 90 or 180 days). Calling 90 days 'standard' invites the model to assume it rather than read the clause, and a fixed 120-day window already falls inside the notice period on a 180-day contract.
issues.fix: Compute the notice deadline from the actual clause and open the window a fixed runway before it (e.g. deadline minus 30-60 days). Set a schedule_followup reminder.

issues.section: Plan the exit when health or math says so
issues.quote: Exits are staged as drafts with their evidence. The owner makes the call.
issues.problem: There is no Legal gate on exits or terminations. Cause vs convenience, cure periods, and distributor or commercial-agent protection laws (EU agent indemnity, Belgian distribution law, Puerto Rico Law 75) can create liability.
issues.fix: Require Legal review of any termination or non-renewal notice and a jurisdiction check before the owner's yes.

issues.section: Plan the exit when health or math says so
issues.quote: The notice-period timeline, the client and pipeline transition, the
issues.problem: The exit plan omits in-flight deal registrations and tail commissions, inventory buyback, customer support continuity, data return or deletion, trademark and logo cessation, marketplace listing removal, and surviving clauses.
issues.fix: Add an exit checklist covering post-termination obligations, each with an owner and a date.

issues.quote: wins-and-gaps record, and the renewal motion: auto-renew, renegotiate,
issues.problem: There are four motions and no decision rule (health band, economics vs plan, strategic fit, cost-to-serve), so the choice is arbitrary.
issues.fix: Add a decision table mapping health grade and economics to a motion, with the evidence required for each.

issues.quote: means running the portfolio health scan before the renewal play.
issues.problem: 'Portfolio health scan' is not a skill in the package or the kit. It is the persona's routine, so the model has nothing to load, and the health grade is never defined.
issues.fix: Point to a named skill or scorecard (shared with handle-partner-conflict-and-churn) or define the grade inline.

issues.section: Plan the exit when health or math says so
issues.quote: Plan the exit when health or math says so
issues.problem: handle-partner-conflict-and-churn also sets an exit bar and wind-down, with no handoff between the two skills.
issues.fix: State that the save-or-exit decision lives in the conflict skill and the exit execution lives here.

issues.quote: A renegotiation draft pairs every ask with a concession, and every
issues.problem: The guardrail bands are referenced with no source or link to model-the-partnership-commercials.
issues.fix: Pull the bands from the commercials skill's output, or ask the owner for them.

scenarios.prompt: Our reseller agreement with Brightline renews 1 February. Here's the contract and their last four QBR grades. Build the renewal play.
scenarios.why: With the contract and grades in hand, the model opens the window, sets a health grade and a wins-and-gaps record, picks a motion and drafts give-get pairs within bands. The weaknesses are no decision rule for the motion and bands with no source, but a capable model will still produce a usable play.

scenarios.prompt: We need to exit our Belgian distributor early. They're underperforming, the contract has a six-month notice clause, they hold our stock, and there are 14 registered deals open. Draft the exit.
scenarios.why: The model gets a notice timeline, a client and pipeline transition and a joint-statement draft. It misses what decides this case: Belgian distribution law's notice and indemnity exposure, termination for cause vs convenience, inventory buyback, tail commissions on in-flight registrations, and data and trademark wind-down. No Legal gate is required before the notice is staged.

map-the-partner-ecosystem.job: map partner ecosystem whitespace and build-buy-partner
map-the-partner-ecosystem.summary: Builds a category-by-category map of who plays and our coverage, scores and ranks whitespace gaps, makes a build/buy/partner call per gap, and hands opportunity cards to sourcing.
strengths: 'A category with no evidence behind it is UNKNOWN, not empty' is good evidence discipline.
Integration-attached retention as a value signal is a sharp, practitioner-level idea.
Gaps with no path are cut instead of padding the list.
Partner gaps get a candidate thesis (partner type, value exchange, first prospects) rather than a bare list.
Tight and short.
missing: Build/buy/partner decision criteria
A single anchored and weighted scorecard
Named research sources and platform tools
Competitor ecosystem benchmark
Customer demand evidence (integration requests, lost deals)
Account-mapping tool usage with a CSV fallback
A visual map or table template
Explicit handoffs to M&A, product and sourcing

issues.quote: One paragraph of rationale per gap. A partner gap gets a candidate
issues.problem: The skill's central decision has no criteria (core vs context, time to market, build cost vs partner economics, control and differentiation, customer demand evidence, partner availability), and 'buy' and 'build' are not routed anywhere.
issues.fix: Add a criteria table scored per gap. Route 'buy' to drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments and 'build' to the product teammate.

issues.quote: Each gap gets potential, strategic fit, and reachability, with one
issues.problem: Whitespace uses potential/fit/reachability while the cards use potential/impact/fit. Neither has a scale, anchors or weights, so rankings can't be reproduced.
issues.fix: Use one scorecard with 1-5 anchors and weights, computed in bash_exec, and reuse it on the cards.

issues.quote: Thin CRM data means a shorter map built from public research, marked
issues.problem: No research method or sources are given: integration requests, lost-deal reasons, support tickets, competitors' partner directories and marketplace listings, tech-stack enrichment. No tools are named (web_search, Exa/Firecrawl blocks, a HubSpot export).
issues.fix: List the sources and tools, and ask for a CRM or account-mapping export (Crossbeam/Reveal CSV) when no integration is connected.

issues.quote: Use this when the question is category-level rather than partner-level.
issues.problem: 'Category-level' collides with build-partner-led-category-creation, and the persona routes 'a category question' to both skills.
issues.fix: Reword the description around coverage and whitespace across capability categories, and leave 'new market category' to category creation.

issues.quote: accounts with an integration live retain better, and that is worth
issues.problem: This is asserted as a general truth instead of measured. The persona forbids unsourced claims.
issues.fix: Compute retention with vs without the integration from the user's own data, or label it INFERENCE with a source.

issues.quote: Who plays in each category, split by motion — solutions and services
issues.problem: There is no competitor-ecosystem comparison, which is the usual way to find where we lose on coverage.
issues.fix: Add a column for competitors' partner coverage in each category.

issues.quote: qualified names to the sourcing motion with the thesis attached, rather
issues.problem: The handoff target (source-and-qualify-partners) isn't named, and the names are called 'qualified' before any qualification has happened.
issues.fix: Name the skill and call the handoff 'candidate names'.

scenarios.prompt: Map the partner ecosystem around our HR analytics product. Where are we under-covered, and should we build, buy or partner for payroll and ATS integrations?
scenarios.why: The model will draw a category map and rank gaps. The build/buy/partner paragraph has no criteria to reason from (core vs context, time to market, cost, control, demand evidence, partner availability), and the scoring has no scale, so the call is plausible but unsupported.

scenarios.prompt: We have no CRM overlap data, our product spans three categories, and leadership wants a whitespace map by Friday plus a recommendation on whether to acquire a small scheduling ISV.
scenarios.why: The thin-CRM fallback (public research marked INFERENCE) applies. No sources or tools are named (competitor partner directories, marketplaces, web_search/Exa), 'buy' isn't routed to drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments, and nothing tells the model to measure integration-attached retention from its own data.

technical-diagnostics-with-tools.job: diagnose customer bug with logs and APIs
technical-diagnostics-with-tools.summary: Tells Robin to reproduce first, then check account/data state, recent changes, the API call by request ID, auth/SSO and error logs, redacting at capture, rank causes and file an engineering repro against the ticket.
strengths: Redact at the point of capture, before quoting in chat or filing, is a senior and uncommon instruction
Any check that could not be run is labelled UNKNOWN with the access it needs, rather than guessed
Ranks causes with one confirming step each and says what evidence would prove a different cause
Labels a workaround as one, with an expiry, when it masks a defect
missing: Read-only / no-impersonation rule and customer consent for account access
Mapping of each check to AutoGPT tools (run_mcp_tool, run_block HTTP, bash_exec log parsing, browser repro) with an ask-for-export fallback
Defined checks-table columns and an engineering repro/defect template
Status page, known-issue and duplicate-signature check with an incident threshold
HAR/console capture guidance and timestamp/timezone normalisation
Regression window ('when did it last work', release/deploy correlation)
Advice to rotate exposed secrets and a hand-off to sensitive-data-safe-handling

issues.quote: edits, then file it against the ticket with the defect link, request
issues.problem: The diagnosis is filed to the ticket after one round of edits with no explicit approval step. This contradicts the later 'as a draft they approve first' and Robin's boundary that nothing is written without the owner's yes.
issues.fix: Stage the ticket note and defect as drafts, file only on the owner's explicit yes to that action, and log the approval.

issues.quote: Work through account and data state via the store lookup, recent
issues.problem: 'Store lookup' is undefined. The skill never says queries must be read-only, never forbids replaying API calls or impersonating the customer, and never mentions customer consent before accessing their account.
issues.fix: Add: read-only queries and GETs only; no writes, replays, impersonation or 'log in as' without owner yes and customer consent. Map each check to a platform tool (run_mcp_tool DB/log server, run_block HTTP, bash_exec on uploaded logs or HAR files) or to ask_question for an export.

issues.section: Repro on the customer path first
issues.quote: Recreate exactly as Troubleshoot and resolve runs it. No repro means
issues.problem: The skill leans on troubleshoot-and-resolve and then repeats its cause-ranking and workaround-expiry text almost word for word. The trigger boundary between the two skills is fuzzy, so they will compete for the same requests.
issues.fix: Cut the duplicated steps and scope this skill to the evidence-gathering stage troubleshoot-and-resolve calls, or merge its check list into that skill as references/system-checks.md.

issues.quote: Show the diagnosis plus the checks table in chat, take one round of
issues.problem: The 'checks table' is the core deliverable but its columns are never defined, and there is no engineering repro template.
issues.fix: Define the table (check, tool/source, query or request ID, time window in UTC, redacted result, verdict confirms/rules out/UNKNOWN, access needed) and a defect template (summary, severity, affected accounts/count, first seen, env/version, steps, expected vs actual, request IDs, attachments).

issues.problem: There is no step to check the status page, known issues or matching open tickets before digging into one account, and no threshold that turns a repeated signature into an incident handoff.
issues.fix: Open with a check of status, known issues and duplicate signatures; when two or more accounts share the signature, hand off to escalations-and-incidents (or enterprise-identity-sso-support for login failures).

issues.quote: around the incident time. Redact what each check returns before you quote
issues.problem: 'Around the incident time' gives no window and no timezone normalisation. Customer-reported times are often local while logs are in UTC.
issues.fix: Normalise every timestamp to UTC with its source timezone and search a stated window (for example −30/+15 min), widening it deliberately.

issues.quote: No store or log access means relief from the most likely setup causes,
issues.problem: The heading promises prohibitions but holds a fallback. The fallback never asks the customer for cheap evidence such as a HAR file, console log, request IDs or exact timestamps.
issues.fix: Rename to 'When access is missing' and list the three artefacts to request, with a redaction reminder.

scenarios.prompt: Acme's webhooks to their endpoint started returning 401 yesterday around 14:00 UTC. Here's the request ID req_8f2c and a screenshot of the error. Figure out what's going on and write up the engineering ticket.
scenarios.why: The 'Check the systems in order' list (account state, recent changes, API call by request ID, auth, logs) points a capable model the right way, and rotated-secret/auth causes would be ranked. But the skill never says how to reach logs or the API (run_mcp_tool, run_block HTTP GET, bash_exec on an uploaded export). The 'checks table' has no columns, and the defect has no template beyond 'request IDs, and date'. The result would read well but be uneven.

scenarios.prompt: Three enterprise customers can't log in since 9am. One pasted a full SAML response, another sent a screenshot with their live API key visible, and we have no log access connected.
scenarios.why: Redaction at the point of capture handles the SAML assertion and the key, and the no-access fallback marks relief UNVERIFIED. But there is no step that treats a multi-customer pattern as a likely incident and routes it to escalations-and-incidents or enterprise-identity-sso-support. Nothing tells the model to advise rotating the exposed key or to route the spill to sensitive-data-safe-handling.

travel-disruption-and-rebooking.job: rebook travelers after flight or hotel disruption
travel-disruption-and-rebooking.summary: Guides recovery of a disrupted trip: locate the traveler, order rebooking options (same carrier, partner, reroute, hold), apply the route's passenger-rights regime, and handle hotel walks. It keeps money moves pending approval and ends with a short traveler brief.
strengths: Recovery options in a sensible order, with hold-and-wait for short delays
'Protect every downstream leg and the hotel', which guards against cascade and no-show cancellations
Hotel walk policy stated concretely, confirmed in writing before the traveler leaves
Tells the model to keep receipts and the carrier notice for later claims
Refuses to invent flights, times or rights; each UNKNOWN names the record (PNR, notice, fare rules) that would settle it
missing: Passenger-rights reference (EU261/UK261, US DOT 2024 refund rule, Canada APPR, Montreal Convention) with thresholds and date stamp
Explicit approval gate before any booking change, cancellation or new ticket
Check of the carrier's auto-rebooking, weather/travel waivers and live flight status
Options table and traveler-brief template
Transit-visa, passport-validity and accessibility/special-assistance checks
Group and mass-disruption handling with a hand-off to mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms
Corporate duty-of-care steps (traveler safety check-in, TMC contact)

issues.quote: Confirm the new itinerary against the record, leg by leg, with confirmation
issues.problem: The skill never says who executes the rebook or that changing or cancelling a booking needs the traveler's and owner's yes. Only money moves are gated, yet dropping a segment can void the rest of the ticket under no-show rules.
issues.fix: Present up to three options with the fare-rule and waiver impact of each; execute only after the traveler and owner pick one; never cancel or skip a segment without checking the fare rule; log the approval.

issues.quote: rebook — and cite the rule you are applying rather than guessing at it.
issues.problem: The skill demands a rule citation but ships no reference, so the model must recall EU261/UK261 thresholds, extraordinary circumstances (including strikes), the US DOT automatic-refund rule, Canada APPR or the Montreal Convention from memory.
issues.fix: Add references/passenger-rights.md with each regime's scope, delay and cancellation thresholds, care and compensation amounts, refund rights and an 'as of' date, plus an instruction to web_fetch the carrier's conditions of carriage when unsure.

issues.quote: Fastest confirmed alternative first: the same carrier, then a partner or
issues.problem: There is no way to confirm availability: no GDS or booking tool, and no instruction to check flight status or the carrier's automatic re-protection first. The model will present unverified flights as options.
issues.fix: Step 0: check whether the carrier has already re-protected the traveler and check live status (web_fetch or browser on the carrier's status page, or ask the TMC agent). Label each option CONFIRMED or UNVERIFIED with its source.

issues.quote: interline option, then a different routing; then hold-and-wait if the delay
issues.problem: Rerouting through a new country can need a transit visa, and passport validity rules can deny boarding. Neither is checked, and passport data is handled without a privacy note.
issues.fix: Add a documents check for each reroute (transit visa, passport validity, ESTA/ETA) and route passport or ID data through sensitive-data-safe-handling.

issues.quote: connections, hotel overbooks — or at check-in, check-out, and the front
issues.problem: The description and triggers ('check-in problem') claim routine front-desk and check-in/out work, but the body covers only overbooking, so the skill loads for requests it cannot serve.
issues.fix: Drop front-desk operations from the description, or add a short check-in/out section (deposits, early/late check-out, key/room issues).

issues.quote: The rebooked or held itinerary with confirmations, the rights and
issues.problem: There is no options table or traveler-brief template, so output will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Add an options table (option, carrier/flight, depart/arrive in local time, fare difference, waiver/rule, confirmed?, recommendation) and a five-line brief template.

issues.section: Locate the traveler and the break
issues.problem: There is no multi-traveler or group handling, and no hand-off when a disruption hits many travelers (weather event, strike).
issues.fix: Add a group or mass-disruption branch that ranks travelers by deadline and hands off to mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms.

scenarios.prompt: Priya's LH430 FRA→ORD was just cancelled (crew shortage). She's at the Frankfurt gate and has to be in Chicago for a 9am meeting tomorrow. Here's the PNR and our travel policy. What do we do?
scenarios.why: 'Option the recovery in order' gives the right sequence (Lufthansa, then Star Alliance partners, then reroute), and the rights step prompts a carrier-fault call under EU261. But the model gets no thresholds or amounts to cite, and no instruction to check whether the airline has already auto-rebooked her or to verify seats via web_fetch or the browser. It also doesn't say who actually tickets the change, so 'confirmed' options can't really be confirmed.

scenarios.prompt: Our Lisbon hotel is overbooked for our group of 12 tonight. Three of them connect on TAP tomorrow, and those flights are delayed by a strike. Client policy caps hotels at €180/night, and one traveler's passport expires in 5 months.
scenarios.why: The walk policy (comparable room, transport, first night covered) and the 'stranded tonight first' rule help. But the skill gives no group handling, no way to decide whether the carrier's own staff strike or an ATC strike counts as extraordinary, no check of passport validity or transit visas when rerouting, and no approval gate before rebooking 12 people.

triage-and-prioritize.job: triage support tickets by priority and route
triage-and-prioritize.summary: Reads each ticket for impact and sentiment, assigns P1-P4 with a one-line reason, ranks the queue by impact, affected count, SLA clock and risk weight, links duplicates, and routes each ticket to a lane. The result is saved as the day's work list.
strengths: P1-P4 definitions are concrete and match Robin's persona
SLA clock starts at first contact and carries across handoffs, so near-breach cases outrank new arrivals
Every priority carries a one-line reason, and a category is logged for trend reporting
Thin records produce a shorter confident list rather than padded priorities
missing: Category taxonomy and duplicate criterion
SLA targets per priority and tier as named inputs, with a time-left column
Status-page/known-issue check and spike-to-incident threshold
Dedicated safety route to trust-and-safety-escalations
Severity mapping consistent with escalations-and-incidents
Re-triage rule when new information arrives
Output template (Toran's support-ticket-triage has a good one)

issues.quote: reply plus instant ack with expected reply time), answer now,
issues.problem: The macro fast lane implies sending a canned reply and an instant acknowledgement, with no approval step. This breaks Robin's 'nothing customer-facing without the owner's yes' boundary.
issues.fix: Stage fast-lane replies and acks as a batch of drafts for one owner approval, or require a standing approval stored in memory before any auto-ack.

issues.quote: with a repro doc when sentiment is hot, legal or safety words appear, or
issues.problem: Self-harm, threats and child-safety cases are lumped into a generic escalation with a 'repro doc', and the skill never names trust-and-safety-escalations. The at-risk person gets no immediate staged response.
issues.fix: Add a pre-ranking step: any imminent-harm, self-harm, child-safety or illegal-content signal jumps straight to trust-and-safety-escalations before the rest of the queue is ranked.

issues.quote: loss, a security or fraud event, imminent safety harm, or a VIP down; P2
issues.problem: 'VIP down' is P1 here but SEV2 in escalations-and-incidents. The two skills in the same kit will give conflicting urgency calls for the same case.
issues.fix: Publish one mapping (P1↔SEV1/2 and so on) in both skills, or have triage reference the escalation matrix in memory.

issues.problem: There is no spike detection or status-page/known-issue check. Many tickets with the same symptom are linked as duplicates but never escalated as a possible incident.
issues.fix: After the duplicate check: when N or more tickets share a symptom within a window, or the status page shows an incident, open an incident handoff to escalations-and-incidents and hold the individual replies for a macro.

issues.quote: The ticket text plus channel, the customer's history and sentiment, order
