issues.problem: The named inputs omit SLA targets per priority and tier, customer entitlements, and the escalation matrix, all of which the ranking depends on. There is also no fallback for a helpdesk with no block (ask for a CSV export).
issues.fix: Add SLA targets, tiers and the escalation matrix (from memory, or asked once), plus the fallback 'paste or upload a queue export'.

issues.quote: for duplicates and link them, and log a category so trends surface
issues.problem: No category taxonomy and no duplicate criterion. Linking duplicates in the helpdesk is also a write action with no gate.
issues.fix: Ship a short taxonomy (bug, how-to, billing, account, integration, security, data, feature request) and a rule (same symptom plus one more matching piece of evidence), and propose links as drafts.

issues.quote: round of edits, then save it as the day's work list.
issues.problem: There is no destination or format for the saved work list, and no time-left column.
issues.fix: Save to a workspace file or a sheet via run_block, with columns rank | ticket | P | reason | SLA time left | category | dup-of | route | owner | FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN.

scenarios.prompt: Here are the 23 tickets that came in overnight (CSV export from Zendesk). Triage them and tell me what to handle first.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-4 give a capable model everything for a strong ordered list: P1-P4 with reasons, rank by SLA clock and impact, linked duplicates, a route and owner for each, and one round of edits. SLA targets are not a named input, so time-left may be missing, but the ranking will still be senior quality.

scenarios.prompt: Queue's on fire: 40 tickets, 12 saying 'can't export reports' since 10am, an enterprise admin threatening to cancel and mentioning their lawyer, and one user who wrote they 'don't want to be here anymore'. No SLA doc, no CRM access.
scenarios.why: P1 for imminent safety and escalation on legal words are covered, and the thin-records fallback keeps the list honest. But the self-harm message goes to 'escalate to a human with a repro doc' instead of trust-and-safety-escalations with a crisis reply. The 12-ticket spike is only linked as duplicates, never raised as an incident. And the 'instant ack' fast lane could send canned replies without approval.

troubleshoot-and-resolve.job: troubleshoot customer-reported bug to root cause
troubleshoot-and-resolve.summary: Four-step support troubleshooting: recreate on the customer path, diagnose in order (setup, recent change, misuse, defect) with ranked causes, ship labelled relief, and stage a minimal-repro defect and ticket update for the owner's yes.
strengths: Repro on the exact customer path before theorising; with no repro it names two questions or logs and who asks
Differential diagnosis: each ranked cause gets one confirm step, plus what would prove a different cause
A workaround ships labelled as one, with an expiry, and names the defect it masks
Explicit gate: nothing writes to the tracker of record on its own
Sets timeline expectations at the start of diagnosis
missing: Status page, known-issue and recent-release check before account-level diagnosis
Multi-customer threshold for incident escalation
Routing to technical-diagnostics-with-tools, enterprise-identity-sso-support, billing and escalations
Practical repro methods without product access (test account, HAR/console, recording, isolation checks)
Full defect template with severity, frequency, version and request IDs
Workaround safety check (reversible, no data loss)
Closure loop: notify customer on fix, hand off to own-to-closure

issues.quote: or data setup, recent change on either side, misuse or missed step, then
issues.problem: Diagnosis starts at one account's setup and skips the cheapest, highest-value check: an active incident, the status page, known issues, or a recent release. Nothing escalates a multi-customer pattern.
issues.fix: Make step 0 a check of status, known issues, release notes and matching open tickets; when two or more accounts share the symptom, hand off to escalations-and-incidents.

issues.quote: Use this when something is broken. Recreate it, find the root cause, ship
issues.problem: The trigger is extremely broad, and the skill never routes to its siblings: technical-diagnostics-with-tools for log/API proof, enterprise-identity-sso-support for login failures, billing for payment errors. The two diagnostic skills compete for the same requests.
issues.fix: Add a 'Route out' line naming each sibling with its boundary, or merge technical-diagnostics-with-tools in as this skill's evidence step.

issues.quote: state. Walk it yourself from the records before theorizing. No repro means
issues.problem: The skill never says how to walk the path. The model usually has no product access, and the skill doesn't mention a test account, browser_navigate, or asking for a HAR/console log or screen recording.
issues.fix: List repro routes in order: the owner's test account via browser tools; the customer's artefacts (HAR, console, recording, exact timestamps with timezone); isolation checks (incognito, other browser, other user or role).

issues.quote: or the defect filed with minimal repro (steps, environment, expected vs
issues.problem: The defect template lacks severity, frequency and affected-account count, first seen or last known good, version/build, request IDs, attachments and linked tickets, which engineering needs to prioritise.
issues.fix: Ship templates/defect.md with those fields and FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels.

issues.quote: Ship relief: the workaround or fix steps the customer runs now, labeled
issues.problem: There is no safety check on workarounds (reversibility, data loss, security downgrade), and 'ship' reads as sending, although step 4 stages drafts.
issues.fix: Require that each relief step is reversible and data-safe (otherwise flag it), and say relief reaches the customer only as an approved draft.

issues.quote: The cause with evidence, customer relief steps, and the staged defect waiting
issues.problem: The skill does not close the loop: nothing links the ticket to the defect, notifies the customer when the fix ships, or hands off to own-to-closure.
issues.fix: End with: link ticket to defect, set a follow-up via schedule_followup, and hand the case to own-to-closure.

scenarios.prompt: Customer says CSV exports from the Reports page come out empty since Tuesday. They're on Chrome, Pro plan, screenshot attached. Figure it out and draft the bug for eng.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-4 lead a capable model through the path to recreate, the 'since Tuesday' change question, ranked causes with confirm steps, labelled relief (for example another browser or a date-range workaround), and a staged defect with steps, environment and expected vs actual after a duplicate check. That is senior-quality output even without product access.

scenarios.prompt: Their Zapier contact sync silently stopped. They've already deleted and reconnected it twice, there are no logs, they're furious, renewal is next week, and two other tickets mention sync delays.
scenarios.why: The no-repro fallback asks two questions and ranks setup causes as UNVERIFIED, and the duplicate check finds the other tickets. But nothing turns three accounts with one symptom into an incident, and the skill never checks status or known issues first. There is no caution that delete-and-reconnect style workarounds can lose data, and no hand-off of the renewal risk to account-health-and-qbrs or upsell-and-retention-offers.

trust-and-safety-escalations.job: escalate abuse, self-harm and illegal content reports
trust-and-safety-escalations.summary: Severity-triages abuse, self-harm, youth-safety and illegal-content reports (imminent harm, CSAM, trafficking and credible threats go to a human now). It stages playbook safety actions, writes a warm handoff packet with verbatim quotes, and logs facts only, plus a defect-reduction note.
strengths: Imminent harm outranks everything, with a one-line who/what/where/time packet
Never contact the reported party or promise an outcome without the owner's yes
Warm handoff: the owner confirms receipt before Robin stands down
Facts-only case log with no adjectives about the people involved
A defect-reduction note after each case (what signal caught it, what nearly missed it)
missing: No-touch handling rule for suspected CSAM (reference by ID only)
Self-harm crisis-response template with locale-specific resources
After-hours or unreachable-owner path with acknowledgement timeouts
Legal reporting duties (NCMEC/§2258A, DSA Art. 18, UK OSA) and law-enforcement request handling
Protection of reporter identity and confidentiality
Default enforcement ladder and reporter-reply template
Grooming and youth-safety signals, and reviewer wellbeing (limiting exposure to harmful content)

issues.quote: material, trafficking, and credible threats follow the same now-path.
issues.problem: Suspected CSAM gets only a routing priority. Combined with 'preserve evidence' and 'verbatim quotes', a model with web_fetch or browser tools could open, describe, copy or forward the material, which creates legal exposure for possession or distribution.
issues.fix: Add a hard rule: never open, fetch, download, describe, quote or forward suspected CSAM; reference it only by content or message ID; restrict access; hand it to the legal reporting owner. Say explicitly that filing reports (for example the NCMEC CyberTipline in the US) is the owner's action.

issues.quote: Imminent harm to a person outranks everything and goes to a human now
issues.problem: The person at risk gets nothing while the handoff happens. The skill has no staged crisis reply with locale-appropriate resources (988 in the US, Samaritans 116 123 in the UK and Ireland, findahelpline.com), no guidance on not promising confidentiality, and no request for location when life is at immediate risk.
issues.fix: Add a self-harm protocol: stage an immediate supportive reply template with crisis resources for the approver's first yes, then ask the owner to contact emergency services when a specific imminent threat and a location are known.

issues.quote: with the raw report and say the path is UNKNOWN. Never sit on imminent
issues.problem: 'Never sit on imminent harm' is not actionable when the owner is offline. There is no on-call chain, acknowledgement timeout, or instruction to tell whoever is reachable to call emergency services.
issues.fix: Define an acknowledgement timeout (for example 10 minutes), then the next contact in the escalation matrix, then telling the user in chat to call local emergency services; log every attempt with its time.

issues.problem: There are no legal or regulatory duties: provider reporting of CSAM (18 U.S.C. §2258A), EU DSA Art. 18 notification of threats to life or safety, UK Online Safety Act duties, law-enforcement request handling, or evidence-preservation holds.
issues.fix: Add references/legal-duties.md listing each duty, who owns it, and the facts the packet must carry, and route every one to the legal or T&S owner as a draft.

issues.quote: Write the handoff packet: severity with reason, verbatim quotes,
issues.problem: 'Verbatim quotes' is right for threats but wrong for sexual content involving minors and for doxxing (it re-spreads personal data). The skill also never protects the reporter's identity from the reported party.
issues.fix: Quote verbatim only for threats and harassment text; reference IDs for sexual or illegal content and for personal data; add 'never reveal the reporter's identity or the enforcement outcome to the reported party'.

issues.quote: alone. An abusive customer is not an angry customer: loop a lead, never
issues.problem: Customers who abuse staff are a different job, mixed into platform safety. The 'part-ways line with any cancel or refund owed' is a money move with no stated gate.
issues.fix: Move abusive-customer handling to escalations-and-incidents, or give it its own short section with the refund staged for approval.

issues.quote: Stage the safety action the playbook allows (limit reach, preserve
issues.problem: There is no default enforcement ladder (warn, restrict, suspend, remove content, report) and no reply template for the reporter when the playbook is missing.
issues.fix: Add a default ladder, marked as needing policy confirmation, and a reporter-acknowledgement template that promises review, not outcomes.

scenarios.prompt: A user reported another user for weeks of harassing DMs and attached screenshots. What do we do?
scenarios.why: Severity triage puts it in the impact-and-reach queue. 'Protect first' stages limiting reach and preserving evidence without contacting the reported party, the handoff packet carries IDs, timestamps and quotes, and the log stays factual. A capable model would produce a sound packet, though with no enforcement options ladder and no reply template for the reporter.

scenarios.prompt: Ticket from a 14-year-old: an adult on our platform asked them for photos and now they want to hurt themselves. They linked the chat. It's 2am and our T&S lead is offline.
scenarios.why: The skill routes this to 'a human now' but gives no staged crisis reply to the minor (crisis lines, stay with them, don't promise secrecy). 'Preserve evidence' plus 'verbatim quotes' could lead the model to open or copy possible CSAM. It doesn't mention NCMEC or other legal reporting. With the lead offline, 'escalate to the owner directly… Never sit on imminent harm' gives no on-call or emergency-services path.

upsell-and-retention-offers.job: make retention or upsell offer during support
upsell-and-retention-offers.summary: Reads a support touch for a real signal (cap hit, upgrade ask, competitor named, cancellation, silent sponsor), matches one sourced offer drafted inside the fix, runs a one-rung-at-a-time save ladder for churn, stages anything past the discount limit, and logs the revenue touch.
strengths: 'No signal means no pitch — solve the case and stop' prevents tone-deaf upselling
Offer drafted inside the fix, not instead of it: one paragraph, price, easy yes
Terms that cannot be sourced are UNKNOWN; never invent prices, plans or discount authority
A lost save gets a graceful close draft, not pressure
Explicit hand-off to account-health-and-qbrs when renewal is at risk
missing: Cancellation-rights guardrail (honour an explicit cancel, cap save attempts, note jurisdiction)
Cancel-reason taxonomy mapped to pause, downgrade and training offers before discounts
Hand-off to billing-refunds-and-exceptions for proration and refunds
Defined log-line and offer-draft templates
Rule against disparaging a named competitor
Tracking of save and attach rates over time

issues.quote: For churn in motion, run the save ladder one rung at a time: understand,
issues.problem: A multi-touch save ladder applied to a customer who has clearly asked to cancel can obstruct cancellation. State auto-renewal and consumer-protection rules (for example California's ARL as amended in 2025, and EU/German online-cancellation requirements) limit save attempts.
issues.fix: When the customer has explicitly asked to cancel, draft the cancel confirmation path with at most one save offer in the same message, never make cancellation conditional on engaging, and have the owner confirm the jurisdiction's rules.

issues.quote: Discounts, credits, and exceptions stay inside the approval limit —
issues.problem: This implies Robin can offer discounts or credits within the limit on its own, which contradicts the persona boundary (no credits or goodwill without the owner's yes).
issues.fix: Say every offer is a draft; the limit only decides who approves it (the desk owner inside the limit, the save owner above it).

issues.quote: Match one offer to the signal: the plan that removes the cap, the add-on
issues.problem: There is no cancel-reason taxonomy mapped to non-discount levers (pause, downgrade, training/onboarding, feature workaround, annual switch), so the model defaults to discounting.
issues.fix: Add a reason→offer table: price→downgrade, annual or targeted discount; not using→onboarding session or pause; missing feature→workaround or roadmap check; switching→comparison plus one offer; temporary→pause.

issues.quote: with the reporter on what changed, triage complaints separately from
issues.problem: Step 5 drifts into general feedback-program instructions that belong to voice-of-customer-and-feedback, which dilutes the skill.
issues.fix: Replace it with one line: 'Tag the save reason; repeat reasons go to voice-of-customer-and-feedback.'

issues.problem: No hand-off to billing-refunds-and-exceptions for mid-term refunds or proration on cancel, and no check of plan and usage via connected Stripe or HubSpot.
issues.fix: Route money-back questions to billing-refunds-and-exceptions; pull plan and usage via run_block (Stripe/HubSpot) when connected, or ask for them.

issues.quote: The matched offer draft or save-ladder plan with its approval state, and
issues.problem: No template for the offer draft or the log line, and 'revenue touch' is undefined.
issues.fix: Define the log line (date, account, signal, customer's words, offer, price or terms source, approval state, outcome, MRR/ARR delta if sourced).

scenarios.prompt: A Starter-plan customer keeps hitting the 3-seat cap and asked how to add a 4th user. Answer them and see if there's an upgrade fit; our offer sheet is in memory.
scenarios.why: Step 1 finds a 'usage capped' signal, step 2 matches the plan that removes the cap with prices from the offer sheet, and step 3 answers the how-to first with one plain offer paragraph. A capable model would produce a clean, non-pushy draft and a log line.

scenarios.prompt: Customer emailed: 'Cancel my account today, you're too expensive, we're moving to Competitor X.' They're annual with 4 months left, based in California. My discount limit is 15% but sales wants to offer 30%.
scenarios.why: Staging the 30% for owner yes is handled, and 'understand, fix, offer, escalate' gives structure. But 'one rung at a time' across touches can delay an explicit cancel, and there is no rule to honour the request alongside at most one save offer (state auto-renewal laws such as California's). The skill offers no pause or downgrade alternatives and no hand-off to billing-refunds-and-exceptions for proration or refund on the remaining term.

cohort-and-retention-analysis.summary: A 49-line, single-file checklist for building a cohort retention view. It sets a cohort contract (entity, entry event, return event, windows, censoring), then reconciles, segments and interprets the result, with no template, script or retention-definition options.
strengths: Right-censoring handled correctly: 'Mark right-censored cells as unavailable, not zero' and no comparing cohorts at unreached ages.
Segments only on fields known at decision time, which prevents look-ahead leakage.
Separates acquisition-mix shifts from within-cohort change and requires absolute percentage-point differences.
Guardrails against redefining churn after the fact and against filling unobserved future periods.
missing: Menu of retention definitions (N-day, unbounded, bracket) with formulas
Revenue retention (NRR/GRR, expansion, contraction, churn) or explicit handoff to finance
Cohort triangle and retention-curve template
Size-weighted blended curve over matured cohorts / survival analysis
bash_exec script and CSV-export fallback
Feature-adoption cohorts (present in Toran's user-cohort-analysis)
Worked example

issues.quote: Retention has no single default definition. Define it before calculating it.
issues.problem: It tells the model to define retention but offers none of the standard options: N-day/bounded, unbounded/rolling, bracket, logo versus revenue (NRR, GRR), and active-use versus paid. The model will improvise the definition, and results will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Add a short references/retention-definitions.md with each definition's formula, when to use it, and its pitfalls. Have the skill ask the owner to pick one via ask_question.

issues.quote: Show starting cohort size, retained count, retention rate, and available follow-
issues.problem: No deliverable format. There is no cohort triangle layout, no retention-curve guidance, no size-weighted average across matured cohorts, and no summary section. Each run will produce a different shape of output.
issues.fix: Ship templates/cohort-readout.md covering the contract block, the triangle (cohort x age with n per cell), a weighted average curve over matured cohorts only, key findings as FACT/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN, and data limits.

issues.problem: No compute or tool guidance. It never says to run the calculation in bash_exec, to ask for a CSV export when no billing or analytics integration exists, or to use the dataviz skill for the curve. The arithmetic ends up done by hand in prose.
issues.fix: Add a step: load the export in bash_exec, build the triangle with a bundled scripts/cohort_triangle.py, and print control totals against source starts. If no data is attached, ask for an export with the named columns.

issues.quote: "retention", "churn", "return rate"
issues.problem: The bare 'churn' trigger collides with churn-prevention (save offers) and Daniel's saas-gtm-finance (revenue churn math). Nothing marks where Quinn's analytical view hands off.
issues.fix: Say in the description that this skill covers behavioural or logo retention analysis, and add a line routing revenue-churn reporting to the finance expert and save plays to the retention/CS expert.

issues.quote: Mark right-censored cells as unavailable, not zero.
issues.problem: Masking alone leaves aggregate curves biased when cohorts have uneven follow-up. There is no guidance on averaging only across cohorts that reached each age, or on survival (Kaplan-Meier) estimates for continuous-time churn.
issues.fix: Add one line: compute blended curves only over cohorts with full follow-up at each age, and use a survival estimate when entry dates are continuous.

issues.quote: suppress or group very small cells when they could expose a person
issues.problem: No threshold is given, so 'very small' is left to the model. Stability and privacy suppression will be applied inconsistently.
issues.fix: State a default, for example suppress cells with n < 10 for privacy and flag rates where n < 30 as unstable, unless the owner supplies a rule.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Stripe subscriptions export for 2025. Build monthly logo-retention cohorts and tell me whether newer cohorts retain worse than older ones.
scenarios.why: The cohort contract forces entity, entry and return events to be fixed. The right-censoring rule stops the model from comparing young cohorts at ages they have not reached, and 'Separate changes in acquisition mix' plus percentage-point differences give a sound interpretation. A capable model with pandas would produce a correct triangle, even without a template.

scenarios.prompt: Compute net revenue retention by signup cohort. Invoices include upgrades and downgrades, we merged duplicate accounts in March, and some customers have two subscriptions.
scenarios.why: The skill lists 'treatment of reactivation, upgrades, downgrades' and identity merges as fields to record, but it never defines NRR/GRR, the expansion/contraction/churn components, or how to roll multiple subscriptions up to an account. The model has to improvise the revenue-retention formula, and there is no handoff to Daniel's saas-gtm-finance for the financial version.

experiment-readout.summary: A 50-line, single-file guide for writing an A/B or quasi-experiment readout. It records the design, validates execution (SRM, balance, exposure), reports primary and guardrail effects with uncertainty and practical size, and lists limits, but specifies no statistical method or template.
strengths: Refuses to call a before-and-after comparison an A/B test and requires quasi-experiments to be labelled.
Validation list names SRM, duplicate and cross-variant exposure, unequal data delay, pre-test balance, and novelty effects.
Puts practical size alongside significance and names 'harmful on a guardrail' as a possible outcome.
The decision stays with the named owner under a pre-agreed rule, and fields chosen after seeing results must be disclosed.
missing: Default test per metric type and delta method for ratio metrics
SRM chi-square threshold and blocking consequence
Peeking/sequential-testing guidance
Multiple-comparison correction for segments and guardrails
Achieved power / MDE for null results
Variance reduction (CUPED) mention
Readout template and bash_exec stats script
Novelty/primacy check via effect-over-time plot
Worked example

issues.quote: raw values, absolute effect, relative effect where useful, uncertainty interval
issues.problem: No default statistical method. It does not name a test for proportions (two-proportion z or Wilson) or means (Welch), the delta method or bootstrap for ratio metrics such as revenue per visitor, or a script to compute them. Correctness depends on the model's recall.
issues.fix: Add references/stats-methods.md (test per metric type, delta method, bootstrap) and scripts/readout_stats.py, run via bash_exec, to output n, rates, absolute and relative effect, CI, and p per metric.

issues.quote: Check sample-ratio mismatch, duplicate assignment, cross-variant exposure,
issues.problem: SRM is named, but there is no test (chi-square goodness of fit), no threshold (commonly p < 0.001), and no consequence (do not interpret effects until explained). Peeking and optional stopping are not in the validation list at all.
issues.fix: State the SRM test and threshold, and that a failed SRM blocks the readout. Add 'early stopping or repeated looks without a sequential design', with a note that the nominal p-value is invalid.

issues.quote: Keep exploratory metrics and segments in a separate section.
issues.problem: Exploratory segments are kept apart, but there is no multiple-comparison control (Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg), no warning about heterogeneous-effect fishing, and no rule against shipping to a winning segment without a confirmatory test.
issues.fix: Add a rule: correct p-values across segments and guardrails, label segment effects as hypotheses, and require a follow-up test before a segment-targeted ship.

issues.problem: No power or MDE check. An inconclusive result cannot be told apart from 'too small to matter' without reporting the minimum detectable effect the test achieved.
issues.fix: Require the achieved MDE at 80% power for the primary metric, and say whether the effect the owner cared about was detectable.

issues.quote: pre-agreed rule; the named owner makes the decision.
issues.problem: It assumes a pre-agreed decision rule exists. The skill gives no fallback when none was written, which is common, so the model either blocks or improvises a rule.
issues.fix: If no rule exists, state that, propose one explicitly labelled post-hoc, and present the data against it without making a recommendation.

issues.quote: "A/B test", "test readout"
issues.problem: The bare 'A/B test' trigger also catches design requests ('set up an A/B test'). This skill does not cover design, Quinn's kit has no design skill, and Alex's product-experiment-design covers both design and readout.
issues.fix: Narrow the triggers to readout phrasing, and add a line routing test design and sample sizing to Alex's product-experiment-design (or add a design skill to Quinn).

issues.problem: No readout template. Section order is implied, but there is no reusable document with a summary line, decision table, metric table, validity checks, and limits.
issues.fix: Ship templates/experiment-readout.md with a one-line verdict, design block, validity checks (pass/fail), a primary/guardrail table, an exploratory appendix, and limits.

scenarios.prompt: We ran a 50/50 test on the new pricing page for 14 days. Here's the export with visitors and conversions per variant plus revenue per visitor. Write the readout.
scenarios.why: Design capture, the SRM and exposure checks, primary-first reporting with absolute and relative effects and an interval, and the ship / don't ship / continue call under the owner's rule would give a senior-quality readout. A capable model supplies the two-proportion interval itself.

scenarios.prompt: The PM stopped the test on day 5 when it hit p<0.05. The split came out 52/48 on 40k users, there was no written hypothesis, and they want to know which of 12 segments 'won' so they can ship to those.
scenarios.why: The skill does flag SRM, fields chosen after results, stopping-rule deviations, and keeping segments exploratory. But it gives no SRM test or threshold, never explains that optional stopping inflates false positives, and has no multiple-comparison correction across 12 segments. A model may report the segment winners with too little warning.

funnel-conversion-analysis.summary: A 48-line, single-file guide to defining an ordered funnel (events, windows, identity, closed versus open), validating events, computing a step table, and turning the largest drop into testable hypotheses, with no uncertainty method, template or script.
strengths: Requires stating whether the funnel is closed to a starting cohort or open to all events in a period.
Validation covers out-of-order events, client versus server disagreement, late arrival, and bot/test traffic rules.
Includes time to next step as well as conversion.
Warns that a sharp fall in a low-volume segment may not drive the business result.
missing: Confidence intervals on step rates and changes
Rate vs mix decomposition method
Identity-stitching rules and unmatched-share bounds
Conversion-window selection and sensitivity
Fallback for aggregate-only funnel exports
Output template and bash_exec script
Handoff to experiment-readout / metric-movement-analysis

issues.quote: For each step show entrants, completions, step conversion, overall conversion,
issues.problem: No uncertainty on step rates or on period-over-period changes. A drop from 3.1% to 2.6% on a small base may be noise, and nothing tells the model to test or bound it.
issues.fix: Require a confidence interval (Wilson) for each step rate and for the change, and flag changes whose interval spans zero as not established.

issues.quote: Break down the largest drop by approved segments, then report sample size and
issues.problem: It asks whether a segment 'explains the total change' but gives no rate/mix decomposition. Without it the model eyeballs segments and may double count across overlapping dimensions.
issues.fix: Add a rate-versus-mix decomposition (change = sum of mix effect + rate effect per segment) with a bash_exec snippet, and forbid summing contributions from overlapping segment dimensions.

issues.quote: disagreement, identity changes, late arrival, version changes, and bot or test
issues.problem: Identity is listed as a check, with no rule. There is no guidance on anonymous-to-identified merges or cross-source joins (Segment to Stripe), and no requirement to report the unmatched share and its effect on conversion.
issues.fix: Add an identity step: declare the stitch key and precedence, report matched, unmatched and ambiguous shares, and give conversion bounds with unmatched counted both ways. Point to metric-definition-and-data-quality for join checks.

issues.quote: For every step record the exact event, eligible population, entity key, required
issues.problem: The conversion window must be recorded, but there is no method for choosing one: time-to-convert distribution (median, p90), or sensitivity of the result to the window.
issues.fix: Add: plot time-to-next-step, choose a window that covers about p90 unless the owner supplies one, and report whether the conclusion changes at a shorter or longer window.

issues.problem: No platform fallback. It never says to compute in bash_exec from an uploaded export, or what to do when only aggregated funnel reports are available, where event order and deduplication cannot be verified.
issues.fix: Add: with event-level data, compute in the sandbox; with aggregates only, label validation checks as not possible and results as provisional; ask for a raw export when event order matters.

issues.quote: "funnel analysis", "conversion rate", "drop off"
issues.problem: The bare 'conversion rate' trigger overlaps with Alex's product-metrics-and-instrumentation ('read my funnel') and with marketing conversion-optimisation skills, which could route CRO copy requests here.
issues.fix: Frame the description as analysing measured funnel data, and route page or copy optimisation to the marketing expert.

issues.problem: No reusable output template (definition block, step table, segment contribution table, FACT/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN list).
issues.fix: Ship templates/funnel-readout.md.

scenarios.prompt: Checkout conversion fell from 3.1% to 2.6% last week. Here's the step-level event export (view cart, shipping, payment, order). Where are we losing people and why?
scenarios.why: Define-validate-calculate-hypothesise leads to a correct step table with denominators. The segment rule ('whether the segment explains the total change or only has a low rate') steers the model to the right driver, and each hypothesis gets a disproof check. The model may not add confidence intervals, but the core answer would be sound.

scenarios.prompt: Build a signup → activation → paid funnel. Signups are in Segment (anonymous IDs until email), paid is in Stripe, about 30% of users have no shared ID, and I only have Mixpanel's aggregated funnel screenshot for last quarter.
scenarios.why: The skill mentions 'identity changes' and reconciling starts with an independent source. It gives no stitching rule (anonymous-to-identified merge, email match), no instruction to report the unmatched share as a bound, and no fallback when only aggregated funnel numbers exist and event order cannot be checked.

kpi-analysis-getting-started.job: frame KPI question and define metrics
kpi-analysis-getting-started.summary: A 55-line intake skill that frames a KPI question: the decision it serves, a nine-field definition for every metric, a data inventory, and an analysis plan listing blockers. It defines no deliverable and gives no routing to Quinn's analysis skills.
strengths: Opens with the decision, its user, deadline, and the cost of a wrong call.
Separates a descriptive question from a causal one up front.
A nine-field metric definition including grain, windows, timezone, owner and known breaks.
'Version a changed definition and state where comparison stops.'
missing: KPI definition sheet template (persona day_one deliverable)
Routing from question type to the next Quinn skill
Draft-for-approval path for missing definitions with memory_store persistence
ask_question for minimum inputs
Metric role / driver tree / guardrail classification
Data access fallbacks (CSV, Sheets block)
Worked example

issues.problem: No named deliverable. Quinn's day_one promises 'A KPI definition sheet', but the skill gives no sheet layout, intake-brief format, or template, so every run produces freeform notes that the weekly digest cannot reuse.
issues.fix: Ship templates/kpi-definition-sheet.md (one row per metric with the nine fields plus version and status PROPOSED/APPROVED) and a one-page intake brief (question, decision, metrics, data inventory, plan, blockers).

issues.quote: "analyze metrics", "analytics intake", "business metrics", "data analysis"
issues.problem: 'analyze metrics' and 'data analysis' match almost every Quinn request, so this intake skill will compete with the cohort, funnel, experiment, and movement skills. The description also lacks a 'Use when' clause.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Use when a KPI question arrives without agreed definitions, sources, or a stated decision…', and replace the generic triggers with intake phrasing ('define our KPIs', 'set up metrics', 'which numbers should we track').

issues.quote: question (`what changed?`) from a causal one (`what caused it?`).
issues.problem: It classifies the question but never routes on it: causal questions should go to experiment-readout or a quasi-experimental design, 'what moved' questions to metric-movement-analysis, and recurring reporting to weekly-kpi-digest. The intake has no next step.
issues.fix: Add a routing table from question type to the Quinn skill that handles it, plus data-quality as a mandatory next step before any calculation.

issues.quote: Never invent data, infer a missing definition, or change a metric after seeing
issues.problem: This blocks with no path forward. In practice definitions are often missing, and a senior analyst drafts a candidate definition, labels it PROPOSED, and gets owner sign-off rather than stopping.
issues.fix: Allow drafting a proposed definition clearly marked PROPOSED, confirm it via ask_question with the named owner, and store the approved version with memory_store for later skills.

issues.quote: For each file or table, capture its name, extract time, covered dates, row count,
issues.problem: No tool guidance: it does not say to compute row counts and date ranges with bash_exec, pull Sheets and HubSpot via run_block, or ask for a CSV export when no integration is connected.
issues.fix: Add one line per access path (uploaded file → bash_exec profile; connected source → run_block; none → ask for a named export).

issues.quote: plain business meaning;
issues.problem: The definition lacks metric role (north star, input/driver, guardrail), aggregation type (sum, ratio, distinct count), leading versus lagging, and target or threshold. A senior analyst would capture these for a KPI set.
issues.fix: Add role, aggregation, target/threshold, and the parent metric in the driver tree to the definition fields.

scenarios.prompt: We want to know whether the new onboarding flow improved activation. Here's a Mixpanel export. Where do we start?
scenarios.why: The model would separate the causal question from the descriptive one, list the definition fields and inventory the file. But no deliverable is specified, and when the question is causal the skill never routes to experiment-readout or explains what design is needed. The output is a loose plan, not a reusable intake brief.

scenarios.prompt: The CEO wants board KPIs by Friday. Stripe, HubSpot, and a finance Google Sheet all show different MRR, and nobody owns the definitions.
scenarios.why: 'Do not accept the same label for two formulas' correctly surfaces the conflict. But 'Never ... infer a missing definition' with no draft-for-approval path leaves the model to block or improvise. Nothing says to use ask_question to get an owner's decision, to persist the approved definition with memory_store, or to pull the Sheet via run_block.

metric-anomaly-detection.summary: A 50-line guide to flagging metric anomalies. It sets a detection rule, runs data-fault checks before business explanations, compares against multiple baselines, and returns an anomaly card with status, but gives no detection method, monitoring setup, or persistence for the alert log.
strengths: Frames an anomaly as a signal for review, not proof of a problem or a cause.
Runs data-fault checks (freshness, schema, lost rows, numerator/denominator) before business explanations.
Requires absolute as well as relative thresholds when low volumes distort rates.
'Do not close an alert because the metric returned to normal; record whether anyone found a cause.'
Forbids tuning the rule after the event without recording it, and forbids labelling fraud from aggregates.
missing: Default, explainable detection methods with parameters
Multi-metric false-alarm / alert-fatigue control
schedule_routine setup for recurring monitoring
Alert log persisted via memory_store or workspace file
Handoff boundary to metric-movement-analysis
Draft-then-approve for outward alerts
Worked anomaly card example and detection script

issues.quote: owner supplied or explain the proposed rule before applying it. Keep absolute
issues.problem: No default detection method. There is no seasonal-naive or same-weekday baseline, no rolling median ± k·MAD, no STL residual or prediction-interval approach, and no default k. The core of a detection skill is left to improvisation.
issues.fix: Add references/detection-methods.md with two or three explainable defaults (same-weekday rolling median ± 3·MAD; STL residual z-score; prediction interval from the trailing 8 weeks), when to use each, and a bash_exec script that flags points.

issues.quote: Track alert status and owner. Do not close an alert because the metric returned
issues.problem: It assumes a persistent alert log and recurring checks but never names the platform mechanism. The model has no instruction to keep the log with memory_store or a workspace file, or to set up schedule_routine for daily detection.
issues.fix: Specify: keep an alert log (id, metric, date, status, owner, cause) in a workspace file or memory_store, and offer a schedule_routine for recurring detection after the user approves the rule.

issues.quote: "spike", "drop", "outlier", "unexpected KPI change"
issues.problem: 'drop' and 'unexpected KPI change' collide with metric-movement-analysis ('KPI decline', 'metric changed'), and the body repeats much of that skill's decomposition. Neither says where one ends and the other begins.
issues.fix: Scope this skill to 'is this abnormal against baseline, and is it data or real'. Hand confirmed business changes to metric-movement-analysis for explanation, and say so in both descriptions.

issues.problem: No handling of alert fatigue across many metrics. With dozens of metrics at a 2-sigma rule, several false alerts a day are expected, and nothing tells the model to adjust thresholds or rank alerts.
issues.fix: Add a rule for multi-metric monitoring: stricter thresholds or a false-discovery control, alert ranking by business impact, and a weekly false-positive count.

issues.quote: sample, segment concentration, quality-check result, confidence, ranked
issues.problem: 'confidence' has no scale or criteria, so it will be reported inconsistently across cards and weeks.
issues.fix: Define a three-level confidence scale tied to data-quality result and baseline agreement.

issues.section: Check the data before the business
issues.quote: Compare against more than one useful baseline when available: prior period,
issues.problem: No rule for when the baselines disagree (for example, anomalous against last week but normal against the same week last year).
issues.fix: Require the card to report each baseline's verdict, and set status to 'expected pattern' only when the seasonal baseline explains the move.

issues.problem: No draft-and-approve step before sending alerts outward (Slack, email). Outward posting goes through platform approval, but the skill should draft first.
issues.fix: Add: draft the alert message for approval before the first send, and have the recurring routine post only to the approved destination.

scenarios.prompt: Signups were down 35% yesterday compared with last Tuesday. Is that real or a tracking problem? Here's the daily series for the last 90 days.
scenarios.why: The data-first checklist (freshness, schema, duplicates, numerator/denominator, calendar effects, single-account dominance) plus same-weekday and recent-range baselines would give a well-reasoned anomaly card with a status and disproof tests. The model can pick a sensible threshold and explain it.

scenarios.prompt: Set up daily anomaly monitoring on our 40 KPIs from the ops Google Sheet and ping #metrics in Slack when something breaks. Don't spam us.
scenarios.why: The skill gives no detection method or parameters, nothing on false alarms across 40 metrics, no schedule_routine setup, and nowhere to keep 'alert status and owner' between runs. It also has no draft-then-approve step before posting to Slack. The request is outside what the skill actually teaches.

metric-definition-and-data-quality.job: audit data quality before trusting metrics
metric-definition-and-data-quality.summary: A 48-line checklist that pins a source's expected shape, runs eight ordered data-quality tests (freshness through join fan-out), and reports each issue with its metric impact and a blocked or provisional status. It includes no drift method, severity scale, template, or script.
strengths: A clear eight-step order from freshness to join quality, including many-to-many row multiplication.
Requires showing results before and after any proposed exclusion; no silent drops.
A blocked/provisional status tied to whether the issue can change the decision.
Treats a pipeline change as a possible cause until an independent source confirms the business change.
missing: Definition-drift and distribution-drift test method
Severity rubric tied to quantified metric impact
Data-quality report template (persona day_one deliverable)
bash_exec profiling/check script
Fallback when expected schema/owner unknown
Volume, bot/test traffic, sampling, and referential-integrity checks
Worked example

issues.quote: totals across independent supplied sources and stable metric
issues.problem: The name and description promise metric-definition testing and 'drift', but this half-line is the only coverage. There is no method for detecting definition drift (recomputing under old and new definitions over an overlap window, event-version counts) or distribution drift.
issues.fix: Add a definition-drift step: list definition and event-version changes, recompute the metric both ways over an overlap period, and report the gap. Add a distribution check against a trailing baseline.

issues.quote: latest event and extract time against the expected delay.
issues.problem: No compute path. There is no bundled script and no instruction to run the eight checks in bash_exec, so the audit is done by eye and cannot be reproduced week to week.
issues.fix: Ship scripts/dq_checks.py (input CSV plus a small config of keys, required fields, and ranges) that emits one row per check, and tell the model to run it in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Record the source, covered period, extraction time, expected grain, primary or
issues.problem: It assumes the expected shape is known. When there is no schema doc or owner, which is common, the skill gives no fallback, so the model either stalls or silently guesses keys and ranges.
issues.fix: Add: infer a candidate shape from the data, label each field ASSUMED, and confirm keys and allowed ranges with the owner via ask_question before marking any check failed.

issues.quote: likely metric impact, severity, and owner
issues.problem: Severity has no scale and impact has no method, and there is no overall report structure (dataset status, checks passed, open issues). Quinn's day_one 'data-quality report' has no template.
issues.fix: Define severity (blocker / material / minor) by quantified metric impact (recompute with and without the affected rows), and ship templates/data-quality-report.md.

issues.problem: Missing common analytics-data checks: row volume against a trailing baseline, bot/test/internal traffic, analytics-tool sampling or thresholding (GA4), referential integrity, and timezone-boundary effects at period edges.
issues.fix: Add these as sub-checks under coverage and validity.

issues.quote: "data quality", "metric definition", "validate data"
issues.problem: The 'metric definition' trigger collides with kpi-analysis-getting-started, which actually defines metrics, while this body only tests data. Profiling a new dataset also overlaps Toran's dataset-exploration.
issues.fix: Rename or re-scope to 'data-quality audit', drop the 'metric definition' trigger, and merge in dataset-exploration's profiling steps rather than keeping two skills.

scenarios.prompt: Before I compute monthly revenue, can you check this orders CSV against the Stripe payouts export?
scenarios.why: The ordered checks (freshness, coverage with control totals, schema, key uniqueness, nulls, validity including currency, cross-source consistency, join matched/unmatched/fan-out), plus before/after exclusion reporting and a blocked/provisional status, would give a senior-quality audit. A capable model would run it with pandas unprompted.

scenarios.prompt: DAU fell 20% overnight on the dashboard. All I have is a screenshot of the Looker tile and a partial event export with no schema docs. Is the data broken?
scenarios.why: 'Pin the expected shape' assumes known keys, ranges, and late-arrival windows. There is no fallback for inferring and labelling an assumed shape, no volume-versus-trailing-baseline check, and no path for screenshot-only evidence. 'Treat a pipeline change as a possible cause' points the right way but gives no method.

14:invoice-drafting-and-issue.job: draft customer invoice from approved terms
14:invoice-drafting-and-issue.summary: Builds a sourced draft.json from contract, SOW, PO or approval emails, runs stdlib scripts for exact totals, UK/other required fields and register-based double billing, renders a DRAFT-watermarked HTML/PDF, and uses one ask_question card with a SHA-256-bound approval log before its only permitted write: creating the invoice as a Draft in the billing system.
strengths: Five working stdlib-only scripts, all passing --selftest: Decimal totals that show per-line versus per-invoice VAT rounding and withhold the grand total until the method is chosen; regime field checks that split BLOCKS APPROVAL from BLOCKS ISSUE; line-key double billing, including repeats inside one draft; a DRAFT watermark that cannot be removed, with HTML escaping; and a SHA-256-bound approval log that rejects edited artefacts.

Exemplary approval design. Each action needs its own yes. A bare 'yes' is refused where it is ambiguous. An edit voids the approval. Mina never chooses an invoice number. The single allowed write (create as Draft) follows find, describe, validate_only, then create, with explicit fallbacks.

Correct, sourced domain detail: GOV.UK and HMRC VAT Notice 700/21 field lists, tax shown as a liability, a changed bank detail treated as a BEC exception, Xero 'authorised' meaning posted, and VIES REST checks with data minimisation ('Do not paste it into web search').

Excellent worked example (oriel-april) covering a double-billed retainer, a rate conflict between the SOW and an email, missing VAT, and an incomplete register, with a 'what a wrong answer would look like' section and a follow-on after the answers arrive.

Platform fit checked against the backend. find, describe, run and resume capability with validate_only exist. Packages land at /home/user/skills/<slug> and ~/workspace is durable. The THREAD routine prompt forbids external actions in unattended runs. The skill falls back cleanly when Python, headless Chrome or a billing integration is missing.
missing: Double-billing match against billing-export rows (customer + period + amount) when the register is empty or incomplete
Guard that a billing-system 'Draft' cannot auto-finalize or auto-email (for example Stripe auto_advance)
Time-and-materials, usage and rebillable-expense billing rules (approved timesheets, billable flags, rate cards, increments, receipts)
Deposit, milestone, advance and pro-forma invoices handled in-skill instead of routed away
Tax-inclusive pricing and percentage discounts in invoice_totals.py
Structured e-invoicing mandates and customer AP-portal or PO-matching requirements
US sales-tax basics at the invoice level (exemption certificates on file, taxable versus non-taxable lines) beyond 'ask the accountant'
Light intake path for a one-off invoice
Currency-formatted money (symbol, thousands separators) in the rendered draft, and late-payment or terms wording

issues.quote: Register empty or gappy → ask for the billing export; the export wins.
issues.problem: register_check.py compares line keys only against the register. It uses a billing export only for invoice numbers. On a first run, or with a gappy register, a period already billed in the export raises no REPEAT and the script exits 0. Tested: an export row 'Design retainer April 2026' as INV-1060 against the April retainer draft. The model is told the export 'wins' but gets no check that uses it for double billing.
issues.fix: Extend register_check.py to match export rows by customer plus service period or description and amount, and report likely repeats. Until then, tell the model to compare export rows by hand and to write 'double billing: unchecked' in the review block when neither source can prove it.

issues.quote: the status field is Draft, validate_only, then create)
issues.problem: Checking only the status field misses billing systems where a Draft is not inert. For example, a Stripe draft with automatic advancement can finalize and email the customer about an hour after creation, and some tools email on create. An approval to create a draft could then become an unapproved send.
issues.fix: In the describe step, also require any auto-finalize, auto-advance or email-on-create setting to be explicitly off (for example Stripe auto_advance=false) and shown in the approval question. If it cannot be set, fall back to owner entry.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: No intake → load `run_capability(id="skill:bookkeeping-getting-started", input={})`
issues.problem: A new user who asks for one invoice is sent through full bookkeeping onboarding (sources, chart, opening balances) before any draft appears. The invoice needs only the seller's legal name, address, contact, tax registration and approver.
issues.fix: Add a lightweight path: one ask_question for the five seller fields that writes a partial intake.json, then continue. Offer the full getting-started only if the user wants ongoing bookkeeping.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: Contract, SOW, PO, signed change, approver email
issues.problem: Time-and-materials, usage and rebillable-expense lines are among the most common small-team invoices, and the skill has no source rules for them: approved timesheets, billable flags, role rates, rounding increments, receipts and markup. A model would treat a raw timesheet as an approved source.
issues.fix: Add an input row for time, usage and expenses, plus a short reference: who approved the hours or usage, billable filter, rate card source, increment rounding, and whether expense receipts are attached.

issues.quote: otherwise `other` (`references/invoice-field-checklists.md`) [48][28].
issues.problem: The skill is UK-centric and never mentions structured e-invoicing mandates that are live in 2026 (Belgium Peppol B2B since January 2026, Poland KSeF, France's reform from September 2026, Italy SDI) or customer AP portals. In those cases a watermarked PDF is not the legal invoice and the 'other' field minimum is the wrong check.
issues.fix: In regime selection, flag seller countries with e-invoicing mandates, and customers that require an AP portal or PO format. Say the owner must issue through the compliant channel, and route format questions to the accountant.

issues.quote: from `templates/draft.json`: one line per approved
issues.problem: templates/draft.json ships a placeholder conflicts entry ({"field": null, "resolved": null}). A draft with no real conflicts that keeps it fails field_check.py with 'unresolved conflict on None' and blocks approval for no reason (verified).
issues.fix: Ship "conflicts": [] in the template and document the entry shape in a reference, or have field_check skip entries whose field is null.

issues.quote: it in that system, records an approval for Mina to act; a bare "yes" does
issues.problem: Step 8 packs question design, capability discovery, hashing, logging and yes-parsing into a 19-line paragraph. The same rules are restated in approval-and-ledger-draft.md section 2, approval-questions.md and the log_approval.py docstring, so a model can easily miss a clause.
issues.fix: Cut step 8 to four bullets (discover capability, ask with the template, record with log_approval.py, branch on its exit code). Leave the detailed rules in the template and the script only.

issues.quote: Extra workshop day | 14 Apr | 1 | £900.00 | £900.00 | Email approval, M. Ode, 10 Apr
issues.problem: The short example prices the line at £900 and shows 'Subtotal £900.00' while the £850 versus £900 conflict is still unresolved. That is the behaviour the walkthrough lists as wrong ('£900 because it is newer'), and the walkthrough itself shows '£900.00 or £850.00'.
issues.fix: Show the rate as '£850 or £900 (conflict)' and give the subtotal as either figure, matching the walkthrough.

scenarios.prompt: Invoice Oriel Health for September: the £3,500 retainer under SOW-014 plus the two extra workshop days Mark approved by email (attached). Same as last month otherwise.
scenarios.why: The intake and register already exist from earlier months. Step 2 builds keyed, sourced lines (SOW-014/retainer/2026-09, extra days). Step 3 compares each line with the August invoice. Step 4 runs invoice_totals, field_check (uk-vat) and register_check, and a REPEAT would catch a re-billed retainer. Steps 6-8 render the watermarked draft, fill the review block, put conflicts and missing fields on one ask_question card, and hash-log the answer. Nothing is numbered or sent. The only friction is that the VAT rate must be re-supplied or stored as a rule, which is correct under 'Tax fields: the owner or accountant only'.

scenarios.prompt: We just started with you. Invoice Harbour Florists for September. Hours are in the attached Harvest CSV and our Xero invoice export is attached too. Create it in Xero and send it today; the last number was INV-1102.
scenarios.why: The guardrails hold. Sending is refused. Step 8 plus approval-and-ledger-draft section 3 limit the Xero write to create-as-DRAFT after a verified, hash-bound approval, Mina passes no number of her own, and Xero's auto-assigned number is recorded. Three gaps remain. (1) With no intake, the Inputs table sends the user into the full bookkeeping-getting-started onboarding before any draft. (2) The register is empty, so register_check.py reads only invoice numbers from the export. It exits 0 with no REPEAT even when the export already holds a September Harbour invoice (verified with a test export), and nothing tells the model to compare export rows by customer and period by hand. (3) The skill has no guidance for time-based lines: whether the Harvest hours were approved, which are billable, role rates, or rounding increments.

better: Adds executable, self-tested checks (Decimal totals with rounding comparison, regime field checks, double billing, rendering, approval log) where main only said 'Recalculate line totals'
Sourced jurisdiction field lists (GOV.UK general, HMRC VAT Notice 700/21, a stated minimum for other jurisdictions)
Double-billing detection through contract/line/period keys and an invoice register, with a next-number suggestion that is never an assignment
Precise action menu via ask_question and hash-bound approval logging. Defines the single permitted write (create as Draft) with a find, describe, validate_only, create sequence and fallbacks
Recurring-billing checks, customer VAT ID checks, a before-approval checklist, and a full worked example with wrong-answer contrasts
Sharper description and triggers, with explicit do-not-use routing to accounts-receivable-follow-up and the accountant
worse: About 3x longer SKILL.md, with the approval rules restated in four places; step 8 is hard to follow
New hard dependency on the bookkeeping intake and state folder, even for a one-off invoice
The double-billing check looks authoritative but passes silently on export-only data, where main at least asked for a manual comparison against the contract
A template placeholder conflict adds a spurious approval blocker, and a bare 'yes' is now re-asked, adding user friction

communications-getting-started.job: set up comms facts, spokespeople and approvals
communications-getting-started.summary: A 38-line onboarding checklist. It collects the company's facts with their sources, the spokespeople and their approved quotes, customer naming permissions, who approves what, off-limits topics and the embargo process, then returns a five-part setup brief.
strengths: The source map records where each fact lives and when it was last checked, which is real PR hygiene
Sets an approval owner for each asset type (release, pitch, quote, figure, incident statement) and says who may contact reporters
Names the usual off-limits topics and requires an agreed embargo process
Clear no-guess and no-self-approval guardrails that match Noor's boundaries
missing: Persisting the setup to memory, and memory_search before asking
A minimum-question intake that pre-fills from the website and Drive
Disclosure and regulatory constraints (listed company, regulated sector, fundraising)
Crisis contact tree and out-of-hours approvers
PR goals, KPIs and priority audiences/outlets
Existing reporter relationships, past coverage and do-not-contact list
Boilerplate drafting when none exists
Approvals log format

issues.problem: The setup brief is only returned in chat. Nothing is written to durable memory or a workspace file, so later Noor skills (angle, release, pitch, holding statement) can't read the approval owners, off-limits topics or approved quotes, and have to ask again.
issues.fix: Add a step to memory_store the source map, spokespeople/approved quotes, approval matrix, off-limits list and embargo rule, and to write a comms-setup doc to the workspace. Start the skill with memory_search so it only asks about what is missing or stale.

issues.quote: Ask for the company boilerplate, current products, recent news, figures the
issues.problem: The model asks for everything in one turn, with no minimum set and no attempt to gather it itself. That's a heavy intake for a small-company user.
issues.fix: Ask three things first: the next announcement and its date, who approves, and what can't be said. Pre-fill the boilerplate, products and published figures from the company site/newsroom (web_fetch) and from workspace or Drive files, then ask the user to confirm them. Offer to draft a boilerplate for approval if none exists.

issues.quote: List off-limits topics: funding,
issues.problem: There are no disclosure or regulatory limits: listed-company rules (Reg FD, MAR/inside information, quiet periods), regulated-sector claims (health, finance), or rules on comparative or advertising claims. These decide what Noor may ever write.
issues.fix: Add a question on whether the company is listed, raising money or regulated, and record the disclosure rules and the named legal reviewer in the setup.

issues.problem: There is no crisis contact tree or out-of-hours escalation. holding-statement-draft depends on knowing who approves at 2am and whether legal or security must review.
issues.fix: Record incident approvers, legal/security reviewers, the status-page owner and their out-of-hours contacts as part of setup.

issues.quote: Ask for the company boilerplate, current products, recent news, figures the
issues.problem: It never asks about PR goals, target audiences, priority outlets, existing reporter relationships, past coverage or the brand voice guide. A senior comms hire would learn these first.
issues.fix: Add goals and success measures, target audiences/outlets, known reporter relationships and do-not-contact list, and links to past coverage and voice guidelines to the brief.

issues.quote: The first three pieces of work, with reasons.
issues.problem: There are no criteria for choosing the first work, and no first win delivered in the same session.
issues.fix: Rank by the nearest dated announcement and the biggest missing approval, and offer to run news-angle-and-key-messages on the next announcement right away.

issues.problem: It doesn't say how an approval is recorded (who, when, which channel), so later 'approved' labels can't be traced.
issues.fix: Keep an approvals log with approver, date and evidence (email or message link) and point the other skills to it.

issues.quote: Set up communications work from facts, spokespeople, approved messages, approval owners, and off-limits topics.
issues.problem: The description doesn't say to load this first or when memory has no comms setup. The 'media relations' trigger overlaps media-list-research and media-pitch-email.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Use on the first comms conversation, or when memory holds no approved facts, spokespeople or approvers...' and drop the generic 'media relations' trigger.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Noor, we're a 15-person fintech in Manchester launching our SME invoicing app in six weeks. Get yourself set up for our PR.
scenarios.why: 'Map facts and people' and 'Set the approval rules' lead the model to collect the right things, and the 5-item brief is a sensible result. But it asks about a dozen questions in one turn with no minimum set, and doesn't say to pull the boilerplate and published figures from the website (web_fetch) or from Drive. Nothing is saved with memory_store, so news-angle-and-key-messages and press-release-draft will ask for the same approvals and off-limits list again.

scenarios.prompt: It's just me, the founder. No boilerplate, no approved quotes. Our Series A closes next month but isn't public, and I want to announce our three new enterprise customers next week.
scenarios.why: The skill flags funding as off-limits and asks which customers agreed to be named, which is correct. But it has no decision path for a single approver who is also the spokesperson, no step to draft a boilerplate for approval, no way to get customer consent in writing, and no warning that talking about the announcement before the round closes can conflict with investor or securities constraints. 'The first three pieces of work' has no rule for choosing them, so the model may not sequence customer consent before the announcement.

holding-statement-draft.summary: A 39-line guide to drafting a holding statement of under 100 words in the first hours of an incident: confirm the facts with their time and source, then write what happened, what is being done, what people can do and when the next update comes. It leaves out cause, blame, scale and 'data is safe' claims, and lists the questions that remain open.
strengths: Under 100 words with a fixed 4-part structure, including the next-update time and place
Explicit 'we do not yet know' wording and a clear list of what not to say (cause, blame, suppliers, staff, scale, refunds, unconfirmed data safety)
Records the source and time of each fact, and asks whether legal or security must review
Short social and longer status-page/reporter versions, plus an open-questions list for the owner
missing: Regulatory notification flags and sequencing (breach, securities, recall)
Acknowledgment/apology line with legal clearance
Reactive reporter Q&A holding lines and a named responder
Update cadence and versioned log across channels
Internal staff and support-macro versions
Safety-first ordering for physical-harm incidents
Handoff to incident owners (Casey/Robin) and a scheduled next update
Proactive vs reactive decision

issues.quote: Ask who approves the statement and whether legal or
issues.problem: Regulatory and legal duties are left to the user to raise: breach notification to regulators and individuals (GDPR/UK GDPR 72h, US state laws), material-incident disclosure for listed companies, product-recall authority notices. The order of those notices and the public statement matters.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: if personal data, money, safety or a listed company is involved, flag the likely notification duties, make legal review mandatory before release, and note that affected customers or the regulator may need to hear first.

issues.quote: What happened, with the time and who is affected.
issues.problem: There's no acknowledgment of impact or apology line. Standard crisis practice pairs facts with a human acknowledgment, cleared with legal so it doesn't admit liability.
issues.fix: Add an optional line such as 'We know this is disrupting your work and we are sorry', with a note that legal approves apology wording in breach or safety cases.

issues.quote: social posts and a longer one for a status page or reporter.
issues.problem: There are no reactive press lines. When a reporter asks for comment, the skill offers no Q&A holding lines for likely questions, no named responder, no on/off-record guidance, and no alternative to 'no comment', even though 'press response' is a trigger.
issues.fix: Add a reporter-response block: a 2-3 sentence on-record reply, answers to the 5 likely questions ('was data taken?', 'who is the vendor?', 'how many affected?') built only from confirmed facts, and who sends it after approval.

issues.quote: When the next update comes, and where.
issues.problem: There's no update cadence or version control. The next update has to happen even when nothing is new, versions need timestamps, and the status page, support macros, social posts and staff notes must all match.
issues.fix: Add an update log (version, time, approver, channels), a rule to post at the promised time even with 'no change yet', and a staff/support version so frontline teams say the same thing.

issues.quote: What people can do meanwhile, if anything.
issues.problem: When safety is involved (recall, physical harm), the protective action must come first. Here it is item 3 and 'if anything'.
issues.fix: If safety is at risk, put the protective instruction first ('Stop using X now') and escalate straight to the named approver.

issues.problem: No handoff or scheduling. It doesn't consult the incident owner (Casey for software incidents, Robin for mass customer recovery) for facts, and doesn't schedule a follow-up for the promised update time.
issues.fix: Use consult_teammate or handoff_to_expert for incident facts and bulk customer comms, and schedule_followup at the next-update time to draft version 2.

issues.quote: Use this in the first hours of an outage, breach, recall, or public complaint.
issues.problem: No step decides whether a statement is warranted and in which mode (proactive publish vs reactive, held until asked), which matters for a single public complaint.
issues.fix: Add a quick severity/visibility check: who knows, how public it is, and whether to hold the line reactively or post proactively.

scenarios.prompt: Our app has been down since 9:40, customers are complaining on X. Draft something we can post now.
scenarios.why: 'Confirm what is known' covers start time, who is affected, what they can't do and the current action. The 4-part structure plus the short social version and longer status-page version, with open questions listed for the owner, gives a usable, safe statement, much like Noor's voice sample.

scenarios.prompt: We think customer emails were exposed through a vendor misconfiguration. A reporter at The Register wants comment by 4pm and legal says say nothing. What do we put out?
scenarios.why: The skill rightly leaves out the supplier and any 'data is safe' claim, and asks whether legal/security review. But it doesn't flag breach notification duties (e.g. GDPR 72-hour regulator notice, telling affected individuals before or alongside public statements) or securities disclosure. It gives no reporter-response line as an alternative to 'no comment', no way to settle legal's 'say nothing' against a press deadline, and no handoff to the incident owner (Casey/Robin).

launch-communications-plan.job: plan launch communications timeline and owners
launch-communications-plan.summary: A 39-line one-page launch comms plan: an audience-by-message-by-channel matrix, a dated timeline table with owner, approver and status, and a risk list with holding lines, with no scheduling or sending by the agent.
strengths: The timeline table has date, time and time zone, owner, approver and a four-state status
'Put the embargo lift time in one place and use it everywhere' is a strong single-source-of-truth rule
Staff and key customers hear first; sales and support notes and first-week follow-ups are included
Each risk has a holding line and a decision-maker, and the agent never schedules or sends
missing: Launch tiering and go/no-go gate
Schedule worked back from launch day with lead times
Asset and readiness checklist (press kit, visuals, Q&A, spokesperson prep)
Success metrics and post-launch readout
Partner and investor co-approval gates
Provisional-date and slip handling
Handoffs to sibling Noor skills
Sheet/Doc export and approval-chase follow-ups

issues.quote: Use this for a product, funding, partnership, or company announcement.
issues.problem: There's no launch tier or go/no-go step. Every announcement gets the same plan, even though a minor feature needs a blog post and changelog while a funding round needs embargoed briefings. Partner co-approval (partnerships) and investor sign-off (funding) are not called out.
issues.fix: Start with a tier decision (e.g. T1 press push / T2 owned plus a few pitches / T3 owned only) with criteria. Add required co-approvers per type (partner comms team, lead investor), and a go/no-go check 48 hours before launch.

issues.quote: Build a table with one row per action:
issues.problem: Rows are listed but not worked back from launch day. There are no lead times (monthlies months ahead, trade 2-6 weeks, embargoed briefings T-5 to T-2) and no critical path, so the model may produce a flat list with missing milestones.
issues.fix: Generate the timeline in T-minus form from the confirmed launch date, with standard milestones (angle locked, release approved, media list agreed, briefings, assets final, go/no-go), and flag any milestone already missed.

issues.quote: Cover briefings under embargo, the release, the blog post, email, social posts,
issues.problem: Channels are listed but not the assets and readiness items (press kit, images, demo video, Q&A/FAQ, spokesperson briefing, internal FAQ). There are no handoffs to the sibling skills that produce them.
issues.fix: Add an asset checklist with owners and route each item to its sibling: press-release-draft, media-list-research, media-pitch-email, spokesperson-briefing, holding-statement-draft.

issues.problem: No measurement. The plan has no success measures (coverage targets, share of voice, referral traffic, sign-ups) and no first-week results report, so the team can't judge the launch.
issues.fix: Add a 'Measure' section with 2-3 agreed metrics, their source, and a dated post-launch readout owner.

issues.quote: List each audience: customers, prospects, press, partners, staff, and
issues.problem: It doesn't name inputs up front: confirmed date, whether the date is firm, agreed key messages, spokesperson availability, embargo terms, budget. It also doesn't reuse the setup or the key messages from news-angle-and-key-messages.
issues.fix: Add a 'What you need' block and pull approved messages and approvers from memory before drafting.

issues.quote: Plan a launch's messages, channels, owners, timing, and approvals on one page.
issues.problem: The 'launch plan' / 'launch day' triggers overlap Toran's product-launch-marketing, Alex's product-launch-plan and Zara's commercial-launch-strategy when several experts are hired together.
issues.fix: Scope the description to the 'PR and communications side of an announcement (press, owned channels, staff, customers)' and say that pricing, enablement and GTM go to Alex or Zara.

issues.quote: For each, give the holding line and who decides.
issues.problem: Holding lines are asked for inline with no standard, and there's no link to holding-statement-draft for launch-day incidents (site outage, leak).
issues.fix: Point to holding-statement-draft for the outage and leak scenarios, and keep inline holding lines to one approved sentence each.

issues.problem: There's no platform route for the artefact or follow-through. The table isn't written to a Sheet/Doc, and there are no reminders to chase approvals marked pending or blocked.
issues.fix: Offer to write the plan to Google Sheets or Docs via run_block (as a draft) and use schedule_followup to chase blocked approvals before each milestone.

scenarios.prompt: We announce our partnership with Xero on 3 March at 9am GMT. Build the comms plan.
scenarios.why: The audience matrix, timeline table and risk list give a usable one-pager. But the skill never makes partner co-approval of the release and quotes a separate gate, gives no work-back milestones (angle lock, release approval, media list, embargoed briefings), no asset checklist, and no success measures. A capable model may fill some of these in, but the skill doesn't make it.

scenarios.prompt: Launch is in 5 days, the date might slip, there's no press release yet, and marketing has already scheduled social posts for Tuesday.
scenarios.why: 'Risks and approvals' covers a delay with a holding line, and statuses can mark items blocked. But there's no guidance on compressing a timeline (drop embargoed briefings, go with a blog plus a few exclusive pitches), no provisional-date handling, and no step to reconcile or pause already-scheduled assets. The 'one embargo time' rule doesn't cover a date that may move.

media-list-research.summary: A 40-line procedure to agree the beat, search recent coverage (ideally the last six months), record each reporter's outlet, role, recent pieces with links, fit, public contact route and pitching preferences, then rank them strong/possible/weak, with no contacting and nothing added to mailing tools.
strengths: Every reporter needs recent, dated, linked evidence and a one-line fit
A public contact route is recorded only with its source, and unverified contacts are flagged
Transparent exclusion: skip links older than a year and report how many were skipped
Firm ban on inventing reporters, articles, emails or interest, and on loading names into mailing tools
missing: Search and verification recipe using web_search/web_fetch
Ingesting, re-verifying and deduping an existing list
Fixed table/CSV/Sheet output that is saved for the pitch skill
Journalist personal-data/privacy rules and do-not-contact tracking
Outlet tier/reach alongside fit
Exclusive candidates and staff/freelancer distinction
Beat-change and departure checks

issues.quote: Search for recent coverage of the subject, ideally from the last six months.
issues.problem: No method or tools: it doesn't say to use web_search with outlet/topic/byline queries, web_fetch the author page to confirm byline and current outlet, or check that the reporter hasn't moved beat or job. A model can easily attribute articles to the wrong person.
issues.fix: Add a search recipe (topic + 'reporter'/'by' queries, outlet section pages, author archive pages), require web_fetch confirmation of each cited article's byline and date, and a check that the latest byline at the outlet is recent.

issues.quote: Ask for any reporters the company already knows or must
issues.problem: No path for an inherited or existing list (agency CSV, CRM export). Old lists are the most common starting point and the main source of stale or wrong contacts.
issues.fix: Accept a CSV or Sheet, process it with bash_exec, re-verify each row against recent work, dedupe, and mark departed or changed-beat reporters and do-not-contact names.

issues.quote: For each reporter record:
issues.problem: Fields are listed but there's no reusable table/CSV/Sheet format and nothing is saved, so media-pitch-email ('after the media list is agreed') can't reliably consume it.
