issues.fix: Output a fixed-column table (name, outlet, role, tier, fit, evidence links and dates, contact route and source, preferences, status). Save it with write_workspace_file or as a Google Sheet via run_block, and memory_store the agreed list.

issues.quote: where a public contact route is listed, with its source;
issues.problem: No privacy limit. Journalist contact data is personal data (GDPR legitimate-interest basis). There's no rule to record only professional routes, avoid personal phones and addresses, or honour opt-outs.
issues.fix: Record only professional, publicly listed routes. Never collect personal phone numbers, home addresses or guessed emails. Keep a do-not-contact column, and note that the list is for relevant pitching only.

issues.quote: kinds of outlet (trade, local, national, newsletter, podcast), and how many
issues.problem: Fit is ranked but there's no outlet priority or reach tier, no staff vs freelancer distinction, and no candidate for an exclusive, which is how senior practitioners order a list.
issues.fix: Add an outlet tier (T1/T2/T3 by audience relevance and reach) alongside fit, and suggest 1-2 exclusive candidates with a reason.

issues.problem: It doesn't tie the list to the agreed angle or key messages, so fit is judged against a loosely described 'subject'.
issues.fix: Read the chosen angle from news-angle-and-key-messages (memory or user) and judge each name's fit against that angle.

scenarios.prompt: Build me a list of 20 UK reporters who cover SME fintech for our invoicing launch.
scenarios.why: 'Define the beat' fixes region, outlet type and count. 'Research and record' makes each name carry dated linked pieces and a sourced contact route, and the ranked list flags unchecked contacts. With web_search, a capable model produces a credible, honest list, though tool use is implied, not stated.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our 2022 agency media list (CSV, 80 names). Update it for our climate-tech launch across the US, Germany and Japan and give me the top 40.
scenarios.why: The one-year stale rule helps. But there's no step to ingest and re-verify an existing list (current outlet, beat change, departures), no dedupe, no non-English search guidance, and no batching (bash_exec to process the CSV, a Sheet as output). A model may simply re-rank old names without confirming they still work there.

media-pitch-email.summary: A 40-line guide to a pitch of under 150 words for one reporter: cite their recent piece with date and link (or recommend a better name), state the news with one proof fact, the embargo, the ask and the contact. It marks the approval state of every figure and quote and allows at most one value-adding follow-up after three working days, with no sending.
strengths: The decision point to suggest a better name instead of forcing a weak pitch
Under 150 words with a clear structure: plain subject line, tie-in to recent work, one proof fact, explicit ask, reply route
Embargo with date, time and time zone, and approval state on every figure and quote
Follow-up etiquette: one follow-up, three working days later, adding something new, stop on decline, no inducements or false claims of other coverage
missing: Embargo-agreement step before sharing embargoed details
Exclusive offer logic and sequencing
Verifying the cited article with web_fetch
Pitch tracker for sends, replies, declines and do-not-contact
Batch personalisation for a full list
Timing and lead-time guidance by outlet type
Inputs block and use of reporter channel preferences
Gmail draft creation after approval

issues.quote: embargo date, time, and time zone, if any;
issues.problem: It treats the embargo as a line in the pitch. It doesn't secure the reporter's agreement to the embargo before sharing embargoed specifics, and has no exclusive option. Both are standard practice, and ignoring them risks a broken embargo.
issues.fix: Add an 'Embargo or exclusive' decision: first email offers the story under embargo, or as an exclusive with a reply-by deadline, and asks for agreement. Embargoed details and the release go only after they agree. Offer an exclusive to one outlet at a time.

issues.quote: Name the recent piece that makes the story a fit, with its date and link. If
issues.problem: No verification step. The cited article is the whole basis of the pitch, and nothing requires confirming it exists and is by this reporter. A hallucinated or misattributed article badly damages the pitch.
issues.fix: Require web_fetch of the cited URL to confirm byline, date and topic before drafting. If it can't be confirmed, say so and don't use it.

issues.quote: Stop if the reporter declines
issues.problem: No pitch log. Sends, replies, declines and do-not-contact requests aren't recorded, so the one-follow-up and stop rules can't be enforced across sessions or reporters.
issues.fix: Keep a pitch tracker (reporter, date sent by user, status, follow-up due, outcome) in memory or a Sheet, and schedule_followup for the day-3 check.

issues.quote: Use this for one reporter at a time, after the media list is agreed.
issues.problem: There's no workflow for pitching a list: personalised variants in bulk, sequencing around an exclusive or embargo, or pulling the reporter's row and preferences from media-list-research.
issues.fix: Allow a batch mode: read the agreed list, draft one personalised pitch per row, list the rows with no clear fit, and present everything as drafts for approval.

issues.problem: Inputs aren't named up front: chosen angle, approved facts and quotes, spokesperson availability, available assets (press kit, images, data), and the reporter's stated channel preferences.
issues.fix: Add a 'What you need' block and use the reporter's recorded channel preference (email vs DM) from the media list.

issues.quote: the ask: an interview, an early look, or data;
issues.problem: No timing guidance: reporter's time zone, lead times for monthlies or broadcast vs daily/online, and not pitching on the embargo day itself.
issues.fix: Add send-window guidance per outlet type and have the pitch date sit well before the embargo lift.

issues.quote: Keep it under 150 words:
issues.problem: There's no platform path to put the approved pitch where the user sends it, so users will copy and paste.
issues.fix: After approval, offer to create a Gmail draft via run_block (draft only, never send) so the user reviews and sends it themselves.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a pitch to Priya Shah at Sifted about our launch — she wrote about SME cash-flow problems last month. Embargo is 14 May, 9am BST.
scenarios.why: 'Why this reporter' anchors on her piece, and 'Write the pitch' gives a plain subject line, a tie-in, the news and proof fact, the embargo with time zone, a specific ask and a reply route under 150 words, with approval states marked. That matches the persona's voice sample and would pass a senior review.

scenarios.prompt: Pitch our launch to the 30 reporters on the list tomorrow. Embargo is 9am ET Thursday, but we want to give TechCrunch an exclusive first.
scenarios.why: The skill is one-reporter-at-a-time with no batch workflow or tracking. It has no exclusive logic (offer to one outlet, set a deadline, pitch the others only after it expires or is declined), and it writes the embargo details into the first email without asking the reporter to agree to the embargo first, which risks a leak and conflicts with offering an exclusive.

news-angle-and-key-messages.job: find news angle and key messages
news-angle-and-key-messages.summary: A 37-line guide to stating what changed in one sentence, testing newsworthiness against news values (a number moved, a problem solved, a first, a trend, a local link), calling out thin news, offering up to three angles by reader and outlet type, writing three one-sentence key messages, and logging every claim with source, confirmer and status.
strengths: The newsworthiness test uses real news values rather than company excitement
Explicit permission and duty to say the news is thin and suggest how to strengthen it (customer result, fresh data, better date)
A claims ledger with exact wording, source and date, who confirms, and confirmed/pending/cut status
A clear ban on inventing figures, customers, awards or trends
missing: Verifying 'first' and trend claims and checking prior coverage
A recommended angle with rationale
Message house structure and audience variants
Rules against misleading statistics and unsubstantiated superlatives
Inputs block and reuse of the setup brief
Timing and news-hook check
Angle archetypes and data-story guidance (e.g. from public-relations story-angles.md)

issues.quote: a first, a trend it fits, or a local link.
issues.problem: 'First' and 'trend' angles are suggested with no step to verify them. There's no web_search for prior announcements or competitor coverage, and no dated trend source. Unverified 'first' claims are a classic way to lose a reporter's trust.
issues.fix: Add a check: search recent coverage and competitor announcements for the claimed first or trend. Cite 2-3 dated pieces for any trend, or drop the angle.

issues.quote: Offer up to three angles. For each, name the reader it suits and the kind of
issues.problem: It offers options but no recommendation. A senior communicator picks one angle and explains why (target outlet, timing, proof strength). Leaving it all to the user weakens the deliverable.
issues.fix: Rank the angles on proof strength, audience relevance and timeliness, recommend one, and say what would change the recommendation.

issues.quote: Then write three key messages, each one sentence long,
issues.problem: The messages aren't structured as a message house (one umbrella statement, three pillars, proof points under each), and there are no audience variants (press vs customers vs staff). Downstream release, pitch and briefing skills need that structure.
issues.fix: Output an umbrella line plus three pillars, each with 1-2 proof points from the ledger, and a one-line variant per audience.

issues.quote: Do not invent a figure, customer, award, or trend to make the angle work.
issues.problem: It bans invented figures but not misleading framing of real ones: percentages from tiny bases, cherry-picked periods, and unsubstantiated superlatives or comparisons ('first', 'only', 'leading') that fall under advertising-standards rules.
issues.fix: Require the base and period for every percentage or growth figure, and evidence for any superlative or comparative claim. Otherwise rewrite it as a plain fact or cut it.

issues.problem: No inputs block and no reuse of setup. It doesn't name the announcement facts, date, approved spokespeople or off-limits topics it needs, and doesn't read them from communications-getting-started memory.
issues.fix: Add a 'What you need' block and memory_search for the approved source map and off-limits list before drafting.

issues.quote: stronger, such as a customer result, fresh data, or a better date.
issues.problem: Timing and news hooks are only mentioned as a fix for thin news. There's no check against competing news, seasonal or industry calendars, or embargo timing.
issues.fix: Add a timing check: planned date, competing events that week, and any calendar hook that strengthens the angle.

issues.quote: "story angle", "messaging"
issues.problem: The generic 'messaging' trigger will fire for brand positioning requests that belong to Zara's positioning-and-messaging or Maya's messaging-and-tone-matrix when those experts are on the team.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'announcement messaging' or 'press messages', and say in the description that this is for a specific announcement, not brand positioning.

scenarios.prompt: We're releasing v2 of our scheduling app with AI rescheduling next month. What's the story and what are our key messages?
scenarios.why: The one-sentence change, the news-values test, up to three angles by reader and outlet, three sourced messages and the claims ledger give a usable, honest output. It may miss whether competitors already announced the same feature, because nothing asks for a coverage check.

scenarios.prompt: We're the first UK platform to do X and our growth is 300% — make it newsworthy, our CEO wants TechCrunch.
scenarios.why: The ledger would mark '300%' and 'first' as pending, and the thin-news rule lets the model push back. But there's no step to verify 'first' via web_search, no rule to show the base and period behind a percentage, no substantiation rule for superlative or comparative claims, and no guidance on matching the angle to outlet tier. A model might still write messages around unverified claims.

compliance-evidence-tracking.job: track compliance evidence and audit readiness
compliance-evidence-tracking.summary: A 40-line outline that lists five compliance frameworks and four tracking components (control inventory, audit calendar, evidence management, gap analysis), then says to produce dashboards and checklists, with no steps, template or rules.
strengths: Names the right four artefacts for audit readiness: control inventory, audit calendar, evidence management and gap analysis.
Tracking 'when evidence was last collected' is the correct instinct for audit prep.
Short, and uses no Claude-Code-only constructs or connector placeholders.
missing: An evidence register schema with status values and a link per control
Evidence cadence driven by each control's frequency, plus freshness rules against the audit observation window
Handling of auditor request lists (PBC) and population and sample requests
Common-controls mapping so one control and its evidence satisfies several frameworks
An exceptions and deviations log with compensating controls
A no-compliance-claim rule, a not-legal-advice line, and a counsel or auditor handoff
An approval gate before any status goes to customers or auditors
FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN labelling per James's persona
Save to the workspace and a scheduled freshness reminder

issues.quote: Help track compliance requirements, prepare for audits, and maintain regulatory readiness.
issues.problem: This sentence is the whole procedure. It asks for no inputs (framework and version, scope, audit date, control list, evidence locations) and gives no ordered steps or decision points, so each run is improvised.
issues.fix: Add 'What you need first' (framework and version, audit type and window, in-scope systems, control list, owners, where evidence lives). Then add numbered steps: build the register, map evidence to each control, rate freshness against control frequency, flag gaps, and set reminders.

issues.quote: Produce compliance status dashboards, gap analyses, audit prep checklists, and evidence collection plans.
issues.problem: Nothing stops the model claiming compliance, calling a control effective without dated evidence, giving legal advice, or sharing a status with customers or auditors without approval. This contradicts Lena's boundaries ('never state that the company is compliant') and James's ('a control passes only on evidence').
issues.fix: Add rules. A control is 'evidenced' only with a dated artefact link. Never state compliance or readiness. This is not legal advice or an audit opinion. Legal judgements go to counsel via compliance-escalation-brief. Anything shared externally is a draft awaiting the owner's approval.

issues.problem: No deliverable schema is defined. 'Dashboards' and 'checklists' have no columns, statuses or layout, so the output can't be reused or compared from one run to the next.
issues.fix: Ship templates/evidence-register.csv (control ID, framework refs, owner, frequency, evidence artefact, link, period covered, last collected, next due, status: evidenced / stale / missing / exception) and a one-page audit-calendar template.

issues.quote: Trigger with "compliance", "audit prep", "SOC 2", "ISO 27001", "GDPR", "regulatory requirement"
issues.problem: Bare keywords like 'compliance' and 'GDPR' match almost every Lena request (questionnaires, DPA review, DSRs, data map). They also collide with ops-controls-and-escalations ('audit readiness') and policy-gap-review ('SOC 2 readiness', 'ISO 27001 gaps'), so the thinnest skill can win the routing.
issues.fix: If it is kept, narrow the description to 'maintain an evidence register and audit calendar for an upcoming audit window', and state that policy mapping and control design belong to the other skills.

issues.quote: Security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy
issues.problem: The table lists the Trust Services Criteria but misses what drives evidence work: only Security is required, Type I tests design at a point in time while Type II tests operation across an observation window, and auditors sample from populations across that window.
issues.fix: Add a short framework note on Type I vs Type II, the observation period, population and sample requests (PBC lists), the ISO 27001:2022 Statement of Applicability, and PCI DSS v4.0.x.

issues.quote: Consent, data rights, breach notification, DPO
issues.problem: This misstates GDPR as an auditable framework with fixed controls. Consent is only one of six lawful bases, a DPO is required only in certain cases, and it leaves out Article 30 records, DPIAs and the 72-hour breach clock.
issues.fix: Correct the row, mark GDPR as a regulation and not a certification, and route lawful-basis or DPO questions to counsel.

issues.quote: Track control effectiveness
issues.problem: Operating effectiveness is the auditor's opinion. The skill should track evidence that each control operated and leave the effectiveness judgement to the auditor.
issues.fix: Reword to 'track evidence of operation per control period; effectiveness is the auditor's conclusion'.

issues.quote: Where evidence is stored
issues.problem: It never says how to reach the evidence or where to keep the register. There is no use of run_block (Drive, Notion, Airtable), no pasted-export fallback, no write_workspace_file save, and no schedule_routine for freshness reminders.
issues.fix: Add a sources step: read connected Drive or Notion folders or ask for an export. Save the register to the workspace, and offer a monthly freshness check using schedule_routine.

scenarios.prompt: Our SOC 2 Type II observation window opens 1 March. Here's our control list as a CSV. Build an evidence tracker and tell me which evidence is stale or missing.
scenarios.why: The 'Evidence Management' bullets point at the right fields (what evidence, where stored, when last collected), but the skill defines no register columns and no freshness rule tied to each control's frequency or the observation window. It also has no order of work. The model would build a generic table and have to guess what 'stale' means.

scenarios.prompt: A prospect asks whether we're GDPR compliant and wants our ISO 27001 cert. We only have a SOC 2 Type I from last year. Can you prep a readiness status dashboard sales can send them today?
scenarios.why: 'Produce compliance status dashboards' and 'Timeline to compliance' invite a status claim. Nothing forbids saying the company is compliant, separates Type I from Type II, says GDPR is not a certification, routes the question to counsel, or requires approval before anything goes to a customer. All of that is in Lena's boundaries, and the skill would push the model to break them.

operational-runbook-writing.job: write operational runbook for recurring procedure
operational-runbook-writing.summary: Gives a solid Markdown runbook template (purpose, prerequisites, steps with expected result and failure action, verification, troubleshooting, rollback, escalation, history) wrapped in a /runbook slash command, with connector placeholders and three tips.
strengths: A reusable template with 'Expected result' and 'If it fails' for every step: the right structure for on-call use.
Rollback, Verification, Escalation and History sections are built in.
The tips are correct practitioner instincts: be exact, include failure modes, and have someone unfamiliar with the process test the runbook.
The description names concrete situations (tribal knowledge, adding rollback, escalation paths).
missing: Inputs named up front and an update/diff flow for existing runbooks
A source-of-truth rule for commands, with UNVERIFIED marking
Pre-checks, state capture, abort criteria and point of no return for risky steps
A blast-radius or risk rating and a change-approval requirement to run
Secrets handling
An owner, review date and staleness trigger (James's SOP convention)
A handoff to the engineering owner or Casey for code-level procedures
A route for automation candidates to ops-automate-a-workflow
Save a draft to the workspace, then approval before publishing

issues.quote: **Be painfully specific** — "Run the script" is not a step.
issues.problem: It demands exact commands and flags but never requires them to come from the owner, existing docs or a verified run. A model will invent plausible commands (like the example 'python sync.py --prod --dry-run'), and an on-call engineer may run them against production.
issues.fix: Add a rule: every command, path and flag must be quoted from supplied material or marked UNVERIFIED with a question for the owner. Before publishing, commands are dry-run or run in non-prod, or the cold-user test is completed.

issues.quote: Publish the completed runbook to your ops wiki
issues.problem: This is an external side effect with no approval step. James's boundaries forbid publishing an SOP-type document without the process-change approver's yes.
issues.fix: Save the draft with write_workspace_file, show it to the owner, and publish to Notion or Confluence only after an explicit approval. Log who approved and when.

issues.section: Create a step-by-step operational runbook for a recurring task or procedure.
issues.quote: Create a step-by-step operational runbook for a recurring task or procedure.
issues.problem: This is the entire procedure. It names no inputs (task, systems, access, who runs it, frequency, source material, existing runbook) and has no steps for extracting from notes, interviewing, updating an existing runbook, or deciding when to escalate to an engineering owner.
issues.fix: Add 'What you need first' and numbered steps: gather sources, then draft steps, list gaps as questions, add failure modes and rollback, run the cold-user test, get owner approval, publish, and set a review date.

issues.quote: /runbook $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command with $ARGUMENTS, which does not exist in the AutoGPT harness. The argument-hint frontmatter is dropped, and the H1 '/runbook' is a command name, not a title.
issues.fix: Delete the Usage block, retitle to 'Write an operational runbook', and move the argument into a named input.

issues.quote: If **~~ITSM** is connected:
issues.problem: The ~~placeholders point to references/CONNECTORS.md, which lists plugin MCP servers (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management) and an upstream .mcp.json. AutoGPT has no ITSM block, and there is no fallback when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Map the placeholders to real options (Notion or Google Docs via run_block, Confluence or PagerDuty via run_mcp_tool if connected). Otherwise ask for a pasted runbook or on-call export using ask_question. Drop CONNECTORS.md.

issues.quote: Runbook: [Task Name]
issues.problem: The template has no risk or blast-radius rating, approval-to-run, time estimate, abort or stop criteria, or point of no return. Also, the inner ``` fences at each step close the outer ```markdown block early, so the template renders broken.
issues.fix: Add Risk / Approvals / Est. duration to the header and an 'Abort if' line per step. Use ~~~ or indented code for the inner command blocks, or ship the template as templates/runbook.md.

issues.quote: turning tribal knowledge into exact step-by-step commands
issues.problem: This overlaps James's ops-write-an-sop ('document this process', 'turn this into a playbook') and ops-controls-and-escalations ('build an escalation path'), with no line saying which skill to load.
issues.fix: Add: 'For command-level or system procedures run by on-call; business processes go to ops-write-an-sop; org-wide escalation design goes to ops-controls-and-escalations.'

issues.quote: **Test the runbook** — Have someone unfamiliar with the process follow it.
issues.problem: This is a tip, not a gate. The skill also never covers secrets: nothing stops credentials or tokens being pasted into steps.
issues.fix: Make the cold-user test a required step before approval. Add 'reference the secret's vault location; never paste credentials into the runbook'.

scenarios.prompt: Our month-end invoice export to the accountant lives in Sam's head. Here's his walkthrough transcript. Turn it into a runbook anyone on ops can follow.
scenarios.why: The Output template maps cleanly onto the transcript, and 'Be painfully specific' plus 'Test the runbook' push toward usable steps. But no step says to pull steps only from the transcript, list what Sam left out, or ask about ambiguous steps. The 'If it fails' and Troubleshooting rows will be filled with plausible guesses. 'Publish the completed runbook to your ops wiki' would publish without James's approval.

scenarios.prompt: Update our existing Confluence runbook for failing over the Postgres replica: add rollback and escalation. I can't connect Confluence, PagerDuty isn't set up, and the on-call rota is in a Google Sheet.
scenarios.why: The update flow and escalation contacts only work 'If **~~knowledge base** is connected' or '~~ITSM'. There is no fallback to pasting the current runbook or reading the Sheet, and no diff/update procedure. There is also no failover safety content (pre-checks, data-loss point of no return, abort criteria). Meanwhile 'Be painfully specific' pushes the model to write exact failover commands it has never seen, and nothing hands off to the engineering owner even though James's persona excludes engineering implementation.

team-capacity-planning.job: plan team capacity against upcoming demand
team-capacity-planning.summary: A /capacity-plan slash-command skill that asks for team, workload, upcoming work and constraints, lists people/budget/time dimensions, suggests utilization targets by role type, and gives a Markdown capacity-plan template with a per-person utilization table and scenarios.
strengths: Names the inputs up front (team and roles, current workload, upcoming work, constraints).
The template includes a per-person utilization table, bottlenecks, and explicit do-nothing / hire / deprioritize scenarios.
Role-type utilization targets (IC 75-80%, manager 60-70%, on-call 50-60%) are sensible defaults.
The pitfalls name real failure modes: planning to 100%, ignoring meeting load and context switching, forgetting PTO.
missing: A shrinkage or net-availability formula with the maths shown (the sibling skill has one)
Estimating demand from backlog with ranges and confidence
A skills matrix and single-point-of-failure roles, not just hours
New-hire ramp time and fully loaded cost in the scenarios
Handling of part-time staff, contractors and multi-project splits
FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN labels and an assumptions block
Capacity-owner approval before requisitions or reallocation
A privacy note on per-person utilization
Save the plan to the workspace and a monthly review via schedule_routine
A boundary against ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan and support workforce scheduling

issues.quote: Use when heading into quarterly planning, the team feels overallocated and you need the numbers, deciding whether to hire or deprioritize
issues.problem: This is the same job as James's ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan ('capacity plan for next quarter', 'do we have enough people', 'how many heads do we need'), with no boundary. Routing between the two is a coin flip, and this one lacks that skill's guardrails.
issues.fix: Merge into ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan as a 'team-level utilization' section. If it is kept, scope it to a single team's per-person allocation and point to the other skill for headcount decisions.

issues.quote: **Current workload**: What are they working on? (Upload from project tracker or describe)
issues.problem: It accepts a description but gives no rule for turning it into hours and no requirement to label estimated vs measured figures. James's persona forbids 'presenting a guessed headcount as modeled', yet the skill will produce precise-looking utilization percentages from guesses.
issues.fix: Require each hours figure to be tagged FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN. Add an Assumptions and Sources block to the output, and do the arithmetic in bash_exec with the maths shown.

issues.quote: Analyze team capacity and plan resource allocation.
issues.problem: There are no ordered steps or decision points: nothing about computing net available hours, estimating demand with ranges, matching skills as well as hours, finding the crunch period, or deciding when to hire, contract, reskill or delay.
issues.fix: Add numbered steps: net availability (hours minus PTO, holidays, meetings, KTLO), then demand estimate with a range, per-skill, per-period gap, bottleneck, two scenarios with ramp time and cost, and recommendation. Include a decision rule for hire vs contract vs deprioritize.

issues.quote: /capacity-plan $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command. $ARGUMENTS and argument-hint do nothing in AutoGPT. The ~~project tracker and ~~calendar placeholders point to CONNECTORS.md, which lists plugin MCP servers and an upstream .mcp.json rather than the Linear, Google Calendar or Airtable blocks.
issues.fix: Delete the Usage block and CONNECTORS.md. Name run_block (Linear, GitHub, Google Calendar, Sheets) with a CSV or paste fallback.

issues.quote: [Name/Role]
issues.problem: A utilization table by named person carries no note on privacy or appropriate use. These figures are easily misread as performance data and shared widely, and nothing gates sharing or reallocating people on the capacity owner's approval.
issues.fix: Default to role-level rows unless the owner asks for names. Mark the plan as a planning estimate, not a performance measure. Require the capacity owner's approval before sharing it or before changing any allocation or requisition.

issues.quote: Critical path analysis
issues.problem: Budget variance and critical path are listed as dimensions with no method and no place in the output template. This is filler that drifts into ops-govern-a-program and finance territory.
issues.fix: Remove the Budget and Time dimensions, or keep one line pointing to ops-govern-a-program for timelines and the finance teammate for budget.

issues.quote: [Covered/Gap]
issues.problem: Demand is in FTEs while capacity is in hrs/wk, with no conversion. The gap is binary rather than quantified by period and skill, so 'Bottlenecks' cannot be derived from the tables.
issues.fix: Use one unit (hours or FTE with a stated hours/FTE). Show the gap as a number per month and per skill, and add an assumptions row.

issues.quote: **Plan for buffer** — Target 80% utilization. 100% means no room for surprises.
issues.problem: A single 80% target contradicts the role-type table (managers 60-70%, on-call 50-60%), and both are stated as norms without a source or confirmation from the owner.
issues.fix: Present the targets as defaults labelled ASSUMPTION and ask the owner to confirm or override them for their team.

scenarios.prompt: Q1 planning: here's our 6-person product team and the Linear backlog for next quarter. Can we fit the three projects, or do we need to hire?
scenarios.why: 'What I Need From You' collects the right inputs, and the Output template gives utilization, demand, bottlenecks and do-nothing/hire/deprioritize scenarios. But no step turns backlog items into hours, nets out PTO, holidays and meeting load, or gives ranges. Demand is in FTEs and capacity in hrs/wk with no conversion. The result looks rigorous, but its hour estimates are unlabelled.

scenarios.prompt: Calendar isn't connected, half the team are part-time contractors, several people are split across three projects, and the CEO wants a hire-or-delay answer by Friday. All I have is a rough spreadsheet of who's on what.
scenarios.why: Availability netting happens only 'If **~~calendar** is connected', with no default or question when it isn't. There is no method for part-time capacity or for cost of multi-project splitting beyond a pitfall bullet, and no hire ramp time or cost in the scenarios. No rule labels assumptions or bars guessed hours from being presented as measured, and there is no approval before the recommendation goes to the CEO. It also competes with ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan for the same request.

15:interview-plan-and-scorecard.job: plan structured interview loop, questions and scorecards
15:interview-plan-and-scorecard.summary: Turns an approved hiring rubric into a checked interview loop (one scoring interviewer per criterion), a linted question bank with job-related rewrites, one anchored scorecard per interviewer with a CSV copy, and a draft candidate note, using three standard-library scripts, and never sends or books anything.
strengths: The scripts work as described. I ran both selftests and the whole billing-ops-lead example (draft loop with 5 errors, fixed loop OK, 4 lint hits on the draft then 0, three scorecards), and the output matched the walkthrough.

The research behind it is sound and cited: Campion's 15 structure components, Sackett 2022 validities (.42/.40/.33/.31), the Mediating Assessments Protocol, Kahneman's 'do not skip around', OPM anchored scales, and EEOC/ADA pre-offer rules.

The guardrails are well built. The loop never adds criteria. Scorecards have no fit, affect or overall field. Interviewers file before seeing peer scores. Physical and schedule requirements go in an unscored section using 'with or without reasonable accommodation' wording. Unknowns stay [OWNER TO CONFIRM]. Legal questions go to counsel. Nothing is sent or booked.
Boundaries with sibling skills are clear: hiring-rubric-design, resume-screening and candidate-interview-debrief. The scorecard CSV has fixed columns that the debrief skill reads.

It fits the platform well, and I checked this against the backend: ~/workspace is a durable volume, packages are copied to ~/skills/<slug>, and run_capability, TodoWrite and workspace:// URIs all exist. The scripts use only the standard library, and there is a hand-check fallback when Python is missing.
It ships a worked hard case (an unapproved 'team fit' round, a question about where the candidate is from, a question about health and childcare) that reproduces exactly.
missing: A hiring-jurisdiction input, and coverage of law outside the US and UK (EU/GDPR, Germany's AGG, Canada, Australia)
An interviewer brief or prep packet per slot, and an anchor calibration session before the first candidate
Work-sample design rules (time cap, paid take-homes, synthetic data, identical materials, accessibility)
A 'check my questions only' mode that works before the rubric is approved
A master blank scorecard mode for when no candidate IDs exist yet
Handling of non-English question banks
Candidate Q&A or sell time in the loop, and candidate-experience checks
Consent for recording and AI note-takers, and how long scorecards are kept
Panel composition guidance (backup interviewers, conflicts of interest, varied panel)

issues.quote: For each hit, rewrite it with `references/unlawful-question-rewrites.md`, or
issues.problem: The lint deliberately over-flags, but step 5 offers only two outcomes: rewrite the question, or keep it as a stated job requirement. There is no branch for a false positive. I tested ordinary job questions and got hits on 'race condition' (ORIGIN), 'weigh the trade-offs' (APPEARANCE), 'miss a deadline' (SEX), 'account health' and 'medical billing' (HEALTH), 'Photoshop' (APPEARANCE), 'retire the legacy system' (AGE) and 'shift priorities' (SCHEDULE). A model following the text literally will rewrite valid technical questions or fill the owner's was/now/why table with noise.
issues.fix: Add a third outcome: 'false positive, the word is used in a job-content sense; mark it "lint false positive" in the table and keep the question.' Tighten the regexes too: weigh only in 'how much do you weigh', miss only before a surname, exclude 'race condition', exclude 'photoshop', exclude 'retire' when it refers to systems.

issues.quote: python3 scripts/question_lint.py <bank.md>
issues.problem: The lexicon is English-only, and its only language guard is a check for any Latin letter. A German, Spanish or French bank therefore gets 'No hits', exit 0, even with 'Wie alt sind Sie?' or '¿tienes hijos?' in it. SKILL.md never says this, so a clean lint gives false assurance.
issues.fix: State in step 5 that the lint covers English only and is grounded in US and UK law. For a non-English bank, review it by hand against the reference and label the result 'not lint-checked'. In the script, add a stopword heuristic that detects non-English text and exits 2.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.problem: The hiring jurisdiction is never collected. The rewrites depend on it: state salary-history bans, UK s.60, the wording of work-authorisation questions, fair-chance timing for conviction questions, and the EU AI Act and GDPR. The reference covers only US federal law, California and UK s.60, so a hire in Germany, Canada or Australia gets US rules applied silently.
issues.fix: Add an input row: 'Hiring location (country/state/city): from the hiring plan, or ask_question.' Use it to choose which reference rows apply. When the location is not covered, flag 'jurisdiction not covered by the reference, confirm with counsel' in the open items.

issues.quote: python3 scripts/make_scorecards.py <rubric.csv> <loop.csv> ~/workspace/hiring/<role-slug>/scorecards/<candidate-id>/blank --candidate <candidate-id>
issues.problem: The description says to use this skill 'before candidates are invited', but step 6 needs a candidate ID. There is no rule for the usual case where no candidates exist yet, so the model will make up a placeholder or stall. There is also no step for regenerating cards when candidates arrive.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: with no candidates yet, generate a master set with --candidate TEMPLATE into scorecards/_template/blank and tell the owner to re-run per candidate ID (or have the coordinator do it). When IDs are known, generate one folder per candidate.

issues.problem: The output has no interviewer brief and no calibration step. question-bank-patterns.md admits interviewer training is 'a gap the owner covers'. It points to a research dossier that is not shipped. A senior recruiting ops partner would give each interviewer a one-page brief (their criterion, anchors, timing, note-taking, no discussion, how to handle accommodation requests and candidate questions) and would calibrate anchors before the first candidate.
issues.fix: Add output item 8: a per-slot interviewer brief generated from loop.csv and the bank, plus a 15-minute anchor calibration agenda. Remove the pointer to the unshipped dossier.

issues.quote: method: structured question, work sample, portfolio review, or reference
issues.problem: Work samples are an allowed method, but there are no design rules for them: a time cap, pay or a length limit for take-homes, no real client or unpaid production work, the same materials and tools for everyone, extra time as an accommodation, and a per-task AI policy. A poorly designed take-home is one of the most common fairness and candidate-experience failures.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Work sample rules' section to references/question-bank-patterns.md and link it from step 2: time-boxed (for example, 90 minutes or less unless paid), synthetic data, identical brief, and scoring against the anchors only.

issues.problem: Interview recording, transcription and AI note-takers are not covered. That includes candidate consent (two-party-consent states, GDPR), NYC LL144 and Illinois AI Video Interview Act duties if any AI scoring is used, and how long scorecards are kept. The skill does handle the candidate's own AI use, but not the employer's.
issues.fix: Add a guardrail: 'No recording or AI note-taker unless the owner's policy allows it and the candidate note discloses it and asks for consent. Never use AI to score answers. Scorecard retention follows the owner's stated policy, or [OWNER TO CONFIRM].'

issues.quote: Scorecards never carry demeanour, confidence, enthusiasm, honesty, affect
issues.problem: The AFFECT lint rule only catches the exact phrase 'culture fit' plus a few affect phrases. 'Would you be a good team fit?', 'cultural fit' and 'fit with us' pass clean. In the walkthrough, the owner's 'team fit' round was caught only because check_loop saw an unknown criterion, not by the lint.
issues.fix: Extend the AFFECT regex to catch (team|cultural|culture|good) fit, 'fit (in|with)', 'personality' and 'likeable', and add those lines to the selftest.

scenarios.prompt: Rubric v2 for our Senior Data Analyst role is approved and it's in the hiring folder. Plan a 3-hour loop with Dana (hiring manager), Raj and Kim, write the questions, and give me the scorecards and the candidate prep email.
scenarios.why: The Inputs table finds rubric.csv or hiring-plan.md under ~/workspace/hiring/<slug>. Step 1 records the approver. Step 2 drafts loop.csv. Step 3 runs check_loop.py --loop-minutes 180, which catches criteria with no owner, criteria scored twice, a wrong minute total and more than 4 slots; I confirmed this on the example. Step 4 defaults to past-behaviour questions plus a work sample for SQL. Step 5 lints the bank. Step 6 makes one card per interviewer with the anchors copied word for word. Step 7 drafts the note with [OWNER TO CONFIRM] for AI policy and timing, and step 8 delivers workspace:// links. The only friction is small: step 6 asks for a candidate ID the owner has not given, and the lint may flag harmless words such as 'weigh' or 'shift', which the model has to judge without guidance.

scenarios.prompt: We're hiring a warehouse shift lead in Munich. The rubric is still a draft but interviews start Monday. Here are the hiring manager's questions (in German; a couple ask about Kinder and Alter). Check them, add a culture-fit round, and just generate the scorecards.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly refuses the culture-fit round (guardrail plus step 1). It also stops scorecard generation and sends the user to hiring-rubric-design, because no rubric is approved. But the German bank goes through question_lint.py with 'No hits', exit 0. I tested 'Wie alt sind Sie? / Haben Sie Kinder?' myself. SKILL.md never says the lexicon is English-only. The rewrite reference covers US law and UK s.60 only, and the inputs never ask for the hiring jurisdiction, so German law (AGG) and GDPR are never raised. The user's 'just check the questions' request, which should still work without a rubric, is not clearly separated from the full loop flow.

better: The main version was a 24-line placeholder with no inputs, no numbered procedure and no templates. The PR adds an inputs table with sources, an 8-step procedure with a decision at each check, and a 7-item output contract.

check_loop.py enforces one scoring interviewer per criterion, catches unknown criteria, checks the minute total, and flags more than 4 slots unless a reason is given. The main version only stated the one-owner rule in prose.

question_lint.py (15 rules, with a selftest) plus a rewrite table replace main's single line banning protected-trait notes. Physical and schedule requirements get ADA-compliant 'with or without reasonable accommodation' wording in an unscored section.

make_scorecards.py produces per-interviewer cards with the anchors copied word for word, a 'not assessed' option, a file-before-peers line, and a CSV copy that candidate-interview-debrief reads. Main only listed the fields a scorecard should have.
A candidate note template adds a per-stage AI-use policy, an accommodation contact who asks for no medical details, decision timing, and [OWNER TO CONFIRM] placeholders.
The triggers are specific phrases instead of generic ones like 'interview questions', and the description spells out the checks the skill runs.
A worked hard-case example ships and reproduces exactly.
worse: SKILL.md is about 6 times longer (151 lines against 24), with roughly 1,300 lines of supporting files, so it is heavier to load.

The lint over-flags common job words (race condition, weigh trade-offs, miss a deadline, account health, Photoshop) and step 5 has no way to dismiss them, which can push the model to rewrite valid questions.
The lint returns 'No hits' on non-English banks and applies only US and UK law without asking where the role is hired. This is a false assurance that main's plain prose did not create.
It points to a research dossier (docs/research/recruiting.md, 'section 7.3') that the package does not ship.

jobs-to-be-done.job: identify the job customers hire product for
jobs-to-be-done.summary: A vendored wondelai (MIT, v1.5.0) Christensen-school JTBD framework reference. It explains job statements, the three job dimensions, the four forces, Big and Little Hire, non-obvious competition, timeline interviews and designing for the job, adds marketing copy patterns and a self-scoring 10-point diagnostic, and routes to five sound reference files. It gives no workflow, no deliverable template and no evidence rules, and no expert has it assigned.
strengths: Correct, well-organised rendering of the Christensen/Moesta core: progress in circumstances, functional/emotional/social dimensions, Push+Pull > Habit+Anxiety, Big versus Little Hire, and non-consumption as the main competitor.
Good progressive disclosure: each section ends with a 'See references/... when ...' pointer, and all five reference paths resolve to shipped files.

references/diagnostics.md is practical: a symptom-to-cause table ('they buy but don't use' maps to Little Hire lost), churn-pattern tables, firing-interview questions, and traditional-versus-JTBD metric swaps.
references/innovation-process.md has a usable, time-boxed timeline interview guide and job-statement abstraction checks (too narrow, too broad, just right).
The Quick Diagnostic and Common Mistakes tables give a fast way to spot product-first or demographic-first framing.
missing: A named JTBD brief or job atlas output template the user can save and compare against later
Named inputs and a branch for 'no primary research yet' versus 'transcripts in hand', with graceful fallbacks (Drive, Notion or HubSpot via run_block, or upload, CSV or paste)
A synthesis method: coding transcripts for struggling moment, forces and dimensions, clustering, a frequency threshold (three accounts make a pattern), and thin-sample refusal

Outcome-Driven Innovation elements: desired-outcome statements, the 8-step job map, and importance-versus-satisfaction opportunity scoring (the Job Atlas mentions a 'satisfaction gap' but never gives the method)
A four-forces diagram or worksheet format and a switch-interview timeline canvas as shipped templates
Evidence labelling (FACT, INFERENCE, UNKNOWN) and marking unvalidated job statements as hypotheses
An approval gate for recruiting outreach and customer-facing copy, plus recording consent and PII handling for transcripts
Hand-off rules to teammates: roadmap and prioritization (Alex), positioning (obviously-awesome or marketing), retention plays (Riley)
Use of memory and workspace files to keep the job atlas and interview log across sessions

issues.problem: The skill has no workflow and names no inputs. It never asks what the user has (transcripts, tickets, churn exports, analytics, nothing), what decision the JTBD work feeds (positioning, roadmap, churn fix, new market), or which segment and circumstance is in scope. It gives six parallel concept sections and no branches such as 'no interviews, so plan them first' versus 'have transcripts, so synthesize'.
issues.fix: Add a 'What you need first' block (decision served, segment or circumstance, available evidence and where it lives). Follow it with an ordered procedure: gather evidence (connector, upload or paste), code each source for struggling moment, forces and dimensions, cluster into candidate jobs, write job statements, map competing hires including non-consumption, split Big and Little Hire signals, and close with implications and an interview plan for the gaps. Move the concept prose to a references/framework.md.

issues.quote: Always state the current score and the specific diagnostic rows to fix.
issues.problem: The only defined output is a self-graded 10-point score of the analysis. It is a rubric for the model, not a deliverable the user can reuse, and it makes a quality number the headline of every answer.
issues.fix: Replace it with a named 'JTBD brief' template: job statement(s) with evidence count and grade; functional, emotional and social dimensions; a four-forces map; competing hires including non-consumption and workarounds; Big and Little Hire metrics; implications for the decision at hand; open questions with an interview plan. Keep the diagnostic as an internal checklist and do not print the score.

issues.quote: "We heard you say [verbatim quote] -- so we built [feature]"
issues.problem: Copy patterns invite customer quotes and product claims, but nothing requires quotes to come from real, attributed sources or requires claims to be labelled sourced or assumed. Nothing forbids inventing jobs, quotes or numbers when no research exists, which conflicts with the evidence rules of Alex's persona.
issues.fix: Add evidence rules. Every job statement cites its sources and a count (one account is an anecdote). Label claims FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN. Jobs inferred without switch or firing interviews are marked as hypotheses. Quotes are used verbatim, with speaker role and date, only from supplied material. Customer-facing copy is a draft for approval.

issues.quote: Ask only about past events, never hypotheticals ("would you...", "do you wish...")
issues.problem: The bundled interview guides contradict this rule. innovation-process.md asks 'If you could wave a magic wand, what would change?', 'What would make you try something in this area?' and 'What would make this perfect for your situation?', and diagnostics.md asks 'If we could change one thing, what would make you stay?'. A model that hands over the reference guide gives the user leading, hypothetical questions.
issues.fix: Rewrite those reference questions as past-behaviour probes (for example 'Tell me about the last time you tried X instead; what happened?'), or tag them as optional closing questions not to be treated as evidence. Keep the guides consistent with the Mom Test rule this skill already states.

issues.quote: Interview churned customers on their timeline
issues.problem: The skill directs the model to recruit and interview recent switchers and churned customers. It has no step to draft recruiting outreach for approval before anything is sent, no consent-to-record step (that appears only in a reference file), and no handling rules for transcripts that contain customer PII.
issues.fix: Add a recruiting step: draft the screener and outreach email and hold them for the owner's approval before sending through Gmail or HubSpot. Require recording consent in the guide opener, store transcripts in the workspace with names redacted in shared synthesis, and never contact a customer directly.

issues.quote: Use when the user mentions "customer discovery", "why customers churn", "what job does this solve", "competing against luck", "product-market fit"
issues.problem: The triggers are broad and collide with other catalog skills. customer-insight-research also triggers on 'jobs to be done', 'JTBD' and 'find out why customers churn'. product-discovery-and-user-research, mom-test and the retention skills cover interviews and churn. No boundary says when this skill wins. The description also points to 'design-sprint', which does not exist in the catalog.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to the JTBD lens itself: job statements, forces of progress, switch or firing analysis, and non-obvious competition. Say it hands raw research synthesis to product-discovery-and-user-research or customer-insight-research and interview technique to mom-test. Remove the design-sprint pointer.

issues.quote: Retention problems are almost always Little Hire failures -- purchased but never used
issues.problem: This overclaim contradicts the skill's own diagnostics.md, which lists five firing causes: job changed, better employee appeared, job never done, friction, priorities shifted. The skill also claims 'demographics are useless'. Both push the model toward a single-cause answer.
issues.fix: Soften the claim to 'Early churn is often a Little Hire failure', then point to the firing-causes table and require the analysis to test each cause against the evidence.

issues.quote: https://www.amazon.com/Competing-Against-Luck-Innovation-Customer/dp/0062435612?tag=wondelai00-20
issues.problem: It ships the upstream author's Amazon affiliate tag inside the product, a vendor-link signal the platform brief flags. The Further Reading and About the Author sections are tokens that never help the task.
issues.fix: Remove the affiliate URL and the About the Author section. At most keep a plain citation (title, authors, year), with the MIT attribution kept in LICENSE.

scenarios.prompt: I've got 9 churn interview transcripts from last quarter in our Drive folder. What job were these customers hiring us for, and why did they fire us?
scenarios.why: The model would find the right lenses: the churn interview framework and 'Why Firing Happens' categories in references/diagnostics.md, the Big/Little Hire split in section 3, the job statement format, and the three dimensions. What it gets back is correct vocabulary. The skill gives no synthesis steps: it never says to read the transcripts one at a time, code each against the forces and dimensions, count how often each job appears, lead each job with attributed verbatims, or treat 9 interviews as thin. It never says where to get the files (Drive via run_block, or ask for an upload). It has no output template, and the only instruction on output is 'Always state the current score', so the user gets a diagnostic score and prose instead of a reusable jobs and firing-reasons brief.

scenarios.prompt: We haven't done any interviews. All I have is an NPS comments CSV and some retention numbers from Mixpanel. Leadership wants JTBD-based positioning and a roadmap by Friday. Just write the job statements and the positioning line.
scenarios.why: Quick Diagnostic row 7 ('Job understanding based on assumptions', run 10+ interviews) would likely make the model add a caveat. Nothing tells it how to infer candidate jobs from secondary data, to label the job statements as unvalidated hypotheses (FACT/INFERENCE per Alex's persona), or to refuse a verdict on thin evidence. The copy patterns ('No lock-in, cancel anytime', 'We heard you say [verbatim quote]') and the positioning formula in competitive-strategy.md push toward confident, shippable copy with unsupported claims. There is no gate that turns the result into a draft for approval, and no hand-off of the roadmap part to Alex's roadmap or prioritization skill. The likely result is plausible-sounding jobs presented with more certainty than the data supports.

software-debugging.job: find root cause of software bug
software-debugging.summary: A generic, human-oriented debugging tutorial: scientific-method phases (reproduce, gather, hypothesise, test), language snippets for JS/Python/Go debuggers and profilers, git bisect, differential debugging, and a 'when stuck' checklist. It defines no deliverable and no stopping point.
strengths: Sound core frame: reproduce first, isolate, change one thing at a time, fix the root cause rather than the symptom.
The differential-debugging table (working vs broken by environment, version, data, user, time) is a genuinely useful artefact.
git bisect and 'profile before optimising' are correct, current practice.
'Don't change production' and 'Test fixes in staging' give it a basic production-safety instinct.
Clean MIT licence and attribution, no broken links, no Claude-Code-only constructs.
missing: Named inputs up front: symptom, expected vs actual, environment, repro status, recent changes, and what access exists (repo, logs, CI)
Hypothesis log with evidence for and against, one confirm step per hypothesis, and confidence
Method for reading a stack trace or log against the diff (first in-app frame, error chain, correlation IDs)
Failing regression test before the fix, and verification after it
No-repro / heisenbug branch with the two logs or questions that would reveal it
Time-box and escalation or handoff rules (bug-reproduction-report, flaky-test-triage, incident response)
Root-cause / debug report template as the deliverable
Secret and PII redaction and approval gates for production access
Observability-first production debugging: distributed traces, metrics, feature-flag bisection
Sandbox-runnable examples (git bisect run, pytest -x --lf, cProfile to file)

issues.problem: No deliverable. The skill never says what the model hands back: no root-cause write-up, hypothesis log, evidence table or fix recommendation. Casey's persona needs file:line and confidence for every claim, and nothing here produces that.
issues.fix: Add an Output section with a debug/RCA report template: symptom, expected vs actual, environment, repro status, a hypotheses table (evidence for, evidence against, confirm step, status), root cause with confidence and file:line, fix proposal, regression test, and what stays unverified.

issues.quote: Use when investigating bugs, performance issues, or unexpected behavior.
issues.problem: The trigger is so broad it fires on any bug mention. In Robin's kit it collides with troubleshoot-and-resolve and technical-diagnostics-with-tools for customer-reported breakage. In Casey's kit it overlaps flaky-test-triage and bug-reproduction-report. The 'Master systematic debugging...' lead-in is marketing copy, not a trigger.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description for Casey only: 'Use when a failing test, stack trace, error log or regression needs a root cause traced in code; not for flaky-test history (flaky-test-triage) or writing the report (bug-reproduction-report).' Remove it from Robin.

issues.quote: Phase 4: Test & Verify
issues.problem: The process stops at testing hypotheses. There is no phase to confirm the root cause, fix it, add a regression test, verify in the target environment, or write up. There are no decision points: no time-box, no rule for when to stop or escalate, and no rule for when evidence is too thin to name a cause.
issues.fix: Add Phase 5 'Confirm and fix' (failing test first, minimal fix, verify, check for siblings of the same bug) and Phase 6 'Report and hand off'. Add explicit branches: no repro, so name the two logs or questions that would reveal it; hypothesis not confirmed after N experiments, so escalate with what was ruled out.

issues.quote: Use production data (anonymized)
issues.problem: Tells the model to pull production data locally with no approval gate, no data-handling rule and no instruction to redact. Phase 2 also asks for 'Environment variables' with no secret-redaction rule. Nothing says 'never invent a stack trace or root cause' or 'label fact vs inference', both of which Casey's boundaries require.
issues.fix: Add a guardrails block: redact secrets and PII from logs and env dumps; get the owner's approval before touching prod data, prod config or deploys; never claim a fix or root cause without evidence; state confidence; the model proposes fixes and people merge and ship.

issues.quote: VS Code Debugger Configuration:
issues.problem: Much of the body assumes a human at an IDE. It relies on VS Code launch.json, Chrome DevTools, `debugger;` statements, interactive pdb/ipdb/Delve sessions and 'Visit http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/'. An agent in the E2B bash_exec sandbox cannot drive these, and the skill never says how to get the code in (GitHub block) or how to run tests or a bisect there.
issues.fix: Replace IDE instructions with sandbox-runnable methods: clone via GitHub, run the failing test, add temporary logging, run `git bisect run <test>`, cProfile/pstats to file, `node --inspect`-free heap analysis. Ask the user to paste logs or traces when there is no access.

issues.quote: require("v8").writeHeapSnapshot();
issues.problem: Recommends a threshold-triggered heap snapshot inside running code. writeHeapSnapshot is synchronous, blocks the event loop and needs about 2x heap, so in a process already near OOM it can crash prod. The afterEach heap-diff test does not force GC, so its 10MB threshold produces noisy false positives.
issues.fix: Caveat the snapshot call (off-peak, a canary instance, approval required). Recommend comparing three snapshots over time with retainer/dominator analysis. Use --expose-gc with global.gc() before measuring in tests.

issues.quote: Debugging distributed systems
issues.problem: Promises coverage of distributed systems and crash dumps ('Analyzing crash dumps and stack traces'), but the body has nothing on tracing, correlation IDs, clock skew, core-dump analysis or reading stack traces.
issues.fix: Either add a short reference on distributed tracing and correlation-ID log joins plus stack-trace and core-dump reading, or remove those bullets.

issues.quote: Take breaks when stuck
issues.problem: Human-motivation filler (take breaks, rubber duck, 'Giving Up Too Soon') plus about 250 lines of generic snippets the model already knows, all inline. No progressive disclosure.
issues.fix: Cut the mindset filler. Move per-language snippets to references/javascript.md, python.md and go.md, and keep SKILL.md to the procedure, decision points and output template (under about 120 lines).

scenarios.prompt: Casey: our /checkout endpoint started returning 500s after yesterday's deploy. Here's the Sentry stack trace and the diffs of the three PRs that went out. Find the root cause.
scenarios.why: Phase 2 and Phase 3 ('What changed?', 'Recent code changes') and Technique 1 (git bisect) point the model at the diffs, so a capable model gets there. The skill gives no method for mapping stack frames to changed lines, no ranked hypotheses with a confirm step each, no advice to write a failing test before the fix, and no report format. The file:line, confidence-stated rigour comes from Casey's persona, not from the skill.

scenarios.prompt: Casey: our Node queue worker's memory climbs until it OOMs about every 6 hours in prod. We can't reproduce locally, we can't attach a debugger in prod, and all I have is Grafana screenshots and one heap snapshot. What's leaking?
scenarios.why: Technique 4 assumes two heap snapshots and local DevTools. Its Node snippet adds a threshold-triggered v8.writeHeapSnapshot() to prod code. That call blocks the event loop and needs roughly 2x heap memory, so it can cause the very OOM being diagnosed, and nothing asks for approval before changing prod. The skill has no guidance for reading a single snapshot (retainers, dominators) and no no-repro fallback. 'Reproduce locally' is its only production path.

support-ticket-triage.summary: Triages a single support ticket in six steps: parse, categorise against a 9-category taxonomy, prioritise P1-P4 with SLA timings, check for duplicates via connector placeholders, route to a tier or team, and emit a structured triage block with a drafted first response from category templates.
strengths: Clear 9-category taxonomy with signal words and sensible tie-break rules (root cause drives the category, and a bug outranks a feature request).
P1-P4 criteria are concrete and match the persona's scale, with explicit escalation triggers (pattern detected, workaround stops working, scope expands).
The routing matrix by tier and team (Tier 1/2, Engineering, Product, Security, Billing) is practical and reusable.
The Step 5 triage output template is a strong, copyable artefact, with workaround, known-issue and internal-notes fields.
Best-practice list covers the right habits: read the whole thread, note what was ruled out, flag patterns even on low-priority tickets.
missing: Queue or batch mode: rank many tickets, cluster duplicates within the batch, and produce a queue brief with counts and owners
Fact / inference / unknown labels on each triage field (both personas require them)
Sensitive-data handling: redact card, health and credentials before routing, and route to sensitive-data-safe-handling
Categories or routes for fraud, trust and safety, legal threats and self-harm, which Robin's routing covers
SLA clock from first contact, time-to-breach, and customer tier or contract entitlements
Graceful fallback when no help desk is connected (CSV or paste, bash_exec clustering)
Explicit approval gate and log before any reply, link, merge or priority change is written back
Logging the category for trend reporting (weekly-ticket-themes / voice-of-customer)

issues.quote: Notify the customer that this is a known issue being tracked
issues.problem: Tells the model to act directly: notify the customer, link tickets, add information to the existing ticket, bump priority. None of it is framed as a draft or gated on approval. Robin's and Sasha's boundaries both say nothing reaches a customer or changes a ticket without a person's yes.
issues.fix: Reword as proposals: 'Propose linking to #X; draft the known-issue note to the customer; list the new info to add to the parent ticket; recommend any priority change.' Then add 'nothing is sent, linked or re-prioritised until the user approves'.

issues.quote: I've escalated this to our security team for investigation.
issues.problem: The auto-response templates assert actions that have not happened ('I've escalated...', 'I've documented this and shared it with our product team', 'I've logged this as a [priority] issue') and commit to timelines. That is invented fact in customer-facing copy and breaks both personas' never-invent rule. They also expose internal priority labels to the customer and use scripted openers ('Great question!') that Sasha's voice forbids.
issues.fix: Rewrite the templates in conditional or placeholder form tied to verified actions ('[Once escalated:] our security team is reviewing...'). Pull the timeframe from the desk's configured SLA or leave it blank for the approver. Drop internal P-labels and scripted sympathy.

issues.quote: Respond within 1 hour. Continuous work until resolved or mitigated. Updates every 1-2 hours.
issues.problem: SLA timings are hardcoded as universal (1h, 4h, 1 business day, 2 business days). Its own ATTRIBUTION says the skill is only valid where the desk's SLA matches. The skill never reads contract or plan entitlements and never notes that the SLA clock starts at first contact and carries across handoffs.
issues.fix: Treat these as defaults only. Tell the model to read the desk's SLA and entitlement table from memory_search or the workspace, or ask once and store it, and to compute time-to-breach from first customer contact.

issues.section: 3. Check for Duplicates and Known Issues
issues.quote: Search for similar open or recently resolved tickets
issues.problem: Duplicate and known-issue checks depend on '~~support platform', '~~knowledge base' and '~~project tracker'. references/CONNECTORS.md maps these to Intercom, Guru and Atlassian MCP servers and an upstream .mcp.json. There is no mapping to AutoGPT blocks (HubSpot, Linear, Notion, GitHub, Gmail, Sheets) and no fallback when nothing is connected, so 'Known issue: Checking' is left dangling.
issues.fix: Replace the placeholders with 'the connected help desk (run_mcp_tool) or HubSpot/Linear/Notion/GitHub via run_block'. If none is connected, ask for a CSV export or paste of open tickets and the known-issues list, cluster duplicates with bash_exec, and record which sources were not checked.

issues.quote: /ticket-triage <ticket text, customer message, or issue description>
issues.problem: The skill is framed as a Claude Code plugin slash command: the '# /ticket-triage' title, the Usage block and the ignored argument-hint frontmatter. AutoGPT experts load skills via read_skill, and these invocations mean nothing there.
issues.fix: Remove the slash-command Usage block and argument-hint. Replace them with a 'What you need first' section: ticket text and thread, customer and plan, channel, first-contact time, and access to the open queue and known-issue list.

issues.quote: Triage and prioritize a support ticket or customer issue.
issues.problem: The trigger overlaps almost word for word with Robin's triage-and-prioritize (same P1-P4 scale, routing and duplicate checks) and Sasha's ticket-triage (queue sort and duplicate grouping). Both would compete for the same requests.
issues.fix: Resolve as a merge. Keep one triage skill per expert (single ticket plus queue mode) and fold in this package's taxonomy, category tips, routing matrix and output template as references/. Do not assign this package alongside the existing ones.

issues.quote: Should I escalate this? I can package it with /customer-escalation.
issues.problem: Points to a /customer-escalation command that this package does not ship and that does not exist on the platform.
issues.fix: Route to the expert's own skill instead (Robin: escalations-and-incidents; Sasha: bug-report-handoff or refund-and-exception-brief), or to handoff_to_expert.

issues.quote: When in doubt on priority, err on the side of higher
issues.problem: Paired with the rule that auto-bumps priority when a customer 'mentions executive involvement', this inflates priority on tone rather than impact. It conflicts with Sasha's identity ('A loud customer is not automatically urgent') and dilutes P1 and P2 on a busy desk.
issues.fix: Keep impact and urgency as the priority driver. Treat executive or escalation mentions as a flag for a manager or escalation path, not an automatic priority bump. When unsure, state the uncertainty and the one fact that would settle it.

scenarios.prompt: Robin: new ticket from Acme (Enterprise plan): 'Since this morning every CSV export comes back empty and our finance close is today.' Triage it and draft the first reply.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-2 extract the urgency signals. The tips ('It used to work and now it doesn't' = Bug) and the P2 criteria ('core workflow broken... blocking time-sensitive work... key account') give a defensible Bug/Data P2 routed to Tier 2 or Engineering. The Step 5 template produces a reusable triage block. One weakness: the Bug template's 'I'll update you within [SLA timeframe]' pulls the hardcoded 4-hour SLA rather than Acme's contracted one.

scenarios.prompt: Sasha: here's a CSV export of 40 open Zendesk tickets (Zendesk isn't connected). Sort out what's urgent and group duplicates. One customer is threatening to go to our CEO over a double charge, and a few mention a Safari login loop.
scenarios.why: The skill is built for one ticket at a time. Nothing in it produces a ranked queue brief or clusters duplicates within a batch, so the model either emits 40 verbose triage blocks or improvises. Step 3's duplicate search relies on '~~support platform', which has no fallback to the pasted CSV, and there is no hint to use bash_exec. 'Priority Escalation Triggers' auto-bumps the double charge because the customer 'mentions executive involvement'. That contradicts Sasha's rule that a loud customer is not automatically urgent.

project-status-report.job: write project status report for leadership
project-status-report.summary: Supplies a markdown status-report template (executive summary, overall G/Y/R, KPI table, accomplishments, in-progress items, risks, decisions needed, next priorities), with optional pulls from a connected tracker, chat and calendar, three writing tips, and a bundled copy of the Anthropic operational risk-assessment matrix.
strengths: Conventional, reusable exec status template, including a Decisions Needed table that requires context, a deadline and a recommendation for each decision.
The description is specific and easy to trigger on: weekly or monthly leadership update, G/Y/R health, turning tracker activity into a narrative.
Short. Both references are shipped and linked by relative path.
The Tips have the right instincts: lead with the headline, surface risks early, make each decision easy with a recommendation.
Licence and attribution are preserved cleanly.
missing: Ordered steps naming the required inputs: audience, cadence and period, sources, destination, prior report
Written G/Y/R criteria, status change against last period with a reason, and a path to green
Comparison with the previous saved report (workspace file or memory), and saving the new report with a date
Milestone table with baseline and forecast dates; schedule, budget and scope dimensions
Source label on every number, with UNKNOWN handling for missing targets or actuals
Fallback when no tracker is connected (pasted export, CSV, Google Sheet) and mapping to AutoGPT blocks and MCP tools
Explicit draft-and-approve step before posting or emailing, with recipients named
Audience variants (team, exec, board) with length and detail limits
Boundaries and handoffs to ops-govern-a-program's RAID log, ops-run-the-operating-rhythm and product-stakeholder-update
A worked example of a finished report

issues.quote: | [KPI] | [Target] | [Actual] | [up/down/flat] | 🟢/🟡/🔴 |
issues.problem: The KPI table requires a target, an actual and a trend for every metric, but nothing says where each number comes from or what to do when one is missing. The model is pushed to invent targets and trends. That breaks both the platform's no-invented-numbers rule and James's FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN rule.
issues.fix: Add a Source column, and a rule: every number is quoted from a named source or written UNKNOWN; missing targets are listed under 'Needs from you', never estimated; trend is computed against the saved prior report, with the arithmetic done in bash_exec.

issues.problem: There is no ordered procedure. Inputs (audience, cadence and period, sources, the prior report) are never named, and there are no decision points for missing data, how to turn tracker activity into a narrative, or how to choose the overall status. The description promises 'turning a pile of project tracker activity into a readable narrative' but gives no steps for it.
issues.fix: Add a 'Steps' section: 1) confirm the audience, cadence, period and destination, one question at a time with ask_question; 2) gather sources, falling back to paste or CSV; 3) load last period's report from the workspace or memory; 4) score status against defined criteria; 5) draft; 6) show the draft and get approval; 7) save the dated report.

issues.quote: ### Overall Status: 🟢 On Track / 🟡 At Risk / 🔴 Off Track
issues.problem: G/Y/R is never defined. There are no schedule, budget or scope thresholds, no previous-period status, no reason for a change and no path to green. That invites 'watermelon' reporting (green outside, red inside) and inconsistent calls from week to week.
issues.fix: Add a criteria table: for example, Green = within 5% of plan on the baseline dates; Amber = a slip or overrun with a recovery plan; Red = needs leadership help or a decision. Show 'Last period → This period' with a one-line reason and a path-to-green for anything Amber or Red.

issues.quote: If **~~project tracker** is connected:
issues.problem: `~~category` placeholders are an upstream plugin convention that sends the model to CONNECTORS.md, which describes Asana, Jira and ServiceNow MCP servers from an external .mcp.json. There is no mapping to AutoGPT blocks and no fallback when nothing is connected, which is the common case for this user base.
issues.fix: Name the real options: run_block for Linear, Notion, GitHub, Google Sheets, Slack and Google Calendar; run_mcp_tool for other connected trackers; connect_integration to offer a connection; otherwise ask for a pasted export or CSV as an equal alternative. Drop the plugin placeholder text.

issues.quote: /status-report $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command and `$ARGUMENTS` do nothing in the AutoGPT harness, and the H1 '/status-report' does not match the skill name. argument-hint is dropped, so the weekly/monthly/quarterly cadence it carried is lost.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block and rename the H1 to 'Project status report'. Turn the cadence and project arguments into required inputs in the new Steps section.

issues.quote: Offer to post the finished report to a channel
issues.problem: The only approval language is a soft 'offer'. Nothing says to show the final text, name the destination and recipients, and wait for an explicit yes. When the user has already asked for posting, this gate disappears. Emailing the report is not covered at all.
issues.fix: Add: 'Stage the report as a draft; show the full text and the destination (channel or recipients); post or email only after the user's explicit yes to that text; log the approval.'

issues.quote: | Risk/Issue | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
issues.problem: The risk table has no likelihood, level, status or due date, although the bundled reference defines a likelihood × impact matrix and a register format. The reference is also a verbatim copy of the catalog's operational-risk-assessment skill, frontmatter included, so it is duplicated content that does not reach the template.
issues.fix: Add Likelihood, Level (from the reference matrix), Status and Due columns, and trim the reference to the matrix and severity definitions without its skill frontmatter. Alternatively, point to the operational-risk-assessment skill instead of shipping a copy.

issues.quote: Use when writing a weekly or monthly update for leadership, summarizing project health with green/yellow/red status
issues.problem: For James, this overlaps almost entirely with ops-govern-a-program (which triggers on 'program status report') and ops-run-the-operating-rhythm (the weekly/monthly RAG review). It also duplicates product-stakeholder-update, which comes from the same Anthropic source. Nothing tells the model which one to pick.
issues.fix: Narrow the scope to a single-project written status report for stakeholders, and add 'Not for: the business-wide KPI review (ops-run-the-operating-rhythm) or the RAID log and phase gates (ops-govern-a-program)'. Otherwise, merge it into ops-govern-a-program for James.

scenarios.prompt: Write this week's status report on the warehouse-migration project for our COO. The Linear project is connected, and last Friday's notes are in the doc I shared.
scenarios.why: The Output template gives the model a clean shape, and 'If ~~project tracker is connected' tells it to pull completed and overdue items, so a readable report comes out. But nothing fixes the period, compares against last week's report, or defines when the project is Green, Amber or Red. The Key Metrics table asks for Target/Actual/Trend with no rule to source or mark them unknown. James's persona requires FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels and a like-for-like period, and the skill does not ask for either. Result: a tidy draft whose RAG call and metric targets may be unsupported.

scenarios.prompt: Pull together the monthly update on the website relaunch for the board. We don't use a tracker, so here's a Slack export and a half-filled sheet with no targets. Post it to #leadership when it's done.
