issues.fix: Tag activities by entity profile (single-entity/cash basis, accrual, multi-entity) and include only those that apply after intake.

issues.quote: Typical 5-Day Close Calendar
issues.problem: The same task set appears four times (day checklist, dependency map, 5-day table, 3-day table), which inflates the skill body loaded on every trigger.
issues.fix: Keep one canonical task list with day and level attributes in SKILL.md, and move the calendars and bottleneck table to references/.

issues.quote: user-invocable: false
issues.problem: Upstream meant this as background knowledge. The harness drops the flag, so the skill appears in available_skills and competes on 'month end' triggers with month-end-close-checklist and close-controls-and-accounting.
issues.fix: Either drop the package, or rewrite the description so it triggers only for close-sequencing questions that the checklist skills send to it.

scenarios.prompt: We're a 3-person team closing September next week. Build us a close calendar with owners and a tracker we can update daily.
scenarios.why: The 5-day calendar, day-by-day checklist and dashboard columns give a ready structure. But with no intake of team size, systems or applicable activities, the output includes tax provision, equity roll-forward, consolidation and FX revaluation that a small single-entity team does not run. The dashboard has no preparer, reviewer or evidence columns, and nothing says where the tracker lives (workspace file, Google Sheet, Notion), so 'update daily' has no persistent state.

scenarios.prompt: It's T+3. Two department heads still haven't confirmed AP accruals, the bank feed broke on the 29th so the bank rec isn't done, and the CEO wants draft financials tomorrow morning. What's blocked and what can we still give her?
scenarios.why: The Level 1-5 dependency map lets a model trace bank rec → balance-sheet recs → draft financials and mark those tasks Blocked. But the skill gives no guidance on delivering a preliminary P&L with estimated accruals flagged as estimates, on triaging by materiality, or on getting bank data another way (a downloaded statement CSV). Its checklist would also have the model 'Distribute financial reporting package' and send reminders without approval.

quality-csat-and-coaching.job: score support QA and coach reps
quality-csat-and-coaching.summary: Scores a weekly per-rep thread sample against a five-dimension rubric with a quote behind every mark, reads CSAT and AHT alongside response rate, FCR and reopen rate, and drafts one coaching fix per rep for the owner to deliver.
strengths: Pairs every score with the quoted line that earned it, and does not score a thread it cannot read
Reads CSAT with response rate and sample size, AHT beside FCR, and uses reopen rate as the check on 'resolved': correct metric hygiene
Calibration before scoring is named as a prerequisite, not an afterthought
One fix plus one praised win per rep, with a re-check date; shared misses become a macro, KB or talk-track fix
Coaching notes and scores stay drafts for the owner; it never delivers or publishes them
missing: Default scoring scale with weights and auto-fail or critical-error items
CSAT definition (top-2-box %) and minimum n before trending
DSAT reason coding: agent vs product vs policy
Calibration protocol with a named second scorer and an agreement threshold
Stratified random sampling, or all-thread AI scoring when volume allows
Scorecard and coaching-note templates
PII redaction of quoted customer text
HR boundary and a rep dispute/appeal path
Sandbox computation of the metrics from an export

issues.quote: Score on weighted dimensions the team agreed: acknowledgement speed,
issues.problem: No scale, no default weights and no critical/auto-fail items (wrong information, policy or compliance breach, exposed PII). The fallback rubric has five dimensions but no way to turn them into a comparable score.
issues.fix: Ship a default rubric in references/: per-dimension scale (e.g. 0/1/2), weights summing to 100, auto-fail items that zero the thread, and a bash_exec snippet that totals scores per rep.

issues.section: Read the numbers from the records
issues.quote: CSAT with its response rate and sample size — a 4.6 on nine responses is
issues.problem: CSAT is never defined: the example treats it as a mean, while most desks report top-2-box %. DSAT is never split into agent-controllable vs product or policy causes, so reps get blamed for dissatisfaction they did not cause.
issues.fix: Define CSAT as % of 4-5 ratings with n, set a minimum n before trending, and reason-code every DSAT (agent / product / policy / process) before it is attributed to a rep.

issues.section: Sample fairly and score with quotes
issues.quote: quoted line behind every mark. A thread you cannot read is not scored.
issues.problem: Quoted customer lines go straight into coaching drafts and scorecards with no redaction step. Card numbers, health details and addresses in threads end up in HR-facing documents.
issues.fix: Before quoting, run the text through sensitive-data-safe-handling (mask to type plus fragment), and quote the rep's words over the customer's where possible.

issues.quote: scoring — two reviewers score the same three threads and settle the
issues.problem: The AI is a single reviewer. The skill never says who the second reviewer is or what level of agreement ends calibration, so the model either skips calibration or fakes it.
issues.fix: Have the owner or team lead blind-score the same three threads, compare dimension by dimension, set a tolerance (e.g. within one point per dimension), and log the calibration result with the date.

issues.section: Sample fairly and score with quotes
issues.quote: A fixed sample per rep per week — newest, oldest, one escalated, one
issues.problem: Newest plus oldest is a convenience sample, not a random one, and four threads a week gives per-rep scores with huge variance. It also ignores that current practice scores every thread with AI when volume allows.
issues.fix: Take a stratified random sample by channel and contact reason plus targeted slices, report n per rep, never rank reps on fewer than N threads, and offer to score all threads when the export allows.

issues.quote: One quoted miss, the better line, why it is better, and a re-check date.
issues.problem: Per-rep scores are employment-sensitive, and there is no boundary on using them for discipline, ranking or public leaderboards. There is also no dispute or appeal path.
issues.fix: State that scores inform coaching, not discipline; any performance action is the manager's call with a larger sample. Add a rep dispute line to the note.

issues.quote: The scored sample with quotes, the metric read with trends and sources, and
issues.problem: The output is described but has no template, so scorecard columns and coaching-note shape change from run to run and are hard to compare week over week.
issues.fix: Add templates/qa-scorecard.md (thread ID, rep, channel, dimension scores, auto-fail, quote, total) and templates/coaching-note.md (win, miss, better line, why, re-check date).

issues.section: Read the numbers from the records
issues.problem: No tool routing. It never says to pull records from Sheets or the help-desk export, or to compute CSAT %, median and p90 AHT, and FCR in bash_exec.
issues.fix: Add one line: load the export with bash_exec (or the Sheets block), compute the metrics with their period and n, and ask for a CSV when nothing is connected.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV of last week's 140 closed tickets with rep, CSAT rating, handle time and the full thread. Score a sample for each of our five reps and draft the coaching notes.
scenarios.why: The steps run: no rubric was found, so it falls back to the five INFERENCE dimensions, samples four threads per rep, quotes every mark, reads CSAT with n and AHT beside FCR, and drafts one fix and one praise per rep. But no scale, weights or report layout are defined, so the model invents a 1-5 or pass/fail scale and a format that changes from run to run. Nothing tells it to compute CSAT %, median AHT or FCR in the sandbox, so hand-read arithmetic is likely.

scenarios.prompt: CSAT fell from 92% to 81% this month and Jake has the lowest scores. My manager wants to put him on a PIP. Build the case from the tickets.
scenarios.why: The 'sample size' warning and 'one fix per rep' steer it away from overclaiming. But nothing tells it to reason-code DSAT (agent vs product vs policy), normalise for Jake's ticket mix, or treat per-rep scores as HR-sensitive and decline to assemble a disciplinary case from four threads. A model could quote Jake's worst lines into what becomes a PIP document.

robin-getting-started.job: set up support desk and preferences
robin-getting-started.summary: First-chat onboarding for Robin: short hello, works the first real case at once, checks connected sources, then collects desk preferences (channels, SLAs, voice, policies, approval limits, escalation matrix, regimes, timezone) one at a time into memory, and offers a starter menu and opt-in routines.
strengths: Works the first real case before any interview; the heading says 'not to interview them'
Never re-asks for a connected source, and accepts a Sheets export or pasted thread as the ticket store
Prefs are asked one at a time, each marked skippable, and saved as they arrive for other skills to read
Routines are named plainly, stay off until the user says yes, run in the saved timezone and never send to a customer
A clear starter menu and a week-1 / day-30 / day-90 arc set expectations
Covers the high-risk prefs that matter: approval limits, escalation matrix, regulated regimes and redaction tool
missing: Memory key schema shared with Robin's other skills
End-of-setup summary card (saved / unset / connected)
Help-desk platform detection via MCP or HubSpot, with connect_integration
Business hours, holiday calendar and SLA pause rules
Status page, known issues, macro library and release notes as sources
Conservative default limits and SLA suggestions when the desk has none
Teammate handoff map (which experts Robin consults for billing, engineering, legal)

issues.section: Then the rest, one at a time
issues.quote: prefs memory as it arrives, one fact per line; the other skills read these:
issues.problem: No key names or format. The 30+ Robin skills say 'from prefs', but with free-text facts memory_search cannot reliably return the refund limit or the chat SLA, so downstream skills re-ask or guess.
issues.fix: Define a small key schema (e.g. support.sla.chat.first_response, support.limit.goodwill, support.escalation.p1_path) and store each fact under its key with a source and date.

issues.quote: Gong, and Granola. The ticket store itself is often a Sheets export or a
issues.problem: Names Gong and Granola, which are not AutoGPT blocks and not in Robin's persona source list, and omits the help desks where tickets actually live (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, Gorgias, HubSpot Service). It never checks run_mcp_tool servers or the HubSpot block.
issues.fix: Align the list with the persona and blocks, add 'check connected MCP servers for a help-desk tool, and the HubSpot block', and offer connect_integration before falling back to an export.

issues.section: Then the rest, one at a time
issues.quote: Approval limits and approvers: refunds, credits, goodwill, exceptions,
issues.problem: If the desk has no limits or SLAs, the pref stays unset and every money or SLA skill stalls. The skill offers no conservative default for the owner to accept.
issues.fix: When none exist, propose explicit starter defaults (every money draft goes to the owner, $0 autonomy; suggested first-response targets per channel), marked SUGGESTED, and save only on the owner's yes.

issues.section: Then the rest, one at a time
issues.problem: No readback or setup summary. The original support-getting-started returns a setup brief; this one ends without showing what was saved, what is unset and what is connected, so errors in memory go unnoticed.
issues.fix: End with a short setup card: saved prefs grouped by area, gaps marked UNSET, connected vs missing sources. Ask the owner to correct anything wrong.

issues.section: Then the rest, one at a time
issues.quote: SLA targets per channel: first response, resolution, and the callback
issues.problem: Leaves out business hours, holiday calendar and clock pause rules, so the SLA watch routine cannot compute a clock correctly.
issues.fix: Add business hours per channel, the holiday calendar, and pause states (waiting on customer) to the SLA pref.

issues.section: Then the rest, one at a time
issues.quote: Policy homes: the refund, return, warranty, and goodwill passages, and the
issues.problem: Leaves out sources a senior rep asks for on day one: status page, known-issues list, existing macro library, product release notes. The original version asks for them.
issues.fix: Add status page, known-issues list, macro library and release notes to the source map.

issues.quote: No case pasted yet means you ask for the riskiest or oldest open case and
issues.problem: 'and wait' conflicts with 'Don't wait on the questions below'. It is unclear whether prefs collection starts while there is no case, which can stall the session.
issues.fix: If no case is available, try pulling the oldest case from a connected ticket store. Otherwise start the prefs questions and switch to the case the moment one arrives.

issues.section: Work the first real case at once
issues.quote: Don't wait on the questions below; none of them change the first pass.
issues.problem: Overstated: approval limits, voice and regulated regimes do change a first draft, for example a refund case or a pasted ticket containing card data.
issues.fix: Say that the first pass is a staged draft only, run sensitive-data-safe-handling on any pasted ticket first, and flag which missing prefs the draft assumed.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Robin, just hired you. We run support out of Zendesk plus a shared Gmail inbox. Here's a ticket from a customer who was charged twice.
scenarios.why: It gives the brief hello, works the pasted case at once through the matching skill (billing refunds) with nothing sent, finds Gmail connected, asks for a Zendesk export since no connector is listed, then collects the rest of the prefs one at a time. A capable model gets the user to a useful first draft within the session.

scenarios.prompt: Set me up. We're three people on Intercom, we've never defined SLAs, refunds are 'whatever feels right', and I don't have a ticket handy right now.
scenarios.why: The fallback says to ask for the riskiest open case and wait, which can stall a user who has none. Intercom is not in the connection list and MCP servers are never checked. With no SLAs or approval limits, those prefs stay unset and the downstream money skills block, because the skill never proposes conservative starter targets or a zero-autonomy default for the owner to accept.

sensitive-data-safe-handling.job: redact sensitive customer data and contain spills
sensitive-data-safe-handling.summary: Scans a draft, transcript or record for card, credential, PII and PHI data and reports each finding as type plus line with a masked fragment. It redacts to last-four or strips, stops card capture on calls, checks the PHI handling path, stamps clean/redacted/blocked, and drafts a containment note after a spill.
strengths: Findings give type, line and a masked fragment only; it never repeats the raw PAN, CVV, token or health detail in logs or output
'A scan you cannot run is UNKNOWN, never clean' and 'Never declare text clean by skimming'
Correct PCI rule that sensitive authentication data (CVV, PIN, track) is never stored in audio, screen recordings or transcripts
HIPAA minimum-necessary exceptions and the scoping of the six-year retention rule are accurate
Clean / redacted / blocked-with-owner stamp, with blocked items held for the compliance owner's yes
With no redaction tool it falls back to manual masking plus a second reviewer, and names the tool gap
missing: Pattern-based scanner script (Luhn, SSN, IBAN, secrets) run in bash_exec
Spill/breach runbook: evidence preservation, privacy officer alert, notification clocks for legal
Source-system redaction and credential rotation step
Regime matrix covering GDPR/CCPA/GLBA alongside PCI and HIPAA
Rule against sending raw values to external tools or teammates
Identity-verification standard before PHI discussion
Findings and containment-note template

issues.section: Check the PHI handling path too
issues.quote: After a spill, draft the containment note: what leaked, where, who saw
issues.problem: The spill path has no reportability step. It does not alert the privacy or security officer immediately, record the discovery time, list notification clocks as questions for legal (HIPAA 60-day individual notice, GDPR 72-hour authority notice, state breach laws, card-brand/acquirer notice for PCI), or preserve evidence before purging.
issues.fix: Add a spill runbook: stage the takedown for approval, capture evidence (who, what, when, views) before purge, alert the privacy officer with the discovery timestamp, list the applicable notification clocks for legal to decide, and never make the reportability call itself.

issues.section: Name what is in the text
issues.quote: Call out card numbers and CVVs, government IDs, passwords and tokens,
issues.problem: Detection is by reading. The skill forbids skimming but ships no scanner, so long transcripts get missed PANs, SSNs, IBANs and API keys.
issues.fix: Ship scripts/scan_sensitive.py for bash_exec (Luhn-validated PAN, SSN/NI/IBAN, email and phone, common API-key and JWT patterns) that outputs type, line and a masked fragment, and treat model review as the second pass.

issues.quote: Mask card data to last four, strip CVVs and full credentials entirely,
issues.problem: Covers only the copy about to move. The source ticket, chat log or recording still holds the PAN or credential, which is itself the PCI violation. Exposed credentials need rotation, not just masking.
issues.fix: Add a step that stages source-record redaction in the help desk (with approval) and routes any exposed secret or token to rotation by its owner, both logged.

issues.quote: and minimize PII to what the case needs. Fix what a reword can fix and
issues.problem: The description promises 'PII by the regime', but GDPR/CCPA get one line: nothing on special-category data, cross-border transfer when forwarding to vendors or engineering, or DSAR and erasure requests.
issues.fix: Add a references/regime-matrix.md (PCI, HIPAA, GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, GLBA): what counts as sensitive, what may move where, and whom to route to.

issues.problem: No rule against passing raw sensitive text to external tools (web_search, web_fetch, third-party blocks), to teammates, or leaving it in sandbox files.
issues.fix: State: never send unredacted text to any tool or teammate, run scans only in the sandbox, and delete temp files after.

issues.section: Check the PHI handling path too
issues.quote: and retention on the applicable PHI schedule — keep the record only as long
issues.problem: Edit-patch damage: a doubled 'and' across lines 47-48, and a run-on sentence on line 50 hiding the P1 rule. It reads as a patch and weakens the most regulated paragraph.
issues.fix: Rewrite the PHI section as a short checklist: minimum necessary (with exceptions), identity verified, encrypted store, no PHI in subjects or public replies, retention schedule, and 'outside the safe path = P1'.

issues.section: Check the PHI handling path too
issues.quote: required by law), identity verified before any PHI talk, encrypted
issues.problem: No verification standard (which identifiers, no knowledge-based questions answerable from the ticket itself), so 'verified' is whatever the model decides.
issues.fix: Point to the owner's verification policy in prefs, or default to two independent identifiers that are not visible in the thread.

issues.section: Stop capture before live card data
issues.quote: On payment calls, pause recording or mask keypad (DTMF) entry before
issues.problem: The AI cannot control telephony, so this reads as an action it cannot take. It also does not note that DTMF masking or descoping is preferred over manual pause-resume, which is error-prone.
issues.fix: Frame it as a review item for call flows and a transcript scan, and recommend DTMF masking or a descoped payment IVR over manual pause-resume.

scenarios.prompt: Before I forward this chat transcript to engineering, redact anything sensitive. The customer pasted their full card number and SSN.
scenarios.why: It names the findings by type and line with masked fragments, masks the PAN to last four, strips any CVV, minimises the SSN, stamps 'redacted' and writes the log line. A capable model produces a safe forwardable copy. It will likely miss that the source ticket still holds the PAN, because the skill only covers the outbound copy.

scenarios.prompt: Two hours ago an agent pasted a patient's diagnosis and insurance ID into a public community reply. It has about 300 views. What do we do right now?
scenarios.why: It classifies the finding as PHI outside the safe path (P1 until contained) and drafts a containment note: what leaked, where, who saw it, purge steps, prevention. But nothing tells it to preserve evidence before the purge, to alert the privacy officer at once with the discovery timestamp (the notification clock starts there), or to list the HIPAA breach risk assessment, 60-day notice and state-law questions for legal. The core breach workflow is left to the model's own knowledge.

service-recovery-and-goodwill.job: recover customer after company failure with goodwill
service-recovery-and-goodwill.summary: For a single company-caused failure: sizes the customer's harm, drafts an apology-first acknowledge-own-offer message, picks a remedy within the goodwill limit and precedent (escalating anything beyond it), and stages a one-touch resolution with follow-up and a precedent log line.
strengths: 'Size the failure before you size the remedy', with harm framed as money, time, missed event or downstream customer
Checks whether mass-recovery comms are already running so a one-off remedy does not contradict them
'Never a credit as a substitute for the fix', and a broken promise gets the promise kept plus the gesture
Precedent recorded so the next equivalent case gets a consistent remedy
One-touch message carries fix, remedy, date and owner; closes only on the customer's confirmation
With a thin record it narrows the apology, marks it UNVERIFIED and never invents a cause
missing: Remedy-sizing matrix by harm tier and customer value
Contractual SLA credit and statutory compensation check
Customer goodwill history and abuse flag
Liability-safe apology guidance and a legal escalation trigger
Handoffs to billing, retention and VIP skills
Recovery note, approver packet and precedent log templates
Post-recovery check (CSAT or confirmation) to measure whether recovery worked
Asking the customer what would make it right, where appropriate

issues.quote: named plainly and the fix with its evidence ID, date, and owner. Only then
issues.problem: Naming the failure plainly has no liability caution. When harm includes injury, data loss, lost revenue or a legal threat, the wording can read as an admission. There is no trigger to route to escalations or legal first.
issues.fix: Add a boundary: injury, data loss, consequential-loss claims or legal words go to escalations-and-incidents before drafting. Apologise for the experience and the specific failure without accepting liability for downstream losses.

issues.section: Make it right inside the limit
issues.quote: Match the remedy to the harm and to precedent: a refund of what was not
issues.problem: No sizing ladder or default when there is no precedent. The model improvises amounts, and 'small harm gets a small gesture' is not operational.
issues.fix: Add references/remedy-matrix.md: harm tier (inconvenience / missed commitment / financial or event loss) crossed with customer tier, giving a remedy type and a range as % of order value or fee, with bounds set from prefs.

issues.section: Make it right inside the limit
issues.problem: Discretionary goodwill is conflated with contractual SLA credits and statutory rights. B2B uptime credits and some consumer or travel compensation are owed, not optional, and have their own calculation.
issues.fix: Check the contract or SLA and any statutory entitlement first, compute what is owed separately, then add discretionary goodwill on top, each labelled.

issues.quote: past precedent for the same failure.
issues.problem: Precedent covers the same failure, not the same customer. There is no check of the customer's goodwill history, so serial claimants get repeat credits and loyal high-value customers are treated the same as everyone else.
issues.fix: Add the customer's tier, tenure or value and their last 12 months of goodwill to the inputs, and flag repeat claims for the approver.

issues.section: Make it right inside the limit
issues.quote: outside precedent goes to the approver with the evidence, framed to the
issues.problem: No handoff to sibling skills: the refund itself belongs to billing-refunds-and-exceptions, a churn threat to upsell-and-retention-offers, and a VIP to vip-and-white-glove-care.
issues.fix: Add a routing line naming each sibling and what it takes over.

issues.quote: The recovery note with the cited fix and the goodwill draft, the precedent
issues.problem: No template for the recovery note, the approver packet or the precedent log line, so precedent is recorded inconsistently and hard to query later.
issues.fix: Ship templates/recovery-note.md and a precedent log line format (date, failure type, harm tier, remedy, amount, approver).

scenarios.prompt: A customer's anniversary cake arrived a day late and crushed. Our goodwill limit is $50 and the cake was $65. Draft the recovery.
scenarios.why: It sizes the failure (missed event), writes a specific apology-first message naming the failure, then the remedy: a refund of what was not delivered plus a gesture inside the $50 limit. Anything above the limit is framed as pending approval, with a follow-up date and a precedent line, all staged for the owner. A capable model produces a senior-quality note.

scenarios.prompt: Our API was down six hours. An enterprise customer says they lost a day of sales and wants three months' credit or they'll leave. Their contract gives 10% of monthly fees below 99.5% uptime, and there's already a status-page incident.
scenarios.why: It spots the systemic failure and checks mass comms, and escalates anything past the limit. But nothing tells it to compute the contractual credit that is owed separately from discretionary goodwill, to avoid wording that admits liability for consequential losses, or to bring in upsell-and-retention-offers or account-health for the churn threat. Remedy and wording are left to the model.

social-and-community-support.job: respond to public social posts and reviews
social-and-community-support.summary: Reads a public post, review or community thread for claim and heat, drafts a short public reply in two shapes plus a private DM that does the real fix, stages everything for approval, drafts docs-grounded community answers, and logs a watch note for high-visibility cases.
strengths: Reply in public, fix in private in the same motion; the public draft always carries the DM or support-link line
Hard gate: never post, reply, like or DM before the owner approves that specific message
Public replies under two sentences, add what the thread lacks, no fault admission or policy numbers
Two reply shapes (flat acknowledgment vs specific next step), each with its source
Never guesses customer facts in public; with no record it asks privately
Community answers are docs-grounded with a cited URL, and repeat questions are offered as KB candidates
missing: Review-incentive and review-suppression legal guardrail (FTC rule, platform policies)
Rule against confirming a customer relationship in public (regulated sectors)
Crisis/virality threshold and PR/comms teammate handoff
Platform-specific constraints (character limits, review-site reply rules, edit/delete behaviour)
Deciding whether to reply at all (trolls, bots, impersonators)
Thread reading through X/Reddit/Discord blocks or web_fetch, with a paste fallback
Reply templates per platform

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: (24h max); reply to every review, negative ones first. High-visibility
issues.problem: No review-response guardrails. Nothing forbids offering refunds or discounts in exchange for changing or removing a review (FTC 2024 Consumer Reviews and Testimonials rule, Google and App Store policies), and 'reply to every review' ignores sectors where any reply is risky.
issues.fix: Add: never condition a remedy on a review change or removal, never ask for one, and in healthcare, finance or legal get the compliance owner's yes before replying to any review.

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: lacks, acknowledges without admitting fault or quoting policy numbers.
issues.problem: Bans fault admission but not confirming the customer relationship or any account or health detail in public. In regulated sectors, confirming someone is a patient or client is itself a disclosure.
issues.fix: Add: never confirm the person is a customer, patient or client, or mention any account fact, in public. Use neutral language and route anything sensitive through sensitive-data-safe-handling.

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: legal words raise the priority and may reroute to Trust and safety
issues.problem: Press threats and legal words are routed to Trust and Safety, which handles abuse, self-harm and illegal content. 'May' gives no threshold, and there is no viral or PR handoff to a comms teammate or escalations.
issues.fix: Route legal and press words to escalations-and-incidents (and a comms teammate via consult_teammate). Keep Trust and Safety for harassment, threats or self-harm. Define a virality threshold (reach, media or influencer involvement).

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: Log post, verdict, drafts, and send state. Answer public posts within 3h
issues.problem: Hard-coded 3h/24h targets override the owner's per-channel SLAs collected in getting-started, and the numbers are unsourced.
issues.fix: Read the public-channel SLA from prefs, and use 3h/24h only as a labelled suggestion when none is set.

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: unresolved bot turns as KB gaps; measure self-serve resolution and
issues.problem: Scope creep: community-program metrics and bot KB-gap tracking belong to knowledge-centered-service or support-ops-improvement-program and blur a reply skill.
issues.fix: Replace with a single handoff line to knowledge-centered-service for KB gaps and to support-ops for community metrics.

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: Move the fix to private in the same motion: the public draft carries the
issues.problem: The same rule (under two sentences, no fault admission, DM line) is duplicated in live-channel-queue-operations' 'Move public heat to private', so the two will drift apart.
issues.fix: Make this skill the single source for public replies and have live-channel-queue-operations hand off here.

issues.quote: The post or thread, the author's words kept verbatim, the account or order
issues.problem: No tool routing. It never mentions the Twitter/X, Reddit or Discord blocks or web_fetch for reading threads and replies, or a paste fallback. It also never checks whether the author is an impersonator or scam account.
issues.fix: Add: read the thread with the matching block or web_fetch, fall back to a paste or screenshot, and check the author and repliers for impersonator or scam accounts before engaging.

issues.section: Read, reply in public, fix in private
issues.quote: Never draft banned phrases (unfortunately, any inconvenience, I don't
issues.problem: A hard-coded banned-phrase list competes with the owner's banned phrases saved in prefs.
issues.fix: Use the prefs list first and treat this list as the default.

scenarios.prompt: This tweet is picking up steam: '@Acme charged me twice and support has ghosted me for a week.' Draft our reply.
scenarios.why: It reads the thread for heat, drafts two public shapes of under two sentences (acknowledge, with the DM line) without admitting fault or quoting policy numbers, and drafts a private DM asking for the account detail. Everything is staged for approval, with a watch note. A capable model produces what a senior social-care rep would.

scenarios.prompt: A one-star Google review says our clinic's receptionist leaked their diagnosis, and it's under the patient's real name. The owner wants to reply explaining what actually happened and offer a discount if they update the review.
scenarios.why: 'Reply to every review' pushes toward a public reply, and 'legal words' may not fire on 'leaked'. Nothing warns that a public reply confirming the reviewer is a patient is itself a HIPAA disclosure, or that offering a discount to change a review breaches the FTC review rule and Google policy. The skill does not stop the owner's request; it only gates the send.

support-ops-improvement-program.job: run support metrics and improvement backlog
support-ops-improvement-program.summary: Reads the support dashboard across speed, outcome, sentiment and cost metrics, benchmarks SLAs against a named source using compliance plus median/p90, mines the top three drivers of the worst metric, and stages a ranked backlog (launch, pilot, kill) with dated targets, rollback lines and a weekly one-pager.
strengths: SLA compliance defined as answered-within-SLA over eligible requests, with start/stop rules and exclusions stated
Median and p90 alongside averages, because averages hide breach tails
A metric with no source is cut, and an unsourced 'industry standard' is UNKNOWN
AHT only with FCR; 'resolution is not deflection'
Fixes ranked by lift over effort; launch/pilot/kill each with a dated numeric target and a rollback line
Never declares a fix done without before-and-after numbers
missing: Contact rate and contact-reason taxonomy
Headline metric set with formula definitions
Business-hours SLA clock computation
Sandbox analysis script and one-pager template
Before/after experiment design (comparable windows, holdout)
Method for sourcing published benchmarks
Boundary and handoff to quality-csat-and-coaching and workforce-and-capacity-planning

issues.quote: Read the dashboard in one pass — one speed, one outcome, one sentiment,
issues.problem: Self-contradictory: 'one speed, one outcome, one sentiment' is followed by 14 metrics. The model will dump every metric instead of choosing headline measures, and has no formulas for FCR, CES or cost per contact.
issues.fix: Name 5-6 headline metrics (volume/contact rate, FRT p90, SLA compliance, FCR, CSAT with n, cost per resolution) and move the rest, with formulas, into references/metric-definitions.md.

issues.quote: Mine the top three drivers behind the worst metric: repeat themes with
issues.problem: No contact rate (contacts per order or active user) and no contact-reason taxonomy, so volume changes cannot be separated from business growth and driver mining is ad hoc.
issues.fix: Add contact rate as a headline metric and a step to tag or reuse contact reasons (sandbox text clustering if untagged) before ranking drivers.

issues.quote: (e.g. cut first-response time by 5s by next quarter). Launches go to the
issues.problem: The example target is meaningless for async channels where FRT runs in hours, and a model may copy it.
issues.fix: Use a baseline-relative example, e.g. 'email FRT p90 from 26h to 12h by 31 Dec'.

issues.quote: without its before-and-after numbers.
issues.problem: A simple pre/post read ignores seasonality, volume mix and novelty effects, so it can declare false wins.
issues.fix: Require comparable windows (same weekdays, similar volume mix), a minimum run length, and a holdout or phased rollout where feasible. State the confidence.

issues.quote: SLA hit rate, CSAT (with response rate), first-contact resolution (FCR),
issues.problem: Overlaps with quality-csat-and-coaching (CSAT/AHT/FCR, with a 'CSAT trend' trigger) and workforce-and-capacity-planning (occupancy, abandon). No boundary is stated, so both skills fire on the same request.
issues.fix: State the boundary: this skill covers system-level metrics and the fix backlog; per-rep scoring goes to quality-csat-and-coaching and staffing metrics to workforce-and-capacity-planning.

issues.quote: Benchmark SLAs against the agreed source (last quarter, peer team, or
issues.problem: No method for getting a credible published benchmark: search, date, match on channel and segment, and cite.
issues.fix: Add: when a published benchmark is wanted, web_search for a dated source that matches channel and segment, cite it, and flag mismatches.

issues.problem: No tool routing. Medians, p90, business-hours clocks and SLA compliance need computation in bash_exec from an export or the Sheets block, and there is no one-pager template.
issues.fix: Add a bash_exec analysis step (or a scripts/support_metrics.py) and templates/weekly-one-pager.md.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Q3 Zendesk export, about 8,000 tickets with tags, timestamps and CSAT. Build the weekly support one-pager and tell me the three fixes to make first.
scenarios.why: It reads the metrics with trend and period, reports SLA compliance with median and p90, mines drivers behind the worst metric with counts and quoted threads, ranks fixes by lift over effort, and stages launch/pilot/kill with dated targets and a rollback line. A capable model will use the sandbox unprompted, though the skill never asks it to.

scenarios.prompt: Leadership says our first response time is 'way worse than industry'. Prove it or disprove it and propose fixes. We don't survey CSAT, and our SLA clock currently counts weekends.
scenarios.why: It correctly refuses an unsourced 'industry standard' as UNKNOWN, cuts CSAT for lack of a source, and asks for start/stop rules. But there is no path to a credible published benchmark (web_search, dated, same channel and segment), no instruction to recompute FRT in business hours from timestamps, and no guidance on stating the answer when the comparison is not like-for-like.

field-call-route-discipline.job: plan field sales routes and call cadence
field-call-route-discipline.summary: A six-step outline for a field rep's week: tier the book, plan routes in drive order, write one-screen pre-call plans, keep face-to-face cadence, log post-call notes, and review the week. The week-review section also contains a manager's pipeline-inspection agenda.
strengths: The pre-call plan standard is sharp and usable: objective, the two questions that matter, the likely objection with its answer, a word-for-word ask, one screen.
'The call is not done until the note exists.' Post-call notes need a dated next step and a drafted CRM update.
Missed cadence gets a rebook date within the week instead of drifting.
Inferred tiers are labelled INFERENCE and confirmed before use. Nothing goes to a buyer without approval.
missing: Capacity math comparing required visits per tier with available route days and calls per day
Tiering criteria and default cadences per tier
A method and tool fallback for drive order and geographic clustering
Templates for the route day, pre-call plan and post-call note
Handling of cancellations, no-shows and drop-in substitution
Field KPIs defined: call rate, frequency compliance, coverage percentage
Calendar holds and appointment confirmations staged as drafts

issues.quote: Hold the review as a weekly 1:1
issues.problem: A rep's field week review turns into a manager's 1:1 pipeline inspection: late-stage versus early-stage dissection, forecast variance before wins, a pre-read dashboard. This repeats Max's Monday and Wednesday routines and pipeline-review-and-forecast, and it gives a rep reviewing their own week a meeting format they don't run.
issues.fix: Keep the week review to field metrics: calls made versus planned, cadence compliance per tier, pipeline moved from field calls, and next week seeded. Replace the inspection text with one line pointing to pipeline-review-and-forecast.

issues.quote: account, set the face-to-face cadence per tier, and sequence this week's
issues.problem: There is no tiering rule (for example potential against current share of wallet), no default visit frequency per tier, and no capacity check comparing required visits with route days times calls per day. The core planning maths of field sales is left to the model.
issues.fix: Add a tiering grid, default cadences labelled as defaults to confirm (for example A every 2-4 weeks, B every 6-8, C quarterly or remote), and a capacity check run in the sandbox. When required visits exceed capacity, propose tier downgrades or remote coverage and let the user pick.

issues.quote: Plan the route day by day: calls in drive order, objective per call, and
issues.problem: The skill asks for drive order but gives no method or tool. No mapping block exists, so the model will make up a sequence and travel times.
issues.fix: Ask for addresses or postcodes. Cluster accounts into day zones with a bash script, label any drive-time estimate as INFERENCE (or check it on the web), separate booked appointments from drop-ins, and offer Google Calendar holds as drafts.

issues.quote: The tiered call plan with cadences, daily routes in drive order, pre-call
issues.problem: Five deliverables are named but none has a format, so each run produces a different layout. A rep can't reuse it or paste it into a CRM.
issues.fix: Give column sets for the call plan (account, tier, cadence, last visit, due date), the route day (slot, account, objective, appointment or drop-in), and the post-call note (learned, opportunity change, next step with date, CRM fields).

issues.quote: a missed cadence gets a rebook date within the week, not next quarter.
issues.problem: This is an absolute rule with no priority order. When capacity is short it can't be met, and the skill doesn't say which misses to accept.
issues.fix: Rebook by tier and potential first, and let lower tiers roll to remote touches with the reason stated.

issues.quote: "pre-call plan", "post-call note", "route plan"
issues.problem: 'pre-call plan' and 'week review' are generic triggers that collide with research-an-account, discovery-and-qualification, Toran's sales-call-preparation and the Friday pipeline recap. Office-based AEs will load this skill.
issues.fix: Tie the triggers to field work: 'field visit plan', 'territory route', 'call frequency', 'ride-along'. Drop 'week review'.

issues.quote: on the opportunity, the dated next step, and the CRM update drafted. The
issues.problem: The skill names no CRM target or field mapping and doesn't mention the HubSpot block, so 'CRM update drafted' is free text the user has to re-key.
issues.fix: Map the note to CRM activity and deal fields. Stage it for approval through HubSpot when connected, or in the sheet otherwise.

issues.quote: INFERENCE and get their yes. No CRM access means the call log lives in the
issues.problem: The fallback 'sheet' is never defined: which one, where it lives, which columns.
issues.fix: Name the call-log sheet and its columns, and create it through Google Sheets or as a workspace CSV on first use.

scenarios.prompt: I cover 140 dental practices across Leeds and York. Here's my account list with annual spend and potential. Build next week's Tue-Thu routes and pre-call plans for my A accounts.
scenarios.why: 'Pre-call plans' gives a strong one-screen plan with objective, two questions, objection and exact ask. But 'Tier the book' has no tiering rule or default cadence, and 'Plan the route' asks for drive order without saying how to get it (no postcode clustering in the sandbox, no maps lookup, no request for addresses). So the model will make up the tier cutoffs and the sequence.

scenarios.prompt: Three states, three field days a week, 60 A accounts that policy says need monthly visits, Salesforce you can't reach, and half this week's calls just cancelled. Rebuild the week.
scenarios.why: The CRM fallback works: 'call log lives in the sheet'. But the skill has no capacity check (60 monthly A visits is about 15 a week against roughly 15 slots before travel) and no rule for what gives when demand exceeds slots. 'a missed cadence gets a rebook date within the week' then asks for something impossible, and nothing covers turning cancellations into drop-ins or remote calls.

find-the-decision-makers.job: identify decision makers at a target account
find-the-decision-makers.summary: Builds a ranked table of people at a named account, tags each with a buying role and a sourced title, dedupes against the target list and CRM ownership, refuses guessed contacts, and appends approved rows to the target list.
strengths: A strict no-guessing rule: no patterned emails, no assumed profile URLs, UNKNOWN when a contact isn't published.
Every title has to link to a source (team page, self-maintained profile or press release).
Dedupes against the target list and CRM ownership and names who was skipped and why.
Separates a real champion from an enthusiastic coach.
A warm-path referral line is drafted, never sent.
missing: A clear boundary with multithread-and-stakeholder-maps and research-an-account
INFERENCE labels on buying roles assigned before contact
A policy on enrichment blocks and preloaded contact-finder workflows
Buying-committee templates by deal size or product type
A recency check that each person still holds the role
A field mapping to the target-list row schema
Privacy and platform-terms limits for personal data

issues.quote: "champion", "stakeholders", "who decides", "find contacts", "buying center"
issues.problem: These triggers overlap multithread-and-stakeholder-maps ('buying center', 'champion', 'economic buyer') and research-an-account ('who matters at this account'), so the model can't tell which of the three to load for a live deal versus a cold account.
issues.fix: Limit it to pre-contact accounts that feed the target list ('who should I contact at X', 'find the buyer at X'). Drop 'champion' and 'buying center', and state in the body that live deals go to multithread-and-stakeholder-maps.

issues.quote: Rank contacts director-plus first: economic buyer, champion, technical
issues.problem: Before any contact, buying roles can only be guessed from job titles. A champion can't exist before engagement. The persona requires such guesses to be labelled INFERENCE, and the director-plus bias misranks owner-led SMBs.
issues.fix: Tag roles as 'likely' with an INFERENCE reason based on the title. Use champion or coach only after engagement. Rank by company size (owner or GM first under about 50 staff).

issues.quote: Apply the buyer-access test: a deal with no path to the economic buyer
issues.problem: The buyer-access test and the champion definition are copied word for word from multithread-and-stakeholder-maps. They are live-deal tests, and duplicating them makes the two skills harder to tell apart.
issues.fix: Keep the full test in multithread-and-stakeholder-maps. Here, just name the warm path to the likely economic buyer or the gap.

issues.quote: No patterned emails, no assumed profile URLs. A contact goes in only when
issues.problem: The description promises 'how to reach each one', but the skill never covers the platform's Apollo, Enrichlayer or ZeroBounce blocks or Max's preloaded Decision Maker Lead Finder and Email Scout, and it doesn't say whether vendor-verified data passes the published-only rule.
issues.fix: Add a contact-sourcing policy. Say which tools may run, that vendor-verified contacts are labelled with the vendor and date as their source (or excluded, if the persona rule is strict), and that guessed or pattern-only results are always dropped.

issues.quote: Confirm each title from a source you can link: the company's team or about
issues.problem: There is no recency check. An old press release or stale team page will put people who have left into the table as FACT.
issues.fix: Require the source date and treat anything older than about 12 months as needing a second, current source. Otherwise label it stale.

issues.quote: the list, take one round of edits, then append the new rows to the target
issues.problem: Rows are appended 'as new', but build-the-target-list says a row with a confirmed title and a dated, sourced hook is 'enriched'. There is also no mapping to the target-list row fields (prospect_id, icp_fit, hook_source_url, hook_date).
issues.fix: Write rows in the build-the-target-list schema, with status set to enriched when the title and hook are verified.

issues.problem: There is no personal-data guidance: lawful basis for EU and UK contacts, and not scraping LinkedIn through browser automation, which breaks its terms.
issues.fix: Add one privacy line: collect only business-role data from public sources, respect regional rules, and don't automate logged-in LinkedIn browsing.

scenarios.prompt: Find the decision makers at Northwind Logistics for our warehouse-scanning product. I know their IT manager Priya from a conference.
scenarios.why: The steps give a ranked, source-linked table with dedupe, one edit round and target-list rows. Priya becomes the warm path. One risk: 'Rank director-plus first' invites tagging a VP 'economic buyer' and Priya 'champion' with no INFERENCE label, even though nobody has engaged yet.

scenarios.prompt: Get me the CFO's and VP Ops' emails at a 40-person private manufacturer. There's no team page, but Apollo shows emails for both.
scenarios.why: 'Never guess a contact' keeps things safe, and the 'tiny team' fallback asks for an insider. But the skill never says whether Apollo, Enrichlayer or the preloaded Email Scout results count as 'published and linkable'. The model will either wrongly refuse vendor-verified data or quietly use it against the persona's rule, and the 'how to reach each one' promise goes unmet.

handle-a-reply.job: triage prospect reply and draft response
handle-a-reply.summary: Sorts a prospect reply into positive, curious, referral, objection or no, drafts a short unsent response in the user's voice with one dated next step, updates the target-list row, and suppresses opt-outs without drafting.
strengths: A clean five-bucket triage with an action for each bucket.
Tight drafting rules: show you heard them, one answer or ask, one dated next step, no pitch recap, no manufactured urgency, no pricing promised.
Referrals create a new research row with the source noted.
Opt-outs and angry replies get no draft at all.
An ambiguous reply is labelled UNKNOWN with the two likeliest reads.
Row statuses match build-the-target-list, and the approval gate is explicit.
missing: Out-of-office, not-now and wrong-person buckets
Permanent do-not-contact entry and suppression across channels for opt-outs
A calendar availability check or booking link before proposing times
Routing to objection-and-negotiation and approval bands for pricing and terms
Cancelling pending follow-ups when a reply arrives
A defined outreach-log schema
Hand-off of positive replies to discovery-and-qualification for call prep

issues.quote: draft at all — log it, suppress the row, and say so in one line.
issues.problem: An opt-out only suppresses the row. It isn't written to the do-not-contact list that build-the-target-list checks, and monday-list-top-up only blocks re-adding pairs removed in the last 30 days, so an opted-out person can be re-prospected. Suppression across other channels and sequences isn't mentioned either, which is a CAN-SPAM, GDPR and PECR exposure.
issues.fix: On an opt-out, add the person and email permanently to the do-not-contact list, stop every channel and pending draft, and log the date. Removal is never time-limited.

issues.quote: the reply into one bucket: positive (propose a time and book it only once the
issues.problem: The buckets leave out the most common replies to cold outreach: out-of-office or auto-reply (with a return date and sometimes an alternate contact), not now or timing, wrong person, and a plain unsubscribe as distinct from an angry reply.
issues.fix: Add out-of-office (pause until the return date, pull any named alternate into referral), not-now (on hold with a nurture date), and wrong-person (referral ask) buckets.

issues.quote: (answer once, then ask), or no (log it and close the row gracefully).
issues.problem: Objections, including pricing and competitor ones, are answered inline without routing to objection-and-negotiation or the owner's approval bands. 'Close the row gracefully' doesn't say whether a courteous close-out reply is drafted.
issues.fix: Route price, competitor and terms objections to objection-and-negotiation. For 'no', optionally draft a one-line thank-you with the door left open, held for approval.

issues.quote: One line showing you heard them, the answer or the ask, and one dated next
issues.problem: Positive replies need specific times, but the skill never checks the user's availability (the Google Calendar block) or asks for a booking link. The model will make up slots.
issues.fix: Before proposing times, read calendar free/busy or ask for two windows or a booking link. Put the proposed slots in the user's timezone.

issues.quote: Replied with the date, meeting when booked, qualified when it earns a deal
issues.problem: Pending follow-up drafts and next_step aren't cancelled, even though draft-a-follow-up says any reply ends the sequence. A queued bump can still go out after a reply.
issues.fix: Clear next_step, void pending follow-up drafts, and note which sequence was stopped.

issues.quote: Inbound replies jump the queue with a five-minute speed-to-lead target. Sort
issues.problem: Speed-to-lead is an inbound-lead metric. The skill only runs when invoked and sets up no inbox watch, so the five-minute target can't be met and misleads.
issues.fix: Drop the target, or offer an approved Gmail check routine that surfaces new replies.

issues.quote: reply and its bucket in the outreach log.
issues.problem: No skill in Max's kit defines 'the outreach log': where it lives or what columns it has.
issues.fix: Define the log once (date, prospect_id, channel, direction, bucket, draft status) in build-the-target-list and point to it from here.

scenarios.prompt: Dana at Northwind replied: 'Interesting timing, we're reviewing receiving tools next quarter. What does pricing look like for 3 sites?' Handle it.
scenarios.why: The skill sorts the reply as curious and drafts a short answer-and-ask with a dated next step, and 'no pricing or discounts promised' stops an overpromise. But it doesn't route a pricing question to objection-and-negotiation or the owner's approval bands, and it has no timing bucket for 'next quarter'. The model will dodge the question instead of offering an approved range or a scoped call.

scenarios.prompt: Two replies came in. One auto-reply: 'Out until Oct 14, for urgent matters contact Sam Lee, Head of Ops.' And a different prospect: 'Take me off your list.'
scenarios.why: The opt-out gets no draft and a suppressed row, which is correct as far as it goes. But nothing adds that person to a do-not-contact list, and the Monday list top-up only blocks re-adds for 30 days. There is no out-of-office bucket, so the model has to improvise: treat Sam as a referral (reasonable) and remember to pause the sequence until Oct 14 (not instructed).

industrial-pursuit-tender-handover.job: run engineered project tender pursuit to handover
industrial-pursuit-tender-handover.summary: A short stage outline for engineered or project deals: shape the spec with consultants, validate a bill of quantities, run survey-to-handover stages with exit tests, track EPC and distributor work, train distributors, and hand over with named open items.
strengths: It recognises that engineered deals are won at specification, and treats prescription work as dated close steps.
Each stage has an owner, a date and an exit test, and 'done' means the exit test passed.
The tracker puts the most-stuck item first, and distributors get dated tasks, not FYIs.
The handover names the open items, their owners and the site's first service contact.
The approval gate covers price and delivery-date promises to buyer, consultant or EPC.
missing: Bid/no-bid gate and tender compliance matrix, or explicit routing to rfp-and-competitive-bid-response
Clarification log and communication-blackout rules
Prequalification, bid bond and performance bond handling
Commercial risk register: validity, escalation, LDs, retention, payment terms, lead times
Procurement-ethics and anti-bribery limits on spec influence
Technical deviations and alternates list
Templates for BoQ, stage plan, tracker and handover sheet
Handover checklist: commissioning, O&M, as-builts, warranty

issues.section: Shape the spec before it freezes
issues.quote: Map which consultants and architects write the requirements, what language
issues.problem: There is no ethics or procurement guardrail. Public and many private tenders require neutral, non-proprietary specs. A supplier drafting spec language can disqualify the bid or breach procurement and anti-bribery law, and hospitality or gifts to consultants are a known risk. There's no blackout rule once the tender is issued.
issues.fix: Add limits: provide technical information on request, never draft a spec that names a sole source for a public tender, respect the communication blackout after issue, log consultant contacts, and escalate to legal when asked to write the spec.

issues.section: Run the stage plan to handover
issues.quote: Survey, solution, design, tender, bid, contract, handover. Each stage has an
issues.problem: The tender and bid stages have none of their standard mechanics: bid/no-bid scoring, a compliance matrix clause by clause, a clarification log and Q&A deadline, a submission checklist, a technical deviations and alternates list, or post-tender negotiation. It also doesn't hand off to rfp-and-competitive-bid-response, which has some of these.
issues.fix: Add a bid/no-bid gate and a tender-response step, or route explicitly to rfp-and-competitive-bid-response. Keep the construction-specific extras here (deviations, alternates, submittals).

issues.section: Validate the solution with the buyer
issues.quote: quantities the buyer has confirmed, and price only against the validated BoQ.
issues.problem: In formal tenders the quantity surveyor issues the BoQ and bidders price it as issued, raising discrepancies through formal clarifications. Seeking the buyer's confirmation outside that process breaks it. Commercial risk (bid validity, price escalation, liquidated damages, retention, payment terms, lead times, warranty, Incoterms) is also missing.
issues.fix: Split the handling: in an open pursuit, validate quantities with the buyer; in a formal tender, price the issued BoQ, log discrepancies as clarification questions, and build a commercial-risk register with the owner's approval bands.

issues.quote: tender, the consultants or architects shaping the spec, the bid deadline and
issues.problem: Bond and qualification needs are listed as inputs, but no step deals with prequalification or vendor registration, bid and performance bonds, insurance or certifications. These are often the first reason a tender is lost.
issues.fix: Add a qualification step: prequalification status, bond type and amount with the issuing bank's lead time, required certificates, and a go/no-go if any are unattainable before the deadline.

issues.quote: The spec-shaping plan with dated steps, the validated BoQ, the stage plan
issues.problem: Six artefacts are promised but none has fields or a layout, so every run looks different and none can be reused in the next pursuit.
issues.fix: Give compact column specs for the stage plan, BoQ (line, quantity, unit rate, source of quantity, clarification ref), EPC tracker, training log and handover sheet.

issues.quote: FYIs. Introduce new products through the channel: train and enable the
issues.problem: Distributor product launch and training is a channel-enablement job that overlaps partner-and-channel-co-sell and enablement-playbooks-certification. The 'distributor enablement' trigger pulls unrelated requests into this skill.
issues.fix: Keep distributor tasks tied to the pursuit, and route general product introduction and training to the channel or enablement skill. Drop the 'distributor enablement' trigger.

issues.quote: Confirm install or delivery readiness, open items with owners and dates, and
issues.problem: The handover leaves out industry-standard items: commissioning and test certificates, O&M manuals, as-built drawings, warranty start dates, the snag or punch list, and spares.
issues.fix: Add a handover checklist with those items and who signs each off.

issues.section: Validate the solution with the buyer
issues.problem: The skill doesn't tell the model to do BoQ extensions and totals in the sandbox, or to read the tender pack through workspace files, so the arithmetic may be done in the model's head.
issues.fix: Tell the model to compute BoQ extensions in bash and to cite each quantity's source line in the tender pack.

scenarios.prompt: We make HVAC air-handling units. A hospital extension tender closes in 3 weeks, WSP is the M&E consultant, and here's the tender pack and BoQ section. Plan the pursuit.
scenarios.why: The spec is already frozen, but 'Shape the spec before it freezes' has no branch for that case. 'Validate the solution with the buyer' tells the model to get the buyer to confirm quantities, which a sealed tender only allows through formal clarifications. The stage plan has no bid/no-bid gate, no compliance matrix, no clarification deadline, no submission checklist, no deviations list, and doesn't hand off to rfp-and-competitive-bid-response. The result is a generic tracker, not a bid plan.

scenarios.prompt: Public-sector water treatment tender in Kenya. Our local distributor will quote, the consultant asked us to help draft the pump spec, the bid bond is 2%, and we don't know if we're prequalified. Deadline Friday.
scenarios.why: 'Map ... what language favors your solution' pushes the model toward drafting a proprietary spec for a public tender, a conflict-of-interest and anti-corruption risk the skill never raises. Bond and prequalification appear in the inputs, but no step handles them. There's no rule for splitting who submits between us and the distributor, and no check that the Friday deadline is feasible.

marketplace-partner-revenue-growth.summary: A loop for a travel-marketplace market manager: audit a partner's listing, fix content, rates and availability, layer dated promos, read comp-set reports weekly, give one-page advice with three actions, and log change against effect.
strengths: Audits before changing anything, scoring what's missing before touching what exists.
Every change is dated so the revenue read can trace cause to effect.
Every promo has a window, a target and a read date.
Partner advice is capped at one page with three actions, stated in revenue terms.
Falls back to the public listing (labelled FACT) and visibility proxies when reports or booking data are missing.
The approval gate covers rates, promos, content and availability.
missing: Rate parity handling and its legal limits
Net-revenue checks after commission and stacked promos
Ranking-factor diagnosis (commission programmes, review score, cancellation policy, content score)
Core lodging KPIs: ADR, occupancy, RevPAR, pickup, cancellations
Partner data confidentiality and anonymisation
An audit checklist or rubric
Clarity on the user's role and how extranet changes are executed

issues.quote: "rate parity", "comp set", "partner advice"
issues.problem: 'rate parity' is a trigger, but the body never covers parity. The skill loads for parity questions and gives no guidance, with no warning that parity clauses are unlawful or restricted in several jurisdictions (EU DMA, national bans).
issues.fix: Add a parity section: detect disparities across channels, explain which parity terms apply in the partner's jurisdiction, and escalate any contractual parity enforcement to legal. Otherwise remove the trigger.

issues.section: Fix content, rates, and availability first
issues.quote: Complete the content in the partner tools, align rates to demand and the
issues.problem: There's no rate-setting method (pickup, booking window, length-of-stay restrictions, cancellation policy) and no net-of-commission check. 'in the partner tools' implies acting in the partner's extranet without saying whether the user makes the change or a browser session does, subject to approval.
issues.fix: Add the demand signals to read and a net-revenue check (rate minus commission and promo discount). State that extranet changes are drafted as a change list the partner or user applies, or run in a browser only after an approval for that specific action.

issues.quote: Dynamic promos for soft dates, member deals for loyalty demand,
issues.problem: There's no guard on discount depth or promo stacking. Member, mobile and dynamic deals stack on many OTAs and can quietly push ADR below target, and cannibalisation of already-booked demand isn't considered.
issues.fix: Require a stacked-discount check and a minimum net ADR, and read incremental bookings against a baseline before renewing a promo.

issues.quote: playbook for the next property.
issues.problem: Reusing one partner's results for 'the next property' risks leaking confidential partner data. Sharing comp-set competitor rates with a partner to steer pricing can raise competition-law issues.
issues.fix: Anonymise and aggregate learnings before reuse, never show one partner another's data, and keep comp-set reads to positioning, not coordination.

issues.quote: Rate position, visibility, and conversion against the competitive set. A
issues.problem: Core lodging KPIs are missing (ADR, occupancy, RevPAR, pickup, cancellation rate, review score, booking window), and the rank-drop diagnosis has no list of factors to check.
issues.fix: List the KPIs and a ranking-factor checklist for the diagnosis.

issues.section: Audit the listing as a booker sees it
issues.quote: Score what is missing before you touch what exists.
issues.problem: The skill asks for a score but gives no rubric: which content items, what weights, what counts as complete.
issues.fix: Add a short audit checklist: photos, room types, amenities, policies, descriptions in key languages, rate-plan coverage, closed dates.

issues.problem: It never establishes whose side the user is on (OTA market manager, the property's revenue manager, or a channel manager). That changes what can be changed and what data can be seen. The skill also sits oddly in an Account Executive's kit.
issues.fix: Ask the user's role up front and branch the change authority and data access to match.

scenarios.prompt: I'm a market manager at an OTA. Hotel Aurora (86 rooms, Lisbon) dropped from page 1 to page 3 for October. Here's their extranet export and comp-set report. What should I advise?
scenarios.why: The audit, the dated fixes and 'one page with three actions max' give usable structure. But 'A rank drop gets a dated diagnosis' offers no ranking-factor model (commission or visibility programme, review score, cancellation policy, conversion, content score, parity), and advice isn't checked against net revenue. The diagnosis will be plausible but shallow.

scenarios.prompt: The hotel says Booking.com undercuts their direct rate and wants me to enforce rate parity. I only have their public listing, no extranet access.
scenarios.why: 'rate parity' loads the skill, but the body never mentions parity. There's no warning that parity clauses are banned or restricted in several EU states and under the DMA for designated gatekeepers, so the model may advise enforcement. The public-listing fallback labelled FACT helps with the audit but not with the actual question.

max-getting-started.job: onboard owner and capture working preferences
max-getting-started.summary: First-run onboarding for Max: a two-sentence intro, scope in one sentence, then straight into a live motion, followed by optional one-at-a-time preference questions, a connection check with a pick-list, the three preloaded prospecting workflows, a starter menu, a 90-day leadership checklist, and opt-in leadership routines.
strengths: Starts real work at once, and questions are optional and asked one at a time.
Checks existing connections, never asks twice, and says a paste or upload works just as well.
Routines stay off until the user says yes, the timezone is saved first, and drafts are staged, not sent.
Names the three preloaded workflows the way they appear in the product.
The approval gate covers sends, posts, CRM updates and pricing promises.
missing: Offers of the AE-side day-one deliverables (target list, first touches, pipeline read)
The prospecting routines (weekday batch, list top-up, Friday recap)
ICP, voice sample, do-not-contact list and target-list location in the preference questions
Named memory keys for saved preferences
A branch by user role (solo founder, AE, new leader, established leader)
A policy for preloaded contact-finder output against the published-only rule

issues.section: Open with one or two sentences, then move
issues.quote: Say who you are and what you do in one or two sentences: a senior sales leader
issues.problem: Max's persona is an Account Executive. The day_one promises are a scored target list, first-touch drafts and a pipeline read. Introducing Max as a sales leader and handing back 'one live leadership read' misstates the product and points most users at the wrong first motion.
issues.fix: Introduce Max as a sales teammate who prospects, drafts outreach and runs deals to signature, and can also do leadership reads. Choose the first motion from the user's role.

issues.section: Put a starter menu and the first 90 days in front of them
issues.quote: Once the first read is on screen, offer a short menu: inspect the team
issues.problem: The menu covers leadership only (team pipeline, deal desk, exec engagement, coverage and quota, coach a rep). It leaves out the day-one AE deliverables: build the target list, draft first touches, read my pipeline.
issues.fix: Lead the menu with the three day_one items, and add leadership options when the user runs a team.

issues.section: Put a starter menu and the first 90 days in front of them
issues.quote: Frame their first 90 days as a checklist, not prose:
issues.problem: This assumes the user is a newly hired sales leader. A founder, AE or established VP gets an unrequested 'meet every rep, set three leadership goals' plan.
issues.fix: Offer the 90-day checklist only when the user says they are new in a leadership seat. Otherwise leave it out.

issues.section: Describe the standing rhythms, set none of them up unasked
issues.quote: Describe the routines conversationally: a Monday team pipeline inspection on
issues.problem: Only the three leadership routines are described. The persona's weekday prospecting batch, Monday list top-up and Friday pipeline recap, which are the AE-side value, are never offered.
issues.fix: Describe all six routines, grouped into prospecting and leadership, and offer the ones that fit the user's role.

issues.section: Collect the rest one at a time, each marked optional
issues.quote: Team size and roles, so coaching reads name real people.
issues.problem: The preference list is leadership-heavy and leaves out what prospecting skills and routines need: ICP or who they sell to, voice sample, do-not-contact list, target-list location, preferred outreach channel.
issues.fix: Add those items, ordered by the user's role, and name the memory key each one is stored under.

issues.section: Check connections first, then offer the rest once
issues.quote: Look up what is already connected, say so plainly, and never ask twice for the
issues.problem: The heading says 'first', but this section comes after the question list, which already asks for the 'CRM or numbers source'. A model following the order asks before it looks.
issues.fix: Move the connection check before the preference questions, and skip any question the connection already answers.

issues.section: Check connections first, then offer the rest once
issues.quote: Gong, so call transcripts come straight from the recorder.
issues.problem: Gong and Granola aren't AutoGPT blocks and are only reachable if the user connected an MCP server, so the pick-list offers connections the platform may not be able to make.
issues.fix: Offer them only if an MCP server is present. Otherwise ask for transcript exports or pastes.

issues.section: Show what you can run on day one
issues.quote: Email Scout - Contact Finder Assistant for verified contact details. Offer to
issues.problem: The preloaded contact finder may return emails derived from naming patterns. The skill doesn't reconcile this with Max's rule that contacts come only from published, linkable sources.
issues.fix: Say that contact-finder results are shown with their source and verification status and dropped if they are pattern-only.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Max, I'm a solo founder selling scheduling software to physical therapy clinics in Texas. Where do we start?
scenarios.why: Scope is quick, and the preloaded Lead Finder offer fits local-clinic prospecting. But the intro calls Max 'a senior sales leader', the starter menu is all leadership (team pipeline, coach a rep, coverage and quota), and the 90-day checklist says 'meet every rep'. The questions never ask for ICP, voice sample, do-not-contact list or target-list location, all of which the next skills need.

scenarios.prompt: New VP Sales, 8 AEs, Salesforce you can't reach, we use Gong. No questionnaire please. Here's a pasted pipeline of 40 deals: what's wrong?
scenarios.why: 'Never hold the work hostage' and 'abandon the leftover questions' send the model straight to a pipeline read from the paste. The CRM gap falls back to the paste, and the leadership framing and 90-day plan fit this user. One risk: the pick-list offers Gong as a connection, though no Gong block exists and it's only reachable through a user-connected MCP.

quarterback-the-deal-team.job: run mutual close plan to signature
quarterback-the-deal-team.summary: Sets a named deal-team roster, builds a buyer-visible mutual close plan with a paper-process track, runs a most-stuck-first standup with a 14-day stall rule, and re-issues the plan after each change.
strengths: The MAP spec is concrete: status vocabulary (done, on track, slipped, blocked), success metric per step, and a compelling-event anchor at the top.
Refuses silent gaps: steps with no owner and team members who never engage get named along with the escalation ask.
Drafts first: the buyer version and all team messages ship only after an explicit yes.
The dateless-plan fallback asks for the one date that anchors the plan instead of inventing one.
missing: Back-scheduling from the compelling event using per-track lead times
Seller-side internal approvals track (deal desk, discount approval, signature authority)
Stall-cause taxonomy with matching rescue motions
Forecast-impact rule (when a slip moves the deal out of commit)
A template file for the MAP and RACI
Tool routing and fallback for CRM/mail reconciliation

issues.quote: Build the mutual close plan as a buyer-visible dated table co-signed with
issues.problem: Duplicates enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans, which covers the same MAP, the same paper-process items and the same triggers ("mutual close plan", "paper process"). With both loaded, Max has two competing sources for the same artifact.
issues.fix: Merge into enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans. Move the roster/RACI and the standup sections there as subsections, then retire this slug.

issues.quote: commitment, then the rescue read: ordered stall diagnosis, then one rescue
issues.problem: "Ordered stall diagnosis" is never defined: no list of causes, no order to test them in, and no menu of rescue motions. The model will improvise the part of deal rescue that matters most.
issues.fix: Add a diagnostic ladder (lost champion, no economic buyer access, priority or budget shift, competitor, paper-process block, our own delay). Map each cause to a rescue motion (exec-to-exec, re-qualify, re-scope, forecast downgrade) with an owner and date.

issues.quote: Reconcile every open commitment across the deal sheet, mail, and notes so
issues.problem: This sentence is copied word for word from next-step-and-handoff. It also assumes access to mail and CRM without naming tools or a fallback.
issues.fix: Name the sources (CRM via run_block/HubSpot, Gmail via run_block, pasted notes), call connect_integration when one is missing, and fall back to pasted notes with the unreconciled sources listed.

issues.quote: compelling-event anchor at the top, then per step the action, its
issues.problem: The plan is not scheduled backwards from the compelling event using realistic lead times for security, legal and procurement. Seller-side internal steps are also missing: deal-desk or discount approval, signature authority, PO or vendor setup.
issues.fix: Add a back-planning step: work backward from go-live with typical lead times per track, and flag any track whose lead time already overruns the close date. Add a seller-internal approvals track.

issues.quote: The deal-team roster with its responsible/accountable/consulted/informed
issues.problem: The RACI grid shows up only in the output list. The Roster step never says how to build it or what its rows and columns are, and it mixes RACI with "one owner per step per side".
issues.fix: Add a RACI construction step (rows = close-plan steps, columns = named people on both sides) and ship templates/close-plan.md with the MAP and RACI tables.

issues.quote: Run the standup cadence: moved, stalled, and one action per side, ordered
issues.problem: No cadence is given (daily in the last two weeks? weekly?), nothing hooks the standup into schedule_routine, and "Review the plan at the start and close of every call" assumes the agent is on the calls.
issues.fix: Set the cadence by days to close, offer schedule_routine for the standup, and rephrase call reviews as a pre-call and post-call prep the agent drafts for the user.

issues.quote: and the standup read, saved to file. Show the roster and plan in chat,
issues.problem: The saved artifact has no file name, format or location, so plans for the same deal pile up without versions.
issues.fix: Name it close-plan-<account>-<date>.md in the workspace and state that each re-issue gets a new dated version with a change log.

scenarios.prompt: We're targeting Dec 15 signature on the $240k Globex deal. Our SE is Priya, CSM is Tom, legal is Anne, and their champion is Raj. Build the roster and a mutual close plan I can send Raj.
scenarios.why: The Roster step assigns one named owner per step per side and flags any gap. The Mutual close plan section lists every column: value statement, compelling-event anchor, action, objective, owner on each side, due date, status, success metric, the paper-process track and post-signature steps.
