issues.problem: No guidance on judging a report's scope or freshness (SOC 2 Type I vs II, period covered, bridge letter, exceptions, carve-outs, complementary user-entity controls). Without it the register records 'PRESENT' for weak evidence.
issues.fix: Add a reading checklist: report type, period end within 12 months, bridge letter, qualified opinion or exceptions, systems in scope vs the purchased service, carve-outs, and user-entity controls the buyer must operate.

issues.section: Build the checklist from the purchase
issues.quote: Assign each check to its real owner:
issues.problem: No path when a reviewer role doesn't exist, which is common at small companies.
issues.fix: If no owner exists, record the check as BLOCKED - NO REVIEWER and ask the user to name one or accept the risk in writing. Never self-assign.

issues.quote: For each item, keep the vendor claim, document name, scope, issuer, date, expiry, relevant passage, reviewer, status, and open question.
issues.problem: No instruction to gather public evidence (trust center, breach history, sanctions lists) with web_search/web_fetch, and no rule for NDA-restricted documents such as SOC 2 reports.
issues.fix: Use web_search/web_fetch for public evidence with retrieval date. Keep NDA-restricted reports inside the workspace and cite them without redistributing.

issues.quote: Return the evidence register, missing items, conflicts, and a reviewer queue with due dates.
issues.problem: No register template, and no re-check cadence even though every record has an expiry.
issues.fix: Ship templates/evidence-register.csv and offer, with approval, a schedule_routine re-check 30 days before the earliest expiry.

scenarios.prompt: We're about to sign an AI note-taker that will record customer calls. Vet them. Here's their trust-center link and SOC 2 report.
scenarios.why: The skill would build a register with owners and statuses, and 'Do not accept a badge or summary as proof beyond its stated scope' helps. But it gives no guidance on reading a SOC 2 (Type I vs II, report period, exceptions, carve-outs, user-entity controls). It doesn't prompt AI-specific checks (training on customer data, LLM subprocessors, recording-consent law) or say to use web_search for breach history and sanctions.

scenarios.prompt: Small vendor, no SOC 2, just a filled questionnaire and a 2022 pen-test letter. We have no security team and need a go/no-go by tomorrow.
scenarios.why: The statuses handle it well (EXPIRED for the pen test, MISSING for SOC 2) and the skill rightly refuses to give a go/no-go. But 'Assign each check to its real owner' has no path when the reviewer role doesn't exist, and there is no guidance on compensating evidence or on escalating a missing reviewer as a blocker for the user.

vendor-performance-review.job: review vendor performance against agreed SLAs
vendor-performance-review.summary: Builds a period record comparing vendor delivery to signed service terms and approved outcomes, labels each measure MET/MISSED/DISPUTED/NOT MEASURED, and returns a scorecard, strengths, misses and owned actions, with no breach claims, credit demands or scope changes.
strengths: Measures against signed terms and approved outcomes, not impressions
Four clear result labels, including DISPUTED with both records and NOT MEASURED
Tracks service credits claimed or not claimed, plus invoice accuracy and adoption
Separates vendor explanations from facts and refuses to trend one complaint
No breach claims, credit demands, scope changes or termination threats; contract questions go to counsel
missing: Service-credit claim deadlines and procedure
Baseline and trend vs prior periods
Path when there is no written SLA
Tiered review cadence by vendor criticality
Vendor corrective-action plan with dates
Scorecard template and worked example
Link from performance results to renewal decisions

issues.quote: service credits claimed or not claimed
issues.problem: Records credit status but ignores that most contracts require credits to be claimed within a window (often 30 days) in a set form, so money is lost silently.
issues.fix: Record each credit's claim deadline and procedure from the contract. Flag credits whose window closes within 14 days to the contract owner as a decision, drafted but not sent.

issues.quote: Return the scorecard, three strengths, material misses, unresolved evidence, and an action table with owner and date.
issues.problem: Requiring exactly three strengths invites padding or invented positives when evidence supports fewer.
issues.fix: Change to 'up to three strengths, each with source evidence; write none if the evidence shows none'.

issues.quote: Compare delivery with the signed service terms and the business outcomes approved for the purchase.
issues.problem: No path when there is no written SLA or approved outcome, and no comparison with prior periods, so the most common problem vendors produce an empty scorecard.
issues.fix: If no agreed measure exists, mark it NOT MEASURED, build a factual baseline from delivery records, flag 'no written SLA' as a contract gap for the renewal, and compare with prior periods where the same method applies.

issues.quote: Report agreed measures, actual values, calculation method, exclusions, incidents
issues.problem: No guidance on standard calculations (uptime net of maintenance windows, percentile vs mean response time), and no instruction to compute in the sandbox.
issues.fix: Compute attainment in bash_exec using the contract's own definition and exclusions, and show the formula next to the result.

issues.quote: Draft review questions or a meeting brief if asked.
issues.problem: No explicit approval gate before anything reaches the vendor, and no cadence by vendor tier or link back to the renewal decision.
issues.fix: State that vendor-facing drafts are held for owner approval. Offer a schedule_routine review cadence by tier (strategic quarterly, others annually) and feed results into contract-renewal-tracker.

scenarios.prompt: Run the Q3 review for our managed IT provider. Here's the SLA schedule, the ticket export and the three invoices.
scenarios.why: 'Build the period record' lists the right measures (response/resolution, exclusions, credits, invoice accuracy), and the MET/MISSED/DISPUTED/NOT MEASURED labels plus the action table give a usable scorecard. It would not check whether a service-credit claim window is about to close, and it forces exactly three strengths.

scenarios.prompt: Our logistics vendor keeps missing delivery dates and ops is furious, but there's no written SLA, just the PO. Build the case for next week's renewal meeting and draft the email to the vendor.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly yields NOT MEASURED, refuses to claim breach, and warns against turning complaints into trends. But it has no step to treat the missing SLA as a contract gap, to build a baseline from delivery records, or to propose measurable terms for the renewal. 'Draft review questions or a meeting brief if asked' doesn't cover the vendor email or its approval-before-send gate.

14:month-end-close-checklist.job: run month-end close and track readiness
14:month-end-close-checklist.summary: Orchestrates a small-business month-end close. A standard-library script enforces 21 levelled controls (sources S1-S6 plus controls 1-15) in dependency order and loads the sibling Mina skill that does each control. Approvals are tied to each file's SHA-256, prior open items carry forward, and the skill produces a close report and a masked review binder, never posting, locking or sending without the owner's yes.
strengths: Real enforcement, not prose: close_status.py refuses ready_for_review while a dependency is open. Approval needs a timestamped approving row whose SHA-256 matches the file as it is now, and reopening an upstream control resets everything downstream. All three scripts' selftests pass.

Small-business depth a hiring manager would recognise: processor clearing, Undeposited Funds and suspense, Opening Balance Equity, bills not yet received as accrual candidates, and the owner's sign-off on each reconciliation as the compensating control where duties cannot be separated (cited to COSO and ACFE). It also has qualitative materiality per SAB 99 and records the lock date only after review, so the accountant's adjustments still land in the open period.
Clear orchestrator boundary: it names the sibling skill that performs each control, loads it only when that control is reached, and brings back only a summary and file links.

Graceful degradation: a hand-tracked label if Python is missing, delivery of every file if the state volume fails, 'default - confirm with the owner' on calendar and thresholds, and stopping after two failures.

Carefully handled external side effects: a recipient-named yes before sending the binder, a note that workspace:// links cannot be opened by an outside accountant, and routine prompts that forbid external actions with grants_credentials set to false.
Reusable deliverables: a close report template, a status CSV, and a binder zip with index.md, a SHA-256 manifest, register rows cut to the period, and a refusal on any unmasked account number.
missing: Trial balance or balance sheet and GL export at cutoff as a named source, with each reconciliation tied back to it
Sales tax payable reconciled to the return or filing, and payroll liability accounts cleared to zero
Roll-forward schedules for prepaids, accruals and deferred revenue, and a fixed-asset register tie-out (at least listed for the accountant)
Inventory and cost-of-goods cutoff for product businesses, with a not_applicable path for service businesses
Explicit flux thresholds for control 8 (or a stated handoff of thresholds to the P&L skill)
Jurisdiction and ledger switch (US or UK; QuickBooks or Xero) for payroll-tax wording and the Undeposited Funds and OBE controls
Close retrospective: days to close and recurring blockers, fed into next month's calendar
Strict approving-reply rule: exact option match, conditional replies treated as not approved

issues.quote: and record the reply verbatim with `log_approval.py record`
issues.problem: log_approval.py treats any reply whose first word is approve, yes, signed off or reviewed as an approval (a prefix match). I recorded 'Reviewed - not approved, fix line 3' and it was logged as an APPROVAL, and close_status.py then accepts it. A conditional or negative reply can turn a period into approved, which breaks the skill's central prepared-versus-approved rule.
issues.fix: Count only an exact match to the ask_question option ('Approve exactly as shown'), or an allow-list of whole-reply matches. Drop 'reviewed' and bare 'yes' prefixes. Treat any reply with a qualifier (but, hold, until, not, except) as not an approval, and add a selftest for that case.

issues.quote: Sources S1-S6: statements, sales list, bills and receipts, payroll report,
issues.problem: The ledger itself is never a named input. There is no trial balance, balance sheet or GL export at cutoff, yet controls 8, 11 and 12 need ledger balances, and the worked example quietly cites a 'balance sheet export'. The report's statement-to-ledger control totals have no defined source.
issues.fix: Add S0 for a trial balance or balance sheet and GL export at cutoff, with a control total, as a Level 1 dependency of 1, 8, 11 and 12. Name it in the Inputs table with an ask-for-export fallback.

issues.quote: Dependencies: `references/close-dependency-map.md` (enforced by the script).
issues.problem: In close-controls.csv, control 8 (P&L review) depends on 1;2;3;7;10;11 but not on 5 (payroll tie-out) or 6 (loans and interest). The P&L can be marked ready_for_review while payroll, often the largest expense, is untied. Because 5 is not upstream of 8, a later payroll change never reopens the P&L review.
issues.fix: Add 5, 6 and 12 to control 8's depends_on, update the dependency map and the selftest, and re-check that the example fixture still reports the expected blockers.

issues.quote: --prior <state>/close/<prior>/status.csv
issues.problem: Step 1 always passes --prior, but close_status.py refuses ('file not found') when there is no prior status file, which is always the case on a first close. The Inputs table says 'First close: say so; carry nothing' but the command does not show that. When there is a prior file, init also marks every not-done prior control, including not_started ones and control 15, as a 'carried' blocker, which is noisy.
issues.fix: Show the first-close command without --prior, or make the script treat a missing prior file as a first close with a notice. Carry only blocked or in-progress rows with real blockers.

issues.quote: points to a recorded approving reply for each named file whose logged
issues.problem: Step 5 packs the script's refusal rules, control 14's special case and the reopen behaviour into one run-on sentence. With the inline schedule_followup, schedule_routine and send-email JSON in steps 3, 10 and 11, the body runs to about 200 lines when the procedure fits in about half that.
issues.fix: Move the script rules into a short table in references/controls-guide.md. Move the follow-up, routine and send recipes into a references/actions.md file. Keep SKILL.md at the decision level with one-line pointers.

issues.quote: Never suggest ordering payments ahead of payroll tax deposits.
issues.problem: The rationale is the US Trust Fund Recovery Penalty (IRS), but the skill applies it universally. The worked example is a UK Ltd reporting in GBP, and the supporting references are QuickBooks-specific (Undeposited Funds found by Detail type) with no Xero or UK note.
issues.fix: Keep the rule, since it is sound everywhere, but label the cited liability as US. Add a jurisdiction line from intake ('UK: PAYE/NIC arrears; route to the accountant'), and note that Xero has no Undeposited Funds or OBE, so those controls become not_applicable with a reason.

issues.quote: skill it names for that file; never hand-edit an approved file (its hash
issues.problem: SKILL.md says to re-run the producing skill. build_binder.py's refusal instead tells the model to hand-edit register rows and cites 'register.py', which this package does not ship (it lives in bookkeeping-exception-escalation).
issues.fix: Align the two. Say in SKILL.md that working registers get the offending field masked and approved outputs get re-run, and make the script name the escalation skill rather than register.py.

issues.quote: (late statement, refused shortcut)
issues.problem: The supporting files are inconsistent. ATTRIBUTION.md puts bills-not-yet-received at Level 3 and owner sign-off at Level 5, but the CSV and the map have 13 at Level 2 and 14 at Level 3. The worked example cites line 194 in one place and line 191 in another. The example status.csv is stamped 2026-09-27 while the narrative is set on 6 May. The example's schedule_followup call leaves out the session_id that step 3 says is required.
issues.fix: Reconcile the level numbers in ATTRIBUTION.md, align the example's dates and line references, and add session_id to the example call.

scenarios.prompt: Can you run the March close for Acme Coffee LLC? Chase and Amex statements, the Stripe payout report and the Gusto payroll register are uploaded. What's left before our accountant Priya can review?
scenarios.why: The steps are all present. Step 1 opens the close with close_status.py init. Step 2 ties to the prior period with a log_approval check. Step 3 compares list_workspace_files with the intake sources S1-S6. Step 4 works eligible controls in dependency order: statement-reconciliation for 1, 6 and 10, expense-categorization for 3, AR for 4, escalation for 11 and 12, and the P&L skill for 8. Step 5 records each change through the script, which refuses out-of-order readiness. Step 8 fills templates/close-report.md with the script's markdown table and critical path. Step 9 asks for approval on a hashed report, and step 10 builds a masked binder and waits for a yes that names the recipient before sending. One gap: controls 11 and 12 need a balance-sheet export that the inputs table never asks for, so the model has to improvise that request.

scenarios.prompt: First close with you. We're on Xero, so here's a trial balance export and the bank statement. Payroll hasn't come in yet. Jo already replied 'Reviewed - hold until Dev checks the Stripe fees'. Mark whatever you can as done and set the lock date for the 10th.
scenarios.why: Several parts go right. The lock request is correctly held until after the report is approved (step 9, control 15). The payroll source S4 is blocked with an owner. Undeposited Funds, which Xero does not have, can be marked not_applicable with a reason. Three parts go wrong. The step 1 command always passes --prior, and close_status.py refuses when that file is missing ('file not found'), so the model has to drop the flag on its own. The trial balance has no source slot among S1-S6. Most seriously, log_approval.py treats any reply starting with 'reviewed' or 'yes' as approving: I ran 'Reviewed - not approved, fix line 3' through it and it logged an APPROVAL. Jo's conditional reply could therefore satisfy the hash check and let a control be set to approved, which defeats the skill's own prepared-versus-approved rule.

better: Moves from a 51-line prose list to enforced dependency tracking. close_status.py refuses out-of-order readiness and reopens downstream work, where v1 only listed statuses.

Adds the controls v1 lacked and a small-business close needs: processor clearing, Undeposited Funds and suspense, Opening Balance Equity, bills not yet received, owner sign-off on each reconciliation, and a lock date recorded only after approval.
Turns v1's one-line 'preserve the approval record' into approvals bound to each file's SHA-256, so an edited file loses its approval.
Makes the deliverable concrete: v1 said 'return control totals...', and v2 has a close-report template, a status CSV and a masked binder with a manifest.
Routes each control to the sibling Mina skill that performs it, carries open items and exceptions from earlier periods, and offers follow-ups for late sources.
Makes the trigger usable: v1 had generic triggers ('month end', 'finance close'), and v2 adds natural-language triggers and scope exclusions against statement-reconciliation and the P&L skill.
Adds a worked example of the hardest real case: a late statement plus a request to skip ahead to the P&L.
worse: The body is about four times longer, with inline tool-call JSON, so it costs more context on every load.
A new failure mode that v1 did not have: the approval-prefix heuristic can record a conditional reply as an approval.
It is tightly coupled to the shared state layout and to sibling packages' file names (recs/*/workpaper.md, exceptions.csv), so a change in one kit skill can break the close.
The first-close command fails as written (--prior on a missing file), where v1 had no such trap.

contract-amendment-history.summary: Loads a base agreement and its amendments in chronological order, then produces either a chronological change summary with a net-current-state table or a quote-exact Was/Now trace of one provision to its current controlling language, with watch items; it is wrapped in Claude-for-Legal plugin scaffolding (practice-profile gate, ~/.claude paths, slash commands).
strengths: Clear two-mode design (whole-contract summary vs. single-provision trace) with mode-detection phrases, a map from common terms to provisions, and a single clarifying question only when the request is genuinely ambiguous.
The section-reference rule and the exact-quote Was/Now blocks let the reviewer check every finding against the source without searching.
Practical watch items: an amendment that modifies an already-deleted provision, a party name change without a formal assignment, section renumbering, and liability-cap carve-outs.

Ordering logic is sound: execution metadata first, then recitals ('This Amendment, dated as of...'), then cross-references to confirm the chain. It asks for confirmation only when order is truly unclear.
Guards against invention: 'If not stated, omit rather than guess' for amendment purpose; ambiguous language is quoted and flagged, not interpreted.
Scope limits fit Ellis's non-advisory boundary: it does not decide which document controls in a conflict, does not draft amendments, and does not apply the playbook.
missing: Handling of effective date vs. execution date, including retroactive and future-effective amendments
A rule that an amended-and-restated agreement or novation starts a new chain, plus coverage of SOWs, order forms, side letters and change orders that change terms
Extraction of each amendment's precedence and 'remainder unchanged' clauses
A check that each document was actually signed, and detection of gaps in amendment numbering
Tracking of amended definitions that ripple into other clauses
A visible document inventory for the reviewer to check
An optional consolidated 'as-amended' text with change markers, and export of changed key terms to Ellis's tracker
Alignment with Ellis's MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR labels (or an explicit statement that they do not apply here) and a handoff to counsel-escalation-brief
Use of AutoGPT's Drive/workspace blocks and the sandbox for text extraction, OCR and exact-quote checks, with upload or paste as the fallback

issues.quote: If setup is missing or contains placeholders, follow its original stop-and-setup rule; never fill legal positions or approvers with defaults.
issues.problem: The linked template says that if ~/.claude/plugins/config/claude-for-legal/commercial-legal/CLAUDE.md is missing or has placeholders, the model must STOP and tell the user to run /commercial-legal:cold-start-interview. On AutoGPT that file never exists and the command is never registered, so a faithful model refuses every request. This skill is purely historical and does not need a playbook, and the mandatory pre-read loads a 44 KB profile that is mostly irrelevant.
issues.fix: Delete the gate and the mandatory pre-read. Ask up front only for what this skill uses: the documents, the provision (optional), the user's role (lawyer or non-lawyer, for the output marking) and the counsel contact, via ask_question or memory_search. Then proceed.

issues.quote: Prepend the work-product header from `~/.claude/plugins/config/claude-for-legal/commercial-legal/CLAUDE.md` `## Outputs` to every output below
issues.problem: The file is not shipped (the header options sit in references/practice-profile-template.md under a different name), and the choice depends on a Role field that is never collected. Ellis is explicitly not a lawyer, so a model that defaults to 'ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT' would falsely claim a protection that does not apply.
issues.fix: State the marking inline: default to 'CONFIDENTIAL — CONTRACT RECORD SUMMARY — NOT LEGAL ADVICE — REVIEW WITH COUNSEL'. Add a privilege marking only when counsel directs the work, and keep the destination check (strip the marking or ask before anything goes outside legal).

issues.quote: Execution date
issues.problem: The index records only the execution date. It misses the effective date (amendments are often retroactive or take effect later), whether each document was actually signed, amended-and-restated agreements that replace the earlier chain, each amendment's 'remainder unchanged' and order-of-precedence clauses, amendments to defined terms that ripple into other clauses, and gaps in numbering (Amendment 1 and 3 present, 2 missing). Any of these can make 'Current controlling language' wrong.
issues.fix: Add index fields for effective date, execution status (signature blocks and counterparts), supersession (A&R or novation), precedence clause and defined terms changed. Add a rule that an A&R starts a new chain, and make unsigned documents and numbering gaps mandatory watch items.

issues.quote: drive the output — do not show it to the user.
issues.problem: Hiding the document index means the reviewer cannot see which files were read, how they were ordered, which dates were used, or that an amendment is missing or unsigned. That cuts against Ellis's source-cited record-keeping.
issues.fix: Put a short document inventory table at the top of both modes: document, source file, execution and effective dates, signed yes/no, sections modified, and ordering confidence.

issues.quote: Write outputs to the matter folder at `~/.claude/plugins/config/claude-for-legal/commercial-legal/matters/<matter-slug>/`.
issues.problem: This is Claude Code plugin state. The section also tells the user to run /commercial-legal:matter-workspace, and the Examples block uses /commercial-legal:amendment-history slash commands, none of which exist on AutoGPT.
issues.fix: Remove the Matter context section and the slash-command examples. If the user wants the output saved, save it with write_workspace_file to a named file (e.g. amendment-history-<counterparty>-<date>.md), and replace the examples with plain-language requests.

issues.quote: (routes to vendor-agreement-review)
issues.problem: The follow-ups route to vendor-agreement-review and stakeholder-summary, which are not in the catalog. The closing decision tree ('per CLAUDE.md ## Outputs') is a second, conflicting way to end, and its 'Escalate' branch points to an approver from a practice profile that does not exist.
issues.fix: Keep a single closing block that routes to Ellis's own skills: msa-playbook-review or nda-playbook-review for a playbook check of the amended agreement, counsel-escalation-brief for conflicts, and contract-key-term-extraction or contract-obligation-tracker to update the tracker.

issues.quote: From file upload, [CLM ID (coming soon)], or [repository link (coming soon)]. Accept multiple files in one invocation.
issues.problem: It advertises integrations that were never built and ignores what AutoGPT does have: Google Drive and Docs blocks, read_workspace_file, and bash_exec for OCR on scanned PDFs and for diffing text to confirm Was/Now quotes are exact.
issues.fix: List the real sources: upload or paste, workspace files, Google Drive via run_block, or a connected CLM through MCP if present. If the documents cannot be fetched, ask for an upload. Use the sandbox to extract text and to check that every quote matches the source exactly.

issues.quote: [Provision deleted] (§[X.X]): [what was removed and why it matters]
issues.problem: 'Why it matters' asks for a significance or risk judgment, which Ellis's boundary forbids ('describe the operational effect in neutral terms'). Other slots such as 'practical effect on the parties' are fine only if kept neutral.
issues.fix: Replace it with '[what was removed and the neutral operational effect, e.g. notice period no longer applies]'. Add a line saying the skill does not judge whether a change is favourable, standard or risky, and that any such question goes to counsel.

scenarios.prompt: Here are our 2022 MSA with Northwind and Amendments 1-3 (PDFs). What does termination for convenience say now, and how did it get there?
scenarios.why: Mode detection sends this straight to Mode 2 (provision trace). Ordering comes from the titles and the recitals, and the Was/Now exact-quote format with section references and a Current controlling language block would be a senior-quality trace. But the preamble requires reading the persistent profile at ~/.claude/plugins/config/..., which is never there on AutoGPT, and the template it links says STOP and run /commercial-legal:cold-start-interview. A literal model halts before doing any work. The privilege header and the closing decision tree also point to a CLAUDE.md that is not shipped, and the follow-ups route to vendor-agreement-review and stakeholder-summary, which do not exist.

scenarios.prompt: Pull the Acme contract set from our shared Drive folder: the 2021 MSA, the 2023 Amended and Restated MSA, an undated 'Amendment 1' scan with no signature page, and a side letter on SLA credits. What's the liability cap today, and did the side letter change it?
scenarios.why: Step 1 treats repository retrieval as 'coming soon' and never uses the available Google Drive block. It also gives no upload or paste fallback. Nothing says an amended-and-restated agreement replaces the earlier chain, so the trace can show 2021 language as 'Original' and the A&R as just another amendment. Step 2 records only the execution date, not the effective date or whether the document was signed, so the unsigned scan could be quoted as current controlling language. The ordering-confirmation rule does fire for the undated document (good), but side letters are missing from the document patterns, and the setup gate still blocks the run.

16:candidate-sourcing-strategy.job: source evidence-backed candidates for an open role
16:candidate-sourcing-strategy.summary: Runs a scripted sourcing batch: it loads the scorecard, shortlist and DNC list, builds variant X-ray, GitHub and benchmark-orbit queries, checks every evidence link once per person, dedupes and gates cards with bundled Python scripts, shows tiered evidence cards, adds names to the shortlist only after approval, and can produce a market read that uses posted pay only.
strengths: Deterministic gates turn 'no link, no card' into per-person verification: links.csv holds one row per person per URL, and card_check.py catches evidence borrowed from a co-author's repo. I ran the worked example (batch-raw.json plus links-verified.csv) and it reproduces the documented dedupe and gate output exactly.
DNC handling is careful: token-subset and fuzzy matching lean toward excluding, the DNC count is reported but never the names, and an unattended routine run holds the batch when dnc.csv is missing.

The legal grounding is current and specific: GINA treats a search as a 'request', UK ICO sets retention limits for re-engaging past candidates, and the OFCCP search-log duty carries its 2026-10-26 rescission date. Legal items are dated, with a note to confirm with counsel.

Query craft is senior-level: three variants per must-have, including a Cathey 'dark matter' variant and a venue variant. Recruiter Boolean rules and export limits are covered. The GitHub table separates real signal (merged third-party PRs, release credits) from vanity signal (stars, followers).
A calibration loop is built in: three passes for the same reason trigger a proposed scorecard change, routed through role-intake-and-scorecard and applied only on a yes.
The market read refuses to estimate bands. posted_pay.py separates funding and OTE figures from base pay, flags implausible rows, and computes no average.

Scope boundaries against sibling skills (outreach, screening, intake) are explicit, and the persona's platform tools are used correctly: run_capability connect_integration, web_search deep flag, the ~/skills/<slug> package dir and the ~/workspace durable volume.
missing: A sanctioned path to turn owner-supplied exports or ATS rows into verifiable cards (the evidence-source type and how it is labelled).
A fallback for when the Task sub-agent tool is unavailable (run clusters one after another, or use run_sub_session).
Use of the platform's people-search blocks (Apollo, Exa, Enrichlayer) with contact-field stripping, especially for non-engineering roles.
Handling benchmark B-ids when the scorecard has none (write them back with approval, or relax the id check).
A talent-map deliverable: target companies mapped to teams and likely seniority bands, reused across batches rather than rebuilt per batch.
Incremental gating so 'show names early' is compatible with the verify, dedupe and gate pipeline.
A way to pull a DNC or pipeline list held in a connected Google Sheet or ATS into the expected CSV before dedupe runs.
Guidance for a slate built entirely from one channel or company type, e.g. widen channels and communities without using protected attributes.

issues.quote: If a site blocks you, name it and ask for an export or a few
issues.problem: The skill asks owners for LinkedIn Recruiter or ATS exports in several places, but gives no way to turn an export row into verified evidence. Export URLs are login-walled, and links.csv or card_check only accept fetched pages, so every export-sourced candidate is dropped as 'could not verify'. The 'owner-export' channel in append_rows.py can never produce a card.
issues.fix: Add a sanctioned evidence type for owner-supplied data, e.g. a links.csv status 'owner-supplied' naming the file, which card_check accepts and labels as 'from your export, not publicly verified'. Or tell the model to find one public link per export row before carding it.

issues.quote: Run up to 3 `Task` sub-agents at once, each with
issues.problem: Task is an SDK-only built-in. The platform's baseline mode has no Task tool (the backend points to run_sub_session instead). The hedge only covers 'sub-agent returned no queries', not the tool being absent, so a baseline session is left with an instruction it cannot follow.
issues.fix: Add: 'If no sub-agent tool is available, run the clusters one after another yourself with the same subtask rules.' Optionally name run_sub_session as the platform-native option.

issues.quote: person the bar (the scorecard's B-ids, if intake listed them), ignoring
issues.problem: When intake did not list B-ids, the model makes up B1-B6 for the benchmark traits. Step 6 always passes --scorecard, and card_check's must_ids() removes any evidence line whose id is not on the scorecard. Benchmark-search cards therefore lose their evidence or are dropped with 'cite ids not on the scorecard'.
issues.fix: When the scorecard has no B-ids, append the agreed traits as '- B<n>: ...' under a '## Benchmark' heading in the scorecard (with the owner's yes), or have step 6 omit --scorecard for a benchmark-only batch and say so in the header.

issues.quote: `web_search` quick mode (`deep=true` only for an explicit
issues.problem: For non-engineering roles, discovery rests entirely on web_search (a Perplexity sonar answer engine that may ignore X-ray operators) plus web_fetch. The skill ignores the platform's people-search blocks (Apollo, Exa, Enrichlayer) and any connected ATS, which a senior sourcer on this platform would use to list candidates.
issues.fix: Add an optional branch: if Apollo, Exa or Enrichlayer blocks are available, use them to list candidates by title and company. Strip any email or phone fields, and still require a public evidence URL checked per person before a card is made.

issues.quote: Get the first cards up quickly and keep adding; a
issues.problem: This conflicts with steps 5-6, which require every link fetched plus dedupe and card_check before any card is shown. The skill never says to gate in small increments, so the model either waits for the full batch or shows ungated cards. The persona promises something inside a minute.
issues.fix: State that the verify, dedupe and gate steps run on each group of 3-5 cards as soon as it is ready, and only gated cards are shown.

issues.quote: drops exact duplicates (name plus company after normalising case,
issues.problem: The nickname union-find in dedupe_names.py merges 'Christina' and 'Christopher' (both map to 'chris') and 'Alexandra' and 'Alexander' (both to 'alec'). I tested it: two different people at the same company are dropped as an exact duplicate rather than held on 'check these'. The docstring claims over-grouping only makes flagging more likely.
issues.fix: Treat a match that only succeeds through the nickname table as a CHECK THESE hold, not an EXACT drop, or stop cross-gender groups from merging in the nickname table.

issues.quote: Its word lists also over-catch: a card
issues.problem: In testing, card_check also over-catches outside protected wording: ', 16' in 'PostgreSQL 15, 16' reads as an age, 'payments veteran' as veteran status, 'MIT-licensed' as pedigree, and 'the next role' in a gap line as intent. The skill sanctions a rephrase-and-rerun only for protected-wording hits, so intent and pedigree false positives have no documented path.
issues.fix: Widen the rephrase rule to intent and pedigree false positives, with the same rule against adding or removing anything about the person. Tighten the regexes: skip ', NN' after version words, and match 'MIT' only as a school.

issues.quote: then read the matched text of every row and drop any that is not pay (a
issues.problem: Step 10 packs the whole market read, including posted_pay.py internals, into one run-on step. The same rules also appear across Guardrails, Output contract, Quality self-check, checklists/batch-run.md and references/sourcing-guardrails.md, which makes the 254-line body heavy to load and hard to follow.
issues.fix: Move the market-read procedure into a references/market-read.md next to the template. Keep one Guardrails list, point the self-check at the checklist, and cut step 6 down to commands plus one line about script limits.

scenarios.prompt: The Senior Backend Engineer scorecard is approved and GitHub is connected. Source me 10 names from fintechs this week, deduped against the pipeline.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-9 cover this end to end. The batch target comes from preferences. Pattern search runs 3+ variants per must-have, including a dark-matter variant, with a 15-query cap, and each query is logged via append_rows.py. The gh commands in references/github-sourcing.md find real work. links.csv records one row per person per URL. dedupe_names.py catches Bob/Robert and Inc/GmbH and drops DNC by count. card_check.py drops borrowed links, pedigree reasons and unquoted intent. Cards follow templates/card.md, and the shortlist is written only on a yes. One small snag: evidence text such as 'PostgreSQL 15, 16' trips the age regex (I tested it). The step-6 rephrase path covers this.

scenarios.prompt: No scorecard yet. Find me five more people like Priya Nair, our best PM. I've uploaded a LinkedIn Recruiter CSV of 40 profiles, and our do-not-contact list is a Google Sheet, not dnc.csv.
scenarios.why: The good parts hold: the batch is labelled uncalibrated, the benchmark traits ignore school and brand, and the orbit search comes first. Then it stalls on three gaps. (1) Recruiter export rows carry only login-walled URLs, so card_check drops every one as 'could not verify'. The skill keeps asking for exports but never says how an owner-supplied row becomes verifiable evidence. (2) The model invents B1-B4 for Priya's traits, but step 6 always passes --scorecard, and must_ids() removes ids the scorecard lacks, so benchmark evidence is stripped or cards are dropped. (3) dedupe reports DNC under files_missing. The skill never says to pull the Sheet via run_block into dnc.csv, so it only writes a header note. A PM role also has no GitHub path, and web_search (Perplexity sonar) finds people poorly.

better: Prose rules become enforced gates: card_check.py checks each evidence link for the named person, catches borrowed links, refuses 'unranked' tiers, pedigree reasons and unquoted intent, and caps a thin card below strong. v1 only said 'no working source link, no card'.
Deterministic dedupe (nicknames, accents, company suffixes, token-subset DNC matching) with a 'check these' hold and count-only DNC reporting. v1 described the matching rule but had no tool.
New handling for unattended routine runs: the weekly batch size is split per run, re-engagements are skipped when retention_policy is UNSET, and the batch is held when DNC is missing.
Adds retention and GINA legal grounding with dated sources. Re-engaging near-misses is now limited to what the retention policy allows, which v1 encouraged without any limit.
Query craft, Recruiter Boolean and GitHub evidence references, plus a per-query search log (searches.csv) and dark-matter variants.
The market read gains posted_pay.py, with funding and OTE separation and no averages, and a template. v1 only said 'only figures printed in postings'.
A defined output contract, card, JSON, links and market-read templates, and a worked example with hard cases that reproduces exactly when run.
Explicit use and do-not-use boundaries and a Siblings section, so it triggers more cleanly than v1.
worse: The SKILL.md body roughly doubles, from 122 to 254 lines, with run-on steps and guardrails restated in four or five places, making each load heavier than v1's compact prose.
Introduces a dependency on the SDK-only Task tool with no fallback for when it is absent.
The owner-export route is requested repeatedly but cannot pass the new link gate, a dead end v1 did not have (v1 would have used the export informally).
Benchmark search, which v1 handled in prose, can now lose all its evidence to the scorecard id check when B-ids were never written down.
The new nickname grouping can drop a different person at the same company as an exact duplicate (Christina and Christopher Lee), a failure mode v1's 'never merge on a guess' did not have in practice.
The regex gates add false positives on ordinary engineering text (version lists, 'veteran', 'MIT-licensed'), which v1 did not have.
v1's concrete 'first cards within about a minute' became 'quickly', and cards now wait on the full verify, dedupe and gate chain.
The worked example tells the reader which batch card was the DNC entry ('a DNC entry "Marta Silva"'), modelling the leak the guardrail forbids.

negotiation.job: prepare negotiation strategy and talk tracks
negotiation.summary: A summary of Chris Voss's 'Never Split the Difference' toolkit (mirroring, labeling, calibrated questions, accusation audit, Ackerman bargaining, Black Swans) with copy patterns, a self-scoring rubric and a 21-technique reference. It has no intake, no ordered prep procedure, no reusable deliverable and no guardrails.
strengths: Faithful, well-organised coverage of the Voss toolkit, with concrete copy patterns for mirroring, labeling, calibrated questions and the accusation audit that a user can lift directly.
Good progressive-disclosure pointers: each section names the exact references/techniques.md section to open, and when (for example sections 16, 20 and 21 when a hidden decision-maker is suspected).
The Common Mistakes and Handling Common Situations tables give crisp counters, such as answering an extreme anchor with 'How did you arrive at that figure?' and handling 'That's not fair'.
The Quick Diagnostic table works as a pre-meeting checklist (accusation audit, 3-5 calibrated questions, BATNA, counterpart style, Black Swan hunt).
MIT licence with upstream commit provenance; the only file it links to, references/techniques.md, is shipped.
missing: An intake step: parties, issues on the table, target, reservation point, BATNA, deadline or notice dates, authority to concede, relationship stakes, channel
BATNA improvement, counterpart-BATNA and ZOPA estimation, and multi-issue packaging (MESOs, logrolling) with a give-get concession log
A reusable Negotiation One Sheet / prep brief template saved to the workspace
A benchmark research step (market comp, vendor pricing) using web_search, with every number labeled sourced or assumed
Side-aware anchoring (buyer vs seller) and sandbox arithmetic for the concession schedule, including percentage-uplift cases
Written and email negotiation guidance, with drafts approved before any send
Guardrails: authority limits, no deception or misrepresentation, escalation to counsel/HR/finance, and awareness of pay-transparency and salary-history laws
Contract-term awareness for vendor and renewal cases (auto-renewal notice windows, price-increase caps, term length)
Multi-round memory: memory_store for counterpart profile, concessions made and commitments, plus a post-round debrief
Handoff boundaries to teammates (Max for sales deals, Jordan for renewals, Vera for vendors, counsel for clauses)
Worked examples or evals demonstrating a full prep for a salary case and a vendor case

issues.quote: Target $120K: open at $78K, move to $102K, $114K, final $120,350 + extra PTO
issues.problem: Ackerman is a buyer's concession schedule, but this row applies it to 'Salary negotiation … counter-offers'. A candidate who follows it opens 35% below their own target. Nowhere does the skill say which side the user is on, even though 'salary negotiation' and 'how do I ask for a raise' are headline triggers.
issues.fix: Make anchoring side-aware: buyers ascend from below target and sellers or candidates descend from a justified anchor above target. Replace the salary row with a candidate example anchored on sourced market comp. Compute the schedule in bash_exec from the user's stated target and reservation point.

issues.quote: Send "Have you given up on [the project]?" -- triggers a "No" response
issues.problem: This tells the model to send an outward message with no draft or approval step, and the skill has no guardrails anywhere. It sets no authority or concession limits, no ban on misrepresenting a BATNA or material facts (its 'tactical mislabeling' deliberately states something false), no escalation of contract clauses to counsel or of offers to HR/finance, and no note on pay-transparency or salary-history rules.
issues.fix: Add a Guardrails section. Draft every counterpart message for user approval, confirm what the user is authorised to concede, never state false facts or invented alternatives, label every number as sourced or assumed, and escalate legal terms to counsel and discounts or comp to the approver or teammate named.

issues.problem: There are no inputs named up front and no ordered procedure: eight technique essays with no decision points on what to do first or which technique fits the situation. The model is never told to gather the parties, issues, target, reservation point, BATNA, deadline, authority, relationship or channel.
issues.fix: Open with an intake (ask_question for the missing items), then ordered steps: interests and BATNA → benchmark research → counterpart profile and style → anchor and concession plan → accusation audit, labels and calibrated questions → draft opening message or script → rehearsal → post-round debrief.

issues.quote: Always state the current score and the specific gaps to reach 10/10.
issues.problem: The only defined output is a self-score, and most of its points depend on live events the agent cannot observe during prep ('That's right' achieved, emotions labeled out loud). No reusable prep artefact is defined, not even Voss's own Negotiation One Sheet.
issues.fix: Replace the score with a one-sheet template saved via write_workspace_file: goal/target, reservation point and BATNA, anchor with justification, give-get concession ladder, non-cash tradeables, accusation audit, 3-5 labels, 3-5 calibrated questions, Black Swan hypotheses, open questions. Use the Quick Diagnostic as its QA check.

issues.quote: Define your walk-away point before negotiating
issues.problem: The description advertises BATNA and anchoring, but BATNA gets one diagnostic row. The skill never covers improving the BATNA, estimating the counterpart's BATNA or the ZOPA, setting a reservation price, trading across multiple issues (logrolling, MESOs) or logging concessions. 'No deal is better than a bad deal' is stated as dogma instead of being tested against the BATNA.
issues.fix: Add a short interests/BATNA/ZOPA section (Fisher-Ury), multi-issue packaging and a give-get log, and move the Voss tactics under it as the execution layer.

issues.quote: Use when the user mentions "salary negotiation", "contract terms", "handling objections", "mirroring and labeling", "difficult conversation"
issues.problem: The triggers are very broad and overlap objection-and-negotiation (Max: 'objection handling', 'negotiation'), renewal-negotiation-brief (Jordan) and employment-offer-drafting. The skill is assigned to no expert, and the description points to 'influence-psychology', which the catalog does not ship.
issues.fix: Scope the description to general negotiation prep outside sales deals (raises and offers, vendor purchasing, partner terms). Name the sibling skills for sales objections and renewals, remove the influence-psychology pointer, and assign it to an expert or merge it.

issues.quote: 7% words, 38% tone, 55% body language
issues.problem: The Mehrabian 7-38-55 figures are misapplied as a general rule. The section is also written for in-person delivery (DJ voice, 4-second pauses, body language) when the agent's real channel is prep and written messages, and the skill has no email or written-negotiation guidance.
issues.fix: Drop the statistic. Recast voice and silence advice as coaching notes for the user, and add a written-channel section: short emails, labels in writing, no-oriented subject lines, one ask per message, pacing replies.

issues.quote: dp/0062407805?tag=wondelai00-20
issues.problem: Amazon affiliate links and an author bio are filler, and the affiliate links are vendor promotion inside a product skill. Throughout, 'Product applications' tables (user interviews, churn, support) pad the body with non-negotiation uses, and about half of SKILL.md repeats references/techniques.md almost word for word.
issues.fix: Delete Further Reading and About the Author. Cut the product-application tables. Keep technique detail only in the reference, leaving SKILL.md as procedure, one-sheet and routing.

scenarios.prompt: I got an offer for a Senior PM role: $148K base and 0.1% equity. I want closer to $170K. Help me plan Thursday's recruiter call and draft what I'll say.
scenarios.why: Framework sections 1-6 give usable labels, calibrated questions ('How am I supposed to do that?') and an accusation audit, and the Quick Diagnostic reminds the model about BATNA. But the skill never asks for inputs (competing offers, total comp, flexibility on equity or sign-on) and has no step to research comp benchmarks with web_search. Its only salary guidance is the buyer-side Ackerman row ('Target $120K: open at $78K'), which would have the candidate anchor below their own target if followed literally. The deliverable is a 10/10 self-score, not a call plan. The scripts are good but the number strategy is weak and possibly harmful.

scenarios.prompt: Our main data vendor sent a renewal at +22%. It auto-renews in 9 days, they won't give me usage exports, and finance caps us at +5%. Plan the negotiation and draft my reply to their account exec.
scenarios.why: Nothing in the skill covers contract notice dates or protecting the BATNA before the auto-renewal window closes (a notice of intent not to auto-renew, or a request for an extension). Ackerman assumes an absolute price target and does not map to a percentage-uplift cap. There is no multi-issue trade (term length, caps on future increases, volume tiers, payment terms), no escalation to procurement or counsel, and no draft-and-approve step before the email goes out. A model following it would write a warm, Voss-style email and miss the time-critical protective moves a senior procurement lead would make first.

source-and-qualify-partners.job: build and qualify partner prospect shortlist
source-and-qualify-partners.summary: A 62-line SKILL.md with no supporting files. It builds a cited long list of partner firms, scores each on fit, evidence and access, tags warm versus cold, runs a qualification scorecard on the top tier and records kill decisions.
strengths: The rule that evidence decides is clear: 'A firm with no evidence line is a research task, not a list row.'
Kill criteria kill one pursuit, not the whole list, and each kill is written down with its reason.
The fit/evidence/access axes and the warm-versus-cold tag line up with the persona and with partner-first-touch-outreach downstream.
The Fallbacks refuse to pad a thin list and keep UNKNOWNs visible.
missing: A scoring rubric with anchors and weights
A shortlist template with fixed columns
Partner-side value proposition and capacity/capability checks
A check on alliances with our competitors
Tool routing: memory_search for the ICP, web_search/Exa/Apollo/Enrichlayer, HubSpot via run_block, bash_exec for scoring
Data-sharing/NDA gate before any account mapping
Handoff to partner-first-touch-outreach for the first move
A dated log of scores, which the persona promises
A worked example

issues.quote: Fit is not the same as qualified. Grade inbound referrals on BANT —
issues.problem: BANT qualifies customer deals, not partners. Here it blurs referred customer leads with partner candidates. Partner qualification needs partner-side criteria: capacity (practice size, certified staff), commitment (executive sponsor, willingness to certify), compatibility (competing vendor alliances), and the partner's own economics.
issues.fix: Replace BANT with a partner-qualification checklist (capacity, capability, commitment, conflict, economics for the partner) and send inbound customer referrals to run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence registration rules.

issues.section: Map accounts before you list firms
issues.quote: Pull account and contact overlaps against partner-side records wherever
issues.problem: Net-new prospects have no partner-side records until a conversation and data-sharing arrangement exist. The line also mixes up ranking accounts with ranking partner firms. And sharing account or contact lists with a prospect needs an NDA or data-sharing terms, which the skill never mentions.
issues.fix: Reorder: build the long list first and estimate overlap from public proxies (case studies, customer logos, integration listings). Keep true account mapping (CSV exchange or an account-mapping tool) for prospects in active talks, and only after the owner approves the data-sharing terms.

issues.quote: Score every candidate on three axes: fit against the profile, evidence
issues.problem: No scale, anchors, weights or cut-off are given, so two runs on the same data can rank differently and 'top tier' is undefined.
issues.fix: Define 1-5 anchors per axis, the weights (for example fit 0.5, evidence 0.3, access 0.2), a qualification threshold and a tie-breaker, and compute scores in bash_exec.

issues.quote: The ranked, scored shortlist with its evidence, the kill decisions named,
issues.problem: The deliverable has no column schema or template, so it can't be reused or diffed across runs and the dated score log the persona promises has nothing to hold.
issues.fix: Ship templates/partner-shortlist.csv (firm, type, tier, fit/evidence/access scores, evidence URL, label, warm path, kill reason, first move, date) and log each run to memory or a workspace file.

issues.quote: saved partner ICP (or a rough motion), the target count, the geographies
issues.problem: No tools are named. The model isn't told to memory_search for the ICP that define-the-partner-icp saved, to use web_search/Exa/Apollo/Enrichlayer for enrichment, or to use HubSpot via run_block for the already-touched check, and there's no CSV fallback.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Where the inputs come from' block naming each tool, with a fallback of asking for a CRM export.

issues.quote: No profile on file means you draft one
issues.problem: It drafts the ICP inline instead of routing to define-the-partner-icp, so profiles drift apart. That is the drift define-the-partner-icp's shared saved profile is meant to prevent.
issues.fix: Route to define-the-partner-icp (or run its five blocks) and save the result before scoring.

issues.quote: lead partner-qualified (net-new, no introduction yet) or
issues.problem: 'Partner-qualified' usually means a lead the partner qualified. Using it for 'cold prospect' will clash with the pipeline vocabulary in track-partner-pipeline.
issues.fix: Rename the tags cold / warm-path and keep partner-sourced/influenced terms for pipeline.

issues.quote: Rank them, and tier past roughly twenty-five names so the
issues.problem: It's unclear whether this means tiering only when there are more than 25 names or cutting at 25, and there's no default target count when the user gives none.
issues.fix: State the rule plainly (for example: top 10 = Tier 1, next 15 = Tier 2, rest parked) and a default target count.

scenarios.prompt: We sell SOC 2 compliance automation to mid-market SaaS. Find me 20 North American MSPs or vCISO firms that could resell or refer us, ranked, with a go/no-go on the top five.
scenarios.why: The model would build a cited long list, score fit/evidence/access, tier it, and qualify the top tier against the scorecard (audience overlap, complementary offer, no fatal conflict, champion), then give one first move per firm. That is a reasonable list. But no score scale or weights are defined, so the ranking can't be reproduced. The top five get a BANT grade, which does not apply to a partner. Nothing checks partner capacity: security-practice size, existing Vanta/Drata alliances, what the partner gains. A senior partner manager would weigh all of those.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV of 140 agencies from a conference attendee list, half with no website. We've never written down a partner profile, and three of these are already our customers. Tell me which to chase and kill the rest.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks tell the model to draft a profile first, and thin data leaves UNKNOWNs visible, which is good. But it drafts the ICP inline instead of routing to define-the-partner-icp. Nothing says to dedupe and score 140 rows in bash_exec. The customer-as-partner conflict is not addressed. 'Map accounts before you list firms' can't run with no partner-side records. And the 'tier past roughly twenty-five' rule gives no cut line for 140 rows.

source-partners-via-investor-ecosystems.summary: A 55-line SKILL.md with no supporting files. It sketches four steps for sourcing through VCs, PE firms and accelerators: an investor map ranked by portfolio fit times reachability, a per-portfolio commercial play, a startup intake-to-convert-or-park pipeline, and a monthly per-portfolio report.
strengths: Warm paths must be evidenced, never invented, and 'No path means research, not outreach' is a good gate.
Parked startups get a revisit trigger, which avoids silent drop-off.
Outreach to firms, founders and portfolio companies is explicitly held for the owner's yes.
Report numbers must name the portfolio and the window before the count.
missing: Offer design for the investor or VC platform team (portfolio perk program)
A startup evaluation rubric and a convert/park threshold
NDA, confidentiality and IP-contamination intake policy
Boundaries with drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments and scope-the-tech-partnership
Attribution rules for portfolio referrals
Templates for the investor map, startup pipeline and monthly report
Tool routing and data sources for portfolios
Gate on pilot/POC resource commitments

issues.quote: Intake, technical fit check, evaluation, and the convert-or-park call
issues.problem: No evaluation criteria, scale or gate are defined (problem fit, integration effort, security/compliance posture, runway, customer references, dependency risk), so 'technical fit check' means whatever the model improvises.
issues.fix: Add a startup evaluation scorecard with anchors and a convert/park/decline threshold, and route converts to scope-the-tech-partnership.

issues.problem: Nothing covers confidentiality or IP when taking startup materials. Evaluating a startup whose product overlaps the internal roadmap invites trade-secret or IP-contamination claims.
issues.fix: Add an intake gate: no confidential materials without an owner-approved NDA posture, flag roadmap overlap to Legal before evaluation, and log what was received.

issues.quote: A commercial target per portfolio — referrals, sourced pipeline,
issues.problem: There is no value exchange for the investor (portfolio perk or discount, founder education, deal flow) and no VC platform team persona, so the 'play' has no offer and targets have no basis.
issues.fix: Add an offer-design step naming the platform-team contact, the perk or offer, the owner-approved discount band, and how targets are set from portfolio size and fit rate.

issues.quote: Use this when the sourcing motion runs through investors and startups.
issues.problem: Two jobs are combined: investors as a channel to portfolio companies, and startups as technology partners. The scope is also fuzzy against partner-first-touch-outreach (shared investors as a warm path) and drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments.
issues.fix: Split or clearly scope the two motions. State the boundary: equity or investment asks go to alliance M&A, integration builds go to tech scoping.

issues.quote: No outreach to a firm, a founder, or a portfolio company goes out without
issues.problem: The gate covers messages only. It does not cover signing NDAs, committing pilot or POC resources or spend, portfolio discounts, or anything touching investment, all of which the persona says need the owner's yes.
issues.fix: Extend the gate to NDAs, pilot/POC commitments, portfolio perk pricing, and any equity conversation (Legal and Finance).

issues.quote: Rank by portfolio fit multiplied by reachability. No path means research,
issues.problem: Neither factor has a scale, so the product can't be reproduced.
issues.fix: Define 1-5 anchors for fit (thesis match, count of portfolio companies in the ICP) and reachability (warm path strength) and compute in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Introductions made, evaluations opened, referrals converted, and pipeline
issues.problem: 'Pipeline sourced' ignores the sourced/influenced proof rules in track-partner-pipeline, and a monthly report is promised with no routine or stored log to compare against.
issues.fix: Apply track-partner-pipeline's attribution rules, store each month's snapshot, and offer schedule_routine behind the owner's yes.

issues.quote: No portfolio data means building the map from owner knowledge marked
issues.problem: It says enrichment is 'the first action' but names no tool (web_search/web_fetch on fund portfolio pages, Exa/Perplexity blocks, or asking for a Crunchbase export).
issues.fix: Name the tools and the fallback to asking for an export.

scenarios.prompt: We want to become a preferred vendor across the portfolios of five Series A/B dev-tools VCs. Build the investor map and the play for each.
scenarios.why: The model would list firms, theses and warm paths (no invented ties), rank by fit × reachability, and draft intro asks held for approval. But the skill never mentions the VC platform team as the gatekeeper or the offer that makes a portfolio play work (a portfolio perk or discount, founder content, deal flow for the fund). The per-portfolio targets are taken as inputs with no help setting them. The result is a contact plan, not a senior playbook.

scenarios.prompt: A corporate VC arm just sent 12 accelerator startups for us to evaluate as integration partners. Two decks are marked confidential, one startup overlaps a feature we're building, and the CVC wants a monthly report. We have no evaluation criteria.
scenarios.why: 'Run the startup pipeline' says only 'Intake, technical fit check, evaluation, and the convert-or-park call'. There are no criteria, no NDA or IP-contamination guidance for confidential decks from a startup that overlaps the roadmap, no escalation to Legal, and no route to scope-the-tech-partnership. The monthly report has no attribution rules. A model following this would improvise the most legally sensitive part.

structure-the-partner-agreement.summary: A 71-line SKILL.md with no supporting files. It picks one of four partner models (referral, reseller, co-sell, MSP/SI) with the reasoning and the ruled-out option, drafts a one-page term sheet in a fixed section order with default deal-registration mechanics, routes it to named internal approvers, and logs the version.
strengths: The four-model framing requires stating which model was ruled out, and a mixed motion gets one lead model plus named add-ons, never a blend.
The term sheet has a fixed section order and includes who owns the customer relationship, which is often forgotten.
Money checks are strong: exclusivity, revenue share and spend need the owner's yes in the same conversation, and every commercial number stays 'awaiting Finance' without a shell.
Registration mechanics are concrete (2-business-day SLA, 90-day protection, a single 30-day renewal) with pre-written edge rulings.
missing: A legal checklist per model (confidentiality, IP/trademark, DPA/BAA, liability, anti-bribery, non-solicit)
Money mechanics: fee basis, duration, clawback, cash-received trigger, minimums
A path for reviewing and redlining the partner's paper
Exclusivity counter-structures
Handoff to model-the-partnership-commercials for bands
Term sheet template file
A named storage tool for the version log
Routing for regulated motions

issues.quote: One page, in this order: parties and scope; the money (fees, margins,
issues.problem: Legal and compliance terms are missing: confidentiality, trademark/co-branding licence, data protection role (DPA, or BAA when the partner touches customer data), liability and indemnity, anti-bribery for referral fees paid to third parties, non-solicit, and IP ownership of SI deliverables.
issues.fix: Add a per-model legal checklist that pre-populates the 'open items for Legal' line, flagging regulated data and routing it to run-regulated-partnership-motions.

issues.quote: revenue share, payment triggers); term and renewal; exit and termination;
issues.problem: The money block is thin. It omits the fee basis (first-year ACV or recurring), duration and cap, payment on customer cash received, clawback on refund or churn, minimum commitments for resellers, and the rule that payouts follow sourced attribution proof.
issues.fix: Expand the money line with these fields and hand the numbers to model-the-partnership-commercials for bands before Finance review.

issues.quote: Non-exclusive by default. Exclusivity is a red flag that needs the
issues.problem: The gate is right, but no alternatives are offered, so the owner can't decide well when a strategic partner insists.
issues.fix: Add standard counter-structures (time-boxed, segment or geo-limited, performance minimums with automatic fall-away, right of first refusal) for the owner to choose from.

issues.quote: the same defaults the program design and the channel operations use, so
issues.problem: This isn't quite true. design-the-partner-program and scale-the-partner-channel say 'renewable on activity' without the one-30-day-with-sign-off limit, and unlike run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence there's no rule that published program rules win.
issues.fix: Point to one source of the defaults and add 'where the program's published rules differ, they win — cite them.'

issues.quote: term and geography needs, and any standard shells already on file.
issues.problem: It assumes we draft on our own paper. There is no branch for reviewing and redlining the partner's paper, which is common with SIs and large resellers.
issues.fix: Add a 'their paper' path: extract terms into the same one-page structure, mark deviations from our defaults, and route them to Legal.

issues.quote: Write the draft down with its date and version, so renewals and redlines
issues.problem: No storage location or tool is named, and no term-sheet template ships, so logging and 'standard shells on file' depend on the model guessing.
issues.fix: Name write_workspace_file or Google Drive via run_block plus memory_store for the version index, and ship templates/term-sheet.md.

issues.quote: Four models cover almost everything:
issues.problem: OEM/embed, marketplace resale and technology/integration partnerships aren't named or routed, so those requests get forced into the wrong model.
issues.fix: Add one line routing OEM to run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships, marketplace to run-hyperscaler-marketplace-co-sell, and integrations to scope-the-tech-partnership.

scenarios.prompt: Acme Consulting wants to resell us in DACH at a 30% margin with deal registration. Draft the term sheet and tell me who needs to sign off.
scenarios.why: The model picks reseller and rules out referral, fills the term sheet in the fixed order (parties and scope, money at 30% marked awaiting Finance, term, exit, customer ownership, registration block with SLA and 90-day window, open items), defaults to non-exclusive, names Legal and Finance with owners and dates, and logs v1. The result is usable. It would still miss the GDPR processor role and governing law unless the model adds them unprompted.

scenarios.prompt: A large SI wants two-year healthcare exclusivity, a 25% recurring revenue share on anything they touch, and to use their own paper. Finance hasn't set a margin floor, we have no standard shell, and they'll handle PHI during implementation.
scenarios.why: Exclusivity is flagged for the owner, numbers are marked awaiting Finance, and the draft is staged behind Legal. All correct. But there's no guidance on reviewing the partner's paper as opposed to drafting ours. Nothing prompts a BAA or data-protection terms for PHI, or routing to run-regulated-partnership-motions. 'Anything they touch' is not tied to sourced-only attribution proof. And there are no counter-structures for exclusivity (time-boxed, segment-limited, performance minimums), so the owner gets a red flag with no options.

track-partner-pipeline.summary: A 70-line SKILL.md with no supporting files. It splits partner deals into sourced or influenced, each with a named proof, and puts unproven deals on their own list. It runs sourced coverage against target (flag below 3x, alarm below 2x), forecast grades, hygiene flags and with/without-partner velocity, drafts a half-page leadership report, and saves a dated snapshot.
strengths: 'Two buckets, never both' with proof per deal and credit split across partners, never across buckets, matches mature partner-attribution practice.
The unproven list, with the one record that would prove each deal, keeps the headline honest.
Declined introductions are logged as evidence.
The leadership report has a tight defined shape (totals plus unattributed, movement, top three partners, top three risks, leading indicators, one ask).
The Fallbacks mark coverage UNKNOWN instead of computing it on guesses.
missing: A precise coverage formula and window definition
A default split rule for competing partner claims
Reconciliation of partner-reported numbers with ours
An attribution claim window
Forecast grade definitions
CRM field mapping and a schema check
An explicit no-CRM-writes gate
A report template and example
Tool routing and snapshot storage

issues.quote: Sourced coverage against target, with a flag below 3x and an alarm below
issues.problem: Coverage is undefined: which pipeline (open, with close dates in the window, which stages) against which target (full or remaining after closed-won). The 3x/2x thresholds can swing by a factor of two depending on the choice.
issues.fix: Define coverage as open sourced pipeline with close dates in the window, stages X+, divided by (sourced target minus sourced closed-won to date), and print the definition above the number.

issues.quote: Several partners may share one deal's credit under a named split rule.
issues.problem: There's no default when no split rule exists, so conflicting claims (a common case) leave the model to invent the rule.
issues.fix: Default to the program's rule if cited, otherwise the first valid registration or earliest dated introduction gets full sourced credit and the other claimants are listed for owner review, with the dispute noted.

issues.quote: Every number traces to a record. A number with no record is UNKNOWN.
issues.problem: There's no step for partner-reported figures. The persona requires showing their number beside ours and naming the gap rather than averaging, but the skill never mentions reconciling partner claims.
issues.fix: Add a reconciliation block: partner claim (their words, their source), our count, the gap, and the records that would close it.

issues.quote: introduction date, the activity record, or the date the account first
issues.problem: An account-mapping match date is listed as proof, but it proves neither sourcing nor influence under the definitions just given. This gives the model a loophole.
issues.fix: Remove it, or allow it only as supporting evidence alongside a logged joint activity.

issues.quote: Sourced: the partner brought the deal, proven by a deal registration or
issues.problem: There's no claim window, so a two-year-old introduction could count as sourced. own-the-alliance-pnl has an attribution claim window this skill ignores.
issues.fix: State the claim window (for example, introduction within 90 days before opportunity creation, or the program's window) and reuse it across skills.

issues.quote: Forecast grades per partner. Hygiene flags — stale stages, missing
issues.problem: The grading scheme is undefined. The skill also doesn't say hygiene fixes are proposals, not CRM edits (the persona's routine says never move a stage).
issues.fix: Define grade anchors (for example A-D on commit ratio and hygiene) and state that no CRM field is changed without the owner's yes.

issues.quote: Add the velocity lines: close rate and time-to-close with partners
issues.problem: The raw with/without comparison suffers from selection bias, since partner deals skew larger and more enterprise. Leaders will read it as causal.
issues.fix: Compare within segment or deal-size bands and caveat it as correlation.

issues.quote: CRM pull or export, the sourced target, the attribution proofs
issues.problem: No tool routing (HubSpot or Salesforce via run_block or MCP, Sheets export, bash_exec for arithmetic) and no field-mapping step. The snapshot storage location is unnamed.
issues.fix: Add an inputs block with tools, a confirm-the-schema step (as the persona routines do), bash_exec for the math, and memory_store or a workspace file for the dated snapshot.

scenarios.prompt: Pull our Q3 HubSpot deals and tell me what partners sourced versus influenced against our $500K partner-sourced target, then give me the half-page for the exec meeting.
scenarios.why: The model follows the steps in order: bucket each deal with its proof, send deals without proof to the unproven list, run coverage against 3x/2x, add hygiene flags with owners, compare velocity with and without partners, write the half-page report (totals, movement, top three partners, top three risks, leading indicators, one ask), and date the snapshot. The skill doesn't say which HubSpot properties hold partner source or registration ID, or whether coverage uses in-window open pipe, so the model must ask. That is fine.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a spreadsheet export. Reps filled a 'Partner' column on 60% of deals, there are no registration IDs, two partners both claim the same $200K deal, and the partner's own report says they sourced $1.2M against our $400K. Leadership wants one number by tomorrow.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly refuses to count rep-entered tags as proof and sends those deals to the unproven list with the record that would prove them. But the two-partner claim hits 'a named split rule' with no default. The partner's $1.2M claim has no step for showing both numbers and naming the gap (the persona requires this, the skill doesn't). There's no guidance on acceptable proxies such as an intro email in Gmail, so the headline could collapse to near zero without a path to recover it.

ticket-triage.job: triage and prioritise support ticket queue
ticket-triage.summary: Ranks a batch of open support tickets into four impact tiers, groups duplicates only on shared symptom plus corroborating evidence, and returns a queue brief naming owners and unknowns without acting on any ticket.
strengths: 'Rank by impact and urgency, not tone', together with the loud/polite rule, explicitly counters sentiment bias in prioritisation.
Duplicate grouping requires the same symptom plus at least one other piece of evidence, with ticket ids cited. This prevents the common mistake of over-merging.
Hard no-action guardrail (no close, merge, reassign or reply), plus 'mark anything you could not verify', matches Sasha's boundaries exactly.
The brief separates docs-answerable tickets, tickets needing engineering or finance, and unknowns. That feeds directly into Sasha's support-reply-draft and bug-report-handoff skills.
Very concise, with no filler.
missing: SLA and first-response clock, ticket age, and breach or near-breach ordering
Plan, contract and VIP entitlements drawn from the team's agreed rules (memory)
Incident or spike threshold with immediate escalation, and a separate security/abuse/legal path
Per-ticket output template (id, tier, reason, clock, group, owner, unverified)
Input fallback (CSV/paste) and tool routing for status page, known issues and account records
Churn or cancellation signal routed to the account owner
Category tag per ticket so weekly-ticket-themes can trend it
PII and secret redaction in the brief
A 'use when' description that sets it apart from support-ticket-triage and triage-and-prioritize

issues.quote: Rank by impact and urgency, not tone:
issues.problem: Urgency is never operationalised. The four tiers describe impact only, and the 'first message date' captured in step 1 is never used, so ticket age, SLA or first-response breach risk, and plan or contract entitlement play no part in ordering.
issues.fix: Add urgency factors: time since first contact against the team's response target, breach or near-breach first, and plan/contract priority. Order tickets within each tier by SLA risk, and show the clock in the brief.

issues.quote: many users blocked, data at risk, payment failing, or security;
issues.problem: No threshold defines 'many', and nothing says to break out of the batch when a same-symptom spike appears (for example after a deploy). The skill never says to alert engineering on-call or check the status page straight away, and gives no special path for security, abuse or legal tickets.
issues.fix: Define an incident trigger (e.g. 3 or more accounts with the same symptom inside a set window, or any data-loss or security report). When it fires, stop, draft an immediate alert to the named escalation owner for approval, and route security tickets without quoting sensitive content.

issues.quote: Use this for a full queue or a batch of new tickets.
issues.problem: The skill hard-codes its own four tiers and ignores the priority rules, response targets and approval owners agreed in support-getting-started. The result can contradict the team's own definitions.
issues.fix: Start with memory_search for the team's priority rules, entitlements and escalation owners from support-getting-started. Use these tiers only as a labelled default when none are stored.

issues.quote: Check the account record, known-issue list, and status page.
issues.problem: The skill names none of the required inputs, gives no tool route (web_fetch for the status page, run_block for Linear or GitHub known issues, HubSpot for account records), and has no fallback when the help desk is not connected.
issues.fix: Add an inputs step: the queue export (fields needed), known-issue source and status page URL. Use connected blocks or MCP tools where they exist, and otherwise ask_question for a CSV export or paste, noting which checks were skipped.

issues.quote: Return the counts by rank, the duplicate groups, tickets that the docs already
issues.problem: There is no reusable format. 'Name the next owner for each' is ambiguous (each ticket? each group?), and there is no per-ticket ordered list with a one-line reason, so a lead cannot work straight from the output.
