issues.fix: Supply a template: a headline line (as in Sasha's voice sample) and a table with id, tier, one-line reason, SLA clock, group, next owner and unverified items, followed by duplicate groups and an unknowns list.

issues.quote: For each ticket note the customer, plan, channel, first message date, what
issues.problem: Reading every ticket in full by hand does not scale to a queue of hundreds, and nothing says to use the sandbox for parsing, counting or first-pass clustering.
issues.fix: For more than about 50 tickets, parse the export with bash_exec, pre-cluster by symptom keywords and time, then read the candidates and state coverage.

issues.quote: a workaround exists or the question is answered in the docs;
issues.problem: This mixes answerability into priority. A blocked customer whose answer happens to be in the docs is still blocked, and the brief lists docs-answered tickets separately anyway.
issues.fix: Keep tiers about impact and urgency only. Treat 'answered in docs' as a routing flag (macro or reply-draft fast lane), not as a tier.

issues.problem: No privacy rule. Tickets often contain emails, payment details or pasted credentials, and the brief could repeat them.
issues.fix: Tell the model to refer to customers by account or ticket id in the brief, redact secrets and payment data, and flag any exposed credential to the security owner.

scenarios.prompt: Here are our 23 open Zendesk tickets pasted as CSV (id, subject, body, plan, created_at). Triage the queue and tell me what's urgent and who should pick up what.
scenarios.why: Following 'Read each ticket' and 'Rank and group', the model would sort tickets into urgent/high/normal/low and form cited duplicate groups, with tone ignored as intended. However, the 'first message date' it collects is never used, so a ticket that has been blocked for 3 days sits in the same tier as one from this morning, with no SLA-risk ordering. 'Queue brief' gives no per-ticket table, so the output is counts plus groups, not the ordered work list a lead would act on.

scenarios.prompt: Intercom isn't connected. I exported 400 rows (subject, body, created_at, plan), with no account data. Five enterprise customers say SSO has failed since this morning's deploy, one says they'll cancel, and one pasted an API key into the ticket. Triage it.
scenarios.why: 'Mark anything you could not verify' handles the missing account records, and the grouping rule would correctly cluster the SSO reports. But nothing tells the model to use bash_exec for a 400-row file. Nothing defines 'many users blocked' or says to raise a same-symptom spike right after a deploy as a live incident before finishing the brief. There is no path for the churn threat to reach an account owner, and nothing about redacting the pasted secret. A senior lead would escalate the SSO cluster within minutes. The skill only lists it in the end-of-queue brief.

weekly-ticket-themes.job: summarise support tickets into periodic themes report
weekly-ticket-themes.summary: Turns a period's ticket export into problem-based themes with counts, change from the prior period, verbatim quotes, reply and resolution medians, and a close listing product signals, help-centre gaps and macro or article candidates.
strengths: Groups by 'the problem behind them, not the tag alone', which is the right answer to messy or inconsistent tagging.
Verbatim quotes with ticket ids, and it keeps what customers said separate from what the model infers.
'A small theme with blocked users can matter more than a large how-to theme' is the correct severity-over-volume judgment.
Explicitly reports export gaps and channels the data cannot see.
The closing section feeds Sasha's other skills: product bugs, help-centre gaps, and macros or articles to write next.
Strong anti-fabrication rule for thin weeks: 'Never invent counts, quotes, or trends'.
missing: Stable theme codebook stored between periods, and the size of the 'other' bucket
Baseline source for prior-period deltas, a small-number noise caveat, and volume normalisation
CSAT, reopen or repeat-contact rate, and escalations per theme
Link from themes to releases, incidents and known issues
Redaction of personal data in quotes
Reusable report template
Sandbox computation of counts and medians, with a business-hours definition
Weekly schedule_routine and named hand-offs to Sasha's article, macro and bug skills
A 'use when' description that sets it apart from voice-of-customer-and-feedback and product-research-synthesis

issues.quote: the count, the change from the prior period, the plans and segments affected,
issues.problem: The skill asks for a period-over-period change with no baseline source (prior export or stored table), no stable theme definitions across periods, and no caution about noise on small counts or normalising by volume. The trend line will be missing, inconsistent or overstated.
issues.fix: Store each period's theme table and definitions with memory_store and reload them next run, or ask for the prior export. Report deltas only for themes defined the same way both periods, flag changes under a minimum count as noise, and normalise by ticket volume or active accounts when available.

issues.quote: tickets by the problem behind them, not the tag alone.
issues.problem: There is no method for building themes: no codebook, no inclusion rules, no primary theme for tickets that raise several issues, no 'other/unclear' share. The result is not reproducible week to week.
issues.fix: Add steps: draft candidate themes from a sample, write a one-line inclusion rule for each, assign one primary theme per ticket, report the size of the unclassified or other bucket, and keep the codebook for next period.

issues.quote: For each top theme quote two or three short lines from customers, word for
issues.problem: Verbatim quotes go to product and other owners with no instruction to strip names, emails, account ids, order numbers or payment details.
issues.fix: Redact personal and account identifiers from quotes (keep the ticket id as the reference), and drop quotes that cannot be anonymised.

issues.quote: Note the median time to first reply and to resolution
issues.problem: Counts, deltas and medians over hundreds of rows are left to in-context arithmetic. That risks the invented numbers the skill forbids, and it gives no rule for business hours versus calendar hours or for unresolved tickets.
issues.fix: Compute counts, deltas and medians in bash_exec from the export, state whether they use business or calendar hours, exclude still-open tickets from the resolution median and say so.

issues.quote: State the period, the number of tickets, and any gaps in the export.
issues.problem: The skill names no required inputs (fields needed, prior period, other channels) and gives no fallback when the help desk is not connected.
issues.fix: List the required fields (id, created, first reply, solved, plan, tags, body). Use a connected source or ask_question for a CSV, and optionally pull Slack or Discord support channels via run_block, labelled as a separate source.

issues.quote: Do not share the report outside the team or edit tickets yourself.
issues.problem: This contradicts the report's purpose of telling 'who should see them', and doesn't say that sharing means drafting and waiting for approval.
issues.fix: Reword: draft the report and per-owner excerpts, share only after the user approves through the platform approval flow, and never edit tickets.

issues.quote: Close with:
issues.problem: There is no report template, so each week's output has a different shape and cannot be compared or diffed.
issues.fix: Supply a fixed layout: headline (period, volume, change), a theme table (theme, count, delta, severity, segments, ids, medians), quotes, then signals with a named owner and next skill.

issues.quote: Use this for a weekly or monthly look at what customers asked about.
issues.problem: The skill is recurring by name, yet it neither offers a routine nor hands off by name to help-article-from-tickets, support-macro-library, bug-report-handoff or a product teammate.
issues.fix: Offer schedule_routine for the weekly cadence, and name the follow-on skill or teammate (consult_teammate or delegate_to_expert) for each signal type.

scenarios.prompt: Here's last week's Zendesk export: 180 tickets with tags, plan, created, first-reply and solved timestamps. Give me the weekly themes report for Thursday's product sync.
scenarios.why: The model would state the period and count, group by underlying problem, cite ticket ids, quote customers verbatim and close with signals. That part is solid. But 'the change from the prior period' has no prior data and no instruction on where to get it. Medians over 180 timestamps are computed without bash_exec and with no business-hours rule. Quotes that go to product are not redacted. And 'Do not share the report outside the team' conflicts with the stated audience.

scenarios.prompt: Do this month's themes. We moved from Freshdesk to Intercom mid-month so tags don't match, enterprise customers also report in a Slack channel, and leadership wants to know if the new onboarding flow cut tickets.
scenarios.why: 'not the tag alone' handles the tag mismatch, and 'anything the data cannot show, such as tickets outside the help desk' covers Slack as a gap. But the skill never says to pull Slack via run_block. It has no codebook method for reconciling two taxonomies. It gives no guidance on normalising by signups or active users, or on declining a causal claim from a pre/post count on small numbers. So the onboarding question could get an unsupported answer or none.

partner-co-marketing.job: find co-marketing partners and plan joint campaigns
partner-co-marketing.summary: A reference-style co-marketing playbook (partner-identification heuristics, a 1-5 scoring rubric, campaign-format menus, a cold-outreach template, an agreement outline and metrics) plus a partnership-types reference and two provider CLIs (Crossbeam read-only, PartnerStack read/write) that need API-key env vars.
strengths: Sharp partner-selection heuristics: same buyer persona with a different problem, adjacent in the workflow, complementary not competing for the same budget.
A partner scoring rubric with sensible criteria, including reciprocity and ease of execution.
A broad campaign-format menu with effort and lead-sharing columns across content, events, product/integration and community plays.
An agreement outline that covers lead handling, promotion minimums, branding approval, costs and metrics sharing.
The partnership-types reference has a useful 'choosing where to start' decision list and the permissionless co-marketing idea.
missing: An ordered intake-to-deliverable procedure with branches for finding partners and for a campaign with a named partner
A scored partner-shortlist template with an evidence/source column and UNKNOWN handling
A one-page joint campaign brief template (goal, audience, offer, assets, owners, dates, lead split, KPIs)
A draft-first and approval gate for outreach, agreements, spend and any PRM writes
Lead-sharing consent and privacy rules, and legal review of the co-marketing agreement
A graceful fallback when Crossbeam or PartnerStack is not connected (overlap CSV, customer survey export)
Attribution definitions agreed up front (partner-sourced vs influenced) and how MDF or cost splits are recorded
Handoffs to Anika's sibling partnership skills

issues.quote: For implementation, see the [tools registry]
issues.problem: The registry link points to an upstream REGISTRY.md that the package does not ship. The bundled crossbeam.js and partnerstack.js need API-key env vars that bash_exec does not have, and no Crossbeam or PartnerStack block exists. partnerstack.js also exposes live create/update/delete on partnerships, customers, transactions, rewards and webhooks, and the skill puts no approval gate on any of it.
issues.fix: Remove the registry link. Say the CLIs are optional and read-only here. By default, ask for a Crossbeam/Reveal overlap CSV export or use a run_mcp_tool connection. Forbid PartnerStack write commands without the owner's explicit yes, or remove partnerstack.js.

issues.quote: **Flagship proof:** HubSpot's partner program = **$100M ARR, ~40% of revenue, 3,400+ partners.** Mature programs average **~28% of revenue and 2× growth**.
issues.problem: These statistics, like the '83% of enterprise buyers' and '~12× monthly commission' figures in the same section, are uncited and dated. A model will repeat them to users as fact, which breaks the Max/Anika rule 'never invent a number'. The same table and statistics also appear again in references/partnership-types.md.
issues.fix: Cut the statistics from SKILL.md. Keep them only in the reference, with source and year, labelled illustrative. Add the rule that no benchmark enters a user deliverable without a cited source.

issues.quote: Subject: [Your Company] + [Their Company] co-marketing idea
issues.problem: The partner outreach template has no draft-only or approval rule. The overlap claim it asks for has no evidence requirement, so the model could invent the overlap or send through a Gmail block.
issues.fix: Label it as a draft. Require the overlap line to cite its source (overlap export, customer survey, public integration page). Send only after the owner approves through the approval flow. For Anika, defer to partner-first-touch-outreach.

issues.quote: Are you looking for partners or planning a campaign with a specific partner?
issues.problem: The only routing and intake questions come at line 295, after about 270 lines of reference. There are no ordered steps or decision points, so the model is not told to gather ICP, customer tool stack, audience metrics, budget and timeline before it scores or brainstorms.
issues.fix: Make this Step 1 intake, after checking memory_search. Then branch. A) Find partners: sources, score with evidence, shortlist. B) Specific partner: shared moments and assets, 2-3 ideas, campaign brief, agreement outline, measurement plan.

issues.quote: Rate potential partners (1-5) on:
issues.problem: The skill defines no deliverable and no evidence rule. Audience size, engagement and ease of execution will be scored from guesses. There are no weights and no disqualifiers (for example, the partner competes for the same budget or has a conflicting integration).
issues.fix: Ship templates/partner-shortlist.md (partner, each criterion's score with evidence link or UNKNOWN, total, first campaign idea, warm path) and templates/campaign-brief.md (goal, audience, offer, assets and owners, dates, lead split, KPIs). Add hard disqualifiers.

issues.quote: For customer referral programs, see referrals. For launch-specific partnerships, see launch.
issues.problem: 'referrals' and 'launch' do not exist in the catalog; neither does 'content-strategy' in Related Skills. The skill never points to Anika's overlapping skills (define-the-partner-icp, partner-first-touch-outreach, run-the-partner-marketing-engine). It is also proposed for Max, whose persona puts marketing campaigns out of scope.
issues.fix: Re-point to real slugs (product-launch-marketing, marketing-content-strategy, sales-enablement-content). Assign it to Anika only. Add 'not for an ongoing co-marketing calendar: use run-the-partner-marketing-engine'.

issues.quote: **Lead handling**: How leads are captured, shared, followed up
issues.problem: Sharing leads between companies needs consent language that names both parties on the form, a lawful basis for the transfer (GDPR/CASL/CAN-SPAM) and legal review of the agreement. Logo use and spend commitments also need owner sign-off. The skill says none of this.
issues.fix: Add a compliance line: joint-form consent wording, a data-sharing clause or DPA, trademark approval, and agreement to Legal. No spend or promotion commitment without the owner's yes.

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups), read it
issues.problem: These are Claude-Code local project-state paths, which the platform does not keep.
issues.fix: Use memory_search for product and ICP context, and read_workspace_file if the user names a doc. Otherwise ask the intake questions and memory_store the answers.

scenarios.prompt: We're a Series A interview-scheduling tool for recruiting teams. Who should we co-market with this quarter, and give me three campaign ideas for the best one.
scenarios.why: The Partner Identification Framework (same buyer, different problem; before/after in the workflow) and the campaign-format tables will give a plausible shortlist and ideas. But the intake questions sit at the very end (Task-Specific Questions), so the model is not told to collect the customer tech stack or audience metrics first. The 1-5 scoring has no evidence rule, so audience size and engagement get guessed. There is no shortlist or brief template, and the model may pad the answer with the uncited HubSpot/83% statistics.

scenarios.prompt: Pull our Crossbeam overlaps to see which partner shares the most open pipeline, set the top one up in PartnerStack, and email their partnerships lead a joint-webinar pitch today.
scenarios.why: Tool Integrations points to crossbeam.js and partnerstack.js, which need CROSSBEAM_API_KEY and PARTNERSTACK_* env vars. bash_exec has no user secrets and there is no Crossbeam or PartnerStack block, and the skill gives no fallback (such as asking for an overlap CSV export). If keys were somehow present, `partnerships create` makes a live record with no approval gate. The Cold Outreach Template has no draft-only rule, so nothing stops a send, and nothing requires the '[specific observation about overlap]' to be sourced.

sales-account-research.job: research a prospect account before outreach
sales-account-research.summary: Grounds the ICP, checks CRM ownership first, researches the company (and optionally one contact) for dated signals, scores ICP fit in an evidence table, writes 2-3 sourced outreach hooks and ends with a CRM-status-aware next step, with file-only fallbacks and strong untrusted-content rules.
strengths: Checks CRM ownership before researching, so the rep does not step on a colleague's account. This is a real practitioner concern.
The ICP fit table marks each dimension with evidence and says so plainly when a dimension could not be verified.
Hooks must be specific and sourced, with a concrete good-vs-generic example.
Strong untrusted-content and prompt-injection rules for enrichment and scraped pages.
Clear files-only / read-only tiers with honest disclosure of what was not used.
missing: Buying-committee or stakeholder map with role tags, limited to published sources
A source ledger with dates and FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels matching Max's persona
Persisting the ICP and value prop to memory
Guidance on public-company sources (10-K, earnings-call remarks) and on detecting incumbent or competitor tech (job posts, integration pages)
Privacy limits on researching a named individual
A worked example brief

issues.quote: Research a target company and optionally a specific contact - company overview, recent news, likely priorities, and fit against your ICP.
issues.problem: Duplicates Max's research-an-account, whose triggers include 'research this account', 'prospect company research' and 'brief me on this prospect'. Both would load for 'research Acme', with different output shapes (fit table vs stakeholder map) and different labelling schemes.
issues.fix: Merge into one skill with this skill's CRM check, ICP fit table and hooks, plus research-an-account's stakeholder map, meeting-strategy handoff and FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN source ledger. Retire the other slug.

issues.quote: If a contact was specified: role, tenure, prior companies, public
issues.problem: Research stops at one optional contact. An AE brief needs the buying committee (economic buyer, champion, evaluators, blockers). There is also no personal-data limit when profiling a named individual.
issues.fix: Add a verified-stakeholders table limited to linkable published sources, with role tags and 'who is missing', or hand off to find-the-decision-makers. State: professional, published information only; no guessed emails, no personal social accounts.

issues.quote: Permissions live in each connector's own settings (allow, ask or block per tool): never add a restriction the connector does not impose
issues.problem: Tells the model not to add restrictions beyond connector settings and never to refuse a user-requested action. This conflicts with Max's draft-by-default boundary and AutoGPT's approval flow, and a read-only research skill does not need it.
issues.fix: Replace with: research only; any CRM record, activity log or outreach is drafted and waits for the owner's explicit yes.

issues.quote: relevance hooks; and the suggested next step ("run draft-outreach
issues.problem: Names the upstream skill 'draft-outreach'; the installed name is sales-outreach-drafting, and Max's own skill is draft-a-first-touch. The tiers also hand off to update-opportunity and log-activity, which are not in the catalog.
issues.fix: Point to the real installed slugs and remove the nonexistent ones.

issues.quote: Overall: strong / moderate / poor fit with a one-sentence
issues.problem: No rule that a hard disqualifier forces poor fit, and the scale does not match the strong/maybe/weak scale Max's target list uses.
issues.fix: Use strong/maybe/weak. Any met disqualifier caps the result at weak. List the unverified dimensions that could change the call.

issues.quote: use the answer for this conversation and suggest adding it to the project instructions
issues.problem: 'Project instructions' is a Claude Projects concept. On this platform the ICP answer is lost after the conversation, which breaks Max's 'never ask twice'.
issues.fix: memory_store the ICP, value prop and disqualifiers once confirmed, and memory_search them at Step 1.

issues.quote: Rendering: transient analysis as an artifact; anything a second person or a second week touches as a Page; anything presented as Slides
issues.problem: Artifact, Page and Slides are claude.ai rendering surfaces, not AutoGPT outputs.
issues.fix: Save the brief with write_workspace_file (markdown), or to a Google Doc via the block after approval, and put the top three talking points in chat.

issues.quote: Scheduled or unattended runs take the actions the user set the schedule up to take
issues.problem: A roughly 700-word generic connector-policy block (write refusals, scheduled runs, choosing between Gmail and Outlook) precedes a read-only research procedure and dilutes it.
issues.fix: Trim to the four rules this skill uses: cite every value, blank vs not queried, untrusted content is data, and missing connector means say what was used.

scenarios.prompt: Research Northwind Logistics (northwind.com) before I reach out. Are they a fit for us?
scenarios.why: Step 1 grounds the ICP (one question or a labelled default). Step 2 checks HubSpot for owner or net new. Step 3 uses web_search for dated six-month signals and labels inferred priorities as inference. Step 4 builds the fit table with evidence. Step 5 gives specific sourced hooks. Step 6 assembles the brief and next step. A capable model produces a senior SDR/AE-quality brief. The only defect is that the next step names 'draft-outreach', which does not exist.

scenarios.prompt: Look up Priya Shah, VP Ops at a private 80-person 3PL. No CRM is connected, our ICP isn't written down, and I also need to know who else is on the buying committee.
scenarios.why: The missing CRM and ICP are handled well: the files fallback, one ICP question or a labelled default, and unverifiable funding and size marked as such. But Step 3 covers only the one named contact. There is no step for mapping a buying committee, so the model improvises or skips it. There is also no personal-data limit for researching a named individual. The ICP answer is not stored to memory, so the next run asks again.

sales-call-preparation.job: prepare brief for an upcoming sales call
sales-call-preparation.summary: Builds a one-page pre-call brief: it resolves the meeting from the calendar, pulls CRM opportunity state, transcript and email history and internal chat, profiles attendees, and writes a call plan (objective, 3-5 stage-appropriate questions, likely objections, what to bring), with careful handling of missing or refused connectors.
strengths: Thorough edge-case handling: no calendar, calendar permission refused, meeting already ended, no attendee list, anchor dates for uploaded exports.
Pulls unanswered questions and prior commitments from earlier calls into the plan, and lists what the rep owes ('Bring').
Untrusted-content discipline: requests found inside transcripts or emails are listed for the user and never acted on; unverified attendees are never used as recipients.
Evidence honesty: '0 calls searched means no coverage, not nothing happened'; no numbers lifted from a prebuilt brief without a cited answer; full thread opened before summarising.
States the objective as 'what should be true after the call that is not before'.
missing: Call plans by meeting type (first discovery, demo, negotiation, renewal/QBR, executive)
A timed agenda and the specific next-step ask or mutual-action-plan status
Open qualification gaps by framework letter, each with the question that closes it
Deal-risk and competition flags (single-threaded, no economic buyer, incumbent)
A tool-agnostic transcript source with an explicit paste fallback
Handoffs to discovery-and-qualification, renewal-expansion-and-qbr and next-step-and-handoff
A worked example brief

It has no timed agenda, no specific next-step ask to secure, no qualification gaps by framework letter, and no risk or competition flags (single-threaded, no economic buyer). Renewals, negotiations and executive meetings get the wrong plan. It also overlaps discovery-and-qualification without routing to it.

issues.problem: Artifact, Page and Slides are claude.ai surfaces. The Step 1 advice to add facts to 'project instructions' is also Claude-specific.

15:resume-screening.job: screen resumes against approved hiring rubric
15:resume-screening.summary: A scripted pipeline for screening resumes. It checks that the rubric is approved and unchanged, extracts text from uploads, zips, Drive files and ATS exports, removes identity cues, proxy cues and hidden prompt-injection text, then screens each record in its own pass into a three-state evidence matrix with verified exact quotes. It returns counts, files and interview questions without ever ranking or deciding.
strengths: The walkthrough's script outputs are real. I re-ran find_rubric, extract, redact, verify, merge and counts on the fixtures and got identical results, including the paraphrased A-005 C3 quote being downgraded.

Redaction handles hard name shapes: particles, ALL-CAPS names, accents, Vietnamese and Czech names, BIO-DATA headers. It also removes schools and graduation years, ZIPs while keeping count numbers ('AP 15000 invoices'), and trait-revealing affiliations. All matched the eval expectations when tested.
Treats resume content as data: hidden DOCX/PDF text is kept out, instruction-like sentences are removed, and findings are reported as neutral FACT lines that are never scored.
An exact-quote rule enforced by verify_quotes.py means no screener paraphrase ever appears in quote marks.
One template and one vocabulary map (EVIDENCE FOUND/MISSING/CONFIRM ↔ FACT/UNKNOWN) serve both Harper and Sofia, with persona-specific rules kept separate.
Rank and shortlist requests are declined with a concrete alternative (evidence-complete ids in id order), and a worked refusal example ships with it.
Dated, sourced law-watch lines (NYC LL144, Illinois HB 3773, California FEHA, Colorado SB 26-189, UK DUAA, EU AI Act) end with 'may apply; confirm with counsel' and never assert compliance.

Uses real platform tools (run_capability, read_workspace_file save_to_path, run_sub_session, Task with a 3-agent limit, write_workspace_file), with a fallback ladder down to single-context screening and hand-counted numbers.
24 eval scenarios with fixture-backed pass criteria.
missing: Do-not-contact matching for ATS-export inputs
A fallback when the ATS export has only resume attachment links and no text column (the usual Greenhouse/Lever export)
A re-screen pass for downgraded must-have quotes before counts are final
Guidance on legitimate eligibility knock-outs (work authorisation, required licence, on-site availability) as rubric criteria, as opposed to proxies
A notice for recorded jurisdictions that map to no law-watch region, plus a Canada/Ontario row
A hand-off to draft the candidate-facing AI-use notice where law-watch flags one (NYC LL144, Illinois, Ontario)
A time and throughput estimate for large batches (200+ applicants) against the owner's results-due date
How the batch-file retention period interacts with same-turn deletion requests

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: Save it, then `python3 ~/skills/resume-screening/scripts/redact_export.py <export> <dir>/txt --text-cols "<resume text column>"
issues.problem: The ATS-export path skips the do-not-contact check. redact_export.py has no --dnc option, and step 1's --dnc only applies when extract_resumes.py runs over in/. With Sofia, an applicant on dnc.csv who arrives in a CSV/XLSX export is redacted and screened, breaking her 'left out of every batch' rule.
issues.fix: Add --dnc to redact_export.py, using screenio.name_in_lines on the name columns and setting parse_status 'held'. Make the table row say '(Sofia: add --dnc ~/workspace/hiring/dnc.csv)'. Add an eval scenario covering a do-not-contact name in an export.

issues.quote: A downgraded quote stays downgraded.
issues.problem: When the screener paraphrases real evidence (fixture A-005's refund-policy line actually exists in the resume), the row drops to CONFIRM IN INTERVIEW. On a must-have, that moves the candidate from evidence-complete to needs interview because of a model error, not anything in the resume. That is a fairness defect.
issues.fix: When a must-have row is downgraded, re-screen only that criterion in one fresh isolated pass. Keep the downgrade only if the second quote also fails verification, and report how many were re-screened.

issues.quote: `templates/screen-subtask-prompt.md` with that record's redacted text only.
issues.problem: Filling {{REDACTED_TEXT}} means the orchestrator reads every candidate's text into its own context before dispatching. On batches of 40 or more that fills the main context (tens of thousands of tokens) and undercuts the isolation the step is built around.
issues.fix: Pass the path red/<id>.txt and the criteria lines instead. Have each sub-pass read its file with bash_exec and write records/<id>.json itself, so the orchestrator only sees script output.

issues.quote: that id's `name_hint` column in `idmap.csv` (the name stays out of chat),
issues.problem: idmap.csv sits in the expert's ~/workspace batch folder, but the owner edits the copy delivered with write_workspace_file. Nothing explains how the owner's edit gets back to the file redact.py reads, so records with no name line stay stuck on 'needs a look'.
issues.fix: Spell out the round trip: deliver idmap.csv, and once the owner says it is filled in, pull it back with read_workspace_file(save_to_path=<batch>/idmap.csv) without displaying it, then re-run redact.py.

issues.quote: If jurisdictions are not recorded, say so once. Do not advise.
issues.problem: A jurisdiction that is recorded but matches no region ('Toronto, Canada', 'Singapore', 'Remote') returns an empty law_watch and triggers no notice at all, so the owner may read silence as 'no rules'. Ontario has required AI-use disclosure in job postings since 2026-01-01.
issues.fix: Have find_rubric.py list unmapped places and the skill say 'no law-watch entry for <place>; AI-screening rules may still apply; confirm with counsel'. Add a Canada (Ontario) row to ai-hiring-law-watch.md.

issues.quote: (Harper's `rubric-v<N>.md` or Sofia's `scorecard.md`), or the owner wants a
issues.problem: Sofia's path needs ~/workspace/hiring/roles/<slug>/scorecard.md with status: approved and approved_by headers. In PR 15, role-intake-and-scorecard is still the thin v1 and never writes that file. Only PR 16's rebuild does, so Sofia always exits 3 unless PR 16 lands too.
issues.fix: Merge together with PR 16, or document the --file fallback for Sofia. Add a cross-PR note to the release.

issues.quote: list delivered copies and tracker rows it did not touch.
issues.problem: Sofia's persona requires deletion in the same reply. The skill only lists the tracker row and the delivered workspace copies, which leaves the candidate's name and stage in the tracker of record.
issues.fix: For Sofia, remove the tracker row, or ask in that same reply, and call delete_workspace_file on the delivered copies (subject to platform approval). Route retention conflicts to counsel.

issues.quote: Fictional record, for shape only. Role: Billing Operations Lead; rubric v1
issues.problem: At 231 lines the body is long for a loaded skill. The no-ranking and no-decision rules appear in the Output contract, Approval gate, Guardrails and Quality self-check. The inline Example repeats the walkthrough, and the Package files section repeats what read_skill already lists.
issues.fix: Drop the inline Example and link the walkthrough instead. Fold Guardrails into the self-check. Move the Drive/ATS CLI detail and step 11 into a reference, aiming for about 150 lines.

scenarios.prompt: (Harper) Here's a zip of 22 resumes for the Billing Ops Lead role. Maya approved rubric v1 yesterday. Screen them and give me the evidence matrices.
scenarios.why: Prerequisite: find_rubric.py exits 0 with a checksum and emits criteria.json. The UK law-watch line goes first. extract_resumes.py unzips and flags scanned PDFs. redact.py strips identity. Step 4 runs one pass per record, at most 3 Task sub-agents at a time. verify_quotes, merge_matrices and batch_counts produce numbers used verbatim. The batch-summary template gives a reusable reply with matrices.md, matrix.csv and an owner-only idmap. I reproduced this flow on the fixtures and the output matched the walkthrough exactly.

scenarios.prompt: (Sofia) Attached is our Greenhouse CSV export for the SDR req: 140 applicants, a resume-text column, plus EEO columns. We hire in Toronto and NYC. Just give me the top 10 to call this week.
scenarios.why: Handled well: redact_export.py drops EEO columns and moves proxy columns to the owner-only file (verified). NYC and US federal law-watch lines appear. The skill works in turns of about 20 records, and the top-10 request is declined with the evidence-complete ids in id order. Gaps: redact_export.py has no --dnc option and step 1's --dnc only runs on in/, so applicants on the do-not-contact list are screened, breaking Sofia's hard rule. Toronto maps to no law-watch region and produces no notice at all (Ontario's AI-disclosure rule is not covered). The Sofia scorecard must carry status: approved, which only PR 16's role-intake-and-scorecard writes.

better: Moves from a 44-line prose placeholder to an executable pipeline: a rubric approval and checksum gate, extraction with a hidden-text scan, redaction, quote verification, merge checks and script-generated counts
Adds prompt-injection handling (white or tiny text is kept out, instruction sentences removed, FACT lines reported) that main lacks entirely
Enforces exact quotes, where main allowed a paraphrased 'passage'
Main called an unexplained gap a red flag to confirm; the rebuild never notes a gap
Adds per-record isolation, so the screener never compares candidates
Adds a law-watch notice, handling for ATS-export EEO columns, do-not-contact holds (for file uploads), same-turn deletion and a counterfactual consistency check
Adds a defined output contract, templates, a worked fixture walkthrough whose outputs reproduce exactly, and 24 evals
The description now names prerequisites and exclusions, so it is clearly distinct from sourcing and rubric-building
worse: The body grows from 44 to 231 lines, with rules repeated across four sections
Adds runtime dependencies (pip install of pdfplumber, pypdf and openpyxl; the sub-agent/run_sub_session ladder) where main needed none
Sofia's path now depends on PR 16's scorecard header format; main had no such coupling
A downgraded quote can now lower a candidate's status because of a model paraphrase, a failure mode main's prose did not have

productivity-setup.job: bootstrap assistant memory of user's people, terms
productivity-setup.summary: Creates TASKS.md, copies a 98KB browser dashboard and a CLAUDE.md plus memory/ folder into a working directory, then decodes the nicknames, acronyms and codenames in the user's task list (with an optional scan of chat, email, docs and calendar) into a file-based two-tier memory.
strengths: Good insight: the user's own task list is the best source of their real shorthand, and decoding it by asking the user builds context a colleague would have.
Scan findings are sorted by confidence (ready to add / needs clarification / low frequency / unclear), so a confident finding gets offered and an uncertain one gets asked about.
Clear two-tier memory design: a compact working-memory index plus a deeper glossary, people, projects and company files, with a concrete template.
Detects existing state and skips the bootstrap when memory already exists; skips unavailable sources and notes the gap.
missing: Use of memory_store/memory_search as the durable memory, with a search before asking the user
Batched, frequency-ranked decoding with proposed meanings for the user to confirm, instead of one round of questions per task
The core of EA onboarding (priorities, key-people tiers, approval rules per action, writing voice, calendar rules), or an explicit handoff to executive-assistant-getting-started
Sensitivity rules for people profiles: what is never stored, minimising data about third parties, and letting the user view and delete memory
Preview and approval of the full memory summary before anything is written
Mapping of sources to run_block integrations, with connect_integration and paste/export fallbacks
A reusable setup-brief deliverable in place of the dashboard link
A scheduled refresh via schedule_routine in place of the /productivity:update command
Rules for flagging stale memory entries and retiring them

issues.quote: **CLAUDE.md** (working memory, ~50-80 lines):
issues.problem: Memory is written to a CLAUDE.md file and a memory/ tree. CLAUDE.md is a Claude-Code-only construct, and the platform's durable memory is memory_store/memory_search, which the skill ignores. Anything written to the E2B sandbox may not survive to the next session.
issues.fix: Store the people, terms, projects and preferences as memory_store entries with clear keys. Call memory_search before asking about any term. Optionally export a readable glossary with write_workspace_file.

issues.quote: **If `dashboard.html` doesn't exist:** Copy it from `assets/dashboard.html` in this skill package to the current working directory.
issues.problem: The bundled dashboard, 98KB of the package, only works on local files the user opens with Chromium's File System Access pickers. It can't read the platform workspace or the sandbox, so the 'open the dashboard' deliverable is a dead end.
issues.fix: Remove the dashboard and step 3. Deliver a setup summary in chat or as a workspace file, or point to a platform-native view of tasks and memory.

issues.quote: All workflows must use the same persistent working directory for their task and memory state.
issues.problem: Assumes a persistent local working directory shared across sessions and sibling skills. The platform doesn't keep one; the sandbox is ephemeral.
issues.fix: Use memory_store for memory, write_workspace_file for any task file, and name those locations explicitly.

issues.quote: /productivity:update to sync tasks and check memory
issues.problem: The orientation and final report point users to /productivity:update and --comprehensive slash commands. The package says itself that these aren't registered, so users hit a dead end.
issues.fix: Replace these with a pointer to the productivity-task-sync skill, or offer schedule_routine for a weekly refresh.

issues.quote: Do you want me to do a comprehensive scan of your messages, emails, and documents?
issues.problem: The scan has no scope (accounts, date range, folders) and no rules for sensitive data: health, HR, compensation, personal matters, or third parties' private details. It builds per-person profiles, which conflicts with Kai's 'keep what you read private' boundary.
issues.fix: Ask the user to scope the scan. List the categories never to store. Store only work-role facts about third parties. Show the proposed memory entries for approval before saving, and let the user view and delete them.

issues.quote: Use when setting up the plugin for the first time, bootstrapping working memory from your existing task list
issues.problem: 'The plugin' means nothing inside an AutoGPT expert. The trigger overlaps with executive-assistant-getting-started (Kai) and workplace-memory-management, so the model can't tell which setup skill to load.
issues.fix: If kept, merge into the expert's getting-started skill as a 'learn my shorthand' step and drop the standalone description.

issues.quote: Continue through each task, asking only about terms you haven't already decoded.
issues.problem: The decode loop has no bound, no batching and no priority order. A realistic list of 100+ tasks produces question fatigue, and the model isn't asked to propose likely meanings for the user to confirm.
issues.fix: Extract all candidate terms, rank them by frequency, propose best guesses, and ask about the top 10-15 in one ask_question batch. Defer the rest to 'learn as we go'.

issues.quote: Gather data from available MCP sources:
issues.problem: Only MCP sources are named. The skill doesn't map to AutoGPT's run_block integrations (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear, Todoist), offer connect_integration, or fall back to a paste or export.
issues.fix: Name the block for each source. When a source isn't connected, offer connect_integration or accept a CSV, export or paste.

scenarios.prompt: Kai, get yourself set up on my work. My todos are in Todoist. Learn who and what I mean in them so I don't have to explain every time.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-3 create TASKS.md and dashboard.html in a sandbox directory and tell the user to open a file they can't reach; the dashboard also needs showOpenFilePicker/showDirectoryPicker on local files. Step 5 asks where the todos are even though the user already said, and never says to use the Todoist run_block or connect_integration. The per-task decode Q&A would build a useful glossary. But step 7 writes it to CLAUDE.md/memory/ files instead of memory_store, so the next session may lose it, and step 8 sends the user to /productivity:update, which doesn't exist.

scenarios.prompt: Frankie, I've got about 250 tasks across Linear and a messy notes paste, and Slack isn't connected. Build your picture of my people and projects, and skim my Gmail too. Don't keep anything about my team's performance issues or anyone's health.
scenarios.why: Step 5 says to 'Continue through each task', with no batching, no frequency ranking and no guess-and-confirm, so 250 tasks become dozens of rounds of questions. Step 6 says to gather from 'available MCP sources' and never mentions the Gmail block. Nothing covers sensitive data, and the memory/people/{name}.md profiles would take in whatever the scan finds. The user's exclusion depends entirely on the model's own judgement. Only the 'skip it and note the gap' note handles the missing Slack connection correctly.

16:interview-coordination.job: schedule interview loops and track candidate pipeline
16:interview-coordination.summary: Rebuilt Sofia skill that runs interview logistics end to end: keeps a three-file CSV hiring tracker (import, merge, refresh), builds DST-safe two-timezone loop options with tz_slots.py, gates every calendar/mail write behind an approval, drafts candidate and interviewer messages with an FCRA gate on declines, sweeps for stalls (with history and escalation) to feed the morning brief and mail sweep, and removes a candidate from the hiring folder on request.
strengths: All five scripts are real and ship with passing selftests: tz_slots, merge_tracker, stall_sweep, flag_ledger and forget_candidate. Both walkthroughs reproduce the scripts' output exactly, including the Lisbon/New York gap shrinking from 5 to 4 hours across the October DST change.

Calendar write rules are precise. It states that Google Calendar has no 'draft invite', so an event with attendees sends real invitations. Each write goes through validate_only, then a one-line description of the effect, then its own yes. approval_required is handled without retrying, and unattended routine runs make no external writes.

Before drafting any decline it asks whether a background check or consumer report played a part and, if so, routes to the FCRA adverse-action process. Identity verification is applied to every candidate at a stage, and a location-based ID check is explicitly refused as a national-origin risk.

Tracker hygiene is careful. Protected and self-ID columns are dropped at import, day/month-ambiguous dates are never guessed, it never merges on a guess (near-duplicates go to needs-a-look), and prospects are kept separate from applicants.

forget_candidate.py has thoughtful safeguards against same-name collisions. It won't touch Jo Parker when removing Jo Park, leaves interviewer-context mentions and other candidates' scorecards alone, keeps DNC name-plus-flag only, and walks the whole plan read-only before deleting anything.
Clear 'Do not use for' routing to the sibling Sofia skills (kit design, debrief, offer, outreach, analytics).

Platform calls match the actual AutoGPT codebase: run_capability with skill: and tool: ids, list_workspace_files include_all_sessions, read_workspace_file save_to_path, the ~/workspace durable volume and ~/skills/<slug> package mount. It also has explicit fallbacks for missing Python, calendar or Gmail.
missing: Per-interviewer timezone and working hours, with interviewer-local times in options and notes
Interviewer load caps and fatigue limits, plus shadow/reverse-shadow pairing for training interviewers
Candidate confirmation handshake, day-before reminders, video-link or room creation, and a no-show / late-cancel procedure
A proactive accommodation question at booking, not just an accommodation contact in the confirmation
Deadline-aware escalation for stall items tied to a loop today or tomorrow
Legal-hold and retention check before irreversible deletion; GDPR/UK erasure-request handling (deadline, Art. 17(3) exceptions) for non-US candidates
Fair-chance / ban-the-box (state and local) note alongside the FCRA route
FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN labelling that Sofia's persona requires on load-bearing lines

issues.quote: carries two labelled times, the candidate's and the owner's; a time with
issues.problem: The booking model has only two timezones. tz_slots.py validates owner_hours and busy spans but has no per-interviewer timezone or working hours, and prints only candidate and owner times. issues.fix: Keep the same-reply removal the persona requires, but check for a recorded legal hold or open claim before applying, and skip those items. Put the retention line with the dry-run list, before the irreversible step. Note GDPR Art. 17(3) exceptions for candidate-initiated requests.

issues.fix: Align the column names across the two skills in this PR (or add aliases in funnel.py), then remove the known-gap caveat.

issues.quote: and removes a candidate from the hiring records on request.

issues.quote: hand over three things at once: holds (a

issues.quote: and write `/home/user/coord/availability.json` in the
issues.problem: The availability format takes interviewer busy spans only, and nothing explains how to convert the pasted free windows that the Fallbacks invite. An alternate whose calendar was never read has no busy list, so tz_slots treats them as free all day.
issues.fix: Accept `free` windows per person, or document the conversion. Require that alternates' calendars are read, or label a stand-in option 'alternate's availability unchecked'.

scenarios.prompt: Book the onsite for Priya Nair (Senior Backend). She's in Dublin and free Tue 13 to Thu 15 Oct, 09:00-13:00 her time. Panel: Dev on system design, Ana on coding, Lena for the HM close. My Google Calendar is connected.
scenarios.why: Section A reads the tracker fresh. B1 confirms slot lengths, buffers and the midpoint break. B2 reads free/busy read-only through find_capability/run_capability and writes availability.json. B3 runs tz_slots.py, which returns 2-3 ranked options with Dublin and Lisbon times on every slot, each naming its one compromise. I checked the DST handling. In B4, calendar-and-booking.md asks exactly what to write (holds, invites or table), runs validate_only, says 'this sends 3 invitations', writes only on a yes, drafts the candidate email and per-interviewer notes from templates/messages.md, and updates loops.csv. The whole panel shares the owner's timezone, so the script's gaps don't show.

scenarios.prompt: Marco (SF) just dropped Kenji's system-design slot on Thursday. Kenji's in Tokyo and can only do 18:00-21:30 his time; I'm in London. No calendar connected, so here are everyone's free times pasted. Jen (also SF) is our other calibrated system-design interviewer.
scenarios.why: B5 correctly keeps the competency covered by putting Jen in `alternates`. The Fallbacks section correctly proceeds from the paste. But availability.json only accepts interviewer busy spans, and nothing explains how to turn pasted free times into busy spans. tz_slots.py checks only owner_hours. I ran this case: it put Jen's slot at Tokyo 18:00 / London 10:00, which is 02:00 in San Francisco, with no warning. The output shows only the candidate and owner zones, and B3 says to present options 'verbatim'. So the model would offer an unworkable loop. The approvals, drafts and tracker updates would still be correct.

james-getting-started.job: onboard owner and capture working preferences
james-getting-started.summary: First-conversation onboarding for James: a short hello, one question on business and size followed by a two-line diagnosis, optional one-at-a-time preference questions saved to memory under named keys, a check of existing connections, a five-item starter menu, opt-in cadences, and a switch straight to real work as soon as the owner hands any over.
strengths: Leads with value: two facts in, then a diagnosis the owner can correct before effort is spent
One optional question per message, a skipped question stays unset, and every answer goes to named memory keys
'Drop the questions the moment work arrives' stops interview theatre
Checks existing connections before asking, and treats a pasted CSV as equal to a live connection
The three standing cadences match the persona's routines and switch on only with approval, in the owner's timezone
Refuses to build an SOP or map for an invented example
missing: Size-band and business-model heuristics for the opening diagnosis
A mapping from each starter-menu item to the sibling skill it loads
Handling for partly filled memory
A teammate handoff map (Daniel, Sofia, Robin, Lena) at the scope boundaries
A memory schema that matches the questions, including a review destination

issues.section: Ask one thing first, then give something back
issues.quote: those two facts, tell them in two lines where operations tends to break
issues.problem: The skill calls this diagnosis the first real contribution but gives no size-band heuristics (for example founder bottleneck under 10 people, handoffs and vendor sprawl at 10-50, missing controls and middle-management gaps at 50-200). It also does not require an INFERENCE label, so the model improvises and presents a guess with authority.
issues.fix: Add a compact table of typical failure points by headcount band and business model, and require the read to be tagged INFERENCE with the one question that would confirm it.

issues.quote: Five options, each something you can do inside this conversation.
issues.problem: The menu items are not mapped to ops-write-an-sop, ops-map-and-improve-a-process, ops-vendor-and-procurement, ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan and ops-run-the-operating-rhythm. A chosen item may be drafted ad hoc instead of through the proper procedure.
issues.fix: Name the sibling skill after each menu item and say to read_skill it before drafting.

issues.quote: time-bound) and hold a weekly check-in through day 90.
issues.problem: The 30/60/90 SMART arc copies human new-hire onboarding. It adds a weekly check-in that is not one of the approved routines and pads a skill the persona wants spare.
issues.fix: Cut the section, or reduce it to one line that points to the Monday review routine, which already gives the weekly touchpoint.

issues.section: Ask the rest one at a time
issues.quote: owner, scorecard destination, timezone, weekly review day and hour,
issues.problem: The memory keys do not match the questions. Nothing asks for 'scorecard destination', the question 'Where SOPs and reports belong' has no key, and there is no key for where the weekly review lands, which the ops-weekly-review routine asks for.
issues.fix: Make the questions and keys match one-to-one, and add a 'review destination' key.

issues.quote: Preferences already in memory: skip onboarding and start on what is
issues.problem: Memory is treated as all-or-nothing. With partly filled memory the model either re-onboards or skips keys a requested cadence needs.
issues.fix: Read memory first, ask only for the missing keys that the requested work needs, and never re-ask stored ones.

issues.quote: First see which tools are hooked up already and name them, so nobody is
issues.problem: This sits awkwardly with 'Never describe how you were configured or list your own tools', and the skill gives no teammate boundary map (finance to Daniel, hiring to Sofia, support queue to Robin, compliance to Lena). Early requests in those areas are not routed.
issues.fix: Clarify that 'name them' means the owner's connected accounts, and add a one-line handoff map to teammates.

scenarios.prompt: Hi James, we're a 25-person DTC skincare brand. Fulfilment and returns are a mess and I don't know where to start.
scenarios.why: The owner already gave the business and headcount, so 'Ask one thing first' yields the two-line diagnosis. Returns counts as a handed-over process, so 'Drop the questions the moment work arrives' moves straight to a map or an SOP. The diagnosis is improvised from general knowledge with no size heuristics and no INFERENCE label, but a capable model gets a useful first session.

scenarios.prompt: I already told you last week we use Notion for SOPs and Airtable for vendors. I don't want 10 questions — just get the Monday ops review running.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks treat memory as all-or-nothing ('Preferences already in memory: skip onboarding'). Partly filled memory is not handled, so the model may re-ask or may skip the metrics source, review destination and timezone that the Monday routine needs. The skill also never says to load ops-run-the-operating-rhythm. The cadence gate ('Switch on only the ones they approve, in their timezone') does hold.

ops-automate-a-workflow.job: size and pilot automation of recurring task
ops-automate-a-workflow.summary: Sizes an automation idea: maps the manual job, checks existing coverage, picks one route from a smallest-first ladder (from no change up to a new agent), scopes a pilot with rollback and a before-after metric, then reports the ROI in hours saved and logs a backlog.
strengths: The route ladder from 'no change' up to a new agent, with 'Say why the smaller options fail', blocks automate-first bias
Maps the job (trigger, inputs, decisions, handoffs, proof of done) before recommending anything
Checks for existing SOPs and automations to avoid running two systems for one job
Pilot has a slice, a window, a rollback and a test before touching live work
Separates estimated savings from measured ones
missing: Net ROI with build, run and maintenance cost, plus payback period
A build path on AutoGPT (blocks, schedule_routine, agent) or a spec handed to engineering
Failure monitoring, alerting, kill switch and a named failure owner
Data, PII and credential review of what the automation touches
Human-in-the-loop for outbound or irreversible automated actions
A control-risk check when the automation removes an approval step
A backlog scoring formula and a decision-brief template

issues.section: Run it on a yes, then measure
issues.quote: Report before-after and the ROI in hours saved.
issues.problem: ROI counts only the benefit. Build effort, tooling or run cost, ongoing maintenance and exception handling are not netted out, and there is no payback period, so a go/no-go can be badly skewed.
issues.fix: Define net ROI as (hours saved x loaded rate + error cost avoided) minus (build + run + maintenance), with payback in weeks. Compute it in bash_exec and label each input FACT or INFERENCE.

issues.section: Run it on a yes, then measure
issues.quote: Run it on a yes, then measure
issues.problem: The skill never says who builds the automation or how. It has no AutoGPT build path (run_block integrations, schedule_routine, a new agent) and no handoff to engineering, even though the persona says James does not do engineering implementation.
issues.fix: Add a build step: name the platform route (existing blocks, a scheduled routine or an agent) or draft a spec for engineering, and state who owns it after launch.

issues.problem: The skill has no automation-specific safeguards. Nothing requires human approval for automated outbound sends or system writes, and nothing covers PII or credential handling, failure alerting, a kill switch, or who is paged when it breaks.
issues.fix: Add rules: automated external actions stay draft-and-approve until the pilot proves them; list the data and credentials touched; define the failure alert, the kill switch and the failure owner before go-live.

issues.section: Run it on a yes, then measure
issues.quote: into the SOP and into the automation backlog with effort and impact on
issues.problem: The backlog has no scoring method, so ranking is subjective.
issues.fix: Score impact as frequency x minutes per run x error cost and effort in build hours, then rank by impact/effort.

issues.section: Pick exactly one route, smallest first
issues.quote: In order: no change; stop or simplify the job; clarify ownership; fix
issues.problem: A broken process should go to ops-map-and-improve-a-process first, but the boundary is not stated. The two skills also share the smallest-first logic, which risks double-loading.
issues.fix: Add: if the job is slow or broken rather than merely manual, load ops-map-and-improve-a-process first and return here only for the automate step.

issues.quote: Save under automations: the decision brief, the pilot read, and the
issues.problem: The decision brief and the pilot read have no defined sections, so outputs vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Add a short template: job map, existing coverage, route chosen and smaller routes rejected, net ROI, pilot scope, test, rollback, owner.

issues.quote: The desired outcome, the current trigger, the steps, the owner, the
issues.problem: Seven inputs are listed with no instruction to ask one at a time or to start from whatever is given. Only volume and owner have fallbacks.
issues.fix: Say to start from what was given, ask only for what changes the route, and ask one question per message.

scenarios.prompt: Every Monday our ops coordinator spends about 3 hours copying Shopify orders into a Google Sheet and emailing each supplier their list. Can we automate this?
scenarios.why: Following the skill yields a job map, the route ladder, a pilot slice with rollback, and ROI of about 3 hours a week marked INFERENCE. It does not weigh build and maintenance time against the saving. It never points to the Sheets and Gmail blocks or a scheduled routine as the build path. It never flags that the automated supplier emails are external sends that need a draft-and-approve step or a monitored failure path.

scenarios.prompt: Our finance lead wants AI to auto-approve vendor invoices under $500. We don't know the monthly volume, and AP is owned by Daniel's team.
scenarios.why: The missing volume gets INFERENCE and 'No owner means nothing automates' stalls correctly. But automating an approval removes a financial control, and nothing prompts a segregation-of-duties or control-risk review, a handoff to Daniel or to ops-controls-and-escalations, or a human-in-the-loop route. The quality of the answer depends on the model's own knowledge.

ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan.job: plan team capacity and headcount against demand
ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan.summary: Company-wide headcount plan: forecasts demand per function from history, converts it to required heads with a shrinkage formula, gaps it against heads and open requisitions, runs base and high scenarios with hiring cost and slip impact, keeps a skills inventory, and tracks monthly.
strengths: Explicit scope boundary: business-wide headcount, not support shift scheduling (which belongs to Robin's workforce-and-capacity-planning)
Forecasts from demand history, never from headcount totals, with the horizon and miss band stated
Shows the math in one block the capacity owner can check
Slip scenarios, loaded cost per hire, an internal-move check before external hiring, and single-point-of-failure roles
Missing data gets a labelled INFERENCE fallback, and requisitions or budgets move only with the capacity owner's yes
missing: A demand-to-workload conversion (volume x effort / productive hours)
Utilization targets by role type
Attrition modelled as backfill, separate from shrinkage
Ramp to productivity and time-to-fill in the gap
Do-nothing and budget-constrained scenarios
A fully loaded cost total against budget, with a handoff to finance
A privacy rule for individual HR data
A plan template

issues.section: Turn the forecast into required heads
issues.quote: shrinkage covers time off, training, and attrition.
issues.problem: Attrition is not shrinkage. Shrinkage is paid time that is not productive, while attrition is lost headcount that needs backfill hires over the horizon. Mixing them gives wrong required-heads figures.
issues.fix: Limit shrinkage to PTO, sick leave, training and meetings. Model attrition separately as expected leavers over the horizon, added to hires needed with time-to-fill.

issues.section: Turn the forecast into required heads
issues.quote: Required heads = base workload heads / (1 - shrinkage/100), where
issues.problem: 'Base workload heads' is never derived. The skill has no demand-to-workload conversion (volume x effort per unit / productive hours per FTE) and no utilization ceiling, so the key step is left to the model.
issues.fix: Add: workload hours = forecast volume x hours per unit; base heads = workload hours / (period hours x target utilization by role, e.g. 75-80% for ICs). Run it in bash_exec and show each input as FACT or INFERENCE.

issues.quote: Heads on hand, open requisitions with start dates, and the shortfall
issues.problem: New hires are counted at full capacity from their start date. Ramp to productivity and time-to-fill do not affect the monthly shortfall.
issues.fix: Apply a ramp curve (for example 25/50/75/100% by month) and time-to-fill when placing hires in the gap table.

issues.quote: Base and high demand. Each carries hiring targets, start-by dates, cost
issues.problem: The scenarios have no downside case, no do-nothing case and no budget-constrained or flat-headcount case, which is where most real headcount debates happen.
issues.fix: Add a do-nothing case and a budget-capped case beside base and high, each with what breaks and the tradeoff.

issues.quote: data need named. No shrinkage figure means you plan at 20% and say so.
issues.problem: A single 20% default ignores role mix. Interrupt-driven and support-like roles often run at 30% or more.
issues.fix: Give a default by role type, labelled INFERENCE, and ask for actual PTO and training data to replace it.

issues.problem: The skill has no privacy rule for individual-level HR data (salaries, sick days, per-person skills inventory) and no handoff for budget sign-off (Daniel) or requisitions (Sofia).
issues.fix: Plan at role and function level, keep named compensation and health data out of shared artefacts, and route budget and requisition drafts to the right teammate and approver.

issues.quote: Save the capacity plan under capacity, dated, with its scenarios.
issues.problem: The plan has no output template, so the forecast, math block, gap table and scenarios come out in a different shape each run.
issues.fix: Add a template: assumptions table, demand forecast per function, required-heads math, monthly gap table, scenario table, skills and SPOF list.

scenarios.prompt: We're a 40-person agency. The weighted pipeline says delivery hours go up about 30% next quarter. Do we need to hire, and how many per function?
scenarios.why: The skill forecasts per function, applies the formula with 20% shrinkage flagged as assumed, gaps against current heads and runs base and high scenarios. It never says how to turn 30% more hours into 'base workload heads' (productive hours per FTE at a target utilization) and counts new hires at full output from their start date. The model may plan at 100% utilization, the pitfall Toran's version warns about.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV with every employee's name, salary and sick days. Attrition is 25%. The board wants flat headcount but sales wants 5 more AEs next quarter.
scenarios.why: The skill defines shrinkage as 'time off, training, and attrition', so the model divides by (1 - 0.45) and inflates required heads about 1.8x instead of modelling backfill hires. It has no budget-constrained or flat-headcount scenario to set against the sales ask, no privacy handling for named salary and sick-day data, and no handoff to Daniel for budget or Sofia for the AE requisitions.

ops-controls-and-escalations.job: track controls, evidence, and escalation paths
ops-controls-and-escalations.summary: Builds an operational control checklist with evidence links, draws a one-page escalation path with severity levels and response targets, tracks findings to evidence-based closure, and re-runs the checklist monthly for a pass rate.
strengths: Every control needs an evidence link, and a control or finding closes only on evidence
Reads existing controls and past findings and says them back before adding anything
The escalation path is kept to one page with names and triggers ('no org-chart theater')
Unknown standards are marked UNKNOWN rather than invented
missing: A risk-control matrix with control objective and type
Test of design versus operating effectiveness, with sampling
Segregation-of-duties checks
A SEV-level criteria table and post-incident review
Boundaries and handoffs to Lena, Daniel, Robin and counsel
A 'not legal advice' statement and flags for regulatory reporting deadlines
Root cause and retest before closing a finding

issues.quote: No policy named means you draft against common practice and mark the
issues.problem: For audits and inspections the skill drafts from 'common practice' with no handoff to Lena (compliance), Daniel (financial controls and close), Robin (case-level escalations) or counsel. It also never states the persona's no-legal-advice rule, so regulatory interpretation can slip in unflagged.
issues.fix: Add a boundary section: regulatory interpretation and framework scoping go to Lena or counsel, financial controls to Daniel, and live case escalations to Robin. State that James designs operational controls and paths and does not give legal or regulatory advice.

issues.quote: Each control with what it checks, how often, who runs it, what evidence
issues.problem: Controls are not linked to the risk they mitigate, and there is no control type (preventive or detective, manual or automated), no key-control flag, no segregation-of-duties check, and no test method or sample size. The monthly 'pass rate' therefore has no defined basis.
issues.fix: Use a risk-control matrix row: risk, control objective, control, type, frequency, owner, test step, sample size, evidence location, last tested, result.

issues.quote: asks who handles what when something breaks, or wants audit or inspection readiness
issues.problem: One skill carries two jobs: control and audit readiness, and incident escalation design. When Robin is also hired, the triggers ('severity levels and on-call') can collide with escalations-and-incidents.
issues.fix: Split into two skills, or state that this skill designs the path and SLA framework while live incidents go to Robin.

issues.quote: severity levels, response targets, and the comms line. One page, names
issues.problem: The skill gives no severity definitions or example criteria and no post-incident review loop, so every path defines SEV levels from scratch and the lessons never feed back into controls.
issues.fix: Ship a SEV1-SEV4 criteria table with response targets, and add a post-incident review step that opens findings.

issues.quote: Each finding with severity, owner, due date, and the corrective action.
issues.problem: Findings have no root cause and no retest step, so a corrective action can close the finding without proof the control now works.
issues.fix: Add root cause and a retest with fresh evidence before closure.

issues.quote: on-call coverage without the owner's yes.
issues.problem: The only approval gate is reassigning on-call. Publishing the escalation path, naming people on it, and sending incident comms are not gated.
issues.fix: Extend the rule: the path and any comms stay drafts until the owner approves, and named people are told only after approval.

issues.quote: Pass rate, findings opened and closed, and the one control fix for next
issues.problem: The monthly re-run does not say how to test (sampling, walkthrough, evidence freshness), so the pass rate can amount to checking that evidence links exist.
issues.fix: Define the monthly test: re-perform or sample N items per control and check that evidence is dated inside the period.

scenarios.prompt: We have a SOC 2 Type I audit in 8 weeks. What do we need to have ready?
scenarios.why: The skill reads existing controls and writes a checklist with owners, frequency and evidence location, and it opens findings with severity and due dates. It gives no guidance on mapping to the Trust Services Criteria, on design versus operating-effectiveness testing, or on evidence sampling. It does not hand off to Lena, who owns compliance in this roster, so the result is a generic checklist rather than audit-ready prep.

scenarios.prompt: We had a forklift incident in the warehouse last week. I need an escalation path, and I'm worried about an OSHA inspection. We have no written safety policies.
scenarios.why: 'No policy named' leads to drafting against common practice with the standard marked UNKNOWN, and the escalation path gets severity levels and a comms line. Nothing flags regulatory reporting deadlines or routes the incident to counsel or a safety professional. Nothing says the output is not legal advice, and there is no post-incident review, which a regulated safety event requires.

ops-govern-a-program.job: govern cross-functional program with RAID log
ops-govern-a-program.summary: Stands up governance for a cross-functional program: a SMART goal, milestones with owners and dates, a dependency map and change rule, a RAID log with owner, date, status, priority and escalation trigger, a weekly one-line-per-item status read, and evidence-gated promote/hold/kill phase gates.
strengths: Reads the existing plan and reports its R/Y/G state rather than rebuilding it
Scales down: one workstream gets a simple plan, not padded governance
A full RAID log: assumptions with validators, dependencies with the blocked party, P1-P3 priority, and trigger signals that turn a risk into an issue
A change rule: scope, date or owner moves go through the program owner
Phase gates on quoted evidence with a plain promote, hold or kill call
Never closes a risk on its own say-so
missing: RACI and decision rights per workstream
Baseline versus forecast dates, and the critical path
R/Y/G definitions and escalation thresholds
Gate criteria agreed up front, with the sponsor deciding
Unowned items surfaced rather than dropped
Program close-out and benefits realisation
A status report template and approval before circulating it

issues.quote: Every entry carries an owner and a date, or it is not on the log.
issues.problem: Unowned risks and issues are usually the most dangerous, and this rule drops them from the log instead of surfacing them.
issues.fix: Log them as UNOWNED, show them first in the weekly read, and escalate them to the program owner for assignment.

issues.quote: Promote, hold, or kill — said plainly, with the reason.
issues.problem: The skill does not say who decides a gate. James should recommend and the sponsor or program owner decides, and gate criteria must be agreed before the gate, not after it.
issues.fix: Add: criteria are set and approved when the phase opens; James presents the evidence and a recommendation; the program owner or sponsor makes the call, logged with date and approver.

issues.quote: Say back what you found: milestones by red/yellow/green (R/Y/G), open
issues.problem: R/Y/G has no definitions or slip thresholds, so statuses are subjective and not comparable week to week.
issues.fix: Define R/Y/G by forecast slip against baseline (for example green on track, yellow slip within buffer or recoverable, red misses the gate) and apply it consistently.

issues.quote: (SMART) line. Milestones with an owner and a date each. Dependencies
issues.problem: The plan has no RACI or decision rights, no baseline versus forecast dates, no critical path and no steering cadence. Weekly 'slipped by how far' needs a baseline.
issues.fix: Add a RACI per workstream, baseline and forecast date columns, the critical path through the dependencies, and the steering meeting cadence.

issues.quote: entry also carries a status (open, monitoring, closed), a priority P1
issues.problem: 'P1 to P3 from likelihood times impact' gives no scale or cut-offs.
issues.fix: Specify a 1-3 or 1-5 scale and the score bands that map to P1, P2 and P3.

issues.quote: What moved, what slipped and by how far, what is newly at risk, and the
issues.problem: The weekly report has no audience, no destination and no approval gate for circulating it, and setting it up as a routine is not mentioned.
issues.fix: Add the destination, a draft-then-owner-approval step before posting, and an optional schedule_routine switched on only with approval.

issues.problem: The skill has no program close-out: no benefits-realisation check against the SMART goal, no lessons learned, no archiving of the RAID log.
issues.fix: Add a close-out step: goal met or not with evidence, benefits owner, lessons learned, and residual risks handed to business as usual.

scenarios.prompt: We're launching in Canada in Q1: legal entity, payroll, a 3PL, and marketing. Owners are Sam, Priya and Lee. Set up governance and tell me what's at risk.
scenarios.why: 'Write the plan' gives a SMART goal, milestones with owners and dates, dependencies and the change rule. 'Hold the RAID log' produces owned, prioritised entries with escalation triggers, and the weekly report format is clear. A capable model produces a credible program pack; only RACI and the critical path would be missing.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a messy Asana export: 140 tasks, half with no owner. The CEO wants a go/no-go on Phase 2 by Friday.
scenarios.why: 'Never rebuild a plan they already run' and 'Say back what you found' fit this request. But 'Every entry carries an owner and a date, or it is not on the log' pushes ownerless risks off the log instead of flagging them. 'Gate the gates' assumes criteria already exist and does not say who decides, so the model may issue a go/no-go itself rather than recommend one to the CEO.

ops-map-and-improve-a-process.job: map process and fix the bottleneck
ops-map-and-improve-a-process.summary: A DMAIC-lite process improvement: a high-level COPIS/SIPOC map, a named bottleneck with evidence, 5-whys or fishbone root cause, fixes proposed smallest-first (kill, simplify, reorder, automate) with effort, impact and baseline, a pilot on approval with rollback, and a control metric checked at 30, 60 and 90 days.
strengths: An ordered define, measure, analyse, improve, control loop that closes with a control metric at 30, 60 and 90 days
The bottleneck must be named with the step, the wait and the evidence; unsupported causes are labelled INFERENCE
Fixes go smallest-first (kill, simplify, reorder, then automate), each with effort, owner, impact and baseline
Pilot on approval with a slice, a window and a rollback; the SOP is updated when a fix sticks
Refuses to present a guessed cycle time as measured
missing: A step-level value-stream or swimlane map with touch, wait, rework and flow efficiency
Scope boundaries (start trigger and end state)
A baseline measurement method: timestamp analysis in the sandbox, or a manual sample
Validation of the map with step owners
Waste categories and future-state design moves
A run chart or control chart with a reaction plan
Routing to ops-automate-a-workflow and ops-write-an-sop
Map and improvement-log templates

issues.quote: (SIPOC) map: the process in four to five high-level steps, then
issues.problem: A 4-5-step SIPOC is a scoping tool. It is too coarse to find where work waits or is reworked, and the skill asks for no step-level measures such as touch time, wait time, % complete and accurate, WIP or flow efficiency.
issues.fix: After the SIPOC, draw a step-level swimlane or value-stream map with touch time, wait time and first-pass yield per step, and compute flow efficiency, labelling each figure FACT or UNKNOWN.

issues.quote: Work in customers-outputs-process-inputs-suppliers (COPIS) order, the
issues.problem: The skill says 'COPIS order' but then prescribes process, then outputs, customers, inputs, suppliers, which is not COPIS and contradicts the heading.
issues.fix: Pick one: 'Start with the customer and the output they need (COPIS), then the process steps, inputs and suppliers', and drop the SIPOC aside.

issues.quote: Where work waits, where it gets reworked, where one person is the
issues.problem: The skill gives no method to measure waits or rework when data exists (timestamped exports) and no fallback when it does not (a manual sample of 10-20 items).
issues.fix: If an export with timestamps exists, compute per-step durations and queues in bash_exec. Otherwise time a sample of 10-20 items and label the result as a sample.

issues.quote: Show the map in chat before you diagnose anything. The map is the
