issues.problem: Scope boundaries (start trigger, end state, in and out of scope) are not set, and the map is not checked with the people who run each step. Disputes over where the process starts go unresolved.
issues.fix: Fix the start trigger and end state first, and confirm the map with each step owner (or mark the step UNVERIFIED) before diagnosing.

issues.quote: Kill the step, simplify it, reorder it, then automate it — in that
issues.problem: The fix list has no waste lens (waiting, rework, handoffs, over-processing) and no routing to ops-automate-a-workflow when automation is the chosen fix, which duplicates sizing logic.
issues.fix: Tag each candidate with its waste type, and hand automation fixes to ops-automate-a-workflow for sizing.

issues.quote: Name the ongoing control metric, its owner, and the check cadence that
issues.problem: The control has no variation handling (run chart or noise band) and no reaction plan when the metric drifts back.
issues.fix: Plot the control metric as a run chart against the baseline, define the drift threshold, and name the action and owner when it is breached.

issues.quote: Save the map and the improvement log under processes, dated, one folder
issues.problem: The map and improvement log have no templates, so reruns cannot compare against the last saved one consistently.
issues.fix: Add templates for the map table (step, owner, handoff, touch, wait, rework) and the improvement log (fix, waste type, baseline, target, pilot window, result, control status).

scenarios.prompt: Customer onboarding takes three weeks from signed contract to go-live and customers are complaining. Where's the bottleneck?
scenarios.why: The skill takes the pain and cycle time as inputs, shows the map with owners and handoffs, lists bottleneck candidates with evidence, root-causes the chosen one, and proposes fixes smallest-first with baselines. The pilot and 30/60/90 control carry through, and UNKNOWN labels cover missing figures. The map is coarse, but the flow still gives a senior-shaped answer.

scenarios.prompt: Invoice approvals are slow. Here's a Jira export of 800 tickets with status timestamps, but finance, procurement and ops disagree on where the process starts and ends.
scenarios.why: The skill gives no step to set scope boundaries (start trigger, end state) and no instruction to compute per-step wait and touch time from the timestamps with bash_exec. A 4-5-step COPIS map cannot absorb 800 tickets of flow data. The model may produce a qualitative map and a guessed bottleneck instead of a measured one.

icp-and-segmentation.job: define ICP and tier target segments
icp-and-segmentation.summary: A 65-line single-file skill. It has Zara define an ICP in six blocks from best customers, split fit from intent, sort accounts into strategic, growth and watch tiers, count segments (with Apollo when connected), name the segments to stop chasing, and save a dated ICP memo.
strengths: Six ICP blocks cover firmographics and technographics, trigger event, personas including the blocker, required capabilities, fit signals and anti-signals
'Largest is not best': it builds from retention, deal size, health and advocacy
The fit-versus-ready split adds an intent layer on top of firmographics
Each tier carries its motion and its graduation or kill bar; deprioritized segments are named with a reason
Honest fallbacks: a segment that can't be counted stays a hypothesis, and it never invents a customer, a segment size or a win rate
missing: Quantitative best-customer and over-index analysis with sample sizes
Anti-signals derived from churned and closed-lost accounts
A segment attractiveness versus ability-to-win matrix for ranking segments
A pain- or jobs-based segmentation layer beyond firmographics
Shipped ICP memo template and Best/Good/Bad scoring rubric
A test plan for unvalidated segments (hypothesis, experiment, kill bar)
A PII-minimisation rule for customer exports

issues.section: Define the ICP in six blocks
issues.quote: retention, deal size, health, advocacy — never the whole base; largest
issues.problem: It names what 'best' means but gives no method to find best customers in the data or to derive fit signals and anti-signals from won, lost and churned accounts. Nothing uses the sandbox for the analysis.
issues.fix: Add a numbered analysis step: define the best-customer cut (for example, retained over 12 months and top quartile by NRR or ACV); in bash_exec, compute attribute share and lift for best customers against the whole base and against lost or churned accounts, with n per cell; promote only attributes with lift and adequate n into fit signals, and the churn and loss over-indexers into anti-signals.

issues.quote: The ICP memo with segments and targeting priorities: the ranked account
issues.problem: The deliverable is described only in prose. There is no memo template and no layout for the Best/Good/Bad Fit rubric, so outputs will vary run to run and cannot easily be reused for routing.
issues.fix: Ship templates/icp-memo.md with sections for the six blocks with evidence and labels, the tier table (tier, why, motion, entry and kill bar, count), anti-segments, and a scoring rubric table (criterion, Best, Good, Bad, source field).

issues.quote: Split fit accounts from ready accounts: an intent layer (behavioral and
issues.problem: It calls for behavioral and surge intent without naming any source the platform has; there is no intent-data block, and there is no fallback. The model may invent 'surge' signals.
issues.fix: Name the sources that are actually available (HubSpot web and email engagement, Apollo job-change and hiring signals, web_search for funding and leadership news) and say that with no intent source the ready layer stays UNKNOWN.

issues.quote: and never brief the same list twice — fold in what the scorecard routine
issues.problem: This is copy-paste from competitive-intelligence: the weekly scorecard routine does not log ICP lists, so the instruction points at nothing.
issues.fix: Replace it with: read the last saved ICP memo first and show a dated diff of what changed and why.

issues.quote: Use this when the user asks who to sell to, names a segment, or hands over
issues.problem: 'Names a segment' collides with gtm-planning-and-market-entry ('a new market or segment'), and an industry-named request collides with vertical-industry-plays, so routing is ambiguous.
issues.fix: State the boundary: this skill chooses and ranks targets; planning motion and coverage for a chosen segment goes to gtm-planning-and-market-entry; a dedicated industry motion goes to vertical-industry-plays.

issues.quote: Revisit it quarterly — an ICP goes stale after
issues.problem: It asserts an unsourced shelf-life benchmark, in a persona that forbids unsourced numbers. It also sits oddly next to the quarterly revisit.
issues.fix: Frame it as a review trigger instead: quarterly review, plus immediate review on a win-loss theme shift or a tier missing its bar.

issues.problem: There is no handling for personal data in customer and contact exports. The memo and account list could carry contact-level PII into saved files.
issues.fix: Keep analysis at account level, drop contact PII from saved memos, and keep raw exports out of shared folders.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our HubSpot closed-won and closed-lost export for the last two years (about 180 deals) plus the churn list. Who should we actually be selling to?
scenarios.why: The six blocks and three tiers give the memo a sensible shape, and 'Build from best customers' points the right way. But no step says how to define 'best' (for example, top quartile by NRR or LTV), how to join churn and lost data, or how to measure attribute over-index against the base with n per cell in bash_exec. So the model will likely eyeball the data and produce plausible but weakly evidenced tiers.

scenarios.prompt: We have 12 customers, 5 of them unpaid pilots. The CEO wants enterprise healthcare, sales says mid-market SaaS. Tell me our ICP; Apollo isn't connected.
scenarios.why: Fallbacks correctly say to mark lines INFERENCE and to use graduation bars rather than false precision. The skill does not say to exclude or weight unpaid pilots, how to settle competing stakeholder hypotheses (for example, with a time-boxed segment test and a kill bar), or when to hand the healthcare question to vertical-industry-plays.

opportunity-sizing-and-business-case.job: size market and build investment case
opportunity-sizing-and-business-case.summary: A 57-line single-file skill. It sizes TAM, SAM and SOM with at least two methods, flags gaps between methods and implausible SOM, builds an investment case (return, payback, NRR and LTV/CAC), stresses it under Base, Adverse and Opportunity scenarios, and returns a fund, fund-with-conditions or pass verdict with a saved model and assumptions log.
strengths: Requires two methods and names the gap between them as the honest range
Every band carries method, source and date, and uses an Apollo count as a real bottom-up denominator when available
Scenarios carry the breaking driver and a leading indicator; 'never silently rebaseline'
Clear verdict vocabulary: fund, fund-with-conditions or pass, with finance validating before money moves
Strong no-invention rule with FACT, INFERENCE and UNKNOWN labeling
missing: Capacity- and ramp-driven SOM and bookings model
Time-phased cash flow, breakeven quarter, and NPV at a stated discount rate
Owner-set investment hurdles driving the verdict
Defined evidence grades
Sensitivity analysis on the top drivers
Cannibalization and opportunity cost of the bet
Growth projection of TAM and SAM over the horizon
Shipped business-case and assumptions-log templates

issues.quote: Investment, expected return, payback, and the net revenue retention,
issues.problem: It lists metrics but gives no model structure. There is no time-phasing, no hiring or ramp capacity, no CAC payback or LTV formulas, and no discounting, so a GTM bet like new reps or a new region cannot be modelled correctly.
issues.fix: Add a quarter-by-quarter model spec: investment by line, capacity-driven bookings (heads x ramp curve x quota x attainment), gross margin, CAC payback = CAC / (new ARR x GM%), LTV/CAC, cumulative cash and breakeven quarter. Compute it in bash_exec, or in Sheets when connected.

issues.quote: The verdict and the risks: fund, fund-with-conditions, or pass, each with
issues.problem: The verdict has no decision rule, and 'evidence grade' is never defined, so two runs on the same data can reach different verdicts.
issues.fix: Define evidence grades (A = owner or system data, B = dated third-party source, C = assumption), and tie the verdict to owner-set hurdles (for example, payback under N months and LTV/CAC over X). Ask for the hurdle once if it is missing.

issues.quote: the model — a sheet when Sheets is connected — the assumptions log, and
issues.problem: No template is shipped for the case document, the sizing table or the assumptions log, so the output format is improvised every time.
issues.fix: Ship templates/business-case.md (ask, sizing table with method and source per band, unit economics, phased P&L, scenarios, risks, verdict) and an assumptions-log CSV layout (assumption, value, label, source, date, sensitivity).

issues.quote: year one as needing extraordinary proof — 1–5% is the usual range for a
issues.problem: It hardcodes an unsourced share benchmark in a skill that forbids unsourced numbers. It also leaves SOM as a share heuristic instead of constraining it by go-to-market capacity.
issues.fix: Label it a heuristic, and require SOM to be the lower of the share heuristic and capacity-based bookings from the business-case model.

issues.section: Bound the market in three bands
issues.quote: top-down, bottom-up, or value-theory, said plainly.
issues.problem: The methods are named but not specified. There is no formula for bottom-up (accounts x ACV x adoption), no guidance on finding top-down sources with web_search, and no handling of paywalled analyst figures quoted secondhand.
issues.fix: Give one-line formulas per method, direct top-down research through web_search and web_fetch, and mark secondhand analyst numbers as secondary with their original publisher and date.

issues.quote: Base, Adverse, Opportunity. Each grade gets the driver that breaks it and
issues.problem: There is no single-variable sensitivity on the top drivers, and 'grade' is used for scenarios, which reads as confusing next to 'evidence grade'.
issues.fix: Add a sensitivity table (or tornado) on the top three drivers, and rename 'grade' to 'scenario'.

issues.quote: Use this when the user asks how big an opportunity is, names TAM, SAM, or
issues.problem: This duplicates Toran's market-size-estimation, which is proposed for Zara, and alex's product-strategy-and-bets business case. The description does not say it is the GTM-bet version.
issues.fix: On merge, keep this one: Toran's uses $ARGUMENTS, which is a poor platform fit. Fold in Toran's growth-projection and assumption-mapping sections, and state in the description that product build-or-not cases go to Alex.

scenarios.prompt: Give me TAM/SAM/SOM for our AP-automation product for US mid-market construction firms; I need it for the board deck next week.
scenarios.why: Three bands, each with method, source and date, at least two methods, an Apollo bottom-up count when connected, and the 3x delta flag are enough for a capable model to produce a defensible, triangulated range with its sources.

scenarios.prompt: Should we spend $400k to hire 2 AEs and an SDR to open the UK? We have zero UK customers, US ACV is $18k, and no idea of UK conversion.
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly says to size the ceiling and flag the case as direction-only. But 'Build the business case' gives no capacity or ramp model (reps x ramped quota x attainment), no cash-flow timeline or payback formula, and no hurdle for fund versus pass, so the verdict will rest on loose narrative math.

positioning-and-messaging.summary: A 64-line single-file skill. It builds positioning from win-loss evidence using Dunford's five components in order, adds the three whys narrative, a message house with claims never to make, per-persona variants by buying stage, and substitute objection counters, then saves a positioning doc per audience after one round of edits.
strengths: Dunford's five components in the correct order, derived from best-fit customers only, with bad-fit voices filtered out
Win-loss and call evidence read before any claim is drafted
Three whys each carry proof or a gap flag
Message house includes the claims we will never make, with reasons
A persona x buying-stage matrix with objection pre-handles, and one round of edits before saving; a rewrite rather than an append when strategy shifts
missing: Category strategy decision (existing category, subcategory, or new category)
Substantiation rules for comparative and superlative claims
Message validation and testing plan with success metrics
Shipped positioning-doc and message-house templates
Customer-quote permission rule
Explicit handoff for copy production (homepage, ads) to marketing or copywriting

issues.quote: the target customer characteristics, and the market category you compete
issues.problem: The market category is set in one line, with no decision on category strategy: head-to-head in an existing category, a subcategory, or creating a new one. That choice is the highest-stakes call in positioning.
issues.fix: Add a decision step: test two or three candidate category frames against what best-fit buyers already search for and compare with, choose between existing category, subcategory, or new category using stated criteria, and record the rejected frames with reasons.

issues.quote: No proof means the claim stays out or ships flagged UNKNOWN.
issues.problem: 'Ships flagged UNKNOWN' allows an unproven claim into a deliverable that feeds customer-facing copy. There is also no substantiation rule for comparative or superlative claims ('only', 'fastest').
issues.fix: Unproven claims may appear only in internal drafts, marked UNKNOWN. Comparative and superlative claims need dated evidence and the owner's (or legal's) sign-off before any external use.

issues.quote: The positioning doc plus the message house per audience, shown in chat.
issues.problem: There is no template for the positioning doc, message house or persona-by-stage matrix, so structure and length will vary widely.
issues.fix: Ship templates/positioning-doc.md (spine table, three whys with proof, category rationale) and templates/message-house.md (roof, three pillars x proof, never-claim list, persona x stage grid).

issues.quote: counter in rep register. Two counters max per objection, each under 30
issues.problem: This nearly duplicates field-enablement-content's objection rule and competitive-intelligence's counters, so there are three places to maintain the same objection library.
issues.fix: Keep a short substitute check here that validates the positioning, and route the full objection library and talk tracks to field-enablement-content.

issues.quote: Quote a customer line or a call excerpt
issues.problem: Customer quotes and call excerpts are placed into messaging variants with no check that the customer permits attribution or public use.
issues.fix: Keep quotes anonymised internally. Public attribution requires a recorded customer permission.

issues.problem: There is no validation step. Messaging ships without testing against buyers, reps, or conversion and win-rate signals.
issues.fix: Add a validation step: five-buyer or rep message tests, or an A/B headline test, and name the metric that will show the positioning is working.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our homepage copy and three win notes. Sharpen our positioning and give me a message house for ops leads and for CFOs.
scenarios.why: It reads the win notes first, sets the five-part spine from best-fit customers, adds the three whys with proof or gap flags, and builds a message house with pillars and proof plus per-persona and per-stage variants. That is a senior-quality flow, and the model knows the frameworks it names.

scenarios.prompt: We're repositioning from 'AI chatbot' to 'support automation platform'. Sales wants to say we're 'the only SOC 2 AI agent', we have no win-loss data, and marketing needs the homepage hero by Friday.
scenarios.why: Fallbacks keep unproven claims out and default to 'doing nothing' as the alternative. But there is no step for choosing a category strategy (existing category, subcategory, or new category), which is the actual question here. There is no substantiation check on superlatives like 'the only', and no handoff for homepage copy to marketing or copywriting.

pricing-and-packaging.job: recommend pricing model, tiers, and discount guardrails
pricing-and-packaging.summary: A 69-line single-file skill. It restates the current pricing model (grounded in Stripe plan mix when connected), prescribes WTP research methods (Van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, conjoint), reads competitor price pages verbatim with fetch dates, recommends a value metric and tiers, sets discount approval bands with give-gets, models mix impact and grandfathering, and drafts a rollout note.
strengths: Requires the current model to be said back in three lines before anything changes
Competitor read uses vendor wording with fetch dates; call-for-pricing stays UNKNOWN
Discount bands prescribe give-gets; anything outside the bands routes to the owner and is never self-approved
Mix-impact table specifies revenue, margin in currency and percent, and grandfathering cost
Rollout note covers existing customers, the grandfathering rule, and a talk track for the first hard call; it never announces a price
missing: Value-metric selection criteria and a packaging fence matrix
Proxy WTP methods when surveys are infeasible
Behavioral response (churn, downgrade, expansion) in the mix model, with sensitivity
Contract notice periods and legal checks for price increases
A pricing experiment design for PLG and self-serve
Clear boundary and handoff with deal-desk and finance experts
Price-increase communication sequence

issues.quote: Use this when the user names pricing, packaging, tiers, or discounts, or
issues.problem: 'Discounts' and 'deal terms' pull single-deal discount requests into strategic pricing. That duplicates Daniel's deal-economics-and-pricing-guardrails (the same bands, mix and grandfathering language) and Max's objection-and-negotiation, and the description never draws the boundary.
issues.fix: Scope this skill to list price, packaging and discount policy. Route a live deal's discount ask to the deal-economics owner or the AE via consult_teammate, and say so in the description.

issues.section: Measure willingness to pay before you price
issues.quote: The Van Westendorp four questions (too expensive, getting expensive, a
issues.problem: It requires survey research that most small teams cannot run, and gives no decision point or proxy path. Surveys to customers and prospects are external outreach, yet there is no draft-and-approve gate.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: if a survey is infeasible, use proxies (discount distribution, win-loss on price, churn and downgrade by tier, price reactions in calls) labeled INFERENCE. Survey instruments are drafted and sent only on the owner's yes.

issues.quote: One table across tiers: current vs proposed, revenue, margin in currency
issues.problem: The mix model is static. It has no assumptions for churn, downgrade, upgrade or new-logo conversion response to the change and no sensitivity range, so any price rise looks like pure upside.
issues.fix: Add labeled behavioral assumptions per tier with a low, base and high sensitivity table, computed in bash_exec or in Sheets when connected.

issues.quote: rollout note: what changes for existing customers, the grandfathering
issues.problem: There is no check of contract terms, renewal notice periods, or auto-renewal and consumer-protection rules before changing prices for existing customers.
issues.fix: Require a contract and notice-period check, and a legal review flag for regulated or consumer plans, before the rollout note is final.

issues.section: Measure willingness to pay before you price
issues.quote: Revisit pricing quarterly
issues.problem: This conflates the review cadence with the change cadence. Quarterly price changes erode trust and are not standard practice.
issues.fix: Review pricing signals quarterly, and change list price only on a triggered decision, typically no more than once a year.

issues.quote: to adapt: 0–15% rep or manager same-day; 16–25% deal desk on a 4-hour
issues.problem: The unsourced default bands are presented before the owner's own policy is asked for, and they duplicate Daniel's bands, which risks two conflicting policies in one team.
issues.fix: Read the saved discount policy from memory or ask for it first. Present these as illustrative only, and keep one policy source shared with the finance expert.

issues.quote: Value metric, tier shape, and what moves up or down a tier.
issues.problem: There are no criteria for choosing a value metric and no packaging matrix format (feature fences per tier, usage limits, add-ons).
issues.fix: Add value-metric criteria (scales with value, easy to understand and predict, hard to game) and a tier-by-feature fence table template.

scenarios.prompt: Competitor X just raised prices. Here's our price list and 6 months of closed deals with discounts; Stripe is connected. Are we underpriced, and are reps over-discounting?
scenarios.why: It reads Stripe plan mix as the FACT layer, says back the model in three lines, reads competitor pages verbatim with fetch dates, sets discount bands with give-gets, and builds the current-versus-proposed mix table. Together these cover the question well.

scenarios.prompt: A rep wants 40% off a $60k deal closing Friday. Separately, should we raise list prices 20% for everyone next quarter? No margin data, Stripe not connected.
scenarios.why: The guardrails correctly route anything over 35% to the owner, and the fallback holds the verdict without a margin floor. But the description invites the single-deal ask, which belongs with Daniel's deal-economics and Max's negotiation work. The price-increase path has no churn or downgrade assumptions, no contract notice-period check, and no proxy when WTP surveys are infeasible.

sales-marketing-alignment-and-sla.job: define lead handoff SLA between sales and marketing
sales-marketing-alignment-and-sla.summary: A 71-line single-file skill. It defines the Lead-MQL-SAL-SQL-Opportunity lifecycle with ownership and reason codes, a 100-point lead-scoring starter with backtesting, handoff and bounce rules, speed-to-lead time bars, a joint scorecard with starter bars, and a feedback loop, then delivers an SLA doc for both sides to edit and the approver to sign.
strengths: SAL with reason codes as the accountability mechanism, and clear ownership of lifecycle stage versus lead status
Entry bars in observable terms, one definition per stage signed by both sides
Scoring is backtested against real wins and losses, with decay of stale activity
Speed-to-lead as a non-negotiable bar, with a same-day escalation owner
Feedback loop: weekly quality grading with quotes and monthly tuning on triangulated evidence; published benchmarks treated as direction-only
missing: Root-cause diagnosis before prescribing an SLA
A small-volume or early-stage variant without points scoring
SQL defined by discovery criteria rather than score
Attribution rule for sourced versus influenced pipeline
Recycle and nurture path for rejected leads
Buying-group or account-level handoff
Approval gate for CRM workflow and routing changes
Shipped SLA doc, scorecard and routing-log templates

issues.quote: or asks why marketing pipeline never closes. Start from the lead tiers
issues.problem: The skill claims the 'why doesn't pipeline close' question but has no diagnostic step. It jumps straight to designing an SLA, even when the cause is ICP fit, attribution, or deal execution.
issues.fix: Add step 1: diagnose stage conversion by source and segment, lead aging, disposition reason codes and the ICP fit of MQLs. Decide whether the issue is fit, speed, follow-up or measurement before drafting. Route pure metric reads to gtm-performance-diagnostics and fit problems to icp-and-segmentation.

issues.quote: at 65–75, SQL at 85. Weight behavior over demographics, decay stale
issues.problem: Making SQL a score threshold conflicts with the skill's own SAL/SQL design. SQL is normally set by sales discovery criteria, not points, so the rule muddles who owns qualification.
issues.fix: Use the score only to gate MQL. Define SQL as sales-confirmed qualification criteria (for example, a subset of BANT or MEDDICC agreed with sales), and explain what the '10 negative' points mean.

issues.quote: activity, and backtest the bars against the last 100 won and 100 lost
issues.problem: There is no path for low data volumes. Early-stage teams lack 100 wins and losses, so the prescribed backtest and points model cannot run.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: under roughly 30 wins, skip points scoring and use rules-based routing (ICP fit plus a hand-raise); backtest whatever exists in bash_exec and label the bars INFERENCE.

issues.quote: First response inside 4 business hours — inbound inside 5 minutes, social
issues.problem: The time bars are ambiguous. It is unclear which leads get 4 business hours when inbound gets 5 minutes, and whether '6 touches over 14 days' applies to every source.
issues.fix: Present the time bars as a table by lead source and tier: first response, touch cadence, disposition deadline and escalation owner.

issues.quote: a breached bar escalates to the named owner the same day.
issues.problem: The escalation, and implementing scoring and routing in HubSpot, are external side effects, but the skill has no draft-and-approve gate for CRM configuration changes or escalation messages.
issues.fix: Draft HubSpot property, workflow and routing changes and escalation messages as a change list; apply or send only on the owner's yes, and log the approval.

issues.quote: influenced pipeline split with named proofs. Starter bars: MQL-to-SAL
issues.problem: The sourced-versus-influenced split is the classic alignment fight, but the attribution rule is never defined, so the scorecard will be disputed.
issues.fix: Require one agreed attribution rule (for example, first touch for sourced, and any touch within N days before opportunity creation for influenced) written into the SLA.

issues.problem: There is no recycle or nurture path for rejected or disqualified leads, and no account or buying-group handoff for multi-contact B2B deals.
issues.fix: Add a recycle rule (the reason code drives nurture re-entry and a re-score window) and an account-level handoff when several contacts from one account engage.

scenarios.prompt: Sales says our MQLs are junk and marketing says sales never follows up. Here's our HubSpot funnel export. Write us an SLA both teams will sign.
scenarios.why: It covers shared stage definitions with observable entry bars, SAL reason codes, a scoring model backtested on wins and losses, handoff payload, time bars, the joint scorecard, and the weekly and monthly feedback loop. Both sides edit before the approver signs. That is a complete, senior-recognisable SLA.

scenarios.prompt: We're 6 people with one AE, no marketing automation, and about 40 demo requests a month, mostly from our free tool. Marketing pipeline isn't closing. Fix it.
scenarios.why: Fallbacks cover the missing CRM with a routing-log template. But the skill never diagnoses why pipeline doesn't close (fit of free-tool leads, speed, or follow-up) before prescribing an SLA. It also applies a 100-point model and a backtest on '100 won and 100 lost' that this company cannot have, with no small-volume alternative.

vertical-industry-plays.job: build a vertical industry go-to-market playbook
vertical-industry-plays.summary: A 56-line single-file skill. For a named industry it writes a one-page narrative, maps incumbents, partners, analysts and the buying committee, stacks proof and compliance badges as dated milestones, writes a vertical play, and sequences entry from lighthouse accounts to a repeatable motion.
strengths: Industry narrative written in the sector's own language, with an adoption journey from first team to standard
Incumbent lines graded confirmed, likely or unknown, with link and date
Missing proof becomes a dated milestone with an owner
Lighthouse-then-repeatable sequencing with entry and exit criteria
Partner-led fallback when direct access is missing; never invents reference customers or badges
missing: Vertical selection and prioritisation scoring, including a 'don't verticalise' outcome
Product-gap and integration requirements per vertical
Vertical-specific regulations and procurement cycle detail
Industry channels: associations, events, marketplaces, analysts
Economics of a dedicated vertical team versus overlay
Defined pipeline, win-rate and cycle bars
Permission and legal gates on references and compliance claims
Shipped playbook template

issues.problem: There is no vertical selection or go/no-go step. The skill never asks whether this vertical deserves a dedicated motion, or how it compares with others, before writing the playbook.
issues.fix: Add step 0: score candidate verticals on own-data win rate, ACV and cycle (from HubSpot or an export), reachable account count, specialisation needs (compliance, integrations), access through partners and events, and cost to staff. Recommend one, several, or none, with the kill bar.

issues.quote: Use this when the user names an industry, a vertical motion, or asks how
issues.problem: 'Names an industry' fires on almost any GTM request (an ICP for logistics firms, positioning for fintech), so it collides with icp-and-segmentation and gtm-planning-and-market-entry.
issues.fix: Narrow the trigger to building or evaluating a dedicated industry motion. An industry mentioned inside an ICP or positioning request stays with those skills.

issues.quote: Trigger accounts, the talk track in vertical language, the battlecard
issues.problem: This repeats the play structure of field-enablement-content (trigger, talk track, battlecard lines, exit criteria), and 'Sequence the entry' mirrors gtm-planning-and-market-entry. That is maintenance duplication inside one expert.
issues.fix: Keep only the vertical deltas here (vocabulary, regulations, incumbent, buying committee), and hand the play build to field-enablement-content and the sequencing to gtm-planning-and-market-entry by name.

issues.quote: Reference customers, quantified outcomes, and the compliance or
issues.problem: There is no legal or security gate on compliance claims (HIPAA, PCI, FedRAMP) and no customer permission check before naming reference accounts or outcomes.
issues.fix: Compliance and certification claims need evidence and security or legal sign-off. Reference names and quantified outcomes need the customer's recorded permission before any external use.

issues.quote: Incumbents, partners, analysts, and the buying committee shape. One
issues.problem: No research method or tool routing is given, and industry associations, events, regulators and channels are omitted.
issues.fix: Direct research through web_search and web_fetch (regulations, associations, events, analyst coverage) and the CRM (own deals by industry), with every line dated and linked.

issues.quote: sequence, saved dated under verticals. Review it when the vertical misses
issues.problem: 'Its pipeline bar' is never defined anywhere in the playbook, so the review trigger cannot fire.
issues.fix: Require the playbook to set the vertical's pipeline, win-rate and cycle bars with a review date.

issues.problem: No playbook template is shipped, so section depth and format will vary.
issues.fix: Ship templates/vertical-playbook.md with narrative, use-case table, ecosystem map, proof plan with owners and dates, play deltas, entry waves and bars.

scenarios.prompt: How do we win in healthcare? We have two hospital customers and SOC 2, and a partner who resells into health systems.
scenarios.why: The narrative, the ecosystem map with confirmed, likely or unknown grading, the proof stack (the HIPAA/BAA gap becomes a dated milestone), the play with exit criteria, and lighthouse-first sequencing give a capable model a usable playbook skeleton for a named sector.

scenarios.prompt: We're getting traction in both fintech and logistics, 9 customers across the two, and no budget for a dedicated vertical team. Which one should we build a play for first, if either?
scenarios.why: The skill starts at 'Frame the industry narrative' for a vertical that is already chosen. It has no step to compare candidate verticals (win rate, ACV, cycle, size, specialisation need, access, product gaps) or to decide not to verticalise, so the core question gets no guidance.

account-health-and-qbrs.job: score account health and prep QBR
account-health-and-qbrs.summary: Scores a support account 0-100 from usage, support and outcome signals, drafts a success plan for yellow or red accounts, and outlines a QBR deck with a five-line exec summary, citing every number or cutting it.
strengths: Cuts any number it cannot source instead of estimating, and marks a score with no quoted signal UNKNOWN.
The five-line exec summary (health, top win, top risk, plan, ask) is a crisp, reusable artefact.
The success plan (risk in one line, two fixes, an owner and date each) is tight and waits for the owner's yes before a customer sees it.
missing: Signal definitions, a raw-to-score rule, a missing-data rule and a confidence level
Customer goals, success criteria, and value realised against them
A stakeholder and sponsor map, and last QBR's commitments with their status
Separate internal pre-brief and customer-facing deck
A handoff boundary to the CSM or account owner for commercial renewal and expansion
A defined save play, or a pointer to the one skill that owns it
Distinction between leading and lagging indicators

issues.quote: Score 0-100 weighted roughly 40% usage,
issues.problem: The weights come with no component definitions, no raw-to-score rule and no missing-data rule. Sponsor change and days to renewal are read but never weighted. The model also conflicts with Max's renewal-expansion-and-qbr (40/20/20/20, safe/watch/at risk), so the same account gets different grades from two experts.
issues.fix: Define each component with its source, its raw-to-score rule and its missing-data rule (never zero, never healthy), and output a confidence level. Adopt one health model across the catalog, for example Riley's customer-health-score structure.

issues.section: Prep the QBR from the record
issues.quote: issues with resolutions, health score with trend, and asks of the
issues.problem: The internal health score, built partly from sentiment and renewal risk, goes into a customer-facing QBR deck.
issues.fix: Split the output into an internal pre-brief (health, risks, save plan) and a customer deck (goals, outcomes against goals, adoption, resolved issues, roadmap, mutual asks).

issues.quote: Threshold crossings trigger the save play.
issues.problem: The skill never defines the save play, and upsell-and-retention-offers routes renewal-at-risk saves back to this skill, so the two form a loop.
issues.fix: Either define the save play here (risk, sponsor path, remedy, concession ladder within approved bands, owner and date) or name the one skill that owns it and route to it.

issues.problem: There is no boundary to the account owner or CSM. A support specialist is made to own renewal saves and QBRs, duplicating Riley's and Max's skills.
issues.fix: Rescope the skill to the support-health section of a QBR and a support-risk alert. Use consult_teammate or handoff_to_expert to the CSM or account owner for the renewal and the full QBR.

issues.section: Prep the QBR from the record
issues.quote: Build the deck outline from evidence: wins with numbers and dates,
issues.problem: The outline leaves out customer goals and success criteria, attendees and stakeholders, whether last QBR's commitments were met, the roadmap and the agenda.
issues.fix: Ship a templates/qbr-outline.md with those sections and the source slot for each number.

issues.section: Prep the QBR from the record
issues.quote: Log health, plan state, and QBR
issues.problem: It writes to the account record with no approval gate and no named destination.
issues.fix: Stage the log line and write it to the CRM (HubSpot block) only on the owner's yes. Otherwise save it to a workspace file.

issues.section: Prep the QBR from the record
issues.quote: offer to watch the risk signals in the
issues.problem: No Robin routine watches account signals. The Monday pulse covers knowledge-base and staffing, so this offer points at nothing.
issues.fix: Offer a schedule_routine for the named account with its signals and stop condition, or remove the offer.

issues.quote: signals and renewal-risk owners from prefs, and the last QBR or
issues.problem: robin-getting-started never collects health signals or renewal-risk owners, so these prefs will always be empty.
issues.fix: Ask for them on first use and save them to memory, or state defaults the owner can override.

scenarios.prompt: Acme's QBR is on the 14th. Here's their usage export for the last two quarters and the ticket CSV. Prep the review.
scenarios.why: It produces sourced numbers, a five-line exec summary and an outline. But the 40/30/30 score has no raw-to-score rule, so two runs can grade the account differently. The 'outcomes' component has no source in these inputs. The outline puts the internal health score in the customer deck and leaves out customer goals, stakeholders and last QBR's commitments.

scenarios.prompt: Beta Corp's champion just left, usage is down about 30% per a Slack thread, we have no CRM access, and renewal is in 45 days. Are they at risk and what do we do?
scenarios.why: The data is partial and there is no missing-data rule, so the model either returns an all-UNKNOWN read or invents a composite score. 'Threshold crossings trigger the save play' points to a play the skill never defines, and upsell-and-retention-offers hands renewal saves back to this skill, so the two skills loop. A commercial renewal 45 days out gets no handoff to the account owner or CSM.

billing-refunds-and-exceptions.job: handle refund or billing exception request
billing-refunds-and-exceptions.summary: Verifies the disputed charge from records, cites the governing refund policy, and stages a customer message plus evidence pack; anything above the approval limit or outside policy goes to the approver, and nothing is promised before the owner's yes.
strengths: Clear order of verify, then policy, then draft, with a hard rule that a missing record holds the draft and names the record that would release it.
Refunds default to the original payment method; anything above the limit or outside policy goes to the approver, framed to the customer as pending.
Shows the evidence pack (records, policy citation, amount, draft) in chat before staging it.
missing: A pending-authorisation versus settled-duplicate check, and refund posting times by payment method
An open chargeback check with a route to fraud-and-chargeback-defense
Statutory consumer rights that override posted policy
Approver options with cost, precedent and a decision deadline
Proration, tax/VAT reversal, and cancel-versus-refund handling for subscriptions
Account-holder verification and card-data masking

issues.section: Verify, then check policy, then draft
issues.problem: There is no check for an open card dispute or chargeback before refunding. A refund on top of a chargeback loses the money twice, and the 'charge dispute' trigger draws exactly these cases in.
issues.fix: Add a step that checks dispute status. If a chargeback is open, do not refund; route the case to fraud-and-chargeback-defense.

issues.section: Verify, then check policy, then draft
issues.quote: policy — it is legally enforceable.
issues.problem: This overstates the law. Statutory consumer rights (EU/UK withdrawal and faulty-goods rights, US state auto-renewal laws) and card-network rules can override a posted policy, and this line pushes the model toward a policy-only denial.
issues.fix: Replace it with: check the statutory rights for the customer's jurisdiction; where law and policy conflict, flag it to the approver, because the law wins.

issues.section: Verify, then check policy, then draft
issues.quote: Verify first: the exact charge, date, and what the customer paid for,
issues.problem: There is no auth-versus-capture check, no proration or tax reversal, and no refund posting time. The common 'double charged' case is usually an authorisation hold.
issues.fix: Add a verify checklist: auth versus capture, duplicate transaction IDs, proration, tax/VAT, and refund timing by payment method. Pull from the Stripe block when connected; otherwise ask for the charge or invoice export.

issues.section: Verify, then check policy, then draft
issues.quote: goes to the approver with the evidence pack, never a promise.
issues.problem: The approver gets evidence but no options, costs, precedent or decision deadline. The original refund-and-exception-brief supplies all of these.
issues.fix: Merge in the original's options block: policy as written, partial, or full or credit, each with cost, precedent and any chargeback or legal deadline, plus the approver and a decide-by date.

issues.quote: charge dispute
issues.problem: This trigger collides with fraud-and-chargeback-defense ('chargeback notice'), and 'credit request' collides with service-recovery-and-goodwill. No boundary rule says which skill wins.
issues.fix: Add a boundary line: bank disputes go to the fraud skill, company-error goodwill goes to service recovery, and this skill handles customer-initiated refund and fee requests.

issues.section: Verify, then check policy, then draft
issues.quote: As much as I'd love to help...
issues.problem: A fixed scripted opener in a skill that otherwise enforces company voice; it reads as canned.
issues.fix: Tell the model to lead the no with the policy reason and the closest thing it can do, in company voice, with no fixed phrase.

issues.problem: There is no requirement to verify the requester is the account holder before discussing billing, and no rule for card numbers pasted into the thread.
issues.fix: Verify the requester is the account holder or billing contact. Mask card data to the last four digits and route exposures to sensitive-data-safe-handling.

scenarios.prompt: Jordan says we charged his card twice for the $49 Pro plan on 3 Sept. Here's the ticket. Can you draft the reply?
scenarios.why: The verify, policy, draft steps are right and nothing is promised. But step 1 never separates a pending authorisation from a settled duplicate and never gives refund posting times, so the draft can promise a refund of a hold that will drop off by itself.

scenarios.prompt: Annual customer, 4 months in, wants a full $2,400 refund. Policy is 30 days. They're in Germany and have already filed a dispute with their bank. My approval limit is $500.
scenarios.why: It correctly sends the above-limit request to the approver without promising anything. It misses three things: the open chargeback (a refund plus a chargeback loses the money twice, and the case belongs with fraud-and-chargeback-defense), EU statutory rights (the 'legally enforceable' line pushes a policy-only answer), and approver options (pro-rata, credit, full) with cost and precedent.

bpo-vendor-quality-ops.summary: Audits an outsourced support vendor by scoring a small ticket sample against a six-point rubric with quotes, comparing it to target and the last audit, and staging a vendor coaching note with a re-audit date.
strengths: Every mark carries a quote, and a sample it cannot source is not scored.
It explicitly refuses vendor-wide claims from a small sample.
Performance plans and uplifts are staged as owner decisions, and the top miss becomes a macro or KB fix for the whole tier.
missing: Stratified random sampling with a minimum size
Contract SLAs/KPIs (service level, AHT, adherence, attrition) and service-credit calculation
A calibration method with the vendor QA team and an agreement target
Vendor-versus-client root-cause attribution
Governance cadence (weekly ops review, monthly scorecard, vendor QBR) and an escalation ladder
New-hire and nesting cohort analysis, and knowledge-transfer checks
Review of vendor agents' access and data handling

issues.quote: lever: fast first response is the top CSAT driver.
issues.problem: This conflates first-contact resolution with first response time and states an unsourced claim about what drives CSAT, which would misdirect coaching.
issues.fix: Drop the claim. Tell the model to read FCR, reopen rate and CSAT together from the vendor's data, each with its source and period.

issues.quote: Pull a fair sample: newest, oldest, one escalated, one refund-adjacent —
issues.problem: Four hand-picked tickets with no size or stratification cannot support a vendor pass rate or trend. The method is copied from quality-csat-and-coaching.
issues.fix: Specify random sampling stratified by agent, queue and contact reason, with a minimum n, and report the margin of error. Reuse quality-csat-and-coaching's rubric instead of redefining it.

issues.problem: The contract layer is missing: SLAs and KPIs from the SOW, service credits and penalties, and a governance cadence. That layer is what separates vendor management from internal QA.
issues.fix: Add a step that reads contract targets, computes credits from sourced numbers, and stages the credit decision for the owner, with a weekly, monthly and quarterly governance rhythm.

issues.problem: Misses are not attributed to vendor-controllable causes versus client-side ones (KB gaps, policy ambiguity, tooling, routing), so the vendor note can blame the vendor for the client's defects.
issues.fix: Tag each miss vendor, client or shared before drafting the note, and route client-side causes to the owner's backlog.

issues.quote: joint review with the evidence attached, not argued in chat.
issues.problem: The description promises vendor calibration, but the body gives no method for it.
issues.fix: Add a method: both QA teams blind-score a shared sample, set an agreement target (for example within 5 points), and rewrite rubric items where scores diverge.

issues.quote: Draft the vendor note: the score, the two quoted misses, the one fix to
issues.problem: Nothing says the note reaches the vendor only on the owner's yes, and nothing stops customer identifiers going out in the quoted misses.
issues.fix: Stage the note, redact customer identifiers in the quotes, and send only on the owner's yes.

issues.quote: The vendor queue sample, the scorecard rubric and targets from prefs, past
issues.problem: robin-getting-started never collects the vendor rubric or targets, and there is no fallback for getting the data in.
issues.fix: Ask for the vendor export (CSV or Sheets) and the contract targets on first use, and save them to memory.

scenarios.prompt: Our BPO handled about 1,200 tickets last week. Here's the CSV export and our QA rubric. Audit them and draft the vendor note.
scenarios.why: It produces quoted scores, a scorecard and a staged note. But the 'fair sample' is four named tickets with no size and no stratification by agent or contact reason, so the pass rate and trend can't be defended. The FCR/first-response line may also misdirect the coaching fix.

scenarios.prompt: Vendor CSAT fell from 88 to 79 after they onboarded 20 new agents. They dispute our QA scores, and the contract gives us service credits below 85% QA. Should we invoke the credits?
scenarios.why: No step reads the contract SLAs or computes service credits. Calibration gets only 'joint review', with no method. Nothing separates the new-hire cohort or vendor causes from client causes. The model would have to improvise the commercial decision.

compliance-and-regulated-support.summary: Pre-checks a support reply, script, macro or KB article against the regimes in play (securities, PHI, PCI) with a generic four-point line check, marks rewordable fixes, routes the rest to the compliance owner, and stamps pass, pass-with-edits or blocked.
strengths: A clear three-way verdict, and blocked drafts wait for the compliance owner's yes.
It quotes the failing line and the rule it breaks, and never softens a required disclosure.
Safe default: money, health and card topics count as regulated until the owner says otherwise.
missing: Per-regime reference checklists and an approved-language source
Complaint identification and regulatory complaint clocks
A distinction between an AI pre-check and required human pre-approval
A template for the compliance-owner packet
A containment route to sensitive-data-safe-handling
Recording-consent and identity-verification checks for phone scripts

issues.problem: There is no complaint identification. Under FCA, CFPB and FINRA rules an expression of dissatisfaction is a complaint with recording and response-time duties, but the check only scans the draft's wording.
issues.fix: Add a step that classifies the inbound message as a complaint or not. If it is one, apply the regime's acknowledgement, final-response and referral-rights requirements and log it as a complaint.

issues.quote: Required disclosures present, no promised returns or outcomes, no PHI or
issues.problem: The checklist is four generic items. No per-regime rules or approved-language source ship with the skill, so the model checks FINRA, HIPAA or PCI from memory.
issues.fix: Ship references/regimes.md with per-regime checks: FINRA 2210/2211, HIPAA identity verification and minimum necessary, PCI, GDPR/CCPA, TCPA, Reg E/Z, FDCPA/Reg F, FCA Consumer Duty/DISP. Give each what to look for and who approves.

issues.quote: A draft outside every regime passes with a one-line note;
issues.problem: An AI 'pass' reads as compliance approval, yet some regimes require principal or compliance pre-approval regardless of wording.
issues.fix: Rename the stamp to 'pre-check clear' and state when human pre-approval is still mandatory before sending.

issues.quote: fix — missing license, barred claim, exposed sensitive data — to the
issues.problem: Exposed data goes straight to the compliance owner, but Robin's persona says containment comes first, which is the job of sensitive-data-safe-handling.
issues.fix: Route exposures to sensitive-data-safe-handling for containment first, then send the compliance packet.

issues.quote: Fix what a reword can fix and mark each change. Route what a reword cannot
issues.problem: Free-form AI rewording can introduce regulated language that was never approved.
issues.fix: Take rewords from the approved-language library. Mark any free-form reword as pending compliance review.

issues.quote: compliance owner with a short packet.
issues.problem: The contents of the packet are undefined.
issues.fix: Define the packet: regime, rule, failing line, proposed fix, customer-facing deadline, and case link.

issues.quote: can I quote this policy
issues.problem: This trigger collides with ordinary policy quoting in draft-the-reply and billing-refunds-and-exceptions.
issues.fix: Replace it with regulated-specific triggers such as 'HIPAA check this reply' or 'complaint response review'.

issues.problem: There is no 'not legal advice' boundary and no handoff to a compliance teammate (such as Lena) for judgement calls.
issues.fix: Add a consult_teammate or handoff path and a line saying the stamp is not legal sign-off.

scenarios.prompt: We're FINRA-registered. Check this reply to a client explaining why their trade settled late before I send it.
scenarios.why: The regime, line check, stamp flow catches promissory language and missing disclosures. But nothing tells the model to decide whether this is correspondence or a complaint response, that a written complaint must be recorded, or which approved-language source to check against, and the 'pass' stamp may be read as compliance approval.

scenarios.prompt: A UK customer emailed 'this is unacceptable, I want the arrangement fee back' about a personal loan. Our draft says we can't refund. We have no regimes set up yet.
scenarios.why: The fallback asks for regimes and treats money as regulated. But the skill has no complaint-identification step, so it misses that under FCA DISP this is a complaint needing an acknowledgement, a final response within 8 weeks and Financial Ombudsman referral rights; the line check only looks for disclosures and promised outcomes.

draft-the-reply.summary: Drafts a channel-shaped customer reply in company voice, grounded in a cited help-center or policy passage, with apology-first handling for heated threads, then stages it for the owner's yes.
strengths: Strong grounding rule: cite the governing passage; an unwritten answer becomes a KB candidate, never a quoted rule.
Concrete channel shaping: email subject line, two chat messages at most per turn, a phone talk track, and public-safe social wording with a move to private.
Banned-phrase list and 'state what you CAN do' framing.
A clear gate: nothing is sent, posted, refunded or promised without the owner's yes.
missing: List and answer every customer question in order
At most one clarifying question for a missing load-bearing fact
Account, plan and region checks
Routing to the billing, compliance, sensitive-data and social skills
An approval note format above the draft
Reply in the customer's language, and read the thread history to avoid re-asking

issues.problem: There is no step to list every question the customer asked and answer each in order, and no rule to ask one clarifying question when a load-bearing fact is missing. The original support-reply-draft and Robin's persona both have these.
issues.fix: Merge in the original's rules: list the asks in order, answer each, and ask at most one clear question for missing facts.

issues.problem: Nothing routes the ticket when it involves money, a regulated segment, exposed card or health data, or a public post, so the model drafts those replies inline.
issues.fix: Add a pre-draft routing line: money goes to billing-refunds-and-exceptions, a regulated segment goes through the compliance check, card or health data goes to sensitive-data-safe-handling, and public threads go to social-and-community-support.

issues.quote: externally visible waits for the owner's yes in the same conversation.
issues.problem: The wording implies some replies need not wait, yet every customer reply is externally visible.
issues.fix: Say every reply waits for the owner's yes, and money or exceptions also need the named approver.

issues.quote: apology first (it wins back more than credit), then repeat the problem,
issues.problem: It states an unsourced claim as fact and blends two frameworks (acknowledge-own-offer and problem-solution-benefit) into a contradictory order.
issues.fix: Drop the parenthetical and give one sequence: acknowledge and apologise, restate the problem, the fix, the next step with date and owner.

issues.quote: apology to a customer
issues.problem: This nearly duplicates service-recovery-and-goodwill's 'apology note to a customer'. Company-error cases land here instead of in service recovery.
issues.fix: Add a boundary: a failure the company caused goes to service-recovery-and-goodwill; this skill covers the general reply.

issues.quote: Deliver the staged reply above, channel-shaped, with its citation.
issues.problem: There is no format for the approval note, so the owner can't see which lines are sourced, unverified or placeholders.
issues.fix: Put an approval note above the draft listing sources, UNVERIFIED lines, placeholders, the channel and the approver.

issues.quote: Find the governing help-center or policy passage and cite it; anything
issues.problem: It never checks the account, plan or region facts that change the answer.
issues.fix: Check the customer's plan, limits and region against the record before applying the passage, and mark each such fact FACT or UNKNOWN.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a reply to Priya's email. She's asking how to export invoices and why her last invoice shows VAT.
scenarios.why: Grounding, her name, the next step with a date and owner, and an email subject line cover it, and a capable model answers both asks. The risk: the skill never says to answer each question in order or to check her plan and region, so the VAT answer may come out generic.

scenarios.prompt: An angry customer replied to our post on X with their order number, saying the parcel is lost and they want a refund. We have no lost-in-transit policy doc. Draft our response.
scenarios.why: The channel rules give public-safe wording and a move to DM, the heat handling is apology-first, and the missing doc means UNVERIFIED lines. But nothing routes the exposed order number to sensitive-data or the refund decision to billing or orders, so the model may improvise a refund position in public.

enterprise-identity-sso-support.job: troubleshoot SSO and identity login failures
enterprise-identity-sso-support.summary: Triages SAML, OIDC, SCIM and API-auth login failures by walking the handshake layer by layer, ranking causes with confirm steps, drafting the config fix for the customer's admin, and verifying every reply step against a quoted doc or log line.
strengths: Layer-by-layer handshake walk, with each layer marked FACT or UNKNOWN and causes ranked with a confirm step each.
The common-cause list is correct: expired cert, mis-mapped attribute, deprovisioned user, clock skew, wrong audience.
Never edits IdP config itself, and requires a quoted doc or log line behind every instruction in a reply or KB step.
missing: Blast-radius triage (all users, a group, or one user) and a change timeline
SAML trace or HAR capture and decode steps, and the fields to inspect
IdP-specific error-code lookup
Redaction and secure handling of HAR files, assertions and tokens
Verification of the requester's authority before bypass, reset or enforcement changes
Cert rollover with dual-cert overlap, SCIM conflict and deprovision patterns, JIT versus SCIM, and NameID changes that create duplicate accounts

issues.quote: edit IdP config yourself — draft the change for the owner's admin.
issues.problem: This guards IdP config only. Nothing requires checking the requester's authority before SP-side changes such as disabling SSO enforcement, break-glass login, an MFA reset, or reversing a SCIM deprovision. That is the classic social-engineering route to account takeover.
issues.fix: Verify the requester against the customer's admin list through a known channel. Stage any bypass, reset or enforcement change for the owner's yes, and log who approved it.

issues.quote: config changes, and the auth logs when available.
issues.problem: It asks for auth logs, and implicitly HAR files and assertions, with no redaction or secure-handling rule, although these carry session cookies, tokens and PII. Nothing forbids requesting private keys or client secrets.
issues.fix: Redact tokens, cookies and PII at capture, and never request private keys, client secrets or full API tokens over the ticket. Route exposures to sensitive-data-safe-handling.

issues.quote: Walk the handshake in order: user exists and is licensed, group and role
issues.problem: A fixed linear walk with no blast-radius branch. 'All users since time T' points to a cert, metadata or IdP change; a subset points to mapping or SCIM; one user points to that user's state or NameID.
issues.fix: Start with blast radius and change timeline, then pick the first layer from that branch.

issues.quote: mapping, the SAML assertion or OIDC (OpenID Connect) claims, certificate
issues.problem: No guidance on how to capture and read the assertion or claims.
issues.fix: Add a reference covering SAML-tracer or HAR capture, decoding in bash_exec, the fields to check (Issuer, Audience, Recipient/ACS, NameID format, NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter, signature), and IdP error-code lookup (Entra AADSTS, Okta).

issues.quote: SP-initiated, which app, which user. No repro, no diagnosis — collect
issues.problem: The agent can rarely reproduce a failure on the customer's IdP, so a strict repro-first rule can stall the case.
issues.fix: Reword to 'no evidence, no diagnosis': the error string, timestamp, affected users and a SAML trace or token.

issues.quote: API token expired
issues.problem: API-token auth overlaps technical-diagnostics-with-tools, and 'certificate expired' also matches TLS certificate issues.
issues.fix: Scope the triggers to the identity layer (SSO, SCIM, IdP names) and state the boundary with technical diagnostics for API auth.

issues.quote: verify every AI-drafted word before it ships
issues.problem: The description spends words on internal process instead of the user's intent, which weakens triggering.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description in user terms, for example: users can't sign in via Okta, Entra or Google SSO, or SCIM isn't provisioning or deprovisioning.

scenarios.prompt: Since 09:00 none of Acme's users can sign in via Okta. They get 'Invalid SAML signature'. Here's the ticket.
scenarios.why: The layer walk and ranked causes include the certificate and its expiry, so with a confirm step and a fix drafted for the customer's admin, a capable model lands on cert rotation or a metadata mismatch. The missing blast-radius rule costs time, not the answer.

scenarios.prompt: Someone emailing from a Gmail address says they're Contoso's IT admin, locked out after an Entra ID cert rotation. They attach a HAR file and ask us to turn off SSO enforcement so they can log in.
scenarios.why: The skill never says to verify the requester is an authorised admin through a known channel. It only forbids editing IdP config, not SP-side enforcement toggles or break-glass access, and gives no handling for a HAR file that carries session tokens. A model following it could draft an SSO bypass for an unverified requester.

accounts-receivable-follow-up.summary: Builds a verified open-receivables queue in five status groups and drafts calm, factual payment reminders plus a contact-log row, without sending anything or asserting late fees.
strengths: Refuses to call an invoice overdue unless the due date and balance are proven ('status unconfirmed'), which prevents the most embarrassing collections error
Keeps part-payments, credits, disputes and promised dates visible and puts disputed items in their own group
Bans unsupported threats (late fees, service stop, collections, legal consequences) and exposure of other customers' data
Adds a contact-log row with evidence cutoff, approval state and next review date
missing: Defined reminder stage ladder with timing and tone
Aging buckets and summary totals, optionally DSO
Per-stage email templates
Customer-level statement consolidation
Unapplied cash and payment-matching check before chasing
Payment plan and promise-to-pay tracking
Integration routing (Stripe, Gmail drafts, Sheets) with CSV fallback
Scheduled follow-ups
Owner-decided escalation to a collections agency or counsel, with jurisdiction note on late fees

issues.quote: Prepare a contact log row with draft stage, evidence cutoff, owner, approval
issues.problem: The description promises 'staged' follow-ups and the log records a 'draft stage', but no stages are defined (pre-due reminder, first notice, second notice, final notice, owner handoff), and neither is the timing or tone of each.
issues.fix: Add a stage ladder table (trigger in days past due, tone, required content, who approves, next step) and a short email template per stage in references/.

issues.quote: Never send a message, call a customer, apply a fee, stop service, change an
issues.problem: This is an absolute ban, even after the owner approves. The persona says 'without your approval', and the platform's approval flow can send a Gmail draft, so the skill forces the user to copy and paste.
issues.fix: Change to: never send without explicit approval of the exact draft; once approved, send through the connected channel (or save as a Gmail draft), log it, and schedule the next review.

issues.quote: Group items as:
issues.problem: The status groups have no standard aging buckets or per-bucket totals, so the owner gets no aging summary or view of total overdue exposure.
issues.fix: Add an aging summary (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+) with count and open balance per bucket and per customer, calculated in bash_exec.

issues.section: Verify before calling an invoice overdue
issues.quote: For each open invoice, collect the invoice record, customer, currency, issued
issues.problem: The skill never says where receivables data comes from (Stripe block, accounting export, Google Sheet) or what to do when no integration is connected.
issues.fix: Name the sources in order: Stripe via run_block if connected, else ask for an AR aging CSV or paste. Use connect_integration or ask_question for the gap.

issues.section: Verify before calling an invoice overdue
issues.quote: Check payment records through the stated
issues.problem: No step checks unapplied cash, unmatched bank receipts or credits on account before chasing, which is the usual cause of 'we already paid'.
issues.fix: Add a pre-chase check that searches bank receipts and unapplied payments for the customer, amount or reference, and holds the chase when a likely match exists.

issues.quote: Each draft should state the invoice number, issue and due dates, open balance,
issues.problem: Drafts are per invoice. Senior AR practice sends one statement-style message per customer, addressed to the verified AP contact, with a payment link or remittance details.
issues.fix: Draft one message per customer listing all open items, and include payment instructions and the verified billing contact.

issues.quote: state, and next review date. Drafts must not claim a late fee, service stop,
issues.problem: The next review date is recorded but never scheduled, so follow-up depends on the user remembering it.
issues.fix: After approval, offer schedule_followup for the next review date, and keep the contact log in a workspace file or memory.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our AR aging export from QuickBooks as of 30 Sept. Which invoices are overdue, and can you draft chase emails for them?
scenarios.why: The verify step and the five-group queue produce a sound list, and the drafts carry the invoice facts in a calm tone. But no stage ladder or tone progression is defined, so an invoice 75 days late gets the same 'has payment been made?' note as one 3 days late. The skill also defines no 0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ aging summary.

scenarios.prompt: Acme says they paid INV-1042 last week but I can't see it. They have three other open invoices, one of them disputed, and our terms allow a 1.5% monthly late fee. Draft something firm and add the fee.
scenarios.why: The skill rightly marks 1042 `status unconfirmed`, routes the dispute, and allows a fee only under an approved policy. It gives no step to search bank receipts or unapplied cash for the claimed payment, and no way to combine a customer's invoices into one statement. It also never flags that late-fee enforceability depends on jurisdiction.

bookkeeping-exception-escalation.job: escalate bookkeeping exception with evidence pack
bookkeeping-exception-escalation.summary: Classifies a bookkeeping exception into factual classes and assembles an eight-part evidence pack with one decision request, routed to the accountant, counsel, finance owner or security owner.
strengths: Clear factual exception classes, including bank-detail changes (business email compromise, or BEC, awareness) and privacy or access concerns
Requires 'suspected' wording and cites the record that raised concern, so nobody is accused without evidence
Refuses to claim materiality without an owner-supplied threshold
Names a safe interim state and a single decision request, which makes escalations actionable
Minimum-necessary data sharing and an unchanged source record
missing: Urgency or severity tiers with response expectations
A time-critical payment-fraud and bank-detail-change playbook (recall, preserve, call-back verification)
A multi-item exception queue or log format
Collecting the materiality threshold up front
A delivery mechanism for escalations (drafted message, teammate handoff)
Follow-up and ageing of open exceptions

issues.quote: For a possible unauthorised payment, raise it at
issues.problem: The most time-critical case has no playbook: no bank recall or fraud-line call, no evidence preservation, no call-back verification on an independently sourced number, and no channel for 'raise it'.
issues.fix: Add an urgent path: notify the payment owner now via an approved Slack or email draft, recommend an immediate bank recall, preserve the source emails, and verify with the vendor using contact details from the master file rather than the email.

issues.quote: Deadline or operational impact, if a source proves it.
issues.problem: The description promises 'urgency', but the skill has no urgency levels, so a $12 duplicate and a diverted payment are packaged the same way.
issues.fix: Add three tiers, such as act-now (suspected fraud, bank-detail change, privacy exposure), before-close, and next-review, with a response expectation for each.

issues.problem: There is no batch format for several exceptions at once, although the persona's day-one deliverable is 'Your exception queue' with one owner and next step per item.
issues.fix: Add an exception-log table (ID, class, amount, source, owner, decision needed, urgency, interim state, status) and keep it in a workspace file or memory.

issues.quote: "accounting question", "financial discrepancy"
issues.problem: These generic triggers overlap with every other Mina skill and with Daniel's finance kit, so the skill may load for routine questions that need no escalation.
issues.fix: Narrow the triggers to escalation language (e.g. 'escalate to accountant', 'can't resolve this transaction', 'suspicious payment', 'changed bank details').

issues.quote: Route tax and policy questions to the qualified accountant; legal claims to
issues.problem: The routing names people but no mechanism: no drafted message for approval, and no consult_teammate or handoff_to_expert when the owner is another expert.
issues.fix: Say that the pack is delivered as a drafted email or Slack message for approval, or through a teammate handoff when the owner is another expert.

issues.quote: Choose the best factual class:
issues.problem: Forcing one class hides compound cases, e.g. a duplicate payment made to changed bank details.
issues.fix: Allow a primary class plus secondary flags, and route by the most severe class.

issues.quote: owner's supplied decision and the evidence for any later action.
issues.problem: The skill never says where decisions are recorded, so they are lost between sessions.
issues.fix: Write the decision and its evidence to the exception log with memory_store or a workspace file.

scenarios.prompt: I've got six items I can't clear for August: a $2,400 transfer to an account I don't recognise, two Adobe charges that look duplicated, and three receipts with no matching transaction. Package these for my accountant.
scenarios.why: Each item gets a class and an eight-part pack, but the output is six separate packs with no combined queue, no ordering by urgency and no single summary for the accountant. The persona's day-one 'exception queue' deliverable has no format here.

scenarios.prompt: A supplier emailed new bank details two weeks ago and we paid $18,000 to the new account yesterday. Now the real supplier says they never changed banks. What do I do?
scenarios.why: The skill classifies this correctly (bank-detail change, suspected unauthorised payment) and says to raise it at once without accusing anyone. It gives no time-critical steps: call the bank's fraud line for a recall, preserve the email and headers, and verify with the supplier on an independently sourced number. 'Do not contact the suspected party' is also ambiguous when the legitimate supplier must be contacted.

bookkeeping-getting-started.job: set up bookkeeping intake and source inventory
bookkeeping-getting-started.summary: Collects an eight-point bookkeeping intake (entity, period, currency, basis, chart of accounts, sources, opening balances, approvers) and sorts each source into ready, usable-with-warning or blocked lists.
strengths: Requires filename, dates, export time, row count, currency and control total for every source, the right traceability standard
Clear ready / usable-with-warning / blocked triage with one question per blocking gap
Refuses to choose an accounting basis or merge entities or periods without confirmation
Names approvers for invoices, adjustments, customer contact and final reports up front
Ends with work that can start now versus blocked work, each with an owner
missing: Persisting the intake to memory or a workspace file for sibling skills
A minimum viable intake and progressive collection
A starter chart-of-accounts path when none exists
Integration routing and an export fallback checklist
Materiality threshold, fiscal year-end, accounting software, and tax registration facts
Handling for commingled personal and business accounts
A reusable intake-sheet template

issues.quote: End with the work that can start now, the blocked work, and the owner of every
issues.problem: The intake is never saved. On this platform, the other skills (expense-categorization, month-end-close-checklist) depend on these facts but have no instruction to reuse them.
issues.fix: Save the confirmed intake (entity, period, currency, chart of accounts location, approvers, accountant, thresholds) with memory_store, write an intake sheet to the workspace, and have sibling skills read it first.

issues.quote: Approved chart of accounts and the person who owns changes to it.
issues.problem: If the user has no chart of accounts (common for small businesses), the skill blocks with no way forward.
issues.fix: Offer a clearly labelled provisional starter chart for the owner or accountant to approve, and keep items coded to it flagged as provisional.

issues.quote: Source systems and exports supplied: bank, card, billing, payroll, expenses,
issues.problem: There is no routing to integrations (Stripe, Sheets or Drive blocks, an accounting-system MCP) and no fallback instructions for which exports to request and how.
issues.fix: List the preferred source per record type, offer connect_integration where a block or MCP exists, and otherwise give the exact export to request (e.g. a CSV bank statement with running balance).

issues.quote: For each source, state its filename or record name, covered dates, export time,
issues.problem: It asks for the full intake up front with no minimum viable set or priority order, which overwhelms a small-business owner on day one.
issues.fix: Define a minimum set (entity, period, currency, one bank source) to start work, and collect the rest progressively with ask_question.

issues.quote: "finance records", "books"
issues.problem: 'books' and 'finance records' are so broad the skill may load for unrelated requests or crowd out the specific Mina skills.
issues.fix: Use intake-specific triggers such as 'set up bookkeeping', 'new client books', 'what do you need from me', or 'first time'.

issues.problem: The intake omits facts later skills need: accounting software, fiscal year-end, materiality or review threshold, written coding rules, sales-tax or VAT registration status (as a fact), prior close status, and document storage location.
issues.fix: Add these as optional intake fields.

issues.quote: Ask one question per blocking gap. Prefer a source record over a recollection.
issues.problem: There is no order for the questions and no batching, which can mean many round trips.
issues.fix: Batch the blocking questions in one ask_question call, ordered by how much work each unblocks.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Mina, I run a five-person agency on Xero with a Chase business account and a Brex card. Can you help me get Q3's books in order?
scenarios.why: The model would build the eight-point intake and the three readiness lists. But the skill never says to try a connected integration or ask for specific exports, and it never says to save the result, so the next skill (e.g. expense-categorization) asks for the period, currency and chart of accounts again.

scenarios.prompt: I've got a folder of receipt photos and PDF bank statements for Jan-Aug, no chart of accounts, no accountant yet, and my side business runs through the same account.
scenarios.why: The safety behaviour is correct: basis marked open, entities not merged, commingling flagged. But with no chart of accounts or opening balance, almost everything lands in 'Blocked'. The skill offers no provisional starter chart for later approval and no step to separate the two businesses, so the user leaves with little that 'can start now'.

expense-categorization.job: categorize expenses to chart of accounts
expense-categorization.summary: Produces a per-transaction review table (source, date, vendor, amount, evidence, proposed account or unresolved, reason, confidence, review need) with control checks for totals, duplicates, transfers and foreign currency.
