strengths: A clear column spec with rules per field, including separate transaction and posting dates and no inferred legal vendor names
A precise confidence rubric (high only when evidence and written rules point to one account)
Keeps refunds, reversals, transfers, owner transactions and payments out of operating expenses
Finds duplicates without deleting either copy, and shows excluded rows with reasons
Routes fixed assets, loans, owner distributions, gifts, settlements and suspected fraud to the accountant
missing: A receipt-to-transaction matching procedure and missing-receipt list
A fallback or provisional mapping when there is no chart of accounts
Net, tax and gross capture from receipts
Saved vendor coding rules
Sandbox or file output for large exports
Handling of mixed-use (split personal and business) items beyond routing
A defined rule for spotting likely duplicates

issues.quote: Exact approved account name, or `unresolved`
issues.problem: With no approved chart of accounts, every row becomes unresolved and the skill gives no fallback.
issues.fix: When no chart exists, route to bookkeeping-getting-started or propose provisional accounts clearly marked 'provisional, pending approval', with low confidence.

issues.quote: Ask for the transaction export, available receipts or invoices, the approved
issues.problem: Receipts are requested but there is no matching procedure (amount, date window, vendor) and no missing-receipt list, which is the core of routine expense review.
issues.fix: Add a matching step: match on exact amount and a ±3-day window with vendor similarity, then list unmatched transactions and orphan receipts separately.

issues.quote: Keep sign and currency
issues.problem: The net, tax and gross amounts printed on receipts are not captured. They are source facts, not tax treatment, and the accountant needs them for VAT/GST.
issues.fix: Add optional net, tax-shown and gross columns copied from the receipt, and keep the treatment column blank for the accountant.

issues.problem: Vendor-to-account decisions the owner confirms are not saved, so each month starts from scratch and coding drifts.
issues.fix: Save confirmed vendor rules with memory_store and apply them first next time, citing the rule as evidence.

issues.quote: Total source rows, total amount, categorized rows, and unresolved rows.
issues.problem: No direction to compute control totals and detect duplicates in the sandbox, or to return the table as a file for large exports.
issues.fix: Tell the model to load the CSV in bash_exec, compute totals and flag duplicates there, and write a review CSV or Sheet to the workspace.

issues.quote: Find exact and likely duplicates without deleting either one.
issues.problem: 'Likely duplicate' is undefined, so results will vary between runs.
issues.fix: Define it, e.g. same amount and vendor within 5 days, or same receipt number.

scenarios.prompt: Attached is our August Amex CSV (212 rows) and our chart of accounts. Categorize everything and tell me what needs my input.
scenarios.why: The field table, confidence rules and checks (row and amount totals, duplicates, transfers and refunds kept apart) would give a solid review table and an unresolved list. The skill does not point the model to bash_exec or a CSV output for 212 rows, but a capable model would probably do that anyway.

scenarios.prompt: Categorize these card transactions. I don't have a chart of accounts, the receipts are phone photos in a Drive folder, I use the card for some personal stuff too, and about 20 charges are in EUR.
scenarios.why: Personal (owner) items and foreign-currency items are handled correctly. With no chart of accounts, the rule 'Exact approved account name, or unresolved' marks every row unresolved, so the output is useless. The skill also has no procedure for matching receipt photos to transactions or listing missing receipts.

invoice-drafting-and-issue.summary: Drafts a customer invoice from approved terms with sourced lines, recalculated totals and a contract-difference check, then returns an approval block and records (but never performs) issue or send.
strengths: Requires the seller's and customer's legal names, PO or contract reference, service period and remittance reference, which covers the substantive invoice fields
Recalculates totals, states rounding and lists every difference from the contract
'Do not copy a bank detail, tax ID, or customer address from an unrelated invoice', a sharp anti-fraud and anti-error control
'Do not claim the invoice exists outside the draft until a supplied record proves it', which stops the model claiming the invoice was issued
A review block naming the exact action awaiting approval
missing: An invoice template or file output
A Stripe or billing-system path after approval
A double-billing and billed-to-date check
Invoice numbering sequence control
A checklist of jurisdiction-required fields and e-invoicing mandates
A credit-note and correction path
Recurring or retainer invoice handling

issues.quote: do not perform the action yourself.
issues.problem: This bans execution even after explicit approval, though a Stripe block exists and the persona only requires approval. Users who want an invoice created or sent must do it by hand.
issues.fix: Allow the approved action through a connected channel (e.g. Stripe draft invoice, a Gmail draft or send) once the owner approves the exact draft, and log who approved it and when.

issues.quote: against the contract or approved order and list every difference.
issues.problem: There is no check against prior invoices, so double billing of the same period or PO and billing past a contract cap go undetected.
issues.fix: Add a step that compares invoices already issued for this customer, PO and period, and billed-to-date against the contract value.

issues.problem: No template or artefact is produced (Google Doc or PDF, Stripe draft, CSV import), so the output stays as chat text the user must re-key.
issues.fix: Ship a templates/invoice template and say how to render it (write_workspace_file, a Docs block) or how to create a Stripe draft after approval.

issues.quote: fields supplied by the owner or accountant.
issues.problem: The skill never flags invoice fields that some jurisdictions require (seller tax ID, sequential number, supply date, reverse-charge wording) or e-invoicing mandates. The model won't know to ask.
issues.fix: Add a checklist of 'jurisdiction may require these fields; confirm with the accountant', without choosing the tax treatment.

issues.quote: Draft invoice number or `to be assigned`.
issues.problem: There is no check that invoice numbers run in sequence without gaps or duplicates.
issues.fix: Ask for the last issued number or pull it from the billing system, and flag gaps or collisions.

issues.quote: Recalculate line totals and the grand total. State rounding.
issues.problem: The model is not told to use the sandbox for arithmetic, which matters for multi-line or currency-converted invoices.
issues.fix: Recalculate in bash_exec with decimal arithmetic and show the check.

issues.quote: Route tax, withholding, cross-border,
issues.problem: It never says that an issued invoice is corrected with a credit note and a reissue, not edited.
issues.fix: Add: never edit an issued invoice; prepare a credit-note draft for the accountant or owner instead.

scenarios.prompt: Draft the September invoice for Acme: 40 hours at $150/hr per our SOW, net 30, PO 7781.
scenarios.why: Gather, build and approval gate produce a draft with sourced lines, recalculated totals, marked blanks for missing addresses and payment details, and a review block naming the action awaiting approval. That is a sound result, though there is no file or template to hand over.

scenarios.prompt: Invoice Globex (Germany) in EUR for the Q3 retainer plus 12% of the usage overage. We're a US LLC. Push it through Stripe and send it today.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly routes cross-border and VAT questions to the accountant, leaves the tax fields blank, and needs a source for the overage figure. But it bans performing the action even after approval, so the Stripe path the user asked for is blocked. It also never checks whether Q3 was already billed, or whether German e-invoicing or reverse-charge fields apply.

month-end-close-checklist.summary: Opens a month-end close (entity, period, cutoff, owners, sources), tracks nine control areas through five statuses, and returns a close report labelled 'prepared for review' until the owner approves.
strengths: Separates prepared work from approved work and never lets the model approve its own work or call the books closed
A sensible small-business control list covering bank and card recs, sales and bills cutoff, AR/AP aging, payroll tie-out, loans and intercompany, and accountant-owned areas
Every adjustment needs a source, reason, preparer and approver
The report states which checks were and were not performed
Guardrails against backdating and removing exceptions
missing: Close calendar with sequencing and dependencies
Saved open items and a recurring monthly routine
Delegation to sibling reconciliation, expense, AR and P&L skills
Flux thresholds
Balance-sheet sweep (clearing, suspense, sales tax, credit cards)
Close tracker template
Close KPIs (days to close, open items)
Period lock after approval

issues.quote: Carry prior open items forward with their owners.
issues.problem: The skill assumes last month's open items are available but gives no way to store or retrieve them, and does not set the close up as a recurring monthly routine.
issues.fix: Save the close log and open items with memory_store or a workspace tracker, read them when opening the next close, and offer schedule_routine for a monthly close kickoff.

issues.quote: Track each item as not started, in progress, ready for review, approved, or
issues.problem: The nine areas have no order, dependencies or day targets (recs before P&L review, cutoff before accruals), so the close has no critical path.
issues.fix: Add a sequenced close calendar (e.g. by business day 1, 2-3, 5) with dependencies between items.

issues.quote: Bank and card statements reconciled.
issues.problem: The checklist never routes to Mina's own skills (statement-reconciliation, expense-categorization, accounts-receivable-follow-up, monthly-profit-and-loss-summary), which risks duplicate or inconsistent work.
issues.fix: Name the sibling skill for each control item and use its output as the evidence.

issues.quote: Profit-and-loss and balance movements reviewed against prior period and
issues.problem: The flux review has no threshold, so every movement or none gets explained.
issues.fix: Ask for an owner-set threshold (e.g. >10% and >$X) and require a sourced explanation or open item for each breach.

issues.problem: Common small-business balance-sheet risks are missing: clearing and undeposited-funds accounts, suspense or uncategorised balances, sales-tax payable tie-out, and credit-card liability recs.
issues.fix: Add a balance-sheet sweep step that lists each of these, with its expected balance and supporting source.

issues.quote: Return the control totals, tasks ready for review, blockers, late sources,
issues.problem: No tracker or report template, so formats vary each month and are hard to compare.
issues.fix: Ship a close-tracker template (Sheet or CSV) and a one-page report layout.

issues.quote: Only call the period `prepared for review` until the named owner confirms
issues.problem: The wording is ambiguous ('Only call ... until'), and nothing covers what happens after approval, such as recommending the owner lock the period in the accounting system.
issues.fix: Reword as 'Label the period prepared for review until...' and add a post-approval step recommending a period lock, done by the owner.

scenarios.prompt: Let's close August. Here's the bank statement, the Stripe payout report and the QuickBooks P&L export.
scenarios.why: The model would open the close, mark each of the nine areas with a status and list blockers, which is a usable status report. But it never delegates the bank rec to statement-reconciliation or runs the flux review against a threshold. Clearing and undeposited-funds accounts are not checked, so the report is thinner than a senior bookkeeper's.

scenarios.prompt: Our accountant wants July closed by Friday, the payroll export is late, there's $3k of uncategorised spend, and the owner is on holiday. Can you just mark it closed so we hit the deadline?
scenarios.why: The skill forbids marking the books closed or approving its own work. It labels the period 'prepared for review', lists payroll as a late source and the $3k as an unresolved exception, and routes accrual estimates to the accountant. That is the right senior behaviour under deadline pressure.

vendor-quote-comparison.job: compare vendor quotes on like-for-like cost
vendor-quote-comparison.summary: A 32-line checklist that puts vendor quotes on one term and currency, lists the cost lines to capture, and marks each requirement as MET WITH EVIDENCE, CLAIMED, GAP or UNKNOWN, without choosing a winner.
strengths: 'Do not fill a missing fee with zero' and 'total stated cost and total calculated cost' stop the most common quote-comparison errors.
The cost fields include renewal uplift, notice period, discount conditions and expiry, and termination and data-export cost, which junior comparisons usually miss.
The four evidence labels (MET WITH EVIDENCE / CLAIMED / GAP / UNKNOWN) separate vendor claims from proof.
Keeps service, security, legal, implementation and commercial gaps separate instead of blending them into one score.
The 'Never select a vendor' and transparent-weights rules match Vera's boundaries exactly.
missing: A reusable comparison template (CSV/Sheet) with year-by-year columns and source/assumption columns
A fallback when no requirements brief exists
Rules for converting usage-based, tiered, ramped and bundled pricing to a common basis
FX rate source and as-of date
An NPV or cash-timing view for multi-year deals with different payment terms
Renewal price caps, price holds and true-up mechanics
Defined sensitivity scenarios (usage, seats, uplift)
Draft clarification questions sent identically to all vendors, gated on approval
A worked example of a completed comparison
A handoff to procurement-decision-memo

issues.quote: Use the approved requirements brief and original quotes.
issues.problem: Assumes a brief exists. If none does, the coverage step has no musts or shoulds and the skill gives no fallback.
issues.fix: Add a step: if there is no brief, use ask_question for the top 5 must-haves and the decision owner, or route to vendor-requirements-brief, and mark coverage UNKNOWN until they are supplied.

issues.quote: Return the normalized table, assumptions, missing questions, material gaps, and scenarios when cost changes.
issues.problem: No table layout, no year-by-year columns, and 'scenarios' is undefined, so output structure changes from run to run and cannot be reused.
issues.fix: Ship templates/quote-comparison.csv (a row per cost line, Y1/Y2/Y3/total columns per vendor, plus source and assumption columns) and define the standard scenarios: usage low/base/high, seat growth, and renewal uplift at the cap.

issues.quote: Write each formula and label exchange rates or volume assumptions.
issues.problem: Does not tell the model to calculate in bash_exec or produce a spreadsheet, and does not require the FX rate's source and date, so in-context arithmetic errors and untraceable conversions are likely.
issues.fix: Tell the model to compute totals in the sandbox and write a workspace CSV or Google Sheet. Record the FX rate, its source and its as-of date, and show each formula beside the result.

issues.quote: Choose one comparison term and currency.
issues.problem: No rule for choosing the term, and nothing on ramped multi-year pricing, co-terming, payment terms, or when to show a discounted (NPV) or cash-timing view.
issues.fix: Default to the longest committed term (or 3 years) in the budget owner's currency. Expand ramps year by year, note payment terms and prepay discounts, and add an optional NPV line when terms differ.

issues.quote: recurring unit price, committed quantity, and minimum;
issues.problem: Treats pricing as per-unit only. Usage-based, tiered, platform-fee-plus-seat and bundled SKUs need to be mapped to a common unit before they can be compared.
issues.fix: Add a short 'pricing model mapping' step: split bundles, map SKUs to the brief's requirements, convert usage pricing to the brief's volume, and flag true-up and overage mechanics.

issues.quote: missing questions, material gaps
issues.problem: Missing questions naturally become a vendor email, but there is no draft-and-approve gate and no rule that every vendor gets the same question set.
issues.fix: Return the missing questions as a draft clarification list, sent identically to all vendors and only after the request owner approves.

issues.quote: vendor pricing
issues.problem: Too broad as a trigger: it overlaps spend-anomaly-review and the Toran vendor-evaluation package, which also claims side-by-side TCO.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'normalize quotes' or 'like-for-like vendor cost', and resolve the duplication with vendor-evaluation by keeping this skill as the cost-normalization step.

scenarios.prompt: Here are three helpdesk quotes (two PDFs and an email) for about 50 agents. Put them side by side on a 3-year basis against the requirements brief we wrote last week.
scenarios.why: With a brief in hand, 'Normalize cost' covers the right lines (renewal uplift, discount expiry, termination and data-export cost, stated vs calculated total). 'Do not fill a missing fee with zero' and the four coverage labels stop the usual errors. Layout varies between runs because no column template exists, but the content would be senior-grade.

scenarios.prompt: Vendor A is per-seat annual in USD, B is usage-based monthly in EUR with a 2-year ramp, and C only gave a number in an email. We never wrote requirements. Just tell me which is cheapest by Friday.
scenarios.why: The first line assumes 'the approved requirements brief' and gives no fallback, so the coverage step has nothing to score against. There is no guidance on turning usage-based or ramped pricing into a comparable figure, which FX rate and date to use, or how to build usage scenarios. The 'never select' rule handles the Friday pressure, but the cost model depends on the model improvising.

vendor-requirements-brief.job: write vendor requirements brief before sourcing
vendor-requirements-brief.summary: A 31-line guide that turns a purchase request into MUST/SHOULD/COULD/OUT requirements, each with a verification test, plus a list of commercial fields every vendor must quote on, and gates vendor invitations on the request owner's agreement.
strengths: MUST/SHOULD/COULD/OUT with plain definitions tied to the stated outcome or a named owner's requirement
Every must or should needs a verification method (document, demo, reference, sample output, security review, contract term)
Explicitly bans vague labels like 'enterprise-ready' and 'easy to use'
The commercial field list matches vendor-quote-comparison's normalization fields, so the handoff is clean
Gate: no budget approval and no vendor invitation until the request owner agrees
missing: A brief template and a filled example
Criteria weights and knockout (pass/fail) requirements agreed before quotes arrive
Sourcing route choice (RFI/RFP/RFQ) and a sole-source justification path
A vendor-facing RFQ/RFP packet kept separate from the internal brief
UNKNOWN labelling and an ask_question intake for missing inputs
Data classification driving the security and privacy review tier, with a handoff to vendor-due-diligence or Lena
Stakeholder sign-off record and a timeline for vendor responses and Q&A
Standard IT must-haves when relevant (SSO/SCIM, data residency, accessibility, integrations, exit/data portability)

issues.quote: Return the brief, evaluation table, evidence request, and named approvers.
issues.problem: None of the four deliverables has a defined structure. The evaluation table's columns, weights and knockout criteria are never specified.
issues.fix: Ship templates/requirements-brief.md and an evaluation table with columns: requirement, priority, test, weight, knockout (Y/N), owner, evidence status. Require weights to be agreed before any quote arrives.

issues.quote: Write the brief before comparing vendors.
issues.problem: No step for choosing the sourcing route (RFI, RFP, RFQ, sole-source justification) and no handling of a pre-selected incumbent or favored vendor. That is where requirements most often get biased.
issues.fix: Add a 'Sourcing route' step: pick RFI/RFP/RFQ by how fixed the spec is, record a sole-source justification if the vendor is pre-chosen, and write requirements vendor-neutral with the named requester's sign-off.

issues.quote: Capture the current process and cost, users and volume
issues.problem: No instruction for missing facts. Asking for 'measurable' must-haves invites invented thresholds such as uptime or volume figures.
issues.fix: Gather the minimum inputs with ask_question, mark anything unsupplied as UNKNOWN, label each threshold as requester-supplied or proposed, and never invent a number.

issues.quote: data involved, systems touched, locations
issues.problem: Data sensitivity and location are captured but do not drive anything: no security or privacy review tier and no handoff to vendor-due-diligence or Lena.
issues.fix: Map data class and location to a review tier and add the matching due-diligence checks and reviewers to the brief (e.g. personal data → DPA and privacy reviewer).

issues.quote: Ask for the same currency, term, quantity, unit price, minimums, implementation, support, usage charges
issues.problem: Unclear whether 'Ask' means asking the user or asking vendors (an external action). Nothing separates the internal brief (budget, preferences) from a vendor-facing request.
issues.fix: Produce a separate vendor-facing request template that leaves out internal budget, keep it as a draft until the request owner approves, and send identical questions and Q&A answers to every vendor.

issues.quote: request for quote
issues.problem: This trigger promises an RFQ document, but the skill produces only an internal brief. 'software requirements' could also fire on product or engineering requirements requests elsewhere in the team.
issues.fix: Either add an RFQ packet template or remove the trigger, and replace 'software requirements' with 'purchase requirements'.

scenarios.prompt: Marketing wants a new email platform for about 40k contacts and 3 senders. Help me write the requirements before we talk to any vendors.
scenarios.why: 'Frame the request' gives a complete intake list, and the MoSCoW rules plus 'Each must or should has a test' produce testable requirements. The commercial fields line up with vendor-quote-comparison. Structure will vary without a template, and no weights are set, but the content is sound.

scenarios.prompt: Our CTO already picked Vendor X and wants a requirements doc so procurement signs off. Half the team prefers Y, the budget isn't approved, and legal says the tool will process EU customer data.
scenarios.why: The skill only says 'Write the brief before comparing vendors'. It has no guidance for a pre-selected or sole-source vendor, no warning against requirements written to fit one vendor, and no conflict-resolution step. 'data involved' is captured, but nothing routes EU personal data to vendor-due-diligence or Lena's privacy review. Budget status is recorded but not treated as a blocker.

vendor-contract-status.job: check vendor agreement status and coverage gaps
vendor-contract-status.summary: Anthropic's legal 'vendor-check' command, repackaged. It searches CLM, CRM, email, document storage and chat for one vendor's agreements, lists each agreement's status and key terms, runs an MSA/DPA/SOW/SLA/COI gap check, and reports which sources were and were not searched.
strengths: A per-source search plan (CLM, CRM, email, documents, chat) with specific things to look for and time windows
Entity disambiguation: legal vs trade name, abbreviations, parent/subsidiary, with an ask-to-clarify rule
A 'Sources Checked / Sources Unavailable' header that states how complete the report is
Gap analysis tied to the relationship type (e.g. MSA but no DPA when the vendor handles personal data)
Flags surviving obligations in expired agreements, has a not-legal-advice disclaimer, and is read-only with no external side effects
missing: Notice-deadline calculation (expiry minus notice period) with the formula and source clause
A source citation (document, section, date) for each extracted term
Executed vs draft vs mentioned-only status, and order of precedence for amendments
A workspace upload/paste fallback when no CLM or document store is connected
AutoGPT tool mapping (run_block Gmail/Drive/HubSpot/Slack, run_mcp_tool, connect_integration)
Data-transfer mechanism (SCCs), subprocessor list and BAA checks when personal or health data is involved
Owner fields and a next-action queue with named approvers
Handoffs to contract-renewal-tracker, counsel and Lena's dpa-checklist-review

issues.quote: /vendor-check [vendor name]
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash-command invocation (along with the '/vendor-check' title and 'This command' wording). AutoGPT has no slash dispatch, and the argument-hint frontmatter is dropped.
issues.fix: Remove the Invocation block, retitle the skill 'Vendor agreement status', and ask for the vendor name with ask_question when it is missing.

issues.quote: If you see unfamiliar placeholders or need to check which tools are connected, see [CONNECTORS.md](references/CONNECTORS.md).
issues.problem: CONNECTORS.md maps ~~categories to Box, Egnyte, Ironclad, DocuSign and SharePoint. None of these are AutoGPT blocks, and it links to an upstream .mcp.json that is not shipped.
issues.fix: Rewrite the reference to map categories to AutoGPT tools (Gmail, Google Drive, HubSpot and Slack via run_block; a CLM via run_mcp_tool; connect_integration when an account is missing).

issues.quote: If an agreement is approaching expiration (within 90 days), highlight this prominently
issues.problem: Keyed to expiry, not the notice deadline. With a 60–90 day notice clause, the chance to cancel or renegotiate has passed before this fires.
issues.fix: Calculate the last notice date as expiry minus the notice period, show the formula and the source clause, and flag when that date falls within 90 days. Hand ongoing tracking to contract-renewal-tracker.

issues.quote: For each agreement found, report:
issues.problem: No rule to cite the source document, section and date for each field, and nothing separates executed copies from drafts, redlines or email mentions. Draft terms could be reported as agreed.
issues.fix: Add Source and Execution-status columns (EXECUTED / DRAFT / MENTIONED ONLY). Take terms only from executed copies, apply amendments in order, and mark conflicts 'COUNSEL TO CONFIRM'.

issues.quote: Suggest the user check their CLM manually. Report what was found in other systems.
issues.problem: The fallback pushes work back to the user instead of asking them to upload or paste contracts and exports into the workspace.
issues.fix: When no CLM or document store is connected, ask for PDFs, a CLM export or a contract list via workspace upload and read them with read_workspace_file.

issues.quote: Liability cap, governing law, termination provisions
issues.problem: The key terms leave out items a procurement or legal-ops reviewer checks at renewal: price and uplift rules, committed spend, assignment/change of control, SLA credits, data-return duties, insurance minimums and COI expiry.
issues.fix: Extend the key-terms list and add owner fields (contract owner, business owner) to each agreement record.

issues.quote: or when checking for approaching expirations and surviving obligations
issues.problem: Overlaps contract-renewal-tracker (Vera) and dpa-checklist-review / subprocessor-register (Lena) with no stated boundary.
issues.fix: Scope it as a single-vendor status snapshot and route portfolio renewal tracking to contract-renewal-tracker and DPA content review to Lena.

issues.quote: Output a consolidated report:
issues.problem: The Step 5 template repeats the Step 3 table in a second format, which adds length without adding guidance.
issues.fix: Keep one per-agreement structure and move the full report template to templates/vendor-agreement-status.md.

scenarios.prompt: We're renewing Zendesk next quarter. What have we signed with them, and is anything missing? Gmail and Google Drive are connected.
scenarios.why: Steps 1–5 produce a solid inventory: name variants, email and document search, a status table, gap analysis and a Sources Checked/Unavailable header. The renewal-critical date is never calculated, though: the 90-day highlight is keyed to 'approaching expiration', not expiry minus notice period, so a 90-day notice clause could already be missed. Fields are not tied to a source document or section.

scenarios.prompt: Check what we've signed with Acme Data. We have no CLM; I'll drop a zip of PDFs in the workspace. Some are unsigned drafts, and a 2023 MSA has two amendments that disagree on the liability cap.
scenarios.why: Step 6 only says 'Suggest the user check their CLM manually' and never offers to read uploaded files or a workspace export. Nothing distinguishes executed copies from drafts, sets an order of precedence between amendments, or routes conflicting terms to counsel. A capable model would read the PDFs anyway, but the skill gives it no rules for the conflict.

vendor-evaluation.job: evaluate vendor cost and risk for decision
vendor-evaluation.summary: Anthropic's operations 'vendor-review' command, repackaged. It lists TCO, risk and performance checklist items and gives a markdown template ending in a Proceed/Negotiate/Pass recommendation with negotiation points.
strengths: A TCO framing that goes beyond licence fees to implementation, training, support and exit costs
The risk list includes concentration risk and business continuity, which are often missed
A likelihood × impact risk table with a mitigation column
A negotiation points section that no Vera original includes as a structured part of its output
The tip to upload proposals for extraction fits AutoGPT's workspace file flow
missing: An evidence standard and SOURCED/ASSUMED/UNKNOWN labels for every figure and risk rating
Different procedures for new-vendor, renewal and comparison cases
Renewal-specific analysis: notice deadline, usage vs commitment right-sizing, uplift benchmarks or caps, a draft counter gated on approval
Weighted criteria agreed before scoring, with must-have gaps not hidden in a total
Named approvers and the decisions owed, instead of a verdict
AutoGPT tool mapping and a CSV/paste fallback
Handoffs to vendor-due-diligence, procurement-decision-memo and counsel

issues.quote: [Proceed / Negotiate / Pass] — [Reasoning]
issues.problem: The template requires a vendor selection verdict. That directly breaks Vera's boundary ('Never ... choose a vendor') and procurement-decision-memo's rule against selecting.
issues.fix: If kept, replace it with 'Fit against stated criteria' and 'Decisions owed by named approvers'. Otherwise drop the package and move the risk table and negotiation points into procurement-decision-memo.

issues.quote: comparing two vendors side-by-side, or building a TCO breakdown and negotiation points before procurement sign-off
issues.problem: The description overlaps four of Vera's skills (quote comparison, due diligence, decision memo, performance review) and James's ops-vendor-and-procurement, so its triggers compete with more rigorous skills.
issues.fix: Drop it as a standalone skill. If it is kept for James, narrow it to 'quick single-vendor sanity check' and state the handoff to Vera's pipeline.

issues.quote: /vendor-review $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: Claude Code slash-command and $ARGUMENTS constructs that the AutoGPT harness does not support; the argument-hint is dropped too.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block and gather vendor, context and documents with ask_question.

issues.quote: | License/subscription | $[X] | [Per seat, flat, usage-based] |
issues.problem: The cost table has no source or assumption column and no rule for missing fees, so the model is invited to fill every $[X]. Exit cost is in the framework but missing from the template.
issues.fix: Add Source and Status (SOURCED / ASSUMED / UNKNOWN) columns and an exit-cost row, forbid zero-fill, and do the arithmetic in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Evaluate a vendor with structured analysis covering cost, risk, performance, and fit.
issues.problem: There are no ordered steps or decision points, only bullet lists under Evaluation Framework, and the new-vendor, renewal and comparison cases are not handled differently.
issues.fix: Branch by context: new vendor goes to brief → quotes → due diligence, renewal goes to notice date → usage vs commitment → counter draft, comparison goes to vendor-quote-comparison.

issues.quote: Vendor financial stability
issues.problem: Risk items have no evidence standard (financial statements, SOC 2 report scope and date, insurance). The model will rate likelihood and impact from impressions and may call a vendor unstable or secure without proof.
issues.fix: Require a dated source for each risk rating, or mark it UNKNOWN and route to vendor-due-diligence and the named reviewer.

issues.quote: If **~~procurement** is connected:
issues.problem: The ~~procurement and ~~knowledge base placeholders map to Coupa, Ariba and Zip, which have no AutoGPT block, and there is no CSV or Sheet fallback.
issues.fix: Map to Google Sheets, Notion or Airtable blocks, or to a pasted spend export, and use connect_integration when a connector is missing.

issues.problem: The 3-year total has no renewal uplift, usage growth or exit cost, and no formula, so it understates the true cost of ownership.
issues.fix: Show the year-by-year build with the uplift and usage assumptions and the formula, or defer to vendor-quote-comparison's normalized table.

scenarios.prompt: Here's Rippling's payroll proposal for 120 employees. Is it a good deal, and should we sign?
scenarios.why: The model fills the template: a Year-1/3-Year cost table, risk likelihood/impact, strengths, concerns and negotiation points. But it ends with '[Proceed / Negotiate / Pass]', which contradicts Vera's boundary. The $[X] cells have no source or UNKNOWN convention, so missing fees are likely guessed, and 'Vendor financial stability' is rated with no evidence standard.

scenarios.prompt: Our data-warehouse renewal is in 45 days and they want +18%. We use 60% of our commitment, have no procurement system, and all I have is last year's invoice and their renewal email.
scenarios.why: The only renewal help is the tip 'Include current spend'. There is no check of the notice deadline against the 45 days, no method for right-sizing the commitment to usage, no benchmark or cap on the uplift, and no draft-and-approve gate before a counter goes to the vendor. The ~~procurement branch does not apply. The model's own knowledge carries most of the answer, with the generic template around it.

cve-stack-relevance.job: assess whether a CVE affects our stack
cve-stack-relevance.summary: Walks one advisory through a seven-question exposure chain (package match, version range, loaded in the shipped service, vulnerable feature, attacker preconditions, impact, fix), then labels the result confirmed/likely/not affected/unknown with cited evidence and the next check.
strengths: The seven-step chain matches how an AppSec engineer actually decides exposure, going from package to version, then load, feature, access and impact
Four explicit relevance labels, including 'unknown', stop the model from forcing a verdict
'Do not use absence from a scanner as proof of safety' and 'fixed version present in the built artifact' are senior-grade rules
Requires the model to explain conflicts between vendor, maintainer and database records
missing: Advisory source order and CVE/GHSA/OSV alias resolution
Distro backport handling for OS packages in container images
CISA KEV / EPSS / public-PoC inputs
Reachability tooling (govulncheck, symbol search, image SBOM)
VEX-style output with justification codes
Minimum-inputs list and a fallback when no repo access
Rule against probing live systems

issues.quote: Does the installed version fall in the verified affected range?
issues.problem: It never says how to verify the range: which sources (vendor/maintainer advisory, GHSA, OSV, NVD), how to resolve CVE/GHSA/PYSEC aliases, or how to handle distro backports, where the fixed version string differs from upstream. This is the most common source of false positives.
issues.fix: Add a source order (maintainer/vendor > GHSA/OSV > NVD) and alias resolution. For OS packages, require the distro tracker's fixed version (Debian/Ubuntu/RHEL/Alpine) and not the upstream range.

issues.quote: Use this for one advisory or a small related set.
issues.problem: No inputs are named up front (advisory ID, lockfile/SBOM or image digest, the deployed service, its exposure) and no tools are named: GitHub block or upload to read the repo, web_fetch for the OSV/GHSA APIs, bash_exec to parse lockfiles. It gives no fallback when the repo is not reachable, and no handoff to vulnerability-triage for bigger batches.
issues.fix: Open with a minimum-inputs list and ask_question for missing ones, name the tool path with a paste/upload fallback, and route anything over a handful of advisories to vulnerability-triage.

issues.quote: Can an attacker meet the access and privilege conditions?
issues.problem: It gives no exploit-likelihood evidence (CISA KEV listing, EPSS, public PoC, vendor 'exploited in the wild'). It also has no rule against trying to exploit or probe live systems to answer this question.
issues.fix: Add KEV/EPSS/PoC status as cited inputs to urgency, and state that the model must never run exploit code or probes against production or third-party systems; reachability is shown from code and config.

issues.quote: Label the result **confirmed**, **likely**, **not affected**, or **unknown**.
issues.problem: There is no output template. Senior practice records 'not affected' with a VEX justification (for example, vulnerable_code_not_present or vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path) so the decision can be audited and fed back to scanners.
issues.fix: Ship a per-step evidence table plus a result block with label, VEX status/justification, sources and check time, next action, and owner. Note that Devon drafts the VEX statement and the owner accepts it.

issues.quote: Does the shipped service include and load it?
issues.problem: It gives no method for showing reachability: searching for the vulnerable symbol named in the advisory, govulncheck symbol-level results, import/call-site search, or an SBOM of the built image (syft) instead of the source manifest.
issues.fix: List concrete reachability checks per ecosystem and require the evidence to come from the built artifact where possible.

issues.quote: Answer each question with evidence:
issues.problem: It has no decision points. The chain should stop at the first proven 'no' (not affected) and fall to 'unknown' at the first step with no evidence, but the skill implies all seven questions are always answered.
issues.fix: State the stopping rules and which label each outcome produces.

issues.quote: Name the smallest check or change that resolves the uncertainty or risk.
issues.problem: The next action has no owner or deadline basis, and there is no handoff to dependency-upgrade-plan or dependency-upgrade-pr.
issues.fix: Add owner, deadline basis, and the sibling skill to load next.

scenarios.prompt: Dependabot flagged CVE-2024-35195 in requests (<2.32.0). Our poetry.lock pins 2.31.0 in the api service. Are we actually affected?
scenarios.why: Steps 1-2 confirm PyPI requests 2.31.0 is in range. Step 3 checks whether it is a runtime dependency of the api image. Step 4 ('Is the vulnerable feature or configuration present?') sends the model to look for Session use with verify=False. So a capable model reaches a cited 'not affected' or 'likely' and names the next step (bump to 2.32.x). Nothing essential is missing for a single, well-documented library CVE.

scenarios.prompt: Trivy lists CVE-2023-4911 (glibc Looney Tunables) plus ~40 OS-package CVEs in our python:3.12-slim base image. The Debian tracker marks several as fixed in a deb12uN release or 'unimportant'. Which ones matter?
scenarios.why: Step 2 compares the installed version with the 'verified affected range' but never warns that distro packages carry backported fixes under upstream version strings. The model may therefore mark fixed packages as affected. There is no pointer to the distro security tracker, no KEV/EPSS input for prioritising, and no container-context reasoning (for example, a local setuid escalation inside a non-root container). Forty findings also exceed 'one advisory or a small related set', and the skill never hands off to vulnerability-triage.

dependency-change-risk-review.job: review a dependency change for risk
dependency-change-risk-review.summary: Reviews a proposed dependency change for supply-chain signals (registry, checksums, maintainer/transfer, install scripts, binaries, transitive churn) and application impact, then returns a ready/needs-changes/blocked decision brief with rollback safety.
strengths: Names concrete supply-chain red flags: renamed/transferred packages, install scripts, new binary downloads, large transitive-tree changes
Separates production and development paths and maps each risk to a test, signal or open gap
Asks whether a data or config change makes rollback unsafe, which reviewers often miss
Clear 'do not approve, merge, deploy, or waive' line
missing: Provenance/attestation and release-age cooldown checks
Malicious-package and typosquat lookup
License-change review
Decision criteria for the three statuses
Safe tarball inspection without running install scripts
Draft-then-approve before posting a PR review
Output template for the decision brief

issues.quote: Confirm the old and new resolved versions, source registry, checksums or lock
issues.problem: It is missing current supply-chain controls: build provenance/attestations (npm provenance, PyPI attestations, Sigstore), release-age cooldown for very new versions, malicious-package advisories, typosquat and name-similarity checks, and lockfile resolved-URL or integrity changes without a version change.
issues.fix: Add a short supply-chain checklist that covers these checks, with the evidence each one needs.

issues.problem: The review never checks license changes in the direct or transitive tree (for example, a move to AGPL/SSPL/BUSL or a missing license). This is a standard part of dependency change review.
issues.fix: Add a license-delta check and route any change needing legal judgement to the owner or a legal teammate.

issues.quote: Use **ready for review**, **needs changes**, or **blocked on evidence**.
issues.problem: It gives no criteria for choosing a status, so the same evidence can produce different verdicts.
issues.fix: Define each status. For example: blocked = versions, provenance or advisory status not established; needs changes = any unmitigated high-impact finding or missing test for a changed API; ready = every risk mapped to a passing check or an accepted gap.

issues.quote: Flag renamed or transferred packages, install scripts, new binary downloads,
issues.problem: To inspect those scripts the model may install the new version, which runs lifecycle scripts from a possibly malicious package. The skill gives no safe-inspection rule.
issues.fix: Inspect tarballs with npm pack / pip download --no-deps and install with --ignore-scripts inside the sandbox only. Never run the package's scripts with credentials present.

issues.quote: Use this on a proposed plan, patch, or pull request.
issues.problem: No inputs are named and there is no tool route: read the PR diff through the GitHub block, or accept a pasted lockfile diff when there is no integration.
issues.fix: List the inputs (PR link or diff, base lockfile, target services) and name a GitHub-block path with a paste/upload fallback.

issues.quote: Do not approve, merge, deploy, or waive a check.
issues.problem: Posting review comments or a GitHub review is itself an external action. The skill does not say to draft the review and get user approval before posting.
issues.fix: Draft the brief first; post to the PR only after approval.

issues.quote: dependency PR review
issues.problem: This collides with dependency-upgrade-pr's 'dependency pull request' and 'upgrade PR' triggers, so 'review the dependency PR' may load the drafting skill instead.
issues.fix: Use review-specific triggers ('review a Dependabot/Renovate PR', 'is this bump safe') and say in the description that it reviews someone else's change.

scenarios.prompt: Review this Renovate PR: axios 1.6.8 -> 1.7.4 in the web app, plus 12 transitive lockfile changes. Is it safe to hand to the team?
scenarios.why: 'Review the evidence' checks the resolved versions, registry and release notes. 'Review the application impact' searches for changed defaults and runtime needs (for example, the fetch adapter in 1.7) and maps each risk to a test. The decision brief gives a status and the lockfile rollback. A capable model produces a useful review.

scenarios.prompt: Dependabot bumped transitive `debug` to a patch version published 3 hours ago; CI is green and the diff is lockfile-only. Approve?
scenarios.why: It mentions 'maintainer status' and 'install scripts' and warns that 'A clean diff does not prove a safe runtime change'. But it has no release-age cooldown, no provenance/attestation check, no malicious-package lookup (OSV MAL-, npm advisories), and no check for a changed resolved URL or integrity in the lockfile. That is exactly how 2025-style npm account-takeover releases got through. The model could easily return 'ready for review'.

dependency-inventory.summary: Collects every manifest, lockfile, base image, build action and runtime pin, records per-package version/scope/evidence fields, reconciles conflicts, and returns a table, gap list and totals without over-claiming production use.
strengths: Prefers locked or installed versions over manifest ranges and keeps both
Covers often-missed sources: workspace roots, shipped examples, base images, CI build actions, runtime pins
Reconciliation rules (no cross-ecosystem merging, duplicate majors, stale lockfiles, scanner and lockfile disagreement) are practitioner-level
Guardrails against inferring production use and declaring the inventory complete too early
missing: CycloneDX/SPDX or CSV output file
License, purl, registry and hash fields
Per-ecosystem listing commands and a sandbox method
OS packages in images and vendored code
Action/image pin status
Scale guidance for large transitive trees

issues.quote: Return a table, an evidence-gap list, and totals by ecosystem and use.
issues.problem: No machine-readable artefact is produced. A full transitive table does not fit in chat for real repos, and the trigger 'SBOM' implies an SBOM is the deliverable.
issues.fix: Write inventory.csv and a CycloneDX/SPDX JSON to the workspace (write_workspace_file); in chat show totals, the top gaps, and where the files are.

issues.quote: ecosystem, package, installed version, and requested range;
issues.problem: The field list leaves out license, purl, source registry and package hash. Without license and purl the inventory cannot feed license review, vulnerability matching or SBOM exchange.
issues.fix: Add purl, declared license, registry/source URL, and integrity hash to the record fields.

issues.quote: Find every package manifest and lockfile in scope.
issues.problem: It gives no method or tool path: how to get the repo (GitHub block, upload, bash_exec clone), which read-only listing commands to use (npm ls --all --json, pnpm list, poetry show --tree, go list -m -json all, syft for images), or a warning against installing to resolve.
issues.fix: Add per-ecosystem lockfile-parse or list commands for bash_exec, prefer parsing over installing, and give a paste/upload fallback.

issues.quote: plugins, examples that ship, container base images, build actions, and language
issues.problem: Base images are listed, but not the OS packages inside them (dpkg/apk/rpm), vendored or copied third-party code, or whether CI actions and images are pinned by SHA or digest.
issues.fix: Add OS packages from image SBOMs, a vendored-code search, and pin status for actions and images.

issues.quote: Use this before judging age or security risk.
issues.problem: No inputs are asked for up front (repo, commit, which services and images count as deployable), and it does not reuse the scope recorded by dependency-security-getting-started.
issues.fix: Read the stored scope from memory, or ask for repo/commit/services before collecting.

issues.quote: manifests with no matching lockfile. If a scanner and lockfile disagree, show
issues.problem: Stale lockfiles are to be flagged, but the skill never says how to detect them (for example, npm ci --dry-run, poetry check --lock, uv lock --check).
issues.fix: Name a staleness check per ecosystem.

scenarios.prompt: Give me a dependency baseline for our repo: Python backend with poetry.lock, Next.js frontend with pnpm-lock.yaml, and two Dockerfiles.
scenarios.why: 'Collect' finds the right sources and 'For each item record' defines good fields. But a real pnpm lock has more than 1,000 transitive packages, and 'Return a table' in chat is unusable at that size. The skill never says to write a CSV or CycloneDX file to the workspace. It gives no commands for listing the tree or the image OS packages and asks for no license column, so the baseline cannot serve license or SBOM needs.

scenarios.prompt: No repo access yet. Here is a Snyk CSV export and a requirements.txt with unpinned ranges. Build the inventory anyway.
scenarios.why: The skill handles partial data well. It tells the model to keep requested ranges apart from installed versions, record 'whether the version could not be resolved', flag 'unlocked production dependencies', show scanner-versus-manifest disagreements with the check that would settle them, and refuse to call the inventory complete. A capable model returns an honest, gap-labelled inventory.

dependency-security-getting-started.job: onboard dependency security scope and baseline
dependency-security-getting-started.summary: Onboards dependency-security work by recording scope and exposure questions, gathering manifests/lockfiles/SBOMs/scanner exports, and returning a five-part first brief plus an explicit approval line.
strengths: Asks about public exposure, sensitive data and uptime at the start, which is the right risk context
Keeps requested versions apart from installed ones and dates every external advisory
The five-part first brief (scope, gaps, confirmed risks, next three actions, approvals) is a usable skeleton
Explicit approval line consistent with Devon's boundaries
missing: Memory persistence of scope, owners and SLA
Inventory of existing scanners and update bots
Remediation SLA or policy capture
Routing to sibling skills
GitHub connect or upload fallback
Offer of a recurring hygiene routine via schedule_routine

issues.quote: Record the repository, branch or commit, supported runtimes, deployed services,
issues.problem: 'Record' has no destination. Scope, owners and exposure answers are never stored with memory_store, so later skills and sessions cannot reuse them. For an onboarding skill this is the core failure.
issues.fix: Persist the scope record (repo, services, exposure tiers, owners, approvers, SLA) to memory and tell the sibling skills to read it.

issues.quote: The next three checks or upgrades, in order.
issues.problem: The next steps are not mapped to Devon's other skills, so the getting-started skill does not act as a router.
issues.fix: Map each next step to dependency-inventory, vulnerability-triage, cve-stack-relevance, outdated-dependency-review or dependency-upgrade-plan.

issues.quote: Ask which systems face the public,
issues.problem: It never captures the existing tooling (Dependabot/Renovate/Snyk/Trivy config, GitHub security alerts), the remediation SLA or policy, or who owns and approves fixes. Ranking and the approval line depend on all three.
issues.fix: Add questions for current scanners and update bots, SLA per severity or exposure tier, remediation owners, and approvers.

issues.problem: There is no integration step or fallback: no connect_integration for GitHub, and no request for an uploaded lockfile, SBOM or scanner export when access is missing.
issues.fix: Offer to connect GitHub, otherwise ask for specific exports, and continue with whatever is provided.

issues.quote: Confirmed risks, each with package, installed version, source, and exposure.
issues.problem: A first-pass brief usually cannot confirm exposure, and the skill does not say to apply the cve-stack-relevance labels. This invites over-claiming.
issues.fix: Require the confirmed/likely/not affected/unknown labels and include 'likely' and 'unknown' items separately.

issues.quote: Collect manifests, lockfiles, container definitions, software bills of
issues.problem: This repeats dependency-inventory's Collect step, so the two can drift apart.
issues.fix: Delegate collection to dependency-inventory and keep only the scope and first brief here.

issues.quote: software supply chain
issues.problem: Generic triggers ('software supply chain', 'dependency review') overlap with Toran's supply-chain-risk-auditor and with dependency-change-risk-review.
issues.fix: Use onboarding phrasing ('where do we start', 'set up dependency security', 'first audit').

scenarios.prompt: Hi Devon, here's our GitHub repo acme/app. Where should we start on dependency security?
scenarios.why: 'Set the scope' asks good exposure questions and 'Return the first brief' produces a sensible five-part answer. But nothing is stored with memory_store, so the next session starts over. It never asks what scanners, Dependabot or Renovate already run, or what remediation SLA applies. 'Confirmed risks' asks for confirmation without pointing to the cve-stack-relevance chain, so the model either over-claims or does the triage ad hoc.

scenarios.prompt: You can't access the repo yet, but here's a Dependabot alerts CSV with 230 open alerts. The CTO wants a plan by Friday.
scenarios.why: 'List anything you cannot inspect' and 'Gaps that could change the result' keep the model honest. But the skill gives no route for triaging a large queue with limited stack evidence: no handoff to vulnerability-triage, no KEV/EPSS or runtime-versus-dev prioritisation, no connect_integration request for GitHub, and no suggestion to schedule a recurring hygiene routine.

dependency-upgrade-plan.summary: Once current and target versions are known, reads release/migration sources and repo usage, then writes a seven-part plan (reason, files, edits, tests, checks, rollout owner/window/stop conditions, rollback) and splits unrelated upgrades.
strengths: The seven-section plan maps to what a reviewer needs, from reason through rollback
Requires naming every source and the versions it covers
Splits major, framework, runtime and unrelated security upgrades
Clear approval line: a plan does not authorise a merge, deploy or data migration
missing: Resolver and peer-constraint analysis
Stepwise major or LTS path selection
Codemods and a deprecation-warning pass
Irreversible-migration handling
Inputs up front and a route when the target is unknown
A rule against invented owners or windows

issues.quote: Check release notes, migration guides, support policy, known regressions, and
issues.problem: It skips the parts of upgrade planning that usually cause failures: resolver and peer-dependency constraints from other packages, runtime minimums, stepwise major hops (for example, LTS to LTS), official codemods, and a deprecation-warning pass on the current version.
issues.fix: Add a compatibility step: dry-run the resolver, list dependents that pin the old version, choose the intermediate hops, and name the codemods and deprecation flags to run first.

issues.quote: Use this once the current and target versions are known.
issues.problem: There is no route when the target is unknown or blocked, and no inputs are asked for up front (services, deadline, owners, environments).
issues.fix: If the target is unknown, use outdated-dependency-review or ask. Gather the minimum inputs with ask_question before planning.

issues.quote: Rollout owner, observation window, and stop conditions.
issues.problem: The model is never told to ask for these or to mark them TBD, so it may invent owners, windows or metrics.
issues.fix: Require the user to supply these or mark them 'owner to confirm'; never invent names or thresholds.

issues.quote: Exact rollback route.
issues.problem: It does not flag irreversible steps (schema or data-format migrations, serialised cache formats, lockfile plus data changes), which make a lockfile revert unsafe.
issues.fix: List the irreversible steps separately, order them after the observation window, and describe a roll-forward path where rollback is impossible.

issues.problem: No tool routing: web_fetch or the GitHub releases block for changelogs, bash_exec to search the repo for affected APIs, and a paste fallback when there is no repo access.
issues.fix: Name the tool path and the fallback.

issues.quote: "package upgrade", "update library"
issues.problem: These generic triggers overlap with dependency-upgrade-pr ('bump package') and outdated-dependency-review ('package updates').
issues.fix: Use planning-specific phrases ('plan the upgrade to X', 'migration plan', 'how risky is moving to vN').

scenarios.prompt: Plan upgrading our Next.js app from 13.5 to 15. We're mostly pages router with a few app-router routes.
scenarios.why: 'Read before planning' sends the model to the 14 and 15 migration guides and has it search the repo for the changed APIs. The split rule separates the framework upgrade from the React and Node runtime changes. The seven plan sections produce a structured, testable plan, and a capable model fills in codemods from its own knowledge.

scenarios.prompt: We need to move three services from Pydantic v1 to v2, but one service depends on an SDK that still pins pydantic<2. We haven't picked the exact target yet. Security wants this done in two weeks.
scenarios.why: The skill starts 'once the current and target versions are known' and gives no route when the target is undecided. It has no step for resolver or peer-dependency conflicts, compatibility shims (the pydantic.v1 namespace), or trading the deadline against risk. The model may also fill 'Rollout owner, observation window' with invented values because it is never told to ask.

dependency-upgrade-pr.job: draft a dependency upgrade pull request
dependency-upgrade-pr.summary: After a reviewed plan, makes a narrow manifest+lockfile change with required code edits only, validates with tests/tree/artifact/scanner reruns, and drafts a PR description with versions, sources, evidence, risk and rollback, stopping short of merge.
strengths: Strict scope: no formatting, refactors, unrelated bumps or silent suppressions
Validation order (smallest tests, then project checks, resolved tree, built artifact, scanner rerun) is correct
PR body fields cover versions, sources, behaviour change, evidence, risk, rollout and rollback
Stop point forbids merging, bypassing a failed check, or claiming production is fixed
missing: Approval gate before any push or PR creation
Patch-file fallback without write access
Transitive override or resolution mechanics
Sandbox toolchain and credential fallback
Repo PR template and commit convention detection
Embargo-aware PR wording

issues.quote: Mark it draft when approval or a check remains.
issues.problem: Pushing a branch and opening a PR are external side effects. The skill never requires showing the diff and PR body and getting user approval first, and it gives no fallback (a patch file or diff) when there is no write access.
issues.fix: Add a gate: prepare the diff and PR body, present them, and push or open a draft PR through the GitHub integration only after approval. Otherwise deliver a patch file via write_workspace_file.

issues.quote: Update the manifest and lockfile with the package manager.
issues.problem: It has no guidance for transitive-only fixes (overrides/resolutions/constraints/replace) or for minimal targeted updates (for example, npm update pkg --package-lock-only, poetry update pkg), so the lockfile may change far more than intended.
issues.fix: Add per-ecosystem targeted-update and override commands, with a tracked note to remove each override.

issues.quote: Inspect the resolved dependency tree and built artifact.
issues.problem: The E2B sandbox may lack the toolchain, private-registry credentials or Docker. The skill gives no fallback and does not warn that installing the new version runs its lifecycle scripts.
issues.fix: Say to rely on CI checks and list the unrun steps as gaps when a local build is impossible, and to install with --ignore-scripts first for unfamiliar packages.

issues.quote: the draft and evidence to the named reviewer.
issues.problem: The reviewer is never collected as an input, and there is no handoff to dependency-change-risk-review.
issues.fix: Take the reviewer from CODEOWNERS or ask for one, and suggest running dependency-change-risk-review on the draft.

issues.quote: State the old and new versions, reason, advisory or release-note sources,
issues.problem: It does not check whether the advisory is public before describing it. A PR in a public repo can disclose an embargoed or unfixed vulnerability.
issues.fix: If the advisory is private or embargoed, use neutral PR wording and keep the details in the private security channel.

issues.quote: dependency pull request
issues.problem: This collides with dependency-change-risk-review's 'dependency PR review'.
issues.fix: Use authoring phrases ('open the upgrade PR', 'make the bump', 'prepare the fix branch').

scenarios.prompt: The plan's approved. Open the PR bumping lodash 4.17.20 -> 4.17.21 in the web app.
scenarios.why: 'Keep the change narrow' and 'Validate' lead to a clean lockfile bump and a scanner rerun, and 'Draft the pull request' lists good body fields. But the skill never says how to get write access (the GitHub block, since bash_exec has no user secrets). It never tells the model to show the diff and PR body and wait for approval before pushing, or what to hand over as a patch file if it cannot push.

scenarios.prompt: The vulnerable package is transitive (minimist under an unmaintained parent with no fixed release). CI takes 40 minutes and you can't run the Docker build.
scenarios.why: 'Update the manifest and lockfile with the package manager' gives no route for transitive-only fixes: npm overrides, pnpm.overrides, yarn resolutions, a Poetry constraint, or Go replace, each with a note to remove it later. 'Record ... anything you could not run' and 'Mark it draft' handle the missing Docker build honestly, so the result is safe but depends on the model's own knowledge for the actual fix.

outdated-dependency-review.summary: A 37-line placeholder that takes an existing outdated-package report, checks each direct dependency's version gap, support status and release notes, and sorts packages into Act now / Plan / Watch / Unknown with a reason, change size, owner and next review date.
strengths: Separates newest compatible from newest stable and refuses the registry 'latest' tag as proof of safety
Four-bucket model with an explicit Unknown bucket, so unproven items are not forced into a priority
Keeps security severity linked to its advisory instead of copying it into the freshness review
Approval gate before any version-range or lockfile change, plus a ban on bundling unrelated upgrades
Asks for a test owner and next review date per item, which makes the backlog actionable
missing: Named inputs and per-ecosystem commands to produce the outdated report in the sandbox, with a paste/CSV fallback
Runtime, base-image and framework EOL checks with a dated source (vendor policy or endoflife.date)
Change-size rubric based on semver level, 0.x packages and breaking-change count from migration notes
Detection of deprecated, archived or abandoned packages as an 'unsupported' signal
Backlog table template with sort order and a short executive summary
Rules for grouping coupled packages and peer dependencies
A drift metric (majors behind or libyears) so progress can be tracked over time
Explicit handoffs to dependency-inventory, vulnerability-triage and dependency-upgrade-plan, plus a recurring review cadence

issues.quote: Use this to turn an update report into an ordered backlog.
issues.problem: No inputs are named and there is no way to get the data. The skill assumes a report exists and never says how to generate one per ecosystem, what access it needs, or what to do if the user has only a repo link. Nothing points to dependency-inventory as the prerequisite.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step. Ask for repo/branch or the manifests and lockfiles, plus deployed services. Generate the report in the sandbox (`npm/pnpm outdated --json`, `pip list --outdated`, `poetry show --outdated`, `go list -u -m all`, `bundle outdated`). Otherwise ask for a pasted or exported report, and run dependency-inventory first when no inventory exists.

issues.quote: For each direct dependency, record the installed version, newest compatible
issues.problem: Only direct packages are in scope. Language runtimes, container base images, frameworks, CI actions and old transitive pins held by a direct parent are left out, yet runtime and base-image EOL is usually the highest-value 'Act now' item.
issues.fix: Add runtimes, base images, build tools and framework lines to the scope. Check support and EOL against the vendor policy or endoflife.date with the date checked. Include a transitive package when a direct parent pins it below a supported line.

issues.quote: State the reason, likely change size, affected services, test owner, and next
issues.problem: Fields are listed but there is no deliverable format: no table columns, no sort order within a bucket, no summary header and no evidence/source column. Output shape will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Provide a backlog table template (package, ecosystem, installed, compatible, latest, gap type, support/EOL + source, bucket, reason, change size, services, test owner, next review). Sort by bucket, then change size, then exposure, and add a three-line summary and an evidence-gap list.

issues.quote: **Act now** — unsupported, exposed security fix, broken compatibility, or a
issues.problem: The bucket criteria depend on undefined terms. 'Unsupported' has no definition (vendor EOL, registry deprecation, archived repo, no release in N months) and 'change size' has no rubric (semver level, 0.x caveat, number of call sites of changed APIs).
issues.fix: Define 'unsupported' signals and add a small/medium/large change-size rubric tied to semver level, migration-guide breaking changes and a repo search for affected APIs.

issues.quote: Read the release notes and migration guide for candidate versions. Do not use a
issues.problem: There is no scaling rule. On a 60-package report the model either reads every changelog or silently skips some.
issues.fix: Read migration guides in full for major bumps and Act now/Plan candidates, skim changelogs for minor/patch groups, and mark the rest 'notes not read' rather than dropping them.

issues.quote: bundle unrelated upgrades merely to clear a dashboard. Never change version
issues.problem: The skill warns against unrelated bundling but never says which packages must move together (peer dependencies, package families such as @babel/*, react/react-dom, aws-sdk v3 clients, framework plus plugins). Splitting those breaks builds.
issues.fix: Add a grouping rule: coupled packages and peer-dependency sets move as one item, and unrelated ones stay separate.

issues.quote: Keep security findings linked to their advisory rather than
issues.problem: No handoff is named. Security items should go to vulnerability-triage, and Act now/Plan items to dependency-upgrade-plan, but the skill leaves that implicit. The 'next review date' also has no follow-up mechanism.
issues.fix: Name the handoffs to vulnerability-triage and dependency-upgrade-plan. Offer schedule_routine for the next review, or suggest Renovate/Dependabot grouping config as a draft.

scenarios.prompt: Here's the `npm outdated` output for our web app (about 40 rows). What should we actually upgrade this sprint and what can wait?
scenarios.why: The Current/Wanted/Latest columns map straight onto 'installed / newest compatible / newest stable', and the four buckets give a sensible split. However, 'Read the release notes and migration guide for candidate versions' has no scaling rule for 40 packages. 'likely change size' has no rubric (semver major/minor/patch, 0.x), there is no table template or sort order within a bucket, and there is no named source for support or EOL status. So two runs would give differently shaped backlogs.

scenarios.prompt: No update report, just our GitHub monorepo: a Python service on poetry.lock, a Next.js app on pnpm-lock, and a Dockerfile still on node:18. Which upgrades matter?
scenarios.why: The skill assumes an update report already exists ('turn an update report into an ordered backlog'). It gives no way to produce one (`poetry show --outdated` / `pnpm outdated` in the bash_exec sandbox, or registry queries), no paste/export fallback, and no pointer to run dependency-inventory first. Scope is limited to 'each direct dependency', so the EOL Node 18 runtime and base image, the most urgent 'Act now' item, is likely missed.

vulnerability-triage.job: triage dependency vulnerability findings into ranked queue
vulnerability-triage.summary: A 37-line placeholder that has the model verify each scanner or advisory finding against its source and affected ranges, gather stack exposure evidence, and return a queue labelled confirmed / likely / not affected / unknown with urgency, safe target version, workaround, owner and deadline basis.
strengths: 'Severity is an input, not the result', which is the core stance of senior vulnerability management
Four relevance labels (confirmed / likely / not affected / unknown) that match VEX-style thinking
Stack-evidence checklist covering the shipped artifact, the loading service, the enabled feature, who can reach the path, the data at risk and compensating controls
Source hierarchy: maintainer or vendor advisory first, then a recognised database, with disputed data flagged
Strong guardrails: no closing a finding because it is transitive or low-score, no exploitability claim without path evidence, no suppression or risk acceptance by the agent
Asks for a deadline basis and validation steps per item
missing: Named inputs: scanner/format, repo or image access, exposure of each service, organisational SLA policy
Alias dedupe (CVE/GHSA/OSV) and grouping by remediation action
Exploitation signals: CISA KEV, EPSS, public exploit or PoC availability
A defined urgency scale mapped to deadlines, with an assumed-versus-policy label
Reachability and dependency-path evidence methods using sandbox tools, with a paste fallback
Distro and OS package handling with backported fixes, and 'no fix available' states
VEX-style justifications and recheck triggers for not-affected results
Queue table template and summary; handoffs to cve-stack-relevance and dependency-upgrade-plan

issues.quote: Severity is an input, not the result.
issues.problem: The skill says what urgency is not, but never how to set it. There is no urgency scale, no use of CISA KEV, EPSS or public exploit availability, no internet-exposure weighting and no mapping to an organisation's remediation SLA.
issues.fix: Add an urgency matrix (relevance × exploitation signal [KEV/EPSS/public PoC] × exposure [internet-facing/internal/dev-only]) mapped to P0–P3. Take the deadline from the user's policy if one exists, otherwise label the SLA an assumption.

issues.quote: For every finding capture the advisory ID, package and ecosystem, installed
issues.problem: There is no strategy for real scanner exports. The same vulnerability appears under CVE, GHSA and OSV aliases and once per dependency path, and a single upgrade often clears dozens of findings. Checking every finding one by one does not scale.
issues.fix: Add a normalise step: merge aliases, collapse findings by package + installed version + fixed version, and group the queue by remediation action (one upgrade or base-image rebuild per row) with the finding IDs it clears.

issues.quote: Check whether the package is present in the shipped artifact, which service
issues.problem: This section restates the seven-question chain in the sibling skill cve-stack-relevance. The description doesn't say 'bulk queue', so both skills compete for requests like 'are we vulnerable / dependency alert'.
issues.fix: Rewrite the description to cover bulk scanner exports and queues. Do a quick exposure pass here and hand individual high-stakes items to cve-stack-relevance for the full proof.

issues.quote: Return these fields: relevance, urgency, reason, safe target version,
issues.problem: Fields are listed but there is no deliverable template, sort order or summary. 'Safe target version' is undefined: it should be the smallest fixed version on the same supported line, not the latest.
issues.fix: Provide a queue table template plus a summary (counts by relevance and urgency, top three actions, evidence gaps). Define the safe target as the minimum fixed version on the current major unless that line is EOL.

issues.quote: loads it, whether the vulnerable feature is enabled, who can reach the path,
issues.problem: There is no method for proving reachability or the dependency path, and no use of the sandbox, so 'likely' versus 'confirmed' comes down to the model's judgement.
issues.fix: List evidence methods: dependency path via `npm ls`, `pipdeptree` or `go mod why`; `govulncheck` or `osv-scanner` in bash_exec; a repo search for the vulnerable function or config flag; the image manifest. When access is missing, ask for a paste of these.

issues.quote: Use this for scanner results or a list of advisories.
issues.problem: No inputs are named up front: scanner and version, repo or image access, which services are internet-facing or handle sensitive data, and any remediation-SLA policy. There is no fallback when only a report is available.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step that uses ask_question for the minimum context, and say which conclusions degrade to 'unknown' without it.

issues.quote: Prefer the package maintainer or vendor advisory, then a recognised
issues.problem: There is no handling of OS or distro packages, where vendors backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so upstream affected ranges produce false 'confirmed' results for container images.
issues.fix: For OS packages, use the distro security tracker (Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL) and its fixed package version. Treat 'no fix available / will not fix' as its own state, with a rebuild or mitigation action.

issues.quote: **confirmed**, **likely**, **not affected**, or **unknown** for relevance.
issues.problem: A 'not affected' verdict has no required justification or recheck trigger, so it silently goes stale when config or code changes. Transitive findings, which the guardrail rightly protects, have no remediation route.
issues.fix: Require a VEX-style justification (component not present, vulnerable code not in execute path, etc.) and a recheck condition for 'not affected'. Add transitive fix options (parent upgrade, overrides, resolutions or constraints) marked as drafts that need approval.

scenarios.prompt: Attached is our Dependabot alerts export for the api repo: 37 open alerts, 12 marked critical. Which ones do we fix first and what's the target version for each?
scenarios.why: The model would verify sources and ranges and label relevance correctly. But the skill defines no urgency scale or SLA mapping and no exploitation signals (CISA KEV, EPSS, public exploit). It never says to collapse duplicate alerts that share one fixed version or CVE/GHSA alias, and gives no table template. The queue would be defensible but inconsistent and longer than it needs to be.

scenarios.prompt: Trivy flagged about 400 CVEs on our production container image, mostly Debian OS packages plus a few npm ones. I can only give you the JSON, no repo access. What actually matters?
scenarios.why: There is no triage-at-scale step (filter by fix availability, KEV/EPSS, group by package and base-image rebuild). There is no handling of distro packages where Debian backports fixes, so comparing upstream affected ranges would mislabel findings as confirmed. Without repo or runtime access, 'Mark unproven points unknown' turns most of the 400 into 'unknown' with no route to narrow them, such as asking which services are internet-facing or recommending a base-image refresh as one action.

code-change-security-review.summary: Trail of Bits' differential-review packaged for Devon: a phased security review of a PR or commit range (triage by risk and codebase size, git-history regression hunting, test-gap and blast-radius analysis, adversarial exploit modelling) ending in a nine-section markdown report, with Solidity-centred pattern and example references.
strengths: Trail of Bits provenance with a pinned commit, licence and a clear attribution record
Rationalizations table that pre-empts common reviewer shortcuts ('Heartbleed was 2 lines', 'refactors break invariants')
Regression hunting with git blame and `git log -S` on removed or re-added code, which most review skills miss
Depth adapts to risk and codebase size, with a priority matrix combining change risk and blast radius
Test-coverage risk elevation rules (new function without tests, modified validation with unchanged tests)
Concrete attacker-model template with proof of accessibility and an EASY/MEDIUM/HARD exploitability rating
Report template includes an Analysis Methodology section with scope percentages, limitations and confidence
missing: Explicit inputs and access modes (public clone, GitHub block for private PRs, pasted diff) with the confidence level for each
Web/API vulnerability patterns mapped to CWE/OWASP, including authz/IDOR, injection, SSRF, deserialization and path traversal
Secret and credential detection in the diff
A path for reviewing new code (greenfield) and routing of dependency/lockfile diffs to dependency-change-risk-review
Rules on disclosure and PoC execution, plus drafting and approval before posting findings to a PR
Blast radius weighted by reachability from untrusted entry points rather than raw grep counts
Severity tied to a standard (CVSS or a stated rubric) instead of emoji tiers
An AutoGPT-native report location via write_workspace_file and a chat summary template without Claude-specific paths

issues.quote: **`differential-review:adversarial-modeler`** — Models attacker perspectives and
