issues.problem: This tells the model to dispatch a namespaced Claude Code subagent via `subagent_type`. That agent isn't shipped and AutoGPT has no Task tool, so the dispatch fails. The decision tree also offers it as a route.
issues.fix: Delete the Agents section and the decision-tree branch, and route Phase 5 straight to adversarial.md. For a second opinion, use consult_teammate with a named expert.

issues.quote: Pre-Analysis → Phase 0: Triage → Phase 1: Code Analysis → Phase 2: Test Coverage
issues.problem: Inputs are never named (repo URL, PR number, base/head refs, access). The workflow assumes a local git checkout with full history and an authenticated `gh`, but the AutoGPT sandbox has no user secrets, and there is no fallback for a private repo or a pasted diff.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs & access step with three modes. (1) Public repo: clone in bash_exec with full history. (2) Private repo: fetch PR files and diff through the GitHub block, or ask the user to connect GitHub. (3) Pasted diff: run a reduced-confidence review that skips blame and blast radius and says so in the report.

issues.quote: **Risk-First**: Focus on auth, crypto, value transfer, external calls
issues.problem: The risk triggers and all of patterns.md are smart-contract material (value transfer, reentrancy, onlyOwner, SafeMath, block.timestamp). The ~15-second timestamp-manipulation claim is stale for post-Merge Ethereum. Devon's typical users review web and API code, and none of those vulnerability classes are covered.
issues.fix: Add a web/API patterns reference mapped to CWE/OWASP (injection, broken authz/IDOR, SSRF, deserialization, path traversal, secrets in diff, crypto misuse, CSRF/XSS) and move the Solidity content to a domain appendix. Extend the HIGH-risk triggers to include parsing of untrusted input, file handling and outbound fetches.

issues.quote: **Output-Driven**: Always generate comprehensive markdown report file
issues.problem: reporting.md sends the file to the current working directory, then the user's Desktop, then `~/.claude/skills/differential-review/output/`. The last two don't exist in AutoGPT, and the first writes into the user's repo.
issues.fix: Save the report with write_workspace_file under a named path (e.g. security-reviews/<repo>_<pr>_<date>.md), never inside the reviewed repo unless the user approves, and post a short summary in chat.

issues.quote: Command: `issue-writer --input DIFFERENTIAL_REVIEW_REPORT.md --format audit-report`
issues.problem: issue-writer and audit-context-building are not in the catalog or the package. The command is not runnable, and methodology.md opens with `audit-context-building --scope ...` as the 'FIRST ACTION', so the model may try to run commands that don't exist.
issues.fix: Remove the Integration section and the audit-context-building command blocks. Keep only the manual baseline-context checklist (invariants, trust boundaries, validation patterns) as the default path.

issues.quote: **Evidence-Based**: Every finding backed by git history, line numbers, attack scenarios
issues.problem: The skill has no rules for handling what it finds. Nothing forbids running PoCs against live systems, discussing a confirmed vulnerability in a public PR thread, or `git checkout` of the baseline in a user's working tree (methodology.md). The adversarial.md example invents an 'Estimated $50K impact', which contradicts evidence-based reporting.
issues.fix: Add rules: run PoCs only in the sandbox against local code; draft PR comments and get approval before posting, and never disclose in public threads; clone into the sandbox rather than checking out in the user's tree; label impact figures as sourced or assumed.

issues.section: When NOT to Use This Skill
issues.quote: **Greenfield code** (no baseline to compare)
issues.problem: This excludes new-feature PRs (new endpoints, new upload handlers), which is where most web vulnerabilities land, and points to an unnamed 'standard code review'. Dependency or lockfile-only diffs are not routed to Devon's dependency-change-risk-review either.
issues.fix: Keep a new-code path (attacker model plus patterns on the added surface without blame). Name the alternatives: code-review-quality for general review and dependency-change-risk-review for lockfile bumps.

issues.quote: Time: ~30 minutes
issues.problem: Human-auditor time estimates mean nothing for an agent. Example Usage, Tips for Best Results and the Quality Checklist repeat each other, and the Quick Reference tables appear again in methodology.md, so about 90 lines of SKILL.md are duplicated.
issues.fix: Drop the time estimates and the Tips section, fold the examples into one short routing table, and leave the details to the reference files.

scenarios.prompt: Can you security-review PR #482 in our api repo? It refactors the session middleware and drops an old token-expiry check.
scenarios.why: The method fits this case well: Phase 1 git blame and `git log -S` on the removed check, the red flag 'Validation removed without replacement' forcing adversarial analysis, and the test-gap elevation rules. In AutoGPT, though, `gh pr view` and cloning a private repo need credentials the sandbox doesn't have, and the skill offers no fallback to the GitHub block, fetched PR files or a pasted diff. The Phase 5 'delegate to differential-review:adversarial-modeler' dispatch doesn't exist, and patterns.md has nothing on session, token or authz flaws in web code.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a pasted diff (no repo access) adding a file-upload endpoint to our Django app. Is it safe to merge today?
scenarios.why: The skill has no diff-only mode: every phase assumes git history, blame and grep across the codebase. 'When NOT to Use' excludes 'Greenfield code (no baseline to compare)' and points to an unnamed 'standard code review'. patterns.md covers reentrancy, SafeMath, onlyOwner and block.timestamp but not path traversal, content-type or size limits, SSRF or authz. A model would either refuse or improvise without guidance.

security-questionnaire-answers.job: answer customer security questionnaire from evidence
security-questionnaire-answers.summary: Walks Lena through matching each questionnaire item to a policy, report or past approved answer, then drafting a yes/no/partial/N/A answer with source, version, section and evidence date, and listing gaps, owners, counsel-only questions and counts.
strengths: The answer schema (answer, one or two sentences, source document/version/section, evidence date) is specific and reusable.
The rules 'Answer partial ... and say which' and 'Do not soften a no into a vague yes' are the right senior instinct.
It never claims a certification, control or audit result without evidence and marks it as a gap instead.
Legal questions (liability, legal basis, breach terms) go on a separate list for counsel, which matches Lena's non-advisory boundary.
It has a clear no-submit rule and gives answered/partial/gap counts for the owner.
It is short and free of filler.
missing: Intake of customer, deadline, format, and NDA/trust-centre status
Filling the customer's xlsx in place with the sandbox, and a fallback for portals
A test for current evidence: SOC 2 scope, period, exceptions, CUECs, carve-outs, bridge letters, pentest age
Saving approved answers back to the answer library
A consistency check across repeated controls
A pattern for roadmap/planned and compensating-control answers
A warning that answers may become contractual representations
Owner routes for finance/insurance and AI data-use questions
Mapping to common frameworks (SIG Lite/Core, CAIQ v4/CCM, HECVAT, ISO 27001 Annex A) to speed evidence matching

issues.quote: Use this for a customer questionnaire, a SIG, a CAIQ, or a portal form.
issues.problem: The skill names the formats but never says how to handle them, and it never asks for the basic inputs up front: customer, due date, file format, where the evidence library is, and NDA status. For portal forms there is no fallback, and nothing says to write answers back into the customer's spreadsheet while keeping its structure.
issues.fix: Add an intake step: customer, deadline, format, evidence location, and whether an NDA is signed. For xlsx/csv, read and fill the answer columns in place with bash_exec (openpyxl) and keep the customer's layout. For a portal, ask for its export or template; otherwise draft in a sheet the user pastes from. Never log in to a portal alone.

issues.quote: evidence behind it is still current.
issues.problem: 'Current' is not defined. The skill never checks a SOC 2 report's period end, its noted exceptions, carved-out subservice organisations or complementary user entity controls. It also doesn't check for a bridge letter, pentest age, or whether a policy is approved rather than a draft. So 'Yes, see SOC 2' can be cited against evidence that is stale or out of scope.
issues.fix: Add a short evidence test. The policy must be approved and within its review cycle. The SOC 2 or ISO report must cover the system in question, and its period must end within about 12 months, or a bridge letter must exist. Check the report's exceptions and carve-outs before answering yes. Anything that fails the test becomes partial or a gap.

issues.quote: Reuse a past answer only when the question truly asks the same thing and the
issues.problem: Answers are reused, but approved final answers are never saved back. The answer library does not grow, so every questionnaire starts over and wording drifts between customers.
issues.fix: After the owner approves, write each final answer to the evidence/answer library (workspace file or memory_store). Record the question text, answer, source, evidence date, approver and customer, and flag entries whose evidence has since changed.

issues.quote: questionnaire or send it; the owner reviews and submits.
issues.problem: The skill has no guardrail on sharing evidence or on the legal weight of answers. SOC 2 reports and pentest summaries are usually shared only under NDA or through a trust centre. Questionnaire answers are often attached to the contract as representations, so an optimistic partial answer creates contractual exposure.
issues.fix: Add rules. Name the attachments the owner may share and flag any that need an NDA first. Never paste internal policy text into a customer portal unless the owner approves. Warn the owner that answers may become contractual representations, and send any question on warranties or contract language to the counsel list.

issues.quote: Answer "partial" when a control covers some systems and not others, and say
issues.problem: The skill has no consistency pass and no pattern for roadmap or compensating-control answers. In long questionnaires the same control (MFA, encryption, backups) often comes up several times and gets different answers.
issues.fix: Add a consistency check before handoff: group answers by control and make sure they agree. Add formats for a 'planned' answer (control, target date, owner, only if the owner approved it) and a compensating-control answer.

issues.quote: For each answer give:
issues.problem: The deliverable is defined only as per-answer fields. There is no named artefact (a filled questionnaire, a gap and owner list, a counsel list, a cover note to the owner), so the output shape varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Name three outputs: (1) the filled questionnaire or answer sheet with source/date columns, (2) a gap tracker with owner and ask-by date, (3) a short owner summary with counts and the counsel list.

issues.quote: and the owner-approved date to ask by.
issues.problem: The wording is confusing. The ask-by date should be worked back from the customer's due date, not waited on from the owner.
issues.fix: Set each gap's ask-by date from the customer deadline minus review time. Show it as proposed and let the owner change it.

issues.quote: vendor assessment
issues.problem: The trigger is ambiguous. It can fire when the user wants to assess a vendor (Vera's vendor-due-diligence), which is the opposite direction from answering a customer's questionnaire.
issues.fix: Change the trigger to phrases that point one way, such as 'customer security questionnaire', 'HECVAT' or 'security review from a prospect'. Add 'Use when a customer or prospect sends...' to the description.

scenarios.prompt: Acme sent a 190-row SIG Lite spreadsheet due Friday. Here are our Security Policy v3, the 2025 SOC 2 Type II report and last year's approved answers to Globex. Draft the answers and tell me what's missing.
scenarios.why: The steps map straight onto the request. Count and check the import, match each row to policy, SOC 2 or a past answer, write the four-field answer, and list gaps with owners, counsel items and counts. A capable model produces a reviewable, evidence-cited draft. The main weakness is that nothing tells it to fill the customer's spreadsheet columns in place, so the result may come back as a separate list.

scenarios.prompt: Big prospect's OneTrust portal questionnaire, ~300 questions. We only have draft policies and a SOC 2 Type I in progress. Sales wants 'Yes' on SOC 2 and 'in progress' on ISO 27001. They also ask whether we train AI models on customer data and what our cyber insurance limits are.
scenarios.why: 'Never answer yes to a certification... without evidence' and 'Do not soften a no' handle the pressure from sales correctly. But the skill never says whether a draft, unapproved policy counts as evidence. It has no pattern for roadmap or 'in progress' answers with dates, and nothing for a portal that must be exported or filled in the browser with the user present. There is no owner route for insurance or finance questions and no guidance on AI or data-use questions. The model has to improvise on the parts that carry the most risk.

subprocessor-register.job: maintain subprocessor register and change notices
subprocessor-register.summary: Builds or checks a subprocessor register from contracts, DPAs, the finance vendor list and vendor pages, recording service, data, locations, DPA, transfer mechanism and last check. It diffs the register against the last published list and gives each contract's notice period and when it runs out.
strengths: It says to record what the documents say and to show both sources when a vendor page and the contract disagree.
It flags vendors that touch personal data but have no signed DPA.
The field list is solid: data and whose, locations as the vendor states them, DPA dates and filing location, transfer mechanism, last check and source.
The change diff against the last published list takes notice periods and expiry dates from the contract text.
It never invents a location, DPA or transfer mechanism, and it never publishes or sends.
missing: A test for what counts as a subprocessor, and sources beyond the finance list (SSO apps, affiliates, free tools)
Consent vs notice vs objection handling and the earliest safe go-live date
DPF, SCC module and UK Addendum checks for restricted transfers
Fields for purpose, entity, assurance, fourth parties and product scope
A template for the internal register and the public page
A recheck routine and change log
A handoff to compliance-escalation-brief and a sync with personal-data-map
A draft customer notice for the owner to send

issues.quote: Collect signed contracts and DPAs, the finance list of paid vendors, and each
issues.problem: There is no test for who belongs on the register. The finance list includes vendors that are not subprocessors (company-side tools, office services) and misses unpaid or free-tier tools, intra-group affiliates and SSO-connected apps that process customer data.
issues.fix: Define a subprocessor: a third party, affiliates included, that processes customer personal data on the company's behalf. Add sources: the SSO/IdP app list, cloud and integrations inventory, the personal-data-map recipients, and affiliates. Keep company-side vendors on a separate tab rather than the published list.

issues.quote: the notice period and the date it runs out, from the contract text.
issues.problem: Only the notice side is covered. The skill ignores contracts that require specific prior consent rather than notice, customers' right to object, and the rule that the subprocessor must not receive customer data until notice has run out or consent has arrived.
issues.fix: Sort each contract into general authorisation (notice plus objection) or specific consent. List the customers who must consent. Give the earliest safe go-live date. Draft, but do not send, the notice or consent request. Send conflicts with the launch date and any objections to counsel through compliance-escalation-brief.

issues.quote: transfer mechanism, if the contract names one;
issues.problem: The transfer mechanism is checked only passively. For restricted transfers the register should show whether a mechanism exists (SCC module, UK Addendum/IDTA, EU-US DPF certification) and flag its absence. Otherwise a missing safeguard goes unnoticed.
issues.fix: For locations outside the EEA/UK, record the mechanism the contract or DPA shows. Check the vendor's claimed DPF status on the public DPF list with web_fetch and record the URL and date. Mark 'none shown' as a gap for counsel, and don't decide whether a transfer is lawful.

issues.quote: the date you last checked, and the source.
issues.problem: There is no defined artefact, no place to keep it, and no recheck schedule. Vendor subprocessor pages change without notice, so the register goes stale between requests.
issues.fix: Give a table template with an internal version and a public-page version, and store it as a workspace file or Google Sheet. Offer schedule_routine for a quarterly recheck of vendor pages and DPAs, with a diff report to the owner.

issues.quote: personal data it receives, and whose;
issues.problem: The fields senior practitioners expect are missing: purpose, contracting entity and country, security assurance (SOC 2/ISO date), the vendor's own subprocessors (fourth parties), and the customer products or services that use the vendor.
issues.fix: Add columns for purpose, entity/country, assurance evidence and date, link to the vendor's own subprocessor list, and product scope.

issues.quote: has no signed DPA, and any page you could not reach.
issues.problem: Gaps are noted, but there is no escalation route and no instruction for fetching pages. A missing DPA stays a note, and the register is never reconciled with personal-data-map.
issues.fix: Fetch vendor pages with web_fetch and record the URL and retrieval date. If a page is blocked, ask the user for a PDF or pasted text. Send missing DPAs to the owner, and to counsel through compliance-escalation-brief. Sync the recipient list with personal-data-map.

issues.quote: vendor list
issues.problem: The triggers 'vendor list' and 'third parties' are broad and overlap Vera's procurement skills. The description also leaves out the common request 'we're adding a new subprocessor'.
issues.fix: Narrow the triggers to 'subprocessor list', 'new subprocessor' and 'subprocessor notice'. Add to the description: 'Use when building the list, checking it, or preparing notice of a new or changed subprocessor.'

scenarios.prompt: We need a subprocessor list for our trust page. Here's the DPA folder in Drive and the finance export of 140 paid vendors. Build the register and tell me what changed since the list we published in March.
scenarios.why: 'Gather from contracts' and 'Build the register' produce the right columns and flag missing DPAs, and the change diff against March works. But the skill never says how to tell a subprocessor (processes customer personal data for us) from an ordinary vendor. The model either includes most of the 140 vendors or filters by its own judgement. Free-tier tools and affiliates missing from the finance list stay invisible. There is also no format difference between the internal register and the public page.

scenarios.prompt: Product wants to start sending support tickets to an LLM API next week. Several enterprise DPAs say 30 days' notice with a right to object; two say 'prior written consent'. The vendor's subprocessor page won't load. What do we do?
scenarios.why: 'Changes to announce' gets the model to list each contract's notice period and expiry date, and 'any page you could not reach' covers the fetch failure. It does not separate general authorisation (notice plus objection) from specific prior consent. It never says the new subprocessor must not go live before notice runs out or consent arrives, and it has no plan for objections. It doesn't check the transfer mechanism (DPF certification, SCCs) or hand the conflict with the launch date to counsel through compliance-escalation-brief. The riskiest part of the request goes unanswered.

legal-response-drafting.job: draft templated reply to routine legal inquiry
legal-response-drafting.summary: Anthropic's legal-response command, repackaged. It picks an inquiry type (DSR, litigation hold, vendor, NDA, privacy, subpoena, insurance), loads a template from legal.local.md, runs universal and per-category escalation triggers, collects details and fills a templated reply, and includes a guide to creating and managing templates.
strengths: It has universal and per-category escalation triggers (minors, special-category data, employees with active disputes, holds that conflict with deletion, competitor NDAs, subpoenas always) with a clear Stop/Alert/Explain/Recommend/Offer protocol.
Drafts are marked 'DRAFT - FOR COUNSEL REVIEW ONLY' and are always shown for review before any send.
The reusable template format includes a 'Do NOT Use When' section, a variables table, the approver and a last-reviewed date.
The output format builds in an escalation check and follow-up actions.
The customisation and tone guidance covers audience, relationship, sensitivity, urgency and jurisdiction.
Attribution, licence and upstream commit are recorded cleanly.
missing: Platform-native template storage (workspace/memory) and an approval log
Steps to verify identity and to avoid disclosing data before verification, tied to company procedure
A statutory deadline reference marked 'verify against current law' (GDPR Art. 12(3), CCPA/CPRA acknowledgement and response windows)
An immediate preservation step when a hold conflicts with deletion
A route for law-enforcement and government data requests, including the customer-notice policy
A handoff to compliance-escalation-brief and data-subject-request-draft instead of parallel workflows
A response log (received, deadline, sent by, date) for regulated replies
A worked example of a filled template

issues.quote: /legal-response [inquiry-type]
issues.problem: It is a Claude Code slash command with an argument-hint that the harness ignores. The H1 and Invocation section frame the skill as a command the user types. CONNECTORS.md explains ~~category placeholders that SKILL.md never uses and points to an upstream .mcp.json.
issues.fix: Remove the slash-command framing and argument-hint. Infer the inquiry type from the request, or use ask_question to pick a category. Drop CONNECTORS.md or replace it with platform routes: the Gmail/Outlook block for a draft email, schedule_followup for deadlines.

issues.quote: Look for templates in local settings (e.g., `legal.local.md` or a templates directory).
issues.problem: It assumes a persistent local settings file the platform doesn't keep, so every run takes the no-template path. Approved templates are never saved anywhere the next run can find them.
issues.fix: Load templates from workspace files (read_workspace_file) or memory_search under a named 'legal-templates' location. Ask the user to upload approved templates if none exist. After approval, save them with write_workspace_file and record the approver and date.

issues.quote: Use when responding to data subject requests, litigation hold notices, vendor legal questions, NDA requests from business teams, or subpoenas.
issues.problem: It competes with Lena's data-subject-request-draft on every DSR and with Ellis's nda-risk-review on NDAs. It also advertises litigation holds and subpoenas, which a non-advisory compliance analyst should not own, so the kit becomes ambiguous about which skill to load.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to privacy-inquiry and vendor privacy/legal question replies. Send DSR correspondence to data-subject-request-draft, give NDAs to Ellis, and turn holds and subpoenas into escalation-only routes through compliance-escalation-brief.

issues.quote: Before generating any response, evaluate whether this situation has characteristics that should NOT use a templated response.
issues.problem: Escalation runs before Step 4 collects the facts it depends on: requester is an employee in dispute, a minor, special-category data, jurisdiction, an existing hold. So the check is run on missing information.
issues.fix: Collect the minimum triage facts first, run the trigger check, then collect the details for drafting and run the check again before output. Record which triggers were evaluated and what answered each.

issues.quote: Accepting a counterparty's NDA (with markup)
issues.problem: Several sub-categories call for legal judgement: NDA markup, partial or full DSR denial 'with explanation', subpoena objection letters, insurance reservation-of-rights responses. That conflicts with Lena's boundary: 'You draft; owners and counsel decide... do not give legal advice.'
issues.fix: For Lena, limit drafts to acknowledgements, information requests and factual replies built from approved templates. Anything that asserts a legal basis, objection, denial or position goes to counsel as a brief, not a draft letter.

issues.quote: Provide a reasonable default response structure based on the inquiry type
issues.problem: With no approved template, the model writes legal correspondence from general knowledge. 'Includes all required legal elements for the response type' is never spelled out, which invites invented legal content and deadlines.
issues.fix: When no approved template exists, label the output as an unapproved draft. Use only the elements listed in this skill. Take deadlines from the company procedure or mark them 'to confirm with counsel', and ask for the approved template before reuse.

issues.quote: [Specific instructions for systems, email, chat, local files]
issues.problem: The hold template leaves out the step that matters most in practice: telling IT to suspend auto-deletion, retention policies and disappearing-message settings, and to preserve departing employees' accounts and devices. There is also no immediate preservation step when a hold conflicts with a pending erasure.
issues.fix: Add an IT preservation checklist (retention policy suspension, mailbox/chat holds, device retention on offboarding) and a rule: 'pause any pending deletion touching hold scope and escalate'.

issues.quote: Template Management Methodology
issues.problem: About 130 lines of template lifecycle, creation guide and format sit inline and repeat Step 6. Step 4 omits details for the privacy, subpoena and insurance categories it advertises. The body is long, yet coverage is uneven.
issues.fix: Move the template management and creation guide into references/template-guide.md, and move the category details into references/categories.md. Keep SKILL.md to the workflow, the triggers and the output format, and add Step 4 details for every category kept.

scenarios.prompt: Someone emailed privacy@ asking for a copy of everything we hold on them under GDPR. Draft the acknowledgement and ID-verification reply.
scenarios.why: Step 1 resolves to dsr. Step 2 looks for legal.local.md, which does not exist on the platform, so the model falls back to 'a reasonable default response structure'. Step 3 checks escalation before Step 4 has gathered the facts, so triggers like employee dispute or minor cannot yet be judged. The sample DSR template gives a decent letter. But this collides with data-subject-request-draft, which owns the log, verify and systems-search workflow, and no deadline or verification method comes from company procedure, so the model supplies them from memory.

scenarios.prompt: We got a state-court subpoena for a German customer's account records, due in 10 days. The same customer filed a GDPR erasure request last week. Help me respond.
scenarios.why: The escalation protocol works well here. Subpoenas always go to counsel, and the multi-jurisdiction and litigation triggers fire, so the model stops, explains the triggers and offers a draft marked 'DRAFT - FOR COUNSEL REVIEW ONLY'. But it never says to pause the erasure at once and preserve the data while counsel decides. It doesn't check that service was valid or look up the customer-notice policy, and it has no handoff to compliance-escalation-brief. It also invites Lena to draft an objection letter, which goes beyond her non-advisory remit.

15:hiring-rubric-design.job: build anchored hiring rubric before screening
15:hiring-rubric-design.summary: Builds a criterion-by-criterion 1-4 anchored hiring rubric from the approved intake brief and requirements.csv. A stdlib validator checks anchors, proxy terms and must-have coverage. The rubric is frozen with a checksum only after the owner approves it in words, and any later change goes into a new version, with the candidates already screened on the old one listed for the owner.
strengths: There is a real, working validator and freeze tool. It catches 'not assessed' written as level 1, comparative anchors, proxy terms, communication criteria with no named work product, removed requirements, and must-haves with no criterion. All of these were verified by running the bundled examples.

A rubric is frozen only after the owner's explicit approval sentence in chat, with a checksum. Approved files are never edited: changes go into a new version, and the candidates already screened on the old one are listed so the owner decides whether to re-screen.
Every criterion traces to a requirement, and --write-back records the mapping in requirements.csv. This closes the loop between the job posting and the rubric.

The scale design is sound. 'Not assessed' is distinct from 1, each criterion is scored before any overall view, and the anchor formula is verb + object + scope + result. The research is cited correctly: Sackett 2022 (r = .42 for structured interviews), Campion's 15 components, and the OPM guidance on rating scales.
The hard-case example shows how to turn 'culture fit' and 'top CS school' into testable behaviours, which is exactly how a senior recruiter would handle that pushback.

It degrades gracefully without Python: the checks are done by hand, labelled 'hand-checked', and no frozen version is claimed. The tools it uses (run_capability, write_workspace_file source_path, ~/skills/<slug>, ~/workspace) all exist in the platform code.
missing: Scorer calibration on sample answers before freezing
Pass/fail handling for licences, certifications, work authorisation and shift or location requirements
Level-specific anchors when one rubric covers several job levels (for example L4 and L5)
Adverse-impact review by criterion after first use, and escalation to counsel for jurisdiction-specific AI-hiring rules
A standalone path when only a pasted, approved JD is available
Guidance for keeping the hiring team's names in the scorer column from tripping the proxy scan

issues.quote: A disallowed word that is part of the job itself: list it in
issues.problem: The proxy regexes scan every text column, including the scorer. Interviewer names like 'Christian', 'Young', 'White' and 'Black' raise hard ERRORs that approve_rubric.py refuses to freeze past (verified). Legitimate job vocabulary also errors: 'race condition', 'gap analysis', 'cloud-native', 'confidence intervals', 'looks for', and 'time off'/'family leave' for payroll or HR roles. The SKILL only lets allowed_terms cover words about the job, so it gives no path for a scorer's name.
issues.fix: Drop the scorer column from the protected-trait scan, or scan it only for role descriptors. Tighten the broad patterns: exclude 'looks for', 'confidence interval', compounds like '-native', 'race condition' and 'gap analysis'. State that a scorer's own name may be listed in allowed_terms, scoped to its row, with the reason 'scorer name'.

issues.quote: an anchor for every level, in observable terms, fixed before any resume is read;
issues.problem: The skill has no way to record threshold requirements such as licences, certifications, work authorisation or shift availability. The validator demands four distinct anchors and a stated result at level 4, so the model has to invent a ladder for a yes/no fact.
issues.fix: Add a 'threshold requirements' section outside the scored table, marked met, not met or not assessed. Have the validator accept it for must-show rows marked threshold. Route work-authorisation and physical-requirement wording to HR or counsel.

issues.problem: There is no calibration step before the rubric is frozen. Senior practitioners check that scorers read the anchors the same way, for example by having two scorers rate a sample answer independently and compare. The structure checklist admits interviewer training has no skill, and nothing else in the kit calibrates.
issues.fix: Between steps 5 and 6, add an optional step: have two named scorers independently score one fictional sample answer per criterion. Rewrite any anchor where their scores differ by 2 or more, then freeze.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: If `requirements.csv` is missing (older plans kept everything in the plan
issues.problem: A user who pastes an already-approved JD and asks for a rubric gets sent to another skill first. There is no light path for building requirements.csv from a pasted JD when the owner confirms it.
issues.fix: Add a branch: if the owner confirms a pasted JD is approved, get role-intake-and-job-description to build requirements.csv in the same turn, then continue here without starting over.

issues.quote: Only an owner's explicit approval freezes a rubric. Harper never approves.
issues.problem: What to do when an owner insists on a disallowed criterion (refuse to freeze, record the disagreement for the decision-maker) appears only in the hard-case example, not in SKILL.md, which is the only part the model always reads.
issues.fix: Add one guardrail line: if the owner insists on a disallowed criterion, do not freeze; record the disagreement in the plan's open questions for the decision-maker, and suggest an HR or counsel review.

issues.problem: There is no follow-up for adverse impact and no legal escalation. Nothing says to review pass rates by criterion after the first group of applicants, or to take jurisdiction-specific AI-hiring rules to counsel when the rubric drives automated screening (NYC Local Law 144, the EU AI Act's high-risk category, Illinois HB 3773).
issues.fix: Add a line: after the first group of applicants, ask the owner or HR to review pass rates for each criterion (four-fifths rule). If an automated tool scores against this rubric, name the local audit or notice rules and escalate to counsel.

issues.quote: owner which candidates (by id) were already screened or scored on vN, so
issues.problem: Step 7 does not say where to find the ids of candidates already scored on vN, even though hiring-state.md defines screens/<batch>/ and scorecards/.
issues.fix: Say to list the candidate ids from ~/workspace/hiring/<role-slug>/screens/*/ and scorecards/ whose files reference rubric-vN.

issues.quote: from `templates/rubric.md` (keep the header lines and the column row exactly),
issues.problem: The template has no allowed_terms header line, so the model has to learn its format from the anchor guide. rubric_io parses only header lines above the first '## ' heading.
issues.fix: Add an empty 'allowed_terms:' line to templates/rubric.md, with a one-line comment showing the '[C2:]term (reason); ...' format.

scenarios.prompt: Maya approved the intake and requirements for the Billing Ops Lead yesterday. Build the rubric so we can start screening next week; Tom and Priya are interviewing.
scenarios.why: Steps 1-6 read the intake brief and requirements.csv. They choose separable criteria that each cite a requirement, write the four anchors from the anchor guide, and loop on validate_rubric.py until it shows no ERROR. The owner then sees the table, the weighting and the structure-checklist components 8 and 9. The rubric is frozen only after Maya's approval sentence, and --write-back records which criterion covers each requirement. The billing-ops example reproduces exactly when run. A capable model would produce a defensible, traceable rubric.

scenarios.prompt: Need a rubric today for an ICU night-shift nurse. Here's the JD pasted: must hold an active RN licence and BLS, work 12-hour nights, and show sound clinical judgment on patient health outcomes. Christian White (charge nurse) will score clinical judgment.
scenarios.why: There is no intake brief or requirements.csv, so the Inputs section sends the user back to role-intake-and-job-description first. That is correct in principle but slow. Step 2 then requires four distinct anchors per criterion, with a stated result at level 4. That forces invented ladders for the licence, BLS and shift requirements, which are binary. The validator then errors on 'health' (fixable with allowed_terms) and also on the scorer 'Christian White' ([religion] and [race]). The SKILL only allows allowed_terms for words about the job, never about the candidate, so the model gets no guidance for a scorer's name. It may rename the scorer or stall.

better: Main is a 30-line placeholder with no inputs, no procedure and no approval mechanism. The PR adds an inputs table, an ordered procedure with decisions for each validator error, and an explicit owner approval gate with the owner's quote.

Adds a working validator that enforces the guardrails main only stated: no proxies, no comparative anchors, 'not assessed' kept separate from 1, and every must-have covered. The PR's own draft example produces 7 correctly caught errors.
Adds freezing with a checksum and versioning (--new-version, --verify), plus fairness handling for candidates already screened on the old version. Main has no concept of changing a rubric.
Links each criterion to a requirement and writes the mapping back to requirements.csv, which main lacks.
The description and triggers are more specific, and a 'Do not use for' line separates it from the role-intake, interview-plan and resume-screening skills.
Adds worked examples, a hard case (culture fit, prestige, change mid-screen), an anchor-writing guide with five ladders, and cited sources.
worse: It now depends heavily on files that sibling skills write (intake-brief.md, requirements.csv, hiring-plan.md). Main could build a rubric from a conversation; the PR sends the user elsewhere first.

The proxy scan wrongly blocks real content: scorer names (Christian, Young, White) and ordinary job words (race condition, gap analysis, cloud-native, confidence intervals). Main's text-only guardrail could not block approval by mistake.

It dropped the generic triggers 'interview rubric' and 'score candidates'. The description now calls the rubric 'the role scorecard', which blurs it with interview-plan-and-scorecard and with Sofia's role-intake-and-scorecard.
It is about five times longer. The inline Example and the Package files list repeat what the example files and the read_skill file listing already give.

nurture-sequence-build-and-readout.summary: A 71-line playbook for building an email nurture for one segment. It maps the stage, the exit and the touch count, writes the in/out segment rules, drafts each email with one goal, sets the experiment and holdout before sending, runs build and domain-authentication checks, waits for a yes, and then reports on clicks, replies, conversions and lift rather than opens.
strengths: The exit rule is hard: 'A sequence with no exit does not ship.'
The experiment is fixed before any send, with one change, one deciding metric and a holdout: 'An experiment designed after the results is a story.'
Opens are correctly treated as a deliverability signal only, because mail privacy features inflate them. Scoring uses clicks, replies, conversions and lift.
The pre-send checks cover SPF, DKIM and DMARC, spam-score and rendering previews, and bounce and complaint watch switched on before the first send.
Segment discipline: who is in and who is out, one line each, and how you know which is which.
Clear approval gate and a ban on invented metrics, with FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels on the readout.
Concise, with no filler.
missing: A reusable deliverable template: journey table, drafts, experiment plan and readout table.
Consent and lawful-basis check, plus re-permission for stale or event-scan lists (GDPR/PECR, CASL, CAN-SPAM postal address).
Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender requirements: one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) and a spam-complaint rate under 0.3%.
List validation and hygiene before the first send to an old list (the ZeroBounce block is available).
Correct hard vs. soft bounce suppression, and a sunset policy for unengaged contacts.
Sample-size and MDE calculation via bash_exec, a fixed read date, and a readout with confidence intervals and a ship/kill rule.
Send spacing, a frequency cap across concurrent sequences, send timezone, and behavioural branching/suppression when someone converts mid-sequence.
Tool routing (HubSpot run_block, Gmail drafts, Sheets) with a CSV fallback, and a saved plan so the later readout can find it.
Named sources for send-type benchmarks, so 'judge against benchmarks' does not invite invented targets.
A handoff boundary to sales/AE for cold prospect outreach and for replies that turn into live opportunities.

issues.problem: No deliverable is defined. There is no 'what you hand back' section, no journey table (stage, trigger, touch, delay, goal, CTA, exit), no experiment-plan format and no readout template. Two runs of this skill will produce differently shaped outputs that the owner cannot reuse or compare week to week.
issues.fix: Add a 'What you hand back' section with (1) a journey table: touch #, trigger/delay, goal, subject, CTA, exit/suppression; (2) the drafts; (3) a one-block experiment plan: hypothesis, control/variant, primary metric, holdout %, sample, read date; (4) a readout table template. Ship it as templates/nurture-plan.md.

issues.section: Check the build, then the domain
issues.quote: Links, names, dates, the unsubscribe line and the reply-to address. Read every
issues.problem: The pre-send checks leave out the regulatory and mailbox-provider requirements a senior lifecycle marketer would check first: consent or lawful basis for the segment (GDPR/PECR, CASL), CAN-SPAM's physical address, one-click List-Unsubscribe (RFC 8058), and the Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender spam-rate ceiling (under 0.3%). Without them, the skill can clear a non-compliant send.
issues.fix: Add a 'Consent and compliance' check before drafting: the source and consent date of each contact, the jurisdiction, a re-permission path for stale lists, and one-click unsubscribe plus postal address confirmed. Name legal/compliance as the escalation when the basis is unclear.

issues.section: Set the experiment before anything sends
issues.quote: The sample you need and how long to wait for it.
issues.problem: This names the sample without giving a way to compute it. There is no baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, power or significance level, no sandbox calculation, no stopping rule, and at readout no confidence interval or decision rule. The model is left to guess, which produces the post-hoc 'story' the skill warns against.
issues.fix: Add inputs (baseline conversion, list size, the smallest lift worth acting on). Tell the model to compute sample and duration with bash_exec (two-proportion power calculation), to set holdout % from that result, to fix the read date and not peek early, and to report lift with a 95% interval and a ship/kill rule.

issues.quote: that has bounced twice — suppress it.
issues.problem: Current practice suppresses a hard bounce (invalid address) after the first bounce. Only soft bounces get a retry threshold. Re-sending to hard bounces damages sender reputation, which the domain checks are meant to protect.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'Suppress any hard bounce immediately; suppress a soft bounce after three consecutive failures; suppress every complaint and unsubscribe across all sequences.'

issues.quote: Use this when someone wants a sequence, a lifecycle journey or a re-engagement
issues.problem: No inputs are named up front: the segment source and size, the ESP or sending tool, the baseline conversion rate, the approver, the sending domain, and the timezone. There is no tool routing (HubSpot block, Gmail drafts, Sheets for the journey) and no fallback when the ESP is not connected, so the model does not know where drafts land or how to get the list.
issues.fix: Open with an inputs list and a connection check: HubSpot via run_block if connected, otherwise ask for a CSV export. Drafts are staged as Gmail drafts or a doc. Store the plan in the workspace so the later readout can find it.

issues.section: Map the journey before you write
issues.quote: Six to eight for a cold one.
issues.problem: A 'cold' segment in a nurture blurs into cold outbound. That is a different legal basis, and in this roster it belongs to sales (Max). The skill has no boundary or handoff. It also gives touch counts but no spacing between sends, no frequency cap across sequences running at the same time, and no behavioural branching (clicked vs. did not), which is where nurture results are usually won.
issues.fix: Define cold here as 'opted-in but unengaged' and route unconsented prospect lists to the sales teammate. Add default spacing tied to triggers, a cap (e.g. no more than one automated email per 48h across all sequences), and a branch-and-suppress rule for people who act mid-sequence.

issues.quote: Build a nurture around one segment: the journey and the exit that stops it, the drafts
issues.problem: The description and triggers miss the words users actually say ('email sequence', 'drip campaign', 'welcome series', 'onboarding emails', 'win-back'). Toran's lifecycle-email-marketing, which is proposed for Maya, claims all of those phrases, so if both are in the kit the upstream skill will win the trigger.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'Use when someone wants an email sequence, drip, welcome, onboarding, re-engagement or win-back series for one segment...' and add those trigger phrases. Resolve the overlap with lifecycle-email-marketing (merge its sequence templates into references/).

issues.section: Check the build, then the domain
issues.quote: Domain-based Message Authentication (DMARC) all passing
issues.problem: DMARC is expanded incorrectly (the full name is Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance). 'Passing' also skips the point that DMARC needs SPF or DKIM alignment with the From domain and a published policy.
issues.fix: Correct the expansion and write the check as: SPF and DKIM pass and align with the From domain, and a DMARC record at p=none or stricter is published.

scenarios.prompt: About 4,000 trial users signed up in the last 60 days and never connected an integration. Build a short nurture to get them to connect one, and tell me how we'll know it worked.
scenarios.why: 'Map the journey' yields the stage, the one action (connect an integration), 3-5 warm touches and the exit. 'Segment tight' and 'Draft each email' produce clean in/out rules and drafts with one ask and gaps left marked. But 'The sample you need and how long to wait for it' gives no method (baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, power), and 'A holdout when the list is big enough' sets no threshold, so a model may pick an arbitrary 10% holdout. Nothing covers the spacing between touches or the shape of the hand-back, so output quality depends on the model rather than the skill.

scenarios.prompt: HubSpot isn't connected. Here's a CSV of 22,000 contacts: a 2021 webinar list plus trade-show badge scans. Build a re-engagement series, schedule it for Tuesday, and I need results by Friday.
scenarios.why: The approval gate ('Never send, schedule or upload a list without a yes') prevents the send itself. But the skill has no step for consent or lawful basis on stale or badge-scan contacts, no list validation or hygiene before the first send (a ZeroBounce block exists), no re-permission approach, and no mention of the Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender limits. 'Six to eight for a cold one' actively pushes toward a long series to an unconsented list. It says nothing about the ESP being missing (e.g. stage drafts in Gmail or a doc). It also never forces the model to tell the user that a Friday readout cannot reach the sample the experiment needs.

weekly-marketing-read.job: report weekly marketing metrics and explain moves
weekly-marketing-read.summary: The weekly (and roll-up monthly/quarterly) marketing read. It fixes equal, complete comparison windows, checks which sources cover which days, computes paid, email, content and pipeline metrics only from the columns present, judges goal against actual by funnel stage, and decomposes the biggest move (e.g. CPA into CPC and conversion rate). It treats small samples as noise and returns a labelled table and narrative as a saved, dated draft.
strengths: The windows must be complete and equal, and a short export is trimmed or flagged 'so a short week never passes for a down week'.
Coverage comes before computation: an empty source 'still appears, marked empty, so nobody reads silence as a zero'.
The metric set depends on which columns exist (spend, email, CRM), which fits partial exports.
Correct CPA decomposition (CPA = CPC / click-to-conversion rate), with the carrying factor named, then anchored to a concrete event.
Changes are shown both absolute and relative, and the 4-week rolling average is checked before anything is called a trend.
ROAS and CPA from the most recent week are flagged preliminary because of attribution windows. Platforms are never compared across mismatched windows.
A small-sample rule (under about 30 conversions is noise). Seasonality or algorithm updates are not accepted as explanations without evidence.
Budget suggestions name their metric, and the named approver decides. Nothing goes out without a yes, and gaps are never estimated.
Formats for a quiet week and fallbacks for no prior week and no targets.
missing: Web and organic traffic metrics (GA4 sessions by channel, landing-page conversion, Search Console), plus social.
A data-health step: platform vs. CRM/analytics reconciliation with the gap shown, tracking-break and UTM checks.
Pipeline lag and cohorting by lead-created date for bottom-funnel figures.
Tool routing (HubSpot, Sheets, Drive via run_block/MCP), a connect_integration offer, a CSV fallback in the skill itself, and bash_exec for the computations.
A defined storage location and schema for the metrics history and saved reads, plus a de-duplication check against the log.
An output template or worked example with fixed row order, columns, sources and labels.
A dated, sourced benchmark reference file instead of inline approximations.
A materiality threshold for which moves make the top-movers list, beyond 'largest'.
Timezone stated on the reporting windows (currently only in the persona).

issues.section: Compute the headline set from the columns you actually have
issues.quote: content shipped against the editorial calendar and what is stuck
issues.problem: Website and organic performance are entirely absent: sessions and conversions by channel/source, organic search, social, and landing-page conversion rate. These are usually the first numbers a marketing manager's weekly read covers, and the most common source of 'why did X change'. The headline set jumps from paid and email straight to content and pipeline.
issues.fix: Add a 'Where web analytics columns exist' bullet: sessions by channel, new users, key-event and conversion rate by landing page, and organic clicks and impressions from Search Console. Add a line to ask for a GA4 export when it is not connected.

issues.quote: so never set one against another unless the windows match. A figure the
issues.problem: The skill says what not to do but not how to handle the routine case where ad platforms report far more conversions than analytics or the CRM. It has no step for tracking breaks, UTM hygiene or partial-tracking days. Senior practice (compare the original paid-performance-report) is to keep platform and CRM figures side by side, show the gap, and check tracking before interpreting any move.
issues.fix: Add a 'Data health' step before 'Find the biggest move': platform-reported and CRM/analytics figures reported side by side with the gap, tracking or tagging changes and zero-days flagged, and UTM coverage checked. Any move coinciding with a tracking break is labelled UNKNOWN.

issues.quote: dated, add this week to the metrics history, and compare against the previous
issues.problem: The skill relies on persistent state but never says where it lives or how to reach it: the metrics history, the previous saved read, and the routine's 'check your log so the same week is never reported twice'. There is no mention of memory_store/memory_search, write_workspace_file or a Sheets block, and no schema for the history rows, so week-over-week comparison breaks on the second run.
issues.fix: Specify storage: the history as a Sheet or workspace CSV with columns date_start, date_end, source, metric, value, label. The read is saved as a dated workspace file, and a memory entry points to both. Read the last saved read first and skip if this period already exists.

issues.section: Check coverage before you compute anything
issues.quote: List the sources you have and the days each one covers. A source that came
issues.problem: No tool routing or fallback in the skill itself. It does not say to check connected HubSpot, Sheets or Drive via run_block or MCP, to offer connect_integration, or to ask for a CSV paste when a source is missing. It never says to do the arithmetic in bash_exec, which matters for decomposition and rolling averages across multiple exports.
issues.fix: Add: check connections first (HubSpot, Sheets, Drive); for anything missing, ask once for an export or paste; load the exports into bash_exec and compute every figure there, showing the formula for any derived metric.

issues.section: Read goal against actual, by funnel stage
issues.quote: Each headline figure against its plan target: engagement at the top, conversion
issues.problem: Bottom-of-funnel figures (SQLs, pipeline, revenue) lag marketing activity by weeks, but the skill reads them against a weekly target with no cohort or lag treatment. The result is false 'pipeline dropped' stories, and only ROAS and CPA get a preliminary flag.
issues.fix: Tell the model to cohort pipeline by lead-created week and report bottom-funnel figures on a lagged or trailing-4-week basis, flagged preliminary like ROAS and CPA.

issues.section: Judge email against benchmarks, not vibes
issues.quote: Published all-industry averages from the big email providers (roughly a third
issues.problem: The skill itself quotes approximate, unsourced benchmark figures while telling the model to cite report and year. These numbers go stale and invite the model to repeat them as fact.
issues.fix: Move the benchmarks to references/email-benchmarks.md with the provider, report year and send type, or instruct a web_search for the current report, and cite whichever is used.

issues.quote: The headline (the period and its biggest move), the table with last week
issues.problem: The sections are listed but there is no concrete template or example: table columns, row order, where the FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels and sources sit. Weekly reads will drift in shape, which undermines the week-over-week comparison the skill depends on.
issues.fix: Ship templates/weekly-read.md with a fixed row order and columns (metric, this week, last week, delta, delta %, 4-wk avg, target, source, label), and one worked example of a short read.

issues.quote: Roll the weeks into one read against plan: the trend per headline metric, what
issues.problem: Monthly and quarterly reads get two sentences and are not in the description or triggers, so a 'monthly marketing report' request may not load this skill. When it does, the model gets no guidance on month-over-month or year-over-year comparison or pacing against a quarterly plan.
issues.fix: Either add 'monthly/quarterly marketing report' to the description and triggers with brief MoM/YoY and plan-pacing guidance, or drop the section and keep the skill weekly.

scenarios.prompt: Here are our HubSpot email export and Google Ads CSV for Sep 14-27. Give me the weekly marketing read, and tell me why CPA jumped.
scenarios.why: 'Fix the period out loud' sets Sep 21-27 against Sep 14-20. 'Check coverage' lists HubSpot email and Google Ads and marks CRM and the calendar as absent. The headline set is computed only from columns present. 'Find the biggest move' splits CPA into CPC and click-to-conversion rate and names which carried it. Recent-week CPA is flagged preliminary for attribution lag, and the under-30-conversions rule stops a story being built on noise. The output follows 'What you hand back'. A capable model produces a senior-quality read.

scenarios.prompt: Monday read: I only have a LinkedIn Ads export through Thursday, GA4 isn't connected, LinkedIn says 140 conversions but HubSpot shows 45 new leads from LinkedIn, and the CMO wants to know why pipeline dropped 25% and whether to halve LinkedIn spend.
scenarios.why: These parts work: the short export triggers trimming or flagging, low conversion volume gets called noise, the pipeline drop gets 'say so in a sentence and name the single input that would settle it', and the budget question goes to the named approver with its metric. But the skill only says 'never set one against another unless the windows match'. It gives no way to reconcile platform-reported conversions against CRM leads (keep both, show the gap, check UTM or tracking). It has no guidance on web traffic or GA4 being missing, and none on pipeline lagging marketing activity by weeks (cohort by lead-created date). So the core question gets a hedge rather than a diagnosis.

msa-playbook-review.summary: A 20-line checklist that compares an MSA and its order forms, SOWs, data, security and amendment terms topic by topic with a user-supplied playbook, citing agreement text, playbook text and fallback per topic and listing inter-document conflicts, missing schedules and counsel decisions.
strengths: Names the full contract stack up front (MSA, order form, SOWs, data and security terms, amendments) and requires missing documents to be stated
Broad, correct topic list, including order of precedence, acceptance, transition, suspension, insurance and audit
Tracks conflicts between the MSA and linked documents without choosing which controls, which is the right non-advisory behaviour
Edits allowed only from an exact supplied fallback, with everything else routed to counsel; never sends a redline or accepts a term
Very lean, with no filler
missing: Branch for when no playbook is supplied
Intake of side, whose paper, counterparty, value, deadline and named counsel
A full-agreement walk that surfaces terms the playbook does not cover
Defined label set and a reusable table template with a header block
Step mapping definitions, cross-references and the order-of-precedence clause
Handling for URL-incorporated terms (fetch, date-stamp, unilateral-change flag)
Current topics: AI/data use, subprocessors, auto-renewal uplifts, sole-remedy SLA credits, cap carve-outs, survival, non-solicit, exclusivity/MFN
Neutral CALCULATED values with formula (cap amount, notice dates)
Handoff to contract-deviation-triage and counsel-escalation-brief
Tool routing for document extraction and a saved workspace artefact
A worked example

issues.quote: Review only topics covered by the supplied playbook
issues.problem: Terms that are in the agreement but not in the playbook (auto-renewal uplifts, AI/data-use rights, exclusivity, MFN, non-solicit, unilateral URL-term changes) get silently dropped. This contradicts the persona's duty to flag missing, changed or unclear language and hides the highest-risk clauses when the playbook is short.
issues.fix: Walk every section of every supplied document. Terms the playbook does not address get a NOT IN PLAYBOOK (or UNCLEAR) label and a counsel question. Never omit them.

issues.problem: There is no path for when no playbook is supplied and no intake of side (customer or vendor), whose paper it is, counterparty, deal value, signature deadline or named counsel. The model cannot pick the right playbook section or date the counsel queue.
issues.fix: Add an intake step using ask_question for side, paper, counterparty, value, deadline and counsel. If no playbook is supplied, limit the work to contract-key-term-extraction plus questions, as contract-ops-getting-started prescribes.

issues.quote: For each topic cite the document, section, agreement text, playbook text, label, difference, supplied fallback, and decision owner.
issues.problem: 'label' is never defined in the skill, there is no table template, and there are no ordered steps: completeness check, definitions and order-of-precedence map, topic walk, conflicts, queue.
issues.fix: Define the label set (MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR/NOT IN PLAYBOOK), number the steps, and ship templates/msa-deviation-table.md with a header block (agreement, version, side, playbook version, date).

issues.quote: Use the complete MSA, order form, statements of work, data terms, security terms, amendments, and the user's supplied playbook.
issues.problem: Terms incorporated by URL (SLA, AUP, security policy, DPA) are common in SaaS MSAs and can change unilaterally. The skill only says to list missing documents, with no fetch, snapshot or date step.
issues.fix: When terms are incorporated by URL, web_fetch them and record the retrieval date and hash. Flag any unilateral-change right as an item for counsel. If the fetch fails, mark the item MISSING.

issues.quote: Return the deviation table, document conflicts, missing schedules, business inputs, and counsel decisions needed before signature.
issues.problem: No handoff to the sibling skills contract-deviation-triage (queue by playbook priority) or counsel-escalation-brief (decision-first brief), and no saved artefact, so the review ends as chat text.
issues.fix: Write the table to the workspace (csv/xlsx or md) with write_workspace_file, pass rows to contract-deviation-triage, and draft one counsel-escalation-brief per COUNSEL DECISION item.

issues.quote: Do not calculate legal exposure, judge enforceability, label market practice, or recommend acceptance.
issues.problem: 'Calculate legal exposure' is ambiguous and may stop neutral arithmetic, such as a cap of 12 months' fees working out to $84,000, which the persona's own counsel-brief sample uses.
issues.fix: Allow CALCULATED values that show formula and sources (as contract-key-term-extraction does, via bash_exec). Forbid only exposure estimates, likelihood and risk scoring.

issues.quote: insurance, audit, compliance, term, suspension, termination, transition, publicity, assignment, notices, governing law, and dispute process
issues.problem: The topic list omits several current MSA hot spots: definitions, auto-renewal and price escalators, subcontractors and subprocessors, AI and customer-data use, SLA credits as the sole remedy, cap carve-outs and super-caps, force majeure, survival, non-solicit and exclusivity.
issues.fix: Extend the list, or move it to references/msa-topic-checklist.md with a one-line 'what to capture' note per topic.

issues.problem: No tool routing: nothing on reading PDF/DOCX from the workspace, extracting text or comparing redline vs clean in the bash_exec sandbox, working through long MSAs section by section, or storing the approved playbook with memory_store for reuse.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Working the documents' step naming read_workspace_file, bash_exec (python-docx/pdfplumber) for extraction and diffing, and memory_store for the playbook, falling back to pasted text.

scenarios.prompt: Attached is Globex's MSA, Order Form #2 and their DPA. Check them against our sales-side contracting playbook (also attached) and list the deviations for our GC before Thursday.
scenarios.why: The inputs paragraph names every document, the topic list covers what a sales-side playbook normally addresses, and the per-topic fields (document, section, agreement text, playbook text, label, difference, fallback, owner) give a cited table. Output lists conflicts and counsel decisions. Labels are not defined here, but the persona supplies MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR, so a capable model still produces a usable counsel-ready table.

scenarios.prompt: Vendor SaaS MSA for signature Friday. SLA and AUP are only linked as URLs, the SOW isn't done, and our playbook is a one-pager covering liability, indemnity and data. Their draft also has auto-renewal with a 7% uplift and lets them train AI models on our data. What do I need to flag?
scenarios.why: 'Review only topics covered by the supplied playbook' tells the model to skip the uplift and AI-training clauses, the two most material terms, because the one-page playbook is silent on them. There is no instruction to fetch and date-stamp URL-incorporated terms (web_fetch) or to mark them as changeable. The model would only say the SLA, AUP and SOW are missing. There is also no deadline or brief handoff. The gates hold (nothing is sent or accepted), but a senior contract manager would call the review incomplete.

nda-playbook-review.summary: A 25-line checklist that compares an NDA clause by clause with a user-supplied NDA playbook, labels each item MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR with exact agreement and playbook text, and returns a comparison table and counsel queue with unsent redlines drawn only from supplied fallbacks.
strengths: Strict non-advisory stance that matches Ellis's persona and boundaries exactly
Explicit label set (MATCH/DEVIATION/MISSING/UNCLEAR) and complete per-item fields including exact text on both sides
Graceful path without a playbook: extract clauses and questions only
Redlines limited to supplied fallbacks, kept as unsent drafts, with counsel approving the text
Solid core NDA clause list, including residuals, representatives, compelled disclosure and retained copies
Concise, with no filler
missing: Direction, side and whose-paper intake, plus counterparty, deadline and named counsel
Scope check for non-confidentiality obligations hidden in an NDA
Explicit handling when the playbook is silent on a term (and optionally recording a counsel-approved position)
Output template with header block and summary counts, saved to the workspace
Handoff to contract-deviation-triage and counsel-escalation-brief
Clauses: non-solicit, feedback licence, no-licence, no-obligation-to-proceed, marking/oral disclosure, trade-secret survival, affiliates
Guard against leaking internal playbook positions to the counterparty
Tool routing for document extraction and diffing
A worked example

issues.quote: Cover parties, purpose, confidential-information definition, exclusions, use and disclosure, representatives, compelled disclosure, security
issues.problem: No scope check for obligations beyond confidentiality: non-solicit, non-compete, standstill, exclusivity, licence or feedback grants, IP assignment, ROFR, broad arbitration. An 'NDA' carrying these can pass with the extra obligations never listed.
issues.fix: Add a first step that scans the whole document for non-confidentiality obligations and routes each one as NOT IN PLAYBOOK plus a counsel decision. Add non-solicit, feedback, no-licence, no-obligation-to-proceed, marking/oral disclosure and trade-secret survival to the list.

issues.quote: Use the complete NDA and the user's supplied NDA playbook.
issues.problem: No intake for direction (mutual or one-way), our side (disclosing or receiving), whose paper, counterparty, purpose, deadline or named counsel. Applying the wrong playbook section yields misleading MATCH/DEVIATION labels.
issues.fix: Ask for or confirm these via ask_question before comparing, select the matching playbook section, and label items UNCLEAR when the playbook does not cover this direction.

issues.quote: Do not infer that silence is acceptance.
issues.problem: It is unclear whose silence is meant, and the skill never says what to do when the playbook is silent on a term the NDA contains, which is the most common real gap.
issues.fix: Spell it out: if the NDA omits a playbook item, label it MISSING; if the playbook omits an NDA term, label it NOT IN PLAYBOOK and raise a counsel question. Offer to record a counsel-approved position in memory for next time.

issues.quote: Return the comparison table and counsel queue.
issues.problem: No template, no header (NDA name, version, counterparty, direction, playbook version, date), no summary counts, no saved artefact, and no handoff to contract-deviation-triage or counsel-escalation-brief.
issues.fix: Ship templates/nda-comparison.md, write the table to the workspace, and draft one counsel-escalation-brief per decision item, including the deadline.

issues.quote: Do not call a clause mutual, standard, reasonable, enforceable, or risky unless that is a label in the supplied playbook
issues.problem: Lumps a factual structural description ('mutual' vs 'one-way') in with evaluative labels, which stops the model from stating a basic, checkable fact about the document.
issues.fix: Allow factual descriptors (mutual or one-way, stated term lengths) and ban only evaluative ones (standard, reasonable, enforceable, risky, market).

issues.problem: No destination or privilege guard. Internal playbook positions and fallbacks can end up pasted into counterparty-facing drafts or broad sales channels.
issues.fix: Mark the comparison as internal and prepared for counsel. Counterparty-facing redline drafts contain only the proposed clause text, never the playbook rationale or other fallbacks.

issues.problem: No tool routing: nothing on reading PDF/DOCX from the workspace, extracting text or diffing against fallback text with bash_exec, or storing the approved playbook with memory_store; no fallback to pasted text.
issues.fix: Add a short step naming read_workspace_file, bash_exec for extraction and diffing, and memory_store for the playbook, with a fallback to pasted text.

scenarios.prompt: Acme sent their mutual NDA (PDF attached) and here's our NDA playbook. Can you check it against the playbook and tell me what legal needs to look at?
scenarios.why: The clause list covers the standard NDA provisions, each item gets section and exact text, playbook text, one of four labels, a neutral difference, the fallback and the decision needed. The output gives a table and counsel queue with drafts only. A capable model produces a clean, cited review.

scenarios.prompt: Vendor's one-way NDA for a pilot; we're the receiving party. Our playbook only covers mutual NDAs. Their draft has a 12-month non-solicit and gives them a licence to any feedback we provide. Legal is out until Monday and sales wants to sign today.
scenarios.why: The gate holds: counsel chooses, and redlines stay unsent. But the skill has no step to establish direction or side, so the mutual playbook gets applied to a one-way receiving NDA. The clause list has no non-solicit and no scope check for non-confidentiality obligations, so the non-solicit may be missed. 'Do not infer that silence is acceptance' does not say what to do when the playbook is silent. There is also no deadline-driven counsel brief or handoff to counsel-escalation-brief.

14:statement-reconciliation.summary: Reconciles one bank, card or processor-clearing account per period against the ledger using bundled, self-tested stdlib Python scripts (prior-period tie, ordered one-to-one matching passes, Stripe/PayPal payout breakdown, running-balance-proven PDF extraction), classifies leftovers with the owner via ask_question, and delivers a masked, SHA-256-signed workpaper plus carry-forward state without ever writing to the ledger.
strengths: Five stdlib scripts, each with --selftest, all pass on the bundled scenarios: clean tie, transposition, plug temptation, opening gap, stale timing, a dropped PDF line, and Stripe/PayPal including two-currency PayPal.

Anti-plugging is enforced in code as well as in prose. Out-of-period rows are refused with an explicit diagnostic when they equal the gap, matches are strictly one-to-one, ambiguous pairs stay unmatched, and no suspense entry is ever produced.
Approval integrity: the workpaper is hashed before it is shown, the reply is logged verbatim against that SHA-256, a stale hash is refused, and the approver is never inferred.
Privacy by default: long digits, IBANs and sort codes are masked in every output, the account label rejects 5 or more digits, and memory never holds amounts or account numbers.

Sourced practitioner detail: QBO R/C statuses and the irreversible undo, the sign convention in Xero's Reconciliation Summary, feed-lag traps, FITID dedup, Undeposited Funds and Opening Balance Equity, divide-by-9 and half-difference hints, and late-clearing deposits flagged as a lapping signal.

Processor clearing is done correctly: gross - fees - refunds - disputes = net for each payout, in-transit payouts at cutoff, rows with no payout id reported rather than dropped, and PayPal currencies never added together.
Month-to-month state: namespaced carried ids, and drafted corrections carried as owned items until the correcting entry is posted.

Tool names were checked against the current AutoGPT copilot backend (run_capability, find_capability/describe_capability, run_sub_session, TodoWrite, ~/workspace durable volume, ~/skills/<slug> workdir). There is a graceful hand-computed fallback when Python is missing.
missing: Ledger-opening vs prior approved ledger-closing tie, which catches edits to reconciled ledger transactions
A normaliser that turns raw bank or card CSV exports (split debit/credit columns, locale dates, no ids, running-balance-only) into the canonical schema, with a balance proof
A PDF path for statements without per-line running balances (typical card statements)
Card statement-cycle handling (cycle close date instead of calendar month-end)
A materiality threshold and clearing-lag threshold captured at intake for escalation
Separate staleness defaults for outstanding payments and deposits in transit
Procedure branches for petty cash (count sheet) and loans (lender schedule, interest/principal split) that match the description
Guidance on foreign-currency bank accounts and period-end revaluation, left for the accountant
A note on scope versus Toran's account-reconciliation (GL-to-subledger, intercompany) so the two are not loaded for the same request

issues.quote: matcher stops (exit 3): report it as a suspected edit to a reconciled period
issues.problem: The prior-period tie compares the bank's statement opening with the prior approved statement closing. Two bank figures only differ when a statement is wrong or missing. An edit to a reconciled ledger transaction (the QBO failure the references cite) changes the ledger opening, which is never checked against the prior rec's ledger_closing. So the control misdiagnoses one case and misses the other. In testing, a +100 ledger-opening change produced an unexplained -100.00 with 0 investigate items and no diagnostic, and the workpaper said '0 item(s) to investigate'.
issues.fix: Add prior_approved_ledger_closing to balances.json (it is already in rec-state.json) and stop when ledger_opening differs, labelled 'suspected edit to a reconciled period'. Relabel a statement-opening gap as 'wrong or missing statement'. When unexplained ≠ 0 with no investigate items, emit an owned 'unexplained difference' line.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: User upload (CSV preferred, PDF accepted); for processors, the payout or activity report
issues.problem: CSV is the preferred input, but no step or script turns a raw bank or card export into the canonical id/date/amount schema. Real exports have split Debit/Credit or Money In/Money Out columns, DD/MM or MM/DD dates, no row id, and often only a running balance in place of explicit opening and closing balances. Each run has to improvise this conversion.
issues.fix: Add a step 3 bullet and a small normalise_csv.py (or a --csv mode on extract_statement.py). It should map columns, require an explicit date format, assign line ids, derive opening and closing from the running balance, and print PROVEN like the PDF path.

issues.quote: Scripts use the standard library only; no install is needed.
issues.problem: extract_statement.py needs pdfplumber or pdftotext, and its error message tells the model to pip install. It also only reads lines that end with a movement plus a running balance. Most card statements (Amex, Chase) and many US bank PDFs print no per-line balance, so the 'PDF statements' promise in the description fails for those, and step 3 stalls after two tries.
issues.fix: State the PDF dependency and the running-balance requirement in step 3. Add a fallback mode that proves the extraction with opening + sum = closing when there is no running balance, and say up front that card PDFs usually need the issuer's CSV.

issues.quote: `stale_days` (the matching window unless the owner set one) of period end
issues.problem: stale_days defaults to the 3-day matching window. So every ordinary outstanding payment dated more than 3 days before period end becomes 'investigate' and blocks RECONCILED until the owner confirms it or a next statement is supplied. This loads the owner with questions, and seniors normally carry such items as timing, aged. The mechanics also fill step 6 with script detail.
issues.fix: Use separate labelled defaults: outstanding payments timing up to about 30-60 days per the aging buckets, deposits in transit stale after about 5 business days. Move the stale_days and late-clearing mechanics into references/input-schema.md and keep one rule line in SKILL.md.

issues.section: When to use, and when not
issues.quote: Use for one account and one period at a time: bank, credit card, loan, petty
issues.problem: The description and scope claim loan and petty-cash coverage, but the procedure and scripts are all statement-CSV shaped. Petty cash has no statement file (it is a count plus receipts), and loans need a lender schedule to split interest from principal. Neither has a procedure branch. Card statement cycles that close mid-month are also not addressed.
issues.fix: Add short branches: petty cash (count sheet → hand layout from account-types.md), loan (lender statement or amortisation schedule as the external record), card (set period to the statement cycle dates and take the ledger balance at the cycle close). Or narrow the description.

issues.quote: withdrawal, changed payee bank details, a duplicate payment, a large or
issues.problem: Two escalation triggers have no threshold: 'large or repeated difference' and 'not cleared within a few business days'. Different runs will escalate inconsistently.
