issues.fix: Take a materiality amount and a clearing lag from intake.json or ask_question at first run, label them 'default — confirm with the owner', and print them in the workpaper header.

issues.quote: Fix or report what it finds. For several accounts, one Task per account (at most 3 at once).
issues.problem: This mixes a Claude-Code-style 'Task' with the run_sub_session call used a line earlier. It is unclear which mechanism to use for multi-account runs.
issues.fix: Say 'one run_sub_session per account (at most 3 at once)' and keep the prompt template shown above.

issues.quote: `examples/worked-example.md` (end to end, with the plugging trap) and `examples/scenarios/`
issues.problem: The worked example keeps 'the original short example (kept from version 1)', which uses the same entity, account and month (Bramble, main-4411, April 2026) with different balances (31,408.19 vs 11,793.00) and a different line number for the same 'CARD FEE REFUND REV' item (191 vs 194). A model reading it could conflate the two.
issues.fix: Delete the v1 example, or move it to a different month or account and label it clearly as a hand-computed layout sample.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our April Barclays statement CSV and the Xero bank register export for the main current account. Can you reconcile April and tell me what doesn't match?
scenarios.why: The inputs table, the list_workspace_files/read_workspace_file pull and the python pre-flight all apply. A missing prior rec is recorded as an open item. rec_match.py proves both files against their opening and closing balances, matches one-to-one in passes, and lists ambiguous and duplicate rows. Step 6 turns leftovers into one ask_question card. write_workpaper.py produces the layout, aging, owners and sign-off block, and step 10 hashes and logs the approval. The output is senior-quality. One friction point: no step tells the model to convert Barclays' Date (DD/MM/YYYY), Money In and Money Out columns into the canonical id/date/amount schema. The model has to improvise that code, though rec_match's balance proof will catch a bad conversion. With the 3-day stale default, any cheque written more than 3 days before month-end also turns up as 'investigate'.

scenarios.prompt: QuickBooks says our Chase checking is off by $1,247.35 from the bank and it's been wrong since around May. I've got the April-June statement PDFs, a QBO register export, and Stripe payout reports; QBO isn't connected.
scenarios.why: extract_statement.py needs a running balance printed on every line. Chase-style PDFs list transactions without one, so extraction fails twice and step 3 falls back to asking for CSVs: safe, but it stalls. The Stripe breakdown (payout_breakdown.py) handles this case well, with gross, fees, refunds, disputes and in-transit payouts. If the gap comes from an edited, already-reconciled QBO transaction, step 1's tie never fires, because it compares the statement opening with the prior statement closing and not the ledger opening with the prior ledger closing. I verified this: raising ledger_opening by 100 on scenario a gives NOT RECONCILED, unexplained -100.00, 0 investigate items and no diagnostic. The model then has to find the month-by-month search in references/ledger-diagnostics.md on its own.

better: Adds prior-period chaining and carries open items and drafted corrections forward month to month with namespaced ids
Replaces prose matching passes with a self-tested one-to-one matcher that lists ambiguous, duplicate and out-of-period rows
Adds Stripe/PayPal clearing breakdown (gross, fees, refunds, disputes, in-transit, per-currency) and running-balance-proven PDF extraction
Turns a loose 'Show:' bullet list into an output contract, a generated workpaper with aging and owners, a before-release checklist, and SHA-256-logged sign-off
Adds hard anti-plug rules enforced in code (out-of-period refusal diagnostic, no suspense entries) and masking of account numbers in every output
Adds QBO/Xero diagnostics, feed-vs-statement checks, and escalation routing to bookkeeping-exception-escalation with exception ids
Names inputs, sources and fallbacks up front, including a labelled hand-computed path when Python is missing
worse: Body grew from 54 to 202 lines, much of it script internals (carried-id namespacing, stale_days rules) that belong in references
The 3-day stale default makes ordinary outstanding payments 'investigate', where v1 simply listed valid timing differences with dates, so it asks the owner more questions
Tighter coupling to harness names and paths (~/skills/<slug>, ~/workspace state, run_capability ids) that will need upkeep if the runtime changes
New opening-tie wording attributes a statement-opening gap to ledger edits, a misleading diagnosis v1 never made, while the real ledger-side tie is absent
extract_statement.py adds a pdfplumber/pdftotext dependency that contradicts the body's 'standard library only; no install' claim

on-page-seo-audit.job: audit a single page's on-page SEO
on-page-seo-audit.summary: A 50-line checklist that tests whether a page's title, URL, H1, opening paragraph and subheads agree, works down eight on-page checks, and reports the top three fixes as paste-ready copy plus an unranked list of everything else.
strengths: The five-element coherence test (title, URL, H1, first paragraph, subheads) is a fast, sharp diagnostic
'Stop when you have three real problems' matches the persona's promise of three fixes, not a list of twenty
A defined report: current state quoted, fix written ready to paste, one line on why it matters, then an unranked list of everything else
Correct framing that the meta description is the ad, not a ranking factor
Names cannibalisation as a finding and asks for a winner
Guardrails: never guess traffic, rankings or volume, and never rewrite a page that already ranks
missing: Indexability and canonical/robots/status checks
Named inputs: URL or paste, target query, Search Console/rank data
Search-results comparison for the target query (page type and shape)
A concrete method for finding internal links pointing to the page
Structured data, mobile and Core Web Vitals checks (at least flagging)
Handling of JS-rendered pages (browser tool) and pages behind auth (ask for a paste)
Consolidation mechanics for cannibalising pages
Baseline and re-check plan to measure whether fixes worked

issues.problem: There is no indexability gate: status code, noindex, robots.txt, canonical target, and whether the page is in Google's index at all. A page that can't be indexed makes every other check moot, and this is the first thing a senior SEO rules out.
issues.fix: Before the checks list, add 'Can it be indexed?': fetch the page, confirm 200, no noindex, not blocked by robots.txt, a self-referencing canonical, and a site:/URL Inspection check. If any fails, that is finding #1.

issues.quote: Use this when someone asks why a page is not ranking, or before a page goes
issues.problem: Inputs are never named: the URL or pasted HTML, the target query, and whether rank or Search Console data exists. The skill also never says how to get the page: web_fetch, or the browser tool for JS-rendered pages. Without a target query, 'why doesn't it rank' has no reference point.
issues.fix: Open with inputs: URL (or pasted HTML/copy), target query, and any Search Console or DataForSEO data. Fetch with web_fetch, use browser_navigate if the content is JS-rendered, and ask for a paste if the page is behind auth.

issues.section: Read the page as a machine would
issues.quote: Strip the design away and ask what the page is about using only the title, the
issues.problem: The page is judged only against itself. The most common reason a page doesn't rank is intent mismatch: the results reward a different page type or shape. The sibling seo-content-brief already reads the top five results, but this audit never does.
issues.fix: Add a step: search the target query, note the page type and shape of the top five, and compare. If the shape differs, that is the lead finding.

issues.quote: does anything on the site point here, using words that
issues.problem: Nothing says how to find links pointing to the page. A model with only the page itself cannot tell whether it is orphaned, so this finding will be guessed.
issues.fix: Name the methods: a Search Console Links report export, a site crawl via the Firecrawl block, or a site: search for the page's topic. If none is available, say the check could not be run rather than asserting 'orphan'.

issues.quote: different from the H1. A title that reads like a filename is a fix.
issues.problem: Requiring the title to differ from the H1 is not an established best practice; many strong pages keep them near-identical. It will produce needless 'fixes'. The 60-character rule is also a proxy for pixel width.
issues.fix: Replace with: the title leads with the query phrase, fits about 580px (~55-60 characters) without truncating, and matches the page's promise. The H1 may match or vary.

issues.quote: triggers: ["seo audit", "why doesn't this rank", "check this page", "meta description", "title tag", "on-page"]
issues.problem: The generic 'seo audit' trigger collides with Toran's website-seo-audit if both land in Maria's kit. The description doesn't say this skill is single-page.
issues.fix: Say 'one page' in the description, drop the bare 'seo audit' trigger, and route whole-site or traffic-opportunity audits to website-seo-audit.

issues.quote: Say which one should win and what happens to the other.
issues.problem: The consolidation mechanics (merge content, 301, canonical, repoint internal links, keep the ranking URL) are left to the model. A bad choice here can lose existing rankings.
issues.fix: List the options in order of preference: merge into the ranking URL and 301 the other; else canonicalise; else re-target the loser to a different intent.

issues.problem: There is no way to verify the fixes worked. The persona says every piece ties to a measurable goal, but the report sets no baseline and no re-check.
issues.fix: Add one line per fix: the baseline metric if known (impressions, position, CTR from Search Console) and when to re-check after recrawl. Offer a schedule_followup.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our landing page https://acme.com/invoice-software. Why isn't it ranking for 'invoice software for freelancers'? Give me the fixes.
scenarios.why: The five-element read and the report of three quoted, paste-ready fixes give good copy-level output. But the skill never tells the model to web_fetch or render the URL, to read the search results for the target query, or to check noindex/canonical. So the real cause can be missed: the results may favour comparison listicles, or the page may canonicalise elsewhere. The 'orphan page' check has no method, so that finding would be a guess.

scenarios.prompt: Our new pricing page is on password-protected staging and goes live tomorrow; the copy is pasted below. We also have /plans, which currently ranks for 'acme pricing'. What should we fix before launch?
scenarios.why: The pasted copy is enough for the five-element read. 'One page per intent' and 'Never recommend a rewrite of a page that is ranking' point to the right decision: pick a winner, most likely /plans. But the skill has no launch checks: noindex or robots rules carried over from staging, the canonical, a 301 from the losing URL, and repointing internal links. These are the most common launch-day SEO failures, and 'what happens to the other' is left undefined.

seo-content-brief.job: write SEO content brief for a writer
seo-content-brief.summary: A short procedure that sorts search intent from the top five results into four page shapes and produces a six-item brief (phrase and variants, intent, ordered questions, angle, target length, one action), with writing rules and no-invention guardrails.
strengths: Intent before keyword, with a practical four-way taxonomy that maps each intent to a page shape
The split-intent rule ('a page that serves two intents serves neither') forces a decision
Questions are ordered the way a reader would ask them, sourced from People Also Ask and competitors' subheads
The angle requirement ('the thing we know because of what we do') asks for something competitors don't have
Strong guardrails: no keyword stuffing, no invented stats (leave a marked gap), no ranking or timeline promises
Very concise, with no filler
missing: Inputs gathered up front (audience, differentiators, proof, voice, goal)
Check for an existing page targeting the phrase
Search-results tool and People Also Ask source (DataForSEO) with a paste fallback
Transactional/commercial and local intent types
Brief template fields: title/meta options, H2 outline, internal links in and out, sources and proof owners
Search-results features and AI Overview considerations
First-hand experience and author requirements for YMYL topics
Success metric for the page

issues.quote: The angle nobody else has taken — the thing we know because of what we do.
issues.problem: The angle, the one action and the voice depend on product differentiators, audience, proof and goal, but the skill never asks for them. The persona says to ask for voice guidelines, audience and differentiators when they are missing. Without them the model will invent an angle.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Inputs' step before the intent read: keyword, audience, product and differentiators, available proof, voice guide (check memory or brand-voice-guide), and the goal/CTA. Ask only for what is missing, using ask_question.

issues.section: Start with the intent, not the keyword
issues.quote: Read the top five results for the exact phrase and decide which of these the
issues.problem: No tool is named and there is no fallback. The People Also Ask box needs search-results data (the DataForSEO block), because plain web_search won't return it. With no search available, the model has no instruction to ask for a paste or to label the intent call as its own read.
issues.fix: Name web_search/web_fetch or the DataForSEO results block for the top five and People Also Ask. If unavailable, ask the user to paste the results page, or label the intent as an unverified read.

issues.section: Start with the intent, not the keyword
issues.problem: There is no check for whether the site already has a page for this phrase. A new brief can create exactly the cannibalisation that on-page-seo-audit warns about.
issues.fix: Add step 0: a site: search or Search Console query check. If a page already exists, recommend refreshing or expanding it and hand off to on-page-seo-audit instead of briefing a new URL.

issues.section: Start with the intent, not the keyword
issues.quote: they are deciding whether to care. Problem framing first,
issues.problem: The four intents leave out transactional/commercial (product or category pages) and local. For queries like 'payroll software', where the results are vendor home pages, the model will be pushed into a blog shape that can't rank.
issues.fix: Add 'Buy/Sign up — product or category page, not a blog post' and 'Local'. When the results are dominated by those, say a blog brief is the wrong asset.

issues.quote: Six things, no more:
issues.problem: The cap leaves out fields a writer needs to execute: title and meta options, an H2 outline, internal link targets (from and to), sources and proof to gather and who holds them, and audience/voice notes. The writer then has to come back with questions.
issues.fix: Keep it tight, but ship a template with those fields, or allow an 'extras' block: title options, meta, outline, links in and out, proof owners.

issues.section: Start with the intent, not the keyword
issues.problem: Search-results features (featured snippets, AI Overviews, video and forum blocks) aren't considered. In 2026 they decide whether an answer-intent page earns clicks at all, and what passage format gets cited.
issues.fix: Add one line: note the features on the results page and shape the opening answer or passage to win or be cited by them. If an AI Overview answers it outright, reconsider the target.

issues.quote: Target length, taken from the median of the top five, not from a habit.
issues.problem: Word counts of top results are noisy and length is not a ranking lever. Coverage of the questions should set length.
issues.fix: Frame the median as a sanity range, with length following from answering every question in the brief.

issues.quote: triggers: ["content brief", "seo brief", "keyword", "write an article", "blog post", "rank for", "search intent"]
issues.problem: 'keyword' and 'blog post' are too broad: they fire on keyword research and social posts. They also collide with Maya's content-brief-writer-handoff ('asset brief', 'brief the writer').
issues.fix: Narrow to brief-specific phrases ('brief for keyword', 'what should this page cover to rank'). If both experts keep a brief skill, make this the SEO-intent half and have the handoff skill call it.

scenarios.prompt: Write a brief for 'how to reconcile a bank statement' for our bookkeeping app's blog.
scenarios.why: The intent section classifies it as How-to from the top five results and sets the shape (steps, prerequisites, what goes wrong). The six-item list gives variants, ordered questions from People Also Ask and competitors' subheads, an angle, a median length and the one action. The rule to leave a marked gap stops invented stats. The only gaps are internal link targets and a sources list, and the model has to work out on its own that it should use web_search.

scenarios.prompt: Brief for 'best payroll software for restaurants'. We're one of the vendors, legal says we can't name competitors, and there's no search integration connected, so I can paste what I see in Google.
scenarios.why: The skill spots Compare intent and prescribes 'Table, criteria, a verdict', which conflicts with the rule against naming competitors. It offers no way out, such as a criteria-led buyer's guide or targeting a different keyword variant. 'Read the top five results' has no fallback for pasted results or People Also Ask. There is no step to ask for the differentiators the angle depends on, and no note on getting comparative claims reviewed.

marketing-content-strategy.job: plan content strategy, pillars and topic priorities
marketing-content-strategy.summary: Corey Haines' upstream content-strategy playbook: searchable vs shareable content, content types, pillars and clusters, buyer-stage keyword modifiers, six ideation sources, weighted topic scoring, a 60/30/10 calendar split and distribution. It also ships headless-CMS selection and Sanity/Contentful/Strapi API guides.
strengths: The searchable-vs-shareable lens gives every piece a job
Buyer-stage keyword modifiers (awareness through implementation) map topics to the funnel
Concrete ideation methods from real evidence: call transcripts, surveys, site: operators for Reddit and Quora, competitors' blogs
A weighted scoring template turns an idea list into a ranked backlog
The 60/30/10 calendar split, explicitly a starting ratio, is useful for negotiating stakeholder conflicts
Link-earning format data is caveated as a single vendor study
A distribution reference with an atomisation checklist per flagship piece
missing: Existing-content inventory and keep/refresh/merge/prune decisions
Keyword-to-URL mapping to prevent cannibalisation
Volume and difficulty sourcing (DataForSEO block or exports) with labelled estimates
Dated roadmap sized to capacity, with owners
Success metrics per pillar and a review cadence
Approval gate before any CMS or publishing action
A handoff to seo-content-brief for each chosen topic
Platform-native context lookup (memory/workspace)

issues.quote: What's the monthly search volume?
issues.problem: Scoring and the keyword table ask for volume and difficulty, but nothing says where those numbers come from when no export is supplied. The model will estimate and present them as data, breaking Maria's 'never invent statistics' boundary.
issues.fix: Add: volumes come only from a supplied export, Search Console, or the DataForSEO block. Otherwise mark the column 'unknown' or 'estimate (assumed)' and score search potential qualitatively.

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy
issues.problem: These are repo-local file paths from coding agents (Claude-Code-style .claude/.agents). AutoGPT experts keep context in memory and the workspace, so the check will always miss.
issues.fix: Replace with: memory_search for product and audience context, then read_workspace_file for a product-marketing context doc if one exists, or run product-marketing-context. Ask only for the gaps.

issues.quote: Do you have existing content? What's working?
issues.problem: For an existing site, a content strategy starts with an inventory: traffic, rankings, decay, cannibalisation, and a keep/refresh/consolidate/prune decision. Here that is a single question with no step, so new topics get planned over the top of decaying or overlapping pages.
issues.fix: Add a 'Content inventory' step: pull a sitemap or crawl plus Search Console/analytics export if available, tag each URL keep/refresh/merge/prune, and map one primary keyword to one URL before proposing new topics.

issues.quote: When creating a content strategy, provide:
issues.problem: The deliverable stops at pillars, topics and a cluster map. There is no dated roadmap or cadence sized to stated capacity, no owners, no distribution plan per flagship, and no success metrics per pillar, even though the body covers 60/30/10 and distribution at length.
issues.fix: Add a 4th and 5th section: a dated calendar (cadence against capacity, owner, ship date, format, mix label) and a measurement plan (KPI per pillar, baseline, review date). Offer to hand the calendar to editorial-calendar-ops.

issues.quote: CMS selection, content modeling for marketing, editorial workflows, platform comparison (Sanity, Contentful, Strapi)
issues.problem: Choosing a headless CMS and the bundled Sanity/Contentful/Strapi API guides (about 670 lines) are outside a content strategist's job. The guides show create/delete/publish mutations and CLI installs with no draft-or-approval gate.
issues.fix: Remove the CMS reference and tools/ from this package, or move them to a separate web/CMS skill. If kept, require draft plus explicit approval before any write or publish call.

issues.quote: For writing individual pieces, see copywriting. For SEO-specific audits, see seo-audit. For social media content specifically, see social.
issues.problem: The description and Related Skills route to skills that aren't installed (copywriting, seo-audit, social, ai-seo, programmatic-seo, site-architecture, free-tools), so read_skill lookups will fail.
issues.fix: Rename to installed skills (marketing-copywriting, website-seo-audit or on-page-seo-audit, social-media-management) and delete the references with no installed equivalent.

issues.quote: Score 1-10 per factor, multiply by the weight, sum for the total. Rank the list; make the top-scoring pieces first.
issues.problem: Subjective 1-10 scores produce decimal totals that look like data. Prompts such as 'What's the potential LTV' invite invented figures, and nothing requires the evidence behind each score to be shown.
issues.fix: Require a one-line evidence note per score (quote, export row, or 'judgement'), compute totals in bash_exec, and present the ranking as a judgement call.

issues.quote: Facebook organic reach fell from ~20% to under 2%; any rented channel can throttle you overnight.
issues.problem: The statistic has no source, and the model may repeat it to users as fact.
issues.fix: Cite a source and date or soften it to a qualitative claim.

scenarios.prompt: We sell scheduling software to dental clinics. Here's our Ahrefs keyword export and notes from six sales calls. What should our blog cover, and what do we write first?
scenarios.why: 'Before Planning' gathers context. 'Keyword Data' turns the export into a prioritised table with real volumes. 'Call Transcripts' pulls questions and objections with quotes. The pillar criteria and weighted scoring template rank ideas, and 'Output Format' delivers pillars, priority topics and a cluster map. The one gap: nothing checks what already exists on the blog before new topics are proposed.

scenarios.prompt: Plan the next 90 days of content. We have no keyword tool, two hours a week of writing time, the CEO wants thought leadership, sales wants SEO leads, and we have 80 old posts with falling traffic.
scenarios.why: The 60/30/10 split, framed as a starting ratio rather than a rule, gives a way to settle the CEO/sales conflict. But 'Search Potential' asks for monthly volume with no sourcing rule (DataForSEO block or a labelled estimate), so volumes will be invented. There is no inventory step for the 80 decaying posts (refresh, consolidate, prune), no capacity maths for two hours a week, and 'Output Format' has no dated 90-day calendar or success metrics.

marketing-copy-editing.job: edit and refresh existing marketing copy
marketing-copy-editing.summary: Corey Haines' upstream copy-editing playbook built on the Seven Sweeps (clarity, voice, so-what, prove-it, specificity, emotion, zero-risk) with cumulative loop-backs. It adds an optional persona-panel scoring gate, quick word/sentence/paragraph checks, a plain-English word list, a QA checklist and a content-refresh checklist.
strengths: The Seven Sweeps is a recognised editing framework (Copyhackers lineage) with clear focus per pass
The Prove It sweep flags unsupported claims and offers softening as an option
A Quick-Pass mode for small edits avoids running the full framework on minor copy
The refresh-vs-rewrite matrix and refresh cadence are practical
The plain-English alternatives reference is sourced and sits in references/
Respects the author's voice and ownership of the copy
missing: Output template: revised copy plus a change log (original, edit, sweep, reason)
Placeholder convention for proof or numbers the user must supply
Claims-substantiation and legal review trigger for comparative, regulated or guarantee claims
SEO-preservation rules for editing ranking pages
House style conformance (spelling variant, capitalisation, numerals, product names)
Readability measurement run in the sandbox rather than eyeballed
Character limits for meta, UI and ad copy
Accessibility and inclusive-language pass

issues.quote: Add numbers, timeframes, or examples
issues.problem: Together with the vague-to-specific table ('Save 4 hours every week', '2,847 teams'), this tells the model to insert figures without saying they must come from supplied evidence. Invented stats in published copy break Maria's boundary and create claims-substantiation risk.
issues.fix: Specify: add numbers only from evidence the user supplied or that has been verified. Otherwise insert a visible placeholder such as [NEED: weekly time saved, source] and list it under open questions.

issues.quote: Add risk reversals or trust signals as needed
issues.problem: Suggesting money-back guarantees, free trials or 'Cancel anytime' can commit the business to policies it doesn't offer, a legal and commercial obligation made by an editor.
issues.fix: Only surface risk reversals the business confirms it offers. Otherwise propose them as a question for the owner, never as inserted copy.

issues.quote: Show what you found, why it's an issue
issues.problem: There is no defined deliverable. The model can't tell whether to return clean revised copy, a tracked-changes table or per-sweep notes, and step 3 ('Request the updated copy') pushes the rewrite back onto the user.
issues.fix: Define the output: (1) the revised copy, ready to paste; (2) a change log table of original, edit, sweep and reason; (3) open questions and proof needed. Save it to the workspace on request.

issues.quote: Use the content refresh framework when traffic is declining, data is stale, or the product has changed.
issues.problem: There are no rules for editing a page that ranks. Changing the title, H1, URL/slug or the headings that rank can lose traffic, and the SEO expert this skill is proposed for needs that guard.
issues.fix: Add a preservation rule: before editing, identify the ranking queries (Search Console export, or ask). Keep the URL, keep the query in title and H1, keep headings that rank, and flag any structural change as needing approval.

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy
issues.problem: These are repo-local paths for coding agents. In AutoGPT, brand voice and customer language live in memory, the workspace or brand-voice-guide, so this check always misses.
issues.fix: Replace with memory_search, read_workspace_file for a voice or product doc, or load brand-voice-guide. Ask for the voice guide if none exists.

issues.quote: iterate until all personas score 7+, with an average of 8+ across the panel
issues.problem: A single model playing the personas and grading its own edits produces made-up scores and a potentially unbounded loop. The stop condition sounds objective but isn't.
issues.fix: Call it a heuristic self-review, cap it at one revision round, and use consult_teammate for a genuine second view on high-stakes copy.

issues.quote: 'update this page,' 'this content is outdated,' or 'content audit.'
issues.problem: The triggers overlap with marketing-copywriting ('improve this copy', 'this copy is weak') and with SEO audits. 'content audit' is usually an inventory task, not copy editing, so the wrong skill will load.
issues.fix: Drop 'content audit' and 'make this better'. Say 'line-level edits to existing copy, keeping the structure', and route rewrites to marketing-copywriting and site audits to the SEO skills.

issues.quote: For broader page optimization beyond copy
issues.problem: cro, marketing-psychology, ab-testing and copywriting (in the 'When to Use' table) are not installed in the catalog, so references to them dead-end.
issues.fix: Map to installed names (marketing-copywriting) and remove the entries with no installed equivalent.

scenarios.prompt: Tighten up our homepage hero and features section (pasted). It's too wordy and feels corporate. Keep our voice.
scenarios.why: The quick-pass checks, the plain-English reference and the Clarity/Voice sweeps handle wordiness and corporate speak well. But the deliverable is undefined ('Working with Copy Sweeps' even says 'Request the updated copy'). Specificity step 3, 'Add numbers, timeframes, or examples', together with the '2,847 teams' table, pushes the model to insert unsupported figures unless it applies Maria's boundary on its own.

scenarios.prompt: Refresh our 2023 'best CRM for startups' post at this URL. Traffic is down 40% since spring. Don't break what still ranks. Search Console isn't connected, and the competitor pricing in the post is probably stale.
scenarios.why: references/content-refresh.md gives freshness, accuracy and SEO passes and a refresh-vs-rewrite matrix, which frame the job. But nothing covers the defining constraint: keep the target query in the title/H1, keep the URL and the headings that rank, and get query data when Search Console is missing (connect_integration or ask for an export). 'Update all dates, stats' has no sourcing rule, so refreshed competitor pricing may be guessed instead of fetched and dated.

14:bookkeeping-getting-started.job: set up bookkeeping intake and records inventory
14:bookkeeping-getting-started.summary: Runs a read-only bookkeeping intake. It masks and profiles uploaded exports with bundled scripts and records entity, period, basis, chart, approvers, system of record and jurisdiction flags in a saved intake.json that later skills read. It sorts every source into Ready, Usable with a warning or Blocked, and prepares one card of blocking questions plus a missing-documents request for the owner.
strengths: Every tool call is real and correctly shaped for the AutoGPT harness: run_capability/find_capability/describe_capability, list_workspace_files with include_all_sessions, read_workspace_file save_to_path, write_workspace_file source_path, schedule_routine with session_mode THREAD, TodoWrite, and ~/skills/<slug> resolving to /home/user/skills. It also falls back cleanly when state or Python is unavailable.

Four stdlib-only scripts with self-tests that pass. They cover exact Decimal money handling, ambiguous day/month detection, running-balance breaks in either row order, ragged rows from unquoted commas, debit+credit shifts, bank preamble lines, and duplicates that are listed and never dropped.
Data minimisation is enforced by a script: redact.py masks identifier columns, IBANs, Luhn-valid card numbers, sort codes and email addresses before any row is read.
It persists state in ~/workspace/bookkeeping/<entity>/intake.json, which downstream kit skills read. A --previous diff makes the owner re-confirm changes to approvers, basis or accountant.

Senior-practitioner judgement: proof of payment versus proof of cost, catch-up one period at a time from the oldest, one intake per entity, a next approver when the usual approver is conflicted, the owner keeping their own export copy (the Bench shutdown lesson), and MTD and retention flags with dated sources.

Guardrails are well built: questions go to the user for forwarding, 'Not sure: ask the accountant' is always an option, connection probes are read-only, a routine is created only on a yes to its exact wording and its prompt forbids external actions, and a step that fails twice is stopped.
missing: Materiality threshold, approval limits and engagement scope captured at intake
A path for non-transaction files (trial balance, chart of accounts, AR/AP aging) and for ledger reports with subtotal rows
A recorded sign-convention value per source for downstream normalisation
Gross/fee/net mapping for payment processors (Stripe, Square, PayPal payouts) and their clearing accounts
Outstanding items from the prior approved reconciliation, carried in as opening reconciling items
Ledger lock or closing-date status and whether prior periods are still open to edits
Owner/personal account policy (owner draws, reimbursements) recorded as a rule, not only as an entity question
A no-uploads-yet branch that yields a document request and a partial intake

issues.quote: charges positive (confirmed)
issues.problem: The worked example models the guesses the skill forbids. The walkthrough's question card held only Q1-Q4, so the Amex sign convention was never asked, yet it is marked 'confirmed' and intake.json sets sign_convention_confirmed true. The bank dates are also reported as '1 to 12 Apr' and Q2 says the export 'stops on 12 April' while the format is still ambiguous, which assumes day/month. Models copy examples, so this undercuts the self-check line 'No date format, sign convention … was guessed'.
issues.fix: Add Q6 (sign convention) to the example's question card and leave the Amex source Usable with a warning until it is answered. Show the bank date range as 'ambiguous: 1-12 Apr or 4 Jan-4 Dec' and make Q2 conditional on Q1. Also reconcile masked_fields ['Reference'] in intake.json with the walkthrough's use of --keep-column Reference.

issues.quote: `SIGN_CHECK` → ask whether positives are charges; record the answer.
issues.problem: templates/intake.json has only a boolean sign_convention_confirmed, so nothing records which way the sign runs. expense-categorization reads the sign convention from intake.json, and normalize_export.py needs --flip-sign, so the answer is lost between chats. SIGN_CHECK also fires whenever positive rows outnumber negative ones, so a revenue-heavy bank account gets the wrong question ('are positives charges?').
issues.fix: Add a per-source sign_convention field ('money_in_positive' or 'charges_positive'). Make intake_check.py block when SIGN_CHECK fired and the field is empty. Word the question by source type: card files get 'are charges positive?', bank files get 'is money in positive?'.

issues.quote: Profile every export:
issues.problem: profile_sources.py only works on transaction lists. A trial balance, chart of accounts or AR/AP aging CSV has no date column, so the script exits with code 2 and suggests --header-line. QuickBooks and Xero ledger reports, which the triggers name, carry group headings and 'Total for …' rows. In testing, the subtotal was summed into the inflow total (6955.00 instead of 3500.00) and the headings were flagged UNREADABLE_AMOUNTS. The only remedy offered is 'ask for a properly quoted export'.
issues.fix: Add a classification step before profiling that sorts files into transaction list, balance report (trial balance, aging), chart of accounts, or PDF. Send trial balances to the opening-balance evidence check and charts of accounts to chart.source. For QBO or Xero, request 'Transaction List by Date' or 'Account Transactions' without subtotals, or make the profiler detect and exclude Total rows and flag REPORT_LAYOUT.

issues.quote: Once the owner confirms format and sign, `scripts/normalize_export.py` writes
issues.problem: No command, input or output path is given. The script's own docstring runs it on the raw /home/user/in file, not the masked copy. /home/user/work is scratch and is lost when the chat expires, and books-state.md has no canonical folder, so the 'canonical CSV that later skills read' does not persist. The downstream skills re-pull exports themselves anyway.
issues.fix: Give the exact command on the .masked.csv with --date-format, --currency and --flip-sign taken from intake.json, writing to ~/workspace/bookkeeping/<slug>/canonical/<file>-<YYYY-MM>.csv, and add that path to the books-state layout. Otherwise drop the claim.

issues.quote: Who approves invoices, adjustments, customer contact, and final reports,
issues.problem: The intake records approvers but no materiality threshold, approval limits or engagement scope. The persona and every downstream skill escalate 'material' items, yet the kit never defines what material means for this entity.
issues.fix: Add an intake item: the materiality or escalation threshold and approval limits as stated by the owner or accountant, plus the services in scope (bookkeeping, AR, payroll tie-out). Record them in intake.json and have intake_check.py warn when they are missing.

issues.problem: The triggers include 'what finance records do you need' and 'bookkeeping intake checklist', but every procedure step assumes uploaded files. There is no short path for a user who has not uploaded anything yet, so the model may run pre-flight and profiling steps for no reason.
issues.fix: Add step 0: if no files are supplied, collect entity, period, system and accountant with ask_question. Then build the missing-documents request from references/source-document-checklist.md, save a partial intake.json and stop.

issues.quote: here are my bank statements
issues.problem: This trigger and 'QuickBooks export' will also fire when a user who already has an intake just wants a statement reconciled or expenses coded, so the skill competes with statement-reconciliation and expense-categorization.
issues.fix: Narrow the trigger to 'here are my bank statements, get me set up', or add a line under Use when: if intake.json already exists and covers the period, hand straight to the requested skill.

issues.quote: The profile of `<name>.masked.csv` is matched to the intake source
issues.problem: The body is about 13KB and includes script internals (join rules), a flag-by-flag decision list, a Package files list that duplicates what read_skill already returns, and a short-form example that repeats the walkthrough. All of it is loaded on every trigger.
issues.fix: Move the flag-to-decision mapping into references/profile-flags.md, drop the join explanation (it is already in intake_check.py's docstring) and the Package files section, and keep only a 3-line pointer to the example.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Mina, we're a 6-person UK design studio. I've uploaded our April Barclays CSV and our Amex export. We use Xero and Priya is our accountant. Can you get set up to do our books?
scenarios.why: Pre-flight (state check, Python check, redact.py) masks the Barclays Account column to the last 4 digits. profile_sources.py resolves day/month once any day is above 12, fires SIGN_CHECK on the Amex file and lists duplicates. Step 4 fills the intake. Step 5's intake_check.py blocks on the missing opening-balance evidence. Step 6 puts the questions in one ask_question card, and steps 7-8 write the missing-documents request (signed March trial balance) and save intake.json plus intake.md. A senior bookkeeper would sign off on this output.

scenarios.prompt: I'm 7 months behind. Attached: a QuickBooks Online General Ledger CSV (Jan-Jul), last year's trial balance as a PDF, my Chase checking CSV (some Venmo transfers in it are personal), and a Square payouts export. Please catch up my books.
scenarios.why: Step 1 is handled well: it separates personal from business activity, works oldest period first, and asks for the PDF's balances as printed. The QBO GL report is the gap. Its group-heading rows trigger UNREADABLE_AMOUNTS, and its 'Total for …' rows are summed into the inflow total (tested: In 6955.00 against a true 3500.00). Step 3's only remedy is 'ask for a properly quoted export', which will not fix a report layout; the skill never says to request a transaction-list export without subtotals. A trial balance supplied as CSV makes the profiler exit with code 2 and a misleading --header-line hint. Square payouts are net of fees, and the intake has no gross/fee/net guidance for them.

better: Main's 55-line placeholder only listed intake fields. The PR adds a persisted intake.json state chain that downstream kit skills load, plus a --previous diff for re-confirming changes.

Scripted, self-tested profiling replaces hand review: ambiguous day/month dates, balance breaks, ragged rows, debit+credit shifts, empty exports and duplicates each map to a Ready, Usable-with-warning or Blocked decision.
Data minimisation is enforced by redact.py before any row is read; main had only a one-line 'least detail' rule.
The description and triggers are sharper (main's bare 'books' trigger was far too broad) and name the adjacent skills that should be used instead.

New senior content: system-of-record probe and owner export copy, jurisdiction flags (MTD, retention, sales-tax nexus, fiscal year end), a next approver when the usual one is conflicted, catch-up oldest period first, and a mixed-entity hard case.

Blocking questions are batched into one ask_question card with 'Not sure: ask the accountant'. The PR also adds a missing-documents request per document holder, open-items.csv tracking, and an optional cadence routine that forbids external actions.
worse: Token cost rises from about 55 lines to about 205 lines plus 20 supporting files, and a simple 'what records do you need?' question has no short path.
The worked example guesses the sign convention and the day/month order, contradicting the no-guess rule that main stated plainly.
New failure surface: the profiler exits with code 2 on trial balance and chart-of-accounts files, and it sums QuickBooks and Xero subtotal rows into control totals.
It claims a canonical CSV 'that later skills read' but gives it no durable path.

ops-run-the-operating-rhythm.summary: Sets up and runs a weekly, monthly or quarterly business review: it fixes the period, builds a pack that scores KPIs red/yellow/green and tags them input or output, lists movers, stuck items and decisions, runs an exception-based agenda and closes with a decision log and the open actions carried forward.
strengths: An exception-based review where the metric owner explains each miss and 'still analysing' beats a made-up cause
Enforces INPUT/OUTPUT tagging with at least two to three leading metrics per review
A decision needs an owner and a date, and a metric red two reviews running gets a corrective action plan
Reads existing rhythm and open actions before building, and says the baseline starts next time when no prior review exists
FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN on every line and no email or post without the owner's yes
missing: R/Y/G threshold definitions and a signal-vs-noise method (XmR or natural process limits)
Separate MBR and QBR content (forecast vs plan, OKR and strategy review, next-period plan)
Review pack and decision log templates
Year-over-year and seasonality comparisons
An explicit handoff to ops-scorecard-and-kpis for metric definitions
An approval step before circulating the pre-read

issues.quote: how the business is doing this period, or hands over numbers for a
issues.problem: 'How is the business doing' plus 'hands over numbers' is almost the same trigger as ops-scorecard-and-kpis ('how operations is doing, hands over numbers for a read'), so the model cannot tell which to load. Scoring logic (fix period, R/Y/G, movers) is also duplicated across both.
issues.fix: Narrow this skill to the meeting: the pack, agenda, decision log and action carry-forward. Tell it to load ops-scorecard-and-kpis for metric definitions and scoring, and change the description to 'set up or run the review meeting/pack'.

issues.section: Run the agenda in this order
issues.quote: The review is exception-based. Metrics inside expected variance get
issues.problem: 'Expected variance' and the R/Y/G bands are never defined, so the model cannot separate exceptions from noise consistently and will make up thresholds.
issues.fix: Define R/Y/G bands, for example green at or above target, yellow within an owner-set tolerance, red beyond it. Define expected variance with trailing-period natural process limits (XmR), computed in bash_exec.

issues.section: Run the agenda in this order
issues.quote: Numbers (ten minutes), stuck items (ten minutes), decisions (fifteen
issues.problem: One 40-minute agenda serves WBR, MBR and QBR alike. An MBR needs a month-vs-plan and forecast read. A QBR needs a strategy and OKR review, a plan reset for next quarter and resource trade-offs.
issues.fix: Add a short per-cadence table covering length, comparisons (WoW with a trailing 6 weeks, MoM with YoY, QoQ against plan) and the extra sections for MBR and QBR.

issues.problem: The pack is described in prose bullets with no template, so each run lays it out differently and review-to-review comparison gets harder.
issues.fix: Ship templates/review-pack.md with a headline line, KPI table (metric, type, actual, target, prior, R/Y/G, label), movers, shipped, stuck, decisions and actions.

issues.section: Fix the period and say it out loud
issues.quote: Never compare a partial period to a full one.
issues.problem: It forbids the error but gives no alternative, and it leaves out the like-for-like holiday comparison and trailing trend that James's own weekly routine uses.
issues.fix: Add the alternatives: compare the same elapsed days, or label a run-rate projection as INFERENCE, or move the review. Add the holiday-week and trailing-6-week comparison rule.

issues.quote: No KPI set means you propose five to seven from what they already
issues.problem: KPI design is duplicated here instead of routed to the scorecard skill, so there is a second, lighter definition path with no formulas or owners.
issues.fix: Route to ops-scorecard-and-kpis to define the KPI set, and use its definitions.

issues.quote: night before: the meeting decides, it does not present.
issues.problem: 'Circulate the pack the night before' conflicts with the rule that nothing is emailed or posted without a yes. No step gets that approval or schedules the send.
issues.fix: Add a step: stage the pack as a draft, ask the owner to approve distribution, then circulate, optionally with schedule_followup.

issues.quote: Save dated under reviews, one folder per cadence. The action list is
issues.problem: The action list is called the source of truth, but its file, format and fields are never named, so persistence between reviews is left to chance.
issues.fix: Name the file (for example reviews/actions.csv with id, action, owner, due, status, opened, closed) and the pack filename pattern.

scenarios.prompt: Set up a weekly business review for us. The Google Sheet has 8 weeks of revenue, orders, on-time delivery and support tickets with targets, and last week's action list is in Notion.
scenarios.why: The path is clear: 'Read what exists' (last review, overdue actions, KPIs with and without targets), then fix the period, then build the pack (R/Y/G, INPUT/OUTPUT tags, top three movers, stuck items, decisions), then the timed agenda and the close-the-loop decision log. A capable model produces a usable WBR pack. The one weakness is the R/Y/G bands, which the model has to invent because the skill never defines yellow.

scenarios.prompt: Do the Q3 QBR. I only have July, August and half of September exported, we never set targets, and the CEO wants it emailed to the board tomorrow.
scenarios.why: The skill does handle two pieces: missing targets (propose five to seven KPIs, targets UNKNOWN) and the send gate ('never email... without the owner's yes'). It falls short on the rest. 'Never compare a partial period to a full one' says what not to do but offers no alternative, such as comparing like-for-like days, a run-rate, or delaying the review. The QBR gets the same 10/10/15/5 agenda as a weekly review, with no strategy or plan-reset section. There is no guidance on a board audience or on confidentiality.

ops-scorecard-and-kpis.summary: Defines operational KPIs (formula, source column, target, owner, input/output type), checks source coverage and period, scores each metric red/yellow/green, ranks and decomposes the movers, flags thin samples and audits metric definitions every quarter.
strengths: Every metric is defined once with a formula, source column, target, owner and INPUT/OUTPUT type
A coverage check comes before computation, and a missing source is named, never dropped quietly
Movers are ranked and decomposed, with an honest 'the numbers cannot explain this, here's the one read I'd need'
A quarterly metric audit retires dead metrics and names who certifies accuracy
'The plan proposes, the approver disposes' blocks spend or cut recommendations that no metric backs
missing: R/Y/G banding rules and metric direction
A signal-vs-noise method (XmR or natural process limits)
A baseline-to-proposed-target method for owner approval
Cross-source reconciliation and data-quality checks
Counter-metric pairing and a driver tree from inputs to outputs
A metric dictionary template and a scorecard layout template
Using bash_exec for the calculations

issues.quote: Use this when the user asks how operations is doing, hands over numbers
issues.problem: This trigger duplicates ops-run-the-operating-rhythm ('asks how the business is doing... hands over numbers'), so both skills compete for the same request.
issues.fix: Make this skill own KPI definition and scoring (the metric dictionary plus the scored read), and point the rhythm skill here. Drop 'hands over numbers for a read' or add 'outside a review meeting'.

issues.quote: Score every metric against its target with red/yellow/green (R/Y/G),
issues.problem: No rule turns actual-vs-target into R/Y/G, so status colours will be arbitrary and will differ from run to run.
issues.fix: Add each metric's direction (higher or lower is better) and a green/yellow/red band (for example a tolerance % set by the owner) to the metric definition, and compute the status in bash_exec.

issues.section: Call a thin sample what it is
issues.quote: Fewer than about 30 observations in the period gets a line saying the
issues.problem: A flat n<30 rule is a poor test of whether a period-over-period move is signal. It ignores the metric's own history of variation, which is the 'normal variance' the owner is supposed to know.
issues.fix: Use a process behaviour chart (XmR) on trailing periods: a move outside the natural process limits, or a run of 8 on one side, is a signal. Keep the thin-sample note for rates with small denominators.

issues.quote: and mark every target UNKNOWN.
issues.problem: Users who ask for KPIs 'with targets' get nothing usable. The skill gives no method to propose a starting target from baseline and business goal for the owner to set.
issues.fix: Allow a proposed target derived from the baseline (for example current median plus an improvement step), labeled INFERENCE and PROPOSED until the owner confirms it.

issues.section: Check coverage before you compute anything
issues.quote: Name which sources you have and which days they cover.
issues.problem: Coverage is checked but data quality and cross-source conflicts are not (duplicates, missing days, two systems disagreeing on a count).
issues.fix: Add a reconciliation step: compare the overlapping measures across sources, name the variance, pick the system of record with the owner, and label the choice.

issues.quote: Name, formula, source column, target, owner, and type — INPUT
issues.problem: The definition has no counter-metric or pairing, so speed metrics can be gamed at the expense of quality (Goodhart's law). There is also no link from each input to the output it drives.
issues.fix: Add a 'paired with' field (for example cycle time paired with rework rate) and a one-line driver link from each input to its output metric.

issues.quote: write the period's figures to the metrics
issues.problem: The metrics history file is never named or given a format, so later runs cannot reliably find it to compare against.
issues.fix: Name the file and columns (for example metrics/history.csv with period_start, period_end, metric_id, value, source, label).

scenarios.prompt: How did ops do in August? Here are exports of orders, on-time shipments and support tickets for July and August, and targets are in the Metrics tab.
scenarios.why: The steps are clear: fix the period (Aug vs Jul), check coverage (name sources and days), define each metric once, score R/Y/G, rank movers biggest miss first, decompose them against visible causes, and flag thin samples. It saves the scorecard dated. The result is a credible read, though R/Y/G bands are improvised.

scenarios.prompt: We've never tracked KPIs. Set targets for fulfilment. I have 5 weeks of data from Shopify and our 3PL portal, and they disagree on order counts.
scenarios.why: 'Check coverage' names both sources but gives no reconciliation step for conflicting counts, so the model may pick one silently. 'Mark every target UNKNOWN' leaves the user without the targets they asked for, because there is no baseline-to-proposed-target method labeled for owner approval. Five weeks falls under the rough 30-observation rule, but the skill has no week-over-week variance method.

ops-vendor-and-procurement.summary: Builds a vendor inventory from a spend source and segments it by tier, evaluates new vendors on TCO and weighted criteria with RFI/RFP/RFQ selection, works renewals inside a 90-day window, drafts SOWs and POs for Legal and the approver, and scores vendors on a tiered cadence.
strengths: TCO including switching cost, downtime risk and residual value, never sticker price alone
Choosing the instrument by purchase type (RFI, RFP or RFQ), criteria agreed before quotes, batched Q&A, negotiation only after scoring
Vendors segmented into strategic, preferred, transactional and tail, with review effort following the tier
Renewals worked inside 90 days, with the term end and notice period checked before any proposal
Every score cites an SLA or contract clause, a vendor with no SLA is flagged, and spend without outcomes is never auto-renewed
A clear boundary: draft only, SOWs to Legal, POs to the approver, no legal advice
missing: Security, privacy and DPA due diligence with a handoff to compliance
Approval thresholds and a competitive-bid policy
Merchant name normalisation and billing cadence inference from card exports
Staged renewal actions at 90/60/30 days and a missed-notice path
Negotiation levers (BATNA, multi-year vs flexibility, price caps)
Inventory, evaluation matrix and SOW templates
Concentration and single-source risk

issues.problem: New-vendor evaluation has no security, privacy or data-processing diligence (SOC 2 or ISO report, DPA, data residency, subprocessors, access to PII). That is standard for any SaaS or data-handling vendor and matters most for payroll, HR and finance tools.
issues.fix: Add a risk gate: data classification, requesting the SOC 2 report or security questionnaire, DPA status, and a handoff to the compliance teammate (Lena) for vendors touching personal or financial data.

issues.quote: The instrument flags.
issues.problem: This line is garbled. 'Three-wide' and 'the instrument flags' do not say what the third evaluation dimension is, so the model has to guess.
issues.fix: Rewrite as three explicit dimensions, for example TCO, switching cost, and risk flags (security, financial viability, concentration or single-source).

issues.quote: Agree the weighted 1-5 criteria before quotes arrive — default 35 cost,
issues.problem: Selection weights (35/30/20/15) and the ongoing scorecard weights (30/30/20/20) are two different defaults with no label for when each applies, and the selection set has no risk criterion.
issues.fix: Label them 'selection criteria' and 'performance scorecard', and add a risk or security criterion to selection.

issues.quote: Dedupe on vendor name.
issues.problem: Card and accounting exports carry merchant descriptors ('AMZN Mktp', 'AWS EMEA', 'Google *GSuite'). Deduping on the raw name leaves duplicates and splits spend.
issues.fix: Normalise merchant descriptors to a canonical vendor in bash_exec, show the mapping for confirmation, and infer billing cadence (monthly or annual) from charge history, labelled INFERENCE.

issues.quote: and the notice period before you propose anything.
issues.problem: No path covers a notice date that has already passed, and the skill skips the 60/30-day staged actions that James's renewal routine uses. It also never checks auto-renew clauses or price escalators.
issues.fix: Add 90/60/30 staging (review, negotiate, sign or exit) and a missed-notice branch (request an extension or month-to-month, document the exposure). Check auto-renew and uplift clauses.

issues.problem: There is no spend policy or approval matrix, such as the quote count by spend band, budget check, or card vs PO threshold, so 'approval-ready' is undefined.
issues.fix: Ask for or propose approval thresholds up front (for example under X on card, X-Y one quote plus approver, over Y three quotes) and include the budget line in every request.

issues.section: Draft SOWs and purchase orders from the facts
issues.quote: Scope, deliverables, term, price, and exit.
issues.problem: The SOW skeleton leaves out acceptance criteria, milestones and payment schedule, change control, and IP or data ownership, which are the clauses that cause disputes.
issues.fix: Add those fields to a shipped templates/sow.md and keep the route to Legal.

scenarios.prompt: What renews in the next 90 days? Here's our vendor sheet with contract end dates, notice periods and monthly cost.
scenarios.why: It builds the inventory (one row per vendor, owner, spend, renewal), segments by tier, and works each renewal inside 90 days: current terms, usage against commitment, SLA, and a counter as a comparison table with a draft note. It checks the notice period first, and no vendor is contacted without a yes. The model will ask for usage data it lacks and mark it UNKNOWN, which is correct.

scenarios.prompt: Pick between three payroll providers from these quotes (one is per-employee-per-month, one is flat plus per-run fees, one is a PDF). Our incumbent auto-renews in 20 days and I think we missed the 30-day notice. The CFO wants a recommendation today.
scenarios.why: The weighted criteria and TCO formula give it structure. It gives no guidance on normalising different pricing units to a common TCO basis, and nothing on a missed notice period (negotiate a short extension or month-to-month, check the auto-renew clause). Worst, the evaluation has no security or privacy due diligence for a vendor that will hold employee SSNs and bank details (SOC 1/SOC 2, DPA) and no handoff to compliance.

ops-write-an-sop.job: document a process as an SOP
ops-write-an-sop.summary: Turns notes, a transcript or a walkthrough into an SOP. It picks a checklist, hierarchical or flowchart format by the process's shape, writes the standard sections and a document-control header, gates publication on a cold-user test and owner approval, and re-verifies on a cadence and on trigger events.
strengths: The format fits the process's shape: a checklist for ten or fewer linear steps, hierarchical steps for exceptions, a flowchart for branches
Complete document control: SOP ID, approver and date, effective, last-verified and review dates, revision history. 'An unapproved SOP carries no authority'
A cold-user test before publication, and every step names who does it and what done looks like
Re-verification on a cadence and on trigger events (regulation, incident, new tools), rewriting rather than appending contradictions
Never states an unconfirmed step as fact, and never publishes without the owner's yes
missing: Searching for and updating an existing SOP before drafting a new one
RACI or swimlane for multi-role processes
A procedure for reconciling conflicting accounts
A no-secrets and redaction rule, and escalation for regulated processes
Training and acknowledgement records (who has been trained on which revision)
A shipped SOP template file and library index format
Retiring and archiving superseded versions

issues.quote: a transcript, or asks what the standard way of doing something is.
issues.problem: When the user asks what the standard way is, the skill drafts a new SOP without first searching the SOP library or wiki. That creates duplicate or contradictory SOPs and fails a plain lookup question.
issues.fix: Add a first step: search the saved SOP home and index (and the connected Notion or Drive). If an SOP exists, answer from it or update it, and draft new only when none exists.

issues.section: Say the process back in one line
issues.problem: There is no rule for when sources disagree (several people describe the process differently). A model tends to blend the accounts into a plausible-looking step.
issues.fix: List each divergence as an open decision for the owner, with who said what, and keep those steps UNKNOWN until resolved.

issues.quote: roles with one owner
issues.problem: Cross-team processes with several handoffs need a RACI or swimlane. A single owner field does not show who is consulted or informed at each step.
issues.fix: For processes with two or more roles, add a RACI table with exactly one Accountable per step, or a swimlane flow.

issues.section: Test it cold before it publishes
issues.quote: someone who has never done the task follows the draft exactly, and it
issues.problem: The model cannot run the test itself, and a small team may have no uninvolved person. There is no fallback, so the gate can block every publish.
issues.fix: Say how to arrange it (ask the owner to name a tester, using schedule_followup), with a fallback: the model walks the steps one by one with the least-experienced person and records gaps.

issues.problem: Nothing forbids putting passwords, API keys or personal data into SOP text. Transcripts of people doing a task often contain them. There is also no escalation for regulated processes.
issues.fix: Add a rule to replace secrets with a pointer to the password manager and redact personal data. SOPs in regulated areas (finance controls, health, safety) go to the compliance teammate before approval.

issues.section: Test it cold before it publishes
issues.quote: add it to the library index with owner and review
issues.problem: The library index file and its fields are never named, so later lookups and re-verification cannot find it reliably.
issues.fix: Name the index (for example sops/index.csv with id, title, owner, approver, effective, review_due, revision, link).

scenarios.prompt: Here's a transcript of Sarah doing our month-end customer invoicing in QuickBooks. Turn it into an SOP.
scenarios.why: It says the process back in one line, picks hierarchical steps for the sub-steps, and writes purpose, scope, one owner, prerequisites, definitions, numbered who/done steps, exceptions, metrics and linked systems. It adds the SOP ID, approval, effective, verified and review header with a revision table, shows the draft in chat and gates publishing on a cold-user test and the owner's yes.

scenarios.prompt: Document how we onboard new clients. Three people told me different versions (notes attached), and there's an old version in Notion already.
scenarios.why: The skill has no step to find and read the existing Notion SOP, so it may write a duplicate. It has no rule for conflicting accounts: they should be surfaced as open questions for the owner rather than merged into a guessed step. 'Never append contradictions' only covers re-verification. The INFERENCE labelling and owner-approval gate stop outright fabrication.

business-process-documentation.job: document a process as an SOP
business-process-documentation.summary: Anthropic's upstream /process-doc command. It asks the user to walk through a process and fills a markdown SOP template with RACI, flow, per-step who/when/how/output, exceptions, metrics and related docs, with optional wiki and tracker actions through placeholder connectors.
strengths: A clean reusable output template with a RACI matrix and per-step Who/When/How/Output
'Include the exceptions' tip and an exceptions table, which is often the most valuable part of an SOP
The description names concrete occasions (a process in someone's head, a handoff, an audit)
missing: An ordered procedure and an intake question list
FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN labelling and a no-invention rule
An approval gate before publishing
Document control (approver, version, revision history)
A cold-user test and trigger-based review
Harness-native tools and a fallback

issues.quote: Publish the completed SOP to your wiki
issues.problem: This is an external write with no draft review, owner approval or sign-off step, which breaks the platform's draft-then-approve rule and James's 'never publish an SOP without the owner's yes'.
issues.fix: If merged, keep ops-write-an-sop's gate: show the draft, then get the owner's yes, then publish.

issues.quote: Walk me through the process — describe it, paste existing docs, or just tell me the name and I'll ask the right questions.
issues.problem: There is no procedure: no question list, no decision points, and no instruction about steps nobody confirmed. From a bare name, the model will invent the process.
issues.fix: Drop in favour of ops-write-an-sop, which labels unwalked steps INFERENCE and keeps the SOP a draft until an owner exists.

issues.quote: /process-doc $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: A Claude Code slash command with $ARGUMENTS does nothing in AutoGPT's harness, and argument-hint is dropped.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block if kept. Better, drop the package.

issues.quote: Document a business process as a complete standard operating procedure (SOP).
issues.problem: The job is the same as ops-write-an-sop in James's kit. Loading both would compete for the same triggers and produce inconsistent SOP formats.
issues.fix: Drop. Merge the RACI table (with an exactly-one-Accountable rule) and the per-step Who/When/How/Output fields into ops-write-an-sop.

issues.quote: If **~~knowledge base** is connected:
issues.problem: The ~~category placeholders and CONNECTORS.md point at Claude plugin MCP servers (Confluence, ServiceNow, Asana, Coupa), not AutoGPT blocks. There is no fallback when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Map to the Notion, Google Docs or Linear blocks or run_mcp_tool, and fall back to a workspace file.

issues.quote: **Owner:** [Person/Team] | **Last Updated:** [Date] | **Review Cadence:** [Quarterly/Annually]
issues.problem: The header has no approver or sign-off, version or revision history, or effective and last-verified dates, so the SOP carries no authority and cannot be audited.
issues.fix: Use ops-write-an-sop's document-control header.

issues.quote: | Step | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
issues.problem: The RACI has no rule of exactly one Accountable per step and no check for steps with nobody Responsible, which are the usual RACI failure modes.
issues.fix: Add the rule 'one A per row, at least one R, flag rows that break it' when merging.

scenarios.prompt: Build a RACI and an SOP for our purchase approval process. My notes are below.
scenarios.why: The output template (RACI matrix, process flow, per-step Who/When/How/Output, exceptions table, metrics) turns decent notes into a usable, well-structured SOP draft. It lacks an approval sign-off, a version and a cold test, but the artifact itself is sound.

scenarios.prompt: Just the name: 'customer refunds'. Write the SOP and put it in our Confluence.
scenarios.why: 'I'll ask the right questions' gives no question list and no rule against inventing steps, so the model will likely write plausible fiction as fact. Confluence is a ~~knowledge base placeholder with no AutoGPT block and no fallback. 'Publish the completed SOP to your wiki' has no approval gate.

business-process-optimization.job: map and improve a slow process
business-process-optimization.summary: Anthropic's upstream process-optimization skill. It is a four-step generic framework (map the current state, identify five lean wastes, design the future state, measure impact) that asks for a before/after comparison with estimated impact and an implementation plan.
strengths: A concise, ordered framing: current state, waste, future state, impact
Useful future-state moves: parallelize independent steps, reduce handoffs, 'checkpoints (not gates)'
The description carries natural-language trigger phrases users actually say
missing: Named inputs and a fallback for missing data
A bottleneck or constraint identification method
Root-cause analysis (5 whys or fishbone)
A pilot with rollback and an approval gate before changing a live process
A control plan so the gain holds
FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN labelling of impact estimates
A deliverable template

issues.problem: There are no guardrails. Nothing requires approval before changing a live process, no pilot or rollback, and nothing labels estimates vs measurements. That conflicts with James's boundary ('never change a live process without your yes').
issues.fix: Drop. ops-map-and-improve-a-process has the process-change approver gate and the 'never present a guessed cycle time as measured' rule.

issues.quote: Produce a before/after process comparison with specific improvement recommendations, estimated impact, and an implementation plan.
issues.problem: 'Estimated impact' has no baseline requirement, calculation method or labelling, so the model will produce invented savings figures. The deliverable has no template.
issues.fix: If kept, require a measured baseline per metric, show the arithmetic, label figures FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN and ship a before/after template.

issues.quote: Analyze existing processes and recommend improvements.
issues.problem: The job is the same as ops-map-and-improve-a-process in James's kit, with near-identical triggers ('slow', 'bottleneck'), so the two would compete while this one is the weaker.
issues.fix: Drop, and fold 'parallelize independent steps' and 'checkpoints not gates' into the NICK skill's fix ladder.

issues.quote: Identify who does what and how long each step takes
issues.problem: Inputs are never named and there is no fallback when durations are unknown, so the model will fill step times with guesses.
issues.fix: Ask up front for volume, cycle time and an event log or export. Mark unknowns and name the one read that would settle each.

issues.quote: **Manual work**: Tasks that could be automated
issues.problem: The waste list is a partial, non-standard lean set (it omits defects vs rework, WIP or inventory, motion, transport and unused talent). It has no constraint or bottleneck identification even though 'bottleneck' is a trigger.
issues.fix: Use TIMWOODS plus a theory-of-constraints step (find where work queues, then measure wait vs touch time).

issues.quote: Automate where possible
issues.problem: Automation is recommended with no ROI sizing or check that it follows eliminating and simplifying, which invites automating a broken step.
issues.fix: Order the fixes kill, simplify, reorder, then automate, with effort and payback per fix, and hand automation to ops-automate-a-workflow.

issues.quote: Employee satisfaction improvement
issues.problem: The impact metrics have no baseline, owner or control period, and nothing checks that the gain holds.
issues.fix: Add a control metric with an owner and 30/60/90-day checks, as in ops-map-and-improve-a-process.

scenarios.prompt: Our invoice approval takes 12 days on average. Here's the step list and who approves each one. Streamline it.
scenarios.why: The four-step framework yields a plausible before/after with generic lean recommendations. Nothing requires a per-step wait-time baseline, a named bottleneck with evidence, a pilot or rollback, a control metric, or approval before changing the live process. 'Estimated impact' will contain unlabelled guesses.

scenarios.prompt: Hiring is too slow and I don't know where it's stuck. No data, just complaints from managers.
scenarios.why: Step 1 assumes durations are known ('how long each step takes') and gives no instruction to ask for an ATS export, mark figures UNKNOWN, or name the one measurement that would locate the constraint. Step 4 invites invented time and cost savings. Despite the 'bottleneck' trigger, the skill has no bottleneck-finding method.

predictable-revenue.job: design outbound SDR team and pipeline math
predictable-revenue.summary: A condensed Aaron Ross 'Predictable Revenue' playbook (wondelai upstream, MIT) covering role specialization, seeds/nets/spears, Cold Calling 2.0 referral emails, ANUM qualification and reverse-funnel pipeline math, with a 5-row 0-10 diagnostic score and eight long reference files (~105KB).
strengths: A coherent, faithful summary of the Predictable Revenue model: separate prospecting from closing, the seeds/nets/spears lead mix, reverse-funnel pipeline math, ANUM for SDR qualification handing off to MEDDIC.
Good progressive disclosure: each of the 8 shipped references is linked by relative path with a 'when to open' clause.
The Quick Diagnostic plus 0-10 score gives a concrete audit output, and the instruction to name the rows blocking 10/10 makes it actionable.
The references contain reusable templates: a pipeline-math spreadsheet column guide, a plan-vs-actual monthly tracker, a lead-mix gap analysis, an ANUM scoring matrix and SDR-to-AE handoff contents.
Some sound guardrails: honor opt-outs immediately, 'only reference things you actually verified' for personalization, a deliverability checklist, and compensation marked as US-only benchmarks.
missing: An intake of required inputs and time horizon, with every rate labelled as sourced from the user or assumed from a benchmark
A draft-only rule and an approval gate before any send, sequence enrolment or CRM write, with the approval logged
Current deliverability requirements (Google/Yahoo bulk-sender rules, one-click unsubscribe, spam-rate ceiling) and the unreliability of open rates
A jurisdiction check (CASL, PECR, UWG, GDPR legitimate interest) with escalation to counsel
A ramp-adjusted capacity model computed in the sandbox (bash_exec) and returned as a reusable sheet with conservative, realistic and optimistic scenarios
A named deliverable: an outbound operating plan with diagnostic score, funnel model, org and hiring plan, handoff SLA and a review cadence
Current practice: multichannel and phone, signal- and intent-based targeting, account-based outbound for enterprise ACV, and the role of AI SDR tooling
A go/no-go check on whether outbound suits the ACV and stage before recommending an SDR team
Mapping to platform integrations (HubSpot, Apollo, Smartlead, ZeroBounce blocks), with CSV or export fallback when not connected

Handoffs to teammate skills: Max's draft-a-first-touch/follow-up for copy, sales-ops-coverage-and-quota for AE capacity, sales-team-leadership for hiring, and Zara's sales-marketing-alignment-and-sla for inbound

issues.quote: 20,000 emails ≈ 2-3 SDRs (each sends 300-500/month)
issues.problem: The arithmetic is wrong. 20,000 emails at 300-500 per SDR per month is 3.3-5.6 SDR-years. At the benchmark in the same section (50-100 emails/day) it is under 2 SDRs. 200 opps at the stated 10-20 opps per SDR per month is 1-2 SDRs. The time horizon is never stated. pipeline-math.md repeats the conflicts: 6,000 emails/yr vs 15,750 standard capacity, 48,000 emails for '4 SDRs', and 4 SDRs to 6 AEs against a 2-3:1 ratio. A model copying these will give wrong headcount advice.
issues.fix: Pick one capacity figure and state the horizon (annual) and ramp. Compute the model with bash_exec, sourcing each rate from the user or marking it ASSUMPTION, and check the SDR:AE ratio against AE capacity before recommending headcount.

issues.quote: mass, personalized cold emails that generate referrals to the right person
issues.problem: The skill frames the work as mass sending, but no instruction says to draft only, get the owner's approval before any send or sequence enrolment, or log the approval. AutoGPT has Gmail, Smartlead, HubSpot and Apollo blocks that can send.
issues.fix: Add a 'Draft, never send' rule: stage sequences and contact lists as drafts, require explicit approval per send or enrolment through the platform approval flow, and record who approved what.

issues.quote: Response rate: 9-15% vs. 1-3% for traditional cold emails.
issues.problem: Benchmarks from the 2000s are presented as current fact. Typical 2025-26 cold email reply rates are low single digits, so the skill will misdiagnose healthy programs and set unreachable quotas. The open-rate subject-line table in cold-calling-2.md is also unreliable since Apple Mail Privacy Protection. The claim that 'cold calling is dead' ignores the phone's continuing role in multichannel outbound.
issues.fix: Mark the benchmarks as historical or illustrative, use the user's own actuals first, drop open-rate targets, and add current multichannel and signal-based prospecting practice.

issues.problem: The skill names no required inputs: revenue target, horizon, ACV, historical win and conversion rates, current team, ICP, lead mix. It has no ordered workflow for the model. The numbered Cold Calling 2.0 steps describe what a human SDR does, not what the assistant should produce, and there are no decision points on when to recommend outbound at all (for example ACV too low, or no product-market fit).
issues.fix: Open with an intake (ask_question for missing inputs), then ordered steps: diagnose and score, build the funnel model in three scenarios, write the org and hiring plan, hand copy to the drafting skills, and define the handoff SLA. Put a go/no-go check on outbound fit in the middle.

issues.quote: Comply with spam laws (CAN-SPAM, GDPR) and honor opt-outs immediately
issues.problem: The only legal guardrail is buried under the AE handoff step and names only two regimes. It omits CASL, UK PECR, Germany's UWG consent rule for B2B email, the GDPR legitimate-interest assessment, and the Google/Yahoo bulk-sender requirements (one-click unsubscribe, spam-rate ceiling).
