There is no escalation path.
issues.fix: Move it into a pre-send compliance check by recipient jurisdiction, list the regimes and sender requirements, and route unclear cases to the owner or counsel.

issues.quote: "cold email sequences", "sales pipeline", "SDR process"
issues.problem: Generic triggers ('sales pipeline', 'fill my pipeline', 'cold email sequences') overlap Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast, draft-a-first-touch and draft-a-follow-up, and the unassigned cold-email, outreach-playbook and prospecting skills. This 12KB framework would load for a routine pipeline review or a single email draft.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to designing or sizing an outbound sales development function and reverse-funnel headcount math, and state that copy and pipeline reviews go to the named sibling skills.

issues.quote: it walks through Salesforce, HubSpot, and other implementations with starting state, results, and failure modes
issues.problem: case-studies.md presents precise before/after metrics for anonymized firms (DataFlow, LaunchPad, Meridian, BrightPath) and an unsourced HubSpot account as if they were evidence. The Salesforce profile looks factually off: Ross's team predates the 2004 IPO, when revenue was well above $30M, and 'Market Response Reps' was the inbound team, not the SDRs. A model may cite these numbers to users as fact.
issues.fix: Label the anonymized cases as illustrative composites, cite a source for the Salesforce and HubSpot facts or remove the numbers, and tell the model not to quote case metrics as benchmarks.

issues.quote: For offer design, see hundred-million-offers. For persuasion science, see influence-psychology.
issues.problem: Neither referenced skill exists in the catalog. The 'Further Reading' links carry an Amazon affiliate tag (tag=wondelai00-20), and 'About the Author' is filler the model does not need.
issues.fix: Point to catalog skills that exist (e.g. pricing-and-packaging, positioning-and-messaging, cold-email) or remove the cross-references, and delete the affiliate-tagged Further Reading and About the Author sections.

scenarios.prompt: We're a $4M ARR B2B SaaS, ACV around $25K. The board wants $2M of new ARR next year from outbound, and right now our AEs prospect for themselves. How many SDRs do we need, and how should we set up the team?
scenarios.why: The Quick Diagnostic and Scoring sections would give a useful score (about 2-4/10, blocked on role separation and pipeline predictability). pipeline-math.md's worked example matches this case exactly: 80 deals, 320 opps, 19,400 emails, 4 SDRs and 6 AEs. But that example assumes 6,000 emails per SDR per year, while the capacity table on the same page says 15,750 (standard) and SKILL.md says 50-100 a day. It applies no ramp even though 'Ignoring ramp time' is listed as a mistake. Its 4 SDRs to 6 AEs contradicts the 2:1 ratio in roles.md and the '2-3 SDRs per AE' in SKILL.md. Nothing tells the model to ask for the company's own win rate, conversion rates or time horizon, or to label benchmark rates as assumptions. The framing would be senior-level, but the headcount answer is unreliable.

scenarios.prompt: Our outbound reply rate is about 2%, and our 3 SDRs book roughly 8 meetings a month between them. We sell ~$150K ACV to hospital groups in the US and Germany. Fix the sequence and push the new version into our Smartlead campaign. We don't have clean win-rate data.
scenarios.why: The skill's benchmarks (9-15% response, 'Poor <5%') would call a roughly normal 2026 reply rate broken and prescribe the referral-up 'Quick question' email with the Day 1/3/7/14/30 break-up cadence. That is a poor fit for enterprise healthcare buyers; multi-thread account-based outbound appears only in case study 5. The only legal guidance is 'CAN-SPAM, GDPR'. Nothing covers Germany's UWG consent requirement for B2B cold email, Google/Yahoo bulk-sender rules, or escalation to counsel. No step says to draft and get approval before loading contacts into Smartlead, and nothing handles the missing win-rate data beyond industry benchmarks.

prep-the-partner-qbr.summary: A single-file brief that grades a partner's quarter on red/yellow/green metric bands, sets a 60-90 minute agenda with the champion, stages a one-page pre-read three days out for owner approval, and drafts a recap within 24 hours.
strengths: The inputs are named up front: partner, date, joint targets, CRM, call notes, and the champion's own view.
A useful agenda shape: forecast-accuracy review by stage, repeat over- and under-promisers, registration disputes, and 'the one decision the review has to make'.
A concrete escalation rule: a two-quarter health miss triggers a 45-day improvement plan.
An evidence discipline: 'A grade with no evidence stays UNKNOWN'.
The pre-read timing (three days out, one page, numbers first) is what practitioners actually use.
missing: A two-way commitments scorecard (what we promised the partner, and whether we delivered)
Partner-reported and our-system numbers side by side, with the gap named
A review of last QBR's action items
Default metric weights and a band-to-score conversion
Where benchmarks come from and how each is labelled
Joint business plan progress check
A pack, pre-read and recap template
Memory persistence of quarterly grades for the trend
Tool routing: calendar/CRM via blocks or an export request, sandbox for the chart

issues.section: Grade the quarter before you write a word
issues.quote: Weight the metrics into one overall score, add a qualitative note per
issues.problem: No default weights, and no way to turn red/yellow/green bands into the 10-point score the improvement-plan trigger uses later, so the model will invent both.
issues.fix: Add a default weighting table (e.g. revenue/pipeline 40, win rate 15, enablement 15, MDF return 10, engagement 10, support 10), a band-to-points mapping, and an instruction to confirm the weights with the owner before the first QBR and store them in memory.

issues.section: Grade the quarter before you write a word
issues.quote: Set a benchmark per metric first, then grade against its band — red,
issues.problem: The skill doesn't say where benchmarks come from (the joint business plan, tier minimums, trailing quarters, peer partners) and doesn't require each benchmark to be labelled with its source, so benchmarks can be fabricated.
issues.fix: List the benchmark sources in priority order, require a FACT/INFERENCE label per benchmark, and ask the owner when none exists.

issues.section: Co-draft the agenda with the champion
issues.quote: 45-day review, and tier demotion if it fails.
issues.problem: The improvement plan and the demotion read as automatic consequences, and the rule sits inside the agenda section. The persona requires tier changes to be staged as drafts for the owner.
issues.fix: Move the rule to its own 'Escalation' section and say the improvement plan and any demotion are drafted with evidence for the owner's decision.

issues.section: Grade the quarter before you write a word
issues.problem: The grading is one-sided. There's no scorecard of what we owed the partner (leads passed, MDF approved, enablement delivered, registration SLA), and no rule to put the partner's reported numbers beside ours and name the gap.
issues.fix: Add a 'Two-way scorecard' step: our commitments against delivery, plus partner-reported and our-system numbers side by side with the gap named. Link sourced/influenced figures to track-partner-pipeline's proofs.

issues.section: Co-draft the agenda with the champion
issues.quote: Sixty to ninety minutes, timed, in this shape: the results snapshot;
issues.problem: The agenda doesn't open on last QBR's action items, and it has no slot for the partner's asks of us.
issues.fix: Open the agenda with a last-quarter action review (done, slipped with reason) and add a 'partner asks' block.

issues.quote: Decisions, owners, dates, and what changes in the plan because of them.
issues.problem: The recap goes to the partner but has no approval gate, and Fallbacks lacks the 'nothing goes out without your yes' line that sibling skills carry.
issues.fix: State that the recap is staged for the owner's yes before it reaches the partner, and add the standard closing gate.

issues.section: Grade the quarter before you write a word
issues.quote: metric, and chart the trend over time. A grade with no evidence stays
issues.problem: The trend needs prior quarters, but the skill never says to pull earlier QBR snapshots from memory, to save this one, or to use the sandbox for the chart.
issues.fix: Read prior QBR grades via memory_search, save this quarter's graded snapshot, and compute and chart the trend with bash_exec.

issues.quote: The graded review pack, the co-drafted agenda, the staged pre-read, and
issues.problem: The deliverables are named but have no template, so the pack's format changes from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/qbr-pack.md with a scorecard table, the agenda with timings, a one-page pre-read skeleton, and a recap/actions table.

scenarios.prompt: Our QBR with Northwind Consulting is on 14 October. Here's the HubSpot export of joint deals and our joint-targets sheet. Prep the agenda and the pre-read.
scenarios.why: With joint targets on file, the targets can serve as benchmarks. The grading bands, the timed agenda shape (results, win/loss and push/pull, forecast accuracy, issues, next-quarter targets, the one decision), the one-page pre-read gated on the owner's yes and the 24-hour recap all give a senior-looking pack. The model will still invent the metric weights, because 'Weight the metrics into one overall score' gives none.

scenarios.prompt: QBR Thursday with a reseller. They claim $1.2M sourced; our CRM shows $600K with registrations. We never set joint targets, they've looked weak for two quarters, and leadership wants them demoted.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks step does handle the missing targets: grade activity and make target-setting the first decision. But the skill says nothing on putting the partner's claimed numbers beside ours and naming the gap. The PIP rule assumes an 'agreed bar' that doesn't exist here, and 'tier demotion if it fails' is written as automatic rather than staged for the owner. The model has to fall back on persona rules the skill never points to.

run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships.job: manage sponsorship, OEM and supply partner portfolios
run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships.summary: A thin catch-all that lists what to track for sponsorship properties, OEM attach, 'agent' and supply-side partners, and a quarterly spend-versus-return reallocation draft, gated on the owner's approval.
strengths: Clear owner gates: spend with no outcome gets flagged and never auto-renewed; nothing goes out without an explicit yes.
A Legal-review flag when no contracts are on file before any renewal.
The INFERENCE label for owner-stated numbers, with feed setup as the first action.
A decisive framing for coverage gaps: a named recruit-or-drop call, not an open question.
missing: Sponsorship ROI measurement framework and rights-fee-to-activation ratio
Renewal negotiation levers (make-goods, exclusivity, opt-outs)
OEM royalty and licence models, minimum commits, true-ups, audit rights
Default bundling and SKU configuration as the primary OEM lever
A definition of 'agent ecosystem' and its metrics
A common return definition across line types
Templates for each read
Handoff to Legal on contract changes and to Max for sell-side media

issues.section: Run brand, OEM, and supply partnerships
issues.quote: Use this when the portfolio is not a resale motion. Start from the
issues.problem: The negative, catch-all trigger ('not resell') bundles sponsorship, OEM, agent and supply-side motions that share almost no method. It will fire loosely, and it blurs boundaries with own-the-alliance-pnl and Max's media-plan-measure-optimize.
issues.fix: Split into 'run sponsorship portfolio' and 'run OEM and embedded partnerships' (fold supply-side into the channel or marketplace skills), each with a positive trigger naming the motion.

issues.quote: Properties, activation plans, budgets, and the measured outcome per
issues.problem: It says 'measured outcome' but gives no measurement method, no rights-fee versus activation budget guidance, no rights inventory, and no renewal negotiation levers.
issues.fix: Add a measurement menu (leads and pipeline attributed with a window, cost per qualified lead, reach and brand lift, hospitality meetings sourced), an activation-to-rights-fee ratio check, and a renewal lever list (make-goods, category exclusivity, price hold, opt-out clause).

issues.quote: Attach rates per product line, pipeline per OEM, enablement for each
issues.problem: The OEM commercial core is missing: per-unit royalty or licence model, minimum commitments and true-ups, OEM forecast accuracy, royalty-report reconciliation and audit rights, and default bundling configuration as the main attach lever.
issues.fix: Add an OEM economics step (royalty model, minimums, true-up dates), a royalty-report reconciliation step using bash_exec on the exported or parsed reports, and a lever list (default SKU placement, seller SPIFs, co-branding, roadmap commitments).

issues.quote: The agent or supply-partner roster, the referral or attach motion per
issues.problem: 'Agent' is never defined (AI agent marketplace? insurance or travel agents?), so the model can't tell what motion this is. 'Monthly throughput read' names no metric.
issues.fix: Define the motion explicitly or drop it. If kept, name its metrics (active agents, throughput per agent, supply liquidity or fill, time to first transaction).

issues.quote: Spend against return per line, the winners to feed, the losers to exit,
issues.problem: 'Return' has no common definition across brand sponsorships and OEM revenue, so the reallocation compares incomparable lines. It also duplicates own-the-alliance-pnl's reallocation step.
issues.fix: Define return per line type with its window and attribution rule, or route cross-portfolio reallocation to own-the-alliance-pnl and keep only the line-level reads here.

issues.quote: The sponsorship read, the OEM sell-through read, the agent and supply
issues.problem: The four 'reads' have no format, sections or table columns.
issues.fix: Provide a template per read (for example, a sponsorship scorecard table: property, rights fee, activation spend, outcome metric, source, renewal date, recommendation).

issues.quote: No attach data means running from owner-stated numbers marked INFERENCE,
issues.problem: It ignores the common case where the data exists as partner PDFs or portal exports. There's no instruction to ask for the files and extract them in the sandbox.
issues.fix: Ask for the royalty or sell-through reports, parse them with bash_exec, and label the numbers FACT with the report date.

scenarios.prompt: We sponsor three industry conferences and a college esports league. The league renewal is due in 60 days at $180K. Should we renew, and on what terms?
scenarios.why: The skill says to pair spend with evidence and to flag, not auto-renew, a line with no outcome, and that gate is correct. It gives no measurement method (cost per qualified lead, pipeline influenced, audience reach and brand lift, value of the rights inventory), no rights-fee-to-activation ratio, and no renewal levers (make-goods, exclusivity, category rights, price holds). The model will improvise the actual recommendation.

scenarios.prompt: Our laptop OEM partner bundles our security suite. Attach fell from 22% to 9% after they changed the default SKU configuration. The contract has a minimum royalty guarantee, and we only get their monthly royalty reports as PDFs.
scenarios.why: 'Run OEM sell-through' only says to track attach per product line and give a stalled OEM 'one dated activation window'. There's nothing on royalty or minimum-commit mechanics, reconciling or auditing royalty reports, contract levers when a partner changes default bundling, or parsing PDF reports. The fallback ('owner-stated numbers marked INFERENCE') doesn't address data that exists but has to be extracted.

run-creator-and-affiliate-partner-progra.job: run affiliate and creator partner program
run-creator-and-affiliate-partner-progra.summary: Sets affiliate and creator commission tiers, entry vetting and fraud-vector bans in program terms, attribution and coupon-share rules, per-placement yield tracking, and a monthly program-health read, all gated on the owner's approval.
strengths: A concrete fraud-vector list: brand bidding, typosquats, cookie stuffing, self-referral, sub-affiliate layering.
Program terms ban each vector before activation, with clawback.
The attribution spine is stated explicitly, including a payout lock at least as long as the refund window.
Coupon-share thresholds are clearly labelled as rules of thumb.
'A trend names its window before its number' and payout rules name their data source.
A clear owner gate on compensation changes, payouts and removals.
missing: Commission rates derived from margin, allowable CPA or LTV
Advertiser-side metrics (EPC, ROAS, AOV, new-customer share, reversal rate)
Incrementality and holdout testing; channel dedupe
FTC/ASA disclosure standards and Legal review of the terms
Tax and KYC onboarding before payouts
Creator contract terms: usage rights, whitelisting, exclusivity, deliverables
Revenue concentration risk
Templates for the sheet, log and report

issues.quote: Track cost per click, fill, click-through rate, and effective cost per
issues.problem: Fill rate and eCPM are publisher-side ad-monetisation metrics, mixed into what is otherwise a brand's affiliate program. The metrics an advertiser actually runs on are missing: EPC, CPA against allowable CPA, ROAS, AOV, new-customer share.
issues.fix: Split the metrics by perspective: advertiser (EPC, CPA vs target, ROAS, AOV, new-customer rate, reversal rate) and, only when we are the publisher or network, fill and eCPM.

issues.quote: Tiers with earn bars, commission rates, bonus triggers, and loyalty
issues.problem: Commission rates aren't anchored to gross margin, allowable CPA or LTV. The flat-fee plus performance hybrid, usage rights and whitelisting terms common in creator deals aren't covered.
issues.fix: Require margin and target CPA as inputs, derive the rate ceiling in the sandbox, and add creator deal structures (flat plus CPA, usage-rights term, exclusivity window).

issues.quote: brand-bidding ban, coupon and code rules, a self-referral ban, disclosure
issues.problem: Disclosure is named with no regulatory frame (FTC Endorsement Guides, UK ASA/CMA, EU UCPD) and no Legal routing. Payouts need tax onboarding (W-9/W-8BEN, 1099) and none is mentioned.
issues.fix: Add a compliance step: the disclosure standard per market, a Legal review of the program terms, tax and KYC onboarding before the first payout, and a privacy note on creator personal data.

issues.quote: The attribution spine: last affiliate click wins; a 30-day cookie that is
issues.problem: Last-click is presented as the universal default, with no incrementality or holdout testing, no dedupe against paid search and other channels, and no new-versus-returning customer rule. These are the main levers against paying for sales that would have happened anyway.
issues.fix: Add dedupe rules against owned and paid channels, a new-customer commission differential, and a periodic holdout or incrementality test for the top partners.

issues.quote: A flagged creator pauses payouts first. Removal needs the owner's yes.
issues.problem: Pausing a contracted payout is itself a financial and contractual action, but here it happens before any owner decision.
issues.fix: Stage the payout hold as a recommendation with its evidence, for the owner's yes, and check the contract's hold or clawback clause first.

issues.quote: Active creators, revenue per creator, payout ratio, fraud and safety
issues.problem: The health read omits concentration risk (top-N revenue share), activation rate (the share of recruits who ever convert) and EPC trend.
issues.fix: Add concentration, activation rate and EPC to the monthly read.

issues.quote: No platform data means running from owner-pasted exports marked with
issues.problem: No tool routing: the affiliate networks (Impact, PartnerStack, CJ, Awin) have no block, and the skill doesn't say to use bash_exec for the tier and yield math.
issues.fix: Ask for the network CSV export by name, run the calculations in bash_exec, and store the tier sheet as a workspace file.

issues.quote: The compensation sheet, the vetting and safety log, the yield read, and
issues.problem: No templates or column definitions for the four deliverables.
issues.fix: Ship templates: a commission sheet (tier, bar, rate, bonus, data source), a vetting log (creator, check, result, evidence, date), and a monthly health report.

scenarios.prompt: Design a three-tier commission structure for our 400 affiliates on Impact. The top 20 drive 70% of revenue, and coupon sites are 45% of orders.
scenarios.why: It flags that 45% coupon share means 'cannibalising rather than acquiring' and says the middle tier must be reachable. But it never asks for gross margin, allowable CPA or LTV, so the commission rates the model proposes will be ungrounded. It also doesn't treat the top-20 concentration as a risk.

scenarios.prompt: A creator we pay $5K a month flat plus 10% looks like they bought followers and are brand-bidding on our name. We only have a CSV of clicks and orders, no API. They've delivered 3 of 6 posts under contract.
scenarios.why: The skill names brand bidding as a vector, says to pause payouts, and requires the owner's yes before removal. It gives no evidence standard (SERP ad screenshots, follower-audit signals), nothing on flat-fee contract obligations or clawback enforceability mid-contract, and no Legal routing. It also has pausing payouts happen before any owner decision, which could itself breach the contract.

run-global-partner-executive-councils.summary: Charters a bilateral executive council (roster, decision rights, cadence, board line), runs regional lead-ins into a global session on one scorecard, preps board-style packs with a 24-hour recap, and keeps an open-decisions log between sessions.
strengths: A complete charter checklist that includes decision rights and an escalation bar into the council.
A hard gate that makes executive sponsorship real: no named sponsor per side, no meeting.
'No region re-litigates its numbers live': regional reads roll into the global pack.
Strong follow-through: an open-decisions log with owners and dates, a mid-cycle nudge, and undone items carried forward with their reason.
Per-metric bands instead of one global red/yellow/green default.
missing: An antitrust and confidentiality guardrail for multi-partner councils
A multi-partner advisory council variant (seat rotation, NDA, partner-feedback loop into the program)
Named scorecard metrics
Templates for the charter, pack and decisions log
A persistence mechanism for the decisions log
A recovery step for missing prior minutes
A clear boundary against the alliance steering and QBR skills

issues.problem: There's no competition-law guardrail. When competing partners sit on one council, pricing, margin, territory and customer-allocation talk is an antitrust risk. Senior programs use counsel-reviewed agendas, an antitrust statement read at the start, and reviewed minutes.
issues.fix: Add a rule: for any multi-partner council, Legal reviews the agenda and minutes, an antitrust reminder opens each session, and pricing, margin and territory topics are excluded.

issues.quote: One charter document, both sides signed, with a periodic charter-review
issues.problem: It assumes a bilateral alliance forum and never covers the multi-partner Partner Advisory Council format, which is the more common meaning of 'partner executive council'.
issues.fix: Add a first decision point: bilateral alliance council or multi-partner advisory council. Give each its own charter variant (signatories, seat rotation, confidentiality/NDA).

issues.section: Prep each session like a board read
issues.quote: A champion co-drafted agenda, the pre-read to members three business days
issues.problem: The pack, pre-read and recap mechanics repeat prep-the-partner-qbr and govern-the-strategic-alliance's steering pack, and run-partner-strategy-and-operations also runs per-alliance steering committees. Trigger boundaries blur.
issues.fix: State the boundary in the intro (multi-region or multi-alliance executive forum only; a single alliance's steering goes to govern-the-strategic-alliance) and reference the QBR skill's grading rather than restating it.

issues.quote: reviewed define-measure-analyze-improve-control style, and per-metric
issues.problem: 'DMAIC style' is jargon with no operational meaning here, and the shared scorecard's metrics are never named.
issues.fix: Replace it with a concrete scorecard definition: 5-7 named metrics with owners and sources, plus a qualitative health line.

issues.quote: An open-decisions log with an owner and a due date per item. A mid-cycle
issues.problem: The skill doesn't say where the log lives or how the mid-cycle nudge fires, so continuity across sessions isn't guaranteed.
issues.fix: Keep the log as a workspace file or a Sheet via run_block, save a summary with memory_store, and use schedule_followup for the mid-cycle nudge.

issues.quote: The signed charter, the regional-to-global cadence, the session pack with
issues.problem: The skill can only produce a charter draft, not a signed one. There are no templates for the charter, pack or log.
issues.fix: Rename it to 'charter draft for signature' and ship templates/charter.md, templates/session-pack.md and templates/decisions-log.csv.

issues.quote: A council with no named sponsor per side does not meet until it has one.
issues.problem: This hard block can stall an existing council over a vacancy. It should be flagged for the owner, not enforced silently.
issues.fix: Turn it into a flag with a sponsor-ask draft and let the owner decide whether the session runs.

issues.quote: Revisit council composition annually, and map the handoffs at each
issues.problem: Alliance-lifecycle handoffs (deal to execution to scale to exit) are out of scope for a council skill and belong to lifecycle skills.
issues.fix: Drop the line or route it to plan-the-multi-year-partnership or manage-partner-renewals-and-exits.

scenarios.prompt: Draft the charter for a quarterly executive council with our Microsoft alliance, with regional lead-ins from NA, EMEA and APAC, and prep the first session pack. Here are last quarter's metrics.
scenarios.why: The charter checklist (purpose, sponsors per side and per region, decision rights, cadence, comms plan, minutes, board line, escalation bar), the no-re-litigating rule for regional reads, the value/gaps/roadmap/asks pack, pre-read three business days out, and 24-hour recap produce a credible charter draft and pack. The owner's approval is gated.

scenarios.prompt: Our partner advisory council brings together our 8 top resellers, some of whom compete, twice a year. The next one is in 3 weeks, last session's minutes are missing, and two partner sponsors have left. Prep it.
scenarios.why: The skill's 'both sides signed' model doesn't fit a multi-party council, and 'does not meet until it has one' would wrongly block the session over two vacant seats. Nothing warns against competitors discussing pricing, margins or territories (antitrust). The missing minutes get no recovery step beyond 'where they exist'.

run-hyperscaler-marketplace-co-sell.job: run cloud marketplace co-sell with hyperscalers
run-hyperscaler-marketplace-co-sell.summary: Runs the partner side of an AWS, Azure or Google Cloud marketplace motion: an ordered listing and private-offer checklist, co-sell registration and validation-state tracking, field-team pairing, a fund-capture table, and proof-based pipeline attribution.
strengths: A clear boundary: 'This is the partner side only. Deal execution stays with sales.'
Anti-staleness: program clocks change yearly, so read and cite the current guide rather than carrying remembered numbers.
'A listing with no co-sell registration behind it is visibility, not pipeline.'
The fund-capture table columns are specified (amount, owner, claim window, claim date, proof), with a 90-day expiry rescue.
The attribution proof rule (offer, registration or co-sell record ID) and an unproven list that never pads the headline.
missing: An approval gate on co-sell registration
Channel partner private offers (CPPO)
Commit-drawdown eligibility checks
Marketplace fee modelling
Program tiers and incentive eligibility per cloud
A named handoff to Max for deal execution
Tool routing for program guides and portal exports
Templates for the checklist state and fund table

issues.quote: Register the motion in the hyperscaler's co-sell system before
issues.problem: The skill tells the model to register co-sell with no approval gate. The closing gate covers only offer terms and fund claims, while the persona forbids registering deals without the owner's yes.
issues.fix: Stage the registration as a draft (fields filled, rule cited) for the owner's yes, and add 'no registration' to the closing gate.

issues.quote: Track the validation states — Pending, Approved, Review Pending, Action
issues.problem: Program-specific validation states and fields (tenant type, solution value) are presented as generic, without saying which hyperscaler they belong to. That contradicts the skill's own 'cite the rule' instruction, and they'll be wrong for other clouds.
issues.fix: Label each state and field set by program (AWS ACE, Microsoft Partner Center, Google Cloud Partner Network), or say to read them from the current guide.

issues.quote: Keep the one-exception-per-referral appeal path ready with its
issues.problem: This is an unsourced, possibly program-specific or invented rule that the model will present as fact.
issues.fix: Remove it, or rephrase as 'check the current guide for the appeal or exception path and cite it'.

issues.problem: Core partner-side mechanics are missing: channel partner private offers, whether a purchase draws down the buyer's commit (MACC/EDP/Google), marketplace listing fees, and program tiers and incentive eligibility (e.g. ISV Accelerate, Azure IP co-sell, Partner Advantage).
issues.fix: Add a program-eligibility step (tier, incentive eligibility, drawdown eligibility, CPPO path, fee), each read from the current guide and cited.

issues.quote: This is the partner side only. Deal execution stays with sales.
issues.problem: The boundary names no handoff, and the checklist text nearly duplicates Max's cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling.
issues.fix: Name the handoff: deal vehicle, burn-down and MEDDPICC go to Max's cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling via handoff_to_expert, with a brief. Share the checklist rather than keeping two copies.

issues.quote: field contact means working the partner-development representative first,
issues.problem: Non-standard role name. Hyperscalers use Partner Development Manager (PDM) and partner or co-sell solution architects.
issues.fix: Use the standard role names per cloud.

issues.quote: qualify — and they change yearly, so read the current program guide for
issues.problem: No tool path: ACE, Partner Center and the Google partner portal have no block. The skill doesn't say to use web_fetch for the guide or to ask for a pipeline or offer export.
issues.fix: Say: web_search/web_fetch the current program guide and cite its URL and date; ask for the ACE or Partner Center export as CSV; build the tables in bash_exec.

scenarios.prompt: We just went transactable on AWS Marketplace. Walk me through getting our first private offer to Acme out, registering co-sell with AWS, and using the $50K of POC funds we have this quarter.
scenarios.why: The ordered checklist (live offer, terms match, duration covers procurement, acceptance owner and date), the register-before-offer rule with an instruction to cite the current program guide, the fund line with a claim window and proof, and the proof-based attribution give a solid partner-side plan. It relies on the model fetching the current guide, which is implied but not tool-routed.

scenarios.prompt: The customer wants to buy through Azure Marketplace via their reseller and burn down their MACC. Our co-sell referral shows 'Action required', it's five months after signature, and our Microsoft partner manager just left.
scenarios.why: The skill covers the validation-state tracking, the appeal path and the 'no field contact' fallback. It has nothing on channel partner private offers or MACC-eligibility checks, which decide this deal, and it doesn't hand off to Max's cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling. The 'one-exception-per-referral' rule it cites may not apply to Microsoft at all.

run-partner-strategy-and-operations.job: plan partnerships annual strategy and operations
run-partner-strategy-and-operations.summary: Gives the partnerships org an operating layer: per-partner invest/divest/hold calls, tier revenue targets and capacity sizing, a sourced/influenced revenue model with ecosystem-led growth metrics, OKRs, a rhythm of business, and system-of-record plumbing.
strengths: 'A bet with no capacity line is a wish, not a plan': capacity is tied to each invest bet.
Invest bets are scored on both quantitative and qualitative evidence, including account-mapping status.
Current ecosystem-led growth metrics (sourced revenue and pipeline, co-sell win rate against baseline, deal size, cycle time).
Every forum names its owner, its inputs and the one decision it exists to make.
'Fix the feed before arguing about the number': a system of record and owner per metric.
missing: Partner segmentation and invest/divest criteria
A capacity-sizing method and default productivity ratios
Base, stretch and downside scenarios and budget-cut trade-offs
Reconciling conflicting sources (show both, name the gap)
A planning timeline aligned to the fiscal calendar (when targets lock)
Partner-manager compensation and quota design (sourced vs influenced)
Templates for the plan and model
Routing to own-the-alliance-pnl and set-board-level-alliance-strategy

issues.quote: Draft an invest, divest, or hold call per partner with one line of
issues.problem: No segmentation or thresholds for the call, and one line of evidence is thin for a divest that ends a relationship.
issues.fix: Add a segmentation step (strategic, growth, long tail) and explicit invest/hold/divest criteria (e.g. trailing sourced revenue, pipeline trend, capability score, strategic fit), with a fuller evidence block for any divest.

issues.quote: evidence each. Set the revenue target per tier. Size the capacity — heads,
issues.problem: No capacity-sizing method, so headcount, MDF and SE hours will be invented.
issues.fix: Give default productivity ratios for the owner to confirm (partners per manager by tier, sourced revenue per manager, MDF as a % of the influenced target, SE hours per co-sell deal) and compute the capacity in bash_exec.

issues.section: Set the objectives and the rhythm of business
issues.quote: Per strategic alliance, pair an executive sponsor on each side and run a
issues.problem: Per-alliance steering committees are owned by govern-the-strategic-alliance, plan-the-multi-year-partnership and the executive-council skill. Restating them here blurs triggers and invites conflicting guidance.
issues.fix: Replace it with a one-line route: per-alliance governance goes to govern-the-strategic-alliance, and multi-region forums to run-global-partner-executive-councils.

issues.section: Build the revenue and capacity model
issues.quote: against baseline, deal size, and cycle time — with a percentage influence
issues.problem: 'Percentage influence attribution per partner' is undefined, may conflict with the persona's two-bucket rule, and overlaps own-the-alliance-pnl's attribution models.
issues.fix: State that influence percentages split credit across partners inside one bucket and sum to 100% per deal, and defer the attribution model to track-partner-pipeline and own-the-alliance-pnl.

issues.section: Build the revenue and capacity model
issues.problem: No base, stretch or downside scenarios and no budget-constraint trade-offs, which are the core of an annual plan. No model template or sandbox use either.
issues.fix: Add a scenario step (three cases with their assumptions at the top) and ship templates/partner-plan-model.csv, computed in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Include the account-mapping feed and a no-naked-deals coverage norm, so
issues.problem: 'No naked deals' is unexplained vendor jargon, and account-mapping tools have no block. There's no fallback.
issues.fix: Define the norm (every key open deal has at least one mapped partner touch logged) and fall back to an owner-provided overlap export.

issues.quote: Run a bilateral executive health-check survey with each strategic partner
issues.problem: The survey goes to partners, but the closing gate covers only plans, targets and calls, not surveys.
issues.fix: Draft the survey and stage it for the owner's yes before it reaches any partner.

issues.quote: The annual plan with its invest and divest calls, the revenue and
issues.problem: No template or format for the plan, model, objective set or calendar.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the plan (per-partner call table), the model, the OKR set and the rhythm-of-business calendar.

scenarios.prompt: Build our FY27 partnerships plan: 40 partners, $4M partner-sourced last year, 5 partner managers, and a target of $6.5M sourced. Which partners do we invest in, and what capacity do we need?
scenarios.why: The skill produces the right artefacts: a per-partner call with evidence, a target per tier, capacity per bet, the model with sources, OKRs and a rhythm. But 'Size the capacity' gives no method (partners per manager by tier, sourced revenue per manager, SE hours per co-sell deal), so the model will invent ratios. There are no base, stretch or downside scenarios.

scenarios.prompt: Leadership wants a 30% cut to the partner budget. Our data is split between Salesforce and a PRM nobody maintains, the two disagree on partner-sourced revenue, and the board meets in three weeks.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks and 'Fix the feed before arguing about the number' steps help: owner numbers marked INFERENCE, and a system of record per metric. There's no step for reconciling two conflicting sources (show both, name the gap), no budget-constraint scenario or divest ranking, and no routing to own-the-alliance-pnl or set-board-level-alliance-strategy for the board read.

model-the-partnership-commercials.job: model partnership business case and deal P&L
model-the-partnership-commercials.summary: A 55-line outline that lists what a partnership business case, deal P&L with base/low/high sensitivity, guardrail bands and reusable templates should contain, but gives no model structure, formulas or templates.
strengths: Every load-bearing number carries FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN with its source, and it never invents a number.
Requires a break-even line ('A range without a break-even is a vibe, not a model').
Anything outside a band becomes an exception draft for the owner, never a quiet yes.
Missing volume data is named with the report or contact that fills it, not estimated into place.
missing: Cost-to-serve lines (partner manager time, SE hours, enablement, MDF)
Incrementality and cannibalisation against direct sales
Partner-side economics (their margin stack, services attach, profitability)
Per-model revenue formulas (referral fee, reseller discount, marketplace fee, MSP/SI)
NPV/payback definition and a go/no-go threshold
A way to value exclusivity
Payment timing, clawbacks and FX
Spreadsheet or CSV template and a worked example
bash_exec script for sensitivity and break-even
Finance review gate and handoff to structure-the-partner-agreement

issues.section: Model the deal profit and loss
issues.quote: Fees, margins, revenue share, payout triggers, and marketplace fees where
issues.problem: Only revenue and payout mechanics are listed. There is no cost-to-serve (partner manager time, SE hours, enablement, MDF), no incrementality or cannibalisation against direct, and no partner-side P&L, so the 'profit' can't be computed and the model can't show whether the deal is worth it to either side.
issues.fix: Add a two-sided P&L template: our revenue by agreement model, partner payouts, cost-to-serve lines, an incrementality haircut, and the partner's margin and services attach. Compute sensitivity and break-even in bash_exec.

issues.quote: The business case, the profit-and-loss model with its sensitivity, the
issues.problem: No format for any deliverable: no table columns, no sensitivity-grid layout, no business-case sections, no band table. The skill promises 'reusable templates' but ships none, so output changes every run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/business-case.md, templates/deal-pnl.csv (base/low/high columns plus a break-even row), templates/guardrail-bands.md, and one worked example.

issues.quote: Revenue-share bands, MDF caps, discount floors, and the
issues.problem: Nearly verbatim duplicate of own-the-alliance-pnl's 'Set the guardrail bands', and it overlaps design-the-partner-program's incentive bands and Daniel's deal-economics-and-pricing-guardrails. The deal model re-derives bands instead of inheriting the portfolio bands that own-the-alliance-pnl says it saves for deal-level skills.
issues.fix: Read the saved portfolio bands first (memory_search or the workspace file) and propose only deal-level exceptions. Consult Daniel for margin floors.

issues.quote: means wider bands, and you say so.
issues.problem: Ambiguous and possibly backwards. If 'bands' means guardrail bands, widening them without precedent loosens approval controls exactly when risk is highest.
issues.fix: Widen the sensitivity range instead. Keep guardrail bands provisional and conservative until the owner and Finance ratify them.

issues.quote: Upside, cost, payback window, and the top three risks. Every load-bearing
issues.problem: No method: no payback or NPV definition, no comparison with direct sales or doing nothing, no go/no-go threshold, and the break-even variable is never specified.
issues.fix: Define payback months and break-even volume, compare against direct CAC, and state the decision threshold up front.

issues.quote: from, and score the portfolio on one prioritisation card — potential,
issues.problem: Portfolio prioritisation is scope creep; it belongs to run-partner-strategy-and-operations or own-the-alliance-pnl. The card also has no scale, weights or evidence rule.
issues.fix: Drop it, or define 1-5 scales with evidence and route portfolio calls to the strategy skill.

issues.quote: Turn the modelled terms into deal templates the next partnership starts
issues.problem: No persistence mechanism is named. On the platform the template disappears unless it is written to the workspace or to memory.
issues.fix: Write the template with write_workspace_file, memory_store a pointer to it, and log the version and date.

issues.quote: Every number here is a draft. Committed terms need your explicit yes.
issues.problem: No Finance review of cost and margin inputs, and no handoff to structure-the-partner-agreement when the numbers turn into a term sheet.
issues.fix: Add Finance sign-off before any number enters a term sheet, and route to structure-the-partner-agreement.

scenarios.prompt: We're about to sign Brightline as a reseller at 25% margin. They forecast 40 deals a year at $30k ACV. Build the business case and the deal P&L with sensitivity, and tell me the break-even.
scenarios.why: 'Model the deal profit and loss' gets the model to produce revenue, margin and a base/low/high volume table with a break-even. The skill never asks for cost-to-serve (partner manager time, SE hours, enablement, MDF) or an incrementality haircut against direct, so profit and break-even rest only on revenue-side lines. With no template, the layout is improvised each run.

scenarios.prompt: Finance hasn't given me any cost numbers. The partner wants a 30% revenue share, $50k MDF and DACH exclusivity, and our usual band is 15-20%. Is this worth doing?
scenarios.why: Fallbacks leave missing inputs blank, and 'Set the guardrail bands' turns the 30% into an exception draft, which is correct. With costs blank the break-even can't be solved, and the skill gives no way to still produce a useful read (solve for break-even volume, ask_question for cost-to-serve). Exclusivity is never valued, and 'No precedent deals means wider bands' may loosen controls.

onboard-and-enable-partners.summary: Runs a newly signed partner through a kickoff within five business days, a dated 30/60/90 arc with month-6 and month-12 checks, an enablement kit tiered by model, one dated first co-marketing item, and 30-day health checks.
strengths: Dated arc with a five-business-day start, a month-6 'without training wheels' check and a month-12 revisit.
Concrete kit contents: three qualifying questions with exact wording, top objections with answers, a Legal-reviewed battle card.
Only certified sellers lead co-sell, and every artefact carries an owner and a refresh date.
An undated idea stays a backlog line, and each health-check miss gets a dated rescue line with an owner.
missing: Time-to-first-deal and time-to-certification KPIs
Internal enablement of our own AEs/CSMs (rules of engagement, champion)
Per-model kit matrix for co-sell and MSP/SI
Demo or NFR licences and a sandbox for technical partners
Incentives or SPIFs for the partner's sellers
Kickoff agenda and JBP templates
Deal-registration and PRM walkthrough in the first 30 days
Day-90 handoff to run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence and build-partner-academies-at-scale

issues.section: Stand up the kit, tiered by model
issues.quote: A reseller gets the full playbook; a referral partner gets a one-pager.
issues.problem: Only two of the persona's four agreement models are tiered. Co-sell and MSP/SI partners need technical certification, demo or NFR environments and delivery-readiness checks, and get no kit definition.
issues.fix: Add a per-model kit matrix (referral, reseller, co-sell, MSP/SI) listing the required items and the certification bar for each.

issues.section: Stand up the kit, tiered by model
issues.problem: No internal enablement. Our own AEs and CSMs are never briefed on the new partner (rules of engagement, when to bring them in, how deal registration works), which is a common reason new partnerships produce no first deal.
issues.fix: Add an internal-field enablement step: a rules-of-engagement one-pager, a named internal champion and a field announcement draft.

issues.quote: Then set the arc and file it where the owner actually looks:
issues.problem: No tool or approval path. Filing milestones, sending calendar invites and provisioning portal access are external side effects with no draft-first gate at this step, and 'where the owner actually looks' is undefined.
issues.fix: ask_question for the system of record. Draft Calendar, Docs, Notion or Linear items via run_block pending approval, and memory_store the arc so the health checks and weekly pulse can find it.

issues.section: Stand up the kit, tiered by model
issues.quote: Foundation passes at 80, Pro at 85, Expert at 90
issues.problem: Program-level certification policy is stated as fixed fact inside a single-partner skill, and it can conflict with design-the-partner-program and build-partner-academies-at-scale, which own the bars.
issues.fix: Read the program's certification bars if they are on file. Otherwise label these as suggested defaults for the owner to confirm.

issues.quote: Check the MDF fiscal-year expiry, and reallocate unspent or
issues.problem: Quarterly MDF reallocation is portfolio work, repeated nearly word for word in design-the-partner-program and run-the-partner-marketing-engine. It is out of scope for a first motion, and there is no no-budget fallback.
issues.fix: Keep the fiscal-year expiry check, route reallocation to program design, and add an organic-only fallback.

issues.quote: kickoff: a timed two-hour agenda covering introductions, goals, access,
issues.problem: Promises a timed agenda but gives no timings or template. The joint business plan is described but not shipped either.
issues.fix: Ship templates/kickoff-agenda.md with timed blocks and templates/joint-business-plan.md.

issues.section: Stand up the kit, tiered by model
issues.quote: return-on-investment calculator, case studies, an FAQ, a security pack,
issues.problem: The security pack, roadmap material and competitive battle card are confidential, and nothing checks that an NDA or confidentiality clause covers them before they are shared.
issues.fix: Gate confidential artefacts on confirming the NDA and on Legal/Security sign-off.

issues.quote: One owner on each side. Every milestone dated.
issues.problem: No fallback when the partner has no named owner or sponsor, so the arc proceeds without one.
issues.fix: Pause the arc and draft an owner/sponsor ask; the day-30 health check escalates if the gap is still open.

scenarios.prompt: We signed Brightline as a reseller last Friday. Set up their onboarding and enablement.
scenarios.why: The kickoff inside five business days, the dated 0-30/31-60/61-90 arc, the month-6 independence check, the full reseller kit list, a dated first co-marketing item and the 30-day health checks together give a senior-quality plan. Only the timed agenda and the JBP skeleton have to be improvised.

scenarios.prompt: We just signed a co-sell agreement with a GSI. They have no portal access, their sponsor left last week, we have no MDF budget, and they want a joint webinar next month.
scenarios.why: The fallback covers the missing portal (documents and live sessions). But kit tiering defines only reseller and referral, so the GSI/co-sell kit is guessed. 'One owner on each side' has no fallback for the departed sponsor, there is no no-MDF path for the webinar, and briefing our own sellers for co-sell is never mentioned.

orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids.job: orchestrate multi-party teaming and joint bids
orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids.summary: Outlines tri-party orchestration (party map, decision rights, workstream owners), coopetition guardrails with a sell-to/with/through model, a one-line teaming and bid plan with a red team, and a generic AI delivery gate.
strengths: Pause rules with teeth: a workstream with no owner pauses, and a party that won't acknowledge the guardrails pauses joint work.
Names the transaction model per workstream (selling to, with or through) and who leads it.
A regulated frame takes precedence, with these mechanics running inside it.
A teaming spine drafted from stated intent is marked INFERENCE and goes to Legal first.
missing: Bid/no-bid gate with Pwin
Prime/sub decision and workshare split
Compliance matrix and colour-team reviews
Three-way NDA and a competition-law clean-team protocol
Price-to-win and a single-price roll-up method
Credit and attribution split across parties
Customer-relationship owner
Post-award handoff to assure-partner-led-delivery
Templates and a worked example

issues.quote: Where the parties compete and where they cooperate, the information
issues.problem: No competition-law check. Teaming with a competitor invites exchange of pricing, discounts, customer allocation and bid intent, which is antitrust exposure. Information barriers are named, but there is no clean-team protocol, no counsel review and no NDA precondition.
issues.fix: Require a three-way NDA and Legal/competition-counsel review before any exchange, plus clean-team rules listing what is never shared (pricing, margins, other bids, customer lists).

issues.section: Run the bid or the build
issues.quote: The shaping plan, the teaming agreement spine (scope split, pricing,
issues.problem: The bid mechanics the skill is named for are one sentence: no bid/no-bid gate with Pwin, no prime/sub or workshare decision, no compliance matrix, win themes or price-to-win, and no exclusivity or non-solicit terms in the teaming agreement.
issues.fix: Add ordered steps: bid/no-bid with criteria, the prime/sub call, workshare percentages, a compliance matrix, colour-team reviews, a pricing roll-up and a submission gate.

issues.quote: The orchestration map, the guardrails document, the bid or build plan
issues.problem: No templates for the map (decision-rights/RACI grid), the guardrails document or the teaming term list, so the output shape varies each run.
issues.fix: Ship a template for each deliverable plus one worked tri-party example.

issues.section: Hold the AI line where it applies
issues.quote: Intellectual property, safety, and delivery guardrails for AI work, with
issues.problem: A grafted, generic AI section with no concrete content: which IP, whose data, what review gate. Its 'AI delivery guardrails' trigger also pulls non-multi-party AI requests into a bid skill.
issues.fix: Move it to assure-partner-led-delivery, or make it specific (IP ownership of outputs, client data use and training rights, human review gate), and drop the trigger.

issues.section: Run the bid or the build
issues.quote: the milestone dates, and a red-team review before
issues.problem: The red team has no criteria, reviewer independence or timing, and there is no handoff to Max's rfp-and-competitive-bid-response, which owns writing the proposal.
issues.fix: Define review criteria and timing, and consult or delegate the response document to Max.

issues.quote: a single-threaded owner per workstream.
issues.problem: No overall capture lead or prime, no named owner of the customer relationship (which the persona requires every agreement to name), and no credit split across parties.
issues.fix: Add the prime/capture lead, the customer-relationship owner, and a credit split under the persona's multi-partner rule.

issues.quote: No bilateral terms on file means drafting the teaming spine from
issues.problem: The compressed-deadline case (submission due in days, no terms in place) is not handled, and there is no split between what must be signed before submission and what can follow award.
issues.fix: Define the minimum pre-submission set (NDA, teaming letter of intent, workshare) and the post-award items.

scenarios.prompt: We're teaming with a consulting firm and a data-platform vendor on a retail bank's data modernisation deal. Map the roles and draft the teaming spine.
scenarios.why: It produces an orchestration map with decision rights and owners, coopetition guardrails and a sell-to/with/through model. 'Run the bid or the build' gives no bid/no-bid, prime/sub or workshare decision, compliance matrix or win themes, and the red team has no criteria.

scenarios.prompt: The client wants one price from us and our competitor Vendor X on a tri-party bid due in 9 days. X's team keeps asking for our discount levels, and we have no bilateral terms.
scenarios.why: Information barriers and 'Legal review first' point the right way. But nothing says pricing or discount exchange between competitors is off-limits, nothing explains how to assemble one price (clean team, client-side roll-up), and nothing triages what must be signed before a 9-day submission.

own-the-alliance-pnl.job: run quarterly alliance P&L close and reallocation
own-the-alliance-pnl.summary: Builds a rolled-up alliance P&L, runs the quarterly close against plan with a reallocation draft and fund-or-exit calls, sets portfolio guardrail bands, and writes a half-page quarterly read with partner-vs-direct comparators.
strengths: Inputs named up front, including the fiscal calendar, the attribution model and the claim window in force.
A line that misses two quarters running gets a fund-or-exit call with its evidence.
Partner-vs-direct comparators (cycle velocity, deal size, retention/LTV) and attach rate in the quarterly read.
One number feeds the board and council packs, so every forum quotes the same figure.
Reallocations and guardrail changes are drafts gated on the owner's yes.
missing: Partner payout cost lines (referral fees, reseller margin, rebates, marketplace fees)
Contribution margin per alliance
Incrementality or holdout view of partner revenue
Reconciliation of CRM bookings to finance-recognised revenue
Partner-reported vs our numbers side by side
Handling of duplicate partner claims
P&L and quarterly-read templates with a worked example
Named persistence for guardrail bands

issues.section: Build the rolled-up profit and loss
issues.quote: Revenue lines: ecosystem-sourced revenue, influenced pipeline value,
issues.problem: Influenced pipeline value is not revenue. Putting it on a revenue line inflates the P&L and double-counts once that pipeline closes.
issues.fix: Revenue means recognised or booked revenue only. Carry influenced pipeline as a memo KPI below the P&L.

issues.section: Build the rolled-up profit and loss
issues.quote: (MDF) and co-marketing spend, alliance heads, sales-engineering hours,
issues.problem: Cost lines leave out partner payouts (referral fees, reseller discounts or margins, rebates, SPIFs, marketplace fees, revenue share paid out), often the largest alliance cost. Profit and partner return are overstated.
issues.fix: Add payout lines per agreement model and report contribution margin per alliance.

issues.section: Build the rolled-up profit and loss
issues.quote: last-touch, multi-touch, or influence-based — inside an explicit 90-day
issues.problem: Contradicts Anika's persona rule of two buckets (sourced or influenced, never both, each with proof). It also hard-codes a 90-day window while the inputs ask for 'the claim window in force'.
issues.fix: Use the persona's two-bucket rule with proof per deal and the window from the inputs. Unproven deals go to the unproven list.

issues.quote: (attributed revenue divided by program cost), partner-against-direct
issues.problem: Partner return is computed on gross attributed revenue with no margin or incrementality, which rewards partners for deals that would have closed anyway.
issues.fix: Report contribution-margin ROI plus an incrementality note (win rate and cycle time against a matched direct cohort).

issues.quote: Save the bands where the deal-level skills can read them, so per-deal
issues.problem: No mechanism is named, and model-the-partnership-commercials doesn't read them anyway. The two skills carry near-identical band sections.
issues.fix: memory_store or write_workspace_file under a named key, make the commercials skill read it, and keep the band definition in one skill.

issues.quote: Between closes, score alliance key results weekly (one objective plus two
issues.problem: Weekly OKR scoring duplicates run-partner-strategy-and-operations and the weekly partner pulse routine, and is scope creep for a quarterly close.
issues.fix: Remove it, or route to run-partner-strategy-and-operations.

issues.quote: No finance feed means building from CRM and owner-stated lines marked
issues.problem: No reconciliation of CRM bookings to finance-recognised revenue, and the persona's rule to show partner-reported and our numbers side by side, naming the gap, is missing.
issues.fix: Add a reconciliation table (CRM vs finance vs partner-reported) with each gap named.

issues.section: Build the rolled-up profit and loss
issues.quote: Every line names its source system and its window. Modelled lines stay
issues.problem: No tool path for pulling sources or doing the arithmetic, even though the platform has HubSpot and Sheets blocks and bash_exec.
issues.fix: Pull via run_block or ask for a CSV export, compute the P&L and variances in bash_exec, and ship a P&L template.

scenarios.prompt: Q3 just closed. Here's our alliance spend sheet and a HubSpot export for our six alliances. Run the close against plan and give me the half-page read.
scenarios.why: The skill gives per-alliance actuals vs plan, variance causes, a reallocation draft and a half-page read with partner-vs-direct comparators. But 'Build the rolled-up profit and loss' books influenced pipeline as revenue and leaves partner payouts out of costs, so profit and partner return are overstated.

scenarios.prompt: There's no finance export. Our CRO counts any partner-touched deal as partner revenue, two partners both claim sourced on the same deals, and the board wants one number in two weeks.
scenarios.why: The fallback builds from CRM data marked INFERENCE, and 'Feed the board pack' aims at one number. But the multi-touch attribution guidance contradicts the persona's sourced-or-influenced, never-both rule. Nothing handles duplicate partner claims or shows partner-reported and our numbers side by side as the persona requires.

partner-first-touch-outreach.job: draft cold outreach and follow-up sequence
partner-first-touch-outreach.summary: Drafts partner-prospect outreach, draft-only: rank evidenced warm paths and draft the connector ask first, then a short cold opener (why them, the motion, a 20-minute ask), then a day 5/12/20 follow-up and breakup cadence.
strengths: Drafts only, and nothing sends without the owner's yes in the same conversation.
Never invents familiarity, a mutual contact or a past meeting, and an unevidenced tie stays out of the message.
Won't guess a name or build an email address from a pattern; it drafts to the role and names the research gap.
No terms in an opener ('A first touch that promises margin, exclusivity, or funds is a commitment').
Warm path ranked with evidence before anything cold, and the cadence is capped with a clean breakup.
missing: A partner-value (what's in it for them) line
Cold-email compliance and suppression-list check
Stop-and-route rule for existing relationships
Batch mode for a shortlist
Email verification (e.g. ZeroBounce) before any send
Subject line, channel choice and example drafts
Outreach log and schedule_followup for the cadence
Reply handling that routes to qualification or structure-the-partner-agreement

issues.quote: Keep it plain and short: one line on why them, cited; one line on the
issues.problem: The opener has no line on what the partner gains (their margin, services attach, customer demand they are already seeing). Partner recruitment replies hinge on partner economics, and 'why them' only explains why we picked them.
issues.fix: Add a partner-value line grounded in evidence, such as shared customers or a services-revenue estimate labelled INFERENCE.

issues.problem: No cold-outreach compliance: no lawful basis for B2B cold email in the EU/UK (GDPR/PECR) or Germany (UWG), no opt-out line, no do-not-contact or suppression check.
issues.fix: Add a pre-draft check for jurisdiction, the suppression list and opt-out wording, and route unclear cases to Legal.

issues.quote: Day 12: a nudge carrying urgency.
issues.problem: Invites manufactured urgency, which sits badly with the never-invent rule; partner recruitment rarely has a real deadline.
issues.fix: Use an evidenced timing reason only (their launch, our program intake date); otherwise take a different value angle.

issues.quote: Look for shared investors, shared customers, ex-colleagues, or community
issues.problem: No method or tools for finding ties, so the model will guess where to look.
issues.fix: Name sources with fallbacks: CRM contact overlap via HubSpot, web_search on investor portfolios, Apollo or Enrichlayer lookups, otherwise ask the owner about their network.

issues.quote: want from them, and every prior touch on record.
issues.problem: Prior touches are an input, but nothing says to stop when someone in our org already has a live thread (the CEO, for example), so a warm relationship can get a duplicate cold email.
issues.fix: If an open thread exists, stop, route to that owner and draft an internal note instead.

issues.quote: The staged drafts, the warm-path ranking with its evidence, and the
issues.problem: No logging or scheduling. The persona requires a dated outreach log, and nudges are never scheduled or staged as drafts in a mail tool.
issues.fix: Log each batch with its date, create Gmail drafts via run_block pending approval, and schedule_followup for day 5, 12 and 20.

issues.quote: No attachments, no decks, no committed terms. A first touch that promises
issues.problem: No guidance on subject line, channel choice (email, LinkedIn or a connector intro) or length, and no example draft, so quality varies.
issues.fix: Add subject-line rules, a channel decision and one annotated example in examples/.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a first touch to the head of partnerships at Northwind, a US Salesforce consultancy we shortlisted, for a referral partnership.
scenarios.why: It searches for a warm path with evidence and drafts a connector ask first, then a three-line cold draft (why them with a citation, the motion, a 20-minute fit call) with no terms, plus the day 5/12/20 cadence. The result is solid and safe; only a partner-value line and a subject line are left to the model.

scenarios.prompt: Here are 15 shortlisted partners. Half have no named contact, two are already talking with our CEO, and three are in Germany. Draft outreach for all of them this week.
scenarios.why: The draft-to-role fallback covers missing contacts and 'Never invent familiarity' holds. But there is no batch procedure, nothing stops outreach to the two firms already in a CEO thread, and nothing addresses German UWG or GDPR limits on cold B2B email.

plan-the-multi-year-partnership.job: build multi-year joint partner business plan
plan-the-multi-year-partnership.summary: For engaged strategic partners only: drafts a one/three/five-year plan across four lanes, scores partner capability 1-5 with evidence, maps sponsors and governance, and sets at most five dated metrics with dual owners.
strengths: Gates multi-year plans to actively engaged partners and says so plainly to everyone else.
Year one holds dated commitments; years three and five are directional, each with the gate that unlocks it.
Every capability score needs one line of evidence or stays UNKNOWN, and each gap below 3 becomes a dated build item with an owner.
At most five metrics, each with a band, dual owners, a source and a sourced/influenced tag.
A sponsor who is only a title gets a sponsor-ask draft, not a seat.
missing: Mutual resource and investment commitments per side
The partner's own strategic goals and alignment
Lane definitions aligned to the capability scorecard
Criteria for the engagement gate
Gate-miss consequences and exit or renegotiation triggers
Joint product or integration roadmap alignment
Risk register and base/stretch scenarios
Plan and scorecard templates with an example

issues.section: Draft the skeleton in four lanes
issues.problem: No mutual investment commitments (heads, certifications, funds, engineering capacity each side puts in per horizon) and nothing capturing the partner's own strategic priorities. A multi-year plan without resources in from both sides isn't signable.
issues.fix: Add a resources-in / value-out block per side per horizon, and a partner-goals section at the top.

issues.section: Draft the skeleton in four lanes
issues.quote: Build, Develop, Market, Sell — across one, three, and five-year horizons,
issues.problem: The lanes are undefined (Build vs Develop is ambiguous) and don't match the scorecard dimensions (Sell, Implement, Market, Support), so capability gaps can't map to lanes consistently.
issues.fix: Define each lane in one line and align the scorecard dimensions to the lanes.

issues.quote: Multi-year plans are earned by actively engaged partners. Everyone else
issues.problem: The gate has no criterion for what counts as actively engaged.
issues.fix: Define it, e.g. two consecutive QBR grades at or above target, an active sponsor on each side, and joint pipeline in the last two quarters.

issues.section: Draft the skeleton in four lanes
issues.quote: Year one is dated commitments. Years three and five are directional, each
issues.problem: Gates are named, but nothing says what happens when one is missed (re-plan, drop to an annual plan, or route to renewals and exits or conflict and churn).
issues.fix: Add gate-miss handling and routing.

issues.quote: One sponsor per side. An operating committee plus a tiered review rhythm
issues.problem: Duplicates govern-the-strategic-alliance and run-partner-strategy-and-operations (sponsor pairing, steering committee, escalation path). For a GSI all three can fire and produce divergent governance.
issues.fix: Reuse the alliance operating model when one exists, and keep only the plan-specific review cadence here.

issues.quote: Score the partner 1 to 5 on Sell, Implement, Market, and Support, with
issues.problem: A numeric grade of the partner is relationship-sensitive, and there is no split between the internal scorecard and what the partner sees.
issues.fix: Keep the scores internal and share a gap-and-build-plan view with the partner.

issues.section: Draft the skeleton in four lanes
issues.quote: on the standard plan shape: goals, dated commitments, milestones,
issues.problem: 'Standard plan shape' and, in Fallbacks, 'standard joint-plan shape' imply a shared template the package doesn't ship.
issues.fix: Ship templates/joint-plan.md and point to it from both places.

issues.quote: The multi-year plan under three pages, the capability scorecard, the
issues.problem: No persistence for the annual refresh or QBR grading, and no tool path to draft into Docs or Slides.
issues.fix: Write the plan to the workspace, memory_store its key dates and metrics for the QBR countdown, and draft via run_block pending approval.

scenarios.prompt: Our alliance with a data-warehouse vendor is going well. Draft a three-year joint plan for the executive sponsors on both sides.
scenarios.why: It produces lanes by horizon with assumptions up top, a 1-5 capability scorecard with evidence, a sponsor map and at most five metrics. But the lanes are undefined (Build vs Develop), and no resources-in commitment is asked of either side, so the plan isn't signable as written.

scenarios.prompt: The partner's VP sponsor just left and their last two QBRs graded C, but our CEO wants a five-year plan announced at their conference next month.
scenarios.why: The engagement gate ('Everyone else gets the annual plan, and you say so plainly') and 'No sponsor means the sponsor ask comes before the governance document' steer the model to push back, offer the annual plan and draft the sponsor ask first, even though 'actively engaged' is never defined.

ad-copy-variants.job: write ad copy variants for testing
ad-copy-variants.summary: A 35-line placeholder that has the model pick 2-4 test ideas, write one variant per idea with character counts and landing-page wording, then check every claim against a source and flag likely policy rejections.
strengths: Every variant is tied to one hypothesis, so results can be read later
The claim-source requirement (product page, published price, linked review, owner confirmation) with strike-if-unsourced is a senior-grade guardrail
Explicitly flags policy-sensitive categories and competitor mentions
Carries landing-page wording into the ad for message match
Draft-only; no upload or launch
missing: Per-platform format and character-limit reference
RSA asset strategy (headline/description coverage, pinning, ad strength) and Meta dynamic-creative handling
Named inputs with ask_question and a landing-page fetch
Angle frameworks (awareness stage, pain/gain/proof/offer/urgency) and hook guidance for social
Compliant-rewrite patterns for restricted categories and trademark rules
Output template with character counts computed in the sandbox
Hypothesis and metric logged for creative-test-readout
Brand voice / banned-words input and localisation notes

issues.quote: Keep within the platform's character limits and show
issues.problem: It requires platform limits but supplies none and never asks which platform or format (Google RSA, Meta, LinkedIn, Microsoft). The counts depend on the model's memory, and nothing verifies them.
issues.fix: Add references/platform-specs.md with current field limits per platform and format (RSA 15x30 headlines, 4x90 descriptions, 2x15 paths; Meta primary text, headline and description guidance; LinkedIn intro text). Have the model count characters with bash_exec and show over-limit fields in red.

issues.quote: Each variant tests one idea, so a result can be read.
issues.problem: Formats that mix assets dynamically (Google RSAs, Meta Advantage+ creative and dynamic creative) break this model, because the platform recombines and weights assets. The skill never says how to keep a test readable in them (pinning, separate ads or ad sets, platform experiments) or when to use asset-level reporting instead.
issues.fix: Add a format branch. For RSAs, cover theme coverage across 15 headlines, pinning trade-offs and asset reports. For Meta and LinkedIn, one idea per ad inside a proper A/B test. Point to creative-test-readout for how the test will be read.

issues.quote: Use this for one campaign or ad group at a time.
issues.problem: No inputs are named up front: platform and format, keywords or audience, offer, landing URL, brand voice and banned words, prior results, the claims approver. Nothing says to fetch the landing page (web_fetch or browser) or to reuse the setup brief.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs section that uses ask_question for the missing items, memory_search for the paid-ads setup brief and past tests, and web_fetch to read the landing page. If the page is unreachable, ask for a paste.

issues.quote: is likely to reject, such as health, finance, or personal attributes, and
issues.problem: It flags risk but offers no policy reference, no compliant rewrite and no escalation. Trademark use in ad text and regulated-category certification are not mentioned.
issues.fix: Add a short policy checklist (Google and Meta restricted categories, the Meta personal-attributes rule, trademarks, superlatives and comparative claims). Give a compliant alternative for each struck line, and route anything flagged to the claims owner from the setup brief.

issues.quote: For each variant give the idea, the headlines, descriptions or primary text,
issues.problem: The deliverable is loosely described, with no reusable table or file.
issues.fix: Ship templates/ad-variants.md with these columns: variant, hypothesis/idea, field, text, char count/limit, claim + source, policy flag, landing-page phrase matched. Offer to write it to the workspace.

issues.quote: Note which ideas have run before and what happened.
issues.problem: It does not say where past results come from, and it does not record the new hypothesis or success metric, so later readouts have nothing to judge against.
issues.fix: Read prior tests via memory_search or the creative-test-readout log. For each variant, store the hypothesis, primary metric and planned read date with memory_store.

scenarios.prompt: Write responsive search ads for our 'emergency plumber London' ad group. Landing page is example.com/emergency, we promise 60-minute arrival and fixed call-out fee of £89.
scenarios.why: The claim check would correctly tie '60-minute' and '£89' to the page. But 'Each variant tests one idea' yields 2-4 thin RSAs and never covers what an RSA needs: up to 15 headlines of 30 characters, 4 descriptions of 90, 2 paths of 15, pinning, ad strength, and Google mixing assets so that one idea per ad cannot be read cleanly. 'Show the count' relies on the model knowing the limits and counting correctly, with no bash_exec check.

scenarios.prompt: Write Meta ads for our supplement: it 'boosts immunity', we have a 4.8-star average on our own site, and we want to say we're better than VitaCo. Budget is tight so make them punchy.
scenarios.why: The Claim check step would strike or flag the health claim, the unlinked rating and the competitor comparison, which is correct. It does not give policy-safe rewrites, name the regimes involved (Meta health and personal-attributes policy, trademark, FTC/ASA substantiation), or route to the claims approver recorded in paid-ads-getting-started. The user gets a list of refusals rather than usable compliant copy.

budget-pacing-review.job: check ad spend pacing against budget
budget-pacing-review.summary: A 38-line placeholder that compares planned with actual spend per campaign, projects month-end from the last seven days' daily rate as a range, and sets out hold, reallocate or rebudget options for the budget owner.
strengths: Currency and date-alignment check with a stated conversion rate
Asks for a range, not a point estimate, when spend is uneven
Knows platforms can spend above the daily budget on some days
Options include the owner and a decision date
Clear approval boundary; never changes budgets
missing: Definition of the planned-to-date curve and tolerance thresholds
Flight- or weekday-weighted projection with scenarios, run in the sandbox
Budget-constraint evidence (impression share lost to budget, limited-by-budget status) before a raise
Lifetime, shared and CBO budget handling
Learning-phase impact of budget changes
Marginal rather than average CPA when estimating the effect of moving money
Platform spend against invoiced or billed reconciliation
Recurring schedule option and a pacing table template

issues.quote: Project month-end spend from the last seven days' daily rate, and show the
issues.problem: A linear 7-day run rate ignores planned flighting (promos, launches), day-of-week patterns, lifetime or flight budgets, and changes already scheduled for the rest of the period. There is no fallback when only totals are available.
issues.fix: Define projection = actual to date + expected spend for the remaining days, using planned flight weights or a weekday profile, plus scheduled changes. Run it in bash_exec, and show low/base/high cases. If only totals exist, ask for a daily export or state the linear assumption.

issues.quote: each campaign show planned spend to date, actual spend to date, and the gap
issues.problem: 'Planned spend to date' is undefined (even daily split or weighted plan), and there is no tolerance band for when a gap matters.
issues.fix: Define planned-to-date from the owner's flight plan, or a linear split if none exists, and label which one was used. Report pacing % and flag outside an agreed band (for example ±10%, confirmed with the owner).

issues.quote: lower or raise daily budgets, with the new figures.
issues.problem: It suggests raising budgets without checking whether the campaign can use the money (Google 'limited by budget', search impression share lost to budget) or what the change costs (Meta learning resets after significant edits, shared budgets or campaign budget optimisation).
issues.fix: Before any raise or move, require evidence of budget constraint (IS lost to budget, limited status) and note the learning-phase and shared-budget effects of each option.

issues.quote: For each give the effect on results where data supports it, and say where it
issues.problem: There is no method for estimating the effect, so a model will probably apply average CPA to extra spend, which overstates returns because marginal CPA is usually higher.
issues.fix: Tell the model to use marginal rather than average cost where data allows (the platform's budget simulator or Performance Planner output, labelled as a platform forecast). Otherwise state 'effect unknown'.

issues.quote: campaign, or platform limits that let daily spend run above the daily
