issues.problem: The overdelivery rule is vague. For example, Google can spend up to 2x the average daily budget in a day but bills no more than about 30.4x it per month, and Meta averages over the week. Without these rules, day-level overspend can be misread as a problem.
issues.fix: Add a short reference covering each platform's budget mechanics (daily, lifetime and shared budgets, overdelivery and billing caps), with a note to confirm them against current platform help.

issues.quote: State the budget period, the planned total, and the owner who set it.
issues.problem: Required inputs and their source are not named: a daily spend export by campaign, the plan per campaign, and billing and invoicing differences. The recurring nature of pacing is not used either.
issues.fix: List inputs up front and ask for a daily campaign export or paste. Offer schedule_routine for a weekly pacing check, and ship a pacing table template.

scenarios.prompt: It's the 18th. Here's our Google Ads daily spend export by campaign for this month; the monthly budget is £6,000. Are we going to overspend?
scenarios.why: It follows planned against actual per campaign, then a 7-day run-rate projection with the working shown and a range if spend is uneven, then options with the owner and a decision date. A capable model would produce a correct, useful pacing note. The main weakness is that 'planned spend to date' is undefined, so the model will probably assume linear pacing.

scenarios.prompt: We run Meta (EUR, one lifetime-budget campaign) and Google (USD). One campaign was paused on the 10th, Black Friday is next week and we planned to spend 40% of the month in it. I only have month-to-date totals from screenshots, no daily data.
scenarios.why: Currency conversion at a stated rate and date is handled, and seasonality is noted. The 7-day run rate cannot be computed from totals, and the skill gives no fallback for that. It also ignores the planned flight weighting for Black Friday and lifetime budgets, and has no way to project with a known future change in rate. A linear run rate would badly misread the plan here.

campaign-structure-plan.summary: A 39-line placeholder that works back from one goal and success measure to per-campaign objective, bidding, ad groups, targeting, negatives, landing pages, budget split and conversion, then lists launch prerequisites with owners.
strengths: Works backward from one goal and one deciding measure
Separates past data (with dates) from first guesses
The consolidation principle for small budgets is correct and important
Each group gets a landing page and an optimisation event
Launch checklist with a named owner per item and a review date
missing: Campaign-type and bid-strategy decision table
Budget-to-conversion sizing against learning thresholds
Sourced CPC and volume route (DataForSEO, Keyword Planner export, history)
Guidance on automated formats (PMax, Advantage+)
Brand/non-brand split, match types, exclusions and naming convention
Measurement plan and review criteria at launch
Reusable campaign plan template (sheet or markdown)
Test-and-scale staging for new channels

issues.quote: objective and bidding approach, with the reason;
issues.problem: It asks for a bidding approach but gives no decision rules: campaign type (Search, PMax, Demand Gen, Meta sales/leads/Advantage+), when to use Max Conversions, tCPA/tROAS or manual, or the conversion-volume prerequisites for smart bidding.
issues.fix: Add references/structure-decisions.md: a decision table by goal, conversion volume and budget, giving campaign type and bid strategy, with the reason template.

issues.quote: Keep the structure as simple as the budget allows. Too many groups on a small
issues.problem: The rule is right but unquantified, so the model cannot tell whether a plan is over-split.
issues.fix: Add a sizing step in bash_exec: budget ÷ expected CPA (sourced) = conversions per group per week, compared with the learning threshold for the platform. Merge groups until each clears it, or say the budget cannot support smart bidding yet.

issues.quote: invent benchmarks or promise a cost per result.
issues.problem: The rule is correct, but the skill offers no legitimate data route for CPC, volume or CPA, so sizing and budget splits are either skipped or invented.
issues.fix: Route estimates to named sources: account history, a Keyword Planner export, DataForSEO keyword data via run_block, or a platform reach/forecast export. Label each figure as sourced or assumed, with a date.

issues.quote: ad groups or ad sets, each built around one theme or audience;
issues.problem: It assumes manual themed groups. Current practice relies heavily on automated formats (PMax asset groups, Advantage+ campaigns, broad match plus smart bidding) that change what 'structure' means.
issues.fix: Add a branch for automated campaign types covering asset groups and audience signals, brand exclusions, and feed or catalog prerequisites, and say when manual control is still worth it.

issues.quote: keywords or targeting, and the first negatives or exclusions;
issues.problem: Standard structure decisions are missing: brand vs non-brand split, match-type strategy, existing-customer exclusions, geo and schedule, naming convention, and conversion values.
issues.fix: Add these as required fields in a campaign plan template.

issues.quote: List what must be true before launch: tracking tested, pages live, copy
issues.problem: The checklist omits primary/secondary conversion actions, auto-tagging or UTMs, CAPI or enhanced conversions, policy review of copy, and a measurement plan (what result at the review date means keep, change or stop).
issues.fix: Extend the checklist, and link copy approval to ad-copy-variants and tracking to the setup brief.

issues.quote: State the one goal, the one measure that decides success, and the target
issues.problem: It does not load the setup brief from paid-ads-getting-started or ask for missing inputs, and it never asks which platforms are in scope.
issues.fix: Start with memory_search for the setup brief. If it is absent, ask_question for goal, platform(s), budget, geography, offer, landing pages and conversion definition.

scenarios.prompt: We're a B2B SaaS with £5k/month for Google Ads, goal is demo requests. Plan the account structure.
scenarios.why: The model would list campaigns with the required fields and a launch checklist. It gets no rule for choosing Search vs PMax, brand vs non-brand, match types or bid strategy, and no way to check whether £5k supports the proposed ad groups. Sizing needs CPC and volume data, but the skill forbids invented benchmarks and never points to DataForSEO via run_block, a Keyword Planner export or account history. The result is either unsized or quietly invented.

scenarios.prompt: Rebuild our messy Meta account: 38 ad sets, €3k/month, e-commerce with a catalog, and we also want to try TikTok. Tracking is via pixel only.
scenarios.why: 'Keep the structure as simple as the budget allows' points the right way. The skill does not quantify it (Meta needs roughly 50 optimisation events per ad set per week to exit learning), and it says nothing about Advantage+ sales/catalog campaigns, the Conversions API gap, or how to stage a new channel test. The launch checklist would miss CAPI and event-match checks.

creative-test-readout.job: read out ad creative A/B test
creative-test-readout.summary: A 43-line placeholder that checks test setup for fairness, reports per-variant metrics against noise using power, minimum effect and confidence, handles multiple comparisons, and returns clear winner, leaning or not enough data with a recommendation and next test.
strengths: Requires the agreed measure and a single differing idea before reading
Explicit power, minimum effect and confidence requirement before any winner
Handles more than two variants with pre-set comparisons or a correction
Three-way verdict with the sample still needed and the days to reach it
Strong 'never call a winner early' guardrail matching Marco's voice
missing: Bundled statistics script (proportion test, intervals, correction, sample-size and days calculation)
Distinction between a randomised platform experiment and algorithmic ad rotation
Pre-registration captured at setup; peeking and sequential-testing guidance
Handling of CPA or ROAS as non-proportion metrics (bootstrap)
Conversion lag and attribution-window treatment
Creative fatigue and novelty checks before roll-out
Test log persisted in memory; boundary with Quinn's experiment-readout

issues.quote: share of spend, ran over the same days, and pointed to the same page.
issues.problem: Ads in one ad set, or RSA assets, are served by an optimising algorithm, not by random assignment. Even spend does not make them a controlled test, and uneven spend is itself selection bias. Senior buyers separate platform experiments from ordinary ad rotation.
issues.fix: Add a setup gate. If the test was a platform A/B test or experiment, read it as a test. If it was in-ad-set rotation, label the result observational, soften the verdict, and propose a proper test design.

issues.quote: Use a stated method and show it.
issues.problem: No default method or tool is given, so results vary run to run and arithmetic errors are likely.
issues.fix: Ship scripts/ab_readout.py for bash_exec: two-proportion z-test with Wilson intervals, Holm correction for more than two variants, sample-size and days-to-significance calculation, and bootstrap for CPA or ROAS. Show the output table.

issues.quote: a winner, state the baseline rate, minimum effect worth detecting, power, and
issues.problem: The sample-size parameters come after the results are read, which invites choosing them after the fact. Peeking and sequential stopping are not addressed.
issues.fix: Move the baseline, minimum effect, power and alpha to Check the setup, taken from the pre-test plan. If none existed, say so and treat the readout as exploratory. Warn against repeated peeking, or use a sequential method.

issues.quote: For each variant show impressions, clicks, conversions, spend, and the rate
issues.problem: It does not warn that a CTR winner may lose on CVR or CPA, or that cost metrics are not proportions. Conversion lag and attribution-window effects on recent days are ignored.
issues.fix: Require the pre-agreed primary metric to be a business outcome where volume allows, report CTR as secondary, and exclude or flag days still inside the conversion lag.

issues.quote: For more than two variants, call a winner only for the comparison set before
issues.problem: This repeats the multiple-comparison instruction from Check the setup almost word for word.
issues.fix: Keep it once in setup, and in Read the result reference the correction the script applies.

issues.quote: Recommend keep running, stop, or roll out, and the next idea worth testing.
issues.problem: Nothing is logged, so learnings are lost between tests. There is no handoff to ad-copy-variants for the next test, and fatigue and novelty are not considered for roll-out.
issues.fix: memory_store each test (hypothesis, dates, result, verdict) as a test log, hand the next idea to ad-copy-variants, and note frequency and fatigue checks before scaling.

scenarios.prompt: Ad A: 12,000 impressions, 410 clicks, 22 conversions, £620. Ad B: 11,500 impressions, 395 clicks, 31 conversions, £605. Same ad set, 10 days. Which one won?
scenarios.why: Setup check notes even spend and dates. Read-result shows the rates, and a two-proportion test (about 5.4% vs 7.8% CVR, not significant at this n) leads to 'not enough data' with the required sample and days at current spend. A capable model gets the verdict right. The caveat about same-ad-set delivery is missing but does not flip the answer here.

scenarios.prompt: We ran 5 creatives in one Advantage+ campaign. Meta gave 70% of spend to #3, which has the best CPA, and one creative only started last week. Meta says #3 is the winner. Can we kill the rest?
scenarios.why: The skill would say the setup was uneven and apply its multiple-comparison rule, so it would not call a winner. It never explains why: algorithmic delivery is non-random selection, not a test. It also says nothing about the fact that CPA is not a simple proportion, or about novelty and fatigue, and gives no design for a proper test (Meta A/B test or Experiments, equal-budget ad sets). The user gets 'unclear' without a path forward.

landing-page-message-match.summary: A 39-line placeholder that pairs each ad with its final URL and results, checks that the page loads on mobile and desktop, compares ad promise, offer, CTA and searcher words with the page, and ranks fixes by spend at stake and effort.
strengths: Concrete five-point comparison: promise vs headline, offer and terms, CTA vs first action, searcher words vs page words, promised-but-missing
Checks that pages load on mobile and desktop, plus redirects, errors and regional variants
Separates observation from guessed effect
Fixes ranked by spend at stake, with type (copy, design, ad-side) and page owner
No invented conversion lifts
missing: Triage for sudden drops (tracking, form submission, consent banner) before a copy audit
Named browser, screenshot and PageSpeed tool routes with fallbacks
Analytics landing-page conversion by device, and search-term source
Above-the-fold, proof and trust, and mobile layout checks
Google landing-page experience / Quality Score component
Dynamic keyword insertion and per-keyword landing page options
Scoring rubric and output template
Boundary with conversion-rate-optimization

issues.quote: "landing page review", "conversion drop"
issues.problem: 'Conversion drop' routes a diagnostic problem (often tracking, forms, consent or auction) to a copy-comparison skill. 'Landing page review' will also collide with conversion-rate-optimization if that Toran skill is assigned to Marco.
issues.fix: Drop 'conversion drop', or add a first triage step: confirm tracking fired, submit the form, check the consent banner, compare with the prior period. Route tracking issues to paid-performance-report or the setup brief. Narrow the description to ad-to-page scent.

issues.quote: Open each page and confirm it loads, on
issues.problem: It does not say how (browser_navigate and browser_screenshot at mobile and desktop widths, or web_fetch as a fallback). It does not test that the CTA or form actually submits, or whether a consent or cookie wall blocks it, and there is no fallback when pages are gated or geo-locked.
issues.fix: Name the tools and fallbacks: screenshot above the fold at 390px and desktop, click through the primary CTA without submitting real data (or ask the owner to test), and ask for screenshots when a page cannot be reached.

issues.quote: Note load time and form length where you can measure them.
issues.problem: There is no measurement method, so it will usually be skipped. Senior checks such as above-the-fold content, trust and proof, mobile layout and Core Web Vitals are also missing.
issues.fix: Use the PageSpeed Insights API via web_fetch for field LCP/INP/CLS where available. Add above-the-fold, proof and trust elements, form field count and mobile tap-target checks to the comparison list.

issues.quote: List each live ad or ad group with its final URL, spend, clicks, and
issues.problem: It uses ad-side numbers only. It does not pull landing-page conversion rate by device from analytics or search-term data, so 'words the searcher used' has no stated source.
issues.fix: Ask for the analytics landing-page report (sessions, engagement, conversion rate by device) and the search-terms export. Label each figure with its source and period.

issues.quote: Use this when ads get clicks but the page does not convert, or before a launch.
issues.problem: The boundary with full-page CRO (conversion-rate-optimization, Toran, proposed for Marco) and with ad-copy-variants is not stated.
issues.fix: Scope this skill to ad-to-page consistency. Hand deeper page redesign to conversion-rate-optimization, or to a designer or web teammate, and ad-side rewrites to ad-copy-variants.

issues.quote: Rank fixes by spend at stake and effort, cheapest and largest first.
issues.problem: 'Cheapest and largest first' is ambiguous when the two conflict, and there is no reusable output table.
issues.fix: Score each fix on spend at stake × confidence ÷ effort, and ship templates/message-match-audit.md (ad, URL, gap, evidence, fix, type, owner, score).

scenarios.prompt: Our 'accounting software for contractors' ads have a 6% CTR but only 0.8% of clicks convert. Here are the 4 ad groups, their final URLs and last month's numbers.
scenarios.why: The steps map directly: pair ads to pages with spend and conversions, open each page, compare promise, offer, CTA and searcher language, then rank fixes by spend at stake. A capable model with browser tools would produce a sound, prioritised message-match review, with observations kept separate from guesses.

scenarios.prompt: Conversions dropped 40% this week on the same landing pages and nothing changed in the ads. What's wrong with the pages?
scenarios.why: The 'conversion drop' trigger loads this skill, but sudden drops usually come from tracking breaks, form or consent-banner failures, or auction shifts. The skill has no triage step to rule those out and never tells the model to submit the form or check conversion tags. It would audit copy while the likely cause goes unchecked. Only the 'return an error' check catches part of it.

paid-ads-getting-started.job: onboard paid ads accounts and tracking
paid-ads-getting-started.summary: A 41-line onboarding placeholder that gathers accounts, goals, budgets, targets, offers, pages and 90-day exports, checks conversion definitions against the business's own counts, agrees approval owners, and returns a five-part setup brief.
strengths: Names inputs explicitly up front (platforms, goals, budgets and owners, targets, offers, pages, 90-day exports)
Records date range, currency and attribution per source
Reconciles platform conversions with the analytics tool or CRM and logs tracking breaks with dates
Agrees approval owners for budgets, launches, pauses, copy and legal claims
Clear numbered setup brief and a strong no-estimates-for-tracking-gaps rule
missing: New-advertiser branch (no accounts, no history)
Concrete tracking checklist (primary/secondary, double counting, enhanced conversions or CAPI, Consent Mode, offline import, call tracking)
Persisted setup brief (memory plus workspace template) that the other skills read
Named export list and columns; read-only access rather than credentials
PII and consent handling for exports and audience lists
Normal-gap drivers when reconciling platform and CRM figures
Handoff to campaign-structure-plan or wasted-spend-audit based on findings

issues.quote: covering at least the last 90 days, and record the date range, currency, and
issues.problem: The triggers ('start advertising', 'PPC setup') invite brand-new advertisers, but the procedure assumes accounts and history exist. There is no decision point for zero history.
issues.fix: Add a branch. With history, run the current flow. With none, set up a tracking and measurement plan (conversion actions, call tracking, GA4 linking, auto-tagging), account and billing prerequisites, and hand to campaign-structure-plan.

issues.quote: Confirm which conversions each platform counts, how each is defined, and
issues.problem: It gives no concrete checklist, so common senior-level findings are missed: primary vs secondary actions, double counting (GA4 import plus the Ads tag), micro-conversions set as primary, view-through inclusion, auto-tagging or gclid, enhanced conversions, Meta CAPI and event match, Consent Mode in the EU/UK, offline conversion import.
issues.fix: Ship references/tracking-checklist.md covering these items, with what to ask for (a screenshot of the conversion actions page, the event manager) and how to record each state.

issues.quote: Give the user:
issues.problem: The brief is only returned in chat, although every other Marco skill needs its facts (currency, attribution, conversion definitions, approvers). The platform has memory_store and workspace files, but they are not used, so later skills re-ask or guess.
issues.fix: Save the brief with memory_store and write_workspace_file (templates/setup-brief.md). Have the other Marco skills load it first, and set a re-check date for tracking.

issues.quote: analytics tool or CRM for the same period and record the gap.
issues.problem: There is no guidance on normal causes of a gap (attribution windows, click-date vs conversion-date, view-through, cross-device, modelled conversions, spam leads), so a normal gap may be reported as a tracking fault, or a real fault dismissed.
issues.fix: List expected gap drivers and a threshold for when a gap needs investigation, and record which platform is treated as the source of truth for each metric.

issues.quote: Ask for the ad platforms and accounts in use, the business goal for each,
issues.problem: It does not say which reports or columns to export, has no structured intake, and never says to request read-only access rather than credentials. Exports may contain customer PII (Customer Match lists, lead forms) with no handling rule.
issues.fix: Use ask_question for the intake. Specify the exports (campaign, ad group, search term, placement and daily reports with named columns). Never ask for passwords, and exclude or minimise personal data.

issues.quote: "ad account review"
issues.problem: This overlaps with wasted-spend-audit's 'account audit' and 'ad audit' triggers, so a request to audit may load setup instead, or setup may be run again every time.
issues.fix: Say in the description that this runs once per client, before other Marco skills, and is skipped when a current setup brief exists in memory. Drop or rename the overlapping trigger.

scenarios.prompt: We just hired Marco. We run Google and Meta at about $8k/month for lead gen; here are 90-day exports and our HubSpot lead counts.
scenarios.why: Map accounts and goals, record currency, attribution and date ranges, compare platform conversions with HubSpot and record the gap, agree approvers, then return the five-part brief with the first three checks. A capable model would produce a solid onboarding brief. It would not save the brief for later skills.

scenarios.prompt: We've never run ads. We want to start Google Ads at $1,500/month; we don't have GA4 set up and most leads phone us.
scenarios.why: The triggers 'start advertising' and 'PPC setup' load the skill, but the procedure assumes existing accounts and 90 days of exports. It has no branch for a new advertiser (account and billing setup, conversion tracking from scratch, call tracking, GA4 linking), so the model has to improvise the most important part. The brief's 'first three checks' also assume data that does not exist.

churn-risk-review.job: diagnose churn risk for customer accounts
churn-risk-review.summary: A 37-line placeholder with no supporting files: it compares period-over-period signals, splits each risk into observation, cause, unknowns, impact and next check, sorts accounts into four tiers, and drafts recovery outreach for approval.
strengths: Makes the model state the baseline and prior period, cite the source and date range for every signal, and list unknowns, which stops vague red/yellow/green labels
States outright that quiet accounts or accounts with support tickets are not automatically at risk
Has an 'insufficient evidence' tier, so weak data does not get reported as a risk
Separates the observed change, possible causes with evidence for each, business impact and the smallest next check
Drafts outreach only, with no promised concessions or product changes
missing: Tier definitions and thresholds
ARR-at-risk and notice-date weighting for portfolio ranking
Churn reason-code taxonomy (sponsor loss, budget/M&A, competitor, value gap, involuntary)
Save-play library per reason and an escalation ladder
Data intake step with an integration fallback (CSV/export) and sandbox trend computation
Handoffs to renewal-readiness-review, customer-escalation and the renewal negotiator
Portfolio output template
Follow-up scheduling and persistence of prior baselines

issues.quote: Rank as **urgent**, **review**, **watch**, or **insufficient evidence**.
issues.problem: The four tiers have no criteria, so the same account can be ranked differently from run to run and teams cannot audit the ranking.
issues.fix: Define each tier. For example: urgent = a verified negative change in 2+ components, or champion/sponsor loss, inside the notice window. Review = one verified negative trend. Watch = an early signal with no confirmed trend. State the rule in the output.

issues.quote: Compare current and prior periods for adoption, progress toward stated outcomes,
issues.problem: No inputs are named up front. The skill doesn't define the comparison window, where data comes from, or what to do when a source is missing.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step. It should cover the account list with ARR, renewal and notice dates, the usage export and the ticket export; the default window (e.g. trailing 4 weeks vs the prior 4 weeks); pulling data through run_block (HubSpot/Sheets) or a connected MCP, or asking for a CSV; and computing deltas in bash_exec.

issues.quote: Use this for one account or a ranked portfolio.
issues.problem: It promises a ranked portfolio but gives no ranking basis: no ARR at risk, no days to notice date, no ranking of logo versus contraction risk.
issues.fix: Rank within each tier by ARR at risk, then by days to notice date. Output a portfolio table: account, tier, ARR, notice date, top signal, cause hypothesis, next check, owner, due date.

issues.quote: support volume and severity, unresolved commitments, sponsor or champion change,
issues.problem: The signal list leaves out canonical churn drivers and has no reason-code taxonomy, so the causes it produces are shallow.
issues.fix: Add reason codes (product fit, value not realised, sponsor loss, budget/M&A, competitor, service failure, involuntary/billing). Add leading signals: seat-reduction or downgrade requests, failed payments, competitor mentions, declining exec engagement, NPS/CSAT detractors.

issues.quote: Propose a recovery step tied to the customer's goal.
issues.problem: There is no save playbook, no escalation ladder and no teammate handoff, so the recovery step stays generic.
issues.fix: Add a short play per reason code and an escalation path: CSM, then exec sponsor, then AE. Route renewal prep to renewal-readiness-review, product issues to customer-escalation, and commercial concessions to Jordan's renewal-negotiation-brief.

issues.problem: No deliverable template, so single-account and portfolio outputs will vary in shape.
issues.fix: Ship templates/churn_review.md with the per-risk block and portfolio table, and link it from the SKILL.md body.

issues.quote: the smallest next check;
issues.problem: Next checks and baselines are not saved or scheduled, so the next review cannot compare against this one.
issues.fix: Write each review to a dated workspace file and store the baseline with memory_store. Offer schedule_followup on each check's due date.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV of our 40 accounts with weekly active users for the last 8 weeks, ticket counts by severity, ARR and renewal dates. Which ones are at risk this quarter and what should I do first?
scenarios.why: 'Check the signals' and 'Separate fact from cause' produce a cited per-account write-up. But the skill never defines what makes an account urgent versus review versus watch, never says to weight by ARR or days to notice date, and never says to compute trends in the sandbox. Tiers will be arbitrary and vary from run to run, and there is no portfolio table format.

scenarios.prompt: Acme's champion just left, usage is flat, renewal is in 45 days, and I can't get at Zendesk. Are they going to churn and what do I do?
scenarios.why: The skill will avoid overclaiming (the 'insufficient evidence' tier, the smallest next check, drafts only). But it has no fallback for the missing support source: no connect_integration call and no request for an export. It has no champion-loss play (multi-threading, reaching the exec sponsor) and no rule that raises urgency inside the notice window. It also never hands off to renewal-readiness-review or customer-escalation.

customer-health-score.job: build and apply customer health score
customer-health-score.summary: A 32-line placeholder with no supporting files: it defines each health signal (source, thresholds, weight, missing-data rule), scores accounts by component with evidence, and returns a reproducible formula, confidence, missing data and change since last period.
strengths: Keeps adoption, outcome, support, relationship and commercial components visible rather than hiding them in one number
Missing values are never counted as zero or healthy
Warns against using logins as proof of value when the outcome calls for another measure
Requires the formula or rules so a person can reproduce every score
Labels manual judgement and requires an explanation for it
missing: Weighting and threshold method, with per-segment thresholds
Normalisation and combination rules, including gating overrides
Back-test and calibration against historical churn and renewals
Persistence of the model and prior-period scores
Scoring script and output template
Definition of confidence
Leading versus lagging indicator guidance
Governance for manual overrides and model changes

issues.quote: health score directs review; it does not prove renewal or churn.
issues.problem: It admits the score is not predictive but never validates it against outcomes, so a miscalibrated model looks as trustworthy as a good one.
issues.fix: Add a calibration step: score the last 2-4 quarters of renewed and churned accounts, report false greens and false reds, adjust weights and thresholds, and state the hit rate. Re-check every quarter.

issues.quote: For every signal record its meaning, source, date range, refresh rate, good and
issues.problem: It says to record weights and thresholds but gives no method for setting them, normalising raw values into component scores, or combining components. Segments (SMB vs enterprise) are not distinguished.
issues.fix: Provide a default component set with starter weights marked as assumptions, a normalisation rule (e.g. against baseline/target to 0-100), gating overrides (e.g. an open Sev1 or sponsor loss caps the account at yellow) and per-segment thresholds.

issues.quote: change since the last period, and next check.
issues.problem: Reporting change since the last period needs stored prior scores, and the platform keeps no local state. No save/load step is given.
issues.fix: Write the model definition and each period's scores to workspace files (e.g. health_model.yml, health_scores_YYYY-MM.csv), store the model version with memory_store, and load both before rescoring.

issues.quote: For each account show the raw value, baseline or target, trend period, component
issues.problem: There is no scoring script or output template, so portfolio-scale arithmetic happens in the model's context.
issues.fix: Ship scripts/score.py that reads the CSV and model file and writes a component-level CSV, run it with bash_exec, and add a template for the summary view.

issues.quote: Give the component view, overall result, confidence, missing data, material
issues.problem: 'Confidence' is never defined, so every run will interpret it differently.
issues.fix: Define confidence as the weighted share of components with fresh, sourced data (e.g. high ≥80%, medium 50-79%, low <50%).

issues.problem: No input step names the minimum data or says what to do when a source (usage, CRM, support) is not connected.
issues.fix: Name minimum inputs. Pull them through run_block (HubSpot/Sheets) or a connected MCP, or ask for a CSV via ask_question; score only the components that have data and mark the rest missing.

issues.quote: customer score
issues.problem: This trigger is vague enough to fire on lead-scoring or credit-scoring requests handled by other experts.
issues.fix: Replace it with specific phrases such as 'customer health model' or 'which accounts are red'.

scenarios.prompt: Build us a health score for our 120 accounts from this HubSpot export and our product-usage CSV, and tell me which accounts are red.
scenarios.why: 'Define before scoring' makes the model write down each signal's source, thresholds, weight and missing-data rule, and 'Return' gives an auditable result. But the skill never says how to choose weights or thresholds, normalise raw values, or combine components (weighted average or worst-component cap). It never says to get the user to agree the model before scoring, or to compute 120 rows in bash_exec. The model will invent weights and do arithmetic in context.

scenarios.prompt: Our health score shows 80% of accounts green but we lost six green accounts last quarter. Fix the model.
scenarios.why: The skill has no calibration or back-test step. It never compares scores with actual renewals and churn, finds false greens, or reweights components, and it only notes that a score 'does not prove renewal or churn'. Following it, the model would redefine signals without testing them against the six lost accounts.

customer-onboarding-plan.job: plan customer onboarding to first value
customer-onboarding-plan.summary: A 33-line placeholder with no supporting files: it builds an onboarding plan from the customer's stated outcome, with owned milestones, completion evidence, four-state tracking, and customer updates drafted for approval.
strengths: Anchors onboarding to the customer's stated outcome in their own words
'A meeting is not a milestone unless it produces a named decision or artifact' is a sharp, practitioner-grade rule
A step is marked done only on completion evidence
Keeps dates the user gave separate from estimated dates
Asks about security, data, training and procurement steps instead of assuming they are complete
missing: Stalled-onboarding diagnosis and escalation ladder
Sales-to-CS handoff intake (scope, promises, SOW)
Time-to-first-value target and onboarding exit criteria
Kickoff agenda and RACI for both sides
Onboarding plan template, with internal and customer-facing versions
Segmented onboarding motions (high-touch vs tech-touch)
Tracker persistence and milestone follow-up scheduling

issues.quote: Use this for a new customer or a stalled onboarding.
issues.problem: Stalled onboarding is named as a use case but has no diagnosis or recovery procedure.
issues.fix: Add a stall branch: find the stuck milestone and days stalled, classify the cause (access, resourcing, priority, sponsor, oversold scope), escalate CSM → exec sponsor → AE, and re-baseline dates as a draft for approval.

issues.quote: evidence, and risk. Cover access, data readiness, configuration, first use,
issues.problem: No time-to-first-value target and no exit criteria, so there is no definition of when onboarding ends and ongoing success work begins.
issues.fix: Define a first-value milestone in the customer's outcome terms, a target time to first value, go-live/exit criteria, and a handoff to customer-success-plan.

issues.quote: Record the outcome in the customer's words, sponsor, day-to-day owner, users,
issues.problem: No intake from the sales handoff (what was sold, scope, promises, start date), so oversold commitments surface late.
issues.fix: Start by reading the closed-won record or SOW, via run_block (HubSpot) or a paste. List every sales commitment and flag any the delivery team has not confirmed.

issues.problem: No deliverable template, and no split between the internal tracker and a customer-facing version.
issues.fix: Ship templates/onboarding_plan.md with a milestone table (milestone, owner side, date source, dependency, evidence, status, next action) and a customer-facing summary that leaves out internal risks.

issues.quote: only from its completion evidence. Give the next action and owner for every
issues.problem: Status tracking assumes persistent state, but no tracker is created and no follow-ups are scheduled.
issues.fix: Offer to write the tracker to Sheets or Notion via run_block after approval, keep a dated workspace copy, and schedule_followup on milestone due dates.

issues.quote: launch plan
issues.problem: 'launch plan' and 'implementation plan' clash with product/marketing launch skills and with Max's signature-to-launch skill, which uses the same trigger. The boundary with customer-success-plan is also unstated.
issues.fix: Use 'customer go-live plan' or 'new customer onboarding milestones', and state that this skill ends at first value.

scenarios.prompt: We just closed Northwind: 200 seats, and they want to cut ticket resolution time 30% by Q1. SSO and a data import are needed. Build their onboarding plan.
scenarios.why: 'Start from the outcome' captures the goal, sponsor, owners, systems and constraints and asks about security steps. 'Build milestones' covers access, data readiness, configuration, first use, training and the adoption check, with owners and evidence. A capable model gives a solid plan, though with no first-value target or standard template.

scenarios.prompt: Globex's onboarding has stalled for 5 weeks: the admin isn't responding, IT hasn't approved SSO, and sales promised a custom integration we don't have. Fix it.
scenarios.why: The description covers stalled onboarding, but the body only says to mark items blocked and name a next action and owner. It gives no stall diagnosis, no escalation ladder (champion, exec sponsor, AE), no way to handle an oversold commitment (log it as an unresolved promise and route it to sales/product), and no re-baselining of dates with approval.

customer-success-getting-started.job: set up customer success operating rules
customer-success-getting-started.summary: A 36-line placeholder with no supporting files: it gathers segments, outcomes, data sources, renewal dates and approval rules, agrees success and risk measures, and returns a five-part setup brief naming the first three account reviews.
strengths: Records system, field, date range and last refresh for every source
Defines up front who may approve external messages, offers, terms or product commitments
Explicitly treats silence as not proof of health
Ends with a concrete, prioritised first action (three account reviews)
Positions itself before scoring and outreach, which gives the kit a clear entry point
missing: Persistence of agreed rules for other skills
Minimum-input path and progressive collection
Rule for choosing the first accounts to review
Segmentation, coverage model and baseline CS KPIs (GRR/NRR)
Fallback setup when there is no CRM or usage data
A routine suggestion (e.g. a weekly portfolio review via schedule_routine)
Handoff to Vera for contract facts

issues.quote: commercial readiness. Define missing-data handling and who may approve an
issues.problem: The agreed rules, source map and approval authority exist only in chat, so customer-health-score, churn-risk-review and the renewal skills cannot reuse them in later sessions.
issues.fix: Save the rules to a workspace file (e.g. cs_operating_rules.md) plus memory_store keys, and have every other Riley skill load them first.

issues.quote: Ask for the customer segments, stated outcomes, onboarding stages, product
issues.problem: It asks for nine-plus inputs at once, with no minimum set and no path to continue while partial.
issues.fix: Ask via ask_question for the minimum (account list with ARR, renewal and notice dates, owner, one usage source) and continue. Offer connect_integration for HubSpot/Sheets or accept a CSV; collect the rest progressively.

issues.quote: The first three account reviews, with reasons.
issues.problem: No selection rule, so the choice of first reviews is arbitrary.
issues.fix: Rank by days to notice date, then ARR, then known risk signals, and state the rule in the brief.

issues.quote: Agree which measures describe adoption, outcomes, support, relationship, and
issues.problem: Missing a segmentation and coverage model and baseline portfolio KPIs, which a CS lead would set on day one.
issues.fix: Add segment tiers with a coverage model (high-touch, scaled, pooled) and baseline GRR, NRR, logo churn and time to first value, each labelled sourced or assumed.

issues.problem: No fallback when there is no CRM or usage system.
issues.fix: Offer a starter Sheets tracker via run_block and consult Vera to extract renewal and notice dates from contracts. Define a minimum signal set for accounts with no telemetry.

issues.quote: account management
issues.problem: 'account management' and 'customer portfolio' are broad enough to collide with sales and account-management skills on other experts.
issues.fix: Narrow to 'set up customer success', 'CS operating rules' or 'start managing my customer book'.

scenarios.prompt: I'm the only CSM for 60 accounts. Here's our HubSpot export with renewal dates and a Mixpanel usage CSV. Help me get set up.
scenarios.why: 'Define success' and 'Set the working rules' produce a source map with stale fields, agreed signals, missing-data handling and approval rules. The five-item brief is concrete. The weak points are that the three first reviews have no stated ranking rule and the rules are not saved.

scenarios.prompt: We don't have a CRM. Renewal dates are in contract PDFs in Drive and usage is only what customers tell us on calls. Set up customer success.
scenarios.why: The skill will correctly refuse to guess and will list missing sources. It gives no fallback: no contract-date extraction or consult with Vera's contract-renewal-tracker, no starter Sheets tracker, and no minimum viable signal set when there is no product telemetry. The user ends up with a gap list rather than a working setup.

customer-success-plan.summary: A 32-line placeholder with no supporting files: it drafts a joint success plan anchoring outcomes in the customer's words with baseline, target, milestones on both sides, risks, and a review loop with a decision log.
strengths: Outcomes recorded in the customer's words, each with a stated reason, baseline, measure and target
Proposed targets stay marked proposed until the customer agrees
Every action must link to an outcome; routine activity is removed
Keeps an assumption and decision log
Clear guardrail against turning an internal plan into a customer commitment
missing: Load and save of prior plan versions
Boundary with and handoff from customer-onboarding-plan
Stakeholder map and exec alignment
Value-realisation evidence feeding renewal review and EBR/QBR
Plan template with internal and customer-facing views
Handling of sponsor change or outcome change
Review cadence scheduling

issues.quote: At each review, show what changed, evidence received, decisions made, blocked
issues.problem: The review loop needs the prior plan and log, but there is no step to load or save versions on a platform with no local state.
issues.fix: Load the prior plan from the workspace or Google Docs (run_block) or ask for a paste. Save each version as a dated workspace file, append to the decision log, and schedule_followup for the next review date.

issues.quote: For each outcome list milestones, owner on each side, due date, dependencies,
issues.problem: The milestone fields duplicate customer-onboarding-plan and the boundary between the two is never stated, so both skills can fire on the same request.
issues.fix: State that onboarding ends at first value and this plan covers post-onboarding outcomes, value realisation and renewal readiness. Import the onboarding exit state as the starting baseline.

issues.quote: Record the customer's outcomes in their words, why each matters, baseline,
issues.problem: No stakeholder map and no value-realisation evidence, and nothing feeds the renewal review or an exec business review.
issues.fix: Add a stakeholder map (economic buyer, sponsor, champion, users) and a value-evidence table per outcome that renewal-readiness-review can reuse, plus an EBR/QBR cadence.

issues.quote: Use this for a shared account plan or an internal working draft.
issues.problem: Two audiences, but no rules for what is removed before the customer sees the plan.
issues.fix: Provide a template with customer-facing sections and internal-only sections (risks, commercial notes, health) and a strip-before-sharing checklist.

issues.quote: "account plan", "mutual success plan"
issues.problem: 'account plan' collides with sales account-planning skills on Max and Jordan.
issues.fix: Use 'joint success plan', 'customer success plan' or 'mutual success plan' only.

issues.problem: No rule for when the sponsor or outcomes change mid-plan.
issues.fix: Re-confirm outcomes with the new sponsor before editing targets, mark the old ones superseded in the log, and run churn-risk-review when a sponsor change coincides with an adoption drop.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a joint success plan for Initech. They want to cut new-hire ramp from 3 weeks to 1 with our LMS, and their VP People is the exec sponsor.
scenarios.why: 'Anchor the plan' captures the outcome, baseline (3 weeks), target (1 week, marked proposed), measure, sponsor and review date. 'Add the work' ties milestones on both sides to that outcome. A capable model produces a credible draft, though with no standard template.

scenarios.prompt: Update Initech's success plan for this quarter's review. Last quarter's plan is in a Google Doc, usage dropped 30%, their sponsor changed, and the new VP wants different goals.
scenarios.why: 'Keep it current' says to show what changed and keep a decision log, but never says to retrieve the prior plan (Docs via run_block or a paste). It gives no guidance on re-anchoring outcomes with a new sponsor, on treating sponsor change plus a usage drop as a risk to route to churn-risk-review, or on versioning the updated plan.

expansion-opportunity-brief.job: qualify account expansion opportunity from evidence
expansion-opportunity-brief.summary: A 31-line placeholder with no supporting files: it gates any expansion idea on a documented customer signal, builds a brief (need, evidence, fit, value hypothesis, disconfirming evidence, gaps), classifies readiness, and recommends one customer question and one internal check.
strengths: Requires a documented customer signal; high usage alone is not permission to sell
A 'disconfirming evidence' field forces the model to argue against the opportunity
Price, availability, roadmap and terms are unknown unless an approved source supports them
Clear readiness labels, ending in exactly one customer question and one internal check
Explicit ban on inventing demand, savings, capability or intent
missing: Health and renewal gate before expansion
Handoff to the commercial owner (Max/Jordan)
Named inputs including entitlements and usage over time
Whitespace mapping and assumption-labelled sizing
Portfolio screening mode
Timing relative to the renewal cycle
Brief template

issues.problem: No check of account health or renewal status before pursuing expansion, so it can recommend an upsell into an account with an open Sev1 or a renewal at risk.
issues.fix: Before building the brief, check the health score, churn-risk tier and open escalations. If the account is at risk or inside the notice window with unresolved issues, classify it 'not a fit now' and route it to renewal-readiness-review (renewal first, expansion second).

issues.quote: one customer question and one internal check.
issues.problem: It ends without naming who owns the commercial conversation, and there is no handoff to sales for pricing or quotes.
issues.fix: Name the commercial owner and draft a handoff note (via consult_teammate or handoff_to_expert to Max or Jordan) with the evidence pack, gated on user approval.

issues.quote: Look for an explicit request, repeated limit, new team or use case, sustained
issues.problem: No inputs are named. 'Near capacity' needs contract entitlements and usage over time, and the skill never says where to get them.
issues.fix: List the inputs: contract scope and entitlements, usage vs entitlement for ≥3 periods, requests log. Pull them via run_block (HubSpot/Stripe) or a CSV and compute utilisation in bash_exec.

issues.quote: State the customer need, observed evidence, people affected, present workaround,
issues.problem: No sizing or whitespace view, so the brief can't be prioritised against other opportunities.
issues.fix: Add an optional whitespace map (products × teams) and a seat or usage delta range labelled as an assumption, never as price or ARR unless an approved price book is supplied.

issues.quote: Use this when an account may need more scope, seats, products, or services.
issues.problem: Single-account only, although screening a whole portfolio is a common request.
issues.fix: Add a portfolio mode that applies the signal gate and the health gate to each account and returns a ranked table of ready / needs evidence / not a fit now.

scenarios.prompt: Beta Corp has been at 96% of their 50-seat licence for three months and their ops team asked about the reporting module. Is there an expansion opportunity?
scenarios.why: 'Require a customer signal' finds sustained near-capacity adoption plus an explicit request. 'Build the brief' fills in need, evidence, people affected, workaround, fit, value hypothesis and disconfirming evidence, and marks price unknown. The result is 'ready to validate' with one customer question and one internal check.

scenarios.prompt: Leadership wants every account over 80% seat utilisation flagged for upsell this quarter. One of them, Delta, has an open Sev1 and renews in 30 days.
scenarios.why: The gate correctly says high usage alone is not permission to sell, so most accounts become 'needs evidence'. But the skill has no portfolio screening mode, no rule that an open Sev1 or an at-risk renewal makes an account 'not a fit now' and sends it to renewal-readiness-review, and no handoff of qualified opportunities to the commercial owner (Max/Jordan).

bug-reproduction-report.job: write reproducible bug report for engineering
bug-reproduction-report.summary: Collects and redacts evidence for a reported fault, pushes toward a minimal reproduction with an observed frequency, and returns an eight-field bug report draft without filing it.
strengths: Sets redaction of credentials, personal data and account identifiers before any evidence is copied, and keeps only what is needed to reproduce the fault
Makes the model say whether it reproduced the fault, saw it in logs, or only has the report
Asks for frequency as observed N-of-M rather than 'sometimes'
Clear bans on inventing a stack trace, a step or a root cause
Very tight; no filler
missing: Regression window and last known good version
A decision path for faults that cannot be reproduced
Duplicate search in the tracker or known-issues list
Severity scale, kept separate from priority
A runnable reproduction artefact (script, curl command, failing test, HAR or console capture)
Filing through the GitHub or Linear block after approval
Report template and a worked example
Tool routing (browser for web apps, sandbox for scripts)

issues.quote: State whether you reproduced it yourself, saw it in logs, or only have the
issues.problem: There is no branch for 'could not reproduce' and no instruction on how to attempt a reproduction with the tools available (browser_navigate for web apps, bash_exec when code or a script is supplied). Many real reports end here.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: if not reproduced, list the environment differences tried, give hypothesised conditions labelled as unconfirmed, and write specific questions for the reporter. If a web app is reachable, try the steps in the browser; if code is supplied, try a minimal script in the sandbox.

issues.problem: The report never asks for the last known good version, recent deploys or the regression window, so reports skip the single most useful routing clue for engineers.
issues.fix: Add 'last version or date it worked, and what shipped between then and first seen'. Suggest a bisect range as a check the owner can run, without claiming a cause.

issues.quote: Do not file the issue or assign it;
issues.problem: The platform supports approved outward actions through the GitHub and Linear blocks, and one of the triggers is 'file an issue', yet the skill refuses to file even after approval. It also never checks the tracker for an existing duplicate.
issues.fix: Search the tracker or known-issues list for duplicates first. Draft the issue, show it, and file it through the GitHub or Linear block only after explicit approval. Never assign an owner or set a priority unless the user asks.

issues.quote: Severity and who is affected.
issues.problem: No severity scale is defined, so different reports will rate the same kind of fault differently. Severity (impact) is also not separated from priority (the owner's call).
issues.fix: Define a short scale, for example blocker with data loss or money or security, major with no workaround, minor with a workaround, cosmetic. State that priority belongs to the owner.

issues.quote: Work toward the fewest steps and the least data that still show the fault.
issues.problem: Gives the goal but no method: removing steps one at a time, shrinking the data, or producing a runnable reproduction such as a script, curl command or failing test.
issues.fix: Add a reduction method and ask for a runnable reproduction when possible, such as a curl command, a minimal script or a failing test, attached to the report.

issues.problem: No template or example report ships with the package, and there are no fields for a workaround or for the reporter's contact route.
issues.fix: Ship templates/bug-report.md with the fields in order, including a tested workaround and open questions, plus one worked example.

scenarios.prompt: Since yesterday's deploy the Export CSV button on /reports downloads an empty file for some users. Here's a screenshot, the Sentry event and our version tag v2.14.3. Write this up for the backend team.
scenarios.why: Gather the evidence captures version, first seen and the Sentry text. Smallest reproduction asks for the fewest steps and a frequency. The Report list gives title, steps, expected and actual, environment, evidence quoted exactly and open questions. A capable model will produce a usable ticket, though it will not be prompted to state the last good version (v2.14.2) as a regression window.

scenarios.prompt: A customer says checkout sometimes double-charges on mobile Safari. I can't reproduce it. Here are three support tickets and a Stripe log excerpt with card last4 and emails. File it in Linear as P1.
scenarios.why: The redaction step and 'State whether you reproduced it yourself' handle the privacy and honesty parts well. Nothing covers what to do when it cannot be reproduced: no environment matrix, no hypothesised conditions, no questions for the customer. There is no severity scale for a money-moving bug and no search for duplicates in Linear. 'Do not file the issue' refuses the Linear filing outright instead of drafting it and filing after approval through the Linear block.

code-quality-getting-started.job: set up code review and QA workspace
code-quality-getting-started.summary: Asks the user for the repository, test, CI, release and tracker details, agrees merge and blocker rules, and returns a five-part setup brief naming the first three reviews.
strengths: Covers the right surface: tests, CI jobs, flaky tests, release, logs, tracker and merge rules
Asks for agreement on what counts as a blocker and what evidence is needed to call a bug fixed, which sets up every later skill
Five-part setup brief ending in the first three concrete reviews or test plans
Clear bans on merge, deploy, push, skipping checks and disabling tests
Separates what can be read directly from what must be pasted
missing: Memory persistence and a check for an existing setup
Reading CI config, CODEOWNERS, branch protection and the PR template before asking
GitHub access through connect_integration or the GitHub block, with a paste or zip fallback
Provisional default rules when owners are unavailable
Secrets-handling rule
A first-value review in the session
Map of environments, feature flags and observability

issues.problem: The setup is never saved with memory_store, so the agreed rules, CI map and owners are lost between conversations, and the other Casey skills cannot rely on them.
issues.fix: Save the brief (repositories, required checks, blocker definition, owners, access gaps) to memory. Search memory at the start and skip setup when a record exists; offer to update it when facts change.

issues.quote: Ask for the repository, main branches, languages, how to run the tests
issues.problem: Asks the user for about ten facts up front that the repository answers (CI workflow files, CODEOWNERS, branch protection, PR template, CONTRIBUTING, test commands). This goes against 'ask for the minimum inputs'.
issues.fix: Ask only for the repository and access (connect_integration or the GitHub block; a paste or zip as fallback). Read the config files first, then ask only for what remains: owners, release process, incident log location.

issues.quote: Use this before reviewing a pull request or planning tests.
issues.problem: Read literally, this loads setup before every review or test plan and collides with pull-request-review and test-plan-draft.
issues.fix: Change to: use on the first conversation, or when memory holds no QA setup for this repository, or when the user says the process changed.

issues.quote: Agree who approves and merges a pull request, who can deploy, which checks
issues.problem: There is no fallback when the decision owners are unavailable, so setup can stall indefinitely.
issues.fix: Offer default rules (for example: blocker = incorrect behaviour, data loss or security issue; required checks = those enforced by branch protection), mark them 'provisional, not confirmed', and continue.

issues.problem: A setup skill that asks for repository, log and CI access never warns against pasting tokens or secrets into chat, and never says to use the platform's integration connection instead.
issues.fix: Add: never ask for or accept raw tokens; use connect_integration. If a secret is pasted, do not repeat it and advise the user to rotate it.

issues.quote: The first three reviews or test plans, with reasons.
issues.problem: The session ends with a plan rather than a result. Other experts' getting-started skills put one real read on screen, and Casey's day_one promises a PR review after access.
issues.fix: Once access works, run pull-request-review on the most recent open PR, or offer to do it immediately.

issues.quote: engineering onboarding
issues.problem: The trigger 'engineering onboarding' collides with new-hire onboarding (Ines), and 'start testing' collides with test-plan-draft.
issues.fix: Replace them with 'set up Casey', 'connect my repo for review' and 'QA process setup'.

scenarios.prompt: I just hired Casey. Our repo is github.com/acme/api (Python, pytest, GitHub Actions). Get set up so you can review our PRs.
scenarios.why: 'Ask for the repository, main branches, languages...' produces a long questionnaire of about ten items instead of reading .github/workflows, CODEOWNERS, the PR template and branch protection through the GitHub block and asking only about gaps. The brief is reasonable, but nothing is saved with memory_store, so the next session starts over. No first review is done in the session, even though day_one promises one.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our monorepo link. I honestly don't know how CI works and our tech lead is on leave for two weeks, so just start reviewing.
scenarios.why: 'Never guess how a check works' correctly stops invention, and 'Note which of these can be read directly' hints at reading the config. However, 'Agree who approves and merges' has no fallback when no owner is available: no provisional defaults marked unconfirmed and no path to proceed. The model is likely to stall on questions the user cannot answer instead of reading the CI config and starting a first review.

flaky-test-triage.job: triage intermittent flaky test from run history
flaky-test-triage.summary: Gathers 30-100 CI runs for an intermittent test, groups failures by job, runner, order, time and error, names candidate causes with evidence and confidence, and proposes the smallest confirming check plus fix, quarantine or watch options.
strengths: Refuses to call a test flaky, or a cause found, without run history, and says how many runs were seen and over what dates
Gives the correct cause list (timing, shared state, order, clocks, network, random data, resource limits) with evidence for and against
Proposes the smallest confirming check (rerun loop on one job, fixed seed, run alone) before any change
Quarantine requires an issue and a date, which is senior practice
Bans skipping, disabling, retry-wrapping and deleting tests
missing: A path for real product bugs, with handoff to bug-reproduction-report
CI history source routing and a fallback for expired logs
A flake record template
Decision criteria for quarantine, fix or watch
Rerun sample-size guidance
Suite-level triage for many flaky tests
Finding the commit where the flake first appeared

issues.quote: Look for common causes: timing and waits, shared state between tests,
issues.problem: All candidate causes are test or infrastructure faults. There is no branch for the flake being a real non-deterministic product bug (a race, ordering or timezone bug that users can hit). Quarantine would then hide a production defect.
issues.fix: Add a 'product bug?' check: if the failure reflects behaviour users could hit (a race, lost update, wrong ordering), recommend against quarantine and route to bug-reproduction-report.

issues.quote: Gather the last 30 to 100 runs where possible: pass or fail, job, runner,
issues.problem: Does not say where the history comes from (the GitHub Actions API through the GitHub block or web_fetch, CI exports, JUnit XML) or what to do when logs have expired. Does not use the sandbox to compute failure rates.
issues.fix: Route to the GitHub block or CI export, fall back to a pasted CSV or JUnit files, and compute failure rate per job and runner in bash_exec. If history is short, propose a controlled rerun loop as the evidence source.

issues.quote: Then list who owns the test and the options: fix, quarantine with an issue
issues.problem: Gives no criteria for choosing between fix, quarantine and watch (failure rate, how often it blocks merges, how critical the covered path is).
issues.fix: Add a short rule, for example: quarantine only with an issue, owner and expiry date when it blocks merges and is not a product bug; watch when the rate is below an agreed threshold; fix now when the test covers a critical path.

issues.problem: There is no defined deliverable. The output is spread across the three sections, with no reusable flake record.
issues.fix: Add a template: test id, window and runs seen, failure rate by job, candidate causes table (evidence for and against, confidence), next check, owner, recommendation and review date.

issues.quote: Say when there are too few failures to tell.
issues.problem: Never says how many reruns would be enough. At a 2% failure rate, 20 reruns will usually show nothing, which invites a false 'fixed'.
issues.fix: Have the model compute in the sandbox the number of reruns needed to see at least one failure with about 95% confidence at the observed rate, and use that N in the rerun-loop check.

issues.problem: No guidance when many tests flake together, which usually points to a shared fixture, environment or runner rather than to each test.
issues.fix: Add a suite-level step: cluster the failing tests by shared fixture, job and runner, rank them by failure rate times merge-blocking cost, and triage the shared cause first.

scenarios.prompt: test_checkout_total fails about once a day in GitHub Actions. Here are the last 40 run logs. Is it flaky, and what should we do?
scenarios.why: The skill counts the runs seen and the date range, groups failures by job, runner and error, checks the standard causes (waits, shared state, order, clocks, network, random data, resources) with evidence for and against, proposes a rerun loop or fixed seed, and lists fix, quarantine or watch with the owner. This matches Casey's voice sample.

scenarios.prompt: About 15 of our Playwright e2e tests fail randomly. CI only keeps the last 5 runs, and the team wants to add retries: 3 to everything. Can you sort this out?
scenarios.why: 'Say when there are too few failures to tell' and the ban on retry-wrapping keep the model honest. The skill is built for one test, though: there is no suite-level grouping (a shared fixture, environment or infrastructure cause across 15 tests), no way to create history when logs have expired (a controlled rerun loop with N runs computed in the sandbox), and no guidance on the trade-offs of blanket retries or on the risk that a flake hides a real product race.

incident-postmortem-draft.job: draft blameless incident postmortem from evidence
incident-postmortem-draft.summary: Builds a sourced single-timezone incident timeline with impact, separates the trigger from contributing conditions without blame, and lists owned, dated follow-ups for the incident owner to approve.
strengths: Blameless framing: describe what systems and steps did, not what people failed to do
Separates the trigger from the conditions that let it cause harm (missing tests, alerts, limits, docs, rollback)
Timeline in one time zone, with a source for every entry and gaps marked
Prefers system fixes over reminders, and keeps follow-ups short enough to finish
Unproven causes are stated as unproven, with the evidence that would prove them
missing: Detection and response analysis (time to detect, mitigate, resolve; what went well; where the team got lucky)
Severity level and summary header
Postmortem template
Escalation for personal-data and security incidents, plus redaction
Handoff to comms (Noor) for customer or public statements
Follow-up categories (prevent, detect, mitigate) and a no-invented-owners rule
Source routing through the Slack and GitHub blocks

issues.quote: affected, for how long, and what data or money was involved.
issues.problem: The skill covers data incidents but has no escalation when personal data or security is involved (notification deadlines, counsel or compliance review, the comms owner). Nor does it redact personal data drawn from chat and logs.
issues.fix: Add: if personal data, security or money movement is involved, stop and flag it to the incident owner for compliance or counsel review (hand off to Lena) and for customer comms (Noor), and redact customer identifiers in the draft.

issues.problem: Detection and response are never analysed: how the incident was noticed, time to detect, mitigate and resolve, what went well, where the team got lucky. This is where much of a postmortem's learning comes from.
issues.fix: Add a 'Detection and response' step with the key durations computed from the timeline, how it was noticed (alert or customer), what helped, what slowed the response, and near-misses.

issues.problem: No postmortem template ships with the package, and there is no summary, severity or status header, so structure varies from one incident to the next.
issues.fix: Ship templates/postmortem.md: summary, severity and duration, impact, timeline, trigger and contributing factors, detection and response, what went well, follow-ups table, open questions.

issues.quote: For each follow-up give the action, the problem it prevents, the owner, and a
issues.problem: The skill requires an owner and a due date but does not forbid inventing them, and gives no category (prevent, detect, mitigate) or priority.
issues.fix: Use owners and dates the user supplied, otherwise write 'owner TBD'. Tag each follow-up as prevent, detect or mitigate, with a priority.

issues.quote: Collect alerts, logs, deploys, chat messages, and status updates with
issues.problem: No source routing (the Slack block for channel history, the GitHub block for deploys and PRs) and no fallback to pasted exports. Chat content is copied without a redaction rule.
issues.fix: Name the blocks to use, fall back to pasted exports, and redact customer data and credentials before quoting.

issues.quote: what went wrong
issues.problem: 'what went wrong' and 'root cause analysis' are broad enough to fire for marketing or sales retrospectives, or for bug debugging handled by other experts.
issues.fix: Narrow them to 'incident postmortem', 'outage write-up', 'incident retro', 'post-incident review'.

scenarios.prompt: Our API was down for 47 minutes yesterday after a bad migration. Here's the Slack incident channel export, the deploy log and the PagerDuty alerts. Draft the postmortem.
scenarios.why: The timeline step (one time zone, cited sources, gaps marked), the trigger-vs-conditions step and the owned follow-ups give a solid skeleton. Nothing prompts time to detect, time to mitigate and time to resolve, how the incident was noticed, what went well, or where the team got lucky, and there is no template or summary. The draft will be accurate but thinner than a senior SRE's.

scenarios.prompt: Last week a queue bug sent about 2,000 customer emails to the wrong recipients for 3 hours. I only have a few Slack screenshots and the fix PR. The CTO wants the postmortem by tomorrow and says it was Dave's fault.
scenarios.why: 'Never name a person as the cause' and 'mark gaps' handle the blame pressure and the thin evidence well. The skill misses that this is a personal-data breach: no escalation to compliance or counsel, no mention of notification deadlines, no redaction of the email addresses in the screenshots, and no handoff to comms for the customer statement.

pull-request-review.job: review pull request for bugs and risk
pull-request-review.summary: Reads a PR's description, diff, callers, callees and tests, then lists findings ranked blocker, should fix, question or style, each with file and line, trigger input, confidence (read vs run) and a fix, plus unresolved questions.
strengths: Reads the code the change calls and the code that calls it, not only the changed lines
Each finding gives file and line, trigger input, confidence, and whether it comes from reading or running the code
Four-level ranking that keeps style notes apart and short
Says when the change looks sound instead of padding the list
Will not call code safe, invent untraceable failures, or approve, merge or push
missing: Review lenses: security, compatibility and migrations, concurrency, performance, test quality
Severity definitions and an overall recommendation or summary
Large-diff triage strategy
Drafting inline GitHub comments and posting only after approval
Tool routing (GitHub block, sandbox test run) with a pasted-diff fallback
Handoffs to Devon (security) and regression-risk-review

issues.problem: No review lenses tell the model what to look for beyond generic bugs: authorisation and input validation, secrets, SQL or command injection, backward compatibility and migrations, concurrency, error handling, performance, and whether the tests assert the right thing.
issues.fix: Add a short checklist in a reference file (for example references/review-lenses.md). Route security-sensitive changes to Devon, and changes with a wide blast radius to regression-risk-review.

issues.problem: The four labels have no definitions, and there is no overall recommendation or summary line, so 'is this mergeable?' has no answer format.
issues.fix: Define the labels (blocker = incorrect behaviour, data loss or a security issue on a reachable path; should fix = real defect, lower impact) and open the review with a two-line summary and a recommendation (request changes / comment / no blockers found) that is advisory only.

issues.quote: Note what could not be read, such as a truncated diff or a
issues.problem: No strategy for large or truncated diffs. The model will skim evenly instead of focusing on risky files.
issues.fix: For large diffs: list the files, rank them by risk (data, auth, public API, migrations), review the top ones in depth, state which files were not reviewed, and suggest splitting the PR.

issues.quote: Do not approve, merge, or push
issues.problem: Posting inline review comments to GitHub is an external action the skill never mentions. It needs a draft-then-approve step.
issues.fix: Draft the comments in chat. Post them as a pending GitHub review through the GitHub block only after the user approves the text.

issues.quote: Read the description and linked issue first, then the diff, then the code the
issues.problem: No tool routing for fetching the PR and its surrounding code, and no fallback. The confidence field mentions running code, but the skill never says when to use the sandbox to run the tests.
issues.fix: Fetch the PR through the GitHub block or a .diff URL, or accept a pasted diff. When the repository is accessible, optionally run the affected tests in bash_exec and label those findings 'from running'.

scenarios.prompt: Review PR #482 in acme/api. It adds a refund endpoint for partially shipped orders.
scenarios.why: The reading order (description, linked issue, diff, then callers and callees, then tests and CI) plus per-finding file, line, trigger and confidence produce the review shown in the persona's voice sample. The skill never says how to fetch the PR, but a capable model will use the GitHub block.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a pasted 3,000-line diff (it got cut off at the end). There's no PR description and the tests haven't run. Is it safe to merge today?
scenarios.why: 'Note what could not be read' and 'Never say code is safe' stop false assurance. The skill gives no large-diff strategy (triage files by risk, state coverage, ask to split the PR), no security or compatibility lens to direct attention, and no overall recommendation format to answer 'safe to merge today?'. The result will be honest but unfocused.

regression-risk-review.job: map regression blast radius of code change
regression-risk-review.summary: Traces callers, stored data, configuration and flags, scheduled jobs, public APIs and integrations affected by a change, ranks each risk high, medium, low or unknown with path and test coverage, and lists pre-release checks with owners.
strengths: Looks beyond the diff to stored data written by the old code, flags, scheduled jobs, public APIs and third-party integrations
Each risk carries a traced path with file and line, current test coverage, and how it would show in production
Keeps unknowns visible instead of folding them into low
Records what was searched and what could not be reached
Checks to run each name who should run them before release
missing: Deploy-ordering, mixed-version and rollback compatibility analysis
Caller search method and tool routing, with a coverage count
A likelihood and impact scale
Boundaries and handoffs to pull-request-review, test-plan-draft and Devon
Read-only, draft-only rule for data queries
Summary-first risk table template

issues.problem: Deploy-time risk is missing: old and new versions running side by side during rolling deploys, clients or caches holding old formats, whether a migration or rollback is safe after new writes, and the order in which dependent services deploy.
issues.fix: Add a 'Deploy and rollback' step: can old and new code coexist, is the change expand-then-contract, can it roll back after new data is written, and which consumers must deploy first.

issues.quote: Find every caller of the changed functions, endpoints, events, and database
issues.problem: 'Every' is unachievable without a method. There is no guidance on search (code search, string and reflection references, cross-repository consumers) or on the tools to use.
issues.fix: Name the method: grep or code search in the sandbox on a clone, or through the GitHub block, including string-based and dynamic references. List external consumers from dependency manifests or by asking their owners, and report coverage as a count of callers found vs unreachable.

issues.quote: Use this for a change that touches shared code, data, or other services.
issues.problem: Overlaps pull-request-review (which also reads callers) and test-plan-draft ('List what can break'), with no rule for which to load.
issues.fix: State the boundary: use this for pre-release or cross-service impact on shared code, schemas or APIs; use pull-request-review for line-level defects; hand the top risks to test-plan-draft for cases.

issues.quote: likelihood and impact, with the reason;
issues.problem: No scale maps likelihood and impact to high, medium or low, so rankings are inconsistent.
issues.fix: Define a 3x3 grid (for example, impact high = data loss, money or security, or all users) and derive the rank from it.

issues.quote: List the checks that would reduce the top risks: a test to add, a query on
issues.problem: A 'query on real data' could be read as Casey running production queries. There is no draft-only or read-only rule, and no personal-data caution.
issues.fix: Say the query is drafted as read-only for the data owner to run, returns aggregates rather than personal rows, and is never run against production by Casey.

issues.problem: No summary or template: the top risks and the go/no-go-relevant unknowns are not surfaced first.
issues.fix: Open with a three-line summary (top risk, number of unknowns, recommended checks) followed by a risk table.

scenarios.prompt: This PR changes the signature and rounding of calculate_discount(). What else could this break before we ship Friday?
scenarios.why: 'Trace the callers' finds every call site, stored values and jobs. The risk fields (path with file and line, likelihood and impact, test coverage, how it would show in production) and 'Checks to run' with owners produce a usable risk list. Keeping unknowns separate from low prevents false comfort.

scenarios.prompt: We're renaming orders.status to orders.state and updating the ORM. The table is also read by a BI dashboard and two services in repos you can't access, and we do rolling deploys.
scenarios.why: 'Check stored data written by the old code' and 'Note what you... could not reach' help, and unknowns stay visible. The skill never raises deploy ordering: old and new code running side by side, the expand-and-contract approach to renaming a column, whether rollback is safe after new writes. It also gives no method for listing consumers you cannot read (dependency manifests, org-wide code search, asking the owning teams). The central risk of this change may be missed.

storybrand-messaging.job: build brand messaging framework and one-liner
storybrand-messaging.summary: A vendored wondelai summary of Donald Miller's StoryBrand SB7 framework with a 10-point copy-scoring rubric, a Quick Diagnostic, and six references (BrandScript worksheet, one-liners, website wireframe, email sequences, sales scripts, multi-channel playbooks). No expert has it assigned yet.
strengths: Faithful, well-organised summary of SB7. Each element has a core concept, the reason it works, per-context examples and copy patterns.
Clear 'open when…' routing to six references. Every relative link resolves inside the package.
The Quick Diagnostic and 10-point score give a repeatable audit output with 'changes needed to reach 10/10'.
