job-description-drafting.summary: Drafts or rewrites a job posting in a fixed structure from the role scorecard, writes requirements as outcomes, screens hype and gendered language, never invents pay or title, and returns a paste-ready block as a draft.
strengths: Outcome-based requirements ('Has shipped a service handling production traffic' over '5+ years'), with degree and years floors cut unless the HM defends them.
Hard rule never to guess or derive pay from company size or funding, with UNKNOWN marking.
Every cut line gets a one-line reason; a rewrite shows before and after.
A consistent posting structure including a 90-day ownership section.
Drafts only; never posts or publishes without an explicit yes.
missing: Pay-transparency jurisdiction check and posting-law field list
Categorised inclusive-language lint list (age, ability, gender, nationality)
Posting template with a length target
Searchable external title and job-board formatting guidance
Accommodation statement and required-notice checklist
Requirement sorting (must show before hire, testable in process, learnable after hire, drop), as in the original role-intake-and-job-description

issues.quote: the facts that must appear: title, level, location and work setup, pay band if
issues.problem: Pay is treated as optional ('if it is shareable'). Pay-transparency laws (CO, CA, WA, NY, IL, MN, MA, NJ, VT, DC and others, often including remote roles fillable there; the EU Pay Transparency Directive from June 2026) require a range in the posting or before interview, and the skill never flags this or escalates.
issues.fix: Add a jurisdiction check: if the role can be filled in a covered location, the range is required. Ask the owner for it, mark it UNKNOWN (blocking), and route questions to the attorney. Add a posting-law reference.

issues.quote: No gendered superlatives, no "rockstar" or "ninja", no laundry list of
issues.problem: The language screen covers only gender-coded words and hype. It misses age-coded ('digital native', 'recent grad', 'young team'), ability-coded physical requirements not essential to the job, 'native English speaker' and 'culture fit', and has no word list, so results vary by run.
issues.fix: Ship a references/ lint list by category with suggested replacements, and run it in bash_exec over the draft.

issues.quote: With no scorecard, draft from the title plus the four intake questions and
issues.problem: 'The four intake questions' are defined only in role-intake-and-scorecard's fallback; this skill neither lists them nor tells the model to load that skill, so the model will guess.
issues.fix: List the four questions inline (year-one deliverable, two rule-outs, benchmark person, fill date) or say to read_skill role-intake-and-scorecard.

issues.section: Structure every posting the same way
issues.quote: Pull the day-in-the-life lines verbatim from the intake conversation into the
issues.problem: Pasting HM intake lines verbatim imports internal jargon and possibly coded language, contradicting the language screen that follows.
issues.fix: Use the intake lines as source, then rewrite and run them through the language screen, noting any line that changed meaning.

issues.section: Structure every posting the same way
issues.quote: equal-opportunity close.
issues.problem: The close has no reasonable-accommodation contact line and no check for required notices (e.g. AI-use notices where applicants are screened by automated tools under NYC LL144 or Illinois rules, E-Verify participation).
issues.fix: Add an accommodation line with a named contact, and a checklist of jurisdiction-dependent notices for the owner or attorney to confirm.

issues.quote: The finished posting shown in chat, one round of edits, then a clean block
issues.problem: There is no reusable posting template, length target or guidance on a searchable external title (internal levels like 'MTS III' hurt discoverability), so output shape and length drift.
issues.fix: Ship templates/posting.md with the section headings, a 350-700 word target, and a title rule (market title plus level in brackets).

scenarios.prompt: Write the posting for our Senior Backend Engineer, remote US, band $170-200k, scorecard attached.
scenarios.why: The fixed structure (mission, 90-day ownership, 3-6 outcome must-haves, labelled nice-to-haves, offer with the band as given, EEO close), outcome-style requirements and a language screen yield a clean, paste-ready posting with UNKNOWNs listed, gated as a draft.

scenarios.prompt: Rewrite our old product designer ad for a remote-anywhere-US role: '10+ years, BA required, digital native, rockstar'. Leave salary off — the founder won't publish it.
scenarios.why: 'Rockstar', the years floor and the degree get cut with the one-line reasons and before/after. But 'digital native' (age-coded) is not on the skill's list. More seriously, 'pay band if it is shareable' plus 'pay... only as the user stated' leads the model to quietly omit the range. It never flags that CO, CA, WA, NY, IL and others require a range for roles fillable there, and never routes to the attorney, so the owner gets a posting that may be unlawful to publish, with no warning.

automate-finance-reporting.job: load and QA data into finance ledger
automate-finance-reporting.summary: A short principles list for moving an export into Daniel's finance ledger: show a column mapping, dedupe on a natural key, send bad rows to a needs-a-look list, re-read and QA each write, and name the refresh path.
strengths: Makes the mapping visible before loading and lists unmapped columns instead of dropping them
Unparseable rows go to a needs-a-look list with row numbers and never reach the totals
Holds the read when a QA check fails and names the failed check
Defines staleness against the ledger's own refresh promise and flags it in every read that uses it
Fallback refuses to write the ledger when no dedupe key exists
missing: Ledger schema/template shared across Daniel's skills
Closed-period lock and restatement log with approval
Normalisation rules for sign, gross vs net, currency/FX date and period assignment
Independent control-total check with a tolerance
Load-summary and mapping-table templates
Tool routing (Sheets/Gmail blocks, bash_exec for parse, dedupe and totals)
PII handling for payroll and card exports
A worked example mapping (e.g. Stripe or QuickBooks export to ledger)

issues.quote: Replace on the natural key — date plus line plus source — newest wins.
issues.problem: A re-pulled export silently overwrites actuals in closed periods with no restatement record. At transaction grain the key also merges legitimate rows (two bills on the same day to the same line), so totals come out too low.
issues.fix: Define the grain. Key on period + line + source + source record ID. Refuse writes into periods marked closed unless the owner approves a restatement, and log the old and new value for every replaced row.

issues.quote: and the target ledger shape.
issues.problem: The ledger schema is never defined here or in any sibling skill, so each load invents its own columns and the dedupe and QA can't stay consistent across sources.
issues.fix: Ship templates/ledger-schema.md (period, line/account, cost center, amount, currency, basis, source, source_ref, load_id, loaded_at) and map every source to it.

issues.section: Map the columns before loading anything
issues.quote: Source column to ledger column, one row per mapping, with the transform
issues.problem: There are no normalisation rules for sign convention (credits and refunds), gross vs net, currency and FX rate date, or assigning periods by posting date vs transaction date. These are the usual causes of a load that ties but is wrong.
issues.fix: Add a normalisation checklist that must be filled in on the mapping table before the first load.

issues.section: Map the columns before loading anything
issues.quote: Show the mapping table before the first load, not after.
issues.problem: Showing the mapping is not the same as getting approval, so the first write to the shared ledger can go ahead without the owner confirming it.
issues.fix: Run a dry-run load summary and wait for the owner's yes before the first write. Later loads with an unchanged mapping can proceed and report.

issues.section: QA every write with a live re-read
issues.quote: Row counts match, rollups reconcile to the source total, and dates
issues.problem: QA only compares the ledger with the file that was just loaded. That catches load errors but not a bad export. There is no independent control total and no tolerance.
issues.fix: Tie to an independent control total (the source system's own report, the bank, or the prior period roll-forward) with a stated tolerance.

issues.quote: intelligence (BI) workspace, a report email, or a plain export file —
issues.problem: No tool routing. It never says to read via the Sheets or Gmail blocks or read_workspace_file, or to parse, dedupe and total in bash_exec, so the arithmetic may be done in-context.
issues.fix: Name the read path per source type and require the sandbox for parsing, dedupe and totals.

issues.quote: What triggers the refresh, who owns the source, and what stale looks
issues.problem: The description promises to 'connect a number source', but the body never uses connect_integration or schedule_routine to set up the refresh it asks to be named.
issues.fix: Add steps: connect_integration when a source is missing, and schedule_routine for the refresh on the owner's yes.

issues.problem: No privacy handling for payroll, card or bill exports, which carry employee salaries, names and card numbers.
issues.fix: Aggregate or strip employee-level pay and card data before loading, and never write it to memory.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Stripe balance-transactions CSV for August. Load it into the finance ledger sheet and tell me if it ties.
scenarios.why: The model will show a mapping table, dedupe, re-read and report counts, which matches the sections in order. Nothing tells it about gross vs net (payouts are net of fees and refunds), sign convention for refunds, or which ledger columns exist ('the target ledger shape' is never defined). So 'rollups reconcile to the source total' can pass while revenue sits net of fees on the wrong lines.

scenarios.prompt: Our accountant re-exported July from QuickBooks after the close. A few amounts changed. Reload it and dedupe against what's already there.
scenarios.why: 'Replace on the natural key — date plus line plus source — newest wins' tells the model to overwrite July, a closed period, with no restatement flag, no before/after diff and no owner approval. The only gate covers structural changes and new writers, not changing locked actuals, so board-reported numbers change silently.

budget-vs-actuals-and-reforecast.job: check budget pacing and reforecast plan
budget-vs-actuals-and-reforecast.summary: Reads every budget line against plan with a straight-line run-rate landing, flags overs and 15%-unders, grades the forecast Base/Adverse/Opportunity, and sets rules for driver-based re-forecasts and draft reallocations.
strengths: Driver-first forecasting with an owner per driver in an assumption log
Explicit ban on silent re-baselining; restate the prior forecast and name what moved
Tracks forecast accuracy (bias direction and miss size) and feeds repeat misses back into drivers
Names missing periods and asks for the export instead of projecting across them
Reallocations are drafts with total held flat and the approving owner named
missing: Mode selector (pace / re-forecast / annual plan)
Committed and one-off vs recurring split, and seasonality in landings
Direction logic for revenue lines vs cost lines
Use of the saved variance threshold and quiet floor
Re-forecast bridge and pace-table templates
Dated forecast snapshot/version log for accuracy tracking
Headcount-plan handling (start dates, loaded cost)
Handoff to variance-and-flux-analysis for 'why' and to cash for cash impact

issues.quote: under plan too — budget left on the table is a miss, not a saving.
issues.problem: The hardcoded 15% ignores the variance threshold and quiet floor saved at onboarding. Every cost underspend is labelled a miss even when it is a real saving. For revenue lines, 'projected to pass its plan' flags good news as a problem.
issues.fix: Use the saved threshold and quiet floor. Classify under-pace as timing, deferred or true saving. Reverse the flag direction for revenue and income lines.

issues.section: Read every line against its plan
issues.quote: current run rate holds. Show the math, not just the verdict.
issues.problem: Only a straight-line projection is described. Annual prepaids, payroll cycles, one-off invoices and seasonal lines land wrong, which the persona's own 'pull-forward' voice sample shows.
issues.fix: Split each line into committed or scheduled spend plus recurring run rate. Use prior-year seasonality or the payment schedule when available, and state the method per line.

issues.quote: Use when the user asks about budgets, pacing against plan, forecasts, re-forecasts, annual plans, or where a period lands at the current run rate.
issues.problem: 'forecasts' and the trigger 'budget vs actuals' overlap with variance-and-flux-analysis ('actual vs plan', 'why did we miss plan') and cash-treasury-and-fx ('cash forecast'), so a 'budget vs actuals, why did marketing miss?' request can load the wrong skill.
issues.fix: Scope it to pacing, landing and re-forecasting the operating plan, and add routing: why a line moved → variance-and-flux-analysis; cash forecasts → cash-treasury-and-fx.

issues.section: Name the drivers before the dollars
issues.quote: Forecast driver-first: name the 5-15 drivers that actually move the
issues.problem: No mode selector. A Monday pace check is told to build 5-15 drivers first, and pace check, re-forecast and annual plan need different inputs and outputs.
issues.fix: Open with a step that picks the mode (pace check / re-forecast / annual plan) and lists the inputs and output for each.

issues.quote: at 30% of the source line, and say which owner approved each move.
issues.problem: The 30% cap is an invented policy stated as a rule, which goes against the persona's ban on inventing figures.
issues.fix: Use the owner's saved reallocation policy, and ask once if none is saved.

issues.quote: One line per budget line, then the total, then the forecast grade and
issues.problem: There is no re-forecast bridge template, and 'under 200 words' can't hold one line per budget line for a 30-line budget.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the pace table and the re-forecast bridge (prior → driver deltas → new). Attach the table and keep the narrative under 200 words.

issues.quote: re-baseline. Track accuracy against the prior forecast — bias direction
issues.problem: Nothing tells the model to save a dated forecast snapshot, so accuracy can't be tracked across sessions.
issues.fix: Write a dated forecast version to a forecast log in the ledger workbook on every re-forecast.

issues.section: Read every line against its plan
issues.quote: Per line: actuals to date, the share of the plan already used, days
issues.problem: No tool routing for the per-line arithmetic across dozens of lines, and no instruction to save the dated read.
issues.fix: Compute in bash_exec from the ledger export and write the dated read to the workspace.

scenarios.prompt: Are we on plan for September? Budget sheet and ledger are connected. It's the 16th.
scenarios.why: 'Read every line against its plan' gives run-rate landings and flags, which is what's wanted. But run rate is straight-line only, so an annual software renewal booked on the 3rd projects to roughly double. The fixed 15% under-pace flag ignores the saved variance threshold and quiet floor, and calls cost savings misses.

scenarios.prompt: Q3 reforecast: we hired 3 fewer AEs than planned, our biggest customer churned in August, and August actuals aren't in the ledger yet. Rebuild the full-year forecast.
scenarios.why: 'Name the gaps' correctly asks for the August export instead of projecting, and 'Re-forecast without re-baselining' asks to restate the prior forecast and name what moved. There is no bridge template (prior → driver deltas → new), no dated snapshot to measure accuracy against, and no link to saas-gtm-finance for the churn/ARR effect, so the result depends on the model's own FP&A habits.

cash-treasury-and-fx.summary: Builds a direct-method 13-week cash view with Week-0 actuals and variance tagging, dual-basis runway, minimum-cash floor and stress case, working-capital read, renewal-window commitment scan, FX exposure sizing and covenant headroom.
strengths: Correct direct-method build with a Week-0 actuals column and a fixed timing / assumption-miss picklist
Runway computed on current and forecast burn, with a stated preference
Minimum-cash policy, liquidity headroom line and a concrete default stress case
Roll-forward discipline: replace with actuals, drop the oldest week, carry flags until cleared
Hard limits: no payment, draw, hedge or vendor contact; FX rates dated and never blended
missing: Receipts timing from aging buckets and collection history
Checklist of often-missed outflows (payroll tax, VAT/sales tax, annual prepaids, estimated tax, capex)
Bank concentration, insured-limit and placement checks
Cash by entity, restricted and trapped cash, intercompany flows
Covenant calendar with test dates and agreement definitions
13-week template
FX transaction vs translation distinction and a named reference-rate source (e.g. central bank via web_fetch)
Handoff of the chase list to the AR/bookkeeping teammate

issues.section: Build the 13-week cash view by the direct method
issues.problem: No method for timing receipts (aging buckets × historical collection rates, customer-level for the top accounts) and no checklist of commonly missed outflows: payroll taxes and benefits, sales tax/VAT, annual prepaids, estimated tax, debt service, capex.
issues.fix: Add a receipts-timing method and a disbursement checklist to run before the view is shown.

issues.problem: The skill is named treasury but has no bank counterparty or concentration check (insured limits, single-bank exposure), no idle-cash placement policy, and no cash-by-entity or trapped-cash view.
issues.fix: Add a treasury block: balances by bank and entity, concentration against insured limits, restricted and trapped cash, and placement questions sized for the owner.

issues.quote: numbers, and flag any quarter that lands inside 20% of a covenant line.
issues.problem: Covenants are often tested monthly or at all times (minimum liquidity), and their definitions (adjusted EBITDA, eligible cash) come from the credit agreement, not plain-words restatement.
issues.fix: Build a covenant calendar with test dates and definitions quoted from the agreement. Check headroom at each test date and route interpretation to counsel or the lender.

issues.section: Build the 13-week cash view by the direct method
issues.quote: opening balance, operating inflows by week from collections and
issues.problem: 'from collections and revenue' brings accrual revenue into a direct-method view and risks double-counting billings already in AR.
issues.fix: Use receipts only: AR collections plus new billings expected to be collected within the window.

issues.quote: a reasonable default stress is a 30% collection delay plus
issues.problem: '30% collection delay' is ambiguous (30% of receipts delayed, or all receipts 30% later, and by how many weeks), so stress results aren't comparable week to week.
issues.fix: Specify it, e.g. shift 30% of expected receipts out by 3 weeks, and save the definition.

issues.quote: The 13-week table, runway with its basis, the working-capital read, the
issues.problem: There is no template, and the full stack exceeds the persona's 200-word reads, so the shape drifts week to week.
issues.fix: Ship a 13-week template and lead the message with runway, the floor-cross week and the top flags, with the table attached.

issues.quote: needle most, largest first, each with the owner who can chase it.
issues.problem: No handoff for the chase. AR follow-up belongs to Mina's accounts-receivable-follow-up on the team.
issues.fix: Offer to hand the list to the bookkeeper/AR teammate as a drafted follow-up brief.

issues.quote: Bank balances, the accounts receivable (AR) aging, the accounts payable
issues.problem: Six inputs are listed with no priority, and there is no minimum-viable set for a fast first read.
issues.fix: Rank them: bank balance + payroll + recurring payables unlock a first view; AR/AP aging, vendor inventory and facility terms refine it.

scenarios.prompt: Build me a 13-week cash forecast. Attached: bank balances, AR aging and AP aging CSVs. Payroll is biweekly at $85k and our floor is $250k.
scenarios.why: The direct-method section, the Week-0 column, 'Compute runway twice' with the floor and a stress case, and the top-five-invoices read give a senior-shaped view. The gap: nothing says how to turn aging buckets into weekly receipts, or to add payroll taxes and benefits on top of the $85k.

scenarios.prompt: We have a UK parent and a US sub, a revolver with a minimum-liquidity covenant, and I only have bank balances — no AR detail. When do we breach?
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly runs cash-only from bank history with collections UNKNOWN, and 'Never blend rates' covers translation. But covenant headroom is checked per quarter only, while minimum-liquidity covenants are usually tested monthly or at all times. There is no entity-level or trapped-cash view and no step to quote the covenant definition from the credit agreement, so the breach week can be wrong.

close-controls-and-accounting.summary: Supports month-end close with a checklist (owner, reviewer, risk, dates, status), day targets and KPIs, a list of accrual categories, the reconciliation order, a flux hand-off, preparer/reviewer segregation, and PBC folder staging.
strengths: Every checklist item has a separate owner and reviewer, risk level, dates and status; open items carry forward
Realistic small-team day targets (flash day 2, hard close day 5-7) and close KPIs (days-to-close, manual JE count)
Reconciliation order starts with cash, and nothing is forced to tie
Soft-close preliminary vs hard-close final labelling
Clear limits: never book, file or sign off; tax and legal to CPA/attorney with a one-line brief
missing: Shipped close-checklist template with day-by-day dependencies
Reconciliation standard: reconciling-item categories, aging, materiality, sign-off
Completeness tests for unrecorded liabilities
Deferred revenue, prepaid and fixed-asset roll-forwards
JE review criteria
Period-lock step that feeds automate-finance-reporting
Escalation when the reviewer role is vacant
Handoff to the bookkeeper teammate (Mina) for entries and statement reconciliation

issues.section: Build the checklist from the template
issues.quote: Build the checklist from the template
issues.problem: It names a template the package doesn't ship. The five block names don't give a close calendar, task dependencies or day-by-day sequence.
issues.fix: Ship templates/close-checklist.csv with business day, dependency, owner, reviewer, risk and evidence-link columns, pre-filled for a small team.

issues.quote: Cash to bank first, then AR (accounts receivable) to the aging, AP
issues.problem: It gives an order but no method: book vs statement balance, reconciling-item categories (timing, error, unrecorded), aging of open items, materiality threshold, preparer/reviewer sign-off.
issues.fix: Add a reconciliation standard with a one-page recon template, or route to a merged account-reconciliation package.

issues.quote: Prepaid burn-down, unpaid vendor bills, payroll cut-off, deferred
issues.problem: It lists categories but not how to find missing accruals: subsequent-disbursement search, recurring-vendor comparison with prior months, open POs and receipts, reversal of last month's accruals.
issues.fix: Add the four completeness tests and a missing-accrual list format with estimate basis labelled INFERENCE.

issues.quote: (SOX) basics come down to the same thing — preparer and reviewer are
issues.problem: This misstates SOX, which covers scoping, key controls, ITGCs, management-review precision and operating-effectiveness testing. Most small private teams aren't SOX-scoped, so the framing misleads either way.
issues.fix: Reframe as small-team internal-control basics. If the company is SOX-scoped or preparing for it, route to the controller or auditor.

issues.quote: Compare against last period and against plan using the variance skill,
issues.problem: The sibling is named vaguely, and the flux review has no materiality threshold.
issues.fix: Name variance-and-flux-analysis and apply the saved variance threshold and quiet floor.

issues.section: Build the checklist from the template
issues.problem: No journal-entry review criteria: manual, top-side, round-number, post-close and self-approved entries.
issues.fix: Add a JE review screen to the checklist and log exceptions.

issues.problem: No deferred-revenue or fixed-asset roll-forward (opening + additions − releases/depreciation = closing), even though both appear in the categories.
issues.fix: Add roll-forward tie-outs for deferred revenue, prepaids and fixed assets.

issues.quote: segregation, and keep the evidence trail in Drive.
issues.problem: It assumes Google Drive with no fallback or naming convention.
issues.fix: Use Drive when connected, otherwise the workspace, with a period/account/preparer naming convention.

scenarios.prompt: It's close week. Build our September close checklist from the attached sheet and tell me what's overdue.
scenarios.why: 'Build the checklist from the template' specifies owner, separate reviewer, risk, frequency, due and completion dates and status, and 'Watch the close on request' gives done, due and overdue with owners. That is a usable close watch, although day-by-day dependencies are missing.

scenarios.prompt: Auditors sent a 60-item PBC list, deferred revenue doesn't tie to our Stripe subscription report by $42k, and our controller left last month.
scenarios.why: PBC staging (one folder per request ID) and 'Nothing is forced to tie' are right. There is no deferred-revenue roll-forward method and no reconciling-item categorisation to break down the $42k. The skill also doesn't address the missing reviewer when the controller leaves (a segregation gap to escalate), so the model improvises the core accounting work.

daniel-getting-started.job: onboard user and capture finance preferences
daniel-getting-started.summary: Onboards the user to Daniel: a brief hello, an immediate read on anything handed over, the revenue model first, a one-line connection check, then skippable one-at-a-time preference questions saved to memory, working files set up, a starter menu and four opt-in routines.
strengths: Gets to a real read before asking setup questions
Checks connections once, never re-asks, never blocks on a connector; paste or upload always works
Questions are skippable and one per message, saved to memory as they arrive
Sensible default variance threshold and quiet floor
Routines stay off until yes, run in the user's timezone, and only stage drafts
missing: Budget-set and ledger schema templates, created with approval
Cash floor, discount bands and approval authority, renewal window
Entity structure and reporting vs functional currencies
Accounting system, CPA and controller contacts for handoffs
Urgent-ask override
Question priority and inference from uploaded data
SAMPLE labelling for demo reads

issues.section: Ask the rest one at a time
issues.quote: Each is skippable, one question per message: fiscal year end, currency,
issues.problem: This is a 14-question serial interview with no priority order and no inference from data already handed over (FYE, currency and basis are usually visible in the export).
issues.fix: Ask only the 2-3 facts that block the next read. Infer the rest from exports and confirm in one line, and ask the others when a skill first needs them.

issues.section: Ask the rest one at a time
issues.problem: It never collects facts its siblings rely on: the cash floor (cash-treasury-and-fx), discount bands and approval authority (deal-economics), the renewal window, legal entities and reporting currency, and CPA/controller contacts for handoffs.
issues.fix: Add these to the question bank, tagged by the skill that needs each one.

issues.section: Save every answer as one fact per line
issues.quote: destination — then set up the files that hold working state: the budget
issues.problem: It creates the budget set and ledger in the user's workspace with no location asked, no approval and no column schema, so every later skill works on an undefined shape.
issues.fix: Ask where the files should live, propose a shipped schema (templates/budget-set, templates/ledger), and create them on yes.

issues.section: Ask the revenue model first, and nothing else yet
issues.quote: Ask the revenue model first, and nothing else yet
issues.problem: This conflicts with 'Check connections first, never re-ask' and 'Start the first real read at once', leaving the order unclear.
issues.fix: State one order: read anything handed over, check connections silently, then ask the revenue model if it isn't already clear.

issues.section: Start the first real read at once
issues.quote: If they hand over anything with numbers in it, start the matching skill
issues.problem: No override for an urgent first ask (payroll, runway, a live deal), which should skip onboarding and route straight to that skill.
issues.fix: Add: if the first message is a time-bound question, route to that skill now and defer onboarding to after the answer.

issues.quote: Nothing handed over: run one line of the starter menu on an example so
issues.problem: Example figures could be taken as the user's numbers, which goes against the persona's no-invented-figures rule.
issues.fix: Label every example figure SAMPLE and never write it to the ledger or memory.

issues.quote: Google Sheets for the budget set and the finance ledger, Google Drive
issues.problem: The connector paragraph repeats the persona identity almost word for word, which wastes tokens every time the skill loads.
issues.fix: Cut it to one line pointing to the persona's connection list.

issues.section: Save every answer as one fact per line
issues.quote: Write each answer to memory as it arrives — company, fiscal year end,
issues.problem: No memory hygiene rule. Bank account numbers, credentials or salary data could end up in durable memory.
issues.fix: Store preferences and pointers only, never account numbers, credentials or employee pay.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Daniel — we're a 12-person B2B SaaS. Here's our 2026 budget sheet and August's P&L from QuickBooks.
scenarios.why: 'Start the first real read at once' runs a pace read on the budget and P&L, then the connection check and one-at-a-time questions follow. A capable model will skip asking the revenue model the user already gave, save facts to memory and show the starter menu.

scenarios.prompt: I don't have a budget, our Xero is a mess I can't export yet, we're UK with a US sub, and I need to know if we can make payroll in 6 weeks.
scenarios.why: Nothing tells the model to put an urgent question ahead of onboarding. With no numbers, the fallback says to 'run one line of the starter menu on an example', which is the wrong move here. The model should ask for bank balances and payroll dates and route to cash-treasury-and-fx. The question list also assumes a single currency and entity.

deal-economics-and-pricing-guardrails.job: check deal discount against pricing guardrails
deal-economics-and-pricing-guardrails.summary: Builds a current/proposed/ask deal P&L, checks the discount against saved bands and routes it to the right approver, frames give-get counters, logs concessions, and models the per-tier mix impact and grandfathering cost of a price change.
strengths: One table with current, proposed and ask so the gap is visible
Never approves or rounds into a band; out-of-band asks go to a named approver with margin impact
Every concession is logged with approver, reason and margin impact; no concession exists only in a thread
Grandfathering cost is sized as its own line and per-segment effects are called out
Holds the verdict when no bands are saved; revenue-only math labelled INFERENCE
missing: Effective-discount math (ramps, free months, escalators, payment terms)
Cost-to-serve component list
Approval matrix by discount % and deal size
Non-standard terms, MFN/precedent and revenue-recognition flags
Elasticity/churn scenarios for price changes
Handoff to sales, deal desk and pricing strategy teammates
Deal P&L and concession-log templates

issues.problem: No effective-price math: multi-year ramps, free months, escalators, TCV vs ACV, the time value of payment terms, or non-cash concessions (waived services, extended terms). The discount checked against the band understates the real give.
issues.fix: Compute the effective discount including all concessions and the payment-term cost, and check that figure against the band.

issues.quote: Revenue, cost to serve, margin in currency and in percent, and payback
issues.problem: Cost to serve has no defined components, so margin-floor checks aren't comparable across deals.
issues.fix: Define the components (hosting/COGS, support, onboarding/implementation, payment fees, partner rev share) and label each FACT or INFERENCE.

issues.section: Model a pricing change before it ships
issues.quote: Model the mix impact across tiers, state plainly who wins and who pays
issues.problem: No elasticity or churn assumptions, ranges or scenarios, and no handoff to the teammate who owns pricing strategy.
issues.fix: Require base/adverse/upside churn and downgrade assumptions labelled INFERENCE, and consult Zara's pricing-and-packaging for the strategy call.

issues.section: Check the ask against the bands
issues.problem: No flag for non-standard terms that carry risk beyond margin: MFN or price-precedent clauses, termination for convenience, payment terms over 12 months, and their revenue-recognition effects.
issues.fix: Add a non-standard-terms check that routes to the CPA or legal with a one-line brief.

issues.quote: Counter with cited numbers, trade give-get concessions — term, volume,
issues.problem: Walk-away lines and live counters are sales negotiation. The persona says closing a sale goes to sales with the deal math.
issues.fix: Frame this as a drafted give-get menu for the sales or deal-desk teammate (Max/Jordan) via consult or handoff.

issues.section: Check the ask against the bands
issues.quote: Discount floors, revenue-share bands, and cap rules. Inside the bands
issues.problem: No approval-matrix structure (tiers by discount % and deal size, term and payment-term limits), so routing is ad hoc.
issues.fix: Save the matrix as a table at onboarding and route by looking it up.

issues.quote: Approver, reason, and margin impact, written to the deal and pricing
issues.problem: The log schema is too thin to audit precedent or expiry.
issues.fix: Log date, deal, list price, net price, effective discount, give, get, approver, expiry and precedent flag.

issues.quote: The comparison table, the guardrail check with its routing, the
issues.problem: No template for the comparison table or the approval note, so outputs vary deal to deal.
issues.fix: Ship templates for the deal P&L table and the approval/routing note.

scenarios.prompt: Acme wants 25% off a 3-year $120k/yr deal on net-60. Floor is 70% gross margin; AEs can give 15%, VP up to 25%. Does it clear?
scenarios.why: 'Build the deal P&L' and 'Check the ask against the bands' produce the comparison table and route it to the VP with the margin impact, and give-get framing is supplied. A senior would also price net-60 and the three-year commitment into the effective discount, which the skill never mentions, but a capable model gets the core call right.

scenarios.prompt: We want to raise Pro from $49 to $69 next quarter and grandfather existing customers for 6 months. We have no churn data by tier — what's the revenue impact?
scenarios.why: 'Model a pricing change before it ships' asks for mix impact, winners and payers, and grandfathering cost as its own line, which is the right shape. There is no guidance on churn or elasticity assumptions, labelled ranges or scenarios when data is missing, and no handoff to Zara's pricing-and-packaging, so the result is a single-point guess.

commercial-launch-strategy.job: plan product launch and go/no-go readiness
commercial-launch-strategy.summary: Walks Zara through the commercial side of a release (say-back, tier call, market story, enablement/partner spec with owners, a 24-hour commercial go/no-go gate, pre-mortem and a 30/60/90 measure) as a single inline SKILL.md with no templates.
strengths: Separates the commercial 'sell' gate from the product owner's 'ship' gate and saves beside the product owner's plan rather than duplicating it
Clear tier ladder (quiet, standard, tentpole) that frames the tier as the owner's budget decision and says what a bigger tier would add
Strong no-invention and per-asset approval rules; claims-you-will-not-make and UNKNOWN labelling built in
Includes a commercial pre-mortem with trigger and contingency per failure mode
missing: Scored launch-tier rubric
T-minus back-planned timeline
Legal/claims and regulatory review in the gate
Descope / delay / accept-risk decision options
Existing-customer communication and pricing migration/grandfathering
Press embargo and analyst briefing guidance
Pre-launch baselines and targets for the 90-day measure
Explicit handoff to the product owner / Alex's launch plan
Channel plan (owned, rented, borrowed) for standard and tentpole tiers
Launch brief template

issues.quote: Hold it 24 hours before launch: pricing signed off, sales and success
issues.problem: The gate omits legal/claims review and a rollback or comms-holdback plan, both of which Zara's launch-readiness-check routine scores ('legal vetted', 'rollback written'). A gate held 24 hours out also leaves no time to clear a red item.
issues.fix: Use a two-stage gate: go/no-go at about T-10 business days with descope/delay/accept-risk options, then a T-1 confirmation. Add legal/claims review, rollback/holdback and the support runbook, matching the routine's checklist item for item.

issues.quote: Net-new revenue, competitive shift, and press-worthiness decide it. A quiet
issues.problem: The tier has no scoring rubric or thresholds, so two runs can give different tier calls. The paragraph is also copied almost word for word from Alex's product-launch-plan.
issues.fix: Add a scored tier matrix (revenue at stake, share of base affected, competitive shift, press value, pricing change) with cut-offs per tier, and ship it as references/tier-matrix.md.

issues.quote: owner runs the ship itself. Start from the release, the positioning, the
issues.problem: The skill names the product owner but never tells the model to read or consult that owner's launch plan. On a team with Alex, both skills fire on 'launch tier', 'go/no-go' and 'launch retrospective' and produce competing tier calls and gates.
issues.fix: Add step 0: memory_search / read_workspace_file for the product launch plan, or consult_teammate with the product expert. Take the ship date and tier from that plan. Drop 'go/no-go' and 'launch retrospective' from the triggers or qualify them as 'commercial'.

issues.section: Spec what the field needs in hand
issues.quote: due date working back from launch day.
issues.problem: The description promises a 'sequenced plan', but only the enablement assets are back-planned. There is no T-minus timeline for pricing sign-off, partner and marketplace listings, the press embargo, the campaign or the internal launch.
issues.fix: Add a 'Back-plan the launch' step with a T-minus milestone table (T-6w to T+90) listing owner, dependency and gate per milestone.

issues.quote: blocks the commercial launch even if the software ships. Hold a pre-mortem
issues.problem: The pre-mortem sits inside the 24-hour gate section but is meant to run before the plan is locked, so a step-by-step model runs it too late.
issues.fix: Move the pre-mortem to its own step directly after the market-facing story.

issues.quote: Launch pipeline created, sales-accepted leads from launch sources, asset
issues.problem: The skill sets no baseline or target before launch, gives no attribution window, and has no mechanism to actually produce the 30/60/90 reads.
issues.fix: Require a target and baseline per metric before launch, state the attribution rule, and schedule_followup the 30/60/90 reads after approval.

issues.section: Say back what is shipping, and for whom
issues.quote: guessing. If the positioning has not been locked, do that first — a
issues.problem: The skill doesn't route to the positioning-and-messaging skill. It also has no existing-customer lens (migration, grandfathering, notice periods) when a release changes pricing or packaging.
issues.fix: Name the sibling skill explicitly, and add an existing-customer comms and pricing-migration line to the market-facing story.

issues.problem: No launch-brief template ships with the package, so the six hand-back parts come out in a different shape on every run.
issues.fix: Add templates/launch-brief.md (tier call, story, enablement spec table, T-minus plan, gate checklist, pre-mortem, 90-day measure).

scenarios.prompt: We're shipping SSO and audit logs for the Enterprise tier on Nov 12. What tier should this launch be, and what does sales need in hand?
scenarios.why: The steps map directly onto the ask. Say back what ships, size the tier on revenue, competitive shift and press-worthiness, draft the one-line message with three proofs, then spec the pitch sheet, talk track, battlecard lines and pricing state with owners and dates. A capable model produces a usable commercial plan. The tier call rests on the model's own judgement because the skill gives no criteria thresholds.

scenarios.prompt: Launch is in 9 days. Pricing still isn't approved, positioning is a draft, and Alex (product) wants to announce on the date anyway. Are we ready?
scenarios.why: The skill says to lock positioning first, and 'anything untrue blocks the commercial launch', so the model will say not ready. It gives no descope, delay or accept-risk options, which the persona's routine expects. It has no soft-launch pattern (ship without new pricing, 'contact sales'), no step to consult Alex's ship plan, and no legal check on claims. The answer becomes a block without a workable path.

competitive-intelligence.summary: Builds a tiered competitor watch list, logs dated and linked changes, writes a 'so-what' per material move, converts it into win strategy, and maintains one-page battlecards with win/battle/lose zones and Know/Say/Show under an owner and a refresh policy.
strengths: Battlecard spec is current practice: win/battle/lose zones, Know/Say/Show, head-to-head vs rip-and-replace variants, 90-day deal-intel pane
Refresh on signal with a same-week versioned diff and a biweekly floor for Tier 1; ownerless cards are retired
Hard evidence discipline: every line linked and dated, failed fetches logged, a quiet market gets one line
So-what mapped by move type (launch to positioning, price to packaging, content to enablement)
missing: Competitor pricing comparison table method
Landscape / positioning map
Win-loss interview and reason-coding method
Landmine / trap-setting discovery questions on the card
Source evidence grading and watch/notify/act triage
CI ethics and comparative-claims legal review
Intake of field-reported intel (rep submissions)
Brief and battlecard templates

issues.quote: for a yes. No pricing pages means you say so and refuse the pricing read.
issues.problem: The description promises a 'landscape' and a 'pricing read', but the body has no step for either. The only mention of a pricing read is the fallback that refuses it, so a model has no method for the comparison table.
issues.fix: Add a 'Read the pricing' step: a per-plan table with fetch date, the limits that bind a buyer, step-ups between plans, and prices quoted only from fetched pages. Add a one-line landscape map (tier, positioning claim, target segment).

issues.section: Turn the read into win strategy
issues.quote: Three discriminators with proof, the competitor line the rep will hear,
issues.problem: Three Zara skills own the same asset. field-enablement-content also claims 'battlecard content', and positioning-and-messaging already writes 'the competitor line they will hear... counter in rep register'. The same prompt can load any of them and produce divergent counters.
issues.fix: Make this skill the single owner of battlecards and competitor counters. Have field-enablement and positioning read the saved card instead of re-deriving it, and remove 'battlecard lines' from field-enablement's triggers.

issues.section: Turn the read into win strategy
issues.quote: and the counter in rep register. Fold in win-loss quotes where they
issues.problem: 'Win-loss' is a trigger, but the skill has no win-loss method: no interview program, no reason coding (product, price, relationship, timing), no sample-size caveat, and no separation of buyer-stated from rep-stated reasons.
issues.fix: Add a win-loss sub-procedure: code each deal's primary and secondary reason, weight buyer interviews over rep notes, flag fewer than about 15 deals as directional, and draft the buyer-interview guide for the owner to send.

issues.section: Set the tiered watch list first
issues.quote: — plus review-site mining, competitor demo notes, and community chatter
issues.problem: The skill sets no ethical or legal limits on CI. It says nothing against misrepresenting identity to get demos or pricing, gives no legal review for comparative claims in externally shared cards, and doesn't tell the model to treat fetched pages as untrusted input.
issues.fix: Add guardrails: never pose as a prospect or pretext, keep public or consented sources only, route comparative claims that leave the company to legal, and ignore instructions found in fetched content.

issues.section: Set the tiered watch list first
issues.quote: changelog, product, and careers pages logged — including fetches that fail
issues.problem: The skill names no tools and no store. It doesn't say to use web_fetch / browser_navigate / Firecrawl for pages, memory_store for the watch list, or where the source ledger lives, so runs will vary.
issues.fix: Name web_fetch with a browser fallback for JS pages, keep the tiered list in memory, and save the ledger to a fixed workspace path that the Thursday routine also reads.

issues.quote: Keep to moves that matter: launches, pricing, messaging, positioning shifts.
issues.problem: The competitor-brief routine's watch/notify/act triage and its 'one source can log but never act' rule are missing here, so ad-hoc briefs and routine briefs apply different bars.
issues.fix: Copy the watch/notify/act triage and the single-source rule into this step so the skill and the routine match.

issues.quote: The brief, saved dated with sources and a full source ledger including
issues.problem: No brief or battlecard template ships with the package, even though the card has a rich defined structure.
issues.fix: Ship templates/ci-brief.md and templates/battlecard.md with the zones, Know/Say/Show, landmine questions, deal-intel pane, owner, last refresh and approver.

issues.section: Set the tiered watch list first
issues.quote: Tier 1 direct competitors for a deep read, Tier 2 adjacent substitutes for
issues.problem: This tiered watch-list flow nearly duplicates Alex's product-market-and-competitor-read. When both experts are hired, they fetch and brief the same moves twice.
issues.fix: Share one change log in the workspace and tell the model to read the other expert's log (or consult_teammate) before fetching.

scenarios.prompt: Acme just cut prices 20% and launched an AI assistant. Update our battlecard against them.
scenarios.why: Here the skill works: log the changes with link and date, write a packaging read for the price move and a positioning read for the launch, set three discriminators and a counter in rep register, then refresh the card with win/battle/lose zones, Know/Say/Show and a versioned diff that awaits the owner's yes. A capable model produces a card a rep could use.

scenarios.prompt: We keep losing mid-market deals to Beta Corp. Here are 6 lost-deal notes. No Gong, and their pricing page is 'contact sales'.
scenarios.why: The fallback correctly refuses the pricing read. But the skill has no win-loss method: no reason coding, no caveat about six deals being inside the noise, and no interview plan to grow the sample. It also doesn't suggest legitimate proxy pricing sources (marketplace listings, review-site pricing mentions, rep-reported quotes graded by evidence). The win strategy ends up resting on anecdotes.

developer-and-api-motion.job: plan developer and API adoption motion
developer-and-api-motion.summary: Outlines a developer GTM plan in five short moves (funnel stages, golden-path timing, content spine, community layer, scorecard with guardrails) with no-invention and publish-on-yes fallbacks.
strengths: Time-to-first-call and the golden path framed as a conversion tax with a fix per step
Scorecard metrics paired with experience guardrails so growth never trades against developer experience
Clean boundary: docs stay with product; Zara specs what the motion needs
Never invents adoption numbers, community sizes or benchmarks; developer-facing content ships only on the owner's yes
missing: Developer personas and the developer-to-buyer bridge
PQL/PQA definition and sales-assist handoff
Free tier, usage pricing and rate-limit packaging lens
Measured golden-path walk with a friction log
Docs information architecture (tutorials, how-to, reference, explanation)
SDK / language prioritisation and launch sequencing
API changelog, versioning and deprecation communications
Developer channel plan (GitHub, HN, Reddit, Discord, Stack Overflow)
Metric formulas and a plan template

issues.quote: Discover, first call, first success, production, expand. Each stage gets
issues.problem: The description promises 'conversion points', but the skill never defines the product-qualified signal (PQL/PQA), the threshold, or how the account routes to sales-assist. In bottom-up motions that handoff is the commercial core.
issues.fix: Add a step that defines PQL/PQA signals (usage depth, team invites, rate-limit hits, production keys), the threshold, the routing rule, and the sales-assist play, with HubSpot as the destination on approval.

issues.quote: Minutes from landing to first successful call. Every step that is not
issues.problem: The skill gives no method for timing the path, so the model will estimate minutes instead of measuring them.
issues.fix: Walk the public quickstart with browser_navigate, and run the documented curl/SDK call in bash_exec with a test key the user supplies (never a production secret). Record a friction log (step, minutes, blocker, fix). Mark anything not walked as INFERENCE.

issues.quote: The developer motion plan with funnel, content spine, and conversion
issues.problem: The plan has no defined sections or template. The five moves are one to three sentences each, so the deliverable's shape varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/dev-motion-plan.md: personas, funnel table (stage, event, formula, current, target), friction log, content spine matrix (stage × question × asset), PQL definition, channel plan and scorecard.

issues.problem: The skill has no developer segmentation (hobbyist, startup builder, enterprise platform team) and no link from the developer user to the economic buyer. It also has no pricing, free-tier or rate-limit lens, although these decide bottom-up conversion.
issues.fix: Add a 'Name who is building and who pays' step, and a packaging check that routes to pricing-and-packaging for free-tier limits and usage pricing.

issues.quote: First-call conversion, activation rate, time-to-production, and expansion
issues.problem: Metrics have no formula, denominator or window, unlike gtm-performance-diagnostics. The guardrail metrics are never named.
issues.fix: Define each metric with formula and window. Name guardrails such as API error rate, p95 latency, support tickets per 100 active developers, and docs CSAT.

issues.section: Design the community and reach layer
issues.quote: The watering holes where your developers already gather, the event or
issues.problem: The skill gives no method to find or size the channels, so a model may assert community sizes it can't source.
issues.fix: Use web_search to check GitHub topics, Stack Overflow tag volume, subreddits and Discord communities, and cite what was found. Mark reach as UNKNOWN where it can't be counted.

issues.quote: No funnel numbers means you define the instrumentation spec before any
issues.problem: The instrumentation spec is never described (events, properties, account vs key identity, consent). The fallback also ignores the data most API companies already have: billing usage, gateway logs, API-key creation.
issues.fix: List the minimum event set and identity rule. Accept Stripe usage, gateway logs or a key-creation export as a first read before new instrumentation.

issues.quote: Amplitude where connected.
issues.problem: The only named analytics source is Amplitude, which has no block in the harness. Without an MCP connection there is no stated alternative.
issues.fix: List Amplitude via MCP, then HubSpot or Stripe usage, then a pasted CSV, and never block on a connection.

scenarios.prompt: API signups look fine but very few developers reach production. Build me a developer motion plan.
scenarios.why: The skill tells the model to map five stages, time the golden path and spec content per stage. It gives no stage formulas, no instruction to cohort developers by signup week, and no friction-log method, so the diagnosis of where production drop-off happens stays generic. The plan comes back as headings plus suggestions.

scenarios.prompt: We launch Python and TypeScript SDKs next month. We only have Stripe usage-based billing data, no Amplitude, and sales wants to know which free-tier accounts to call.
scenarios.why: The skill has no PQL/PQA definition or sales-assist handoff, so it can't answer 'which accounts to call'. It never mentions Stripe or usage logs as a data fallback; its only fallback is to write an instrumentation spec first. It gives no guidance on SDK launch sequencing and doesn't route that to commercial-launch-strategy.

field-enablement-content.job: create sales enablement content and plays
field-enablement-content.summary: Specs sales plays (trigger, ICP slice, talk track, battlecard lines, exit criteria, owner, review date), 30-second objection responses, a four-slide Why Change/Why Now/Why Us deck outline, a cert step and a quarterly refresh, all drafted for approval.
strengths: Objection responses in rep register: under 30 seconds spoken, ending in the question that moves the deal, indexed by objection kind
Plays are dated with an owner and review date; ownerless plays are retired
Every deck number is sourced in speaker notes; one artifact per audience
Clear boundary: Zara authors assets, AEs run the motion, and nothing publishes rep-wide without an explicit yes
missing: Explicit play schema with discovery questions and success metric
Persona-specific deck variants and a value/ROI slide
Customer logo/quote permission and claims review
One-pager, demo script and ROI worksheet formats
Play adoption and effectiveness measurement
Boundary with Max's enablement system and CI-owned battlecards
Templates for play, talk track and deck outline

issues.quote: objection handling, or battlecard content for the field. Start from the
issues.problem: The trigger collides with competitive-intelligence (battlecards) and positioning-and-messaging (objections, rep-register counters) inside Zara's own kit. The play and refresh text is also copied from Max's enablement-playbooks-certification, so on a shared team both experts claim 'talk track'.
issues.fix: Consume battlecards and counters from the saved CI card and positioning doc instead of re-deriving them. Drop 'battlecard lines' from the triggers. Hand the selling-system work (curriculum, certification) to Max via consult_teammate.

issues.section: Write the play as a dated play
issues.quote: Trigger, ICP slice, talk track, battlecard lines, and exit criteria.
issues.problem: 'Exit criteria' is ambiguous: it could mean deal-stage exit or play retirement. The play also lacks discovery questions, proof points, the target persona and a success measure (adoption, stage conversion, win rate on play-tagged deals).
issues.fix: Define the play schema explicitly: trigger, persona, discovery questions, value hypothesis, proof, talk track, battlecard pointer, stage exit criteria, success metric, owner and review date. Ship it as templates/sales-play.md.

issues.quote: Why Change, Why Now, Why Us, plus the path: four core slides, every
issues.problem: Beyond 'one artifact per audience' the skill has no buyer-type variation (CFO vs practitioner vs IT). It has no value/ROI slide or business-case link and no proof-gap handling, and the four-slide outline alone is thin for a real pitch.
issues.fix: Add persona cuts, a business-value slide that pulls from opportunity-sizing-and-business-case, and a rule to mark missing proof as UNKNOWN on the slide rather than filling it.

issues.quote: Nothing publishes rep-wide without
issues.problem: The only guardrail is internal publishing. There is no rule on customer permission for logos, names or quotes in external decks, and no legal/claims review for comparative or quantified claims.
issues.fix: Add: customer names and quotes appear externally only with recorded permission; comparative or quantified claims go to the claims approver; call excerpts stay internal.

issues.quote: No call record means you draft from top-rep shadows and mark bars
issues.problem: The agent can't shadow reps, and 'a recorded role-play' needs humans. The fallback doesn't say what the model should do instead.
issues.fix: Ask the user for top-rep notes or a pasted transcript via ask_question. Offer to run the role-play in chat and score it against the bar.

issues.quote: Scored dimensions with what good sounds like, quoted from real calls where
issues.problem: The dimensions are never named or scaled, and the section duplicates Max's quality rubric, so two experts would publish two rubrics.
issues.fix: Name four to six dimensions on a 1-4 scale, or defer the rubric to Max's enablement skill and reference it.

issues.quote: message, one proof set. Draft it as an outline in a doc; the design team
issues.problem: It assumes a design team exists and ignores the Google Slides block, although small-team users are the target.
issues.fix: Draft the outline in a doc, and offer a Google Slides draft via run_block on approval when no design team exists.

issues.problem: The pitch-deck trigger is covered, but the other common field assets (one-pager, demo script, follow-up email, ROI worksheet, case-study brief) have no format, although 'enablement content' is a trigger.
issues.fix: Add a references/asset-formats.md with short specs per asset, or reuse Toran's sales-enablement-content references (deck-frameworks, objection-library, demo-scripts, one-pager-templates).

scenarios.prompt: Write objection handling for 'too expensive' and 'we already use Salesforce' for our mid-market AEs.
scenarios.why: The talk-track section is precise: name the objection kind, give two responses under 30 seconds each ending in a deal-advancing question, and source from Gong or pasted notes. A capable model produces rep-ready tracks drafted for review.

scenarios.prompt: I need a pitch deck for a CFO audience by Friday. We have no quantified case studies, only notes from 3 SMB deals, and no design team.
scenarios.why: The deck spec (four slides, every number sourced in speaker notes, one audience) keeps the model honest. It gives no guidance for a proof gap: no route to opportunity-sizing for a CFO-grade ROI case, and nothing on marking a slide UNKNOWN versus dropping it. It assumes a design team exists rather than drafting in Google Slides. It says nothing about customer-quote permission.

gtm-performance-diagnostics.job: score GTM funnel performance and forecast
gtm-performance-diagnostics.summary: Scores the commercial funnel for a fixed period, with each metric defined once by formula and denominator: coverage, win rate, velocity, stage conversion, activation, NRR/churn, forecast accuracy and attribution. It rates each against target R/Y/G, decomposes the top movers, flags thin samples, adds a forecast and hygiene read, and ends with owned interventions.
strengths: Every metric defined once with formula and denominator; win rate on closed deals only; zero denominators reported as N/A with counts
Thin-sample rule (under about 30 observations sits in the noise) prevents manufactured trends
Movers decomposed into volume, conversion, deal size and cycle, and tied to a visible cause, or one line saying why not
Forecast read with Commit/Best-Case/Pipeline grades, hygiene flags and backward funnel math
Clear boundary: diagnose and recommend, while CRM hygiene stays with sales ops and reporting with finance
missing: Period-to-date vs same-point-prior-period method
Default R/Y/G thresholds
Cohort-based stage conversion with a window
Count vs value win rate and no-decision treatment
CAC payback / magic number, or an explicit handoff to Daniel
Scorecard table template aligned with the weekly routine
Sandbox computation of rates
Approval before writing to the shared metrics sheet

issues.quote: No targets means you propose them from history and mark every target
issues.problem: Proposed targets are marked UNKNOWN, yet they are the model's own inference. R/Y/G against a target labelled unknown is meaningless, and the owner can't tell a proposal from a gap.
issues.fix: Label history-derived targets PROPOSED (INFERENCE) with the method (e.g. last-4-period median +10%). Score R/Y/G against them with a banner, and ask the owner to confirm.

issues.section: Fix the period and the funnel first
issues.quote: never compare a partial period to a full one.
issues.problem: The rule forbids mid-period comparison but gives no method, so the most common request (mid-quarter check) stalls or gets improvised.
issues.fix: Add: for a partial period, compare period-to-date against the same elapsed days of the prior period, and show a run-rate projection labelled INFERENCE.

issues.quote: target red, yellow, or green:
issues.problem: R/Y/G has no thresholds, so the same actual can be yellow in one run and red in the next.
issues.fix: State a default band (e.g. green at 95% of target or better, yellow 80-95%, red under 80%, inverted for cost or cycle metrics), editable by the owner and stored in memory.

issues.quote: Stage conversion: each stage into the next, against last period.
issues.problem: Period-based stage conversion mixes cohorts, and long-cycle stages will look like they are collapsing or spiking.
issues.fix: Use cohort-based conversion (entered stage in window X, converted within N days), and state the window.

issues.quote: Win rate: won over won plus lost, by segment and by source, on closed
issues.problem: The rule doesn't say count-based versus value-based, or how to treat no-decision and disqualified closes, both of which swing win rate materially.
issues.fix: Report count and value win rate side by side, and state whether no-decision counts as lost.

issues.quote: Beside the scorecard: Commit, Best-Case, and Pipeline grades with the
issues.problem: This nearly duplicates Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast (same grades and hygiene flags), and NRR/coverage overlaps Daniel's saas-gtm-finance. On one team, two experts would issue competing forecasts.
issues.fix: When Max or Daniel is hired, consult_teammate for the deal-level forecast and NRR bridge, and keep this read at the funnel and segment level.

issues.quote: dated and write the period's figures to the metrics history — a sheet the
issues.problem: Writing to a team-edited shared sheet is an external side effect with no draft or approval step.
issues.fix: Show the rows to be appended, and write to the shared sheet only after the owner's yes (or on a routine they already approved).

issues.quote: The scorecard table, the top movers with their drivers, the forecast read,
issues.problem: The table columns are never specified here, although the weekly routine defines them (metric, actual, target, R/Y/G, cause). The arithmetic is also never routed to the sandbox.
issues.fix: Fix the table columns to match the routine, and compute every rate in bash_exec with the formula shown.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our HubSpot export for Q3 and Q2. How is GTM doing?
scenarios.why: The steps cover it: fix both periods, map lead-to-won stages to sources, compute each metric by its stated formula, score R/Y/G, rank movers and decompose them into volume, conversion, deal size and cycle, flag rates under about 30 observations, add the forecast read and hygiene flags, and close with two or three owned interventions. A capable model produces a board-quality read.

scenarios.prompt: Q4 is five weeks in. Here's a pasted pipeline CSV with no closed-lost field and no targets. The board wants a win rate and forecast tomorrow.
scenarios.why: The guardrails hold: win rate goes to N/A with counts, the missing stage is named, and the hygiene flags and backward funnel math still run. But 'never compare a partial period to a full one' comes with no quarter-to-date or same-point-last-quarter method. The no-target fallback says to propose targets and label them UNKNOWN, which contradicts itself and leaves R/Y/G undefined.

gtm-planning-and-market-entry.job: build go-to-market plan and market entry
gtm-planning-and-market-entry.summary: Builds a GTM plan: one numeric objective, a motion per segment, land-then-expand sequencing with entry and exit criteria, coverage and quota sanity math, a readiness checklist with owners, and an operating cadence with RACI inputs.
strengths: Forces one numeric objective with a date before any planning
Sequencing with explicit entry and exit criteria and what must be true before the next segment opens
Honest coverage framing: unstaffable coverage math is a risk, not a plan; top-down vs bottom-up quota gap named
Clear ownership boundary: quota stays with sales and process with ops; never invents market size, headcount or dates
missing: Market attractiveness / ability-to-win selection step
Reverse-funnel pipeline math from target
Capacity model with ramp and attainment
Regulatory, data-residency, entity and localisation entry gates
Budget and channel-mix plan
Risks and kill criteria for the entry
GTM plan template
Routing to ICP, sizing, vertical and pricing siblings

issues.quote: Positioning locked, pricing signed off, enablement packed, systems and
issues.problem: A market-entry checklist with no legal, regulatory, data-residency, tax/entity or localisation gate. A new geography or regulated segment can enter the plan with uncleared blockers.
issues.fix: Add a regulatory and localisation gate: legal, data residency, entity/tax, language and currency. A market with uncleared gates stays in the plan but out of the forecast, and legal gets the handoff.

issues.quote: Books per rep, capacity per book, and the top-down vs bottom-up quota
issues.problem: Coverage math has no method. It omits ramp time, attainment rate and the reverse funnel from target to pipeline to opportunities to leads at current conversion, so the core staffing answer is improvised.
issues.fix: Give the formula: ramped-rep equivalents × quota × expected attainment against the target, plus the reverse funnel at historical conversion from HubSpot. Compute it in bash_exec and show the gap.

issues.quote: Land segment first, expand segments next, each with entry and exit
issues.problem: This overlaps icp-and-segmentation ('names a segment') and near-duplicates vertical-industry-plays' entry sequence inside Zara's own kit. Across the team it overlaps Max's regional-category-gtm-strategy and Toran's go-to-market-strategy, so 'new segment' and 'market entry' route unpredictably.
issues.fix: Route segment choice to icp-and-segmentation and sector entry to vertical-industry-plays. Keep this skill for multi-segment, horizon-level plans, and narrow the triggers to match.

issues.problem: The skill has no market-selection step. It never evaluates which market to enter and why (attractiveness × ability to win, competitive intensity, cost to enter), so it jumps straight to motion.
issues.fix: Add a 'Choose where to play' step with a short scoring matrix. Route sizing to opportunity-sizing-and-business-case and competitors to competitive-intelligence.

issues.quote: You design the plan and the motion — quota ownership stays with sales,
issues.problem: The skill has no budget or channel plan, and doesn't state that budget, headcount and dates are drafts the owner approves, which the persona's boundaries require.
issues.fix: Add a budget and channel-mix line to the plan, and a closing rule: every dollar, hire and date is a proposal until the owner says yes.

issues.quote: RACI inputs — who decides, who executes — and the weekly or monthly forum
issues.problem: The output has no template, and 'RACI inputs' is vague, so plans vary in shape and are hard to review against the scorecard.
issues.fix: Ship templates/gtm-plan.md: objective, where to play, motion per segment, sequence with gates, capacity math, budget, readiness, RACI, cadence, risks and kill criteria.

issues.quote: No segment sizing means you sequence on qualitative fit and flag sizing
issues.problem: The fallback flags sizing but doesn't route to the sibling sizing skill or use Apollo/HubSpot counts that may already be connected.
issues.fix: Offer to run opportunity-sizing-and-business-case now, or pull an Apollo account count for the segment's firmographics.

issues.quote: One motion per tier; a segment with no motion is
issues.problem: 'Tier' and 'segment' are used interchangeably, and 'one motion' rules out the hybrid PLG plus sales-assist motions common in practice.
issues.fix: Say 'one primary motion per segment', and allow a named assist motion with its handoff point.

scenarios.prompt: Build our FY27 GTM plan: $4M new ARR target, 6 AEs, moving from SMB into mid-market.
scenarios.why: The model will fix the $4M objective, pick motions per segment, sequence SMB then mid-market with entry and exit bars, and write the readiness checklist and cadence. But the key question, whether 6 AEs can carry $4M, rests on 'books per rep, capacity per book' with no ramp, attainment, or reverse funnel from target to pipeline to opportunities to leads. The answer depends on the model's own knowledge.

scenarios.prompt: We want to enter Germany next quarter with our HR data product. No German customers, no sizing, no headcount decided, and legal hasn't looked at GDPR or works councils yet.
scenarios.why: The fallbacks cover sequencing on qualitative fit, flagging sizing, and holding the coverage math. Neither the procedure nor the readiness checklist has a regulatory, data-residency, localisation or entity gate, and nothing hands off to legal or Max's regional strategy. A model might mention GDPR because the user did, but the skill won't hold Germany out of the forecast until those gates clear.

marketplace-two-sided-mediation.summary: Has the model name the dispute type, weigh each side's records against the policy passage (platform-seen evidence first), rule with a cited outcome or send it up past the approval limit, and stage one neutral message per side, with all money moves held for the owner's yes.
strengths: Separate draft per side, and a hard rule never to pass one side's private details or identity to the other
'Weigh evidence the platform saw over evidence one side describes' is a real mediator heuristic
Treats partial remedies as normal, and requires a written reason for any exception inside the approval limit
A case no dispute type fits goes to the owner or legal rather than to an invented rule; thin records mean a narrower ruling, and it names the record that would settle each UNKNOWN
missing: Per-dispute-type evidence and burden-of-proof matrix
Request-for-response step with deadlines and a default outcome on silence
Handling of parallel chargebacks and off-platform transactions
Who funds each remedy (seller payout, escrow, platform guarantee)
Repeat-claimant and seller-defect pattern check
Carrier insurance claim path for transit damage
Ruling template and a worked example

issues.section: Hear both sides from the records
issues.quote: What each claims, what the evidence confirms — timestamps, photos, tracking,
issues.problem: 'Hearing' both sides means reading existing records only. There is no step to ask the respondent for a statement and evidence with a deadline, no dispute timelines, and no rule for what happens when a side does not respond.
issues.fix: Add an 'Open the case' step: stage a neutral request-for-evidence draft to each side with the policy's response deadline, and state the default outcome on non-response.

issues.quote: its own evidence standard; a case that fits none goes to the owner rather
issues.problem: It says each type has its own evidence standard but never states any, so the model will invent burden-of-proof rules.
issues.fix: Ship references/dispute-types.md. For each type give the required evidence, who carries the burden, and the default remedy: INR = tracking to the buyer's address; SNAD = listing vs photos, return-for-refund; damaged = carrier claim; host late-cancel = rebooking help plus cost difference; guest no-show = cancellation tier.

issues.quote: Item not received, not as described, damaged, cancelled late, a no-show, a
issues.problem: No check for a parallel external payment dispute (card chargeback, PayPal claim) or off-platform payment. Either one changes whether the platform case can rule at all, and where the evidence should go.
issues.fix: Before ruling, check for open chargebacks or external claims and any off-platform payment. If there is one, pause the remedy and hand the evidence to fraud-and-chargeback-defense.

issues.quote: remedies are normal: a partial refund for a partial failure, a fee waived
issues.problem: It never says who funds a remedy: a seller payout clawback, an escrow release, or platform-funded goodwill. It also never says when a return must happen before a refund. Two-sided money moves need both ledgers stated.
issues.fix: Make every remedy line state its funding source (seller-liable, platform guarantee or split) and any condition, such as a refund released on return tracking.

issues.section: Hear both sides from the records
issues.problem: No check on either party's claim history (serial INR buyer, seller with a high defect rate). A senior mediator weighs this, and abuse patterns should leave the single-case path.
issues.fix: Add a prior-disputes check for both parties over the last 12 months. Route suspected abuse to trust-and-safety-escalations or the fraud path instead of ruling on it.

issues.quote: marketplace fee waiver
issues.problem: Collides with billing-refunds-and-exceptions ('waive a fee'). A one-party fee question with no counterparty would wrongly load this skill.
issues.fix: Replace it with two-sided phrasings ('seller disputes buyer claim', 'host disputes guest refund'). Add a boundary line in the body: one-party money asks go to billing-refunds-and-exceptions.

issues.quote: The dispute read with the policy citation, the ruling with its evidence, and
issues.problem: No reusable ruling format, so the evidence tables and appeal terms will differ from case to case.
issues.fix: Ship templates/ruling.md with: type, policy cite, claims per side, evidence table (item, source, platform-seen, supports whom), UNKNOWNs with the settling record, ruling, remedy and funding, approvals needed, per-side drafts, appeal window.

issues.quote: next step with a date and an owner, and how to appeal. Plain, neutral, no
issues.problem: 'How to appeal' has no appeal window and no test for what new evidence reopens a ruling, so each draft invents its own.
issues.fix: Take the appeal window and the new-evidence criterion from the policy passage or prefs. Mark them UNKNOWN if they are absent.

scenarios.prompt: Buyer says the vintage lamp arrived cracked; seller has a pre-ship photo showing it intact. Here are the order, the message thread and both photos. Mediate and draft replies to both.
scenarios.why: The model would type it as 'damaged', compare the photos, quote the policy and stage one draft per side. Nothing tells it that transit damage normally becomes a carrier insurance claim, whether the buyer must return the item before the refund, or who funds the refund (seller payout or platform). The ruling is plausible, but the remedy mechanics are guessed.

scenarios.prompt: Guest says the host cancelled two days before check-in and she paid $400 more elsewhere. Host says she agreed over WhatsApp to cancel. She has also opened a chargeback with her bank. No policy doc is uploaded.
scenarios.why: 'Weigh evidence the platform saw' correctly downweights the WhatsApp claim, and 'Thin records' asks for missing records. Nothing handles the open chargeback (pause and route to fraud-and-chargeback-defense), the off-platform arrangement, or a missing policy passage as distinct from missing records. There is also no rule for reimbursing rebooking costs, so the model would improvise the most important part.

mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms.job: run mass-incident customer recovery and comms
mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms.summary: For an outage, breach, recall or disaster, has the model size the affected population, stage bulk refunds or credits as one approval packet, draft a short alert and a full update, run war-room beats, and draft a postmortem prompt, publishing nothing before the owner's yes.
strengths: 'Size the blast first' with list verification before any bulk move, and 'Never blast from a guessed list' in the fallback
Two comms shapes (short alert and full update), each claim carrying its source and time
The whole bulk money move goes to the owner as one packet with count, amount and policy quote
Dedupes pages against the last update, and ends with a postmortem prompt and backlog offer
missing: Legal and regulatory notification path for breach and recall
Linking inbound tickets to a master incident, holding macro, deflection banner or IVR, and the final mass reply
Bulk execution controls: dedupe, exclusions, pilot batch, reconciliation
Severity-linked update cadence and a 'next update at' commitment
Coordination with the incident commander, PR or comms teammate, and service-recovery-and-goodwill so one-off remedies match the mass remedy
Contractual SLA-credit calculation per affected account
Comms and packet templates

issues.quote: Use this when many customers break at once — outage, breach, recall, or
issues.problem: Breach and recall have statutory content and deadlines: GDPR 72h to the regulator, US state breach laws, HIPAA 60 days, and recalls coordinated with the regulator. The skill treats them like outage comms gated only by the owner's yes.
