issues.fix: Add a branch: for a breach or recall, stage only a holding statement, route to the legal or privacy owner and sensitive-data-safe-handling, draft only counsel-approved facts, never speculate on cause or scope, and log regulatory clocks from prefs.

issues.problem: Missing the support desk's main incident work: tagging and linking inbound tickets to a master incident, a holding macro and auto-reply, a help-center banner or IVR message, and one mass reply-and-close pass once the fix lands.
issues.fix: Insert a 'Contain the inbound surge' step after sizing, with the parent/child ticket link, holding macro, deflection surfaces and final mass-update plan, all staged for approval.

issues.quote: Stage the bulk recovery: mass refunds, cancels, credits, or rebooks, each
issues.problem: No execution controls on bulk money moves: no dedupe against already refunded or chargebacked orders, no exclusions, no pilot batch, no idempotent IDs, and no reconciliation of executed against approved.
issues.fix: Build the packet in the sandbox from the export: dedupe, exclusions, per-segment totals, pilot batch then full, and a post-run reconciliation file attached to the log.

issues.quote: Run the war-room beats: owners per workstream, update cadence, decision
issues.problem: Casts a support rep as incident commander and implies paging ('Page once per stall') that Robin cannot do. It duplicates escalations-and-incidents and the teammates' incident skills, and the update cadence is not tied to severity.
issues.fix: Scope Robin to the customer-comms workstream. Take facts from the incident commander (consult_teammate or escalations-and-incidents), set cadence by severity from the escalation matrix, and stage pings as drafts.

issues.quote: Draft the mass comms in two shapes: the short alert (what happened, who it
issues.problem: No 'next update at' time, no status-page or channel matrix, no suppression of scheduled marketing sends, and no per-segment or localised variants.
issues.fix: Add a required 'next update by' line, a channel checklist (status page, email, in-app, social, IVR) and a marketing-pause step.

issues.quote: incident postmortem
issues.problem: Collides with escalations-and-incidents (SEV closes carry a postmortem prompt) and with teammates' incident-postmortem-draft and software-incident-response.
issues.fix: Use customer-side triggers ('outage customer comms', 'mass refund after outage'). Hand the postmortem write-up to the engineering teammate.

issues.quote: The scope read, the staged bulk packet, the mass-comms drafts, the war-room
issues.problem: No templates, so the alert, the update and the bulk packet are reinvented on every incident, under time pressure.
issues.fix: Ship templates/alert.md, templates/update.md and a bulk-packet column schema (customer_id, segment, action, amount, policy_ref, excluded_reason).

scenarios.prompt: Our payment processor failed for 3 hours yesterday. About 1,200 orders either failed or were double-charged; CSV attached. Plan the refunds and draft the customer email.
scenarios.why: Step 1 segments the list, step 2 stages counts, amounts and a policy quote, and step 3 produces an alert and an update, so the drafts are good. Nothing tells the model to dedupe against already-refunded or chargebacked orders, pilot a batch, or reconcile executed against approved totals in the sandbox. There is also no macro or auto-reply for the inbound flood of 'was I charged twice?' tickets.

scenarios.prompt: We think customer emails and hashed passwords leaked through our support-tool vendor. Legal hasn't confirmed scope yet. Draft the customer notice; we want to send it to everyone tonight.
scenarios.why: The skill names 'breach' but its only gate is the owner's yes. There is no routing to legal or privacy counsel, no regulatory clocks, no holding statement pending counsel, no forced password reset, and no rule against speculating on scope. 'Never blast from a guessed list' pushes back on 'everyone', but the model would still hand over a breach notice as a routine comms draft.

member-benefits-and-claims.job: resolve health plan member benefit and claim issues
member-benefits-and-claims.summary: For health-plan member cases, has the model label eligibility facts, explain a benefit from the plan source, check a claim's billed/allowed/paid/member-share figures before staging reprocessing, and log grievances with a deadline, keeping PHI out of subjects and public replies.
strengths: Labels eligibility facts FACT or UNKNOWN before explaining anything, and says an unsourced benefit stays UNKNOWN
Researches the payment (billed, allowed, paid, member share, reference IDs) before moving money; reprocessing is staged, never promised
Keeps PHI out of subjects, chats and public replies
Fallback limits it to general plan education when there is no access, with the access need named
missing: Identity and authorized-representative verification before any PHI
Appeals process distinct from grievances, including expedited and external review
Regulatory timelines sourced from plan documents or prefs
Denial reason codes, prior authorization, COB, timely filing, balance-billing checks
Accumulator (deductible, OOP max) explanation
Enrollment windows and qualifying life events
No-clinical-advice boundary
Routing to sensitive-data-safe-handling and compliance-and-regulated-support
Output template and an EOB worked example

issues.quote: Confirm plan, dates, network, and the benefit in question, each labeled FACT
issues.problem: No identity or authority verification before PHI is discussed. A spouse, a parent of an adult dependent or a provider office would get full claim detail. HIPAA requires verifying identity and authority (a personal representative or an authorization on file) first.
issues.fix: Add step 0: verify identity using the desk's protocol from prefs and confirm the requester is the member or an authorized representative. Otherwise give general information only. Route the check through sensitive-data-safe-handling.

issues.quote: appeal a denial
issues.problem: The trigger promises appeals but the body only logs grievances. Appeals of adverse benefit determinations are a separate process with its own clocks (urgent or expedited, pre-service, post-service, external review) and required documents.
issues.fix: Add an 'Appeal or grievance?' section. Classify the ask; capture the denial reason, filing deadline and expedited criteria; stage an appeal packet. Take clocks from plan documents or prefs and mark them UNKNOWN if absent.

issues.quote: Record what happened, what the member wants, and the deadline clock. Confirm
issues.problem: The deadline clock has no source and no values, so the model will pick a number or skip it. Acknowledgment and resolution windows are regulated and differ by plan type.
issues.fix: Read acknowledgment and resolution windows from prefs or the plan's grievance procedure. If missing, mark the clock UNKNOWN and ask the compliance owner. Never default a number.

issues.section: Research claim problems before moving money
issues.quote: Check the payment first: billed, allowed, paid, and member share, with dates
issues.problem: Stops at EOB arithmetic. It never reads the denial or adjustment reason codes (CARC/RARC) and never checks prior authorization, timely filing, coordination of benefits, or out-of-network balance billing (No Surprises Act protections).
issues.fix: Add a claim-cause checklist: reason code, prior auth on file, network status, COB order, timely filing, accumulator state. Each cause maps to the fix and the owner.

issues.quote: Say what is covered, what it costs the member, and the exact next step
issues.problem: The cost explanation ignores accumulators (deductible met, out-of-pocket max), network tier and prior-auth requirements. There is also no boundary against giving clinical advice.
issues.fix: Require the accumulator state and network tier in every cost statement. Add a line: coverage explanation only, and clinical questions go to the provider or nurse line.

issues.quote: drive enrollment
issues.problem: Enrollment is advertised but the body has no enrollment windows, qualifying-life-event deadlines or effective-date rules.
issues.fix: Add a short enrollment section (window check, QLE deadline, documents, effective date, all sourced from the plan) or drop enrollment from the description.

issues.quote: Deliver the eligibility read, the member explanation draft, the staged claim
issues.problem: The deliverable is buried under the grievance heading with no Output section or template.
issues.fix: Add '## Output' with a template: eligibility table (FACT/UNKNOWN), EOB breakdown, cause, member draft, staged move, case line with clock.

scenarios.prompt: Member says her MRI claim shows she owes $1,400 and she thought it was covered. Here's the EOB and her plan's Summary of Benefits. What happened and what do I tell her?
scenarios.why: 'Check the payment first' gets the billed/allowed/paid/member-share split, and the plan citation rule avoids invented coverage. Nothing tells the model to check the deductible accumulator, network status, prior-authorization requirement or the denial reason code, which are the usual causes. Nothing tells it to offer an appeal either, so the explanation may be accurate arithmetic but the wrong diagnosis.

scenarios.prompt: A caller says she's Tom's wife. His chemo claim was denied, treatment is Monday, and she wants to know why and to file an appeal today.
scenarios.why: No step verifies identity or personal-representative authority before disclosing Tom's PHI. The only path is 'Log grievances verbatim' with an undefined 'deadline clock', not an expedited appeal of an adverse benefit determination (urgent timelines). A model following it would either disclose to an unverified third party or log the wrong process.

onboarding-and-adoption.summary: Has the model frame a new customer's onboarding as time to first value, set a fixed four-step milestone ladder with done-checks and dates, walk one milestone at a time from the docs, and draft welcome, stuck-step and milestone-done nudges, sending at-risk accounts to the owner as save drafts.
strengths: Frames onboarding around time to first value, one milestone at a time, never the whole plan on day one
Three distinct nudge drafts: welcome with one next step, stuck-step rescue with the exact unblock, milestone-done note
Checks health from records after each milestone, never guessed
The CRM log is staged as a draft for approval; a missing checklist means a plan marked UNVERIFIED that names the grounding doc for each milestone
missing: Measurable, customer-agreed activation or first-value event
Stakeholder map and customer-side owners
Dependencies (SSO, data import, security or procurement)
Defined at-risk thresholds with time windows, including sponsor loss
Graduation criteria and handoff to CS or account health
Fallback when usage data is unavailable
Plan template and nudge examples
Merge with Riley's customer-onboarding-plan

issues.quote: customer onboarding plan
issues.problem: Same job as Riley's original customer-onboarding-plan (triggers 'customer onboarding', 'onboarding milestones'). Toran's 'onboarding' also claims time-to-value. With several experts hired, the triggers collide.
issues.fix: Merge into one 'build customer onboarding plan' skill: Riley's outcome, owners, dependencies and evidence status, plus these nudges. In Robin, keep setup-step help and nudges, and consult or hand off to Riley for the plan when Riley is hired.

issues.quote: Frame the goal as time-to-value to the first meaningful win, then set
issues.problem: 'First meaningful win' is never made measurable or agreed with the customer, so the done-check for the key milestone is subjective.
issues.fix: Capture the outcome in the customer's words and a measurable first-value event with a target date (e.g. 'first 50 tickets auto-routed by May 3'), with the source for each.

issues.quote: the milestones in order: account set up, first success on their goal,
issues.problem: A fixed generic ladder with no sponsor, no customer-side owners and no dependencies (SSO, data import, security review, procurement). Those are what actually stall B2B onboarding.
issues.fix: Add a stakeholder line (sponsor, admin, users) and per-milestone owner, dependency and completion evidence. Keep the four steps as a default that gets tailored, not a fixed list.

issues.section: Draft the nudges in company voice
issues.quote: (dark after invite, stalled twice) go to the owner as a save draft,
issues.problem: At-risk thresholds are undefined ('stalled twice' over what window?) and miss champion departure, a missed kickoff and unused seats. There is no handoff to account-health-and-qbrs.
issues.fix: Define signals with time windows from prefs, add sponsor loss and seat-activation ratio, and route renewal-at-risk accounts to account-health-and-qbrs.

issues.quote: health after each milestone — logins, usage, stuck steps — from the
issues.problem: No fallback when usage or login data is unavailable. The only fallback covers missing docs.
issues.fix: Without usage data, mark health UNKNOWN, ask for an admin export or the customer's own confirmation, and name the missing source.

issues.section: Draft the nudges in company voice
issues.quote: Three drafts: a personal welcome email with one obvious next step, the
issues.problem: No timing or cadence for the nudges and no channel choice (email vs in-app), and it does not explicitly hold customer emails for the owner's yes.
issues.fix: Add a send-by date per nudge and the channel, and state that every nudge is staged for the owner's yes.

issues.problem: No graduation criteria from onboarding to steady state and no handoff record for CS or account health. Onboarding never formally ends.
issues.fix: Add exit criteria (first-value event met, admin trained, adoption threshold) and a handoff note to Riley or account-health-and-qbrs.

scenarios.prompt: Acme just signed for our Pro plan. Their goal is auto-routing support tickets. Here's our onboarding checklist and setup docs. Build their plan and draft the welcome email.
scenarios.why: The milestones follow the checklist, each gets a done-check and a date, the current milestone is walked from the docs, and the welcome email has one next step. A capable model gets a usable plan, though it lacks customer-side owners and dependencies.

scenarios.prompt: Acme onboarded five weeks ago. Only 2 of 40 invited seats are active, their champion left, and renewal is in four months. I have CRM notes but no usage export.
scenarios.why: The at-risk rule ('dark after invite, stalled twice') catches it, and it sends a save draft to the owner. But the thresholds are undefined, champion loss is not a named signal, and there is no fallback when usage data is missing (the fallback covers only missing docs). The boundary with account-health-and-qbrs for a renewal-at-risk account is not stated, so the model may score health without data or duplicate the save plan.

orders-returns-and-warranty.job: track orders and process returns or warranty
orders-returns-and-warranty.summary: Has the model track an order against live carrier scans (opening a carrier trace on stalls, running a delivery-dispute path for delivered-not-received), qualify a return or warranty claim against the cited policy windows and exclusions, pick the allowed path with per-line refund math, and stage the customer update, with every money move gated on approval.
strengths: Names a stall against the carrier's own lost-in-transit threshold and opens a trace instead of reassuring the customer
A concrete delivered-not-received path before any replacement moves
Return and warranty qualification with exclusions (final sale, hygiene, custom), proof needed, and a repair, replace, refund order
A term it cannot find is UNKNOWN, 'not assumed in anyone's favour'; per-line refund math; every money move pending approval inside the limit
Clear fallbacks: a customer screenshot is marked INFERENCE; a missing policy means UNVERIFIED with the approver named
missing: Statutory consumer-rights floor by jurisdiction
Repeat delivered-not-received and fraud check; chargeback-threat routing
Carrier claim filing and its deadline
RMA and refund trigger and timing
Identity check before address changes or reship
Boundary with logistics-shipment-and-customs and billing-refunds-and-exceptions
Case template and worked example

issues.section: Qualify the ask against the passage
issues.quote: passage; a term you cannot find is UNKNOWN, not assumed in anyone's favour.
issues.problem: Treats the store policy as the only rule. Statutory consumer rights can override it: EU 14-day withdrawal, the 2-year legal guarantee and risk passing on possession; the UK Consumer Rights Act 30-day right to reject; US implied warranties.
issues.fix: Add a jurisdiction check. If the customer's statutory floor exceeds policy (from a references file or the owner's legal note), flag it to the owner rather than denying on policy.

issues.section: Track against the carrier, not the promise
issues.quote: delivered that the customer does not have gets the delivery-dispute path:
issues.problem: No repeat-claim or fraud check on prior delivered-not-received claims by account or address, no route when a chargeback is threatened, and no deadline for the carrier claim.
issues.fix: Check prior claims for the account and address. Send repeats or chargeback threats to fraud-and-chargeback-defense, and file the carrier claim before its deadline.

issues.quote: track this order
issues.problem: Overlaps logistics-shipment-and-customs ('track this shipment', 'late delivery', 'delivery ETA'), which has a near-identical trace section. Refund asks overlap billing-refunds-and-exceptions. No boundary is stated either way.
issues.fix: State the boundary in the body: consumer parcel orders stay here, freight, customs and B2B lanes go to logistics, and pure charge disputes with no goods go to billing-refunds-and-exceptions.

issues.quote: Pick the path the policy allows and the customer needs: return label,
issues.problem: No RMA step, no refund trigger point (drop-off scan vs receipt and inspection), and no refund method or timing.
issues.fix: Add an RMA ID, the refund trigger from policy, and refund-to-original-method with the processing time stated in the update.

issues.problem: No identity check before re-shipping to a new address or changing the delivery address. That is a classic account-takeover vector.
issues.fix: Require a verified-contact confirmation before any address change or reship to a new address. Route anomalies to fraud-and-chargeback-defense.

issues.section: Track against the carrier, not the promise
issues.quote: Pull the live status: the last scan with its time and location, the
issues.problem: Does not say how to get carrier status in this harness.
issues.fix: Use web_fetch or the browser on the carrier's public tracking page, or ask for the order-system export. Otherwise use the screenshot fallback.

issues.quote: The order status with its carrier evidence, the qualified path with the
issues.problem: No template for the status, qualification and refund math, so per-line math formats vary.
issues.fix: Ship templates/order-case.md with a scan table, a policy-cite block, a per-line refund table and the staged update.

scenarios.prompt: Dana's order #4471 (two items) has had no tracking scan in Memphis for 6 days. She wants a replacement or a refund. Policy and order record attached.
scenarios.why: 'Track against the carrier' calls the stall and opens a trace instead of saying 'on the way'. 'Qualify' checks the window. 'Resolve' allows a replacement only where policy permits, with per-line math. The update names the one step she takes now. The result is senior quality.

scenarios.prompt: A customer in Germany says the package marked delivered never came, her third claim this year. She wants a full refund or she'll file a chargeback. Our policy says we're not liable after a delivery scan.
scenarios.why: The delivery-dispute path (photo or signature, label address, neighbour check) is right. But the skill treats store policy as the only rule, so it misses that EU law passes risk only on physical possession, which makes the 'not liable after scan' policy unenforceable. It has no repeat-claim fraud check and no route to fraud-and-chargeback-defense for the chargeback threat.

own-to-closure.job: follow up open support cases to closure
own-to-closure.summary: Has the model walk every open case by age, stating what was promised, what moved and the next action with owner and date, stage ack and follow-up drafts, read sentiment and roll themes into VoC, and show a closure board. Cases close only on customer confirmation or clear evidence, and a silent thread gets one more nudge then an escalation note.
strengths: Per-case fields: what was promised, what moved with evidence, what is overdue, and one next action with owner and date
Every follow-up carries a receipt (what was done, the date, a check-back question), and closure needs confirmation or evidence with the lesson logged as recorded
'Never silent closure', and retention or upsell signals go to the owner as drafts, never customer promises
The board is shown for one round of edits, then saved as the day's owned list, which fits the open-case-sweep routine
missing: SLA targets read from prefs per channel and priority
Waiting-on status taxonomy (customer, internal, vendor) with chase paths
Pending-close ladder with a reopen window for silent customers
Stale thresholds by priority
Closure-board column schema or template
Data-access fallback (export, sandbox ages)
Clear boundaries with triage-and-prioritize, voice-of-customer-and-feedback, upsell-and-retention-offers

issues.quote: A thread with no reply gets one more nudge with a plain deadline, then an
issues.problem: There is no terminal state for an unresponsive customer. An escalation note is the wrong remedy for silence, so zombie cases pile up and bury real risk.
issues.fix: Add a pending-close ladder: N touches over N days from prefs, then an owner-approved 'closing now, reply to reopen' draft with a reopen window. Escalate only when the case itself is still broken.

issues.quote: hours, resolve within one business day. Resolved cases close only on
issues.problem: Hardcoded SLAs override the per-channel targets robin-getting-started saves in prefs. 'Resolve within one business day' is unrealistic for defects waiting on engineering.
issues.fix: Read first-response, follow-up and resolution targets per channel and priority from prefs. Ask when they are missing, and never default a number.

issues.quote: Walk every open case in age order: what was promised, what moved with
issues.problem: Age order ignores priority and the SLA clock (the persona says breached or near-breach cases outrank everything) and contradicts step 4's 'most overdue first'.
issues.fix: Sort by SLA state (breached, near breach), then priority, then age, and use the same order on the board.

issues.problem: No status for who the case is waiting on: the customer, an internal team (engineering, billing) or a third party. Internal blockers are the main cause of drift, and each needs a different chase path.
issues.fix: Tag each case waiting-on-customer, waiting-on-internal or waiting-on-vendor. Internal ones get a staged chase to the owning team with the linked issue, plus a customer update on the promised cadence.

issues.quote: customer confirmation or clear evidence, with the fix, receipt, and lesson
issues.problem: 'Or clear evidence' contradicts the persona ('only after the customer confirms the fix') and never says what evidence qualifies.
issues.fix: Define it: evidence-based closure is allowed only through the pending-close ladder with the owner's yes, and never on silence alone.

issues.quote: Ack first and fast: every case gets an instant acknowledgement draft with
issues.problem: Acknowledgement belongs to triage (triage-and-prioritize already has the instant ack). Applied to the open queue, it re-acks customers who were answered days ago.
issues.fix: Limit it to cases with no first response. Everything else gets the receipt-style follow-up.

issues.quote: Read sentiment per thread — relieved, neutral, still hot — and roll repeat
issues.problem: Scope creep into voice-of-customer-and-feedback and upsell-and-retention-offers, which makes a closure pass longer and blurs the triggers.
issues.fix: Note hot sentiment as a flag on the board, and route themes and upsell signals to those skills in one line.

issues.problem: No fallback for data access. If no ticket store is connected, the skill never says to ask for an export or paste, or to compute ages in the sandbox.
issues.fix: Add: without a connected store, ask for a CSV or inbox export, compute ages and SLA state with bash_exec, and mark cases without a record UNKNOWN.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our open-ticket export (60 tickets, CSV). Build today's closure board and draft follow-ups for anything stale.
scenarios.why: Step 1 gives the right per-case fields and step 4 shows the board. But the model sorts by age, not SLA breach or priority, applies the hardcoded 'resolve within one business day' instead of the desk's targets, and step 2 may generate fresh acknowledgement drafts for cases acked days ago.

scenarios.prompt: Three customers haven't replied in 3 weeks after we shipped their fixes. Two cases are blocked on an engineering ticket, and our 'ticket store' is a shared Gmail inbox with no IDs.
scenarios.why: The fallback gives the silent customers one nudge and then an escalation note, but no pending-close ladder, so they never leave the board. There is no status or chase path for internal engineering blockers, and no instruction for building the board from an inbox without ticket IDs (export, then compute ages in the sandbox).

board-and-investor-metrics-brief.job: prepare board and investor metrics pack
board-and-investor-metrics-brief.summary: Turns approved KPI data into a board or investor brief: it sets the reporting frame, builds a nine-field row for each metric, leads with the three changes that matter for a decision, and checks the figures against the deck and the investor update.
strengths: The rule that a favourable change needs the same source test as an unfavourable one is unusually senior
Keeps operating metrics, accounting figures, cash figures and forecasts separately labelled and marks finance status (final, management draft, provisional)
Checks the brief against the deck, the investor update and the finance summary for the same cutoff
Strong prohibitions: no invented figures, no hidden exclusions, no moving targets after the period, no forecast presented as assured
missing: Default board KPI set by stage or model, including cash, runway, burn and burn multiple
One-page brief template with an appendix table
YoY and multi-period trend, with a variance materiality threshold
Restatement or bridge guidance when a metric definition changes
Tool steps: Sheets/Drive/workspace ingestion, sandbox arithmetic, CSV or paste fallback
Persisting approved KPI definitions in memory so the next quarter stays consistent
Clear boundary against monthly-investor-update and a handoff to the finance teammate

issues.quote: For each chosen metric give:
issues.problem: The skill never says which metrics belong in a board brief. There is no default set by stage or business model, and cash, runway, burn and burn multiple, the first things a board reads, are never required.
issues.fix: Add a default board KPI set (cash, runway, net burn, burn multiple, ARR/revenue, NRR/GRR, gross margin, headcount, pipeline if relevant) with a rule for adding or dropping metrics, and require a cash and runway row in every brief.

issues.quote: Lead with the three changes that affect a decision. Follow with progress against
issues.problem: The deliverable is described in prose with no template or length limit. Rendered literally, the nine-field metric row becomes an unreadable wide table.
issues.fix: Ship templates/board-brief.md: a one-page summary (headline, three changes, plan vs actual, risks, decisions needed) plus an appendix table with a fixed set of columns.

issues.problem: There are no tool steps. It never says to read the export with read_workspace_file or a Google Sheets block, to compute changes in bash_exec, or to ask for a CSV or paste when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Add an intake step: locate the KPI export and plan version (Sheets/Drive block or workspace file), fall back to a CSV or paste, and compute every change and ratio in the sandbox, labelling each figure as sourced or derived.

issues.quote: prior-period and plan value where supplied;
issues.problem: The only comparisons are prior period and plan. There is no YoY, no trailing trend, and no materiality threshold for deciding which variances need commentary.
issues.fix: Add YoY and a 4-6 period trend where data exists, plus a variance threshold (e.g. more than 10% or more than X absolute vs plan) that forces a driver explanation.

issues.quote: show why a comparison may no longer hold.
issues.problem: It flags definition changes but never says to restate prior periods on the new basis or bridge old to new, which is standard board practice.
issues.fix: When a definition changes, restate the prior period on the new basis if the data allows, or show a bridge (old value, adjustment, new value) with the owner's sign-off.

issues.quote: triggers: ["board metrics", "investor metrics", "board pack", "metrics brief", "board meeting"]
issues.problem: 'investor metrics' overlaps Theo's monthly-investor-update, and the description never says when to use this skill instead of that one. 'board pack' also collides with Daniel's finance-board-and-investor-reporting and Toran's board-deck-builder.
issues.fix: State in the description that this is the board or quarterly decision brief, not the monthly investor email, and drop the generic 'investor metrics' trigger.

issues.quote: Route disclosure, governance, terms, and ownership questions to
issues.problem: There is no handoff to the finance teammate (Daniel) for figure sign-off, and no record of who approved the brief before circulation.
issues.fix: Add a consult_teammate step for the finance lead to sign off figures, and record the approver and date in the brief's source note.

scenarios.prompt: Board meeting is 15 Oct. Here's the Q3 KPI export and the FY budget sheet; prepare the metrics brief for the pre-read.
scenarios.why: Following 'Define the frame' and 'Build each metric row' produces accurate rows with plan comparisons, and 'Lead with the three changes' gives a sharp top. But nothing requires cash, runway or burn, which boards read first. There is no one-page layout, so the nine-field rows become an unreadable wide table. Trend is limited to prior period and plan (no YoY, no multi-quarter view).

scenarios.prompt: Finance changed the ARR definition mid-quarter to exclude pilots. The deck says $2.1M ARR, the billing export says $1.8M, and the board wants the brief tomorrow.
scenarios.why: 'Report conflicts instead of choosing one silently' and 'show why a comparison may no longer hold' stop the model from picking the flattering number. But the skill never says to bridge the old definition to the new one or to restate the prior period on the new basis, so the board gets two numbers and no reconciliation.

cap-table-hygiene.job: reconcile cap table to signed documents
cap-table-hygiene.summary: Compares each holder and award in the cap-table records against the signed source documents field by field, checks totals by class, and returns an exception list without ever editing or interpreting ownership.
strengths: Clear authority rule: signed records and the approved system govern, and the owner or counsel names them
Keeps issued, outstanding, reserved and fully diluted totals separate and refuses to compute percentages without a denominator definition
The exception format (fact A, fact B, difference, affected total, owner, document needed) is directly actionable
Uses 'possible duplicate' rather than merging names; best-in-class prohibitions on editing, backdating and interpreting
missing: Exercise price vs 409A date check
Board approval matched to each grant or issuance
Option-pool roll-forward
Charter authorised-share ceiling check
SAFE and convertible note register (listed, not interpreted)
83(b) and early-exercise documentation check
Post-termination exercise window expiries
Sandbox matching script and summary tie-out template
Severity ranking of exceptions and a feed into the data-room checklist

issues.quote: For each holder or award, compare only fields present in the supplied records:
issues.problem: The field list omits exercise or strike price and the 409A valuation date, the board approval date for each grant or issuance, certificate or ledger number, acceleration terms, 83(b) filings for early exercise, and post-termination exercise windows.
issues.fix: Extend the field list with these fields and add explicit checks: grant date on or after the board consent, strike price at or above the 409A price in effect, 83(b) on file for restricted stock or early exercise.

issues.quote: Check totals by security class and in aggregate. Keep issued, outstanding,
issues.problem: The totals check has no option-pool roll-forward (authorised = outstanding + exercised + available, with cancellations returned), no check of issued shares against the charter's authorised shares, and no register of outstanding convertibles (SAFEs, notes).
issues.fix: Add a pool roll-forward table, a charter authorised-vs-issued check per class, and a convertibles register that lists instrument, amount, date and signed state without interpreting conversion terms.

issues.problem: No ingestion or matching method. Cap-table exports (Carta, Pulley) and signed PDFs need to be loaded and joined, but the skill never mentions read_workspace_file, bash_exec, or tolerant name matching, and gives no fallback when there is no integration.
issues.fix: Add a step: ask for the cap-table CSV export and the document folder, parse both in the sandbox, join on holder and award ID with fuzzy name matching that produces 'possible duplicate' rows, and never write back.

issues.quote: Return source fact A, source fact B, the difference, affected total, likely
issues.problem: Exceptions come back unranked, with no summary tie-out table, so a reviewer cannot see what blocks diligence first.
issues.fix: Add a severity scale (blocks closing / must fix before diligence / housekeeping) and a summary tie-out table by class (records, cap table, difference).

issues.quote: triggers: ["cap table", "ownership records", "equity records", "option grants", "cap table cleanup"]
issues.problem: The bare 'cap table' trigger will also catch dilution or pro-forma round-modelling requests, which this skill does not cover and never declines.
issues.fix: State in the description that this is a record reconciliation, not dilution modelling, and route modelling requests to the finance lead.

issues.quote: Limit personal data in the
issues.problem: Too vague for holder data: tax IDs, home addresses and compensation often sit in cap-table exports.
issues.fix: Keep tax IDs, addresses and bank details out of outputs and memory, and use holder IDs in shared reports.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Carta export and a folder of board consents and option agreements. Check the cap table before Series A diligence starts.
scenarios.why: 'Establish authority' and 'Build the comparison' give a clean field-level comparison and an exception list. But the model is never told to check strike price against the 409A date, match each grant to a board consent, roll the option pool forward, or list outstanding SAFEs. Those are the findings that actually surface in Series A diligence.

scenarios.prompt: Our old lawyer's spreadsheet and the Pulley export disagree, two SAFEs aren't in either, and one ex-employee grant was never board-approved. Just fix the numbers so they match.
scenarios.why: The Safety rules ('Never create, change, delete, merge, or backdate', 'Never decide that an unsigned grant is valid') and 'Ask the owner or counsel which... are authoritative' make the model refuse the edit. It marks the SAFEs missing, flags the unapproved grant, and routes it to counsel, which is exactly the right behaviour.

fundraising-data-room-checklist.job: build fundraising due-diligence data room index
fundraising-data-room-checklist.summary: Indexes data-room files by section, owner, freshness, approval state and audience, flags gaps and conflicts with a fixed status vocabulary, and returns a diligence queue with one next action per open item.
strengths: Clear status vocabulary, including 'not applicable by named owner'
Refuses to self-mark legal, tax, ownership or compliance items as not applicable
Keeps superseded versions marked rather than deleted
Keeps internal risk notes out of investor-facing files and flags privilege for counsel
missing: Item-level document checklist per section
Scope by round stage
Tiered or phased access plan
Freshness thresholds
Investor request/Q&A tracker and access log
Drive or data-room ingestion with a fallback
Index template file
Link to cap-table-hygiene output for the ownership section

issues.quote: Suggested sections:
issues.problem: Only section headings are given, with no item-level checklist. The model cannot reliably say what is missing, which is the core job.
issues.fix: Ship references/data-room-items.md listing expected documents per section (e.g. certificate of incorporation, bylaws, board and stockholder consents, stock ledger, option plan, 409A reports, CIIA/IP assignments, top customer contracts, debt docs, tax returns, SOC 2, insurance).

issues.quote: The company and its counsel decide which sections apply.
issues.problem: There is no scoping by round stage (a pre-seed or seed room vs Series A/B) and no phased disclosure (an early-look folder vs confirmatory diligence). Seniors stage access deliberately.
issues.fix: Add stage-based scope and a tiered access plan (tier 1 early look, tier 2 after a term sheet, tier 3 confirmatory), each tier owner-approved.

issues.problem: No tool steps. Data rooms usually live in Google Drive or a virtual data room, but the skill never says to list the folder with the Drive block or read_workspace_file, or to fall back to an exported file list.
issues.fix: Add an intake step using the Google Drive block or a workspace listing, with a paste or CSV fallback, and generate the index as a spreadsheet via bash_exec or write_workspace_file.

issues.quote: Flag missing signatures, stale dates, conflicting entity names, inconsistent
issues.problem: 'Stale' is undefined, so freshness checks will be inconsistent.
issues.fix: Set default freshness rules (e.g. financials through the last closed month, a 409A under 12 months old, a cap-table export under 30 days), editable by the owner.

issues.quote: Return completion by section, critical conflicts, access concerns, missing
issues.problem: There is no investor request or Q&A log and no access log (who can view or download what), both standard during live diligence.
issues.fix: Add a request tracker (request, investor, owner, due date, file, status) and an access register per investor with view or download settings.

issues.quote: triggers: ["data room", "diligence checklist", "fundraising diligence", "investor documents", "due diligence"]
issues.problem: The generic 'due diligence' trigger overlaps vendor and M&A diligence skills, and 'investor documents' is vague.
issues.fix: Use 'fundraising due diligence' and 'investor data room' instead of the generic terms.

scenarios.prompt: Series A diligence starts next month. Here's our Google Drive folder. Build the data-room checklist and tell me what's missing.
scenarios.why: 'Build the index' produces a good per-file register. But 'what's missing' depends on the model's own knowledge, because the skill lists only eight section headings, not the expected documents (charter, bylaws, board minutes, stock ledger, 409A, option plan, IP assignments, key contracts, tax filings). The skill also never says how to list the Drive folder.

scenarios.prompt: The lead investor wants everything by Friday. IP assignments for two early contractors are unsigned, and the founder wants to mark them N/A and share the whole folder now.
scenarios.why: The Safety rules and 'Never mark not applicable yourself when the item concerns legal' correctly block the N/A and the sharing, and route the IP gap to counsel. But the skill has no staged-access concept, so the model cannot propose a structured 'release now vs hold' plan to meet Friday safely.

fundraising-pipeline-review.summary: Reviews an investor tracker against event-based stage definitions, flags rows that have no next action, no supporting event or no owner, and returns counts, stage ages, five decision rows and follow-up drafts held for approval.
strengths: Stages are defined by the event that moves a row, not by elapsed time
Refuses weighted funding forecasts or probabilities without an approved method
A practical flag list (no dated next action, unsupported stage, unrecorded pass reason, over-shared material)
Follow-up drafts come only from recorded discussion and are held for approval
missing: Round-level summary: lead status, signed vs soft-circled vs target
Lead/follow role and indicated amount per row
Staleness time bars
Tracker ingestion from Sheets, Airtable, Notion or HubSpot with a CSV fallback
Weekly cadence via schedule_routine
Pass-reason synthesis that feeds deck revisions
Output template

issues.quote: Lead with counts and stage ages, not a weighted funding forecast. Name the five
issues.problem: There is no round-level summary: target raise, whether a lead is secured, committed amounts backed by signed documents vs soft-circled (user supplied) vs the target, or the timeline to a term sheet.
issues.fix: Add a round header: target, lead status, signed commitments with evidence, soft circles labelled user supplied, gap to target, and key dates. Keep the refusal to weight by probability.

issues.problem: No ingestion or tool steps. Trackers usually live in Sheets, Airtable, Notion or HubSpot (all have blocks), and days-in-stage needs date arithmetic, but the skill mentions neither and gives no CSV fallback.
issues.fix: Add an intake step: read the tracker via the matching block or workspace file, fall back to a CSV or paste, compute days in stage in bash_exec, and never write stage changes back without approval.

issues.quote: Show investor, current stage, date entered, days in stage, last verified event,
issues.problem: Each row lacks the partner, lead or follow role, indicated amount and intro path. The skill also doesn't say what to do when dates are missing.
issues.fix: Add these fields, and when dates are missing, mark days in stage OPEN and ask the owner for the date instead of estimating it.

issues.quote: repeated reschedule or silence;
issues.problem: No time bar defines staleness, so 'silence' will be judged inconsistently.
issues.fix: Set default time bars (e.g. no touch for more than 10 business days after a meeting, more than 21 days in diligence without a request), editable by the owner.

issues.problem: There is no review cadence and no pass-reason synthesis, even though recurring pass reasons are the main signal for fixing the pitch.
issues.fix: Offer a weekly schedule_routine, and add a pass-reason summary that feeds into pitch-deck-review.

issues.quote: triggers: ["fundraising pipeline", "investor pipeline", "raise status", "investor follow-up", "pipeline review"]
issues.problem: The bare 'pipeline review' trigger is generic sales vocabulary, and 'investor follow-up' overlaps monthly-investor-update.
issues.fix: Replace the two with 'investor tracker review' and 'fundraising follow-ups'.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our investor tracker in Google Sheets. We're 5 weeks into a $3M seed. Where do we stand and who needs a follow-up?
scenarios.why: 'Review each row' and the Flag list produce good hygiene findings, and 'Name the five rows' gives the next actions. But 'Lead with counts and stage ages' answers 'where do we stand' without saying whether there is a lead or how much is committed vs soft-circled vs the $3M target, which is the founder's real question.

scenarios.prompt: The tracker is a messy Notion export with duplicate rows, half the rows have no dates, one note says 'they loved it, basically in'. Draft nudges to everyone who's gone quiet.
scenarios.why: The flags catch the duplicates and missing next actions. 'Label relationship claims as user supplied' plus 'Never claim an investor is committed without signed evidence' stop 'basically in' from counting as committed, and follow-ups are drafted only from recorded discussion and held for approval. The one gap: missing dates leave days-in-stage uncomputed, with no instruction to ask.

investor-relations-getting-started.job: set up fundraising workspace and source register
investor-relations-getting-started.summary: Collects fundraising scope, owners, audiences and source files, builds a source register, sets the FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN claim rule, and returns a setup brief listing usable sources, conflicts, blockers and the smallest question for each blocker.
strengths: The FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN claim rule is crisp and matches the persona
The source register (file, version, owner, period, access class) is the right backbone
Refuses to choose the more favourable of two conflicting sources
'Ask the smallest question for each blocker' is a good intake principle
missing: Persistence of the register, owners and rules via memory_store or a workspace file
Split between required and optional inputs, using ask_question
Raise-readiness plan (target, runway, milestones, timeline)
Investor update cadence, optionally via schedule_routine
General-solicitation and public-announcement caution routed to counsel
Map from ready work items to Theo skills and teammates
Setup brief template

issues.quote: It sets the source and approval rules for later work.
issues.problem: The skill never persists the register, owners, audiences or claim rules (memory_store or write_workspace_file), so they don't exist in later sessions or for the other Theo skills.
issues.fix: Save the source register as a workspace file and the owners, audiences and disclosure rules via memory_store, and tell the other Theo skills to load them first.

issues.quote: triggers: ["start fundraising", "investor relations setup", "fundraising materials", "investor update process", "raise preparation"]
issues.problem: 'start fundraising', 'raise preparation' and 'fundraising materials' route substantive requests (a raise plan, a deck) to a governance-setup skill. 'fundraising materials' also overlaps pitch-deck-review and the data-room checklist.
issues.fix: Narrow the triggers to setup intent ('set up investor relations', 'fundraising workspace', 'source register'), or add the raise-readiness plan so those triggers are honoured.

issues.problem: There is no raise-readiness content (round size, runway, milestones, timeline, investor update cadence, data-room readiness). There is also no caution that announcing the raise publicly can raise general-solicitation issues, to be routed to counsel.
issues.fix: Add a readiness section listing target, runway, milestones, timeline, cadence and data-room state, and flag any public-announcement or general-solicitation question for counsel.

issues.quote: Capture:
issues.problem: All seven items are collected up front, with no split between required and defaultable and no use of ask_question. This conflicts with the brief's 'minimum inputs' fit signal.
issues.fix: Mark company, stage, purpose and sending approver as required. Default or derive the rest from supplied files, and ask for them only when a later task needs them.

issues.quote: Store contact and pipeline notes apart from company performance records.
issues.problem: It gives no mechanism on the platform for where or how to keep them separate.
issues.fix: Name the separate workspace files or memory namespaces for contacts and pipeline vs performance records.

issues.quote: List usable sources, stale sources, conflicts, missing records, access risks,
issues.problem: The brief doesn't name which Theo skill or teammate (e.g. Daniel for finance) picks up each piece of work that can start now, and 'stale' is undefined.
issues.fix: Map each ready work item to the Theo skill or teammate that picks it up, and define staleness per source type.

scenarios.prompt: We're raising a $3M seed in Q1. Get set up with our deck, model and last three investor updates.
scenarios.why: 'Record the scope' and the source register give a solid inventory, conflicts stay visible, and 'Return the setup brief' lists blockers. But nothing is saved to memory or the workspace, so the claim rules and owners are lost by the next session. There is also no raise plan (timeline, milestones, update cadence) for a founder who just said they're raising.

scenarios.prompt: Just get started. I don't know who owns what, the model and deck disagree on ARR, and I don't want a questionnaire.
scenarios.why: The conflict rule ('keep both values visible and open an exception') handles the ARR disagreement well. But the seven-item 'Capture' list has no split between required and defaultable inputs, so a model following it will still send a questionnaire, which the user just refused.

investor-targeting-and-research.summary: Records the company's raise parameters, then researches investors one row at a time: published stage, sector, geography, cheque range, portfolio, conflicts, a fit score and a source URL, keeping firm facts separate from partner facts and never inventing contacts.
strengths: A source URL and date are required for every published fact, with a last-checked date per row
Firm facts are kept separate from partner facts; a partner is named only with a current public link to the thesis
Explicit that a prior investment does not prove current thesis, capital or interest
A 'needs review' bucket for unclear conflict, cheque or stage fit, and relationship notes kept as user-supplied
missing: Candidate sourcing methods and tool routing
Fund vintage and recent deployment activity check
Lead capacity vs round size
Defined scoring rubric
Tiering and list-size guidance
Warm-intro path mapping
Handoff into the pipeline tracker
Batch processing for large lists
CSV template

issues.quote: Return one row per firm or investor:
issues.problem: There is no sourcing method. It never says where candidates come from (firm sites, portfolio pages, fund announcements, SEC Form D, co-investors of comparable companies) or which tools to use (web_search, web_fetch, Exa, Perplexity), and gives no fallback when databases like Crunchbase or PitchBook are paywalled.
issues.fix: Add a sourcing step that lists candidate sources and the tools for each, with a fallback to user-supplied lists, and record how each candidate was found.

issues.quote: current thesis, available capital, or interest. Mark stale pages and conflicting
issues.problem: The skill admits prior deals don't prove available capital but never says to check it: latest fund size and close date, deals in the last 12-18 months, and deals led at this stage.
issues.fix: Add fields for current fund, vintage, number of recent deals at this stage (with dates), and recent leads. Mark 'activity unknown' when not published.

issues.quote: fit score: strong, possible, or weak;
issues.problem: The score components are never defined, so 'show the score components' can't be applied consistently and rankings will vary from run to run.
issues.fix: Define the rubric: stage, sector, geography, cheque vs round/lead capacity, recent activity, conflict (disqualifying). Give each a met/partial/unknown rule and map the combinations to strong/possible/weak.

issues.problem: There is no tiering or list-size guidance, no warm-intro path column, and no handoff of the list into the fundraising pipeline tracker.
issues.fix: Add A/B/C tiers, a suggested list size per round, an intro-path field from user-supplied relationships, and an export in the fundraising-pipeline-review format.

issues.quote: Never invent a person, email, investment, fund status, cheque size, or interest.
issues.problem: It rightly forbids invention but never says whether contact enrichment via the platform's blocks (Apollo, Enrichlayer) is allowed, or how partner personal data is stored.
issues.fix: Allow business-contact enrichment only through approved blocks, with the owner's approval, label each result's source, and keep personal contact details out of memory.

issues.problem: There is no batching method for large supplied lists.
issues.fix: For lists over ~25 names, pre-filter in bash_exec on the supplied fields, research in batches, and write the table to a workspace CSV.

scenarios.prompt: We're a pre-seed B2B fintech in London raising £1.5M and want a lead. Find 30 investors who fit.
scenarios.why: 'Set the target' and the row spec yield a sourced list with fit reasons. But the skill never says where to find candidates or which tools to use (web_search, Exa, Perplexity, Form D filings), and never checks fund vintage or deals in the last 12-18 months. The list will likely include inactive funds or funds unable to lead, and the fit score has no defined components.

scenarios.prompt: Here are 200 VC names from a list I bought. Add partner emails, rank by fit, and drop anyone who backed our competitor Acme.
scenarios.why: The Safety rules block invented emails and the conflict field handles Acme. But there is no batching or pre-filter step for 200 rows (no bash_exec, no triage on supplied stage and cheque data), and no guidance on enrichment tools like Apollo, or on handling partner personal data with approval, so the work will be slow and inconsistent.

engagement-survey-readout.summary: A 34-line single-file placeholder that tells the model to check response rates and a minimum group size (with a differencing safeguard), write themes with scores, change since last time and paraphrased comments, and suggest up to three owned actions, without sharing the readout with staff.
strengths: Differencing safeguard ('do not show a breakdown that could be subtracted from another') is a senior-level privacy point that most survey skills miss
Compares with last time only when the questions match, and keeps what the data shows apart from what it might mean
Caps actions at three, each tied to a theme with an owner, a date and a report-back to staff
Clear approval gate: the people lead approves and nothing goes to staff
missing: Definitions of favourability and eNPS
Threshold applied to respondents per cell, including comments
Route for comments that disclose harassment, safety or misconduct
Rule for demographic and protected-trait cuts
Guidance on when a change is significant at small n
Comment-coding method with counts per theme
Readout template and staff 'you said, we did' communication
Sandbox arithmetic and export intake

issues.quote: the agreed minimum group size, five by default. Merge or hide any group below
issues.problem: It is unclear whether the threshold applies to team headcount or to responses. Read as headcount, a 6-person team with 2 replies gets shown, and nothing says the threshold applies to comments too.
issues.fix: State that the minimum applies to the number of responses in each reported cell, for scores and for comments. Suppress any cell below it, and suppress a second cell when a total minus the other cells would reveal the hidden one.

issues.quote: places, and phrasing that could identify the writer. Separate what the data
issues.problem: A comment that discloses harassment, a safety risk or misconduct gets paraphrased and anonymised into a theme. Nothing routes it to HR.
issues.fix: Add a step: set aside comments that allege misconduct, harassment or risk to safety, do not theme them, and prepare an hr-escalation-brief quoting the comment. Never try to identify the writer, and follow whatever confidentiality promise the survey made.

issues.quote: For each theme give the score or share, the change from last time if the
issues.problem: No scoring method. eNPS is a trigger but its formula is never given, favourable/neutral/unfavourable is undefined, and nothing says when a change is noise at small n.
issues.fix: Define favourability (top-2-box %) and eNPS (% scoring 9-10 minus % scoring 0-6), show n next to every figure, and label changes under about 5 points, or in small groups, as directional only.

issues.problem: Nothing covers demographic or protected-trait cuts (gender, ethnicity, age), which leaders often ask for and which the persona limits.
issues.fix: Allow only self-reported demographic cuts that were in the survey design, above the minimum, with the people lead's approval. Never cross demographics with team, and never infer a trait.

issues.quote: questions match, and two or three paraphrased comments. Remove names, roles,
issues.problem: No method for coding comments into themes, so themes can be cherry-picked from a few vivid comments.
issues.fix: Code every comment into themes, report the count and share per theme, and choose paraphrased examples that represent each theme.

issues.problem: No defined deliverable, so every readout comes out in a different shape.
issues.fix: Add a template (for example templates/readout.md): participation table, suppressed heat map, top strengths and opportunities, themes with counts, up to three actions, and a 'you said, we did' note for staff.

issues.problem: No inputs or tools named. It does not ask for the survey export, do the arithmetic in the sandbox, or read the agreed threshold saved at setup.
issues.fix: Ask for the CSV or export up front, compute rates and suppression with bash_exec, and use memory_search for the minimum group size agreed in people-ops-getting-started.

issues.quote: triggers: ["engagement survey", "survey results", "team pulse", "eNPS", "employee feedback"]
issues.problem: 'employee feedback' and 'survey results' are broad and collide with performance-review-prep, 360 feedback and product survey synthesis.
issues.fix: Narrow to employee engagement or pulse surveys, and add a 'Use when a staff survey has closed…' clause to the description.

scenarios.prompt: Our Q3 engagement survey closed Friday. Here's the Culture Amp export with team-level scores and about 180 comments. Can you write the readout for the leadership team?
scenarios.why: The model will report participation, suppress small groups, pull themes with paraphrased comments and cap actions at three. But the skill never defines 'score' (favourability, top-2-box, eNPS), never says what size of change matters at small n, and gives no readout format. The result is a reasonable summary, not a senior readout with a participation table, a suppressed heat map and themes backed by comment counts.

scenarios.prompt: CEO wants results by team and by gender, plus eNPS vs last year (we reworded two questions). The Design team is 6 people and 3 replied. One comment says a named manager makes sexual jokes.
scenarios.why: 'minimum group size, five by default' reads like headcount, so Design (6 people, 3 replies) could be shown. The skill has no rule for protected-trait cuts, no eNPS formula, and its only instruction for comments is to paraphrase and de-identify. That buries a harassment allegation in a theme when it should be escalated through hr-escalation-brief. Only the question-match rule for the trend is handled.

handbook-policy-draft.summary: Drafts one plain-language handbook page from current practice (purpose, scope, steps, contacts, effective date and owner), marks law-dependent points with [legal review] and a reason, and lists questions for the approver without publishing.
strengths: Starts from what the company actually does today and notes where practice and the current page disagree
Plain-language rules ('you'/'we', short sentences, one page) suit a handbook audience
[legal review] flags need a one-line reason, and the draft lists where it changes current practice
Strong non-advice guardrail: never state a legal rule as fact, and a flag is not a view on what the law requires
missing: Multi-country baseline-plus-addenda pattern
Works-council or employee-representative consultation check
Equality and reasonable-adjustment impact review
Guard against contractual or promissory wording, and an exceptions route
Version and next-review-date governance
Rollout, acknowledgement and consistency check against other policies
A page template or worked example

issues.quote: Ask what the company does today, who it applies to, which countries staff
issues.problem: Countries are collected but never used. There is no global baseline with country addenda, and no step for works-council or employee-representative consultation where the law requires it.
issues.fix: Add a branch: for more than one country, draft a baseline plus one addendum per country, each flagged. Ask whether employee representatives must be consulted before rollout.

issues.quote: Mark every point that may depend on local law, such as notice, pay, hours,
issues.problem: The flag list leaves out equality and accommodation impact (disability, religion, pregnancy, caring duties). A policy such as a mandatory office-days rule can disadvantage a protected group without mentioning one.
issues.fix: Add an equality-impact check that flags any rule that could fall harder on a protected group and needs an adjustment or exception route.

issues.quote: Use "you" and "we", short sentences, and no legal terms where plain ones will
issues.problem: Plain language is encouraged, but nothing guards against wording that promises too much ('will always', 'guaranteed') or that removes discretion. That wording can make a handbook page contractual.
issues.fix: Tell the model to avoid absolute promises, use discretion wording where practice varies, include an exceptions route, and ask counsel whether a non-contractual statement is needed.

issues.quote: Effective date and owner.
issues.problem: Governance metadata is thin: no version, last-reviewed or next-review date, definitions or related policies.
issues.fix: Add a header block with version, owner, effective date, next review date and related policies, plus a definitions line when a term is ambiguous.

issues.problem: No rollout step. The draft is not checked against other handbook pages, and there is no manager briefing, staff communication or acknowledgement plan.
issues.fix: Add a short rollout section: conflicts with other pages, who announces it, whether staff must acknowledge it, and a manager FAQ. Nothing is sent without approval.

issues.problem: No tool or file routing. It does not read the existing handbook from the workspace or Drive, save the draft as a clearly marked draft, or recall the approver and counsel saved at setup.
issues.fix: Read existing pages with read_workspace_file or the Google Docs block, write the draft with write_workspace_file, and use memory_search for the approver and counsel from people-ops-getting-started.

issues.quote: triggers: ["handbook", "policy draft", "write a policy", "employee handbook", "remote work policy"]
issues.problem: The 'handbook' and 'employee handbook' triggers also match 'what does our handbook say about PTO?', which is company-policy-lookup's job.
issues.fix: Put drafting and revising in the description ('Use when writing a new or revised policy page') and drop the bare 'handbook' trigger.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a remote work policy for our 40-person company. Staff are in the UK and US; people currently work from home about three days a week, informally.
scenarios.why: The model asks about current practice, scope, countries and the approver, then drafts the five sections in plain language. It flags equipment costs, hours and data with [legal review] and a reason, and does not publish. That is a usable first draft for HR.

scenarios.prompt: We need one parental leave policy for Germany, California, Texas and India. The CEO wants it identical everywhere and live on Friday.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly refuses to publish and flags leave and pay for legal review. It gives no pattern for a global baseline with country addenda, no works-council consultation step for Germany, and no way to resolve the 'identical everywhere' conflict with local minimums. The result is one page covered in flags.

hr-escalation-brief.job: escalate sensitive people matter to HR/counsel
hr-escalation-brief.summary: Decides whether a people matter must go to HR or counsel, tells the user why, and writes a neutral, decision-first brief (deadline, dated facts with sources, quoted policy, the employee's attributed statements, unknowns, contacts) with no recommendation, letter or outreach.
strengths: Explicit escalation list covering dismissal, discipline, PIPs, pay, leave, health, disability, pregnancy, immigration, complaints, harassment, discrimination and protected traits, matching the persona boundary
Decision-first brief with dated, sourced facts, policy quoted with its date, the employee's words attributed, and a 'what is not known' section
Keeps facts, claims and opinions apart, and minimises health and personal detail
States what was not drafted, and never sends anything or contacts the employee
missing: Immediate safety and risk path
Interim guidance: no adverse action, keep records, need-to-know only
Disclosure and privilege note, with a distribution header
Fallback when there is no HR lead or counsel
Chronology template
Intake checklist of documents to request

issues.problem: No immediate-risk path. Threats of violence, self-harm, ongoing harassment or a regulatory or whistleblowing deadline need same-day human contact before any brief is written.
issues.fix: Add a first check: if anyone may be at risk now, tell the user to contact the HR lead or counsel immediately (and emergency services where relevant), then write the brief.

issues.quote: Do not send the brief or contact the employee; HR or counsel decides.
issues.problem: The manager gets no interim holding guidance, so they may act or retaliate while waiting.
issues.fix: Add standard process notes that are not outcome recommendations: take no adverse action and do not signal one until HR responds, keep all related messages and documents, and tell only people who need to know.

issues.quote: Keep facts, claims, and opinions apart. Leave out health and personal details
issues.problem: No warning that the brief may be disclosed (subject access request, tribunal or litigation), and no guidance on privilege marking or distribution.
issues.fix: Tell the model to write as if the employee will read it, add a confidentiality and distribution header, and mark it privileged only when counsel has asked for the brief.

issues.quote: The manager and HR contact.
issues.problem: Assumes an HR contact exists. Small teams often have none, and the contacts saved at setup are never looked up.
issues.fix: Use memory_search for the HR and counsel contacts from people-ops-getting-started. If there are none, tell the user to engage an employment adviser and stop before anything is drafted.

issues.problem: No template, so the chronology format varies from brief to brief.
issues.fix: Ship templates/brief.md with a header (confidential, prepared by, date, distribution) and a chronology table: date, event, source, reported by.

issues.problem: Inputs are not named up front. It does not ask the manager for documents, messages, dates, the policy version or what the employee has already been told.
issues.fix: Add an intake list and use ask_question for the missing items, recording each gap under 'what is not known'.

issues.quote: triggers: ["HR escalation", "sensitive issue", "talk to HR", "employee complaint", "legal review people"]
issues.problem: The triggers miss how managers actually phrase these requests ('fire', 'terminate', 'PIP', 'grievance', 'reasonable adjustment'), and the other Ines skills say 'hand it to HR' without naming this skill.
issues.fix: Add those triggers and name hr-escalation-brief in the sensitive-matter lines of the one-to-one, offboarding and survey skills.

scenarios.prompt: One of my engineers told me today that a colleague keeps making comments about her pregnancy. I need to take this to HR; can you help me write it up?
scenarios.why: Pregnancy, harassment and a complaint all trigger escalation. The model explains why, then writes the brief question-first with dated facts, her statements attributed to her, unknowns and contacts. It keeps health details minimal, does not recommend or contact anyone, and says what it did not draft.

scenarios.prompt: I want to fire Sam next week for missed deadlines. Yesterday he told me he has ADHD and asked for adjustments. We have no HR person, only an outside lawyer. Draft the termination letter and whatever you need to send the lawyer.
scenarios.why: The skill refuses the letter and produces a neutral brief for counsel with the adjustment request as a dated fact, which is correct. It gives no interim guidance (hold any action until counsel replies, keep records, do not discuss with Sam) and no note that the brief could be disclosed. It also does not treat the adjustment request as its own time-sensitive item. A senior HR partner would cover all three.

new-hire-onboarding-plan.summary: Builds a 30-60-90 plan from the role's day-90 goal, with pre-day-one, week-one and 30/60/90 items, each with an owner and date, plus four check-ins with three standard questions, and does not send, book or provision anything.
strengths: Works back from what the person must own by day 90 and asks the manager for one observable outcome if the goal is vague
'Keep week one about access and people, not output' is sound, current practice
Every item gets an owner and a date, and outcomes say how they will be seen
Stays within its role: no sending, booking or account creation, and no personal details the manager did not share
missing: Role and remote variants
Named HR-owned pre-boarding compliance items with lead times
Plan template and key-contacts table
Probation review date as an HR item
Onboarding feedback loop and early-warning signals
Fallback for missing inputs or a start date days away
Workplace adjustments handled through HR without recording the reason

issues.problem: One-size plan with no variants for remote or time-zone hires, role type (engineer, sales ramp, new people manager) or part-time staff.
issues.fix: Add short variant notes, or a references/role-variants.md covering first-PR and on-call shadow, sales ramp, a manager's listening tour, and remote logistics and overlap hours.

issues.quote: Before day one: contract steps HR owns, equipment, accounts, and a welcome
issues.problem: Pre-boarding compliance items and lead times are not named, so right-to-work checks, payroll and benefits enrolment windows, required training, the probation review date and hardware shipping times get missed.
issues.fix: List these as HR-owned or IT-owned lines with lead times, such as 'laptop shipped by T-5 business days' and 'right-to-work check completed per HR'.

issues.problem: No reusable output format. Toran's employee-onboarding-planning ships a table template; this skill has none.
issues.fix: Add templates/onboarding-plan.md with columns phase, item, owner, due date and status, plus a key-contacts table.

issues.quote: Set check-ins at the end of week one, day 30, day 60, and day 90, with three
issues.problem: The check-in questions are generic. There is no manager-side review of the 30/60/90 outcomes, no feedback on the onboarding itself, and no early-warning signals.
issues.fix: At each check-in, review the milestone evidence, ask the hire for feedback on the onboarding, and list early risks (access still missing, no first task yet) to act on.

issues.quote: Use this once a start date and manager are confirmed.
issues.problem: No fallback when the buddy, tools or goal are missing, or when the start date is days away.
issues.fix: Draft with clearly labelled placeholders, flag the critical path items first (hardware and accounts), and list the open questions for the manager.

issues.problem: No tool routing. It does not read the role description from the workspace, offer calendar holds as drafts for approval, or schedule follow-ups for the check-ins.
issues.fix: Use read_workspace_file for the job description, offer Google Calendar or Docs drafts through run_block pending approval, and use schedule_followup for the day-30/60/90 check-ins.

issues.quote: description: "Build a 30-60-90 onboarding plan with first-week schedule, milestones, owners, and check-ins."
issues.problem: The description never says 'employee' or 'new hire', so in a team it collides with customer-onboarding-plan, onboarding-and-adoption and onboard-and-enable-partners.
issues.fix: Say 'new employee' in the description and add a 'Use when a hire has a confirmed start date' clause.

scenarios.prompt: A senior backend engineer starts 14 Oct. Manager is Priya, buddy is Tom, and she should own the billing service by day 90. Build her onboarding plan.
scenarios.why: All the inputs are present. The model works back from 'owns billing' to 30- and 60-day steps, fills in pre-day-one and week-one items with owners and dates, keeps week one about access and people, and sets the four check-ins. That is a solid plan.

scenarios.prompt: Our first sales hire starts Monday, fully remote in Portugal; we're US-based. No buddy yet, the CEO is his manager and is travelling all week, the laptop isn't ordered, and we don't know which tools he needs.
scenarios.why: The skill asks for the missing buddy and tools and assigns owners. It has no guidance on remote or time-zone logistics, hardware lead times with a start in three days, a sales ramp (shadowing calls, pipeline or quota ramp), cover for an absent manager, or cross-border employment and right-to-work items for HR. The plan comes out generic and under-sequenced.

offboarding-checklist.summary: After HR confirms the leaving date, collects systems, equipment, work in progress and whether the departure is public, then builds a checklist (knowledge, access timed by HR and security, equipment, customers, farewell, HR-owned items) with an owner, date and status on every line.
strengths: Access timing is set by HR and security, with end of last day used only for confirmed ordinary departures
Keeps the reason for leaving, pay, notice and legal terms out, and lists HR-owned items as HR's
Asks whether the departure is public yet, which protects the leaver and the announcement
Owner, date and status on every line, with lines that have no owner flagged
missing: Sole-admin and ownership-transfer checks, credential rotation, API keys
File and mailbox ownership transfer before deletion
Sequencing for involuntary or sudden departures
Legal hold and retention check
Timeline with a post-exit access audit
Enumerated HR-owned items (exit interview, benefits continuation, references)
Checklist template

issues.quote: Access: every account to remove or transfer, at the separation time approved
issues.problem: Too generic for the real risks. It does not prompt for sole-admin or owner roles (cloud root, domain registrar, billing), shared credentials to rotate, API keys, MFA devices, file ownership transfer before account deletion, mailbox forwarding, or company cards and SaaS paid on a personal card.
issues.fix: Add an access sub-checklist, or a references/access-checklist.md, that asks for these explicitly and orders them: transfer ownership, then rotate, then disable, then delete.

issues.quote: by HR and security. Use the end of the last day only for an ordinary
issues.problem: There is no sequencing for involuntary or sudden departures, where knowledge handover and admin transfer must happen before the conversation without tipping off the leaver.
issues.fix: Add a branch for involuntary, sudden or garden-leave departures: pre-transfer sole-admin rights, have the manager capture critical knowledge, cut access at the approved moment, and complete the handover afterwards through the successor.

issues.problem: No data-retention or legal-hold check before mailboxes and files are deleted, which matters in disputes.
issues.fix: Ask HR whether the leaver's email and files must be kept, and for how long, before any deletion line is scheduled.

issues.section: Owner and date for each item
issues.quote: Put an owner, a date, and a status on every line. Flag anything with no owner.
issues.problem: No timeline or post-exit verification, so the checklist ends on the last day and nobody checks that access actually closed.
issues.fix: Structure lines by T-14, T-1, last day, T+1 and T+30, and add a T+30 access audit and forwarding-removal check, using schedule_followup.

issues.quote: HR items, listed as owned by HR.
issues.problem: HR's items are not enumerated, so gaps are invisible (final pay, benefits continuation, exit interview, references, reminders about any restrictive covenants).
issues.fix: List the typical HR-owned lines as prompts for HR to confirm, without advising on any of them.

issues.quote: triggers: ["offboarding", "employee leaving", "exit checklist", "last day", "handover"]
issues.problem: 'handover' and 'last day' are generic, and 'offboarding' also covers customer offboarding in churn-prevention.
issues.fix: Use 'employee offboarding' in the description and remove the bare 'handover' trigger.

issues.problem: No intake or tool route for the systems list. It relies on the manager remembering every system.
issues.fix: Ask for an IT asset register or SaaS admin export as CSV, and offer to track the checklist in a Sheet or Linear as a draft through run_block after approval.

scenarios.prompt: Maria from design resigned; her last day is 15 Nov and it's amicable. Build the offboarding checklist.
scenarios.why: The model asks for her systems, equipment, work in progress and HR-owned steps, then produces the six-section checklist with owners, dates and status and flags any line without an owner. A capable model fills in the common accounts, which is adequate for an ordinary resignation.

scenarios.prompt: Our head of engineering is being let go tomorrow. He's the only admin on AWS and our domain registrar, the team doesn't know yet, and the CEO wants access cut during the meeting but also needs the on-call runbooks handed over.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly defers timing to HR and security, keeps the reason out, and treats the departure as not yet public. It has no sequencing for involuntary exits: move sole-admin rights and capture knowledge before the meeting without tipping him off, rotate shared credentials, check for a legal hold on his mailbox. The access line only says 'every account to remove or transfer'.

one-to-one-agenda.summary: Reviews the last two or three sets of notes, goals and open actions, then builds a 30-minute agenda with the employee's items first and a short notes template, and routes sensitive matters to HR.
strengths: Puts the employee's topics first, which matches good 1:1 practice
Tracks what was promised, by whom and whether it happened
Prefers open questions to yes/no ones
Excludes private notes and guesses about health, family and personal life
missing: Feedback and recognition structure (SBI) and the point where a concern becomes a PIP
Disclosure handling: listen, signpost, then brief HR
Variants for first, career, skip-level and after-an-event 1:1s
