Notes fallback and open actions carried between meetings
Question bank and time boxes
Note-retention and subject-access awareness

issues.quote: discipline, suggest the manager pause and bring in HR.
issues.problem: 'Pause' can shut down an employee's disclosure. The rule also escalates normal 1:1 topics such as asking about a raise, and it never names the hr-escalation-brief skill.
issues.fix: Tell the manager to listen, not probe or diagnose, point to support (EAP, the HR contact), and agree a next step. Then prepare an hr-escalation-brief for complaints, health adjustments, discipline or pay decisions, while treating an ordinary compensation question as a normal topic to take to HR.

issues.problem: No guidance for giving feedback, raising a performance concern or recognising good work, which are among the most common 1:1 needs. No line is drawn where a concern becomes performance-review-prep or a PIP escalation.
issues.fix: Add a feedback item using situation-behaviour-impact with one dated example and an agreed next step, and send patterns that could lead to a PIP to hr-escalation-brief.

issues.quote: Read the last two or three sets of notes, the person's current goals, and
issues.problem: Assumes the notes are to hand, with no fallback, and does not carry open actions between meetings.
issues.fix: Fetch notes through run_block or run_mcp_tool (Docs, Notion) or ask for a paste, and keep open actions with memory_store so the next agenda starts from them.

issues.problem: No variants for a first 1:1 with a new report, a quarterly career conversation, a skip-level or a 1:1 after a hard event.
issues.fix: Add short variant agendas (for example references/variants.md) with the questions suited to each.

issues.quote: Suggest open questions such as "what is getting in your way?" rather than
issues.problem: Only one example question and no time boxes for the 30 minutes, so agendas drift.
issues.fix: Give a small question bank by theme (blockers, workload, growth, wellbeing without probing) and suggested minutes per item.

issues.quote: dates, and anything to follow up. Keep notes factual and about work.
issues.problem: No mention that the employee can request 1:1 notes (subject access request) or that they may be used in a dispute, and no guidance on shared versus private notes or where they are kept.
issues.fix: Tell the model to write notes as if the employee will read them, and to keep agreed actions in the shared record.

issues.quote: triggers: ["1:1 agenda", "one to one", "manager meeting", "check-in agenda", "1-1 prep"]
issues.problem: 'manager meeting' and 'check-in agenda' are generic and collide with onboarding check-ins and ordinary meeting prep.
issues.fix: Replace them with 'weekly 1:1', 'one-on-one with my report' and 'skip-level'.

scenarios.prompt: I have my weekly 1:1 with Jordan tomorrow. Here are my notes from the last two and her Q4 goals; prep an agenda.
scenarios.why: The model checks what was promised and whether it happened, puts Jordan's topics first, adds one fact per goal and one open question, and returns the notes template. That is a usable 30-minute agenda.

scenarios.prompt: Prep my 1:1 with Alex. My notes are somewhere in Notion. He's missed two deadlines and seems down (I think something's going on at home), and I need to tell him he isn't getting the promotion this cycle.
scenarios.why: The skill rightly stops the model recording guesses about his home life. It gives no fallback for the missing notes (Notion through run_mcp_tool or run_block, or a paste) and no feedback structure for the missed deadlines. It also has no guidance on delivering the promotion news or on checking in on wellbeing without probing. The blanket 'pause and bring in HR' may lead the model to push the whole conversation to HR.

14:monthly-profit-and-loss-summary.job: summarise monthly P&L and explain variances
14:monthly-profit-and-loss-summary.summary: Has Mina draft a monthly or year-to-date P&L brief from ledger exports. Bundled scripts refuse comparisons across different bases, tie detail to report totals, compute changes and plan variances, trace each driver to GL, invoice or expense rows with the untraced amount stated, and log the owner's review against a hash of the brief.
strengths: pl_variance.py refuses to compare different or unknown bases (exit 2). It holds back the net result unless the detail ties to report totals and nothing is unmapped, and it prints 'n/m' with the reason for zero, tiny or sign-changed bases. All three script selftests pass.

Each driver quotes traced and untraced amounts from trace_movement.py. Unproven causes must be labelled as hypotheses. A clean-context run_sub_session re-checks the brief for a first month or a large movement.

The references are sourced and practitioner-grade: IRS Pub 538 and QBO basis switching, SAB 99 qualitative materiality, and traps such as 1099-K revenue, net processor payouts, loan principal, owner draws and suspense accounts.

Fallbacks are graceful: with no Python, figures are hand-computed and labelled as such; with no ledger integration, the user uploads an export; if the state volume is missing, every file is delivered to the user. Ledger access is read-only.
YTD handling never assumes a January fiscal year, and it refuses a missing or repeated month, mixed bases or currencies, and a YTD file summed into another YTD.
The pl-brief.md template has a reusable header (basis, gross/net, source, DRAFT), Coverage, open items marked included or excluded, decisions needed, and a cash section kept apart from profit.
Review status only becomes 'reviewed' when the owner's reply is logged by log_approval.py against the brief's SHA-256.
missing: A check that the books are closed before summarising: bank/card reconciliations done and recurring journals (payroll accrual, depreciation, prepaid amortisation) posted
Favourable/unfavourable labels and a % on budget variances, plus a warning when plan periods do not match
KPIs owners expect: gross and operating margin %, trend against the trailing 3-month average or run-rate
A reshape recipe or helper for standard QBO and Xero P&L exports (section headings, Total rows, parentheses, US dates)
De-duplication and an over-trace guard across trace sources
A default materiality threshold for which movements need explaining when the owner has not set one
A note on multi-currency entities (FX gains and losses, translated versus original currency)

issues.quote: --sources /home/user/in/trace-*.csv
issues.problem: The reshape step writes '<out>.skipped.csv' and '<out>.unmapped.csv' side files (for example trace-invoices.csv.skipped.csv), and this glob matches them. Run on the package's own example register, trace_movement.py then exits 2 with 'needs date, account, amount'. Following the step literally fails whenever any row is skipped or unmapped, which the worked example has.
issues.fix: Write the side files outside the glob (for example /home/user/in/skipped/) or name them skipped-*.csv. Tell the model to pass the reshaped files explicitly.

issues.quote: Get them, in this order of preference:
issues.problem: The skill never says to use one source per account. A full GL detail export and the invoice register both carry the revenue postings. Passing both doubled the traced amount (7,000 against a 3,500 change, untraced -3,500) with exit 0 and no warning. The brief would then quote a traced figure that is not true.
issues.fix: State 'use the GL detail for every account it covers; use the register or expense table only for accounts the GL does not cover'. Make trace_movement.py refuse duplicate refs across sources and any case where |traced| exceeds |change|.

issues.quote: Unmapped accounts are excluded from subtotals and listed; the net result
issues.problem: Only the net result is held back. The operating result is still printed, and its +109% headline, even though 1,040.20 of 'Uncategorised Expense' is left out of operating expenses. Owners will read an overstated operating result; only the chart title says unmapped items are excluded.
issues.fix: Label every subtotal an unmapped account could affect as 'before unmapped items (X)' in pl_table.md and the brief. Where the unmapped account is plainly an expense, hold back the operating result or its % change as well.

issues.quote: Plan comparison, only from a supplied plan, with its source.
issues.problem: Plan variance is actual minus plan with no favourable/unfavourable label and no %. A 900.00 cost overrun appears as '900.00', the same way as a revenue beat. A budget whose period labels do not match (monthly rows in a YTD run) gives an empty table without a warning.
issues.fix: Add F/U (with the cost sign inverted) and variance % columns. Have the script warn when no plan rows match the period, and give a step for summing monthly plan rows into YTD.

issues.quote: State entity, period, currency, accounting basis, source
issues.problem: Scoping never checks whether the month is closed. It does not read recs/<account>-<YYYY-MM>.json or close/<YYYY-MM>/status.csv, and does not confirm that recurring journals (payroll accrual, depreciation, prepaid amortisation) were posted. So a P&L on unreconciled books carries no 'books not closed' flag. The worked example only mentions the unreconciled Amex account in passing.
issues.fix: Add a pre-step that reads the reconciliation and close status for the period. Print 'books closed / not closed; unreconciled: …; journals not confirmed: …' in the header and Coverage.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: User upload (`templates/pl-export.csv` shape), or a read-only ledger report (step 2)
issues.problem: Real QBO or Xero P&L exports have section headings, Parent:Child nesting, Total rows, amounts in parentheses and MM/DD/YYYY dates. The skill gives no recipe for turning them into account,group,amount. trace_movement.py rejects amounts in parentheses (pl_variance.py accepts them) and US dates, and no conversion step is given.
issues.fix: Add a reference that maps QBO and Xero sections to groups, plus a small reshape helper. Make trace_movement.money() accept parentheses like pl_variance.py does. Ask for the date order once and convert.

issues.quote: Traps the script flags (sales tax in the P&L, 1099-K revenue, owner items,
issues.problem: The sales-tax/VAT pattern only fires on cost groups or unmapped rows. 'VAT collected' mapped to revenue was not flagged in testing, although pl-traps.md says tax collected is never revenue.
issues.fix: Add revenue and other_income to the scope of the sales-tax trap.

issues.quote: The kit invoice register has no account column, and its `line_key` is one
issues.problem: SKILL.md runs to 190 lines. It carries source-specific reshape detail inline: key stripping, invoice statuses, the --negate rule for expenses, and full command lines. It also asks for a same-month-last-year comparison without saying to use a separate --out, so that run would overwrite the pl_variance.json the trace step reads.
issues.fix: Move the three source recipes into references/trace-sources.md and keep one line per source in the body. Give the year-on-year run its own --out directory.

scenarios.prompt: Here are our Xero P&L exports for August and September, both accrual. How did we do last month, and why is profit down?
scenarios.why: The model follows these steps in order: pre-flight, fix the scope (step 1), map the Xero section headings to the five groups and the 'Total ...' rows into reported-totals.csv (step 3 and the inputs table), then run pl_variance.py. It gets script-verified changes, 'n/m' for tiny bases, and the net result held back unless everything ties. With no GL detail supplied, step 5 leaves drivers 'not traced' and the model asks for the transaction-detail export instead of inventing causes. The pl-brief.md template gives a reusable draft with a Coverage section and a list of decisions needed. The one weak point is that turning Xero's hierarchical export into the account,group,amount shape is left to the model's own judgement.

scenarios.prompt: Give me year-to-date profit against budget. I've uploaded the QuickBooks cash-basis P&L for Jan–Aug as one file, our budget is monthly and on accrual, and I've also dropped in the GL detail and the invoice register so you can explain what's driving it.
scenarios.why: Good: step 4 YTD asks for the fiscal-year start and never assumes January. The accrual plan against cash actuals raises NOT COMPARABLE, so no plan variance is made up. Gaps: (1) a monthly budget has no 'ytd-2026-08' rows, so the plan table comes out empty without a warning and no step says how to sum the plan. (2) Step 5 reshapes both the GL detail and the register, then passes '--sources /home/user/in/trace-*.csv'. That glob picks up the register's .skipped.csv and .unmapped.csv side files, and the trace fails ('needs date, account, amount'). If the files are listed explicitly instead, revenue is counted twice (traced 7,000 against a 3,500 change, untraced -3,500, exit 0). The skill does say the register is for accrual only, which a careful model would apply on a cash basis, but nothing warns about overlapping sources. (3) QuickBooks US dates (MM/DD/YYYY) and amounts in parentheses are refused by trace_movement.py, and no conversion step is given.

better: Main v1 is 53 lines of prose with no mechanism. The rebuild enforces basis comparability, detail-to-total tie-out and n/m percentages in a tested script, not just in instructions
Adds driver tracing that states traced and untraced amounts, where v1 only said 'explain the largest movements with linked source items'
Adds YTD and budget comparisons with refusal rules (no assumed January fiscal year, no invented plan figures, no estimate for a missing month)
Adds an explicit inputs table with fallbacks for each input, a missing-Python fallback, a missing-integration fallback and a read-only ledger rule
Adds a reusable brief template, a review checklist, a worked example with fixtures, and sourced references on traps and materiality
Review status is now logged against the brief's hash, and escalation goes to bookkeeping-exception-escalation
Expanded triggers ('how did we do last month', 'P&L vs budget', 'management accounts') and a clear 'not for' boundary
worse: SKILL.md grew from 53 to 190 lines, with dense inline command lines and source recipes that belong in references
The trace step as written fails (the glob picks up side files) or double-counts overlapping sources, which v1's plain instructions could not do
Tied to the Mina kit's state layout and invoice-register key conventions, so it is less portable to a user without the rest of the kit
The worked example still carries the 'original example (kept from version 1)' section as filler

press-release-draft.summary: A 38-line skill that collects facts, drafts a news-first release under 500 words, and returns it with a table showing whether each quote, figure and customer is approved, pending or missing.
strengths: The approval ledger (approved, pending, missing, plus an owner) is a reusable artefact that directly enforces Noor's 'never invent a quote' boundary.
Opens with the right boundary: use it once the angle and key messages are agreed, which keeps it distinct from news-angle-and-key-messages.
Sound practitioner rules: the headline states the news, not the mood; figures a reporter can check; quotes add a view rather than repeat facts; a banned-hype list.
Explicitly will not publish or send to a wire service or reporter.
Lean, with no filler.
missing: A release template with the embargo header, dateline, end mark and notes to editors
A definition of acceptable approval evidence and a persistent approval log
Escalation for public-company or regulated disclosure and legal review
Structure variants by release type (funding, product, partnership, customer win, hire)
A worked example of a good release
Reuse of stored boilerplate and media contact from communications-getting-started
Online newsroom, SEO and social short-form versions

issues.quote: Boilerplate and media contact.
issues.problem: There is no release template. The skill has no FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE or EMBARGOED UNTIL header, no dateline (CITY, date), no end mark (### or ENDS) and no notes to editors. It collects the embargo date and time but never says where it goes in the draft, so output format varies from run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/press-release.md with the header and embargo line, dateline, headline and subhead, body, quotes, availability, boilerplate, media contact, end mark and notes to editors, and route to it from this step.

issues.quote: approved on the user's say-so alone. Do not publish the release or send it to
issues.problem: The skill never defines what evidence of approval is acceptable. When the user is the approver, or pastes a Slack or email sign-off, the model either stalls or ignores the rule.
issues.fix: Define approval evidence: approver name, date, and channel or link. Accept the user as approver when they are the named owner from communications-getting-started. Record each approval with memory_store.

issues.problem: There is no escalation for material or regulated disclosures: public or listed companies (Reg FD, EU MAR), forward-looking statements, health or financial claims, or partner co-approval. A senior practitioner routes these to legal or IR before drafting the final version.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: if the company or its parent is listed, or the news covers results, M&A, funding terms or regulated claims, flag it for counsel or IR review, add a safe-harbour placeholder, and hand off to the relevant teammate.

issues.quote: Use this once the angle and key messages are agreed.
issues.problem: There is no fallback when the angle is not agreed or the news is thin, so the model will draft anyway and dress up weak news.
issues.fix: Add: if no agreed angle or key messages exist, run news-angle-and-key-messages first, and if the news is thin, say so before drafting.

issues.quote: Collect the headline fact, date, place, product or company names, figures with
issues.problem: The skill does not reuse the boilerplate, media contact or approved-facts map that communications-getting-started already set up, and it names no destination for the finished draft.
issues.fix: Check memory_search or the workspace for stored boilerplate and fact sources first. Write the draft and the ledger to a workspace file or a Google Doc via run_block.

issues.quote: "announcement", "news release", "media announcement"
issues.problem: The bare 'announcement' trigger overlaps with launch-communications-plan and with internal or customer announcements owned by other experts.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'press announcement' or 'announce to the press', and keep 'press release' and 'news release'.

issues.quote: Keep it under 500 words. Cut superlatives, "leading", "revolutionary", and
issues.problem: No variants are offered: the online-newsroom or SEO version, a short social version, and regional conventions (AP style for the US, notes to editors for the UK) are all missing, and there is no worked example of good versus bad.
issues.fix: Add an examples/ file with one annotated release and optional short-form variants.

scenarios.prompt: We launch our clinic scheduling feature on 14 May. 30 pilot clinics cut admin time from 40 to 6 minutes per patient (source: pilot report). The CEO quote below was approved by her yesterday. Write the release.
scenarios.why: 'Confirm the facts' names every input. 'Draft the release' gives the inverted-pyramid order, and 'Approval list' produces the ledger. A capable model returns a tight release under 500 words with the proof in paragraph two. One weakness: there is no header or dateline convention, so the format will vary between runs.

scenarios.prompt: Draft our $8M Series A release for Tuesday 6am ET under embargo. We can't name the lead investor until they confirm. The CEO quote is in this Slack thread I'm pasting. Call us 'the leading AI scheduling platform'. Our parent company is listed on the LSE.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly brackets the investor, cuts 'leading', and refuses to mark the pasted quote approved. It has no funding-release structure and never says where the embargo line goes, even though it collects the embargo. It also gives no escalation for a listed parent's disclosure duties (MAR, Reg FD) or for legal review. The 'say-so alone' rule does not say what evidence would count, so the Slack thread is left in limbo.

public-relations.job: plan earned media and pitch journalists
public-relations.summary: Corey Haines' upstream earned-media hub for software startups: the PR mix, a press-page checklist, a pitch quality bar and measurement, plus six references covering story angles, newsjacking, journalist pitching templates, inbound press-request platforms, outlet lists and podcast-guest prep.
strengths: Genuinely useful pitch craft: six angle-specific templates, a structure of under 150 words, subject-line rules, and a banned-vocabulary list.
Sound embargo, exclusive and follow-up etiquette: day 0, 3 and 7, and each follow-up must add new value.
The newsjacking rubric has weighted dimensions, a threshold and auto-disqualifiers (tragedy, empty take), plus decay windows by story type.
Good progressive disclosure: the hub SKILL.md routes each 'Common Workflows' request to one reference.
Podcast-guest prep has a clear research fallback order (RSS, site, Apple, web) and a structured brief.
Measurement rejects AVE and ties coverage to referral traffic, brand search and sales conversations.
missing: An explicit draft-then-approve gate before any pitch, press-request reply or social post
A rule never to invent data, quotes, customer names or reporter interest, with claims labelled by source and approval state
Platform-native tooling and fallbacks: web_search, browser_navigate, memory_store, and Google Sheets for the pitch tracker
A consistent journalist-fit scoring scale and tier thresholds
A current, dated inbound-request platform list
Press release guidance, or explicit routing to press-release-draft
Crisis and reputation handling (hand off to holding-statement-draft)
A measurement baseline and reporting cadence aligned with the Barcelona Principles
Non-US and regional media guidance

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups)
issues.problem: Claude-Code-only local state runs through the whole package: .agents and .claude context files, .agents/media-list.md and listening-sources.md, dev-browser, and 'brew install jq' and xmllint in the references. None of these exist in AutoGPT's sandbox or persist between sessions.
issues.fix: Use memory_search or read_workspace_file (or the product-marketing-context skill) for context. Replace dev-browser with web_search, web_fetch and browser_navigate. Keep the media list and pitch tracker in memory_store or a Google Sheet via run_block. Drop the brew instructions.

issues.quote: 'PR,' 'public relations,' 'press,' 'press release,' 'press coverage,'
issues.problem: The description claims 'press release', 'PR', 'media list', 'pitch a journalist' and 'podcast prep', so it hijacks Noor's press-release-draft, media-list-research, media-pitch-email and spokesperson-briefing. It contains no release-writing guidance at all.
issues.fix: Narrow the description to the earned-media strategy, newsjacking and inbound press-request workflows the originals lack. Route release writing to press-release-draft and interview or podcast prep to spokesperson-briefing.

issues.quote: Before sending any pitch, the answer to all of these should be yes:
issues.problem: It assumes the agent sends. No step drafts, then pauses for the user's approval before a pitch, a HARO response or a social post goes out. newsjacking.md step 6 says to publish to the blog, LinkedIn and X outright. This conflicts with Noor's boundary: 'never contact a reporter or publish a statement yourself'.
issues.fix: Add an explicit gate: draft every pitch, response and post, show it with its approval state, and send only through the platform approval flow once the named owner says yes.

issues.quote: Could this journalist write a complete story from this email alone? (Data, quotes, customer name, contact.)
issues.problem: It pushes for data, quotes and customer names without any rule that they must be real, sourced and approved. The reference examples ('Our analysis of 12,000 agent deployments shows 73%...') model invented stats.
issues.fix: Add a rule never to invent figures, quotes, customer names or reporter interest, and to mark each claim with its source and approval state. Label the example stats as illustrative.

issues.quote: use the discovery checklist + dev-browser to research recent articles, build a scored list.
issues.problem: journalist-pitching.md uses four 1-10 scores with weights 3x, 2x, 2x and 1x (8-80). Its profile template says 'X/40', its tiers use 8-10, 5-7 and below 5, and the media-list table shows '9/10'. There is no normalisation, so any 'scored list' is incoherent. It also suggests guessing emails and bounce-checking them.
issues.fix: Pick one scale, for example a weighted sum normalised to 0-10 with tier cut-offs. Update the profile and media-list templates to match. Replace email guessing with verified public contact routes, or ZeroBounce via run_block after approval.

issues.quote: For startup/SaaS/AI directory submissions, see directory-submissions. For product launches, see launch. For social-media engagement, see social.
issues.problem: directory-submissions, launch, social and (in the references) ai-seo do not exist in the catalog, so the routing points nowhere.
issues.fix: Point to real catalog skills (product-launch-marketing, launch-communications-plan, social-media-management) or to teammates via consult_teammate, and remove the dead names.

issues.quote: For inbound press-request platforms (HARO, Qwoted, etc.)
issues.problem: press-platforms.md lists 'Connectively (formerly HARO)', but Connectively shut down in December 2024 and HARO was relaunched under Featured. The outlet list also includes outlets that have since folded or merged. The skill presents both as current.
issues.fix: Refresh the platform table with dates. Tell the model to verify with web_search before recommending a platform or outlet, and to state the check date.

issues.quote: For where to pitch (media outlets, podcasts, newsletters)
issues.problem: media-outlets.md is a 9KB static, US-tech-centric list that the skill admits 'ages fast'. It costs context without producing a reporter-specific result.
issues.fix: Shrink it to outlet categories and search patterns, and let media-list-research do live discovery with dated sources.

scenarios.prompt: Find me 15 journalists who cover clinic and health-IT software and draft pitches about our pilot results.
scenarios.why: The discovery checklist and the pitch templates in journalist-pitching.md are good, and web_search can stand in for dev-browser. However, the scoring gives three incompatible scales: a weighted 8-80 sum, 'Score: [X/40]', and tiers of 8-10. So the scored list is incoherent. It tells the model to store the list in .agents/media-list.md, which the platform does not persist, and suggests guessing email addresses. Nothing says to stop for approval before pitches go out.

scenarios.prompt: There's breaking AI-regulation news from 3 hours ago. Newsjack it today and get me quoted. We don't have any proprietary data.
scenarios.why: The newsjacking rubric and its auto-disqualifiers (no backing, tragedy) would correctly steer toward an insider-explainer angle or a skip, and the speed windows are sound. But detection relies on curl plus 'brew install jq' and xmllint, with no web_search fallback. Loop step 6 says to publish on the blog, LinkedIn and X with no approval gate. The example angles ('12,000 agent deployments... 73%') invite invented stats when the user has none.

spokesperson-briefing.summary: A 37-line skill that assembles a one-page interview brief: outlet and reporter context, three sourced key messages, up to ten likely questions with approved answers, quotable and forbidden figures, a bridge line, and red-line topics with polite ways to decline them.
strengths: Hardest-first Q&A built only from approved facts, with a clear ban on inventing reporter questions, figures or approved answers.
A red-lines section with a plain decline line for each topic is practical and keeps to Noor's boundaries.
A split between figures the spokesperson may quote and those they must not.
Pairs each message with a proof point and source.
Clear ownership: Noor does not contact the reporter or confirm the interview.
Very lean.
missing: An input checklist: spokesperson, date, time and time zone, format, duration, reporter or programme, topic, and source of approved messages
Research tooling and a fallback when the reporter is unknown
A crisis or hostile-interview mode linked to holding-statement-draft and counsel review
Attribution ground-rule definitions, agreed in writing in advance
Format-specific coaching for live broadcast, recorded, print, podcast and panel
Soundbites for each message, an acknowledge-bridge-communicate bridge for each hard question, and a mock-interview rehearsal
A logistics block and post-interview follow-up (promised materials, corrections, coverage log)
A template split into a front sheet and a Q&A appendix

issues.quote: List topics to decline: unannounced plans, funding, legal matters, customers
issues.problem: There is no crisis or hostile-interview branch. When the interview touches an incident, the brief should carry the approved holding line from holding-statement-draft and a counsel or security review gate, not just a decline phrase.
issues.fix: Add a decision point: if the topic involves an incident, a legal matter or negative coverage, pull the approved holding statement, list what is confirmed and what is not, require the named approver or counsel to sign off, and add false-premise handling.

issues.quote: pieces on the subject, with links and dates, and the angle they are likely to
issues.problem: There are no named inputs and no research method. It never says to ask for spokesperson, date, time and time zone, format, duration, topic and the source of approved messages, nor to use web_search or web_fetch, nor what to do when the reporter or presenter is unknown.
issues.fix: Open with an input checklist (via ask_question) and a research step using web_search and web_fetch on the reporter, or on the programme and presenter as a fallback, citing links and dates. If there are no approved messages, run news-angle-and-key-messages first.

issues.quote: recorded, and whether it is on the record.
issues.problem: Attribution ground rules (on the record, on background, off the record, not for attribution, embargo) are neither defined nor required to be agreed in advance. Spokespeople often assume 'off the record' protects them when it does not.
issues.fix: Add definitions and a rule to confirm the ground rules in writing through the approver before the interview. Default to treating everything as on the record.

issues.quote: Use this before any interview, podcast, panel, or press call.
issues.problem: It is one-size-fits-all. There is no format-specific coaching: 10-20 second soundbites for live broadcast, long-form stories for podcasts, fact-check and follow-up norms for print, and the moderator's role on a panel.
issues.fix: Add a short table of format tips, or a references/formats.md, and pick the relevant row from the format the user named.

issues.quote: A bridge back to the messages if the talk drifts.
issues.problem: A single generic bridge is thin. Senior media training gives an acknowledge-bridge-communicate line for each hard question, plus one or two quotable soundbites for each message, and includes a mock-interview run-through.
issues.fix: Ask for a bridge line on each hard question and a soundbite for each message, and offer a mock Q&A rehearsal in which the model plays the reporter.

issues.quote: Keep it to one page the spokesperson can read in five minutes.
issues.problem: The one-page limit conflicts with outlet context, three messages with proof, ten Q&As and red lines, so the model will either break the limit or truncate the answers.
issues.fix: Specify a one-page front sheet (messages, top three hard questions, red lines) plus a Q&A appendix, and ship it as templates/spokesperson-brief.md.

issues.problem: There is no logistics block (time zone, dial-in or location, who attends as minder, whether the company records the interview) and no after-interview step (send promised data, handle fact-check requests, log what was said, watch for the story).
issues.fix: Add 'Logistics' and 'After the interview' sections, the latter creating a follow-up list and optionally a schedule_followup to check for coverage.

issues.quote: "interview prep"
issues.problem: In a multi-expert team, 'interview prep' collides with hiring skills such as candidate-interview-planning and interview-kit-design, and 'podcast' prep overlaps with public-relations' podcast-guest-prep.
issues.fix: Use 'media interview prep', 'press interview prep' and 'podcast guest prep', and make this skill the owner of podcast prep (fold in public-relations' podcast-guest-prep reference).

scenarios.prompt: Our CEO does a 20-minute recorded interview with Sam Lee at Healthcare IT News on Thursday about our clinic launch. Prep her. The key messages are the ones we agreed last week.
scenarios.why: With a named reporter and agreed messages, a capable model uses web_search for Sam's recent pieces and fills every section ('Outlet and reporter', 'Messages and questions', 'Red lines'), producing a usable one-pager with hardest-first Q&A built from approved facts. Weaknesses: there is no logistics block or rehearsal step, and ten Q&As strain the one-page limit.

scenarios.prompt: Our founder is live on BBC Radio 5 tomorrow at 7:40am. We had an outage last week and there's a Reddit thread claiming data loss. We don't know which presenter it is, and legal hasn't cleared anything about the outage.
scenarios.why: 'Red lines' covers declining legal matters, and the ban on inventing figures holds. But the skill assumes a named reporter, with no fallback to research the programme or presenter. It has no crisis mode linking to holding-statement-draft for the approved incident line, no counsel-review gate, and no live-broadcast coaching (soundbite length, no 'no comment', how to correct a false premise). So the brief will be generic exactly where the risk is highest.

16:job-description-drafting.job: draft inclusive job posting from role scorecard
16:job-description-drafting.summary: Turns an approved role scorecard into a public job posting (or rewrites an old one against it). It runs four stdlib scripts: a language/proxy lint, a word-for-word mirror check of must-haves and nice-to-haves against the scorecard, a before/after diff, and an HTML/TXT render that refuses to produce paste-ready copies while [OWNER TO CONFIRM] fields remain. It flags pay-transparency fields that may be legally required instead of advising on them.
strengths: The posting cannot set the bar. mirror_check.py compares must-haves by M-id and treats any nice-to-have not on the scorecard as ADDED, and 'Preferred/Bonus' headings are also caught. I verified this on an edge case: a scorecard with 'none agreed' plus a posting that adds a nice-to-have exits 1.

The scripts work as documented. On the adversarial posting the lint gives exactly 14 FLAG / 5 CHECK, the example gives 10 FLAG, the mirror check exits 0, and render refuses to write copies while 4 fields are unresolved unless --draft stamps them.
Legal hedging is disciplined: 'may be required' wording, dated sourced table, people-lead line, never supplies a figure, flag not advise.
Current-practice lines are built in: an accommodation route, an optional candidate AI-use line tied to the owner's policy, and an anti-scam line.
The worked example includes a realistic hard case: the owner wants pay left out, keeps 'open until filled', and adds Kubernetes, which the skill routes to a scorecard revision.

Platform usage checks out against the backend: ~/skills/<slug> materialisation, the durable ~/workspace volume, run_capability tool:browser_navigate as a fallback for JS job boards, web_fetch extract_text with the 100 KB cap, write_workspace_file source_path, and workspace:// links.
The output contract is explicit and ends with 'Not posted anywhere.'
missing: EU Pay Transparency Directive posting duties (in force from June 2026) and verified rows for the major US state pay-posting laws, with a rule that remote postings consider every place the work could be performed
A 'what happens next' section (stages and timeline) taken from the scorecard's hiring plan
A report format and save path for a bias-check-only request, including pedigree floors (years, degree, 'top university')
A gendered-wording balance score in place of per-word FLAGs, with a caveat on how current the evidence is
Title searchability and length guidance (market-standard title, word count, job-board field limits, Google for Jobs JobPosting structured data)
A work-authorisation / visa-sponsorship statement pattern
Lexicon coverage for common variants: 'cultural fit', 'employment gaps', 'native <any language>', 'between NN and NN', numeric ZIP/postcodes

issues.quote: every field it lists that the owner has not given (pay range, benefits,
issues.problem: Step 4 only marks fields the reference table lists. The EU/UK row and the 'other US states' row list no fields and are 'Not verified'. So a posting for Portugal or Spain, which are the worked example's own jurisdictions, gets no pay flag, even though the EU Pay Transparency Directive (2023/970, transposition deadline 7 June 2026) requires pay-range information to applicants and gender-neutral vacancy notices. A remote-US role never considers NY, WA, IL, MN, MA, NJ and similar laws that apply wherever the work could be done.
issues.fix: Add dated rows for EU Directive 2023/970 Art. 5 (pay info, no pay history, gender-neutral titles) and the main US state laws. State a rule that a remote posting looks up every place the work could be performed. Have 'Not verified' rows still mark pay as [OWNER TO CONFIRM — may be required for <place>].

issues.quote: Every `FLAG` gets a swap or a one-line owner defence; `CHECK` hits are read
issues.problem: lint-terms.csv gives about 30 masculine-coded stems FLAG severity. I ran neutral engineering copy and got 7 FLAGs: 'determine the root cause', 'test assertions', 'hierarchical data', 'intellectual property', 'opinionated framework', 'superior', 'ambitious'. Each one needs a defence before the self-check passes. This contradicts the skill's own reference, which says the Gaucher et al. finding is about overall balance. Recent field evidence finds little applicant effect from coded wording.
issues.fix: Downgrade masculine-coded to CHECK or info and report a masculine/feminine balance ratio. Keep FLAG for legal and proxy categories. Add benign uses (determine, assertion, hierarchical data, intellectual property) to the lexicon notes.

issues.quote: (step 5) and the posting-law lookup (step 4) on it as-is; report the lint
issues.problem: A bias-only review has no save location, because step 5 writes into a role folder that does not exist for an ad-hoc paste. It has no report format, because the output contract assumes a full posting with Mirror and rendered files. It never checks pedigree floors ('10+ years', degree), which the lint does not catch and which are the main disparate-impact risk in old ads.
issues.fix: Define a bias-report output: line, text, category, severity, swap, source, plus proxies and years/degree floors found by reading. Name a scratch or role-less save path for pasted postings.

issues.quote: How and by when to apply.
issues.problem: The posting tells candidates what to send and by when, but not what happens next: stages, rough timeline, who they meet. The approved scorecard already holds this in its hiring plan. Stating it is standard candidate-experience practice and reduces drop-off.
issues.fix: Add an optional 'What happens next' line drawn from the scorecard's hiring plan (stage names and lengths only, no interviewer names unless the owner approves).

issues.quote: The scorecard's must-haves, word for word as checkable outcomes; the
issues.problem: Requiring verbatim scorecard wording puts internal, evaluative phrasing into candidate-facing copy. mirror_check only tolerates a leading 'Has/You have', so a natural candidate-voice rewrite shows as CHANGED and must go back through a scorecard revision.
issues.fix: Allow a candidate-voice rewording tagged with its M-id, and have mirror_check accept an owner-approved paraphrase map (M-id to posting text) instead of exact text only.

issues.quote: agreed there, every posting nice-to-have is `ADDED`; "Bonus points", "Preferred qualifications" and "Even better if" headings count
issues.problem: Script internals (which headings the regex treats as nice-to-have) leak into SKILL.md. The draft-pending-calibration fallback and the nice-to-have rule are each restated across step 1, step 3, step 6, Decisions, the self-check and the checklist, so 196 lines carry about 40 lines of repetition.
issues.fix: State each rule once in Decisions. Leave heading-detection details in the script docstring or a reference. Point the self-check at the checklist instead of duplicating it.

issues.quote: confirm with the owner it is the right posting. Save it as
issues.problem: The imported old posting goes to a fixed scratch path, /home/user/old-posting.md. That path is not on the durable volume and collides across roles, so the step-8 diff after a later edit round, or on another role, can compare against the wrong or missing file.
issues.fix: Save it as ~/workspace/hiring/roles/<role-slug>/old-posting.md.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: Ask once; else leave the AI-use line out
issues.problem: There is no memory_search fallback for hiring preferences, although sibling interview-kit-design uses one. The owner may be asked again for jurisdictions and policy they already gave.
issues.fix: Read preferences.md, else memory_search('hiring preferences'), else one ask_question. Then store the answer.

scenarios.prompt: Lena approved the Senior Backend Engineer, Billing scorecard. Write the posting: remote within the EU, pay EUR 85-100k, apply by 31 October, accommodation requests to people@northwind.example.
scenarios.why: Step 1 finds status approved. Step 3 fills templates/posting.md in a fixed order with must-haves copied verbatim. Step 4 finds the EU row, which lists no fields, and pay is given anyway. Step 5 lint gives 0 FLAG plus 1 CHECK ('lead' in 'lead the on-call rotation'), which the model reads in context. Step 6 mirror_check exits 0. Step 9 render writes clean HTML/TXT because nothing is unresolved, and delivers them via write_workspace_file with 'Not posted anywhere.' I ran the scripts on the example files and they behave as the example shows. A recruiter would accept the result. The posting never tells candidates the interview stages or timeline, even though the scorecard's hiring plan has them.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our old Customer Success Manager ad (pasted). No scorecard yet, we hire remote anywhere in the US, we don't publish pay. Just check it for bias and tidy it up fast. It says '10+ years', 'strong cultural fit', 'no employment gaps', and 'determine root causes of churn'.
scenarios.why: The Decisions section routes a no-scorecard bias check to lint plus posting-law lookup as-is, but three things go wrong. (1) The lint misses 'cultural fit' and 'no employment gaps' (the lexicon only has 'culture fit', 'no gaps' and 'gaps in employment'). It also misses the '10+ years' pedigree floor, which is not in the lexicon, and the bias-only path adds no pedigree check. All three depend on the model reading the text itself. (2) It raises a FLAG on 'determine' as masculine-coded, which forces a pointless owner defence. (3) The posting-law table verifies only CA and CO, and nothing says a remote-US role can fall under every state pay law (NY, WA, IL, MN, MA, NJ...), so the pay flag may name too few places. There is also no save path for an ad-hoc paste outside a role folder, and no report format for this path. A careful model fills most of these gaps, but the skill does not make it.

better: Main is a 64-line list of principles. PR16 adds an ordered 9-step procedure with an inputs table (where each input comes from, what to do if it is missing) and explicit decision branches.

Adds working stdlib scripts: jd_lint (about 130-term sourced lexicon), mirror_check against the approved scorecard, diff_postings for before/after, and render_posting, which blocks paste-ready output while fields are unresolved. All ran correctly on the examples.
Adds a dated, sourced posting-law reference and a protected-traits/proxy rewrite table. Main only said 'no gendered superlatives, no rockstar'.
Adds accommodation, candidate AI-use and anti-scam lines, and a template with a fixed section order.
Nice-to-haves and years/degree floors are now tied to the scorecard ('HM defended'), so the posting cannot quietly raise or lower the bar.
Adds a worked example with a hard case, a pre-publish checklist and an explicit output contract.
worse: Much longer (12 KB vs 2.5 KB), with rules restated across steps, decisions, self-check and checklist.
Stricter gate: a plain 'write a JD for X' is routed to role-intake-and-scorecard unless the owner insists. Main drafted straight away from the title plus four questions.
Masculine-coded FLAG severity adds false-positive noise on ordinary job content that main's lighter screen avoided.
Verbatim must-have wording limits candidate-facing tone compared with main's freer 'checkable outcomes' guidance.

paid-performance-report.job: report paid ads performance for a period
paid-performance-report.summary: A 39-line placeholder telling the model to report a period's paid spend and results. Each figure carries its source, platform numbers sit apart from CRM or analytics numbers, large changes are explained with evidence, and the report ends with owned next actions and open questions.
strengths: Every figure must carry its period, currency, attribution setting and source.
Keeps platform-reported results apart from analytics or CRM results and reports the gap, which is the core honesty rule for paid reporting.
Says outright to call a cause 'unknown' and to flag broken or partial tracking days.
Next actions carry owners, a read date for each running test, and a list of data the next report needs.
Clear boundaries: no invented benchmarks, no estimates filling tracking gaps, no return promises, no campaign edits.
missing: An inputs and fallback step: which exports and columns, and what to do when an ad platform has no connector.
Conversion-lag handling and a comparability check across attribution-window or definition changes.
Splitting each change into CPC, CTR, CVR and AOV drivers, plus a materiality threshold.
A report template with KPI, drivers and actions tables, and different depth for weekly, monthly and quarterly.
Brand versus non-brand split and blended MER or CAC across channels.
Lead-quality or pipeline tie-back from the CRM, not only as an open question.
A memory and schedule_routine hook for recurring reports.
Draft-then-approve rules for sending to stakeholders.

issues.quote: State the period, accounts, currency, attribution setting, and the source of
issues.problem: There is no inputs or intake step. The skill never says which exports or columns to get, or what to do when an account or the CRM data is missing. Google Ads, Meta and LinkedIn have no AutoGPT block, so the model has no route to the data and no instruction to do the arithmetic in the sandbox.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs step. Ask via ask_question for a per-account CSV export (date, campaign, spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, conversion value), the analytics or CRM export for the same dates, and the targets. Pull Sheets through run_block where available. Compute in bash_exec. Mark any source that is not supplied as 'not available' rather than skipping it.

issues.quote: For each large change, show the campaigns, terms, or audiences behind it.
issues.problem: 'Large' is not defined, and changes are only broken down by segment. A senior analyst splits each movement into its drivers (impressions × CTR × CVR, CPC, AOV) so the report says why CPA moved, not just where.
issues.fix: Define materiality: a threshold agreed in paid-ads-getting-started, or a default such as ±15% and a minimum currency amount. For each material change, show the driver split (volume versus CPC versus CVR versus AOV) before listing segments and causes.

issues.quote: return where tracked, against the prior period and the target. Keep
issues.problem: The comparison with the prior period is taken as valid without checks. Nothing covers conversion lag (the most recent days are not yet complete), attribution-window or model changes between periods, different day counts or weekday mix, or year-on-year for seasonal businesses.
issues.fix: Add a comparability check. Align the windows, compare year-on-year where the business is seasonal, and flag any attribution or conversion-definition change between the periods. Mark the last N days inside the conversion window as immature and do not read trends from them.

issues.quote: Use this for a weekly, monthly, or quarterly look at paid results.
issues.problem: There is no reusable deliverable. The sections are described in prose, but there is no KPI table, no executive summary shape, and no difference in depth between weekly, monthly and quarterly reports.
issues.fix: Ship templates/paid-report.md. Include a three-line summary; a KPI table with columns metric, this period, prior, target, source and note; a table of changes and drivers; and an actions table with owner and date. Add a note on the extra depth a quarterly report needs.

issues.quote: tracking breaks, seasonality, competitor activity, or page changes. Say
issues.problem: Causes are listed without saying where the evidence for each comes from. A 'competitor activity' claim needs auction insights or impression-share loss, and budget or ad changes need the change history.
issues.fix: Pair each cause with its evidence source: change history for budgets, bids and ads; auction insights and impression share lost to budget or rank for competitors; tag or GA4 checks for tracking; the site release log for page changes.

issues.quote: Give spend, conversions, cost per conversion, and revenue or
issues.problem: The metric set is last-click and per platform only. There is no brand versus non-brand split (wasted-spend-audit flags this) and no blended view such as MER or blended CAC across channels. Mid-funnel rates are not requested.
issues.fix: Split brand and non-brand, add a blended cross-channel line where revenue is known, and include CTR, CPC and CVR (plus frequency for social) so the model has what it needs to diagnose changes.

issues.quote: Do not share the report outside the team or change campaigns yourself. Never
issues.problem: There is no draft-and-approve route. Users will often ask for the report to be emailed to leadership or posted to Slack, and 'outside the team' is not defined.
issues.fix: Have the skill draft the report and name the recipients, then send or post only after approval through the platform's approval flow. Log who approved it.

issues.quote: data the next report needs.
issues.problem: The report is meant to recur, but nothing is kept between runs: no memory of targets, baselines or definitions, and no offer to schedule it.
issues.fix: Save targets, conversion definitions and this period's headline figures with memory_store. Offer schedule_routine for a weekly or monthly run that uses the same template.

scenarios.prompt: Here are our Google Ads and Meta exports for September and August. Target CPA is £45. Write the monthly paid report for the leadership team.
scenarios.why: Headline numbers force the period, currency, attribution setting and a source for each figure, compared with the prior period and the target. 'What changed and why' ties changes to campaigns and says when a cause is unknown. Next actions carry owners. A capable model gets a sourced, honest report. Layout will vary between runs because there is no template, and the CRM gap is only noted, not requested.

scenarios.prompt: ROAS fell from 4.1 to 2.3 this week. Meta shows 180 purchases, Shopify shows 95. We switched Meta to 7-day click only mid-month and the last three days look terrible. I need the weekly report for the CEO today.
scenarios.why: The skill keeps platform and store numbers apart and flags broken-tracking days, which is the right instinct. It says nothing about an attribution-window change mid-period making the periods non-comparable, or about conversion lag under-reporting the last few days. It gives no way to split the ROAS drop into CPC, CVR and AOV. The model may present lag and a settings change as a real performance collapse.

wasted-spend-audit.job: find and cut wasted ad spend
wasted-spend-audit.summary: A 39-line placeholder for auditing one ad account over at least 30 days. It confirms tracking and exports, finds spend with no or poor return by search term, placement, audience, location, device and time of day, and lists cuts ranked by risk with the spend at stake and a two-week check, all recommended rather than applied.
strengths: Checks the data before judging: tracking gaps and truncated exports are called out first.
Covers the right leak dimensions: terms and match types, placements and apps, audiences and locations, devices and time of day.
Flags brand-campaign efficiency as mostly non-incremental, which is a genuinely senior caveat.
Each cut carries spend at stake, possible loss, a two-week check and a small-sample flag, ranked from lowest to highest risk.
Recommend-only, with no negatives, exclusions or bid changes made by the agent.
missing: A numeric waste threshold tied to target CPA and expected conversions.
N-gram rollup of search terms, plus a check that negatives do not block converting terms.
A per-platform structural checklist: location settings, Search Partners, Display expansion, PMax and Advantage+ visibility, Audience Network, keyword overlap.
Checks for conversion lag, assisted or view-through conversions, and value before calling spend wasted.
CRM lead-quality check for lead-gen accounts.
Named export list, CSV intake and sandbox computation.
A cuts table template with a total estimate and the realistic caveat that spend is redirected rather than saved.
A fallback for under 30 days or low volume, and handoffs to message-match and pacing skills.

issues.quote: Look at spend with no conversions, or cost far above target, by:
issues.problem: There is no evidence threshold. 'No conversions' and 'far above target' are left to judgement, so trivial spend gets called waste and real waste in mid-volume segments goes unranked.
issues.fix: Flag zero-conversion segments only when spend is at least about 2× target CPA (or expected conversions at the account CVR are at least 2–3). Flag high-CPA segments only above about 1.5× target with enough conversions. Show expected versus observed for each, and label everything else 'watch list, too small to call'.

issues.quote: search terms and match types;
issues.problem: Search terms are treated row by row. The main senior technique, grouping terms into n-grams (words like 'free', 'jobs' or 'login'), is missing. So is checking proposed negatives against terms that do convert.
issues.fix: Run a 1-, 2- and 3-word n-gram rollup of spend, clicks and conversions in bash_exec. For each proposed negative, check it would not block converting queries. Recommend the negative's match type and level (shared list, campaign, or account-level).

issues.quote: audiences and locations;
issues.problem: Structural and platform-specific leaks are missing. On Google: location 'presence or interest' settings, Search Partners, Display expansion on Search campaigns, broad match without smart bidding, overlapping or cannibalising keywords, auto-applied recommendations. On Meta: Audience Network placements, audience overlap, frequency. PMax and Advantage+ reporting limits are not covered either.
issues.fix: Add references/leak-checklist.md with a per-platform checklist of settings and structure checks, including how to get PMax search-term insights and placement data. Point to it from this step.

issues.quote: Check that tracking worked across the whole period and
issues.problem: Nothing covers conversion lag, assisted or view-through conversions, or conversion value. Spend with no last-click conversions in the last days of the window, or in upper-funnel terms that assist, gets labelled waste. The reverse leak is also missed: lead-gen spend that 'converts' on junk leads.
issues.fix: Leave the last conversion-window days out of zero-conversion judgements. Check assisted and value metrics before calling a cut. Where a CRM export exists, check lead quality per segment, so spend with platform conversions but no qualified pipeline also counts as a leak.

issues.quote: State the account, date range, currency, attribution setting, and the
issues.problem: The skill does not name the exports the audit needs. Google Ads and Meta have no AutoGPT block, and there is no fallback or intake step.
issues.fix: List the required exports: search terms, where ads showed or placements, audience, geography, device, hour of day, change history and existing negatives. Ask for them as CSV via ask_question and process them in bash_exec. Say which leak checks cannot run when an export is missing.

issues.quote: List suggested cuts from lowest to highest risk. For each give the spend
issues.problem: 'Spend saved' overstates the effect. On budget-capped or smart-bidding campaigns, excluded spend moves elsewhere rather than being saved, and exclusions can reset learning.
issues.fix: Report 'spend redirected (upper bound)' and say where it is likely to go. Flag cuts that touch a smart-bidding campaign in learning. Give a total, labelled as an estimate.

issues.quote: Use this for one ad account over a period of at least 30 days.
issues.problem: The skill sets a 30-day minimum but gives no path when the user has less data or low volume, which is common for small teams.
issues.fix: If under 30 days or under about 30 conversions, widen the window if an export allows it. Otherwise deliver a watch list with the date by which each segment can be called, and schedule_followup for that date.

issues.quote: For each leak give the spend, clicks, conversions, and the rows behind it.
issues.problem: There is no handoff when the leak is after the click: segments with healthy CTR but no conversions often point to a landing-page or tracking problem, not the targeting.
issues.fix: Route segments with good CTR but zero conversions to landing-page-message-match, and pacing-driven overspend to budget-pacing-review. Say so in the output.

scenarios.prompt: Attached are our Google Ads search terms and placement reports for the last 60 days. Target CPA is $80. Where are we wasting money and what should we cut?
scenarios.why: 'Confirm the data' and 'Cuts ranked by risk' give a safe, well-shaped answer. 'Find the leaks' sets no threshold, though. A $14 term with zero conversions against an $80 target is not evidence, yet nothing stops the model listing it. The skill also never says to group terms by n-gram, which is where most search-term waste sits (the persona's own 'free'/'jobs' example needs it). The result is a noisy list of individual rows rather than a few large, defensible cuts.

scenarios.prompt: Performance Max takes 60% of our budget. I only have the campaign-level export and a screenshot from Meta Ads Manager, there are 3 weeks of data, and conversion tracking moved to a GA4 import 10 days ago. Tell me what to cut.
scenarios.why: The guardrails work: 'say so before judging anything' makes the model flag the tracking switch and thin data. But the skill covers only accounts with 30+ days and gives no fallback for shorter windows. It says nothing about PMax's limited visibility (search-term insights, placement report, brand exclusions, account-level negatives) and does not tell the model which reports to request. The user gets caveats but no senior-level next step or watch list.

conversion-rate-optimization.job: audit page or form to lift conversions
conversion-rate-optimization.summary: Corey Haines' upstream 'cro' skill. It audits a marketing page across seven heuristic dimensions ordered by impact (value proposition, headline, CTA, hierarchy, proof, objections, friction) and returns quick wins, high-impact changes, test ideas and copy alternatives. Two long references cover A/B-test ideas by page type and a full form-CRO playbook.
strengths: The analysis order runs by impact, from value proposition down to friction, which gives the model a sensible priority.
Page-type frameworks (homepage, landing, pricing, feature, blog) with a message-match check for traffic sources.
The output separates direct fixes from test ideas and asks for 2-3 copy alternatives with rationale.
Progressive disclosure: the long experiment catalogue and form playbook live in references/ and resolve by relative path.
Rich trigger phrasing that catches casual requests ('my landing page sucks', 'just shares a URL').
Clean attribution and MIT licence retained.
missing: A guardrail against invented social proof, testimonials, counts and lift percentages, and against dark patterns.
A traffic and sample-size feasibility check before proposing A/B tests.
An evidence-first step: funnel and segment analysis by device and source, and use of recordings or surveys.
Instructions to view the page with web_fetch and browser_screenshot at mobile and desktop widths.
A prioritisation method (ICE or PIE) and per-recommendation evidence, effort and owner fields.
Trade-off analysis of lead quality against volume (cost per qualified lead, pipeline per visitor) for form changes.
Privacy and consent guidance for forms (GDPR lawful basis, consent wording).
A source for, or removal of, form.md's field-count drop percentages, and an update to the stale vendor example (Clearbit).

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups)
issues.problem: This relies on Claude Code project-state paths that do not exist in AutoGPT's workspace. The model will look for them, find nothing, and never draw on Marco's own setup brief or memory. The same path is repeated in references/form.md.
issues.fix: Replace with: run memory_search for product, audience and offer context and for the paid-ads-getting-started brief, then ask only for what is missing. Drop the .agents and .claude paths in both files.

issues.quote: For signup/registration flows, see signup. For post-signup activation, see onboarding. For popups/modals, see popups.
issues.problem: The description and the Related Skills section route to skills that are not in the catalog: signup, popups and ab-testing (and 'cro' in form.md). 'onboarding' exists but is not assigned to Marco. PR #13 relabels these as 'not installed' and maps ab-testing to product-experiment-design, which is Alex's skill, not Marco's.
issues.fix: Route to skills Marco actually has: creative-test-readout for reading tests, landing-page-message-match for pairing ads with pages. Use consult_teammate for Alex (product-experiment-design) and Maria or Maya (marketing-copywriting). Remove signup and popups from the description.

issues.quote: Social proof: "Join 10,000+ teams who..."
issues.problem: There is no guardrail against invented proof. The skill models headline patterns with specific customer counts and suggests testimonials, logos and review scores, but never says they must be real and approved. Marco's boundary forbids inventing testimonials or claims. Dark patterns (fake urgency, confirmshaming) are also not ruled out.
issues.fix: Add a Guardrails section. Use only counts, logos, quotes and ratings the user confirms and has permission to use; mark proposed ones [VERIFY]. No fake scarcity or urgency and no dark patterns. Never state a percentage lift for a change.

issues.quote: Hypotheses worth A/B testing rather than assuming.
issues.problem: It proposes A/B tests with no check that the page has the traffic. For the small teams Marco serves, most landing pages cannot power a test, so the advice cannot be carried out and invites winners called too early.
issues.fix: Before listing tests, compute the required sample from baseline CVR and minimum detectable effect in bash_exec, and give the number of days at current traffic. If that is not feasible, recommend implementing and monitoring against a pre-change baseline, or testing a higher-traffic step. Send the readout to creative-test-readout.

issues.quote: What's your current conversion rate and goal?
issues.problem: The key inputs come at the bottom, after the framework and output format. The procedure also never says how to see the page: fetch the copy, and take mobile and desktop screenshots to judge above-the-fold content and hierarchy.
issues.fix: Move these questions into Initial Assessment as a short ask_question. Add a step: web_fetch the page copy, then browser_screenshot at mobile and desktop widths. If there is no URL, accept a screenshot or paste and note what cannot be judged, such as load time.

issues.quote: Easy changes with likely immediate impact.
issues.problem: Recommendations have no evidence or priority fields. The skill never separates what was observed from what is guessed, and uses no prioritisation method, so the output is a list of opinions. form.md's 'Impact: Estimated effect on conversions' invites invented numbers.
issues.fix: For each item record: the element (quote or screenshot), evidence type (observed, analytics or heuristic), expected direction rather than a % lift, effort, owner and how it will be measured. Rank with ICE or PIE and show the scores.

issues.quote: Do you have user research, heatmaps, or session recordings?
issues.problem: Research data is asked for but never used. There is no step to read the funnel by device and source, or to weigh recordings, surveys or on-site polls before the heuristic pass. Senior CRO work is led by research, not only by a checklist.
issues.fix: Add an 'Evidence first' step. Before the heuristic pass, pull the funnel and drop-off by device and source, plus any recordings or survey quotes. Tie each finding to a data point or label it as a heuristic.

issues.quote: Message match with traffic source
issues.problem: This overlaps Marco's landing-page-message-match, which already pairs each ad with its page by spend. Both will trigger on 'landing page isn't converting', with different outputs.
issues.fix: Merge. Keep CRO as the page-audit engine and make landing-page-message-match its paid-traffic mode: per-ad pairing, ranked by spend at stake. Alternatively, make CRO defer ad-to-page pairing to it explicitly.

scenarios.prompt: Here's the landing page for our Google Ads 'free trial – project management' campaign: https://example.com/trial. It got 2,400 clicks last month and converts at 1.1%. Why isn't it converting?
scenarios.why: Initial Assessment identifies page type, goal and paid traffic. The seven-dimension framework and the 'Landing Page CRO' message-match check produce a credible heuristic audit in the defined four-part output. But 'Test Ideas' says to A/B test with no traffic check, and at about 26 conversions a month most tests cannot reach significance. The skill never says to look at the page on mobile (browser_screenshot) or to label guesses apart from observations. The key questions ('What's your current conversion rate...') come at the end rather than up front.

scenarios.prompt: Demo-request conversion fell from 6% to 3.5% after sales made us add 4 qualification fields. Sales says lead quality is better. The page is behind a preview login, so I can only paste a screenshot. We sell in the EU.
scenarios.why: references/form.md covers field cost, multi-step forms, progressive profiling and a compliance question, so the model gets useful form mechanics. But neither file frames the real decision: cost per qualified lead, or pipeline per visitor, before and after. form.md's 'Every Field Has a Cost' cites unsourced drop percentages (4-6 fields: 10-25%) that the model may repeat as fact, against Marco's no-invented-benchmarks boundary. GDPR consent and lawful basis for the new fields get no specific guidance.

onboarding.job: optimize product onboarding and user activation
onboarding.summary: This is the vendored Corey Haines onboarding CRO skill. It asks three context questions, then lays out principles, onboarding psychology, checklist, empty-state and tour patterns, activation models, metrics and experiment ideas for improving self-serve product activation, and it ends in either an audit table or a flow-design outline.
strengths: The description is rich in phrases real users type ('users sign up but don't use the product', 'nobody completes setup') and separates onboarding from signup and email.

Its frameworks are correct and practical: the aha moment, the Minimum Path to Value with an inventory → remove → reconstruct process, the Fogg behaviour model, and best practice for checklists, empty states and tours.
references/activation-models.md ties onboarding design to the business model (freemium, trial, paid trial, consultation, card vs no card, Model-Market Fit).
Progressive disclosure works: three references are linked by relative path and ship in the package.
It defines two output shapes, an audit table and a flow-design outline covering activation goal, steps, checklist, empty-state copy, email triggers and a metrics plan.
missing: A numbered workflow with an audit-vs-design branch and a fallback when no analytics are connected
A method for finding the aha moment from exported event data (retention correlation by cohort in bash_exec, with caveats about confounders)
Account-level (B2B team) activation and the setup → aha → habit milestone ladder
Qualitative diagnostics: session recordings, user interviews and 'what's stopping you' surveys
A prioritisation score (ICE/RICE) for audit findings, with an evidence source per finding
Experiment rigor: hypothesis, guardrail metrics, sample size/MDE, and a plan for low traffic
Labelling of external benchmarks, kept separate from the user's numbers
Handoffs: lifecycle emails to Remy or Maya, sales-assisted activation to Max, implementation onboarding to Riley or Robin
A reusable deliverable template (audit table, flow spec, checklist and empty-state copy, email trigger map)
A dark-pattern and consent check

issues.quote: "empty states," "onboarding checklist," "aha moment,"
issues.problem: The description never says 'self-serve product / in-app'. 'Onboarding' and 'onboarding checklist' also match new-hire onboarding (new-hire-onboarding-plan, employee-onboarding-planning), customer-success onboarding (customer-onboarding-plan, onboarding-and-adoption) and partner onboarding in the same catalog, so the wrong skill will load on shared teams.
issues.fix: Lead the description with 'self-serve product (PLG) in-app onboarding and user activation', state 'not employee, partner or customer-success implementation onboarding', and drop the bare 'onboarding checklist' trigger.

issues.quote: drives roughly **+40% completion** vs. starting at 0%
issues.problem: The number is unsourced and does not match the underlying study (Nunes & Drèze car-wash cards: 19% vs 34% completion). The references present more unsourced numbers as fact: 40–60% abandonment after one session, a 50–70% card-required signup drop, and Stripe '~60% activation'. The model will pass these to users as benchmarks, which breaks the no-invented-numbers rule.
issues.fix: Cite a source for each benchmark or reword it as directional. Tell the model to label external benchmarks as unverified and never mix them with the user's own metrics.

issues.quote: Before providing recommendations, understand:
issues.problem: After three context questions the skill becomes a catalogue of principles. There is no ordered workflow (get the funnel data → validate the activation event → inventory the steps → locate the biggest drop → form hypotheses → prioritise experiments), no decision point between Audit and Flow Design, and no path when the user has no data. 'Task-Specific Questions' at the end repeats the assessment.
issues.fix: Replace it with a numbered procedure that has an audit/design branch, a no-analytics fallback (ask for a CSV export and analyse it in bash_exec), and the merged question list at step 1.

issues.quote: Judge activation by lead→customer conversion + 90-day retention, not lead volume.
issues.problem: This conflates activation with monetisation and retention outcomes. Activation should be the earliest in-product behaviour that predicts retention, validated against retention. Measuring it by 90-day retention makes weekly iteration impossible and contradicts the skill's own 'Activation Metrics' list.
issues.fix: Define activation as a leading behavioural event (setup → aha → habit) and say to validate it by comparing retention or conversion between users who hit it and users who do not.

issues.quote: If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`
issues.problem: The first instruction points at local paths from Claude Code. In AutoGPT, product context lives in memory or the workspace and is read with memory_search or read_workspace_file, and there is no fallback when the file is absent.
issues.fix: Tell the model to check memory_search for product context, then read the product-marketing workspace file if one exists, and otherwise ask the three assessment questions.

issues.quote: **signup**: For optimizing the signup before onboarding
issues.problem: The skill points to skills that do not exist in the catalog: signup, paywalls and ab-testing here, and 'signup' and 'emails' in the description. The model will try to route to them or read them.
issues.fix: Point to real catalog skills (lifecycle-email-marketing, pricing-and-packaging-strategy, the product experiment skill) or delete the routes. For handoffs, name teammates (Remy or Maya for emails).

issues.quote: When recommending experiments, consider tests for:
issues.problem: There is no experiment design: no hypothesis format, no primary or guardrail metric, no MDE or sample size, and no alternative for low-traffic products. In references/experiments.md the 'Hypothesis' column holds test names such as 'Tools like Navattic, Storylane', not hypotheses.
issues.fix: Add a short experiment spec (hypothesis, primary metric, guardrail metric, minimum sample or run length, and a low-traffic alternative such as sequential rollout or qualitative tests), and rewrite the reference column as real hypotheses.

issues.problem: The skill has no guardrails. Trigger emails and re-engagement sequences are recommended with no draft-and-approve step, no check on marketing consent or unsubscribe, and no warning against dark patterns (untrappable tours, pre-checked consent, notification permission ambushes).
issues.fix: Add a short guardrail block: proposals and copy are drafts for approval, emails respect consent and opt-out, and a dark-pattern checklist applies before any recommendation.

scenarios.prompt: Our self-serve analytics tool gets about 1,200 signups a month, but only 18% install the tracking snippet in week one. Here's our Mixpanel funnel export. Audit our onboarding and tell me what to fix first.
scenarios.why: The Initial Assessment questions, the Funnel Analysis rule ('Identify biggest drops and focus there'), the analytics aha example ('Install tracking + see first report') and the audit format (Finding → Impact → Recommendation → Priority) together give a usable shape. Three gaps keep it below senior quality. The skill never says to compute the funnel in the sandbox, segment by source or role, or size impact. It has no prioritisation method. It does not cover the B2B developer-handoff pattern (invite the engineer who installs the snippet). The unsourced benchmarks (+40% completion, 40–60% abandonment) are likely to be quoted to the user as fact.

scenarios.prompt: We don't know our aha moment and have no analytics connected, just a CSV of 3,000 users with signup date, a few event counts and whether they paid. Sales wants a mandatory demo before access, and product wants a self-serve free trial. Design our onboarding.
scenarios.why: 'Find Your Aha Moment' gives only two questions ('What do retained users do that churned users don't?'), with no method for correlating events with retention or payment in the CSV and no caution about confounders or small samples. Task-Specific Q5 just asks whether a cohort analysis exists, which the user has already answered. The model would probably take the aha moment from the generic 'Examples by product type'. The sales-versus-self-serve conflict gets only the Model-Market Fit maxim in references/activation-models.md, with no decision criteria such as ACV, setup complexity or buyer.

outreach-playbook.job: write cold outreach email and follow-up sequence
outreach-playbook.summary: A platform-written, roughly 50-line seed playbook. It tells the model to find a recent account trigger (or decline the touch), write a four-sentence first email ending in a question the prospect can answer in one line, follow up on days 3, 8 and 17, stop, and record any 'not now' reason.
strengths: Trigger-first discipline, including the rule that no trigger means the account is not worth a first touch yet
A tight four-sentence structure: trigger stated as a fact, problem in their words, a comparable proof, and a question answerable in one line
Concrete craft rules: no 30-minute call ask, at most one link, lowercase trigger subject, no 'just bumping'
Every follow-up must add something new, with a clean stop and an easy out
Treats the 'not now' reason and date as the most valuable output of outreach
Honest-claims rules: no fake mutual connections, no invented prior conversations, no unnamed results, no personal addresses
Very concise, with no filler
missing: Named inputs: offer, ICP, voice sample, allowed proof points, channel
A research method with tools, and a cited, dated trigger
A drafts-only approval gate before any send, plus send confirmation before logging
Compliance: opt-out line, CAN-SPAM/GDPR/PECR/UWG/CASL consent limits, suppression lists
Deliverability: address verification, volume caps, sending-domain health
State: logging touches and dormancy to the CRM or memory, and schedule_followup for each follow-up day
An output template: a sequence table with send dates and source links, plus a batch mode for lists
A reply-handling taxonomy (positive, referral, objection, unsubscribe, OOO, bounce)
Multichannel touches and multi-threading across personas

issues.quote: Use this for any first contact with someone who did not ask to hear from us.
