issues.problem: The skill describes 'running' outreach (and catalog.yml lists a google provider) but never says the output is a draft or that sending needs the user's explicit yes. It also never says a follow-up is only drafted once the user confirms the opener was sent.
issues.fix: Add a drafts-only approval gate: show the drafts, create Gmail drafts only through run_block on request, send nothing without explicit approval, and log a touch only after the user confirms the send.

issues.quote: Three follow-ups, then stop and mark the account dormant for a quarter.
issues.problem: This contradicts Max's draft-a-follow-up (eight multichannel touches, never stop before five, recycle after 60–90 days) and cold-email's sequence guidance, so two loaded skills give opposite cadences. 'Mark the account dormant' also has nowhere to be stored and no reminder.
issues.fix: Settle one cadence in the merge. Record dormancy and the 'not now' date in the CRM or memory_store, and use schedule_followup for the revisit and each follow-up date.

issues.quote: One sentence on what we did about it for someone comparably sized.
issues.problem: Proof has no source. With no case study supplied, the model will invent a 'comparably sized' result. The 'What not to do' rule forbids unnamed results but does not require proof to come from the user or be cleared for external use.
issues.fix: Use only proof points the user supplied and approved for external use. If there are none, drop sentence 3 and ask for one.

issues.problem: There are no compliance or deliverability rules: nothing on CAN-SPAM (address, opt-out), GDPR/PECR/UWG/CASL consent for cold B2B email, honouring unsubscribes and suppression lists, verifying addresses (ZeroBounce) or volume caps. Only the personal-address rule touches privacy.
issues.fix: Add a short pre-send checklist: jurisdiction check, opt-out line, suppression list, address verification, and daily volume limits. Escalate to the user or counsel when the law is unclear.

issues.quote: "follow up", "sales sequence", "reach out to"
issues.problem: 'follow up', 'outreach' and 'reach out to' also match invoice chasing (accounts-receivable-follow-up), meeting follow-ups, and candidate, partner and press outreach. 'prospecting' overlaps list-building skills (prospecting, build-the-target-list).
issues.fix: Narrow the triggers to 'cold sales email', 'cold outreach sequence' and 'prospect follow-up after no reply', or retire the skill in favour of Max's skills.

issues.quote: Spend the research effort on one question: what changed for this account
issues.problem: Inputs are never named (the sender's offer, ICP, voice sample, allowed proof, channel), no research tools are named (web_search, web_fetch, news, job posts), and the trigger is not required to carry a source link and date, so a stale or made-up trigger can end up stated as fact.
issues.fix: Add an Inputs block and a research step that records each trigger with its URL and date. If the trigger can't be verified, don't use it.

issues.problem: No deliverable is defined. There is no format for the draft plus subject plus trigger source, no sequence table with send dates, and no batch output for a list of prospects.
issues.fix: Add an Output section: the first-touch draft with subject and trigger source, then a table of follow-ups (day, angle, draft), then what was left out and why, plus a batch table when given a list.

issues.quote: Day 3: forward your own message with one new fact, not a nudge.
issues.problem: The cadence is email-only, with no LinkedIn or phone touches and no multi-threading to a second persona. 'New facts' are not required to be sourced. Reply handling covers only 'not now', leaving out positive replies, referrals, objections, unsubscribes, out-of-office and bounces.
issues.fix: Require sources for new facts, and hand reply handling to handle-a-reply (or add a short reply taxonomy) with an unsubscribe/stop rule.

scenarios.prompt: Write a cold email to the VP of Operations at Acme Logistics. They just announced a Series B and opened a new Dallas warehouse. We sell route-optimisation software and cut fuel costs 12% for Hartwell Freight. Add the follow-ups too.
scenarios.why: The skill maps cleanly onto this request. The trigger is the Series B and the warehouse. It gives the four-sentence order (trigger → problem in their words → Hartwell proof → one-line question), a lowercase subject of the trigger under six words, no meeting ask, and follow-ups on days 3, 8 and 17, each adding something new. A capable model would write a sharp, senior-sounding sequence, and nothing is sent because the user supplied the proof and asked only for drafts.

scenarios.prompt: Here's a CSV of 150 Apollo leads. About half have no recent news, some addresses are @gmail.com, and 20 are in Germany. Draft sequences for all of them and send from my Gmail starting tomorrow.
scenarios.why: 'If you cannot find a trigger, say so' would correctly cut the no-news half, and the personal-address rule partly covers @gmail.com. But the skill says nothing about drafting before sending or getting approval, and it has no compliance guidance: German UWG/GDPR consent for cold B2B email, an opt-out line, suppression lists. It gives no deliverability or volume limits, no batch triage or output table, and no way to schedule days 3, 8 and 17 (schedule_followup) or record dormancy (memory_store or a CRM). A model following it could send non-compliant mail in bulk.

travel-plan.job: plan business trip with options and itinerary
travel-plan.summary: Collects trip constraints, checks the calendar across the travel window, compares up to three sourced, time-stamped transport and hotel options with a one-line recommendation, then lays out a day-by-day itinerary and a book-or-approve-by list, never booking without a yes.
strengths: Every price must carry currency, refundability, source and time checked, and currency is never converted by guess.
Door-to-door timing to the first meeting and a calendar check across the whole window, buffer days included, reflect real EA practice.
The skill says so honestly when no option meets the constraints, instead of padding the list.
It ends with a book-or-approve-by list and a clear rule against booking, holding or paying without an explicit yes.
missing: Entry, visa, passport-validity and travel-advisory check with sources
Per-option travel-policy compliance and exception approval routing
Named sourcing path for live fares and a stale-price warning
Local times with time zones, and jet-lag-aware scheduling for long-haul trips
Airport transfers, ground transport and minimum connection times
Fare rules: change and cancel fees, and a backup option
Fallback when the calendar or booking tool is not connected
Reusable itinerary and booking-deadline template
Post-approval steps: calendar holds, confirmation tracking, expense receipts
Traveller profile (preferences, loyalty) saved to memory with consent

issues.problem: Nothing covers entry requirements: visas or e-visas, passport validity (often six months), transit visas, health entry rules or travel advisories. A senior EA checks these first because they can make the whole plan invalid.
issues.fix: Add a step to check entry and passport-validity requirements for each country, including transit, from official government sources via web_fetch, citing the source and date. Flag any risk before presenting options.

issues.quote: Give up to three available options for flights or trains and for hotels.
issues.problem: The skill never says how to find availability and prices (web_search, browser_navigate to the carrier or hotel site, a corporate booking tool the user can export from), and never warns that search snippets are stale. Ground transport and minimum connection times are also left out.
issues.fix: Name the sourcing path: browser_navigate or web_fetch on the carrier or hotel site, and if the company uses a booking tool, ask the user to paste its results. Mark search-snippet prices as indicative. Include airport transfers and connection-time checks.

issues.quote: Name the option you would pick and why, in one line.
issues.problem: The travel policy is recorded but never applied. Options are not marked in-policy or out-of-policy, and nothing says who approves an exception.
issues.fix: Add a policy column per option (class, fare cap, hotel cap, advance-booking rule) and send out-of-policy picks to the named approver as a drafted request.

issues.quote: calendar for clashes on every date in the full itinerary window, including
issues.problem: The step assumes the calendar is connected. If it is not, there is no fallback, which risks a false 'you're free' or repeated failed lookups.
issues.fix: Say which calendars were read. If none are connected, ask once for the busy dates or an export (or suggest connect_integration), and label availability as user-stated.

issues.quote: Lay out the trip day by day: travel, meetings with addresses, buffers, and
issues.problem: There is no reusable itinerary format. It never asks for local times with time zones, confirmation numbers, contacts, or a one-page summary the traveller can carry.
issues.fix: Ship a templates/itinerary.md with a per-day table (local time and zone, item, address, confirmation or reference, contact, notes) and a booking-deadline table.

issues.quote: free time. Then list what must be booked or approved, by what date.
issues.problem: The skill stops at the list. Nothing covers the step after the yes: placing calendar holds, capturing confirmations, adding travel blocks, and receipts for expenses.
issues.fix: Add a post-approval step: after each confirmed booking, draft calendar entries for travel time (with approval), record confirmation details, and note receipts for the expense claim.

issues.quote: Do not invent a price, time, or availability, and keep travel details private.
issues.problem: 'Private' is vague for the most sensitive data this skill touches: passport numbers, dates of birth, loyalty IDs and home address.
issues.fix: Say that passport and ID numbers are never stored in memory or put in drafts to third parties, and that traveller profile preferences are saved only with consent.

issues.quote: Use this for a business trip, from one night to a multi-city week.
issues.problem: No boundary is set for mid-trip disruption or rebooking, and nothing says whether personal trips are in scope, so the model is left guessing.
issues.fix: State that disruption and rebooking during the trip use a different flow (draft rebooking options, never change a booking without a yes), and say whether personal travel is in scope.

scenarios.prompt: Plan my trip to Berlin for the Siemens meeting next Tuesday 10:00 at Friedrichstrasse 68. I'm in London, want to be back Wednesday night, budget is £800, I prefer BA and a hotel near the office.
scenarios.why: The steps line up well. Confirm the constraints records the purpose, fixed meeting, budget and preferences and checks the calendar window. Compare options gives up to three flights and hotels with door-to-door time, refundability, source, check time and fare expiry. The itinerary adds buffers and a deadline list. The one gap is that the skill never says where live fares come from (web_search or browser_navigate against the airline or hotel site), but the source and check-time rule keeps the numbers honest.

scenarios.prompt: I need to see customers in São Paulo and Mexico City sometime between the 10th and 21st next month, order doesn't matter. Company policy is economy for flights under 6 hours. My passport expires in February, and my calendar isn't connected to you yet.
scenarios.why: The skill gives no guidance on sequencing a multi-city trip with flexible dates. It never checks entry requirements (the Brazil e-visa for some nationalities, passport validity), so a trip-blocking issue could go unflagged. It records the travel policy but never tests options against it or routes a business-class exception to an approver. Its calendar step has no fallback when the calendar is not connected (ask for busy dates or an export). A capable model would still return sensible options but would likely miss the passport and visa risk.

weekly-priorities-review.summary: Gathers the week's meetings, deadlines and owed promises, measures meeting hours and remaining focus hours against the principal's own priority list, flags unfunded priorities, at-risk promises and purposeless recurring meetings, and proposes three to five changes with drafted messages, without acting on any of them unapproved.
strengths: Uses the principal's own priority list and explicitly forbids adding or re-ranking priorities.
Covers the right lenses: hours per priority, time going to no priority, unfunded priorities, at-risk promises, and recurring meetings with no purpose.
Each proposed change states the time it frees and who it affects, and comes with a drafted message.
Clear no-action-without-yes rule and a no-invented-commitments guardrail.
missing: Path when no priority list exists (ask, or route to setup)
memory_search and memory_store for the previous review and the commitments ledger
Fallback when mail or calendar is disconnected (paste or export)
Confirmable meeting-to-priority mapping with an 'unclear' bucket
Contiguous focus-block definition, with fragmented time reported separately
Look-back on last week's promises and a two-to-three-week deadline lookahead
Waiting-for list of what others owe the principal
Reusable weekly-review output template
Offer to schedule the review as a weekly routine
Sandbox arithmetic for hour totals

issues.quote: Use the principal's own priority list; do not add or rank priorities for them.
issues.problem: The skill assumes a priority list exists. With none, or a stale one, the model has no instruction and may quietly infer priorities, which is exactly what the rule forbids.
issues.fix: Check memory for the priorities from setup. If they are missing or older than the quarter, ask for them with ask_question or point to executive-assistant-getting-started before building the comparison.

issues.quote: the principal owes, from the calendar, mail, and last week's review. Give the
issues.problem: Assumes last week's review persists and every source is connected. The platform keeps no state unless it is written to memory, and a disconnected inbox silently drops owed promises.
issues.fix: Use memory_search for the previous review and commitments ledger, and memory_store the new one at the end. Say which sources were read, and ask once for a paste or export of anything missing.

issues.quote: hours going to each priority, and to none;
issues.problem: Tagging meetings to priorities is judgement, but the output presents the result as fact. Ambiguous meetings get silently assigned, and the hours per priority look more precise than they are.
issues.fix: Show the meeting-to-priority mapping as a table with an 'unclear' bucket, ask the principal to confirm the unclear items, and do the hour totals in bash_exec.

issues.quote: hours in meetings, the hours left for focused work, and each promise with who
issues.problem: Raw leftover hours overstate focus capacity. Fragmented gaps between meetings are not usable deep-work time.
issues.fix: Define focus time as contiguous unbooked blocks of at least 60 to 90 minutes inside working hours, and report fragmented time separately.

issues.quote: Use this at the end of one week or the start of the next.
issues.problem: There is no look-back (what slipped or carried over from last week) and no look-ahead beyond the current week. Deadlines two to three weeks out that need prep time this week are missed.
issues.fix: Add a short look-back of last week's promises (done, slipped, carried over) and a two-to-three-week lookahead for deadlines and big meetings that need prep blocks now.

issues.problem: Only promises the principal owes are tracked. What others owe the principal (the waiting-for list) is a core part of a weekly review and is absent.
issues.fix: Add a waiting-for list with the item, the person, the date promised, and a drafted nudge where one is overdue.

issues.quote: the time it frees and the person it affects, and draft any message it needs.
issues.problem: Nothing defines the deliverable format, and nothing guards bulk declines or tells drafts to avoid exposing private reasons to the recipient.
issues.fix: Ship a templates/weekly-review.md (commitments, hours by priority, gaps, at-risk items, changes A to E answerable by letter). List bulk declines before drafting, and keep draft wording free of private context.

issues.quote: triggers: ["weekly review", "plan my week", "priorities", "week ahead", "time audit"]
issues.problem: 'priorities' is too generic in a multi-expert team, where it collides with product roadmap prioritisation skills. 'plan my week' overlaps calendar-conflict-review's 'busy week'. There is also no offer to run the review as a weekly routine.
issues.fix: Replace 'priorities' with 'time vs priorities' or 'where is my time going'. Differentiate from calendar-conflict-review in the description, and offer schedule_routine for a weekly run.

scenarios.prompt: It's Sunday. Do my weekly review for next week. My priorities this quarter are closing the Series A, hiring a VP Engineering, and the Q4 board deck.
scenarios.why: List commitments pulls the meetings, deadlines and owed promises. Compare with priorities maps hours to each of the three priorities and to none, flags zero-time priorities and at-risk promises, and questions purposeless recurring meetings. Changes to consider gives three to five moves with the time freed, the person affected and draft messages. This produces a useful review. Its main weakness is that 'hours left for focused work' may count fragmented 30-minute gaps as focus time.

scenarios.prompt: Can you do a time audit? I feel like I'm spending nothing on hiring. Only my work calendar is connected, not my email, and I've never written my priorities down. Didn't you do one of these for me last week?
scenarios.why: The skill forbids adding or ranking priorities but never says what to do when there is no list: ask with ask_question, or run the getting-started setup. It assumes mail and 'last week's review' are available, with no memory_search step and no fallback for the missing inbox, so owed promises from email are silently missed. Mapping meetings to priorities like 'hiring' is a judgement call the skill never asks the model to show or confirm. A capable model would improvise, but the hours per priority could look authoritative without being checked.

renewal-readiness-review.job: assess account renewal readiness and risks
renewal-readiness-review.summary: A 32-line checklist that tells Riley to verify contract and stakeholder facts, weigh achieved against hoped-for value and open risks, and return a sectioned renewal brief without inventing terms.
strengths: Separates achieved value from hoped-for value, which is exactly Riley's evidence discipline
Forbids predicting renewal from a health score alone and forbids inventing terms, discounts, savings or quotes
Names notice date, procurement steps and approval needs as items to verify, which many renewal templates skip
Short, with no filler
missing: Readiness or forecast rating with criteria
Days-to-notice computation and a T-minus renewal plan
Auto-renew, uplift and notice-clause check
Stakeholder map (economic buyer, champion, procurement) with single-thread risk
Value realisation against the success-plan baseline
Mutual close plan including procurement, security and legal lead times
Named handoffs to the commercial owner, legal and expansion
Data-source routing (CRM, contract, usage) with CSV fallback
Saved artefact and scheduled follow-up
Worked example or template

issues.quote: Use sections for readiness, risks, unknowns, proof to gather, customer questions,
issues.problem: 'Readiness' is a section name with no scale, criteria or forecast category, and there is no template, so the brief cannot answer 'will this renew and what is blocking it'.
issues.fix: Add a readiness rating (e.g. On track / At risk / Blocked / Insufficient evidence) with explicit criteria: sponsor confirmed, value proven against the success plan, no open Sev1/2, procurement path known, notice date runway. Ship a templates/renewal-review.md with a one-line call and rationale at the top.

issues.quote: Confirm contract end, notice date, commercial owner, customer sponsor, decision
issues.problem: Dates are collected but not used. The skill does not compute days to notice, check auto-renew or uplift clauses, or plan back from notice for procurement, security review and legal lead times, and it has no branch for a notice date that is imminent or already passed.
issues.fix: Compute days-to-notice and days-to-end in bash_exec. Add a T-minus plan (120/90/60/30 days from notice). Branch: if notice is under 30 days away or has passed, flag it urgent to the commercial owner before anything else.

issues.problem: The skill never says where the facts come from or what to do when a source is not connected, so the model has no route to CRM, contract files or usage data.
issues.fix: Name the sources: HubSpot via run_block, the contract in Drive or the workspace via read_workspace_file, and a usage export. When a source is missing, ask for a CSV or paste with ask_question. memory_store the renewal and notice dates, and offer schedule_followup at the next T-minus checkpoint.

issues.quote: State the next approval or decision needed.
issues.problem: No approver or handoff is named. Price uplift, discount and multi-year terms belong to the commercial owner (Jordan's renewal-negotiation-brief), contract interpretation to Vera or legal, and expansion to expansion-opportunity-brief.
issues.fix: Add a handoff table saying who decides pricing and terms, who confirms contract facts, and when to consult_teammate. Keep the renewal brief free of commercial recommendations Riley is not authorised to make.

issues.quote: open support or delivery issues, unresolved promises, relationship changes, and
issues.problem: 'Relationship changes' is the only stakeholder guidance. There is no map of economic buyer, champion, users and procurement, no single-threaded risk, and no specific play for champion departure.
issues.fix: Add a stakeholder map (role, name, stance, last contact, source). Flag single-threaded accounts and a departed champion as named risks, each with a next step.

issues.quote: the agreed next meeting. Separate achieved value from hoped-for value.
issues.problem: There is no method for showing value. Outcomes are not tied to the success plan's baseline, current value, source and date, so 'achieved value' remains a claim rather than evidence.
issues.fix: Pull the outcomes from customer-success-plan. For each one show baseline, current value, source and date range, and mark anything unsourced as unproven.

issues.quote: "renewal risk"
issues.problem: This trigger overlaps churn-risk-review (same expert) and Max's renewal-expansion-and-qbr, so the wrong skill may load.
issues.fix: Scope the description: renewal readiness is contract-dated prep for a renewal decision; ongoing risk signals belong to churn-risk-review.

scenarios.prompt: Acme renews on 30 Nov. Here are the order form PDF, last quarter's usage export and their open tickets. Prep the renewal review for Thursday's forecast call.
scenarios.why: Verify the record and Review the case would produce a correct list of facts, risks and unknowns. But the skill claims to support a 'forecast update' and gives no readiness scale, no forecast category and no rule for making the call. The brief ends without the one judgement the forecast meeting needs, and there is no template, so each run is shaped differently.

scenarios.prompt: Globex's contract isn't in HubSpot, I think the notice date was last week, their champion left in August, and sales wants a 7% uplift. Where do we stand?
scenarios.why: The skill correctly marks missing contract data 'for the authorised team to verify' and forbids inventing terms. It has no branch for a notice date that may have passed (auto-renew or lapse), no play for champion loss, and no route for the uplift to the commercial owner or Jordan's renewal-negotiation-brief. The model has to improvise the parts that matter most.

renewal-touchpoint-draft.job: draft renewal outreach message to customer
renewal-touchpoint-draft.summary: A 30-line recipe for drafting one renewal message from approved facts only: at most three verified outcomes, one clear ask, price kept out unless approved, returned with the facts used, placeholders and an approval checklist.
strengths: Clear reusable deliverable: subject, message, facts used, placeholders and approval checklist
One ask and at most three outcomes keeps the message tight and credible
Price and terms are kept out unless the authorised owner supplied the wording
Tells the model to surface a serious unresolved issue rather than bury it under value claims
Bans pressure, false scarcity and unapproved concessions
missing: Touch types by renewal stage (T-120/90/60/30)
Audience variants: champion, economic buyer, procurement
Follow-up plan when there is no reply
Precondition branch when the renewal record is unverified
Contractual price-change notice path with approved wording
Worked example in Riley's voice
Staging as an email draft after approval, with an approval log

issues.quote: Use this after the renewal record has been checked.
issues.problem: This is a precondition with no branch. The model is not told what to do if the record has not been checked, so it may draft from unverified dates or terms.
issues.fix: If there is no verified renewal record, run renewal-readiness-review's Verify step first, or ask for the contract end and notice dates, and draft only with placeholders for anything unverified.

issues.problem: Every touchpoint is treated as one generic message. There are no stage types (value check-in around T-120, renewal kickoff T-90, proposal T-60, paperwork T-30, post-renewal thanks) and no plan for no reply.
issues.fix: Add a short table of touch types by days-to-notice, each with its purpose and one ask, plus a no-reply rule (one follow-up after N business days, staged via schedule_followup).

issues.quote: Use the recipient, relationship, contract or notice date, stated goals, verified
issues.problem: The recipient is an input but the skill gives no audience tailoring. Champion, economic buyer and procurement need different content, and multithreading is not mentioned.
issues.fix: Add audience variants: outcome-led for the economic buyer, adoption-led for the champion, logistics-only for procurement. Suggest a second-thread draft when the account relies on one contact.

issues.quote: purpose. Keep price and terms out unless the authorised owner supplied approved
issues.problem: Some renewals contractually require written notice of a price change. The skill gives no route for that case beyond omitting the price.
issues.fix: When a price change must be communicated, hand off to the commercial owner (or consult Jordan), quote the approved wording verbatim, and record who approved it and when.

issues.quote: If the account has a serious unresolved issue, acknowledge it plainly and do
issues.problem: The skill does not say whether to pause the commercial ask while a Sev1/2 is open, or to coordinate with the support owner on the issue status.
issues.fix: If a Sev1/2 is open, recommend a status-first message with the issue owner and date, and defer the renewal ask until there is a fix plan. Confirm the status line with the support owner.

issues.quote: Return a subject line, message, facts used, placeholders, and approval checklist.
issues.problem: The output has no example or template file and no staging path in the harness, such as creating a Gmail draft after approval or logging the approval.
issues.fix: Ship examples/renewal-touch.md. After approval, offer to stage it as a Gmail draft via run_block and log the approver and date to memory.

scenarios.prompt: Draft the 90-day renewal email to Maya at Acme. Kickoff goals were SSO rollout and cutting onboarding time; SSO is live and onboarding went from 14 to 9 days per their dashboard.
scenarios.why: Following Draft and the return list, the model produces a subject line, opens with the renewal date, cites the two verified outcomes, asks one question or proposes one meeting, and lists the facts used and an approval checklist. That is senior-quality for a simple case.

scenarios.prompt: Write the renewal note to Globex. They had a P1 outage last month with the RCA still open, finance wants the 8% uplift mentioned, and I don't know who the new sponsor is.
scenarios.why: Guardrails hold: the issue is acknowledged plainly, price stays a placeholder without approved wording, and the recipient becomes a placeholder. But the skill does not say whether to hold the commercial touch until the RCA lands, how to find or confirm the new sponsor, or how to handle a contractual uplift notice. 'Use this after the renewal record has been checked' has no else-branch.

customer-escalation.job: package customer issue escalation for internal teams
customer-escalation.summary: An upstream Anthropic support skill that decides whether an issue warrants escalation, gathers context, assesses impact, picks the target tier and fills a structured escalation brief with repro steps, follow-up cadence and de-escalation rules.
strengths: Clear 'handle in support vs escalate' criteria that act as a real decision gate
Tier map (L2, Engineering, Product, Security, Leadership) saying what each audience needs
The best repro-step guidance in the catalog: clean state, exact values, frequency, what was ruled out
Follow-up cadence by severity and explicit de-escalation rules
Reusable escalation brief template with a specific ask and deadline
missing: Duplicate check linking an existing Linear or GitHub issue before filing
PII and secret redaction before sharing evidence
Sourcing labels on impact numbers (FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN)
Company severity matrix from memory, with a fallback
Drafted customer interim update in the same packet
schedule_followup for the follow-up cadence instead of human-style 'every 2 hours'
Graceful fallback when no support platform or CRM is connected
Approval log for posts and pages

issues.quote: Always quantify impact — vague escalations get deprioritized
issues.problem: It demands quantification (ARR at risk, customers affected) with no rule that numbers must be sourced, so the model will estimate revenue and counts.
issues.fix: Every number must carry a source and date or be marked UNKNOWN or assumed. Ask the user for ARR and counts via ask_question rather than estimate. Add FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels to the template fields.

issues.quote: /customer-escalation <issue description> [customer name or account]
issues.problem: Slash-command usage, an H1 of '/customer-escalation' and argument-hint are Claude Code constructs that the harness ignores or that mislead the model.
issues.fix: Replace the Usage block with 'Inputs to ask for': issue, affected accounts, timeline, what was tried, and the desired decision.

issues.quote: **~~support platform**: Related tickets, timeline of communications, previous troubleshooting
issues.problem: The ~~category placeholders resolve (via CONNECTORS.md) to Intercom, Zendesk and Jira MCP servers, not AutoGPT blocks. There is no fallback when nothing is connected.
issues.fix: Map to run_block sources (HubSpot, Linear, GitHub, Slack, Notion, Gmail) and run_mcp_tool. If none are connected, ask for pasted tickets or an export, and mark context gaps in the brief.

issues.quote: **Include evidence**: Screenshots, error messages (exact text), network logs, console output
issues.problem: Logs, screenshots and network captures often contain tokens, PII or payment data. The skill never says to redact before the brief goes to Slack or Linear.
issues.fix: Add a redaction rule: strip secrets, tokens, card numbers and personal data, and hand to sensitive-data handling if exposure is found.

issues.quote: **Note:** Security escalations bypass normal tier progression — escalate immediately regardless of your level
issues.problem: Written for a human agent. It implies acting on the escalation and on 'containment steps taken' without the owner's approval.
issues.fix: For an AI teammate: alert the owner immediately with a drafted security packet, take no containment action itself, and hand off to the security or compliance owner.

issues.quote: "Want me to post this in a ~~chat channel for the target team?"
issues.problem: Posting and customer updates are offered as questions only. There is no explicit draft-then-approve step, no approval log and no customer-update draft.
issues.fix: State that every post, page and customer update is staged as a draft for the owner's yes through the approval flow, and log who approved it.

issues.quote: **Critical**: Production down, data at risk, security breach, or multiple high-value customers affected. Needs immediate attention.
issues.problem: The generic three-level scale ignores the company's own severity matrix and SLA, and it conflicts with Robin's SEV1-4 and P1-P4 definitions.
issues.fix: Use the escalation matrix from memory if one is saved, fall back to this scale marked as unverified, and add a Low level.

issues.quote: a customer is threatening to churn
issues.problem: Overlaps Robin's escalations-and-incidents, Sasha's bug-report-handoff and Riley's churn-risk-review, so the triggers would compete in any of those kits.
issues.fix: Merge into Robin's escalations-and-incidents (or Sasha's bug-report-handoff) rather than assign it alongside them, or scope it to cross-functional product and leadership escalations only.

scenarios.prompt: Three customers reported CSV exports dropping rows since Tuesday's release. Here are the tickets. Package it for engineering.
scenarios.why: Step 1's escalate criteria (3+ customers), the L2 to Engineering tier, the repro best practices and the brief template give an engineer-ready packet with scope, frequency, what was tried and a specific ask with a deadline.

scenarios.prompt: Globex renews in 45 days and says they'll churn unless audit logs ship. No CRM is connected and I don't know their ARR. Escalate to leadership.
scenarios.why: The Any to Leadership tier and the 'What's Needed' section fit. But 'Always quantify impact' and the 'Revenue at risk' field push the model to estimate ARR, with no rule to mark it unknown or ask. Context gathering is all '~~CRM (if connected)' with no ask-the-user fallback. It also offers to post to a chat channel with no draft-and-approve step or approval log.

customer-response-drafting.job: draft customer support reply for approval
customer-response-drafting.summary: An upstream Anthropic support skill that researches context, drafts a channel-appropriate customer response with internal notes, runs a quality checklist, and carries long guidance on tone, situation playbooks, templates, follow-up cadence and escalation.
strengths: Internal 'Notes for You (do not send)' block with things to verify, risk factors and escalation note
Tone spectrum by situation and relationship stage is practical and reusable
Situation-specific playbooks (bad news, declining, outage, escalation) are sound
Quality checklist includes 'no commitments beyond what's authorized' and no roadmap leaks
Length guidance by channel
missing: No-invention rule for dates, names, ETAs and policy
Citation of the governing KB or policy passage
Explicit draft-only and approval-flow statement
Fallback when no email, CRM or support tool is connected
Banned-phrase list and use of the expert's voice
Guidance on SLA credits, liability and legal wording in incident replies
Progressive disclosure (templates in references/)
Channel-specific public-safe rules for social replies

issues.quote: I've confirmed the issue and escalated it to our engineering team as a
issues.problem: The template hard-codes actions (confirmed, escalated, and in the billing template 'I've looked into your account') that may not have happened, so filled drafts will assert false facts.
issues.fix: Make these lines conditional placeholders and state only actions verified in the record. Otherwise mark them for the owner to confirm.

issues.quote: Include specific dates and times, not relative terms ("by Friday January 24" not "in a few days")
issues.problem: This rule and 'Name specific people' push for specifics with no rule on where they come from, so the model will invent dates, owners and ETAs.
issues.fix: Use only dates, names and ETAs from the record or the owner. Otherwise insert a marked placeholder and list it under Things to verify.

issues.quote: /draft-response <context about the customer question, issue, or request>
issues.problem: Slash-command usage and the H1 '/draft-response' are Claude Code constructs, and they do not match the installed name customer-response-drafting.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block and rename the H1. List the inputs to collect: the thread, customer, channel, governing policy or KB passage, and what the owner has authorised.

issues.quote: **Customer**: Who is the communication for? Look up account context if available.
issues.problem: All research goes through ~~placeholders that map to Intercom and Zendesk MCPs. There is no AutoGPT block mapping, no fallback of asking for the pasted thread, and no requirement to cite the governing KB or policy passage.
issues.fix: Route to Gmail, HubSpot, Notion and Slack via run_block. If none are connected, ask for the thread and policy text. Require a citation of the passage each factual claim rests on.

issues.quote: "Should I prepare a follow-up message to send after [X days] if no response?"
issues.problem: The skill never says outright that it only drafts and that sending goes through the owner's approval.
issues.fix: State 'draft only; nothing sends without the owner's yes'. Use schedule_followup to re-draft the follow-up rather than implying an automated send.

issues.quote: and [what you're doing to prevent recurrence if known].
issues.problem: Invites prevention promises and liability language in incident comms, which conflicts with Sasha's 'never promise that a problem will not happen again'. There is also no guidance on SLA credits or admissions.
issues.fix: Allow only approved RCA or prevention statements. Route SLA credits, liability and legal language to the owner or legal before drafting.

issues.section: Acknowledging a Billing or Account Issue
issues.quote: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Let me know if you have any
issues.problem: Scripted sympathy and filler closings, which Sasha's voice ('no scripted sympathy') and Robin's banned-phrase list reject.
issues.fix: Replace with a specific acknowledgement of the customer's impact. Add a banned-phrase list and defer to the expert's voice notes.

issues.quote: Use when answering a product question, responding to an escalation or outage
issues.problem: Near-total trigger overlap with Robin's draft-the-reply and Sasha's support-reply-draft, and 430 lines load with no progressive disclosure.
issues.fix: Merge into the expert's reply skill. Move the tone tables, templates and follow-up cadence into references/ files that are loaded on demand.

scenarios.prompt: Northwind's integration has been down two days and their admin is furious. Engineering says the fix ETA is Thursday. Draft a reply.
scenarios.why: The Handling an escalation playbook, the Escalated tone, the response structure and the Notes for You block (things to verify, risk factors) give a senior-quality draft with ownership, the Thursday ETA from the user and an update cadence.

scenarios.prompt: Draft a reply to Acme's VP declining their request for a 20% renewal discount. I don't have our concession policy and nothing is connected.
scenarios.why: The 'Declining a request' playbook and the internal notes help. But research is all '~~CRM (if connected)' with no ask-for-paste fallback, and nothing routes commercial authority to the owner or approved wording. 'Explain the why' and 'Name specific people' invite invented reasons and names, and the only guard is the 'Things to verify' note.

customer-support-research.job: research customer question across sources with citations
customer-support-research.summary: An upstream Anthropic support skill that researches a customer question across tiered internal and external sources, synthesises a brief with a confidence level, sources, gaps and next steps, handles contradictions and escalation, and suggests capturing the answer in the knowledge base.
strengths: Source-tier model with a confidence level per tier, flagging inference as inference
Explicit contradiction handling that gives customers the conservative answer until resolved
Clear 'answer directly vs escalate' list covering roadmap, pricing, legal, security and precedent
Graceful fallback when sources are empty: web research plus asking the user, with transparency lines
Reusable research brief template with Gaps & Unknowns and next steps
missing: Privacy boundary on cross-customer data and PII in searched email and CRM
Per-claim FACT/INFERENCE labels and an 'as of' date on each finding
Customer contract as the governing source for account-specific answers
Tool mapping to AutoGPT blocks and web_search
memory_store of the verified answer for reuse
Handoff to the reply-drafting skill with the brief attached

issues.quote: /customer-research <question or topic>
issues.problem: Slash-command usage and the H1 '/customer-research' are Claude Code constructs that do not match the installed name customer-support-research.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block and rename the H1. State the inputs: the question verbatim, the customer or account, the audience, and the deadline.

issues.quote: Analogous customers: what worked for comparable accounts
issues.problem: Drawing on other customers' situations risks leaking another customer's name, configuration or terms into a customer-facing answer. The skill has no privacy boundary.
issues.fix: Tier-5 analogues are internal-only. Never name or quote another customer or their terms in anything customer-facing, and redact before the brief is shared.

issues.quote: ~~knowledge base (if connected): product docs, runbooks, FAQs, policy documents
issues.problem: The ~~placeholders map via CONNECTORS.md to Guru, Intercom and Jira MCPs rather than the tools the harness has.
issues.fix: Map the tiers to Notion, Drive, Docs, HubSpot, Linear, Slack and Gmail via run_block, plus web_search and web_fetch for tier 4. Keep the ask-the-user fallback.

issues.quote: Trust unless clearly outdated — check dates
issues.problem: Tier 1 lumps general KB and policy together and does not rank the customer's signed contract or order form, which governs account-specific commitments, above public docs.
issues.fix: Add 'customer contract or order form' as the top authority for account-specific questions, and require a last-updated date on every tier-1 source cited.

issues.quote: "Should I save these findings to your knowledge base for future reference?"
issues.problem: KB writes are offered without saying they are drafts that need approval, and this duplicates dedicated KB skills (knowledge-centered-service, help-article-from-tickets, knowledge-base-article-writing).
issues.fix: Stage KB entries as drafts for the owner's yes, or hand off to the expert's KB skill instead of duplicating the format.

issues.section: Research Documentation for Team Knowledge Base
issues.quote: After completing research, capture the knowledge for future use.
issues.problem: About 40 lines of KB documentation format and hygiene guidance load on every run, and they repeat step 6 and other KB skills.
issues.fix: Move them to references/kb-entry-format.md or drop them in favour of a handoff to the KB skill.

scenarios.prompt: A customer asks whether we support SCIM provisioning with Okta. Find out, and check what we told them last time.
scenarios.why: Step 1 classifies it as a customer question plus account context. Step 2 searches the KB and docs before CRM notes and email. The brief gives a bottom-line answer with a confidence level, sources and gaps, and step 5 flags anything that differs from what was said before.

scenarios.prompt: Acme says we promised a 99.9% uptime SLA. The help centre says 99.5% and a sales Slack thread says 99.9% for enterprise. Only Notion is connected. What do we tell them?
scenarios.why: Handling Contradictions tells the model to name the conflict, weigh authority and recency, and use the most conservative answer for customers. 'Escalate or Verify When' routes contract-specific and legal questions to legal. Step 4 asks the user for missing internal docs. One gap: the tier table does not rank the customer's signed contract above published KB text.

15:role-intake-and-job-description.job: draft job description from role intake
15:role-intake-and-job-description.summary: Runs a scripted intake-to-JD pipeline: intake brief, a four-way requirement sort in requirements.csv checked by req_check.py, a JD drafted from a fixed template, a lint pass for age, proxy and gender-coded wording (jd_lint.py), posting-field lookups by location, a sentence-level diff when rewriting an old posting, and a DOCX review copy plus approval checklist. Nothing is published.
strengths: Real, working deterministic checks. I ran req_check.py, jd_lint.py, diff_postings.py, extract_text.py and to_docx.py against the bundled examples and the output matches the worked example exactly.

The requirements.csv hand-off enforces the three-part must-have test, checks that each must-show requirement is quoted word for word in the JD, and feeds hiring-rubric-design's validator (--write-back exists in the sibling package), which closes the gap where a dropped requirement is still screened on.
Strong guardrails: never publishes, never estimates a band, never claims a posting is compliant, treats lint hits as owner decisions, and marks every fact APPROVED-by or [OWNER TO CONFIRM].
A real rewrite mode: brings in DOCX, PDF, HTML or a URL (with a fallback for script-heavy job boards and the 100 KB cut-off) and produces a sentence-level 'What changed' log.
Degrades cleanly when Python is missing, ~/workspace is not writable, or a PDF is scanned. The paths (~/skills/<slug>, ~/workspace, run_capability, TodoWrite) match the platform code.
The hard-case example (a legacy Denver posting) is realistic. It shows the sort recovering the real outcome behind '5+ years' instead of just deleting it.
missing: Pay-range posting rules for NYC and NY State, WA, IL, MA, NJ, MD, MN, HI, VT and DC, and the EU Pay Transparency Directive (range before interview, gender-neutral titles)
A wording-check-only fast path
Company/team context and why-join section, with a length/readability target
Guidance on a market-standard, searchable job title versus the internal level name
Channel formatting notes (character limits for LinkedIn and job boards) for the owner's own posting

issues.quote: Posting fields: look up each hiring location in
issues.problem: posting-law-fields.md lists pay-posting fields only for California and Colorado. New York City and New York State, Washington, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Maryland, Minnesota, Hawaii, Vermont and DC pay-range laws are missing, and so is the EU Pay Transparency Directive (transposition due 7 June 2026). In the most common hiring locations the checklist therefore gets no pay-range line.
issues.fix: Add dated, sourced rows for those jurisdictions, still worded 'may be required; confirm'. For any location not in the table, always add the line 'posting-pay rules for <location> not checked; people lead to confirm'.

issues.quote: Get the reason for the hire, outcomes due in the first months
issues.problem: There is only one path. A trigger such as 'check this job ad for biased wording', or a one-line revision, is forced through full intake, the CSV sort, req_check, the DOCX and a TodoWrite mirror. That is slow, and it asks the owner questions they did not want to answer.
issues.fix: Add a decision point at the top: for a wording check only, run jd_lint.py on the paste and return the language flags plus posting-field lines. For a new JD or a rewrite, run the full procedure.

issues.quote: from `templates/job-description.md`: outcome first, then the
issues.problem: The template has no company or team context, no reason to join, and no growth line, and gives no target length or reading level. A rewrite removes exclusionary wording but does nothing about the attraction problem. The example's own trigger was 'nobody good applies'.
issues.fix: Add an optional 'About the team and why this role' section filled only from approved facts, set a length target (for example 300-600 words), and add a readability check.

issues.quote: the first session on a role with no owners recorded (start
issues.problem: This line contradicts the Inputs table ('if none, record owners as OPEN'). A user asking for a quick JD with no hiring plan may be bounced to recruiting-getting-started when the skill could carry on.
issues.fix: Choose one rule: proceed with owners OPEN and offer recruiting-getting-started afterwards, or make the redirect explicit and remove the OPEN fallback.

issues.quote: List every flag and check hit with its swap under "Language flags"
issues.problem: The term list misses common variants. I tested 'Strong English (native preferred)' and got no hit. A clean lint run can then be read as a clean review.
issues.fix: Add a regex check row for \bnative\b and say that a clean lint is not a clean review: read the draft once by hand for proxies.

issues.quote: (open items highlighted); deliver the markdown and the DOCX with
issues.problem: to_docx.py skips only lines that start with '<!--'. I tested it: when the template's three-line header comment is left in, its second and third lines are printed into the DOCX review copy.
issues.fix: Strip <!-- ... --> blocks in convert() before rendering. Alternatively, have req_check or the self-check fail if the template comment is still present.

issues.quote: `req_check.py --jd` is clean; every removed requirement has a reason.
issues.problem: The Output contract, the Quality self-check and checklists/review-checks.md restate the same checks, and inline source numbers ([45][34][72]...) add noise to the body.
issues.fix: Keep one checklist in checklists/review-checks.md and point to it. Move source numbers into the references files.

scenarios.prompt: We're opening a Senior Payroll Specialist in Austin, hybrid 3 days, reporting to our Controller Dana. They'd take over multi-state payroll runs and clear the garnishment backlog. Dana approved $85-100k. Can you write the JD?
scenarios.why: Step 1 asks for the missing facts (outcomes, decisions owned, legal text) in one ask_question card. Step 2 sorts requirements into requirements.csv, and req_check turns any 'CPP' or '5+ years' into a WARN that needs a work reason. Step 4 drafts outcome-first from the template, with pay marked APPROVED by Dana. Steps 5 and 7 lint the draft, look up Texas (it falls to the 'Other US states' row, so the people lead is asked), mark open facts, then build the DOCX and approval checklist. A senior recruiter would sign off on this.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Greenhouse link for a Staff Engineer, hiring in New York City and Berlin. Our CTO insists on 'CS degree from a top university' and 8+ years. Just clean it up so we can repost today; pay stays 'competitive'.
scenarios.why: Most of this is handled well. web_fetch, with a browser fallback, brings the posting in. req_check raises an ERROR on 'top' in a must-show and a WARN on the degree and years. The skill will not publish and keeps pay [OWNER TO CONFIRM]. The gap is posting-law-fields.md: its NYC row covers only AEDT, and its EU row covers only AI. So the approval checklist gets no pay-range line for either NYC (the pay-range posting law) or Berlin (the EU Pay Transparency Directive, which member states had to transpose by June 2026). Those are the two issues most likely to block the repost.

better: The main version is a 35-line prose placeholder. This rebuild adds five working stdlib scripts, four templates, two worked examples with real script output, and a checklist.
Adds a real rewrite mode (upload, paste or URL extraction and a sentence-level change log) that main lacked.
The requirement sort is now a machine-checked requirements.csv with the three-part must-have test, JD consistency checks, and a hand-off to hiring-rubric-design.
Adds a sourced language lint with benign-case notes, and posting-field lookups by location with a rule never to claim compliance.
Sharper description and triggers, plus Use-when and Do-not-use boundaries.
Durable state in ~/workspace/hiring/<role-slug>, with fallbacks when Python is missing, the volume is not writable, or a PDF is scanned.
worse: The body is 4x longer, with inline citation numbers and three overlapping checklists.
The full multi-script pipeline is mandatory even for a simple wording check.
It is coupled to a shared hiring-plan layout that has to be kept in sync by hand across every Harper package.
A new internal contradiction: 'Do not use' when no owners are recorded, versus 'record owners as OPEN'.
The posting-law table is narrow and dated, so it needs ongoing maintenance.

candidate-interview-planning.job: design structured interview loop and scorecards
candidate-interview-planning.summary: Lists five structured-interview principles and the parts of an interview kit (4-6 competencies, behavioural and situational questions with probes, a 1-4 scale, a debrief template) and asks for a full kit. It has no steps, no inputs and no guardrails.
strengths: Sound core principles: same questions for every candidate, competency-based, behavioural and situational questions, scored with a rubric rather than gut feel.
A useful question-bank shape: behavioural plus situational questions plus follow-up probes for each competency.
Short and easy to scan, with no Claude-Code-only constructs.
missing: Approved rubric or JD as a required input, with each question mapped to a criterion
Stage design: one owner per competency, timings, and a work sample or job simulation
Independent scorecard submission before the debrief
An interviewer do-not-ask list and a legal/privacy note (recording, AI note-taker consent)
An accommodation line and a candidate-facing agenda
Interviewer calibration or briefing packet
A saved, reusable kit file

issues.quote: Define 4-6 key competencies for the role (e.g., technical skills, communication, leadership, problem-solving).
issues.problem: Competencies are made up fresh from generic examples instead of taken from the approved JD or rubric. The loop can end up testing things the posting never asked for and drift away from the must-show requirements.
issues.fix: Require the approved rubric or requirements as input (ask for them if missing), and map every competency and question to a rubric criterion id.

issues.problem: No guardrails at all. Nothing on questions that must not be asked (age, family, health or disability before an offer, citizenship versus work authorisation, salary history), on accommodations, or on consent for recording or an AI note-taker.
issues.fix: Add a guardrails section: an interviewer do-not-ask list, an accommodation line for the candidate agenda, recording and AI-tool notice, and a rule to route legal questions to the people lead or counsel.

issues.quote: Structured format for interviewers to share findings and make a decision.
issues.problem: There is no requirement that scorecards are submitted independently before the debrief, which invites anchoring. 'Make a decision' also conflicts with Harper's and Sofia's boundaries: the named human decides.
issues.fix: Lock scorecards before the debrief, run the debrief criterion by criterion, and have the expert prepare the evidence while the named decision-maker records the decision.

issues.quote: 2-3 behavioral questions ("Tell me about a time...")
issues.problem: Four to six competencies at 3-5 questions each gives up to 30 questions, with no allocation to stages, no timing, and no work sample. The result is overlapping, overlong loops.
issues.fix: Give each competency one owning stage and interviewer (two only for critical criteria), time-box each stage, and prefer a work sample for skills.

issues.quote: Rate each competency on a consistent scale (1-4) with clear descriptions of what each level looks like.
issues.problem: No guidance on writing behavioural anchors from observable evidence, no 'not assessed' or 'no evidence' option, and no note-taking standard.
issues.fix: Require an observable anchor for each level, a not-assessed option, and verbatim evidence notes for each rating.

issues.quote: Produce a complete interview kit: panel assignment (who interviews for what), question bank by competency, scoring rubric, and debrief template.
issues.problem: No template file, no candidate-facing agenda, no interviewer prep packet, and nowhere to save the kit so later skills (debrief, scheduling) can use it.
issues.fix: Ship templates/interview-kit.md and a candidate agenda template, and save the kit to the role folder.

issues.quote: Trigger with "interview plan for", "interview questions for", "how should we interview", "scorecard for"
issues.problem: 'scorecard for' collides with hiring-rubric-design, role-intake-and-scorecard and interview-plan-and-scorecard. The whole skill duplicates Harper's interview-plan-and-scorecard and Sofia's interview-kit-design.
issues.fix: Drop the skill and fold anything useful into those skills. If it is kept, narrow the triggers and add a 'Do not use for' line.

scenarios.prompt: Put together an interview plan for our Product Designer role. We have four interviewers and want a portfolio review in there.
scenarios.why: A capable model will produce a tidy kit: competencies, question bank, 1-4 scale, panel split, debrief template. But the skill never asks for the JD or rubric, so the competencies are invented from generic examples. It does not assign each competency to one interviewer, gives no guidance on running the portfolio review as a work sample, sets no timings, and does not require scorecards to be submitted before the debrief. The result is generic, not senior-grade.

scenarios.prompt: We have last week's rubric, but the hiring manager wants to add a 'culture add' round, one interviewer is out next week, the candidate is in Illinois, and we'll use an AI note-taker. Replan the loop.
scenarios.why: Nothing tells the model to reuse the existing rubric, to question a culture round that has no job-related criteria, or to rebalance coverage when an interviewer drops out. There is also nothing on notice and consent for recording or an AI note-taker (Illinois requires all-party consent, and the AI Video Interview Act applies if video is analysed) or on accommodations. The model would either improvise or skip these.

employment-offer-drafting.job: draft candidate offer letter from approved terms
employment-offer-drafting.summary: Collects role, level, location, comp and start date, then fills a markdown offer template: a comp table including total first-year comp, terms, a benefits summary, a placeholder letter and negotiation notes. Optional HRIS and ATS placeholder connectors can pull bands and update the pipeline.
strengths: The total-comp table (base, equity, sign-on, target bonus) is a clear candidate-facing summary.
A good tip on being specific about vesting schedule and share count.
Short, with a clear list of inputs up front.
missing: Draft-only rule and an approval gate before any send or ATS/HRIS write
Source and approver for every term, with [OWNER TO CONFIRM] for gaps
Contingencies: background check (FCRA), right to work or I-9, references
Offer expiry, acceptance mechanics, and at-will or notice/probation terms by jurisdiction
Salary-history prohibition, and consistency with the posted pay range
Filling the company's own offer template without changing its clauses
A close plan: verbal offer script and follow-up dates
Hand-off to onboarding once the offer is accepted

issues.quote: If you don't have all details, I'll help you think through them.
issues.problem: When base, equity or the band is missing, the model is told to help work out the numbers. That leads to invented figures in a candidate-facing letter and contradicts both Harper's and Sofia's boundaries.
issues.fix: Missing terms stay [OWNER TO CONFIRM], with the owner named. Band and comp questions go to the comp owner, and figures are never derived or estimated.

issues.quote: Update offer status in the pipeline
issues.problem: This writes to the ATS with no approval step, and nowhere does the skill say the letter is a draft that must not be sent or recorded before the signatory approves.
issues.fix: Draft only. Add an approval checklist (terms, signatory, legal text), and route any ATS, HRIS or email action through the platform approval flow after sign-off.

issues.quote: /draft-offer $ARGUMENTS
issues.problem: Slash commands and $ARGUMENTS don't exist in AutoGPT, argument-hint is dropped, and the ~~HRIS/~~ATS placeholders never resolve to a block or MCP tool, so there is no fallback.
issues.fix: Remove the Usage block. Name real routes (a Google Docs or Gmail draft through run_block, connected MCP tools) and fall back to a pasted term sheet or the company template.

issues.quote: [Complete offer letter text]
issues.problem: The letter body is an empty placeholder. Nothing prompts for contingencies (background check with FCRA disclosure, right to work or I-9), at-will or notice and probation terms by jurisdiction, offer expiry, acceptance and signature, or references to the confidentiality and IP agreement.
issues.fix: Fill the company's own template without editing its clauses. If there is none, use a section list with those elements, and flag jurisdiction-specific terms for counsel.

issues.quote: Share count, current valuation method, vesting schedule.
issues.problem: Together with 'Total First-Year Comp', this invites putting a dollar value on equity or describing its value without an approved 409A or strike price, which risks misrepresentation.
issues.fix: State share count, strike price and vesting only as approved. Never compute a dollar value for equity unless the company supplies approved valuation wording.

issues.quote: [Comp band context]
issues.problem: The negotiation notes have no limits. Nothing forbids asking for or using current pay or salary history (banned in many jurisdictions), and there is no approval ladder for counters or matching a competing offer.
issues.fix: Limit negotiation notes to the approved flexibility, forbid salary-history use, and require the approver's sign-off for any counter.

issues.quote: [Full-time, Exempt]
issues.problem: The default assumes US FLSA exempt status and a US legal frame. Other countries have different mandatory written terms (the UK s.1 statement of particulars, Germany's Nachweisgesetz).
issues.fix: Ask for the jurisdiction, take the employment classification from an approved source, and flag non-US mandatory terms for the people lead.

issues.quote: Draft an offer letter with comp details and terms.
issues.problem: It triggers on the same requests as Harper's candidate-offer-draft and Sofia's job-offer-and-close-plan, so loading it alongside them creates a routing conflict.
issues.fix: Drop it and merge the total-comp table into candidate-offer-draft.

scenarios.prompt: Draft an offer for Priya: Senior Backend Engineer, L5, $180k base, 0.1% options with 4-year vesting and a 1-year cliff, $15k sign-on, start Nov 3, reports to Alex, remote US.
scenarios.why: The template gets filled in, but the letter body is just '[Complete offer letter text]', so the model improvises. It will likely leave out contingencies (background check, I-9), at-will wording, an offer expiry and a signature block. 'Total First-Year Comp' tempts the model to put a dollar value on the options. The draft is not marked as awaiting approval, and 'Exempt' is assumed rather than checked.

scenarios.prompt: Candidate wants 20% over our range and has a competing offer. We don't know the Berlin band yet. Draft the offer and tell the hiring manager how to negotiate.
scenarios.why: 'I'll help you think through them' plus the 'Comp band context' notes push the model to estimate a Berlin band and suggest a counter figure. That breaks Harper's rule against compensation decisions and Sofia's rule against estimating a band. There is no guard against using current pay or salary history, no approval ladder for going over the range, and no handling of German written-terms requirements (Nachweisgesetz, probation, notice). The US-centric 'Full-time, Exempt' and at-will framing would carry into a Berlin letter.

14:accounts-receivable-follow-up.summary: Builds a cutoff-dated AR aging from invoice, payment and bank exports with bundled scripts. It flags unapplied cash and bank-coverage gaps before any chase, then drafts one next-stage reminder or statement per customer, with hash-bound owner approval, logging and optional scheduling.
strengths: Looks for unapplied cash before any chase (bank matching by invoice number, amount and name, plus undeposited funds and unapplied credits). Chasing a customer who has already paid is the costliest collections error.
BANK_COVERAGE_GAP detection holds every chase until the owner uploads a newer bank export or confirms, in words recorded verbatim, that nothing arrived after the bank end date.
Deterministic scripts with self-tests: exact-decimal aging, refusal of duplicate invoice rows, near-match of unknown invoice numbers, accent-folded name matching, and ambiguous-credit marking.

Hash-bound approval log with a closed list of answers that count as yes. 'I will send it myself' is never logged as approval to send. The recipient must equal the billing contact on file. The send path uses find, describe, validate_only, then send.
UK statutory interest is opt-in only, with four stated conditions. The figures are correct (8% plus the reference rate, and fixed sums of £40, £70 and £100). A base rate is never taken from memory.
The worked example ships with fixtures and a 'what a wrong answer would look like' list, and the reminder templates are calm and threat-free.
Harness-native: run_capability and skill: ids, the ~/skills/<slug> script paths, the durable ~/workspace state, and fallbacks for a missing Python, mail tool or state volume.
missing: An account-level view: total exposure per customer, and one consolidated reminder per customer
Summary KPIs for the owner: total overdue, percentage over 60 days, DSO or CEI, and change since the last review
A check that the invoice was received, approved and has a PO or portal submission before the second reminder
Payment instructions or a pay link in every reminder, with the invoice attached
A recommendation to the owner on credit hold or stop-supply thresholds, which the owner decides
Payment-plan proposal and letter-before-claim handoff templates, prepared for the owner or counsel
A statutory-interest pointer for jurisdictions outside the UK (for example the EU Late Payment Directive), or an explicit 'UK only' note in the description
A list of write-off or bad-debt candidates for the accountant

issues.quote: Payments after the cutoff are ignored
issues.problem: A payment or bank credit dated after the cutoff is excluded from the aging, which is right for an as-at report. It also does not stop the chase: ar_aging still proposes a reminder for an invoice fully paid after the cutoff (I reproduced this), and find_unapplied.py treats that invoice as paid, so nothing else flags it. For month-end cutoffs, this drafts chasers to customers who have already paid.
issues.fix: Keep the aging as at the cutoff, but move any invoice with a receipt dated after the cutoff (payments file or bank) to status unconfirmed with a note, and hold next_stage. Add a checklist line: 'no receipt since the cutoff for any invoice being chased'.

issues.quote: dispute, remittance or promise, and log them.
issues.problem: The mailbox evidence step comes after aging, and there is no instruction to rerun the aging. ar_aging reads promised_date only from contact-log rows whose approval_state is approved or sent, so a logged customer reply with a promise is ignored. I reproduced this: the invoice still got 'second reminder'.
issues.fix: Move the evidence check before aging. Define how to log a customer-reply row (for example, stage 'customer reply' with approval_state 'n/a') and make ar_aging take the latest promised_date from any row. Say to rerun aging after new disputes or promises are logged.

issues.quote: Each draft states the invoice number, issue and due dates, open balance,
issues.problem: Reminders and statements carry no payment instructions, no invoice copy and no check that the customer received and approved the invoice (PO, AP portal). In B2B these are the most common reasons an invoice goes unpaid, and a senior credit controller includes them in every reminder.
issues.fix: Add payment details or a pay link (from intake), attach the invoice PDF, and in the first reminder ask whether the invoice reached AP and whether a PO is needed.

issues.quote: contact log so no stage repeats: first reminder → second reminder → statement
issues.problem: Stages and templates are per invoice, so a customer with three overdue invoices gets three separate reminders at different stages. Credit control is normally run at account level.
issues.fix: Make one draft per customer that lists every chaseable invoice, and set the stage by the most advanced invoice. This also satisfies 'one customer per draft'.

issues.quote: one customer only; it leaves off disputed, unconfirmed and promised items) → owner call.
issues.problem: render_statement always prints the banner 'DRAFT for approval by <approver>. Not sent.' The approved hash covers that file, and sends must be byte for byte, so a statement sent through the mail tool reaches the customer with the banner. Leaving out disputed items and account credits also means the document is not a true statement of account.
issues.fix: Hash and approve a clean final render, showing the banner only in the preview. List disputed items marked 'in query' and include unallocated credits, rather than silently leaving them off.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: Upload; normalised with `scripts/normalize_export.py`
issues.problem: The body never says that normalize_export needs an owner-confirmed --date-format (dd/mm versus mm/dd). When that is missing, the script's error tells the model to run profile_sources.py, which this package does not ship.
issues.fix: Add an explicit normalise step: detect the date format, ask the owner if it is ambiguous, and point to bookkeeping-getting-started (loaded via run_capability) for profile_sources.py, or drop that reference.

issues.quote: `find_unapplied.py` ran before any draft, or its absence is stated.
issues.problem: With no bank export at all, the procedure has no decision point. The coverage-gap question in step 2 only fires when a bank export exists but ends early, so saying 'its absence is stated' lets chases go ahead without the bank check.
issues.fix: Treat 'no bank export' as a coverage gap and ask the same question with the same options, and hold drafts until it is answered.

issues.quote: wrote beside it (`unapplied.coverage.json`); while the bank export ends before
issues.problem: SKILL.md carries script internals (the sidecar file, exit codes, match-strength labels) and an inline example that repeats the walkthrough. This inflates the body the model reads on every load.
issues.fix: Move the script mechanics into references/aging-and-terms.md and shorten the Example section to a 3-line pointer to the walkthrough.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our invoice export and payments report from Xero as of today 5pm, plus the business bank CSV to today. Who hasn't paid us, and can you draft reminders for anything overdue?
scenarios.why: The inputs table names every file and column (templates/invoice-export.csv). The pre-flight states the cutoff. Step 2 runs find_unapplied.py first, so a customer who paid but whose payment was never applied to the invoice goes to status unconfirmed. Step 3 ages the ledger by default buckets with exact decimal, step 4 groups the queue, and step 6 drafts only the next stage from the contact log. Step 8 asks one ask_question per draft and logs the answer against the draft's hash. I reran the bundled fixture end to end and got the walkthrough's table exactly. The one friction point is that the model must map Xero's column names to the template columns by hand.

scenarios.prompt: For the March month-end pack, run the aged debtors as at 31 March and draft chasers for anything past due. The payments export and bank CSV run through today (8 April). Also Kestrel emailed on the 2nd saying they'd pay on the 12th.
scenarios.why: The aging as at the cutoff is correct. But ar_aging.py drops payments dated after the cutoff and still sets next_stage to a reminder: I added a full INV-1039 payment dated after the cutoff and got 'second reminder', with only an 'ignored payment' line on stderr. find_unapplied.py treats the same invoice as paid, so nothing else flags it. The Kestrel promise found in step 5 is logged after aging, and ar_aging reads promised_date only from contact-log rows marked approved or sent. A logged 'customer reply' row therefore still produced 'second reminder'. The guardrail 'never chase ... a promised date still to come' may save a careful model, but the procedure and the script output push toward drafting both chasers.

better: Main v1 never checks for money that already arrived. v2 runs find_unapplied.py against the bank before any chase and adds the bank-coverage-gap hold.
v1 computes days past due by hand. v2 has scripts with self-tests for aging, statements, UK interest and approvals, and labels hand-computed figures when Python is unavailable.
v1 has no templates. v2 ships staged reminder templates, a dispute acknowledgement, an HTML statement of account, and contact-log and dispute-log CSV templates.
v1 says the owner approves but gives no mechanism. v2 adds an ask_question card with fixed options, hash-bound approval logging, a recipient check and a mail-tool send path using validate_only.
The trigger surface grows from 5 generic phrases to 10 user-voiced triggers and a 'Do not use for' list that names sibling skills.
A fixture-backed worked example, a pre-drafting checklist, and an opt-in follow-up and weekly routine with a prompt that forbids sending.
worse: The body is nearly 4x longer and exposes script internals, which costs context on every load.
It depends on the shared bookkeeping state folder and intake.json from bookkeeping-getting-started, so there are more failure points than v1's self-contained text.
Script output now drives the queue. Post-cutoff payments and promises logged on non-approved rows fall through, whereas v1's plain instruction left the model to reason about all known evidence.
The worked example and extras lean UK and GBP, which v1 did not.

16:role-intake-and-scorecard.job: scope role and agree hiring scorecard
16:role-intake-and-scorecard.summary: Turns a hiring manager's ask into a versioned role scorecard file. It holds 3-6 must-haves (M1..Mn), each with an evidence method, plus a proxy-free fairness pass, a benchmark person (B1..Bn), a link-checked target-company CSV, title variants and a staged hiring plan. A stdlib linter checks it and stamps HM approval with the HM's quoted words.
strengths: Every must-have must carry an evidence_method, an agree_test and what_fails_without_it. That turns the three-part test (objective, non-comparative, job-relevant) into something the loop can actually score.
The proxy rewrite table is concrete (digital native, native speaker, culture fit, postcode, gaps, photo) and is enforced by a working linter. I tested it: the example passes with 0 errors.
Approval is stamped only with the HM's quoted words. --revise keeps the prior version and tells the owner which downstream work used the old bar.
Target companies must have a fetched link (ok/blocked/dead), and anything from memory without a link is dropped. This removes invented companies.

The platform integration is accurate. I verified that read_skill materialises the package at ~/skills/<slug>, that ~/workspace is durable, and that write_workspace_file source_path, the find_capability/describe/run chain, Granola via MCP with a paste fallback, and Linear writes on a yes all exist.
The worked example handles a realistic biased-HM case and a rescope, and it shows the undefended '5+ years' being cut.
missing: Level, scope and title-band agreement
Headcount and budget approval confirmation (FACT or UNKNOWN)
Selling points and candidate value proposition captured from the HM
HM commitments: feedback SLA and weekly interview slots
Feasibility and trade-off discussion (which must-have to relax if the slate is thin)
Calibration on 3-5 sample profiles with the HM beyond a single benchmark person
A path for frontline, hourly or licensed roles without public work evidence
Internal candidates and internal posting consideration

issues.quote: keep a proxy; every other term is rewritten or cut. Counts are not ages:
issues.problem: The linter raises ERROR on lawful requirements and gives no override. Statutory age minimums ('must be over 21' to serve alcohol, 'be over 18' to drive a forklift), 'man-in-the-middle' in a security role, and 'church' for a faith-based employer all fail, and lint_ok is limited to family, health and photo terms. Since the step says fix every ERROR, a legitimate bar cannot be saved.
issues.fix: Add an 'age_minimum' category that allows lint_ok with a cited legal basis (licence or statute) and still blocks upper age limits. Make the sex/gender regex skip common technical compounds, and let religion terms be overridden with a 'religious organisation exemption, counsel confirmed' note.

issues.quote: If it warns that the approver is not the header's `hiring_manager`, stop
issues.problem: scorecard_check.py --approve writes status: approved before it prints the approver-mismatch warning, so 'stop and confirm' comes after the file already reads approved. I reproduced this: 'Someone Else' was stamped as approver. job-description-drafting and sourcing treat 'approved' as the go signal.
issues.fix: Make --approve refuse, exiting 1 with the status unchanged, when the approver does not match hiring_manager unless --as-owner is passed. Update step 10 to match.

issues.problem: Intake skips things a senior recruiter always settles in the sitting: level and scope (IC level or title band), whether headcount and budget are approved, the selling points (why a strong person would take this job, which postings and outreach need), a feasibility and trade-off talk, and HM commitments (feedback SLA, interview availability).
issues.fix: Add a step between 3 and 4 and matching template fields: level, headcount_approved (FACT/UNKNOWN), why_join (2-3 selling points in the HM's words), hm_commitments (feedback within N hours, slots per week). Add a one-line feasibility note that hands off to candidate-sourcing-strategy for the market read.

issues.quote: Role in NYC, Illinois, California, Colorado, the EU or the UK?
issues.problem: The jurisdiction flag list is incomplete for 2026.
