It omits other US pay-transparency jurisdictions (New York State, Washington, Massachusetts, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey and others) and the EU Pay Transparency Directive, whose transposition deadline was June 2026 (pay range before interview, no pay-history questions). An EU or Washington role gets no posting-law flag.
issues.fix: Use a dated list of pay-transparency and AI-in-hiring jurisdictions, or keep the existing list and also say that pay-transparency posting rules exist in many other US states and in the EU Pay Transparency Directive, so the owner should confirm with counsel.

issues.quote: is confirmable from public work or a structured interview question, so
issues.problem: The model of evidence and sourcing (public work, engineering blogs, dark-matter titles, 10-20 fetched target companies) fits knowledge-work roles. Frontline, hourly and licensed roles have no public work, and inbound-only searches do not need a target map. There is no decision point to scale the map down or skip it.
issues.fix: Add a decision: for roles with no public-work trail or no outbound sourcing, use work samples, licence checks or structured screen questions as evidence methods, and mark target companies and title variants 'not needed (inbound only)'.

issues.quote: owner. The lexicon sometimes hits a plain job word: a preschool bar that
issues.problem: Step 9 inlines the linter's override mechanics (term list, child-line syntax, count-versus-age rule). The body gets longer and duplicates the script docstring and the checklist, which hurts efficiency.
issues.fix: Move the lint_ok mechanics into a short references/linter.md and leave one line in step 9: 'Fix every ERROR; for WARNs and job-word overrides see references/linter.md.'

issues.quote: product), 10 to 20 named examples (default — confirm with the owner).
issues.problem: Fetching 10-20 company sites during the sitting conflicts with the persona's 'within a minute'. The output contract also puts the target map in chat ahead of the hiring plan, so the plan waits on research.
issues.fix: Show outcomes, bar and plan first. Run the target map as a follow-up turn, or start with 5 fetched companies and offer to extend.

scenarios.prompt: Here are my notes from the intake call with Priya (HM) for a Senior Product Designer on our mobile app. Turn this into the bar and a hiring plan.
scenarios.why: Steps 2-4 quote Priya's sentences as FACT and write 3-6 must-haves, each with an evidence method, agree_test and what_fails_without_it. Step 7's evidence table routes designers to portfolios and case studies. Step 8 maps each must-have to one stage, and step 9 validates and delivers the file. A senior recruiter would accept the result.

scenarios.prompt: Ops wants a weekend shift supervisor for our Ohio warehouse: must be over 18 to run the forklift, lift 50 lbs, no job hoppers, lives within 20 miles. The HM is off this week, so just draft it.
scenarios.why: The 'No hiring manager to hand' decision correctly gives draft-pending-calibration. Step 5 rewrites the commute radius and the lift requirement, and job-hopping becomes an interviewer note. But scorecard_check.py raises ERROR on 'be over 18' (a lawful FLSA minimum), the SKILL says 'every other term is rewritten or cut', and lint_ok cannot clear it. Step 7's public-work evidence, dark-matter titles and target-company fetches also have no path for hourly or frontline roles.

better: The inputs table has explicit fallbacks, and step 1 looks for an existing scorecard so a rescope becomes a versioned revision instead of an overwrite.
Each must-have now names its evidence method, agree_test and what_fails_without_it (main had only 'confirmable').
The fairness pass gains a rewrite reference, location written as work terms, accommodation phrasing for physical demands, and a working proxy linter.
HM approval is stamped with a quote. Version history (--revise) and a downstream-impact notice are added.
Target companies are verified by fetching each site and recorded in a CSV, and boundaries are kept on the list so sourcing skips them deliberately.
It adds an output contract, a template, a quality self-check, a worked hard-case example, dated sources and Granola/Drive/Linear integration with paste fallbacks.
worse: It is more than twice as long (95 to 210 lines), with linter mechanics and citation brackets in the body.
The new linter can block lawful requirements (age minimums, 'church', 'man-in-the-middle') and give no override, where main relied on judgement.
--approve can mark a scorecard approved by someone other than the HM before the model is told to stop.

16:sofia-getting-started.job: onboard owner and set up hiring desk
16:sofia-getting-started.summary: First-session onboarding for Sofia. It detects returning owners from memory and a durable preferences file, reports connected tools without probing, gets the role and a draft scorecard on screen first, creates ~/workspace/hiring with tracker CSVs, and collects up to 21 skippable preferences one at a time through a validating prefs.py. It keeps do-not-contact names only in dnc.csv, offers routines one yes at a time, and closes with a session summary.
strengths: Returning-owner detection reads both memory and the durable file (the file wins) and skips the questions, which matches the persona's 'don't rerun intake'.
The connection check uses find_capability's connected state and never calls run_capability, which would raise sign-in cards. I verified this against the platform tools.

prefs.py is a real guardrail: it refuses unknown keys so candidate data cannot land in prefs, rejects fixed-offset zones like EST in favour of IANA city zones, and keeps DNC names separate, deduplicated and case-folded. I tested all of this in a sandbox copy.
Routine setup is careful: it lists routines first to avoid duplicates, requires the timezone, takes one yes per routine, handles approval_required and records routines_on.
The hard-case example (a pregnancy remark, 'turn everything on', a postcode filter) models the right refusals without repeating the protected detail.

The preference bank covers operating parameters a senior recruiting-ops lead would set: offer approval chain, scorecard SLA, stalled bar, retention and talent-pool notice, background-check owner (FCRA), and candidate AI-use policy.
missing: A route for a first input that is a pipeline export, resumes, or a headcount goal instead of a single role
Handling for multi-location or multi-timezone teams (one owner zone versus a candidate or panel zone per role)
A current EU pay-transparency flag and a broader list of US pay-transparency states
Priority tiers in the preference bank (ask now versus ask when needed)
A short statement of Sofia's approval model at first meeting (drafts only; nothing sends without a yes), which sets expectations early

issues.quote: stay out unless they are evidence about the job; you neither store them nor
issues.problem: This exception contradicts the persona's absolute rule that age, family, health and similar traits are never recorded or inferred. A model could store a health or family remark it judges 'job-related'.
issues.fix: Replace it with: 'Remarks on age, family, health, pregnancy or background are never stored, repeated or used. If one seems relevant to the job, restate the job requirement instead (for example "can travel two weeks a quarter") and flag legal questions to counsel.'

issues.quote: As soon as you have one, load `role-intake-and-scorecard` and put the draft
issues.problem: Step 4 runs role-intake, whose step 9 saves to ~/workspace/hiring/roles/<slug>/, before step 5 creates the hiring folder. The skill also applies 'draft pending calibration' to every first-session bar, while role-intake reserves the hyphenated status draft-pending-calibration for when no HM is available.
issues.fix: Run init_hiring_folder.sh silently before step 4, since it is idempotent and fast. Tell role-intake to set status 'draft' when the HM is known and reachable, and 'draft-pending-calibration' only when they are not.

issues.section: Inputs and where they come from
issues.quote: The role (JD, link, title plus a line about the team)
issues.problem: Main accepted whatever arrived first: a pipeline export, a stack of resumes, or a goal like 'two engineers by March'. The rebuild's inputs and step 4 are role-only and never say where a pipeline export or a batch of resumes goes, even though step 11 calls those work.
issues.fix: Add a decision: a pipeline or ATS export goes to interview-coordination (load into tracker/candidates.csv) and hiring-pipeline-analytics; resumes go to resume-screening after a one-line bar via role-intake; a headcount goal becomes one role-intake per role.

issues.quote: Role in NYC, Illinois, California, Colorado, the EU or the UK (from
issues.problem: The jurisdiction flags (and references/jurisdiction-flags.md) omit the EU Pay Transparency Directive (transposition due June 2026), other US pay-transparency states (NY State, WA, MA, MD, MN, NJ and others), and works-council rules on screening tools in Germany and France. The worked example is an EU hire and gets only the AI Act line.
issues.fix: Add the EU pay-transparency line (pay range before interview, no pay-history questions) and a catch-all 'pay-transparency posting laws in many other US states', each ending 'confirm with counsel'. Date the table.

issues.quote: Run step 5 only if `~/workspace/hiring/` is missing.
issues.problem: The returning-owner branch says 'skip to step 11' and then adds a conditional step 5, which is hard to follow. prefs.py 'missing' also lists only plain keys, so the per-role hiring_manager, panel and loop_shape keys never show up as gaps for a returning owner.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'Returning owner: ensure the folder exists (run init if missing), then go to step 11.' Make prefs.py missing report role keys for every role in roles_open.

issues.quote: Collect the rest one at a time, each skippable, never as a form.
issues.problem: The linked bank has 21 questions, including policy items (retention, AI-use policy, background-check owner, Linear team) that no first-session task needs. Step 11 lets the model stop early, but nothing prioritises which 4-5 questions matter now.
issues.fix: Mark questions 1-4 (HM, timezone, interview hours, pipeline source) as first-session. Mark the rest 'ask when a skill needs it' and have each owning skill ask its own keys.

issues.quote: help me start a search
issues.problem: This trigger overlaps role-intake-and-scorecard ('kick off a new req') and candidate-sourcing-strategy, so a known owner saying it could load onboarding again instead of the intended skill.
issues.fix: Drop it, or replace it with an onboarding-specific phrase such as 'I'm new here, set up hiring'.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Sofia, we're hiring our first Customer Success Manager. Here's a rough JD. Where do we start?
scenarios.why: Step 1 finds no prefs and treats this as a first run. Step 2 gives a one-line connected report, and steps 3-4 hand the pasted JD to role-intake-and-scorecard so a draft bar is on screen before any question. Step 5 creates the folder and records roles_open. Steps 6-10 ask skippable questions one at a time, offer the connector pick-list and starter menu, and describe routines singly, ending with the session summary.

scenarios.prompt: I've got ~40 resumes in a Drive folder for two roles (no JDs yet), our ATS is Ashby, the team is split Berlin/NYC, and just turn on the daily brief at 8.
scenarios.why: The skill handles the missing Drive connection (pick-list, then paste or upload), the Ashby gap (export), and the bundled routine request ('one yes per routine'; the timezone must be saved first). It flags NYC AEDT and the EU AI Act. But the Inputs table and step 4 insist on the role first and give no route for resumes-first or pipeline-first owners. prefs.py stores one timezone, with no guidance for a split team. The EU flag omits the Pay Transparency Directive and German works-council co-determination on screening tools.

better: Returning-owner detection now checks memory, the durable preferences file and existing scorecards before any question.
The connection check is concrete (find_capability connected state, no probing), with a one-line report format.
A durable ~/workspace/hiring folder is created by an idempotent init script, with fixed tracker headers the sibling skills share.
prefs.py validates timezones, hours and counts, refuses unknown keys so candidate data cannot enter prefs, and isolates DNC names.
Routine setup lists existing routines first, requires the timezone, takes one yes per routine and handles approval_required, following a reference that mirrors the persona's crons.
It adds jurisdiction flags, policy questions (retention, background checks, AI use), an output contract, a session-summary template, a checklist and a worked hard case.
worse: It is longer and heavier (142 to 197 lines), and the preference bank grows to 21 questions with no priority tiers.
Inputs narrow to 'the role first'. Main's acceptance of a pipeline export, resumes or a hiring goal as the first thing is gone.
A step-order dependency is introduced: role-intake runs before the hiring folder exists, and the status label disagrees with role-intake's.
The 'unless they are evidence about the job' loophole is carried over unchanged, and still conflicts with the persona.

anika-getting-started.job: onboard new user and capture preferences
anika-getting-started.summary: First-session onboarding for Anika: a short self-introduction, routing the user's first item to the matching skill, checking which integrations are connected, collecting partnership preferences into memory, and offering the six routines and a starter menu.
strengths: Work comes first: it starts the matching skill as soon as a name or goal appears and does not hold work behind questions.
Stores the timezone before offering any routine, and every routine stays off until the user says yes. This matches the six routines in anika.yml.
Asks for missing sources one at a time and never re-asks for a linked integration.
Fallbacks are clear for no connections, no partner and no goal.
missing: Priority rule when the user arrives with a dated, urgent item
Defined preference record schema that other skills read
Full routing table or pointer to the persona's routing
Named tools to use (memory_store, connect_integration, schedule_routine)
Handoff note for direct-sales or support asks the user may raise first

issues.section: Offer the routines in plain words
issues.quote: Offer the routines in plain words
issues.problem: The whole routines section (heading and paragraph) is duplicated word for word at lines 79-97. That wastes tokens and invites the model to offer the routines twice.
issues.fix: Delete the second copy of the section.

issues.section: Check what is connected, then ask for the rest one at a time
issues.quote: Then collect the rest singly, each marked skippable, saving every answer
issues.problem: The skill asks for seven preferences one at a time, plus an integration pick-list, a routines offer and a starter menu, with no cap and no priority order. That contradicts 'not to interview them' and can bury an urgent first task.
issues.fix: Rank the preferences (timezone and active partner list first), cap them at two or three this session, defer the rest to when a skill needs them, and never ask while the first draft is still pending.

issues.quote: Close with a single pick-list, one short clause each: define the partner
issues.problem: A starter menu at the close conflicts with the instruction to have already started the first real motion, and the model is not told when to skip it.
issues.fix: Show the menu only when no motion started in this session; otherwise close with the one next step on the draft in progress.

issues.quote: The started first draft, the saved preferences, and the answered menu.
issues.problem: The deliverable is vague. There is no defined preference record (field names or format) that sibling skills can reliably read back.
issues.fix: Define a named preferences memory record with its fields (timezone, fiscal year, MDF year, plan location, ICP pointer, partner list, tiers, marketplace vehicles, review rhythm) and say that sibling skills read it.

issues.section: Start the first real motion at once
issues.quote: Route by what they hand you. A new motion goes to the partner ICP. A list
issues.problem: The routing covers 12 of Anika's 34 skills. Delivery, academies, marketplace, GSI governance, data and R&D, category creation and councils are left to the persona, so the first session can misroute.
issues.fix: Either point to the persona's full routing or add a compact route table covering all skills.

issues.section: Check what is connected, then ask for the rest one at a time
issues.quote: Granola, to pull notes from recorded partner calls.
issues.problem: Granola is not an AutoGPT block and is only reachable if the user has connected an MCP server, so the offer may be impossible to fulfil.
issues.fix: Say 'Granola or any call-notes tool via MCP, or paste the transcript', or drop it.

issues.section: Open with one or two sentences, then move
issues.quote: Say who you are and the span you run in one or two sentences: a
issues.problem: The introduction it asks for is a 12-line run-on list of every capability, which defeats 'one or two sentences' and delays the work.
issues.fix: Give one example sentence naming three or four core motions and cut the rest of the list.

scenarios.prompt: Hi Anika, I run partnerships at a 60-person SaaS. We have about 12 resellers and I want to get co-selling working properly.
scenarios.why: 'Start the first real motion at once' sends the stalled or weak joint motion to the co-sell cadence. After that it checks connections and collects preferences one at a time. A capable model would start the co-sell prep and ask for the partner list or CRM, which is the right first minute.

scenarios.prompt: Just connected HubSpot. I own our AWS Marketplace listing and two GSI alliances, the Accenture QBR is Thursday, I'm in Singapore but our fiscal year runs on US time, and I don't have a partner ICP.
scenarios.why: The routing does send 'a review on the calendar' to QBR prep. Marketplace and GSI governance are missing from the skill's routing list, so it has to fall back on the persona. Nothing tells it to put the Thursday QBR ahead of the seven preference questions, the integration pick-list and the closing starter menu. Because of the duplicated 'Offer the routines' section, the model may offer the routines twice. The user gets over-interviewed, which the skill itself warns against.

assure-partner-led-delivery.summary: Runs a weekly graded book of partner-delivered client engagements, using peer-to-peer escalation, restaff lines, time-based rescue and save-or-exit triggers, and produces a quarterly per-partner delivery-quality read that feeds renewals.
strengths: Every grade needs a line of evidence, and ungraded rows stay UNKNOWN.
It uses peer-to-peer escalation, with a peer map built before going executive.
Clear time-based triggers: an executive draft after two red weeks, the save-or-exit call after three.
It closes the loop by feeding delivery quality into the renewal and commercial decision.
It has an approval gate on staffing changes, escalations and client-facing messages.
missing: Red/yellow/green grading rubric with thresholds
SOW or subcontract accountability and remedies (credits, change orders)
Severity-based immediate escalation
Client communication plan and CS/account-owner handoff
Budget burn and margin tracking per engagement
A reusable engagement-book template (columns) as a template file

issues.quote: staffed team, and a red/yellow/green delivery grade with one line of
issues.problem: There is no definition of red, yellow or green (schedule slip, budget burn, open blockers, client sentiment), so grades are arbitrary and will not compare across weeks or partners.
issues.fix: Add a grading rubric, for example: green means on plan; yellow means a milestone at risk inside 14 days, burn over 10 percent of plan, or a client concern logged; red means a milestone missed, a staffing gap past its date, or an executive complaint.

issues.quote: A staffing gap gets a dated restaff line with an owner. Anything red two
issues.problem: Escalation is purely time-based. A go-live inside a week or an executive-level client complaint should escalate immediately, not after two red weeks.
issues.fix: Add a severity override: go-live or a contractual milestone inside 14 days, or a client-executive escalation, triggers the escalation draft the same day.

issues.quote: Name the failure mode — staffing, skill, scope, or client-side — pick one
issues.problem: The rescue plan ignores the contract: the SOW or subcontract, who is prime, SLA credits, change orders and remedies. That leaves the owner without leverage and risks promises the contract does not support.
issues.fix: Add a step that reads the SOW or subcontract, names who is accountable to the client, lists the available remedies and change-order path, and routes any credit or penalty to the owner and Legal.

issues.quote: in-flight engagement book (partner, client, scope, dates, staffing), the
issues.problem: The inputs omit the contract and SOW, the budget or effort baseline and the client-side owner, all of which the rescue and grading need.
issues.fix: Add the SOW or subcontract, the budget or hours baseline, and the client's named owner to the starting inputs.

issues.quote: A per-partner delivery-quality read: on-time rate, escalation count,
issues.problem: The quality read is thin. It misses budget variance or margin, time-to-staff, certified-staff ratio, rework or defects, and reference-ability.
issues.fix: Extend the metrics and label each one with its window and system of record.

issues.quote: No staffing change, escalation, or client-facing message goes out without
issues.problem: Client communication is gated but never planned, and there is no handoff to the customer-success or account owner who holds the client relationship.
issues.fix: Add a client-communication draft step and a named handoff to the account or success owner (consult_teammate).

issues.quote: A third straight red week triggers the save-or-exit call with its
issues.problem: It duplicates the save-or-exit logic in handle-partner-conflict-and-churn and manage-partner-renewals-and-exits instead of routing to them.
issues.fix: Route the save-or-exit decision to handle-partner-conflict-and-churn, carrying the delivery evidence.

scenarios.prompt: Our SI partners are running 14 implementations for us. Here's the tracker export, so run this week's delivery review and tell me what needs my push.
scenarios.why: 'Own the book' builds one row per engagement with a graded red/yellow/green and one line of evidence, with UNKNOWN when there is no evidence. 'Run the weekly delivery review' sorts most-at-risk first and assigns one decision each, plus restaff lines and escalation drafts. A capable model will invent reasonable red/yellow/green thresholds, but results may vary between runs.

scenarios.prompt: The client's CIO just emailed our CEO that next week's partner-led go-live will slip. The partner says the client never gave them data access. We don't have a tracker, and the SOW makes the partner prime.
scenarios.why: The fallback builds the book from pasted notes marked INFERENCE, and 'Rescue' names the failure mode as client-side and picks a save motion. However, the escalation rule waits for 'red two weeks running' even though go-live is seven days out. Nothing covers SOW or prime accountability, a client communication plan, or a handoff to the customer-success owner, so the executive-visible response is under-specified.

build-data-and-r-d-alliances.job: structure data licensing and research alliances
build-data-and-r-d-alliances.summary: Scopes a data or research alliance, drafts a generic terms outline routed to Legal, keeps a red/yellow/green compliance tracker, and runs a quarterly renew/expand/exit read.
strengths: An absolute Legal gate: every clause routes to Legal before it leaves.
Evaluation access is dated and has a conversion path to a licence, so nothing stays open-ended.
A per-alliance compliance tracker with key dates (expiry, review, publication windows).
The quarterly produce-or-exit review ties alliances to papers, products or revenue.
missing: Personal-data classification and privacy/Legal gate
AI training and derivative-model rights
Background vs foreground IP and results ownership
Publication review/delay window and tech-transfer office process
Instrument selection (DUA, MTA, SRA, evaluation, commercial licence)
Data-licence pricing approach routed to Finance
Clause checklist or term-sheet template file

issues.quote: Licence scope and fees, data-sharing rights, publication and IP
issues.problem: The terms outline is generic. It omits model-training and derivative-work rights, background versus foreground IP, residuals, deletion or return on termination, audit rights, attribution and warranty limits on data quality.
issues.fix: Add a references/data-rd-clause-checklist.md covering these clauses and requiring each to be answered or marked UNKNOWN.

issues.quote: intellectual property (IP) and compliance constraints.
issues.problem: There is no personal-data gate: consent and provenance chain, de-identification and re-identification risk, GDPR/HIPAA/CCPA lawful basis, data use agreements, cross-border transfer and export controls. That is the main legal risk in a data alliance.
issues.fix: Add a first step that classifies the data (personal or sensitive or not, source contracts, jurisdictions) and stops for Legal or Privacy when personal data or third-party-restricted data is involved.

issues.problem: Academic collaboration mechanics are missing: sponsored research versus collaboration agreements, the tech-transfer office, publication review and delay windows for patent filing, indirect-cost rates, student and postdoc IP, and federal-funding obligations.
issues.fix: Add an academic branch with these items and name the university's tech-transfer office as the counterparty process owner.

issues.quote: Define the asset — a dataset, a model, a protocol, physical samples — the
issues.problem: Nothing helps the model pick the instrument (evaluation licence, data use agreement, MTA, sponsored research agreement, joint development, commercial licence), so the model has to guess the agreement type.
issues.fix: Add a short decision table mapping asset and purpose to agreement type.

issues.quote: Anything yellow gets a dated cure line with an owner.
issues.problem: The compliance grade has no criteria, and red is never handled (for example, a breach, overdue deletion or unauthorised publication).
issues.fix: Define red, yellow and green, and add a red path: immediate owner and Legal notice plus a draft notice-of-breach for approval.

issues.quote: Every clause routes to Legal before it leaves. There are no exceptions to
issues.problem: Fees are routed only to Legal, with no Finance involvement, pricing model (flat, per-record, royalty, revenue share) or handoff to model-the-partnership-commercials. The data-licence fee gate from the persona is not restated here.
issues.fix: Route fees to Finance and the commercials skill, and state that fees and exclusivity need the owner's explicit yes.

issues.quote: the renew, expand, or exit call per alliance with its evidence.
issues.problem: The exit decision is not linked to data-return or deletion obligations, or to manage-partner-renewals-and-exits.
issues.fix: Add an exit checklist (data return or destruction certificate, survival clauses, publication rights after term) and route to the renewals skill.

scenarios.prompt: A university lab wants to use our anonymised product-usage dataset for a research paper. Draft the terms and tell me what to watch.
scenarios.why: 'Scope the alliance' defines the asset and permitted uses, 'Draft the terms spine' lists licence, sharing, publication and IP, and everything routes to Legal. There is no prompt to check re-identification risk, publication review and delay rights, ownership of results, the tech-transfer office or indirect costs, so the draft is generic rather than senior-grade.

scenarios.prompt: An AI startup wants to train its model on our customer support transcripts. We only have an old mutual NDA, many customers are in the EU, and they're asking for exclusivity at a fee they named.
scenarios.why: The skill never raises whether the customer contracts and privacy law even allow licensing personal data. It has nothing on GDPR lawful basis or cross-border transfer, and no model-training or derivative-model rights, output ownership, or deletion on termination. The exclusivity and fee gates live only in the persona. A model following the skill would draft a licence spine for data it probably cannot license.

build-partner-academies-at-scale.job: design partner academy and certification program
build-partner-academies-at-scale.summary: Designs a role-based partner academy with a certification ladder, runs certification operations tied to business impact, stands up train-the-trainer, and makes evidence-backed readiness calls with a 1-to-5 rubric.
strengths: It treats a missing refresh date as the failure mode to design out, and every path has an owner and a refresh SLA.
Measures academy success against partner revenue, retention and delivery quality, not completions alone.
The train-the-trainer bar has teeth: trainers who miss re-certify and do not scale.
Readiness calls are rubric-scored and evidence-backed before a team takes client work.
missing: Single source of truth for certification bars across sibling skills
Prioritisation and localisation decisions
Diagnostic method for low pass rates
Exam integrity and credential verification
Academy budget and economics
Rubric templates shipped in the package
Learner PII and exam-data privacy note

issues.quote: name their outcomes, and a certification ladder with pass bars and a
issues.problem: Certification is specified in three sibling skills (onboard-and-enable-partners sets Foundation 80/Pro 85/Expert 90, design-the-partner-program sets 60/30-day renewal reminders), and this one leaves the bars unstated. None of them says which is the source of truth.
issues.fix: Make this skill own the certification ladder with explicit default bars, and have the onboarding and program skills point here.

issues.quote: Start from the learner population (roles, count, geographies), the
issues.problem: There is no sequencing or build decision: which roles, partners or regions go first, build versus buy content, cohort versus self-paced, and localisation and translation QA for geographies.
issues.fix: Add a prioritisation step (revenue-weighted partner and role order) and a delivery-format and localisation decision.

issues.quote: Read throughput and pass rates monthly, tied to business impact — partner
issues.problem: It asks for business-impact linkage but gives no method, so a model may claim certification caused revenue. It also has no diagnostic for a failing path.
issues.fix: Specify a certified-versus-uncertified cohort comparison over the same window, label the results as correlation, and add item-level exam analysis before the fix window.

issues.quote: Enrolment targets, exam operations, the tracking dashboard, and the
issues.problem: Exam integrity and credential operations are absent: question-bank rotation, proctoring, verifiable badges and fraud or sharing controls.
issues.fix: Add an exam-integrity checklist line and credential-verification method.

issues.quote: Certify partner trainers against a quoted rubric, hand them the kit
issues.problem: 'Quoted rubric' is undefined and the package ships no rubric. The 1-to-5 readiness rubric in 'Coach to readiness' also has no template.
issues.fix: Ship templates/trainer-rubric.md and templates/readiness-rubric.md with bands.

issues.quote: Delivery-readiness checks per team, adoption coaching where AI tooling is
issues.problem: 'Adoption coaching where AI tooling is in play' is vague and not actionable.
issues.fix: Either define what adoption coaching covers (usage thresholds, workflows) or cut it.

issues.quote: The academy blueprint, the certification dashboard read, the trainer
issues.problem: The deliverables are named but have no structure, and there is no academy budget or economics (cost per certified head, paid certifications).
issues.fix: Define the blueprint sections, add a cost line, and use bash_exec for throughput and pass-rate arithmetic.

scenarios.prompt: We have about 400 partner SEs across three regions, and certification pass rates fell to 55% after our last release. Redesign the academy.
scenarios.why: 'Design the academy' produces role paths with owners and refresh SLAs, and 'Run certification at scale' reads pass rates and gives 'one dated fix window'. There is no step to diagnose why pass rates fell (item analysis, stale content after the release, prerequisite gaps). The pass bars are not stated here, while onboard-and-enable-partners fixes them at 80/85/90.

scenarios.prompt: Stand up train-the-trainer for our LATAM distributor. Their trainers will teach in Spanish and Portuguese, we have no LMS, and none of their trainers are certified yet.
scenarios.why: 'Stand up train-the-trainer' (certify trainers against a rubric, hand over the kit, audit first cohorts) and the no-platform fallback both apply. The skill never addresses localisation and translation QA, distributor contractual obligations or budget, or how to certify trainers before any certified pool exists. The model has to improvise the hard parts.

build-partner-led-category-creation.job: create market category with partner coalition
build-partner-led-category-creation.summary: Builds a partner-led category-design plan: a one-page thesis with naming tests and required proof, a coalition of up to five lighthouse partners with dated deliverables, a shared narrative with sourced proof, and a launch moment followed by dated beats and quarterly category signals.
strengths: A useful gate: a thesis with no named shift is positioning, not a category.
Every coalition member needs a role and a dated deliverable ('a logo, not a coalition partner').
Proof rules: closest customer first, every number sourced, partner claims kept in their own words.
Success criteria are set before the launch moment fires, and a beat that misses twice gets one fix before it is cut.
A strong approval gate covering partners, analysts and the public.
missing: Create-vs-reframe go/no-go with rival-term check
Competition-law and trademark guardrails
Coalition MOU / commitment instrument
Buyer-language evidence for the category name
Signal sources and pre-launch baselines
Cross-expert handoffs for positioning and PR

issues.quote: At most five lighthouse partners, each with a named executive sponsor and
issues.problem: A multi-vendor coalition coordinating market messaging has no competition-law guardrail (no discussion of pricing, customer allocation or boycotts) and no Legal check on joint claims or the category-name trademark.
issues.fix: Add a Legal gate: competition-law guidelines for coalition meetings, trademark clearance on the category name, and substantiation review for joint claims.

issues.section: Write the category thesis in one page
issues.problem: There is no create-versus-reframe decision before committing. It does not check for an existing or rival category, the multi-year cost, or the risk that a larger vendor takes the name, so the model starts building even when a subcategory or repositioning is the better call.
issues.fix: Add a go/no-go step that maps adjacent and rival categories and terms, estimates the multi-year investment, and requires the owner's yes to proceed.

issues.section: Write the category thesis in one page
issues.quote: budget-line-item test, and the would-this-have-an-encyclopedia-entry-in-
issues.problem: The naming tests are idiosyncratic and miss buyer-language validation (search demand, how buyers describe the problem) and trademark availability.
issues.fix: Add buyer-language evidence (interviews, search volume via web_search or DataForSEO) and trademark clearance to the name tests.

issues.quote: a dated commitment. Two analysts briefed early. One lighthouse customer
issues.problem: 'Dated commitment' is not given an instrument (MOU or letter), and there are no cost-sharing or co-branding terms, so commitments stay soft.
issues.fix: Stage a short coalition MOU draft covering role, deliverable, date, co-branding rights and cost split, subject to the owner's and Legal's yes.

issues.section: Strike once, then compound in beats
issues.quote: After launch, track the category signals quarterly — analyst mentions,
issues.problem: The signals have no sources, baselines or fallback (which CRM field measures win-rate lift, and where analyst mentions come from).
issues.fix: Name the sources (web_search or alliance sensing brief, CRM win-rate by tagged deals), set baselines before launch, and fall back to owner-supplied exports.

issues.section: Run the joint narrative and the proof
issues.quote: One shared story every partner tells. Objection-mapped proof:
issues.problem: It overlaps with the positioning, launch-comms and PR skills of other experts (Zara, Noor, Maya) and names no handoff.
issues.fix: Add a handoff line: messaging polish to the positioning teammate and launch press to the communications teammate via consult_teammate.

scenarios.prompt: We and three integration partners think 'AI revenue orchestration' is a new category. Build the thesis and a coalition plan for a Q2 launch.
scenarios.why: 'Write the category thesis in one page' supplies the shift, old way, new way, point of view, name tests and three proof points. 'Build the coalition' gives each member a role and a dated deliverable, and 'Strike once' sets 30-day success criteria before the launch. A capable model would produce a senior-quality plan.

scenarios.prompt: Our biggest competitor coined a similar term last month, two of our lighthouse partners also partner with them, and there's no budget.
scenarios.why: The no-budget fallback (proof first: the narrative plus one lighthouse win) and 'a thesis with no named shift is positioning' help. Nothing covers an existing rival term (reframe versus subcategory versus concede), partners shared with a competitor, or the competition-law care needed when vendors coordinate. The model would miss the real decision.

define-the-partner-icp.job: define ideal partner profile and tiers
define-the-partner-icp.summary: Drafts an ideal partner profile per partner type in five blocks (firmographics, personas, capabilities, fit signals, anti-signals), adds strategic, growth and watch tiers with graduation and kill bars and a partner-facing tier sheet, and saves the profile to memory for sibling skills.
strengths: One profile per partner type or tier, with the reason that blended profiles produce unrecruitable lists.
A scale gate: a handful of strategic partners get named accounts, not a formal profile.
Explicit anti-signals and a kill bar.
The profile is saved verbatim so sourcing, qualification and coverage read one definition.
No-history fallback: every line labelled INFERENCE and the first three recruits framed as calibration.
missing: Evidence-derived profile method (top vs bottom partner analysis, signal weights)
Partner-side economics / value exchange block
Clear boundary with design-the-partner-program on tiers
Account-overlap data as an input
Coverage of ISV, marketplace, OEM and affiliate types
Versioning of the saved profile

issues.quote: Add three tiers: strategic (few, joint plans, executive sponsors), growth
issues.problem: Tier design and the tier sheet duplicate design-the-partner-program, which uses a different model (a weighted earn scorecard, 3-4 tiers, a shadow-score pilot). The user can get two conflicting tier systems, and the triggers 'partner tiers' and 'tier sheet' collide.
issues.fix: Limit this skill to recruit-tier targeting (who to recruit into which tier) and hand earn criteria, unlocks and the tier sheet to design-the-partner-program. Remove the colliding triggers.

issues.quote: partner. Publish a partner-facing tier sheet alongside the internal
issues.problem: 'Publish' conflicts with the approval gate. The only 'waits for the owner's yes' line is inside the no-history fallback, and the tier sheet carries money terms (MDF, margin) the persona says need the owner's yes.
issues.fix: Change to 'Draft a partner-facing tier sheet' and move the approval line into the main body, covering all cases and naming MDF and margin as owner decisions.

issues.quote: Draft the profile in five blocks:
issues.problem: There is no method for deriving the profile from evidence. Deal history is listed as an input but never analysed, and there is no top-versus-bottom partner comparison, signal weighting or fit-score threshold.
issues.fix: Add a step: compare top-quartile and bottom-quartile partners on firmographics and capabilities (bash_exec on the CRM or HubSpot export), weight the signals and set a minimum fit score for sourcing.

issues.quote: Partner capabilities: audience access, services muscle, sales motion.
issues.problem: The partner-side value exchange is missing: why the partner would commit (revenue per customer, services attach, customer demand). This is a core ICP dimension for recruitability.
issues.fix: Add a 'Partner economics' block covering what they earn, their attach or services pull-through, and the evidence.

issues.quote: buyer, the current best partners and why they work, deal history, and any
issues.problem: Account-overlap data (CRM or account-mapping exports) is not among the inputs, although source-and-qualify-partners relies on it.
issues.fix: Add account-overlap exports as an optional input and use overlap as a fit signal.

issues.quote: referral, reseller, co-sell, or managed service provider (MSP) and
issues.problem: The partner types omit technology/ISV integration, marketplace, OEM and affiliate partners, all of which the persona's portfolio covers.
issues.fix: Extend the type list or say that other types get their own profile using the same five blocks.

issues.section: Save it so the rest of the desk reuses it
issues.quote: Write the finished profile into the preferences memory verbatim, so
issues.problem: The saved profile has no version or date, so later edits drift silently, and a long profile may be better as a workspace file.
issues.fix: Save a dated, versioned profile (write_workspace_file) and store a pointer plus summary in memory.

scenarios.prompt: Help me define our ideal reseller profile for EMEA. Here are our top five partners and last year's partner deal history.
scenarios.why: The two conditional questions are skipped because the inputs answer them. The model drafts the five blocks for the reseller type only, adds tiers with graduation and kill bars, drafts the tier sheet and saves the profile to memory. The result would be a usable one-page profile.

scenarios.prompt: We have 40 partners, a mix of resellers and SIs. Only three produce revenue, CRM attribution is messy, and leadership wants tiers published to partners next month.
scenarios.why: 'Scope one profile per partner type' and 'Gate on evidence and scale' help. There is no method for pulling signals from messy performance data (top versus bottom comparison, attribution caveats). The tier work collides with design-the-partner-program, which has the shadow-scoring pilot and 60-90 day notice this skill lacks. 'Publish a partner-facing tier sheet' could push an early release.

discovery-and-qualification.job: plan discovery call and score deal qualification
discovery-and-qualification.summary: Builds a pre-call discovery plan (outcome, agenda, 8-10 grounded questions, likely objections, dual close) and, after the call, scores the deal letter by letter on MEDDICC/MEDDPICC/SPICED using buyer quotes, ending in an advance/stay/close recommendation.
strengths: Met bars are sharp and practitioner-correct: a metric is a number the buyer said out loud; a champion spends political capital (a friendly contact doesn't count); a critical event must be tested for what happens if it slips.
Evidence discipline: every met letter carries the quoted line, open letters carry the exact next-call question, and evidence 90 or more days old reopens the letter.
The dual close (qualified gets a dated next step; unqualified gets a polite no plus a referral ask) is a mature, often-missed practice.
Stage moves and CRM updates are explicitly held for the user's yes.
missing: Stage-to-letter exit criteria table
Scorecard and discovery-plan templates
BANT/CHAMP mapping
Transcript read path (Gong/Granola/HubSpot) and approved CRM write-back
Handoff to multithread-and-stakeholder-maps for Champion/EB gaps and business-case-and-roi-selling for Metrics
A worked example (plan plus scored deal)

issues.quote: Advance, stay, or close. Advance needs every must-have letter met. Anything
issues.problem: 'Must-have' letters are never defined for any framework, and nothing maps letters to stage exit criteria. The advance/stay/close verdict is therefore not reproducible from deal to deal.
issues.fix: Add a short table of required letters per stage (e.g. Discovery→Evaluation needs Pain, Metrics, Champion identified; Commit needs EB confirmed, Decision Process and Paper Process dated), with a user-override line.

issues.quote: The discovery plan before the call, and the scored framework with quotes
issues.problem: There's no template for either deliverable. Scorecard shape (columns, status values, where the next-call question goes) will vary run to run, and the plan isn't reusable as a call sheet.
issues.fix: Ship templates/discovery-plan.md and templates/qualification-scorecard.md (Letter | Status met/open/inference | Buyer quote | Source & date | Next-call question | Owner). Route to them from this section.

issues.quote: unsourced recollection are marked INFERENCE until a quote lands
issues.problem: It never says whether an INFERENCE letter counts as met or open for the verdict. Notes-only deals, the most common case, therefore get an undefined verdict.
issues.fix: State that INFERENCE letters count as open for the verdict but are shown separately, and that the verdict line names how many letters rest on inference.

issues.quote: the account brief, and which qualification framework the user runs —
issues.problem: Only MEDDICC, MEDDPICC and SPICED are supported. Many SMB and mid-market teams run BANT, CHAMP or GPCTBA/C&I, and the skill gives no mapping or default for them.
issues.fix: Add a one-line mapping of BANT/CHAMP onto the MEDDICC letters, or say to score on the nearest MEDDICC equivalents and name the mapping in the output.

issues.problem: There's no read path for transcripts or deal sheets (Gong/Granola via MCP, HubSpot block, pasted notes). There's also no staged write-back of the scorecard to the CRM or memory after approval. The skill is tool-agnostic to a fault.
issues.fix: Add: pull the transcript via connected recorder (run_mcp_tool) or HubSpot notes (run_block), else ask for a paste; after the user's yes, stage the HubSpot field updates and memory_store the scorecard for the next call.

issues.quote: buyer buy-in up top, eight to ten ordered questions — including one
issues.problem: The plan is fixed at 8-10 questions regardless of call length or deal size, which is overbuilt for a 15-minute SMB call. There's also no prioritisation for when time runs short.
issues.fix: Size the question count to call length and mark the three must-ask questions to cover if the call is cut short.

issues.quote: Score the deal against the framework after the call. Each letter is met
issues.problem: Buyer quotes from recorded calls are personal data. Nothing says to check recording consent or to keep verbatim quotes internal.
issues.fix: Add one line: quotes stay in internal deal records; confirm recordings were made with the buyer's consent before quoting them.

scenarios.prompt: First call Thursday with Northwind's VP Finance. Here's the account brief and the notes from the SDR. Build me the discovery plan; we run MEDDICC.
scenarios.why: 'Discovery plan before the call' names every component (one-ask outcome, agenda with buyer buy-in, 8-10 ordered questions including implication, quantified-impact and cost-of-inaction, two likely objections, dual close) and requires grounding each question in the brief. A capable model produces a usable senior plan.

scenarios.prompt: No recording, just my scribbled notes from yesterday's call. We actually use BANT, and my manager wants to know by EOD whether this goes in commit. The champion 'seemed keen'.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks correctly score from notes and the Champion bar correctly rejects 'seemed keen'. But BANT isn't supported or mapped. 'Advance needs every must-have letter met' never says which letters are must-have, and INFERENCE letters aren't classed as met or open. The model has to improvise the commit call, which is exactly the judgement the skill should settle.

draft-a-first-touch.summary: Drafts a single unsent opening message (email, social, phone or short public post) from an enriched target-list row: one sourced dated fact, one pain, and a soft reply ask, in the user's voice. It then marks the row drafted without logging a touch.
strengths: Strict no-invention rule with concrete examples (no assumed funding, no guessed headcount, no 'I noticed' without the link).
The soft reply ask instead of a meeting ask, and the four-to-five-word sentence-case subject, reflect current cold-email practice.
It separates 'drafted' from 'contacted' so the CRM never shows a touch that didn't happen.
'One line on what you left out' makes dropped claims visible to the user.
missing: Outreach law and consent checks by geography
Suppression, existing-customer and owner conflict check
Per-channel formats (LinkedIn limits, call opener structure, voicemail)
Batch output block for the routine
Deliverability basics (plain text, no attachments or links in the first email)
A worked example beyond the persona's voice sample

issues.problem: There are no outreach compliance limits: CAN-SPAM identification and opt-out, GDPR legitimate-interest basis for EU/UK prospects, CASL consent for Canada, TCPA/do-not-call for phone. The skill drafts for all four channels with no geography check.
issues.fix: Add a compliance line: check the prospect's country; for EU/UK/Canada flag the lawful basis or consent requirement before drafting; email drafts carry the user's standard opt-out line; phone drafts check DNC status or ask the user to.

issues.quote: The target-list row with its hook and sources, the user's voice sample, the
issues.problem: There's no pre-draft suppression check. Opted-out contacts, existing customers, open opportunities owned by another rep, and rows touched recently can all get a fresh cold opener.
issues.fix: Add step 0: check status (skip no/on hold/suppressed), check the CRM for an existing account owner or open deal, and stop with a one-line reason when any match.

issues.quote: Mark the row drafted with today's date in drafted_on, and save.
issues.problem: This conflicts with Max's weekday-prospecting-batch routine ('no row on the list changes until the user tells you to mark it') and the persona's 'no CRM field moves without explicit yes'. It also names no tool or location for the save.
issues.fix: Stage the row update (status drafted, drafted_on) as a proposed change shown with the draft. Write it via the Sheets/HubSpot block only after the user approves or when the list is a workspace file the user designated as Max-editable.

issues.quote: characters for a short public post, and under 30 seconds spoken for phone
issues.problem: Channel formats are thin. There's no structure for a cold-call opener (permission or reason line, question) and no LinkedIn connection-note (300 chars) vs InMail distinction. A 'short public post' as a first touch to a named prospect is an odd, rarely appropriate channel.
issues.fix: Add a per-channel block: email, LinkedIn connection note / InMail / DM with limits, call opener plus voicemail script. Drop public post or restrict it to replying in a thread the prospect started.

issues.quote: Match the user's voice sample; if there is none, keep it plain and under
issues.problem: As worded, the length caps apply only when there's no voice sample, so a long-winded voice sample licenses 250-word cold emails.
issues.fix: Make the caps unconditional and have voice govern tone and wording only.

issues.quote: Show the draft in chat with the source links under it and one line on what
issues.problem: There's no batch mode or A/B variant option, though Max's routine works five rows per run, and no template for the delivered block.
issues.fix: Add a per-row output block (row id, channel, subject, body, sources, dropped claims, proposed row change) and allow one alternate angle when the user asks for variants.

issues.quote: not been enriched yet, stop and route it to research before writing a word.
issues.problem: 'Research' isn't tied to the sibling skill that does it, so the model may improvise research inline instead of loading research-an-account.
issues.fix: Name the sibling: 'load research-an-account (or build-the-target-list enrichment) and come back'.

scenarios.prompt: Draft the email opener for Dana at Northwind, row 14. Hook is their new Denver DC (link in the row). Use my voice sample.
scenarios.why: 'Writing the draft' gives a clear structure (sourced dated fact, their pain, soft reply ask). The subject rules, length cap, banned openers and 'Delivering the draft' (sources under the draft, one line on what was dropped) yield a clean, senior-quality opener.

scenarios.prompt: Do LinkedIn and cold-call openers for these 20 rows from my HubSpot export. Half have no trigger, a few are in Germany and Canada, and two are existing customers.
scenarios.why: The thin-row fallback handles missing hooks. But the skill is single-row with no batch pattern. It gives no LinkedIn connection-note limit or call-opener structure, only 'under 30 seconds'. It has no suppression or existing-customer check and no GDPR/CASL caution. Marking 20 rows drafted also contradicts the routine's 'no row on the list changes until the user tells you'.

draft-a-follow-up.job: draft next touch in outreach sequence
draft-a-follow-up.summary: Drafts the next unsent touch for a no-reply prospect inside an eight-touch, multi-channel, front-loaded cadence ending in a breakup and a nurture recycle, with state rules that keep last_touch_on unchanged until the user confirms the send.
strengths: Clear front-loaded, multi-channel cadence with a graceful breakup and a 60-90 day nurture recycle.
Never writes last_touch_on or an outreach touch from an unsent draft, and explains why (false CRM state shifts cadence dates).
Each touch is shorter than the last, with a new angle on the same pain: current, correct practice.
Routes to handle-a-reply when a reply arrives mid-sequence.
missing: Auto-reply/OOO/bounce handling
Explicit day table and shared ask ladder with first-touch
Sequence table output
Channel-specific call/voicemail/LinkedIn formats and threading
schedule_followup for next-touch reminders
Outreach compliance and frequency caps

issues.quote: days 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, then spaced a week apart. Never stop before
issues.problem: It's internally inconsistent. Eight touches on this spacing end around day 31, beyond 'three to four weeks'. 'Never stop before attempt five' also contradicts the Fallback 'suggest waiting for a trigger instead of burning the row'.
issues.fix: Publish the explicit day table (e.g. D1, D3, D5, D7, D10, D17, D24, D31 labelled ~4.5 weeks) and state that the no-new-angle pause overrides the five-touch floor only with the user's yes.

issues.quote: revisit. Any reply at any point ends the sequence.
issues.problem: Auto-replies/OOO, bounces and opt-outs aren't distinguished from real replies. An OOO wrongly ends the sequence, a bounce isn't flagged for contact re-verification, and opt-out handling depends on a sibling.
issues.fix: Add: an OOO pauses and re-dates to the return date; a hard bounce stops, blanks the contact and flags re-verification; an opt-out stops and suppresses; only a human reply ends the sequence and routes to handle-a-reply.

issues.quote: with a new angle on the same pain each time. Touch two lowers the
issues.problem: This conflicts with draft-a-first-touch, which saves 'the dated ask for the follow-up'. Here touch two instead offers a smaller ask than a reply request, so the ask ladder across the two skills is incoherent.
issues.fix: Define one ask ladder shared by both skills (touch 1 reply ask → touch 2 dated meeting ask or micro-yes → middle value and referral → breakup) and reference it from both.

issues.quote: this angle. Mark the row with next_step, record the draft as pending, and
issues.problem: 'Pending' isn't a status in build-the-target-list's schema (new…sent, replied, meeting, qualified). The row write also conflicts with the routine's no-row-change rule, and no tool or location is named.
issues.fix: Use the schema's fields (next_step with the dated touch) and stage the change for approval. Use schedule_followup to remind the user on the next touch's send date.

issues.quote: attempt five. Rotate the channel per touch — email, call, social —
issues.problem: It rotates into call and social but gives no call or voicemail structure, no LinkedIn etiquette (connect before DM, note limits), and no email threading rule (reply in-thread vs new subject).
issues.fix: Add a per-channel line for each rotation and a threading rule for email follow-ups.

issues.quote: The unsent follow-up draft with its touch number, plus the row update.
issues.problem: There's no touch-plan view, so the user sees one draft without the remaining sequence, dates, channels and angles.
issues.fix: Output a sequence table (touch | day | date | channel | angle | ask | status) with the current draft highlighted.

issues.quote: Say the send date on each draft. Each touch holds the no-invented-facts
issues.problem: There's no opt-out line, frequency cap, or geography check (CAN-SPAM/GDPR/CASL) for repeated unsolicited touches, and no send-window guidance for the prospect's timezone.
issues.fix: Add compliance and send-window rules shared with draft-a-first-touch.

scenarios.prompt: Dana at Northwind never replied to my email from Sept 20. Draft the next touch.
scenarios.why: The inputs (row, prior touches with dates) let the model place this as touch two. 'Run the eight-touch cadence' gives the angle guidance (smaller ask, rotate channel) and 'Draft rules' give send date, shorter length and voice. The output is sensible, though the channel choice (call vs email) is under-specified.

scenarios.prompt: We're on touch 6 for the Acme VP. Last email got an out-of-office until Oct 10, the one before bounced for her colleague, and she's in France.
scenarios.why: 'Any reply at any point ends the sequence' treats the OOO as a reply and routes to handle-a-reply, which has no auto-reply bucket. Nothing addresses bounces, re-timing around the OOO date, or EU outreach rules, so the model has to improvise every judgement call here.

enablement-playbooks-certification.job: build sales playbooks, onboarding and certification
enablement-playbooks-certification.summary: Outlines a sales enablement system: an owned and dated play library, a Learn/Apply/Lead onboarding curriculum with certification gates, a call-quality rubric from real calls, program-style training, and a quarterly field refresh.
strengths: Each play carries a trigger, ICP slice, talk track, battlecard, exit criteria, owner and review date, and an unowned play is retired.
Certification gates before solo calls, with role-plays scored against the same rubric used in live call review.
The quarterly refresh ties win/loss and objection learning back into the library.
Approval gate: nothing rep-wide publishes and no gate blocks a rep without the user's yes.
missing: Rubric template with dimensions and anchors
Play card and curriculum templates
Enablement metrics (ramp time, cert pass rate, win rate by play)
Sizing by team maturity
Redaction and consent for quoted calls
Clear boundary with sales-team-leadership, field-enablement-content and sales-enablement-content

issues.quote: triggers: ["playbook", "onboarding", "certification", "call quality", "sales training", "talk track", "ramp plan"]
issues.problem: 'Onboarding' and 'ramp plan' are also sales-team-leadership triggers in Max's kit, and 'playbook' and 'talk track' overlap field-enablement-content and sales-enablement-content. Routing between the enablement system and per-rep ramp is ambiguous.
issues.fix: Use system-level triggers ('enablement program', 'sales certification', 'call scoring rubric', 'play library'). State that per-rep ramp and coaching go to sales-team-leadership and single assets (deck, battlecard) go to the content skill.

issues.quote: Scored dimensions for calls and deals with what good sounds like,
issues.problem: No dimensions, scale or weights are given (e.g. agenda set, discovery depth, quantified pain, talk ratio, next step secured, MEDDICC coverage), so every run invents a different rubric.
issues.fix: Ship templates/call-quality-rubric.md with 6-8 default dimensions, a 1-4 behavioural scale with anchors, and slots for quoted examples.

issues.quote: quoted from real calls. Review calls against it weekly; feed the
issues.problem: Quoting real customer calls in a rep-wide rubric exposes customer names and data and rep performance. There's no redaction, recording-consent or anonymisation rule.
issues.fix: Require redacting customer identifiers and anonymising the rep in published examples, and confirm the recordings were captured with consent.

issues.problem: There are no enablement success measures (ramp time, time to first deal, certification pass rate, play adoption, win rate by play), so the 'programs not events' claim can't be verified.
issues.fix: Add a metrics block to the output and the quarterly refresh log: baseline, target and source for each measure, labelled FACT or INFERENCE.

issues.quote: The plays in use, the call record sample, the onboarding material on
issues.problem: There's no sizing step. A five-rep startup gets the same library, three-stage certification and weekly review program as a 200-rep org.
issues.fix: Ask for team size, motion and product complexity first, and scale the deliverable: minimum viable at under 10 reps, the full system above that.

issues.section: Run training as programs, not events
issues.quote: incentive bonuses (SPIFs) and deal-registration mechanics are played in the
issues.problem: This is an off-scope detour. Deal registration is a partner/channel mechanic and SPIF tracking is sales-ops, and the sentence is garbled, so it muddies the skill's boundary.
issues.fix: Replace it with a one-line boundary: SPIFs and comp live in sales-ops-coverage-and-quota; deal registration lives in partner-and-channel-co-sell.

issues.quote: and a live-deal shadow with a scored debrief. No cert, no solo calls.
issues.problem: Certification gates that block reps are an employment-adjacent decision, but there's no pass mark, no retake path, and no handoff to the sales leader or HR when a rep repeatedly fails.
issues.fix: Define the pass mark and retake rule, and route repeated failure to sales-team-leadership, not an automatic block.

issues.quote: Playbook library with owners and dates, onboarding curriculum with
issues.problem: Five deliverables are listed with no templates or storage location (Notion/Drive/Docs), so none is reusable across runs.
issues.fix: Add templates/play-card.md and templates/curriculum.md, and say where to stage them (Notion or Google Docs via run_block, else a workspace file).

scenarios.prompt: We're hiring four AEs next quarter. Build the onboarding curriculum and certification they have to pass before taking solo calls.
scenarios.why: 'Write the onboarding curriculum' gives Learn/Apply/Lead and the gate types (quizzes, recorded role-plays, live shadow), but no week-by-week content, pass marks or scoring. sales-team-leadership also claims onboarding and ramp plans, so either skill may load. The result is a plausible outline, not a ready curriculum.

scenarios.prompt: Build a call-quality rubric. I've got 12 Gong transcripts exported and five reps, but no enablement owner, and I don't want anything that looks like a PIP.
scenarios.why: The Fallbacks cover the missing owner, and the approval gate covers blocking reps. But 'Scored dimensions' is undefined, so the rubric content is improvised. Nothing says to redact customer names from quoted calls before publishing rep-wide, and there's no guidance on keeping rubric scoring separate from performance management.

enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans.job: run mutual close plan to signature
enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans.summary: Orchestrates a large deal to signature: a buyer-visible mutual close plan with procurement, legal, security and commercial tracks, a paper-process map and proactive security readiness packet, deal-desk give/get with a concession log, multi-entity contracting, redline rounds, and a MEDDPICC commit gate.
strengths: Ships the security readiness packet with the plan rather than waiting for the questionnaire, which shortens enterprise cycles in practice.
Deal desk discipline: every ask pairs with a give, ranked easy to hard, walk-away set first, and every concession logged with date and owner.
Multi-entity contracting: a master track with dated sub-tracks per entity; a region with no owner is blocked.
Firm approval gate on pricing, terms, concessions and anything buyer-facing.
missing: Counsel and finance escalation paths (and teammate consult to contract-ops/deal-desk experts)
Security questionnaire method (SIG/CAIQ, answer library, SME routing, NDA before reports)
Deal-desk approval matrix template
Concession log template
E-signature and signature-authority check
Clear boundary with quarterback-the-deal-team and objection-and-negotiation

issues.quote: Write the buyer-visible mutual close plan first: the buyer outcome and
issues.problem: This duplicates quarterback-the-deal-team, which builds the same buyer-visible dated mutual close plan with the same paper-process track and shares the 'mutual close plan' and 'paper process' triggers. The two skills compete to load and will drift apart.
issues.fix: Make quarterback own the mutual close plan. Re-scope this skill to deal desk, paper process and global contracting, and have it add tracks to quarterback's plan instead of writing its own.

issues.quote: resolve internally against the approval bands, and return one clean draft
issues.problem: Legal redlines (liability cap, DPA, SLA, indemnity) are legal positions, not commercial approval bands. Having the AE-persona 'resolve' them with no counsel step is an expertise error and a guardrail gap.
issues.fix: Route each redline to the user's counsel or legal playbook (consult Ellis/contract-ops if hired). Track positions as standard, fallback or walk-away per clause, and only return drafts counsel approved.

issues.quote: (a SOC 2 Type II security audit report, single sign-on, audit logging,
issues.problem: It assumes the vendor has SOC 2 Type II, SSO and audit logging, and tells the model to ship the report with the plan. SOC 2 reports are normally shared only under NDA, and listing controls the vendor lacks is a false claim.
issues.fix: Say: include only evidence the user confirms exists; SOC 2 and pen-test reports go out under a signed NDA or via the trust portal; missing controls are named as gaps with a remediation answer.

issues.quote: for the intro path. No approval bands means you draft inside the last
issues.problem: When no bands exist, it drafts concessions from another customer's terms, which is an arbitrary baseline that can silently expand discount authority.
issues.fix: With no bands, draft asks and gives without numbers and ask the user for their discount, payment-term and term-length authority before pricing anything.

issues.quote: Gate every commit on full MEDDPICC: Metrics, Economic Buyer with confirmed
issues.problem: This re-implements the qualification scoring owned by discovery-and-qualification, with slightly different bars (e.g. 'confirmed budget'), so a deal can pass one skill and fail the other.
issues.fix: Reference discovery-and-qualification's scorecard and require its Paper Process letter be met before Contract Sent.

issues.quote: Run bespoke terms through the deal desk: every commercial ask names the
issues.problem: The approval matrix dimensions are never named (discount %, payment terms, term length, auto-renew, price caps, MFN, termination for convenience, liability cap), so 'inside approval bands' has nothing to check against.
issues.fix: Add a default deal-desk matrix template with these dimensions and the approver per band, filled from the user's policy.

issues.quote: region, the currency and tax treatment, and which subsidiary signs what and
issues.problem: Tax treatment, withholding, transfer pricing and revenue recognition of non-standard terms are finance and tax decisions. The skill gives no escalation.
issues.fix: Mark entity, tax and rev-rec items as requiring finance sign-off, and list them as a finance track with an owner.

issues.quote: The mutual close plan with dated tracks, the paper-process map, the
issues.problem: Seven deliverables are listed with no templates (close plan columns, concession log fields, paper-process map), and there's no storage or approval path (Drive/Docs, HubSpot fields).
issues.fix: Ship templates for the concession log and paper-process map, and stage them to Drive/Docs via run_block after approval.

scenarios.prompt: $480K, 3-year deal with a regional bank. Procurement sent a 300-question security questionnaire and their legal redlined our liability cap and DPA. Target signature Dec 15. Build the close plan.
scenarios.why: 'Mutual close plan first' and 'Paper process and readiness packet' give the tracks, owners, dates and the idea of shipping evidence early. But there's no questionnaire method (SIG/CAIQ, answer library, SME routing), and liability and DPA redlines are 'resolved internally against the approval bands' with no counsel escalation. quarterback-the-deal-team shares the triggers, so the wrong skill may load.

scenarios.prompt: They want to sign via their UK subsidiary, pay in EUR on net-90, and get 20% off. We don't have formal approval bands yet.
scenarios.why: 'Global mechanics' prompts for the contracting entity, currency and tax, and the Fallbacks flag everything as INFERENCE. But the fallback drafts 'inside the last approved deal's terms', which isn't a sound baseline. Nothing routes tax, revenue recognition or entity decisions to finance, or payment terms to credit review, so the model may produce confident-looking terms no one has authority for.

exec-engagement-and-sponsorship.job: run executive sponsorship program for account
exec-engagement-and-sponsorship.summary: Runs an account-level executive program: key-account selection by weighted scoring, sponsor-state mapping (mapped/engaged/sponsoring), gap naming, peer-matched C-level connects with sponsor briefs and recaps, Why Change/Why Now/Why Us briefing packs, and a governance cadence with a joint issue log.
strengths: Exec connects done right: peer-matched by seniority, a business topic each time, the sponsor briefed with logistics, contact, terms, agenda and goal, then a sourced recap and the next touch dated.
Sponsor states (mapped, engaged, sponsoring), where 'sponsoring' requires evidence of advocacy, not a title.
Data minimisation: anything external carries the minimum customer data, redacted and approved by the account owner.
Briefing packs use a recognised Why Change/Why Now/Why Us arc, with value delivered stated only in FACT numbers.
missing: Internal exec sponsor roster, charter and time budget
Sponsor-turnover playbook
Sponsor brief and briefing-pack templates
Program success measures (renewal/expansion rate on sponsored vs unsponsored accounts)
Boundary with multithread-and-stakeholder-maps, territory-and-account-planning and renewal-expansion-and-qbr
Calendar/CRM tool path

issues.quote: stakeholder map with the champion, economic buyer, technical evaluators,
issues.problem: This duplicates multithread-and-stakeholder-maps (same map, same roles, same 'stakeholder map' trigger) and territory-and-account-planning's account plans. Business reviews also overlap renewal-expansion-and-qbr, so trigger routing within Max's kit is ambiguous.
issues.fix: Consume the stakeholder map from multithread-and-stakeholder-maps and the account plan from territory-and-account-planning. Drop the 'stakeholder map' and 'key account' triggers for exec-specific ones ('exec sponsor program', 'EBC', 'C-level connect').

issues.quote: Select key accounts on a weighted 1-10 scoring matrix across fit, size,
issues.problem: Key-account selection is a portfolio decision that belongs to account or territory planning, and it forces a scoring pass even when the user names one account. The criteria also carry no weights or scale anchors.
issues.fix: Move selection to territory-and-account-planning, or make it an optional branch that runs only when the user asks which accounts deserve an exec program, with default weights.

issues.quote: relationships went stale past 30 days. One gap, one close plan, one owner,
issues.problem: A 30-day staleness rule contradicts 'dated touches per exec per quarter' and flags most healthy exec relationships as gaps.
issues.fix: Set staleness relative to the agreed cadence (e.g. stale when a planned touch is missed by more than two weeks, or when there's no exec touch in 90 days).

issues.problem: There's no internal side of the program: which of your execs sponsor which accounts, their time budget, a sponsor charter, or how to prioritise when exec time is scarce.
issues.fix: Add an internal sponsor roster with hours per quarter per exec, allocated by account score, plus a one-paragraph sponsor charter.

issues.problem: Sponsor or champion turnover, one of the most common exec-program failures, isn't handled.
issues.fix: Add: when a sponsor leaves, flag risk on the open deal or renewal, request an intro to the successor through the departing sponsor, and re-run the gap check.

issues.quote: next. Keep the sponsor on every subsequent thread until the deal closes.
issues.problem: This assumes an open deal and puts execs on every thread. An account exec program continues after close, and cc'ing executives on routine threads burns their attention.
issues.fix: Loop the sponsor in on decision and escalation threads only, and keep the program running after close via the governance cadence.

issues.quote: Hold account governance cadence with customer execs: a dated rhythm of
issues.problem: There's no default frequency, attendee list or agenda for the governance rhythm, and no template for the sponsor brief or briefing pack.
issues.fix: Add default cadences (e.g. quarterly EBR, monthly operating review) and ship templates for the sponsor brief and briefing pack.

issues.quote: No stakeholder map means you build one from the CRM and call record and
issues.problem: No read path is named (HubSpot block, Gong/Granola MCP, pasted export), and there's no calendar integration for connects or schedule_routine for the governance cadence.
issues.fix: Name the tool path with a paste fallback. Offer to stage connects on Google Calendar and a schedule_routine for cadence reminders after the user approves.

scenarios.prompt: Acme is our biggest account, renewing in Q2. Their CIO, our sponsor, left last month. Build me the exec engagement plan.
scenarios.why: 'Name the gaps' and 'Executive connects' produce a gap, owner, date and peer-matched connect plan with a sponsor brief, which is useful. But nothing covers sponsor departure (re-sponsoring, meeting the successor, a risk flag to the renewal). The skill also first runs key-account scoring, which isn't needed, and it overlaps renewal-expansion-and-qbr on the business review.

scenarios.prompt: Set up an exec sponsor program across our top 20 accounts. Our CEO can give 4 hours a month, and half the CRM contacts are stale.
scenarios.why: Key-account scoring and the INFERENCE fallback for a missing stakeholder map help. But there's no internal exec capacity allocation or sponsor charter, and the 30-day staleness rule flags nearly every account against the quarterly cadence. No tool path is given for calendar or CRM, so the model builds a plan the CEO's four hours can't support.

media-plan-measure-optimize.job: sell media from RFP to renewal
media-plan-measure-optimize.summary: A single-file outline for a media or sponsorship seller that runs RFP to plan, proposal, IO, tracking, in-flight test-and-learn, post-campaign report and renewal, with an approval gate on rates, make-goods and tracking setup.
strengths: Correct sell-side lifecycle ordering (plan, proposal, negotiation, IO, measured renewal) with a dated buyer owner on each step
Strong approval gate that explicitly covers rates, bonuses, make-goods and any pixel/MMP/postback configuration
'Scarcity is stated as FACT with the calendar attached, never as pressure copy' is a sharp, senior guardrail
Ties the renewal to lift and conversion measurement rather than impressions, and labels an inferred success metric INFERENCE until the buyer agrees
missing: Pricing models and rate-card or floor logic
IO terms checklist (cancellation, make-good, count of record, discrepancy tolerance, payment terms)
Under-delivery and make-good playbook with discrepancy reconciliation
Reach/frequency, viewability and invalid-traffic standards in the plan and report
Templates for the media plan, IO summary, tracking checklist and post-campaign report
Privacy and consent handling for pixels, MMPs and postbacks
Tool routing (sandbox for flight and pacing math, where io_state and the logs are stored)

issues.section: Answer the RFP as plan, proposal, negotiation, IO
issues.quote: The plan shows audience, mix, and why; the proposal prices it; the
issues.problem: No pricing guidance at all. It does not cover CPM/vCPM/CPCV/flat-fee sponsorship models, rate-card floors, value-add ratios, or package discounting. Pricing is the core of the proposal step, so a model would invent its approach.
issues.fix: Add a short pricing step: choose the pricing unit per line, start from the rate card and floor, state the value-add ratio, and label every rate FACT (from the rate card) or proposed-for-approval. Use bash_exec for the flight math.

issues.section: Answer the RFP as plan, proposal, negotiation, IO
issues.quote: negotiation trades rate against value-adds; the insertion order locks
issues.problem: The IO has no terms beyond flight, spend and metrics: no cancellation window, make-good and under-delivery policy, ad server of record, discrepancy tolerance (commonly around 10%), payment terms or standard T&Cs reference. These are the clauses that decide disputes.
issues.fix: Add an IO terms checklist (cancellation, make-good policy, count of record plus discrepancy threshold, payment terms, creative deadlines, T&Cs version) and route any non-standard clause to the owner and counsel.

issues.quote: Plan-to-insertion-order package with dated steps, tracking checklist with setup
