issues.problem: Five deliverables are named, but none has a template, section list or example. The user cannot reuse a consistent IO summary, tracking checklist or post-campaign report.
issues.fix: Ship templates/ for the media plan, IO summary, tracking checklist, in-flight optimisation log and post-campaign report, and route to them by relative path.

issues.section: Set up tracking before anything flies
issues.quote: Tracking pixels or mobile measurement partners placed, a setup check
issues.problem: There is no privacy or consent limit for pixels, MMPs and postbacks (GDPR/CCPA, app-tracking consent), no third-party verification or brand-safety vendor step, and no statement of who places the buyer's tags. The skill also cannot verify that a pixel 'fires and attributes correctly' without access.
issues.fix: Add a consent and data-sharing check before any tag, name verification (viewability, invalid traffic, brand safety) as a buyer-agreed line, and say the setup check uses buyer-supplied screenshots or test-event logs, or browser_navigate on a test page, with the result labelled.

issues.section: Report post-campaign in the buyer's language
issues.quote: Run account audits on pacing and delivery while
issues.problem: In-flight pacing audits sit in the post-campaign section, and programmatic floor and pacing notes sit under 'Optimize'. It has no pacing threshold (for example, behind even delivery by more than X%) and no under-delivery playbook.
issues.fix: Move pacing into a dedicated in-flight section with a pacing tolerance, an escalation trigger and make-good options, and keep the post-campaign section purely retrospective.

issues.section: Run Test and Learn inside the flight
issues.quote: The hypothesis, the control, the read date. Pair delivery metrics
issues.problem: Brand-lift and conversion-lift studies have minimum spend or sample thresholds and need a vendor or platform set-up. The skill does not say when a lift study is feasible, so it may promise one the budget cannot power.
issues.fix: Add a feasibility check (budget, audience size, vendor availability), and a fallback to a matched-market or holdout read labelled directional.

issues.section: Answer the RFP as plan, proposal, negotiation, IO
issues.quote: Label the io_state planned, live, or wrapped as the IO moves.
issues.problem: io_state is a field name with no defined store. Nothing says where it lives (workspace file, CRM property, memory), so the state will not persist across sessions.
issues.fix: Name the store (for example, a dated workspace file or a CRM deal property via run_block) and read it back at the start of each run.

issues.quote: "media RFP", "ad campaign", "sponsorship"
issues.problem: 'ad campaign' will match buy-side requests (a user running their own ads), which Max's persona puts out of scope. 'media RFP' collides with rfp-and-competitive-bid-response.
issues.fix: Use sell-side trigger phrases ('sell sponsorship', 'rate card', 'make-good', 'advertiser IO') and drop 'ad campaign'.

scenarios.prompt: An agency sent an RFP for a $120K Q4 sponsorship across our podcast network. Build the plan and proposal and draft the IO so I can review it.
scenarios.why: The 'Answer the RFP as plan, proposal, negotiation, IO' and 'Handle premium inventory' sections give a sound sequence and the approval gate stops rates going out. But 'the proposal prices it' says nothing about the pricing model (CPM, flat sponsorship, value-add ratio, rate-card floor). The IO section only says it 'locks flight, spend, and success metrics', with no cancellation, make-good, ad-server-of-record or payment terms. The model would produce a plausible but generic package.

scenarios.prompt: We are mid-flight with a week left, 30% under-delivered, and the buyer's third-party verification shows a 15% impression discrepancy against our ad server. They want a make-good. What do I do?
scenarios.why: The skill only offers 'Run account audits on pacing and delivery while live', which is misplaced under post-campaign reporting, and 'Shift working spend to working placements', plus the gate that no make-good is promised. It has no discrepancy tolerance, no rule for which count bills, and no make-good options (extend the flight, bonus impressions, reallocate, credit). So the model has to improvise the part a senior ad-sales lead would know cold.

multithread-and-stakeholder-maps.job: map buying center and multithread deal
multithread-and-stakeholder-maps.summary: Builds a role-tagged buying-center map from names the user already has and sources it can link, names role and access gaps against deal-size thread targets, and drafts evidence-only warm-path asks and a champion enablement pack for approval.
strengths: Champion versus coach test and 'Economic buyer needs a named person plus a buyer quote' are exactly how senior AEs qualify
Evidence-only warm paths ('never invented mutuals') and 'Never guess a title, a reporting line, or a contact' align with the persona's no-fabrication rule
Deal-size thread targets and dual sponsors above a threshold give a concrete bar for 'multithreaded enough'
Champion enablement pack (forwarding line, ROI one-pager, exec summary, CFO/procurement objection answer) is a practical deliverable
missing: Champion-departure and blocker-conversion plays
Influence and reporting-line mapping (power map)
Fixed map template and workspace location
Clear boundary with find-the-decision-makers and exec-engagement-and-sponsorship
A rule that personal sentiment data stays internal

issues.quote: A champion proves out only when they sell
issues.problem: Several passages copy find-the-decision-makers verbatim: the champion test, the buyer-access test, 'Confirm each title from a source you can link', and the stealth-team fallback. The triggers 'champion', 'economic buyer' and 'buying center' are also shared, so the two skills compete for the same requests in Max's kit.
issues.fix: Split the jobs: find-the-decision-makers finds and verifies new names; this skill owns the map state, gap analysis and thread strategy, and calls the other for sourcing. Move the shared rules into one place and dedupe the triggers.

issues.quote: "stakeholder map", "multithread", "buying center", "champion", "economic buyer"
issues.problem: 'stakeholder map' is also a trigger of exec-engagement-and-sponsorship, and the other terms collide with find-the-decision-makers. Loading will be ambiguous for the most common phrasings.
issues.fix: Keep deal-level phrases ('single-threaded deal', 'multithread this deal', 'open another thread', 'champion left') and leave exec-program and contact-finding phrases to the sibling skills.

issues.problem: It has no plays for blockers or detractors, no plan for a champion who leaves, and no mapping of relationships (who reports to or influences whom). These are the moments multithreading exists for.
issues.fix: Add a short 'Rescue plays' block covering champion departure (follow, successor intro, re-qualify), a blocker (surface their criteria early, peer-match, never go around without a plan), and influence lines on the map.

issues.quote: sentiment (champion, neutral, skeptical, blocker) plus an influence band,
issues.problem: The sentiment scale reuses 'champion' and 'blocker' from the role list, which blurs role and stance. The skill also stores candid judgments about named individuals without saying they stay internal.
issues.fix: Use a distinct sentiment scale (for example, advocate/supportive/neutral/skeptical/opposed) and state that per-person sentiment and influence stay internal and are never forwarded in champion packs.

issues.quote: Output: the stakeholder map with roles, gaps, warm paths, and the
issues.problem: The map has no column template or file location, so repeated re-runs will drift in shape and cannot be diffed when 'a new name shows up'.
issues.fix: Ship templates/stakeholder-map.md (or a CSV) with fixed columns: name, title, source URL, role, sentiment, influence, thread state, last touch, next action. Name the workspace path.

issues.quote: from public connections only, never invented mutuals, and draft the
issues.problem: Mutual connections are mostly not public, and scraping LinkedIn is out of bounds. The skill gives no workable way to find a warm path.
issues.fix: Ask the user for their own and their team's connection exports or names, check shared employers and investors via web_search, and label any path UNKNOWN when none is evidenced.

issues.quote: four-plus engaged threads over $50K, five to seven with dual sponsors
issues.problem: Hard thresholds are stated as fact, with no source and no currency or segment context. The persona forbids unlabeled numbers.
issues.fix: Label these as default heuristics the user can override, and store the user's own thresholds in memory.

issues.quote: for the internal sell: one forwarding line, a one-page ROI summary, an
issues.problem: Drafting the ROI one-pager here duplicates business-case-and-roi-selling and risks a second, inconsistent ROI model.
issues.fix: Route the ROI summary to business-case-and-roi-selling and embed its output.

scenarios.prompt: Our $80K deal with Acme is single-threaded through Jane, the IT manager. Map the buying center and help me open a second thread.
scenarios.why: 'Build the map' starts from Jane and the user's notes, tags roles, verifies titles from linkable sources, and holds empty roles as placeholders. 'Name the gaps' applies the buyer-access test and the four-plus-threads-over-$50K target. 'Open the next thread' drafts a warm-path ask and a champion pack for approval. That is a senior-quality multithreading plan.

scenarios.prompt: Our champion on a $200K deal just left the company. The only other contact is a procurement analyst, and I can't find anything public on the new VP who replaced her.
scenarios.why: The skill covers 'not findable publicly' and asking for an insider. It has no champion-departure play: follow the champion to her new company, get a successor intro through her, re-test the qualification, reset the forecast. It also has no guidance for using procurement as a coach, and 'Never go around the champion' has no answer when the champion is gone. The model would handle the research and miss the recovery strategy.

next-step-and-handoff.job: lock next step, re-open, hand off deal
next-step-and-handoff.summary: Grades a call's next step against four tests (date, time, on both calendars, buyer homework), rewrites the moment it should have been locked, and drafts a structured follow-up, a re-open for a silent deal, or a quoted-promise handoff packet.
strengths: The four-test next step (date, time, on both calendars, buyer homework) is a crisp, adoptable bar
Coaching move of quoting the transcript moment where the next step should have been locked, plus the better line
Follow-up email has a defined order (buyer's problem in their words, agreement, our deliverables, theirs, one dated ask) and bans invented deadlines
Handoff promises are quoted, never paraphrased into more, and unowned loops block the packet
missing: Routing step choosing among the three moments
Handoff fields for commercial terms, success criteria, technical context and out-of-scope items
Escalation for verbal promises beyond the signed scope
A re-open cadence and a close-lost rule
Clear boundary with signature-to-launch-and-account-ops and draft-a-follow-up

issues.quote: The four-test verdict with the better line, plus whichever the moment
issues.problem: Three different jobs (grade a call, re-open a silent deal, hand off a won deal) share one flow with no routing step, and the four-test verdict is mandatory even for a handoff or a re-open where no call transcript exists.
issues.fix: Open with a routing decision (just-ended call / silent deal / signed deal) and make the four-test grade apply only to the first branch.

issues.quote: Reconcile every open commitment across the deal sheet, mail, and notes so no
issues.problem: This sentence is copied verbatim from quarterback-the-deal-team. The won-deal handoff also overlaps signature-to-launch-and-account-ops, and nothing states where one skill ends and the other begins.
issues.fix: State that this skill produces the sales-to-delivery packet and that signature-to-launch owns the launch plan from kickoff. Remove the duplicated reconciliation text or point to one shared rule.

issues.quote: Buyer outcome, key contacts with roles, what was promised (quoted, never
issues.problem: The packet leaves out fields a CS or implementation lead expects: commercial terms and special concessions, contract and renewal dates, success criteria and definition of done, technical environment, explicitly out-of-scope items, and a warm handoff meeting. It also has no escalation when a verbal promise exceeds the contract.
issues.fix: Extend the packet template with those fields and add a rule: a promise not in the signed scope is flagged to the owner and deal desk before the packet ships.

issues.quote: For a deal already gone quiet, write a short re-open instead: the last
issues.problem: The re-open is a single email. It has no cadence, no channel switch, no move to another thread (multithread skill), no no-oriented breakup ask, and no rule for when to mark the deal lost.
issues.fix: Add a 2-3 touch re-open sequence with a channel switch, a handoff to multithread-and-stakeholder-maps when the contact stays silent, and a close-out rule.

issues.quote: "handoff packet", "follow-up draft", "stalled deal"
issues.problem: 'follow-up draft' collides with draft-a-follow-up (the prospecting cadence), and 'stalled deal' is an exact trigger of quarterback-the-deal-team.
issues.fix: Use live-deal phrasing ('recap email after the call', 'deal went dark', 'sales-to-CS handoff') and drop the shared triggers.

issues.quote: on both calendars, and the buyer has homework due before it.
issues.problem: The model cannot see the buyer's calendar. The test needs a verification source or it becomes guesswork.
issues.fix: Check the user's Google Calendar via run_block for an accepted invite; otherwise ask the user and mark the test UNKNOWN.

issues.quote: Show the draft or packet in chat, then save it dated.
issues.problem: It gives no save location or format, and reconciling 'mail' assumes a connected inbox with no fallback.
issues.fix: Name the workspace path and file naming, and fall back to pasted threads when Gmail is not connected, listing which sources were not checked.

scenarios.prompt: Here is the transcript of my demo with Globex. We ended on 'let's reconnect in a couple of weeks'. Grade it and write the follow-up.
scenarios.why: 'Grade the next step' fails it on date, time, calendar and homework, then quotes the moment and writes the better closing line. 'Draft the follow-up' gives the subject line and an ordered 4-6 sentence body, using the buyer's words and nothing they did not agree to. That is senior-quality coaching plus an email.

scenarios.prompt: We closed Initech yesterday. Implementation needs the handoff today, half the promises were made on unrecorded calls, and our SE promised a custom SSO integration by Q1 that isn't in the order form.
scenarios.why: 'Build the handoff packet' quotes promises and reconciles commitments across the deal sheet, mail and notes, and the fallback names unowned loops. But nothing covers a verbal promise that exceeds the signed scope (escalate to the deal desk or legal, reset expectations with the buyer). Nothing covers unrecorded calls beyond reconciliation, and it has no Gmail fallback. 'What you hand back' also demands a four-test verdict that is irrelevant here.

objection-and-negotiation.job: handle sales objections and negotiate pricing
objection-and-negotiation.summary: Classifies a buyer objection, runs LAER to draft two short spoken responses ending in a question, builds a sourced pricing counter with an ask-in-return, tracks the paper process with dated owners, and offers a role-play drill.
strengths: Names the objection type before answering and uses LAER with one root-cause question, which is standard, teachable practice
Responses are short, spoken-length and end in a question that moves the deal
'Every number is FACT with a source or it stays out' and discounts are flagged for owner approval, never promised
The live drill (Max plays the buyer, grades the answer with one fix) is a useful coaching loop
missing: BATNA, walk-away and target price set before countering
Give-get trade matrix and concession sequencing
Procurement tactic recognition (claimed competitor offers, quarter-end pressure, 'standard discount')
Counsel and finance escalation for legal and payment terms
Routing of objection types to competitive, business-case and multithread skills
A template for the pricing counter

issues.quote: The ask line, a current-vs-proposal comparison with cited numbers only, the
issues.problem: The negotiation substance is missing: no BATNA or walk-away set first, no give-get trade list (term length, prepay, volume, case study, signature date), no rule of shrinking concessions, and no anchoring. 'The concession you want in return' is a single line.
issues.fix: Add a negotiation plan block: walk-away and target, a ranked give-get matrix inside the owner's bands, concession sequencing, and the trades to offer before any price move.

issues.quote: Missed dates get named with the slip
issues.problem: This section duplicates the paper-process tracks in enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans and quarterback-the-deal-team, down to the verbatim 'never carried forward as news', so three Max skills compete to own procurement.
issues.fix: Remove the paper-process track and route to enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans (or quarterback-the-deal-team) when procurement, legal or security steps are needed. Drop the 'procurement plan' trigger.

issues.quote: Name each step (security review, legal redlines, procurement sign-off), its
issues.problem: Legal redlines (liability caps, indemnity, data processing) and non-standard payment terms have no escalation path to counsel or finance.
issues.fix: State that liability, indemnity, data-protection and payment-term changes go to counsel or finance via a consult or handoff, with the buyer's markup attached.

issues.section: Name the kind, then run LAER
issues.quote: Name it first: price, timing, authority, competition, status quo, or terms.
issues.problem: The types are named, but nothing routes them: competition should pull the battlecard or competitive skill, status quo the business-case skill, and authority the multithread skill.
issues.fix: Add a one-line route per type to the sibling skill that holds the evidence (rfp-and-competitive-bid-response, business-case-and-roi-selling, multithread-and-stakeholder-maps).

issues.section: Name the kind, then run LAER
issues.quote: Never concede, discount, or promise terms inside a draft response.
issues.problem: The inputs ask for 'what the user is actually allowed to concede', but this line bans using it, while the persona says Max counters 'only inside the approval bands the owner gave you'. The skill contradicts itself on approved bands.
issues.fix: Allow counters inside owner-approved bands (logged with date), and require approval only outside them.

issues.section: Name the kind, then run LAER
issues.quote: objection without interrupting,
issues.problem: 'Listen without interrupting' and 'confirm the answer landed' are live-call behaviours the model cannot perform. As written they are instructions to the model, not coaching for the user.
issues.fix: Rephrase as coaching notes for the user on the live call, and have the model work from the buyer's verbatim words supplied up front.

issues.quote: "negotiation", "discount request", "competitor objection", "stall"
issues.problem: 'stall' collides with the stalled-deal triggers in next-step-and-handoff and quarterback-the-deal-team. 'negotiation' collides with the unassigned original negotiation skill.
issues.fix: Replace with specific phrases ('buyer pushback', 'they want a discount', 'price objection', 'procurement squeeze').

scenarios.prompt: The buyer says we're 30% more expensive than Competitor X and asked if we can match. I can go to 10% off at most. How do I respond?
scenarios.why: 'Name the kind, then run LAER' classifies it as price or competition, explores the root cause and drafts two sub-30-second responses ending in a question. 'Build the pricing counter' uses a sourced comparison and names the concession wanted in return, and the discount is flagged for approval. A capable model would produce a good talk track, though the give-get is a single line and it does not use the user's 10% band.

scenarios.prompt: Procurement wants a 25% 'standard' discount, net-90 terms and uncapped liability, and claims the competitor already agreed. My VP hasn't set approval bands and signature is due Friday for quarter-end.
scenarios.why: The fallback drafts a hold line and flags the approval need, and the paper-process track dates the steps. Nothing covers procurement tactics (claimed competitor concessions, quarter-end leverage), trading terms against price, a walk-away point, or sending liability and indemnity redlines to counsel. The model would stall at 'flag for approval' rather than prepare the negotiation plan a senior AE would bring to the VP.

partner-and-channel-co-sell.summary: Writes a joint co-sell play in a shared schema (trigger, ICP overlap, value story, land motion, dual owners, target accounts, exit criteria), splits the work, runs a most-stuck-first partner standup with joint metrics, and stages partner-facing drafts for approval.
strengths: A single joint-play schema both sides can run, with an exec sponsor named on each side
'A split nobody agreed to is a draft, never presented as agreed' is a sharp guardrail
Joint metrics (sourced pipe, co-sell win rate, partner-attached revenue) are graded from sources only, and the fallback reconciles two exports with each number's source labelled
Never commits partner resources or discounts inside a draft
missing: Deal registration, rules of engagement and channel-conflict resolution
Partner economics (margin, discount stacking, referral fees, MDF) and motion type
Data-sharing, NDA and antitrust guard for account mapping
Close-stage mechanics (order path, credit and booking)
Metric definitions for sourced vs influenced
Boundary with Anika's partner skills and routing to them
Joint play template

issues.problem: Deal registration and rules of engagement are absent: registration eligibility and state, conflict check, first-to-register or protection window, what happens when direct and partner both claim a deal. These are the core co-sell mechanics.
issues.fix: Add a 'Register and de-conflict' step before the split: check or submit registration, cite the program's rules, run the conflict check and log the ruling. Route program-level registration hygiene to Anika's run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence.

issues.quote: overlap, value story, land motion, owners one per side, target account
issues.problem: Building ICP overlap and a joint target list means exchanging account and customer data with a third party. The skill has no NDA or data-sharing check and no minimum-data or antitrust caution.
issues.fix: Require a confirmed NDA or data-sharing agreement before any account list leaves, share only overlap outputs or minimum fields, and send exceptions to legal.

issues.quote: Split the work plainly: who sources, who technical-wins, who owns paper,
issues.problem: The split ignores motion type (resell, referral, influence, marketplace) and partner economics (margin, discount stacking, referral fee, MDF, rebates). These decide who holds paper and what the deal is worth.
issues.fix: Add the motion type and economics to the play schema, keeping every figure FACT from the partner agreement or flagged for owner approval. Route marketplace deals to cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling.

issues.quote: "co-sell", "partner deal", "channel partner", "joint plan"
issues.problem: It overlaps Anika's run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence (standup, stuck joint deals) and scale-the-partner-channel. Within Max it also overlaps alliance-co-commercialization and cloud-commit-and-marketplace-selling, and it states no boundary.
issues.fix: State the scope as deal-level co-sell from the AE seat, and hand program, cadence and registration operations to Anika via consult_teammate or handoff. Tighten the triggers to deal-level phrasing.

issues.quote: co-sell win rate, partner-attached revenue) from ledger numbers only.
issues.problem: 'Ledger' is never defined. The metrics also lack definitions (partner-sourced vs partner-influenced attribution), so two sides will count the same deal differently.
issues.fix: Define each metric and its attribution rule, and name the source (CRM export, partner portal, shared sheet).

issues.quote: Run the partner standup like the deal-team pulse
issues.problem: This relies on a concept ('deal-team pulse') defined only in another skill, so a model that loaded only this skill has to guess.
issues.fix: Spell out the standup format inline or point explicitly to quarterback-the-deal-team.

issues.quote: from joint plan to joint close
issues.problem: The description promises the flow through to joint close, but the body has no close-stage steps: partner paper or order flow, distributor quote and PO, and who books the revenue.
issues.fix: Add a close step: order path, quote ownership, booking and credit, and the handoff to delivery.

issues.quote: Show the play and the read in chat, take one round
issues.problem: 'Saved to file' has no path or template, so the joint play will not be reusable across partners.
issues.fix: Ship templates/joint-co-sell-play.md and name the workspace location.

scenarios.prompt: We're co-selling a $150K deal into Initech with our SI partner Northwind. Set up the joint plan and who does what.
scenarios.why: 'The joint play' and 'Split the work' produce a usable schema with dual owners, sponsors and a sourcing/tech-win/paper/renewal split, and the drafts are staged. But nothing tells the model to register the deal, confirm the motion (resell, referral or influence), or settle margin or fees. The plan would look complete while missing what usually breaks co-sell deals.

scenarios.prompt: Two resellers both claim the Globex account, our own rep also sourced it, the partner wants 20% margin plus MDF, and they want our customer list to map the overlap.
scenarios.why: The skill has no deal registration, conflict or first-to-register rule, no partner economics or MDF guidance, and no data-sharing or confidentiality guard for handing over a customer list. The only relevant line is 'Never commit the partner's resources or your own discounts inside a draft', so the model would improvise channel conflict and could propose sharing customer data.

pipeline-review-and-forecast.job: review pipeline and grade sales forecast
pipeline-review-and-forecast.summary: Reads the user's CRM view or export to report stage counts, movement, coverage against quota, the five oldest stuck deals and pacing, grades each deal commit/best case/pipeline/omitted on qualification evidence, flags hygiene breaks, and stages paste-ready next-step updates.
strengths: Separates the pipeline review (move deals) from the forecast review (defend the number)
'Anything untraceable is UNKNOWN, never estimated', with a fallback that names the checks it could not run
Every hygiene flag carries one fix and one owner, and CRM updates are staged as paste-ready text, never applied
Off-cycle review triggers (a third close-date move, a top-five deal leaving commit) are a senior touch
missing: Weighted vs rep-called forecast kept apart, with the gap explained
Close-date push history and forecast accuracy tracking
Data-quality check (as-of date, currency, missing fields, duplicates)
Stored snapshot for week-over-week movement
Win-rate-derived coverage bar consistent with the persona
Report template (sections and table layout)

issues.quote: over quota — flag under 3x, alarm under 2x — the oldest stuck five
issues.problem: A flat coverage multiple contradicts Max's own Monday inspection routine, which requires a win-rate-derived segment bar ('never a flat multiple', enterprise typically 4-6x). The same expert gives two different answers to 'is my coverage OK?'.
issues.fix: Compute the bar as 1 / historical win rate on qualified pipeline per segment (bash_exec). Fall back to a labelled default only when no history exists.

issues.quote: Commit, best case, pipeline, or omitted per deal, with the
issues.problem: There is no forecast method beyond categories. It has no weighted figure alongside the rep-called number, no close-date push history, no backward funnel math from commit, and no tracking of forecast accuracy across calls.
issues.fix: Add a rollup that keeps weighted (stated stage probabilities) and called figures apart, shows the gap and its driving deals, and questions any pushed close date before it counts as commit.

issues.quote: The CRM view or export they trust, their quota, their commit style,
issues.problem: It has no data-quality pass before reporting: as-of date, currency, duplicates, deals missing amount, close date or owner, and past-dated close dates. Messy exports are the norm, and totals will be wrong without this.
issues.fix: Add a 'Check the data' step: record the as-of date and currency, list broken records and keep them marked in the count, and never combine currencies without an owner-supplied rate.

issues.quote: Counts by stage, movement since last review, coverage as open pipe
issues.problem: 'Movement since last review' assumes a stored prior snapshot, but the skill never says to save one, so the first and every later run cannot compute movement reliably.
issues.fix: Save a dated snapshot (workspace file or memory_store) at the end of each run, and on first run say movement starts from this baseline.

issues.quote: Stale next steps, deals with no activity in 14 days, single-threaded
issues.problem: 'No activity' counts seller activity, which hides stalls. The persona defines stuck as no buyer-owned commitment in 14-21 days.
issues.fix: Define staleness as no buyer-side action or commitment, not seller activity, and align the window with the persona.

issues.quote: "commit", "quota pacing", "CRM hygiene"
issues.problem: 'CRM hygiene' is also a trigger of sales-ops-coverage-and-quota, and the skill overlaps Max's Monday and Wednesday inspection routines without saying which owns team-level inspection.
issues.fix: Scope this to the individual book (with team inspection in the routine or in sales-team-leadership) and leave CRM hygiene at scale to sales-ops.

issues.quote: must-have letters and best-case deals with no dated next step.
issues.problem: 'Must-have letters' refers to the framework defined in discovery-and-qualification, which is not named here, so the rule is opaque when this skill loads alone.
issues.fix: Name the framework (MEDDICC/MEDDPICC/SPICED from the user's memory) and point to discovery-and-qualification.

issues.quote: No CRM access: review from their export or pasted numbers and say
issues.problem: It has no tool routing: it never mentions the HubSpot block or connect_integration for a live read, or bash_exec for the stage, coverage and pacing arithmetic.
issues.fix: Check for a connected CRM first (run_block HubSpot or an MCP), offer connect_integration once, and do all totals in bash_exec with the formula shown.

scenarios.prompt: Here's my HubSpot export for Q3 and my quota is $1.2M. Give me the honest read on my pipeline and forecast.
scenarios.why: 'Report the book' yields stage counts, coverage, the five oldest stuck deals with stall ages and pacing. 'Grade the forecast' tags each deal with its evidence, 'Name the hygiene breaks' pairs each flag with a fix and an owner, and the next steps come back paste-ready. A capable model produces a useful read, though the flat 3x coverage bar may misjudge an enterprise book.

scenarios.prompt: Forecast call in an hour. The export mixes USD and EUR, 40% of deals have no close date, there's no previous snapshot, and my manager wants a commit number.
scenarios.why: 'Anything untraceable is UNKNOWN' and the no-quota fallback help, and 'commit calls wait for your yes' keeps Max from calling the number. But the skill has no data-quality triage step, no currency rule, and nothing for 'movement since last review' when no prior snapshot exists. It gives no method for building a defensible commit (weighted vs called, push history). The original sales-forecast-rollup handles this case better.

recruiting-getting-started.job: set up hiring process for new role
recruiting-getting-started.summary: Sets out a seven-step fair-hiring sequence (outcome, must-haves, job description, rubric, interview mapping, independent scoring, comms ownership), captures owners and decision rights, adds a fairness guard, and returns a one-page hiring plan.
strengths: Captures decision rights up front and refuses to assume authority from a title ('Unknown owners remain open').
Correct ordering: must-have vs learnable split and rubric before any candidate is read; independent scores before the debrief.
The fairness guard names concrete proxies (graduation year, employment gap, accent, school prestige) and replaces 'culture fit' with behaviour that can be observed.
Clear rule that a human decides, consistent with Harper's persona boundaries.
missing: first-run memory of owners, approvers, policies and tooling
stage timeline with SLAs and target dates
posting/sourcing and resume-screening stages
routing to the sibling skill for each step
jurisdiction checklist incl. pay transparency and AI-in-hiring notice, routed to counsel
hiring-plan template and pipeline tracker
interviewer training and calibration step
candidate communication cadence and privacy notice

issues.quote: Use this when a team opens a role or has no written hiring process.
issues.problem: This is Harper's getting-started skill, yet it never checks memory for, or saves, lasting hiring preferences (owners, approval chain, local policies, ATS, message templates, retention rules). Every new role repeats intake, and later skills cannot find the answers.
issues.fix: Add a first-run branch: memory_search for a saved hiring setup; ask_question for the gaps in one batch; memory_store owners, approvers, policies, tooling and templates; then show a 'what I can do today' menu.

issues.quote: Draft the job description and have the owner approve it.
issues.problem: Steps 1-7 repeat what role-intake-and-job-description, hiring-rubric-design, interview-plan-and-scorecard and the candidate-* skills do, without naming them. The model tends to do every stage inline at checklist depth instead of loading the deeper skill.
issues.fix: Name the sibling skill for each step (e.g. 'Step 3: load role-intake-and-job-description') and keep this skill as the router and owner of the plan.

issues.quote: Ask which local policy, employment rules, accommodation process, and data-retention rules the company follows. Record them; do not invent them.
issues.problem: No fallback when the user does not know and no escalation target. It also does not prompt the checks a 2026 recruiter expects: pay-range posting rules, a candidate privacy notice, and whether AI-assisted screening triggers notice or bias-audit duties (e.g. NYC Local Law 144, EU AI Act).
issues.fix: Ship a list of jurisdiction questions marked 'confirm with counsel/people lead'. Record each as open with an owner, and hand off to the People Ops expert when no policy owner exists.

issues.quote: A one-page hiring plan with role outcome, stages, owners, criteria, evidence sources, decision rights, open approvals, and candidate communication points.
issues.problem: No dates, stage SLAs (feedback within 24h, how often candidates get updates), target counts per stage or tracker, and no template ships. The plan cannot be run or checked against progress.
issues.fix: Add templates/hiring-plan.md with a stage table (stage, owner, entry/exit criteria, SLA, target date) and save it to the workspace; offer a Google Sheets tracker via run_block.

issues.quote: Build the scored rubric before reading candidates.
issues.problem: The sequence leaves out the posting/sourcing and resume-screen stages, so channels, slate breadth and resume-screening never appear in the plan.
issues.fix: Insert 'post and source (consult Sofia for sourcing if she is on the team)' and 'screen against the rubric (resume-screening)' between steps 4 and 5.

issues.quote: new open role
issues.problem: Almost the same as role-intake-and-job-description's 'open a role' trigger, so the two skills compete for the same request.
issues.fix: Keep plan/process phrasing here ('hiring plan', 'set up our hiring process', 'first hire') and leave role/JD phrasing to role intake.

scenarios.prompt: We just got headcount for a Senior Backend Engineer. Can you set up the hiring process so we can start next week?
scenarios.why: The model records owners, walks the seven steps, asks about local policy and produces a sensible one-page plan. But the output has no dates or stage SLAs. The sequence jumps from JD to rubric to interviews with no posting, sourcing or resume-screen stage. Nothing routes to role-intake-and-job-description or hiring-rubric-design, so the result is a checklist, not a dated plan with owners.

scenarios.prompt: I'm the founder of a 12-person startup with no HR. I need 5 support reps split between Austin and Manila in 4 weeks. I don't know what rules apply, just give me a process.
scenarios.why: The fairness guard and 'do not invent them' keep it safe. But the policy step only says to ask and record. When the founder doesn't know, there is no fallback: no checklist to take to counsel or an EOR, and no handoff to People Ops. There is also no adaptation for volume hiring, no flags for two jurisdictions (pay-range posting, notice of AI-assisted screening), and no guidance when one person holds every owner role.

hiring-rubric-design.job: define role criteria and scoring rubric
hiring-rubric-design.summary: Derives four to seven job-related criteria from approved role outcomes, each with an evidence source, a 1-4 observable anchor, a confirming question or work sample and a scorer, plus a 'not assessed' rule and a list of disallowed signals.
strengths: Keeps 'not assessed' separate from a score of one, so a resume that omits a criterion is not penalised. This is a senior, bias-reducing rule.
Each criterion carries an evidence source, an anchor, a confirming question or work sample, and a scorer, so the rubric can drive screening and interviews.
Specific disallowed signals (employer prestige, gaps, accents, likability); a communication criterion must name the work product and the level.
Very tight, with no filler.
missing: pass/fail minimum requirements separate from scored criteria
version/freeze and re-score rule
saved artifact location and approval record
weighting and evidence-bar guidance
calibration against sample profiles or past hires
example of anchors written for a specific level
adverse-impact review of the criteria
worked example rubric

issues.problem: resume-screening, interview-plan-and-scorecard and candidate-interview-debrief all require 'the approved rubric', yet this skill never says where to save it, how to mark it approved, or how a later session finds it.
issues.fix: Write the rubric to the workspace (e.g. hiring/<role>/rubric-v1.md) with approver and date, and memory_store a pointer and its approval status for the downstream skills.

issues.quote: Derive four to seven criteria from the approved role outcomes.
issues.problem: Inputs are not named up front and there is no fallback when approved outcomes are missing. Pass/fail requirements (licence, work authorisation, required certification) are not separated from scored competencies, and role intake's must-have/learnable split is not used.
issues.fix: Name the inputs; if there are no approved outcomes, route to role-intake-and-job-description; add a separate yes/no 'minimum requirements' block with its evidence source.

issues.quote: Build the rubric before reading a resume.
issues.problem: No change control. Nothing freezes and versions the rubric once screening starts or re-scores earlier candidates when a criterion changes, which is where inconsistent treatment usually creeps in.
issues.fix: Add a rule: once screening begins, any edit creates v2, needs owner approval, and triggers re-scoring of all prior candidates.

issues.quote: weight or equal-weight choice
issues.problem: No guidance on choosing weights or defining the evidence bar the owner approves before screening, so people fall back on gut feel at decision time.
issues.fix: Default to equal weights, require any weights to be set and approved before screening, and have the owner state the minimum evidence profile (e.g. no 1 on a must-have).

issues.quote: A four means clear evidence at greater scope with a stated result.
issues.problem: The generic anchors are not calibrated to the role's level, and 'stated result' rewards candidates who put numbers on their own resumes.
issues.fix: Require behavioural anchors written per criterion for this level, and note that results can be confirmed at interview rather than read off the resume.

issues.quote: Do not score protected traits or proxies.
issues.problem: It lists signals not to score but never checks the criteria themselves for adverse impact (degree requirements, years-of-experience ranges, continuous employment, 'native speaker').
issues.fix: Add a criteria check: each requirement cites its work need; flag degree, years and language rules for owner review.

issues.quote: score candidates
issues.problem: A user who says 'score these candidates' wants resume-screening or a debrief, not rubric design, so this trigger misroutes.
issues.fix: Replace it with 'build a hiring rubric', 'define hiring criteria', or 'what should we assess for this role'.

scenarios.prompt: Here's the JD for our Customer Success Manager role. Build me a scoring rubric before we start screening.
scenarios.why: The model derives criteria from the JD outcomes, fills the five fields per criterion, applies the 1-4 scale and the not-assessed rule, lists disallowed signals and adds an owner approval line. A capable model produces a usable rubric table.

scenarios.prompt: We already screened 40 resumes informally. The hiring manager wants a rubric that captures what we liked about the top five, weighted toward Ivy League degrees and culture fit, and it needs to be done today.
scenarios.why: The disallowed-signal list lets the model refuse school prestige and culture fit. But there is no guidance on rubrics built after the fact (working backwards from favoured candidates), no rule to re-screen all 40 against the new version, and no job-related replacement for 'culture fit' in this skill.

interview-plan-and-scorecard.job: design structured interview loop and scorecards
interview-plan-and-scorecard.summary: Maps each approved rubric criterion to one interviewer and one evidence method, sets out good evidence, follow-ups and exclusions for each question, and defines an independent 1-4 scorecard with a not-assessed option.
strengths: Same core questions and time for every candidate, with follow-ups only to clarify. That is the core of structured interviewing.
For each question: what good evidence looks like, the probe that tests ownership and scope, and what must not be scored.
Interviewers submit before seeing peer scores; a gut-feel overall score and notes on protected traits are banned; a not-assessed option exists.
Accommodation note with a named owner and no medical details; no invites or calendar changes without approval.
missing: fallback when there is no approved rubric
two independent signals for must-have criteria
prohibited question topics and salary-history note
time cap, pay and IP policy for work samples
loop order and total candidate time
interviewer prep packet and calibration
scorecard due time and chasers
contents of the candidate information note
template or example kit

issues.quote: Use an approved hiring rubric as the source.
issues.problem: No instruction for when the rubric is missing or not yet approved, so the model either stalls or invents criteria.
issues.fix: Add: if there is no approved rubric, load hiring-rubric-design first and never build questions against unapproved criteria.

issues.quote: Map every criterion to one primary interviewer and one evidence method
issues.problem: With one rater per criterion there is no independent second signal on must-have criteria. It also conflicts with candidate-interview-debrief, which flags score gaps between interviewers on the same criterion.
issues.fix: Require two independent signals (different interviewers or methods) for must-have criteria and one for the rest, and show the coverage matrix.

issues.quote: For each question, state what good evidence looks like, what follow-up tests ownership or scope, and what must not be scored.
issues.problem: It covers what not to score but not what must not be asked: family plans, age, religion, health, citizenship beyond work authorisation, and salary history where banned. These are interviewers' most common legal risk.
issues.fix: Add a list of prohibited topics to the interviewer brief, plus a lawful work-authorisation question.

issues.quote: structured question, work sample, portfolio review, or reference check if company policy allows it
issues.problem: No limits on work samples (time cap, same task for everyone, paid or unpaid, who owns the candidate's work) and no timing or consent rule for reference checks.
issues.fix: Cap take-homes (e.g. 2-3 hours, or pay for longer ones), give everyone the same task, state IP handling, and run references only late-stage with the candidate's consent.

issues.quote: Keep the same core questions and time for each candidate.
issues.problem: No loop design: stage order, slot length, total candidate time, interviewer prep brief or remote logistics.
issues.fix: Add a loop table (slot, criterion, method, interviewer, minutes) with a total-time budget, plus a prep packet for each interviewer.

issues.quote: Require interviewers to submit it before seeing peer scores.
issues.problem: No submission deadline or chase, so scorecards arrive late and the debrief is argued from memory.
issues.fix: Set a due time (e.g. within 24 hours) and draft reminders for the coordinator.

issues.quote: Do not invite candidates or change calendars without approval.
issues.problem: The approval gate exists, but there is no path after approval (Google Calendar or Gmail blocks, or handing off to a coordinator) and no instruction to save the kit where the debrief can find it.
issues.fix: Save the kit to the workspace or Drive and, once approved, create invites through run_block or hand them to whoever does scheduling.

scenarios.prompt: Using the approved rubric for our Product Designer role, build the interview loop and scorecards for our four interviewers.
scenarios.why: The model maps criteria to interviewers and methods, writes a question bank with good-evidence, follow-up and not-scored notes, defines the scorecard fields, and adds the accommodation note. The output list is clear.

scenarios.prompt: We don't have a rubric yet. The hiring manager wants a 5-hour take-home plus six interviews, two interviewers only have 20 minutes each, and a candidate has asked for extra time because of dyslexia.
scenarios.why: The accommodation handling is right (named person, no medical details). But beyond 'Use an approved hiring rubric' there is no fallback for the missing rubric. There is no guidance on total candidate time or on whether a 5-hour take-home is proportionate or paid, and no method for reshaping the loop around interviewer availability.

candidate-interview-debrief.job: synthesize interview scorecards into debrief record
candidate-interview-debrief.summary: Builds a per-criterion evidence table from submitted scorecards with score gaps flagged, sorts notes into confirmed, conflicting, missing and excluded, strips protected-trait and 'not a fit' comments, and records the named human decision-maker and their rationale.
strengths: Refuses new criteria and impressions that cannot name observed evidence; 'not a fit' must map to a criterion or it is excluded.
No hidden overall score; gaps of two or more points are shown with the evidence on each side.
Four-way sort (confirmed, conflicting, missing, excluded) and a list of process risks (missed question, unequal work sample).
Records the named decision-maker and their rationale, and marks either one 'needs human confirmation' when it is not supplied.
missing: handling of missing or late scorecards, with chasers
private escalation of discriminatory remarks
meeting order that resists anchoring, and a path for ties
decision record template with date and retention
routing to the rejection or offer skill after the decision
input sources and fallback
feedback to interviewers on weak scorecards

issues.quote: Remove protected-trait data and proxies from the decision record.
issues.problem: A remark about pregnancy, age or religion is a compliance incident. Removing it silently hides it from the people lead and leaves that interviewer's other scores unquestioned.
issues.fix: Note the removal in one line without repeating the remark, flag it privately to the people lead (or the People Ops expert), and ask whether that scorecard still stands.

issues.quote: Use only submitted scorecards tied to the approved rubric.
issues.problem: No rule for missing or late scorecards, feedback that arrives as free text in Slack or email, or scorecards edited after discussion. The most common real debrief state is not handled.
issues.fix: Check who has filed; list criteria with no written evidence; draft chasers; suggest postponing if must-have criteria are uncovered; keep the original of any edited scorecard.

issues.quote: Give the panel the unresolved questions first, then the evidence table, then process risks such as a missed question or unequal work sample.
issues.problem: No meeting order that resists anchoring (scores locked before talk, junior voices first, hiring manager last), no timebox, and no path for a tied panel.
issues.fix: Add a short facilitation script and state that a tied panel goes back to the named decision-maker.

issues.quote: Return the evidence summary and open questions.
issues.problem: The output leaves out the decision record and process risks described above, and gives no template, save location or retention note. It does not route to candidate-rejection-email or candidate-offer-draft after the human decides.
issues.fix: List the outputs (evidence table, open questions, process risks, decision record with decider, decision, rationale and date), save them to the role folder, and name the next skill.

issues.quote: interview feedback
issues.problem: Also matches requests to write feedback for the candidate, which belongs to candidate-rejection-email.
issues.fix: Use 'panel feedback', 'collate interviewer feedback' or 'where did the panel land'.

issues.problem: No input guidance: where scorecards come from (ATS via MCP, Google Forms or Sheets via run_block, pasted text) or what to do when only a paste is available.
issues.fix: Add an inputs line listing the sources, with a paste or CSV fallback.

scenarios.prompt: All four scorecards are in for Priya's onsite for the Data Analyst role. Pull together the debrief.
scenarios.why: The model builds the per-criterion table (scores, cited evidence, confidence), flags gaps of two or more, fills the four buckets, puts unresolved questions first and adds the decision-maker line.

scenarios.prompt: Only two of four scorecards are in. The hiring manager's notes are a Slack message: 'strong yes, great vibe, reminds me of me'. Another interviewer wrote she 'might not be committed since she just had a baby'. The HM wants your recommendation by 3pm.
scenarios.why: It correctly refuses to recommend, excludes 'great vibe' and removes the pregnancy remark. But nothing says to chase the two missing scorecards or list the criteria they leave uncovered, or to ask the HM to file a real scorecard. The discriminatory remark is simply deleted, not flagged to the people lead with a question about that interviewer's other scores.

candidate-rejection-email.summary: Drafts an unsent rejection email after a confirmed human decision: the decision comes first, the thanks are specific, and only feedback the owner approved is used.
strengths: Only drafts once the decision and stage are confirmed; Harper never decides who is rejected.
Decision stated in the first two sentences, with thanks for the specific time or work rather than generic claims.
Feedback only if the owner approved it verbatim, kept job-related and no broader than the evidence; no 'better candidate' line unless approved.
Covers late-stage expenses and work-sample handling; never sends; never exposes panel notes or legal conclusions.
missing: call-first talking points for final-round and internal candidates
batch decline mode with merge fields
talent-pool consent and retention notice
proxy-language check on approved feedback
stage templates or examples
send timing
escalation path for replies and complaints

issues.quote: For late-stage candidates, include the approved contact and next step for expenses or work-sample handling if applicable.
issues.problem: Final-round and internal candidates usually hear by phone first. The skill treats them as email-only, which reads as cold after a long process.
issues.fix: For final-round or internal candidates, draft call talking points for the decision-maker first, then a short follow-up email.

issues.quote: Do not promise future contact.
issues.problem: This blanket rule blocks a common, legitimate talent-pool invitation, and the skill says nothing about consent to keep the CV or the retention period (GDPR, UK GDPR and similar laws).
issues.fix: Allow a talent-pool line the owner has approved that asks for consent and states the retention period from company policy; otherwise use no future-contact language.

issues.quote: Get the candidate's chosen name, role title, stage, approved sender, whether the company permits feedback
issues.problem: Assumes one candidate at a time. Early-stage declines usually come in batches and need a stage template, merge fields, a check that each row has a confirmed decision, and one approval for the batch.
issues.fix: Add a batch mode: a template plus a CSV of confirmed decisions, a spot-checked sample, and one approval that lists every recipient.

issues.quote: If approved feedback exists, state it in job-related terms and no more broadly than the evidence supports.
issues.problem: Nothing checks that the approved feedback is itself safe; phrases like 'overqualified', 'not a culture fit' or 'energy' can stand in for age or other protected traits.
issues.fix: If approved feedback contains proxy language, return it to the owner with a job-related rewording before drafting.

issues.quote: Return an unsent draft plus an approval line naming the decision-maker and sender.
issues.problem: No stage templates or example, and no expectation for when it goes out (e.g. within a few business days of the decision).
issues.fix: Ship three short stage templates (after screen, after interview, after final round) and state the send-by window.

issues.problem: No path when the candidate replies asking for feedback or alleging unfair treatment.
issues.fix: Route replies to the decision-maker; send any allegation to the people lead or counsel without drafting a substantive response.

issues.quote: candidate decline
issues.problem: Also means a candidate declining an offer, which is a different workflow.
issues.fix: Use 'decline a candidate' or 'turn down an applicant'.

scenarios.prompt: Dana confirmed we're not moving forward with Jordan after the phone screen for the Account Manager role. Can you draft the rejection?
scenarios.why: The model collects the name, stage, sender and whether feedback is allowed, then drafts: decision first, specific thanks, no invented feedback, plain subject, approval line. It stays unsent.

scenarios.prompt: Draft rejections for the 45 applicants who didn't pass the resume screen, and one for Sam, who did a 4-hour take-home and the final round. The hiring manager says to tell Sam he 'wasn't senior enough and we went with someone stronger', and we want everyone in our talent pool.
scenarios.why: Once the owner has approved the comparative line it is allowed, and the feedback is kept job-related. But there is no batch or merge approach and no single approval for the batch, and no advice to call Sam first. 'Do not promise future contact' blocks the talent-pool request without offering a consent-based alternative, and there is no retention or privacy notice.

candidate-offer-draft.job: draft job offer letter from approved terms
candidate-offer-draft.summary: Collects a full list of approved offer terms, marks missing ones [OWNER TO CONFIRM], and drafts an offer email, a templated offer document and an internal approval checklist, without negotiating or sending.
strengths: Complete list of required terms (legal entity, pay period, currency, contingencies, response date, signatory, template clauses).
Missing terms are marked [OWNER TO CONFIRM]; nothing is inferred from other candidates, market data or earlier drafts.
Three useful deliverables, including an internal approval checklist listing each term and its approver.
Clear gate: never negotiate, promise, send, sign or record acceptance, and any change needs fresh written approval.
missing: fallback when there is no template
consistency check across documents and against the pay range
flags for contingency order (fair-chance checks, right to work)
verbal-offer talking points
follow-up before the offer expires
onboarding handoff
confidential storage of drafts
example offer email

issues.quote: the offer document using the supplied template;
issues.problem: Many small companies have no offer template. With legal wording forbidden, the model has no path and either stalls or improvises binding text.
issues.fix: If there is no template, produce a plain term sheet marked 'not an offer letter — counsel to supply binding text', ask for a template, and hand off to the people lead or counsel.

issues.quote: an internal approval checklist with each term and approver.
issues.problem: Nothing checks that the email, the document and the approval record match (annual vs per-period pay, currency, equity units vs %, start date on a working day, response date after send date), or that pay sits within the approved or posted range.
issues.fix: Add a check before returning drafts (use bash_exec for the arithmetic) that lists every mismatch, and any pay outside the posted range, as a blocking item.

issues.quote: benefits source, contingencies, response date, signatory
issues.problem: Contingencies are collected but not checked. Criminal-history checks often must follow a conditional offer under fair-chance laws, and work authorisation must be in place before the start date.
issues.fix: Flag background-check and right-to-work contingencies to the people lead or counsel with the jurisdiction, without stating the law.

issues.quote: Use only after an authorised person approves the candidate and provides the offer terms.
issues.problem: Stops at the letter: no verbal-offer talking points for the manager, no follow-up before the offer expires, and no handoff to onboarding once a human records acceptance.
issues.fix: Add optional drafts: verbal-offer notes, a follow-up before the response date, and an onboarding handoff note.

issues.problem: No guidance on keeping pay confidential or where to store drafts (workspace, or Google Docs via run_block), or on keeping pay details out of shared channels.
issues.fix: Save drafts to a restricted folder for the role and keep compensation out of group messages.

scenarios.prompt: Maria's offer is approved: $142k base, 0.1% options, start Nov 3, reporting to Lee. Draft the letter and email using our attached template.
scenarios.why: The model collects the terms, marks legal entity, pay period, benefits source, contingencies, response date and signatory as [OWNER TO CONFIRM], drafts all three items and holds them for review.

scenarios.prompt: Draft an offer for our first hire in Germany. We don't have a template, the CEO says 'pay about what the last engineer got, maybe a bit more', and we want a background check and a start date before the visa is sorted.
scenarios.why: It correctly refuses to infer pay from another hire and avoids immigration wording. But 'using the supplied template' has no fallback, so the model must stall or improvise legal text. Right-to-work and background-check timing are not flagged, and there is no handoff to counsel, an EOR or People Ops for a first hire in a new country.

finance-board-and-investor-reporting.job: prepare board pack and investor update
finance-board-and-investor-reporting.summary: Guides drafting a board pack, investor update, monthly flash note and post-meeting recap: a graded KPI scorecard, a said/are/moved/next narrative spine, red-teamed metric definitions, slide text in chat before building in Google Docs/Sheets, an asks section, and a drafts-only gate.
strengths: The narrative spine (where we said we'd be, where we are, what moved, what's next) is the right board framing.
Red-teams denominators, periods and cohorts against the prior pack and flags definition changes openly, with no silent restatement.
Drafts slide text in chat before building the layout, and verifies every chart against its source before delivery.
Closes with an asks section (decision, owner, date) and a 24-hour recap whose forecast changes feed the reforecast.
The approval gate is clear: nothing reaches a board member, investor or auditor without the owner's yes.
missing: Board pack section template and investor update template shipped as files
Bad-news-first framing guidance and how to present a miss with a recovery plan
Confidentiality and disclosure checklist (board-only vs investor versions, customer-name consent, counsel routing)
Tie-out check so the deck, investor update and finance summary agree for the same cutoff
Cash, runway and financial statements as standing pack sections
Routing to sibling skills for the numbers (cash, variance, SaaS bridge)
A note that the recap is not the official board minutes
A worked example of a graded scorecard row

issues.section: Grade every KPI against its band
issues.quote: the scorecard at the same three or four annual metrics.
issues.problem: This confuses the flash note's 3-4 fixed metrics with the board scorecard. Boards expect 6-10 fixed KPIs plus P&L, cash and runway. It also conflicts with the next section, which adds NRR, ARR, churn and Rule of 40 on top.
issues.fix: Keep the flash at 3-4 fixed metrics. Define the board scorecard as 6-10 KPIs fixed for the year, graded against bands, with financial statements and runway as standing sections.

issues.quote: close is not done, say so in one line rather than offering a
issues.problem: This contradicts Fallbacks ('No closed books: build from the flash and label every number preliminary'). The model gets opposite instructions for the most common deadline situation.
issues.fix: Give one rule: if the user asks for a pack before close, build from the flash with every figure labelled PRELIMINARY. The routine reminder alone waits for the close-done signal.

issues.section: Draft the text first, then the pack
issues.quote: Distribute the pack and the agenda at
issues.problem: This is an imperative to distribute, which conflicts with the approval gate ('You never message a board member'). It is unclear who sends and when.
issues.fix: Reword to: 'Remind the owner that the pack and agenda should reach the board 48 hours ahead; stage the cover email as a draft for their yes.'

issues.quote: Sequence subscription metrics deliberately: net revenue retention
issues.problem: This hard-codes a SaaS-only sequence (NRR before ARR scale, which is unconventional) for an expert who serves any revenue model. It also recomputes metrics that saas-gtm-finance owns.
issues.fix: Make the sequence conditional on the revenue model and source ARR, NRR and Rule of 40 from saas-gtm-finance rather than recomputing them here.

issues.quote: 40 — revenue growth % plus margin %, at or above 40.
issues.problem: The margin type is undefined (saas-gtm-finance uses EBITDA margin, others use FCF), so the figure can disagree with the sibling skill. Rule of 40 is also not meaningful for very early-stage companies.
issues.fix: Name the margin basis to match saas-gtm-finance, and include Rule of 40 only once growth and margin are both meaningful.

issues.problem: The skill says a board pack and an investor update are different documents but gives no section list for either and ships no template. Output shape will vary run to run.
issues.fix: Add templates/board-pack.md (exec summary, scorecard, financials vs plan, cash/runway, pipeline/ARR, risks, asks, appendix) and templates/investor-update.md (summary, metrics, wins, misses, cash, asks, confidentiality note).

issues.problem: There are no confidentiality or disclosure rules: board-confidential material, naming customers without consent, selective disclosure to some investors, and routing securities or governance questions to counsel.
issues.fix: Add a disclosure check before any draft is marked ready: audience permitted, customer names cleared, board-only items stripped from investor versions, and counsel named for securities questions.

issues.quote: The period close or flash, the KPI set with its bands, and the prior
issues.problem: The inputs omit the cash/runway view and the variance read, and the body never routes to sibling skills. The model will recompute rather than reuse those reads.
issues.fix: List the cash-treasury-and-fx runway, the variance-and-flux read and the saas-gtm-finance bridge as inputs, loaded from their skills.

scenarios.prompt: August is closed. Build the Q3 board pack from the ledger sheet and last quarter's pack in Drive, and draft the asks section.
scenarios.why: Following the order (audience, graded scorecard, narrative spine, red-team against the prior pack, text in chat, Docs/Sheets build on approval, asks) gives a sourced, graded draft. But the scorecard is capped at 'the same three or four annual metrics'. No section list covers P&L, balance sheet, cash and runway, and no step pulls runway from cash-treasury-and-fx or drivers from variance-and-flux-analysis. The pack will likely lack sections a board expects.

scenarios.prompt: Investor update goes out Friday, September isn't closed, we're a services agency not SaaS, and we lost our biggest client last month. Draft it.
scenarios.why: The model hits a contradiction: 'Check the pack on request' says not to offer a preliminary pack when the close is not done, while Fallbacks says to build from the flash and label it preliminary. The narrative spine forces NRR-first plus Rule of 40, which does not apply to a services business. There is no investor-update structure, no bad-news-first framing, and no disclosure check before naming the lost client.

saas-gtm-finance.job: analyze SaaS ARR, retention and GTM efficiency
saas-gtm-finance.summary: Computes the ARR bridge, NRR and GRR on one cohort, pipeline coverage with a Base/Adverse/Opportunity quarter grade, CRM hygiene flags, the renewal base with save plays, and magic number, Rule of 40 and burn multiple, handing CAC and payback to unit economics.
strengths: Refuses to plug a bridge: every term carries a number or UNKNOWN.
NRR and GRR on the same cohort and period with the denominator stated, and benchmarks qualified by segment.
Checks the new-logo share of growth so a strong NRR can't mask a new-logo problem.
Clean ownership boundary: CAC and payback are handed to unit-economics-and-roi and quoted, not recomputed.
Renewal base with named at-risk accounts and owner-directed save plays; no CRM writes or customer contact.
missing: NRR/GRR formulas with the TTM convention
Reactivation and FX buckets in the bridge
ARR definition, including usage-based and multi-year prepay treatment
Reconciliation of ARR to billing or revenue
SaaS quick ratio for MRR movement
Gross margin as an efficiency input
Win-rate-adjusted coverage
Cohort retention curves
Bridge and renewal table templates with a worked example

issues.section: GTM efficiency, on FACT inputs only
issues.quote: Magic Number = (quarterly net new ARR x 4) / sales and marketing
issues.problem: Net new ARR is already annualized, so multiplying by 4 overstates the magic number fourfold (the standard form is quarter-over-quarter revenue change x 4). It also omits the prior-quarter spend lag. A board-facing number would be wrong and graded against the wrong thresholds.
issues.fix: Use: Magic Number = net new ARR in quarter / prior-quarter S&M spend (equivalently (ΔQ revenue x 4) / prior-quarter S&M). State the lag.

issues.section: Pipeline coverage and the quarter grade
issues.quote: Read coverage against target — under 3x is a flag, under 2x is an
issues.problem: The fixed 3x/2x bands ignore the historical win rate, the stage qualification of the pipeline, and the time left in the quarter. A 40% win-rate team is fine at 2.5x; a 15% team is short at 4x. Zara's gtm-performance-diagnostics already adjusts for win rate.
issues.fix: Required coverage = 1 / historical win rate on qualified pipeline closing in-period against the remaining target; use 3x/2x only when no win-rate history exists, and label it.

issues.section: Retention, on one cohort and one period
issues.quote: Compute net revenue retention (NRR) and gross revenue retention (GRR)
issues.problem: No formula and no time basis. NRR/GRR are conventionally trailing-12-month on the cohort's starting ARR, with GRR excluding expansion and capped at 100%. Without that, results vary run to run and won't match benchmarks.
issues.fix: Add the formulas: NRR = (cohort start ARR + expansion − contraction − churn) / cohort start ARR over TTM; GRR = (start − contraction − churn) / start, capped at 100%.

issues.quote: Starting ARR, plus new, plus expansion, minus contraction, minus churn,
issues.problem: No reactivation bucket, no FX-translation line for multi-currency books, no ARR definition (contracted, run-rate or usage-based), and no reconciliation of ending ARR to the billing or revenue ledger.
issues.fix: Add reactivation and FX lines, state the ARR definition used, and tie ending ARR to Stripe or the revenue ledger with the difference explained.

issues.section: GTM efficiency, on FACT inputs only
issues.quote: Show the assumption box, then:
issues.problem: The heading requires FACT inputs only but the body opens an assumption box. It is unclear what happens when S&M spend must be allocated out of G&A, which is common for small teams.
issues.fix: Allow INFERENCE inputs with the allocation rule shown in the box, and block only the grade (not the calculation) when an input is UNKNOWN.

issues.section: GTM efficiency, on FACT inputs only
issues.quote: Burn Multiple = net burn / net new ARR, under 1.5.
issues.problem: No handling for zero or negative net new ARR, where the ratio is meaningless, and no graded bands.
issues.fix: Report N/A with absolute burn and ARR when net new ARR ≤ 0; give bands (<1 excellent, 1-1.5 good, 1.5-2 watch, >2 flag).

issues.quote: The bridge, NRR and GRR with their denominators, the coverage read with
issues.problem: No table layout for the bridge or renewal base, so reads won't be comparable period to period despite the persona's fixed-shape rule.
issues.fix: Ship templates/arr-bridge.md and templates/renewal-base.md with fixed columns.

scenarios.prompt: Here's our Stripe MRR export for the last 12 months. Build the Q2 ARR bridge and give me NRR and GRR.
scenarios.why: The bridge equation and the 'state the denominator' rule produce a clean bridge. But no NRR/GRR formula or trailing-12-month convention is given, so the quarterly-vs-TTM basis is left to chance. There is no reactivation/win-back bucket, so reactivated Stripe subscriptions get forced into new or expansion.

scenarios.prompt: The board wants our magic number and burn multiple for Q3. We're usage-based, no CRM is connected, and S&M salaries sit inside G&A in QuickBooks.
scenarios.why: The skill's formula '(quarterly net new ARR x 4) / sales and marketing spend' multiplies an already-annualized figure by 4, overstating the magic number fourfold, and then grades it against 0.75/1.5. There is no guidance on defining ARR for usage-based revenue. 'On FACT inputs only' gives no path for an allocated S&M figure.

unit-economics-and-roi.job: calculate unit economics and investment ROI
unit-economics-and-roi.summary: Builds contribution margin, fully loaded CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC and payback with formulas shown on one cohort, runs Base/Adverse/Opportunity cases with break-even, and gives a fund/hold/kill verdict from NPV/IRR against a hurdle, plus mechanism-based vendor savings scoring.
strengths: Every input is labelled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN, and 'An UNKNOWN input blocks the verdict, not the draft' is exactly right.
Flags unknown gross margin before LTV math because every downstream ratio inherits the hole.
Formulas are shown with numbers plugged in, expansion is excluded from CAC, and logo vs revenue churn is never blended.
Three cases with a break-even line, plus a fund/hold/kill verdict that names the single deciding number.
A saving with no traced spend line is treated as INFERENCE; partial costs produce a range rather than false precision.
missing: Gross-new-customer CAC definition, spend lag and a paid vs blended CAC split
LTV lifetime cap and discounted LTV
Stage-appropriate default hurdle rates
Incremental cash-flow and sunk-cost rules; ramp modelling for headcount bets
Sensitivity or tornado on the two key drivers computed in the sandbox
Cohort payback curve rather than a single ratio
A contribution-margin definition listing which variable costs are included
Output template and worked example

issues.section: Compute on one cohort definition, formulas shown
issues.quote: salaries + marketing spend + pro-rated tooling) / net new logos.
issues.problem: 'Net new logos' usually means new minus churned. CAC's denominator should be gross new customers acquired, so netting out churn inflates CAC. The numerator also omits commissions and agency fees, and there is no spend-to-close lag.
issues.fix: Use 'new customers acquired in the period (gross, not net of churn)'. Add commissions and agencies to the numerator, and lag spend by the average sales cycle when it exceeds one period.

issues.section: Compute on one cohort definition, formulas shown
issues.quote: Lifetime value (LTV) = (average revenue per user (ARPU) x gross
issues.problem: No period matching between ARPU and churn, no lifetime cap and no discounting. LTV explodes when churn is near zero or revenue churn is negative (NRR over 100%), producing indefensible LTV:CAC ratios.
issues.fix: Require ARPU and churn on the same period basis, cap lifetime at 3-5 years (or 1/churn, whichever is lower), and show a discounted LTV at the hurdle rate.

issues.quote: No hurdle rate on file: run 10% (typical cost of
issues.problem: 10% is not a typical cost of capital for the small venture-backed or bootstrapped teams this expert serves (20-30%+ is common). Presenting it as typical biases the verdict toward funding.
issues.fix: Label the defaults INFERENCE and use a stage-appropriate pair (e.g. 15% and 25%), then ask which the team uses before giving a verdict.

issues.quote: Net present value (NPV) and internal rate of return (IRR) against the
issues.problem: No rules for investment-grade cash flows: incremental only, sunk costs excluded, timing by month or quarter, ramp periods, terminal value, and the IRR pitfalls of non-conventional cash flows. The sandbox isn't mentioned for the arithmetic.
issues.fix: Add a cash-flow table spec (period, incremental inflow, outflow, net, cumulative), exclude sunk costs, and compute NPV/IRR in bash_exec with the script output attached.

issues.quote: Score the savings opportunity by mechanism — switch, renegotiate, or
issues.problem: Thin: no switching and migration cost, contract term or notice dates, or total cost of ownership. It also overlaps cash-treasury-and-fx's renewal scan without routing between them.
issues.fix: Add TCO including switching cost and the notice date, and point to the cash-treasury-and-fx commitment scan as the source of renewal dates.

issues.quote: The unit table, the ratios with their formulas, the three cases with
issues.problem: No template or example, so the unit table and three-case layout vary run to run.
issues.fix: Ship templates/unit-economics.md with fixed rows, the case columns and a break-even row, plus one worked example.

scenarios.prompt: Q2 S&M was $180k, we added 42 customers, ARPU is $450/month, gross margin 78%, monthly logo churn 2.5%. What are CAC payback and LTV:CAC?
scenarios.why: The formulas are shown with numbers plugged in: CAC ≈ $4,286, LTV ≈ $14,040, LTV:CAC ≈ 3.3, payback ≈ 12.2 months. Churn is labelled as logo churn, the benchmarks are segment-qualified, and three cases with break-even follow. Only the 'net new logos' wording could mislead if churned customers were netted out.

scenarios.prompt: Should we fund a $250k outbound SDR team next year? We have no hurdle rate, gross margin is unclear because hosting sits in opex, and NRR is 115%.
scenarios.why: The skill correctly flags the unknown gross margin before any LTV math, lets the UNKNOWN block the verdict, and runs 10%/15% hurdles side by side. But a 10% default understates a startup's cost of capital. There is no guidance on SDR ramp time, attrition or incremental cash flows, and LTV has no lifetime cap when revenue churn is negative, so the deciding number can be inflated.

variance-and-flux-analysis.job: explain variance of actuals versus plan
variance-and-flux-analysis.summary: Explains actual-vs-plan or period-over-period moves: fixes the comparison, decomposes into price/volume/mix/timing drivers, sorts lines into favorable/unfavorable blocks with currency and percent gaps, grades RAG with owners against a threshold, flags thin samples, and carries open items forward.
strengths: Fixes the period and comparison first and refuses to compare a partial month against a full plan ('a timing artifact').
Bans filler attribution ('higher spend is not a driver'); every driver carries a number.
Defines F/UF correctly for expenses, shows the gap in currency AND percent, and applies a quiet floor to cut noise.
RAG definitions tie to action: yellow gets a watch line, red gets the owner's one question.
Calls out thin samples, carries open items until closed, and feeds repeat variances into the next forecast.
missing: An accounting-integrity check (miscoding, accruals, cutoff, reclass, one-offs) before business explanation
PVM formulas with residual handling
A balance-sheet flux method, or removal of the flux trigger
FX-driven variance for multi-currency books
Month vs YTD views side by side
An unambiguous materiality rule
Commentary line template and worked example
A note distinguishing permanent from timing variances, with the expected reversal period
