recommendations.name: Product OKRs and goals
recommendations.purpose: Draft quarterly objectives with outcome key results (baseline, target, date), run the weekly confidence check-in, and score the quarter.
recommendations.why: Setting and tracking OKRs is a routine line in PM job descriptions. The roadmap skill needs 'the goal they serve' as input and marks it INFERENCE when missing, and the weekly review needs a fixed KPI table. No kit skill produces either: metrics defines the North Star and strategy defines the bets. The dropped product-roadmap-planning had an OKR-aligned roadmap format that the merge did not carry over. phuryn brainstorm-okrs gives the method (Wodtke's Radical Focus; outcome key results over output; how OKRs, KPIs and the North Star relate). It is only 80 lines and relies on $ARGUMENTS, so it needs rewriting to fit the platform.

source.ref: phuryn/pm-skills pm-execution/skills/brainstorm-okrs @8607e3b

sketch: Inputs: company goals or the strategy doc, the North Star and its inputs from the metrics skill, and last quarter's scores. With no company goal, propose one marked INFERENCE.

Draft two or three alternative objective sets, each with three outcome key results written as baseline to target by date. Each baseline is FACT with its source, or UNKNOWN plus an instrumentation ask. No 'ship X' key results.
Name the health metrics that must not degrade, and record the confidence when each key result is set.
Place roadmap now-items under the key result they move. An item that moves none goes to the cut discussion in the roadmap skill.
Weekly check-in: confidence per key result, feeding the weekly product review's KPI table. At quarter end, score each 0.0 to 1.0 and decide to carry or kill.
Nothing becomes the team's OKRs without the decision maker's yes. Save as a dated okrs-<quarter>.md from templates/okrs.md.

recommendations.name: Product acceptance review
recommendations.purpose: Walk a staging or preview build against the PRD's acceptance criteria and return an accept, accept-with-follow-ups or reject verdict with screenshot evidence and drafted bugs.
recommendations.why: The merged PRD skill writes Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. The launch plan's go/no-go gate has a 'product stable' line. No skill checks the built feature against either, so the gate has no evidence behind it. Accepting stories against acceptance criteria is standard product-owner work. This platform can do it directly with browser_navigate, browser_act and browser_screenshot on a staging URL. Casey's skills cover QA test plans and bug reports, not the product owner's accept or reject call. Nothing in the catalog covers this. phuryn test-scenarios offers an optional scenario template (MIT; ship its notice if used).

source.ref: new; may borrow the scenario template from phuryn/pm-skills pm-execution/skills/test-scenarios (MIT)

sketch: Inputs: the dated PRD, a staging or preview URL, and a test account the owner supplies. Never use production customer data, and keep no secrets in the sandbox.
Turn each acceptance criterion, plus the empty, loading and error states and the PRD's NFRs, into a check: starting state, steps, expected result.

Walk each check with browser tools and take a screenshot per criterion. Mark it pass, fail, blocked or not testable here. Skip destructive or outward actions (pay, send, delete) unless the owner approves a sandbox.

Verdict table: accept, accept with follow-ups, or reject. Draft each failure as a bug with steps, expected vs actual and the screenshot. File in Linear or GitHub only on a yes, and hand repro depth to Casey.
Save the run dated and compare the next build against it. The result supplies the evidence for the launch plan's 'product stable' gate line.
Stay inside the boundary: no code changes and no design pixels. Report findings only.

recommendations.name: Product activation and onboarding
recommendations.purpose: Define the activation (aha) event from retained-vs-churned behaviour and redesign the first-run path to reach it faster.
recommendations.why: Activation is the input metric small product teams most often own. The metrics skill names a North Star and its inputs but has no method for finding the aha moment. The PRD skill names empty, loading and error states but not the path from first run to value. The unassigned catalog package onboarding (coreyhaines, MIT) supplies the method: minimum path to value, activation models, checklist and empty-state patterns, and experiment ideas. Robin's onboarding-and-adoption covers one customer account at a time for customer success, not product flow design.

source.ref: onboarding (unassigned; coreyhaines31/marketingskills)

sketch: Compatibility pass (PR #13 skipped this package): drop the .agents/product-marketing.md check, mark signup, paywalls, ab-testing and emails as not installed, and label the unsourced abandonment benchmarks as unsourced.
Define activation: compare candidate events for retained vs churned users in bash_exec on an export, stating cohort, window and sample sizes. With a thin sample, refuse the call.
Inventory the real first-run path with a browser walkthrough on a test account and screenshots, then apply minimum path to value: take inventory, remove, reconstruct.
Output an onboarding audit (finding, impact, recommendation, priority) or a flow spec that feeds the PRD skill. Tests go to product-experiment-design.
Lifecycle email triggers stay as drafts and go to Maya or Remy. Per-account onboarding goes to Robin.

recommendations.name: Product release notes and changelog
recommendations.purpose: Turn what actually shipped into customer-facing release notes and a dated changelog, with breaking changes and deprecations called out, staged for approval.
recommendations.why: Writing release notes is a recurring PM task. The launch plan's quiet-ship tier says it 'gets release notes and one post' but gives no method for writing them. The weekly review's 'shipped' block is the raw material. GitHub and Linear are connectable, so merged PRs and closed issues can be pulled directly. Priya's release-notes-draft already has the right gates: confirm each change shipped, list who confirmed it is live, add an approval note, and never publish. phuryn release-notes adds Breaking Changes and Deprecations categories and benefit-first rewrites.

source.ref: release-notes-draft (original, Priya); graft categories from phuryn/pm-skills pm-execution/skills/release-notes (MIT)
source.license: AutoGPT platform-authored base; MIT for the phuryn graft

sketch: Pull merged PRs and closed issues for the window via GitHub or Linear run_block. Confirm each item is live, with its date, plan or platform scope, and flag or rollout percentage. Leave out anything unconfirmed.
Categorise each item as new, improved, fixed, breaking (action required by a date) or deprecated.
Write benefit-first entries in customers' own words: no ticket numbers, codenames or future dates.
Produce audience variants: public changelog, in-app note, and an internal digest for support and sales. Support macros go to Robin.
Put an approval note above the draft (sources, held-back items, approver). Publish to Notion, WordPress or Slack only on a yes, and keep a dated changelog with a log of what was already announced.

recommendations.name: Product feature deprecation and sunset
recommendations.purpose: Decide whether to retire a feature, then plan the migration path, notice timeline and staged customer communications without removing or sending anything on its own.
recommendations.why: Retiring a feature or API version is PM-owned and high-stakes, since it touches contracts, customer data and revenue. No skill in the catalog covers it: the only mentions of 'deprecated' are an ADR status field and a customer-reply template. The launch plan only goes forward, and the strategy skill's not-doing list does not deal with features already in use. Standard practice is a usage read, a notice period, a migration path and, for APIs, staged brownouts. The platform can do each step: usage from exports or Stripe, and communications as Gmail drafts or Notion pages behind approval.

source.ref: new

sketch: Usage read: active users and accounts, frequency, plans, and revenue at stake. Shared outputs use pseudonymised counts, not customer names.
Decision memo: keep, retire or replace, with the cost of carrying it, graded evidence and a recommendation. The decision maker's yes is required.
Send contract, SLA and data-retention questions to Lena or counsel. Give users a data-export path before removal.
Plan the timeline back from the removal date: announce, stop new adoption, migration guide, reminders, optional API brownouts, removal, then monitoring. The owner sets the notice period.
Draft communications per audience (in-app, email, changelog, support macro, sales talk track). Nothing is sent. Hand off to Robin and Noor.
Track migration percentage with the metrics skill and set rollback criteria before announcing.

recommendations.name: Product pre-mortem
recommendations.purpose: Stress-test a PRD or launch plan by assuming failure. Sort risks into Tigers, Paper Tigers and Elephants, and give each launch-blocker an owner, a mitigation and a date.
recommendations.why: The launch plan names risks with contingencies, and the PRD lists assumptions, but neither has a way to draw out risks nobody has said aloud. The Tigers, Paper Tigers and Elephants pre-mortem is a widely used PM ritual. phuryn pre-mortem is a clean, short, MIT base that only needs $ARGUMENTS removed and the output routed to workspace files. If a smaller kit is preferred, it could also be grafted into product-launch-plan instead of shipping on its own.

source.ref: phuryn/pm-skills pm-execution/skills/pre-mortem @8607e3b

sketch: Inputs: the dated PRD and launch plan. Imagine it failed 14 days after launch and work out why.
Classify each risk as a Tiger (real, evidenced), a Paper Tiger (overblown, with the reason) or an Elephant (unspoken, with how to investigate it). Label each FACT or INFERENCE; no invented incidents.
Split Tigers into launch-blocking, fast-follow and track. Each launch-blocker gets a mitigation, an owner and a date.
Optionally draft an async pre-mortem prompt for teammates, as drafts only, and merge their answers.
Feed launch-blockers into the launch plan's go/no-go gate and failed assumptions back into the PRD. Save it dated and revisit 2 to 3 weeks before launch.

proposal.summary: Anika's kit is almost all NICK: 34 PR-2 skills of widely varying depth. Beside them sit three generic candidates, all also Toran-proposed for Max: prospecting (ORIGINAL), sales-enablement-content (TORAN) and partner-co-marketing (TORAN). No open PR rebuilds any of her skills. The proposal keeps the NICK spine and cuts it to 29 skills. Two pairs merge into new slugs: plan-the-multi-year-partnership + govern-the-strategic-alliance become plan-and-govern-the-strategic-alliance, and set-board-level-alliance-strategy + run-partner-strategy-and-operations become set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy. Three thin skills fold into siblings: model-the-partnership-commercials into the agreement skill, source-partners-via-investor-ecosystems into sourcing, and the OEM section of run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships into channel scale. The three generic packages are graft sources only. Repeated rule blocks each get one home, and each block is moved rather than deleted. Tiers, one reconciled deal-registration block and the MDF loop go to design-the-partner-program. Certification bars go to build-partner-academies-at-scale, exit plans to manage-partner-renewals-and-exits, guardrail bands (with discount floors) to own-the-alliance-pnl, attribution to track-partner-pipeline, and the partner health grade to prep-the-partner-qbr. Short checklists that Max also carries, such as the marketplace private-offer checklist, stay in Anika's skills so she works without him; the overlap is handled by consult and handoff lines. Across experts, Anika's alliance, co-sell and marketplace skills repeat Max's near-verbatim, and Max's own review already flags alliance-co-commercialization as duplicating this ground. The expert body needs three fixes. First, update the router in identity and anika-getting-started for the renamed slugs; 'a portfolio question' now collides with the new portfolio-strategy slug. Second, fix the escalation voice sample, whose ruling contradicts first-to-register. Third, add a competition-law line to boundaries.

body_review.summary: Strong, well-gated persona. The two-bucket attribution rule, the money-gate list and the FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN discipline hold across the body, and the routines are read-only, deduped and stay quiet. The body lags the proposed kit. The identity router names about 30 skills, and several would be merged, renamed or dropped. The word 'portfolio' would route to two skills after the merge. The routines rely on artefacts no skill defines: a four-quadrant partner score, a monthly partner-facing review, a 'light' QBR, a fund-utilization bar and a governance-staleness test. They also hardcode renewal windows the renewals skill is moving away from. One voice sample models the wrong first-to-register ruling. Boundaries have no competition-law line, even though four skills put competing partners in one room.
strengths: Attribution rule is exact and testable: 'A deal is never both', credit splits across partners never across buckets, unproven deals listed separately. track-partner-pipeline implements the same rule.
The money-gate list in identity and boundaries is comprehensive (exclusivity through acquisition terms), and every skill closes on the same owner-yes gate.
The three day_one items map one-to-one onto source-and-qualify-partners, partner-first-touch-outreach and track-partner-pipeline, with honest timing ('once your numbers are connected').
Every routine confirms schema first, dedupes against earlier runs, stays quiet when there is nothing to report and is read-only toward partners.
The 'Pipeline read' voice sample models the persona well: sourced vs influenced, 2.1x coverage computed correctly against the thresholds, and unproven deals kept out of the number.
body_review.kit_alignment: day_one aligns with source-and-qualify-partners, partner-first-touch-outreach and track-partner-pipeline. Identity routes to seven skills the proposal merges or folds: plan-the-multi-year-partnership, govern-the-strategic-alliance, run-partner-strategy-and-operations, set-board-level-alliance-strategy, model-the-partnership-commercials, source-partners-via-investor-ecosystems and run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships. Rename those routes to plan-and-govern-the-strategic-alliance, set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy, structure-the-partner-agreement, source-and-qualify-partners and scale-the-partner-channel, and drop the sponsorship route. 'A portfolio question goes to program design' now collides with the new portfolio-strategy slug, and the 'board-level frame' sentence names a retired skill. anika-getting-started carries the same router (horizon, portfolio and board routes) and a starter menu to update. routines[0] has four problems. It relies on a four-quadrant score, a governance-staleness test and a fund-utilization bar that no skill defines. It hardcodes 120- and 90-day renewal windows. It uses invest/divest/hold, while set-board-level-alliance-strategy uses fund/grow/hold/exit and own-the-alliance-pnl uses fund-or-exit. routines[1] promises a monthly partner-facing review that run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence lacks. routines[2] promises a light review tier that prep-the-partner-qbr lacks. routines[4] aligns with assure-partner-led-delivery. routines[5] aligns with run-global-partner-executive-councils and still works once that skill's session mechanics point at prep-the-partner-qbr. The first three preloads are copied from Max's sales kit, and the fourth (smart-meeting-brief) matches Zara's.

issues.quote: ours on 3 March and theirs on 11 March. First-to-register stands, so the deal is theirs to lead and we support.
issues.problem: Our registration (3 March) predates theirs (11 March), so first-to-register makes the deal ours to lead. The sample models the core registration ruling backwards and teaches the wrong precedent.
issues.fix: Swap the dates (theirs 3 March, ours 11 March), or keep the dates and have the ruling say we lead and they support.

issues.quote: a horizon question to the multi-year plan, a global systems integrator to alliance governance
issues.problem: Routes to two skills the proposal merges into plan-and-govern-the-strategic-alliance. They share one sponsor/governance/steering artefact today.
issues.fix: Route both horizon and GSI/alliance-governance questions to plan-and-govern-the-strategic-alliance.

issues.quote: An operating question goes to partner strategy and operations
issues.problem: This route and 'A board or thesis question goes to board-level alliance strategy' go to two skills that make the same per-partner portfolio call. The proposal merges them into set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy.
issues.fix: Route both operating/annual-plan and board/thesis questions to set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy, and use one call vocabulary (invest/hold/divest).

issues.quote: A portfolio question goes to program design
issues.problem: After the merge the kit has a skill named set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy, so 'a portfolio question' has two plausible homes. design-the-partner-program's own description also opens 'Use when the portfolio needs program-level design'. anika-getting-started repeats the route ('a portfolio question to program design').
issues.fix: Route program rules (tiers, incentives, MDF, registration) to program design, and which partners to invest in, hold or divest to portfolio strategy. Take 'portfolio' out of design-the-partner-program's description, and make the same change in anika-getting-started.

issues.quote: a council that needs a board read runs under the board-level frame with the council mechanics inside it
issues.problem: The 'board-level frame' is set-board-level-alliance-strategy, which the proposal retires.
issues.fix: Say the council runs under the portfolio-strategy frame (set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy's board pack) with the council mechanics inside it.

issues.quote: a sponsorship or OEM ask to brand and supply portfolios
issues.problem: run-brand-oem-and-supply-partnerships, a thin catch-all, is folded into the channel skill. Only the OEM section survives, so a sponsorship ask would route to nothing.
issues.fix: Route OEM asks to channel scale. State that buy-side sponsorship is out of scope; no teammate owns it.

issues.quote: and a category question to partner-led category creation
issues.problem: The same paragraph also routes 'a category question to the ecosystem map', so one trigger has two destinations.
issues.fix: Split the routes: whitespace or build/buy/partner questions go to the ecosystem map; a new-category or coalition question goes to partner-led category creation.

issues.quote: a money question to commercials
issues.problem: model-the-partnership-commercials is folded into structure-the-partner-agreement, and portfolio economics already have their own route to the alliance P&L.
issues.fix: Deal-level money goes to agreement structuring and portfolio money to the alliance P&L.

issues.quote: an investor-ecosystem ask to investor sourcing
issues.problem: Investor sourcing becomes a channel inside source-and-qualify-partners.
issues.fix: Route investor-ecosystem asks to sourcing and qualification.

issues.quote: Score each strategic partner on four quadrants: strategy, financial, operations, relationship.
issues.problem: No skill defines a four-quadrant score. Health is scored differently in three places: prep-the-partner-qbr (weighted R/Y/G metrics, a 10-point score), handle-partner-conflict-and-churn (activity, pipeline, sponsorship) and manage-partner-renewals-and-exits (an undefined health grade). Each run will improvise the score.
issues.fix: Make prep-the-partner-qbr the one partner health model. Group its weighted metrics into the four quadrants, add default weights and a band-to-10-point mapping, and have the routine, the conflict skill and the renewals skill read that grade.

issues.quote: widen the pulse into the monthly partner-facing review: one page per partner, one agreed change, tracked to effect
issues.problem: No skill contains a monthly partner-facing review. run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence has weekly, bi-weekly and quarterly layers, but its artefact is the call prep, not a one-page partner review.
issues.fix: Add a 'Monthly partner review' section to run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence (one page, one agreed change, effect tracked, drafted for the owner's yes). The proposed kit commits to this.

issues.quote: the current invest/divest/hold tag
issues.problem: Three vocabularies exist for one call: invest/divest/hold (here and in run-partner-strategy-and-operations), fund/grow/hold/exit (set-board-level-alliance-strategy) and fund-or-exit (own-the-alliance-pnl).
issues.fix: Standardise on invest/hold/divest in the merged portfolio-strategy skill and have own-the-alliance-pnl raise flags into it.

issues.quote: governance gone stale (sponsors or steering body unchanged or disengaged 12-plus months, re-checked at alliance transitions)
issues.problem: No skill defines governance staleness or 'alliance transitions'. The closest is run-global-partner-executive-councils' handoff map at inflection points.
issues.fix: Add the staleness test to plan-and-govern-the-strategic-alliance's operating model, or drop it from the routine.

issues.quote: fund utilization (claimed over allocated) below bar
issues.problem: design-the-partner-program's MDF loop has claim SLAs and a return formula but no utilization bar, so 'below bar' is invented at run time.
issues.fix: Name a utilization bar (owner-set, labelled as an assumption until confirmed) in design-the-partner-program's MDF loop and have the routine read it.

issues.quote: renewal dates inside 120 days
issues.problem: The routine hardcodes a 120-day look-ahead and 'renewal inside 90 days with no play'. The proposal makes manage-partner-renewals-and-exits read each contract's notice clause, so on a 180-day notice the routine would flag too late.
issues.fix: Read each partner's renewal-window open date from the lifecycle log (the earlier of 120 days or the notice period plus 30), and flag any window that has opened with no play.

issues.quote: strategic partners get full prep plus a pre-read; smaller ones get a light review
issues.problem: prep-the-partner-qbr has only one prep depth, so the light-review tier is invented at run time.
issues.fix: Add a short 'light review' variant to prep-the-partner-qbr: graded snapshot, one decision, no pre-read.

issues.quote: thesis alliances, the M&A shortlist, coalition partners, and named execs
issues.problem: The routine already forbids publishing the brief without the owner's yes. But it reads the M&A shortlist, and to dedupe it keeps a record of what it surfaced across runs. Target names in that record, or in a brief that mixes M&A signals with coalition and thesis items, can travel further than intended. drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments' review flags deal details leaking into shared memory or routines.
issues.fix: Put M&A-shortlist signals in a separate section marked confidential, for the owner only. Dedupe on source URL and date rather than storing target names in shared memory.

issues.quote: Regulated motions wait on Legal or Compliance in writing and investment motions on Legal and Finance.
issues.problem: There is no competition-law gate. Councils seat competing partners, the category coalition coordinates messaging, multi-party bids team with competitors, and the conflict skill offers MAP remedies. Evals on four skills flag antitrust exposure.
issues.fix: Add: 'Any discussion among competing partners of pricing, margins, territories or customer allocation, and any resale-price remedy, waits on Legal; no competitor pricing is exchanged, and council and coalition agendas are counsel-reviewed.'

issues.quote: Nothing partner-facing goes out without the owner's yes to that specific action
issues.problem: No line covers data crossing companies: account-mapping overlaps, joint webinar registrants, shared lead lists. run-the-partner-marketing-engine's review flags GDPR/CAN-SPAM exposure.
issues.fix: Add: 'No customer, lead or account list is shared with a partner without a data-sharing basis the owner confirms.'

issues.quote: lead-finder-local-businesses
issues.problem: The first three preloads are identical to Max's sales preloads (the fourth, smart-meeting-brief, matches Zara's). A local-business lead finder does not fit partner sourcing. email-address-finder may cut against partner-first-touch-outreach's rule against 'building an address from a pattern'.
issues.fix: Replace the first three with partner-relevant agents (company research, meeting brief), or confirm that email-address-finder only returns published addresses.

issues.quote: You route rather than improvise.
issues.problem: The routing paragraph lists about 30 routes and repeats anika-getting-started's router. It dilutes the persona and breaks whenever a slug changes, as this proposal shows.
issues.fix: Compress it to lifecycle groups (recruit, sign, enable, co-sell, review, exit; program; alliance; portfolio) and leave per-skill routing to skill descriptions.

issues.quote: Sourced coverage below 3x of target is a flag and below 2x is an alarm
issues.problem: Coverage is undefined: which open pipeline, and whether the target is the full target or what remains after closed-won. The thresholds can swing by a factor of two (track-partner-pipeline eval top issue).
issues.fix: Define coverage in track-partner-pipeline (open sourced pipeline closing in the window, divided by remaining target) and reference it here.

clusters.job: Decide who to recruit as partners, and how partners are tiered and registered

members.note: Solid on its core: the five-block profile per partner type is its own job. But its 'Tiers and bars' section duplicates design-the-partner-program with a different model: strategic/growth/watch, graduation and kill bars, and a partner-facing tier sheet. The triggers 'partner tiers' and 'tier sheet' also collide.

Owns the tier framework (weighted earn scorecard, 3-4 tiers, shadow-score pilot), incentives, the MDF loop and PRM rules, so it should be the single home for tiers, the tier sheet and deal registration. The registration block is restated in structure-the-partner-agreement, run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence and scale-the-partner-channel, and the copies disagree. Here the 90-day window is 'renewable on activity'; the cadence allows 'exactly one 30-day renewal on logged activity with sign-off', and the agreement allows 'one 30-day renewal'. Needs per-partner-type tracks and a 'too small to tier' gate (eval top issue).

proposed.name: Design the partner program
proposed.description: Use when the partner program needs design: whether to tier at all, tier tracks per partner type with earn, graduation and kill bars, the partner-facing tier sheet, incentives, the MDF loop, and the deal-registration and certification rules the partner system enforces.
proposed.rationale: Profile and program are different jobs, so both skills stay. Today the user can get two conflicting tier systems and three differing registration rule sets. Tiers, the tier sheet and one reconciled registration block move into design-the-partner-program. The ICP profiles partners, cites the tiers, and drops 'in what tiers' from its description. Keep strategic/growth/watch as the default ladder names. scale-the-partner-channel ('move a growth partner to strategic'), plan-the-multi-year-partnership and the QBR-countdown routine all use them, and moving only the watch rung would orphan that vocabulary.
drops: define-the-partner-icp: the 'Tiers and bars' section, the tier-sheet deliverable in 'What you hand back', and 'in what tiers' in its description
define-the-partner-icp triggers 'partner tiers' and 'tier sheet'

The registration numbers restated in structure-the-partner-agreement, run-the-partner-co-sell-cadence and scale-the-partner-channel: replace each with a pointer to the reconciled block here (the cadence keeps its hygiene states and its 'program rules win' line)
design-the-partner-program: 'a 90-day protection window renewable on activity' (replaced by the one-renewal rule grafted below)
design-the-partner-program description: 'Use when the portfolio needs program-level design' (the word 'portfolio' now belongs to set-the-partner-portfolio-strategy)

grafts.what: The strategic/growth/watch ladder as the default tier names. Watch is an internal-only rung: one joint motion to prove a partner out. Carry the graduation bar between tiers and an explicit kill bar for dropping a partner.

The 'gate on evidence and scale' rule, restated for tiers: a program with a handful of strategic partners gets named partners with the reason for each, not a tier ladder. This answers the review's 'too small to tier' issue.

The mechanics the program's block lacks: Submitted, In-review, Approved and Action-required states with reviewer comments; a reminder at one business day and escalation at two; an expiry alert 7 days out; exactly one 30-day renewal on logged activity with sign-off; never auto-renew; and reverse registrations (the qualified lead shells handed to partners).
Pre-written rulings for multi-partner claims and for a customer choosing a different partner, so one partner never reads two rule sets.

clusters.job: Build and qualify a ranked partner prospect shortlist

members.note: The only partner-specific sourcer: account overlap first, fit/evidence/access scoring, kill criteria written down. Matches day_one[0] exactly. Its BANT paragraph needs replacing with partner-side qualification (capacity, commitment, compatibility, partner economics), and its High/Medium/Low scale is undefined.

ORIGINAL, unassigned (Toran-proposed for Max and Anika). A customer prospect-list builder with SaaS, B2B, Local SMB and Demand-signal branches and a Hot/Warm/Cold rubric: the wrong target for Anika. Its compliance guardrails, confidence definitions and lead-sheet quality checks are stronger than the partner skill's. Its Hunter/Snov pattern-guessing contradicts partner-first-touch-outreach's rule against building addresses from patterns.

Investor and accelerator portfolios are a sourcing channel, not a separate job. Four thin steps with no evaluation criteria. Carry the investor map, the portfolio play, the monthly report and the parked-candidate revisit trigger.

proposed.name: Source and qualify partners
proposed.description: Use when the user wants partner prospects found or vetted: a cited long list from account overlap, public research and investor or accelerator portfolios, scored on fit, evidence and access, qualified on partner-side criteria, with kill decisions named.
proposed.rationale: One job: produce the shortlist that day_one[0] promises. The base already has a partner-specific method. prospecting adds research hygiene the base lacks, and the investor skill is one more place to find names. Also fix the base's BANT line (eval top issue) during the merge.
drops: prospecting: the Local SMB and Demand-signal branches, the Hot/Warm/Cold rubric and ratio target
prospecting: 'Hunter or Snov | Email pattern guessing' and the Truelist deliverability step
prospecting: the `.agents/product-marketing.md` context lookup and the vendor quick-pick rows with no AutoGPT block (ZoomInfo, Clay, Clearbit, BuiltWith)
source-and-qualify-partners: 'Grade inbound referrals on BANT' (customer-deal qualification; replace with partner capacity, commitment, compatibility and economics)

source-partners-via-investor-ecosystems: the intake and technical-fit steps of 'Run the startup pipeline' (the go/no-go runs through this skill's qualification and kill criteria; technical fit routes to scope-the-tech-partnership)

grafts.what: Rules 1-4, 7 and 8 as a 'Research guardrails' block: no bulk scraping of LinkedIn or Google Maps; no login-wall or CAPTCHA bypass; public business contact channels only; source URL and date captured for every contact; no breached or unprovenanced data; and no targeting or inferring of sensitive traits.

The confidence definitions, replacing the base's undefined High/Medium/Low. High means two independent sources or the official page. Medium means one credible source plus consistent evidence. Low means incomplete evidence, with the uncertainty named.

grafts.section: Phase 2 — Build the candidate list / Phase 5 — Output the lead sheet / Always include after the table / Quality Checks
grafts.what: Source 2-3x the target count before culling. Shortlist columns: score, firm, domain, partner type, why, source URLs, confidence, last verified date. Add the 'Top outreach targets', 'Search parameters' and 'Open questions' footer, dedupe by domain, and switch to CSV above 25 rows. Add one rule the source lacks: prefix any CSV cell that starts with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe, closing the formula-injection gap Toran's review flagged.

grafts.section: Build the investor map / Set the portfolio play / Run the startup pipeline / Report per portfolio monthly
grafts.what: A 'Sourcing through investors and accelerators' channel. Rank the investor map by portfolio fit times reachability, using evidenced warm paths only. Use portfolio intro days and founder briefings as the motion. A parked candidate gets a dated revisit trigger rather than a slow fade. Report monthly per portfolio (intros made, evaluations opened, referrals converted, pipeline sourced), naming the portfolio and window before any count.

clusters.job: Structure a partner's terms and the money behind them

members.note: Model choice (referral, reseller, co-sell, MSP/SI) with the ruled-out option, a one-page term sheet in fixed order, approver routing and a version log. Missing legal terms: confidentiality, trademark licence, DPA/BAA, liability, anti-bribery on referral fees, non-solicit, SI IP.

An outline with no formulas. Its deal P&L is the missing 'money' step before the term sheet. Its 'Set the guardrail bands' is near-verbatim own-the-alliance-pnl ('Anything outside a band is an exception draft for the owner, never a quiet yes'), but it also carries discount floors, which the P&L's band set lacks.

proposed.name: Structure the partner agreement
proposed.description: Use when a qualified partner is ready to talk terms: pick referral, reseller, co-sell or MSP/SI, model the money at base, low and high volume with a break-even line, draft the one-page term sheet, and route it to Legal and Finance.
proposed.rationale: The term sheet's money section and the deal P&L are one decision. A separate thin outline invites two versions of the same numbers. Portfolio bands already live in own-the-alliance-pnl. Also add the missing legal-term checklist (eval top issue).

recommendations.name: Reconcile partner payouts
recommendations.purpose: Turn proven, closed partner deals into what we owe each partner (referral fees, rebates, revenue shares, back-end incentives), check that against the partner's invoice or claim, and stage a payout batch for Finance to approve.
recommendations.why: Payouts are where partner trust is kept or lost, and partner-ops job postings name them as the core monthly task. Payoneer's Partnership Operations Manager posting lists 'execute monthly partner commission processes in alignment with regional and central approvals', 'maintain payout tracking and reconciliation documentation' and handling payout inquiries, adjustments and corrections. PRM vendors (ZINFI and others) ship commissions modules for the same reason. The merged kit stops short of the money going out. track-partner-pipeline proves who sourced a deal. structure-the-partner-agreement names payment triggers. design-the-partner-program has an MDF claim and payout SLA. own-the-alliance-pnl rolls up cost lines. run-creator-and-affiliate-partner-programs sets payout rules for creators only. No skill works out a B2B partner's fee per deal, applies clawbacks or post-termination tails, reconciles a partner invoice, or produces a statement. The platform suits this: the arithmetic runs as a script in the sandbox, the HubSpot, Stripe and Sheets blocks (or a CSV export) feed it, and any payment goes through the approval flow.

source.ref: new skill; reuses track-partner-pipeline's two-bucket proof rule and the agreement fee schedule

sketch: Inputs: the fee, rebate and revenue-share schedule per partner (from the agreement register or the signed agreement); closed-won and collected deals from the CRM or billing (HubSpot or Stripe block, or an export); the sourced proofs from track-partner-pipeline; the partner's invoice or claim.

Calculation script (bash_exec): basis (booked ACV or collected cash), trigger, rate or tier, caps, the multi-partner split rule, the FX date, clawback on refund or churn inside the window, and the post-termination tail. Each line cites the deal ID, its proof and the clause it relies on.

Eligibility gates: no payout on the unproven list, an agreement in force at the trigger date, the integrity and sanctions screen current, and payment and tax details on file (Finance names the forms).
Reconcile against the partner's invoice or claim: a matched, over, under and missing table, a dispute log with evidence, and a staged reply to the partner.
Deliverables: a statement draft per partner, a payout batch for Finance and the owner to approve (never executed), an accrual summary that feeds own-the-alliance-pnl, and payout-SLA tracking.
Dated batch log, with a handoff to Daniel or Mina for booking when they are hired.

recommendations.name: Screen partner integrity and sanctions
recommendations.purpose: Screen a prospective or active partner, before signature and before the first payout, for sanctions and export-list hits, beneficial ownership, government-official links, adverse media and anti-bribery red flags, and record the reviewer's decision.
recommendations.why: Channel intermediaries are the highest-risk third parties a company engages. As reported by Oversight, the Stanford FCPA Clearinghouse estimates that nearly 90% of FCPA bribery matters involve third-party intermediaries. DOJ's Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs asks prosecutors whether a company had a business rationale for each third party, used risk-based due diligence, and paid compensation commensurate with the work. Sanctions screening of distributors and resellers is standard practice, and it should include beneficial owners and be repeated over the life of the relationship. The kit recruits resellers, distributors and MSPs across territories and pays them fees, yet screens none of them. source-and-qualify-partners checks fit and 'no fatal conflict'. scale-the-partner-channel gates territories on licensing, data, tax and employment. Only drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments mentions an anti-bribery program, and only for acquisition targets. The platform can do the core work: the US Consolidated Screening List downloads as a CSV (data.trade.gov, checked returning data), so a bundled script can fuzzy-match names in the sandbox, and web_search covers registries and adverse media.

source.ref: new skill; borrows the evidence-status vocabulary of the catalog's vendor-due-diligence (Vera)

sketch: Risk tier set by partner type (reseller, distributor, agent, or referral partner paid a fee), geography (the owner-supplied corruption index), exposure to government customers and the size of the fee. The tier sets how deep the check goes and how often it is repeated.

Sanctions and export screen: a script pulls the US Consolidated Screening List CSV plus any lists the owner names (UK, EU) and fuzzy-matches the legal entity, trade names, principals and beneficial owners. The output is a match table with scores. Any possible match goes to HOLD; the skill never clears a fuzzy match itself.

Ownership and integrity: registry lookups, links to politically exposed persons or government officials, and dated adverse media and litigation, each labelled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN with its source. A staged due-diligence questionnaire goes to the partner.

Red-flag checklist: payment to offshore or third-party accounts, cash, fees above the norm for the market, refusal of anti-bribery or sanctions clauses, a referral from an official, a shell structure.
Contract controls handed to structure-the-partner-agreement: anti-bribery and sanctions representations, audit rights, a termination right, flow-down to sub-resellers and an annual certification.

Screening record: the date, list versions, matches and the Legal/Compliance reviewer's decision (CLEARED BY REVIEWER, HOLD or REJECT). Re-screen dates are set for list updates, renewal and each payout batch for high-tier partners.

recommendations.name: Keep the partner agreement register
recommendations.purpose: Pull the terms that run the partnership out of every signed partner agreement and amendment into one source-cited register. That covers notice windows, fee schedules, registration overrides, MDF deadlines, minimums, certifications and obligations on both sides, with dates calculated and the formula shown.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review found that the routines hardcode 120- and 90-day renewal windows. After the merge, manage-partner-renewals-and-exits reads each notice clause instead (the window opens at the earlier of 120 days or notice plus 30). The portfolio-review routine needs that data for every partner, not one agreement at a time. The new payout skill needs the fee schedules. The co-sell cadence needs to know where a partner's agreement overrides the program's registration defaults. No kit skill keeps these terms. The catalog already has a disciplined extraction method in Ellis's contract-key-term-extraction and contract-obligation-tracker and Vera's contract-renewal-tracker: statuses STATED, CALCULATED, MISSING, CONFLICT and UNCLEAR, one duty per row, a formula for each calculated date, and unclear items sent to counsel. Those skills are generic (vendor and customer contracts), short, platform-native, and assigned to other experts. A partner-specific adaptation reuses the method and adds the partner field set.

source.ref: contract-obligation-tracker + contract-key-term-extraction (Ellis), contract-renewal-tracker (Vera); adapt into one partner register

sketch: Intake: signed agreements and amendments only (drafts create no rows). One record per partner, with a status (STATED, CALCULATED, MISSING, CONFLICT or UNCLEAR), the document, section and exact passage for every value.

Partner field set: model; term and renewal form; notice period and method; termination for convenience or cause; post-termination fee tail; exclusivity, territory and segment; fee, margin and rebate schedule with payment triggers; registration rules that override the program; MDF entitlement and claim deadlines; minimums; certification headcount; reporting and audit rights; data sharing or a DPA; trademark licence; non-solicit; MFN; anti-bribery and sanctions representations.
Calculated dates with the formula shown: the notice deadline, the renewal window (the earlier of 120 days or notice plus 30), MDF claim cut-offs and certification expiries.
Obligation rows for both sides, each with an owner, the evidence required and a status. A row is never marked complete without the owner's evidence.

Feeds manage-partner-renewals-and-exits, the partner-portfolio-review routine (replacing the hardcoded windows), reconcile-partner-payouts and QBR prep. Conflicts and unclear items go to counsel (Ellis or Lena when hired), and the register is re-checked on every amendment.

recommendations.name: Gate partner competition-law risk
recommendations.purpose: One frame-and-escalate check, run before any motion that puts competing partners in one room or shapes a reseller's pricing, territory or customers. It inventories what information and restraints are in play, sets the controls (an antitrust statement, a counsel-reviewed agenda, clean-team rules) and pauses until counsel clears it in writing.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review says the boundaries have no competition-law line, even though four skills put competing partners in one room. The merge answers that with separate lines in run-global-partner-executive-councils (an antitrust statement and a counsel-reviewed agenda), orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids (a competition-law and clean-team gate), build-partner-led-category-creation (a competition-law line) and handle-partner-conflict-and-churn (a Legal gate on MAP and pricing remedies). Four separate lines will drift unless one canonical check sits behind them. The legal ground is also moving, so the skill must frame questions and hand them to counsel rather than encode thresholds. The FTC and DOJ withdrew the 2000 Competitor Collaboration Guidelines on 11 December 2024 with no replacement, and sought public comment on new collaboration guidance in February 2026. In the EU, resale price maintenance and most territorial and customer restrictions are hardcore restrictions under Article 4 of the Vertical Block Exemption Regulation (EU) 2022/720. Hub-and-spoke exchanges, where the vendor relays one reseller's pricing to another, are a known channel risk the kit never mentions. A public MIT candidate exists (agentcounsel's distribution-restraints-review; see notes), but it could not be verified, so this is written as a new skill.

source.ref: new skill; the counsel handoff reuses Lena's compliance-escalation-brief or Ellis's counsel-escalation-brief

sketch: Triggers: councils, advisory boards, multi-party bids, category coalitions and account mapping between competing partners; any reseller pricing guidance, MAP or RPM remedy, territory or customer allocation, exclusivity, MFN or loyalty-conditioned rebate.

Screen questions, not conclusions: horizontal or vertical; what would pass between the parties (prices, margins, bids, capacity, customer lists, roadmaps) and whether it is current, future or individualised; a hub-and-spoke check (never relay one partner's terms to another); a restraint inventory with a flag per jurisdiction for counsel.

Controls: an antitrust statement and a counsel-reviewed agenda for joint meetings, minutes, a clean-team protocol (who sees what, aggregation, time lag), and account mapping that shares overlaps only with no pricing fields. Personal data in shared lists is routed to Lena.
Escalation: a neutral brief to Legal or counsel, and the motion pauses until written clearance. A verbal clear is not a clear.
A dated log of every screen and ruling, cited by the councils, bids, category, conflict, program and co-sell skills in place of their own separate lines.

recommendations.name: Negotiate the partner deal
recommendations.purpose: Prepare and track a negotiation over partner terms, from the first term call through each redline round: both sides' interests, the BATNA and walk-away, a multi-issue trade matrix inside the guardrail bands, a give-get sequence, and a concession and redline log.
recommendations.why: Partnerships Manager postings routinely list negotiating partner agreements. The kit drafts the term sheet and routes approvers (structure-the-partner-agreement) and pairs each ask with a concession, but only at renewal (manage-partner-renewals-and-exits). Nothing prepares the first negotiation. There is no walk-away set before the first call and no view of which issues trade against which: margin, registration protection, MDF, exclusivity, territory, minimums, term and exit, customer ownership. Nothing tracks what was conceded across redline rounds against the bands in own-the-alliance-pnl. The catalog's unassigned negotiation skill (wondelai, MIT) covers generic Voss tactics. Its Ackerman price-haggling method suits a one-off price and not a multi-year relationship deal, so it is worth citing only for live-call technique. Max's objection-and-negotiation handles buyer objections, not a two-way exchange of value.

source.ref: new skill; live-call technique cites catalog negotiation references/techniques.md (wondelai, MIT)
source.license: MIT (for the cited technique reference only)

sketch: Prep sheet: interests, constraints and deadlines for each side, labelled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN; our BATNA and our best read of theirs; a walk-away the owner sets and dates before the first call.

Issue matrix: fee or margin, registration protection, MDF, exclusivity and territory, term and exit, minimums, certification, payment terms, customer ownership, data and IP. Each issue gets our priority, their likely priority, and a tradeable range inside the guardrail bands.
Give-get plan: every concession paired with something we get, the opening position and sequence, and the owner-only money items flagged.
Live-call support: calibrated questions and labels from the catalog technique reference, and a drill mode where Anika plays the partner.

Redline and concession log per round: the clause, their ask, our response, the band check and the approver. The agreed terms hand off to structure-the-partner-agreement, and anything outside a band becomes an exception draft for the owner.

recommendations.name: NDA playbook review (partner use)
recommendations.purpose: Compare a partner NDA clause by clause against the owner's NDA playbook before any account list, roadmap, pricing or data changes hands, and queue the deviations for counsel.
recommendations.why: After the merge, an NDA is a precondition in orchestrate-multi-party-partner-bids, drive-alliance-ma-and-strategic-investments adds NDA controls, and build-data-and-r-d-alliances expands its confidentiality and IP terms. Account mapping and roadmap sharing in co-sell and tech scoping also start with an NDA. The kit cannot review one. Ellis's catalog original, nda-playbook-review, is short, has no Claude-Code constructs, labels each clause MATCH, DEVIATION, MISSING or UNCLEAR, and leaves decisions to counsel. Sharing it lets Anika work when Ellis is not hired. Toran's nda-risk-review (Apache-2.0) has a useful scope check for non-solicits, standstills, residuals and MFNs hidden inside an 'NDA'. It still depends on ~/.claude config paths and slash commands even in the PR #13 version, so only its scope check is worth borrowing.

source.ref: nda-playbook-review (Ellis); add the hidden-obligation scope check from nda-risk-review

sketch: When it fires: before account mapping, roadmap or API detail, pricing, bid teaming, data evaluation or M&A talks. Whose paper, and the permitted purpose.

Clause-by-clause comparison with the owner's playbook, plus the scope check for non-NDA obligations (non-solicit, standstill, residuals, exclusivity, MFN, IP grants), which automatically goes to counsel.
Counsel queue with the exact text. Any redline uses a fallback from the playbook and stays an unsent draft.
A note on what may be shared at each stage, and the signed NDA logged in the agreement register with its expiry and purpose.

recommendations.name: Run the partner experience survey
recommendations.purpose: Design, field and read a program-wide partner satisfaction (PSAT) survey: value, profitability, ease of doing business, enablement, fairness in conflicts, and likelihood to recommend the program. The readout feeds the QBR relationship quadrant and program design.
recommendations.why: Channel programs measure partner satisfaction by partner type on a 5-point scale, covering support, training, communication, ease of doing business and the portal. Impartner publishes a channel partner satisfaction survey template for this. The kit reads the relationship only from inside: the QBR health model's relationship quadrant is built from activity and sponsorship, and the pre-merge run-partner-strategy-and-operations has a single line asking for an annual bilateral executive health-check with strategic partners, with no instrument or method. Nothing asks the long tail of partners how the program treats them, and that is where registration fairness, payout delays and portal friction show up. The upstream survey-designer (SkillMedev/skills, MIT) supplies a sound method: bias tests, balanced scales, a length budget, a cognitive pilot, and frozen tracking questions. It needs a partner construct set, anonymity rules for small groups, and removal of its references to skills that are not shipped.

source.ref: SkillMedev/skills skills/survey-designer (adapt to partners)

sketch: The decision it informs and the partner constructs: program value, profitability, ease of doing business (registration, portal, payouts), enablement, fairness in conflicts, communication, and 0-10 likelihood to recommend, used only for that question.
Sample by role within each partner (executive, seller, SE, marketer). Report by tier or type only above a minimum group size, and treat fewer than about 100 completes as directional.

Instrument built with survey-designer's bias tests and flow in under 10 minutes, with tracking questions frozen year to year. It is fielded through a Google Forms/Sheets block or a CSV, and the invitation is staged for the owner's yes with an opt-out.

Readout: scores by tier and type, verbatims treated as hypotheses, one owned action per theme, and inputs to the QBR relationship quadrant and the program design review. A staged 'what we heard' note goes back to partners, replacing the separate annual executive health-check line.

recommendations.notes:
I opened every kit skill I claim a gap against: structure, source-and-qualify, commercials, track-pipeline, co-sell, program design, tech scoping, marketing engine, renewals, conflict, onboarding, QBR, alliance P&L, channel scale, creator/affiliate, bids, regulated and ecosystem map. After the merge the kit covers the partner lifecycle thoroughly. The real gaps are money going out to partners (payouts), legal and compliance intake (integrity and sanctions screening, the agreement register, a competition-law gate, NDA review), negotiation prep, and the partner's own view of the program. Findings:

1. **One competition-law check, not four.** Four skills are gaining separate competition-law lines: councils, bids, category creation, and MAP remedies in conflict-and-churn. Once gate-partner-competition-law exists, each of those lines should cite it.
2. **The agreement register fixes the routines' renewal windows.** The body and routine rewrite should point partner-portfolio-review at keep-the-partner-agreement-register instead of the hardcoded 120- and 90-day windows.
3. **Payouts depend on the register and the screen.** reconcile-partner-payouts should gate on screen-partner-integrity-and-sanctions. Both belong in the boundaries text, which already lists the money gates.
4. **Unverified candidate: agentcounsel.** zgbrenner/agentcounsel ('distribution-restraints-review' and a competitor-collaboration/information-sharing review) is listed by skills.lc and web search as MIT. github.com returned 404/403 and raw.githubusercontent returned 404 on 2026-09-28, so I have not given its URL. If a reviewer can reach it, it may seed the competition gate. Its reported dependency on a shared antitrust indicator catalog would need shipping inside the package.
5. **Not recommended:**
   - Deferred referrals: contradictory reward-framing rules, and customer referral programs belong with marketing.
   - Deferred prospecting: its useful parts were already merged into source-and-qualify-partners, with the CSV guard.
   - nda-risk-review as a whole: ~/.claude config paths and slash commands survive PR #13. Only its hidden-obligation scope check is worth borrowing.
   - skillme partnership-strategy (MIT): overlaps structure and program design. But its pilot-before-contract rule is absent from the kit: a 90-day pilot with a numeric bar and a decision date before any multi-year or exclusive agreement, and exclusivity only in exchange for a contractual number. I searched every kit skill for 'pilot', and only program design has one (for tier shadow-scoring). The rule is worth adding as a line in structure-the-partner-agreement.
6. **Joint announcements have no home.** No kit skill drafts a joint partnership announcement or press release (dual approvals, both boilerplates, partner trademark use). Route 'announce the partnership' to Noor (press-release-draft, launch-communications-plan) through the consult pattern rather than adding a skill. If Noor is absent, press-release-draft is a platform-native catalog fallback.
7. **Sources checked:**
   - The Payoneer Partnership Operations Manager posting (TCV job board), on payout work.
   - DOJ's Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs, as summarised in search results, on third-party due diligence and compensation.
   - Stanford's estimate of about 90% of FCPA matters involving intermediaries, via the Oversight blog.
   - The FTC press release of December 2024 withdrawing the collaboration guidelines, and the February 2026 call for comment.
   - Impartner's PSAT survey template.
   - The US Consolidated Screening List CSV, which data.trade.gov served without a key.

   I confirmed that the upstream raw URLs for SkillMedev survey-designer at commit a28c4ce and wondelai negotiation at commit c172996 return HTTP 200.

proposal.summary: Casey's in-scope kit is the 8 ORIGINAL placeholders now assigned plus 5 TORAN packages that Toran proposed for Casey. No NICK skill or open-PR rebuild (#14-#16) touches Casey. PR #13 changes only ATTRIBUTION.md for these five packages, so their SKILL.md bodies are exactly what was evaluated. Three Toran packages duplicate originals, have weaker evidence rules and break the draft-only boundary: code-review-quality ends in an Approve verdict, and software-incident-response pages and posts with no approval step. They are merged in as grafts. pull-request-review gets review lenses (security, performance, correctness and concurrency, test quality) and a review template. test-plan-draft gets the per-component strategy table. incident-postmortem-draft gets the postmortem and status-update templates, a draft-only triage read and a default SEV table. The other two fill real gaps and are added. software-debugging is rewritten in place as an evidence-led root-cause skill that produces a report. It also covers performance and memory regressions, with approval required before any production profiling, and stays separate from bug-reproduction-report. verification-before-completion is retargeted to requests like "confirm the fix" or "is CI really green". The result is a 10-skill kit in which every original still needs its review fixes (memory_store in setup, go/no-go criteria, deploy and rollback risk, a cannot-reproduce branch). incident-postmortem-draft also loses its 'root cause analysis' and 'what went wrong' triggers, so code-level root-cause requests reach software-debugging. Every package that receives upstream text keeps its licence and attribution. Main cross-expert calls: share one bug-report field order with Sasha's bug-report-handoff; separate Casey's code-level repro and root cause from Robin's customer-path troubleshoot-and-resolve; route security-sensitive diffs to Devon; and resolve the 'go/no-go' trigger that release-readiness-checklist shares with Alex's product-launch-plan and Zara's commercial-launch-strategy.

body_review.summary: Casey's persona is one of the sharpest on the roster. The identity sets a finding contract (file and line, what goes wrong, the triggering input, confidence), and the voice samples show honesty about evidence. The gaps are at the edges. The boundaries field leaves out force-push, which the identity lists. It has no rule that review comments and issues go out only after approval, even though the kit drafts both, and no rule that incident updates stay drafts for the incident owner. There are no teammate handoffs (Devon for security, Lena for personal data, Noor for external statements) and no routines. The persona never mentions root-cause debugging, fix verification or mid-incident drafting, all of which the proposed kit adds.
strengths: The identity sets a finding contract ('Every finding names the file and line, what goes wrong, the input that triggers it, and how sure you are') that matches pull-request-review's finding fields one for one.
The voice samples show the evidence discipline rather than just claiming it: 'I have not run it; this is from reading the code.' and 'six failures is thin'.
The bio, identity and boundaries line up with every skill's guardrails: no merge, deploy or disabling a test; no invented trace or root cause; never mark a test passed without seeing it pass.
Both day_one items map directly to skills that stay in the kit as merge bases (pull-request-review, test-plan-draft).
The tagline and bio are concrete and scoped ('small engineering teams'), and they say what Casey will not do.
body_review.kit_alignment: Preloads and routines are empty, and both day_one items map to kept skills (pull-request-review, test-plan-draft), so no body field names a skill that would be dropped. Every slug in the proposed kit is an existing slug: the three merges keep their base slugs, and software-debugging and verification-before-completion keep theirs (only the display names change). The gaps run the other way. The bio and identity do not promise root-cause debugging, fix verification or mid-incident status drafts, all of which the proposed kit adds. code-quality-getting-started ends with a plan ('The first three reviews or test plans, with reasons'), not the review that day_one[0] promises after access.

issues.quote: Never merge, deploy, skip a check, or disable a test yourself.
issues.problem: This leaves out force-push, which the identity lists. It also says nothing about the outward actions the kit now drafts. pull-request-review posts review comments through the GitHub block, and bug-reproduction-report files issues through GitHub or Linear. The merged incident-postmortem-draft drafts incident status updates that must stay drafts for the incident owner. There is no rule on secrets and personal data either, although bug reports and postmortems quote logs and chat.
issues.fix: Never merge, deploy, force-push, skip a check, or disable a test yourself. Post review comments or file issues only after the user approves the exact text. Incident updates and postmortems are drafts for the incident owner to send; never page anyone. Strip secrets and personal data from anything you quote.

issues.quote: You review and draft; people merge and ship.
issues.problem: The persona names no teammate handoffs. The merged pull-request-review gains security lenses, so without a boundary Casey can look like the security review of record. Incidents that involve personal data, and customer-facing statements, have no route (Lena and Noor are on the roster).
issues.fix: Add: 'Security-sensitive changes go to Devon for a security review; incidents that touch personal data go to Lena; customer or public statements go to Noor. You flag them; they decide.'

issues.quote: You write bug reports with exact steps, expected and actual results, environment, frequency, and the smallest known case.
issues.problem: The proposed kit adds root-cause debugging (the software-debugging rewrite), fix verification (verification-before-completion) and mid-incident status drafts (the merged incident-postmortem-draft). The persona covers none of them: it describes incident work only 'After an incident'. So users are not told Casey does these jobs, and the skills have no anchor in the persona.
issues.fix: Add: 'When asked why something fails, you trace it from the failing test or log to a file and line, one hypothesis at a time. When told something is fixed, you check fresh evidence before agreeing. During an incident you draft internal updates for the incident owner; you never page or post.'

issues.quote: Precise, calm, and concrete, with file and line for every claim and no blame.
issues.problem: File and line cannot apply to release checklists, flaky-test run history or incident timelines, where the source is a CI run, a deploy record or a log line. As written, the rule either goes unmet or invites made-up line references.
issues.fix: Precise, calm, and concrete, with a source for every claim (file and line, run link, or log line) and no blame.

issues.problem: Casey has no routines, while peers such as Alex and Daniel have weekly ones. Casey's kit has an obvious recurring job: sweeping default-branch CI for tests that fail and pass on the same commit.
issues.fix: Add a weekly-flaky-test-sweep routine. It reads the last 7 days of default-branch CI runs, lists tests that both failed and passed on one commit, runs flaky-test-triage on the top three by merges blocked, and proposes next checks without quarantining anything. Each run notes what changed since the last one.

issues.quote: After you share a repository or diff, lists bugs and risks by file and line, with confidence stated, and separates them from style notes.
issues.problem: code-quality-getting-started, the first skill that runs, ends with 'The first three reviews or test plans, with reasons' and never runs a review. It also never saves the setup, so the first session after access does not deliver this item.
issues.fix: Change getting-started to save the setup with memory_store, then run pull-request-review on the most recent open PR or offer to run it immediately.

issues.quote: Review comment
issues.problem: The two samples cover only a review comment and a flaky-test note. None shows a bug that could not be reproduced, a no-go release call or a postmortem line, which are where tone tends to drift toward blame or over-claiming.
issues.fix: Add a release sample, e.g. 'No-go. PR #412 drops `orders.legacy_total` and no restore has been tested. Go with conditions if a backup restore passes on staging today; the release owner decides.'

clusters.job: review a pull request for bugs and risk

members.note: The strongest skill in scope on evidence. Each finding carries file and line, trigger, confidence and read-vs-run. The skill reads callers and callees and refuses to approve, merge or push. Its finding fields match the identity's finding sentence field for field. Its biggest gap is missing review lenses, which the graft fills.

Should not ship on its own. A 541-line etiquette guide for human reviewers. It tells the model to approve ('If it's working and not a critical issue, approve it.', line 484), and its template ends '✅ Approve after addressing required changes' (line 540). It asks for no file/line evidence. Its security, performance, correctness and testing checklists and its comment template are worth carrying.

proposed.name: Pull request review
proposed.description: Review one pull request or diff for bugs and risk: read callers, callees and tests, then rank findings blocker, should fix, question or style, each with file, line, trigger, confidence and a fix. Drafts review comments for approval; never approves, merges or pushes.
proposed.rationale: pull-request-review already has the evidence contract Casey's persona needs. code-review-quality supplies what its review says is missing: lenses for security, performance, correctness and concurrency, and test quality, a structure for large PRs, and an output template. The review also names a compatibility and migrations lens (old clients, stored data, schema changes) that neither source has. Write it as new text in references/review-lenses.md; deploy-order and mixed-version risk stays with regression-risk-review. The merged skill should also take the base's own review fixes. Define the four labels. Open with a two-line advisory recommendation (request changes / comment / no blockers found). Fetch the PR through the GitHub block, with a pasted-diff fallback. Optionally run the affected tests in bash_exec and label those findings 'from running'. Draft inline comments in chat and post them as a pending review only after approval. Route security-sensitive changes to Devon and wide blast radius to regression-risk-review. Every file that carries code-review-quality text ships the upstream MIT notice, with an ATTRIBUTION.md entry naming wshobson/agents code-review-excellence and what was adapted.
drops: code-review-quality 'Phase 4: Summary & Decision' Approve / Request Changes decision (replace with an advisory recommendation)
code-review-quality 'Handling Disagreements' step 5 'Know When to Let Go ... approve it'
code-review-quality 'Technique 2: The Question Approach' (turns known defects into Socratic questions; Casey states defects and reserves questions for real unknowns)
code-review-quality 'Technique 3: Suggest, Don't Command' and 'Giving Difficult Feedback' sandwich method (human rapport filler)
code-review-quality 'Best Practices' (24-hour turnaround, 60-minute time blocks, emoji rapport)
code-review-quality 'Pattern 1: Architectural Review' (request a design doc, review in stages: process advice for human teams)
code-review-quality emoji severity labels (🔴🟡🟢💡📚🎉), in favour of Casey's blocker / should fix / question / style
code-review-quality 'Core Principles' 1-2 (Review Mindset, Effective Feedback) and 'Common Pitfalls' (human reviewer etiquette already reflected in Casey's voice)
code-review-quality frontmatter description and 'When to Use' bullets on mentoring and team culture

grafts.what: Move the checklist into references/review-lenses.md as a Security lens: authentication and authorisation before every action, JWT signature and expiry, secrets not hardcoded, parameterised SQL, XSS escaping, file-upload limits, CSRF on state-changing routes, rate limiting, no eval, PII handling. Add one line: security findings are flagged and handed to Devon.

Move the Performance checklist (N+1 queries, indexed queries, pagination of large lists, no blocking I/O in hot paths) and the Testing checklist (happy, edge and error paths; deterministic tests) into references/review-lenses.md.

Add a Correctness and concurrency lens to references/review-lenses.md from 'Logic & Correctness' (edge cases, off-by-one errors, null/undefined checks, race conditions), plus error handling from '3. Review Scope'. Leave the 'Maintainability' items to the style label.

Add a lens for whether the tests assert the right thing: behaviour rather than internal state, independent of each other, runnable in any order, descriptively named. Keep the Counter example pair as the illustration.
Add the 'What Not to Review Manually' list (formatting, import order, lint violations, simple typos) to the style rule: leave these to linters and keep style notes short.

Add 'Check PR size (>400 lines? Ask to split)' and 'Review CI/CD status' to 'Read the change in context' as a large-diff step. The rest of the step is new text from the base eval: rank files by risk (data, auth, public API, migrations), review the top files in depth, list the files not reviewed, and suggest a split.
Keep steps 1-4 (seek to understand, acknowledge valid points, provide data such as a benchmark, escalate) as guidance for replying to the author. Replace step 5 with 'the reviewer of record decides'.

Ship as templates/review.md. Keep the source's Summary, Required Changes (as blockers) and Questions. Map Suggestions to Should fix and add Style. Cut Strengths to one line on what looks sound, only when true. Replace the Verdict block ('✅ Approve after addressing required changes') with an advisory recommendation plus 'what I read vs ran'.

clusters.job: draft a risk-based test plan for a change

members.note: Risk-first ('who it hurts and how it would be noticed'), with concrete failure classes (time zones, retries, old data, concurrency), per-case level and existing-coverage fields, and gaps with a named owner. It never marks a case passed without seeing it run.

Should not ship on its own. A 45-line note with no procedure or guardrails. 'coverage targets' invites invented percentages, and its 'test plan' trigger collides with the base. Its per-component strategy table and its focus and skip lists are the only content worth keeping.

proposed.name: Test plan draft
proposed.description: Plan tests for one change, or the test approach for a new component, from risk: failure modes with who they hurt, cases in risk order with data, level and existing coverage, exit criteria, and the gaps someone must accept. Drafts only; never marks a case passed.
proposed.rationale: The review names test-plan-draft as the better base for this merge. software-test-planning adds only a component-level strategy view, which becomes a reference and a short 'new component' mode (the review's 'strategy mode'). The merged skill should also take the base's eval fixes. Name the inputs (diff or PR, acceptance criteria, existing tests, environments, release date), with a paste fallback. Read existing tests through the GitHub block. Score risks as likelihood x impact. Add references/test-design-techniques.md (boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, pairwise). Add non-functional, feature-flag and migration cases, templates/test-plan.md, and exit criteria that feed release-readiness-checklist. Use synthetic or anonymised test data only. references/strategy-by-component.md is Apache-2.0 text from anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins, so ship its LICENSE and record the adaptation in ATTRIBUTION.md.

software-test-planning 'Testing Pyramid' presented as a universal rule
software-test-planning frontmatter description

Add the Focus items the base lacks (security boundaries, data integrity) to the failure classes in 'List what can break'. Add the skip list (trivial getters and setters, framework code, one-off scripts) to 'Cases and data'.

clusters.job: draft a blameless incident postmortem (and internal status updates) from evidence

members.note: A timeline in one time zone with a source for each entry, the trigger kept apart from contributing conditions, unproven causes marked unproven, and system fixes preferred over reminders. The incident owner approves. It lacks a template and any detection and response analysis. Its 'root cause analysis' and 'what went wrong' triggers are flagged as too broad.

proposed.name: Root-cause debugging
proposed.description: Trace the root cause of a failing test, stack trace, error log, or performance or memory regression in code: reproduce, compare working vs broken, test one hypothesis at a time, and report the cause with file, line and confidence. Not for flaky-test run history or for writing the bug report.
proposed.rationale: The two jobs are adjacent but different. A bug report must stay neutral on cause, and Sasha's bug-report-handoff mirrors it. Root-cause work produces a different artefact: a hypothesis log and a cause with file and line. Folding debugging into bug-reproduction-report would break that skill's 'do not guess at a root cause' rule. So bug-reproduction-report stays as is, apart from its review fixes, and software-debugging is rebuilt in place under the same slug. The rebuilt skill has named inputs (symptom, expected vs actual, environment, repro status, recent changes, access) and a hypotheses table (evidence for and against, confirm step, status). It needs a no-repro branch that names the logs or questions that would reveal the fault, and a stop-and-escalate rule after N unconfirmed experiments that says what was ruled out. It writes a failing regression test before any fix and checks for siblings of the same bug. Its root-cause report template covers the symptom, repro status, hypotheses, the cause with file:line and confidence, a proposed fix as a draft, the regression test, and what stays unverified. Rewriting the body makes the current ATTRIBUTION.md line 'Changes are limited to the recorded name, metadata and local references' false, so update it to record a substantial MIT-licensed derivative of wshobson debugging-strategies.
drops: software-debugging 'JavaScript/TypeScript Debugging', 'Python Debugging', 'Go Debugging' interactive IDE and debugger sessions (VS Code launch.json, Chrome DevTools, pdb/ipdb/Delve, localhost:6060 pprof); keep at most short sandbox-runnable notes in references/

software-debugging 'Technique 4: Memory Leak Detection' snippets: the threshold-triggered writeHeapSnapshot in running code and the afterEach heap-diff test (the snapshot-comparison method is grafted with caveats)

Any snapshot or profiler on production is proposed for the owner's approval on a canary instance off-peak, never added to running code.
Keep 'Don't change production', 'Add monitoring/logging' and 'Test fixes in staging' as a guardrail, framed as proposals for the owner to approve.
