recommendations.name: Automated test draft
recommendations.purpose: Write the actual test code (unit, integration, API or end-to-end) for a bug or change in the repo's own framework, show it fail then pass where it can run, and hand over a patch or a draft PR that goes out only after approval.
recommendations.why: QA Engineer job postings nearly always ask for someone to 'design, write and maintain automated tests' in Playwright, Cypress, pytest or Jest. In the merged kit, test-plan-draft stops at a plan and bug-reproduction-report stops at a report. verification-before-completion's red-green regression check assumes a test already exists, and nothing in the kit writes one. The dropped software-test-planning had a 'write tests for' trigger that no longer has a home. The platform can do this: GithubReadFolder, GithubReadFile and GithubSearchCode can learn the repo's conventions. bash_exec can run the test at the pre-fix and post-fix commits when the repo can be cloned or is uploaded. GithubMakeBranch, GithubMultiFileCommit and GithubMakePullRequest can deliver it behind approval. Casey's identity ('You review and draft; people merge and ship') already allows drafting, and Devon's dependency-upgrade-pr sets a precedent on the roster for a drafted PR. The upstream ai-test-generation (MIT) runs a seven-step pipeline that fits Casey well: extract, risk, coverage matrix, scenarios, oracles, code, review. It also has a mechanical check that catches invented imports, selectors and endpoints.

source.ref: petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/ai-test-generation @ b3bb61bd (graft the unit-testing and api-testing references; 'watch it fail first' rule as in obra/superpowers test-driven-development, MIT)

sketch: Inputs and mode: a bug report (write a test that asserts the expected behaviour and fails now), test-plan-draft case IDs, or a spec or diff. Load the stored setup brief with memory_search, replacing upstream's .agents/qa-project-context.md.

Learn the repo's conventions before writing: framework, fixtures and factories, selector strategy, naming, CI command. Every file, import, selector and endpoint used must be found in the repo (grep check in bash_exec). Anything not found is flagged, never invented.

Write scenarios, then oracles, then code, with a comment in each test tracing it to the plan case or bug. Use specific assertions, synthetic data on example.com, no real personal data, and no sleeps or order dependence (anti-flake rules shared with flaky-test-triage).

Run status is always labelled: 'failed before fix, passed after', 'passed' or 'not run', with the exact command. A test counts as proven only if it was seen failing first; otherwise hand off to verification-before-completion with the user's pasted output.

Deliver a patch in the workspace, or a branch plus draft PR only after approval, with the approval logged. Never edit, skip, retry-wrap, quarantine or delete an existing test, and never push to a protected branch.
Keep references/unit.md, references/api.md and references/e2e.md (drop Claude-Code agent modes, Playwright init-agents and model-name routing) and templates/test-pr-description.md.

recommendations.name: Exploratory test session
recommendations.purpose: Run a time-boxed, chartered exploratory session or a post-deploy smoke check against a running web app through the browser tools, and return a session log that sorts what was seen into confirmed behaviour, questions and anomalies, with honest coverage.
recommendations.why: Exploratory, manual and smoke testing of a running build are core QA duties: session-based test management, ISTQB experience-based techniques, and 'perform exploratory, regression and smoke testing' in most postings. Every skill in the merged kit works from code, diffs, logs or pasted reports, and none drives the product itself. The platform provides browser_navigate, browser_act and browser_screenshot. The bug-reproduction-report review's top issue was that it never tries a reproduction with browser_navigate; this skill supplies that method and feeds that skill. The upstream exploratory-web-testing (MIT) is written for an agent driving a browser. It already has the right guardrails: production stays read-only, the user signs in themselves, credentials never go in chat, there is a timebox, and nothing is filed as a finding without evidence. Its Confirmed / Question / Anomaly buckets stop observed bugs from being written into a spec as intended behaviour.

source.ref: randykaskuser/qa-agent-skills skills/exploratory-web-testing @ 09581ae9 (graft charter, heuristic and debrief templates from petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/exploratory-testing, MIT)

sketch: Rules of engagement, stated back before starting: environment (production means read-only, with no form submits or writes), the user signs in in the browser (never type or request credentials), scope and timebox, and explicit leave to write data on staging.
Charter ('Explore X with Y to discover Z') and a recon inventory of routes, controls, stateful areas and console errors on a clean load, shown to the user before any probing.

Probe using references/heuristics.md (boundaries, state transitions, interruptions, error paths, locale and time zone, double submits, back button). Record each observation with time, exact text or status, and a tag, redacting as bug-reproduction-report does.
Smoke mode for after a deploy: a fixed read-only list of key flows, with results passed to release-readiness-checklist's watch window.

Debrief from templates/session-report.md: each area marked covered, partial or unexplored. Anomalies become bug-reproduction-report drafts, stable behaviours become automated-test-draft candidates, and questions go to the owner.
Drop the upstream Qase CSV export, the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} script path and the 'Casely' coupling. Carry the MIT notice.

recommendations.name: Bug and CI failure triage
recommendations.purpose: Triage a queue of new bug reports or a batch of red CI runs: fingerprint and dedupe them, classify each (product bug, test bug, flaky, environment, dependency), set severity and priority, and propose the routing, with every tracker change applied only after approval.
recommendations.why: QA engineers usually run the bug triage meeting and sort out red builds. The kit handles one bug (bug-reproduction-report) or one intermittent test (flaky-test-triage). Nothing handles a queue, and a deterministic red build on main has no entry point except the much heavier software-debugging. Upstream ai-bug-triage (MIT) is well matched to the platform. It dedupes deterministically, which bash_exec can script: normalise logs, pull stable anchors, hash, cluster. It uses the model only to classify and write. It has a severity-by-priority matrix and a rule that nothing is created, closed or merged without human approval. GithubGetCIResults (with log regex search), GithubListIssues, LinearSearchIssues and LinearGetProjectIssues can read the queues, and label, assign and comment blocks exist for approved actions.

source.ref: petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/ai-bug-triage @ b3bb61bd (with references/ci-failure-analysis.md and classification-taxonomy.md)

sketch: Inputs: a tracker query (Linear or GitHub), or a list of commits or PRs whose CI results to pull; fallback to a CSV export or pasted logs. Say how many items were seen and over what window.

scripts/fingerprint.py in bash_exec: strip timestamps, IDs, ports and ANSI codes, then hash the exception type, top frames and test name. Cluster near-duplicates and match against closed issues, so a match on a fixed bug becomes a proposal to reopen it as a regression.

Classify each cluster with its evidence and route it to one skill: intermittent goes to flaky-test-triage, a deterministic regression to software-debugging, a user-facing defect with no reproduction yet to bug-reproduction-report, security to Devon, personal data to Lena.
Share the severity and priority scale with bug-reproduction-report and templates/bug-report.md (also used by Sasha), so all three use one vocabulary.
Proposed-actions table (create, merge into, label, assign, quarantine proposal, dismiss with reason). Apply nothing until approved and log each approval. Never auto-close.
Remove upstream buy-versus-build vendor tables and model-cost notes.

recommendations.name: Weekly quality health digest
recommendations.purpose: Once a week (or on request), report a few agreed quality measures: default-branch CI pass rate, flake rate, open bugs by severity and age, escaped defects, and change failure rate. Each comes with its denominator, the week-over-week movers, and the follow-up skill each mover calls for.
recommendations.why: The review found that Casey has no routines, and nothing in the kit gives a trend view: every skill handles one PR, bug, test or release. QA leads usually report flakiness, pass rate, defect escape rate and the DORA change-failure rate. Upstream qa-metrics (MIT) supplies formulas, targets by company stage, and 'what to do when it goes red' per metric. The platform supports it: schedule_routine; GithubListCommits plus GithubGetCIResults per SHA; GithubListIssues, GithubListReleases and Linear search; bash_exec for the arithmetic; memory_store for the agreed definitions and last week's baseline. A digest is also the natural routine to set up at the end of code-quality-getting-started.

source.ref: petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/qa-metrics @ b3bb61bd (formulas and stage targets; the routine wrapper and digest template are new)

sketch: First run: agree three to five measures with definitions, data sources and targets (startup-stage defaults from references/metrics.md), then store them with memory_store.

Gather the window's data from blocks, falling back to a CSV export or paste. Compute in bash_exec, showing numerator, denominator and sample size. Label each number as sourced or assumed, and mark a measure 'too few runs' rather than reporting a noisy percentage.

List movers against last week's stored baseline, each paired with the action it triggers: a new flake goes to flaky-test-triage, a spike in escapes to incident-postmortem-draft or regression-risk-review, and a batch of untriaged bugs to bug-and-failure-triage.
Draft from templates/quality-digest.md. Posting to Slack or email happens only after approval, and the digest never states that the build is healthy without run evidence.
Set up the routine with schedule_routine, confirming day, time and time zone. Add a matching entry to casey.yml routines.

recommendations.name: Accessibility check
recommendations.purpose: Check a page or flow against WCAG 2.2 AA using a keyboard pass, structure checks and computed contrast (plus an axe or Lighthouse report when one is available). Findings name the success criterion, the element and the confidence, and no conformance claim is ever made.
recommendations.why: No skill in Casey's kit, or anywhere in the catalog, tests accessibility. The only mention was one line in the dropped software-test-planning. Accessibility checks are a routine QA request, and the EU Accessibility Act has applied since 28 June 2025. Upstream accessibility-testing (MIT) is sound and says plainly that automated tools catch only 30-40% of issues. It orders checks by impact (keyboard first, then screen reader, then automated) and includes keyboard, form and contrast checklists. The platform can run most of it: browser_act for tab order, focus visibility, traps and Escape; page reading for titles, headings, labels, alt text and error association; bash_exec for contrast ratios and for parsing a pasted axe or Lighthouse JSON. Legal and VPAT questions go to Lena and public accessibility statements to Noor.

source.ref: petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/accessibility-testing @ b3bb61bd (checklists and WCAG 2.2 quick reference; drop the Playwright/axe CI recipes as default path)

sketch: Scope: pages, flows and interactive states (modal open, menu expanded), target level (default WCAG 2.2 AA), and environment, using the same read-only production rule as exploratory-test-session.

Automated layer: parse an axe or Lighthouse report the user supplies, or run axe-core in the sandbox only for a publicly reachable page and only with the user's agreement. Say which criteria automation cannot check.
Manual layer through the browser tools: the keyboard checklist, a structure check, and scripts/contrast.py for text and UI contrast.

Findings table: WCAG criterion, element or selector, file and line when source is available, impact, and how it was found (tool, keyboard or reading), with confidence. List what was not tested, such as real screen readers.
Never state conformance or legal compliance. Send VPAT and legal questions to Lena and statements to Noor. Draft fixes as issues or automated-test-draft candidates, filed only after approval.

recommendations.name: Acceptance criteria testability review
recommendations.purpose: Before build starts, review a story, ticket or PRD for testability: flag vague or compound criteria and missing error, limit and permission cases, and propose Given/When/Then scenarios with example data for the spec owner to accept.
recommendations.why: QA engineers join refinement sessions ('three amigos') and are expected to make acceptance criteria testable before code exists (ISTQB static testing, shift-left practice). Casey's kit starts at the diff. Alex (product-prd-and-acceptance-criteria) and Priya (product-requirements-draft) write criteria, but nothing reviews a spec someone else wrote from the tester's side. A QA review before build is cheaper than a regression review afterwards. The ticket can be read through the Linear or GitHub blocks, with paste as the fallback.

source.ref: New, written by us. Optional graft of the ambiguous-step lint rules from petrkindlmann/qa-skills test-case-management and the three-amigos prompts from shift-left-testing (MIT), which would make it upstream and require the MIT notice

sketch: Inputs: the story, PRD or ticket and its linked design. Triggers kept apart from Alex's and Priya's 'acceptance criteria' (for example 'is this story testable', 'review these ACs', 'Gherkin scenarios', 'three amigos').
Lint list: vague words ('fast', 'intuitive', 'etc.'), missing actor, state or data, compound criteria, and outcomes that cannot be observed.
Missing-case sweep: errors, empty and maximum values, permissions, concurrency, time zones, old data, retries and rollback. Each gap names who it would hurt.
Given/When/Then rewrites with example data, each marked 'proposed by Casey' for the owner to accept. Scope and priority stay with the spec owner (consult Alex or Priya).
Comments on the ticket only after approval. Accepted scenarios go on to test-plan-draft and automated-test-draft.

recommendations.name: Test suite gap audit
recommendations.purpose: Audit a whole test suite from coverage and results reports: rank untested code by risk, and list skipped, disabled, slow and never-failing tests. Every change is a proposal for the owner.
recommendations.why: Teams ask QA 'where are our testing gaps?' across the whole suite, not per change. test-plan-draft only covers one change, and flaky-test-triage one test. Coverage and result formats (lcov, Cobertura XML, coverage.py JSON, JUnit XML) are simple to parse in bash_exec, and GithubListCommits and issue history supply churn and bug counts for a risk ranking. Upstream coverage-analysis and test-suite-curation (MIT) bring the right warnings: coverage measures execution, not assertion quality. Deletion is destructive and needs human sign-off. Skipped tests are hidden gaps.

source.ref: petrkindlmann/qa-skills skills/coverage-analysis @ b3bb61bd (plus tiering and destructive-safety references from skills/test-suite-curation)

sketch: Inputs: a coverage report, JUnit or CI results, and repo access. Name the report date and commit, and never estimate coverage without a report.
scripts/parse_reports.py: line and branch coverage per module; inventory of skipped and disabled tests with age; slowest tests; tests with no failure across the sampled history.
Risk rank each module by coverage gap × churn (commits in window) × linked bug count, showing the working and labelling assumptions.
Recommendations: tests to add (sent to automated-test-draft), tests to review, and a smoke/core/extended tiering proposal. Deleting, skipping or quarantining is left to the owner.
Caveats section: coverage is not assertion quality; suggest mutation testing only as an optional next step.

recommendations.notes:
I opened every skill in the kit, including the Toran packages, before calling anything a gap. I read catalog_index.md in full and checked the neighbouring kits: Devon's security skills, Robin's technical-diagnostics-with-tools, Alex's and Priya's spec skills, and Sasha's bug-report-handoff. No catalog skill covers exploratory or browser-driven testing, writing test code, accessibility, bug-queue or CI-failure triage, QA metrics, or suite-level coverage. DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has nothing for engineering or QA.

Sources. Both upstream repos were cloned and read. I checked that both licences are MIT and that the pinned raw URLs return 200:
- petrkindlmann/qa-skills @ b3bb61bd268b147476252c6ed5a0440c87b97441: 50 QA skills; each SKILL.md declares license: MIT.
- randykaskuser/qa-agent-skills @ 09581ae9f8a549369154bd6dae16af3e0d3c4c94: its bundled 'casely' is itself vendored MIT.

Both need the usual harness fixes:
- Replace `.agents/qa-project-context.md` with memory_search on the setup brief.
- Remove model-name routing (Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.8, Fable 5), Playwright MCP and init-agents with `.claude/agents`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, the Qase export and the 'Casely' coupling.
- Rewrite the exploratory-testing passages that assume a human tester (the 'never delegate to an LLM' section) for an AI tester.

I checked the AutoGPT blocks: GithubGetCIResults (per SHA or PR, with log regex), GithubListCommits, GithubListIssues, GithubSearchCode, GithubReadFile and GithubReadFolder, GithubMakeBranch, GithubMultiFileCommit, GithubMakePullRequest, and Linear search, create and comment all exist. The sandbox has no user secrets, so it can only clone a private repo if the user uploads an archive. automated-test-draft therefore needs a 'not run' path that gives the exact command to run and hands the result to verification-before-completion.

Trigger collisions to settle when merging:
- The dropped software-test-planning's 'write tests for' should move to automated-test-draft, and test-plan-draft keeps 'test plan'.
- Triage phrasing splits three ways within Casey's kit: bug-and-failure-triage (a queue or a red build), flaky-test-triage (intermittent) and bug-reproduction-report (one bug). Sasha's customer-ticket triage is separate.
- acceptance-criteria-review must avoid the bare 'acceptance criteria' trigger that Alex and Priya already use.

Persona follow-ups if the must items land:
- bio and identity should mention drafting automated tests and running exploratory or smoke sessions in test environments.
- boundaries should add 'production is read-only in the browser; never type or ask for credentials'.
- routines should gain the weekly quality-health-digest, which also fixes the 'no routines' finding.

Considered and not recommended:
- Load and performance testing (k6): generating load from the sandbox is risky and it is rare for Casey's small-team audience. software-debugging already covers profiling.
- Standalone API contract testing: fold it into automated-test-draft as references/api.md, and run API exploration inside exploratory-test-session.
- CI pipeline design (qa-skills ci-cd-integration): outside a reviewer's remit, since it means writing workflow files.
- anthropics/skills webapp-testing (Apache-2.0): it assumes a local dev server plus a Playwright and Chromium install, which fits worse than the platform's browser tools.
- Security testing: stays with Devon (code-change-security-review is proposed for Devon), and Casey hands off.

proposal.summary: Daniel's live kit is ten NICK skills, all of which need fixes. All five of Toran's upstream packages, each thinner than the live skills, cover jobs that three of those skills already do, so none adds a new job. The proposal keeps all ten slugs in their current order, so the identity routing, the four routines and the getting-started menu need no renames. It merges into three bases. close-controls-and-accounting takes the dependency map and status tracking from month-end-close-management (via Mina's PR #14 adaptation, including its small-business close calendar) plus account-reconciliation's reconciling-item categories, aging and escalation rules; every post, lock or adjust step is handed to the controller. variance-and-flux-analysis takes financial-statement-preparation's volume/price/mix decomposition (written so it sums exactly), scaled materiality and a period-end-adjustment "is it real?" check. finance-board-and-investor-reporting takes board-deck-builder's 6-8 KPI dashboard, CFO finance section and bad-news framework, plus portfolio monitoring's trend and questions-for-management blocks. All five Toran packages drop as standalone skills. PR #13 still leaves the slash command and ~~erp placeholders in financial-statement-preparation. Two packages have ungated posting or locking steps. board-deck-builder assigns sections to C-suite owners. Portfolio monitoring is framed for private equity. Other must-fixes: the saas magic-number x4 blocker, the CAC denominator, the hardcoded 15% in BvA and the Monday routine (it also ignores direction), a board-pack routine that fires once on calendar day 6 against a business-day close, and a voice sample whose straight-line math is wrong (it lands about 81k over, not 41k). Across experts: transaction-level close and reconciliation defer to Mina's PR #14 rebuild. Her P&L skill does not cover balance-sheet or cash-flow statements, so those route to the CPA. Investor updates defer to Theo, pricing design to Zara, CRM hygiene and the deal-level forecast to Omar, and product or funnel metric moves to Quinn.

body_review.summary:
The persona is sharp and internally consistent. FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels, fixed variance shapes, R/Y/G definitions, drafts-only gates and quiet-when-green routines all match the skills. The main defects:
- A voice sample with a wrong number, which is bad for a persona sold on honest numbers.
- The Monday pacing rule and the day-one promise hardcode 15%, ignore the identity's own threshold and quiet floor, and flag in both directions regardless of whether the line is cost or revenue.
- The weekly variance routine produces what the variance skill itself calls a timing artifact.
- The board-pack routine fires once on calendar day 6 against a business-day-5-7 close, so it usually finds the close not done and never re-checks.
- The boundaries read as though Daniel may approve discounts inside the band.
- The handoffs skip the finance and revenue teammates (bookkeeper, investor relations, procurement, RevOps).
strengths: Every load-bearing figure is labeled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN, and a missing period is named rather than projected across. The identity, bio, boundaries, the routines[0] step 5 gap rule and every skill's Fallbacks section all say the same thing.
The identity routing paragraph maps each topic to exactly one kit skill, in kit order, so the model has an unambiguous dispatch table.

Fixed shapes make reads comparable period to period: the variance line format, the R/Y/G definitions, a default threshold of the greater of 10% or 5,000 with a 500 quiet floor, and Base/Adverse/Opportunity grades that each need a named driver.

All four routines are off until switched on, send one line when nothing needs action, and collapse repeat flags (or an unanswered offer) into one line. Each ends with an explicit never-do line: never change a budget, never message a vendor, never book or sign off, never message the board.

The connection check names only integrations the platform has blocks for (Sheets, Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Stripe), asks for an export for card spend, warehouse and ERP data, and never blocks on a connection.
body_review.kit_alignment:
All ten routed slugs survive with unchanged names, so the identity routing, the four routines and daniel-getting-started's starter menu stay valid after the merges. Promise gaps:
(1) day_one[1] promises a price/volume/mix/timing decomposition that variance-and-flux-analysis names but never defines. The financial-statement-preparation graft closes it, as long as the mix line is defined so the three effects still sum.
(2) day_one[0] and routines[0] hardcode a 15% underspend rule and flag any overrun regardless of the threshold or direction. This conflicts with the identity's 10%/5,000 threshold and 500 floor, and it is also BvA's top review issue.
(3) routines[2] runs a weekly actual-vs-plan read, which the variance skill says is a timing artifact unless the plan is phased.
(4) routines[1] promises renewal dates, but no Daniel skill sources them from contracts.
(5) routines[3] fires only on calendar day 6, while the close targets are business days 5-7 (usually calendar day 7-10). It reads close status from the ledger instead of the close checklist and never re-checks.
(6) No route covers preparing the P&L, balance sheet or cash-flow statement. Toran's financial-statement-preparation is not added, and Mina's PR #14 P&L summary excludes the balance sheet and cash flow.
(7) The merged board skill's description should stop claiming 'investor updates' outright; the identity routing line can stay but should say 'the finance numbers for investor updates' once Theo is on the team.

issues.quote: Marketing is at 78% of a 120k plan on day 14 of 30. At that run rate it lands 41k over (INFERENCE, straight-line on 14 days of actuals).
issues.problem: The arithmetic is wrong. 78% of 120k is 93.6k spent in 14 days. Straight-line over 30 days that is about 200.6k, or about 81k over, not 41k. A persona whose tagline is 'Keeps your numbers honest' ships a sample with a wrong INFERENCE, and samples teach the model its style.
issues.fix: Change it to 'lands about 81k over'. Alternatively, change the premise to 'has spent 75k of a 120k plan on day 14 of 30', which gives 160.7k (about 41k over) and keeps the rest of the sample.

issues.quote: flags what lands over and what is pacing 15% under
issues.problem: The hardcoded 15% ignores the variance threshold and quiet floor that the identity defines and getting-started saves. It is also direction-blind: a revenue line landing over plan is good news, and a cost underspend can be a real saving. This is budget-vs-actuals-and-reforecast's top review issue, repeated in the day-one promise.
issues.fix: Rewrite it as: 'flags lines landing past your variance threshold in the unfavorable direction (cost over, revenue under), and marks favorable landings past the threshold as a yellow watch line'. Make the same change in BvA's 'Flag both directions' section.

issues.quote: Flag lines on course to finish over plan, each with the run rate that would bring it back to plan, and lines running 15% or more below pace.
issues.problem: Both halves ignore the identity's 'greater of 10% or 5,000' threshold and the 500 quiet floor, and both ignore direction. A 1-unit overrun fires. A revenue line landing over plan is flagged as a problem. A revenue line 12% under pace never fires. So the Monday read grades lines on a different rule from the Friday variance read.
issues.fix: Replace it with: 'Flag lines whose month-end landing misses plan by more than the saved variance threshold in the unfavorable direction (cost over, revenue under), each with the run rate that brings it back to plan; mark favorable landings past the threshold as one yellow watch line; skip lines under the quiet floor.'

issues.quote: Run the variance read for the week: over-plan, under-plan, and flat-or-timing blocks with gaps in currency AND percent
issues.problem: variance-and-flux-analysis says 'a half-month against a full plan is not a variance, it is a timing artifact'. A weekly Friday run against a monthly plan produces exactly that three weeks in four, unless the plan is phased or prorated.
issues.fix: Add: 'compare month-to-date actuals to the month-to-date phased plan (straight-line if no phasing is saved, labeled INFERENCE); outside close week, grade timing-only gaps yellow at most'.

issues.quote: If the close is not done, say so in one line and wait for the close-done flag instead of offering a preliminary pack.
issues.problem: The cron is 'H 9 6 * *' (calendar day 6 only), but the close skill's targets are business days: flash around business day 2, hard close on day 5-7, which usually falls on calendar day 7-10. In most months the routine therefore says 'not done', and nothing re-checks until next month, so the pack reminder silently skips. Nothing wakes the routine on a close-done flag. Step 1 also reads close status from the finance ledger, but the close checklist holds it. Moving the cron to day 8 still misses a business-day-7 close in months that start on a weekend.
issues.fix: Rewrite step 1: 'Read close status from the close checklist or the saved close-done signal. If the close is not done, schedule_followup for the next business day and re-check, up to business day 10; then say in one line that the close is late and stop.'

issues.quote: Never book a journal entry, post to the books, move a budget line, approve a discount outside the guardrail bands, sign off a close, or write to the CRM.
issues.problem: This implies Daniel may approve a discount inside the bands. deal-economics-and-pricing-guardrails says 'You never approve a discount', and an inside-band ask only gets 'a draft approval note for the owner to send'. The identity repeats the ambiguity with 'no discount approved outside its band'.
issues.fix: Change it to 'approve any discount (an inside-band ask gets a draft approval note for the owner)'. Mirror the change in the identity's drafts paragraph.

issues.quote: closing a sale goes to sales with the deal math, support tickets go to support with the billing facts
issues.problem:
The handoff list names sales, support and engineering but not the finance and revenue teammates Daniel overlaps with most:
- Transaction-level bookkeeping and statement reconciliations belong with Mina (PR #14 statement-reconciliation and month-end-close-checklist).
- Investor distribution belongs with Theo.
- Contract notice dates come from Vera.
- CRM hygiene fixes belong with Omar.
- At-risk renewal save plays belong with Riley.
issues.fix: Add: 'transaction coding and statement reconciliations go to the bookkeeper, investor-update distribution and fundraising records go to investor relations, contract notice dates come from procurement, CRM hygiene fixes go to revenue operations, and save plays for at-risk renewals go to customer success'.

issues.quote: anything partner-, customer-, board-, or investor-facing is a draft that waits for the owner's yes to that specific action
issues.problem: There is no confidentiality or forward-looking rule. Budget lines with owners can expose per-person compensation, and board packs are board-confidential. Theo's board-and-investor-metrics-brief carries 'keep board-confidential material within its approved group' and a rule never to 'present a forecast as assured'. Daniel's boundaries have neither.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: 'Board-confidential figures and per-person pay stay with the owner's approved audience; forecasts are labeled forecasts, never assured; no investment or securities advice.'

issues.quote: Takes the move apart by price, volume, mix and timing
issues.problem: variance-and-flux-analysis lists these drivers but gives no formula. Toran's review flags that no validated price-volume-mix decomposition was selected, since the one found omitted an interaction term. As shipped, this day-one promise has no method behind it.
issues.fix: Keep the line and ship the graft into variance-and-flux-analysis. For one item: volume effect = (Q1 - Q0) x P0 and price effect = (P1 - P0) x Q1, which sum exactly to the total. Across items: split volume into the total-volume change at the prior average price plus a mix line, so volume + mix + price still sum exactly.

issues.quote: Scan commitments inside the renewal window, largest spend first. Each line gets vendor, renewal date, annual spend, and the one question for the owner.
issues.problem: Spend exports and the ledger carry spend, not renewal or notice dates. No Daniel skill extracts dates from contracts; Vera's contract-renewal-tracker and James's ops-vendor-and-procurement do.
issues.fix: Add: 'take renewal and notice dates from the owner's contract tracker (procurement's, when hired); a commitment with no sourced date is listed with renewal date UNKNOWN'.

issues.quote: Runway is 7.4 months on current burn and 5.9 on forecast burn — I trust the forecast one, payroll steps up in March.
issues.problem: voice_preferences requires every figure to be labeled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN, but none of this sample's figures (7.4, 5.9, 250k floor, 18k, 96k) carries a label. The sample teaches the opposite of the preference.
issues.fix: Add labels inline, for example '5.9 on forecast burn (INFERENCE, March payroll step included)' and 'Two invoices totaling 96k (FACT, AR aging)'.

issues.quote: month-end, accruals, reconciliations and audit prep go to close, controls and accounting
issues.problem: No route covers 'prepare our P&L / management accounts / balance sheet'. Toran's financial-statement-preparation is not being added, and Mina's PR #14 monthly-profit-and-loss-summary covers only the P&L: it explicitly excludes balance-sheet and cash-flow statements. The model may improvise a statement build, which crosses into the bookkeeper's and CPA's work.
issues.fix: Add to the routing paragraph: 'a P&L-versus-plan read goes to variance and flux analysis; the monthly P&L summary goes to the bookkeeper; balance-sheet and cash-flow statements go to the CPA with the trial balance attached'.

clusters.job: Run and track the month-end close: checklist, sequencing, accruals, key-account reconciliations, controls evidence, audit prep

members.note: It has Daniel's gates ('You never book an entry and never sign off a close'), preparer/reviewer segregation, PBC staging, the flux hand-off and the close-watch behaviour the Friday routine uses. Top issue: it names a checklist template it doesn't ship, and its five block names give no calendar, dependencies or day sequence. The grafts supply both.

Dropped as a standalone skill. Its structure is the best in the cluster: a five-level dependency map, critical path, status dashboard with a Blocker column, status definitions, close KPIs and retrospective questions. It has no intake or gate. Its checklist says 'Post payroll entries and payroll accrual', 'Lock the period in the ERP/GL system' and 'Finalize financial statements — hard close', and its T+1..T+5 calendar is enterprise (tax provision, equity roll-forward, consolidation). Carry the structure only. Mina's PR #14 already adapts it for a small business: references/close-dependency-map.md keeps posting and locking with the owner, and references/close-calendar.md is a days 1-10 small-business calendar. Both are better graft sources than the raw upstream text.

Dropped as a standalone skill. It has no intake or matching procedure. Category 2 says 'Action: Prepare adjusting journal entry to correct the GL or subledger' with no draft or approval gate. Its three-way item categorization, aging buckets, escalation table and two-sided bank-rec layout fill the base's one-line 'Reconcile the key accounts early'.

proposed.name: Close, controls and accounting
proposed.description: Use for the finance lead's view of month-end close: close status against the calendar and dependency order, accrual completeness, key-account reconciliation status with aged reconciling items, the flux tie-out, control evidence and audit PBC prep. grafts.what:
Show formulas with the numbers plugged in.
- One item: volume effect = (Q1 - Q0) x P0 and price/rate effect = (P1 - P0) x Q1. Together they sum exactly to the total, with no residual.
- Several items with different rates: volume = (total Q1 - total Q0) x prior average price, mix = sum of Q1_i x P0_i minus total Q1 x prior average price, and price = sum of (P1_i - P0_i) x Q1_i. Volume + mix + price still sum exactly.
- New or discontinued items, one-time items, timing and currency effect each get their own line.
This closes Toran's 'omitted an interaction term' gap and backs the day_one[1] promise.

grafts.section: Common Adjustments and Reclassifications > Period-End Adjustments; Reclassifications
grafts.what:
Add a new 'Is it real?' step before decomposition. Rule out:
- a missed or reversed accrual

- depreciation not run
- FX revaluation
- a reclassification
- the three the review names that FSP lacks: cutoff errors, duplicate postings, and miscoding to the wrong account (from account-reconciliation's 'Recording errors' and 'Classification errors')
- one-offs
A gap explained by any of these is labeled accounting/timing and handed to the close skill, not narrated as a business driver. This fixes the review's top issue.

proposal.summary:
Devon's live kit is eight ORIGINAL placeholders of about 37 lines each, and every one needs fixes. PR 2 (NICK) added nothing for Devon. The open rebuild PRs (#14, #15, #16) carry Devon's expert file and skills unchanged. Toran proposed two Trail of Bits packages. supply-chain-risk-auditor is the strongest ref: stdlib-only scripts measure advisories, deprecation, publisher concentration and install scripts, with three-state coverage. code-change-security-review is weaker and needs more platform fixes.

There are two merges. vulnerability-triage absorbs cve-stack-relevance: they share the four relevance labels and the exposure chain, and their triggers compete. The merged skill keeps a full single-advisory path, so no capability is lost. A new dependency-upgrade skill is built on dependency-upgrade-plan. It takes dependency-upgrade-pr's narrow-change, validation and PR-body sections, with an explicit approval gate before any push.

supply-chain-risk-auditor stays separate from dependency-change-risk-review, because one audits the whole tree and the other reviews one change. The change review borrows the auditor's "unassessable is not risk" rule. It uses the auditor's measurements only where they exist (npm), and keeps its own checks for PyPI and Go.

PR #13 changes only one line in the auditor, which still needs harness fixes. It needs a python3 fallback, a gh warning and project intake. It needs OSV detail fetch with a malicious-package branch, a fallback for pnpm, yarn and poetry lockfiles, and a check for private-registry names before public lookups.

code-change-security-review joins only after fixes PR #13 does not make:
- Remove the subagent dispatch.
- Replace the Desktop and ~/.claude report paths.
- Remove the uninstalled issue-writer and audit-context-building commands.
- Add web and API patterns beside the mostly Solidity set.
- Clone into the sandbox rather than check out in the user's tree.

The result is an 8-skill kit. The body needs these changes:
- Rename the entries in its skills list.
- Add a routine for the "keep current" promise.
- Add boundary lines on push approval, live probing, untrusted installs and private package names.
- Add an identity paragraph for source-diff security review and malicious-package incidents.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and evidence-led. The identity's rules match the kit well: requested versus installed versions, four relevance labels, 'Severity alone never decides the order', and a passing test is not proof of safety. The gaps are coverage and boundaries. The skills list names three slugs that this proposal merges or renames, and it omits both Toran adds. The bio promises reachability ranking, SBOM input and keeping dependencies current, and no current skill or routine delivers those. The boundaries do not gate the real side effects of the upgrade and review skills: pushing branches or opening PRs, running exploit code, installing untrusted packages, and sending internal package names to public registries.
strengths: The identity separates the requested manifest range from the locked version, and runtime, development, direct and transitive dependencies. This is exactly dependency-inventory's discipline.
One relevance vocabulary ('confirmed, likely, not affected, or unknown') runs through the identity and the triage skills, so outputs stay consistent.
'A passing test run is evidence for the tested behaviour, not proof that the whole system is safe' is a senior-grade rule that stops over-claiming.

The voice samples are concrete: a locked version, the vulnerable path, a target version, tests to run, a rescan, and the source checked. The upgrade note splits a patch hop from a major hop and says nothing was merged.
The two day_one items map cleanly to the proposed kit: baseline = dependency-inventory + outdated-dependency-review; ranked queue = vulnerability-triage + dependency-upgrade.
body_review.kit_alignment: skills[] lists cve-stack-relevance, dependency-upgrade-plan and dependency-upgrade-pr. Under this proposal they become vulnerability-triage (merged) and dependency-upgrade (new slug). supply-chain-risk-auditor and code-change-security-review are missing. preloads and routines are empty, and day_one names no slugs, so nothing else names a dropped slug. Three promises have no covering skill today. 'Rank the work by reachability' has no reachability method and no KEV or EPSS input in any triage skill. SBOM is promised as an input, but neither inventory nor the auditor ingests CycloneDX or SPDX. 'Keep software dependencies current' has no routine. The identity also says nothing about source-diff security review, the supply-chain metadata audit, or treating a known-malicious package as an incident rather than an upgrade. The two Toran adds introduce all three.

issues.quote: cve-stack-relevance
issues.problem: The list still names cve-stack-relevance, dependency-upgrade-plan and dependency-upgrade-pr, which this proposal merges into vulnerability-triage and dependency-upgrade. It omits supply-chain-risk-auditor and code-change-security-review.
issues.fix: Replace with, in order: dependency-security-getting-started, dependency-inventory, outdated-dependency-review, vulnerability-triage, supply-chain-risk-auditor, dependency-upgrade, dependency-change-risk-review, code-change-security-review.

issues.quote: Never merge, deploy, suppress a finding, or claim a vulnerability is fixed without verified advisory, stack, version, and test evidence.
issues.problem: This covers merge and deploy but none of the kit's other side effects. Pushing a branch, opening a PR or posting review comments through GitHub is not gated. Nothing forbids running exploit code or probing live systems to prove exposure. Nothing stops installing an unfamiliar package, which runs its lifecycle scripts in the sandbox. Nothing keeps undisclosed vulnerability details out of public PRs. The auditor also sends every direct dependency name to public npm, PyPI, OSV, deps.dev and Scorecard, which can leak internal package names.
issues.fix: Append: 'Never push a branch, open a pull request, or post review comments until the user has seen the diff and approved. Never run exploit code or probe live systems. Install unfamiliar packages only with install scripts disabled. Ask before sending private or internal package names to public registries or advisory services. Keep undisclosed vulnerability details out of public PRs and issues.'

issues.quote: You may prepare a branch, patch, commit plan, or pull request draft when asked, but you do not merge or deploy.
issues.problem: 'When asked' lets a general request authorise a push or PR creation. The merged dependency-upgrade skill needs an explicit per-diff approval gate, and the top review issue for dependency-upgrade-pr was exactly this missing gate.
issues.fix: Rewrite: 'You prepare the patch and pull request body, show them, and push or open a draft pull request only after the user approves; without write access you hand over a patch file. You do not merge or deploy.'

issues.quote: You are Devon, a software dependency and security hygiene specialist.
issues.problem: The identity covers dependencies only. It gives no stance for the security review of a source diff (code-change-security-review), the measured supply-chain audit (supply-chain-risk-auditor), or a known-malicious package (an OSV MAL-* entry), which needs incident handling rather than a version bump. It names no teammate handoffs: Casey for general PR, regression and release review; Lena for questionnaire answers and counsel escalation; the owner or counsel for licence changes.
issues.fix: Add a paragraph. When reviewing a code change for security, cite the file, the line and the attacker precondition for each finding, state coverage and confidence, and never run a proof of concept against a live system. Treat a malicious-package advisory as an incident: stop, tell the owner, and do not just bump the version. Route general correctness and release checks to Casey. Route questionnaire answers and licence questions that need counsel to Lena. Supply dated evidence, not answers.

issues.quote: rank the work by reachability, exploit conditions, and business impact
issues.problem: No current skill gives a reachability method (dependency path, govulncheck, symbol search, image SBOM) or exploit signals (CISA KEV, EPSS, public PoC). The top issue in the vulnerability-triage eval is that urgency is never defined.
issues.fix: Add a reachability step and an urgency matrix to the merged vulnerability-triage. The matrix maps relevance × KEV/EPSS/PoC × exposure to P0–P3, with the deadline taken from user policy or labelled as an assumption. Otherwise soften the bio to 'exposure evidence'.

issues.problem: The bio opens with 'I keep software dependencies current', but there is no recurring work. Advisories change weekly, and nothing re-checks the stored inventory.
issues.fix: Add opt-in routines. A weekly advisory re-check runs vulnerability-triage against the inventory.csv that dependency-inventory wrote to the workspace, using the scope stored in memory. A monthly run of outdated-dependency-review. Offer both from dependency-security-getting-started via schedule_routine.

issues.quote: I have not changed production or merged either branch.
issues.problem: supply-chain-risk-auditor's 'Style for what you add' forbids first person ('no first or second person') and applies it to 'the report addendum and the final reply alike'. That conflicts with Devon's first-person voice whenever the auditor runs.
issues.fix: When packaging the auditor, scope its impersonal register to report.md and the addendum, and let the chat reply follow Devon's voice.

issues.quote: Application Security Engineer
issues.problem: Without code-change-security-review the kit is dependency-only, and the title over-promises source-code AppSec work.
issues.fix: Keep the title only if code-change-security-review lands with its fixes. Otherwise retitle to 'Dependency Security Engineer'.

issues.quote: Give me a repository, lockfile, software bill of materials, or scanner export
issues.problem: SBOM input is promised, but dependency-inventory has no CycloneDX or SPDX ingest. supply-chain-risk-auditor reads only package.json, pyproject/requirements, go.mod and three lockfile types.
issues.fix: Have dependency-inventory accept an uploaded CycloneDX or SPDX file as a source and emit inventory.csv. Say in the auditor that SBOM-only input goes through the inventory first.

issues.quote: High priority: GHSA-xxxx affects the locked parser version in the API image.
issues.problem: The placeholder ID reads as a template, and the sample shows no exploit signal, so it does not model the urgency basis the merged triage will require.
issues.fix: Keep a neutral ID, but add the urgency basis, e.g. 'Not in CISA KEV; reachable from the public upload endpoint.'

clusters.job: Decide whether scanner findings or an advisory affect the shipped stack, and rank the fixes

members.note: Batch-queue skeleton: 'Verify before ranking', then 'Add stack evidence', 'Set the queue' and 'Guardrails'. It matches day_one 'A ranked security queue'. Its review says 'Add stack evidence' restates cve-stack-relevance's chain and that the two compete for 'are we vulnerable' and 'dependency alert'. Both evals proposed differentiating with handoffs. A merge with an explicit single-advisory path settles the same competition with one trigger surface. vulnerability-triage is the base even though its sibling is slightly stronger as written, because the merged job is the queue and the chain slots into it section for section.

It uses the same four labels (confirmed/likely/not affected/unknown) and the same exposure checks, as an explicit seven-question chain. It also has the rules 'Do not use absence from a scanner as proof of safety' and fix-present-in-built-artifact, plus conflict explanation across sources. All of that carries over. Its review gaps (source order, alias resolution, KEV/EPSS, VEX justification, stopping rules, no-probing rule) must be written new in the merged skill.

proposed.name: Vulnerability triage
proposed.description: Use when a scanner export, Dependabot alert, SBOM match or a single CVE/GHSA needs a verdict: verify the advisory and affected range, prove exposure in the shipped stack, label confirmed / likely / not affected / unknown, and rank fixes by exploit signals and exposure.
proposed.rationale:
Two 37-line skills with the same labels and overlapping checks split one job by batch size. One skill with two paths removes the trigger competition. The single-advisory path runs the full chain. The batch path normalises, then runs a quick pass, then the full chain on the top rows.

Neither member has the following, which the reviews flagged, so it must be written new:
- Minimum inputs via ask_question: scanner and format, repo or image access, service exposure, SLA policy. State which conclusions degrade to 'unknown' without them.
- A source order: maintainer or vendor, then GHSA/OSV, then NVD. Resolve CVE/GHSA/PYSEC aliases through the OSV API. For OS packages, take the fixed version from the distro tracker (backports), and treat 'no fix / will not fix' as its own state.
- A normalise step that collapses aliases and groups rows by remediation action: one upgrade or image rebuild per row, listing the finding IDs it clears.
- Reachability methods: dependency path via npm ls, pipdeptree or go mod why; govulncheck or osv-scanner when present; symbol or config search; image SBOM rather than the source manifest. Use a paste fallback when access is missing.
- Chain stopping rules: the first proven 'no' gives not affected, and the first step with no evidence gives unknown.
- An urgency matrix: relevance × exploitation signal (CISA KEV, EPSS, public PoC) × exposure (internet-facing, internal, dev-only), mapped to P0–P3. The deadline comes from the user's SLA or is labelled an assumption.
- A 'safe target' definition: the minimum fixed version on the current supported line.
- A VEX-style justification and a recheck trigger for every 'not affected' result. Devon drafts it and the owner accepts it.
- A queue table template and a summary.
- A rule never to run exploit code or probe live systems.
- Handoff of the chosen fix, including transitive override options, to dependency-upgrade.
drops: vulnerability-triage's '## Add stack evidence' prose paragraph, replaced by the grafted seven-question chain. Its clause 'which controls reduce the risk' is kept as a compensating-controls check under questions 5 and 7.
cve-stack-relevance scope line 'Use this for one advisory or a small related set.' (the merged skill handles one or many)
cve-stack-relevance's duplicate definition of the four relevance labels
cve-stack-relevance as a separate description/trigger surface

grafts.what: The seven numbered questions replace '## Add stack evidence': package/ecosystem match; installed version in the verified affected range; shipped service includes and loads it; vulnerable feature or config present; attacker access and privilege conditions; data, control or availability at stake; fixed version or verified mitigation. Add stopping rules, and fold in existing compensating controls from the base. Run all seven for a single advisory and for top-ranked rows. Run questions 1–3 as the quick pass for the rest of a batch.

'Cite the advisory source and the repository, image, configuration, or runtime evidence used for each step. Explain any conflict between vendor, maintainer, and database records.' This becomes a required evidence column in the queue table.

'Name the smallest check or change that resolves the uncertainty or risk', plus the two guardrails 'Do not use absence from a scanner as proof of safety' and 'Do not claim a fix until the fixed version is present in the built artifact and the relevant tests or checks pass'. These go into '## Guardrails'.
Add 'does this CVE affect us', 'are we vulnerable', 'advisory impact' and 'stack exposure' to vulnerability-triage's triggers.

clusters.job: Plan a dependency upgrade and turn it into a narrow draft pull request

members.note: The strongest original. Its seven-part plan (reason, files, edits, tests, checks, rollout, rollback) and the split of unrelated upgrades form the skeleton. Its '## Approval line' already anticipates the next step ('The plan may propose a branch or pull request'), and it names what the plan does not authorise (merge, deploy, data migration, risk acceptance, production change).

Weak on platform fit. Sequential phase two of the same job (TF-IDF 0.417, the highest pair in the kit). The narrow-change rules, validation order and PR-body fields are good. As a separate skill it has no approval gate before push and no patch fallback (its review's top issue). Merging places the gate between plan and change.

proposed.name: Dependency upgrade plan and PR
proposed.description: Use when a package, runtime or base image needs upgrading: read release and migration notes, plan the smallest safe path with tests and rollback, then, after your approval, make the narrow manifest and lockfile change and draft the pull request. Never merges or deploys.
proposed.rationale:
Planning and drafting the PR are two phases of one job. Users ask 'upgrade X safely' and expect both, and splitting them left the side-effect half without a gate. One skill fixes the PR skill's top issue structurally: Phase 1 (plan), then an ask_question approval that shows the diff and PR body, then Phase 2 (change, validate, draft).

New content from the reviews:
- An up-front inputs step, and a route to outdated-dependency-review when no target is set.
- A resolver and peer-constraint dry run, stepwise major or LTS hops, official codemods and a deprecation-warning pass.
- Irreversible data or schema steps listed separately, with a roll-forward path.
- Owners and windows marked 'owner to confirm' rather than invented.
- Targeted updates (npm install pkg@x --package-lock-only, poetry update pkg, go get pkg@vX), and overrides or resolutions for transitive-only fixes, each with a removal note.
- Unfamiliar packages installed with --ignore-scripts first.
- The repo's PR template and commit convention, detected and followed.
- The reviewer taken from CODEOWNERS or asked for.
- Neutral PR wording when an advisory is private or embargoed.
- The draft PR goes through the GitHub block after connect_integration, or as a patch file through write_workspace_file when there is no write access.
- Unrun checks listed as gaps for CI.
- A suggestion to run dependency-change-risk-review on the draft.
drops: dependency-upgrade-pr opening line 'Use this after an upgrade plan has a reviewed target.' (becomes the internal approval gate)

Separate '## Approval line' (plan) and '## Stop point' (PR) sections, collapsed into one stop point that keeps every item either one excluded: merge, deploy, data migration, risk acceptance, production change, bypassing a failed check.

The two competing trigger sets ('upgrade plan' vs 'upgrade PR'/'bump package'), merged into one list. Drop 'dependency pull request', which collides with dependency-change-risk-review's 'dependency PR review', and 'update library', which overlaps outdated-dependency-review.
Both old slugs (dependency-upgrade-plan, dependency-upgrade-pr) in favour of dependency-upgrade

grafts.what: Update manifest and lockfile with the package manager. Make only the code or config edits the verified migration notes require. No formatting, refactors, unrelated bumps or silent alert suppressions. This becomes Phase 2 'Make the change'.

Smallest relevant tests first, then the checks in the contribution guide. Inspect the resolved tree and built artifact. For a security fix, rerun the scanner or version check that found it. Record commands, results and anything not run.

PR body fields: old and new versions, reason, advisory or release-note sources, behaviour changed, files changed, test evidence, known risk, rollout check, rollback. Mark as draft while approval or a check remains.

'Never merge, deploy, bypass a failed check, or claim production is fixed. Hand the draft and evidence to the named reviewer.' Merged with the base's approval line, with the reviewer collected as an input.
Add 'upgrade PR', 'bump package', 'draft update PR' and 'security upgrade patch' to the merged triggers.

clusters.job: Judge the supply-chain risk of dependencies: a measured whole-tree audit versus a review of one proposed change

members.note:
The strongest ref. It runs stdlib-only collect.py and render.py over npm, PyPI and Go manifests, plus the package-lock/uv.lock/go.mod transitive sweep. Criteria are three-state: TIER_A advisories/deprecated/archived/staleness, TIER_B publisher_concentration/install_script, Scorecard, and provenance as info. PR #13 only rewords the report-writing reference, which still points to a skill that is not installed. It needs these harness fixes:
- Run `python3 scripts/collect.py` when uv is absent; the scripts need Python 3.11+ for tomllib and datetime.UTC.
- Check `which gh` and warn up front. sources.gh_token() reads only `gh auth token`, so repo criteria go unassessable past about 10 deps.
- Add a step 0 for getting the project into the sandbox: clone, GitHub block, or uploaded manifests.
- Fetch each advisory from api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> (querybatch returns IDs only), and lead with MAL-* or malware entries as incidents.
- Add a fallback for pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock and poetry.lock, which the SKILL.md and collector already disclose as 'not read'. Run osv-scanner when present, labelled separately, or route through dependency-inventory.
- With no lockfile to record the resolved registry, check .npmrc, pip.conf and index-url for private registries, and ask before public lookups.
- Run the collector in the background and poll on large trees.
- Write findings.json and report.md via write_workspace_file.
- Delete the report-writing:writing-style line.
- Scope the impersonal register to report.md only.
- Add handoffs to vulnerability-triage and dependency-upgrade.

It reviews a delta (a Renovate/Dependabot PR, a new package or a patch) for both supply-chain signals and application impact. It returns ready for review / needs changes / blocked on evidence, with rollback safety. The auditor does not cover the application-impact and rollback half. Its supply-chain half should reuse the auditor's measurements where they exist (npm) rather than hand-collect maintainer counts.

proposed.name: Dependency change risk review
proposed.description: Use when someone's dependency change needs a verdict (a Renovate/Dependabot PR, new package, lockfile-only change or patch): check provenance, publisher, install scripts, licence and API impact, and return ready for review / needs changes / blocked on evidence with rollback safety.
proposed.rationale:
The jobs are adjacent, not duplicates. The auditor answers 'how risky is our whole tree' with measured coverage. The change review answers 'is this one change safe to merge', including API, runtime and rollback impact. Both stay.

The change review is the one that changes. It borrows the auditor's measurement discipline, and hands measurement to it for newly added or changed npm dependencies. For PyPI and Go, the auditor's publisher, provenance and install-script rows are structurally unassessable, so the change review keeps its own checks there, such as PyPI attestations and yank status.

New content from its review:
- Inputs: a PR link or diff through the GitHub block, with a paste fallback.
- A provenance or attestation check (npm provenance, PyPI attestations).
- A release-age cooldown for very new versions.
- An OSV MAL-* check and a typosquat or name-similarity check.
- A check for a lockfile resolved-URL or integrity change without a version change.
- A licence delta routed to the owner, or to counsel through Lena.
- Criteria for the three statuses: blocked on evidence = versions, provenance or advisory status not established; needs changes = an unmitigated high-impact finding or an untested changed API; ready for review = every risk mapped to a passing check or an accepted gap.
- Tarball inspection without installing (npm pack / pip download --no-deps).
- Draft, then approve, before posting a PR review.
drops: dependency-change-risk-review trigger 'upgrade risk' (collides with the merged dependency-upgrade)

Hand-estimated maintainer counts from GitHub contributors, replaced by the auditor's measured npm publisher data. For PyPI and Go, report publisher as unassessable, but keep the base's 'renamed or transferred packages' flag.

grafts.section: ## Why the scripts do the measuring, not you
grafts.what: The three-state rule: every supply-chain check resolves to assessed-clean, assessed-flagged, or unassessable with a reason. It carries the two rules 'Unavailable data is never evidence of risk' and 'An absent measurement is never a clean verdict', applied to each row of the change review's supply-chain checklist.

Run supply-chain-risk-auditor's collect and render on the post-change manifests and lockfile. The auditor audits every direct dependency, so filter to the added or changed ones. Quote its deprecated, install_script, publisher_concentration and provenance rows instead of estimating them. On PyPI and Go those rows are mostly unassessable, so say so and fall back to the review's own checks.

'`gh` can give me maintainer counts faster than the collector': repository contributors and registry publish rights are different populations. Use this to keep the new-publisher check on registry data rather than GitHub contributor counts.

unique.note:
It is the kit's only onboarding entry, so it stays first. Fixes from the review issues:
- Persist scope with memory_store: repos and branches, deployed services, exposure tiers, package managers, existing scanners and update bots (Dependabot, Renovate, Snyk, Trivy), remediation SLA, owners and approvers.
- Read Casey's repo, CI and merge-rule context from memory once Casey's onboarding stores it.
- Offer connect_integration for GitHub; otherwise ask for lockfiles, SBOM or scanner exports.
- Replace brief item 3 'Confirmed risks' with all four relevance labels, so a first pass does not over-claim.
- Map 'The next three checks or upgrades' to the kit slugs: dependency-inventory, vulnerability-triage, supply-chain-risk-auditor, dependency-upgrade.
- Replace '## Build the evidence set' with a pointer to dependency-inventory, which owns collection.
- Swap the generic 'software supply chain' trigger for onboarding phrasing.
- Offer the opt-in weekly and monthly routines.

It is the only all-ecosystem baseline (workspace roots, base images, CI actions, runtime pins). supply-chain-risk-auditor cannot replace it: it reads only npm, PyPI and Go, and states that yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml and poetry.lock 'are not read'. Fixes:
- Write inventory.csv (plus CycloneDX JSON) via write_workspace_file, and show totals in chat.
- Add purl, licence, registry URL and integrity fields.
- Use read-only per-ecosystem commands (npm ls --all --json, pnpm list --depth Infinity --json, poetry show --tree, go list -m -json all), and prefer lockfile parsing over installing.
- Name a lockfile-staleness check per ecosystem (npm ci --dry-run, poetry check --lock, uv lock --check).
- Accept an uploaded SBOM.
- Record CI action and image pin status (SHA or digest), and OS packages in images.

The Act now / Plan / Watch / Unknown freshness backlog is a job no other ref does. The auditor's deprecated and staleness rows feed it but do not replace it. Fixes:
- Add an Inputs step with commands (npm outdated --json, pip list --outdated, poetry show --outdated, go list -u -m all) and a paste fallback. Run dependency-inventory first when no inventory exists.
- Add runtime, framework and base-image EOL from the vendor policy or endoflife.date, with the date checked.
- Add a change-size rubric (semver level, 0.x, breaking-change count).
- Add a rule that coupled packages and peer-dependency sets move as one item.
- Add a backlog table template.
- Hand off security items to vulnerability-triage and Act now/Plan items to dependency-upgrade.

As written it fits the platform poorly. It is the only dedicated security review of source diffs in the catalog, and it fits Devon's 'Application Security Engineer' title. Casey's pull-request-review is general bug review, and code-review-quality has only a security checklist. Keep it only with fixes PR #13 does not make (#13 only annotates upstream skills as not installed):
- Delete the '## Agents' section and the decision-tree route to `differential-review:adversarial-modeler` via `subagent_type`, and point Phase 5 at adversarial.md.
- Delete the '## Integration' `issue-writer --input ...` command and methodology.md's `audit-context-building --scope ...` blocks, keeping the manual baseline checklist.
- Replace reporting.md's output order ('Current working directory', 'User's Desktop', '~/.claude/skills/differential-review/output/') with write_workspace_file outside the reviewed repo.
- Clone into the sandbox instead of running methodology.md's `git checkout <baseline_commit>` in the user's tree.
- Add input modes: a public clone with full history; the GitHub block for a private PR (methodology.md assumes `gh pr view`); a pasted diff at reduced confidence.
- Add web and API patterns (authz/IDOR, injection, SSRF, deserialisation, path traversal, secrets in diff) beside patterns.md's Solidity set (reentrancy, front-running, timestamp manipulation).
- Add a new-code path instead of excluding 'Greenfield code'.
- Run PoCs only in the sandbox against local code, and draft PR comments for approval, with no disclosure in public threads.
- Drop the invented '$50K impact' example.
- Replace 'APPROVE/REJECT/CONDITIONAL' with ready for review / needs changes / blocked on evidence.
- Route lockfile diffs to dependency-change-risk-review.
- Drop 'asking what else a change could break' from the description (Casey overlap).

cross_expert.suggestion: Differentiate. Casey's pull-request-review ranks general bugs (blocker, should fix, question, style) for any diff. Devon's skill should trigger only for security review ('security review this PR', auth, crypto, input handling, secrets). Add a line to Casey's skill to consult_teammate or hand off to Devon when a diff touches auth, validation, crypto or dependencies, and have Devon hand non-security defects back.

Differentiate. Devon's description says 'calculates blast radius by counting callers' and 'asking what else a change could break'. These collide with Casey's triggers 'what could this break' and 'blast radius'. Remove that phrase from Devon's description, and keep blast radius as an internal step weighted by reachability from untrusted input. General impact mapping stays with Casey.

Differentiate. If code-review-quality is assigned to Casey, its 'Security Checklist' and 'Pattern 3: Security Review' blocks stay as a quick lint list, with a pointer to Devon for a full security review of risky diffs. Do not make either skill canonical for both jobs.

Share state. Both ask for the repository and branches. Casey's also collects CI jobs, the test setup and merge, deploy and rollback rules, which Devon's approval line and upgrade PRs rely on. Store that shared repo context under one memory key so whichever expert onboards second reads it instead of re-asking. Devon's onboarding then adds only dependency-specific scope: package managers, scanners and update bots, exposure tiers, remediation SLA.

Handoff. Casey's checklist flags 'new dependencies' in a release. Route those to Devon's dependency-change-risk-review, and feed Devon's rollback-safety and rollout notes back into Casey's go/no-go list.

Handoff. When a change moves a direct or transitive dependency to a restrictive or missing licence (AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, none), Devon records the delta with sources. Lena's compliance-escalation-brief packages it for counsel. Devon does not judge licence acceptability.

Handoff. Questionnaire items on vulnerability management, patch SLAs or dependency scanning go from Lena to Devon for dated evidence: the current queue, SLA policy, scan dates. Lena keeps drafting and answering, and Devon never answers questionnaires.

Handoff. SOC 2 and ISO 27001 vulnerability-management controls need recurring evidence. Devon's dated queue and routine re-check outputs are the evidence, and Lena or James tracks them as audit artefacts. Devon does not assert control status.

proposed_kit.name: Dependency security getting started
proposed_kit.note: Stays first. Apply the fixes: store scope, SLA and tooling with memory_store; GitHub connect or upload fallback; four relevance labels in the first brief; next steps routed to the kit slugs; collection delegated to dependency-inventory; onboarding triggers; offer routines.

proposed_kit.note:

proposed_kit.note: Graft the auditor's three-state rule, and use it to measure new or changed npm deps; PyPI and Go keep their own checks. Add provenance, cooldown, malicious-package or typosquat, and licence-delta checks, status criteria, safe tarball inspection and draft-then-post. Drop the 'upgrade risk' trigger.

proposed_kit.name: Code change security review
proposed_kit.note:
Conditional on these fixes:
- Remove the subagent dispatch and the issue-writer and audit-context-building commands.
- Replace the working-directory, Desktop and ~/.claude paths.
- Clone instead of checking out in the user's tree.
- Add input modes and web and API patterns.
