recommendations.name: Reference check plan and summary
recommendations.purpose: Run structured, consent-based reference checks tied to the approved rubric: referee request, same questions per criterion, call notes with quotes, and a filed evidence record for the debrief.
recommendations.why: PR #15 interview-plan-and-scorecard allows 'reference check' as a scored method (check_loop.py --reference-policy), and its question-bank patterns cite the Who reference method [24]. Sofia's debrief proposes a reference check as the cheapest fix for open questions. No catalog skill runs one. Recruiting-coordinator postings routinely list reference checks. Research favours the structured form: Taylor et al. (2004, Personnel Psychology 57) found a structured telephone reference check predicted performance (r=.25, .36 corrected), and OPM's assessment guidance says the same. There are legal traps a recruiter must avoid. Salary-history bans in CA and NY also cover asking former employers. Questions about health, leave or family are off limits. Off-list 'backdoor' references need a policy decision. The kit's question_lint and verify_quotes patterns can be reused.

Question set built only from the rubric criteria the loop assigned to references, plus the debrief's open questions. The same questions go to every referee, with relationship and observation-window questions first. Run question_lint and add a salary-history and leave check.
Unsent drafts of the referee request email and a candidate note. A call-note template capturing verbatim quotes, criterion, referee relationship and observation window.

File the result as a scorecard (source=reference) in scorecards/<candidate-id>/filed/, which collate_scorecards.py reads. No overall rating and no 'would you rehire' score. Conflicts go to the debrief's resolve-first list.
Data rules: only the minimum about referees is kept, retention follows the plan, and a candidate's access request routes to the data-request skill.

recommendations.name: Pre-hire checks tracker (background, fair chance, right to work)
recommendations.purpose: Track background-check, fair-chance and right-to-work steps per candidate in the lawful order, with dates, and draft only the cover notes that carry the vendor's or counsel's forms.
recommendations.why: The kit stops at these steps but nothing moves them forward. candidate-rejection-email drafts nothing when a consumer report played a part, and says the only way forward is for the owner to confirm the FCRA steps are complete. candidate-offer-draft raises FCRA_DISCLOSURE, and candidate-interview-debrief records an FCRA hold. No skill tracks disclosure and authorisation, the report, the pre-adverse notice with the report copy and Summary of Rights, the waiting period, and the final notice (FTC guidance [48][76], already in the kit's sources). Fair-chance laws add ordering rules: no criminal-history inquiry before a conditional offer, and an individualised assessment with at least 5 business days to respond under the CA Fair Chance Act and the NYC Fair Chance Act. The merge conditions add UK right-to-work and US I-9 trigger rows. The checks behind them need a home: UK checks before employment starts, and I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days of the start date. Facilitating background checks is a standard recruiting-coordinator duty.

It flags steps that are missing or out of order.

Right to work: UK check before the start date; I-9 Section 1 by day one and Section 2 within 3 business days. The same check for every hire, never chosen by name, accent or origin. E-Verify is recorded only if the company says it is enrolled.
Drafts only the cover email that accompanies forms the vendor or counsel supplied. It never writes the legal notice, never decides and never states a legal conclusion.

proposal.summary: Ines's kit has two sources. The first is eight ORIGINAL placeholders, with performance-review-prep and hr-escalation-brief the strongest. The second is four TORAN Anthropic HR packages, generally thinner than the originals. NICK contributes nothing, and no open PR (#14/#15/#16) changes any of her twelve in-scope skills or ines.yml. PR #13 changes only line 9 of ATTRIBUTION.md in the four HR packages, so their SKILL.md files still contain the slash-command `$ARGUMENTS` blocks and `~~` placeholders. Two TORAN packages duplicate stronger originals and are grafted in for their templates only. employee-onboarding-planning goes into new-hire-onboarding-plan. employee-performance-review (blocker: rating, compensation and calibration) goes into performance-review-prep, without its level columns, which would act as a rating. company-policy-lookup is the one genuinely new job. It is added beside handbook-policy-draft after a platform rewrite and a boundary carve-out for individual pay, leave, health and complaint cases. people-analytics-reporting folds into the survey readout, which becomes a group-level people-metrics-readout. It keeps headcount and attrition, adds a cross-dataset differencing check, and drops demographics, flight risk and pay equity; diversity requests go to the HR lead. That gives a 9-skill kit. Carried Apache-2.0 text needs the upstream LICENSE plus an ATTRIBUTION.md with changes, not a one-line credit. The expert body needs four changes. First, a boundary list aligned with the identity and hr-escalation-brief. Second, an immediate-risk path. Third, a weekly routine for onboarding check-ins, offboarding owners and handbook review dates, which only works once the onboarding plan and offboarding checklist save their output and handbook pages carry a next-review date. Fourth, identity and bio text that names 1:1 agendas and policy answers. PR #16 already ends Sofia's close plan at the first-week hand-off, so that seam is agreed. Harper's PR #15 intake brief is the source for day-90 outcomes; Sofia's intake gives year-one outcomes only.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and its privacy and handoff stance is unusually well stated. Its day_one items map directly to kept skills, and it has no preloads or routines, so the merge renames nothing any of them depends on. The gaps: the boundaries field is a shorter list than the identity and hr-escalation-brief. Nothing covers an immediate-risk path. Adding company-policy-lookup and headcount and attrition reporting needs a carve-out in the boundaries and an extension in the identity. The identity and bio never mention 1:1 agendas or policy answers. The check-ins the onboarding plan promises have no routine to drive them, and no kit skill saves the state a routine would need.
strengths: The identity's data rule ('you use the least you need, you do not repeat it, and you never combine records to guess at something private') is a clear test. It justifies dropping flight risk, diversity and calibration from the TORAN packages, and it also calls for a differencing check across the survey, headcount and attrition datasets.

The identity sentence 'never rank people against each other' matches performance-review-prep ('Never compare the person with colleagues') and rules out employee-performance-review's calibration mode cleanly.

Voice sample 'Escalation' demonstrates exactly the stop rule in performance-review-prep ('If the review may lead to a performance plan ... stop and write an HR brief') and the no-recommendation brief in hr-escalation-brief.
Voice sample 'Onboarding note' is concrete (Tomás, one small fix with his buddy, billing alerts by day 30). It mirrors new-hire-onboarding-plan's 'Keep week one about access and people, not output'.
day_one items 'A 30-60-90 plan for your next hire' and 'A handbook page in plain language' map one-to-one to new-hire-onboarding-plan and handbook-policy-draft, and both are kept.
body_review.kit_alignment: No routine, preload or day_one entry names a skill that would be dropped or renamed. day_one[0] maps to the merged new-hire-onboarding-plan and day_one[1] to handbook-policy-draft; both slugs stay. The rename engagement-survey-readout -> people-metrics-readout breaks nothing in the YAML beyond the skills list. Five places need updating. (1) The identity and bio never mention one-to-one agendas (a live skill) or answering policy questions (company-policy-lookup, added). (2) The identity's survey sentence covers surveys only, but the merged readout also reports headcount and attrition. (3) The boundaries ban advising on 'pay, leave, health', while company-policy-lookup answers 'what's our PTO policy'. The boundary must say that quoting and explaining written policy is in scope and applying it to one person's case is not. (4) new-hire-onboarding-plan promises check-ins at week 1 and days 30, 60 and 90, and offboarding-checklist tracks owners and status, but routines is empty, so nothing brings them back up. (5) A routine cannot fix (4) alone. None of the three skills saves anything (no memory_store or write_workspace_file), and handbook-policy-draft records an effective date and owner but no review date, so the skills must be changed to persist the plan, the checklist and a next-review date.

Run cell counts, eNPS and the differencing check in bash_exec. Diversity, representation and pay-equity requests are a deliberate capability loss. Name them in the skill, and route them to the HR lead or counsel via hr-escalation-brief, because on a small team any cut is identifiable. Hiring-funnel metrics belong to Sofia's hiring-pipeline-analytics. Ship the upstream LICENSE and an ATTRIBUTION.md for the carried people-report text. recommendations.name: People ops weekly docket
recommendations.purpose: Every Monday, collect the saved onboarding check-ins, offboarding lines, policy review dates and cycle deadlines into one draft list of what is due, overdue and coming up, grouped by owner.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review found three skills that set dates and nothing that brings them back up. new-hire-onboarding-plan promises check-ins at week 1 and days 30, 60 and 90. offboarding-checklist puts an owner, date and status on every line. handbook-policy-draft is gaining a next-review date. ines.yml has `routines: []`, and no skill reads that saved state. Job descriptions for this role centre on that follow-up. The GitLab People Operations Specialist description (https://handbook.gitlab.com/job-description-library/people-group/people-operations/) says 'Audit onboarding issues to ensure task completion in alignment with applicable deadlines' and also covers work anniversaries and life-event gifts. I read two catalog neighbours and neither fits. ops-run-the-operating-rhythm (James) is a KPI review with red/yellow/green scoring and decisions. weekly-priorities-review (Kai) sets one person's calendar against their priorities. Neither reads people records or carries Ines's privacy rules. On the platform this needs schedule_routine plus memory_search and read_workspace_file. James's `ops-weekly-review` routine in james.yml is the pattern for adding the routine to ines.yml.
sketch: The register: one shared record shape (item, type onboarding/offboarding/policy/cycle/survey, due date, owner, status, source file). It lives in a workspace file such as people-ops/register.md with a memory_store key. Define it here so the kit fixes that save the onboarding plan, the offboarding checklist and the next-review date all write the same fields.

Weekly read: what is due this week, what is overdue, and what falls in the next 14 days. That covers check-ins with their three questions pre-filled, offboarding lines with no owner or a past date, policies past their review date, and review-cycle and survey deadlines. Work anniversaries appear only if the manager opted in.
Output: counts first, then one table per owner, with name and item only. A quiet week gets one line. Dedupe against last week's saved docket.
Routing: items that touch leave, health, pay, a complaint or a failed probation are listed only as 'for HR', with a pointer to hr-escalation-brief. They are never summarised.
First run: offer the Monday routine through schedule_routine and ask where the draft should go. Never message owners or new hires without a yes.
YAML: add a `people-ops-weekly-docket` routine to ines.yml, and optionally a day_one entry such as 'This week's people ops docket'.

recommendations.name: Review cycle coordination
recommendations.purpose: Run the admin side of a performance review cycle: timeline, participant list, kickoff and reminder drafts, completion counts and a close-out note. HR keeps ratings and calibration.
recommendations.why: Role evidence: the Torchora People Ops Specialist spec (https://www.torchora.com/job-specification/people-operations-specialist) says 'Assist with the administrative aspects of the performance management cycle, including system setup, communication tracking, and reporting on completion rates.' Coordinator descriptions summarised by hr.university (https://hr.university/shrm/hr-operations/) list 'collecting information, tracking submissions, and coordinating reminders'. I opened the kit. performance-review-prep (merged) builds one person's review pack plus an optional self-assessment and deliberately drops calibration and ratings. No kit skill plans the cycle, tracks who has submitted, or drafts the manager and staff messages. The dropped employee-performance-review calibration mode is a rating-distribution and compensation document, so it cannot be the source. Platform fit: the tracker goes in the Google Sheets block, reminders are Gmail or Slack drafts behind approval, and reminder dates use schedule_followup or the docket.
sketch: Cycle setup: the review period, the steps (self-assessment, peer input if used, manager draft, HR check, the conversation, sign-off), each step's deadline and owner, and the participant list from the roster the manager may share. People on leave or recently hired are listed as 'HR decides', with no reason recorded.

Comms pack: a kickoff note for managers, a note for staff that points to the self-assessment template in performance-review-prep, one page of manager guidance on dated evidence and wording, and reminder drafts for 7 days and 2 days before each deadline.
Completion tracker: counts per step, plus who has not submitted, visible only to that person's manager and HR. Never open, summarise or score review content.
Close-out: completion rate, late items, process issues raised, and next-cycle dates saved to the register.
Hard stops: no ratings, distributions, forced ranking, calibration grids, promotion or pay recommendations. A review that points to a performance plan or dismissal goes to hr-escalation-brief.

recommendations.name: People announcement draft
recommendations.purpose: Draft routine internal people announcements (new joiner, farewell, policy change, holiday calendar, cycle or survey launch, 'you said, we did') with manager talking points, for approval before anything is posted.
recommendations.why: Several kit skills end in a staff message that no skill drafts. offboarding-checklist has a farewell line ('how and when the team hears'). new-hire-onboarding-plan has a welcome note. handbook-policy-draft produces a page that has to be announced. The survey readout promises to report back to staff. Noor's launch-communications-plan, press-release-draft and holding-statement-draft are built for external news: embargoes, press and customers. Role evidence: the Workable People Operations Specialist description (https://resources.workable.com/people-operations-specialist-job-description) includes 'Assist in the development and implementation of HR policies'. The One Model coordinator posting (https://jobs.techstars.com/companies/one-model/jobs/70057631-people-operations-coordinator) includes 'coordinating activities and communications around survey launches'. The upstream package is MIT-licensed and verified at a pinned commit. Its SKILL.md is only a list of prompts, but content/employee-communications-guide.md is sound and worth shipping as a reference with ATTRIBUTION.md: lead with what it means for the reader, say what is not changing, end with one action and one contact, brief managers first. Platform: Slack and Gmail blocks as drafts through the approval flow.

source.ref: tuanductran/hr-skills@078f2fb skills/hr-employee-communications. Ship content/employee-communications-guide.md as references/; rewrite SKILL.md as a workflow

sketch: Intake: announcement type, audience, channel, approver and effective date. For a named person, only what they agreed to share, such as a joiner's bio or a leaver's own wording.

Templates by type: welcome; farewell (no reason for leaving, no notice or pay terms); policy change (what changes, what does not, effective date, link to the page, acknowledgement if required); holiday or calendar; review-cycle kickoff; survey launch, with an anonymity promise that matches the agreed group size; results back to staff.
Managers first: talking points and a likely-questions list for managers before the all-staff version.
Plain-language check against the reference guide: the first two sentences answer 'what does this mean for me', with one action and one contact.

Hard stops: dismissals, layoffs, restructures, investigations and deaths or health news are not drafted. Route them to hr-escalation-brief, and to Noor for any outside angle. Draft only; never post or email without approval.

recommendations.name: People records audit
recommendations.purpose: Check an exported employee roster, plus optional tool user lists and acknowledgement or training lists, for missing or inconsistent fields, leavers who still have accounts, and overdue acknowledgements. The checks run in bash_exec and produce a fix list for each record owner.
recommendations.why: Record upkeep is the most consistent line in postings for this role. GitLab (https://handbook.gitlab.com/job-description-library/people-group/people-operations/) says 'Conduct regular audits of team member data, including missing data points'. Torchora (https://www.torchora.com/job-specification/people-operations-specialist) says 'maintaining data integrity'. Workable says 'Compile and update employee records'. No kit skill checks the data. people-metrics-readout's headcount and attrition figures depend on a clean roster. offboarding-checklist removes one leaver's access but never sweeps all tools for orphaned accounts. SHRM supplies a handbook receipt acknowledgement form (https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/tools/forms/employee-handbook-receipt-acknowledgment). No kit skill tracks those receipts once handbook-policy-draft's page is published. Omar's crm-field-audit follows a similar field-audit pattern but is built for CRM records. Platform: a CSV or Sheets export goes into a bundled bash_exec script, and results can go to the Google Sheets block. Nothing is ever written back to an HRIS.
sketch: Minimum data: ask for ID, name, manager, team, title, location, start and end date, and status. The script drops pay, demographic, health, national-ID and bank columns before anything else and says so.

scripts/audit_roster.py checks for missing required fields, duplicates, active records with a past end date, managers who are missing, have left or form loops, spelling variants of titles and teams, and future start dates marked active.

Access sweep: compare each tool's user export with the active roster to find accounts held by leavers or unknown people, and tools with a sole admin. Hand the list to IT or the tool owner; never deactivate anything.

Acknowledgements and training: check against a requirement list that HR supplies; the skill never decides what the law requires. List overdue items by person, visible only to that person's manager and HR.
Output: an issue table by record ID with owner and suggested fix, plus counts. Save the audit date to the register. A re-run compares against the last audit.

recommendations.name: Engagement survey design
recommendations.purpose: Design an engagement, pulse or new-hire survey so the readout can protect anonymity: purpose, a short behaviour-anchored question set, breakdowns checked against the minimum group size, the survey tool's anonymity settings, launch messages and cadence.
recommendations.why: The kit reads surveys out (engagement-survey-readout, becoming people-metrics-readout) but has nothing for designing them, and anonymity is fixed at design time. A survey that collects emails, or asks team, tenure and location in a 20-person company, cannot be read out safely later. Role evidence: 'Administers the employee engagement/pulse survey cycle ... coordinating activities and communications around survey launches' (https://jobs.techstars.com/companies/one-model/jobs/70057631-people-operations-coordinator). The upstream package is MIT-licensed and verified at a pinned commit. Its SKILL.md is only a list of prompts, but content/employee-listening-guide.md has usable principles: keep surveys short, anchor items to behaviour, enforce minimum group sizes before results are visible, and plan actions properly. Two parts conflict with Ines's boundaries and must be cut: the tip to 'segment results by manager', and the example that ties one department's survey scores to its resignations. There is no Google Forms block, so the output is a question document or sheet the user loads into their own tool.

source.ref: tuanductran/hr-skills@078f2fb skills/hr-employee-listening. Ship content/employee-listening-guide.md as references/ with the per-manager segmentation removed; rewrite SKILL.md

sketch: Purpose and commitments: what decisions the results feed, who owns the actions, and the date results go back to staff.

Question set: 10-25 items for an annual survey, 3-6 for a pulse, all anchored to behaviour, with an optional eNPS item and one or two open questions. No health, family or protected-trait items, and no items that ask people to name their manager, unless HR and counsel approve.

Breakdown plan: list every planned cut, count each group from the headcount, merge groups below the minimum before launch, and check combinations of cuts that could be subtracted to expose a small group.

Tool settings checklist: anonymous mode on, no email collection, no timestamps or IPs in the export, and a named list of who can see raw responses. Word the anonymity promise to match what the tool actually protects.
Launch pack: invite, reminder, close date and response-rate target. Save the survey dates to the register for the weekly docket.

recommendations.name: Exit interview kit
recommendations.purpose: Prepare a voluntary exit interview or exit survey guide with a consent note, and each quarter turn completed exits into group-level themes under the minimum group size.
recommendations.why: offboarding-checklist deliberately leaves the reason for leaving out, and people-metrics-readout counts attrition. No kit skill collects why people leave or reads those reasons across exits. SHRM treats exit interviews as standard HR work and says HR, not the supervisor, should run them (https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/employment-law-compliance/employees-leave-conduct-comprehensive-exit-interviews). SHRM also suggests breaking exit data down by gender and race, which Ines's boundaries forbid. The skill therefore has to refuse that cut explicitly and route such requests to hr-escalation-brief. The MIT-licensed listening guide above has usable exit advice that can be cited: anonymous written exit surveys, alumni surveys 3-6 months after departure, and patterns across many exits rather than single stories. Ranked could because a small company sees few exits per quarter, so themes often cannot be shown.
sketch: Setup: offered, not required. The interviewer is not the leaver's manager. A consent note says what is recorded, who sees it, and that answers do not affect references.
Guide: 8-10 open questions on the role, manager support, growth, workload, tools and what would have kept them. Nothing about health, family or the new employer's pay.
Notes: themes and paraphrased quotes only. Any allegation of harassment, discrimination, a safety issue or a legal breach goes to hr-escalation-brief the same day, not into the theme log.
Quarterly themes: aggregate only when the period's exits meet the minimum group size. No team breakdown below that size, and never a demographic breakdown.
Save the theme-log dates to the register.

recommendations.name: Employment verification response
recommendations.purpose: Handle an incoming employment verification or reference request: check the requester, the employee's written consent and the reference policy, then draft a confirmation with only the facts the policy allows, for HR to approve and send.
recommendations.why: Role evidence: 'Handle all incoming verification of employment requests and other inquiries for employee data with a strict adherence to confidentiality and company protocol' (https://www.torchora.com/job-specification/people-operations-specialist). GitLab lists 'Process requests for verifications of employment and unemployment claims' (https://handbook.gitlab.com/job-description-library/people-group/people-operations/). Nothing in the kit or the catalog covers it. Harper and Sofia run reference checks the other way, when hiring. Lena's data-subject-request-draft handles a person's request for their own data. A mistake here discloses personal data to a third party, so a narrow skill with a consent gate is safer than general drafting.
sketch: Classify the request: a verification from a lender, landlord or new employer; a reference request; a government agency or unemployment claim, or a subpoena or lawyer's letter, which go to hr-escalation-brief with no draft; or the employee's own data request, which goes to Lena.
Gate: written consent from the employee is on file, the requester's identity is checked against a known contact or domain, and the reference policy has been found with company-policy-lookup.
Draft: confirm only what the policy allows, usually dates, title and status. Performance, reason for leaving and pay are included only if both the policy and the consent cover them. No opinions.
Log: the request, the consent, the fields disclosed, the approver and the date. Nothing is sent without HR's yes.

recommendations.notes:
What I checked: I read all eight kit SKILL.md files, Toran's four TORAN packages, and the catalog neighbours (ops-run-the-operating-rhythm, weekly-priorities-review, launch-communications-plan, sensitive-data-safe-handling, policy-gap-review, onboarding). I also scanned catalog_index.md and DEFERRED_SKILLS.md. Apart from Toran's four packages the catalog holds no other people-ops skill, assigned or unassigned. DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has no HR packages; it is 34 ads skills plus invoice-chase and four marketing packages.

Sources: the only redistributable upstream material worth using is tuanductran/hr-skills (MIT, commit 078f2fb651f1090e73a8cc6ba96f323f8b00b171; licence and paths checked in a local clone; raw URLs return 200). Every SKILL.md there is a list of prompts, not a workflow. Only the content/*.md guides are worth shipping, as references/ with the upstream LICENSE and an ATTRIBUTION.md. The listening guide and its example have to be cut where they conflict with Ines: segmenting by manager, and linking one department's survey scores to its resignations. SHRM's exit-interview guidance also recommends gender and race breakdowns, which Ines must refuse. I rejected the Anthropic human-resources upstream skills that were not already in the catalog. org-planning (Apache-2.0) models compensation cost and headcount, which duplicates James's ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan and crosses the pay boundary. comp-analysis crosses the pay boundary. draft-offer, interview-prep and recruiting-pipeline belong to Harper and Sofia.

Deliberately not recommended:
- Career ladder or levelling: levels map to pay and promotion, and the merge already dropped the level columns.
- Leave and benefits administration: boundary.
- A separate HR-inbox triage skill: company-policy-lookup plus hr-escalation-brief cover it once the carve-out is in.
- Probation reviews: better handled by having new-hire-onboarding-plan write the probation end date to the register and route a 'not passing' outcome to hr-escalation-brief.
- Team events and offsites: Kai's travel-plan.

Dependencies: people-ops-weekly-docket is the must. It is useless unless the kit fixes that persist state (saving the onboarding plan and check-in dates, saving the offboarding checklist, and the handbook next-review date) all write the same register fields. Design the register schema and those three fixes in the same PR. review-cycle-coordination, people-records-audit, engagement-survey-design and exit-interview-kit should also write their dates to that register.

YAML changes if these land:
- routines: add people-ops-weekly-docket, copying the shape of James's ops-weekly-review.
- identity: add surveys designed as well as read, internal announcements drafted for approval, and records audits that are read-only.
- boundaries: never announce a dismissal, layoff or restructure; never disclose an employee's data to a third party without their written consent and HR approval; never decide which training or acknowledgements the law requires.

Slug note: overlaps_with uses people-metrics-readout. If the optional rename is skipped, read it as engagement-survey-readout.

proposal.summary: James's live kit is Nick's ten PR-2 ops skills. Toran proposed eight Anthropic operations packages for him (process-doc, process-optimization, capacity-plan, status-report, risk-assessment, vendor-review, runbook, compliance-tracking). No ORIGINAL or open-PR (#14/#15/#16) versions are in scope. Each Toran package covers a job a Nick skill already covers, and each is thinner than the Nick skill it overlaps. A diff of PR #13 confirms it changes only their ATTRIBUTION.md, so the `$ARGUMENTS` wrappers and `~~` placeholders are still there. None should ship standalone. Each one instead gives a concrete template or checklist to a Nick base: library search, RACI and the runbook format go to the SOP skill; the five-waste scan to process mapping; utilization targets to capacity; exit-cost TCO and a vendor-risk checklist to vendor ops; the risk matrix and audit calendar to controls; the leadership report template to program governance. The one Nick-on-Nick call folds ops-scorecard-and-kpis into ops-run-the-operating-rhythm, because both descriptions trigger on 'how is it doing / hands over numbers'. The merge must also carry the scorecard's metrics-history rule, which routines[0] writes to. That leaves nine skills, and every surviving slug keeps its name, so routines and day_one still resolve. The biggest open risks are four. First, the vendor lane collides with Vera's no-select procurement kit, including an identical 'vendor scorecard' trigger with her vendor-performance-review, and with Daniel's 'is this vendor worth it'. Second, the boundaries lack compliance, finance and support handoffs. Third, the renewal routine re-flags at fixed 60/30-day marks that ignore notice periods, and the inventory row does not even carry a notice period. Fourth, the audit calendar the controls graft adds is not yet read by the monthly routine.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and consistent. Each class of action has a named approver, FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN runs everywhere, and routines dedupe and stay quiet when nothing is due. Every slug the routines and day_one lean on survives the merge. The gaps are elsewhere. The boundaries hand off only to an account executive and Legal, although the kit runs into Lena's, Daniel's, Vera's and Robin's lanes. The vendor day_one, the identity's 'source of truth' line and the renewal routine can each produce an invented renewal or notice date, and the routine never asks where the contracts live. The identity routing paragraph needs updating for the scorecard merge and for what the grafts add: runbooks, risk register, audit calendar, leadership status report. The monthly routine also has to read the new audit calendar.
strengths: Named approvers for each action class (procurement, process-change, program owner, capacity owner) are consistent across identity, boundaries, routines and the skills' Rules sections.

Every routine has a fixed period, a dedupe rule and quiet-when-nothing behaviour, and every one stages a draft rather than posting (e.g. routines[0] 'Never post the pack to a channel or email it to anyone without the owner's yes').
Voice sample 1 shows the FACT/INFERENCE split and the 'one thing before next week' close that the rhythm skill prescribes.
Identity para 3 routes each job type to a named skill, which makes skill selection predictable.
Out-of-scope lines exist for deals, support tickets, engineering and legal advice, and each comes with a handoff behaviour.
body_review.kit_alignment: Every slug that routines and day_one depend on is kept: rhythm (routines[0], day_one[0]), write-an-sop (day_one[1]), vendor (routines[1], day_one[2]), capacity and controls (routines[2]). The routines read 'the scorecard' and write 'the metrics history' as files. The merged rhythm skill has to keep both as maintained workspace artifacts, which is why the scorecard's Rules graft is needed, and then routines[0] needs no change. The `skills:` list loses ops-scorecard-and-kpis. Identity para 3 still routes 'Numbers and targets' to a separate ops scorecard skill and does not mention what the grafts add: runbook format, risk register, audit calendar, leadership status report. The identity promises an ROI sizing that the automate skill computes benefit-only. routines[1] reports 'notice period on each' renewal, but the vendor skill's inventory row has no notice-period column, and its asks never request the contracts. routines[2] does not pull the audit calendar that the controls graft adds. The boundaries have no teammate handoffs for compliance frameworks, financial close controls, vendor security diligence or case escalations, which the merged controls and vendor skills need.

issues.quote: Closing deals, working support tickets, engineering implementation, and legal advice are out of scope
issues.problem: Only four out-of-scope areas are named. The kit's controls skill takes 'audit readiness' requests and drafts 'against common practice', and the vendor skill evaluates SaaS vendors. Neither routes regulatory or framework interpretation (Lena, counsel), financial close controls (Daniel's close-controls-and-accounting also triggers on 'audit prep'), vendor security or privacy diligence (Vera's vendor-due-diligence, Lena's dpa-checklist-review and subprocessor-register) or case-level escalations (Robin's escalations-and-incidents). The ops-controls-and-escalations eval names this as its top issue.
issues.fix: Append: 'Regulatory or framework interpretation (SOC 2, ISO, GDPR) goes to compliance or counsel; month-end close and financial controls go to finance; vendor security and privacy evidence goes to procurement or compliance for review, and you never call a vendor secure, compliant, or financially sound; a live customer escalation goes to support. You design the path, they work the case.'

issues.quote: re-flag at the 60-day mark (negotiate) and the 30-day mark (sign or exit), each with its staged action
issues.problem: The re-flags are keyed to days before term end, not to the notice deadline. Voice sample 2 itself cites a '60-day notice date', and in that case the 30-day 'exit' flag lands after notice has closed, so the contract auto-renews. 'Sign or exit' also reads as James acting, which the boundaries forbid.
issues.fix: Key the staged flags to the notice deadline taken from the contract (e.g. notice date minus 30 days: negotiate; minus 7 days: the owner decides renew, renegotiate, or give notice). When the contract is not on file, mark the notice date UNKNOWN and flag it now.

issues.quote: One row per vendor — purpose, owner, cadence, trailing spend, renewal date — with each renewal inside 90 days flagged
issues.problem: The promise ends 'built from your spend export or a pasted list'. A spend or card export shows charges, not term end or notice period, so delivering a renewal date from that source means inferring it from charge cadence. That breaks 'never invent ... a renewal date'. james-getting-started repeats the problem: a connected spend export means 'every renewal date is a known fact rather than a guess'.
issues.fix: Say 'renewal date and notice period read from the contract or marked UNKNOWN, spend from your export or a pasted list', and correct the same line in james-getting-started ('Check connections first').

issues.quote: Numbers and targets go to the ops scorecard; cross-functional milestones, RAID, and phase gates go to govern a program

recommendations.notes:
What I checked: the brief, the dossier, james.yml, all 10 kit SKILL.md files, the dropped upstream packages, the catalog index, and DEFERRED_SKILLS.md. Nothing in the deferred list is ops-relevant. I searched the catalog for OKR/planning, business continuity, delegation of authority, change management, inventory, SaaS audit and access review; only renewal tracking and incident review had a catalog source. I also read the candidate upstream packages in local clones (anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins, alirezarezvani/claude-skills, rampstackco/claude-skills, phuryn/pm-skills).

Not skills: the expert-body fixes the review lists (new teammate handoffs for Lena, Daniel, Vera and Robin; identity para 3 routing; the notice-period column; the audit calendar in routines[2]) belong in james.yml. Recommendation 1 supplies the "where do signed contracts live" question that routines[1].asks and onboarding are missing.

Considered and rejected:
