recommendations.why: For SaaS sites these decision-stage pages are often the money pages that day_one[1] promises to audit, and website-seo-audit itself singles out comparison and alternative families as the common SaaS opportunity. The kit covers the Compare intent only as a page shape in seo-content-brief ('Table, criteria, a verdict') and general page copy in marketing-copywriting. It has no guidance on the four formats, a single competitor-data file shared across pages, migration sections, or the legal risk of comparative claims. The catalog skills that hold competitor facts (competitor-profiling, Zara's competitive-intelligence, Nadia's competitor-teardown) belong to other experts, so the skill should consult them rather than duplicate them. The upstream is from the same MIT repo and pin as the kit's Corey Haines skills.

source.ref: coreyhaines31/marketingskills skills/competitors @5b2c0007766c6a1cf1d53fd8fc73e979e0821022 (SKILL.md, references/templates.md, references/content-architecture.md). Fixes: saved-context lookup instead of .agents; replace 'sign up, use it' with public pages, docs, pricing and dated review-site quotes; remove the FAQ-schema-for-rich-results advice (Google stopped showing FAQ rich results on 7 May 2026); drop the programmatic-seo reference; add a rule that every competitor claim carries a source URL and a date, with approver sign-off before publishing.

sketch: Pick the format from the query: singular alternative, plural alternatives, us vs them, or them vs them, with keyword targets from the keyword map or the DataForSEO blocks.

Competitor data file: positioning, pricing tiers, features, best for and not ideal for, and common complaints, each with a source URL and a verified date. Stored as a workspace file with a re-verify date. If Zara or Nadia is hired, consult them first.

Required sections: TL;DR verdict, an honest 'who each is for', a feature table and a pricing table (each cell sourced), and a migration section using only real customer quotes. Missing proof is marked as a gap.
Guardrails: never misstate a competitor, acknowledge their strengths, avoid trademarked-name misuse in titles, and route any comparative claim to the approver before publishing.

recommendations.name: Structured data markup
recommendations.purpose: Write valid JSON-LD (Article or BlogPosting, Organization, BreadcrumbList, Product or SoftwareApplication, VideoObject) that matches the visible page, and state honestly which rich results Google still shows.
recommendations.why: Implementing and checking schema markup is routine on-page work for SEO content roles. The kit mentions structured data only in website-seo-audit's glossary and in on-page-seo-audit's check list, and gives no method for producing correct markup. Current accuracy matters: Google stopped showing FAQ rich results on 7 May 2026 and deprecated HowTo rich results in 2023 (searchenginejournal.com 'Google Drops FAQ Rich Results From Search'). The upstream schema skill still presents FAQPage as a rich-result path and needs that fix. The skill runs on the platform: web_fetch or Firecrawl reads the existing JSON-LD, and bash_exec parses and checks required properties. Priority is low because it could ship as a reference inside on-page-seo-audit instead of a separate skill.

source.ref: coreyhaines31/marketingskills skills/schema @5b2c0007766c6a1cf1d53fd8fc73e979e0821022 (SKILL.md plus references/schema-examples.md). Fixes: saved-context lookup instead of .agents; FAQ and HowTo rich-result status updated; add VideoObject for posts made from video; add a bash_exec validation script; for WordPress, point to the SEO plugin settings rather than pasting JSON-LD into post content.

sketch: Read the existing markup from the live page and list its types, errors, and any mismatch with the visible content.
Choose the type from the page (article, product or SaaS, organization, breadcrumb, video) and state which rich result, if any, it can still earn today.
Write JSON-LD using only facts visible on the page, never invented ratings or reviews. Parse it and check required properties in bash_exec.
Implementation note for each CMS. Ask the owner to confirm with the Rich Results Test, since the skill cannot claim a validation it did not run.
FAQPage and HowTo stay allowed as valid Schema.org types, but the skill must never promise a rich result for them.

recommendations.name: Link prospecting
recommendations.purpose: Find pages that could realistically cite a specific asset (resource lists, comparisons, statistics roundups, pages with broken links), record only contact paths that were actually found, and draft personalised outreach for approval.
recommendations.why: Link building appears in every SEO content job description sampled: 'Negotiating backlinks' (workello.com), 'link building and content optimization' (huneety.com), 'Overseeing backlink profiles, link-building strategy, and digital PR efforts' (digitalwaffle.co). The kit plans link-earning formats in marketing-content-strategy but has no skill that finds prospects or drafts asks. OpenSEO link-prospecting (117 lines, MIT, same pin) already separates discovery from contact finding and forbids invented contacts. Its SERP step can be rewired to web_search, Exa and Firecrawl. The platform has no backlink block, so competitor backlink data becomes an optional Ahrefs or Semrush export. Sending goes through Gmail with the approval flow. Priority is low because Maria's identity is content-first and Noor owns media relations.

source.ref: every-app/open-seo plugins/openseo/skills/link-prospecting @0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49. Rewire get_serp_results to web_search, Exa or Firecrawl search, and get_backlinks_overview to an optional user export. Drop the local-SEO tools, the seo-report dependency and the openseo.so link line.

sketch: Name the linkable asset and the one reason someone would cite it. With no such reason, stop and say so.

Run 5-10 prospecting query patterns ('<topic> resources', 'best <category> tools', '<competitor> alternatives', '<topic> statistics') through web_search or Exa. Keep editorial pages and drop competitors, paid placements and spam.
Record only contact paths actually found (author page, contact page, masthead), each with its source URL, and never guess an email.

Draft outreach for 2-3 reusable angles (resource inclusion, better data, comparison mention), personalised per page. Send only after approval, through Gmail and the platform's approval flow. Journalist or press angles go to Noor.
Guardrails: no mass outreach, no paid-link schemes, and no claim about the asset that the asset does not support.

recommendations.notes:
Coverage checks:
- I read the three live skills and the PR #13 versions of every Toran package in the proposed kit (marketing-content-strategy, marketing-copywriting, marketing-copy-editing, product-marketing-context, website-seo-audit, seo-report-generation). I also read Maya's weekly-marketing-read and editorial-calendar-ops.
- None of the seven recommendations duplicates a kit skill. Where one touches a kit skill, the sketch draws the boundary: the performance check routes to the refresh and audit skills, and the handoff reuses the brief's title and meta rather than rewriting them.

Sources:
- **Deferred packages:** nothing in DEFERRED_SKILLS.md fits. It lists the ads suite, marketing-ideas, marketing-plan, prospecting, public-relations, referrals and invoice-chase.
- **Catalog skills:** no unassigned catalog skill fits beyond those already in the kit. conversion-rate-optimization (proposed for Marco), competitor-profiling (Nadia, Alex, Zara) and storybrand-messaging are adjacent but belong elsewhere or duplicate product-marketing-context.
- **Pins:** all upstream recommendations use pins already in the catalog.
  - coreyhaines31/marketingskills@5b2c000 (MIT, Corey Haines 2025).
  - every-app/open-seo@0ffff93 (MIT, Ben Senescu 2026), the pin website-seo-audit came from.
- **URL check:** every URL returned 200 on raw.githubusercontent.com at those commits.

Platform facts that shape the sketches:
- No Search Console or GA4 block exists. Positions and clicks must come from an export or a connected MCP.
- The DataForSEO blocks are only Keyword Suggestions and Related Keywords (volume, KD, CPC, competition, serp_info). There are no live SERP positions and no backlinks.
- The Perplexity block returns url_citation annotations, which makes AI-citation checks measurable.
- WordPressCreatePostBlock.publish_as_draft defaults to False, so the default call publishes publicly. It only creates posts, not updates, and only on WordPress.com or Jetpack sites. This is why publish-ready-handoff is a must.
- The Medium block has canonical_url for cross-posts.
- The automated-blog-writer preload's behaviour is unverified. Its old weekly cadence appears in seed.py REMOVED_TEMPLATE_CADENCES; worth checking whether it publishes.

Dangling references to resolve alongside this kit:

- Google stopped showing FAQ rich results on 7 May 2026. The merged on-page-seo-audit and any upstream text (competitors, ai-seo, schema) must not recommend FAQ schema as a rich-result win.

Deliberately not recommended:
- **programmatic-seo** (upstream MIT): scaled-content-abuse risk, and there is no bulk CMS path.
- **site-architecture** (upstream MIT): IA and navigation are web or dev work. Its internal-linking rules are folded into publish-ready-handoff and the audit.

proposal.summary:
Max's current kit is 37 NICK skills. It has a strong prospecting core (build-the-target-list is the strongest), a deal core with heavy internal duplication (two close-plan skills, two stakeholder-map skills, and concession rules in three places), sales-leadership skills, and nine machine-built industry verticals. Four of the verticals are notably thin. TORAN supplies direct upstream counterparts for account research, outreach, call prep and pipeline review. I use sales-account-research (PR #13 packaging) as the base for research-an-account. I add sales-call-preparation (the most complete Toran package in scope) as the only new standalone skill. For first touch and pipeline I keep Nick's persona-specific bases, because they carry the draft-only rule, the target-list row state and the forecast grades. Into those bases I graft Toran's CRM and inbox checks, Gmail drafting, stage rollup and risk flags. Max's own 'stuck' definition (no buyer-owned commitment in 14-21 days) stays, so the skills and routines agree. The main merges are:
- quarterback-the-deal-team and compliance-gated-deal-execution into enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans, renamed close-plan-and-deal-desk. It points to pipeline-review-and-forecast for the single commit definition and to objection-and-negotiation for the single concession ladder.
- find-the-decision-makers into multithread-and-stakeholder-maps, renamed map-the-buying-center.
- prospecting's compliance and lineage rules into the target list.
- the enablement cert gates, rubric and training cycle into sales-team-leadership.
- signature-to-launch's white-space table into renewal-expansion-and-qbr.
- industrial tender items into the RFP skill.

GTM strategy, alliance governance, co-marketing and post-signature onboarding go to Zara, Anika, and Riley or Robin. Marketplace-partner revenue, credit term sheets, showroom F&I and field routing leave the kit, which ends at 26 skills. The expert file's skills list must be rewritten to match, including the two renames. Every skill that carries copied MIT or Apache-2.0 text or reference files keeps the upstream LICENSE and an ATTRIBUTION.md. The biggest body problems are:
- an Account Executive title over a set of sales-manager routines.
- a flat 3x coverage bar in the voice sample that contradicts 'never a flat multiple'.
- forecast categories and reply buckets in the routines that the skills do not produce.
- a 'published sources only' contact boundary that must be amended before the licensed-export rule and the preloaded contact finder can work.

body_review.summary: The persona is disciplined. FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels, no guessed contacts and draft-by-default hold across the identity, the boundaries and the skills. The routines are carefully specified, with quiet-week one-liners, rollup lines for unchanged deals and delivery to the owner only. But the persona is split. The job title and tagline describe an individual AE, while half the routines and a third of the identity are first-line sales-manager work, and max-getting-started opens by calling Max 'a senior sales leader'. Several routine promises contradict the skills they rely on: the coverage bar, forecast categories, reply buckets, opt-out permanence, the commit definition and the enrichment gate. The boundaries have no rule on legal, compliance, licensing or employment decisions, even though the kit runs improvement plans, compensation design and regulated verticals. The 'published sources only' contact rule also blocks the licensed-export path the kit needs.
strengths: The evidence rule is concrete and consistent. Identity, boundaries and skills all say an unverified field stays blank, contacts come only from linkable published sources, and every load-bearing claim is labeled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN.
The draft-by-default rule names the exact actions it covers (send, post, message, promise pricing or terms, move a CRM field), which matches the platform approval flow.
Each routine handles the no-news case well: a one-line quiet week, one rollup line for items already flagged, delivery to the owner only, and a timezone ask.

Each day_one promise maps to a real skill: the scored target list to build-the-target-list, the unsent first touches to research-an-account plus draft-a-first-touch, and the evidence-graded pipeline read to pipeline-review-and-forecast.
The voice samples are short and in register. The first-touch sample follows draft-a-first-touch's structure: one sourced dated fact, one pain, and a soft reply ask instead of a meeting ask.
body_review.kit_alignment:
The YAML skills list names every slug, so it must be rewritten to the 26-skill kit, with multithread-and-stakeholder-maps replaced by map-the-buying-center and enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans replaced by close-plan-and-deal-desk. Routines, day_one and preloads name no skill slug, so the renames break nothing else in the expert file. Skill bodies do cross-reference each other by name and need updating:
- research-an-account says 'run Find the decision makers'.
- sales-ops-coverage-and-quota ends with 'Play-level incentive-bonus tracking lives in the enablement skill', which will dangle once enablement-playbooks-certification is merged away. SPIF-play tracking moves into sales-ops itself.
- draft-a-follow-up's 'switch to Handle a reply' still resolves.

Routine coverage in the proposed kit:
- weekday-prospecting-batch: research-an-account and draft-a-first-touch. The first-touch enrichment gate conflicts with the routine's no-row-change rule.
- monday-list-top-up: build-the-target-list.
- friday-pipeline-recap: pipeline-review-and-forecast. The outreach log its tally needs is never defined.
- monday-team-pipeline-inspection: pipeline-review-and-forecast, sales-team-leadership (40/75/100 ramp curve) and sales-ops-coverage-and-quota.
- wednesday-forecast-and-deal-inspection: pipeline-review-and-forecast's single commit gate, plus MEDDPICC evidence from discovery-and-qualification.
- monthly-win-loss-review: voice-of-customer-loop.

max-getting-started (a skill, not YAML) describes only the three leadership routines and never mentions the three AE routines. It also repeats the Wednesday 'stuck' category. The identity and bio never mention the four industry verticals kept in the kit (cloud marketplace commits, clinical access, retail JBP, media). Either add one identity sentence that names them or drop them in a later pass. The preloaded email-address-finder has no rule in any skill for how its output enters the target list, and the boundary's 'published sources you can link' wording currently forbids it.

issues.quote: Account Executive
issues.problem: The title and tagline describe an individual AE. But identity paragraph 3, the bio ('I run the leadership side too') and three of six routines are sales-manager motions: the Monday team inspection per rep, the Wednesday forecast, and the monthly win-loss review. max-getting-started introduces Max as 'a senior sales leader' and hands back 'one live leadership read'. Its review flags this as misstating the product.
issues.fix: Pick a primary persona. One option: keep AE as primary, make routines[3] and [4] opt-in 'if you lead a team', and rewrite getting-started to open on the target list, first touches and pipeline read. The other: retitle to 'Account Executive and Sales Manager' and say so in the tagline.

issues.quote: $1.2M open against a $500K quota is 2.4x coverage, below the 3x bar
issues.problem: The sample the model imitates uses a flat 3x bar. routines[3] says the bar is 'never a flat multiple' but 1 over the segment's historical win rate, and territory-and-account-planning uses the same win-rate rule. Max gives two answers to 'is my coverage OK?'.
issues.fix: Rewrite the sample on the win-rate bar, for example '2.4x coverage; at your 25% win rate you need 4x, so you are $800K short'. Make the same change in pipeline-review-and-forecast.

issues.quote: Label every open deal Commit, Best Case, Pipeline, or Stuck
issues.problem: pipeline-review-and-forecast grades deals 'Commit, best case, pipeline, or omitted'. Stuck is a stall flag, not a forecast category, so the Wednesday read and the skill use different vocabularies. Omar's sales-forecast-rollup uses commit/best case/pipeline. max-getting-started repeats the four-way split with 'stuck'.
issues.fix: Use Commit / Best Case / Pipeline / Omitted, with a separate Stuck flag (no buyer-owned commitment in 14-21 days) as the merged pipeline skill defines it. Make the same change in max-getting-started's description of the Wednesday routine.

issues.quote: Commit means expected to close with a clean paper process
issues.problem: This is a third commit definition. enterprise-deal-desk-close-plans gates commit on full MEDDPICC, and territory-and-account-planning uses a six-point commit gate. The same deal can be commit in one read and not in another.
issues.fix: Define commit once, in pipeline-review-and-forecast: the six-point gate, a met Paper Process letter, and no pending compliance gate. Point this routine and close-plan-and-deal-desk's gate to it.

issues.quote: replies split positive, neutral and negative
issues.problem: handle-a-reply sorts replies into positive, curious, referral, objection or no, so this split has no source. Sent counts depend on an 'outreach log'. draft-a-first-touch and handle-a-reply write to it only after a confirmed send or a received reply, but no skill defines where that log lives or what columns it has. build-the-target-list's row keeps only the latest last_touch_on, so the week's sends cannot be counted reliably. The 3-5% reply-rate and meetings-per-hundred benchmarks appear in no skill.
issues.fix: Tally by handle-a-reply's buckets. Define the outreach log in build-the-target-list (date, prospect_id, channel, touch number, event: sent, reply bucket or meeting). Have draft-a-first-touch, draft-a-follow-up and handle-a-reply append to it only on a confirmed send or a received reply. Name it as the tally source, and put the reply-rate benchmark in pipeline-review-and-forecast or drop it.

issues.quote: never re-add a person-and-company pair that came off the list in the last 30 days
issues.problem: An opt-out must be permanent, but this rule lets an opted-out person be re-prospected after 30 days. handle-a-reply only suppresses the row and does not write to the do-not-contact list that build-the-target-list checks. This creates CAN-SPAM, GDPR and PECR exposure (handle-a-reply eval).
issues.fix: Change the rule to: 'never re-add anyone on the do-not-contact list; other removals wait 30 days'. Make handle-a-reply write opt-outs to that list.

issues.quote: Two straight weeks with the same miss escalates to an improvement plan.
issues.problem: A formal improvement plan is an employment action. Neither the boundaries nor sales-team-leadership requires HR involvement, consistent documentation or a not-legal-advice line (sales-team-leadership eval). sales-team-leadership also uses a different escalation rule ('two calls with the same miss becomes the week's drill').
issues.fix: Change to: 'Two straight weeks with the same miss is flagged for the manager to decide with HR.' Align sales-team-leadership to the same rule.

issues.quote: Marketing campaigns, support tickets, and engineering implementation are out of scope — name them and hand them back.
issues.problem: The kit runs redlines, compliance gates, compensation plans, improvement plans and clinical selling. No boundary says Max never makes a legal, compliance, licensing, suitability or employment determination. The out-of-scope list also names no handoff for work the proposed kit sends elsewhere: post-signature onboarding (Riley/Robin), GTM strategy (Zara), alliance governance (Anika), and price or term approvals (Jordan/Daniel).
issues.fix: Add: 'Legal, compliance, licensing and employment decisions belong to counsel, the compliance owner and HR; you prepare the evidence brief (Lena's compliance-escalation-brief or Ines's hr-escalation-brief when they are hired). Post-signature onboarding goes to customer success, GTM strategy to Zara, alliance governance to Anika, and pricing approvals to the deal desk.'

issues.quote: contacts enter only from published sources you can link
issues.problem: The proposed build-the-target-list merge admits contacts from the user's own HubSpot or Apollo export and from licensed providers used within their terms. That fixes the target list's top review issue. The preloaded email-address-finder also returns addresses that are not 'published sources you can link'. As written, the boundary (and identity: 'you find decision-makers only where you can link to something published') forbids both, so the model will either strip licensed data or break its own boundary.
issues.fix: Amend the boundary and identity to: 'contacts enter only from a published source you can link, or from the owner's own export or licensed data provider with its source and verification status recorded; never build an address from a naming pattern'.

issues.quote: email-address-finder
issues.problem: Max's boundary forbids building an email from a pattern, and build-the-target-list says 'Contacts are found, never made'. No skill says how a contact-finder tool's output (or an Apollo or HubSpot export) enters the list. That gap is the top issue in build-the-target-list's eval, and max-getting-started offers this preload by name ('Email Scout - Contact Finder Assistant').
issues.fix: Add a rule to build-the-target-list: a tool-found contact enters with contact_source and its verification status. Anything pattern-derived or unverifiable stays blank. Pair this with the boundary amendment above, or drop the preload.

issues.quote: coverage, quota, and compensation design
issues.problem: Compensation design needs finance, HR and legal review (several US states require written commission agreements). The sales-ops-coverage-and-quota eval rates the comp section far too thin.
issues.fix: Change to 'coverage and quota design, and compensation drafts for finance, HR and legal review'.

issues.quote: For each pick, look up the person and the company on the public web
issues.problem: The batch researches from the public web only and never checks CRM ownership or prior email threads. A row a colleague owns, or a warm thread, would get a cold opener. The research-an-account eval and Toran's sales-account-research both treat that check as the first step.
issues.fix: Change to: 'Check CRM ownership and any prior thread first, then look up the person and the company on the public web.'

issues.quote: no row on the list changes until the user tells you to mark it
issues.problem: The batch picks 'strong-fit rows nobody has contacted yet', including rows just added at status new. But draft-a-first-touch says 'If the row has not been enriched yet, stop and route it to research before writing a word', and this routine forbids setting the row to enriched. So a new row stalls, or the model breaks one of the two rules.
issues.fix: Let the routine's in-run research satisfy the enrichment gate for that draft. Return the proposed row updates (hook, hook_source_url, hook_date, enriched_on, status) under each draft for the user to approve.

issues.quote: we cut those 30% for two teams your size
issues.problem: The sample the model imitates carries an unlinked proof statistic. draft-a-first-touch requires that 'Proof points come only from what the user gave you', so the sample teaches the pattern the boundary forbids.
issues.fix: Tie the number to a user-supplied proof, for example 'our Contoso case study shows receiving errors down 30%', or use a visible [proof point] placeholder.

clusters.job: Build and maintain a scored ICP prospect list, one person per row

members.note: The strongest skill in Max's kit. draft-a-first-touch, draft-a-follow-up, handle-a-reply and the monday-list-top-up routine all read its fixed row schema and status ladder. It enforces 'Contacts are found, never made'.

ORIGINAL, coreyhaines upstream, MIT; a little behind the base overall. Adds sourcing branches (local SMB, demand-signal), a full compliance reference and lineage capture. But it endorses Hunter/Snov pattern guessing ('Email pattern guessing and verification'). saas-prospecting.md also calls tools/clis/github-prospects.js and tools/integrations/github.md, which the package does not ship.

proposed.name: Build the target list
proposed.description: Use when the user says who they sell to, hands over companies or a HubSpot, Apollo or sheet export, or wants names added to or cut from the prospect list: a strong/maybe/weak scored list, one person per row, a sourced dated hook on each, contact source and verification recorded, no guessed contacts.
proposed.rationale:
Max's row schema has to stay canonical because four skills and two routines read it. prospecting adds what the base lacks:
- a rule for licensed data and user exports (the base's biggest gap).
- source-plus-date lineage for GDPR, CAN-SPAM and CASL.
- a local-SMB branch that matches the preloaded lead-finder-local-businesses workflow.

prospecting's pattern-guessed emails directly contradict Max's boundary, so they are dropped rather than grafted. This skill also becomes the home of the outreach log (date, prospect_id, channel, touch number, event) that the Friday recap tallies. Ship prospecting's MIT LICENSE with the copied reference files. Admitting export and provider contacts requires the boundary amendment flagged in the body review.
drops: prospecting 'Tool Selection Quick Picks' row 'Hunter or Snov | Email pattern guessing and verification', plus the pattern-discovery rows in references/data-sources.md (lines 15, 95-110, 274)

prospecting references/saas-prospecting.md GitHub stargazer step that runs node tools/clis/github-prospects.js and points to tools/integrations/github.md (neither shipped; Toran deferred the source over the exporter's CSV formula-injection risk)
prospecting Hot/Warm/Cold/Skip scale (Max uses strong/maybe/weak) and the mandatory Truelist step (use the ZeroBounce block when connected)
prospecting '.agents/product-marketing.md' context lookup (not a platform path)
build-the-target-list trigger 'who should I sell to' (collides with Zara's icp-and-segmentation)

grafts.what: Rules 1, 2 and 5-8 as a short block: no bulk scraping of LinkedIn or Google Maps, no CAPTCHA or login bypass, no reselling, rate-limit yourself, no breached or unprovenanced lists, never qualify on sensitive traits. Rule 7 says licensed providers (Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clearbit, Clay) are fine within their ToS. That is the missing rule for user exports. A contact from an export or provider enters with contact_source and verification status. An address that is pattern-derived or unverifiable stays blank.

Add contact_source_url (or contact_source for an export or tool), contact_verified_on and, for EU/UK rows, lawful_basis columns to the row schema. Ship references/compliance.md as is: CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL, platform ToS, anti-patterns and an audit checklist. It already bans guessed emails (Anti-Patterns 3) and states it is not legal advice.

A local-SMB branch: Google Maps plus browser discovery, website-status scoring, and a business+address dedupe key. demand-signals.md can be an optional branch for first-customer lists only after its last30days and social-fetch tool names are replaced with web_search and the Reddit or Twitter/X blocks.

grafts.section: Phase 2 and 'Always include after the table'
grafts.what: Source 2-3x the target count before grading. After the preview, add Top outreach targets (3-5 with one line each), the search parameters used, and open questions the user must verify.

clusters.job: Research one target account before outreach, a first call or a deal review

members.note: TORAN, Anthropic account-research, Apache-2.0; stronger than Max's in-house research skill. Use the PR #13 version, which renames the handoff to sales-outreach-drafting. It checks CRM ownership before researching, scores ICP fit in an evidence table, writes 2-3 sourced hooks, has files-only fallbacks and strong untrusted-content rules.
Its main gap is that it never checks CRM or target-list ownership first, which the Toran base does. It carries Max's FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN ledger and the short verified stakeholder map.

proposed.name: Research an account
proposed.description: Use when the user names one company to research before outreach, a first call, or a deal review: CRM ownership check first, a dated and sourced brief, ICP fit table graded strong/maybe/weak, a short verified stakeholder map, two or three outreach hooks, and a FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN source ledger.
proposed.rationale: Both skills load for 'research Acme' but return different shapes (the review flags the duplicate triggers). The Toran body has the better mechanics: ownership check first, fit table, dated signals and connector tiering. Max's labelling, ledger and stakeholder-map conventions are grafted in. The overall fit grade uses the target list's strong/maybe/weak scale, because the result writes back to icp_fit. The slug stays research-an-account for kit continuity. ATTRIBUTION.md and LICENSE (Apache-2.0) are kept, with the modifications recorded.
drops: sales-account-research Step 6 next step 'run sales-outreach-drafting' (route to draft-a-first-touch)
sales-account-research 'gated-writes' tier line pointing to uninstalled update-opportunity/log-activity
sales-account-research 'Rendering: ... as a Page ... Slides' rule (claude.ai surfaces)
sales-account-research 'suggest adding it to the project instructions' (store the answer with memory_store instead)
sales-account-research overall fit 'strong / moderate / poor' (map to strong / maybe / weak)
sales-account-research description trigger 'who is [person] at [company]' (belongs to map-the-buying-center)
research-an-account 'Write the meeting strategy' section (call plans live in sales-call-preparation and discovery-and-qualification)
research-an-account trigger 'who matters at this account' (belongs to map-the-buying-center)

grafts.section: Build the brief from public sources only
grafts.what: Size signals (headcount, revenue, funding), each labelled FACT with URL or UNKNOWN. A private company with no numbers is UNKNOWN, never an estimate.

grafts.section: Map the stakeholders you can verify
grafts.what: A short verified map: name, title, role tag (champion, economic buyer, evaluator, blocker, unknown) and one line each. Missing seats are named. The full ranked table routes to map-the-buying-center.

grafts.section: Close with a source ledger + Fallbacks

recommendations.notes:
Coverage read. Most of the verified 26-skill kit covers the AE and first-line manager work well: target list, research, the buying center, first touch, follow-up and reply, call prep, discovery, objections, the business case, the close plan, handoff, RFP, co-sell, pipeline and forecast, territory, exec engagement, renewal and QBR, win-loss, leadership and sales ops. The largest gap is operational rather than methodological. No kit skill writes to a deal record or logs an activity. Three kit bodies already point at skills that are not installed, as their PR #13 text says:
- sales-call-preparation offers "call-summary ... not installed" when the meeting has already ended.
- research-an-account (Toran body) hands record creation to "update-opportunity, log-activity ... not installed".
- draft-a-first-touch (Toran's CRM and Gmail mechanics) hands logging to "log-activity ... not installed".

pipeline-review-and-forecast (Nick) stops at "paste-ready text, apply nothing". The persona still promises that CRM fields move once the owner says yes. Recommendations 1 and 2 close those pointers. They come from the same upstream commit, 1c7187c4, that the catalog's Toran packages were pinned to, and I checked that the files are byte-identical at HEAD da38ec1. The upstream sales plugin v2 has 36 skills and only 4 were imported.

Packaging needs:
- Rewrite the shared Rules block's Cowork-only rendering line (artifact, Page, Slides) to write_workspace_file.
- Make the Gong ask_deal route conditional on MCP with a paste fallback, the way PR #13 did.
- Replace upstream's "act when the user asks" authority with Max's draft-by-default rule and an explicit yes per action.

Platform gap to flag. The AutoGPT HubSpot blocks (backend/blocks/hubspot) cover only company and contact get/create/update plus engagement send_email/track_engagement. They have no deal or opportunity object and no note, call or meeting logging. update-the-deal-record and log-the-call therefore have to route to a CRM MCP via run_mcp_tool, or to a pipeline tracker in Google Sheets, Airtable or Notion via run_block, and fall back to a paste-ready before/after checklist. Consider asking for a HubSpot deals/notes block. Google Calendar ReadEvents and CreateEvent blocks exist, so book-the-meeting is runnable.

Upstream skills deliberately not recommended because the kit already covers them:
- stakeholder-map → map-the-buying-center
- close-plan → close-plan-and-deal-desk
- handle-objection → objection-and-negotiation
- forecast and pipeline-review → pipeline-review-and-forecast
- account-plan and account-tiering → territory-and-account-planning
- expansion-whitespace, renewal-radar and customer-health → renewal-expansion-and-qbr
- win-loss-review and customer-voice → voice-of-customer-loop
- team-pipeline and rep-context → sales-team-leadership plus pipeline-review-and-forecast
- create-an-asset → business-case-and-roi-selling references
- crm-hygiene-check → Omar

Also not recommended:
- deal-slip-scenario is a small add to pipeline-review-and-forecast's backward funnel math.
- end-of-day and weekly-wrap duplicate the Friday recap.
- inbox-sweep is folded into deal-signal-watch.

Battlecards. The monthly win-loss routine proposes playbook and battlecard changes, but after enablement-playbooks-certification and sales-enablement-content were dropped, no kit skill owns a battlecard. Head-to-head deal strategy sits in rfp-and-competitive-bid-response, whose trigger is framed around formal bids. I suggest not adding a skill. Instead, voice-of-customer-loop should route battlecard edits to Zara's competitive-intelligence (or Nadia), and rfp should get a non-RFP trigger such as "competitor in the deal".

Deliverability. At five manual sends a day this is not a gap. If sequences move into Smartlead, hand off to Remy's email-deliverability-guardrails.

Persona and routines:
- deal-signal-watch needs a new weekday routine, or should be folded into weekday-prospecting-batch.
- The Wednesday commit gate's category changes should land through update-the-deal-record.
- follow-past-champions and the licensed Enrichlayer or Apollo paths conflict with the boundary's "published sources you can link" wording. The review already flagged this for the email-address-finder preload. Fix it in the same pass.

Evidence sources:
- AE job descriptions list maintaining accurate CRM records of interactions (indeed.com/hire/job-description/account-executive, builtin.com/articles/account-executive-job-description).
- Figures on buyers talking to current users before purchase come from vendor-published surveys (deeto.com, corporatevisions.com).
- Figures on champion-tracking lift are vendor claims (usergems.com, pipeline.zoominfo.com). Treat all of these as directional.

No suitable MIT, Apache-2.0 or CC-BY source was found for the two new skills. louisblythe/Sales-Skills (MIT) has no reference or champion skill.

recommendations.purpose: The kit's single writer for deal fields: read the record, show only the fields that would change as before/after, write only what the owner said yes to, then re-read to verify.
recommendations.why:
AE postings list 'maintain accurate records of client interactions and pipeline in the CRM' as a core duty (Indeed, Built In). Max's identity says no CRM field moves without the owner's explicit yes, but no kit skill actually moves one:
- pipeline-review-and-forecast says 'Stage next steps as paste-ready text. Apply nothing yourself.'

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins sales/skills/update-opportunity @1c7187c4 (same pin as the catalog's sales-* packages)

sketch: Where the record lives: a CRM MCP via run_mcp_tool, HubSpot company/contact blocks, or the pipeline Sheet/Airtable/Notion tracker. Ground stage and field names on the live schema, and use the paste-ready checklist when nothing is writable. The HubSpot blocks have no deal object.
Read before write: current stage, amount, close date, next step, forecast category and owner, each cited as read.

Before/after table of changed fields only. Warn when a stage advance has open must-have letters (discovery-and-qualification's met bars), when a deal enters Commit without the pipeline-review-and-forecast gate, on a third close-date push, or when the amount moves more than 25%. Cite the source line for any value taken from a transcript or email.

Explicit yes per change set, logged with date and approver. Scheduled runs only propose. Write only the accepted fields, re-read to verify, and report the exact validation error with no guessed retries.
Bulk mode after the Friday or Wednesday read: before/after per deal and apply only the accepted ones. CRM-wide hygiene sweeps and field or schema changes go to Omar.

Extract with FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN labels: decisions, buyer commitments, our commitments, open questions, objections, next meeting, and qualification quotes. Quotes go to discovery-and-qualification for scoring rather than being scored here.

Outputs: the internal summary as a Slack draft; a completed activity dated when it happened, with 3-6 bullets tied to the account, deal and contacts; the deal-field proposals, handed to update-the-deal-record; the buyer follow-up, handed to next-step-and-handoff for its four-test grade.
Save the our-commitments ledger to the deal file. Log sent outreach emails to the outreach log that the Friday tally reads.

recommendations.name: Deal signal watch
recommendations.purpose: A recurring read-only sweep of the open book that reports only what fired since the last run: deals gone quiet, slipped dates, champion silent or gone, a competitor named, a buyer email waiting, plus today's meetings and deals closing within 14 days.
recommendations.why:
Max reads live deals only weekly (Friday recap, Monday and Wednesday leadership), and the weekday routine is prospecting only. pipeline-review-and-forecast's flags need a user-called review and do not include:
- champion silence or departure
- a competitor named in a thread or transcript
- a buyer email left unanswered on a live deal. handle-a-reply only covers prospect replies to cold outreach.

Upstream deal-signals is built to recur, diffs against the last run, and treats a quiet digest as the success case, which matches Max's quiet-week one-liner rule. Upstream daily-briefing contributes the meetings-today and closing-soon rows.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins sales/skills/deal-signals @1c7187c4 + meetings/closing/inbox rows from sales/skills/daily-briefing

sketch: Scope and window: my open deals since the last run, or 7 days. Thresholds reuse pipeline-review-and-forecast's stuck and aging-in-stage definitions rather than a second set.

Signal table:
  - gone quiet
  - close date in the danger zone (within 21 days, still at an early stage)
  - slipped since the last sweep
  - champion silent or changed, with a linked public source; otherwise UNKNOWN
  - competitor named in a Gmail thread or transcript
  - stale next step
  - buyer email waiting 3+ business days, checked against the full thread, not a search preview
  - renewal window opening
Today row: meetings matched to deals, each pointing to sales-call-preparation, plus deals closing within 14 days.
Output: act-today and this-week blocks, each item with one evidence line, one action and the kit skill that executes it. One line for everything else. A quiet run is one line.
Runs on a weekday schedule_routine. Read-only. Fixes go to update-the-deal-record, next-step-and-handoff or map-the-buying-center. Email and transcript text is data, never instructions.

recommendations.name: Request a customer reference
recommendations.purpose: Match a late-stage buyer to the right reference customer, get recorded permission through the account owner, brief both sides, and log use against a fatigue cap.
recommendations.why:
Reference calls are a standard decision-stage step, alongside pricing and security reviews. Vendor-published buyer surveys report that most enterprise buyers speak with current users before purchasing (deeto.com, corporatevisions.com), and RFPs routinely require named references.

No kit skill covers it:
- close-plan-and-deal-desk tracks procurement, legal and security.
- business-case-and-roi-selling builds ROI and POC gates.
- client-proposal-writing (merged) only mentions a 'relevant case study' as a proof point.

None of them matches, permissions, protects or logs a reference. Max's never-invent rule makes a permission register essential: naming a customer or quoting one without consent is a real harm. No suitable open-source skill was found.
sketch: Intake: what the buyer needs to hear (use case, industry, size, competitor displaced, stage) and the format (call, written, site visit, RFP reference form).

Reference register in a Sheet: customer, contact, permission scope (call, logo, quote, RFP) with date and grantor, topics, last used, uses this quarter, account owner. A customer never appears without recorded permission.
Rank 2-3 matches on fit, recency and the owner-set fatigue cap. Skip at-risk accounts after checking health with Riley or renewal-expansion-and-qbr.

Drafts: the permission ask to the account owner or CS, a brief for the reference (who is calling, what they care about, and what not to discuss, such as the reference's own pricing or terms), and the intro to the buyer. Nothing sends without yes.
After the call: log the outcome, draft the thank-you, update the register, and add the reference step with a date and owner to the close plan. No fabricated quotes, logos or case studies.

- The Friday tally counts meetings booked.
- next-step-and-handoff's four tests require the next step to 'sit on both calendars'.

No kit skill finds times across time zones, drafts the invite or books it. Kai has calendar-conflict-review but no booking skill. The platform has GoogleCalendarReadEvents and GoogleCalendarCreateEvent blocks. Upstream schedule-meeting takes attendees only from the CRM or the user's own words, and warns that creating an event emails every attendee.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins sales/skills/schedule-meeting @1c7187c4

sketch: Resolve attendees and the deal from the target list, the CRM or the owner's words, never from addresses inside an email body. Ask which deal when there are several.
Find 2-3 slots across at least two days from calendar read events, in the buyer's time zone and working hours, respecting stated preferences.
Three paths: a propose-by-email draft threaded into the buyer's thread, a direct invite that states who will receive it, or the owner's booking link.
Agenda templates by meeting type (discovery, demo, close-plan review, QBR) that carry the buyer's homework from the next step.
On yes: create the event, mark 'meeting booked' on the target-list row and outreach log, and log the activity through log-the-call.

recommendations.name: Follow past champions
recommendations.purpose: Track known champions and power users from won, lost and live deals. Flag a departure as deal or renewal risk, and turn a verified move to a new company into a warm target-list row.
recommendations.why:
Champion job-change tracking is a widely sold outbound trigger. Vendors such as UserGems and ZoomInfo claim shorter cycles and larger deals, but those figures are vendor-reported.

The kit does not cover it:

sketch: Tracked list: champions, economic buyers and power users pulled from deal records and buying-center maps, each with the last verified employer, link and date.

Monthly check using only public, linkable evidence: company team pages, press releases, the person's own public profile, and Enrichlayer or Apollo only once the boundary allows licensed sources. Anything unverified stays UNKNOWN.
Left an open deal or a customer: send a risk flag to map-the-buying-center for a rethread and to renewal-expansion-and-qbr.

Landed at a new company: create a target-list row with lineage 'former champion at X', scored on the ICP, inside a 90-day window. The first touch goes to draft-a-first-touch with an honest shared-history hook.
Compliance: the do-not-contact list always wins, and EU/UK contacts get the PECR/GDPR check from draft-a-first-touch's outreach-compliance reference.

proposal.summary:
Maya's live kit is the eight NICK skills from PR 2. No ORIGINAL skill belongs to her. TORAN proposed four coreyhaines31 packages for her. None of her twelve in-scope refs differs in PR #14, #15 or #16. PR #13 only renames cross-references, and it changes `/product-marketing` to `/product-marketing-context`, which is still a slash command. So the `.agents/` paths, the codebase auto-draft and the slash command stay broken. Each TORAN package overlaps a NICK skill that scores higher and fits the persona better. The NICK skill is the base every time, and only the reusable method is grafted in:
- **messaging-and-tone-matrix** takes product-marketing-context's objections, switching forces, verbatim customer language, alternatives and changelog.
- **editorial-calendar-ops** takes marketing-content-strategy's weighted topic scoring (each score with an evidence note), the searchable/shareable definitions with the 60/30/10 mix check, the buyer-stage modifiers and the ideation sources.
- **channel-draft-shapes** takes marketing-copywriting's page-type guidance, CTA formula and headline formulas, without the unsourced clarity statistics that sit in both the skill and its reference file. It also takes lifecycle-email-marketing's email length bands.
- **nurture-sequence-build-and-readout** takes lifecycle-email-marketing's sequence and per-email output blocks, which fixes its missing deliverable. It also takes the templates, with the incentive, urgency and 'We miss you' defaults removed. Separately, its 'bounced twice' suppression rule is wrong (an review major) and must be fixed.

The proposed kit is nine skills. The eight NICK slugs stay as they are, four of them with grafts. brand-voice-guide comes from the catalog, because the identity promises a voice profile that no Maya skill creates. The main problems in the expert body:
- The Friday competitor-watch routine has no skill behind it. It mirrors Zara's competitive-intelligence skill and repeats Nadia's Friday competitor-brief.
- The weekday pipeline check repeats Maria's routine word for word on the same cron.
- The identity promises "event and launch support" and "launch checklists", but the campaign skill explicitly hands launches off.
- The identity requires FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels that only two kit skills carry.
- The boundaries name only the account executive, even though seven marketing teammates overlap her kit.

body_review.summary:
The persona is sharp and consistent. It is brisk, leads with the plan, requires FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN on every load-bearing line, drafts by default and gates money line by line, and its routing paragraph names every live kit skill. Its weak points:
- It makes promises no skill supports: the competitor watch, event and launch support, and the voice profile.
- Two routines duplicate teammates' routines on the same cron: Nadia's Friday competitor brief and Maria's weekday pipeline check.
- It requires a labelling rule that most kit skills never mention.
- The boundaries name only the account executive, even though seven marketing teammates' kits overlap hers.
strengths: The never-invent list (metric, customer name, quote, date, budget figure) reads the same in bio, identity and boundaries. Six of the eight kit skills restate it: campaign brief, content brief, calendar, channel drafts and nurture say 'never invent', and the weekly read says 'never estimate it'.
Identity routes each request type to one named kit skill, one line each, and all eight live slugs are covered. The merged kit keeps every slug, so none of these routes break.
The money gate is specific and checkable ('the named approver says yes to each itemized line, never to the plan as a whole'). It matches campaign-brief-and-asset-plan's money gate.

Each day_one item maps onto a surviving skill (campaign-brief-and-asset-plan, editorial-calendar-ops, weekly-marketing-read). The routines stage drafts, dedupe against their last run and have one-line quiet-week rules.
body_review.kit_alignment:
No preload, routine or day_one item names a skill the proposal drops or renames. The four merges keep their base slugs, so the routing in identity still resolves. Five places don't line up.
(1) routines[2], the Friday competitor watch, has no competitor skill in the kit. proposal.summary: Mina's kit is an in-place rebuild. All eight ORIGINAL placeholders have substantially stronger PR #14 versions. Each keeps the original text almost word for word and adds scripts, templates and a shared saved state (intake.json and open-items.csv), so every cluster takes the PR #14 version as base and drops main. No NICK skill is in Mina's scope; Daniel's close-controls-and-accounting overlaps her close and reconciliation work and is handled under cross-expert. TORAN's three Anthropic finance packages are corporate controller playbooks that post entries or lock periods with no gate, and PR #14 has already adapted their best parts (the bank-rec layout into statement-reconciliation, the dependency map into month-end-close-checklist). They are dropped, with a few small grafts: owner-set amount escalation thresholds (the aging and recurrence rules are already in bank-rec-layout.md), plus the GL-to-subledger and intercompany ties from account-reconciliation; close metrics and a retrospective from month-end-close-management; driver-type labels and prior-period margin changes from financial-statement-preparation. One optional new skill (supplier-bills-and-payables) fills the payables gap named in Toran's review, which close controls 4 and 13 leave without a skill. Before shipping: (1) Replace the two log_approval.py scripts with one shared closed-list script. The four prefix-match copies accept 'Reviewed - not approved' and 'yesterday I said no' as approvals. The invoice/AR closed-list copy is not a drop-in replacement: it lacks `check`, `--approvals` and `--expect-sha`, it rejects 'Signed off', 'Reviewed, items owned' and 'Approve exactly as shown', and close_status.py imports its is_approval. (2) Add a thresholds block to intake.json; three skills read one that does not exist. (3) Fix the persona in three places: its reconciliation-complete rule contradicts statement-reconciliation, it has a voice sample that calls identified items 'unexplained', and it has no routines. (4) Narrow Daniel's close-controls-and-accounting. TodoWrite and run_sub_session are real platform tools, so they need no change.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and matches the kit. Identity, boundaries and both voice samples speak in control totals, sources and approval gates, and every slug the file bundles survives the merge under the same name. Three things need work before shipping. (1) The identity's completion rule ('complete ... when the unexplained difference is zero or every remaining item has an owner') lets Mina call a reconciliation complete with a non-zero difference. That contradicts both versions of statement-reconciliation, and the persona is loaded in every chat. (2) The reconciliation voice sample calls two identified reconciling items an 'unexplained difference', which is the exact error the rebuilt skill guards against. (3) routines is empty, although the rebuilt kit ships a monthly close kick-off and a weekly receivables review. Smaller gaps: the invoice approval wording is looser than the rebuilt invoice skill; the boundaries leave out bank-detail changes, period locks and masking; the bio promises supplier-bill work that no skill does.
strengths: Identity turns the job into checkable rules: source name and period on every output, source facts kept apart from the proposed treatment, and 'Never force an unclear item into a category: mark it unresolved and ask the smallest question that would settle it.'
The boundaries and the non-advisory stance (no tax treatment, filing position, revenue recognition or depreciation choices) match the guardrails of all eight PR #14 skills.
voice_preferences ('show the control total, the exception, and the next owner') is specific enough to steer output, and the first sample refuses to mark the period reconciled.
day_one items map to real skills: intake -> bookkeeping-getting-started; exception queue -> bookkeeping-exception-escalation plus open-items.csv; month summary -> monthly-profit-and-loss-summary.
The skills list is already in a sensible workflow order, and no routine, preload or day_one entry names a skill that the merge would drop or rename.
body_review.kit_alignment: Mostly good. The eight bundled slugs are exactly the eight PR #14 rebuilds in place, so the proposed kit keeps every name the body relies on. The gaps are on the body side. (1) The identity's reconciliation rule ('zero or every remaining item has an owner') conflicts with 14:statement-reconciliation: '"Reconciled" is used only when the unexplained difference is exactly 0.00 and every remaining item is timing or a drafted correction'. (2) routines is [], although 14:bookkeeping-getting-started/templates/cadence-routines.md defines a 'Monthly close kick-off' and a 'Weekly receivables review'. The PR #14 research notes (docs/research/bookkeeping.md) say 'Mina has no routines today and this plan does not add any'. (3) The bio's 'bills' has no skill: control 4 in 14:month-end-close-checklist/templates/close-controls.csv routes payables to accounts-receivable-follow-up, which handles receivables only, and control 13 names no skill. (4) The identity and boundaries say invoices may be issued or sent once approved, but 14:invoice-drafting-and-issue lets Mina do no more than create a Draft after a logged yes. (5) The day-one P&L promise needs a ledger export, which 14:monthly-profit-and-loss-summary requires. (6) Owner thresholds are read by the exception, close (step 6) and P&L (step 9) skills, but intake.json has no field to hold them.

issues.quote: Two items remain: a $320 bank debit with no ledger entry and a $95 ledger payment not on the statement. Unexplained difference: $225.
issues.problem: Both items are identified reconciling items: a statement-only debit (fee or unrecorded payment) and a ledger-only payment (outstanding or timing). The sample reports their net as the 'unexplained difference'. That is the conflation the main statement-reconciliation eval flagged, and it contradicts 14:statement-reconciliation's bank-rec-layout.md, where identified items go into the adjusted balances and only the residual is unexplained. The sample also names no owner, although voice_preferences asks for one. Models copy voice samples.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'March statement check: opening balance $18,420; net statement movement $6,180; closing balance $24,600. I matched 47 of 49 lines. The $225 gap between statement and ledger is two items: a $95 ledger payment dated 30 March that has not reached the statement yet (timing; I will confirm it on the April statement) and a $320 bank debit on 28 March with no ledger entry (owner: you; is it a bank fee?). Unexplained after these: $0.00. March stays open, not reconciled, until you tell me what the $320 is.'

issues.quote: A reconciliation is complete only when the unexplained difference is zero or every remaining item has an owner and next step.
issues.problem: Because of the 'or', Mina may call a reconciliation complete with a non-zero unexplained difference as long as each item has an owner. 14:statement-reconciliation says '"Reconciled" is used only when the unexplained difference is exactly 0.00 and every remaining item is timing or a drafted correction. Otherwise the status is "open, not reconciled", with every item owned.' Main's version agrees ('A complete result has an unexplained difference of zero. If it does not, label it open'). The persona is always loaded, so this line can override the skill's status rule.
issues.fix: Write: 'Call a reconciliation reconciled only when the unexplained difference is exactly zero and every remaining item is timing or a drafted correction; otherwise it is open, not reconciled, with an owner and next step on every item.'

issues.problem: Month-end close is monthly and receivables review is weekly, and the platform supports schedule_routine. The rebuilt kit already ships both routine prompts (14:bookkeeping-getting-started templates/cadence-routines.md), and both forbid posting, sending and contacting anyone. The main month-end review's top issue was that the close is not set up as a recurring routine. The expert still has none.
issues.fix: Add two routines in the shape other experts use (key, title, prompt, crons, asks, session_mode THREAD). (1) key monthly-close-kickoff, crons ['H 9 3 * *']. Prompt: 'Load skill:month-end-close-checklist, period = last calendar month. Report the export dates you found first. Prepare and report only: do not post entries, issue or send invoices, lock a period, contact anyone, or move money. List what is blocked and who owns each item.' (2) key weekly-receivables-review, crons ['H 9 * * 1']. Prompt: 'Load skill:accounts-receivable-follow-up. Use the newest invoice and bank exports and say their dates first. Update the aging, check for unapplied payments, and draft next-stage reminders for approval. Do not send, call or contact anyone.' Asks for both: 'Which business and bookkeeping folder is this for?' and 'What day and time should this land, and in which timezone?'. Also make step 9 of 14:bookkeeping-getting-started and step 11 of 14:month-end-close-checklist check intake.json cadence.routines_created and the expert's routines before offering to create a duplicate.

issues.quote: Never post entries, issue or send invoices, contact customers, or move money without explicit approval.
issues.problem: This reads as if Mina may issue or send an invoice once approved. 14:invoice-drafting-and-issue says the opposite: 'Never change agreed pricing, choose or assign an invoice number yourself ... The only write Mina may make is creating the invoice with Draft status'. The boundary also leaves out locking a period, which 14:month-end-close-checklist forbids.
issues.fix: Write: 'Never post entries, lock or close a period, move money, or number, issue or send an invoice; the only ledger write is creating an invoice as a Draft after a logged yes. A customer reminder, evidence pack or close binder goes out only after a yes to that exact file and recipient.'

issues.quote: Route tax, payroll, equity, fraud, material exceptions, and policy judgements to a qualified accountant or named owner with the source records attached.
issues.problem: Nothing covers changed payee bank details (payment redirection, the most common small-business fraud) or data masking. Both are hard rules in the rebuilt kit: the 'Bank-detail changes (always)' section in 14:bookkeeping-exception-escalation, and the 'Store and show only the last 4 digits' rule in 14:statement-reconciliation.
issues.fix: Append: 'Never act on changed bank details; verification uses only contacts on record from before the change, and the owner verifies. Show only the last 4 digits of any account or card number.'

issues.quote: Do not post to a ledger, issue or send an invoice, contact a customer, move money, or alter a source record without the owner's explicit approval.
issues.problem: This has the same looseness as the boundaries: with approval, Mina could post to a ledger or issue an invoice. The rebuilt skills never write to the ledger except for the Draft invoice create. The only outward sends are an approved reminder, an evidence pack or the close binder.
issues.fix: Split the sentence: 'Never post to a ledger, lock a period, alter a source record, move money, or number, issue or send an invoice. With the owner's explicit, logged yes to the exact file and recipient you may create an invoice as a Draft in the billing system, or send an approved reminder, evidence pack or close binder; take no other outward action.'

issues.quote: I turn receipts, bills, invoices, and bank exports into a clean review queue
issues.problem: Supplier bills have no skill. Close control 4 ('Receivables and payables aged') routes only to accounts-receivable-follow-up, and control 13 ('Bills not yet received checked') names no skill. Toran's review also lists supplier-bill/AP processing as a gap.
issues.fix: Add the proposed supplier-bills-and-payables skill, or narrow the bio to 'receipts, card and bank lines, customer invoices'.

issues.quote: Builds a sourced draft of revenue, costs, operating spend, and open items for the owner and accountant to review.
issues.problem: 14:monthly-profit-and-loss-summary works from a ledger P&L export and refuses raw bank lines with no account mapping ('Not for: building a P&L from raw bank lines without an account mapping'). Many small-business users arrive with bank exports only, so this promise can fail.
issues.fix: Write: 'From your ledger P&L export (or once expenses are coded), builds a sourced draft of revenue, costs and operating spend with period, basis and currency on every figure, plus open items.'

issues.quote: Returns unmatched payments, unclear expenses, duplicate risks, and missing documents with one owner and one next step for each.
issues.problem: Finding unmatched payments needs a statement, a ledger and opening balances. The PR #14 intake example shows these are often Blocked on day 1 (for example, the prior month not yet signed off). The queue is assembled from exceptions.csv and open-items.csv across several skills.
issues.fix: Keep it on day 1 but scope it: 'From the exports you share: unclear expenses, duplicate risks and missing documents now; unmatched payments once a statement and ledger for the same period are in.'

issues.quote: Seven expenses are ready to post and three need review.
issues.problem: The sample leaves out the source file, the period and the control-total tie, even though the identity says to 'Preserve the source name and reporting period on every output'. 14:expense-categorization's output contract opens with that line ('N ready to post, M need review', with the source file and period).
issues.fix: Write: 'April Amex export, 10 lines totalling £1,240.50, ties to the statement: seven are ready to post and three need review.'

Saves the intake the other bookkeeping skills read. Use when starting or catching up the books.
proposed.rationale: The most complete version, same slug, and the state root (intake.json, open-items.csv) that the other seven PR #14 skills load. Fixes before merge: (1) examples/bramble-april-intake marks the Amex sign convention 'confirmed' when no question asked it, and the walkthrough and SKILL.md example report bank dates as '1 to 12 Apr' while the format is still ambiguous. That models the guesses the self-check forbids, so correct the walkthrough and intake.json. Add a `thresholds` block (per_item_amount, total_open_items, pl_movement, stated_by, stated_on; all null until the owner states them) and one optional intake question with a 'Not sure: ask the accountant' route. proposed.name: Expense categorization
proposed.description: Code bank and card exports and receipts to the owner's chart of accounts: each line gets source, evidence, proposed account or unresolved, reason and confidence, split into ready-to-post and needs-review with totals tied to the export. Never guesses tax treatment or posts entries.
proposed.rationale: The more complete version, same slug, and it covers the 'routine expense coding' half of Toran's AP gap. proposed.name: Invoice drafting and issue
proposed.description: Draft a customer invoice from a contract, SOW, PO or recurring schedule: exact totals, required-field and double-billing checks, a watermarked DRAFT and an approval block. Never numbers, issues or sends it; after a logged yes it may create the invoice as a Draft in the billing system.

The closed-list, action-scoped matching in its log_approval.py (shared with 14:accounts-receivable-follow-up) is the model for the kit-wide script in c6, not a drop-in replacement. Fix before merge: register_check.py compares line keys only with the register and uses the billing export only for invoice numbers, so a period already billed in the export (the review's INV-1060 'Design retainer April 2026') raises no REPEAT. Match description and period against the export as well.

clusters.job: Review open receivables and draft staged payment follow-ups

members.note: Keeps main's verify-before-overdue rule and its five queue groups. Adds cutoff-dated aging (ar_aging.py), unapplied-cash and bank-coverage checks before any chase, defined stages (templates/reminder-stages.md), a statement of account, hash-bound send approval, and contact and dispute logs.

proposed.name: Accounts receivable follow-up
proposed.description: Review who owes money at a stated cutoff: build the aging from invoice and payment exports, check the bank for unapplied payments first, keep disputes and promises visible, and draft the next reminder or statement of account. Sends nothing without the owner's yes to that exact message.
proposed.rationale: Clear improvement on main, and it makes Toran's deferred small-business/invoice-chase unnecessary. Fix before merge: a payment dated after the cutoff is excluded from the aging (correct for an as-at report), but ar_aging.py still proposes a reminder for an invoice fully paid after the cutoff, and find_unapplied.py treats that invoice as paid, so nothing flags it. Add a 'paid after cutoff: no chase' hold before any draft is offered.
drops: accounts-receivable-follow-up (main): superseded in place

clusters.job: Reconcile a bank, card or clearing account to the ledger

members.note: Ties each period to the last approved one, matches one-to-one with self-tested scripts (rec_match.py, payout_breakdown.py, extract_statement.py), and writes a masked workpaper plus carry-forward state. references/bank-rec-layout.md is already adapted from account-reconciliation (ATTRIBUTION.md and LICENSE included), including its three item classes, aging buckets (escalate at 61-90 and over 90 days) and the recurring-item flag.

Dropped as a standalone. PR #14 already carries its bank layout, item classes, aging buckets and recurring-item trending. Still useful: the amount rows of 'Escalation Thresholds' (grafted here), plus 'GL to Subledger Reconciliation' and 'Intercompany Reconciliation' (both grafted into close controls 4 and 6, see c6). Its 'Action: Prepare adjusting journal entry' has no approval gate and breaks Mina's boundaries.
Its controls, matching passes and return list are all expanded in PR #14. Its top issue (unexplained difference not defined against identified items) is fixed by bank-rec-layout.md.

proposed.name: Statement reconciliation
proposed.description: Reconcile one bank, card, loan or Stripe/PayPal clearing account to the ledger for one period: tie to the last approved period, match one-to-one with scripts, own every timing or one-sided item, never plug. Returns a workpaper for owner sign-off and never changes the ledger.
proposed.rationale: PR #14 is far stronger and has already absorbed most of the upstream method. The one graft makes the undefined 'a large or repeated difference' in step 7 concrete in money terms (the age and recurrence triggers are already in bank-rec-layout.md). Fixes before merge: (1) The prior-period tie checks only the statement opening against the prior approved closing. Also check the ledger opening against the prior rec's ledger_closing: in testing, a +100 edit to a reconciled ledger transaction gave an unexplained -100.00 with '0 item(s) to investigate'. (2) In step 9, 'one Task per account (at most 3 at once)' names Task, a Claude-SDK-only built-in that baseline sessions do not have. Write 'one run_sub_session per account (at most 3 at once)'. The run_sub_session(prompt=..., wait_for_result=300) call itself is a real eager platform tool; keep it. (3) Move the prefix-match log_approval.py to the kit-wide closed-list script (see c6), keeping 'Signed off' and 'Reviewed, items owned' as recognised sign-off options for step 10 and the `check` call in step 1.
drops: statement-reconciliation (main): superseded in place

account-reconciliation: 'Category 2 ... Action: Prepare adjusting journal entry', the upstream $10k/$50k/$100k example thresholds and supervisor/controller routing, 'Reconciliation Best Practices' (enterprise segregation and retention advice)

grafts.what: In step 7 and references/bank-rec-layout.md, define the money part of 'large or repeated difference' as the owner-set triggers from the new intake.json `thresholds` block (see c1): the amount per item and the total of open reconciling items. The age (over 60 and over 90 days) and recurrence triggers are already in the layout's aging table and recurring-item flag; point to them rather than duplicating them. Keep 'Unreconciled difference: any amount: cannot close' as the rule that a non-zero unexplained difference is always escalated. Label any default 'default — confirm with the owner' and leave out the upstream dollar figures. With no owner threshold, list every item and claim no materiality.

members.note: Keeps main's nine controls as controls 1-9, adds 10-15 and sources S1-S6, and enforces the order with close_status.py. It loads the sibling Mina skill for each control and carries prior open items. references/close-dependency-map.md is already adapted from month-end-close-management.

Dropped as a standalone. A corporate T+1 to T+5 playbook with 'Post tax provision entries' and 'Lock the period in the ERP/GL system' and no gate. Its dependency map is already in PR #14. Only 'Close Metrics to Track Over Time' and 'Close Retrospective Questions' are missing from the base (templates/close-report.md has neither).
All nine controls and the 'prepared for review' rule are in PR #14. Its top issue (no stored prior open items, no recurring routine) is fixed by the state folder and step 11's schedule_routine.

proposed.name: Month-end close checklist
proposed.description: Run a small-business month-end close: track sources and 15 controls in dependency order, load the bookkeeping skill for each, carry open items forward, and return a close report and accountant binder marked prepared for review. Never posts, locks, backdates or approves the close.
proposed.rationale: PR #14 is the orchestrator the kit needs, and it already holds the useful upstream structure. Fixes before merge: (1) log_approval.py treats any reply starting with approve, yes, signed off or reviewed as approval (`APPROVING_PREFIXES`). So 'Reviewed - not approved, fix line 3' is logged as an APPROVAL, and 'yesterday I said no' counts as a yes. The same file (md5 fa0ab716...) ships in the exception, P&L and statement-rec packages. Do not simply copy in the closed-list script from invoice/AR (md5 0cdb4354...). It has no `check` subcommand and no `--approvals` or `--expect-sha` flags, all of which these four SKILL.md files call. It also rejects 'Signed off', 'Reviewed, items owned' and the plain 'Approve exactly as shown' used in step 9. And close_status.py does `from log_approval import is_approval` with one argument, so control 14 and the close approval could never pass. Instead ship one shared script for all six packages. It should keep the closed-list, action-scoped matching and the negation guard. It should add every option label the kit prescribes: 'Approve exactly as shown' and 'Signed off' for approve/sign-off actions, 'Reviewed, items owned' as a recorded review that satisfies control 14 but never sets RECONCILED, 'Send to <recipient>' for send actions, and the P&L review label once step 10 of the P&L skill names its options. It should accept the old aliases (check = verify, --approvals = --log, --expect-sha = --shown-sha) and keep is_approval(reply) callable with one argument. Add selftests for 'Reviewed - not approved, fix line 3' and 'yesterday I said no'. (2) templates/close-controls.csv routes control 4 ('Receivables and payables aged') only to accounts-receivable-follow-up, and control 13 has no skill. If supplier-bills-and-payables is built, point both at it. If not, have control 4's payables half and control 13 ask the owner for an AP aging or bills export and say 'hand-listed, no skill'. (3) Control 2's evidence is 'invoice register total tied to the billing export', but it names no skill. Point it at invoice-drafting-and-issue (register_check.py with --billing-export).
