recommendations.notes:
What I read: the brief, the dossier, experts/mina.yml, all eight PR #14 SKILL.md files, and the key templates and references: close-controls.csv, controls-guide.md, cadence-routines.md, special-lines.md, account-types.md, accountant-handoff-pack.md and jurisdiction-flags.md. I also read PR #14's docs/research/bookkeeping.md. Its job table, built from 14 postings, is the main evidence base below.

What the merged kit covers: intake, expense coding, invoice drafting, receivables, and reconciliation of bank, card, loan, petty cash and processor accounts, plus other balance-sheet accounts that have a third-party statement. It also covers close orchestration, the P&L and exceptions. If adopted, supplier-bills-and-payables covers payables (J2, 11/14 postings), so nothing here duplicates it.

What remains uncovered, as the research's own gap list names it (section 7.9):
- Payroll recording. Close control 5 has no skill.
- Journal entries and ledger import files. Close control 9 has no skill.
- Balance-sheet schedules. The P&L skill explicitly excludes the balance sheet.
- VAT and sales-tax preparation.
- The year-end CPA package and the 1099 payee list.
- Clean-up and catch-up.

Each recommendation stays within Mina's boundaries: preparation, ties and drafts only, policy supplied by the accountant, and the kit-wide closed-list log_approval.py for every approval.

Persona edits the reviewer will need if payroll-journal-and-tie-out and vat-and-sales-tax-return-workpaper ship:
- The identity currently routes all 'payroll' and 'tax-sensitive' matters away. Add one line allowing payroll and tax record tie-out ('recording and review only; runs, calculations, treatment and filing stay with the provider or accountant').
- The balance-sheet schedules skill needs the same carve-out for depreciation: 'roll forward the accountant's schedule; never choose the method'.
- Routines and the reconciliation-completion wording are persona fixes, not skill gaps. The review summary already covers them.

Sources checked and rejected:
- Deferred packages: only small-business invoice-chase is relevant, and accounts-receivable-follow-up already covers it.
- Upstream anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins small-business has payroll-prep, tax-season-organizer, pay-the-bills, ap-processor and close-month. That plugin has no LICENSE of its own and relies on the root licence, which carries the same ambiguous appended text that deferred invoice-chase. payroll-prep also stages pay runs, which is a different job from recording. tax-season-organizer computes estimated tax and uses the stale $600 1099 threshold (post-OBBBA it is $2,000 for payments after 31 Dec 2025). I used these only as evidence of demand, not as sources.
- finance/journal-entry-prep and journal-entry (Apache-2.0, pinned commit 1c7187c, same finance/LICENSE as account-reconciliation) are usable only as a partial base.
- Receiptor-AI/bookkeeping-skills (MIT) contractor-1099 hard-codes thresholds and penalty amounts, decides filing requirements and names vendor tools. It is at most a cross-check.
- openaccountant/skills (MIT) is mostly personal finance. Its sales-tax-nexus and depreciation-schedule skills 'determine' requirements, which conflicts with Mina's boundaries. I checked that repo only at listing level.
- Catalog: no catalog skill fills these gaps. Daniel's close-controls-and-accounting is a one-page FP&A close note with no scripts. financial-statement-preparation is corporate GAAP and was dropped in the merge. automate-finance-reporting is an FP&A sheet loader, not journal entries.

Smaller gaps better handled as extensions of kit skills than as new skills:
1. Employee out-of-pocket expense claims. Close control 3 names 'employee claims', but expense-categorization treats a receipt with no card or bank line as an exception, which misfiles every legitimate claim until it is reimbursed. It needs a claims mode that pairs each receipt with its later reimbursement line and applies the owner's supplied mileage rate.
2. Credit notes. invoice-drafting-and-issue sends them all to the accountant, but preparing an owner-agreed credit note from a logged refund decision is routine bookkeeping.

Left to teammates: cash forecasting and runway stay with Daniel's cash-treasury-and-fx (consult or hand off; do not bundle). Nothing in the catalog covers inventory or COGS bookkeeping for product businesses. Revisit it if the persona targets retail or e-commerce.

recommendations.name: Payroll journal and tie-out
recommendations.purpose: Ties each payroll run in the provider's register (Gusto, ADP, QuickBooks or Xero Payroll, UK payroll reports) to the bank lines and the ledger's payroll liabilities, and drafts the payroll journal for approval. Recording only: it never runs payroll or computes pay or tax.
recommendations.why: PR #14 research J9: 'payroll processing or recording' appears in 6 of 14 postings, and the research marks 'recording journal not covered'. Close control 5 ('net pay and tax deposits on the bank tie to the approved payroll register. Recording only') is the only level-2 control besides 2 and 13 with no skill_to_load in close-controls.csv. expense-categorization refuses to code payroll bank lines without the register (special-lines.md), and statement-reconciliation lists payroll liabilities as a balance-sheet account with no register-side method. So payroll never gets tied. BLS lists 'handling payroll' among full-charge bookkeeper duties (https://www.bls.gov/ooh/office-and-administrative-support/bookkeeping-accounting-and-auditing-clerks.htm). Gusto's own guidance is to reconcile from the payroll journal and map it to the GL (https://support.gusto.com/article/221020155120720/Download-mapped-payroll-ledgers-with-the-General-Ledger-Mapper). The kit's payroll-tax-first rule and its payroll-tax-shortfall exception class exist, but no skill surfaces a missed deposit from the register side.

source.ref: New skill built on PR #14's shared bkio.py, normalize_export.py, redact.py and the kit-wide closed-list log_approval.py. Upstream small-business/payroll-prep was rejected: it stages pay runs, and the small-business licence is ambiguous.

sketch: Inputs and minimisation: the provider's payroll register or journal export per run (gross, employee withholdings, deductions, employer taxes, net pay), its tax-liability and payment report, the bank export, and the ledger's payroll accounts. Mask names and IDs with redact.py, and work from totals unless the tie needs per-employee rows. Never store salaries in memory.

payroll_tie.py (with --selftest): (1) checks that gross minus withholdings minus deductions equals net pay within each run; (2) ties the net pay total to bank debits, whether one line or one per employee, allowing for provider impound timing; (3) ties each tax and benefit remittance to its bank line; (4) rolls each liability forward (opening + accrued - remitted = closing) against the ledger balance; (5) flags runs missing against the pay calendar, off-cycle runs and duplicate runs.

Draft payroll journal: an owner-confirmed payroll-mapping.csv (register column to exact chart account, like Gusto's GL mapper) produces one balanced entry per run in the journal-entry-drafting format. Wages earned but unpaid at period end are listed only as an accrual candidate for the accountant.

Exceptions: a liability that is not falling, or a deposit missing against the provider's schedule, is raised at once as payroll-tax-shortfall through bookkeeping-exception-escalation, and the skill never suggests paying other creditors first. A person paid both through payroll and as a contractor goes to the worker-classification class.

Output: a tie-out workpaper per period (runs, tie status, owned differences), the evidence line for close control 5 (so close-controls.csv gains skill_to_load), and the draft journal link, approved through log_approval.py against the file hash.

Guardrails: never compute gross pay, withholding, employer tax or statutory amounts; never run, approve or edit payroll in the provider; never post; route every payroll question to the accountant or the payroll provider.

recommendations.name: Journal entry drafting and ledger import
recommendations.purpose: Turns any proposed adjustment (reconciliation correction, reclass, payroll journal, schedule release, accountant's instruction) into a balanced, sourced draft journal with preparer, approver and reversal date, plus a ledger import file that only the owner or accountant posts.
recommendations.why: Close control 9 ('every proposed adjustment has a source, reason, preparer and approver') has no skill. statement-reconciliation carries 'correction' items forward as 'draft for accountant review' with no entry format, and the escalation hand-off pack lists 'proposed adjustments' the same way, so every skill describes entries differently. PR #14 research: J10 'journal entries, accruals, prepaids, fixed-asset schedules' is in 4 of 14 postings and marked 'proposals only'. Section 7.9 names 'ledger import-file preparation (e.g. QBO CSV)' as a gap. BLS: bookkeepers 'record all transactions and post debits and credits'. Platform fit is good: Xero imports manual journals from CSV as Draft for review before posting (https://central.xero.com/0/article/Add-import-and-post-manual-journals-AU), which matches Mina's draft-then-approve model. QuickBooks Online journal imports need 'Parent: Sub' account names and post on import (https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/import-export-data-files/import-journal-entries-quickbooks-online/L4tQBwbs7_US_en_US), so for QBO the file goes to the owner instead.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins finance/skills/journal-entry-prep at pinned commit 1c7187c4 (same finance/LICENSE as the installed account-reconciliation). Partial base only: reuse its documentation requirements, reviewer checklist and common-errors list with attribution. Drop the ASC 606 guidance, the depreciation and accrual calculations, and the $250K approval tiers, which conflict with Mina's boundaries and small-business scale. Add the scripts new.

sketch: je.json schema: date, period, narration, and lines with the exact chart account, debit or credit, dimension and a tax code only as supplied. Each entry also records the source per line, reason, preparer, named approver, optional auto-reverse date, and the originating skill, exception id or reconciliation item.

je_check.py (--selftest) runs in exact decimal. It checks that debits equal credits, every account exists in the chart, and no dimension falls outside the supplied lists. It refuses a date on or before the recorded lock date (and proposes a current-period correction instead), refuses a suspense, plug or balancing line, and checks a je-register.csv so one reconciliation item is never drafted twice.

render_import.py writes a Xero manual-journal CSV (imports as Draft), a QBO journal-import CSV ('Parent: Sub' names, account numbers off) and a generic CSV. It always delivers the file with write_workspace_file. It creates a Draft journal through a connected ledger tool only after a logged yes naming 'create draft journal <id> in <system>', and only where describe_capability shows a Draft status.

Approval: hash the file and record the owner's option with the kit-wide log_approval.py. Any edit re-renders and asks again. The register row moves draft → approved_to_import → posted_per_owner (posted only when the owner or accountant reports it).
Recurring entries (prepaid release, depreciation from the accountant's schedule, payroll) cite their schedule row. The skill never computes a policy amount itself.
Guardrails: never post, backdate into a locked period, unreconcile, or choose treatment. Every entry is 'draft for accountant review' until a posted record proves otherwise.

recommendations.name: Balance-sheet review and schedules
recommendations.purpose: At period end, maps every balance-sheet account to its support (reconciliation workpaper, aging, lender statement or roll-forward schedule). It keeps the prepaid, accrued-expense, deferred-revenue and fixed-asset schedules current using the accountant's policy, and proposes the period's entries as drafts.
recommendations.why: PR #14 research J5: financial statements and reports appear in 10 of 14 postings, and 'postings also expect balance sheet and cash views', but monthly-profit-and-loss-summary says 'Not for: ... balance sheet or cash-flow statements'. Section 7.9 lists 'balance-sheet view and balance-sheet account schedules (prepaids, accruals, fixed-asset register, loan amortisation)' as a gap. Close control 7 only sends 'accrual and prepayment candidates' to the accountant, and controls-guide.md notes that 'a cash-basis bank export cannot produce an accrual P&L alone'. So no skill keeps the schedules that make an accrual P&L right month to month. Full-charge postings expect journal entries 'for accounts such as fixed assets and depreciation' and a monthly balance sheet sent to the CPA. The kit already produces most balance-sheet evidence (reconciliations, AR and AP aging, Undeposited Funds and Opening Balance Equity checks) but nothing assembles it into one support map.

source.ref: New skill. financial-statement-preparation (dropped in the merge) is corporate GAAP and ASC-oriented. At most its balance-sheet layout can inform the template.

sketch: Support map from a trial-balance export: each balance-sheet account gets a support type (rec workpaper, AR aging, AP aging, lender or third-party statement, schedule, none), the supported balance and the difference. Unsupported or differing balances become owned open items. This is the evidence for close controls 8 and 11.

Schedules (CSV/XLSX), each from a source document: prepaids (invoice, coverage period, monthly release); accrued expenses (from supplier-bills-and-payables' bills-not-yet-received list or an owner-supplied expected-bills list, reversing next period); deferred revenue (invoice-register service periods, accrual basis only); fixed-asset register (additions from itemised invoices flagged 'possible fixed asset' by expense-categorization, disposals).

Policy inputs are the accountant's alone: capitalisation threshold, useful life, depreciation method, amortisation period and revenue policy, each recorded in intake.json with who supplied it and when. Without one, the item is listed, not scheduled.

schedule_rollforward.py (--selftest): checks opening + additions - releases = closing for each schedule against the ledger balance, and flags fully released items that still hold a balance, stale accruals not reversed, and items below the owner's threshold (listed, not proposed, matching close step 6).
Proposed period entries go to journal-entry-drafting. Output: the support table, the schedules and the owned differences, fed into close controls 7-8 and into the P&L brief's basis caveats.

Guardrails: never choose capitalisation, life, method or revenue recognition; never compute depreciation beyond applying the accountant's stated schedule; for cash-basis entities, build schedules only when the accountant asks for them.

recommendations.name: VAT and sales-tax return workpaper
recommendations.purpose: For a VAT or sales-tax return period, ties the ledger's tax report to the tax control account, the invoice register and the purchase records. It lists purchase tax without a valid tax invoice and lines whose treatment needs the accountant, and hands over a review pack. It never chooses treatment, computes what is owed, or submits.
recommendations.why: PR #14 research J12: sales tax and 1099/W-9 support appear in 3-4 of 14 postings and are marked 'routed; no preparation skill', and section 7.9 lists a 'sales tax/VAT summary by jurisdiction for the adviser (preparation only)'. The kit already records VAT registration and MTD status (jurisdiction-flags.md), checks VAT invoice fields, and keeps tax as a liability. jurisdiction-flags.md also tells Mina to 'record per-state sales totals' for US nexus, but no skill produces them or reviews a return. Preparing and verifying VAT returns is core UK bookkeeping (AAT Level 3 unit 'Tax Processes for Businesses'; HMRC VAT Notice 700/12). Every VAT-registered business has kept digital records under Making Tax Digital for VAT since April 2022, with digital links between software (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/vat-notice-70022-making-tax-digital-for-vat). So the right shape is a review workpaper of the software's return, never figures re-keyed by hand. No skill in the catalog covers tax preparation.

source.ref: New skill built on PR #14's shared bkio.py, normalize_export.py and log_approval.py. Nothing in the catalog or the deferred list covers this.

sketch: Inputs: the ledger's VAT return or sales-tax liability report for the period (box or jurisdiction totals, from the MTD software or an export); the tax control account detail; the invoice register; bills and the expense review; the prior return and its payment. The scheme (standard, cash accounting, flat rate) comes from intake as the accountant recorded it.

tax_tie.py (--selftest): (1) checks that output tax in the report equals the tax fields in the invoice register for the period (or cash received under cash accounting); (2) checks that input tax equals tax on bills and receipts that carry a valid tax invoice; (3) rolls the control account forward (opening + output - input - payments = closing); (4) carries prior-period errors as items.

Exception lists for the accountant: input VAT with no VAT invoice or no supplier VAT number; reverse charge, imports and postponed VAT, zero-rated, exempt and out-of-scope lines; partial exemption; flat-rate items. For the US, sales totals by state per period, with thresholds quoted only from a freshly fetched official page with its date.

Output: a workpaper that shows each report figure next to its tie, the differences with owners, and the accountant's questions. It offers a deadline follow-up through schedule_followup only on a yes, and approvals go through log_approval.py.

Guardrails: never choose a rate or treatment, compute an amount owed outside the ledger's own report, submit to HMRC or a state, or give figures to re-key into a return (that breaks MTD digital links). Route every treatment question through bookkeeping-exception-escalation.

recommendations.name: Year-end accountant package
recommendations.purpose: At the entity's fiscal year end, assembles the accountant's year-end pack: final close status, trial balance, every balance-sheet support schedule, fixed-asset additions with invoices, year-end loan and owner statements, inventory count if held, open exceptions and, in the US, contractor payee totals by payment method with W-9 gaps.
recommendations.why: PR #14 research: the CPA hand-off (J11) is in 4 of 14 postings and 1099/W-9 support (J12) in 3-4, and section 7.9 lists 'year-end 1099/W-9 payee list and CPA year-end package' as a gap. The escalation skill's accountant-handoff-pack.md has a 'Payee totals and W-9 / TIN gaps (US; list only)' table, but no script aggregates payees across bank, card, processor and bills exports or splits them by payment method. The research notes that card and third-party-network payments reported on 1099-K are excluded from 1099-NEC. Nothing handles the annual checklist either. Thresholds move: 1099-NEC/MISC went from $600 to $2,000 for payments after 31 Dec 2025, and both upstream candidates (small-business tax-season-organizer, Receiptor-AI contractor-1099) still hard-code figures. A script that takes the threshold as a sourced argument is safer. BLS and full-charge postings describe statements prepared after close and 'submitted to a CPA'.

source.ref: New skill built on the close skill's build_binder.py pattern and the shared bkio.py. Receiptor-AI/bookkeeping-skills contractor-1099 (MIT, https://github.com/Receiptor-AI/bookkeeping-skills/blob/main/skills/contractor-1099/SKILL.md) was considered as a checklist cross-check only: it hard-codes thresholds and penalty amounts, decides filing requirements and names vendor tools.

sketch: Trigger and prerequisites: the fiscal year end comes from intake.json (never assume a calendar year). It runs only after the final month's close is 'prepared for review'. Anything still blocked in that close is carried into the pack as an open item.

payee_totals.py (--selftest): aggregates the year's payments by payee from the normalised bank, card, processor and bills exports; splits them by payment method (card or third-party network vs bank transfer or cheque); joins W-9/TIN status from vendor records; and takes --threshold with --threshold-source and a tax year, without which it lists everyone and flags no one.

Year-end checklist: year-end trial balance; reconciliations for every account at the final month; balance-sheet schedules; fixed-asset additions and disposals with invoices; lender and owner-account statements; owner draws and contributions; inventory count if the business holds stock; payroll year-end forms received from the provider (never prepared); open exceptions with ids.
Build the masked zip on the build_binder.py pattern, cut to the year. Deliver it with write_workspace_file, and send it only after a logged yes naming the accountant in intake.

Guardrails: never decide who gets a 1099, compute backup withholding, file forms, or prepare a tax computation (UK: no Corporation Tax or self-assessment figures). Quote retention and filing rules only from a freshly fetched official page.

recommendations.name: Books clean-up and catch-up
recommendations.purpose: Plans and tracks a clean-up or catch-up across several past periods. It finds where the ledger first went wrong (unreconciled months, uncategorised or suspense balances, Undeposited Funds, Opening Balance Equity, duplicate feed items), then works the periods oldest first through the existing kit skills, with a per-period status board.
recommendations.why: PR #14 research J13: clean-up and catch-up of historical books appear in 2 of 14 postings and are marked 'none (gap)'; section 7.9 says 'books cleanup and catch-up, oldest period first... consider a new skill'. bookkeeping-getting-started profiles catch-up exports and says to work oldest first, one period at a time, but keeps no multi-period plan or status. statement-reconciliation's ledger-diagnostics finds where a gap first appears for one account only. Close controls 11 and 12 test Undeposited Funds and OBE for one period, not the history behind them. Catch-up is a common trigger in the getting-started skill ('catch up my books'), so today a user who asks for it gets an intake and no plan.

source.ref: New orchestrator skill. It adds a diagnostic script and a status board and reuses the kit skills per period.

sketch: Diagnostic (cleanup_scan.py, --selftest): from monthly trial-balance or GL exports, finds the first month each balance-sheet account stops tying to its statement. It counts and totals the uncategorised or 'Ask My Accountant', suspense, Undeposited Funds and OBE balances by month, and lists probable duplicate feed items and missing statements.

Plan: catchup-status.csv with one row per period and control, dependencies (a period's rec needs the prior period's approved closing), an owner, and missing-document requests batched through bookkeeping-exception-escalation's request mode.

Execution: one period at a time, loading statement-reconciliation, expense-categorization and month-end-close-checklist in turn. Nothing is merged across periods or entities. The owner's approval of each period closes it on the board.

Corrections: errors found in reconciled or locked periods become current-period draft entries for the accountant (journal-entry-drafting), never edits to history. Prior-period adjustments are the accountant's call.
Guardrails: never unreconcile, delete, exclude or merge ledger records; never plug an opening balance to make a period tie. Give the owner an effort and scope summary before starting.

proposal.summary: Nadia's live kit is two ORIGINAL placeholders of about 50 lines each: competitor-teardown and icp-and-positioning. Their method matches her identity almost word for word. NICK added nothing for her. TORAN proposed three Corey Haines packages: customer-insight-research, competitor-profiling and product-marketing-context. PR #13 only renames skill references in them, plus product-marketing-context's slash command, so their `.agents/` paths, the repo-first draft and the DataForSEO dependence are all still there. The merge calls are these. Keep competitor-teardown as the base and graft in competitor-profiling's input questions, untrusted-input rule, page and review extraction checklists, a public-evidence claim check, quick/deep and multi-competitor landscape modes, and change log. Drop its DataForSEO phase, because only the keyword_suggestions and related_keywords blocks exist. Keep icp-and-positioning as the base and graft in product-marketing-context's existing-context check, buying roles, three-tier alternatives, anti-persona, four forces, customer language and versioned save. customer-insight-research stays as its own skill, with PII/consent, approval and trigger fixes, because it supplies the evidence-gathering method that icp-and-positioning lacks. Two new skills are proposed. The first is nadia-getting-started, because day_one is empty and nothing captures "us", the watch list or the timezone. The second is competitor-watch-brief, to back her Friday routine. That routine has no skill behind it and repeats the weekly watch routines of Zara (Thursday), Maya (Friday) and Alex (Wednesday), so Nadia should own the canonical version. The unassigned catalog skills obviously-awesome (positioning) and mom-test (interviews) overlap icp-and-positioning and customer-insight-research. Neither should be bundled; at most, lift obviously-awesome's market-category step.

body_review.summary: Sharp, coherent persona: the identity is essentially the competitor-teardown and icp-and-positioning method, and observed/inferred discipline runs through bio, voice and boundaries. The weaknesses are four. day_one is empty. The only routine has no backing skill, repeats Zara's and Maya's watch routines nearly word for word (and Alex's in structure), and does not fetch the changelog and job ads her identity relies on. The one-line boundary covers claim hygiene but not approvals, collection ethics, customer PII or handoffs. The identity does not mention the buyer-research job the kit would add.
strengths: The identity mirrors competitor-teardown/SKILL.md nearly line for line: the same source order (homepage and pricing, then changelog and job ads, then reviews, then unprompted customers), the same five questions and the same 'honest praise' rule. Persona and skill reinforce each other.
The observed/inferred rule is consistent across bio, voice_preferences, voice_samples[0] and boundaries, and it gives the expert a recognisable signature.
voice_samples[0] models the whole job in three sentences: an observed price move, an inference that names its source (three enterprise sales postings), and a decision.
The routine prompt has strong anti-padding rules: log failed fetches, no change without a link, a quiet week is one line, never brief the same change twice.
The identity's positioning paragraph (situation not industry, trigger, pain vs signer, do-nothing cost in their units) is concrete and matches icp-and-positioning.
body_review.kit_alignment: The body promises three things. The first two, single-competitor teardowns and ICP/positioning pushback, are covered by the two ORIGINAL skills. The third is a Friday tiered competitor brief (routines[0]), and no skill covers its watch list, tier cadence or briefed-change dedupe log. A Monday newsletter digest also depends on the personalized-morning-coffee-newsletter preload, which is shared with Frankie. Nothing captures 'us', the competitor list with tiers, the brief destination or the timezone up front: day_one is [] and there is no getting-started skill, yet teardown questions 4 and 5 and the routine's asks depend on them. The proposed kit closes those gaps with nadia-getting-started and competitor-watch-brief. No routine, preload or day_one entry names a skill that would be dropped or renamed, because both original slugs are kept as merge bases. Adding customer-insight-research widens the job beyond what the identity describes, so the identity needs one line on buyer research. The youtube-transcription-scraper preload is not used by any skill or routine.

issues.problem: The bio promises 'From day one I can take a competitor apart' and 'I'll push on who your product is really for', but day_one is empty and no getting-started skill exists. The inputs the teardown's questions 4 and 5 need (our product, our ICP), the routine's asks (watch list with tiers, day, hour, timezone) and the Monday digest inbox are never collected before work starts.
issues.fix: Add nadia-getting-started and three day_one entries (the RELEASE.md maximum): 'One competitor, taken apart' (competitor-teardown quick scan, day 1), 'Who you are really for' (icp-and-positioning, day 1), and 'What buyers say unprompted' (customer-insight-research, on request). Getting-started should also set up the newsletter preload's market and inbox.

issues.quote: Work the tiered watch list: Tier 1 direct competitors get a deep read, Tier 2 adjacent a skim, Tier 3 aspirational a monthly look.
issues.problem: No skill in the kit covers a tiered watch list, a per-tier cadence, a source ledger, or the briefed-change log that 'Never brief the same change twice' needs. competitor-teardown is a one-off deep read. The prompt nearly repeats zara.yml competitor-brief (line 87, cron H 8 * * 4, Thursday) and maya.yml marketing-competitor-watch (line 81, cron H 8 * * 5, Friday), and follows alex.yml competitor-watch in structure (line 69, cron H 9 * * 3, Wednesday). A team that hires Nadia with any of them gets two or more overlapping weekly competitor briefs, and with Maya two on the same Friday morning.
issues.fix: Back the routine with a new competitor-watch-brief skill that reads the tiered list from memory, writes each briefed change to memory_store for dedupe, and keeps the source ledger. Make Nadia's the canonical watch, and have the other experts' routines consult her when she is on the team.

issues.quote: Never state unpublished competitor figures as fact, never repeat rumours, and always mark claims as observed or inferred.
issues.problem: This covers claim hygiene only. It says nothing about: approval before outward actions (customer-insight-research drafts interview outreach with $50 incentives; comparisons could be published); collection ethics (posing as a prospect, signing up under false pretences, logging in to gated competitor content); the legal line on public comparisons, which lives only in the teardown body; customer PII in transcripts and tickets; and handoff edges (battlecards and market sizing to Zara, copy to Maya, roadmap to Alex/Priya).
issues.fix: Append: 'Never contact a customer, competitor or prospect, or publish a comparison, without the owner's yes on that draft; never sign up, log in or pose as a buyer to reach a competitor's gated material, and use gated material only when the owner pastes it and says it may be used; redact customer names and contact details before quoting; battlecards and market sizing go to Zara, copy to Maya, roadmap calls to product.'

issues.quote: Fetch each one's public pages, blog, and pricing, and log every URL you fetched — including the ones that failed.
issues.problem: The fetch list leaves out the changelog and job ads, which the identity names as the source for 'where they are actually spending'. voice_samples[0] even infers from 'three enterprise sales postings', and the routine would never fetch those. The cron is also weekly while Tier 3 is 'a monthly look', but nothing says which run a Tier 3 competitor is due (Maya's version says 'For each one due this run').
issues.fix: Change to: 'For each competitor due this run, fetch pricing, changelog, blog and careers or job pages, and log every URL you fetched, including the ones that failed.' Leave the per-tier due-date logic to competitor-watch-brief.

issues.quote: a launch gets a positioning read, a pricing move a packaging read, a content push a calendar read.
issues.problem: 'Calendar read' is Maya's marketing framing (maya.yml line 85: 'what it does to our calendar'); Nadia owns no content calendar. The routine also never asks for the observed/inferred labels that are the persona's signature, although the so-what lines are inferences.
issues.fix: Change to 'a content push a messaging read' and add: 'Mark each change Observed and each read Inferred, naming what it was inferred from.'

issues.quote: What day and hour should the brief land, and in which timezone?
issues.problem: No ask covers where the brief lands (chat, doc, Slack, email). Alex's equivalent routine asks 'where should I stage what I find?'.
issues.fix: Add an ask: 'Where should the brief land: this chat, a doc, Slack, or an email draft?'

issues.quote: For any competitor you answer five questions and nothing else
issues.problem: 'Nothing else' conflicts with the landscape mode grafted from competitor-profiling (a side-by-side table and a positioning map across 2+ competitors) and with the weekly change brief. The identity also never mentions researching buyers directly, which the kit adds through customer-insight-research.
issues.fix: Change to 'For any single-competitor teardown you answer five questions', and add one sentence: 'When positioning needs evidence, you go to the buyers' own words (reviews, calls, communities) before you write a line.'

issues.quote: They beat us on onboarding and it is not close. The gap is the first ten minutes, not the feature list.
issues.problem: The sample makes a claim with no observed/inferred marking and no source, which contradicts voice_preferences ('every claim marked observed or inferred').
issues.fix: Change to 'Observed, across their last quarter of reviews: they beat us on onboarding and it is not close. Inferred from the same reviews: the gap is the first ten minutes, not the feature list.'

issues.quote: youtube-transcription-scraper
issues.problem: No skill, routine or day_one entry uses this preload. The natural consumers are teardown source 4 (competitor webinars, customer podcasts) and customer-insight-research Mode 2. Note that its source guide ('## YouTube Comments') mines comments, not transcripts, so the preload adds something new there.
issues.fix: Name it in competitor-teardown source 4 and in customer-insight-research Mode 2 as the way to pull webinar, demo and podcast transcripts (the TranscribeYoutubeVideoBlock via run_block is the fallback), or drop the preload.

clusters.job: Analyze a competitor (or a set of competitors) from public evidence and recommend our response

members.note: The stronger of the two competitor skills. It is decision-first: four ordered source types, five fixed questions including honest praise, a one-page output, every claim marked observed or inferred, and a guard against unpublished figures. Its identity text is nearly the same as Nadia's. Top issue: it never gathers the pending decision, our product, the competitor URL or the reader.

Thinner than the teardown overall, but it supplies what the teardown lacks: an up-front input check, an untrusted-input rule, page-by-page extraction and review-mining checklists, quick/deep depth modes, a multi-competitor summary and a change log. Its Phase 2 relies on DataForSEO endpoints that have no blocks (backend/blocks/dataforseo has only keyword_suggestions.py and related_keywords.py). The Firecrawl map/scrape/search/crawl/extract calls do have blocks. It also writes a competitor-profiles/raw disk tree, and its At a Glance asks for 'Team size [estimate]', which conflicts with Nadia's boundary. PR #13 only renames related skills.

proposed.name: Competitor teardown
proposed.description: Use when the user names a competitor, asks how we compare, or wants a competitor profile or landscape: read their pages, pricing, changelog, job ads and reviews in order, answer five questions with every claim marked observed or inferred, and end in one decision.
proposed.rationale: The teardown's decision-first frame, five questions and observed/inferred discipline are Nadia's persona, and it scores higher. competitor-profiling contributes operational scaffolding: inputs, extraction checklists, a claim check, depth modes, landscape and refresh. That fixes the teardown's missing-inputs issue without importing the SEO-tool dependence or the long template.
drops: competitor-profiling Phase 2: SEO & Market Data (DataForSEO backlinks_summary, backlinks_referring_domains, ranked_keywords, domain_rank_overview, keywords_for_site, competitors_domain, relevant_pages), plus the technology-stack, domain_intersection and bulk-rank calls in references/tool-reference.md. No AutoGPT block exists for these endpoints, and competitor search visibility is outside Nadia's lane.

competitor-profiling At a Glance rows Team size [estimate], Funding, Domain rank, Est. organic traffic, Referring domains and Organic keywords. Estimated headcount breaks Nadia's boundary unless it is published, and the SEO rows need endpoints with no block.
competitor-profiling Phase 3's traffic/backlink test of a claimed customer count. The claim check itself is kept as a graft, using public evidence instead.
competitor-profiling Saving Raw Data directory tree competitor-profiles/raw/<slug>/<date>/{scrapes,seo,reviews}: the platform keeps no project root, so it is replaced by a dated workspace file.

competitor-profiling SEO & Content Strategy profile section, the full multi-section profile template, and references/templates.md 'Quick Scan Template' and 'Competitive SWOT' (the five questions and the one-page output replace them)

recommendations.notes:
What I checked: I read the two ORIGINAL skills, which are the merge bases (competitor-teardown, icp-and-positioning). I also read both dropped graft sources (competitor-profiling, product-marketing-context) and the PR #13 version of customer-insight-research, including its interviews-and-surveys and source-guides references. competitor-watch-brief and nadia-getting-started do not exist yet, so I judged them from the verified proposal text and from their named lift sources: Zara's competitive-intelligence and Alex's product-market-and-competitor-read, both of which I read.

What I did not recommend, because the merged kit or another lane already covers it:
- Competitor pricing tables: the watch brief lifts Alex's step 4, and the teardown reads the pricing page.
- Review mining: the teardown has the extraction checklist and customer-insight-research has source-guides.
- JTBD extraction, 5-why laddering and the PMF survey: already in customer-insight-research. So the unassigned jobs-to-be-done and mom-test packages would mostly duplicate it, and obviously-awesome is already an optional line in the ICP merge.
- Battlecards: Zara's competitive-intelligence and field-enablement-content.
- Messaging and value props: Zara and Maya.
- Pricing decisions and Van Westendorp strategy: Zara's pricing-and-packaging and pricing-and-packaging-strategy. The survey skill should only field the price questions and hand the decision to Zara.
- Share of search and SEO metrics: the teardown merge dropped DataForSEO on purpose, so I did not bring it back.

Source verification:
- alirezarezvani/claude-skills research-ops/skills/market-research: MIT, copyright Alireza Rezvani. The latest commit on its history page is short SHA 2058925, which resolves on raw.githubusercontent.com. I could not get the full SHA because GitHub API access is blocked in this session, so the packager must record it. I downloaded market_sizer.py, sample_size_planner.py and segmentation_scorer.py and ran each with --sample in plain Python. They use only the standard library, and the config_loader import is wrapped in try/except, so dropping onboard.py, the ~/.config persistence, the autoresearch bridge and the /ar: and /cs: slash commands is safe.
- The catalog's market-size-estimation still contains `$ARGUMENTS` in both main and PR #13. If the reviewer prefers it as the sizing base (it ranks higher in the source order), that has to be fixed.
- Deferred ads-competitor (AgriciDaniel/claude-ads @ac21644, MIT): the file is 21 lines and I found no suite dependencies in it. It was deferred only because the full ads suite exceeds the file cap. The deferred manifest (provenance/deferred-skills.json) is not in this checkout, so the retained hash/archive should be checked before lifting it alone.
- gtmagents/gtm-agents win-loss-dataset: Apache-2.0 but only 31 lines. Use it for the data model only.

Role evidence: the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook for market research analysts (https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/market-research-analysts.htm) lists these duties: monitor and forecast trends; devise surveys, questionnaires and polls; gather data on consumers, competitors and market conditions; analyse data with statistical software; prepare reports. The Competitive Intelligence Alliance CI analyst description (https://www.competitiveintelligencealliance.io/competitive-intelligence-analyst/) adds win/loss interviews, monitoring competitors' financial performance, and landscape and whitespace mapping. Toran's review had already named market sizing and representative survey methodology as gaps. The kit leaves both open.

Lane collisions to settle when these are added:
- Sizing: Zara's opportunity-sizing-and-business-case also triggers on 'TAM' and 'market size'. Nadia should produce the sourced size and the segment verdicts; Zara turns them into the fund/pass case.
- Win-loss: 'win-loss' is already a trigger on Max's voice-of-customer-loop, Omar's lost-deal-analysis and Zara's competitive-intelligence. Nadia's triggers should be competitor-specific ('why do we lose to', 'competitive win-loss').

Two things belong in nadia.yml rather than in a skill:
- The boundaries line should gain approvals before any contact or spend, collection ethics (SCIP code: no misrepresentation, no confidential information), customer PII handling, and named handoffs.
- The identity needs one line on buyer and market research, sizing and surveys.

sketch: Brief: the decision, the population and sampling frame, the segments to report, and the precision required. Name coverage and non-response risk up front (total survey error), not just sampling error.

Instrument: screener, question order, neutral wording (no leading or double-barrelled items), scale choice, an attention check. Optional modules for monadic concept/message tests and Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger price questions; the pricing decision routes to Zara. Pre-test with 3-5 cognitive interviews.

Sample: scripts/sample_size_planner.py with finite-population correction and per-segment floors. Choose between own list and paid panel. Incentives and invitation copy are drafts for approval. Consent wording is included and raw identifiers are kept out of reports.
Cleaning: flag speeders, straight-liners, duplicates and failed attention checks. Every exclusion is logged with a count.

Analysis in bash_exec: crosstabs with unweighted bases, margins of error and significance tests; distributions, not just means; open-ended answers coded into themes with counts and verbatims; weighting only against stated targets.
Readout: a headline per decision, each number with its base, margin of error and exact question wording, plus an AAPOR-style disclosure block (sponsor, frame, field dates, n, weighting, limitations).

proposal.summary: Noor's live kit is the eight ORIGINAL comms skills. All eight are usable bases that each need fixes. Nick's PR 2 and the open rebuild PRs add nothing for her. Toran proposes three Corey Haines packages: public-relations, product-launch-marketing and marketing-copy-editing. None of them should ship to Noor on its own. The main call is to break up the public-relations hub. Its pitching core (embargo and exclusive practice, six pitch shapes, subject-line rules, pitch killers, the pre-send quality bar) merges into media-pitch-email. Its story-angle, reporter-discovery and tracking, podcast-prep, press-page and coverage-measurement parts go into news-angle-and-key-messages, media-list-research, spokesperson-briefing, communications-getting-started and launch-communications-plan. Its newsjacking and press-request material becomes one new skill, because nothing in Noor's kit covers reactive PR. product-launch-marketing gives launch-communications-plan three things: a channel mix per tier, mapped onto the quiet/standard/tentpole tiers Zara and Alex already set rather than adding a third tier scheme; ORB channel tags; and launch-day rows. marketing-copy-editing gives press-release-draft its Prove It sweep and word/sentence checks. Everything else in those two packages (Product Hunt, SLC gate, Introw, emotion and zero-risk sweeps, the vague-to-specific figure table) conflicts with Noor's persona or is off-job. Across experts, holding-statement-draft needs a clear line with Robin's mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms and with Casey's incident skills. launch-communications-plan and news-angle-and-key-messages must drop triggers that collide exactly with Zara's ('launch plan', 'messaging'). Funding news needs Theo's disclosure rules. The expert body is sharp and matches the skills. Its gaps: no routines, no legal or regulatory gate, no teammate handoffs, no mention of interview or podcast prep, and voice samples that bend their own skills' rules.

body_review.summary: The persona is tight and matches the kit: the identity's pre-writing questions, boundaries and voice samples all repeat the guardrails the eight original skills close on, and both day_one items map to kept skills. The weak spots are operational. There are no routines. Boundaries miss a legal/regulatory gate for incidents and financial news. The identity names no teammate handoffs, and neither bio nor identity mentions spokesperson or podcast prep. Both voice samples bend rules their own skills state.
strengths: The identity's four pre-writing questions ('what is new, why it matters to someone outside the company, who can confirm each claim, and what cannot be said yet') are exactly the inputs news-angle-and-key-messages and press-release-draft collect.

The boundaries line up with the closing guardrail of every original skill: no invented quotes, figures, customers or reporter interest, no speculation on cause, draft-only with no contact or publishing.
voice_preferences ('Clean, factual, and unhyped, with the news first and no superlatives') is concrete and matches press-release-draft's cut list ('leading', 'revolutionary', 'excited to announce').
The voice samples are specific and short, with sourced-looking figures, a named reporter hook and a next-update time, and they show the house style rather than describe it.
day_one maps one-to-one to kept skills: 'Your news, in one clear angle' is news-angle-and-key-messages, and 'A release and pitch ready to approve' is press-release-draft plus media-pitch-email.
body_review.kit_alignment: All eight bundled skills stay in the proposed kit under their current slugs, so no day_one entry points at a dropped or renamed skill (preloads and routines are both empty). Three bundled skills are merge bases: media-pitch-email (from public-relations), launch-communications-plan (from product-launch-marketing, plus public-relations' Measurement table) and press-release-draft (from marketing-copy-editing). Four more take smaller carries from public-relations: communications-getting-started, news-angle-and-key-messages, media-list-research and spokesperson-briefing. One new skill, press-requests-and-news-hooks, is carved from public-relations. The body promises nothing the kit doesn't cover. The reverse gaps: the body never mentions reactive press (journalist requests, news hooks) or interview and podcast prep, and no routine uses Noor's naturally recurring work.

issues.problem: Noor has no recurring work at all, even though PR has natural cadences. Journalist requests and news hooks are time-boxed: the newsjacking.md 'Speed' table puts effective windows between same-day or 4–12 hours and 24–72 hours. Media lists go stale ('journalists move jobs constantly' in journalist-pitching.md), and embargoes count down. Other marketing experts ship routines (maya.yml has three).
issues.fix: If press-requests-and-news-hooks ships, add a weekday routine 'Press requests and news hooks worth answering today' on it. It reads request digests from a connected inbox via run_block, or ones the user pastes, and scans the saved topic list with web_search. It drafts only and sends one line when nothing clears the bar; its asks name the digest source and the topics. In any case, add a monthly 'Is the media list still current' check on media-list-research that re-confirms each reporter's outlet and beat by web_fetch and flags anyone who moved.

issues.quote: Draft for approval and never contact a reporter or publish a statement yourself.
issues.problem: No legal or regulatory gate. Incidents involving personal data, safety or money carry notification duties: GDPR/UK GDPR 72-hour breach notice, listed-company disclosure, recall notices. How those notices are sequenced against a public statement matters. Funding and financial figures are also disclosure-sensitive. holding-statement-draft only says to 'Ask who approves the statement and whether legal or security must review it.'
issues.fix: Add: 'When an incident touches personal data, safety or money, or news includes financial or funding figures, counsel or the named approver reviews before anything is final and sets the order of any required regulator, market or customer notices relative to the public statement.' Mirror it as a gate step in holding-statement-draft.

issues.quote: Never invent quotes, figures, customer names, or reporter interest, and never speculate on cause or blame.
issues.problem: The persona-level list doesn't cover reporter contact details. media-list-research already says 'Never invent a reporter, a past article, an email address, or a sign of interest', and the proposal drops the Tooling block. But the public-relations material being redistributed says 'Use Hunter.io, RocketReach, or just guess and bounce-check' (references/journalist-pitching.md, Tooling), so a one-word addition to the boundary is cheap insurance.
issues.fix: Extend the list to 'quotes, figures, customer names, reporter contact details, or reporter interest', and state that only a publicly listed contact route with its source is recorded.

issues.quote: For launches you plan owners, timing, channels, and approvals.
issues.problem: The identity names no teammate handoffs. Zara (commercial-launch-strategy) and Alex (product-launch-plan) both size the launch tier and run go/no-go. Robin (mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms) drafts customer notices for the same outages, and Theo owns investor-facing disclosure rules for funding news. Without a line, Noor will re-decide the tier, duplicate customer comms and set funding figures on her own.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: take the launch tier and go/no-go from the product or GTM owner (Alex/Zara), leave customer notifications and remedies to support (Robin), check funding figures against Theo's disclosure rules, and send social posts to Jules.

issues.quote: Your pitches are short, specific to the reporter, and honest about the embargo and the ask.
issues.problem: 'Honest about the embargo' stops short of the practice the media-pitch-email review flags as its top issue: getting the reporter to agree to the embargo before embargoed specifics are shared. The identity also doesn't mention reactive press (journalist requests, news hooks) if the new skill is adopted.
issues.fix: Change to 'honest about the embargo, which the reporter agrees to before they see embargoed specifics, and the ask'. If press-requests-and-news-hooks ships, add 'You answer journalist requests and spot news you can credibly comment on, drafting every response for the spokesperson's approval.'

issues.problem: Neither bio nor identity mentions preparing a spokesperson for an interview, panel or podcast. spokesperson-briefing is in the kit and gains the podcast-prep material under this proposal, so a user reading the bio won't know to ask for it.

issues.quote: Launching 14 May, embargo until 9am.
issues.problem: The sample breaks media-pitch-email's own rule ('embargo date, time, and time zone, if any'): it gives no time zone. It also shows the launch figures ('from 40 minutes to 6 for 30 clinics') in a cold first email before any embargo agreement, so replacing only the last sentence would leave that problem in place.

Tidewell, a 12-person startup in Leeds, launches on 14 May with results from 30 clinics. Happy to share the numbers under embargo until 9am BST on 14 May, if that works for you. Worth a 15-minute call with the founder?'

issues.problem: holding-statement-draft says to leave out 'any claim that data is safe unless it has been confirmed'. The sample's softened data line models exactly the kind of claim the skill tells the model to hold back without security sign-off.

issues.quote: Drafts the press release and a reporter-specific pitch, with every quote marked approved or pending.
issues.problem: The skills track three states (press-release-draft: approved, pending or missing) across quotes, figures and named customers, not just quotes. media-pitch-email also needs a chosen reporter ('after the media list is agreed'), which this promise skips.

grafts.section: references/journalist-pitching.md > Embargoes, Exclusives, and Follow-Up Etiquette
grafts.what: Embargoes: offer one only to reporters you have worked with or who have a reputation for honouring them, and state day, time and time zone. Exclusives: be honest about scope ('exclusive to [outlet] in the US') and write the next-day parallel plan. New text, not in the source: get the reporter's agreement to the embargo before sending embargoed specifics. Keep Noor's one-follow-up-after-three-working-days rule instead of the Day 3/Day 7 cadence.

Ship all six shapes (data story, exclusive launch/milestone, op-ed pitch, customer story, trend piece/connector, newsjack response) as templates/pitch-shapes.md. Trim each to 150 words or fewer and put [approved]/[pending] markers on every stat, quote and customer. The customer-story shape requires recorded naming permission, and the trend-connector shape requires a dated link for every signal.

grafts.section: references/journalist-pitching.md > Subject Lines That Get Opened
grafts.what: Under 50 characters, lead with the specific fact, value prefixes ('Exclusive:', 'Data:', 'Op-ed pitch:', 'Re: [their article]'), and the list of patterns that get deleted ('[Company] announces [thing]', 'Following up on my previous email').

Pre-send reject list: wrong name or outlet, CC'ing other reporters, a press release attached as PDF, asking for an NDA before talking, and pitching a story you can't back (no customer willing to talk, no data ready).

grafts.section: SKILL.md > Quick Reference: Pitch Quality Bar
grafts.what: The seven-point final self-check before handing the draft over: covers this beat (last five articles), a clear news hook, a story writable from the email alone, a subject that predicts the headline, 150 words or fewer, no banned hype words, and a clear ask (interview, embargo, exclusive, quote). For embargoed news, apply the 'writable from the email alone' test to the follow-up that carries the specifics after the reporter agrees, not to the first teaser.

proposed.name: Launch communications plan
proposed.description: Plan one announcement's communications on a page: the tier taken from the launch owner, each audience's message and channel, a dated timeline with owner and approver, one embargo lift time, holding lines for what could go wrong, and a first-week coverage recap. Schedules and sends nothing.
proposed.rationale: The base already does the comms job with Noor's approval discipline. The review's top issue is the missing tier and go/no-go step. Zara's commercial-launch-strategy and Alex's product-launch-plan already size launches as quiet/standard/tentpole. Noor should take that tier and use those names. product-launch-marketing's Major/Medium/Minor matrix is carried only as the channel mix for each tier, not as a third tier scheme. That matrix covers product updates only, so funding, partnership and company news need new rows. Those rows are new text: embargoed briefings; investor sign-off under Theo's disclosure rules for funding; partner co-approval for partnerships. Also new text: a comms readiness check 24 hours before the embargo lift that feeds the launch owner's go/no-go rather than running a separate gate. Carry the MIT notices for the carried text.

grafts.section: Ongoing Launch Strategy > How to Prioritize What to Announce
grafts.what: The channel mix for each tier, mapped onto Zara's and Alex's tier names. Tentpole is roughly Major: blog post, email campaign, in-app messages, social. Standard is roughly Medium: email to relevant segments and an in-app banner. Quiet is roughly Minor: changelog and release notes. Press rows (embargoed briefings, release, pitches) are Noor's addition for tentpole and selected standard launches; the source has none. Take the tier from the launch owner's plan when one exists; otherwise propose one and flag it as the owner's decision.
Tag each channel in the audience matrix as owned, rented or borrowed (one line each; case studies dropped), so press and podcasts (borrowed) are planned to point back to an owned destination.

Comms rows for the timeline table, each with owner and approver: in-app announcement for existing users, website banner or notification, team ready to engage and respond (Noor adds a named owner for press questions), and monitoring for issues and feedback.

grafts.section: Post-Launch Product Marketing > Immediate Post-Launch Actions (Reinforce the launch)
grafts.what: Add the announcement to the next roundup or newsletter as a first-week follow-up row.

A first-week and 30-day coverage recap row: placements, referral traffic from coverage, brand search lift and sales conversations citing the coverage, each with its source. Never report AVE. Report AI-citation rate only where the user has a way to measure it.

clusters.job: Draft or edit a press release so it is news-first, checkable and approval-ready

members.note: News-first structure, a 500-word cap, a cut list of superlatives, and an approved/pending/missing table for every quote, figure and customer, with no wire or reporter sends. Its review top issue is the missing release template: no FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE / EMBARGOED UNTIL header, dateline, ### end mark or notes to editors.

General conversion-copy editing (Seven Sweeps) for marketing pages, a different job from drafting a release, so the overlap is adjacent. The two only meet on 'review/polish my copy' requests. Heightened Emotion, Zero Risk (money-back guarantees, FOMO) and the Specificity table ('Save 4 hours every week', '2,847 teams', which invents figures) conflict with Noor's 'unhyped, no superlatives' voice and her never-invent-a-figure boundary. Only the evidence sweep and the plain-word checks fit an edit pass on releases. The canonical copy-editing skill belongs with Maria (see cross_expert).

proposed.name: Press release draft
proposed.description: Draft or edit a press release for approval: embargo or release header, dateline, news-first lead, checkable figures, quotes a named person approved, boilerplate and contact, a plain-language edit pass, and a table marking each quote, figure and customer approved, pending or missing.
proposed.rationale: Requests like 'review my press release' would otherwise go to a conversion-copy editor that pushes emotion and invented specifics. Folding a factual edit pass into the release skill keeps those requests with Noor's guardrails. The header, dateline, end mark and notes-to-editors template (the review top issue) is new text; neither source has it. Add 'edit my press release' and 'review this release' triggers, and drop the bare 'announcement' trigger (see the Priya cross-expert entry).

grafts.what: A final evidence pass: every claim is checked against the approval table, unsupported assertions are flagged and then cut or softened, and 'best'/'leading'/'trusted by thousands' is removed unless a named source is recorded.

The intensifier/filler cut list (very, really, just, actually, in order to), the weak-to-plain table (utilize→use, leverage→use, facilitate→help, innovative→new, robust→strong, seamless→smooth, cutting-edge→new), and the 'Watch for' items: switch passive to active voice and turn nominalisations back into verbs.
One idea per sentence, front-load the important information, and 25 words or fewer as a rule. Apply this when editing a release the user supplies as well as a fresh draft.

recommendations.notes:
Before calling anything a gap, I read all eight kit SKILL.md files, the public-relations package and its six references, the catalog index (no PR/comms skills beyond Noor's own and the three dropped packages), DEFERRED_SKILLS.md (only public-relations applies, and it is already carved up) and the neighbouring teammate kits (Robin, Casey, Ines, Maya, Jules, Theo, Zara, Lena). I checked each upstream source by cloning it at a pinned commit and reading its LICENSE file. The raw files at those commits return HTTP 200.

Coverage findings:
(1) Nothing in the kit owns an ordinary inbound reporter question. The merge drops the 'press response' trigger from holding-statement-draft, press-requests-and-news-hooks explicitly excludes it, and spokesperson-briefing starts only after an interview is agreed. BLS and O*NET both list responding to media requests as a core duty, so media-inquiry-response should take the 'press response' trigger.
(2) Noor has no measurement and no routines. coverage-monitoring-and-report, news-calendar-and-pr-plan and the crisis kit review each give her a natural schedule_routine. The detect step in press-requests-and-news-hooks uses the same Google News RSS / web_search fetch as the coverage scan. The two should share one keyword list in memory and ideally one weekly routine.
(3) Crisis: holding-statement-draft covers only the first hours. Toran's review and the body review both flag the missing specialist workflow and the missing legal/regulatory gate. asgard pr-crisis-response (MIT) is a sound base: its V×(S+Src) score has consistent thresholds up to its maximum of 50. It needs Taiwan-specific sections removed and its stock phrases rewritten into Noor's voice.
(4) Internal comms: launch-communications-plan says staff hear first, but no skill in any kit writes the staff note. Ines's kit has no announcement drafting.

Sources considered and rejected:
- danielrosehill/Claude-PR-Media-Work-Plugin: the README and plugin.json say MIT, but the repo has no LICENSE file, and it is built from Claude Code commands and agents.
- jamditis crisis-communications (MIT): written for newsrooms. Only its respond/don't-respond tree, the lead-with-the-fact misinformation formula and the post-crisis review are worth carrying.
- asgard pr-press-release: duplicates the kit.

Further gaps, not scored:

recommendations.name: Media inquiry response

recommendations.why: BLS lists 'Respond to information requests from the media' as a core PR duty, and so does O*NET 11-2032 task 13 ('Respond to requests for information about employers' activities or status'). In the verified kit nothing owns this. press-requests-and-news-hooks is scoped to HARO/Qwoted platform queries and newsjacking and excludes 'press response'. holding-statement-draft is renamed away from 'press response' and covers incidents only. spokesperson-briefing starts once an interview is agreed. So 'a reporter from X wants comment by 5pm' has no home, even though it is the most frequent comms task in a small company.

sketch: Intake and log: reporter, outlet, the exact questions pasted verbatim, story angle, deadline with time zone and requested format. Confirm the reporter's recent bylines via web_search. Append to a workspace inquiry log and update the media list's Last contact column. Triggers: 'request for comment', 'reporter asked', 'media inquiry', 'right of reply', 'press response'.

Ground rules: define on the record, on background and off the record. Default is on the record. Terms are agreed with the approver before anything is said, and never changed after the fact. Offer a fact-check, never ask for copy approval.

Triage: respond, redirect to the right spokesperson or teammate, or decline with a useful line in place of a bare 'no comment'. Allegations, litigation, regulators, security incidents and personnel matters go to a counsel gate and on to holding-statement-draft or the crisis playbook.

Draft: a 1-3 sentence statement for attribution built only from approved facts, plus an answer to each factual question with its source. For right-of-reply letters, a point-by-point factual response with evidence, reviewed by counsel. Interview requests hand off to spokesperson-briefing.

Approval and deadline: record approver and time. Set a schedule_followup reminder before the deadline. The user sends. Once published, pass the piece to coverage-monitoring-and-report to check what was printed against what was said.
Never speculate, confirm unannounced news, go off the record without the approver's agreement, or contact the reporter directly.

proposal.summary: Omar's kit is eight ORIGINAL outlines of about 40 lines each, all usable but each needing fixes, plus two TORAN packages proposed for him: dataset-exploration and sales-pipeline-review. NICK's PR 2 added nothing for Omar, and no open rebuild PR (#14, #15, #16) touches his skills. PR #13 leaves dataset-exploration's SKILL.md unchanged and only relabels sales-pipeline-review's missing update-opportunity/log-activity handoffs as "not installed". The originals carry the persona's guardrails (never guess, never edit CRM records, keep the weighted figure apart from the rep's call), so they stay as bases and the two TORAN packages are grafted in rather than shipped. sales-pipeline-review's inputs and grounding step, stage rollup, five defined risk flags, closed-deal baseline and a corrected coverage check go into sales-forecast-rollup. dataset-exploration's structure checks, per-type profiling, cardinality checks, completeness bands, consistency/accuracy checks and profile output layout go into crm-field-audit. The other six originals have no duplicate in the kit and stay, each needing its review fixes: sandbox computation, stage-history inputs, and snapshot persistence plus a first-run baseline for crm-hygiene-report. Across experts, Omar should be the canonical home for CRM hygiene, for the deal-level rollup, and for one shared coverage definition: gap = quota minus closed-won, target = 1 / historical win rate. Today Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast uses a flat 3x over quota, and Daniel's saas-gtm-finance and Anika's track-partner-pipeline use 3x over target. Zara's gtm-performance-diagnostics and Max's own Monday routine already use the win-rate bar. Max's monday-team-pipeline-inspection and wednesday-forecast-and-deal-inspection routines already deliver a weekly team forecast read, so Omar should feed them rather than add a competing forecast routine. The expert body is sharp, but it has four gaps. routines is empty even though crm-hygiene-report is a weekly/monthly skill. No skill delivers the day-one "CRM health check" on a first run. The day_one forecast item and the identity describe an open-deals-only forecast. And there are no personal-data or handoff boundaries.

body_review.summary: The persona is exact and consistent: record the export first, never guess, never touch the CRM, keep the rep's call apart from the weighted figure. Every skill's closing guardrail repeats it. The gaps are operational rather than tonal. routines is empty even though crm-hygiene-report is written as a weekly/monthly report. The first day_one promise has no first-run skill behind it. The second day_one promise and the identity describe the open-deals-only forecast that the merge replaces. The boundaries say nothing about personal data in contact/lead exports and name no teammate handoffs. Two voice samples model habits the reviews flag: a domain-plus-surname duplicate rule with no free-mail exclusion, and a forecast built from open deals only with no export date.
strengths: identity sets a concrete provenance habit ('record the export date, the object and filter, the row count'). Five skills repeat it in their first section (revops-getting-started, crm-field-audit, crm-duplicate-review, sales-forecast-rollup, crm-hygiene-report). The other three (pipeline-stage-definitions, lead-routing-rules, lost-deal-analysis) only ask for 'a dated export' and should gain the same line when they are fixed.
boundaries match the closing guardrail of all eight original skills (never guess a missing value; never merge, delete, reassign or edit), so persona and kit do not drift apart.
The voice samples show the right behaviour: counts and dates first, 'I have not merged anything', stale deals left in and marked with the decision handed back.
day_one[1] ('A forecast you can trace') maps directly onto sales-forecast-rollup, which keeps the same slug after the merge.
body_review.kit_alignment: skills: lists the eight originals. The proposed kit keeps all eight slugs, and the two merges land in place in crm-field-audit and sales-forecast-rollup. So no day_one, routine or preload reference breaks, and dataset-exploration and sales-pipeline-review were never on the list. day_one[1] maps to sales-forecast-rollup. day_one[0] maps only partly to crm-hygiene-report, which is framed around 'compared with the last report' and has no first-run baseline. routines and preloads are both empty. The merged forecast adds booked-to-date and coverage of the gap to quota. Three body fields do not reflect this: identity, day_one[1].description ('Builds the forecast from open deals') and voice_samples[1]. Any routine added for Omar must not duplicate Max's monday-team-pipeline-inspection and wednesday-forecast-and-deal-inspection or Zara's weekly-gtm-scorecard.

issues.problem: crm-hygiene-report says 'Use this weekly or monthly, from dated exports compared with the last report', and the platform has schedule_routine. But Omar has no routine, so the recurring health report never runs on its own and no snapshot chain exists for 'against the last period'.
issues.fix: Add a 'weekly-crm-health' routine with crons, asks for where the exports live or whether HubSpot is connected, the key objects, and the time and timezone. It should run crm-hygiene-report on the latest export or a read-only HubSpot pull, save the counts snapshot and a dated deal-level snapshot with write_workspace_file (pointer in memory_store), compare with the last snapshot, and draft the report for approval. The deal-level snapshot also feeds the forecast's movement view. Do not add a default weekly forecast routine: Max's monday-team-pipeline-inspection and wednesday-forecast-and-deal-inspection routines (and Zara's weekly-gtm-scorecard) already deliver a weekly team read for users who hire them. Offer a forecast routine only on request, and let Max's routines read Omar's snapshot.

clusters.job: Profile a CRM export's fields and judge each one's quality and usefulness

members.note: It has the CRM-specific outcome (keep/fix/retire with the report affected and 'what still reads the field'), usage and ownership columns, a placeholder check ('n/a', 'tbc', default date) and the no-edit guardrail, all matching Omar's identity. It lacks a profiling method, applicable-population fill rates, a usage source and an output template.

Weak on guardrails (no personal-data masking), and it is about 340 lines of generic warehouse profiling. Its structure check, per-type profile, cardinality checks, completeness bands, consistency/accuracy indicators and output layout supply the method crm-field-audit lacks. The rest is off-job for Omar: warehouse SQL, correlations, dimension/metric suggestions and the '/explore-data' usage. PR #13 leaves its SKILL.md unchanged, so the slash-command problem remains.

proposed.name: CRM field audit
proposed.description: Use when a CRM export, field list or report needs its fields checked: profiles structure, applicable fill rate, formats, placeholders and usage per field, then proposes keep, fix, merge or retire for the CRM owner. Never fills blanks or edits fields.
proposed.rationale: Both skills do the same measurement on the same input: fill/null rate, distinct and most-common values, placeholders, format consistency. Only crm-field-audit ends in the decision Omar owns (a keep/fix/retire list for the CRM owner) and carries his guardrails, so it stays the base. dataset-exploration supplies the missing 'how'. Alongside the grafts, apply crm-field-audit's own review fixes. Compute fill over the population where the field applies (stage, record type, created after the field existed). Ask for field metadata, and when it is absent mark usage UNKNOWN, which blocks 'retire'. State default label criteria as owner-editable assumptions. Add a staged deprecation path. Do the computation in bash_exec and write a per-field table to the workspace. Grafted text is adapted from Apache-2.0 upstream, so keep an ATTRIBUTION note or paraphrase.
drops: dataset-exploration 'Usage' block ('/explore-data <table_name or file>') and the slash-command title
dataset-exploration 'Schema Exploration Queries' (PostgreSQL information_schema SQL) and the warehouse-first branch of '1. Access the Data'
dataset-exploration 'Correlation Exploration', 'Distribution Analysis', 'Temporal Patterns' and 'Segmentation Discovery'
dataset-exploration '6. Suggest Interesting Dimensions and Metrics', '7. Recommend Follow-Up Analyses' and the 'Recommended Explorations' block of 'Output Format'
dataset-exploration '4. Identify Data Quality Issues' null thresholds ('>5% nulls (warn), >20% nulls (alert)'), which conflict with the completeness bands
dataset-exploration 'Timeliness Assessment' (the export date and last-modified checks are already covered by 'Record the export' and the stale-record indicator)
dataset-exploration 'Tips' claim that profiling queries 'use sampling by default' (false in this harness)
dataset-exploration 'Sparse (<80%): Red -- may not be usable without imputation' (Omar never imputes)
dataset-exploration 'Schema Documentation Template' and 'Lineage and Dependencies'
dataset-exploration references/CONNECTORS.md (~~category placeholders, upstream .mcp.json)

grafts.what: A new first step before 'Measure each field': confirm the grain (one row per record), check that the record ID is unique (duplicate IDs mean a joined or report export), and classify each field as identifier, picklist/dimension, amount/metric, date, free text or boolean so the right checks run.

Per-type checks run in bash_exec. Strings: empty-string count, leading/trailing whitespace, case consistency, pattern/format. Dates: min/max, future dates in historical fields, nulls. Numbers: zero and negative counts, p50/p95. Booleans: true rate. Plus least-common values to spot anomalies. New, not in the source (which prints top and bottom values raw), per the dataset-exploration eval: mask values in email, phone, name and free-text fields rather than printing them.

Cardinality surprises: a picklist field with hundreds of distinct values (free text or picklist sprawl), or an ID-like field with few distinct values. Also distribution skew in amount fields. This covers the review's missing 'picklist value sprawl' check. Its null thresholds are not carried over.

The four bands (Complete >99%, Mostly complete 95-99%, Incomplete 80-95%, Sparse <80%), applied to the applicable population and shown next to the raw fill rate. Replace the imputation remark with 'propose a required rule or a sourced backfill'.

Value-format inconsistency ('USA', 'US', 'United States'), numbers or dates stored as text, referential integrity (contact account IDs missing from the accounts export), business-rule violations (close date before created date, negative amounts) and cross-column consistency (e.g. Stage = Closed Won with a blank close date or amount).

Extend the placeholder list (0, -1, 999999, 'test', 'xxx', default dates). Add 'default values', where one value dominates a field; impossible values; round-number bias in amounts; and stale records by last-modified date.
The 'Redundant columns' check (identical or near-identical information), used to support a new 'merge into <field>' label next to keep/fix/retire, e.g. for two Industry fields.

The output skeleton, adapted. Overview: export date, object, filter, rows, fields by type. Then a per-field table (field, type, applicable fill %, band, placeholder %, distinct values, used by, owner, label, reason, report affected). Then quality issues with severity. 'Recommended Explorations' is replaced by the keep/fix/merge/retire list and a top-5 summary tied to named reports, which answers the crm-field-audit review's missing template.
