recommendations.name: Forecast accuracy review
recommendations.purpose: After a period closes, compare the saved period-start forecast snapshot with what actually closed. Report signed bias and absolute error at each roll-up level, and put every dollar of the miss down to a named deal with one cause, classed as data, behaviour or demand.
recommendations.why: The merged kit builds a forecast (sales-forecast-rollup) but never checks one against the outcome. Omar's tagline, 'forecasts you can trace', has no follow-through over time. Nothing saves a period-start snapshot, and no skill measures the reps' call against the weighted figure after close. Job templates list 'revenue forecasting models with monthly, quarterly and annual accuracy targets' as a core RevOps analyst duty (rework.com RevOps Analyst template). In the catalog the only coverage is one line in Zara's gtm-performance-diagnostics ('last period's commit against what actually closed'), and Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast has none. The upstream mbfinotti sales-forecast-diagnostic is 194 lines with 3 references. It does period reconstruction from a two-file export, signed and absolute error shipped together, a rule of two independent signals before any behaviour verdict, a backtest threshold and a rep calibration scorecard. It also warns off unsourced benchmarks such as 3x coverage and default stage probabilities, which matches the review findings on sales-forecast-rollup. I cloned it and verified it (MIT, commit 2dedb39). A grep found no $ARGUMENTS, slash commands or CLAUDE.md. The skill can also back a period-close routine. That routine would not duplicate Max's monday-team-pipeline-inspection or wednesday-forecast-and-deal-inspection, or Zara's weekly-gtm-scorecard.

source.ref: mbfinotti/revops-skills skills/sales-forecast-diagnostic (v1.3.4, commit 2dedb3934ca74a1572d70e2a3ce8b96d2cbde1ca), with references/evidence-and-metrics.md, root-cause-fingerprints.md, worked-diagnosis-example.md

sketch: Snapshot capture: at period start, save the dated forecast (deal ids, stage, amount, close date, rep call, weighted value) with write_workspace_file and memory_store. Offer schedule_routine for a period-start snapshot and a period-close review. With no snapshot, fall back to field history plus a lower-confidence label.

Quantify the miss: forecast vs actual per level (rep, manager, total) and per category. Show signed bias and absolute error together, with one fixed denominator and WMAPE-style dollar weighting, all computed in bash_exec.

Reconstruct the period: classify each forecast deal as won as called, slipped, lost, removed or still open. Classify each won deal by origin (in the forecast? which category? created when?). Attribute at least 90% of the gap to named deals and label the residual as unexplained.

Root causes: the fingerprint register (zombies, pushed dates, wrong category, stage inflation, late-created deals, override, sandbagging, comp bias), each needing two signals, one of them from recorded history. Split data, behaviour and demand, and never net offsetting errors.

Omar guardrails: keep the rep calibration scorecard for the sales lead only and show n. Never name a rep in a behaviour verdict without the evidence rule, and keep accuracy separate from performance. Send data fixes to crm-hygiene-report or crm-data-governance, and comp and behaviour findings to the sales lead or Max. Never edit the CRM.

Adaptation: replace the mbfinotti cross-references with kit slugs and drop links to skills not shipped (revenue-reporting, sales-skills@sales-pipeline-coverage-modeling). Map 'if your harness can execute code' and 'persistent memory' to bash_exec and memory_store, run the interview through ask_question, and give the Salesforce note an export fallback.

recommendations.name: CRM data governance
recommendations.purpose: Turn the field audit into a standing rulebook. It gives a field dictionary, one named owner per revenue-critical field, a per-field system of record with write precedence across syncs, freshness SLAs, enforcement choices, and a request, approval and deprecation lifecycle.
recommendations.why: crm-field-audit (even merged with dataset-exploration) labels fields keep, fix or retire as a one-off. It does not say which system wins when HubSpot, billing, marketing automation and enrichment all write the same field. It also keeps no durable dictionary and has no process for approving field retirement, which Toran's review flags as a gap: 'does not ... approve field retirement'. Sales and RevOps analyst postings list 'document ... reporting definitions' and 'adherence to established data standards' (Thomson Reuters Sales Operations Analyst posting on builtin.com), and 'ensure data integrity and consistency across systems ... data governance practices' (getguru RevOps analyst reference). The upstream mbfinotti crm-data-governance is 178 lines with 6 references and a pass threshold, and I cloned and verified it (MIT). It is proposal-shaped: it designs rules and a cadence and never edits records, so it fits Omar's rule 'you propose; owners change the system'. It also makes consent and preference fields governed fields, which partly answers the missing personal-data boundary.

source.ref: mbfinotti/revops-skills skills/crm-data-governance (v1.3.1, commit 2dedb3934ca74a1572d70e2a3ce8b96d2cbde1ca), with references/system-of-record-rules.md, freshness-slas.md, field-ownership-and-dictionary.md, field-lifecycle.md, enforcement-menu.md, worked-examples.md

sketch: Scope the governed set: start with the fields that feed the forecast, routing, comp and board reports, taking fill and usage evidence from the crm-field-audit output and the key fields in the working rules. Cap the set deliberately.

Ownership and system of record: for each field, one named person, one authoritative system, the write precedence and conflict rule for each sync, and an enrichment mode (augment, append or overwrite) with a risk tier. Blank never overwrites a populated value.

Freshness and enforcement: a refresh SLA per field category, and last-verified tracked separately from last-modified. Rank enforcement picklist > conditional-required > defaults > permissions > layout > hard-required.

Lifecycle and cadence: a field intake form, approval and rejection criteria, a deprecation process that lists what still reads the field, and a review rhythm with decision rights. Consent, opt-out and retention fields are governed fields, with Lena as the owner contact.

Dictionary artefact: build it from the HubSpot property read (run_block) or an exported field list, and mark unverified rows. Save it as a workspace file plus memory, and spot-check 10-15 fields against the live CRM. Propose only, never create, hide or change a field.

Adaptation: change the mbfinotti@ references to kit slugs and drop revenue-data-governance-strategy (not shipped). Batch the one-question-per-message interview into ask_question, and keep the provenance tags on every threshold.

recommendations.name: CRM import check
recommendations.purpose: Check a list before anyone loads it into the CRM (event leads, bought or partner lists, enrichment files, migration batches). It maps columns, normalises values, matches against existing records, checks consent and suppression, and returns an import-ready file plus an exceptions file for the owner to load.
recommendations.why: Every duplicate and fill-rate skill in the kit cleans up after bad data has arrived. Nothing stops it arriving, and list imports are the main way it gets in. Omar also never edits the CRM, so the file has to be handed over ready to load. Postings name the task directly: 'prepare ... CRM-ready files with the required identifiers and source-system keys for imports' and 'validate, cleanse, and import data into Salesforce' (Thomson Reuters Sales Operations Analyst posting). HubSpot's own guidance says its importer dedupes against the CRM but not inside the file. No catalog skill covers this. automate-finance-reporting (Daniel) has a similar map, dedupe and QA pattern, but for a finance ledger. The public HubSpot/agent-cli-skills crm-data-quality has a known bug that groups every email-less contact into one merge set (issue #65), so it is not a safe base. The platform fits well: bash_exec for matching, a HubSpot block read of existing records and properties, and write_workspace_file for the output CSVs. It is also where contact personal data enters, so it covers the privacy gap in Omar's boundaries.

source.ref: new, written by us; reuse the crm-duplicate-review match rules and the lead-routing-rules owner logic

sketch: Inputs: the file, its origin and date, the target object, the CRM property list (HubSpot block or export), the consent or lawful-basis evidence for the list, and the person who will run the import. Record the row count and source before anything else.

Map and normalise: a column-to-property table with the transforms written out, picklist value mapping, and unmapped columns listed rather than dropped. Normalise email, domain, phone and country in bash_exec, check required fields, and flag placeholder values.

Match: within-file duplicates and matches against the CRM, using crm-duplicate-review rules with free-mail exclusion. Label each row create, update, skip or hold. An update never blanks a populated field and never overwrites a governed field the file does not own.

Consent and suppression: match against unsubscribed, bounced and do-not-contact lists. Hold rows with no consent or lawful-basis evidence where it is required. Drop columns the CRM does not need, and show only masked samples in chat.
Owner preview: apply the approved routing rules to preview owners, add source and campaign tags, and list rows that match no rule.

Output: an import-ready CSV, an exceptions CSV with reasons, and a load summary (rows in, create, update, skip, hold). The owner runs the import. The next export is checked against the summary, and the check is logged.

recommendations.name: CRM-to-billing bookings reconciliation
recommendations.purpose: Tie closed-won deals in the CRM to the billing system (Stripe or an invoice export) for a period. Each gap is sorted into matched, amount difference, timing, won-not-billed, billed-with-no-deal or duplicate, and sent to the owner who can fix it.
recommendations.why: The merged sales-forecast-rollup now uses booked-to-date to work out the gap to quota. That figure comes from CRM closed-won, which often differs from what was actually signed and billed. Omar's identity ('the CRM as a record of what people typed, not of what happened') calls for this check, but no skill in the kit or catalog does it. account-reconciliation (Toran) covers GL, bank and subledger, and Daniel's saas-gtm-finance builds the ARR bridge from the revenue ledger. RevOps analyst templates list 'Collaborate with finance on ... bookings vs. billings tracking' (rework.com template). The upstream mbfinotti revenue-reporting also has a step saying the CRM read and the finance read must be reconciled before any number ships. The platform has a Stripe block and bash_exec for matching, so this runs read-only with a CSV fallback.

source.ref: new, written by us; reconciling-item categories can follow the catalog's account-reconciliation (Apache-2.0) method

sketch: Inputs: a dated closed-won export (deal id, account, amount, currency, close date, term, products), a billing export (Stripe via run_block, or an invoice CSV) and any signed-order list. The source of truth per field comes from the working rules or the governance dictionary.

Match in bash_exec: deal id stored on the subscription or invoice first, then account plus amount inside a date window, then a reviewed fuzzy match. Handle one-to-many cases (annual contracts billed monthly, multi-invoice deals) by comparing contract value with billed-to-date.

Classify each item: matched, amount difference (discount, tax, FX, term), timing, won-not-billed, billed-no-deal, duplicate won deal, or currency mismatch. Quote both values as recorded and never pick the right one.

Tie-out summary: CRM total, billing total, explained differences by class with counts, and the unexplained residual. Show the effect on booked-to-date and the gap to quota used by sales-forecast-rollup.
Handoffs: billing and invoice corrections go to Daniel or Mina, and CRM corrections go to the deal owner as a change list. Omar never edits either system and never issues or voids an invoice.
Save the dated reconciliation and offer a month-end schedule_routine that does not clash with Daniel's close routines.

recommendations.name: Sales metric dictionary
recommendations.purpose: Write down once, and version, how the team computes win rate, stage conversion, cycle length, coverage, pipeline created, booked-to-date, slip rate and forecast accuracy (formula, denominator, inclusions, date basis, source field, owner). Every report then gives the same answer.
recommendations.why: Several merged kit skills compute the same metrics: lost-deal-analysis (win rates with n), pipeline-stage-definitions (stage-to-won rates, medians), sales-forecast-rollup (gap-based coverage, weights) and crm-hygiene-report (stale). The reviews caught wrong denominators (weighted pipeline against a 3x bar, open-only forecasts), and Toran rejected a RevOps source for an incorrect win-rate denominator. Teammates compute the same numbers too: Zara's gtm-performance-diagnostics and weekly-gtm-scorecard, Max's pipeline-review-and-forecast and Daniel's saas-gtm-finance. Nothing makes them agree. Postings list documenting 'reporting definitions' as an analyst duty (Thomson Reuters posting). The mbfinotti revenue-reporting skill has a verified MIT reference, metric-dictionary-entry.md, that gives a good entry shape (formula, inclusions and exclusions, source of truth, owner, window, version). The rest of that skill is board-deck work that belongs to Daniel and Theo, so a short new skill that borrows the entry shape fits better than taking the whole package.

source.ref: new, written by us; entry shape adapted from mbfinotti/revops-skills skills/revenue-reporting/references/metric-dictionary-entry.md (MIT, commit 2dedb39): https://github.com/mbfinotti/revops-skills/blob/2dedb3934ca74a1572d70e2a3ce8b96d2cbde1ca/skills/revenue-reporting/references/metric-dictionary-entry.md

sketch: Metric set: pipeline created, open pipeline, booked-to-date, win rate (won/(won+lost), closed-in-period vs cohort, with no-decision and disqualified rules), stage conversion and stage-to-won, cycle length, days in stage, coverage (unweighted open over remaining gap), slip rate, forecast bias and error.

Entry shape per metric: question answered, formula, denominator, inclusions and exclusions, date basis (close date vs created), currency and FX rule, source field, owner, minimum n, and version with a changelog.

Reconcile with teammates: read Zara's and Max's definitions, use consult_teammate where they conflict, and have the sales lead sign off one definition. Record the ones still disputed as open rather than picking one quietly.
Test on data: compute each metric on the current export in bash_exec and show counts beside every rate. Report N/A with counts when a denominator is zero.
Persist: memory_store plus a workspace file. All kit skills read it, and a definition change gets a new version and a footnote in the next report.

recommendations.name: Account ownership and hierarchy audit
recommendations.purpose: Find records whose owner is deactivated or departed, contacts and deals owned apart from their account, parent and child accounts split across books, and accounts matching no territory rule. Return a reassignment proposal for the sales lead with book-balance counts per active owner.
recommendations.why: crm-hygiene-report counts records with 'no owner'. A departed rep's accounts still show an owner, so they never appear in that count while the leads go unworked and routing sends new records to a dead end. Postings ask analysts to 'identify, document, and route data-quality issues — duplicates, missing IDs, incorrect territory assignment' (Thomson Reuters Sales Operations Analyst posting), and rep offboarding is a routine RevOps request. The public TomGranot/hubspot-admin-skills (MIT) includes reassign-deactivated-owners, which shows the demand and a useful detail: the HubSpot Owners API needs archived=true to list deactivated users. It needs a HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN in .env and uv, and it batch-writes reassignments, so it breaks Omar's never-reassign boundary and the platform's no-secrets sandbox. It is method material only. Territory and quota design itself stays with Max's sales-ops-coverage-and-quota. This skill only finds the gaps and proposes reassignments.

source.ref: new, written by us; detection method can borrow from TomGranot/hubspot-admin-skills reassign-deactivated-owners (MIT, commit cb6a1e8), not packaged because it writes to the CRM and needs a local API token

sketch: Inputs: account, contact and deal exports with owner ids, the active and deactivated user list (HubSpot owners via run_block, or a user CSV), the approved territory or book rules, and the parent-account field. Record dates and row counts.

Checks: inactive owners, contact owner different from account owner, open deals owned by someone other than the account owner, children in a different book from their parent, and accounts matching no rule or two rules. Give counts and value for each.
Book balance per active owner: accounts, open pipeline, and potential where scored, with n. Keep it descriptive and never rank reps.

Reassignment proposal: for each orphaned record, the rule that would assign it. Open deals and parent/child conflicts are flagged for a sales lead decision. Output a CSV the owner can apply. Omar reassigns nothing.
Handoffs: book or territory design questions go to Max (sales-ops-coverage-and-quota), and routing fixes go to lead-routing-rules. Add an inactive-owner count to the weekly hygiene baseline.

recommendations.name: CRM change request and log
recommendations.purpose: Turn any approved proposal from the kit (a field fix, stage rule, routing change, merge batch or reassignment list) into a change request with scope, affected reports and automations, test, rollback and named approver. Keep a dated log of status so later reports can show what was done and what is still open.
recommendations.why: Every kit skill ends with 'propose; the owner approves and makes the change'. Nothing records what was approved, by whom, when it was applied, or whether the next export shows the fix. Toran's review names this gap for crm-hygiene-report: 'action follow-through remain partial'. The hygiene report is also meant to list fixes from the last report that are still open, and the platform keeps no state unless a skill writes it. Change control is standard RevOps admin work: postings mention documenting 'system requirements, standard operating procedures' (Thomson Reuters posting). The platform's approval flow and memory_store and write_workspace_file make a log cheap to keep.

source.ref: new, written by us

sketch: Intake: the proposal and the skill it came from, the approver for that change type taken from the working rules, and the records affected, counted.
Change spec: before and after, reports, automations and routing touched, a test on a sample or sandbox, a rollback step, and a target date.
Approval record: approver, date and wording, captured through the platform approval flow. Omar applies nothing.
Log: a dated entry in a workspace change log plus memory, with status open, approved, applied, verified or rejected.
Verification: on the next export, check that the expected counts moved. crm-hygiene-report reads the open items, and schedule_followup covers overdue ones.

recommendations.name: Commission credit check
recommendations.purpose: Apply an already approved comp plan's crediting and rate rules to closed-won deals. Produce per-rep credit and attainment statements that trace to deal ids, and flag splits, disputes and clawback triggers for finance to approve. Omar never sets or pays compensation.
recommendations.why: RevOps analyst templates list 'Support sales compensation plan design and performance tracking' (rework.com template), and commission crediting is a frequent source of disputes. The catalog has comp design (Max's sales-ops-coverage-and-quota) but no skill that checks crediting or calculations against deals. The job suits Omar's 'every number traces to a deal' method and the bash_exec sandbox. It ranks as could because comp data is sensitive personal data, the persona would need its boundaries widened, and finance (Daniel) owns payouts. NEON-Rutger's comp-plan-architecture has a verified MIT reference, crediting-rules.md, covering credit splits, layered credit, total-credit caps and the failure modes to flag. It can supply method, but the skill itself is design-level and strategy-heavy.

source.ref: new, written by us; crediting mechanics can be adapted from NEON-Rutger/B2B-revops-skills comp-plan-architecture/references/crediting-rules.md (MIT, commit d3d3dd9): https://github.com/NEON-Rutger/B2B-revops-skills/blob/d3d3dd967ffc7da0f2e9282ab124d51357160d69/comp-plan-architecture/references/crediting-rules.md

sketch: Inputs: the approved plan document (rates, crediting and split rules, accelerators, clawback, period), a dated closed-won export, the billing reconciliation status, and the rep roster with quotas. With no approved plan, the skill stops.
Crediting: apply the rules deal by deal, including splits, overlays and a total-credit cap. Ambiguous or disputed deals are marked UNKNOWN with the owner who must decide, never resolved by Omar.
Calculation in bash_exec: per-rep credit, attainment and accelerator tier, with every figure tied to deal ids.
Exceptions: deals not yet billed or paid, amount or date changes after close, and missing split records. Flag possible clawback triggers.
Privacy and approval: statements go only to finance and each rep's manager. Omar makes no pay recommendation, Daniel or the finance owner approves payouts, and nothing is sent without approval.

recommendations.notes:
What the merged kit leaves open. After the merge, Omar's kit handles audit, define and one-off forecast work well. The remaining gaps fall into four groups:
- Over time: forecast accuracy against outcome, and follow-through on proposed changes.
- Prevention: import checks and field governance.
- Across systems: CRM against billing.
- Ownership: inactive owners and hierarchy.
All eight recommendations keep Omar read-only. Each one produces a proposal or a file for an owner to act on.

**Sources checked.**
- The two upstream picks come from mbfinotti/revops-skills (MIT, © 2026 Nativa Labs). I cloned it at commit 2dedb3934ca74a1572d70e2a3ce8b96d2cbde1ca. A grep found no $ARGUMENTS, slash commands or CLAUDE.md. Their `mbfinotti/revops-skills@...` cross-references need rewriting to kit slugs, and some point to skills that won't ship (revenue-reporting, revenue-data-governance-strategy, mbfinotti/sales-skills@sales-pipeline-coverage-modeling).
- Three sibling skills in that repo are useful material for the in-kit fixes, not as separate skills: pipeline-stage-definition-audit (buyer-verifiable exit test, for pipeline-stage-definitions), lead-routing (lead-to-account matching and round-robin variants, for lead-routing-rules) and sales-pipeline-hygiene (push counts and segment stage medians, for crm-hygiene-report).
- DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has nothing relevant; it is the ads suite and marketing-ideas.

**Sources ruled out.**
- coreyhaines31 revops: Toran already rejected it for the win-rate denominator.
- TomGranot/hubspot-admin-skills (MIT, commit cb6a1e8): it needs HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN in .env, uv and slash commands, and it merges, deletes and reassigns records. That conflicts with Omar's boundaries and with the sandbox, which has no user secrets. Use it for method only.
- HubSpot/agent-cli-skills crm-data-quality: it depends on the HubSpot CLI and has a known bug that puts all email-less contacts into one merge set (issue #65).
- NEON-Rutger/B2B-revops-skills (MIT, commit d3d3dd9): the skills are 250-700 lines and heavy on strategy and benchmarks, a better fit for Max and Zara. I only borrowed crediting-rules.md.

**Not recommended because a teammate already owns it.** Name these handoffs in Omar's boundaries:
- Lead scoring and MQL/SQL SLA: Zara, sales-marketing-alignment-and-sla.
- Territory, quota and comp design: Max, sales-ops-coverage-and-quota.
- ARR bridge and retention: Daniel, saas-gtm-finance.
- Board revenue reporting: Daniel and Theo.
- Metric data-quality testing: Quinn, metric-definition-and-data-quality.
I did not propose Robin's sensitive-data-safe-handling for the privacy gap. It is built around card and health data in support work. crm-import-check and crm-data-governance carry consent, minimisation and masking instead. The persona body still needs a boundary line on personal data in contact and lead exports.

**Routines.**
- forecast-accuracy-review backs a period-start snapshot and a period-close retrospective routine (monthly or quarterly). Neither clashes with Max's Monday and Wednesday inspections or Zara's Monday scorecard.
- crm-change-log feeds open items into the proposed weekly-crm-health routine.
- crm-billing-reconciliation could run at month end, but check it against Daniel's close routines first.

**If account-ownership-audit is not taken,** at least add an inactive-owner count to crm-hygiene-report. 'No owner' misses records held by deactivated users.

**Evidence.** Role evidence comes from the rework.com RevOps Analyst template (forecast accuracy targets, bookings vs billings, territory and quota, comp tracking), a Thomson Reuters Sales Operations Analyst posting on builtin.com (CRM-ready import files, validate and import, document reporting definitions, route incorrect territory assignment) and the getguru RevOps analyst reference (data governance across systems). The posting quotes came through search summaries, not full-page fetches. The rework.com quotes came through a page fetch that a small model summarised, so they may not be word-for-word.

proposal.summary: Priya's live kit is eight short ORIGINAL placeholders. NICK added nothing for her, and TORAN proposed five upstream PM packages, roughly on par with her originals. Each of the five duplicates one of her existing jobs, and PR #13 does not make any of them harness-clean. It renames the /write-spec and /roadmap-update slash commands but keeps their $ARGUMENTS blocks and ~~ placeholders. It relabels customer-insight-research's related-skill links but keeps its .claude/product-marketing.md lookup. It leaves the research-synthesis and stakeholder-update SKILL.md files unchanged. I keep all eight original slugs as the skeleton and turn four of them into merges. feedback-synthesis takes the thematic-coding, triangulation and survey method from product-research-synthesis. From customer-insight-research it takes the unprompted, segment, recency and bias guardrails, recast as strong/moderate/thin thresholds counted on distinct accounts and source types, because the upstream 'independent sources' unit is undefined. product-requirements-draft takes P0-P2 tiers, Given/When/Then criteria and leading/lagging metrics from product-requirements-writing. roadmap-prioritisation takes defined RICE/ICE/MoSCoW scales, capacity and allocation rules, dependencies and change communication from product-roadmap-planning, but not its status- and timeline-maintenance operations. release-notes-draft takes the customer and launch template from product-stakeholder-update, minus 'coming soon'. user-interview-guide borrows 5-why laddering and the survey design guardrails from customer-insight-research's interview reference. None of the five Toran packages is bundled on its own. The biggest open call is cross-expert. Alex (NICK, also a 'Product Manager') owns more developed PRD and roadmap skills and a discovery skill that duplicate Priya's, and the roadmap eval even suggests treating Priya's as the smaller side of a merge with Alex's. I recommend differentiating the two: Priya works evidence-first, never guesses effort, never writes to the tracker, and writes release notes only for shipped work. Her identity should also get routing lines. A reviewer may decide instead that the roster needs only one PM.

body_review.summary: Priya's persona is one of the sharper originals. It is evidence-first and puts a count and a source behind every theme. Every original skill ends on a guardrail consistent with its boundaries (no edits, no invented figures), though only five of the eight restate the no-date rule. Every merge keeps an original slug, so day_one still points at live skills. The body has five weaknesses. It never says how Priya differs from Alex or when to hand off to him. It has no rule on personal data, even though the kit quotes customers and interview participants word for word. It has no routines for work that is naturally recurring. Its voice samples overlap Alex's and do not show the strength labels the voice preference promises. And the bio's 'what each option costs you' sits uneasily with the never-invent-effort boundary.
strengths: The identity is concrete and testable: "One loud request is not a pattern, and silence is not satisfaction." It also separates what users said from what Priya infers, and puts a count and a source behind every theme.

The boundaries (never edit the roadmap, tracker or changelog; never invent a quote, metric or estimate; never promise a date) are consistent with the closing guardrail line of every original skill. product-getting-started, opportunity-brief, product-requirements-draft, roadmap-prioritisation and release-notes-draft restate the date rule. feedback-synthesis, feature-request-triage and user-interview-guide carry only the no-invention and no-edit or no-contact parts.
Both voice samples carry sourced numbers and flag guesses explicitly ("Effort is the team's guess of two weeks, not a measured figure").
The day_one items map directly onto feedback-synthesis and product-requirements-draft, and both slugs survive the merge.
body_review.kit_alignment: Alignment holds because every merge keeps the original slug. day_one[0] ('Your feedback, sorted into problems') maps to feedback-synthesis and day_one[1] ('A spec your engineers can build from') maps to product-requirements-draft, and both stay. preloads and routines are empty, so nothing points at a dropped or renamed skill. Every artefact the identity promises is in the kit: opportunity briefs, requirements, prioritisation, interview guides and release notes. Nothing in the body promises the stakeholder or exec updates Toran proposed, which supports dropping product-stakeholder-update. There are four gaps. The body never mentions saving setup to memory, which product-getting-started must now do. It has no hand-off to Alex, whose product-prd-and-acceptance-criteria, product-roadmap-and-prioritization and product-discovery-and-user-research duplicate Priya's skills. The identity's prioritisation promise has no stated rule for items with no effort figure, which the merged roadmap skill has to supply. And opportunity-brief allows effort 'marked as a guess' without saying whose guess, while the boundary forbids Priya inventing one. The skill should say 'the team's guess, labelled'.

issues.quote: You write opportunity briefs and requirements that state the user, the problem, the evidence, the goal, what is out of scope, the open questions
issues.problem: Alex is also a 'Product Manager' with PRD, roadmap, discovery, strategy and exec-brief skills. Priya's identity names no teammate and no hand-off, so on a team with both, the PRD and roadmap requests route arbitrarily. There are also real trigger collisions: opportunity-brief's 'should we build this' against Alex's product-strategy-and-bets, 'RICE score' in both roadmap skills, and 'acceptance criteria' in both PRD skills.
issues.fix: Add a routing paragraph. Priya owns the evidence (feedback synthesis, request triage, interview guides, opportunity briefs), specs built from that evidence, and release notes for shipped work. She hands strategy bets, metrics instrumentation, experiments, launch plans and exec or board briefs to Alex; ticket handling to Sasha or Robin; public announcements to Noor or Maya; and release-readiness checks to Casey (the release owner makes the go/no-go call).

issues.quote: Never invent user quotes, metrics, effort estimates, or competitor claims, and never promise a date.
issues.problem: The kit quotes customers word for word and stores interview participants' identities. Only opportunity-brief redacts. The reviews for feedback-synthesis (major), user-interview-guide (major) and feature-request-triage (minor) all flag missing redaction or consent. The boundary also never says Priya does not contact customers or participants, although the skills say so ('Do not contact participants', 'Do not reply to customers').
issues.fix: Add: 'Redact names, contact details and account identifiers before quoting, and never record or quote a participant without consent. Never contact a customer or participant, reply to a request, or publish notes; draft for approval.'

issues.quote: You prioritise with the team's own goals and a stated method, show the inputs, and say which scores are guesses.
issues.problem: Combined with 'never invent ... an effort estimate', the persona has no answer when effort is missing. That is exactly the roadmap-prioritisation review's top issue: RICE cannot rank a blank.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: 'When effort is missing, rank on value, list the item as needs-sizing, ask the people doing the work for a size, and show how the order would change at small, medium or large effort, without filling the figure in.'

issues.quote: and what each option costs you
issues.problem: This reads as a promise of cost or effort figures. The boundaries forbid inventing effort estimates, and opportunity-brief lets effort be 'marked as a guess' without saying whose guess.
issues.fix: Change it to 'and what each option trades off, with effort only as your team sizes it'. Tighten opportunity-brief's 'or marked as a guess' to 'or the team's guess, labelled as such'.

issues.problem: Priya is in the operations category, and feature-request-triage and feedback-synthesis are recurring jobs by nature, but she has no standing work. Alex's voice-of-customer-pulse fills that slot for him.
issues.fix: Add an opt-in weekly 'request and feedback pulse' that is off until the owner says yes. It reads the connected sources, runs feature-request-triage with a dedupe log against the last run, and stages a draft. It should focus on request triage so it does not duplicate Alex's weekly theme rollup.

issues.quote: Bulk edit ranks first: 14 requests from 9 accounts, three of them on the top plan, and it blocks a job users do weekly.
issues.problem: It mirrors Alex's first sample ('Bulk import wins on reach: 340 accounts a quarter...'), so the two PMs sound alike. It also omits the strength label that voice_preferences promises ('evidence strength stated beside every claim').
issues.fix: Show the label and the gap, e.g. 'Bulk edit ranks first on strong evidence: 14 requests, 9 accounts, tickets and interviews both. Effort not yet sized; it stays first unless it runs past four weeks.' Or swap in a release-note sample, which Alex has none of.

issues.quote: Goal: tag 200 records in under a minute.
issues.problem: The identity and product-requirements-draft require a measurable goal with its current baseline and how it will be tracked. The sample gives a target with no baseline and no measurement.
issues.fix: Add the baseline and its source, e.g. 'Goal: tag 200 records in under a minute (today about 15 minutes, from two session recordings), tracked by the bulk_tag event.'

issues.quote: groups them into problems with counts, sources, and example quotes.
issues.problem: The merged feedback-synthesis now rates each theme strong, moderate or thin on fixed thresholds and redacts quotes. The day_one promise does not mention either, and the strength rating is what sets Priya apart.
issues.fix: Change it to '... groups them into problems with counts, sources, redacted example quotes, and a strong, moderate or thin rating on each.'

issues.quote: Clear, structured, and even-handed, with evidence strength stated beside every claim.
issues.problem: There is no guidance on response shape (answer first, how long, one question at a time). With founders and small teams, the eight skills' multi-question intake steps tend to produce long preambles.
issues.fix: Add: 'Answer or draft first, then at most one question; keep chat replies short and put detail in the artefact.'

clusters.job: Turn a batch of tickets, interview notes, survey answers or reviews into evidence-rated problem themes

members.note: Written for Priya: groups by problem, not solution; evidence table with Items | Accounts | Segments | Sources | Example quote; 'never drop feedback that disagrees'. Has no Claude-Code constructs. Its output vocabulary (strong/moderate/thin) is shared with opportunity-brief. Missing thresholds, a coding method, a coverage rule for missing metadata, redaction and survey handling.

Deepest method (thematic analysis, triangulation, survey interpretation, behaviour vs stated preference). As shipped it has the `/synthesize-research $ARGUMENTS` block and four ~~ connector placeholders, and PR #13 leaves the SKILL.md unchanged (only ATTRIBUTION.md changes). Its persona and opportunity-sizing sections duplicate other jobs.

Another is coding and counting in bash_exec for large exports, with a spot-check of about 10% of rows and the coded file attached. A coverage rule is needed for rows without account or segment data: join to a CRM or Sheets export where possible, otherwise report the share of rows with the field and do not break down below that coverage. The last is intake through run_block (HubSpot, Notion, Google Sheets, Airtable) or run_mcp_tool, with export or paste as the fallback. recommendations.notes:
What I checked. I read all eight live kit SKILL.md files, Priya's review notes, and the PR #13 copies of the grafted Toran packages, to see what the merges actually add. From the catalog I read, before rejecting or recommending them: product-assumption-testing, user-cohort-analysis, jobs-to-be-done, product-experiment-design, product-metrics-and-instrumentation, experiment-readout, funnel-conversion-analysis, voice-of-customer-loop, voice-of-customer-and-feedback, sensitive-data-safe-handling, product-launch-plan, product-discovery-and-user-research, product-prd-and-acceptance-criteria, weekly-ticket-themes and product-stakeholder-update. DEFERRED_SKILLS.md holds only the ads suite, so nothing product-related is deferred. I also read upstream sources that exist locally or were fetched and returned 200: phuryn/pm-skills at 8607e3b (brainstorm-experiments-existing, identify-assumptions-existing, prioritize-assumptions, pre-mortem, opportunity-solution-tree) and product-on-purpose/pm-skills at 1cef1a9 (iterate-pivot-decision and its TEMPLATE.md, measure-experiment-results, define-hypothesis, develop-adr, iterate-lessons-log). The role evidence comes from the GitLab handbook's Product Manager job family ('Defines success metrics pre-launch and conducts post-launch retrospectives', 'maintains deep expertise in usage data', 'Designs and runs experiments to validate strategic bets') and KORE1's PM job template ('track outcomes after launch', 'comfortable pulling your own analysis in SQL or a BI tool').

Coverage shape. The merged kit covers intake through spec through release notes well, but it stops at shipping. Nothing reads the result (feature-outcome-review). Nothing counts usage, even though the bio promises to use it (usage-evidence-pull). Nothing remembers decisions or requesters between sessions (product-decision-log, request-loop-closure). product-signal-digest and feature-outcome-review give the body the routines the review found missing. request-loop-closure needs feature-request-triage to save its requester registry with memory_store; add that to the triage fix if loop closure is accepted.

Considered and not recommended:
- jobs-to-be-done (unassigned, MIT). JTBD extraction tags already come into feedback-synthesis from customer-insight-research, and 5-why laddering into user-interview-guide. Its copy-pattern sections are shaped for marketing.
- opportunity-solution-tree (phuryn, MIT). Overlaps opportunity-brief plus roadmap-prioritisation. At most a reference file inside product-assumption-testing.
- Stakeholder and exec updates. Deliberately dropped, which the review supports. Hand off to Alex's product-exec-briefing.
- Competitor profiling. Hand off to Alex's product-market-and-competitor-read or to Nadia. opportunity-brief already verifies competitor claims.
- Launch/GTM planning. Belongs to Alex's product-launch-plan or Zara.
- A personal-data skill. The review's personal-data gap belongs in the persona body as a rule. The kit skills already carry redaction, and sensitive-data-safe-handling (Robin) is shaped around PCI and PHI in support work, so it is a poor fit.

Alex overlap. Alex's kit covers neighbouring ground: experiment design, metrics and instrumentation, a discovery roll-up and a launch plan. Every recommendation here is sized for Priya's small-team, evidence-first persona, and each names its hand-off to Alex or Quinn. The body still needs the Alex hand-off rule the review asked for. product-assumption-testing is also on Toran's list for Alex. If Alex's merge takes it, both experts should share one fixed copy. Its PR #13 copy is byte-identical to main and still contains $ARGUMENTS, so the fix is still needed.

The bio's 'what each option costs you' tension is not something a skill can fix; it is a body edit.

recommendations.name: Feature outcome review
recommendations.purpose: After a change ships, compare what happened with the spec's pre-declared goal, baseline and guardrail, add the feedback received since release, and recommend keep, iterate, roll back or keep watching for the team to decide.
recommendations.why: The kit runs from feedback to spec to release notes and then stops. The merged product-requirements-draft now sets a goal, baseline, instrumentation and a guardrail metric, but no skill reads them after launch, so the identity's 'how success will be measured' promise is never checked. Role standards put this step in the job. GitLab's PM job family says 'Defines success metrics pre-launch and conducts post-launch retrospectives', and KORE1's template says 'track outcomes after launch to learn what worked and what to change'. The work has natural checkpoints (30/60/90 days after release) that suit schedule_followup, which answers the review finding that Priya has no routines. The closest existing skills are shaped differently. Alex's product-launch-plan has a 90-day measure at GTM scope. Quinn's experiment-readout covers controlled tests only and says 'Do not call a before-and-after comparison an A/B test'. product-on-purpose's iterate-pivot-decision (Apache-2.0) explicitly 'weighs market feedback on something already shipped' and gives a verified template (current vs target table, evidence for and against, hypothesis review, options, dissent) that can be recast at feature scale.

source.ref: product-on-purpose/pm-skills skills/iterate-pivot-decision (template recast to feature scope; before/after validity checks grafted from catalog experiment-readout)

sketch: Inputs from memory first: use memory_search to find the approved spec (goal, baseline, target, guardrail, events, stop conditions) and the release-notes approval record (ship date, rollout %, plans). Then ask only for what is missing: a usage export or dashboard link, and the feedback received since release.

Read the numbers in bash_exec, using the same definition and window as the baseline. Show adoption among eligible accounts, the goal metric against its target, and the guardrail. Label every figure sourced or assumed. Refuse a verdict on a thin sample or a partial rollout, and name the volume or date that would settle it.

Before/after honesty (grafted from experiment-readout): list concurrent releases, seasonality, and pricing or channel shifts, and state that before/after shows change, not cause. Send cohort or causal questions to Quinn. Send a warranted controlled test to Alex's product-experiment-design.

Problem check: re-apply the feedback-synthesis thresholds to items about the original problem since release. Did the item count, account count or strength fall? Record any new complaints the change caused.

Recommendation block, recast from iterate-pivot-decision: a current vs target table; hypotheses marked validated, invalidated or untested; options (keep, iterate, roll back, keep watching); the recommendation; who decides; and any dissent. Never move the goal or target after seeing the data.
On a yes, offer schedule_followup for the next checkpoint and save the decision and a one-line lesson to memory. Never change flags, the roadmap or the tracker.

recommendations.name: Usage evidence pull
recommendations.purpose: Turn a usage or event export into sourced reach, frequency, adoption and baseline figures for one problem or backlog item, with definitions stated and thin samples flagged, so briefs, specs and rankings use counted numbers instead of guesses.
recommendations.why: Priya's bio says 'Give me feedback, interview notes, usage data', and three kit skills consume usage numbers. roadmap-prioritisation needs RICE reach, product-requirements-draft needs a baseline, and the opportunity-sizing guidance grafted into opportunity-brief says to 'use product analytics' to estimate addressable users. No kit skill says how to count them, and the merged feedback-synthesis only discusses triangulation with analytics as method. PM postings expect this directly: KORE1 asks for someone 'comfortable pulling your own analysis in SQL or a BI tool', and GitLab asks PMs to 'maintain deep expertise in usage data'. Quinn owns deep analytics (funnel-conversion-analysis, cohort-and-retention-analysis), and user-cohort-analysis is Toran-proposed for Quinn. Both are broader than Priya's need, which is a small, repeatable count with a clear hand-off. It fits the platform: bash_exec with pandas on a CSV/XLSX export, run_mcp_tool when an analytics MCP is connected, and a paste fallback.

source.ref: new; grafts the step-definition and visible-denominator rules from catalog funnel-conversion-analysis (Quinn) and the feature-adoption steps from catalog user-cohort-analysis (phuryn, MIT)

sketch: Frame the count: which job or feature, which event or proxy stands for it, and which entity counts (account or user, matching the counting unit saved by product-getting-started). Fix the window and the eligible population. If no event exists, stop and write the instrumentation gap as an input to product-requirements-draft.
Get the data from a connected analytics MCP, a CSV/XLSX export or a pasted view. When the data sits in a warehouse, draft a read-only query for the owner to run. Never ask for credentials.

Count in bash_exec and save the script. Report distinct accounts and users doing the task, frequency per active account, the weekly or monthly trend, the plan and segment split, and the share of eligible accounts. Keep denominators visible, along with data freshness and coverage.

One evidence card per item: definition, figure, window, source, refresh date, and a strength label on the same scale as feedback-synthesis. Mark thin samples and missing segments. Never extrapolate beyond the export.

Hand-offs: send cohort, retention, funnel or 'why did it move' questions to Quinn via consult_teammate. The figures feed roadmap-prioritisation reach, the opportunity-brief size section and the spec baseline.

recommendations.name: Assumption test plan
recommendations.purpose: When the evidence behind an opportunity is thin, map the value, usability, viability and feasibility assumptions, rank them by impact and evidence strength, and design the cheapest behavioural test for the riskiest, with pass and fail lines set in advance.
recommendations.why: The merged opportunity-brief adds a 'thin-evidence redirect' and product-requirements-draft adds an 'unvalidated-problem entry check'. Both need somewhere to send the user other than another round of interviews. GitLab's PM ladder expects PMs to 'design and run experiments to validate strategic bets'. Small teams, who are Priya's audience, rarely have A/B traffic, and Alex's product-experiment-design assumes a computed sample size. The unassigned catalog package product-assumption-testing (phuryn brainstorm-experiments-existing, MIT) supplies low-effort methods (fake door, Wizard of Oz, prototype task tests, spikes) and the right principle: 'Measure actual behavior, not users' opinions'. But it is 50 lines, still carries $ARGUMENTS, and its PR #13 copy is byte-identical to main. Its phuryn siblings identify-assumptions-existing and prioritize-assumptions (same repo and commit, MIT) add the four-risk framing and the impact × risk triage it lacks.

source.ref: product-assumption-testing (grafts: phuryn pm-product-discovery identify-assumptions-existing and prioritize-assumptions at the same commit)

sketch: Remove $ARGUMENTS and the course links. Rewrite the description to trigger on 'how can we test this cheaply', 'is this worth building', and a thin evidence rating handed over from opportunity-brief.

Assumption map (grafted from identify-assumptions-existing): the value, usability, viability and feasibility assumptions for one opportunity, each with its current evidence and strength label, taken from the brief and never invented.

Rank (grafted from prioritize-assumptions) by impact if wrong × how thin the evidence is, and test the high-impact, thin-evidence ones first. Hand feasibility spikes to engineering and leave them unsized.

One test card per assumption. Method: fake door, concierge or Wizard of Oz, prototype task test, pre-order or waitlist, or a count via usage-evidence-pull. Add the behavioural metric, pass and fail lines written before the test, what sample a small team can realistically get, and who must approve anything user-facing.

Guardrails: fake doors disclose and never charge, nothing goes live without approval, and participants get no dates. Tests with enough traffic for a controlled A/B go to Alex's product-experiment-design or Quinn's experiment-readout. Save each card and result to memory so opportunity-brief can re-rate the evidence.

recommendations.name: Product signal digest
recommendations.purpose: On a weekly or monthly routine, pull the feedback and requests that arrived since the last run, match them to the problems already saved, and report what is new, rising or fading, which decisions are due for review, and which shipped items still owe requesters an answer.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review found Priya 'has no routines for work that is naturally recurring', and preloads and routines are both empty. feedback-synthesis and feature-request-triage are single-batch methods with no memory of the previous period, so each run starts cold and cannot say what changed. Sasha's weekly-ticket-themes reports 'the change from the prior period', but only for support tickets. Alex's product-discovery-and-user-research has a 'Roll it up' mode that keeps 'a log of briefed themes so the same one is never rolled up twice without saying what is new since'. Priya has nothing like it, although her persona says 'silence is not satisfaction', which only a period-over-period view can check. The platform supports it with schedule_routine, memory_store/memory_search, and run_block readers (Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Airtable, Slack), with a paste fallback.

source.ref: new; grafts the 'Roll it up' rules from catalog product-discovery-and-user-research (Alex) and the prior-period comparison from catalog weekly-ticket-themes (Sasha)

sketch: Setup: read the source map and counting unit that product-getting-started saved. Confirm the cadence and recipients, and schedule_routine only on a yes. Log each source that could not be reached.

Delta: take the items that are new since the last run, dedupe them and match them to saved problems. For each theme show new, rising, steady or fading counts and accounts against the last saved digest, using the shared feedback-synthesis thresholds. Queue unmatched items for the next full synthesis instead of forcing them into a theme.

Flags: problems crossing a threshold; deal-blocker or churn signals, routed to Max or Riley; bugs, routed to Sasha; shipped items whose requesters are still waiting, handed to request-loop-closure; and decisions whose revisit trigger has fired.
A quiet period gets one line and is never padded. Redact personal data and never invent counts. Save the digest to memory as the baseline for the next run.

recommendations.name: Request loop closure
recommendations.purpose: When a requested change ships, is declined or is parked, match it to the accounts that asked and draft a short, honest note per account for the owning CS or sales person to approve and send.
recommendations.why: Toran's review names this gap for feature-request-triage: 'No single native requester-account-revenue counting or follow-up registry'. The merged triage skill names who should follow up to gather evidence, but nothing drafts the answer once the team decides. release-notes-draft writes to everyone, while the accounts that asked need a personal note, and declined or parked asks never appear in release notes at all. Feedback tools build this in (Canny and Productboard both notify the people who asked). Max's voice-of-customer-loop closes the loop from the field side ('what product said, and what the rep tells the account'), which needs a product-side answer to relay. Priya's boundaries fit this design: she never replies to customers, so she drafts for the owner, and sending goes through the platform approval flow.

source.ref: new; grafts 'close the loop back to the field' and 'any promise back to the account waits for your yes' from catalog voice-of-customer-loop (Max)

sketch: Inputs: the decision (shipped per the confirmed release-notes record, declined, or parked with its reason from product-decision-log) and the requester registry saved by feature-request-triage (account, owner, exact ask, date). Ask for a CSV when no registry exists.
Match requesters to the change. Flag partial matches, where what shipped is adjacent to what they asked, rather than claiming it solves their ask.

Draft each note in the customer's own words. Shipped: what they can now do, where to find it, and any plan or rollout limits. Declined: the honest reason and any workaround. Parked: what would reopen it. No 'coming soon', no dates, and no naming other customers without consent.
Group the drafts by owner (CS, sales, support) with an approval checklist. Create Gmail or HubSpot drafts only after the owner's yes, and log who was told what, and when.
Mark each request closed in memory so the digest and triage stop counting it as open.

recommendations.name: Product decision log
recommendations.purpose: Record each product decision the team makes (what was decided, by whom and when, the options considered, the evidence and its strength at the time, and what would reopen it) so later triage, ranking and briefs check past decisions before re-arguing them.
recommendations.why: The persona's central rule is 'You recommend; the team decides', yet no skill records the decision. opportunity-brief ends at 'Decision needed'. feature-request-triage's 'not now' bucket needs a reason and a revisit trigger. The merged roadmap-prioritisation's change note records moves, not decisions and their evidence. Without a log in memory, Priya will reopen settled questions every session. GitLab expects PMs to articulate 'the why behind roadmap decisions'. The dropped product-stakeholder-update (Anthropic knowledge-work-plugins, Apache-2.0, already in the catalog) has a 'Decision Documentation (ADRs)' section with Proposed/Accepted/Superseded status, context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered, and the advice to 'Write ADRs close to when the decision is made'. That section is worth salvaging even though the update workflow was rightly dropped.

source.ref: product-stakeholder-update, 'Decision Documentation (ADRs)' section only, recast for product decisions

sketch: Trigger on 'we decided', 'log this decision' and 'why did we say no to X'. Also run at the end of opportunity-brief, roadmap-prioritisation and feature-outcome-review, once the user reports the team's call.

Entry, recast from the ADR format: title; status (proposed, accepted or superseded); the decision in one sentence; who decided and when, as the user reports it and never inferred; the options considered and why each lost; the evidence, with strength labels and sources; the consequences accepted; and a revisit trigger stated as an observable condition, not a date.
Save each entry with memory_store and to an append-only workspace file. Run memory_search before any triage or ranking pass and surface conflicts, e.g. 'declined in May because …'.
Never record a decision the user did not state, never log Priya's recommendation as the decision, and supersede past entries rather than editing them.

recommendations.name: Spec pre-mortem
recommendations.purpose: Before a spec is approved or a change ships, assume it failed and work back to the risks. Sort them into real, overblown and unspoken, and give each launch-blocking risk an owner and a mitigation; the team sets the dates.
recommendations.why: The merged product-requirements-draft lists risks, stop conditions and a rollout, but it has no structured way to surface risks nobody is voicing. The pre-mortem is standard PM risk practice, and the upstream skill cites Meta/Instagram use. phuryn's pre-mortem (MIT, the same pinned commit as the other phuryn packages in the catalog) supplies the Tigers / Paper Tigers / Elephants split and launch-blocking / fast-follow / track urgency. Alex's product-launch-plan has a go/no-go gate, but at GTM scope. This is the lightest recommendation, and a reviewer could fold it into product-requirements-draft as a section instead.

source.ref: phuryn/pm-skills pm-execution/skills/pre-mortem

sketch: Platform fixes: remove $ARGUMENTS and the 'Save as PreMortem-[name]-[date].md' step, and write the result with write_workspace_file after approval.

Boundary fixes: replace 'Set a decision/completion date' with 'owner to set a date', since Priya names owners but never dates. Keep a competitive or market risk only with a source and date. Ask for the engineering and support views rather than inventing them.
Inputs: the draft or approved spec, the rollout plan and the known support impact.

Output: Tigers (backed by evidence), Paper Tigers (with why not), and Elephants (with how to check). Launch-blocking Tigers get a mitigation and a named owner, and accepted risks go back into the spec's risks and stop-conditions section.

proposal.summary: Quinn's kit today is the eight ORIGINAL placeholder skills. NICK added nothing for Quinn, and TORAN proposed three upstream packages. The proposal keeps an eight-skill kit but resolves three overlaps. First, metric-anomaly-detection folds into metric-movement-analysis. The two share triggers and part of a data-fault checklist, and the anomaly skill's detection-rule and baseline sections fix the movement skill's flaw of explaining noise. The merged description also covers setting an alert rule, so detection is not lost. Second, Toran's dataset-exploration folds into metric-definition-and-data-quality, renamed data-quality-and-profiling. Its data-access order, null thresholds, profile statistics and report layout graft onto the stronger ordered-test base. Its /explore-data slash command and ~~connector wiring are left behind, because PR #13 changes only ATTRIBUTION.md. Third, Toran's user-cohort-analysis, a much thinner generic outline, adds only a feature-adoption variant, a retention-heatmap output, a minimum of 3-4 cohorts and a qualitative follow-up line to cohort-and-retention-analysis. Toran's data-visualization is the one straight addition. Its red/green palette bug is fixed, and the edits are recorded in ATTRIBUTION.md, because a vendor re-run would overwrite them. Every surviving skill still needs the method content its review flags: a KPI definition sheet template, a way to set digest thresholds before seeing the data, detection and interval methods, and a stats script for funnels and experiments. The expert body needs a weekly digest routine written to the real routine schema, rules for working on the platform, and handoffs to Alex, Daniel, Theo, James, Riley and Lena. The weekly digest also has to be scoped against James's weekly business review and Maya's weekly marketing read, which share its triggers.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and maps one-to-one onto the kit, and the FACT/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN discipline carries through identity, voice and skills. The gaps are operational. There is no routine behind the tagline's weekly brief. The day-1 KPI definition sheet has no template in any skill. Nothing says where the data comes from or how outward sharing is approved. There are no teammate handoffs, although the kit overlaps skills owned by Alex, Daniel, Theo, James, Maya and Riley.
strengths: Identity is operational rather than aspirational: it lists the exact metric fields to record (formula, unit, grain, population, filters, timezone, source, data owner, refresh time, comparison period) and the pre-analysis checks, which the skills repeat.
Identity paragraph 3 (decompose, label FACT/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN, name one disproof test per hypothesis) is the exact spine of metric-movement-analysis, so persona and skill agree.
Voice sample 2 shows the refuse-to-publish behaviour with concrete reconciliation numbers (1,204 vs 1,087 starts, 117-account gap isolated, join keys listed) rather than a generic caution.

Boundaries are specific about fabrication, silent repair, hidden exclusions and correlation-as-cause, and the safety rules of all eight original skills match them. The three Toran packages have no safety section, so the grafts and the data-visualization fixes must carry these rules in.
body_review.kit_alignment: Identity paragraph 1 maps to kpi-analysis-getting-started, paragraph 2 to data-quality-and-profiling and weekly-kpi-digest, paragraph 3 to metric-movement-analysis, and paragraph 4 to cohort-and-retention-analysis, funnel-conversion-analysis and experiment-readout. Preloads and routines are empty, and day_one names no skill slugs, so no reference breaks under the proposed merges. Only the skills list changes: remove metric-anomaly-detection, rename metric-definition-and-data-quality to data-quality-and-profiling, and append data-visualization. Some promises have no skill or mechanism behind them. day_one[0] promises 'A KPI definition sheet' that no skill templates. The tagline's 'weekly decision brief' has no routine, and day_one[2] marks it 'on request'. The bio's 'flag material changes' has no scheduled check. The body never mentions charts, although the kit gains data-visualization.

issues.problem: The tagline promises 'turns them into a weekly decision brief', but no routine schedules weekly-kpi-digest, and nothing watches KPIs for material moves. Both jobs only happen if the user remembers to ask.
issues.fix: Add a `weekly-kpi-digest` routine in the RELEASE.md routine schema {key, title, prompt, crons, asks, session_mode}, e.g. crons ['H 8 * * 1'] and session_mode THREAD. The schema has no enable/off flag, so put the gating in `asks` and the prompt. The asks cover where the metrics and the KPI definition sheet live, the agreed thresholds, where to stage the draft, and the delivery time and timezone. The prompt stops and asks when there is no definition sheet or no agreed thresholds, then stages a dated draft and sends nothing. Like James's ops-weekly-review, it logs the reported week so the same week is never reported twice.
