recommendations.notes:
What I checked: the full SKILL.md of all eight kit skills and of the three Toran packages (dataset-exploration, data-visualization, user-cohort-analysis). I searched catalog_index.md and grepped every SKILL.md for SQL, forecasting, survey and segmentation coverage. I also read DEFERRED_SKILLS.md; nothing there fits Quinn, since the ads-* suite belongs to Marco's domain. I downloaded the remaining skills of Anthropic's knowledge-work-plugins `data` plugin at the pinned commit 1c7187c4 (Apache-2.0, LICENSE confirmed): analyze, write-query, sql-queries, validate-data, statistical-analysis, build-dashboard, data-context-extractor and create-viz. Every upstream URL below returned real content. The data-context-extractor reference files (skill-template.md, sql-dialects.md, domain-template.md) also exist upstream.

Coverage findings:
1) No skill anywhere in the catalog writes or runs SQL. This is the biggest gap for a data analyst. The 365 Data Science 2026 study of 855 US postings, cited by https://www.dataquest.io/blog/10-data-analysis-tools-for-entry-level-analysts/, found SQL in about 53% of data analyst postings, Python in 31%, Power BI in 29% and Tableau in 26%.
2) The merged data-quality-and-profiling skill already grafts dataset-exploration's access order and warehouse schema queries. When sql-and-data-queries is added, keep one access order in the SQL skill and have data-quality link to it, so the two don't diverge.
3) The upstream packages need the same fixes PR #13 applied to Toran's packages: drop the `/command` usage, `argument-hint`, `~~data warehouse` placeholders, `../../CONNECTORS.md` links and "open in browser". build-dashboard must lose its "create a realistic sample dataset" path, because it conflicts with Quinn's never-fabricate boundary. data-context-extractor's skill-zip packaging must become a workspace file plus memory.
4) Considered and not recommended:
   - Event-tracking and identity-stitching audit (Toran's "funnel/event-identity protocol" gap). funnel-conversion-analysis already validates events, and Alex's product-metrics-and-instrumentation writes the instrumentation spec. Add an anonymous-to-known identity-stitching check to funnel-conversion-analysis instead of a new skill.
   - RFM or clustering segmentation: overlaps Zara's icp-and-segmentation and Riley's customer-health-score.
   - A spreadsheet or xlsx skill: Anthropic's xlsx skill is not under a redistributable licence. DuckDB in the SQL skill reads Excel and CSV, and Google Sheets output goes through run_block.
   - A separate alerting skill: the unbacked 'flag material changes' promise is best fixed by a daily or weekly routine in quinn.yml that calls metric-movement-analysis and weekly-kpi-digest, not by a new skill.
5) If sql-and-data-queries and kpi-dashboard-build are added, the persona should say so: add a line to identity, and consider a day_one item for the data source map. Today the body never mentions SQL, dashboards or charts.
6) statistical-methods overlaps the stats scripts proposed for experiment-readout, funnel and movement. Skills route only to their own sibling files, so keep the per-skill scripts. statistical-methods should cover only the observational, descriptive and wording gaps.
7) Priority order is by impact: the two musts close gaps that affect every analysis Quinn delivers. The coulds (forecast pacing, survey analysis) extend the role, and neither is promised in the current persona.

recommendations.name: SQL and data queries
recommendations.purpose: Answer a data question by writing, running and checking read-only SQL on a connected warehouse, or on uploaded exports with DuckDB in the sandbox.
recommendations.why: SQL is the most-requested data analyst skill: about 53% of 855 US postings in the 365 Data Science 2026 study, cited by Dataquest. No catalog skill writes SQL; a grep of every SKILL.md found none. Toran's review lists 'End-to-end SQL analysis orchestration: analyze references sql-queries, which was not selected unchanged' as a remaining gap. Every kit skill (cohort, funnel, movement, digest) assumes the numbers already exist, and none says how to pull them. On the platform the skill runs as a warehouse query through run_mcp_tool, DuckDB through bash_exec on CSV, Parquet or Excel files, or a query handed to the user to run.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins data/skills/sql-queries (base) + write-query workflow + analyze question tiers, commit 1c7187c4

sketch: Intake: classify the question as quick lookup, full analysis or formal report (from analyze), confirm dialect and tables, and store the dialect and table map with memory_store.

Access order: warehouse MCP via run_mcp_tool with SELECT only (no DDL or DML), then files loaded into DuckDB via bash_exec, then a query handed to the user to run and paste back. This becomes the kit's single access order; data-quality-and-profiling links to it.

Query standards: one CTE per step, explicit columns, early and partition filters, complete periods only, a stated timezone, COUNT(DISTINCT) through joins, row counts before and after every join, and a control total against the source.

references/dialects.md (Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, DuckDB) and references/patterns.sql (cohort retention, ordered funnel within a window, ROW_NUMBER dedup, week over week with complete weeks, percent of total).

Guardrails: LIMIT on exploration, a BigQuery dry-run bytes estimate before large scans, aggregated output only with no row-level personal data, and the final .sql saved beside the result via write_workspace_file.
Output: the answer with its query, row counts, date range and as-of time. When the question grows, hand it to metric-movement-analysis, cohort-and-retention-analysis or funnel-conversion-analysis.

recommendations.name: Analysis QA and share gate
recommendations.purpose: Check a finished analysis (numbers, method, charts and claims) and mark it ready to share, share with caveats, or needs revision before anything leaves Quinn.
recommendations.why: Toran's review names 'a universal analysis QA gate' as a remaining gap. The merged data-quality-and-profiling skill checks input data, not the finished calculation, chart or narrative. The expert review found that nothing says how outward sharing is approved, and the platform brief requires drafts first, with approval before any external side effect. Upstream validate-data provides a pre-delivery checklist, a pitfall catalogue (join explosion, survivorship, partial periods, denominator shifting, average of averages, timezone mismatch, selection bias, Simpson's paradox, multiple comparisons), calculation spot-checks and a three-level verdict.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins data/skills/validate-data, commit 1c7187c4

sketch: Method review: question framing, population, the metric version against the KPI definition sheet, fairness of the comparison period, and whether any metric or segment was chosen after the result was seen.
Calculation spot-checks: scripts/spot_check.py in bash_exec independently recomputes two headline numbers and checks that subtotals sum, percentages add up and base periods are right.

Pitfall catalogue carried over from upstream, plus a claim check: every sentence is labelled FACT, HYPOTHESIS or OPEN, causal verbs appear only with a valid design, and chart honesty checks (bars start at zero, scales are consistent, titles match the data).
Disclosure check: cells below the owner-agreed minimum are suppressed, identifiers removed and personal data aggregated. Legal, privacy or material finance calls go to the named owner.

Verdict: Ready, Share with caveats (list the required caveats) or Needs revision (list prioritised fixes), plus the reproducibility template (question, sources as-of, definitions, method, limits, queries).
Share gate: drafts only. Use ask_question for approval before posting to Slack, Docs, Sheets or email, and log the approver, time and version with memory_store.

recommendations.name: Data source map and dictionary
recommendations.purpose: Record once where each metric's data lives and how to reach it, what the entities and IDs mean, and which rows are always excluded, then keep the record current.
recommendations.why: The expert review says 'Nothing says where the data comes from.' kpi-analysis-getting-started inventories files for each analysis. It keeps no durable map of connections, entity definitions (user, account or workspace), standard exclusions (test, internal or fraud rows), refresh times or known gotchas, and the weekly routine will need that map to fetch data unattended. Upstream data-context-extractor asks exactly these questions: entity disambiguation, primary identifiers, key metric formulas, data hygiene filters and common analyst mistakes. Its skill-zip output must be replaced with a workspace dictionary plus memory to fit the platform.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins data/skills/data-context-extractor (with references/domain-template.md, sql-dialects.md), commit 1c7187c4

sketch: Discovery: which system holds each KPI. Connect through connect_integration (Google Sheets, Airtable, HubSpot, Stripe blocks) or run_mcp_tool (warehouse, product analytics); fall back to a named export with its owner and cadence.
Entity sheet: definitions of user, account and organisation, ID fields, join keys, and identity-merge rules.
Standard filters and gotchas: test, internal and fraud flags, deleted states, source timezones, late-arrival windows, and historical versus current-state tables.
Per-source record: location, grain, primary key, refresh time, owner, access limits, and personal-data fields never to pull.
templates/data-dictionary.md written with write_workspace_file and mirrored in memory_store. The KPI definition sheet links each metric to its map entry.
Iteration mode: update an entry when a quality check fails or a definition changes, with a dated change log. Drop upstream's skill packaging and '~~' placeholders.

recommendations.name: KPI dashboard build
recommendations.purpose: Turn approved KPI definitions and query results into a self-contained HTML dashboard or a Google Sheets tracker that the weekly routine refreshes.
recommendations.why: Dashboards are a core analyst deliverable: Power BI appears in 29% and Tableau in 26% of US data analyst postings (365 Data Science 2026). In the kit, data-visualization produces single charts and weekly-kpi-digest a written digest; nothing builds a multi-KPI view with cards, trends and filters. Upstream build-dashboard supplies the layout, a KPI card pattern, Chart.js charts, filters and pre-aggregation limits. The catalog's unassigned product-metrics-dashboard-design (MIT) adds the metric-layer table (definition, source, visualisation, target, alert threshold) and a review cadence to graft in.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins data/skills/build-dashboard (base), commit 1c7187c4; graft metric-layer table from catalog product-metrics-dashboard-design (MIT)

sketch: Spec first: audience, 3 to 6 KPIs taken from the definition sheet, comparison rule, target, materiality threshold and filters, using the metric-layer table from product-metrics-dashboard-design.

Build: a single HTML file with embedded aggregated JSON only (no row-level data). KPI cards show current, prior, absolute and relative change, and an as-of date. Save it with write_workspace_file instead of opening a browser.
Alternative delivery: write a KPI tracker to Google Sheets via run_block after approval.
Remove upstream's 'create a realistic sample dataset' path. With no data, deliver the spec and an empty template labelled NO DATA.
Charts use data-visualization's corrected palette. Add a data-freshness banner and definition footnotes, and pass analysis-qa-and-share-gate before sharing.
Refresh: the weekly routine recomputes and re-renders into dated versions. Product-dashboard strategy questions go to Alex.

recommendations.name: Statistical methods for business data
recommendations.purpose: Choose and run the right descriptive statistic, outlier rule or significance test for observational KPI data, and word the result without overclaiming.
recommendations.why: After the merges, statistics live only inside experiment-readout (SRM, Welch and others), funnel-conversion-analysis (Wilson) and metric-movement-analysis (detection rule). Nothing covers describing a skewed distribution (mean against median, percentiles), an outlier policy that never auto-drops rows, testing whether segment A really differs from B outside an experiment, multiple-comparison control, or wording traps (Simpson's paradox, survivorship, ecological fallacy, false precision). Upstream statistical-analysis is a supporting skill that covers exactly these. Python appears in 31% of US postings, and scipy and statsmodels run in the sandbox.

source.ref: anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins data/skills/statistical-analysis, commit 1c7187c4

sketch: Descriptive defaults: always report mean and median together, plus p5, p25, p50, p75, p95, IQR and CV, and name the distribution's shape.
Outlier policy: detect with IQR, z-score or percentile rules, investigate as error, extreme or separate population, and report the effect of any exclusion. Never auto-remove.
Test chooser for observational comparisons (proportions, Welch, Mann-Whitney, chi-squared): effect size and confidence interval first, p-value second, with Holm correction and the count of tests run.
Wording rules tied to FACT/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN: correlation versus cause, Simpson's paradox, survivorship, ecological fallacy, and ranges instead of false precision.
scripts/stats_helpers.py: describe(), compare_proportions(), compare_means(), holm(). Controlled tests go to experiment-readout, and test design goes to Alex's product-experiment-design.

recommendations.name: KPI forecast and target pacing
recommendations.purpose: Project where a non-financial KPI will land by period end or a target date, with a backtested range, and state whether it is on pace.
recommendations.why: Weekly business reviews routinely ask 'will we hit target?'. weekly-kpi-digest compares against the target but projects nothing, and no catalog skill covers simple KPI forecasting: Daniel's budget-vs-actuals-and-reforecast is scoped to finance, and Max's and Omar's forecasts to pipeline. Upstream statistical-analysis has only a short forecasting section (naive, seasonal naive, linear trend, 'give ranges'), so this skill would be written new with a backtest script.

source.ref: new; the statistical-analysis forecasting section (Apache-2.0) may seed it with attribution

sketch: Scope: product and operations KPIs only. Revenue, cash and budget go to Daniel; pipeline and bookings go to Max or Omar.
Method ladder: naive, seasonal naive, drift, then ETS (statsmodels). Backtest on held-out periods and keep the simplest model that beats naive on MASE.
Output: a point forecast with 80% and 95% intervals, the run rate required to hit target, and a pace status (on, at risk or off) under a rule agreed before the data is read.
scripts/forecast.py for backtests and intervals in bash_exec. Use no seasonal model with fewer than two full cycles of history.
Caveats: definition changes, structural breaks and short history. Log each forecast in memory and score it against actuals in the next digest.

recommendations.name: Survey data analysis
recommendations.purpose: Analyse closed-ended customer or market survey results with response rates, bases, margins of error, weighting and small-base suppression.
recommendations.why: Quinn's role and category include research. The catalog covers qualitative synthesis (Priya's feedback-synthesis; the unassigned product-research-synthesis) and HR engagement surveys (Ines's engagement-survey-readout), but nothing analyses quantitative customer or market survey data. Professional practice (AAPOR Standard Definitions and disclosure code) expects the response rate definition, sample, weighting and precision to be reported. The same data checks (speeders, straight-liners, duplicates) fit Quinn's show-every-exclusion discipline.

source.ref: new

sketch: Intake: questionnaire, sampling frame, fielding dates, invitations and completes, and the response rate definition used.
Data checks: duplicates, speeders, straight-liners, partials and failed attention checks, showing the effect of each exclusion.
Weighting only to population margins the owner supplies (raking), reporting the design effect and effective base.
Results: cross-tabs with bases, confidence intervals and margin of error, NPS with an interval, Likert items shown as distributions and not only means, and bases below the agreed minimum suppressed.
scripts/survey_tabs.py for weighted tables and intervals. Open-ended answers go to Priya or Alex for coding, and a cross-sectional survey never supports causal claims.

proposal.summary:
Remy's live kit is two ORIGINAL skills that follow his persona almost word for word: lifecycle-email-map and email-deliverability-guardrails. NICK's PR 2 added nothing for him. Maya's nurture-sequence-build-and-readout still overlaps both skills, and her weekly-marketing-read overlaps his weekly routine. TORAN proposed three Corey Haines packages instead: product-marketing-context, lifecycle-email-marketing and marketing-copy-editing, none as strong as Remy's originals. PR #13 only relabels related-skill names that are not installed and renames product-marketing-context's slash command. It leaves the `.agents/product-marketing.md` lookups in place. The main call is to merge lifecycle-email-marketing into lifecycle-email-map, with the map as the base. From lifecycle-email-marketing, carry over:
- its references/email-types.md audit catalogue, rewritten trigger-first: rows for trial ending and upgrade to paid, new customers, higher-plan limits, failed payment, renewal, invites and win-back;
- a pre-signup moment for people who opted in but are not yet users;
- its per-email output block, the preview-text guidance and its named inputs.

Drop its day-range cadences, its curiosity, urgency and 'We miss you' templates, and its six vendor API guides. The merged map also gains a mode for reviewing an email someone already wrote. email-deliverability-guardrails stays as a unique keep and gains thresholds, the bulk-sender rules and a consent blocker that hands off to Lena or counsel. product-marketing-context and marketing-copy-editing leave Remy's kit. Maria is the natural owner of copy-editing. Whether product-marketing-context has an owner at all is for the Maya and Zara reviews to decide, because Maya's messaging-and-tone-matrix and getting-started already capture most of it. The proposed kit is three skills: a new lifecycle-email-getting-started, the merged map and the fixed guardrails. Body changes, in order of weight:
1. Scope the 48-hour cap, including abandoned-cart flows and cross-programme counting.
2. Make the weekly routine report complaints and bounces instead of opens, and save each read.
3. Fill the empty day_one.
4. Add an approval and consent boundary.
5. Name the teammate edges.

body_review.summary:
The persona is sharp and opinionated, and its identity and bio match the two ORIGINAL skills almost line for line: map before writing, emails only on triggers, partial cancellation, exits on every sequence, the list before DNS. The gaps are around the edges:
- The blanket 48-hour cap in identity would conflict with the merged map's billing, trial and cart rows.
- The weekly routine leads with opens, never reports complaints or bounces, and never saves the read it compares against.
- day_one and preloads are empty.
- The boundaries have no drafts-by-default rule or approval gate, no consent or legal handoff and no teammate edges.
strengths: Identity states a real point of view in testable rules: 'if a moment has no trigger you can detect, you say so rather than filling the gap with a timed send'; partial cancellation; one goal, one link.
The win-back stance is specific and enforceable: no guilt, no false scarcity, no 'we miss you', always an easy way out. This is exactly what justifies dropping Toran's re-engagement templates.
Deliverability is framed as a list problem first, with the rule to stop on a vague list origin, which email-deliverability-guardrails implements.
The anti-fabrication rule includes a working convention: leave a marked gap and list what is missing.
The routine prompt has good discipline: a fixed comparison period, a source on every number, 'unclear, not guessed', never the same week twice, and a quiet-week format.
The voice samples are short and anchored in behaviour, and each includes an exit ('reply 'stop' and I'll leave you alone').
body_review.kit_alignment:
No body field names a skill slug. Merging lifecycle-email-marketing into lifecycle-email-map and leaving out product-marketing-context and marketing-copy-editing therefore breaks no reference. The proposed map and guardrails cover the bio's promises: a map, then drafts; a list and domain check before bulk sends; an exit on every sequence. Four things need to change along with the kit:
1. The identity's blanket 48-hour cap must match the merged map's scoped cap, because failed-payment, trial-ending and cart-abandonment rows now come into the map.
2. The map row described in the identity should include the exit/cancel column that the merged table adds.
3. The lifecycle-performance-read routine has no backing skill except the map's new 'Measure it' section. It should read that section's per-email metric and holdout, and report complaints and bounces against the guardrails thresholds. Maya's weekly-marketing-read already uses the right email columns (delivered, bounced, clicks, conversions or replies, unsubscribes, spam complaints, list growth; opens only as a health check), and the routine should mirror them so the two experts agree when both are hired.
4. day_one is empty, and the new lifecycle-email-getting-started should become its first entry.

Empty preloads are acceptable: the only email-adjacent catalog agents (email-address-finder, personalized-morning-coffee-newsletter) are prospecting or personal-digest tools, not lifecycle ones.

issues.quote: you never queue more than one automated email in 48 hours
issues.problem: The cap has no exemptions. The review flagged the same cap in lifecycle-email-map: it would delay or drop time-critical sends (failed payment, trial ending, receipts, invite reminders) and break a standard abandoned-cart series. The merged map now includes all of these from email-types.md and the ecommerce moments. There is also no rule for when two triggers collide, and nothing says newsletters and campaigns count toward the cap. The identity would override the skill fix.
issues.fix: Reword: 'you never queue more than one automated marketing or nurture email in 48 hours, counting newsletters and campaigns. Transactional and time-critical notices (receipts, failed payment, trial ending) are exempt. A recovery flow the person started, such as an abandoned cart or checkout, keeps its own short spacing. When two triggers collide, the higher-intent one sends and the other is re-queued or cancelled.'

issues.quote: Report what sent, what it did — opens, clicks, replies, unsubscribes, and whatever conversion the user actually cares about
issues.problem: The routine leads with opens and never reports complaints or bounces. That contradicts the identity ('you watch complaints rather than opens') and email-deliverability-guardrails ('Open rates have been unreliable since mail clients started pre-fetching images'). 'A subject line worth retiring' will then be judged on inflated opens.
issues.fix: Report delivered, hard and soft bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes, clicks, replies and each email's conversion event against the holdout or the prior week, matching the email columns in Maya's weekly-marketing-read. Treat opens only as a health check. Any complaint or bounce rate over the guardrails thresholds goes at the top of the report and triggers an email-deliverability-guardrails check before the next send.

issues.problem: There are no day-one deliverables and no getting-started skill, so a new hire gets no first artefact and no intake. Every NICK expert and most ORIGINAL experts have both (e.g. paid-ads-getting-started, communications-getting-started).
issues.fix:
Add three entries:
- 'Your lifecycle email map' (day 1): the activation event, what already sends, and one row per email with trigger, delay, exit and metric, gaps marked.
- 'A go/no-go on your next send' (on request): list origin, consent, complaint and bounce rates, domain setup.
- 'How last week's lifecycle email did' (weekly, from the routine).
Back the first entry with lifecycle-email-getting-started.

issues.quote: never send a sequence without an exit
issues.problem: The wording implies that Remy sends. No boundary says drafts are the default, or that nothing is sent, scheduled, uploaded to an email platform (ESP) or suppressed without the owner's yes, although the platform requires approval for outward actions. There is also no consent boundary: identity says to stop on a vague list origin, but a missing GDPR/PECR/CASL/CAN-SPAM basis has no handoff to counsel or Lena.
issues.fix: Rewrite: 'Drafts by default: nothing sends, schedules, uploads a list or changes a suppression list without the owner's yes on that specific send. Never hand over a sequence without an exit. Never send to a list whose origin or consent basis is unclear. Consent questions go to Lena or counsel and are never answered as legal advice.'

issues.quote: You are Remy, a lifecycle email specialist.
issues.fix: Add one short paragraph: 'Cold outreach goes to Max, 1:1 renewal and account messages go to Riley, positioning and campaign messaging come from Maya or Zara, page copy goes to Maria, and consent questions go to Lena or counsel. You own which automated emails exist and what triggers them. When Maya is on the team, her single-segment nurture experiments run inside your map, and her weekly read takes your lifecycle numbers rather than recomputing them.'

issues.quote: plus the send calendar and your previous read
issues.problem: The routine depends on 'your previous read' and 'Never report the same week twice', but never tells Remy to save a read. Nothing persists, so next week has nothing to compare against or deduplicate. It also has no fallback when no email source is connected, and does not say the read lands as a draft. Maya's weekly routine covers all three.
issues.fix: Add: 'Check your saved log first. After reporting, save the read with its dates using memory_store or write_workspace_file. With no connected ESP or HubSpot, ask for the export and name the figures that are missing. The read lands as a draft where the owner chose.'

issues.quote: First the map: one row per email with the moment, the trigger, the single goal, the subject line and the one action. Then the drafts.
issues.problem: The identity makes exits mandatory, but the map row it describes has no exit or cancel column. It also lacks the delay and success-metric columns that the merged lifecycle-email-map adds, so the persona and the skill will disagree about the table.
issues.fix: '...one row per email with the moment, the trigger, the delay, the single goal, the exit that cancels it, the subject line, the one action and the metric that says it worked.'

issues.quote: Want me to move your old file across so you can see?

proposed.name: Lifecycle email map
proposed.description: Use when someone asks for an email sequence, drip, onboarding, billing, nurture or win-back emails, an audit of what already sends, or a review of an existing email: map which emails should exist to detectable triggers, with delay, exit and success metric per row, then draft only the emails the map keeps.
proposed.rationale:
The base is the much stronger skill and is the persona in skill form. Toran's own kit rationale says 'No bespoke frequency or cancellation rules are imposed on the upstream source', and those rules are exactly what Remy is hired for. The upstream package's lasting value is breadth: the billing, trial, invite, renewal, NPS and win-back rows in email-types.md, which the review names as the base's top gap. So carry that catalogue in as a reference, rewritten trigger-first, and keep the base's stance.

Fixes the review asks for that neither source supplies:
1. Scope the 48-hour cap to marketing and nurture sends, counting newsletters and campaigns. Exempt transactional and time-critical notices, and let a recovery flow the person started (abandoned cart or checkout) keep its own short spacing. Add a collision rule: the higher-intent trigger wins, and the other is re-queued or cancelled.
2. Add ecommerce moments (cart and browse abandonment, post-purchase, replenishment) and a note on the plain-text default by business model: plain text for B2B and product nudges, a light template for retail, always with a plain-text part.
3. Add a 'Measure it' section: one conversion event per email, a holdout where the list allows, a readout date feeding the lifecycle-performance-read routine, and opens used only as a health check.
4. Add a transactional/marketing column that decides how unsubscribes apply.
5. End with an email-deliverability-guardrails check and the owner's approval before anything is built in the ESP. With no ESP connected, export the map and drafts to a workspace file or CSV.
6. Add a short 'Reviewing an email someone already wrote' mode. Check the draft against the 'Writing each one' rules plus trigger, exit and consent, then return it with each change marked and a one-line reason, on the pattern of brand-voice-guide's 'Checking a draft'. This covers the email line-editing that marketing-copy-editing would otherwise supply.
7. Keep the no-welcome-discount default, but include an offer when the owner asks for one and supplies its terms.
8. State the scope: the map covers the emails only. Payment retry logic and in-app cancel flows are out of scope. churn-prevention is the catalog's (unassigned) home for dunning mechanics.

No other in-scope ref does a pre-send go/no-go; the review says lifecycle-email-marketing has 'No deliverability or legal content at all'. It has a stance and output contract (go/no-go on the first line, blockers with evidence, warnings, 'What you could not check') that match Remy word for word. Fixes before shipping:
1. A threshold table with warn and block levels: e.g. Gmail/Yahoo spam rate blocked at 0.3% with an aim under 0.1%, hard bounces around 2%, and an unsubscribe spike.
2. The 2024-25 Gmail/Yahoo/Outlook bulk-sender rules: DMARC alignment, RFC 8058 one-click List-Unsubscribe, unsubscribes honoured within two days.
3. A consent and legal line as a blocker: consent basis and date, postal address, a working opt-out, suppressions applied. It hands off to Lena (compliance-escalation-brief) or counsel.

recommendations.notes:
What I read: the brief, Remy's dossier and expert file, the two ORIGINAL kit skills, the dropped lifecycle-email-marketing package (SKILL.md, references/email-types.md, copy-guidelines.md, tools/integrations/*), and every catalog neighbour I cite: weekly-marketing-read, nurture-sequence-build-and-readout, product-experiment-design, experiment-readout and churn-prevention with its dunning-playbook.md. I also checked the platform blocks (/home/user/AutoGPT/autogpt_platform/backend/backend/blocks). The merged map and guardrails do not exist yet, so I judged gaps against the verified merge description plus the ORIGINAL files. If the merged map's 'Measure it' section ends up holding holdout sizing or a test design, trim recommendation 3.

Coverage and boundaries:
(1) Maya (the marketing generalist) overlaps Remy most. Her nurture-sequence-build-and-readout covers segment, experiment and readout for a single nurture, and her weekly-marketing-read covers the whole marketing week. I recommend Remy-specific forks, not assigning both of hers. Assigning both would give two experts competing Monday reads and two ways to build a sequence. The fork should keep Maya's email column set word for word so the two reads agree when both are hired.
(2) churn-prevention (unassigned, MIT) should not be assigned whole. Its cancel-flow UI, save offers and health score belong to Robin and Riley. Only the dunning email side fits Remy (recommendation 7).
(3) Rejected sources:
- borghei/Claude-Skills email-template-builder: licence is MIT + Commons Clause, so it is not redistribution-compatible, and it builds React Email/MJML codebases.
- coreyhaines31 ab-testing: aimed at web pages, and the catalog already has the method.
- Deferred list: nothing email-related. referrals has a source-quality defect.
- brand-voice-guide (Jules, Maria): not needed, because the new getting-started skill already collects pasted sent emails for voice, and Maya has messaging-and-tone-matrix.
(4) Not recommended now, but a later candidate: list growth, preference centre and double opt-in. The merged guardrails' bulk-sender rules and consent blocker already cover one-click unsubscribe and the consent basis. If Remy is meant to own signup capture, upstream coreyhaines31 popups, lead-magnets and signup (MIT) all resolve at pinned commit 5b2c0007766c6a1cf1d53fd8fc73e979e0821022.
(5) Platform limits: there is no ESP-native block. What exists: HubSpot contact, company and engagement; Gmail; AgentMail drafts; the SMTP email_block; ZeroBounce; ScreenshotOne; and a Stripe subscription trigger (customer.subscription.*). So every ESP build, pull or activation goes through run_mcp_tool or a pasted export, and every skill below needs a CSV fallback. There is no SMS block, so recommendation 8 can only produce drafts.
(6) Job-role grounding comes from web search over lifecycle/email marketing manager postings and templates (100hires, G2 Learn, the Greenhouse Software and Roku Email & Lifecycle Marketing Manager listings). They repeatedly name: campaign production 'from copywriting, segmentation, testing, QA, launch to performance analysis'; QA of links, tracking and cross-device rendering; A/B testing of subject lines, send times, content, offers and flows; segmentation from behavioural and lifecycle data; newsletters and product announcements; and reporting on deliverability, clicks, conversions, revenue and list growth.

recommendations.name: Email pre-send QA
recommendations.purpose: Check a built email or flow step before it goes live: links, tracking, merge fields, size and rendering, accessibility, the compliance footer, the audience, and an approved test send.
recommendations.why: Postings ask the email manager to 'manage email QA & deployment processes to ensure accurate content, design, segmentation, and cross-device rendering' and to 'maintain campaign QA across links, tracking, segmentation, targeting, creative, and deployment'. In the kit, guardrails checks the list, the domain and sender basics, and the map checks preview text and merge fallbacks in the draft. Nothing checks the HTML the ESP will actually send. In an automated flow, a broken link or bare merge tag keeps sending until someone notices. bash_exec can lint HTML and resolve links, and ScreenshotOne can capture a hosted 'view in browser' page.
sketch: Inputs, named up front: the HTML (pasted, as a file, or exported through the ESP MCP), the plain-text part, subject and preview, the map row it belongs to, the UTM convention, and the approved seed addresses. List anything missing.
Test merge fields against edge-case records: missing first name, a very long company name, non-ASCII text, and the wrong locale. Render each in the sandbox and show the result.

Rendering and accessibility: mobile width, dark-mode inversion risks, how it reads with images off, the lang attribute, contrast, minimum font size and link text. Screenshot the hosted version when a URL exists; otherwise list the item under 'could not check'. Never claim client-by-client rendering without seed or Litmus data.
Audience check: the send's segment matches the map row's trigger. Unsubscribed, bounced and complained addresses, and anyone excluded by the cap, are suppressed.

Hand back pass or fail per check, the fix for each failure, and a 'could not check' list. Test sends go only to approved seed addresses, via a Gmail or AgentMail draft after the user approves. Log the approval before anything goes live.

recommendations.name: Email test and holdout design
recommendations.purpose: Design and read email A/B tests and flow holdouts on clicks, conversions, replies or revenue, never opens, with the sample size and decision bands set before anything sends.
recommendations.why: 'Design and execute rigorous A/B testing programs across subject lines, send times, content, design, and segmentation' and 'A/B tests across messaging, creative, segmentation, timing, offers, and flows' are standard lines in lifecycle postings. The merged map's 'Measure it' names a metric and a holdout for each email but not how to size, randomise or read a test. The only testing guidance in the dropped package (copy-guidelines.md) benchmarks on open rate, which Apple Mail Privacy Protection has broken. The catalog already has a sound method in product-experiment-design (Alex, the product manager) and experiment-readout (Quinn, the data analyst). Both are built for product experiments; neither covers email-specific traps such as ESP auto-winner-on-opens or holdouts leaking into other programmes.

source.ref: product-experiment-design (alex) for the design, sample size and precommitted bands; experiment-readout (quinn) for sample-ratio, guardrail and limits checks. Adapt both to email.

sketch: Test one variable per test and decide on one metric: conversion, click-to-conversion, revenue per recipient or reply rate. Opens are barred as a decision metric, and so is any ESP 'auto-send the winner after 2 hours on opens' setting.

Compute the sample size and duration in bash_exec from the baseline and the minimum detectable effect, at 95% significance and 80% power. If the segment cannot reach that size, say so and offer a longer run, a bigger change, or no test.

Flow holdouts: a random 5-10% who get none of the flow's emails, held for the flow's full window and excluded from overlapping programmes. Report incremental lift against the holdout, not against last month.
Write the ship, extend and kill bands with numbers before launch, save them with memory_store, and never move them afterwards.

Readout: check the sample ratio, check guardrails (unsubscribes, complaints and hard bounces against the guardrails thresholds), give the effect with its interval, then make the call. Pass deeper statistics to Quinn through consult_teammate when Quinn is hired.
Write the result back to the map row's 'Measure it' line and the weekly performance read, and log it in a saved test register so the same test is not run twice.

recommendations.name: Email audience segmentation
recommendations.purpose: Turn an ESP or CRM export into lifecycle-stage and engagement segments with counts, plus a sunset group and a suppression file, each defined in the user's ESP filter terms.
recommendations.why: Postings ask the manager to 'create and manage customer segmentation and targeting strategies' and to 'segment audiences and personalize messaging using behavioral, lifecycle, and engagement data'. The merged guardrails sets the rules (engagement judged without opens, re-permission before suppressing, hard-bounce removal) but does not build the segments. The map names moments but not who is in each one or how many people that is. Maya's nurture skill segments one nurture at a time; Zara's icp-and-segmentation is about who to sell to (ICP), not engagement. CSV work in the sandbox suits the platform, and HubSpot is available through run_block.
sketch: Inputs, named up front: email, signup date, last click, last purchase or product activity, plan or stage, consent source and date, bounce and complaint flags, country or timezone. Pull them from the ESP MCP or HubSpot, or take a pasted CSV.

Engagement tiers built from clicks, replies, purchases and product activity, never opens alone: active, lapsing and dormant, with the cut-offs stated. Add RFM tiers for shops and trial, activated, paid, at-risk and churned stages for SaaS.
Compute the counts and a segment-overlap matrix in bash_exec. Flag any segment too small to test or to justify its own email.

Send the sunset group to the guardrails re-permission step. Hard bounces, complaints and unsubscribes go into a suppression CSV. Rows with unknown consent are flagged and handed to Lena (compliance), never mailed.

Hand back a table of segment name, plain-words rule, ESP filter expression, count and data-as-of date, and write the suppression file to the workspace. Nothing is uploaded or synced to the ESP or CRM without approval.
Personal data stays in workspace files. Memory stores only the segment definitions, never contact rows.

Translate the spec into the user's ESP vocabulary, using references/: Customer.io campaigns and segments, Klaviyo flows, HubSpot workflows, Mailchimp journeys. For an unlisted ESP, fall back to a plain spec.
A merge-field source map: for each field, the data source and its fallback text, so QA can test it.

proposal.summary: Riley's kit has no NICK or open-PR versions. It is eight ORIGINAL CSM placeholders (all needing work, renewal-readiness-review most of all) plus four TORAN support and research packages that Toran proposed in their place. Toran's four do not cover health, onboarding, renewal or expansion, so I keep all eight originals as the backbone and make two merges. First, renewal-touchpoint-draft absorbs customer-response-drafting's tone, bad-news and follow-up content and is renamed customer-touchpoint-draft, because day_one promises touchpoint drafts for at-risk and onboarding accounts too. renewal-touchpoint-draft has a live marketplace listing, so the rename also needs an explicit retirement of the old slug. Second, churn-risk-review takes customer-insight-research's churn-reason segmentation and confidence rules, and the rest of that marketing research playbook leaves the kit. customer-support-research joins as a research skill shared with Robin and Sasha. customer-escalation joins only for account-level escalations to product or leadership; its review would otherwise merge it into Robin's escalations-and-incidents. That gives a 10-skill kit. PR #13 leaves both SKILL.md files unchanged, so their slash-command H1s and ~~ placeholders still need fixing. The biggest cross-expert problem: Robin's account-health-and-qbrs (40/30/30) and Max's renewal-expansion-and-qbr (40/20/20/20) repeat Riley's health, churn and renewal jobs, each with one fixed-weight score and bare triggers ('account health', 'health score', 'churn risk'). Robin's onboarding-and-adoption also repeats customer-onboarding-plan. Riley's identity shows each health component separately, which those single scores conflict with, so Riley's versions should be canonical.

body_review.summary: A sharp, evidence-first CSM persona whose identity lines up with the eight original skills almost sentence for sentence. The gaps are operational. There are no routines, though the job runs on a calendar. The boundaries are narrower than the commitments the identity itself makes. There are no stated handoffs to the sales, support, contracts and product teammates whose skills overlap Riley's.
strengths: The identity's two signal rules are each enforced somewhere in the kit. 'A quiet account is not automatically healthy' matches customer-success-getting-started ('Do not ... treat silence as proof of health') and customer-health-score ('Do not convert a missing value to zero or healthy'). '... and a busy support queue is not automatically a churn risk' matches churn-risk-review ('Do not label an account at risk only because it is quiet or has support tickets').

The identity requires a health view split into components ('You show adoption, outcomes, support, relationship, and commercial readiness separately'). That is more rigorous than the single 0-100 scores at fixed 40/30/30 and 40/20/20/20 weights in Robin's account-health-and-qbrs and Max's renewal-expansion-and-qbr, and it is a clear reason for Riley to own account health.

voice_samples[0] ('Risk is rising, not confirmed ... Next step: ask the admin what changed') shows fact versus interpretation and ends on one next check, exactly as churn-risk-review's 'the smallest next check' asks.
bio, identity and boundaries agree on draft-only outreach. Every original skill that touches customer communication repeats it (seven of eight; customer-health-score has no outreach step).
The persona is clearly about accounts rather than tickets, which separates Riley from Robin and Sasha.
body_review.kit_alignment: No routine, preload or day_one entry names a skill slug. Inside riley.yml, renaming renewal-touchpoint-draft to customer-touchpoint-draft and dropping customer-response-drafting and customer-insight-research therefore breaks nothing. The rename still needs catalog.yml and release.json updates, plus an explicit retirements entry for the published renewal-touchpoint-draft listing. day_one[0] (an auditable health model) maps to customer-health-score, but that skill never saves the model or earlier scores, so the audit promise is only half kept. day_one[1] promises a touchpoint draft for at-risk, onboarding or renewal accounts. Today only the renewal-specific skill exists, and the proposed customer-touchpoint-draft closes that gap. The identity covers health, churn, onboarding, renewal, expansion and touchpoints. It says nothing about internal escalation or researching a customer's question, which are the jobs of the two TORAN additions. routines and preloads are empty.

issues.quote: Never invent account health, usage, sentiment, contract terms, or customer outcomes. Draft outreach for approval and never send it yourself.
issues.problem: Covers only invention and sending. It leaves out several things: the commitments the identity itself forbids ('never promise adoption, renewal, savings, or product changes'); price, discount and concession authority, which renewal-touchpoint-draft and expansion-opportunity-brief gate on owner wording; CRM edits, which customer-success-getting-started forbids ('edit customer records'); cross-customer confidentiality, which matters once customer-support-research's Tier 5 'Analogous customers' is in the kit; and posting escalations.
issues.fix: Append: 'Never quote a price, discount, concession, term or roadmap date without the authorised owner's wording. Never edit CRM or customer records. Never put one customer's name, data or terms into another customer's material. Stage internal escalations for approval before posting.'

issues.problem: Customer success runs on a calendar: notice dates, weekly risk movement, success-plan reviews. With no routine, every review waits to be asked for, so a notice date can pass unseen. That is the most expensive failure the kit exists to prevent. The customer-success-getting-started eval lists the missing 'routine suggestion (e.g. a weekly portfolio review via schedule_routine)'.
issues.fix: Add two draft-only routines in the schema's shape (key, title, prompt, crons, asks, session_mode: THREAD). (1) key weekly-portfolio-risk-sweep, cron 'H 8 * * 1': rescore with the saved customer-health-score model, run churn-risk-review only on accounts whose component moved, and stay quiet with one line when nothing changed. Asks: where the account list and usage export live, and the timezone. (2) key renewal-window-check, weekly: list renewals crossing 120/90/60/30 days before notice, run renewal-readiness-review, and stage customer-touchpoint-draft drafts for approval. Asks: where contract end and notice dates live. Both routines only stage drafts and never send.

issues.quote: Turns one at-risk, onboarding, or renewal account into an owner-led plan and a touchpoint draft for your approval.
issues.problem: The only drafting skill in today's kit is renewal-touchpoint-draft ('Use this after the renewal record has been checked'). churn-risk-review ('Draft any message for approval') and customer-onboarding-plan ('Draft customer updates for approval') ask for drafts but have no drafting procedure. customer-success-plan only says 'do not send it without owner approval'. At-risk and onboarding touchpoints are therefore promised with nothing behind them.
issues.fix: Adopt the merged customer-touchpoint-draft (renewal stage, onboarding nudge, risk recovery, success review). If the reviewer keeps renewal-touchpoint-draft as it is, narrow this line to renewal accounts.

issues.quote: After you share account data, defines each signal, source, date range, weight, and missing-data rule before scoring anyone.
issues.problem: The title promises a model 'your team can audit', but customer-health-score keeps the model in chat only. It never stores earlier scores, yet reports 'material change since the last period', and it never checks the model against actual renewals and churn.
issues.fix: Fix the skill: write health_model and period score files to the workspace, save the model version with memory_store, and calibrate against the last 2-4 quarters. Then add 'saved as a model file your team can review and re-run' to this description (it stays under the 240-character limit).

issues.quote: You only raise an expansion idea when usage, need, or an explicit request supports it. You draft touchpoints for approval; you do not send them.
issues.problem: Names no teammate handoffs, although several teammates own the neighbouring work: Max (renewal-expansion-and-qbr), Jordan (renewal-negotiation-brief), Robin and Sasha (ticket replies, bug and incident escalation), Ellis (contract key-term extraction) and Priya (feedback-synthesis). Riley may therefore start pricing, read contracts, fix tickets or run broad VOC research itself.
issues.fix: Add: 'Pricing, quotes and negotiation go to the commercial owner (Max or Jordan). Contract dates and clauses come from Ellis's extraction or the contract owner. Ticket fixes and bug reports go to support (Robin or Sasha). You escalate account-level risk internally with a sourced brief, and you consult Priya for research across many customers.'

issues.quote: Weekly active users fell from 18 to 7 across four weeks, and the admin missed two onboarding sessions.
issues.problem: The identity says 'Every signal carries its source and date range', yet the flagship sample gives a duration but no source and no dates.
issues.fix: Add the source and window, e.g. 'Weekly active users (product analytics, 1-28 Sep) fell from 18 to 7'.

issues.quote: Hi Maya — your renewal review is due next month. Before we meet, I pulled the two goals from kickoff and the progress we can verify so far.
issues.problem: As a message to the customer, it asks Maya to confirm goals it never shows her, and it says 'next month' instead of a date. That goes against renewal-touchpoint-draft's 'Open with the reason and relevant date. Summarise no more than three verified outcomes'.
