recommendations.notes:
Coverage after the merge: the ten kit skills cover the single-account lifecycle well (setup, onboarding, success plan, health, churn risk, renewal readiness, touchpoints, expansion, escalation, research). What is missing is the recurring, portfolio-level and relationship work a CSM does every week and quarter. That means business reviews, a weekly triage of the whole book, a renewal forecast, the product-feedback loop, survey follow-up, advocacy, handovers and learning from churn.

Items 1 and 2 are the must-haves. Riley has no routines, and customer-portfolio-review is the natural first routine. riley.yml should gain a weekly routine entry naming it once it ships. The QBR skill is where day_one[1] ("the next customer action") most often starts in practice.

What I checked before claiming gaps:
- I read all 8 current SKILL.md files and the PR #13 versions of customer-escalation and customer-support-research.
- I also read account-health-and-qbrs (Robin), renewal-expansion-and-qbr (Max), prep-the-partner-qbr (Anika), signature-to-launch-and-account-ops, onboarding-and-adoption, voice-of-customer-loop, voice-of-customer-and-feedback, exec-engagement-and-sponsorship, multithread-and-stakeholder-maps, upsell-and-retention-offers, churn-prevention, saas-gtm-finance, cohort-and-retention-analysis, sales-call-preparation, sales-forecast-rollup, meeting-follow-up-draft, engagement-survey-readout and contract-renewal-tracker.
- Robin's and Max's QBR skills are not good to share as they are. Each bundles its own fixed-weight 0-100 health score (40/30/30, 40/20/20/20), which contradicts Riley's rule of agreed measures first and would duplicate customer-health-score.
- DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has nothing CS-specific. Its 'referrals' entry covers incentive-based referral programs, not reference or advocacy management, and it is deferred for source-quality reasons.

Upstream verification:
- I fetched and checked guard-review-qbr (MIT, shashwatgtm/b2b-customer-success, pinned at commit 6bb06e940a16b0efc6502c9a6ed772f9934bd229). Its SKILL.md is identical at main and at that SHA, and the LICENSE is MIT at both the repo root and the plugin folder.
- A secondary MIT source exists: alirezarezvani/claude-skills business-growth/skills/customer-success-manager (https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-skills/tree/main/business-growth/skills/customer-success-manager). Its assets/qbr_template.md and executive_business_review_template.md are usable as templates. Do not import its scripts or cs-metrics-benchmarks.md: fixed weights, unsourced benchmark tables, and an "Estimated Total Value Delivered $" field that conflict with Riley's evidence rules.

Role evidence: jobdescription.org's CSM description lists QBRs, "own renewal forecasting for the assigned book of business", the internal product-feedback advocate role, and a 30-80 account portfolio. ChurnZero's CS career guide lists "Drive customer advocacy in the form of references, referrals, and case studies".

Cautions:
- Toran's review warned against carrying forward unvalidated renewal forecasting. renewal-forecast-rollup is therefore scoped as a call-based roll-up with evidence. A weighted figure appears only from user-supplied historical rates, and no probability ever comes from a health score.
- Dropping customer-insight-research removed Riley's only NPS and voice-of-customer handling; only segment-by-reason, the confidence table and bias checks went into churn-risk-review. Items 4 and 5 cover that loss.
- Scaled or tech-touch CS (one-to-many journeys, webinars, lifecycle email) is deliberately not recommended. Riley should hand it to Remy (lifecycle-email-marketing, lifecycle-email-map) rather than own it.
- Customer meeting prep and recap is folded into customer-business-review, and customer-touchpoint-draft covers the follow-up email. Kai's generic meeting-prep-brief and meeting-follow-up-draft cover the rest, so no separate call-prep skill is proposed.

recommendations.name: Customer business review (QBR/EBR)
recommendations.purpose: Prepare a sourced QBR or EBR brief, agenda, pre-read and 24-hour recap for one account, with risk never omitted and expansion gated on health and renewal.
recommendations.why: Business reviews are the most common recurring CSM deliverable. jobdescription.org lists 'conduct quarterly or semi-annual business reviews'; ChurnZero lists 'orchestrate value reviews'. No kit skill produces one. customer-success-plan only keeps a review log, and customer-touchpoint-draft only writes the email around the meeting. The catalog QBR skills (account-health-and-qbrs, renewal-expansion-and-qbr) embed their own fixed-weight health scores that contradict customer-health-score. guard-review-qbr is an MIT, evidence-first base with [Missing]/[Assumption] labels, a mandatory risk section, an at-risk variant with no expansion pitch, and a recap email.

source.ref: shashwatgtm/b2b-customer-success plugins/b2b-customer-success/skills/guard-review-qbr (plus references/qbr-structure.md and input-rules.md); timing pattern from catalog prep-the-partner-qbr

sketch: Inputs and review type: account, date, audience; standard, executive, at-risk or first 90-day review. Pull the success plan, health components, readiness rating and open escalations. Ask at most two questions and label gaps [Missing]/[Assumption].

Seven sections: partnership summary, value delivered against agreed outcomes (every number has source and period; no ROI unless there is a customer-agreed baseline), adoption, support and satisfaction, risk and mitigation (never empty), growth (only if the health and renewal gates pass), and a forward plan with owners on both sides.
At-risk variant leads with risk and recovery and drops growth. Roadmap items only from an approved product source, marked 'not a commitment'.
Timeline: co-draft the agenda with the champion, stage the pre-read 3 business days out and the recap draft within 24h. All customer-facing text goes through customer-touchpoint-draft and approval.

Outputs: brief, talking points and slide outline (Google Slides via run_block when connected, else markdown), saved as a dated workspace file. Append decisions to the success-plan log and store the next review date with memory_store.

Adaptation from upstream: remove the vendor credit from the description, replace 'Run Gauge' with customer-health-score and 'renewal probability' with the renewal-readiness rating, drop the PPTX 'sales-proposal-builder' reference, and ship LICENSE plus ATTRIBUTION.md.

recommendations.name: Customer portfolio review
recommendations.purpose: Run a scheduled weekly pass over the whole book and return a ranked worklist of the accounts that need action this week, each with the next skill to run.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review found routines empty although 'the job runs on a calendar'. A CSM manages 30-80 accounts 'maintaining regular communication... through the contract lifecycle' (jobdescription.org). customer-success-getting-started picks the first three reviews once, and customer-health-score scores accounts, but nothing re-triages the book on a cadence. Nothing notices renewals crossing notice windows, stalled onboardings or escalations with no update, or saves a snapshot to diff against. The platform supports this directly via schedule_routine, memory_store and workspace files.

source.ref: new; ranking rule reused from customer-success-getting-started (days to notice, then ARR); output shape can borrow the portfolio summary in shashwatgtm guard-gauge-diagnostic

sketch: Setup: minimum inputs are the account list with ARR, renewal and notice dates and owner; optionally the saved health snapshot, onboarding tracker and escalation log. Offer a weekly schedule_routine and record each source's last refresh.

Diff against last week's snapshot: health component moves, renewals crossing T-180/120/90/60/30 notice windows, onboarding milestones or TTFV target missed, escalations with no update, drafts awaiting approval, and customer commitments due.
Quiet-account rule: an account with no fresh signal is 'unknown', not healthy. List stale sources separately.

Ranked worklist by days to notice, then ARR. Each row gives the reason, evidence and the one next skill (churn-risk-review, renewal-readiness-review, customer-onboarding-plan, customer-touchpoint-draft, customer-escalation).
Save a dated snapshot to the workspace and key facts to memory. An internal Slack or email digest is staged for approval; nothing goes to customers.
Handoffs: expansion signals to expansion-opportunity-brief and then Max or Jordan, ticket issues to Robin, contract-date conflicts to Ellis.

recommendations.name: Renewal forecast roll-up
recommendations.purpose: Roll up the renewals due in a period into CSM-called outcomes with evidence, kept separate from any weighted figure, plus forecast GRR/NRR for that renewal cohort.
recommendations.why: CSMs 'own renewal forecasting for the assigned book of business' (jobdescription.org) and report it in a weekly forecast call. renewal-readiness-review rates one account at a time, and saas-gtm-finance (Daniel) builds the finance ARR bridge, but nothing gives the CSM view across renewals. sales-forecast-rollup (Omar) has the right discipline (dated export, called and weighted kept apart, stale items marked, currencies separate) and forks cleanly. It is scoped to avoid the unvalidated 'renewal forecasting' promise Toran warned about.

source.ref: sales-forecast-rollup (/home/user/skills-catalog/skills/sales-forecast-rollup/SKILL.md), forked for renewals

sketch: Data check: export date, period, currency, renewal count. Flag renewals with no ARR, no notice date, a past date or no owner. Keep them counted and marked.

Per renewal: the readiness rating from renewal-readiness-review and the CSM call (renew flat, expand, contract, churn or unknown) with one evidence line. Expected ARR comes only from an approved quote, otherwise it is a labelled estimate.

Roll-up: called totals by category and owner. A weighted figure appears only from user-supplied historical rates; never a probability from a health score. Forecast GRR and NRR for the cohort, with formula and denominator computed in bash_exec.
Week-over-week movement: category changes with reasons, slipped decisions, and the at-risk ARR list linked to churn-risk-review.
Guardrails and handoffs: no CRM writes. The official ARR bridge goes to Daniel (saas-gtm-finance), CRM forecast fields to Omar, pricing and concessions to Jordan.

recommendations.name: Customer feedback advocacy
recommendations.purpose: Log customer feature asks and product gaps once, with ARR and renewal date attached, turn repeated patterns into a product brief, and close the loop with each account.
recommendations.why: CSMs 'serve as the customer's internal advocate, communicating product feedback' (jobdescription.org). customer-escalation covers urgent account-level escalations only, and dropping customer-insight-research removed Riley's voice-of-customer handling. voice-of-customer-loop (Max) already has the right method: log once with verbatim and source, dedupe on the underlying ask, a 3+ account or named-churn-risk threshold, a one-page product brief, and a closed loop. It needs its sales-specific win-loss section removed and CS inputs added.

source.ref: voice-of-customer-loop (/home/user/skills-catalog/skills/voice-of-customer-loop/SKILL.md), forked without the win-loss program

sketch: Log once: verbatim ask, speaker, account, date and source (call, QBR, ticket, email). Attach ARR, renewal date and health state from records, and dedupe on the underlying need.
Pattern gate: three or more accounts, or one named renewal or churn risk, before anything goes to product. A single urgent blocker routes to customer-escalation instead.
Product brief: the pattern, three quotes, affected ARR with sources, current workaround, blocks vs annoys, and the specific ask. Sent to Priya or Alex via consult_teammate after approval.
Closed loop: record product's answer with its date. Draft account updates through customer-touchpoint-draft, and never state roadmap dates without product-approved wording.
Store the log in the workspace or Sheets via run_block; the weekly portfolio review reads it for accounts whose renewal depends on an open ask.

recommendations.name: Customer survey closed loop
recommendations.purpose: Read relationship NPS/CSAT results at account level with response counts, route detractors, passives and promoters to the right follow-up, and feed dated sentiment into the health view.
recommendations.why: Sentiment is one of Riley's named signals (the identity separates relationship evidence, and the voice sample cites NPS-style signals), and CSM job guides list NPS/CSAT as CSM KPIs. The only NPS and survey guidance for Riley was in customer-insight-research, which was dropped; only segment-by-reason, confidence and bias checks were merged. Nothing in the kit runs detractor follow-up within an SLA or stops a 2-response NPS from being treated as an account score. engagement-survey-readout (Ines) provides reusable response-rate and minimum-group rules.

source.ref: new; reuses response-rate and minimum-group rules from engagement-survey-readout and the NPS verbatim-pairing guidance from customer-insight-research

sketch: Intake: survey type (relationship NPS or CSAT, not transactional ticket CSAT), who was surveyed per account and role, send date, invited vs responded. Refuse an account-level score below the agreed minimum responses.

Readout by account and segment, with counts, the change from the last wave only where the questions match, and score paired with verbatim. Passives and detractors carry more signal for improvement work.

Closed-loop routing within the agreed SLA: detractors get a touchpoint draft, plus churn-risk-review if renewal is inside the window; passives get one clarifying question; promoters become advocacy candidates, only with consent.
Health feed: write sentiment as a dated, sourced component for customer-health-score, not an override. Send themes to customer-feedback-advocacy.
Guardrails: never de-anonymise respondents or contact anyone who answered anonymously, no incentives that bias answers, drafts only.

recommendations.name: Customer advocacy pipeline
recommendations.purpose: Identify reference-ready customers from evidence, draft consent-based advocacy asks (reference call, quote, review, case study), and track asks so no contact is over-used.
recommendations.why: ChurnZero's CS career guide lists 'Drive customer advocacy in the form of references, referrals, and case studies' as a CSM responsibility. Neither the kit nor the catalog has a reference or case-study workflow; the catalog hits for 'case study' are marketing copy skills that assume the story already exists. It fits Riley's boundaries: evidence of achieved value before asking, customer approval of every quote, logo rights checked against the contract, and no send without approval.

source.ref: new

sketch: Candidate gate: an outcome achieved per the success plan, healthy components, no open escalation, and sourced praise or promoter response. List disqualifiers.
Ask ladder: peer call, reference call, quote, review site, case study, speaking. Match the ask to the relationship, one ask at a time.
Consent and rights: check logo and name-use rights with Ellis, get customer approval of all quoted text, and disclose any review incentive per platform and FTC rules.
Fatigue register in the workspace: contact, ask, date, outcome and cap per quarter, checked before every new ask.
Handoffs: case-study brief to Maya or Noor, ask drafts through customer-touchpoint-draft, reference requests from Max logged against the register.

recommendations.name: Account handover brief
recommendations.purpose: Package an account for a new owner (CSM change, segment move, or leave cover) with sourced history, open commitments, stakeholder status and a warm-introduction draft.
recommendations.why: Book reassignments and segment moves are routine CS operations, and the first-contact risk falls on whatever was promised but not recorded. guard-review-qbr even carries an edge case for a CSM inheriting an account mid-cycle. The kit's onboarding plan covers the sales-to-CS handoff only, and customer-success-plan holds outcomes but not a transition package. Relationship continuity 'through the contract lifecycle' is in CSM job descriptions (jobdescription.org).

source.ref: new

sketch: Trigger and scope: CSM change, move from high-touch to scaled, or temporary cover. Record the effective date and the outgoing and incoming owners.

Sourced package: stated outcomes, health components with trend, contract and notice dates, open escalations, promises and commitments made (with where each was made), sensitivities, and stakeholder map with relationship state.
Transition plan: an overlap window, an internal checklist with dates, and the first 30-day actions for the new owner.
Warm-introduction draft to the customer via customer-touchpoint-draft, staged for approval; nothing sent automatically.
Save to workspace and memory_store so the portfolio review and other skills pick up the new owner.

recommendations.name: Churn post-mortem
recommendations.purpose: Review a lost or contracted account after the fact: exit-interview guide, coded reasons, a missed-signal timeline and process fixes, plus a win-back date for sales.
recommendations.why: churn-risk-review is forward-looking (pre-churn) and customer-health-score plans calibration against past churn, but nothing produces the per-account lessons record that calibration needs. Nothing drafts a neutral exit interview or decides win-back eligibility. voice-of-customer-loop's win-loss method (neutral interviewer, open questions, triangulated evidence) transfers to churned accounts, and customer-insight-research's 'segment by reason, don't average across churn causes' was only partly kept.

source.ref: new; exit-interview method adapted from the win-loss section of voice-of-customer-loop, reason codes shared with churn-risk-review

sketch: Inputs: churn or contraction event with dates and ARR, the dated signal history, notes and tickets. The exit-interview guide (neutral interviewer, 15-20 minutes, open 'what and why' questions) is drafted for approval.
Reason coding with churn-risk-review's codes: primary vs contributing, confidence, controllable vs not, and evidence for each.
Missed-signal timeline: when each signal first appeared, what the health view showed, when action started. Output a calibration row for customer-health-score.
Fixes: process changes with owners and dates; product themes to customer-feedback-advocacy.
Win-back: eligibility, earliest sensible date and owner (Max). Offboarding courtesy such as data-export help goes via Robin. No outreach without approval.

proposal.summary: Robin's live kit is 34 NICK skills. No ORIGINAL roster skill and no open rebuild PR (#14/#15/#16) touches Robin. Toran proposes 7 upstream packages that cover only the general desk, and PR #13 changes nothing material in them. Five of the SKILL.md files are byte-identical, the other two only rename the /command, and the ATTRIBUTION.md edits are provenance-only. PR #13 also leaves their Usage blocks, ~~ placeholders and $ARGUMENTS in place, so the merges have to remove them. The proposal keeps Robin's persona-shaped NICK skills as the base for eight jobs: triage, reply, troubleshooting, recovery, live channels, orders, voice of customer and quality. It grafts the upstream method into them in the platform's own words, with an adapted_from entry, because PROVENANCE.md says platform-authored skills carry no copied upstream text. Three Toran packages become bases because they are clearly the stronger versions. customer-support-research absorbs help-center-answers-and-kb. customer-escalation absorbs escalations-and-incidents, VIP care and trust-and-safety on one P1-P4 scale. knowledge-base-article-writing absorbs KCS. The escalation and KB merges rewrite upstream guidance and approval gates. Each must therefore record its changes in ATTRIBUTION.md and come off vendor.py refresh, because a refresh overwrites hand edits (README) and would silently wipe the P1-P4 scale and the CSAM guard. Eleven merges plus two keep-separate pairs turn the 41 refs into a 23-skill kit. Four skills are dropped: onboarding-and-adoption and account-health-and-qbrs (Riley and Max own those jobs), travel-disruption-and-rebooking (a vertical with an ungated rebook) and member-benefits-and-claims (a vertical that needs rebuilding from scratch and has no PHI identity check). Logistics' customs filing is cut, and software-debugging's code-level material goes to Casey. The expert YAML needs its identity router, four routine 'deep pass' offers, its routine schedule and its closure rule updated. The boundaries are also missing three rules: identity and authority checks, ticket-store and access writes, and breach reportability.

body_review.summary: The persona is tightly gated and consistent. The P1-P4 scale, FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labelling and the draft-then-wait rule appear in the bio, identity, boundaries and every routine. The weaknesses come from its breadth. The identity router names about 20 skills, including verticals and slugs the proposal retires, yet it has no route for fraud, public posts, SSO or compliance. The routines duplicate each other: weekly themes run twice, QA calibration runs twice, and SLA breaches are flagged by both the 8am escalation watch and the 8am callback sweep. Three threads fire at 9am on Mondays. The closure rule (only on customer confirmation) appears in the identity, the boundaries and day_one, and it leaves no end state for silent customers. The boundaries miss identity and authority verification, writes to the ticket store or to access, and breach reportability, and several skills' top review issues depend on those.
strengths: The identity's P1 definition ('P1 is an outage, data loss, a security or fraud event, imminent safety harm, or a VIP down') matches triage-and-prioritize word for word, and P2-P4 match almost word for word, so the persona and its triage skill cannot disagree.

Every routine ends with an explicit no-execute line (e.g. 'this run never sends to a customer and never closes a case'), a quiet-when-clean stop and a dedupe-against-last-run rule, which keeps scheduled runs safe and low-noise.

One evidence standard runs through the whole persona. The bio promises to mark every claim as fact, inference or unknown. The identity and boundaries both say 'a case with no record is UNKNOWN, never confirmed'. Step 1 of every routine sets aside any case with no record.
Voice samples model the target shape: the customer's name, the next step, a dated promise and one question.
body_review.kit_alignment: All three day_one items map to kept skills: triage-and-prioritize, draft-the-reply with customer-support-research, and own-to-closure. The robin-getting-started starter menu also maps to kept skills. The misalignments are about naming and duplication. The identity router names five skills the proposal retires or renames (help-center answers and KB, technical diagnostics with tools, escalations and incidents, voice and phone support, knowledge centered service). It also promises travel, logistics, member-benefits and mass-recovery skills. Four routines offer deep passes under names that will not resolve. routines[1], [2] and [4] use old names. routines[4]'s 'knowledge-centred-service' and 'workforce-and-capacity' match no slug even today. routines[5] writes 'quality-CSAT-and-coaching', which is not the lowercase slug. routines[3] and [5] both roll up the week's themes. routines[4] and [5] both run monthly QA calibration. routines[1] and [2] both flag near-breach cases in the same 8am hour. The boundaries do not cover the ticket-store writes and access changes that the triage, troubleshooting and SSO skills stage. They also lack the identity-verification rule that the SSO and member-benefits evals flag.

issues.quote: hot, VIP, legal, or safety cases to escalations and incidents
issues.problem: Under the proposal this job moves to customer-escalation, with VIP care and trust-and-safety folded in. Today's escalations-and-incidents also rates 'VIP down' as SEV2, while this identity calls it P1.
issues.fix: Route 'hot, VIP or exec, SLA-breaching, security, legal or safety cases to customer escalation, rated on the same P1-P4 scale'.

issues.quote: the vertical queues — marketplace, travel, logistics, member benefits, mass recovery — to their matching skill
issues.problem: Travel and member benefits are dropped. Logistics is merged into orders with customs filing cut, and mass recovery is merged into service recovery. The router promises four skills that will not exist.
issues.fix: Replace with 'marketplace disputes to marketplace two-sided mediation; shipments to orders returns and warranty; company-caused failures, one customer or many, to service recovery and goodwill'.

issues.quote: a breakage to troubleshoot and resolve, and to technical diagnostics with tools
issues.problem: The router splits one job across two skills that are being merged. It also names three more retired skills: 'how-tos to help-center answers and KB', 'calls and callbacks to voice and phone support' and 'knowledge capture to knowledge centered service'.
issues.fix: Route breakage to troubleshoot and resolve only; how-tos to customer support research; calls and callbacks to live-channel queue operations; knowledge capture to knowledge base article writing.

issues.quote: money asks to billing refunds and exceptions
issues.problem: Four kept skills have no route. A chargeback or fraud alert, a public post or review, an SSO/SAML login failure and a regulated draft all go through generic paths. The billing-to-fraud handoff the proposal adds therefore has no persona-level anchor.
issues.fix: Add: 'chargebacks and fraud alerts to fraud and chargeback defense; public posts and reviews to social and community support; SSO and SAML login failures to enterprise identity SSO support; drafts in a regulated segment to compliance and regulated support'.

issues.quote: Only the service desk closes a case, and only after the customer confirms the fix.
issues.problem: This has no end state for a customer who never replies, which is own-to-closure's top review issue (zombie cases). It will also contradict the day_one[2] and own-to-closure fixes, which allow an owner-approved close after the no-reply nudges.
issues.fix: Change it to 'A case closes on the customer's confirmation, or after the agreed no-reply nudges with the owner's yes; you propose the close, the desk makes it.'

issues.quote: offer to run the deep escalations-and-incidents pass
issues.problem: This names a slug that the merge into customer-escalation retires.
issues.fix: Change it to 'offer to run the deep customer-escalation pass'.

issues.quote: for SEV1/SEV2 closes
issues.problem: The identity never defines a SEV scale; it uses P1-P4. Postmortems also belong to Casey's incident-postmortem-draft, not to a support routine.
issues.fix: Change it to 'for P1/P2 closes — a postmortem request to the incident owner (Casey's incident-postmortem-draft if hired) with owner and date'.

issues.quote: offer to run the deep voice-and-phone-support pass
issues.problem: voice-and-phone-support merges into live-channel-queue-operations.
issues.fix: Change it to 'offer to run the deep live-channel-queue-operations pass'.

issues.quote: near-breach cases with clocks
issues.problem: The callback sweep (H 8 * * *) re-flags the near-breach and breached cases that the escalation and SLA watch (H 8 * * 1-5) owns. On weekdays two threads page the same breach in the same hour, each deduping only against itself.
issues.fix: Drop near-breach cases and 'breaches inside the hour' from the callback sweep, keep it to callbacks and live queues, and move its morning slot to H 10 * * *.

issues.quote: offer to run the deep knowledge-centred-service or workforce-and-capacity pass
issues.problem: Neither name matches a slug even today: the slug is spelled 'centered', and 'workforce-and-capacity' is missing '-planning'. After the merge, KCS lives in knowledge-base-article-writing.
issues.fix: Change it to 'offer to run the deep knowledge-base-article-writing or workforce-and-capacity-planning pass'.

issues.quote: Once a month, add the QA calibration plus reason-reduction report
issues.problem: This duplicates routines[5] ('Monthly, rescore a shared sample to recalibrate'), so calibration is reported twice from two threads.
issues.fix: Remove the QA calibration line from the knowledge-and-staffing pulse and keep it in quality-and-voc-pulse.

issues.quote: offer to run the deep quality-CSAT-and-coaching pass
issues.problem: The slug is lowercase quality-csat-and-coaching. The other routines name exact slugs, and this one does not.
issues.fix: Change it to 'offer to run the deep quality-csat-and-coaching pass'.

issues.quote: on Mondays, also roll up the week's ticket themes
issues.problem: routines[5] also delivers 'the week's repeat themes with counts plus the top knowledge-base candidate' every Friday. That produces two weekly theme rollups from different threads, each deduping only against itself.
issues.fix: Drop the Monday themes from the resolution pulse and leave the theme rollup to quality-and-voc-pulse.

issues.problem: This is the same hour as routines[0], and on Mondays routines[4] also fires at 9. That is three threads in one hour on Mondays and two on the other weekdays.
issues.fix: Stagger the slots, e.g. run the resolution pulse at H 11 * * 1-5.

issues.quote: Never send, post, reply, like, DM, dial, call back, refund, credit, hold funds, lock an account, publish an article
issues.problem: The list covers customer-facing and money actions but not writes to the ticket store or tracker (link, merge, re-prioritize, close, file a defect) or access changes. Yet triage 'links duplicates', technical-diagnostics files to the ticket without approval, and SSO work can involve MFA resets or disabling SSO enforcement.
issues.fix: Add: 'write to the ticket store or tracker (link, merge, re-prioritize, close, file) or change anyone's access (MFA reset, SSO enforcement, break-glass, SCIM re-provision)'.

issues.quote: exposed sensitive data is contained before anything else moves
issues.problem: The boundaries have no identity or authority check before account, payment or health details are discussed (the member-benefits blocker). They have no reportability step after a spill (the sensitive-data blocker), and no hands-off rule for suspected child sexual abuse material (the trust-and-safety blocker).
issues.fix: Append: 'Verify the requester's identity and authority before discussing account, payment or health details. After a spill, record the discovery time and alert the privacy or security owner at once; notice deadlines are legal's call. Never open, describe, copy or forward suspected child sexual abuse material — record where it is and hand it to the safety owner.'

issues.quote: a case closes only after the customer confirms the fix
issues.problem: This is the same zombie-case gap as day_one[2]. Once own-to-closure gains an owner-approved 'closing for no reply' step, the boundary would forbid the fix the proposal asks for.
issues.fix: Change it to 'a case closes only after the customer confirms the fix, or after the agreed no-reply nudges with the owner's yes'.

issues.quote: closes only once the customer confirms the fix
issues.problem: This conflicts with the identity ('Only the service desk closes a case') and with the routines ('never closes a case'). It also leaves no end state for a customer who goes silent, which is own-to-closure's top review issue: zombie cases pile up.
issues.fix: Change it to 'proposes closure once the customer confirms, or after the agreed no-reply nudges, for your yes'.

issues.quote: links the duplicates, and hands back the ordered work list
issues.problem: Linking tickets is a write to the ticket store that the day-one promise makes without an approval step.
issues.fix: Change it to 'flags likely duplicates to link, and hands back the ordered work list'.

issues.quote: Got it, Maya — I've marked this P2 and I'm on it.
issues.problem: An internal priority code is exposed to the customer, which breaks voice_preferences' 'no jargon' and invites 'why am I only P2?'.
issues.fix: Change it to 'Got it, Maya — this is at the top of my list and I'm on it.'

issues.quote: Heat gets apology-first handling — acknowledge, own, offer — in problem, solution, benefit order.
issues.problem: 'Own' has no liability caution. service-recovery-and-goodwill's top review issue is wording that reads as an admission when the harm includes injury, data loss, lost revenue or a legal threat.
issues.fix: Add: 'where injury, data loss, lost revenue or a legal threat is involved, apologise for the experience without admitting fault and escalate first'.

issues.quote: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear
issues.problem: The list omits Stripe, which billing and fraud need to read charges and disputes, and HubSpot for CRM history. robin-getting-started checks a different list that adds Google Docs, Gong and Granola, and Gong and Granola are not AutoGPT blocks.
issues.fix: Use one list in both places: add Stripe, HubSpot and Google Docs, drop Gong and Granola, and check run_mcp_tool servers for the help desk.

issues.quote: smart-meeting-brief
issues.problem: No skill, routine or day_one item in Robin's kit involves meetings. The preload matches Frankie's preload set (smart-meeting-brief plus automated-support-ai) and adds nothing to a support desk.
issues.fix: Drop it, or name the support meeting it serves (for example, customer escalation calls) in day_one.

issues.quote: Senior support rep who triages, drafts, and owns every case to closure.
issues.problem: The tagline sells a frontline rep, but the identity and routines also run workforce planning, QA calibration, vendor audits and support dashboards. That is a support-ops lead, so buyers and the router see two personas.
issues.fix: Either add ', and runs the desk's quality, knowledge and staffing loops' or move workforce and support-ops to a support-ops expert.

clusters.job: Triage incoming support tickets: priority with reason, category, duplicates, routing, ranked queue

members.note: It is the only version with the persona's exact P1-P4 wording, queue-level ranking by impact, affected count and SLA clock carried across handoffs, route lanes and an UNKNOWN fallback. Its 'macro fast lane (canned reply plus instant ack)' sends without approval, and it has no spike or known-incident check.

It has the richer per-ticket method (nine categories, bump triggers, four-way duplicate search, a structured triage block). But it tells the model to notify the customer, link tickets and bump priority directly, and its auto-response templates assert actions not yet taken. PR #13 only renames the /ticket-triage lines.

proposed.name: Triage and prioritize
proposed.description: Use when new tickets arrive or the queue needs ordering: categorize each ticket, assign P1-P4 with a one-line reason and its SLA clock, check duplicates, known issues and spikes, route it to a lane, and hand back the ranked work list. Links, priority changes and first replies are staged for a yes.
proposed.rationale: The NICK skill has the higher eval and is the only version matching Robin's P1-P4 wording, SLA carry-over and queue ranking. The upstream package adds the per-ticket rigour that the 52-line NICK skill lacks. Write the grafts in the platform's own words and add an adapted_from entry for the Apache-2.0 source rather than pasting the tables (PROVENANCE.md). Fix in the same pass: the fast lane becomes a staged acknowledgement draft, and the fixed SLA timings apply only when prefs hold none. Also new, from the base's eval: three or more tickets sharing a symptom in a window, or a live status-page incident, is flagged to customer-escalation as a possible incident rather than just linked. Self-harm, threats and child-safety words go to customer-escalation's safety path before ranking.
drops: support-ticket-triage '## Auto-Response Templates by Category': the bug, feature-request and security templates claim actions not yet taken ('I've logged this as a [priority] issue', 'I've documented this and shared it with our product team', 'I've escalated this to our security team')
support-ticket-triage 'If a duplicate is found' direct actions (notify the customer, add information to the existing ticket, bump priority), reframed as staged proposals
support-ticket-triage '## Usage' /ticket-triage block and ~~support platform placeholders (PR #13 only renames the command)
triage-and-prioritize step 3 'macro fast lane (canned reply plus instant ack with expected reply time)' as an unapproved send

grafts.what: Nine primary categories (bug, how-to, feature request, billing, account, integration, security, data, performance) with signal words. Categorize by root cause: a login failure caused by a bug is Bug, and the bug is primary when one ticket carries both a bug and a request.
Bump priority when the customer has waited past SLA, several customers report the same symptom, the customer mentions executive involvement, a workaround stops working, or the scope grows.
Search by symptom or error text, by customer, by product area, then against known issues. Propose the link with ticket IDs for the owner's yes.

The per-ticket row behind the ranked queue: category, priority with reason, product area, workaround (available, not available or unknown), related tickets, known issue (yes or no), route with why, and internal notes with the escalation triggers to watch.
Default response and update targets (P1 1h with updates every 1-2h, P2 4h, P3 1 business day, P4 2 business days). Use them only when prefs hold no SLA, and label them as defaults.

clusters.job: Draft a customer-facing support reply for approval

members.note: It has the company voice, banned phrases, apology-first Problem-Solution-Benefit order, channel shaping (public-safe social) and a staged draft, and marks lines UNVERIFIED when no doc exists. It never lists every question the customer asked, it has no one-clarifying-question rule, and it never routes money, regulated, sensitive-data or public-post tickets elsewhere.

A 430-line upstream draft-response with a strong internal-notes block, situation playbooks, and length and relationship-stage guidance. Its templates hard-code 'I've confirmed the issue and escalated it' and 'I've looked into your account', so filled drafts assert actions that may not have happened.

proposed.name: Draft the reply
proposed.description: Use when a customer waits on an answer on any channel: answer every question they asked from a cited doc or record, shape it for the channel and situation (heat, bad news, a no, an outage), add internal notes on what to verify, and stage it for the owner's yes.
proposed.rationale: The two are evenly matched. The NICK skill is short, persona-shaped and already approval-gated, so it is the base. The upstream skill contributes the structure Robin's lacks, rewritten in the platform's own words with an adapted_from entry (PROVENANCE.md). Sasha's original support-reply-draft (not in scope) supplies the fix for the base's top review issue. New in the merge, from the base's second review issue, the reply routes some cases elsewhere before drafting: money asks to billing-refunds-and-exceptions, regulated segments to compliance-and-regulated-support, card or health data to sensitive-data-safe-handling, public posts to social-and-community-support, and company-caused failures to service-recovery-and-goodwill. Drop the base's 'apology to a customer' trigger, which collides with service recovery's 'apology note to a customer'.
drops: customer-response-drafting '## Response Templates for Common Scenarios' (pre-filled claims of actions taken). Only the '### Following Up After Silence' template survives, and it moves to own-to-closure
customer-response-drafting '## Follow-up and Escalation Guidance': the Follow-up Cadence table moves to own-to-closure, and the When to Escalate criteria live in customer-escalation
customer-response-drafting '### 2. Research Context' ~~email, ~~chat and ~~CRM lookups, which customer-support-research does
customer-response-drafting '## Usage' slash block (PR #13 only renames it)

grafts.what: A 'Notes for you (internal — do not send)' block under each draft: why this approach, things to verify before sending, risk factors, follow-up needed, and whether someone else must review.

One-line playbooks for a product question, an issue or bug, an escalation, bad news (delay, sunset, can't-fix) and declining a request (feature, discount, exception): lead with the news, give the reason honestly, offer alternatives, and set a clear path forward.

grafts.section: ### Outage or Incident Communication (field set only)
grafts.what: For an outage reply: what happened, the impact on this customer, the status (investigating, identified, fixing or resolved), the next update time or cadence, and the status page link. Each field is sourced, and there is no 'I'm personally tracking this' line unless it is true.

grafts.section: ### Length Guidelines + ### Tone Adjustments by Relationship Stage
grafts.what: Chat 1-4 sentences, ticket reply 1-3 short paragraphs, email at most 3-5 paragraphs, executive 2-3 paragraphs. New customers get more context; frustrated customers get shorter feedback loops.

clusters.job: Find and cite the answer to a customer question (how-to, known issue, account history) before replying

members.note: The most thorough skill in this group. proposed.name: Customer support research
proposed.description: Use when a customer question needs looking up before anyone answers: search the help center, KB, past tickets, CRM, chat and the web in order, reconcile conflicts, and return a cited answer labelled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN, with gaps, who to ask, and a saved-reply or KB candidate if it repeats.
proposed.rationale: The research package is exactly the retrieval step help-center-answers-and-kb lacks (its biggest gap), and it is the more complete skill, with tiered sources, confidence levels and escalation rules. The NICK skill's customer-answer shape and saved-reply minting graft onto the package's 'Customer-Facing Considerations' and 'Knowledge Capture' steps. Map the confidence levels onto Robin's labels: High is FACT, Medium and Low are INFERENCE with the level kept, and 'Unable to Determine' is UNKNOWN. Low confidence still yields a best-guess answer, so it is not UNKNOWN. New, from the base's review: Tier-5 analogous-customer findings are internal only; never name or quote another customer or their terms in a customer-facing answer. clusters.job: Escalate a hot, VIP, breaching, multi-customer, security or safety case with a complete packet

members.note: It has escalate-versus-handle criteria, tiers (L1, L2, Engineering, Product, Security, Leadership, with Security bypassing the tiers), impact dimensions, repro-writing rules, follow-up cadence by severity, and de-escalation. Its top issue: it asks for ARR and customer counts with no sourcing rule. Its de-escalation and follow-up steps also tell the model to notify teams, update the ticket and inform the customer directly, and its repro evidence has no redaction rule.

A Robin-native packet, a hold path for fraud, abuse, legal and safety, a warm handoff line and staged paging. Its SEV1-SEV4 scale rates 'VIP down' as SEV2 while the persona says P1, and it omits security and data exposure. 'Freeze the state' is undefined.

Tier from the record, a named owner, updates on cadence, a separate exec stakeholder line and a check-in a week out. Its triggers ('exec escalation', 'enterprise customer escalation') collide with escalations-and-incidents.

The now-path for imminent harm and the warm handoff are sound, but the rest needs a rewrite. Its blocker: suspected CSAM gets only a routing priority, next to instructions to 'preserve evidence' and keep 'verbatim quotes'. The person at risk also gets no staged crisis reply.

proposed.name: Customer escalation
proposed.description: Use when a case needs more than the desk: hot, VIP or exec, SLA-breaching, multi-customer, security, legal or safety (abuse, self-harm, threats, illegal content). Decide whether to escalate, set P1-P4 with a reason, build a sourced, redacted impact-and-repro packet, pick the target team, and stage the handoff and update cadence for a yes.
proposed.rationale: The upstream package has the fuller method and the higher eval. Robin's three NICK skills each hold a slice of the same job and collide on triggers. One skill on Robin's P1-P4 scale ends the SEV-versus-P mismatch, and VIP care and safety reports become sections instead of competing skills. Replacing the Severity Shorthand is not enough on its own. The brief template's 'Severity: [Critical / High / Medium]' field and the Follow-up Cadence table are keyed to the same scale and must move to P1-P4: P1 internal every 2h and customer every 2-4h; P2 4h and 4-8h; P3 daily and 1-2 business days; P4 has a watch flag and no escalation. Several steps are rewritten into staged drafts for a yes. De-escalation's 'notify the team, update the ticket, inform the customer' becomes drafts, and so do Follow-up Actions' customer updates. 'Any → Security ... escalate immediately' becomes an immediate alert to the owner with a drafted security packet. Every impact number (customers affected, ARR) carries its source or is marked UNKNOWN. Evidence is redacted of tokens, card data and personal data before the brief goes to Slack or Linear. Suspected CSAM is never opened, described, copied or forwarded; record its location and ID and hand it to the safety or legal owner, who owns any statutory report. If the owner is unreachable on a P1 or imminent-harm case, follow the pre-authorised on-call path from the escalation matrix. Without one, keep alerting the owner and name who should call emergency services. Carry up to 10 triggers from the merged skills, for example 'VIP case', 'SEV1 incident', 'abuse report', 'self-harm in a ticket', 'illegal content report' and 'credible threat', so safety reports still load this skill. These edits rewrite upstream guidance and approval gates, so the package is no longer a light packaging adaptation. Record every change in ATTRIBUTION.md: Apache-2.0 §4(b) requires it, and the current file says AutoGPT did not author the guidance. Stop refreshing the package with vendor.py, because a refresh would silently remove the P1-P4 scale and the CSAM guard. Rename the offer in routines[1] to this slug.

grafts.section: ## Severity-triage in one pass / ## Protect first / ## Hand off warm
grafts.what: Imminent harm goes to a human now, with who, what, where and when. An abusive customer is handled with a lead looped in, never solo. Never contact the reported party. The owner confirms receipt before you stand down. Log facts only, with no adjectives about people.

For self-harm or crisis language, stage an immediate reply for the owner's yes with locale-appropriate crisis resources (for example 988 in the US, Samaritans 116 123 in the UK and Ireland, findahelpline.com). It promises no confidentiality or outcome, and it runs alongside the handoff, not after it.

clusters.job: Make it right after a company-caused failure, for one customer or many

members.note: Size the harm; acknowledge, own and offer; match the remedy to harm and precedent inside the goodwill limit; resolve in one touch; log the precedent. It already checks whether mass-recovery comms are running. It treats owed SLA credits and statutory compensation as discretionary goodwill.

Blast sizing, affected-list verification, one bulk approval packet and two comms shapes. Its blocker: it treats breach and recall like outage comms, with no statutory deadlines. It also adds war-room and postmortem work that belongs to incident owners, and it has no dedupe of bulk money moves.

proposed.name: Service recovery and goodwill
proposed.description: Use when the company caused the failure (botched order, broken promise, delay or outage) for one customer or many: size the harm, verify who was affected, check owed credits, draft the apology and a remedy within the goodwill limit and precedent, and stage one approval packet. Breach and recall notices go to legal.
proposed.rationale: This is the same job at two scales, and the base already points to mass recovery for systemic failures. Folding in the bulk mechanics keeps one remedy and precedent logic whether one customer or a thousand are affected. New in the merge, fixing both skills' main gaps: when the harm includes injury, data loss, lost revenue or a legal threat, apologise for the experience without admitting fault and route to customer-escalation first. Breach and recall notices have statutory content and deadlines, so they go to the compliance owner or legal (Lena's compliance-escalation-brief) and are never drafted as outage comms. Also new, from the base's review: check contractual SLA credits and statutory compensation (owed, not goodwill) before sizing any gesture. Carry the mass-recovery triggers ('outage recovery', 'mass refund', 'bulk customer comms') within the 10-trigger cap.

clusters.job: Handle money disputes: refund and exception requests vs fraud and chargebacks

members.note: Verify the charge, cite the policy, route to the approver above the limit, and give a graceful no. Its top issue: no check for an open card dispute before a refund, so a refund on top of a chargeback loses the money twice.

Separates account takeover from first-party abuse, makes the hold-or-clear call, and builds a reason-code representment. Its top issue: no fight-or-accept decision and no guard against refunding a disputed transaction.

proposed.name: Billing, refunds and exceptions
proposed.description: Use when money is on the table: verify the charge and any open dispute, cite the refund policy, lay out options with cost and precedent for the approver, and stage the customer message. Billing also takes the approver-options block from Sasha's refund-and-exception-brief.

grafts.what: Two or three options for the approver (the policy as written, a partial refund or credit with its amount, the full request), each with its cost, the precedent it sets and any chargeback or legal deadline, plus the date a decision is needed.
