recommendations.notes:
How I checked: I read the platform brief, Robin's dossier, robin.yml and robin's eval file. I read the current SKILL.md of every kit skill and of the retired skills the merges absorb (help-center-answers-and-kb, knowledge-centered-service, technical-diagnostics-with-tools, mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms, voice-and-phone-support), plus these catalog candidates: support-macro-library, data-subject-request-draft, bug-report-handoff, help-article-from-tickets, weekly-ticket-themes, support-getting-started, lead-routing-rules and product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals. I then grepped all 35 kit and absorbed skills for these topics: GDPR/DSAR/deletion, identity verification/recovery/MFA, chatbot/AI agent/deflection, release/launch, translation/language, status page, NPS/detractor. The only hits were passing mentions ("identity check before account talk" in live-channel and voice, "unresolved bot turns" as a KCS metric, launches as a WFM forecast input). DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has nothing on support.

Public sources: I found no redistribution-ready public skill for any gap. Anthropic's knowledge-work-plugins customer-support set is already in the catalog. mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills (MIT) has account-recovery-plan, but it is written for a consumer recovering their own account, not a help desk verifying a caller. wshobson's customer-sales-automation plugin ships agents only, no skills. So the four new recommendations are type "new". Where a catalog skill supplies the pattern, the sketch names it (Omar's lead-routing-rules, Alex's four-rung ladder, Sasha's macro fields).

Deliberately not recommended:
- The four dropped skills (onboarding, account health/QBRs, travel, member benefits) stay dropped.
- Incident and status-page comms are covered by the merged draft-the-reply (outage field set), customer-escalation (cadence table) and service-recovery-and-goodwill (one customer or many). Noor's holding-statement-draft and Casey's software-incident-response are teammate handoffs.
- Macro-library upkeep is folded into product-change-support-readiness. Sasha's support-macro-library only mints macros, and customer-support-research already has saved-reply minting grafted on.
- "Notify every customer when the linked bug ships" fits better as a Linear-linked step in own-to-closure than as a new skill.
- Vulnerable-customer handling (ISO 22458:2022, FCA FG21/1) is a could-have for regulated UK desks. It is partly covered by customer-escalation's safety section and compliance's new complaint identification.

Persona follow-ups these depend on:
- The boundaries need one line on identity and authority verification, pointing at verify-requester-and-account-access. This closes the gap the expert-body review names.
- The identity router should add routes for fraud, public posts, SSO, compliance and any of these skills that are adopted.
- upsell-and-retention-offers should hand an account-deletion or erasure ask to data-subject-request-draft and make no save attempt.
- data-subject-request-draft would be shared with Lena. Its triggers collide only with itself, so a Robin plus Lena team is fine. Robin does intake, verification and the acknowledgement; Lena or the privacy owner does fulfilment.

recommendations.name: Verify the requester and account access
recommendations.purpose: Before Robin discloses account details or stages any account change, confirm who is asking and whether they have authority, and stage account-recovery requests (lost MFA, email change, owner left) for the owner without doing them.
recommendations.why: No skill in the kit says how to verify a requester. live-channel-queue-operations and voice-and-phone-support mention an identity check but give no method, and fraud-and-chargeback-defense only acts after a takeover has happened. The expert-body review says the boundaries lack identity and authority verification and that the SSO and member-benefits evals flag it. The SSO review's top issue is that nothing checks the requester's authority before an MFA reset, a break-glass login or disabling SSO, calling it 'the classic social-engineering route to account takeover'. The member-benefits eval blocker is PHI shared with an unverified spouse or provider. In the field, CISA advisory AA23-320A (Scattered Spider) documents attackers calling help desks to reset passwords and move MFA to devices they control. Verification before disclosure is a standard duty for any support rep. The platform can read the contact of record through the HubSpot and Stripe blocks that robin-getting-started now checks, ask_question can run the challenge, and every reset stays a staged draft.
sketch: When it runs: before any account-specific disclosure (order, billing, usage, PHI) and before staging any change to email, phone, password, MFA, SSO enforcement, owner or seats. It reads the verification policy from a named memory key and asks once if the key is missing.

Verification ladder, strongest first: an authenticated in-product session or a reply from the email of record, then an owner-approved possession factor, then the documented ID process. Knowledge answers found in public sources do not count. Each check is logged as FACT or UNKNOWN.

Authority check: account owner or admin, the authorised-contact list, a B2B org admin confirmed from the contact of record (not from the requester), or a personal representative or authorisation on file for health data. A requester who cannot show authority gets a plain 'I can't share that' reply with the route to gain access.

Red-flag list that forces a hold: urgency or pressure, a channel switch mid-thread, a new or look-alike email, a credential change just before the ask, a request to send to a new address, or a caller claiming to be an exec or IT.

Account-recovery packet staged for the owner: evidence for and against, the proposed change, a cooling-off period, and a drafted notice to the old contact of record. Robin never resets, unlocks or changes access itself.

Output: a one-line verification log on the case (method, result, who approved) plus the customer reply. Suspected takeover goes to fraud-and-chargeback-defense, and exposed data goes to sensitive-data-safe-handling.

recommendations.name: AI support agent review
recommendations.purpose: Sample and grade the automated support agent's conversations for invented answers, missed handoffs and unsafe promises, then stage the knowledge, guardrail and handoff fixes for the owner.
recommendations.why: Robin preloads the automated-support-ai agent, so Robin works next to a bot that answers customers. Nothing in the kit checks what that bot says. The only related coverage is an 'unresolved bot turns' metric in the old KCS and social skills. Quality-csat-and-coaching grades human reps, and Alex's product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals grades AI features before launch, not live support transcripts. Support teams on Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI agents and similar tools now staff exactly this review work. The risk is concrete: in Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024 BCCRT 149), the company was held liable for a refund policy its chatbot invented. EU AI Act Art. 50, applying from 2 Aug 2026, adds an AI-interaction disclosure duty. The platform fits: bash_exec can sample a transcript export and compute rates, and fixes route to knowledge-base-article-writing as drafts.
sketch: Inputs: a transcript export (CSV or JSON) with a period, the bot's knowledge sources, and the handoff rules. Sample in bash_exec, stratified: every handoff, low-CSAT and reopened threads, long loops, and any thread with money, policy, legal or safety words. State the sample size and the period.

Grade each thread on a four-rung ladder (right; usable with caveats; wrong but harmless; harmful or fabricated), adapted from Alex's product-ai-feature-scoping-and-evals, with the quoted bot line and the source passage it should have used.

Auto-fail checks: an invented price, policy, date or refund; a promise of money or an exception; a missed handoff on a P1, safety, legal or identity-sensitive request; personal data echoed back; a missing AI disclosure where required.

Metrics come only from the export and each carries its source: containment versus confirmed resolution (they are not the same), handoff rate, reopen-after-bot rate. The failure taxonomy is given with counts.

Fix list staged for the owner: KB article fixes (to knowledge-base-article-writing), blocked topics, new handoff triggers, and a customer follow-up for any customer given a wrong answer (to draft-the-reply or service-recovery-and-goodwill). Robin never edits the bot's config.
Fallback: no export means grading the pasted threads only, marked as a small sample, with the export request named.

recommendations.name: Data subject request draft
recommendations.purpose: Recognise access, deletion, correction and objection requests that arrive in the support queue, log the statutory clock, verify identity, scope the systems, and draft the acknowledgement for the privacy owner.
recommendations.why: 'Delete my account and my data' and 'what data do you hold on me' reach support first. None of Robin's 35 current or proposed skills mentions GDPR, DSAR, erasure or deletion; the only hit is one taxonomy row in support-ticket-triage. The deadlines are set by law: GDPR Art. 12(3) gives one month, extendable by two; CCPA regulations require confirmation within 10 business days and a response within 45 days. A request missed in a cancellation ticket is a compliance failure. The catalog already has Lena's original data-subject-request-draft, which has the right controls: log and quote the request, check identity before anything else, scope systems from the data map, never delete or export, and draft for the owners. Nothing needs inventing.

source.ref: data-subject-request-draft (Lena, original group)

sketch: Add a recognition step for support: requests hidden in cancellations, complaints or social DMs count, and the clock starts on the date of receipt, not the date it was triaged.

Identity check runs through verify-requester-and-account-access. An authorised agent or parent needs proof of authority, and an unverified request stops at an acknowledgement that names what is needed.
Scope the systems from the data map, including the helpdesk itself, call recordings and chat transcripts, each with an owner. Hold back third-party data.
Draft the acknowledgement with the due date. The retention offer is skipped, and an account-deletion or erasure request is never obstructed by a save attempt.
Hand fulfilment to Lena or the privacy owner as a packet. Robin never deletes, exports or claims a search is complete. This is not legal advice.

recommendations.name: Product change support readiness
recommendations.purpose: When a release, price or policy change, or deprecation is coming, find every macro, KB article, saved reply, talk track and bot answer it breaks, draft the updates, and prepare the desk for the expected tickets.
recommendations.why: Keeping macros and help content current as the product ships, and preparing the desk for launches, is a routine support duty. The kit handles knowledge one article at a time (knowledge-base-article-writing, including its periodic health check) and treats launches only as a forecast input in workforce-and-capacity-planning. No skill starts from the change itself and sweeps everything it invalidates. The catalog skills that touch launches are written from the product side (Alex's product-launch-plan enablement pack, Priya's release-notes-draft, Zara's commercial-launch-strategy). The reviews show the cost: troubleshoot-and-resolve's top issue was skipping the recent-release check, and a stale macro quoting an old price becomes a billing exception later. On the platform, bash_exec can search exported macros and KB pages for changed terms and old prices. Notion, Drive and Linear blocks supply the release notes and linked issues, and everything publishes only after the owner's yes.
sketch: Intake: the change (release notes, Linear issues, pricing or policy diff), the go-live date, who is affected, and what is still unconfirmed. Unconfirmed items are marked UNKNOWN and never written into customer content.

Impact sweep: search macros, KB, saved replies, talk tracks and bot answers for changed feature names, old prices and old policy text. Output one table: asset, the line that breaks, the fix draft, the owner. Macro fields follow Sasha's support-macro-library.
Ticket forecast: the likely contact drivers, with volume taken from a comparable past change (sourced) or marked INFERENCE. The staffing flag goes to workforce-and-capacity-planning.
Desk kit: an internal FAQ, a known-issue article draft, the escalation path and owner for launch bugs, and triage tags so launch tickets can be counted.
Customer side: a proactive notice draft for affected accounts, plus a go-live checklist, all staged for the owner's yes.
Day-after review: which predicted drivers appeared, which assets still failed, and the fixes. This feeds the knowledge and staffing pulse routine.

recommendations.name: Helpdesk SLA and routing rules
recommendations.purpose: Write the helpdesk's SLA policies (per plan, channel and priority, business hours, pause states, clock carry-over) and routing rules so each ticket matches exactly one rule with a fallback, then dry-run them on a real export.
recommendations.why: Toran's review names the remaining triage gap directly: 'fixed native P1-P4 timing must already match policy; no configurable contractual/per-channel clock carry-over or full queue scheduler.' Robin's persona requires that SLA clocks start at first contact and carry across handoffs. That is a helpdesk configuration property, and no kit skill specifies it. triage-and-prioritize routes one ticket at a time, and support-ops-improvement-program measures SLA compliance but does not design the policy. Maintaining views, triggers and SLA policies is a normal duty for senior support reps on Zendesk, Intercom or HubSpot Service Hub. Omar's catalog skill lead-routing-rules already has the right method (first match wins, a fallback owner, test on 90 days of real records), but it is written for leads. On the platform, bash_exec replays the draft rules over a ticket CSV, and the helpdesk admin applies them after approval.
sketch: List the cases from the current rules and a dated export: plan or contract tier, channel, priority, language, VIP, and tickets with missing fields, each with its 90-day count.

SLA policy table: first-response and resolution targets per tier, channel and priority; the business-hours calendar and holidays; pause-on-pending-customer rules; carry-over across handoffs and reopens. Each target cites its contract or policy source.
Routing rules in order, first match wins: condition on filled fields, queue or owner, backup when that owner is away, and one fallback rule owned by a named person.
Dry run in bash_exec over the export: unmatched and double-matched tickets, owner changes, and breach counts before and after, as a median and p90.
Stage the rule set for the helpdesk admin's yes, with a rollback line. Robin never edits helpdesk config.

recommendations.name: Multilingual support replies
recommendations.purpose: Answer customers in their own language without drifting from the approved policy or product wording: a do-not-translate glossary, official localized sources, a back-translation check, and native review for high-risk replies.
recommendations.why: No kit skill has a language rule. Grepping draft-the-reply, customer-response-drafting, social-and-community-support and knowledge-base-article-writing found no translate or locale step, only the phrase 'customer language'. Global desks and many support postings expect replies in the customer's language, and the model can translate natively. The risk is re-translating a refund or warranty passage into a promise the source does not make, or rendering regulated disclosures loosely. Glossaries and approved localized sources can live in named memory keys, and the back-translation goes in the internal notes block that draft-the-reply already carries.
sketch: Detect the language and reply in it unless the owner's prefs say otherwise. The owner sees an English gloss in the internal notes.
Glossary: product and plan names, UI labels and legal terms that stay fixed or use their approved translations, stored under a memory key.
Policy, price and legal text is quoted from the official localized source when one exists. Otherwise it is flagged UNVERIFIED and not paraphrased into a commitment.
Back-translation check on load-bearing lines. Replies that are regulated, involve money over the limit, safety or legal matters, or are public go to a native reviewer before the owner's yes.
Log the language on the case so voice-of-customer-and-feedback and workforce-and-capacity-planning can count demand by language.

proposal.summary: Sasha's live kit is eight short ORIGINAL skills, all with sound draft-only guardrails. NICK added nothing for her. TORAN proposes six Anthropic packages that mostly redo those originals as 260-430-line slash-command plugins. PR #13 barely touches them: it only renames the H1/usage in customer-response-drafting and support-ticket-triage, and product-research-synthesis still carries `$ARGUMENTS`. The recommendation is to keep the originals as bases and graft in the upstream craft. support-ticket-triage gives its taxonomy, routing table and per-ticket template to ticket-triage. customer-response-drafting gives its verify/risk notes, channel lengths, situation playbooks and escalation format to support-reply-draft. knowledge-base-article-writing gives its per-type templates, searchability rules and update-vs-create branch to help-article-from-tickets; that base is kept even though the upstream skill has the stronger article craft, because its guardrails are much stronger and it starts from repeat tickets. customer-escalation gives its escalate-or-not gate, repro practice and security bypass to bug-report-handoff. product-research-synthesis gives only its thematic-coding method to weekly-ticket-themes; that base is kept even though the upstream skill has the more developed method, because the upstream skill is a product-research job, not a periodic support report. customer-support-research is the one upstream package added as its own skill, as the lookup step before a reply. It is added once its slash usage and cross-customer leak risk are fixed and a rule stops tier 3-5 findings being treated as confirmed. Cross-expert, Robin's 34-skill support kit overlaps almost every Sasha skill, so Sasha should be positioned as the small-team help-desk and knowledge specialist. Clear handoffs go to Riley (churn), Lena (security/data exposure), Priya (feature requests and product signals) and Casey (code-level repro), and product-research-synthesis goes to Priya or Alex. The body needs four fixes: a wider draft-only and privacy boundary, a legal/security/churn route, opt-in queue and weekly-themes routines (the queue brief only where a queue source is connected), and a triage skill that delivers the 'urgency' the identity promises.

body_review.summary: The persona is tight and consistent with the kit. The identity, bio and both voice samples model answer-first drafting, evidence-based grouping and draft-only behaviour, and the eight skills implement all three. No routine or preload names a skill that would be dropped or renamed (all merged slugs are unchanged). The gaps fall into three groups. First, the boundaries only cover replies, while the kit also drafts macros, articles, bug reports and refund briefs, and there is no privacy rule. Second, the identity promises urgency-based sorting and no invented timelines, but the current ticket-triage and support-reply-draft do not honour those promises. Third, there are no routines, although the tagline and weekly-ticket-themes are recurring by nature. The persona also needs a sharper line against Robin, the other support expert, and a rule for the looked-up (not confirmed) findings that customer-support-research will bring in.
strengths: Identity has a concrete anti-bias rule ('A loud customer is not automatically urgent, and a polite one is not automatically low priority') that ticket-triage repeats almost word for word ('...a polite one is not automatically low').

The customer-reply voice sample (Dana, 10,000-row Starter limit, two options, one question) is a textbook output of support-reply-draft's rules: answer first, the customer's words, at most one question.
The queue-brief sample shows counts, a duplicate group tied to evidence (Safari, first seen Tuesday) and routing a billing dispute to Finance, which is exactly the ticket-triage brief.
The bug-report fields listed in the identity (steps, expected and actual result, environment, frequency, affected accounts) match bug-report-handoff's report sections.

A consistent never-invent rule. support-reply-draft repeats the identity's full list (fix, workaround, root cause, release date, refund, policy), and every other original closes with a never-invent or never-guess line for its own output (causes, steps, limits, fix dates, counts, quotes).
body_review.kit_alignment: skills[] lists exactly the eight live originals. routines and preloads are empty, so nothing points at a dropped or renamed skill. The proposed merges keep every slug (ticket-triage, support-reply-draft, bug-report-handoff, help-article-from-tickets, weekly-ticket-themes). The skills[] change has two parts. customer-support-research is added after ticket-triage, and the list is reordered into working order (triage, look-up, reply, bug handoff, refund brief, then the macro, article and themes work), which moves bug-report-handoff and refund-and-exception-brief ahead of support-macro-library and help-article-from-tickets. Four promises are not backed by any current skill. (1) The identity promises 'impact, urgency' sorting, but ticket-triage's four tiers are impact-only and never use the first-message date it records. (2) The bio says 'never invent ... a timeline', but support-reply-draft's 'when the team will update' line and customer-response-drafting's 'by Friday January 24' rule both undercut it. (3) The queue-brief sample routes a 'billing dispute' to Finance, but refund-and-exception-brief treats a chargeback only as a deadline and has no dispute path. (4) The tagline promises a recurring view of 'which questions keep coming back', but no routine backs it. The merged skills and the fixes below close all four.

issues.quote: You sort each ticket by impact, urgency, and what is known, and you say which of those you could not verify.
issues.problem: ticket-triage ranks by four impact tiers only. It records 'first message date' but never uses it, and it has no SLA clock, breach risk or plan entitlement, so the persona's urgency promise is unbacked. The review scores expertise 2/5 for exactly this.
issues.fix: Keep the line and make the merged ticket-triage deliver it. Read the team's response targets and entitlements from setup memory and compute time since first contact. Within each tier, order breach and near-breach first, and show the clock in the brief. Use support-ticket-triage's P1-P4 hours only as labelled defaults.

issues.quote: I never invent a fix, a refund, or a timeline, and nothing reaches a customer until a person approves it.
issues.problem: support-reply-draft tells the model to 'say plainly what is not known yet and when the team will update', which invites an invented update time. customer-response-drafting, the graft source, pushes specific dates and named owners with no sourcing rule.
issues.fix: In the merged support-reply-draft, use only an update cadence confirmed in setup memory or by a teammate. Otherwise insert a {next_update} placeholder and list it under 'Things to verify' in the approval note.

issues.quote: Draft replies for approval and never send, close, refund, or edit an account yourself.
issues.problem: The boundary covers replies only. The kit also drafts macros, help articles, bug reports, refund briefs and themes reports, and the platform exposes Notion, WordPress, Linear and GitHub blocks that could publish or file them. Only the individual skill bodies forbid that today.
issues.fix: Widen it: 'Draft replies, macros, help articles, bug reports and refund briefs for approval; never send, publish, file, close, refund, or edit an account or the help centre yourself.'

issues.quote: Never invent a fix, root cause, refund, policy, or release date.
issues.problem: No privacy boundary exists. The kit moves customer words into help articles, bug reports and themes reports that go to product and engineering. weekly-ticket-themes quotes verbatim with no redaction step, and customer-support-research's tier-5 'Analogous customers' can leak another customer's setup into a reply.
issues.fix: Add: 'Strip names, contact details, account ids, payment data and credentials before customer words leave the ticket, and never put one customer's details in another customer's thread.'

issues.quote: When the answer is unknown you say so, ask one clear question, and name who can find out.
issues.problem: There is no path for tickets that should not get a normal answer at all: security or data-exposure reports, legal threats, abuse, and churn threats. support-reply-draft's review flags exactly this gap, and Sasha has no escalation skill beyond bugs and refunds.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: security reports, legal threats and data exposure go straight to the named owner from setup, with a holding reply only; churn threats go to the account owner or customer-success teammate. Back it with support-reply-draft's routing step 0 (which must name legal and security, not only churn and SLA cases) and the security bypass grafted into bug-report-handoff.

issues.quote: You work from the ticket as written, the customer's account record, the help centre, and the product notes the team gives you.
issues.problem: Adding customer-support-research brings in tier-3 chat and email, tier-4 web and tier-5 inference ('Analogous customers', 'General best practices'). The identity's other line, 'using only steps the documentation or a teammate confirmed', does not say how those looked-up findings may be used, so a medium- or low-confidence research answer could be drafted to a customer as fact.
issues.fix: Add: 'When you look something up in team chat, email or the web, treat it as a lead for a teammate to confirm, not as an answer; only the help centre, product notes or a teammate's confirmation go to a customer as fact.'

issues.problem: The tagline ('turns repeat questions into help articles'), the bio ('show which questions keep coming back') and weekly-ticket-themes are all recurring by nature, yet Sasha has no standing work, and support-getting-started never offers any.
issues.fix: Add two opt-in routines, each staging drafts only and asking for the queue location and timezone. The first is a weekday morning queue brief (ticket-triage, quiet when nothing is urgent). Offer it only when a queue source is connected (the HubSpot or Gmail block, or a help-desk MCP), because Zendesk, Intercom and Freshdesk have no block and a routine cannot wait for a pasted export. The second is a Monday weekly-ticket-themes run that reloads last period's codebook and lists the next macro or article candidate.

issues.quote: Drafts answers from your help centre and product notes, with unknowns left as clear questions for the team.
issues.problem: day_one delivers only the first two verbs of the tagline (triage, replies). The knowledge half of the persona (macros, help articles, repeat-question counts) has no first-week deliverable.
issues.fix: Add a third item, e.g. 'Your top repeat questions, counted: from a ticket export, lists the questions that keep coming back with ticket counts and drafts the first macro or help article for approval', timed 'after a ticket export'.

issues.quote: Plain, kind, and specific, with the answer first and no scripted sympathy.
issues.problem: It says what to avoid but not what replaces it for a blocked or upset customer. customer-response-drafting (graft source) says 'Lead with empathy' and Robin's draft-the-reply is apology-first, so the merged reply skill needs a stated rule.
issues.fix: Append: 'When a customer is blocked, name the specific impact in one sentence, then give the answer.' Add a short banned-phrase list (e.g. 'sorry for the inconvenience', 'great question') for support-reply-draft to read.

issues.quote: I help small support teams answer faster without guessing.
issues.problem: Robin ('Customer Support Specialist', 34 skills) covers triage, replies, KB, refunds, escalations and VoC, and Sasha's job_title ('Support Specialist') is almost the same. Sasha's body never says what makes her the right hire over Robin, so the two personas blur when both are on a team.
issues.fix: Sharpen the identity around the small-team help desk and its knowledge base: the queue brief, the cited reply, and the macro or article that stops the next ticket. Name the handoffs: product signals and feature requests go to the product teammate, disputes to finance, churn to customer success, and security reports to the security or compliance owner. Consider a distinguishing job_title such as 'Help Desk & Knowledge Specialist'.

clusters.job: triage and prioritise support tickets

members.note: Queue mode, 'Rank by impact and urgency, not tone', the loud/polite rule, evidence-based duplicate grouping and a strong, hard no-action guardrail match Sasha's identity and day_one. It is thin on urgency.

Single-ticket upstream package. Carry over its 9-category taxonomy, routing table, per-ticket output block and escalation triggers. Its guardrails are weak: its duplicate step links, notifies and bumps priority directly, and its templates assert actions that did not happen. PR #13 only renames the H1.

proposed.name: Ticket triage
proposed.description: Use when open tickets need ordering: rank a queue or one new ticket by impact and SLA clock, not tone; categorise it, group duplicates only on shared evidence, and return a queue brief with route, next owner and unknowns. Proposes links and routes; never replies, merges or reassigns.
proposed.rationale: The two are close overall. The original is the base because its much stronger guardrails and persona rules define Sasha, and because day_one promises a triaged queue while the upstream skill handles only one ticket. The upstream package supplies the structure the original lacks: categories, routes, a per-ticket block and urgency triggers. Its hard-coded SLA is kept only as a labelled default, which matches its own ATTRIBUTION.md: 'Deploy only where the original P1-P4 priority and response-time model fits the support desk'.
drops: support-ticket-triage 'Usage' block, '# /ticket-triage' H1 (PR #13: '# /support-ticket-triage') and argument-hint (Claude Code slash constructs)
~~support platform / ~~knowledge base / ~~project tracker placeholders; replace with run_block (HubSpot, Linear, GitHub, Notion) or run_mcp_tool, else ask for a CSV export or paste

The triage block's 'Suggested Initial Response' section and all 'Auto-Response Templates by Category' ('I've logged this as a [priority] issue', 'I've escalated this to our security team', 'Great question!'); first replies go through support-reply-draft
Duplicate Detection's direct actions ('Link the new ticket', 'Notify the customer', 'Bump priority')
'The customer explicitly escalates or mentions executive involvement' as an automatic bump (becomes a flag for the owner)
Triage Best Practices #3 'err on the side of higher'
Step 6 'Offer Next Steps' with its '/customer-escalation' reference
Original's 'or the question is answered in the docs' as a tier criterion (becomes a routing flag, not a priority)

grafts.what: The 9 categories (bug, how-to, feature request, billing, account, integration, security, data, performance) with signal words, plus the tie-breaks: a bug outranks a feature request; root cause drives category (a login failure caused by a bug is Bug); 'It used to work and now it doesn't' = Bug. Put these in references/category-taxonomy.md and add a category column to the brief.

Urgency factors inside each impact tier: waiting past the team's SLA, multiple customers with the same issue, a workaround that stopped working, and scope expanding. Keep the P1-P4 hour targets (1h/4h/1 business day/2 business days) only as defaults, used when setup memory holds no team targets and marked as such. Compute time since first customer contact.

Single-ticket mode block: Category, Priority with a one-line justification, Workaround (Available / Not available / Unknown), Related tickets, Known issue (Yes / No / Checking), Route to + Why, and Internal notes, adding what was already checked or ruled out from Triage Best Practices #6. Queue mode keeps the original's brief as a table (id, tier, reason, clock, category, group, next owner, unverified).

Route table (Tier 1/2, Engineering, Product, Security, Billing/Finance), mapped to Sasha's own skills: engineering to bug-report-handoff, money asks to refund-and-exception-brief, docs-answered tickets to support-reply-draft or a macro, security to the named owner without quoting sensitive content, feature requests to the product teammate.

The four search passes: symptom/error text, same customer, same product area, known issues. Rewrite them as proposals ('propose linking to #X; list the new details for the parent ticket'), and keep the original's rule that a group needs the same symptom plus one more piece of evidence.

clusters.job: draft a customer support reply for approval

members.note: The most complete of the originals. Lists every question in order, cites a confirming doc for each, answers first in the customer's words, asks at most one question, and puts an approval note above the draft. Matches the Dana voice sample exactly.

430 lines. Carry over the internal verify/risk notes, channel lengths, quality checklist, situation playbooks and escalation format. Its templates assert actions not taken ('I've confirmed the issue and escalated it'), and its 'Lead with empathy' structure conflicts with Sasha's voice.

proposed.name: Support reply draft
proposed.description: Use when a support ticket or thread needs an answer: list each question, cite the doc that confirms it, and draft an answer-first, channel-sized reply with at most one question, under an approval note. Routes refunds, bugs, legal, security or churn threats first. Never sends.
proposed.rationale: The base is the stronger and far leaner skill, is Sasha's voice verbatim, and already has the per-question citation the upstream skill lacks. The upstream skill contributes what the base's review flags as missing: channel adaptation, handling for upset or blocked customers, an internal verify/risk block, and escalation triggers that become a routing step 0.
drops: '# /draft-response' H1 (PR #13: '# /customer-response-drafting'), 'Usage' block and slash examples
~~email / ~~chat / ~~CRM / ~~support platform / ~~knowledge base research list (use a pasted thread plus the connected Gmail/HubSpot/Notion blocks)
'Core Principles' #1 'Lead with empathy' and #7 'Match their energy'; the 'Celebratory' tone row
'Tone Adjustments by Relationship Stage' and the 'Executive communication' length row (account-management tone, not help-desk replies)

The first four 'Response Templates for Common Scenarios' (bug report, billing/account, won't-build feature request, outage) as written. They assert 'I've confirmed the issue and escalated it', 'I've looked into your account' and 'I discussed this with our product team'. They close with 'I'm sorry for the inconvenience' (billing) or '[what you're doing to prevent recurrence if known]' (outage). Only the follow-up-after-silence template survives, rewritten as a variant.
Writing Style Rules lines on 'specific dates and times ... by Friday January 24' and 'Name specific people when assigning actions' unless the date or owner is sourced
Base's 'and when the team will update' (becomes a {next_update} placeholder)

grafts.what: Add 'Things to verify', 'Risk factors', 'Follow-up needed' and 'Escalation note' to the existing approval note, plus a Channel line (email / ticket / chat).

Channel sizing: chat 1-4 sentences, support ticket response 1-3 short paragraphs, email 3-5 paragraphs max. The rule for public or social replies (short acknowledgement, details moved to private) is not in this section. It comes from support-reply-draft's own review fix and matches Robin's social-and-community-support; add it as a base fix, not a graft.

Pre-approval checklist: no commitments beyond what's authorised, no roadmap details that shouldn't be shared, accurate references to previous conversations, a clear next step with an owner, length right for the channel.

Move condensed playbooks for a product question, an issue or bug, handling an escalation, bad news (delay, can't-fix) and declining a request to references/situations.md. Strip every timeline commitment unless the date or cadence is sourced, and use {next_update} otherwise. That covers 'commit to finding out, give a timeline', 'Set expectations for resolution timeline', 'Commit to updates at regular intervals' and 'Provide a clear action plan with timeline'. A blocked customer gets their specific impact named in one sentence instead of a scripted apology. Outage is not in this section. For outages, take only the field structure of the 'Outage or Incident Communication' template (What happened / Impact / Status / next update), not its apology or prevention lines.

Add routing step 0 before drafting. A threat to cancel, an exception request, a case unresolved past SLA or a request for leadership is flagged to the owner, and only a holding reply is drafted. Also cover what this section lacks but the description and the base eval require: legal threats and security or data-exposure reports go straight to the named owner from setup memory (security via bug-report-handoff's security bypass), with a holding reply only. Use the section's 'Escalation format' block (customer, one-line summary, urgency, customer impact, history, what was tried, what is needed, deadline) as the internal flag, so non-bug escalations still get a usable note now that customer-escalation's leadership tier is not carried. Money asks run refund-and-exception-brief; suspected bugs also run bug-report-handoff.
A short follow-up draft variant for unanswered threads. Offer schedule_followup to re-draft it rather than implying an automated send.

clusters.job: write or revise a help-centre article from repeat tickets

members.note: Starts from a counted repeat question, uses customer search words, allows only confirmed steps, redacts customer wording, and keeps the internal source note separate. Its guardrails are strong. It notes that an existing article may need fixing but has no revision branch, and it has no article types or metadata.

Excellent output, but weak guardrails and a poor platform fit. It has no invented-step rule, no PII scrub and no approval gate, and it is still a '/kb-article' slash command (PR #13 leaves SKILL.md unchanged). Its per-type templates and searchability rules are the best article craft in the catalog.

proposed.name: Help article from tickets
proposed.description: Use when a question keeps coming back: count its tickets and draft a new or revised help article (how-to, troubleshooting, FAQ or known issue) in the customer's search words, with only confirmed steps and an internal source note. Never publishes.
proposed.rationale: The upstream package scores 4 points higher, but only on craft. As a base it would bring its unsafe gaps (hallucinated UI paths, public fix dates, no approval gate) and 363 lines. recommendations.notes:
Coverage check. I read all eight live kit SKILL.md files and customer-support-research in full. I also read the upstream sections that the merges say they take in (customer-response-drafting situations, templates and follow-up; customer-escalation gate, tiers, repro steps and follow-up cadence). None of the seven recommendations repeats what the merged kit does. The per-ticket outage reply, the escalate-or-handle gate, repro-step writing, the article-type templates and the medians in weekly-ticket-themes are all already covered, and each sketch hands off to them.

Robin line. Robin, the other support expert, already has skills for four of these gaps: own-to-closure, troubleshoot-and-resolve, mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms and sensitive-data-safe-handling. I read all four and did not recommend sharing any of them.
- own-to-closure hard-codes 'ack within hours, resolve within one business day', acknowledges every case, and adds retention and upsell steps.
- troubleshoot-and-resolve 'ships relief' workarounds and names a root cause. Sasha's identity forbids both.
- mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms is sized for a war room (breach, recall, bulk refunds).
- sensitive-data-safe-handling covers redaction and card/health data, not identity checks.
Sharing any of them would also blur the Sasha/Robin line the body review asked to sharpen. So open-ticket-follow-up and guided-troubleshooting are new, narrower skills that borrow those patterns.

Other catalog skills I considered and left out:
- holding-statement-draft (Noor): a press statement for the first hours. It is the handoff target when an incident goes public.
- data-subject-request-draft (Lena): the privacy owner's side. It is the handoff target for account-access-and-privacy-requests.
- legal-response-drafting: a legal-team skill.
- quality-csat-and-coaching: team-lead scoring of reps.
- knowledge-centered-service: overlaps help-article-from-tickets.

- SkillMedev/skills is MIT-licensed. The LICENSE file reads 'Copyright (c) 2026 Alexander Ouellet'. Both pinned raw files at commit a28c4ce9366b5a8540577bed8f70b6a60f8fde27 returned HTTP 200. Each package is a single SKILL.md with no sibling files.
- status-page-update names skills that are not shipped (postmortem-writer, sev-triage, escalation-summary). Remove those names. Its fixed cadence numbers (first post within 15 min, then every 30-60 min) also need to come from setup memory.
- The repo also has support-macro-library, support-ticket-reply, kb-article-writer, help-documentation and refund-deescalation. The kit already covers these.
- No deferred package fits support.

Suggested follow-ups for the expert file:
- Add a weekday 'follow-up sweep' routine backed by open-ticket-follow-up.
- Use schedule_followup for the next status update while a known issue is open.
- Add a privacy and identity line to the boundaries, e.g. 'never confirm an account exists or change login, owner or data to an unverified requester'.
- Add the new slugs in working order: guided-troubleshooting after customer-support-research; known-issue-updates after bug-report-handoff; account-access-and-privacy-requests beside refund-and-exception-brief; open-ticket-follow-up after support-reply-draft; release-support-readiness and csat-feedback-review before weekly-ticket-themes.

Left out on purpose: SLA and backlog dashboards beyond the medians in weekly-ticket-themes (Robin's support-ops-improvement-program), churn saves (route to Riley or Robin), and shift handoffs (low value for the small teams Sasha serves). A periodic help-centre freshness sweep is folded into release-support-readiness rather than made its own skill.

recommendations.name: Known issue updates
recommendations.purpose: Keeps every customer hit by one known issue or outage informed from first report to confirmed fix: status-page text, one update for all linked tickets, and the resolved notice that asks them to confirm.
recommendations.why: Sasha's queue-brief voice sample (three urgent tickets on one Safari login loop, 'no fix confirmed yet') is this lifecycle. The kit only covers the first three steps: grouping (ticket-triage), the engineering report (bug-report-handoff) and single-ticket replies (support-reply-draft). Nothing sends the group updates on a cadence, drafts the status-page post, or tells every linked ticket when the fix ships. Status-page updates by stage (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), each with a stated next-update time, are standard SaaS support practice. SkillMedev status-page-update (MIT, verified) supplies the stage templates, cadence and no-blame rules. Two catalog skills are near misses. Robin's mass-recovery-and-bulk-comms runs at war-room scale (breach, recall, bulk refunds), and Noor's holding-statement-draft is a press statement for the first hours. Neither keeps track of linked tickets. Adapt the upstream skill this way: cadence and next-update times come from setup memory; a cause goes into the 'identified' stage only in words engineering confirmed; no fix time or postmortem promise without the owner's yes; names of unshipped sibling skills are removed.

source.ref: SkillMedev/skills skills/status-page-update@a28c4ce9366b5a8540577bed8f70b6a60f8fde27

sketch: Known-issue record saved to memory: symptom in the customer's words, exact scope, linked ticket ids from the ticket-triage group, bug report link, engineering owner, and each confirmed fact with its source and time, so every update builds on the last.

Stage templates in references/status-stages.md (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), adapted from upstream. Cadence comes from setup memory. No cause, fix date or postmortem promise without the owner's confirmation; unknowns are written as {next_update}.
Linked-ticket update: one body with per-ticket variables and the list of ticket ids it goes to. Tickets with account-specific wrinkles go to support-reply-draft instead.
Resolved notice that asks each customer to confirm the fix, a reopen rule, and handoffs: the known-issue article to help-article-from-tickets, credit requests to refund-and-exception-brief.

Escalate out: data exposure or security goes to the security owner, and press or public heat goes to Noor (holding-statement-draft). Bulk credits go to the approver as one packet and are never promised to customers.
Every status post and bulk update is staged for the named approver. Nothing goes to the status page or help desk directly; approvals are logged.

recommendations.name: Account access and privacy requests
recommendations.purpose: Handles tickets where the requester's identity is the risk (lost access, login-email or owner change, data access or deletion requests): verify first, leak nothing, and route to the privacy owner with the deadline clock running.
recommendations.why: Support-specialist job descriptions require following GDPR and SOC 2 standards 'during data handling and verification'. Under GDPR Art. 12(3), a data request must be answered within one month of receipt, and that receipt is often the support inbox. Art. 12(6) lets the company ask for information to confirm identity. Account recovery through support is a well-known social-engineering route to account takeover. The body review notes 'there is no privacy rule' in Sasha's persona. The kit never tells Sasha how to answer 'change my login email' or 'delete my data' without confirming to a stranger that the account exists. Lena's data-subject-request-draft covers the privacy owner's side (scoping the search, drafting the fulfilment reply). Robin's sensitive-data-safe-handling covers redaction and card or health data, not identity checks. This skill is the support front door that hands off to both.

source.ref: new; handoff target data-subject-request-draft (catalog, Lena)

sketch: Recognise the request type: access recovery, login-email or owner change, admin or seat transfer, data access, deletion, correction, marketing opt-out, suspected takeover, or a password or card number pasted into a ticket (redact it and advise rotation).

Verification rules come from setup memory: only the company's approved checks, such as a reply from the email on file or confirmation from the account admin. Never confirm the account exists, reveal account details, or accept ID photos unless the written policy allows it. An unclear check means stop.

Clock and routing: log the date received, the channel and the quoted request. Take the deadline from the company procedure; statutory deadlines are marked 'confirm with privacy owner'. Hand off to the privacy owner or Lena via consult_teammate. Signs of takeover go to the security owner at once.
Drafts: a neutral acknowledgement that does not confirm the account, a verification request, and a holding reply ('passed to our privacy team', {next_update}).
Never change email, owner or 2FA, and never delete or export data. Draft only, and log every handoff.
Save the verification policy and privacy owner to memory so ticket-triage and support-reply-draft route these tickets here.

recommendations.name: Open ticket follow-up
recommendations.purpose: Sweeps tickets that are waiting on the customer, on another team, or on a promised update, and stages the nudge, status update or close proposal before anything goes quiet.
recommendations.why: Specialists own pending and on-hold tickets, and common help desks (Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout) auto-close pending tickets after N days. The merged support-reply-draft now writes a {next_update} placeholder and bug-report-handoff passes work to engineering, but no skill checks that the update went out or that an escalated ticket is still moving. The 'Follow-up Cadence After Escalation' table from upstream customer-escalation was not merged. This skill also gives Sasha the recurring routine the body review found missing. Robin's own-to-closure is the near neighbour, but it hard-codes 'resolve within one business day', acknowledges every case and adds upsell steps, so a narrower Sasha version keeps the line between the two experts clear.

source.ref: new; patterned on own-to-closure (catalog, Robin) and the follow-up cadence table in customer-escalation (Apache-2.0)

sketch: Inputs: open, pending and on-hold tickets with last customer touch, last agent touch, promised update dates, and linked bug status (Linear or GitHub via run_block). Ages are computed in bash_exec.

Buckets: promise due or overdue; waiting on the customer (first nudge, final nudge, then a close proposal per the team's auto-close rule in memory); waiting on engineering or finance (internal chaser plus a customer status update); fixed upstream (hand to known-issue-updates or draft a confirm-the-fix reply).
One staged draft per ticket, following support-reply-draft's rules. No 'closing because you did not reply' tone, and a close is proposed only under the written policy.
Board ordered most overdue first, with owner and next date, deduplicated against the last run stored in memory.
Offer a weekday sweep via schedule_routine. A run with nothing due reports in one line.

recommendations.name: Guided troubleshooting
recommendations.purpose: Works a 'something doesn't work' ticket through isolation steps before it becomes a reply or a bug report, and keeps the diagnostic questions for each issue family as a reusable tree.
recommendations.why: Support-specialist job descriptions list 'initial triage and troubleshooting for issues such as login problems, system errors, and application access'. In the kit, customer-support-research looks answers up, and the merged bug-report-handoff has the escalate-or-handle gate and repro-step writing. Nothing tells Sasha how to isolate a fault (environment, account state, plan limit, recent release, known issue) or how to choose the one clear question her identity promises. The voice sample's 'ask for browser version' is exactly that kind of diagnostic choice. Robin's troubleshoot-and-resolve exists, but it ships unlabelled 'relief' workarounds and names a root cause, both of which Sasha's identity forbids.

source.ref: new

sketch: Intake: the symptom in the customer's words, exact error text, start time, what they already tried, their environment, and what customer-support-research and the known-issue list already say.

Isolation ladder: environment (browser, cache, extensions, network), then account state (plan limits, permissions, settings), then a recent change (release notes or status page), then a product defect. Each step names the evidence that rules it in or out.
Reproduce with browser_navigate and browser_screenshot, only on a test account the team supplied. Record the steps and screenshots, and never use customer credentials.
Choose the single question that best splits the remaining causes and hand it to support-reply-draft.
Outcomes: a docs-confirmed fix goes to support-reply-draft; a match with a known issue joins the triage group; a new defect goes to bug-report-handoff with what was ruled out.

Save a diagnostic tree per issue family to the workspace (templates/diagnostic-tree.md), citing the tickets it came from and a last-verified date. The trees feed support-macro-library and the troubleshooting article type in help-article-from-tickets.

recommendations.name: Release support readiness
recommendations.purpose: When a release, price or policy change is about to ship, lists what customers will ask and which macros and help articles it breaks, and drafts the updates before the tickets arrive.
recommendations.why: Support specialists are expected to stay current on product changes and to keep saved replies and help content accurate, and stale macros after a release are a common source of wrong answers. In Sasha's kit, support-macro-library and help-article-from-tickets start only after repeat tickets appear; nothing is triggered by a change. Priya's release-notes-draft writes the customer-facing notes, Casey's release-readiness-checklist is for engineering, and Zara's and Alex's launch plans are at go-to-market scale. None updates support content. The platform can read GitHub releases, Linear and Notion changelogs via run_block, and public changelog or help-centre pages via web_fetch.

source.ref: new

sketch: Inputs: the release notes, changelog, Linear issues or pricing/policy change document; the ship date; the plans affected; and the macro and article inventory from memory or the workspace.
Impact map: each change, its effect for customers, and the macros and articles that describe the old behaviour (found by UI names, limits and prices), with the exact line to change.
Internal FAQ of expected questions with confirmed answers and named owners for unknowns. Decisions such as grandfathering or refunds are flagged to the refund-and-exception-brief approver.
Macro diffs, article edits and a list of screenshots to retake, all staged for approval and written under the rules of support-macro-library and help-article-from-tickets.
After ship: watch tickets that mention the release for a week and feed weekly-ticket-themes. Optionally run a stale-content sweep for broken links and old last-updated dates.

recommendations.name: CSAT feedback review
recommendations.purpose: Reads low satisfaction ratings and their comments, sorts each by cause (the answer, speed, policy or the product), and stages the recovery reply or the macro or article fix it points to.
recommendations.why: Help desks commonly send satisfaction (CSAT) surveys, support staff are often measured on them, and small teams usually review low ratings by hand. In the kit, weekly-ticket-themes groups tickets, not survey comments, and nothing follows up on an unhappy rating. Robin's quality-csat-and-coaching scores reps for a team lead, which is not Sasha's role. SkillMedev csat-root-cause (MIT, verified) supplies a two-level coding scheme, separate analysis of detractors and promoters, a frequency-by-impact matrix, and noise rules (under 30 comments or under 5 per theme is not a trend). Adapt it this way: add a per-ticket recovery branch; make the fixed 15% and 2.5/5 escalation thresholds settings in memory; compute in bash_exec; score no agents; redact quoted comments.

source.ref: SkillMedev/skills skills/csat-root-cause@a28c4ce9366b5a8540577bed8f70b6a60f8fde27

sketch: Inputs: a CSAT or NPS export (CSV or help-desk MCP) with ticket ids, scores, comments and the period. State the response rate.

Per-ticket pass: read the thread for each low rating and classify it (wrong or unclear answer, slow, policy, product bug, not about support). Stage a recovery reply only where there is something to fix or explain.

Coding and counts, adapted from upstream (references/coding-scheme.md): detractors kept separate; frequency and mean score per theme computed in bash_exec; under 30 comments, list them rather than claim a trend.
Route each fix: a wrong answer to a macro or article fix, a product problem to bug-report-handoff or weekly-ticket-themes, a policy complaint to the policy owner.
Report the top themes with quoted, redacted comments and ticket ids. Never name or score an individual agent.

recommendations.name: Multilingual support reply
recommendations.purpose: Drafts a reply to a non-English ticket in the customer's language from the same confirmed sources, with an English back-translation for the approver and a glossary of terms never to translate.
recommendations.why: Small SaaS and e-commerce teams get tickets in several languages without a native speaker on staff, and bilingual support is a common requirement in support-specialist postings. support-reply-draft assumes a single language, and the macros and articles have no locale handling. The model can draft in the major languages with no extra integration. The real risk is that meaning drifts in refund, legal, security or account-access text, so the skill needs a back-translation check and a native-review flag. SkillMedev localization-guide (MIT) is about marketing copy and could inform only the notes format, so this should be written new.

source.ref: new

sketch: Detect the language and formality register, and reply in the customer's language unless they switch.
A glossary in memory keeps product names, plan names and button labels exactly as the customer's interface shows them.
Show the draft and its English back-translation side by side, and flag any sentence whose meaning shifted.
Flag refunds, legal, security and account-access text for native review before approval.
Save localised macro variants with the source macro id and a last-verified date.

proposal.summary:
Sofia's live kit is ten NICK skills plus the ORIGINAL resume-screening she shares with Harper. Every slug has an open rebuild: PR #16 for ten of them and PR #15 for resume-screening. Each rebuild is stronger than its main version except candidate-sourcing-strategy and passive-candidate-outreach, where main is marginally ahead. I still pick the PR version of those two: each adds checks main lacks, and their scripts enforce the persona's "no link, no card", do-not-contact and honesty rules (card_check.py, dedupe_names.py, lint_outreach.py, log_touch.py). Toran's three packages (candidate-interview-planning, recruiting-pipeline, employment-offer-drafting) are thin, generic duplicates. PR #13 changes only ATTRIBUTION.md in all three, plus the slash-command name in employment-offer-drafting, so all three are dropped. The only true merge is job-offer-and-close-plan: PR #16 cut main's resignation-coaching and accept-to-start tracks down to a "first-week hand-off" row, and they should be grafted back. The remaining calls are PR-over-main picks that need these fixes first:
- Remove the "unless they are evidence about the job" exception in getting-started.
- Let prefs.py store the preference keys the sibling skills read (outreach_cadence, outreach_max_words, min_sample, touch_limit, stall.<item>, response_window_hours and others). Today it refuses them.
- Make the "A Slack channel" brief destination a DM.
- Stop KEEPABLE letting age and affect remarks back into the debrief brief.
- Parse every money field in check_terms.py with term_amount(). Today a formatted base pay skips the band check.
- Fix the business-day stall bar in funnel.py so it matches stall_sweep.py.
- Lint the Probe lines in interview kits.
- Add the do-not-contact check to the ATS-export path in resume-screening.
- Add a no-enrichment rule for candidate contact details.

One check covers the whole kit: every PR #16 skill uses find_capability, run_capability and TodoWrite, citing an internal platform code audit [114]. Confirm those names once against the runtime rather than skill by skill.

Across experts, Harper's PR #15 kit ships scripts under the same names (jd_lint.py, collate_scorecards.py, flag_remarks.py, check_terms.py, question_lint.py), and the copies have diverged. Three of the bugs above are Sofia-only:
- Harper's question_lint.py already lints every line.
- Harper's collator has no --keep restore path.
- Harper's check_terms.py has no band check.
So fix those in Sofia's copies, and converge the scripts later. Only the EU pay-transparency gap in posting-law-fields.md needs fixing in both kits.

body_review.summary:
A sharp, well-bounded persona. The identity routes each request type to a kit skill in hiring-lifecycle order, every routine is draft-only and stays quiet when there is nothing to report, and the protected-characteristic, do-not-contact and same-turn-deletion rules are explicit. All 11 kit slugs survive the merge, so nothing in routines, day_one or preloads points at a dropped skill. The gaps fall into two kinds. First, the body lags behind rules the PR #16 skills now enforce: salary-history bans, FCRA-gated declines, off-limits companies, escalating a discriminatory interviewer remark, and record retention before deletion. Second, there are small internal mismatches:
- The first-chat route names Harper's skill.
- The weekly review hard-codes the outreach cadence and ranks 'the best three' names.
- 'Batch size' is ambiguous between weekly and per run.
- A routine asks where to post a review it never posts.
- The bio and the evening-prep routine use a narrower protected list than identity.
strengths: The identity routes every request type to a named kit skill in lifecycle order (role intake through analytics), so trigger ambiguity inside the kit is low.
FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN labelling and 'No link, no card' carry through the bio, identity, day_one[1] and the daily-candidate-batch routine, which gives the skills one evidence standard.

The protected list is complete in identity and boundaries (it includes graduation year used as an age proxy and reading off photos), and the do-not-contact rule (keep name and flag only) and same-turn deletion are both concrete.
Every routine says it sends nothing, collapses unchanged items into a rollup, and goes silent or one-line when empty; urgent-thread-check produces no output without Gmail or Slack.
The voice samples are short and answer-first; the morning brief names who each blocked item is waiting on and ends on one question.
body_review.kit_alignment:
No routine, day_one item or preload names a slug that the proposal drops or renames, and preloads is empty. Point by point:
- identity routes a first chat to 'recruiting getting started', which is Harper's slug (recruiting-getting-started). Sofia's skill is sofia-getting-started, though its H1 is also 'Recruiting getting started'.
- identity routes 'screen plans' to resume screening. Only the PR #15 version has a screen-plan template (templates/screen-plan.md); main does not, so choosing 15:resume-screening closes that promise.
- routines[1] hard-codes a 'day-2/5/8 cadence', while 16:passive-candidate-outreach reads the cadence from an owner preference (outreach_cadence) with 2/5/8 as the default. Note that 16:sofia-getting-started's prefs.py currently refuses to store outreach_cadence, which was tested as 'unknown key'. The skill-side fix is in c1.
- routines[1] asks for 'the best three' new names, which ranks sourced prospects (see the scoring issue).
- routines[3] says 'batch size' (default 10), but sofia-getting-started collects a weekly number (weekly_batch_size), and 16:candidate-sourcing-strategy divides it by five per run.
- routines[4] and the bio list a narrower set of protected traits than identity does.
- daily-hiring-brief reads brief_destination, and onboarding offers 'A Slack channel'. The brief names candidates, which contradicts identity's 'Nothing that identifies a candidate is ever posted to a group channel'. 16:interview-coordination already restricts Slack delivery to a DM, so the fix belongs in c1.
- Several rules the rebuilt skills enforce are missing from the body: never ask for or use pay history (16:job-offer-and-close-plan), FCRA-gated declines (16:interview-coordination), off-limits companies (16:role-intake-and-scorecard), no enrichment of contact details, and record retention before a deletion (16:interview-coordination step E only mentions it after the fact).
- The body's 'You never score a candidate yourself' sits awkwardly beside candidate-sourcing-strategy's tiering of sourced prospects.

issues.quote: never estimate a compensation band or infer one from a company's stage
issues.problem: The persona never forbids asking for or using a candidate's current or past pay. Salary-history bans (CA Labor Code 432.3 and others) are cited in 16:job-offer-and-close-plan references/pay-history-and-transparency.md and 16:interview-kit-design references/unlawful-question-rewrites.md, but the persona-level rule is missing, so an owner request like 'ask what they make now' has no persona backstop.
issues.fix: Append: 'Never ask for, record, or use a candidate's current or past pay, even when volunteered; ask for expectations for this role instead.'

issues.quote: Your raw material is limited to what the owner hands you and what people have put out publicly about their own professional work
issues.problem: Nothing forbids running email-finder or enrichment tools on candidates, and the platform exposes Apollo, Enrichlayer and ZeroBounce blocks. The only explicit contact-detail rules sit in 16:passive-candidate-outreach step 1 ('never guess or pattern-build an email'), in interview-coordination and in the commit-email line of github-sourcing.md. None of them is in the sourcing skill's guardrails.
issues.fix: Add: 'Never run an email-finder or enrichment tool on a candidate, never guess or pattern-build a personal email or phone number, and never store one they did not publish professionally or the owner did not give you.'

issues.quote: none of it reaches a packet, a note, a draft, a scorecard, or a debrief.
issues.problem: The persona only says protected remarks are kept out. It does not say what to do when an interviewer writes one. Both debrief versions just cut and note the remark (the review's top issue for main, and it persists in 16:hiring-debrief-and-decision step 3). Nobody is told to raise it with the owner, to question the rating it came with, or to route it to HR or the attorney.
issues.fix: Add: 'When an interviewer's remark touches a protected characteristic, cut it from every shared brief, tell the owner privately, put the rating it accompanied back to that interviewer, and offer a one-line brief for HR or the attorney.'

issues.quote: You never score a candidate yourself, break a tie, or say who to hire.
issues.problem: candidate-sourcing-strategy tiers sourced prospects (strong fit / worth a look / stretch) and orders cards by strength, and routines[1] asks for 'the best three' new names. The shared 15:resume-screening refuses any rank, shortlist or top-N. The persona sentence doesn't say which is allowed, so the model may either refuse to tier a sourcing batch or rank applicants.
issues.fix: Clarify: 'Sourced prospects may be tiered by evidence against the bar, with the reason shown; applicants are never ranked, shortlisted or scored, and you never say who to hire.'

issues.quote: When the owner asks you to remove a candidate, you do it immediately, in that same reply, without asking why.
issues.problem: US employers generally must keep application and hiring records for at least a year (EEOC 29 CFR 1602.14; ADEA 29 CFR 1627.3), and longer under a charge or litigation hold. 16:interview-coordination step E only mentions retention after it has deleted everything, and onboarding already collects retention_policy. As written, the persona can destroy records the owner is legally required to keep.
issues.fix: Add: 'If the owner's retention_policy or a legal hold covers hiring records, say so in one line in that same reply and remove the person from working files, briefs and batches, keeping only the retained record where the policy says; otherwise delete as asked.'

issues.quote: A first chat or empty memory goes to recruiting getting started;
issues.problem: 'recruiting getting started' is the slug of Harper's skill (recruiting-getting-started). Sofia's onboarding skill is sofia-getting-started. On a team with Harper hired, this routes Sofia to the wrong expert's onboarding.
issues.fix: Change to 'goes to sofia getting started', and rename the skill's H1 from 'Recruiting getting started' to match.

issues.quote: Employment legal questions go to the attorney with a one-line brief and the facts; sales closing goes to sales; support tickets go to support.
issues.problem: The sales and support handoffs are generic boilerplate that never arise for a recruiter. The handoffs that do arise are missing: a signed hire's first week (people ops / Ines's new-hire-onboarding-plan), a headcount decision upstream of a req (James's ops-capacity-and-headcount-plan), adverse-impact or demographic funnel analysis (HR, or people-analytics-reporting), and background-check declines (the owner's FCRA adverse-action process).
issues.fix: Replace the sales and support clauses with: 'A signed hire's onboarding goes to people ops; headcount decisions to operations; any rate by a protected group to HR or counsel; a decline a background check touched to the owner's adverse-action process.'

issues.quote: nothing about age, family, health, or background goes in a packet, a note, or a scorecard
issues.problem: The user-facing bio promises a narrower protected list than identity and boundaries. It omits gender, race, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy and marital status, and 'background' is vague. It repeats the narrow-list defect the review flagged in sofia-getting-started.
issues.fix: Write: 'nothing about a protected characteristic, stated or guessed, goes in a packet, a note, or a scorecard, and I never read anything off a photo.'

issues.quote: Nothing about a candidate's age, family, health, religion, or background goes into any packet.
issues.problem: This is narrower than identity's protected list (it omits gender, race, nationality, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy and marital status), and 'background' is vague. It repeats the narrow-list defect the review flagged in sofia-getting-started.
issues.fix: Write: 'No protected characteristic, stated or guessed, and nothing read off a photo, goes into any packet; each summary line is a direct quote with its source.'

issues.quote: Where is the candidate pipeline tracked, and where should the review be posted?
issues.problem: This asks where to post, but step 6 of the same routine says 'It is not posted to a channel or emailed from this run; the owner sends it.'
issues.fix: Ask: 'Where is the candidate pipeline tracked, and where should I save the review for you to send?'

issues.quote: Follow-ups due: people whose next touch on the day-2/5/8 cadence is due now or overdue
issues.problem: 16:passive-candidate-outreach makes the cadence an owner preference (outreach_cadence, via followups_due.py --cadence), with 2/5/8 only as the default. The routine overrides a saved cadence.
issues.fix: Use: 'on the owner's saved outreach cadence (default day 2/5/8)'. Pair this with the c1 prefs.py fix so the key can actually be saved.

issues.quote: The owner sets the batch size; if they have not, use 10.
issues.problem: Onboarding stores a weekly number (weekly_batch_size: 'How many freshly sourced names a week'), which 16:candidate-sourcing-strategy divides by five for this weekday routine. As written, an owner who answered '50' could get 50 names a day.
issues.fix: Use: 'Aim for the owner's weekly batch size divided by five, rounded up; if it is unset, 10 per run.'

issues.quote: We're hiring one person to own release tooling end to end, and that is the problem. Worth 20 minutes this week?
issues.problem: The sample note names neither the company nor the sender. 16:passive-candidate-outreach requires 'every note names the company, role and real sender' as an anti-scam rule, so the persona's own example would fail its outreach guardrail.
issues.fix: Name the company in the role line and add a sign-off with the sender's name and title, for example '— Maya Chen, Head of Engineering, Northwind'.

issues.quote: the 2:00 slot still has no scorecard owner
issues.problem: This time has no timezone, which contradicts identity's 'every time you write carries its timezone'. The first time in the same sample is labelled ('10:00 your time').
issues.fix: 'the 14:00 slot (your time) still has no scorecard owner'.

issues.quote: Never send, post, book, cancel, reschedule, reject, or make an offer without the owner's yes to that specific action
issues.problem: There is no persona rule for declines where a background check or consumer report played a part. The PR #16 skills (interview-coordination step C, job-offer-and-close-plan guardrails) stop and route these to the owner's FCRA process, but the persona would allow a plain decline draft.
issues.fix: Add: 'If a background check played any part in a decline, draft nothing and route it to the owner's adverse-action process.'

issues.quote: booking, rescheduling, tracker updates, and stall sweeps to interview coordination
issues.problem: Declines and candidate-removal requests are handled in 16:interview-coordination (step C decline shapes, step E forget_candidate.py), but the routing sentence omits both. The same-turn deletion promise therefore has no named skill.
issues.fix: Extend it to 'booking, rescheduling, tracker updates, stall sweeps, decline drafts, and removal requests to interview coordination'.

issues.quote: What time should this land, and in which timezone?
issues.problem: urgent-thread-check runs hourly through the working day (H 9-17 * * 1-5), so 'what time should this land' doesn't fit this routine.

proposed.description: Use on the first chat with Sofia or when no hiring preferences are on file: sets up the hiring folder and tracker, reports connected tools, puts a draft scorecard for their role on screen first, then collects skippable preferences one at a time and offers routines singly.
proposed.rationale:
PR #16 turns the persona's promises (tracker as the record, a do-not-contact list with name and flag only, routines off until a yes, never re-asking what is connected) into files and scripts. Fixes before merge:
1. Guardrails still say remarks on age, family, health or background 'stay out unless they are evidence about the job', which contradicts the persona's 'whether stated or guessed'. Delete the exception and use the persona's full protected list.
2. prefs.py's PLAIN_KEYS whitelist refuses keys the sibling skills read from preferences.md. Tested: 'set outreach_cadence' and 'set min_sample' both exit 1 with 'unknown key'. The refused keys:
   - outreach_cadence and outreach_max_words (16:passive-candidate-outreach)
   - min_sample, touch_limit, attrition_window_days, heavy_day_per_interviewer and outreach_day_kind (16:hiring-pipeline-analytics)
   - stall.<item> and response_window_hours (16:interview-coordination)
   An owner's saved cadence or stall bar therefore can never reach those skills. Add them to PLAIN_KEYS, or a stall.<item> pattern to ROLE_KEY_RE.
3. preference-questions.md offers brief_destination 'A Slack channel', and connectors.md says Slack posts 'in the channel the team already reads'. Briefs and packets name candidates, which breaks the persona's rule that nothing identifying a candidate goes to a group channel. 16:interview-coordination already says a Slack delivery is a DM. Change the option to 'A Slack DM to me'.
4. Rename the H1 'Recruiting getting started' so it cannot be confused with Harper's recruiting-getting-started.
5. Kit-wide check, not specific to this skill: confirm the runtime exposes find_capability, run_capability, list_routines and TodoWrite, which PR #16 cites from an internal platform audit [114]. Otherwise fall back to the brief's memory_store, schedule_routine and todo_write.

Every rule it states (no link no card, warm before cold, benchmark orbit, three-passes-means-the-bar-is-off, market read) is carried into PR #16. It has no contact-details rule (review's top issue) and nothing checks its links.

The KEEPABLE regex in collate_scorecards.py (lines 141-143) includes words that describe a person: young, mature, confident, calm, sick, ill, family, looks, church, hair, weight, polished, energy, retir*. --keep therefore restores 'She is quite young for this.' and labels it a technical term, although SKILL.md step 2 says the script refuses person words.
