recommendations.name: Structured reference checks
recommendations.purpose: Plan, consent-gate, script and record reference calls on the scorecard's competencies, then feed the evidence into the debrief and the offer close plan without scoring the candidate.
recommendations.why: The kit says this is missing. PR #16 hiring-debrief-and-decision/references/debrief-integrity-checklist.md §8 says 'Structured reference calls are a gap in this kit', and job-offer-and-close-plan/references/contingency-order.md §3 says the skill 'records the owner's plan but does not design the calls'. Toran's review also lists no reference coverage. Yet the debrief's competency-brief template sends open questions to 'reference check where the process allows', and identity forbids inventing a reference. Reference calls are a routine recruiter task on nearly every agency and in-house TA job description, and they carry real legal edges: salary-history bans cover asking former employers (e.g. Cal. Lab. Code 432.3, already cited in the kit), FCRA investigative-consumer-report disclosure applies when a vendor runs the checks (15 U.S.C. 1681d), and defamation caution applies to negative references. Two MIT upstreams exist. The tuanductran/hr-skills package is the better base, because its content guides already require candidate consent, competency-anchored questions, caution on compensation history and retention of reference records. The procedure, templates and scripts still have to be written for Sofia. mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills reference-check-script (MIT, f6ca793) was rejected as a base: it recommends back-channel calls, a red/amber/green score and peer ranking, all of which conflict with Sofia's no-scoring and consent rules.

source.ref: tuanductran/hr-skills skills/hr-reference-checking @078f2fb651f1090e73a8cc6ba96f323f8b00b171 (content guides reusable; procedure, templates and scripts new)

sketch: Gates before anything else. The owner's reference_policy is read from preferences.md and needs a prefs.py key: whether checks are allowed, how many, at which stage, and whether only candidate-provided referees are used. Written candidate consent is logged before any referee is contacted. There are no back-channel calls without consent, and a DNC and forget check runs first.

Question plan built from the approved scorecard M-ids and the debrief's open questions, with the same core questions for every referee. Lint it with interview-kit-design's question_lint.py and the protected-traits list: no pay history, health, family, age proxies or 'rank them against peers'.

Drafts only: a consent and referee-request note to the candidate, a referee outreach email, and a 20-minute call guide with pre-written probes. Slots are booked through interview-coordination's tz_slots.py.

Notes template, one per referee: relationship and overlap dates, then quoted answers labelled FACT (the referee said it), INFERENCE or UNKNOWN. 'Policy only confirms dates and title' is recorded as exactly that. There is no score, colour or verdict, and a verify_quotes check runs before the notes are saved.

Legal routing. A vendor-run check gets an FCRA disclosure flag. A decline that a reference or vendor report influenced goes to interview-coordination's FCRA path. A negative or possibly defamatory reference goes to the owner with an attorney brief (job-offer templates/attorney-brief.md).

Hand-offs and records: the summary of which open questions were closed goes to hiring-debrief-and-decision, the contingency row is ticked in job-offer-and-close-plan's close-plan.csv, and files are kept under retention_policy and removed by forget_candidate.py.

recommendations.name: Interviewer training and calibration
recommendations.purpose: Keep a roster of trained interviewers per competency, and produce the training pack, the calibration session and a private scoring-drift read that keep structured loops structured.
recommendations.why: interview-kit-design/references/structured-interview-science.md marks 'Trained interviewers' as 'Out of scope for this skill (gap: interviewer training)', which leaves one of the 15 structure components (Campion et al., source [19] in that file) uncovered. The debrief checklist §9 says to 'calibrate the bar before the loop, not in the debrief', and decision_log.py flags loops that end without a clear call, but no skill runs the calibration. interview-coordination rebuilds a drop-out by naming 'a substitute who can take it (from the kit)', yet nothing records who is trained for which competency, or their timezone and hours (the requested tz_slots.py fix needs exactly that data). Training hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing is a standard line in TA job postings. The upstream interview-system-designer (alirezarezvani/borghei) mostly designs loops and so overlaps interview-kit-design. It was not chosen.
sketch: Interviewer roster CSV at ~/workspace/hiring/tracker/interviewers.csv: name, competencies cleared, shadow and reverse-shadow counts, last refresher date, timezone and working hours. interview-coordination reads it for substitutes and tz_slots.py.

Training pack drafted from the role's kit.md: a 30-minute outline and a one-page cheat sheet covering the same questions for every candidate, evidence-not-impression notes, the unlawful-question rewrites, the candidate-AI policy, and filing the scorecard alone before the debrief. Delivered as a Google Docs or Slides draft.
A rewrite-the-question exercise built from interview-kit-design/references/unlawful-question-rewrites.md, checked for completion only.

Calibration session: two or three mock or anonymised answer transcripts, rated independently against the anchors, with the spread shown per anchor. Anchor fixes are proposed back to interview-kit-design, never edited here.

Drift read script: each interviewer's rating distribution against the panel from filed scorecards, with a minimum-sample rule. It goes privately to the owner only, carries no candidate names, and is never used as a performance rating.
A shadow and reverse-shadow plan, with invites drafted through interview-coordination. Nothing is booked without the owner's yes.

recommendations.name: Candidate privacy requests and retention
recommendations.purpose: Run the owner-set retention schedule over the hiring folder, handle candidate access and deletion requests to their deadlines, and draft the notices owed to sourced or pooled people.
recommendations.why: The expert-body review lists 'record retention before a deletion' as missing, and interview-coordination's forget step only mentions retention after the fact. sofia-getting-started/references/hiring-folder.md sets retention rules (EEOC one-year floor [44], ICO claim period and talent-pool notice [100]) but says 'never purge on your own', and no skill ever sweeps. Candidate-initiated requests are not handled anywhere: GDPR access within one month, California applicants under CPRA since 2023, the Illinois AI Video Interview Act's 30-day deletion (already in jurisdiction-flags.md), and the GDPR Art. 14 notice owed to sourced people who never applied, even though shortlist.csv holds their data. Lena's catalog skill data-subject-request-draft is a generic 38-line placeholder with no knowledge of the hiring folder. It is the right consult target for company-wide requests, not a Sofia kit skill.
sketch: Retention schedule per jurisdiction and record type, set by the owner or counsel in preferences.md (retention_policy plus a litigation-hold flag). It stays UNSET until stated, and Sofia never picks a period.

Sweep script over the tracker, shortlist, outreach log, screens, packets, debriefs and offers. It lists records past their window with counts, skips anything on hold, and deletes nothing without one owner yes. Deletion then reuses forget_candidate.py.

Request intake: date received, the request quoted, the statutory deadline computed and labelled, and an identity check per the owner's procedure. It searches the hiring folder and the connected-systems list. Other people's data (interviewer notes that mention other candidates) is held back for review, and the reply is drafted, not sent.

Conflict rule: an owner or candidate deletion request that hits a retention hold means the person is suppressed from every batch and draft in the same turn, and the owner is told which records are held and why.

Notice drafts: an Art. 14 notice for sourced people at first contact or within a month, and a talent-pool notice before anyone is kept for future roles. Each is tracked per person in the outreach log.
Routing: company-wide or disputed requests go to Lena (data-subject-request-draft) or counsel with a one-line brief.

recommendations.name: Job posting distribution
recommendations.purpose: Take an approved posting live the right way: a channel plan, per-board packages with source-tagged apply links, a register of live posts with refresh and take-down dates, and every publish gated on the owner's yes.
recommendations.why: job-description-drafting deliberately ends at 'Not posted anywhere.' and treats publishing as out of scope, and no other kit skill picks up from there. For a small-team recruiter, choosing boards, niche communities and the careers page, then posting, refreshing and closing jobs, is weekly work. hiring-pipeline-analytics reports source-of-hire and cost per hire from tracker 'source' values and cost lines, but nothing assigns consistent source tags at posting time. Google for Jobs needs JobPosting structured data with validThrough and expects expired posts to be removed. The platform can run this: WordPress blocks and the generic HTTP block for careers pages, browser tools for board forms, and approval-gated outward actions. The Anthropic small-business job-post-builder (Apache-2.0) was checked. It overlaps the kit's posting, kit and offer skills and explicitly refuses to publish, so it does not fill this gap.
sketch: Channel plan per role: free boards, paid or sponsored boards, niche communities, and the careers page. Each channel's cost is labelled FACT or UNKNOWN and any spend is approved by the owner. A thin plan is called thin, not padded.

Per-channel package from posting-v<N>.md: character and field limits, the posting-law fields carried over from job-description-drafting, and apply links tagged with a source code that matches the tracker's source column.
A JobPosting schema.org JSON-LD snippet for the careers page, with validThrough, and a validation step in the sandbox.
Publish gate and approval log: each board post or careers-page update is its own owner yes. Outward actions run through run_block or the browser only after that yes.
Posting register CSV: channel, URL, date live, refresh date, close date. A take-down list is produced when the role fills or pauses.
An inbound acknowledgment auto-reply draft that makes the response-window promise from interview-coordination.

recommendations.name: Employee referral drive
recommendations.purpose: Ask the team for referrals against the approved bar, take them in cleanly with the referred person's consent, keep referrers updated without leaking candidate details, and track bonus eligibility under the owner's policy.
recommendations.why: Referrals are a leading source of hires for small teams. role-intake-and-scorecard/references/requirement-inflation.md §6 cites the referral share [34], and the scorecard template records referral_only. The tracker already carries source=referral and analytics reports on it. Yet no skill drafts the referral ask, handles the intake, dedupes it against the pipeline and DNC list, updates referrers or tracks bonuses. candidate-sourcing-strategy is limited to public professional evidence, and passive-candidate-outreach covers cold approaches only. The one upstream referral prompt found (tuanductran/hr-skills hr-recruiting/prompts/implementing-employee-referral-program.md) asks for 'demographic or cultural considerations' when generating referral candidates and was rejected.
sketch: Referral ask drafted from the approved scorecard: 'who has done M1/M2', never traits or demographics. The owner posts it, and it carries no candidate details, so a group channel is acceptable.

Intake sheet: referrer, referred person, a public professional link, how they know them, and whether the referred person agreed to be contacted. Rows are deduped against the tracker, shortlist and DNC list, and nobody is contacted without consent.

Same bar: referred people go through resume-screening on the same M-ids, with no stage skipped unless the owner's written policy says so. The referral-only-slate caution is repeated once from role-intake.
Referrer updates drafted per stage only, such as 'still in process' or 'not moving forward'. They never give reasons, scores or feedback, and they include a thank-you.
Bonus eligibility register quoting the owner's policy text. Sofia never decides a payout, and eligibility goes to finance or people ops.
Source tagging so hiring-pipeline-analytics can report referral conversion per role.

recommendations.name: Recruitment agency management
recommendations.purpose: Hold agency terms, take in agency submissions against the same bar, settle candidate-ownership questions from timestamps, and flag fees and guarantee windows on a hire.
recommendations.why: Small teams often use contingency agencies for hard roles, but the kit only knows agencies as a tracker source value (interview-coordination/references/tracker-schema.md) and as a fee line in hiring-pipeline-analytics/references/cost-per-hire.md. Stage updates to the agency without candidate-private detail or interviewer feedback beyond what the owner approves.

recommendations.notes:
What I checked: the PR #16 kit (10 skills) and the PR #15 resume-screening, file trees included, grepped for the usual recruiter tasks.

Already covered, so not recommended:
- Accommodation requests: a named contact in the posting, packets and invites.
- Re-engaging past candidates: candidate-sourcing-strategy, gated by retention_policy.
- FCRA-gated declines and identity checks: interview-coordination.
- Quality of hire, 90-day attrition and hiring-manager survey: hiring-pipeline-analytics.
- Pre-boarding: job-offer-and-close-plan hands off to the first-week owner.
- Candidate removal: forget_candidate.py.

Sources checked and not chosen:
- DEFERRED_SKILLS.md holds only the ads suite, invoice-chase and marketing packages. None is relevant.
- Anthropic human-resources plugin: comp-analysis contradicts the rule never to estimate a pay band. Its other hiring skills are the three Toran already imported.
- Anthropic small-business job-post-builder and hiring-screener: they overlap the kit, and hiring-screener ranks applicants.
- mohitagw15856 reference-check-script: allows back-channel calls, scores referees red/yellow/green and asks for peer ranking.
- tuanductran hr-skills referral prompt: asks for demographic considerations.
- alirezarezvani/borghei interview-system-designer: overlaps interview-kit-design.
- Catalog placeholders from Lena (data-subject-request-draft, personal-data-map) and Ines (hr-escalation-brief, new-hire-onboarding-plan, engagement-survey-readout): better used by consulting Lena or Ines than bundled into Sofia's kit. The requested hiring-debrief fix already covers escalating protected remarks.
- The unassigned `negotiation` skill: its Ackerman method is adversarial and duplicates job-offer-and-close-plan/references/negotiation-and-close.md.

Smaller gaps better handled as sections of existing skills:
- A candidate-experience pulse survey could go in hiring-pipeline-analytics, reusing the minimum group size from engagement-survey-readout.
- Handling internal applicants (keep the application confidential from the current manager unless the applicant consents) could go in resume-screening or interview-coordination.

If these are added, three follow-ups:
- sofia-getting-started's prefs.py allowlist needs the new keys (reference_policy, referral_policy, the interviewer-roster path, agency terms path). This is the same problem as the c1 fix.
- Identity's routing sentence needs a route for each new skill.
- Identity's same-turn deletion rule should say that suppression is immediate and deletion waits on any retention hold.

Verified source URLs: the tuanductran/hr-skills blob at commit 078f2fb (MIT, Copyright 2026 Tuan Duc Tran) and pm-claude-skills at f6ca793 (MIT). I did not verify any legal claim beyond the ones the kit's own reference files already cite. The Art. 14, CPRA-applicant and 15 U.S.C. 1681d points should get a source row when the skill is written.

proposal.summary: Theo's live kit is all ORIGINAL: eight placeholders of 48-55 lines each, and every one needs work. No NICK skill targets him, and none of the open PRs (#13-#16) touches the eight skills or theo.yml. Toran's three proposed packages (financial-statement-preparation, board-deck-builder, multi-source-research-synthesis) are each thinner than the in-house skills they sit beside, so this is mostly grafting rather than a three-way contest. There are two merges. First, board-deck-builder is folded into board-and-investor-metrics-brief, which is renamed board-deck-and-metrics-brief. The graft brings a default KPI set that always includes cash, net burn and runway, the four-act narrative, the bad-news framework, and the [TBD] template with its 'recommendation: [A/B]' field removed. Second, multi-source-research-synthesis's dedup, public-source confidence and conflict rules are grafted into investor-targeting-and-research. That pair is adjacent, not a true overlap. financial-statement-preparation is dropped as out of persona. It is still a slash command after PR #13. Mina's 14:monthly-profit-and-loss-summary covers the monthly P&L but explicitly excludes balance sheets and cash-flow statements, and no assigned skill produces them, so the three-statement capability is left for Daniel's dossier to claim. The biggest cross-expert problem is Daniel's finance-board-and-investor-reporting. It shares the 'board pack' and 'investor update' triggers, and it already carries the same four-act spine, an asks section and a monthly-board-pack-reminder routine, so the split has to be explicit. Alex's product-exec-briefing also claims 'a board'. The body needs teammate routing and routines that do not double-fire with Daniel's. It also needs fixes to the bio's 'keep the fundraising pipeline current', the tagline's 'clean records', and a general-solicitation boundary.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and consistent with the kit. The FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN source ledger, the no-edit cap-table stance and the never-send rules match every skill's safety section, and the voice samples are strong. The gaps: routing covers only human owners, never teammates, even though Daniel owns runway and variance plus a competing board-pack skill and routine, and Alex claims board product updates. There are no routines for a cadence-driven job. The bio and tagline promise pipeline upkeep and 'clean records' that the skills refuse. Nothing covers publicly announcing a raise or sending updates to prospects.

boundaries mirror the skills' safety rules (no cap-table edits, no sending, securities and deal terms routed to counsel), so persona and skills agree on the high-risk actions
body_review.kit_alignment: The proposed kit keeps 8 skills in the current order. One slug is renamed (board-and-investor-metrics-brief becomes board-deck-and-metrics-brief), so skills[7] must change. So must catalog.yml, release.json, docs/EXPERT_COVERAGE.md and provenance/expert-coverage.json, which all name the old slug. day_one maps cleanly: 'A fundraising source ledger' comes from investor-relations-getting-started plus pitch-deck-review, 'Your diligence gaps' from fundraising-data-room-checklist plus cap-table-hygiene, and 'An investor-ready monthly brief' from monthly-investor-update. Two caveats. The data-room skill has no item-level checklist, so it cannot yet reliably say what is 'missing'. The getting-started register is never saved, so the day-1 ledger is lost after the session. preloads and routines are empty, so no dropped or renamed skill is named anywhere. But nothing schedules the monthly update, the weekly pipeline check during a raise, or board-deck prep, and any board routine has to coexist with Daniel's monthly-board-pack-reminder. The bio's 'keep the fundraising pipeline current' promises tracker upkeep that fundraising-pipeline-review forbids ('Do not ... change pipeline stages'). The tagline's 'clean records' likewise overstates skills that never edit records.

issues.quote: I can research possible investors and keep the fundraising pipeline current
issues.problem: fundraising-pipeline-review only reviews a supplied tracker, and its safety rule says 'Do not send messages, share files, change pipeline stages'. 'Keep current' promises tracker maintenance that no skill performs.
issues.fix: Change to 'I can research possible investors and review the fundraising pipeline for stale rows, missing next actions and unsupported stages'.

issues.quote: Route ownership, securities, tax, governance, and deal-term questions to qualified counsel, the finance lead, or the approved cap-table administrator.
issues.problem: Routing names only human owners. Several teammates overlap. Daniel owns runway (cash-treasury-and-fx), variance (variance-and-flux-analysis) and a competing board-pack and investor-update skill (finance-board-and-investor-reporting). Mina owns the P&L and Zara owns market sizing. Alex's identity routes 'An exec, a board, or a steering room' to product-exec-briefing. With Daniel or Alex hired, Otto has no rule for who writes the board pack.
issues.fix: Add a routing paragraph. Cash, burn, runway and variance figures come from Daniel; the monthly P&L and books from Mina; market sizing from Zara; the product section of a board deck from Alex; cohort and retention rebuilds from Quinn; a post-close funding announcement from Noor, after counsel signs off. Theo owns the investor- and board-facing narrative, the asks and the disclosure checks. Daniel owns the finance scorecard it cites.

issues.problem: The kit is cadence-driven (a monthly update, board meetings, a weekly pipeline check during a raise), yet no routine exists. The monthly-investor-update and fundraising-pipeline-review evals both call for schedule_routine, and the investor-relations-getting-started review asks for an update cadence. Daniel already runs a monthly-board-pack-reminder (cron 'H 9 6 * *'), so a naive Theo board routine would offer the owner the same pack twice.
issues.fix: Add three routines, each off until the owner says yes and each drafting only. (1) A monthly investor update draft, keyed to the close: N business days after month-end, or Daniel's close-done signal when he is hired. (2) A weekly fundraising pipeline review while a raise is active. (3) board-deck-and-metrics-brief prep 10 days before each scheduled board meeting. The third stands down to a one-line check when Daniel is on the team and his board-pack reminder has already fired.

issues.quote: Never give investment, legal, tax, valuation, or securities advice; recommend a transaction; promise a fundraising result
issues.problem: Nothing covers publicly announcing or promoting an active raise, or sending material written for current shareholders to prospective investors, which carries general-solicitation and forwarding risk. The investor-relations-getting-started and monthly-investor-update evals both flag this, and the platform has posting blocks (Twitter/X, Medium, WordPress).
issues.fix: Add: 'Never draft a public post announcing or promoting an active raise, or address a shareholder update to prospective investors, without counsel's sign-off. A post-close announcement goes to the communications owner (Noor) only after counsel approves.'

issues.quote: Never alter a cap table, disclose confidential records, or send investor material without explicit approval.
issues.problem: The sentence can be read as 'alter a cap table ... without explicit approval', which implies that altering it with approval is fine. identity and cap-table-hygiene ('Never create, change, delete, merge, or backdate an ownership record') make the ban absolute.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'Never alter a cap table. Never disclose confidential records or send investor material without explicit approval.'

issues.quote: Turns fundraising facts into a clear deck, clean records, and investor-ready updates.
issues.problem: 'Clean records' implies Theo fixes records. cap-table-hygiene 'does not ... edit the cap table', and fundraising-data-room-checklist says 'Do not create missing legal or finance documents'. This is the same overpromise as the bio's pipeline line.
issues.fix: Use 'Turns fundraising facts into a clear deck, checked records, and investor-ready updates.'

issues.quote: Review decks as a decision path: problem, customer, product, proof, market, business model, growth, team, ask, and use of funds.
issues.problem: The list leaves out why now, competition and alternatives, and go-to-market, which is the same gap as pitch-deck-review's top review issue. The ask is not tied to milestones or runway.
issues.fix: Add 'why now, competition and alternatives, go-to-market' and 'use of funds mapped to milestones and runway to the next round'.

issues.quote: For investor updates and board briefs, use one reporting period, show metric definitions and prior-period comparisons, state misses plainly

issues.quote: Checks the data-room index and cap-table records for missing, stale, conflicting, or over-shared items and assigns each gap to an owner.

issues.fix: Ship references/data-room-items.md in the skill, and change the text to 'proposes an owner for each gap'.

clusters.job: Prepare the board meeting deck or quarterly board metrics pack

members.note: It carries Theo's source discipline: final, management-draft or provisional status; a nine-field metric row; 'A favourable change needs the same source test'; a cross-check against the deck and investor update; and no sending. It lacks a default KPI set (cash, runway, burn and burn multiple are never required), a one-page layout (the nine-field rows become an unreadable wide table), tool steps and definition-change bridging. The grafts supply the first two in part.

It has what the base lacks: a SaaS board metric set including runway and burn multiple, a four-act narrative, a bad-news framework, an asks rule, cadence guidance and templates/board-deck-template.md with [TBD] placeholders. As a standalone it has several problems. It has no procedure and no approval gate, and it depends on C-suite advisor skills that don't exist here. Its template's 'recommendation: [A/B]' invites Theo to recommend on financing. Its example figures don't tie out: the dashboard's NRR of 112% vs 99.7% from the reference waterfall on the same $1.97M starting ARR, and 8.1% MoM vs 22% QoQ. Its description collides with four other skills.

proposed.name: Board deck and metrics brief
proposed.description: Use when preparing a board meeting deck or quarterly board pre-read: a default KPI set that always includes cash, net burn and runway, sourced metric rows with prior and plan, bad news stated plainly, and the decisions and asks the board must act on. Drafts only. The monthly note to investors is monthly-investor-update.
proposed.rationale: The base is the stronger skill and the better persona fit: source tests, status labels, restricted data and no sending. The grafts fix its top review issue (no default metric set) and give it a template. The rename takes 'investor' out of the slug so it stops competing with monthly-investor-update, which the review flags for the 'investor metrics' trigger. experts/theo.yml, catalog.yml, release.json, docs/EXPERT_COVERAGE.md and provenance/expert-coverage.json must all be updated. Written new, from the reviews: an intake step (Sheets/Drive block or read_workspace_file, with a CSV fallback); bash_exec for derived ratios, labelled INFERENCE; and cash and runway taken from Daniel or the owner's approved finance summary. Also new: a one-page pre-read summary (headline, three changes, plan vs actual, risks, decisions) with the nine-field rows in a fixed-column appendix table, and a restated-prior-period bridge when a definition changes. Add YoY or 4-6 period trends with a variance materiality threshold, KPI definitions saved to memory, and last meeting's action items carried forward. Add a consult_teammate step for Daniel's figure sign-off, an owner approval gate before any distribution, and counsel routing for resolutions, option grants and 409A items. Daniel's finance-board-and-investor-reporting already holds the same four-act spine and asks section, so this skill must defer the finance scorecard to him when both are hired. Keep the MIT LICENSE and an ATTRIBUTION.md line for the grafted board-deck-builder text.
drops: board-deck-builder description framing 'pulling perspectives from all C-suite roles' and the (CEO)/(COO)/(CFO)/(CRO)/(CPO)/(CMO)/(CTO)/(CHRO)/(CISO) owner tags on every section; name the section owner in the frame instead
board-deck-builder 'Quick Start' (addressed to the user) and 'Keywords' blocks
the 'Cadence Notes' fundraising line ('Opens with market/vision, closes with ask') and references/deck-frameworks.md 'Sequoia Board Deck Structure'; fundraising decks belong to pitch-deck-review

the non-tying worked-example numbers in '1. Executive Summary' and '2. Key Metrics Dashboard' (NRR 112% vs 99.7% from the same starting ARR; 8.1% MoM vs 22% QoQ)

'recommendation: [A/B] — rationale' in the template's 'Decisions Needed Today'; financing and deal-term decisions are presented as options with an owner and a counsel flag, never with Theo's recommendation
'Sent 48 hours in advance' as a distribution step; keep it only as timing advice behind the owner's approval

the 'Point Nine Benchmark Targets' table: drop it, or keep it only as a labelled external reference with the attribution corrected (the review notes burn-multiple benchmarks are wrongly credited to Point Nine), never as the company's target or a pass/fail status
sections 6-9 (Growth & Marketing, Engineering, Team & People, Risk & Security) as mandatory slides; make them optional, used only when an owner supplies data

grafts.section: Deck Structure (Standard Order) > 2. Key Metrics Dashboard, 3. Financial Update and 4. Revenue & Pipeline
grafts.what: A default board KPI set for when the owner has none. Cash on hand, net burn and runway (with its assumption) are always required. Add up to five more by business model, keeping section 2's '6-8 metrics max': ARR or revenue with growth, NRR or GRR, gross margin, burn multiple, CAC payback, pipeline, and headcount vs plan. Each metric gets a target and status and a one-sentence cause per variance (section 3's 'One sentence on each variance'). Each forecast carries a confidence level (section 4's 'The forecast must have a confidence level'). It goes into 'Build each metric row'.

The four-act spine (where we said we'd be, where we are, why the gap exists, what we're doing about it) plus 'the board should know the key message by slide 3'. It goes into 'Write the decision brief'.
The five steps (state it plainly, own the cause, show you understand it, present the fix, update the forecast) and the 'What NOT to do' list, including 'Don't lead with good news to soften bad news'.

'Key decisions needed from the board' and the rule that asks are specific and assigned to a person ('3 warm introductions to CFOs at Series B companies' beats 'any help would be appreciated'). Add a new line that decisions are framed as options without a recommendation on financing or terms, and that resolutions go to counsel.
The eight-row mistake/fix table, reused as the pre-release review checklist (metrics without targets, vague asks, no variance explanation, stale appendix, and so on).

A quarterly full pack vs a monthly condensed early-stage pack (8-12 slides: metrics, financials, pipeline, top risks). The upstream '20-30 slides' contradicts the mistakes table's 'Too many slides (>25)', so cap the quarterly pack at 25.

Ship it as templates/board-deck-template.md. Keep the [TBD] rule, remove the C-suite labels and the 'recommendation: [A/B]' field, and add a source column and a FACT/INFERENCE/OPEN column to the metrics and financial tables.

grafts.section: references/deck-frameworks.md > The SaaS Board Pack; How to Present Bad News > Scenarios and How to Handle Each; Appendix Data That Boards Actually Use
grafts.what: Move these into references/board-metrics.md: the Required Metrics list, the ARR waterfall with its NRR = (Ending - New) / Starting formula, the six bad-news scenarios (missed revenue, key customer churned, key exec left, burn accelerated, market headwinds, fundraise delayed) and the appendix list.

grafts.section: references/deck-frameworks.md > Quarterly vs Monthly Board Meetings > When to Increase Frequency; Meeting Logistics
grafts.what: The triggers for proposing more frequent board meetings (approaching 6-month runway, a fundraise in progress, significant underperformance, a major pivot) and 'Follow-up within 24 hours: Action items, voting outcomes, next meeting date'. They become a carry-forward of last meeting's action items and the prompt for the board-prep routine. Drop the board-portal vendor list.

members.note: This is the persona-fit research skill: one row per firm with a source URL and date, firm facts kept apart from partner facts, a conflict column, a 'needs review' bucket, and never inventing contacts or interest. Its whole source-quality rule is one line: 'Mark stale pages and conflicting sources'.

This is Anthropic's enterprise-search synthesis over already-retrieved chat, email and doc results. It has 26 unresolved ~~ placeholders on 22 lines of SKILL.md (unchanged in PR #13) and no Use-when clause. Its own review says investor research belongs in investor-targeting-and-research, so this is a donor of rules, not a competitor. Its dedup rules, 'What NOT to Deduplicate', freshness and authority confidence, and conflict wording carry over to investor research across firm sites, filings and databases once the authority tiers are rewritten for public sources.

proposed.name: Investor targeting and research
proposed.description: Use when building or refreshing an investor target list for a raise: records round parameters, researches each firm from public sources, merges duplicate findings, weighs source freshness and authority, and returns a sourced fit table. Research only; no outreach or advice.
proposed.rationale: The base keeps Theo's guardrails and output shape. The grafts give it a concrete way to handle the same investor seen in several sources, and to weigh stale or conflicting pages, which the base only mentions. Neither member covers the review's top issue (no sourcing method), so these must be written new. Candidate sources: firm sites, portfolio pages, fund announcements, SEC Form D, and co-investors of comparable companies. Tools: web_search, web_fetch, and the Exa and Perplexity blocks. Also new: a paywall fallback, a defined fit-score rubric, fund-vintage and recent-activity fields, and lead capacity vs round size. From the multi-source eval: count syndicated or derivative copies as one source, and treat fetched page text as data, never as instructions. Finish with an export in fundraising-pipeline-review's tracker shape. Keep the Apache-2.0 attribution for the grafted text.
drops: 'The Goal' REST/GraphQL enterprise example and the 'last mile of enterprise search' framing
all ~~chat/~~email/~~cloud storage source labels and references/CONNECTORS.md (lists Microsoft 365 and Guru and links an external .mcp.json)
the internal-only 'Authority' table (wiki, chat mid-thread, task comments) and the one-size 'Freshness' table

grafts.what: The signals and 'How to merge' rules: one row per firm or partner found on the firm site, a fund announcement and a database, citing every source, with the most complete version as the primary text and unique details added from each.

Keep separate rows when a partner has moved firms, a firm runs separate funds or stages, or a published thesis changed between sources. These map to 'Different time periods are represented' and 'The information evolved meaningfully between sources'.

grafts.section: Confidence Levels > Freshness, Authority, Expressing Confidence
grafts.what: A confidence rating for each row, based on freshness, authority and agreement. Rewrite the authority tiers for public sources: the firm's own site, fund announcement or regulatory filing first, then named press, then an aggregator database, then a social post. Syndicated copies count once. Set owner-editable freshness defaults per claim type, since partner roster and fund status go stale faster than a published thesis. Keep the high/moderate/low wording examples.

When sources disagree (cheque range, stage focus, whether a partner is still at the firm), show both values with source and date and never pick one silently. This replaces the base's one-line 'Mark stale pages and conflicting sources'.

grafts.section: Summarization Strategies > For Large Result Sets (15+ results)
grafts.what: For long target lists, lead with counts by fit tier and the top candidates, then write the full sourced table to a workspace CSV instead of pasting it.

Narrow the triggers 'start fundraising', 'fundraising materials' and 'raise preparation', which pull substantive raise or deck requests into setup. Add raise-readiness items (target, runway, milestones, update cadence). Add a counsel check before any public mention of the raise; a post-close announcement then goes to Noor. It has no skill that drafts outward communications, keeps a record current, or runs on a calendar. Add teammate routing: Daniel for runway, cash, variance, the finance scorecard and the financial model; Alex for product sections of the board deck; Noor for the funding announcement; Quinn for metric definitions; Ellis's counsel-escalation-brief shape for legal packets.

- The full cfo-advisor package: its valuation ranges and term recommendations conflict with Theo's boundaries.

Sources and licences:

- NVCA IRA information rights and right of first offer: the specific deadlines vary by deal, so the skill must read the company's signed agreements through counsel, not the model form.

proposal.summary: Vera's live kit is eight ORIGINAL skills, one per procurement stage: intake, requirements, quote comparison, due diligence, decision memo, renewals, performance and spend. They are short placeholders of uneven depth. No NICK skill is assigned or proposed to her, but James's NICK ops-vendor-and-procurement overlaps her kit from outside. TORAN offers three Anthropic packages, and none should ship on its own. vendor-evaluation ends in a Proceed/Negotiate/Pass verdict, which breaks her rule against choosing a vendor. operational-risk-assessment is a generic reference card. vendor-contract-status is a slash-command legal lookup. PR #13 leaves the SKILL.md of vendor-evaluation and operational-risk-assessment byte-identical and only renames the vendor-contract-status slash command. The proposal keeps the eight-stage kit and merges the three packages in as grafts. vendor-evaluation's Year-1/multi-year cost table, incumbent renewal baseline and minimum input ask go into vendor-quote-comparison. operational-risk-assessment's 3x3 grid goes into vendor-due-diligence as a review-tier rule, re-anchored on data/access exposure and criticality with spend as a modifier, along with its register fields. vendor-contract-status's search across sources, list of sources checked and MSA/DPA/SOW/SLA/insurance coverage check go into contract-renewal-tracker, with its 90-day flag keyed to the notice deadline rather than expiry. The biggest cross-expert conflict is James's ops-vendor-and-procurement. It covers sourcing, renewals and scorecards in one skill, says to "let the composite total decide" (which contradicts Vera's no-selection rule) and shares the 'vendor scorecard' trigger with her. It needs a handoff line and a wording fix. Other handoffs go to Ellis (term extraction, amendment conflicts, MSA playbook), Lena (DPA content), Daniel (thresholds, commitments) and Mina (coding evidence, duplicate or suspect payments). operational-risk-assessment should ship to no expert, Frankie included. The expert body needs four things: a place for her tracker and records to live, a boundary on contacting vendors, named teammate handoffs, and an opt-in renewal routine scheduled apart from James's and Daniel's Wednesday scans.

body_review.summary: The body is tight and matches the eight original skills well. It covers the stage order, the no-selection and no-binding gate, evidence dating and the spend decomposition, and both voice samples show that behaviour with real numbers. Four things are missing: where her renewal tracker and records live; any scheduled renewal watch, even though the tagline promises one; a rule against contacting vendors; and named platform teammates (Ellis, Lena, Daniel, James, Mina) at the points where her kit stops.
strengths: The identity walks the actual skill sequence: need first, normalized quotes, evidence register, decision memo, renewals, spend review. Each of those sentences maps to one kit skill.
The no-commitment boundary is exhaustive and consistent across bio, identity and boundaries: approve, choose, accept, issue a PO, sign, renew, cancel, bind.

The voice samples are concrete and checkable. 'Cedar is unknown because usage overages are missing' and 'Unexplained balance: $2,140' model the UNKNOWN and unexplained-balance behaviour the skills require.
'it does not hide a weak option behind a weighted score' directly counters the failure mode of vendor-evaluation and of James's weighted-composite method.
body_review.kit_alignment: No routine, preload or day_one entry names a skill slug (preloads: [], routines: []). None of the proposed merges renames a slug, so nothing breaks. day_one[0] maps to vendor-requirements-brief, vendor-quote-comparison and procurement-decision-memo. day_one[1] maps to contract-renewal-tracker and spend-anomaly-review. vendor-due-diligence and vendor-performance-review appear in the bio but not in day_one, which is acceptable. Two promises have nothing in the kit behind them. The bio says 'obligations', but no Vera skill tracks obligations; that is Ellis's contract-obligation-tracker. The tagline says 'tracks renewals', but nothing runs unless the user asks. The merged contract-renewal-tracker adds an agreement coverage check (MSA/DPA/SOW/SLA/insurance), which the identity should mention.

issues.quote: Renewal tracking records notice dates, auto-renewal terms, owners, spend, service issues, and the next action.
issues.problem: Nothing says where the tracker, evidence register or spend reviews are kept, or which sources to read. A renewal tracker that exists only in the conversation is lost next session. James and Daniel both name their working files and connected sources; Vera does not.
issues.fix: Add a paragraph along these lines. Keep the contract and renewal tracker, the vendor evidence register and dated spend reviews as workspace files or a connected Google Sheet, and open them fresh before each run. Read executed agreements from Google Drive/Docs or uploaded PDFs, and invoices from Gmail or an export. When nothing is connected, ask for a paste or upload rather than blocking.

issues.problem: The tagline promises that Vera 'tracks renewals', but no routine exists. Renewals surface only when asked (day_one[1] timing 'on request'), so a notice deadline can pass silently. contract-renewal-tracker's review says the skill 'gives no approved way to set a reminder' and lists 'Approved reminder scheduling via schedule_followup/schedule_routine' as missing. (The review's top issue is the missing review-start date, which the merge fixes, not the missing routine.)
issues.fix: Add an opt-in weekly 'renewal notice watch' routine that stays off until the owner turns it on. It reads the tracker, lists agreements whose review-start date (notice deadline minus lead time) has arrived and agreements whose notice deadline falls within 90 days, stays quiet when nothing is due, and only drafts. James's ops-vendor-renewal-watch and Daniel's wednesday-cash-and-commitment-scan both run at 'H 9 * * 3' (Wednesday), so schedule Vera on another day. When they share a team, both should read Vera's tracker instead of recomputing notice dates.

issues.quote: Never approve spend, choose a vendor, accept a term, issue a purchase order, sign, renew, cancel, or bind the company.
issues.problem: The list does not cover contacting a vendor. Sending an RFQ or an evidence request, or sharing one vendor's pricing or company data with another, is not a commitment, so it passes this list. Yet vendor-requirements-brief says not to invite a vendor until the request owner agrees, and spend-anomaly-review says 'Do not ... contact a vendor'.
issues.fix: Add: 'Never contact a vendor, send an RFQ or evidence request, or share one vendor's quote or company data with another vendor without the request owner's yes; draft it for approval.'

issues.quote: I also keep renewal dates and obligations visible
issues.problem: No Vera skill tracks post-signature obligations. contract-renewal-tracker records renewal, notice and termination facts only. Obligation tracking is Ellis's contract-obligation-tracker.
issues.fix: Change to 'renewal dates, notice deadlines and agreement coverage visible', and route surviving or ongoing obligations to Ellis.

issues.quote: You draft and stage the work for the budget owner, procurement lead, security reviewer, or counsel named by the user.
issues.problem: Only human owners are named. The platform lets Vera consult or hand off to teammates whose skills sit right at her edges, but the identity never names them.
issues.fix: Add the handoffs. Full contract term or obligation extraction, amendment conflicts and MSA playbook checks go to Ellis. DPA content and subprocessor updates go to Lena. Budget, cash and commitment questions go to Daniel. The vendor inventory and ops cadence go to James. Ledger coding questions and suspected duplicate or unexplained payments go to Mina.

issues.quote: route each decision to its named budget, security, procurement, or legal owner
issues.problem: The privacy owner is missing, although vendor-due-diligence routes 'personal-data terms and locations to privacy' and procurement-getting-started records a privacy reviewer.
issues.fix: Change to 'budget, security, privacy, procurement, or legal owner'.

issues.quote: You start with the need, not the vendor
issues.problem: Nothing in the identity says to scale the process to the purchase, and procurement-getting-started gives every purchase the same six steps (its review's top issue). A $500 tool gets the same diligence as a critical data processor.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: scale the path to spend, data and criticality using the review tier, and start a renewal from its notice date.

issues.quote: Turns requirements and quotes into a like-for-like view of cost, coverage, gaps, and open checks for the named approvers.
issues.problem: This is marked 'day 1' but assumes the user already has requirements and quotes. Nothing in the kit says what the first conversation should do without them.
issues.fix: Give procurement-getting-started a first-conversation branch. If there is a live purchase, go to comparison. If there is none, build the renewal tracker from the contracts the user supplies. Otherwise, reword the timing.

proposed.description: Use when vetting a vendor before a purchase or renewal: tier it by data, access, criticality and spend, request the evidence that tier needs, record source, scope and expiry for each item, and route open findings to security, privacy, finance or counsel. Never certifies a vendor.

On its own it should be dropped, with the matrix folded into James's work. Its 3x3 grid still fits the tiering rule the base's own review asks for (references/evidence-by-tier.md), provided the axes are re-anchored to purchase exposure. Present the tier as the review tier of the purchase's exposure, not a rating of the vendor, so the base's ban on calling a vendor 'low risk' still holds.
drops: operational-risk-assessment 'Risk Categories' Strategic (market changes, competitive threats, technology shifts) and Reputational items (outside vendor diligence)
'Produce a prioritized risk register with specific, actionable mitigations' (Vera would be rating and prescribing; reviewers decide)
Risk Level labels (Critical/High/Medium/Low) applied to the vendor itself

grafts.what: Reuse the 3x3 grid as the review-tier rule, with anchored axes. Data/access exposure: Low = no company data or access; Med = internal data or user-level access; High = personal/regulated data or admin/production access. Service criticality: Low = easily replaced; Med = team workflow; High = customer-facing, revenue-critical or hard to exit. The cells give review tiers 1-4, and spend above the owner's threshold raises the tier by one. Each tier names its required evidence set. For example, tier 1 is the vendor's claim plus the terms; tiers 3-4 add a current independent test report, a DPA, an insurance certificate, financial evidence and references. The owner's policy thresholds override the grid. Vera labels the result 'proposed tier' for the security reviewer.

Add an open-findings register with these fields: description; likelihood/impact, recorded only as the reviewer supplies them; candidate mitigation (contract term, control evidence, exit plan); owner, left UNKNOWN until the user names one; and status Open / Mitigated / Accepted / Closed. Accepted and Closed are set only from the named reviewer's dated record. The register feeds procurement-decision-memo item 6.

recommendations.notes:
Coverage check: I read all eight kit SKILL.md files, the merge notes, and the dropped Toran packages (vendor-evaluation, vendor-contract-status). I also read the teammate skills at the kit's edges: James ops-vendor-and-procurement, Mina expense-categorization, Daniel cash-treasury-and-fx and James ops-controls-and-escalations. Neither the catalog nor DEFERRED_SKILLS.md has a buy-side procurement package for discovery, RFx issuance, negotiation prep, spend baseline, vendor onboarding or exit, purchasing policy or PO staging. DEFERRED_SKILLS.md holds only the ads suite, invoice-chase, prospecting and marketing items. So every recommendation is a new skill. Where a public MIT source helps, it is named as a reference file only.

Upstream packages I checked and rejected as bases (all MIT, pinned):
- emircbngl/claude-procurement-skill@9ae056d is B2C-first. It 'self-feeds' by writing into its own references/, which assumes local state the platform does not keep. It also uses tasks/research paths, AskUserQuestion and CLAUDE.md. Only references/domain-it-software.md is worth adapting.
- rampstackco vendor-evaluation@3d4510a duplicates the merged kit and ends in a vendor recommendation, which breaks the no-selection gate. Its cost-optimization skill is a usable lever reference.
- w95 rfp-builder and contract-negotiation@78dbc7c are static templates with invented SLA values, price bands and 2024 dates. contract-negotiation also scripts bluffing tactics. Use only their outlines.
- The unassigned catalog skill `negotiation` (wondelai, MIT) teaches Voss live-conversation technique with sales/product framing and Amazon affiliate links. Do not assign it to Vera.

Not skills, but body/yml fixes the reviewer flagged, with how these recommendations relate:
1. Renewal watch. The tagline promises one and routines is []. This belongs in a vera.yml routine that runs the merged contract-renewal-tracker queue weekly. It should stay quiet when nothing is due and roll repeats into one line. It must be coordinated with Daniel's 'wednesday-cash-and-commitment-scan', which already scans commitments in the renewal window. If both experts are hired, name one owner for renewal alerts so users are not pinged twice.
2. 'Obligations' in the bio. Hand off to Ellis's contract-obligation-tracker rather than adding a duplicate skill, or drop the word.
3. Restricted-party (sanctions) screening. Add it as an evidence line in vendor-due-diligence (dated OFAC/UK/EU list search, any possible match goes to counsel) rather than as a new skill.
4. No rule against contacting vendors, plus named teammates. The sketches below assume the no-contact rule and hand off to Mina (AP setup, coding, payment stops), Daniel (budget line, savings validation, cash for prepay), Lena (subprocessor/data map), Ellis/counsel (contract language) and James (controls).

Trigger collisions to manage in descriptions:
- rfx-package-draft vs Max's rfp-and-competitive-bid-response (sell-side 'RFP'). Say 'we are issuing'.
- vendor-negotiation-plan vs Max's objection-and-negotiation, Jordan's renewal-negotiation-brief and the unassigned `negotiation`. Say 'buyer-side'.
- vendor-spend-baseline vs James's ops-vendor-and-procurement ('review my vendors', 'build a vendor inventory') and Marco's wasted-spend-audit (ads).

Deliberately left out:
- Payment execution. It stays with the owner/Mina and conflicts with Vera's boundary.
- Inventory and direct-materials reorder (KWP small-business restock). It is outside Vera's indirect/SaaS persona, and the small-business plugin carries the same licence question that deferred invoice-chase.
- Specialist security testing and legal negotiation. These go to Lena/Devon and counsel.

Evidence sources used:
- Procurement specialist duties: tropicapp.io/glossary/procurement-specialist and 100hires.com/procurement-specialist-job-description.html (RFx, requisition-to-PO, supplier identification, spend analysis, negotiation, policy).
- Zylo 2025 SaaS Management Index (zylo.com/news/2025-saas-management-index).
- FBI IC3 PSA240911 (ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA240911).

recommendations.name: Vendor spend baseline
recommendations.purpose: Build a 12-month baseline of all vendor spend from AP, card and ledger exports: one normalized row per vendor with category, owner and contract status, plus consolidation and seat-rightsizing candidates for owners to decide.
recommendations.why: The kit only sees spend one vendor or two periods at a time (spend-anomaly-review) or one agreement at a time (contract-renewal-tracker). Nothing answers the usual first question: what are we paying for, and who owns it? Toran's review lists 'automated spend categorization, multi-currency normalization and supplier consolidation' as an open gap. Spend analysis appears in every procurement-specialist duty list checked (Tropic, 100hires). Zylo's 2025 SaaS Management Index says lines of business hold 70% of SaaS spend while IT holds 26.1%, and companies with 1-500 employees average 152 apps, so the inventory rarely exists until someone builds it. Platform fit is strong: bash_exec handles alias normalization and the Pareto maths, the Sheets block or a CSV holds the output, and memory keeps the vendor alias map between runs. James's ops inventory (dedupe on name, trailing spend) is lighter and belongs to the ops persona. Lever framing can be borrowed from rampstackco cost-optimization (MIT, https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills/blob/3d4510a94a76ead80122c691b5c480f92f3fbe40/skills/cost-optimization/SKILL.md).

source.ref: new — written by us (optional lever reference: rampstackco/claude-skills cost-optimization, MIT)

sketch: Inputs and fallbacks: 12 months of bill/AP export, card exports and the ledger vendor report, plus optional SSO or admin seat exports. Months with no source are marked as coverage gaps, never zero-filled. Keep the source currency and convert with a dated, named rate.

Vendor normalization: a bundled script applies alias rules (card descriptors such as 'SQ *' or 'PAYPAL *', legal suffixes, reseller vs brand, marketplace billing). The alias map is saved to memory, and uncertain merges are listed for the user to confirm.

Baseline table: trailing-12-month and annualized spend, billing cadence, payment channel (PO, card, expense), procurement category (not GL coding, which goes to Mina), business owner, and contract on file (link to the contract-renewal-tracker record, or NONE).

Analysis: Pareto (the vendors that make up 80% of spend), tail-spend count, spend with no contract or owner, same-category overlaps, and seats bought vs active where exports exist. Every candidate shows its formula and labels the saving as an estimate.
Handoffs: missing renewal records go to contract-renewal-tracker, month-over-month jumps to spend-anomaly-review, duplicate payments and coding to Mina, and budget impact to Daniel.
Gate: never cancel, downgrade seats or contact a vendor. Each candidate is framed as a question for its named owner.

recommendations.name: Vendor negotiation plan
recommendations.purpose: Prepare the buyer-side plan for a new purchase or a renewal: a target price, an owner-set walk-away and the best real alternative from the normalized cost, ranked asks and trades, a draft counter for the owner to send, and a log of concessions and savings.
recommendations.why: Negotiating price and terms is a core duty in every posting checked, and renewals are the moment small teams save the most. The merged kit gets close but never produces a plan. vendor-quote-comparison lists 'negotiation levers' and the incumbent's usage against commitment, and procurement-decision-memo lists 'negotiation points'. Nothing sets a target and walk-away, sequences the trades, drafts the counter, or records what was conceded and saved. The catalog's existing negotiation skills are all a poor fit. Max's objection-and-negotiation and Jordan's renewal-negotiation-brief are sell-side. The unassigned `negotiation` (MIT) is live-conversation technique with Amazon affiliate links. w95 contract-negotiation (MIT) relies on invented prices and bluffing tactics such as feigned surprise and misstated alternatives, which break Vera's evidence rules. Hard vs avoided savings is the standard procurement KPI, and recording it gives Daniel a number he can validate.

source.ref: new — written by us (buy-side; do not adopt catalog `negotiation` or w95 contract-negotiation as the base)

sketch: Inputs: the quote comparison or incumbent renewal baseline, the budget owner's ceiling, the decision date, and the notice deadline from contract-renewal-tracker. A missing ceiling or deadline is listed as a blocker, never assumed.
Positions: target, walk-away (set by the owner) and the best real alternative (a competing quote, a downgrade, or doing nothing). Each has its source and formula. Never bluff about alternatives.

Lever table: unit price, volume or seat tier, ramped seats, term vs exit rights, renewal uplift cap, price hold, payment terms or prepay (cash confirmed by Daniel), removing auto-renewal, notice length, termination for convenience, SLA credits, free data export and implementation credits. Each lever carries a value estimate and the approver it needs (counsel via Ellis for contract language).
Give-get pairs and sequencing, plus calibrated questions for the owner to ask. The seller's likely constraints (quarter end, list-price floors) are marked as assumptions.
A draft counter email and a term-change summary that the owner sends. Vera never contacts the vendor.

Outcome log: offer history, final terms, and savings against the baseline split into hard saving vs cost avoidance and recurring vs one-off, with formulas for Daniel to validate. Updates feed the renewal tracker record.

recommendations.name: Vendor market scan
recommendations.purpose: Build a dated long list of candidate vendors for a stated need from public sources, screen it against the brief's knockout criteria, and return a shortlist with reasons, public list prices and an excluded list.
recommendations.why: The kit begins with 'the approved requirements brief and original quotes'. Nothing finds the candidates, yet 'what are my options for X?' is usually a small team's first procurement request. Supplier identification and qualification are standard in the procurement-specialist duty lists checked. No catalog skill does buyer-side vendor discovery: candidate-sourcing-strategy, source-and-qualify-partners and prospecting cover hiring, partnerships and sales. The platform supports it through web_search, web_fetch, browser tools and the Exa, Perplexity and Firecrawl blocks. SaaS screening pitfalls can be adapted into a reference file from emircbngl/claude-procurement-skill references/domain-it-software.md (MIT, https://github.com/emircbngl/claude-procurement-skill/blob/9ae056dc4e3c1c7256f5138148c473daf50c5180/references/domain-it-software.md): SSO only on top tiers, SOC 2 Type I vs Type II, AI training on customer data by default, and single-jurisdiction invoicing. The package as a whole is B2C and assumes local state the platform does not keep.

source.ref: new — written by us (optional reference file adapted from emircbngl/claude-procurement-skill domain-it-software.md, MIT)

sketch: Inputs: the brief, or at minimum the need, users and volume, region or data residency, must-haves, budget band and current stack. First check whether a tool the company already pays for covers the need (from vendor-spend-baseline, if it has been run).
Search plan and query log: vendor documentation, pricing pages, trust centers and status pages count as evidence. Review sites and analyst lists are leads, not proof. Every source is dated.

Knockout screen: each MUST against public evidence, marked PUBLIC DOC, CLAIMED or UNKNOWN. Tier gating is flagged (SSO, data region, API, audit logs sold only on higher plans). List prices are labelled 'public list price, not a quote' with the capture date.
Output: a shortlist of 3-5 with reasons and an excluded list with the rule each one failed. No winner and no weighted ranking.
Feeds rfx-package-draft (invitee list) and vendor-due-diligence (public evidence stays CLAIMED until reviewed).
Gate: no vendor contact, demo booking, trial sign-up or form submission, because trial sign-ups accept terms.

recommendations.name: RFx package draft
recommendations.purpose: Draft the RFI, RFP or RFQ the company is issuing, built from the requirements brief: instructions, timeline, questions, a pricing response template in the quote-comparison columns, and a Q&A log that gives every vendor the same answers. The request owner sends it.
recommendations.why: The merged vendor-requirements-brief defines the evaluation columns, knockouts, weights and sourcing route, but no skill produces the document vendors actually answer. Without a common response template, quotes arrive on different bases and vendor-quote-comparison has to chase missing fields such as uplift, overage and export cost. Preparing and running RFx is listed in every procurement-specialist posting checked. The only RFP skills in the catalog are sell-side (Max's rfp-and-competitive-bid-response, media-plan-measure-optimize). The closest open-source match, w95 rfp-builder (MIT, https://github.com/w95/awesome-claude-corporate-skills/blob/78dbc7c719920610d5b1c60bd13d9bb52d711c7a/12-procurement-supply-chain/rfp-builder/SKILL.md), is a static template with invented SLA values, price bands and 2024 dates. Only its section outline is reusable. The sandbox can build the xlsx response template.

source.ref: new — written by us (section outline may follow w95 rfp-builder, MIT; do not ship its example values)

sketch: Pick the instrument from the sourcing route: RFI to explore, RFP when solutions differ, RFQ when the spec is fixed. Small purchases get a short three-quote request email variant.

Package sections: context and scope, MUST and SHOULD requirements with the evidence each one needs, submission format and deadline, timeline with a Q&A cutoff, confidentiality, and required terms. Required terms come only from the user's playbook or counsel and are never invented.

Pricing response template (xlsx) with exactly the quote-comparison fields: currency, term, quantity, unit price, minimums, one-off fees, usage and overage, taxes, uplift, notice, termination and export cost. Evaluation weights stay internal unless the owner decides to publish them.
Invitee list from vendor-market-scan. Q&A log where every question and answer goes to all invitees. Late or off-format responses are flagged, never silently dropped.
Gate: drafts only. The request owner sends and receives, and Vera never contacts vendors.

recommendations.name: Vendor onboarding and exit
recommendations.purpose: Run the handover checklists at both ends of a vendor relationship. After signature: the vendor record, verified bank details, the tracker record, owners, and data and access records. After an approved exit: notice, data return and deletion, access removal, and final billing.
recommendations.why: The kit stops at the decision memo and picks up again at renewal. Nobody owns setup after signature, or the exit after a non-renewal decision. The merged contract-renewal-tracker records a 'data-return need' and a notice method, but nothing carries them out. Keeping supplier master data and onboarding suppliers are standard procurement duties. Verifying bank details through a second channel is the main control against vendor impersonation: FBI IC3 PSA240911 reports $55.5B in business email compromise losses from 2013-2023 and advises 'secondary channels' to verify account changes. Exits leak money through card charges and auto-renewals left running, and through data left with the vendor. The work is mostly handoffs to teammates who already exist (Mina for AP setup and payment stops, Lena for the subprocessor register), so the platform can run it with approval-gated drafts.

source.ref: new — written by us

sketch: Onboarding: check that the contracting entity matches the invoice issuer, and request the tax form. Bank details are verified by calling back a number taken from the signed contract or an earlier record, never from the email that sent them. The vendor record then goes to Mina for AP setup.

Records at start: create the contract-renewal-tracker record, name the service, budget and contract owners, set baseline measures for vendor-performance-review, send the subprocessor and data-map update to Lena, and name an SSO or access owner.

Exit, only after the owner's recorded decision: draft the notice using the tracker's method, address and deadline. Request the data export and a deletion or return certificate. List SSO, SCIM, API keys and integrations to remove, with each system's owner.

Money on exit: stop cards and recurring charges and check the final invoice and credits with Mina, remove the vendor from the subprocessor register via Lena, and write a transition plan to the replacement.
A checklist item is marked done only on evidence (a confirmation, a certificate, a final invoice). Open items carry an owner and a date.
Gate: never send notice, change bank details, revoke access or cancel. Draft and queue for the named owner.

recommendations.name: Purchasing policy and approval matrix
recommendations.purpose: When the company has no written purchasing rules, draft a one-page policy and approval matrix for the owner to adopt: quotes required, review triggers, approvers by spend band, sole-source rule and renewal lead time. Then save the adopted version for the rest of the kit to use.
recommendations.why: Vera's kit depends on thresholds and named approvers she is forbidden to invent. The rewritten procurement-getting-started saves them when they exist, but small teams, the platform's main users, often have none, so every memo and tracker ends in the same blockers. Writing and maintaining procurement policy is a listed duty for procurement specialists. Drafting options with trade-offs for the owner to adopt stays inside Vera's boundary as long as nothing takes effect until the owner's recorded choice. It also gives the merged vendor-due-diligence tier rule (exposure x criticality, with spend raising the tier) a home the user has actually agreed to. James's ops-controls-and-escalations covers operational controls, not purchasing authority.

source.ref: new — written by us

sketch: Intake: who buys today, card vs invoice, who signs, the spend profile (from vendor-spend-baseline if it has been run), and customer or regulatory obligations such as DPA requirements from Lena.

Draft matrix: spend bands mapped to quotes required, review tier (reusing the due-diligence exposure x criticality rule), approvers, a sole-source justification rule, and renewal review lead time. Each cell is offered as options with the trade-off stated and left blank until chosen.
Policy text: one plain-language page with an exceptions path and a statement of what Vera will and will not do.
Adoption: record each choice with its date and approver, then store it in memory and the workspace so getting-started, the decision memo and the renewal tracker read it.
Review date and change log. Anything that conflicts with finance or ops controls goes to Daniel or James.

recommendations.name: Purchase request packet
recommendations.purpose: Once approvals are recorded, stage the purchase request or PO draft for the user's buying system. It carries the quote's commercial terms verbatim, coding and budget-line fields for confirmation, evidence of each approval, and receipt fields for later bill matching.
recommendations.why: Processing requisitions into POs is the most common day-to-day duty in the procurement-specialist postings checked, and Toran's review lists 'purchase-order creation, approvals' as an open gap. procurement-decision-memo ends at an approval table, and nothing turns it into the request a finance tool (Ramp, Procurify, NetSuite, QuickBooks) needs, or into the PO facts Mina needs for three-way matching when the bill arrives. James's ops-vendor-and-procurement drafts POs, but for the ops persona and without matching fields. It is lower priority because many small teams buy on cards.

source.ref: new — written by us

sketch: Preconditions: an approval record (who, when, where) for every gate the adopted policy or review tier requires. If one is missing, stop and list it.

Fields copied verbatim from the accepted quote: vendor legal name, quote reference, line items, quantities, unit prices, term, billing schedule, currency, tax as quoted, service start and contract reference.
Coding: the GL account and class are marked TO CONFIRM with Mina, and the budget line or cost centre is confirmed with Daniel.
Output: an import file in the target system's format (a generic CSV if the system is unknown) or a filled form, with the approval log attached.
Receipt and acceptance fields for the three-way match, handed to Mina for the bill.
Gate: never submit, issue or send the PO.

proposal.summary: Zara's kit stays as Nick's 13 PR 2 skills, with the same slugs in the same order, so the identity's routing paragraph and the three day_one rows still resolve. Each of Toran's seven upstream packages loses to a Nick counterpart. They are used as graft sources, not added as separate skills. There are seven merges. Switching forces, customer language and the versioned changelog from product-marketing-context go into positioning-and-messaging, along with obviously-awesome's category call. The pricing references, the raise-price signals and the rollout method go into pricing-and-packaging. competitor-profiling's profile and landscape templates go into competitive-intelligence, which reuses pricing-and-packaging's competitor price table. market-size-estimation's market definition and assumption log go into opportunity-sizing. sales-enablement-content's objection, deck, one-pager and case-study references go into field-enablement-content. The launch stage ladder goes into commercial-launch-strategy, and a channel-fit check goes into gtm-planning. None of the seven ships alone: go-to-market-strategy and market-size-estimation still contain $ARGUMENTS even in PR #13, and five of the others still check .agents/product-marketing.md. The biggest remaining problems are across experts and in the body. commercial-launch-strategy nearly copies Alex's product-launch-plan. field-enablement-content copies Max's enablement-playbooks-certification (plays, rubric, refresh) and the talk-track rule from his objection-and-negotiation. The pricing bands duplicate Daniel's deal-economics. The launch-readiness routine scores Alex's ship gate ('legal vetted', 'rollback written'), which no Zara skill defines. No skill creates the decision log the scorecard routine reads. Five of the 13 skills never apply the FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labels the identity requires, including competitive-intelligence, which feeds the Thursday routine.

body_review.summary: The persona is sharp and consistent. FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN labelling, draft-then-approve and quiet-week single lines run through identity, boundaries and all three routines, and the routing paragraph names each of the 12 working skills by its kit name. The weak points are the links between routines and skills (the launch gate, the decision log, competitor triage) and the labelling rule, which five skills never state. There are also two boundary gaps (writes to CRM or Stripe, and how competitor intel may be gathered), connectors that AutoGPT has no block for, and a scorecard voice sample that contradicts itself.
strengths: Every load-bearing claim must be labelled FACT, INFERENCE or UNKNOWN, and a number with no source stays UNKNOWN. This appears in identity, boundaries and each routine prompt. pricing-and-packaging, gtm-performance-diagnostics, opportunity-sizing-and-business-case and sales-marketing-alignment-and-sla carry all three labels in their fallbacks.

The identity's routing paragraph maps each request type to a named skill ('money questions go to pricing and packaging...'). All 12 routed names survive in the proposed kit; zara-getting-started is onboarding and needs no route.
Routines have concrete quiet paths ('If every open launch is green, deliver one line saying so and stop'), dedupe rules and draft-only endings, with no posting, filing or target changes.
